reviews.comment: Pretty easy class. A 89 is an A. Entire grade is 3 exams and a few practice problems a week. Easy GEP, take her
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This class was taught asynchronously and was pretty easy. I recommend reading the text in addition to watching her lecture videos, because the tests ask questions that require understanding, not just memorization. Also use myeconlab's practice quizzes to study (ones with green background) because a lot of the questions there, show up on the tests!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: During COVID, this prof was asynchronous. All exams and homework were online thru MyEconLab and pretty simple. Lectures were just her reading from slides, you won't really need the textbook.

Econ 101 during COVID: This class is the definition of easy. If you need an easy online class here it is. All homework and exam questions are online. The exam was given through Pearson with no webcam or respondus lockdown browser. Not good for people who want to learn the material but great for people who want an A

Prof. Bing Ma's tests are fairly easy. However, if you actually want to learn from a lecture, do not take her class. All she does is reading off of her PowerPoint and using her old examples over and over. So, if you are not an independent learner and want a fun class, you should avoid this class. Also, she is not often available to her students.
Super easy class. Online, but the professor always sends out emails before the exams on exactly what needs to be covered. Not an overwhelming amount of work either.

Professor Ma's class is incredibly straightforward. Pay attention in lecture or read the textbook (you likely won't need to do both), do the homework, lightly review, and the tests should be relatively easy. By the way, she doesn't post *any* grades on Blackboard, so make sure to keep track of your scores!

Shes good at teaching so there's no complaints. She said you should read the book but don't do that. Go to class and write down literally everything and do the practice problems she gives out. Solid experience. You def gotta work though
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Her lecture is very clear. She doesnt take attendance every time, but sometimes she give students class work for attendance. There are only three exams in the course.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Very easy, unlimited hw attempts and easy topic.

Professor Ma's style of ECON 101 is perfect. Lectures on Thursdays, TA sessions that end early on Tuesdays. Weekly online questions and three big tests. Multiple choices are definitions or quick math. Free response questions are exactly like examples in class. There's plenty of time for questions and she makes it clear what content is covered.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Dr. Ma is a great professor! She clearly states what you will be tested on and gives review days before the exam. She also gives out study guides which consist of key words that you need to know for the exam which were also very helpful. She also does a lot of examples in class which was very helpful for the exams. Just study her lectures slides!
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Dr Ma is one of the best professors I have ever had. Her lectures are crystal clear and she clearly explains what she will be testing you on. Day before exams are review days and she tells you exactly what to study. However, the entire grade is 3 exams, and she is a bit hard to reach outside of class. Made a very difficult class interesting.
Wonderful teacher!! One of the best I've ever had. She also talks about the difficulties that she had learning certain concepts and this has shaped the way she teaches others.

Best professor for Econ 311. Goes at a pace where you actually understand stuff. Go to her review sessions, she tells you what's on the exam basically. Go home and redo the problems you did in class (study set questions) because they will show up on the exam but just in a different format.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--Caring

reviews.comment: She's a decent professor. Good with explaining topics but horrible with going over graph examples and connecting concepts because she rushes through em, reviews aren't in-depth, no study guide samples,She'll tell you the topics and the rest is up to you. Another downside is she doesnt post grades. Keep her 1st survey, final exam get 10pt to redo.
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: She's a professor that actually cares about how you learn. Brings up modern topics, encourages thinking, explains the content well and on time, helps students with questions, and it's an overall easy course with simple exam questions. Only downside is that she doesn't post grades online. Regardless, I highly recommend taking her.
She is very nice and clear with explaining things but none of the grades are accessible online and our final grade was not posted until the last possible day.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Dr. Ma is a great professor. She encouraged class collaborations as well as group work to solidify each lesson. She hand back each exams in class so you will know what grade you got and why you got the grade. The effective teaching methods really helped and got me to have interest and enjoy a subject I had always felt remorse.

She doesn't post grades online which is very annoying. Showing up to her class is not mandatory. If you show up on the days of the review and keep up with the homework, you'll be fine. She reads from the slides usually.

She does not post any grades online at all, which is very frustrating if you want to know how you're doing in the class. Her lectures are also pretty useless since the notes are sparse and she just reads off the slides verbatim. But no cumulative final and you can learn all the material by doing the hw and in-class examples.
Best teacher for ECON 101. Really well taught

Her style of teaching changed my entire attitude towards her class. Her lectures are a MUST because the examinations are based on the class materials she covers in class. The class has fairly tough exams, but you'll find that the homework and extra credit can level out for a decent grade boost.

She's very patient and nice professor, but her class is tough if you don't show up every time and take notes of the lectures. Following the slides and go over the problem sets you will pass this class.

ECON311 is a tough course. However, she really taught well and she was as clear as possible while still making sure you learned all of the information. The exams, although difficult as it supposed to be for ECON 311, were always fair. Highly recommend.

If you do bad in this class, it's not her, it's you. Her lectures are crystal clear and she makes the exams as straightforward as possible. This is definitely a less theory, more math type of class but it's really easy if you put in the time to study. Best professor for 311.
One of the best teachers at UMBC. She genuinely cares about students grades and will try to clarify everything. Exams are exactly like her study questions.

Just use her lecture notes. Material is pretty easy. First two exams were just about what you would expect, but final exam had a lot of stuff not covered on her review, so be careful about that. Decent professor.

Don't buy the book. I didn't touch it. Use her lecture notes (posted online) as your notes and you'll be fine. The first 3rd of the class was review of STAT 351, the rest was intro to Econometrics. Pretty simply if you follow her lectures. She tests somewhat based on her Problem Sets, so get those down. Listen to her when she reviews  too.

Econ421 is really a statistics course and therefore tougher than most econ courses. Fortunately she waters the material down somewhat. Overall nice lady and cares for her students. Occasionally she can be moody or difficult to understand. However, she teaches using ppt slides that are pretty clear. Study them/do problems. Book is super confusing.
Three tests each 30% of grade. Last 10% is attendance and involvement. She hands over the material very well and is very organized.
Very organized and clear. Great teacher highly recommend.
Not at all theoretical. Makes us write papers instead of taking exams and goes really easy on the grading. Allowed me to correct a huge error with my final paper days after I gave it in.

Seriously hard to understand, heavy accent. But she writes a lot of what she says on the board, so its not impossible to understand. No need to buy the book. Make sure you go to the review session before the tests, she pretty much gives out the essay questions there

Also for 467. Frequent attendance=extra credit. Don't need book unless you skip class, lecture is very good. 467 way easier than 421. She is very nice and even funny once you get to know her, but it won't seem that way at first. Just answer her questions, go to class, and she will like you. Plus these habits tend to yield high grades.

Most interesting class of the semester! Very little reading, clear idea of what was going to be on tests, no papers, no homework. Easy and fun! Even though attendance isn't counted - Ma offers extra credit to students who are in class via pop quizzes.

Professor Ma is great - a very nice lady with a unique (cute) sense of humor. The class examines the U.S. Health Care system from an economic perspective. There are three exams, which I aced by taking good notes and putting in a couple hours study time. No papers, no final, no need to buy the text, interesting material... this was my kind of class!
pretty easy teacher. not as boring as others. grading is pretty hard tho. If I had a choice, I would've choosen C.Yuan(who's her husband i believe)cuz he is a easy grader...
There's not much econ in it, no real math, not tons of graphs. Go to class, write what's on the board, study. 3 tests total. You will only be tested on whats on the board. Go to class!

She is a good professor. I got a C on the first exam. I did not do any extra credit work because I got flu (there are like 2 chances to get extra credit. I missed both). However, she still did not let me submit the extra credit after deadline. I got an A on the class project and got an A on the final exam. So I ended up getting an A in the class.
Easy teacher, but hard class. She  goes over what's on the exam, but it is still hard. Have to attend lecture to do well. Dont need to buy the book. Final was HARD. Easy to get a B or a C...
Pretty easy class, just copy what she writes on the board and you'll get an easy a.

Don't let her scare you off on the first day... she gets better. She really cares and wants students to understand the material. First two tests were fairly easy; just do the study questions. Watch out for the final. It was tough worth and 50% of your grade.
Very fair professor. Grade based on 3 exams. If you go to class and pay attention during the review sessions, it's very easy to get an A in the class.

Bing Ma is a great professor. She seemed irritated the first few weeks, but since then has gotten so much better. She teaches the material so that  you can understand it. Do her practice problems and the exams will be very simple for you. Her "exam review" classes are really helpful too. Her lectures are online but def. still always go to class!

She really tries to make the class understandable.  She goes through exactly what will be on the test and they aren't tricky. If you pay attention and go to class, she's very willing to help you out.  If you don't, she'll ridicule you in class ;P

OK that person had her for one day before making that review. She has gotten better but still pretty condescending. She expects a bit much which is weird cuz she used to teach at UCLA and I thought they were dumb.

The class is honestly interesting, but he can be quite rude. We do a lot of in class discussions, and when your answer isn't correct he is explicitly like nope you're incorrect. There are several students that he particularly doesn't like and is quite rude to them. He also does not give super clear instructions for assignments.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: This class seem like an easy A but the professor has a harsh, high pressure teaching style and frequently puts students on the spot with little time to respond. If your answer isn't what he expects, he can be openly rude which creates a very uncomfortable classroom environment. Emails are rarely answered, making it difficult to get clarification.
Mean professor, will put you on the spot and call you out if you don't know a certain answer.
Great class! Dr. B. Teaches history different from other professors. More important stuff going on today and stuff. Movies too
Cool class. We went over stuff I never had in other classes. Take home exams were pretty easy. Would take it again!
Pretty easy class and easy “A.” Talked about readings which were cool. Frankenstein, 1984, Dune. Highly recommend for those who want WI.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Dr B is great. I was a bit skeptical of his use of history to describe disease but it made what would have been a boring class okay. Will definitely take him again.
Great class. It wasn't the sort of name and date things we did more discussions. Got cool at the end. Midterm and finals were most of the grade
Cool class. Pretty easy workload based on group projects. Generous grader if you show up and participate.
Not your typical history class. Fun discussions and we even watched documentaries. Looking forward to my next PBHL with Dr B

Dr. B. was great. I've never taken a history class at UMBC. We didnt do like names and dates or anything. instead we just sort of talked about biger ideas in history and how things relate to the present. Some students had trouble with the readings and Dr. B. shortened the work and assignment and even assigned us a documentary to watch instead.

Cool stuff and a fun teacher. Who knew the history of public health could be exciting (yawn, right?). A few of the other students didnt read so that occationally brough things down here and there. lookin forward to taking him in 340 next semester.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Group projects

reviews.comment: Dr. B is great! I highly recommend this class to STEM students. We did a lot of deep thinking about the sciences and read some cool sci-fi books like flowers for algernon and 1984. Really like Frankenstein. It was a bit awkward at times tho as a few of the students didnt read the book but pretended to. All in all lots of fun. See you in teh spring!

great class. i loved all the history stuff dr. b. put in the lectures. fgave so much extra credit that I don't have to take the final. highly recommend. i woudl take him again next semester but i don't need those courses to graduate.

Cool class. Lots of reading. I was cool though. Stuff like Frankenstein and 1984. Pretty kind and chill professor too. I ended up with so much extra credit that I just kind of showed up for the last few weeks nand didn't have to do any homework. Highly recomment
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Group projects

reviews.comment: Very good at facilitating discussion about the multitude of readings across the semester. Not good at all in terms of posting clear instructions for assignments in a timely manner, and there were multiple occasions where he would wait to upload a discussion post until Saturday (due Sunday). Group/final project was poorly-explained but great.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Openly rude to students during class discussions when given an answer he thinks is wrong or doesn't understand. Will not excuse absences for any reason besides jury duty. Does not communicate instructions clearly or let students know when expectations have changed. Difficult to approach due to both his attitude and lack of communication (ironic)

More of an internship than a lecture. we mostly did group projects and stuff in class. one downside, the text book wasn't used very much and I could have used that cash for something else. Still a lot of fun. taking again next semester for a history course.

I had Dr B. in another course this semester. Both were cool but both had a lot of reading. In this one though we read classics like Frankenstein and 1984 so it was pretty fun. I liked the books more than I thought I would. Friends in other schools had courses like this and read more. I think some of the other rating just didn't want to read?

If you want to read and talk about some big ideas this is the class for you. I've had other history classes and it was a lot less reading than those but it was more than we usually do in public health. He tried really hard to bring everyone along and gave lots of extra credit. I'm pretty sure I'm getting an A as I have a 110% going into the final
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment:
Lots of Blackboard discussions and LOTS (3-4 books and other things) of reading as well. Actual classes are mostly discussion, and he expects you to show up and participate. 

Group project was hard. Posted guidelines less than a week before the presentation date, with almost no detail for what he actually was looking for.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Group projects

reviews.comment: He is an absolutely terrible professor. You'd think an online public health history class would be easy, but it's not. He assigns too many readings and expects you to interpret them exactly his way. He's rude, condescending, and never replies to emails. Even real excuses count as absences. Grades harshly and barely gives A's. Avoid this class!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Not the best PBHL professor, he makes things too difficult and he is very degrading.

I wanted to take this class for fun because, I wanted to learn more about the history in Public Health, but he made the class extremely difficult and unenjoyable, maybe he should think about teaching graduate level students instead of undergrads
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: I did not learn much from this class, He makes the class really difficult, randomly picks on you, if you don't know the answer he will give you a zero, answer the questions correctly and in 5sec or you won't pass this class. no recordings, no notes, etc. he won't even repeat questions because "it is a waste of everyone time" Don't take him!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: He gives us 5 second to answer the prompt and if you don't there goes your participation points. He said that If we get a B that means that we are doing good and he usually doesn't give A's out. He said he doesn't care if you get hit by a bus. The only way to get an excused absence is if you have jury duty. DO NOT TAKE HIM!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Group projects

reviews.comment: Overall my experience with this professor was horrible. He was incredibly inflexible when it came to any absence including excused absences. He was constantly belittling and talking down to his students. He requires a ridiculous amount of reading for each class. He talks extremely fast and refuses to post notes or PowerPoints. Avoid if you can.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: He makes the class far more difficult than it has to be, with too many restrictions that are generally really strict, and the exam and quizzes are written (essay format) on the blue book.

A great class but quite different than my other courses (mainly bio and public health). Each we read a chapter from a book on a different part of us history of public health. There was alot of reading but only a midterm and final to worry about although he graded attendance and how much you talk. I am planning to take him again in the spring.

This is a very reading heavy class. Sometimes 30 plus pages due a week and he expects extensive notes and understanding of the material. Overall, he is rude and does not treat students with care and respect, often telling us that we are too dumb to have our own ideas. The class was interesting but he was not.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: A fun class. We kind of bounced around philosophy, sociology, and history. It was sort of your typical 100 level class but with a bit more writing (it was a WI course so that's to be expected). Attendance (and cameras on) is mandatory but there's lots of extra credit if you miss a class. Would DEF take again. (Dr. B. is kind of dorky but funny).
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Taking the summer class right now. Class is MUCH more fun than I thought. Lots of guest lecturers and conversations. With the extra credit I'm going into the last day with an average over 100%. He's a bit passionate and goes off on subjects a bit but its entertaining to watch.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: A kind and understanding professor. Another reviewer that said he gives 0's for absences--not true, but his "attendance policy" gets confusing. If ur absent, Dr. B. gives the whole class a chance at extra credit. Doesn't care if ur absent. If you want a teacher going over the top to make sure you get an "A," this is the one for you.

Rate My Professor really failed me with this one. Dr. Bonneau does not excuse absences for sickness or religious holidays (attendance points taken off). He expects a specific format for projects/papers but does not provide you with any kind of guidelines until days before due date. So disappointed by the lack of understanding in this professor.

I took the Human Context of Science and Technology with Dr. B this semester. It wasn't like any course I've taken at UMBC but that was okay. We had discussions about crazy stuff like Frankenstein, Forsensic Science, and CRISPR. I think I did well becuase I answered questions. He grades on participation. Good guest lecturers too, esp for bio majors.

My favorite class of the semester (Im bio). It was a bit more work than I expected from a 100 level class, but it covered my WI requirement. Also, Dr. B. was really into the subjects and made the subjects easier to understand. There was no final paper. e just did a presentation with our group. (Blah... group work). The guest lectures were cool foo.

While he is a good professor and cares about his work, I found the class boring. I don't believe we needed to meet for the class which lasted 2 and a half hours with no breaks on many occasions. I personally did not learn anything and could have done all the work on my own without meeting with the professor weekly.

I took this class to check off my WI requirement but am starting to like it. We have some pretty entertaining discussions and write up two quick one page papers per week. One is a paragraph long and another two paragraphs long. Lots of EXTRA CREDIT, too (We are about 2/3rds of the way through and I have a 115% average). Funny guy, too
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: A great class. A fun mix of movies and reading. Well, a LOT of reading, but it was a summer class. Dr. B. managed to mix up things with guest lecturers and debates. I took the class for the WI requirement but am interested in the HCST minor.

Class was a "capstone" course for seniors in History and the HCST program and revolved around a long research paper. Was a bit nervous about that but Dr. B. put me (and the other PBHL students) at ease and worked with us individually. Also, REALLY liked the weekly discussions about current issues in public health seen through historical examples.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Took the class to check off my WI req. Class was an intense winter class and online, but discussions were cool and he was pretty fair in his expectations. Got us thinking about ethics and stuff going on in the world. Guest speaker was pretty great too.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: I'm a math major and took the class to fulfill a prerequisite. I didn't expect the history of science to be interesting, but Dr. B. is an entertaining lecturer (and could be a stand up comic if he tires of teaching). We read a lot more than I'm used to (but I suppose that's normal for history courses). Essay exams. Would definitely take him again.

Second time taking Bonneau. Watch out because he is not always clear on his expectations for assignments, but don't be afraid to ask questions. Be prepared to read and write a lot. We read 3 small books this semester on top of having small bi-weekly assignments and a research paper. Bonneau is a really nice professor though and easy to work with.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Dr. Bonneau is great! I'm not sure what one of the previous raters was talking about, it was great when he sometimes moved classes online, and doing readings is just part of being in a history class... But he's a great professor! I'm taking his class again this coming fall!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: A fun research-oriented class. We saw a project though from start to finish. The group work wasn't half as bad as I've seen it in other classes and I enjoyed the readings.

Took this course to fulfill a req (not a hist major) and loved it. Great lectures and fun activities. Not sure what the person below meant--wasn't a hybrid class but did have online activities? Some reading but Dr. B. is good about giving students his time and there are plenty of opportunities for extra credit. Will be taking him again in the Fall!

Does not post lectures online, and forces students to come to class claiming there could be a quiz any day.  The random switch to hybrid halfway through the semester did not help the class.  Gives out more work (reading and assignments) than what should be given for a 100 level course.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Great class so far.

Easily my favorite class at UMBC. The lecture were interesting (especially the Art History stuff) and the discussions were super relevant to everything going on today (epidemics, grief, etc). A few of use weren't sure were ready to be "live" again after Covid but Dr. B. was kind and patient. Wish I was a history not a bio major!

if you do not like participating in group discussions, AVOID THIS CLASS! All assignments were sent through email. grades were always put in late or incorrectly. he rambled too long during class, often going over class time, then would yell at us for not participating. no exams but many essays (easy though). no homework. lots of reading.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Bonneau's requirements were really straightforward. You turn in responses to works of art were along with responses to readings. They're very short in length and you don't even have to do one each week. His lectures are really important to attend, but he makes the lectures interesting and fun. 10/10 Great professor!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: He's not a bad professor but the class is pretty rigorous in terms of writing (it is a WI) but he is a reasonable grader and gives you room for creativity and improvement. You do have to pay attention and do multiple readings which are not too bad. One thing I was not a fan of was the wait time in emails and how hard it is to contact him sometimes.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: A great class with a fun instructor. The quantitative stuff was a bit intimidating at first but blended well with the larger research and left everyone better historians for the trouble. Going to put Dr. Bonneau on my thesis committee right away.
A genuinely caring professor who cares deeply about his home discipline (history). Lectures were entertaining, even over Zoom, and paired well with the readings. Would ABSOLUTELY take Dr. B. again.

Good professor. Was more lenient (probably because of COVID) and so he dropped a few assignments for everyone. Gives extra credit and has opportunities for students to go the extra mile. Participation is part of your grade, so you need to show up and ask questions/give answers. Overall a fun and understanding professor!
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Group projects

reviews.comment: Dr. Bonneau is an amazing professor with great lectures. Attendance & participation are a large part of the grade. At least one of an art reaction and reading reaction every unit, each 400-500 words. There is a group project where you lead a discussion based on lecture. Final project is a 10 min presentation & 3-4k word paper. Great class!
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: What a time for a class on the history of pandemics. Professor B was great. I loved how he brought together art and science to understand the subject matter. Just be prepared to talk in class--he seems to want to hear as much from you as you do from him!

Hes a great person! Although the books are mandatory, he makes sure you learn in every way possible so you can get a better understanding of it. My grade was only low due the writing intensive during the time of the pandemic. If you love writing/science, the class is for you!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Class was super entertaining. Make sure you do all the readings and essays. If you do a quality job on homework and show up to class you will get an A. Easy class but requires a lot of time outside of class. Professor Bonneau is super accessible and he will respond to emails right away. Great class, would definitely take this professor again!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: This could have been a boring class (the history of ancient and medieval science doesn't scream "fun"), but the prof was really into it and made it interesting. I especially liked how he paid attention to the class performance/comprehension and reduced readings if we needed to slow down and get through tough sections. Highly recommended.
So entertaining you forget that youre in class

I don't get the hate. Dr. Bustos is nice and a solid professor. He only got upset once when some students were not showing up at all except for exams, despite attendance being 20. It's a 400 level bio course, ofc its content heavy, but studying his slides is enough to score an A (85). He's not a tough grader, and no final, 4 midterms worth 80.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Dr.Bustos just doesn't know how to teach to put it plainly. There were 3 exams that were worth 20%, then a 4th exam worth 30%. The last 10% was participation/attendance which is based on the questions you ask in class and answers (he deems if they are good enough for points), ask him before but I just wrote questions and answers on paper b4 class.

I think Professor Bustos gets a bad rap. This class is conceptually hard (as is any bio class) but he's very lenient and nice. The grading = 4 exams and 10% participation. There is an automatic curve (85+ is an A). Tests are open note and participation is easy just talk and show up. He is very smart. Even though this class is hard I recommend!!
yeah he's terrible

Dr. Bustos's lecture notes were helpful but I found them too concise. So for each lesson, I took my own detailed notes using Lehninger's (I personally highly recommend utilizing the textbook). He is not the most easygoing or approachable professors out there but, he is an expertise in the field and there certainly is a lot to be learned from him.

Class didn't have a real textbook. Instead, prof wrote his own summary text. Worst thing I've ever read. Graphs and formulas are given no context, topics aren't explained with any depth. I brought these issues to him, he has the gall to tell me our generation "doesnt have the attention span" for textbooks. What does he think other classes give us??

Literally the worst. I'm a senior w/ a 4.0 and I loved chem & bio. One week into his class, I'm crying at my desk, surrounded by bio & chem notes from previous semesters and understanding nothing. Spent like 20 hours one week just trying to understand his review material, and he had the audacity to tell me I just wasn't trying hard enough. RUN!

He sets you up to fail then blames you when you do. Lectures have absolutely no clarity, the "textbook" is a crappy sparknotes-esque summary that doesn't explain anything. He puts things on tests that have never been taught! Has an insane curve (42% grade is a C) bc otherwise nobody would pass. Doesn't listen to student concerns. Feeser is better.

Professor Bustos was the worst prof. ever. He is also a very bad man to his students, often lashing out against them. He picks favorites and knows he can't be fired so uses inane methods to run his class. Nothing on the lecture material was on his exams. He had to curve because of how understandably poor his students were doing. Avoid al all cost

Not worth your time if you have a choice. Content from lecture is not on the tests - 4 tests are 72% of your grade. Goes on tangents bc he thinks he's funny, calls random people out to answer questions by jabbing the mic in their faces. Doesnt take criticism and says he can't get fired bc of tenure, people only pass his class bc he curves 20%.

He just reads the packets of lectures, wldnt've complained if it contained all we needed to know for exams(which r hard)(72%). Participation(10%) is on this website that is annoying but not hard(weekly). Mini essays(18%) not hard, annoying bc he writes smtn and tells you to write it a diff way. Learned nothing in this class, not for lack of trying.

Dr. Bustos is the worst professor Ive had at UMBC. Not because his class is hard, but because he is an awful man. He curses at his students and made participation hard for no reason. He yelled at us and has a small precious ego. Students learned nothing. Do not take a class with him, you will regret it.

I hated this class. Exams were hard but participation was harder. He wanted 105 students to participate and each student needs to say different things. If you say the same thing, It won't count towards your participation like what. Hated when people exploded the chat or complained about participation. Would never listen to us-always yelled at us.

I have never been so frustrated with a professor in my three years of college. This class is just a waste of my time. He only gives you a word doc as your textbook which is not sufficient to study from. Exam questions are sometimes from things we never learned before. His reasonings make no sense. Ridiculous.

1 of the worst profs Ive ever had & Im a senior. Extremely condescending. Always said to read the book, but tests were 100% from tests banks (textbook was useless). Ended up curving everyones grades at the end of the semester b/c didnt want to deal w ppls complaints. Learned absolutely nothing & instead spent most of my time on Khan Academy
reviews.rating_tags: Test heavy--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Infamous at UMBC for his arbitrary style and tough coursework. Class hates him and we hate him back. Can be charismatic at times, but is a bad professor overall. He inflates grades and makes the exams sound easier than they are. Don't listen to him. Study hard. Know your stuff. NEVER underestimate how difficult exams are. Always expect the worst.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Worst professor and class I have taken. Avoid at all costs. His grading system is flaud. His is horrible at getting grades back at a reasonable time. Poor organization. I truly have nothing good to say. Avoid this class if he is teaching it.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Dr. Bustos wrote questions on his take-home tests that were not understandable. He unfortunately chose to explain why he took points away on certain people's tests and not on others. His lectures during class had little-to-nothing to do with the textbook or his tests questions.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Worst professor I have had in the college up to date. He does not care to put any effort into the material that he teaches which is one of the reasons why his class is almost empty half the time. Irrational system of grading, and exams are taken completely from test bank. If you have a good memory you can get an A. No understanding required.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: Gets irritated with students easily, makes unreasonable demands, does not admit when he is wrong. He had horrible designed a system of pop quizzes that are very difficult and detailed. The only grade you get is based on exams and these quizzes. He is not willing to help students, and would much rather spend that time complaining about you instead.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: Your grade is heavily exam based, but his exams are super easy. Good professor, good class, happy GPA.
reviews.rating_tags: TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Grading is heavily dependent on exams, but exams are easy if you attend lecture. Lecture is formatted so that you're fully prepared for the exams. Material is hard, but he's accessible in office hours and really does care for his students success in the class. If you're confused, don't fall behind, seek help. The textbook helps a lot too.

Dr. Bustos truly cares about his students. He presents the lecture in a style that makes difficult material easy to master. Lecture isn't mandatory, but it really helps. Most of the exam questions are from material covered in lecture. Ignore the negative reviews as those 5 negative reviews likely represent the only unhappy students out of 200.

Any of the reviews before Spring 2018 can be disregarded. Bustos has ultimately changed for the worse by creating unfair quiz policies and showing little to no interest in the course as he solely lectured from the textbook and did not write his exams. He's stubborn and not open to any constructive criticism. Hopefully, he changes next semester.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Does not write his own exams and does not include anything from lecture. He changes how he teaches the course throughout the semester so hes kinda unpredictable. He will argue with you if he believes he is right even if its about asking for clarification.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: Teaches concepts, tests for trivia. Exams were multiple choice tests from the textbook publishers' question bank, and a lot of those asked for specific names and details - more than most people can memorize in one semester. Lecture notes were copied and pasted textbook. Understanding isn't rewarded. Cram the text into your head and pray to survive.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: It is a hard course so he understands students cannot memorize all the pathways but you have to try. The fact that he is funny makes the class a little less difficult and best part is his point base grading. If you show up in class as well as get close to the border points say between a C and B, he'll remember you&give you that B. pretty generous!

Dr. Bustos is a very good professor. Though he is very knowledgeable of the topic, he doesn't try to treat students like fellow biochemists. Instead, he makes it very simple for us, probably the simplest it can get. He is not detail oriented and doesn't make you cram the whole book. Also, he actually is funny. Take him, you won't regret.

Bustos liked some more than others. The syllabus was never finished. Class consisted of him going over science articles and randomly calling on students to answer questions. 4 short response/essay exams based off of the articles that were discussed in class, 3 of which were online. Most people got B's. You'd need a B avg on the exams to get an A.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Dr. Bustos may not be the most interesting professor to listen to, I agree and even he himself agrees. But when you show that you are interested in his class and do all of the work possible, he really does notice you. Of course, Biochemistry is not an easy course, but he certainly does make it easier with his grading curriculum,make sure to be avg
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: You CANNOT find any biochemistry professor better than Dr. Bustos. If you don't get A in his class, I'm sorry but you should quit studying, because he makes it very easy to get A.
He is a great professor

Bustos is a mediocre professor at best, just reads off the slides and doesn't make too much of an attempt to make the class interesting. Although a pleasant guy, he's not very approachable outside of class and is horrendous with replying to email. Finally, his grading system of 68% for an A is absurd, but nonetheless helpful to many students.
His point based grading system is a blessing! Thank you Bustos!
Bustos is a really kind and funny professor. His lectures are long but in the spring he gives breaks, and that always gets me back to focus.

Apart from his fun and friendly character, Dr. Bustos is a very good lecturer and he only asks about topics he has covered in class. There are five exams, each worth 35 points, you could take all and every point will count, but u could as well skip one and still get A. As long as you keep a C or a B in all exams, you get A overall. Amazing!!!!!!!!!

Dr. Bustos is extremely unhelpful.  I have visited him several times at his office to ask questions about the class and he does not want to help you at all.  He is very rude and unprofessional.  I don't even know why he is a professor if he does not want to help students.  I just stopped going to lecture and read the textbook instead.  Avoid him!

NO HW, No Quizes only 5 tests. Very hard. worst teacher i have had. Going to the lecture does not help. reading the book is soo much better than hearing him. he start a new sentence in the mid of the one he is telling and you get lost. doesnt explain clearly. not recommended unless u are willing to self study. I am serious!

He has changed a lot. Dr. Bustos loves teaching and helping students. Yes it is hard but thats because biochem is hard and requires a lot of self-studying. He is absolutely hilarious and makes lectures very interesting. I highly recommend taking his class but you need to study. He read his comments from previous semesters and adjusted to correct

Prof. Bustos is a nice professor. Biochem is difficult, just make sure you go through his ppt and also follow his guide to study, you will B easily. For those who wants to get A, you need to put more time to understand and remember more details about these cycles...

I have no idea about how his lectures were because I always snoozed in class(early 8 AM class!). I am here to tell you how I succeeded in his course. 1st, I read all the assigned chapters myself. 2nd, I answered the study guides he has distributed. I got a B+, almost an A, but hey, I passed. I can't say much about him, I never interacted with him.

He is terrible. The worst professor I have ever come across. He was never prepared for class and didn't teach at all. He doesn't know his materials and he is rude and obnoxious. DO NOT TAKE ANY CLASSES TAUGHT BY THIS PROFESSOR

Barely prepared for class, and not good at consistently grading exams or getting back to you if you have questions. Would rather fraternize with the students than teach effectively. Inflexible on deadlines without reason.

BIOCHEM- he's a nice person, and very helpful. He wants his students to do well, just attend class and study his slides. His slides are clear and he is clear on his exams as well. Biochem is hard, period, but he made it so much easier.
Dr Bustos is very helpful. He knows his stuff, so classes are fun and interesting. I hope he is around for a long time.

He is EXTREMELY rude and mean. He tricked the class for one exam, by telling us the wrong materials that would be on the exam ( the class average for that exam was 40 %). He NEVER replied back to my emails, when I asked him for help. He definitely had favorites. He knew very little about the material taught, but would  grade like he was a genius at
He is my advisor. He is so rude he made me cry.

A pleasant man. An all around lazy, rude professor. Hasn't written a new exam in 10 years, and so his lectures and exams don't always match up. He doesn't let students review exams.The last two weeks are group presentations. Has trouble communcating questions to students. Def plays favorites, so always say a nice "hello" to him;)

Bustos is an interesting guy. I had him for Biochem a few years ago and he wasn't a terrific teacher, but there are plenty of stories about him that you can get from people in the know. Ask anyone in the department about the "fiance" he once brought to a dept. Christmas party, for instance. Fair teacher, odd character.

I would have to say, he was one of the better teacher of bio that I have had...His first two exams were clear, the third and fourth exam have alot of ambiguity...or may be I didn't study enough. But you have to read alot by yourself. AND NEVER TAKE A HYBRID CLASS!
He is a very good teacher. He loves the stuff so it makes the class fun. He is very helpful in and out of class. He won't fail you, he would just ask you to drop the class nicely :)

He reads straight from the power point. To pass this class you must learn it ALL on your own and memorize it ALL. He is very rude to students, he insults most of them. He can't teach at all. Our 1st test was the Mon. after Thanksgiving- 12 multiple choice on 15 chapters! Our 2nd test was 2 weeks later (the final) 80 multiple choice.

Very bad professor. Doesn't teach anything. Tests things that weren't stressed in class. Must learn on your own to pass this course, or get anything out of it. Also, doubts about whether he even graded the final exam (the entire class guessed on most of it

This man reads off power point slides, you learn nothing in class. You must memeorize EVERYTHING. There are never any existing back exams. He is so rude to students, telling them they're stupid. You're afraid to ask questions in class.

Grades things super late. Reading responses due before class, yet he uploads them the day of class. Assigns super long readings, which are difficult to do especially with a full class load. While he is nice and I learned a lot from his class, I also felt like it was lacking.

Dr. Brooks runs his classes on the premise that students are adults who are responsible for their own education. If you put in the effort, you will learn so much. He is always ready to help with and discuss anything, from his own coursework, to outside projects, to future plans. Don't waste his time if you want to just coast through school:)
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Caring--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Good professor, but can come off unprepared or underwhelming at times. He will start the semester off very tough-sounding, saying that you can't make up work that you miss, but that will change by the end of the semester. Lots of videos, lots of reading. He does not grade ANYTHING until after the semester is over, except attendance.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Brooks was encouraging, he wants best for his students. In class discussions he is considerate in his responses in a refreshing and engaging way. Grades are slow to come back on assignments (mostly of reading responses, essays, and small quizzes) but he gives feedback & is accommodating and willing to help & explain.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Caring

reviews.comment: Kind of disorganized and confusing. A very nice professor and the content was interesting, but nothing was graded until after the semester, and I felt like my time and effort wasn't being respected. In class, we mostly just read from his PowerPoints and watched documentaries. Lots of writing, which was good for understanding but exhausting.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--So many papers--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Great discussions. Interesting documentaries. Flexible deadlines. Caring personality. Creative and safe space. I finally found books I enjoy reading through this class.

I learned SO much in this course. Dr. Brooks is an absolutely amazing instructor and really works with you wherever you are. He assigns a lot of reading (15 books in my class), but all of them are very up to date and you will learn a ton if you read everything. If you don't think you can handle that, I would suggest taking someone else.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--Caring

reviews.comment: NO idea why rating is so lowwork smart, not hard ppl! Take this class with expectation to get an A, not learn (sadbuttrue). He assigns like 53 books, but you don't ACTUALLY hv to read them all  just get quotes for the reading responses & ur good. Papers never correlate to the booksjust show up to every class, do assignments, and you'll get an A.

There is a lot of reading required for class but he gives you everything you need to be successful. As long as you do the reading and assignments on time, and attend class there is no reason why you should not get an A. He did post some assignments late but always gives extra time when he does. Lots of good insightful group discussions.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Inspirational--So many papers

reviews.comment: The reading material teaches you nothing about actually analyzing arguments but rather is an excuse to talk about subject matter close to him. Way too much reading to actually get any depth out of anything and by the end of the class I wasn't doing it at all and still passed because it isn't necessary. Group work every class that was pointless.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Group projects

reviews.comment: Great professor, you learn a lot even beyond the scope of rhetoric and English in this class. The group project is tricky, but if you ask him questions, you'll be just fine. The paper gets broken up into chunks which helps. Challenging, but super rewarding and fun. MUST do the reading
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Group projects

reviews.comment: Brooks makes you work for your grade but is accessible by email and office hours if you need clarification on any instructions that seem vague. The inclusion of African American rhetoric as the core of the class is an amazing opportunity to learn about texts and contexts outside the white canon. Open communication and try your best
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: I'm stunned that no one has mentioned the absolute worst part of his class: the 30-page paper that you work on all semester, on which he gives no guidance or feedback whatsoever. Also, there is a reading response due every class and missing even one nets you a B, per his ridiculous "grading" contract. Avoid this course at all costs.

Professor Brooks is a nice guy, but this class was incredibly poor. He used a vague contract and didn't grade anything until the end. His online syllabus is poorly laid out, and he changes it without explicitly telling you. The worst part is he runs this class like an African American studies class, not like an English class as advertised. :(
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Enjoyable man. Not an enjoyable class. It felt like he taught the class to only teach African-American studies, not English. I did not learn anything useful related to rhetoric, which the course was supposed to be focused on. The content was boring and unrelated to what I thought it would be. He also uses a grading contract. Avoid if you can.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--So many papers

reviews.comment: He's a nice guy but I haven't learned anything English related. He is obsessed with African-American oppression and lets his fascination with the topic corrupt the subject matter of the class. It feels like he only took the job to spread awareness to a topic close to him as opposed to actually teaching English. It is deliberate and he knows it.

His lectured are extremely boring. He barely teaches anything in class and will allow so much time to go by while you discuss with your peers. Plays very boring videos and podcasts. Terrible class! (He is a nice, intelligent professor) I dislike his teaching style though.

Professor Brooks himself is friendly and intelligent. However, the structure of his class is vague and different, the readings thick and unstimulating, and the projects/assignments unique but unsatisfying. The class teaches one another and interacting with your peers is mandatory. Try your best and use your resources and you should be good.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Group projects

reviews.comment: Professor Brooks is really cool and so nice, but this is one of those classes that doesn't have set grades and you constantly worry about what's being counted because there's no way of knowing. It does involve a lot of interaction with peers. I wouldn't say the class was very difficult, but it does get really boring at times.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: Classes are lead by the students, so I never knew if I was getting the info that the prof wanted us to understand. A lot of reading and some of it was redundant. SSRs were a pain more than helpful, but they are a way to prove that we read. He did give a pop quiz. The projects were vague, but that gave me the freedom to learn new programs and info.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--SO MANY PAPERS--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: Such a nice guy and really cares about what you're saying when you speak up in class. Is very welcoming to all students creative ideas and never makes you feel dumb. The assignments aren't difficult and very enlightening. I love it!
He is so disorganized. His instructions are unclear and indirect. I cannot stand his teaching style. I would never take another class with him again.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--SO MANY PAPERS

reviews.comment: Nice enough but not very passionate. Leaves us to our own devices and pretty much has us teach the class so I haven't really learned anything from him. The projects are easy enough once you get past the vagueness. A lot of reading and the readings are sometimes redundant. Don't skip more than 2 classes because he doesnt take drs. notes
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: I cannot stress this enough, if you want to pursue any kind of business / economics related courses, stay away from this Professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Participation matters--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: I absolutely do not recommend this professor. Not only is Prof. Bernedo rude, she's flat out lax and doesn't want to take any steps to help her students succeed. Ignores questions and just says to read the syllabus, gives pop-quizzes on topics we've barely had time to work on, and she overall makes a difficult class even harder.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Participation matters--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Bernedo is a very good prof. Her class is flipped, so not for everyone, but I liked it because there was more time to understand the content than in a class lecture. If you are decent at math and you like economics, the class is interesting and not too hard if you study for it. She is very nice in office hours and will take the time to help you

im writing this mid semester warn anyone to not take this class, I've had hard classes this is literally on another level, first it is a flipped classroom, she gives "pop quizzes" literally one every class, i go to office hours and she basically talked down on me and said it was my fault im confused when i just write what the videos says. just dont
Awful, if u have a choice, dont take her class

It was an easy class as long as you ask questions and have your fundamentals clear. Class structure was unique but worked for me. Taking notes from the lectures helped a lot. Ask her what kind of explanations she expects from exams, makes it easier to write the paper. Go to office hours early in the semester.
Do not take.

I really, really don't understand what the deal is with her reviews. I suspect that most of them are from students whom this is their first difficult class. So far, they were able to get easy A's in all their pre req classes, and they can't do that here. Watch videos, take notes, study for 1-2 hours before exam, you'll be fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Test heavy--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Her class structure on paper sounds great but WRONG the way she is doing it is horrible. Her lecture notes and hw help the many quizzes she gives you but for the exams they DON'T help you. She grades tough and uses every professors favorite excuse if I do it for you I have to do it for others a-lot. She takes a simple class and makes it 10x hard.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Beware of pop quizzes--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Lectures are important to attend, and studying is important - Leniently allows group work on most assignments - Overall very typical homework, projects, and exams - Provides good study materials and cuts back assignments when time is too compressed

Professor Bernedo is amazing! The content is extremely difficult but if you watch all her homework lectures and put in the work, you will succeed. In every class, there is a chance of a quiz based on the homework, so be prepared by doing your homework. Exams model these quizzes. Short answer: do the work and you will learn and get a good grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: I enjoyed the way her class was set up, you took notes from lecture videos at home and in class did example problems. If you understand and practice the in class problems before tests they were easy. Definitely had to put in some effort to study to do well in her class, but she was very open to helping her students when they did not understand.
If you want to hate economics, you should take her class.
I liked her, she was hard, class was more interactive which I liked

I was uneasy going into this class seeing the other poor reviews for her but Professor Bernedo has far exceeded expectations.  She put in an outstanding amount of effort to make sure we understood the material.  Despite her course being rather tough, she went above and beyond to kindly explain concepts and coursework, inside and outside of class.

Professor Bernedo has clearly put a lot of effort into teaching this course in the most effective manner. We watched recorded lectures beforehand, then worked on problems during class where she would answer questions. This allowed me to absorb the material, and she was very helpful and thorough in her explanations. Surprisingly great class.
lectures are unclear and slow, she shows up to class unprepared, exams are confusing and worded like a non english speaker wrote them.

She has the highest failure rate of all the professors who teach this course. You can go to gradetoday and see the grade distribution for her course. Wish I had checked this before I took her class. If you do not want to fail and have to retake this class, please pick another professor. She acts like she wants you to fail. Makes things too hard

Very bad teacher. Unclear lectures, tough grader, and unprepared teacher. Does not know how to write on a whiteboard while teaching online. She should really get some training on how to teach. DO NOT TAKE HER!!! You will be much better off teaching yourself the material because you if you listen to her you will just get confused.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: For the final exam we could not go back to previous questions which was stressful because it was timed and so if you are confused about a question you just have to answer it quickly because the timer is running. She gives really hard tests and does not offer ANY extra credit or curves. She makes it VERY difficult to pass this class with a C.

I feel like this professor wants you to fail, she spends a lot of time going over in depth mathematical concepts that we won't need to know for exams. She makes the exams unnecessarily hard and gives you practice exams that have very little to do with what will actually be on the exams. She gives pop quizzes that covers material from homework.

Don't take her. Awful professor. Exams are way too difficult and there is no clear indication of what will be on the tests. Her study guides are totally different from the tests, so don't bother studying those. Her lectures are not that helpful either because she goes over things that are different then what she includes on the exams.

Makes the class too difficult. The work is not hard but the way the professor teaches makes the course confusing and difficult. Take this class with her if you want to have a tough time, otherwise please pick another professor. You have been warned...

Dont take ECON311 with this professor. Take it with any other professor. Most people fail her course because her lectures are different from her exams and she explains things in a confusing way. Her study guides are not helpful either.

She spends too much time going over things that are not on the exam. She doesn't really tell you what specific topics you should focus on for exams. She is not a good choice if you want to do well in this course because she does not know how to make concepts clear for students. Take a different professor for this course.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Terrible lecturer do not take. difficult to receive a C. Does not teach from textbook. Goes too in depth for mathematical analysis that you never use on exams.
Make sure to read the textbook so you understand the important concepts. Also make sure to really understand the material because exam questions can be quite difficult.

Horrible professor. Makes the concepts difficult and confusing to understand. I would not take her class again. There are quizzes in this class that are based on the homework so make to do your homework each week. Class is test heavy, so make sure you do well on the exams or your grade will drop fast. Study guides provided were useless.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Terrible Professor. She was not accommodating at all during the switch to online classes. She never answered emails and was very unprepared during online learning. Her grading methods were very harsh. This class is very test heavy. The tests and quizzes make up for 80% of your grade, and only 20% is homework. Does not curve grades at all. AVOID!!!
reviews.rating_tags: Test heavy--Beware of pop quizzes--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Absolutely AWFUL professor. She made this class unnecessarily hard,and overly stressful. The content isn't bad at all, however,the way she teaches and grades are unholy (at best). She also did an awful terrible job during online learning, I literally went to online office hours and she didn't showup. If you like Econ or yourself don't take her
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Not a very good teacher. Her study guides for the exams can be tricky and very not very useful. She is also probably the most harsh grader I've came across. Would definitely not recommend her at all.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Nice professor, but taught the class in a very confusing manner to me. The class is very test heavy, we have 2 exams and one final exam that equal 75% of your grade (other 25% is online homework and quizzes) so basically if you do poorly on a test you're screwed. She doesn't curve exams and the study guides given in my opinion weren't very useful
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Would not recommend taking her. Prof. Bernedo makes the material a lot more confusing than it should be. Tests are very difficult with no clear reference as what to expect on it. She is very nice is you ask her for help. Just would not recommend her for 311. Take somebody else if you get the chance.

She is very nice but the Homework's and quizzes are all on Pearson, which most students despise. The exams are a bit difficult so you do need to study for them. She does teach well if you go to every class and hand-write notes. Basically she is just like most Econ professors at UMBC- Decent but makes you write down everything.

Prof. Bernedo is an average professor, but she's gotten better as the semester has gone on. Homework timelines are inconsistent, but grading is fairly clear. Homework does require effort but it helps you on tests. Lectures are good, better since she started using ppts as opposed to the whiteboard. Looking forward to the rest of the semester.
reviews.rating_tags: TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Good professor, knows how to teach.

Whether you've been coding for years or you're completely new to it, Prof. B makes his class accessible for students of all coding levels. His playful, banter with the TA's was nothing less than corny, but made the environment more fun than most professors. During the semester coding project, he always uplifted our work and encouraged us.

Amazing professor and a great person overall. His TAs are also really cool, and his COMP101 class is perfect for any new student at UMBC. It provides a refreshing start to your college experience!
Keep in mind that you need to learn how to code things on your own. TAs will definitely help, but you're mostly on your own.

one of the best professors I've had so far. He's funny, caring, and loves what he does. I definitely recommend taking this class, but honestly, he doesn't really teach you how to code; that's mainly up to you to learn. But take this class; he's awesome.

Amazing professor. He was so incredibly kind and welcoming. I was struggling due to family issues, and he completely understood and allowed me more time for assignments. Super responsive to emails(never took more than 24 hours). The mid-term was the only test. Final was a 2-month group project that is VERY easy if you just do 30 minutes a day

Prof B was such a great professor! He was so nice and understanding throughout the whole course! He really knew how to explain computing to people who have never done it before.The projects can be a little difficult but the TA's are always there to help.  Take this class.

Prof B. was a great professor and really cared about his students. The coding assignments are really easy. There is one pretty important group project that counts as your "final exam" grade, as long as you choose a good group, its very easy to complete. Time management is crucial for the project!
I took his class 3 years ago and still think abut how much I enjoyed it. He really cares about his students. This guy is wonderful and a great introduction to computing.
Great professor. He understands when you have problems if you send him an email. Lectures are amazing along with the Ta's. Just get ready to work in groups a lot.

Had him in fall, amazing introduction to the computing space. His class was fun, made everyone feel welcome, explained things clearly. Cares very much about ethics in the tech space. Challenging projects, but the TAs and him guided me through it. Language we used in class was Processing.
Prof.B is a great professor and a great person. His class isn't that hard as long as you try and understand processing just a little bit. Chill class and great for beginners!

Such a great professor! I was in the most recent semester and I can confirm after reading the rate my professor beforehand and then taking the course they are right on the money. Prof B takes the time to work with you on the content and genuinely wants his student to do well in the class. Although the exams might be difficult so go to office hours!

he ate. best prof ever, so sweet and understanding. exams can be tough but there are so many office hours, extra credit opportunities, and the TAs are so willing to help. so refreshing to have a professor that cares

As someone who had 0 coding experience, the class was difficult. The TAs helped a lot during office hours, but I needed help with everything. The midterm was long and very difficult. The final group project was hard for a beginner, but my group knew coding. If you go to office hours and show that you're trying, he'll do his best to give you an A!

Prof B is very great choice. He is super funny and I looked forward to his lectures every time. The final project can feel stressful since it's what you focus on for the entire second-half of the semester and you are in groups, but other than that, he is very fun and engaging.

reviews.comment: A hilarious professor who makes COMP classes fun. The unique methods through which he explains concepts almost make you wait to attend his class again. COMP 101 or COMP 101Y is an introductory programming class and it is perfect if you take him as a professor

Overall the class wasn't that bad. As long as you follow the rubrics for the assignments to a tee and pay attention, you should do well.

Prof. B has got to be the best professor at UMBC, he is there for you not only as an instructor but for guidance he will be there to lend an ear even if it doesnt pertain to the class. I'm writing this review during the third week of having him. Hands down he's one of the professors I respect the most. He has good lectures that keep you entertained, he doesn't give too much work, and he respects students.
Extremely kind man who answered all of the questions I had. The class was easy to follow understand with his guidance. Funny guy who made coding enjoyable.

This was my first COMPSCI class, so it was a little difficult for me given my lack of experience. But Prof. B and the TAs are honestly amazing people and they're always willing to help. He is one of the best professors to get started in college. The work is really easy if you have coding experience and he genuinely cares about the class and the students. His office hours are the best and he is the most relatable professor, we even talked about certain upcoming video games.
Great Professor complete all assignments and you'll pass. Come in with some coding knowledge

I loved her and her class! It was very interesting, with clear criteria. We read three books with group presentations on specific chapters. You take a good amount of notes in the class, so have a designated notebook, 3 open note quizzes, and a final project.

Dr.Camee Maddox-Wingfield is an amazing professor and an amazing person! The passion and knowledge she has for the subject is so inspirational. I hope I can be as awesome as her one day. I will take her classes any chance I get! I have had her twice so far.

she cares, few group works, open note quizzes, in person quizzes on paper, class assignments, I would say not a easy A tho. she's like a 7.5 out of 10 for a easy A class. if you are good with all that i would say 8.5 out of 10.

When I first entered class, i thought this was going to be a hard class but i was wrong! he's so nice and very laid back. She is an amazing professors. As long as you pay attention in class and ask her questions she is an amazing professor. She wants you to pass, she replies fast to emails as well. !!A lot of extra credits!!
