If you do well in her class you will really know your stuff. Go to discovery though it might not help but they are serious when they say attendance is mandatory.

Definitely different from high school chemistry (depending on where you went of course). It was a wake-up for me. Everything is very fast-paced. You HAVE to read the textbook, and STUDY STUDY STUDY for tests. Tests are multiple choice but very tricky so read questions&answers slowly and always go check over. Basically, teach yourself college chem.
Fantastic teach she sweats you but completely worth it

I have had Dr.Carpenter for Chem101 and Chem 102, and she is a good teacher, although one that speaks very quickly. The biggest reasons I did so well in this class were becaue of the textbook (read all chapters assigned very carefully) and the CHEMISTRY TUTORIAL CENTER. That place is the greatest help ever; the students know what they are doing.

She does not teach well at all.  She expects you to completely know concepts and problems before she goes over them in class.  She had us do problems before she taught us how to do them.  She sometimes flashes up answers on the screen gives quick explanations and then moves on.  She does not thoroughly explain concepts

If you enjoy reading outside of class, and then going in to do practice problems during lecture, she'll be right up your alley. However, if you're looking for someone to teach material and then do practice problems, you're going to want to find a different teacher.

I personally think she's a very good teacher. A lot of my friends say she's not, but I disagree. She's very into learning. She teaches you the hard stuff and you learn the other stuff by your own. You need to put a lot of time into this class, but overall a very good class
She's hard. But such a good professor with a real desire for you to learn. Expect to study and work hard and you will excel. She is totally fair and reasonable. I really like her class.

She doesn't teach anymore. She posts up problems for like 10 minutes and flashes up the solution very quickly & then another problem for another 10 minutes. That's basically class now. Yea it's our responsibility to read before but it's also her responsibility to lecture. Her exams are super hard. I'm relying on the curve at the end at this point..

She was fine last semester, but she doesn't really teach anymore. She expects that you understand the material before you come to class. Class basically consists of 5-10 minutes of lecturing and then a few problems projected onto the wall. I'd tell you to avoid her, but shes the only intro Chem teacher. Your best bet is to find a smart friend.

She went over the slides much too fast for my taste, so the only way I (surprisingly) managed an A was to basically read the chapters and teach myself with TONS of practice problems. I mean, she's nice and all, but I don't feel like she was all too helpful.
Lets just put it this way, if there was another professor that taught Chem 101, I would try to get the other professor. 600+  students is too much to teach in 2 periods of the day.

she is an easy enough professor, you just have to pay attention in class and look over her slides.  one thing, you need to fully understand what is going on in this class, if you do not, then go get help.
Dr. Carpenter is a great professor teaching a very hard subject. She is helpful, has a great attitude, and does a good job at making the class interesting.

She is an excellent professor, and does a "Friday feature" (experiment) every Friday to encourage attendance. The only bad part is chem discovery, which is dreadful every week as you are placed with people you wonder how the heck they got into college. EXAMS are easy if you realize most questions are tricks.
She goes really fast in her lectures so make sure that you listen and if you don't understand go get HELP!

She goes over a lot of information in her lectures and I usually felt like I understood until I realized how much we actually covered. The exams are pretty difficult because she tries to trick you. Even when I felt confident after an exam, I only got a C.

I don't know what to say about her. I do all the practice problems, I do every review problem in the book, I even study what she teaches, and I STILL fail. In this class, the only way to succeed (with more than a low C) is to pray, or find another professor.

Her exams are RIDICULOUSLY hard. You study every possible way you can and you still get a bad grade on the exams. The discovery section is 2 hours long..UGH. Make sure you go to the tutorial center and get help from them and get old exams AS REFERENCE. Overall she's a really hard teacher.

She's a tough professor, you must attend class and pay attention to have a chance at passing. You can't expect to BS your way through this course at all however she is available and very helpful if you ask.

Dr. Carpenter's lectures are very easy to follow and she makes them exciting when she can. It's important to keep up with the problems she assigns - they're optional, but are important for exams. Overall, I think she's an excellent professor, but she does expect you to work very hard and exams will reflect that expectation.

Carpenter is a pretty good teacher. She teaches the material very clearly and straightforward, and makes the class fun and interesting. She's kind of funny, and a bit nuts, but in a good sort of way. Most people buy her notes for like $20 or so, because she teaches straight from the slides. I barely opened the book this semester.

One of my favorite teachers, funny at times. Teaches straight from her lecture slides. take notes on the examples she gives in class and theres nothing you wont be able to answer for wiley and exams. Never touched the book, and studied straight from her slides.

Dr. Carpenter is a very good professor.The class is very easy. don't fall behind. do all the practice problems and attend lecture. I really loved her class. There was a curve at the end. Her exams might seem tricky but if you pay attention it's not that bad. Discovery is soo boring though.

she knows what she is talking about, but is not very good at communicating it..lectures are straight off of a powerpoint- so they are kind of boring..overall the class is pretty straightforward- just do the homework, go to class and study for the exams..and you should do fine..oh- and discovery is a HUGE waste of time!!
She is amazing
Dr. Carpenter is very moody.  Do the homework (a lot), go to lecture, then you have a chance at passing.  She makes her own slides that you can buy at the bookstore which help.

Completely agree with the last review. She is a good professor and tries to make things easy but in a group with 350 people, she fails to do it!! . You end up TEACHING YOUR SELF the material. The discovery section IS THE WORST PART. If you have to take the course remember YOU ARE BY YOUR SELF.

Fairly good teacher. Very tricky exams. Lecture was a blur, she read from the slide making it like bedtime story time. Got a B in the class but that didnt come very easy. I practically taught myself everything i needed to know in the class. Do a lot of practice problem and the wieyplus that she puts up after every class.
Overall Carpenter is a wonderful professor. I was scared to take her cause I heard her exams were tricky but if you get over the fact that it is tricky than it wont be so tricky.
SOOOOOOOOOOOO HARD. Not too much work. Ok at teaching.

Dr. Carpenter is a really great professor. She is very helpful and makes herself available to students. She makes difficult concepts easier to understand but her exams are almost impossible so study hard!

i had her for chem 101 AND chem 102. her exams are tricky, you really have to know your stuff.. a lot of the time it's application; in class everything makes sense, but when u take her exam it's like ! what the heck is this.; i got an A for 101 and B for 102. just study the textbook and her notes.. it's a hard class!!

there was another site which had over 100 ratings.. the ratings currently here do not reflect the class well enough. It is a difficult class and you either have to have a good understanding of chem or agree to studying hardcore for this class to do well. professor is nice if you catch her on a good day

Its not an easy class, but you'll learn a lot.  Come to class, and be prepared to work hard. This is one of those classes you really have to study for: exams are tricky, but hit the books and take serious notes from the get go and you'll be fine. On the other hand, if you know you hate chemistry or have never taken a challenging course,dont enroll.

This Professor gives me nightmares ever since I been taking her class...... absolute worst professor I ever had. Please someone convince her to retire, she can't teach for nothing. Waste of me time taking this class.
tests/exams are hard as anyone
This class was truly a hard class. She made it seem easy in class, but her tests were really tough. It really is a weed-out course, which stinks cause I'm not a Chem major.
the class is tough but she is a great lecturer and she tries to keep it interesting. She is always ready to help students out with any questions
Don't take this class. Exams are impossible and filled with trick questions that she doesn't even touch upon in class!!! Im a premed student and I have a C right now!
IF you don't want your  GPA to drop I advise you not to take her class. Her questions on the exams are very tricky and she's very rude to her student. Stay farrrrrr away from this class.
terrible teacher...squeezed by with a C but her tests were near impossible....she is most likely the only choice so you will have to suffer through her class and hope to survive

Awesome professor. If you attend class every time and study the slides you'll be fine. The class isn't easy, but it's not because carpenter is a bad professor. She does do a couple of trick questions so pay attention to what the question says.

Outstanding lecturer. She explains conccepts slowly and clearly to students, even though they may seem simple enough. CHEM 102 is a HARD course however, her lecture slides are helpful. However, you do need to work out as many practice problems from the text as possible, review as many old exams and ASK her questions. Her response time is rapid!!!!
The tests are fairly hard but manageable if you know the material well enough. Discovery sucks more than anything. She loves to do demos even though there are only a few. (Go to class on Halloween!)

I had Dr. Carpenter for Chem 101 and 102. She is a great professor. As long as you pay attention and keep up with the work, you will do well. She gives you lots of practice material and is willing to help. It's not an easy A, but if you work hard this class is not bad at all.  She teaches from the book, so if you are confused it's a good reference.

Allows 5 excused Absences. Antendance is mandatory to all Discovery sessions. Class was PACKED. Buy the slide packet from the bookstore! it has all the notes so you dont have to take em. The mandatory online homework sucked. Dont take this class if you are a slacker. Tests very fairly difficult and are 1/3 math.

Dr. Carpentar is an excellent professor. It is obvious she knows her stuff. Her lectures are simply amazing, and her powerpints make the material as clear as it gets. She gives out extra credit and her curve is fair. Read her tests carefully, though, or you will make stupid mistakes. And FYI, she doesn't curve the tests, just the final grade.

Dr. Carpenter is a very good professor with a great sense of humor.  Her lectures can get boring at times since she is reading straight from the power point slides, but they are worth going to. DO THE HOMEWORK PROBLEMS and read from your text book before class and you will be fine.

Awesome teacher in every way. She's funny and knowledgeable about all concepts we cover in 101. I got a 100% on wiley plus, its a free 10% of your grade. Also her exams were very easy if you can get over the fact that she tries to trick you in every problem. Oh, forgot to mention she's hott!

Very nice and funny professor. She is a descent teacher but the discussion is not very helpful and boring. Her tests are moderately difficult but you should have no problem for most of the exams. Only one exam was hard.
No Comments

I am a senior political science major who took this class because I need it for environmental management graduate school.  If I can wrap my head around chem and get a B, you can too.  Carpenter herself is very good and focuses her teaching solely on this class.  Whiny freshmen beware!  Welcome to college.

OMG. Do not take her class. While at the beginning of the semester, she may seem like a nice and funny lecturer...she is NOT! Her exams are HORRIBLY tough, and the lectures are BORING! She is also very sarcastic and expects you to think on her level. Study all you, you are guaranteed horrible grades!

I really like Carpenter and I'm not even a fan of Chemistry.  After taking her class I now like Chemistry much more.  Carpenter is very likeable and does fun little experiments.  Her exams are on the harder side though.

Out of every teacher/professor I have had since I started pre-school Tara Carpenter is by far the absolute worst...I feel like I lost intelligence from attending this class. The test proved life isn't worth it because they were so hard and unfair. 2 options: 1) Try hard and fail or 2) Fail and try hard.  Basically this class will kill all hopes!!!!

Shes a very good teacher, with a quirky sense of humor that matches my own. This class,however, is very dificult. It takes alot of time and effort, but it is not impossible. I would take her 102 class if was offered in the spring.
cant teach at all
No Comments
I hated this class with a passion and I actually enjoy chemistry. Tests are insane and have tons of trick questions.

The class isn't that bad and the lectures are easy to follow, but her exams are absolutely ridiculous. Trick questions and answers that are essentially the same so you have to memorize slides word for word, its just stupid. Also, "Discovery" is unbearable and patronizing

Dr. Carpenter is a strange duck. She has beautiful notes and lectures, then her exams are extremely tricky and frustrating. I started the semester badly, with my first exam in the 50's. But by going to all the discussions, turning in all the (easy) online homework and slowly bringing my exams grades up, she curved me into an A.
Okay

She's really good and a very fair grader. She never spontaneously tests you on anything unless she's definitely  gone over it in class and she's always available during her office hours so those who didn't do well have no right to complain. She also makes class pretty fun with demonstrations and stories about her daughter.

she aight, it all comes down to you and what you put into the class. She curves well, and willing to help if you go to her office hours.  Read book, do problems, previous exams, and go to discussion.  After that, you should get an A.  Its not suppose to be an easy class cuz its chem2, but not ridiculously hard either.  Dont take morning discussion

Great professor, she teaches well and if you pay attention you'll understand the material. Her tests are a bit tricky, you definently have to study for them. Quizes are ridiculous easy. She posts her lecture slides which is convenient. Attendance is not mandatory. I had her both 101 + 102, you should take her !

Dr.Carpenter is really nice and has a bubbly, fun personality. Her class is difficult, but certainly not impossible. Just read the chapters and do the suggested problems and you will be fine for the tests. People whining about how hard she is are slackers. Also, she held onto my backpack when I accidentaly left it after an exam, so mad respect.

EXCELLENT professor.  Explains concepts well and thoroughly, and in a way that makes it interesting.  Tests do require preparation and careful reading, but if you understand the material, they're pretty straightforward.  She's also really nice and helpful; if you have any questions, don't hesitate to ask.  The best science professor I've had.
she is an awesome teacher! I had her for chem 101 and chem 102 and she was extremely helpful, if u asked! slide shows are very helpful and do the practice problems from the book!

Do lots of problems. Tests are tricky. If you didn't take AP Chem, you are screwed. I got 100's on all my tests in AP and got a 5 on the exam and still had trouble in her class. She's really cute though, in a dorky way.

She honestly is a pretty good lecturer. You can tell she knows her stuff, yet it definitely can be hard for her to relay it to everyone. The exams would be really easy without all the trickiness that she includes in the questions, and discussion is absolutely annoying; you're basically treated like 5 year-olds.

A good professor, although not the best. Teaches well, but its still chemistry, so its really hard. You have to study on your own and do tons of problems. No amount of lectures can help you if you dont do the problems.I had to learn this the hard way.

She's interesting. I don't hate her. She's got a poor taste in clothes, but can you blame her? Once my friend and I tried to make her pick her nose with our minds and then she scratched it. Freaky. This class is easy if you a) read b) do problems c) kind of try (importance in that order). I didn't do the above, but got by with a B.She likes her kid

After using ratemyprofessors I thought she'd be horrible but I was pleasantly surprised. This class was way easier than my AP Chem class and the tests were easy but included a few tricky questions that kept you on your toes. Just do your reading and the recommended problems and make sure you understand them and you should get an A easily.

Not an easy A! Take notes in class, but more importantly do most problems in the book, and practice tests online. The curve at the end really helps bring up your grade, tho discussion grade was also very helpfull in that. So go to every class and study, study, study...
She's very sarcastic and blatant. Nice curve, but don't fall behind. You can print out slides if you want, but read the textbook also. I enjoyed AP Chem, but her class was a hindrance!!
I used to like Chemistry... until I took this class.
The class is difficult if you don't put in the work for it. Make sure you do the assigned homework problems.
Good if you try. If you don't plan on working then take some lower chem class.
She is a good teacher and she is hot too. The exams are hard but as long as you do all of the homework problems it isn't that bad.

She is very enthusiastic in teaching and will go over the same material if you need help. Very helpful and the exams are easy, you just have to actually study, not skim over. Don't take it if you're a slacker.

the professor is good in teaching, but she goes too fast. she expects you to know stuff beforehand. tests are impossible, tricky! it is all multiple choice tho!! getting a B is possible but you have to work for it!!

Overall, a nice person. Her exams were well hard and her lectures didn't seem to help much; she expects that you go over her slides prior to class and also expects you to keep up with the reading. During lecture, she goes far too quickly, so be prepared. She does respond to emails fairly quickly, though.

even though her exams were hard i thought she was a good professor.  they re-worked what information is on what exam this past year, so if you ask someone who had her 2 years ago, they will tell you her exams are a lot harder than they are now.

Chem 101 isn't a terrible class, topics covered are pretty basic and Carpenter gives lots of examples in class and explains well. Tests are a bit challenging but not a prob if you study and understand basics. I got C's and D's on high school chem tests, but A's on Carpenter's exams so far.
she is good but sometimes she words the questions weird.
tries to be cute..unsuccessful. seems nice but when speaking to her one on one is very rude and mean. has tricky tests. discussions are the longest two hours of your life

A very nice and helpful professor.  Her exams are tricky if you don't study.  To ensure a B or above:  study the lecture slides before class, participate in discussion, do the homework ( a must), and read the book if still don't get things.  She's very approachable and WILL answer questions.  Semi tricky exams, but getting an A is very possible.
very hard! Must study hard to pass class.
An absolutley stunning professor. Vibrant, enthusiastic and conveys the material in an interesting manner. Recommend her to everyone!

A lot of people give her****, but really she isn't bad at all. She expects you to do the reading before you come to class but she still tries to explain it when people understand. If you study hard before tests, you can get an A.
Tests are tough; you must keep up and study hard to pass.

I know a lot of people dont like carpenter, but i thought she was ok. she teaches straight from the book and makes up the exams. usually one is dropped and the final is worth twice as much. read the questions to the exams clearly. she is one tricky lady and her exams are not easy!! know the material and work on the math problems.

Moves fast through problems, so fast that  you don't have enough time to copy down the solution - but she won't put the solution on the PP slides on Blackboard.  Don't ask her questions, because she expects you to have a 400 level understanding of chemistry in a 100 level course.  Nice curve though.
Good teacher, tough class, pay attention! Nice curve at end for the borderliners like me :)
Good teacher, but you don't realize it till you no longer have her anymore. Print of the slides before class and READ, and you'll do good.

Buy or print out the lecture slides for class.  Go to class.  Do the suggested problem sets.  She's a very good lecturer and helpful. She purposefully tries to trick you on the exams.  Second exam is the hardest, and you get to drop an exam.  You need to be fully alert and focused for the tests, so don't stay up late studying.
Hard class, good teacher.  She explains materials well and helps whenever she can.  Exams are really hard, tricky questions.
everything comes from the problem sets, pay attention because she is a tricky lady (VERY TRICKY), the second exam is the hardest
What can I say? Lecture class and goes from the slides. Do the problem sets. That's the only way you'll get it. It's a lot if info so you'll have to read.

Her lectures r good but her xamz r hard core ones...her online quizes r kinda helpful..she curves @ the end and drops one test which r the only means to climb up tat class..she makes the xamz too hard 4 an intro level chem class..tricky..

Very challenging class. She really does her best to be as clear and thorough as possible, but it's a lot of information. The powerpoint slides help, too, and the hw and practice problems are a MUST as well as all the reading. Tests were absolutely horrid, covered so much information, esp. things that are easily overlooked. Discussion was PAINFUL.

This class was quite a challenge.  The class moves quickly and is quite in-depth, be prepared to pull a few all-nighters (most likely in a row).  She provides all the class slides which is VERY helpful. Oh, and watching her do demonstrations is worth signing up for the class.  She gets giddy like a kid with a magnifying glass! (In a good way!)

Look at the lectures & do the probs from the book, her practice tests, do the "online quizzes" by yourself so you can really know the material (don't get answers from a friend, it doesn't help you when you're taking the final!!!) VERY TRICKY LADY!!!!! but there's a curve at the end that will save u like no other

smart, easygoing, good classroom environmetn, great demos, usually involve fire...attendance is not mandatory, so if u dont like her dont show up, but be prepared for tests, they actually do cover the material, drops one test (usually gonna be test 2); if u keep up and do homework problems, shouldnt hav a problem

I couldn't stay awake in her lectures so I read straight from the book. She forces you to attend discussions but not lectures. If you understand concepts in the book you can nail the tests, although she tries to screw you up so make sure you pay attention to wording.

Not horrible, but moves quickly.  Also, I couldn't stay awake in her lectures; I was better off reading the textbook.  If you've taken AP Chem, you'll be fine.  If not, do ALL the recommended problems for practice and for the love of God, DO THE PRACTICE TESTS.  Tests are worded NOTHING like the rec. problems, even though they test the same skills.

She is a good teacher... however, she doesn't let you know that the bulk of the class work is outside class... lots of studying to be done and before coming to class... at least tha was what i did. She is sweet and charming in the outside, but i think when she sets her questions, she goes into another  dimenion of 'trickery'!!!

the class isn't all that hard...the concepts are easy highschool easy. exams and the quizzes are trivial, annoying, and tricky. i don't mean that these questions are hard.  they're quite easy if you get past the freaking "wording." listen, no scientist in this goddamn world is going to expect you to decipher stuff

Her class is tough. It should be. It is the basis for so many other classes. You cannot come into the class and expect to just get by. You need to but some work into it. Her lectures are fast and cover a lot of material but people need to take the responsibility to study outside of lecture and discussion. She has to cover a lot in only 16 weeks.
She is a horrible teacher!!!  Avoid if possible!
she tricks you with tests

Her lecture is right off the powerpoint slides so if you get them on your computer, don't bother going to lecture.  You can read and fill out the slides on your own and save some time.  The discussion is pretty lame and the grading system doesn't work at all.  The exams will crush you, the quizzes will confuse you, and the curve will save you.

Truly abysmal as a teacher, doesn't know how to teach. Lecture slides are most vague, have stupid things written on them-page "257" title. She tries to cover alot but does a half assed job of it by going extremely fast and not emphasising KEY details.  Nobody understands anything, nobody raises their hands or participates in class LOL!)

She is a great professor, but a horrible teacher.  Don't expect to actually be able to understand the information from lectures (which are straight from the book). Examples are helpful, discussion is not! Use her office hours...she'll be more apt to curve your grade up if she knows your face. 2 things to expect: low exam grades, big curve.

People underrate her entirely. Excellent professor. Has printed slides so easy to follow lecture. To ensure a good grade do the recommended problems! The practice exams can also be very helpful! Showing up to class is not useless, since she does give out exam hints and so forth. So definately get her as your professor!

Ok... all I'm gonna say is...CHANGE THE DISCUSSION GRADING SYSTEM! It does NOT work and it is flat out stupid. The TAs are worthless and don't know what they're doing. As for the lectures, you're better off skipping them and just reading the sections in the textbook. The lecture actually lowers your IQ for the exam. That's why everyone fails.
there are alot of tiles in the lecture hall she teaches

3rd class chemist. jabs all day (and nobody wants to participates). only good thing = doesn't make you memorize the table. don't attend lectures & lecture slides. exams = extremely difficult & from the book. Don’t attend lecture, don’t read the slides. just read the book, then you won’t massacred like the masses who study lectures and get 45’s
fun class, great teacher!!!! Cares about her students.
Professor Carpenter is very helpful, the class is fairly easy.

Not approachable.Will not answer questions she considers "last week questions."Bad online quizzes, there have been instances when the whole class had to take a quiz again.Yes, 350+ plus people.She put up a review-exam up online, and many answers in the answer key were wrong! Brutal exams containing undisclosed and untaught questions. Avoid her...
Low class averages on tests, but the curve will save you at the end.  Just study your butt off for those tests.  She is a very good teacher, especially considering the enormous size of the class.

Chipper, nice pretty cool until test time. rediculous exams and the class depends on them but there is also a rediculous curve, i got a c with a 42 on the final and 45 average on exams, every class is different though, having a baby now so wont be back for a while who knows how she'll change  powerpoints to the max hard class but often mandatory

Hard class, but if you go to class and study, you should be fine.  Class averages tend to be in the 50s, so even though you might have lower scores than you're used to, you'll probabaly get an A.  Carpenter's demos are pretty good-they all involve fire.

Dr.Carpenter is very nice, her exans is really hard and need to study so hrad but it is not impossible. She would be more helpful if the semester was longer. I think the big problem is short time. THe subject is easy if every one read the book.
No Comments

If you have never taken chemistry before, you might be in trouble. This class is not hard if you keep up, it requires a lot of work. I got an A, but you must go to class, read BEFORE you go to class, do the homework and do the chapter studyguides on e-grade. She is a great teacher, but the test are tricky but this is how the MCAT will be, not easy.

shes always well-prepared and very knowledgable in chem. shes funny and likes telling stories to give everyone a break from the notes. her tests are very difficult and you need to be very prepared for them. we like her

Carpenter is a great person, but not a great professor. She honestly does try to teach the material and make it clear, but her lectures are often so basic that the test comes along and takes you by surprise. i feel that her lectures do nothing to prepare you for the exams. to succeed, be sure to print her lecture slides and to study for the exams o

Dr. Carpenter is very nice and you will learn a lot if you pay attention to lectures and do the practice problems. Tests are difficult and you need to study and work hard. She's not the teacher for you if you don't like reading from lecture slides. But she's pretty good.

I think she is a good professor but she needs to make her exams just as she teaches. Her exams are bit more difficult than the way she teaches and the sample questions that she gives us to look over. I don't like that aspect. However, she's very clear, answers questions when asked, and knows what she is doing.

The class starts out very easy but dont be lulled into a false sense of security. exam 2 is very difficult so study very hard or dont study at all because she drops one exam grade. the quizzes are online and hence open book but they are not easy so use your book and your friends. attend the lectures: u will learn alot. shez not very bad once u get

She isn't quite as bad as she seems.  Her slides are a good outline, but you need to read the book as well.  The exams are very difficult and she doesnt prepare you very well for them.  Overall, she is a decent teacher but the subject is a hard one.
her slides doenst help, hard exam..read the textbook instead of attending lectures.
It is meant to be a weeder course... She taught the calculations fairly well, but most of her theory, especially the questions, was worded very poorly.

very hard exams...not at all comformatble in answering questions...tries to avoid answering questions and says "we will cover in the next lecture...hold on to your thought" ..very unconformatble with her knowlwedege  of chemistry...doesnt want to answer questions...doesnt go over any major problems...unless the day before the exams....avoid if u ca

Since I did well on the first exam, I don't really have any complaints.  I normally hold conversations with her about the Pittsburgh Steelers doing mediocre this year before and after the lectures.  The class does require a lot of work.  Do the homework problems!  And don't fall behind either!
No Comments
Do the homework, go to the lectures, print out the slides, study, take the easy online quizes and you'll do fine.

HORRIBLE! Ever had a flu and been vomiting? It was a better experience than going to class. Got nothing out of class; read the book and still did horrible on tests which were very difficult. Quizzes were easy.
Straight forward in class, but everything else goes to shambles.  Maybe Math 151 should be the required class before Chem 101.  but she is nice and the slides don't help.
No Comments
She is really nice

Bad, bad teacher, who has a serious communication problem. She spends the class reading slides, and the slides are taken from the textbook. YOU WILL ONLY PASS THIS CLASS IF YOU PAY FULL ATTENTION TO THE HOMEWORK. Ignore what she says, do the homework and understand it. Self-teach-class all the way. The TA (Marple) basically taught me everything.

in my opinion she was fine-chem 101 is meant to be tough. her explanations of concepts weren't always so clear, but she encouraged questions-plus she makes herself pretty available for questions out of class. her exams are really tough and she puts in a lot of very involved calculations for the exam time. she's not trying to fail you.

Let's face it- Chem 101 is a tough course from any teacher. Dr. Carpenter is just as good a teacher as any. She would re-explain things when asked. Some of her test questions are a bit unclear- read them carefully. My advice: complete and understand the homework probs and use the solutions manual and you will be ok.

Funny...I got an A in this class. Tutoring and curving saved me. This class weeds people out! Don't rely on lectures; DO THE HOMEWORK. The answer guide: practically essential for passing. And Carpenter? I once said hello directly to her, and she ignored me in total disrespect. Don't fall for her false kindness; skepticism will save your grade!
the class was really tough and she had talked about a curve which never happened.

Bad bad teacher. Start teaching yourself everything at the beginning of the class and don't slack off. Also, her slides are worlthless. Forget about asking for help during class, she'll just make up an excuse about posting the problem on blackboard. Horrible class.

This class is the hardest class I have had and it is not even an upper level course! She thinks she is helping with the group work but the problems on the test are different. I hope I pass but if not I wont be taking it with her again.

Lectures sometimes seemed unprepared - the exams are incredibly difficult - the class had a 50% average on the second one.  The middle third of the semester seemed to be the hardest - I don't know if this was her fault or not.
Straight forward class, difficult assesments.  If you test well you should be alright.  Pay attention, and actually go to lecture.  Nice to look at atleast

She is very enthusiastic about the subject and tries to relay her excitment to us, but it doesn't work.  Her lectures are boring and not very helpful. I think she's good at the subject but not at teaching it.  Homework gets you through the quizes but tests are unreasonably hard.
very good and informative

The only, ONLY way to survive this class is to TEACH YOURSELF. Forget about the slides. Forget about coming to this class, actually, it'll just confuse you and put you to sleep. She's too new to know how to teach and you'll fail if you rely on her. Curves = yes. Get the book and sit down with it.

Dr.Carpenter is a nice person, and she is always ready to help you, but infortunately she does not know how to teach. Her lectures are very confusing and boring and they are straight from the book. I managed to get a B, but i put way too much effort on it. BOTTOM LINE DON"T TAKE WITH HER.

Horrid teacher. I hope you've taken this class before, cause if you haven't, i suggest studying for three weeks prior to the exam. i'm completely relying on ap chem and teaching myself. write fast, she speeds thru slides. quizzes in discussion every week, even on the week of an exam. She can't teach

Toughest class I ever took. Lectures are pretty boring, straight out of the book. Tests are darn near impossible...curve was a 50% to get a C. That's an awful lot of curve, but a lot of people would have failed without it.

She is new and does pretty good for a new professor. Its so much easier to skip lectures and teach urself everything from the text but she kinda helps... *kinda* Grades are curved alot ...but also cuz they needa be, the exams are very hard ..class averages are never above a 60. def. a weed out cours

Dr. Carpenter tries really hard to teach and genuinely wants everyone to do well (she curves the grades so much that you can get an A with 80% in the class). Her lectures aren't so great though, so if you aren't good at chem and want to do well, I recommend you not to rely too much on her class note

Dr. carperter tries but fails miserably in her attempt to teach.  She attempts to be funny, but it all ends up in a disappointment.  Her powerpoint slider finger can outshoot Eastwood, and her tests totally ruins student's life.  As a teacher, i give her props 4 trying, but please don't try!

This professor tries to help, but alas, she fails horribly as a new teacher.  I'ld like to give her another chance, but fraknly i don't think the result would be any different.  Her lack of clarification show on the subject is her worse flaw, next to her speedy powerpoint flipping finger and more.

She tried very hard to make sure people understood. She curved grades ridiculously so people could pass with a C (60-76=C)and people should be glad they had her instead of some other porfessors who would have just let them fail. She made a difficult subject manageable but u still have to study hard
She's just out to get people!
she trys reall hard to teach but lectures are a waste. exams are ridicously hard.. to the point of impossible. she is a really nice person who trys to help but it usally doesnt work
She really cares about teaching and making sure you know what you're doing. Not that bad of a class, considering how tough chemistry is here. I totally recommend her.

If you don't read the book, go to class.  She just puts up slides that are pictures from the book.  And if you expect to see how the math problems are done,  you better not blink, she goes over them very quickly.
No Comments
Ahahahahahah!!!!  Carpenter..  Professor..  Hahaha..  sorry.. that's just funny to me.

a difficult class that all science-related majors must take. i won't lie that carpenter TRIED HARD to teach us, well, but didn't work. eventually, stopped going to her class because her lectures only made me more confused about the subject. if possible, try to avoid carpenter AND lacourse.

Not helpful at all, lectures are pointless.  I'm doing well in the class only because I took AP Chem last year and am retaking this class just to get a better background.  I learn more from just reading the book than anything I learned in lectures which is not much

I tally agreed the last comment.She is not helpful at all.She likes to shows up in the middle of the class discussion and says that we have to build up the class average.I guess that she doesnot want to be looked so bad as a professor.The way that she teaches does not seem to be professional.

her lectures are really annoying, i like to show up late and sit in the front row.  over half the class fails each exam.  She is a first year teacher so i guess we should cut her some slack. she loves to show up in the middle of discussion sessions and exams just to tell you how bad u r doing
She tries to be fun, but she could not. She is not a good chem professor. She can't teach, because her lecture doesn't help you to understand; it's all from the book.

I want to start off by saying this is a HARD course.  She is NOT a bad instructor.  She is NOT an easy instructor, this class is supposed to be difficult.  I would recommend taking with her because she WANTS to teach, and is there for the students--NOT for the research; she expects you to succeed.

Probably the most incomprehensible professor I've ever taken, and when writing on the chalkboard his handwriting is still somewhat shaky. Lecture slides aren't his, and was missing some of what was on HW / half of what was on midterm. Reading textbook is necessary to do good on assignments. Do not take Phatak if you want to learn anything.

Lowkey, half the time I don't know what he is talking about. You are better off just taking it with a different professor or just self studying with the lecture slides or textbook than showing up to his class.

Very confusing. Lectures are useless if you don't have some exposure to digital electronics already. I stopped going because he just rambles for a while and it's very difficult to understand him. He seems like a nice guy, just a terrible professor. Labs feel almost entirely separate from the lectures. If you want to learn avoid Phatak.
The professor does not know how to lecture well, so I stopped showing up. Assignments are often unclear and feedback is minimal. Just watch Neso Academy on Youtube and attend labs and you'll pass.

Horrible professor. Doesn't know how to teach. Awful at answering questions as he just reiterates what he just lectured. He even seemed to get annoyed when people didn't understand him. Online resources were infinitely more useful than this professor. The TA taught the labs better than prof taught the lecture material. Take another prof if you can.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: terrible, terrible professor. dont take. he bad. no teach. no help. took him spring21 sem. lectures + lab not in sync. don't take with phatak no matter what. u wont learn a single thing.

Not a fun class. As a person Dr. Phatak seems very genuine and is very smart. I don't feel like this translates as a professor. Lectures are all over the place, tangents go on and on, and the class walks away more confused than at the beginning of lecture. Reading the sections of the book that he covers in class is really all you need.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Had him for 212 and 411. By far the worst CMPE professor I've had. The fact that he is a nice guy doesn't make up for his rambling and incoherent lectures. Would sometimes spend the entire period ranting about something he read in the paper w/o even touching our course material. You'll get an A as long as you show up, but you won't learn anything.

Phatak, while he seems sweet is really difficult to have as a professor. He has a THICCC accent. Throughout the entire course I was confused and I did "well". It was an awful experience and many of the people chose to drop CMPE and go to CMCS instead.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Honestly, he's a really sweet guy. Not as bad as everyone puts him. You might not learn anything from his lectures, but reading the textbook would do just fine. He tries to make lecture entertaining and you'll guarantee pass his class.

Dr. Phatak enertained the class and ensure questions were answered. Sometimes he could be condenscedning but he overall cared for his students. All you have to do is show up to class and try your best and you will pass the class. Dr. Phatak understands classes are difficult and works with you to make sure you understand the material.

Grade depends on labs, 2 midterms, final. Allows cheat sheets. Heavy accent, goes on tangents. Remembers names, likes to call on people. He will tell exam material in class & review sessions. Talk to the TAs in discussions! Go to labs! Exam avg in 30s, 3-4 problems, more complicated than examples he'll do. B/c curve, I needed 25% overall for a B
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Avoid him at any cost. Take it later with Yonis or Smith. You will not understand a single word in this class. Even thought you need at least B to pass, you will earn B or A depending on the fliping coin that he used. You will not learn -> do not be dump proud about your B or A that you got it, harder things are coming in upper level classes

His lectures are confusing and unclear. He speaks extremely fast, making it hard to understand him. When he learns a student's name, he calls them out, randomly selecting them to answer questions that no one knows the answer to. His test averages hover somewhere around a 30%, which he claims is intentional. Keep in mind 212 is a gateway for COMPE.

his accent is difficult at best. His lectures are bland and he crams a ton of information into them. the grading is basically arbitrary, you will fail his exams. i haven't gotten above a 35% but I'm still going to pass.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Like everyone else said, its basically a guaranteed B if you do labs and homework.  Tests can have a ridiculous curve depending on how everyone else does (ie 30% B). If you just wanna pass take it with him, if you want to understand the material you're better off reading on your own and talking to TAs
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Extremely arbitrary grader. If you show up to exams and labs, you are guaranteed to get a B. There is no question about it. The exams are extremely difficult, but he claims to curve the exams. In reality he doesn't curve the exams, but you will still end up with a B. If you want an A sit in the front row and ask questions. The lectures are useless.

Where to begin? He gives grades by flipping a coin. I landed on the 'B' side and I could get past that easily. However, when I showed up in CMPE310 after 212, I was so far behind because he didn't teach us a single thing. He also didn't really care about us too much because he's a research prof and we aren't research so we aren't worth his time.

Try to avoid. Nice. HARD to undrstnd. Cares abt students so ask Qs in office hrs. Read txtbk b4 class if u wnt to follow lecture at all.  Exams: test creative thinking not just undrstnding of material, designing circuits so practice that in txtbk, sometimes open notes computer, similar to past yrs Tlk to him to get at least a B. Aprox40pt curve.
Awful, he gets his information from the various tv channels he seems to be watching over the weekend.

He is a good professor. Really hard exams but he gives a huge curve. Go to class(though it is not mandatory), participate(He likes participation),Read the book yourself(it helps a lot after his lectures). If you try hard, and he sees it, you're probably guaranteed and B.

I have taken two classes (Bs in both) with him and he is probably my favorite professor here.  Sometimes difficult to understad but extremely helpful.  If you look at class as nothing more than a means to a letter grade he might frustrate you; the classes are well-made to really emphasize learning over mindless formula-following or regurgitation.
He's pretty helpful. His exams are very tough but he helps you out on the grade, just go to class and talk to him a bit you'll be okay.

I had heard bad things coming into the course, & at first I didn't like him so much, but after I got used to the way he speaks I found that he was an excellent professor.  I got a B without opening my textbook a single time outside of exams (VERY good exam-style), & I would have gotten an A if I had done more of the labs.  I'd write more butnoroom

EXACTLY like everyone else has said. A HORRIBLE lecturer. Mumbles a lot. When asked a question, incapable of succinctly answering + often goes off on irrelevant tangents. His (Indian?) accent doesn't help matters. You will learn NOTHING unless u do LOTS of independent reading. TA's Shiva + Lottich r a boon. Couldnt have gotten a "B" w/o them.

Phatak knows this material extremely well, but his lectures are almost useless except for him dropping exam hints.  Despite this he is very willing to help outside of class.  Exams are very hard but he gives lots of credit for basic understanding.  Class is curved heavily, so do labs and homework, and make a good overall effort and a B will follow.

Phatak understands the material, but doesn't know how to teach it very well. His lectures are very muddled. His tests are very hard, but he curves them very heavily, and most people end up with a B in the class if they put some effort into the class.

Doesn't seem competent enough to teach the class.  He takes way too long to explain things and afterwards people still don't understand.  He's pretty funny every now and then, but it doesn't excuse his poor teaching method.

I've never enjoyed a class more! I learned so many valuable skills and the discussions were absolutely the best part of this class. Dr. Kate is super understanding and supportive and genuinely wants to help you succeed. Your participation matters more than anything else so if you're passionate about social issues then this is the class for you!

I had her for the Humanities Scholar class. If you're an incoming freshman planning on joining the scholars program, you will LOVE Dr. Kate! She is so genuine, down to earth, and hands down the best professor I had this semester. Graded work is mostly response papers to articles that we read for the week, which were all (imo) so so interesting!
Dr. Kate is a phenomenal teacher! She is well read and respected. She is flexible with deadlines as long as you communicate with her. Lots of reading.
I freaking love Dr.Drabinski... my goat

Literally one of the most inspirational and kind people I've ever met. Dr. Kate takes such an incredibly personal interest in every student, and will do anything to help you succeed regardless of your situation. Classes were so fun and I learned so much from discussions. I absolutely adore Dr. Kate!

If you don't take this professor you are making a mistake!!! If you read the class description for GWST 200 and find it interesting YOU WILL LOVE THIS COURSE. Dr. Kate made my semester amazing and she made me excited to come to class. Coursework is very manageable and you get to do a fun project about an activism topic you care about.

Dr. Kate is an amazing professor who creates a welcoming environment in the classroom. She's very accessible outside of class and understand that we are human (and is therefore flexible w/ deadlines, within reason). This was not the first time I've taken one of her courses and it definitely will not be the last. I could not recommend her more.

Dr. Kate honestly cares about all her students. She wants to hear your opinions and is flexible with extensions and making sure people are getting the grades they want. She's a super easy A and she's the sweetest.

Dr. Kate is amazing, she is extremely knowledgeable on the topics of gender and sexuality studies and is able to explain the topics very well. The class is reading heavy but there are no tests or quizzes, and instead is mostly discussion based. Dr. Kate is also very understanding of absences and late work, and very supportive of her students.

Dr. Kate is a wonderful professor!! She really gets to know all students on a more personal level and facilitates really interesting discussions during class that keep everyone engaged. 

This course was very much a reading + discussion based class. Be prepared to do lots of reading!
My favorite professor on campus. This class you learn so much just by showing up. Light workload and she will give you extensions when needed. She is just so funny and caring.

Dr. Kate is amazing!! This was my highest level class, but literally my easiest. There's a few difficult readings, but going over it in class made it a lot easier to understand. Discussions in class were very interesting and easy to participate in! Dr. Kate is very funny but also approaches everything in a very respectful way. Great professor!!

Amazing professor!!! Would 100% take this class again. Had one short paper due at the start of the week and blog posts/comments twice a month. Really worth it for an upper level course and learned a lot.

Last fall, I enrolled in her GWST220 course and absolutely loved all of her lectures; she made things approachable and had you consider diverse LGBTQ+ views. She has a weekly discussion for the articles you read, and she makes them manageable; she even gives extra credit, extensions on unit papers, and no tests. NL

Convinced Dr. Kate is the best professor ever. There's a reason she has these reviews and everyone is saying they would take her again--she is passionate, smart, funny, engaging, and above all truly cares about and makes an effort to show that she understands her students' needs and concerns. Her love for the subject matter shines through. :)

Dr. Kate is one of the kindest Professors you will find. Is happy to give extensions on course work, course work is quite minimal, and you get out of the class what you put into it. There is no mandatory attendance, and the class is discussion based, so its lots of students sharing thoughts on assigned readings. Blog posts are cool, and easy final.

Dr. Kate is my favorite professor at UMBC. She's knowledgeable, an effective teacher, and flexible when it comes to deadlines. Her lectures are some of the most thought provoking I have ever attended. I find myself looking forward to classes with her because I know they will always be interested.

She is amazing!! Took her class Fall 2020 and I learned so many new, interesting things. Just need to show that you did the reading and understood the material in the weekly one page response papers. There were three exams and you have two weeks to write them.

I took GWST210 over the winter so my experience may be a little different than most, but Dr. Kate was extremely understanding and easy to get along with. The material covered was easy to understand and she was very clear with her expectations. Mostly graded on unit papers but very easy to complete if youve been paying attention
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Dr. Kate is such a great professor. Her obvious care for each of her students comes through in her teaching, and she will genuinely try to form a personal relationship with you, which I appreciated. Realizes that life happens outside of class, and only concrete HW is readings and a page of response on them, besides a few project updates.

Dr Kate is the BEST prof I ever taken at UMBC. She is very understanding of student issues, and is willing to help. Her class is engaging, and teaches important concepts. If you go to class and participate/take notes, you will get an A. She wants everyone to pass.

This is one of the most eye-opening classes I've take in college so far. Dr. Kate is hilarious and very passionate about the subject. She's also extremely understanding when it comes to things like absences and deadline extensions. You're mostly graded on unit essays, which are largely dependent on the readings you do throughout the semester.

Dr. Kate is an amazing professor! Her classes are very relaxed and she makes the content very interesting. She is super understanding of students lives and makes sure everyone is on track for success. There are only about 4 papers and a group project but with the notes from class and the readings, they are easy A's as long as you take notes.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Hilarious

reviews.comment: I was new to UMBC (transfer) and felt so at home in her class that I changed my major to GWST (she's also my advisor now because of it!) The most caring professor I've ever encountered. I can't wait to take her more now due to my major switch! (There is no assigned textbook for this class but there IS readings which I really recommend reading)
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Caring

reviews.comment: This is an excellent course to take and an incredible professor. Dr. Kate is hilarious, teaches with enthusiasm and really grabs your attention in class. While attendance wasn't graded, it is recommended to do well on exams. Be prepared to read a lot, too.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Dr. Kate is a very caring professor and is generous with due dates and extra credit opportunities, she wants you to get an A if you come to class! There are many readings throughout this course but she has a discussion on them in class (so you don't really have to read all of them). The course material is also very interesting, but be open-minded!
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Gives good feedback--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Dr. Kate is absolutely amazing!!! She is caring, genuine, and so so funny!  There are few assignments and not too much reading is required. But when there is a reading assignment, just do it.  (She sees it as a bit disrespectful if you don't.)  She also presents two group projects.  Super great class and amazing lectures! Plus, no exams! Yay!!

Great professor! Hilarious, caring, and understanding. The readings are cool but if you don't do them you'll be fine, as she explains them at the beginning of class. Really interesting subject material and expect fun, discussion based lecture classes. One group project but it's not too difficult. Would love to take another class with her.
My favorite professor always and forever.  Dr. Kate is knowledgeable, hilarious, and makes every lecture interesting.

Dr. Kate's class is so interesting. Attendance is not really mandatory but the content is so interesting and the lectures are important, especially if you slack on the readings. Participation is easy and helps you get a good grade. Three easy online "exams" and one group project but if you keep an open mind and discuss in class, you'll be okay.

Professor is super nice and cool guy. Class was difficult and a lot of material, but shouldn't be hard to get at least a B if you do extra credit opportunities he gives and show up to class. I didn't read the textbook once and almost got an A

Exams and study guides are 78% of the course, already pretty rough for students who aren't the best test takers, but he does drop one at the end of the course. Boring lectures so there's really nothing to do, (no homework besides videos due at he end of the semester).

Bro made me want to rip my hair out. He overcomplicates EVERYTHING. You ask a simple question and he just confuses you more. He makes you do a study guide and grades it but you have to email him seprately to find out what you got wrong and need to study. Whats the point of a study guide if you cant even study from it. HATED this class dont take it
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Fall 2025 | As a first time professor, Dr. Strobach's class was more in-depth than a lot of intro courses, which I loved. He's receptive to student feedback, made exams easier, & cut content as the semester progressed. The content itself isn't difficult. Highly recommend if you're interested in geography. Not recommended if you just want an easy A.

The exams make up most of your grade, which are difficult. It was his first time teaching, and he had a monotone voice that was not engaging. He was very knowledgeable, but not the best professor as his teaching style wasnt my favorite. The exams were based on the lecture slides, which were always jam-packed with information for an intro class.

This is Professor Strobach's first time teaching however I do think he could do a few things to improve. He is very very passionate and obviously smart in his field, yet I think he could make the exams a lot less confusing. I also feel that he could explain topics a lot better than he has in the class.

Professor Strobach is clearly passionate about his field and is an expert. However, as this was his first time teaching, a lot of the class was TOO much- especially for an intro class. The exam questions are confusing and extensive, covering a lot in a short period. Strobach was willing to change styles to help students, but it didn't work for me
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I personally really enjoyed having Professor Strobach. There is a lot of interesting material that he goes very in depth about, and he clearly knows what he is teaching. I would only say that the most crucial information of the course lies in the lectures; if you pay attention and study hard for exams, you will pass.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I'm not sure about my grade yet, but Dr. Strobach did well for a first-time professor. He's funny, detailed, and very supportive. My only concern is the exams; “confusing” is probably the best word. He tries to rephrase questions in a way that ends up being unclear. I really enjoyed the class, but those exams… I don't know, man ToT

He's a new professor and trying his best though his class is very test heavy and it goes into great depth with the topics covered. Expect to study a lot and if you are not disciplined I would not recommend this class.

Professor Strobach is a very clear teacher who communicates well. His lectures and power points are very in depth and detailed and he always posts the slides the day before class so that you can access them when you need. The class itself is pretty test heavy with a lot of content, so make sure that you actually study and prepare! Don't wing it.

Not sure why there are a lot of negative reviews. I do agree that she can improve on grading with time and replying to emails more often, but other than that I've enjoyed her personality and classes. I took 309 and currently 311 with her, 312 next. She is really understanding and easy to talk to.

I think these reviews/rating is inaccurate, this is my second class with Dr. Evans, Her deadlines are extremely lenient and she always so considerate of students. You just need to show up, participate and do the work on time.

Avoid this professor at all costs. Severe time management problems and grading, while very late, was very unforgiving with no feedback whatsoever. Emails sent to the professor asking for help were completely ignored or unhelpful. The class itself was disorganized, with much time spent on tangents that had absolutely nothing to do with the class.

This professor struggles with time management and grading assignments in a timely manner. When students reach out for help, emails often go unanswered or responses are vague and unhelpful. Assignments were dropped due to being behind, which limited learning, and the course felt disorganized with little meaningful instruction blamed not having a TA

She never graded the assignments until the end of the semester, everytime you emailed her, never replied. She just talk and talks at class sometimes stuff that doesn't concern us.We get behind a lot, the worst class.

If you are interested in taking her course in PSYCH 312, please DO NOT REGISTER FOR HER CLASS. The teacher assistant grades everyone work and takes days off during the semester when the class needs her.

She gives terrible feedback takes way too long to grade, like how are you going to be slow and give zero feedback? When I asked for more thorough feedback and quicker grading she threatened to report me for plagiarism all because I forgot to include one source in my reference list. Unhelpful and incredibly discouraging

Perhaps Dr. Evans is respected in her field but as a professor there is a lot to be desired. Delayed grading, lack of encouraging or useful feedback. Uses degradation and threats of reprimand as ways to ensure compliance. This was a miserable experience and hope Dr. Evans finds her true calling.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Not a good teacher, terrible at explaining topics, getting in contact with her is impossible, takes forever to grade, assigns very important and time consuming assignments that take about a week to complete to be done in only 3 days, and she will give poor directions for assignments and be confused how you didn't do well on it.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Worst professor ever!

The professor is irresponsible in her scheduling and takes time off too many times. The grading is done by her teacher assistant so beware. The work is very diffcult and demanding, if you take this class keep up. A research paper is due at the end of the semester (heads up 9-12 pgs).

Very rude and unprofessional. Enforces strict policies but cancels class often for personal trips. Hard to reach, unpleasant in class, and grades harshly. Even if you attend and do your work, she's not reasonable. Avoid taking her if possible it's a frustrating experience overall. Mind you, the class it's self is not hard it's just her.

The single worst professor I've ever had. Snarky, lazy, strict, and unhelpful. Cancelled the third week of classes to go to Disney, and stopped lecturing altogether 3 weeks before the end of the semester. Doesn't accept doctor's notes and has a strict late work policy despite frequently being late herself. Finals week is hectic and exams are tough.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Leaves zero useful feedback. I am a 4.0 student who apparently can't even conduct a proper reference page in her class.

The course material isn't difficult but there are SO MANY modules that are just a repeat of lecture. Part of the group work grade is on how other members rate you, so it's out of your control. She gets off topic a lot when lecturing. There is a sign in sheet every class and it counts towards your total grade. Not difficult but VERY annoying.

Dr. E was a wonderful professor. I found her explanations of difficult content very helpful, and I understood concepts that I had not before because of her. She is very approachable and will hear you out if you disagree with one of her answers. She sticks to her syllabus, which is really helpful for staying organized and on top of everything.
Dr. E is super caring and really wants her students to succeed. She is engaging and enthusiastic about teaching. Overall a great teacher.
Very slow to grade

This teacher is awful! Grades were weeks late for assignments so there was no feedback before doing the next assignment. When asking questions for clarification responses were quick but snarky and unhelpful. The entire class she would be eating, working out, or have distractions like her dog whining. Lecture was boring and lacked valuable info.
Not good. the worst psych professor you could have

She actively seems to want students not to succeed. This semester with her has been detrimental to my emotional and mental well-being. She is disorganized, clueless, expects students to be understanding to her numerous missed classes & mess ups but doesn't try to be understanding to their circumstances AT ALL. A wolf in sheep's clothing. AVOID HER!

"My sincere apologies" is her go to phrase. Unorganized, passive, and careless. Her lectures are boring and her knowledge is limited. She canceled classes many times. Although she does bare minimum as a teacher, she is such a tough grader. She might seem nice but she is really not! Not good in communication either.  Avoid her!

I've never had an experience with a class like I had with Evans. Please avoid taking her if you care about your gpa. She is very stingy with grading and doesn't grade assignment rights away (You'd have to wait a week or two). She never gave us access to the final assignments until the end of the semester,which we now have to cram in a couple weeks.

Worst professor I have ever had. She gets extremely passive aggressive. She is obnoxiously slow with grading, troublesome when assignments build off of each other. When this was pointed out, she got more passive aggressive and didnt attempt to be understanding. She offers feedback for the paper but does not give it. She overexplains simple things.
He is way too petty and stingy with grading. You can literally follow every single criteria, yet never get full credit on an assignment. Avoid!
Avoid taking. Takes too long to enter in grades.
This was a hybrid class, but I never went. All the work is easy to do, just tedious and plenty. Had to write two papers, but those were simple to do. Overall, an easy A.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Nice and personable. During the semester she seemed to have a lot going on in her life which is unfortunate but she seemed to be very unorganized and even unaware of what was going on in her own course. Thankfully, the work was pretty easy and she has very helpful and detailed lecture slides, so detailed you do not even need to come to class.

Dr. Evans is a great person but she is an unorganized professor. Grading is consistently late. I reached out for help on final project, she told me the semester was over (2 days before the project was due). I just got half credit for a homework assignment bc the directions were wrong (the day before the semester is over). Frustrating.
One of the best instructors I had at UMBC. Dr. E is caring ad amazing. She will do the best she can to make her students succeed and she is very accessible outside of the class.

Dr. Evans is super chillll. She really works with everyone to make sure they really understand the material. Material over all is easy as long as u understand basic statistics. Students who didnt understand stat continued to hold the class back (even though stat is a prerequisite). Highly recommend dr. Evans shes it guys she is it.
Random pop quizzes to take attendance. 3 exams make up more than 70% of your grade and there is no study guide. Lectures are long and you can't use electronics to take notes.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Beware of pop quizzes--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Great professor in my opinion. If you pay attention in class and take notes, you will do fine in this class. His lectures are awesome and super entertaining. He doesn't take attendance, but enforces this by giving pop quizzes. To pass those, you need to be in lectures and listen. If you do this, this is a really fun class with a awesome professor.

professor ealick is very funny and nice towards his students. he does not take attendance, but will give pop quizzes every now and then, which are a bit difficult if u don't attend lectures. grade is based on those pop quizzes + a few papers. he is a very slow grader, but is fair and makes up for it by extending deadlines. very understanding!

had this prof for PHIL100, PHIL380, and PHIL478; besides being a very slow grader at times and only basing grades off a small handful of assignments, the assignments are relatively straightforward if you put in any effort and he's very funny and very nice with students

The professor has a great sense of humor and connects concepts to real life. While grading can be tough, attending lectures and using tools like unstuck AI for study prep makes the class manageable. Worth taking if you enjoy writing.

He wasn't a bad professor he just takes way too long to grade. He gives random pop quizzes so look over notes before every class. I got a B because I did bad on all the quizzes but I got As on all the essays which were really easy. Not too much work and overall an easy class.

Amazing lectures!! Made the class participate in a way that caused students to challenge previous beliefs. Every class was interesting. While attendance isn't mandatory, skipping can result in quizzes being more difficult.

Professor Ealick is my favorite professor in college. His lectures were interesting and engaging, I felt that I learned a lot and also there was very little work. He does not take attendance but he does give very easy pop quizzes which are instead of attendance. I also take scientific reasoning online with him and that is great as well.

He is very engaging when he lectures and his class was by far one of my favorites this semester. He is a bit slow on grading but he is very lenient. Hands down one of the easiest classes i've taken, just make sure to go to his lectures because the pop quizzes are based around his lectures.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: He hates all forms of technology and will snap if he sees any. His lectures were okay and the workload was quite easy, but you will get almost 0 to no grades back before the end of the semester. If you do all ur work early you can get it out of the way. He cares abt what he's lecturing and doesn't seem mean or condescending.

I found the lectures super engaging and the concepts interesting. Sometimes his comments would be jarring, but they're meant to stop students from spacing-out, I think. Super slow grader, incredibly so. But he is aware of this and gives extensions. Knock out the 4 essays in the beginning, show up for pop quizzes, and it'll be your easiest class.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Amazing lectures --Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: First PHIL class I've taken, but was still able to understand the material and engage in class. It's part lecture, part discussion. Read the material and be ready to make comments/ask questions in class. Loved how he added humor and made the class laid back.

Professor Ealick's class was not hard. He's not a hard grader, but his ways of teaching may be old school. Unknown amount of quizzes, and 3 very easy papers no exams. Will not allow make-ups unless you provide a sick note or something of the sort. He's kind and funny during lecture. Important to pay attention and do the readings for your papers.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I took Greg Ealick for Philosophy of Mind, and this class was very interesting for me. I believe upper-level philosophy courses in general require a fair level of interest in the material, but Greg Ealick does a great job of getting the class's attention through humor and an obvious breadth of knowledge of the material. He can come off as arrogant.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Inspirational--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Prof. Ealick is genuinely one of my fave professors I've had at UMBC. He's super funny and a very entertaining lecturer. He takes a while getting grades back, but is lenient on deadlines for papers, and often pushes back due dates. If I have room for an AH elective in my schedule, he'll be one one of the top picks.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Hilarious--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Professor Ealick is a great professor and is very good at what he does. He is very understanding and gives great feedback, I would totally recommend taking this class because it was very enjoyable. Be aware that there is a lot of reading and note taking for this class. The assignments are fairly easy and he is very fair when grading.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: There are three papers, weekly quizzes and discussion posts that you have to do for this class. Overall I think it's a pretty easy class and Professor Ealick gives good metaphors and stories to help explain the concepts being taught. He cares about his students and is accessible outside of class!

He is really funny and a great teacher. I enjoyed how he connected the topics to daily life and other funny similarities. He is a very lenient grader and as long as you are listening to what is going on in class, you can do great on the quizzes and assignments.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Professor Ealick's lectures are amazing. This course was the most interesting I encountered, and prof makes the content engaging. Must blog 5 times per week, biweekly quizzes, and 4 papers. Prof's only flaw is that he doesn't grade!!!! The agony of waiting until finals week to receive grades was unacceptable. Beware unless confident in writing!

Great professor would 100% recommend! He made lectures fun and engaging. This class was very enjoyable to take but if you don't like writing it may not be the best fit. Besides that he is super understanding and tries his best to grade papers in a somewhat timely manner so that you know how you're doing in the course and what to do to improve.

His class was lecture heavy and there was around 15+ pages of reading to do before each class. The readings were often confusing but weren't really necessary until you do the unit quiz and essay. His lectures were boring but if you participate it's fine. He is an easy grader and is lenient in working with individual students. Overall a chill prof.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--So many papers--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Absolutely hated this class. It's good if you like logic, bad if you like language, even though it's called Philosophy of Language. His sense of humor is degrading to students and makes you feel bad for asking questions over email. In person is fine, though. He grades rather high while having confusing quizzes that cover things not in the lecture.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--So many papers

reviews.comment: He was fine. Nothing great. Some positives- It is a fairly average class, not much work. His humor is great, always enjoyed the actual lecture. Negatives- Grading, just as others say. There is not a great indication of how to actually study. There is no book, only readings and class notes. He doesn't write notes, you write what he is speaking.

Professor Ealick was hilarious. He plays off the energy from the class. He tries to balance the sophistication of the material with modern references mixing with some profanity and edginess. His end of the class paper is really when you can meet with him outside of class and discover that he truly cares about each students learning.

This class takes more work than you would think. He grades the essays very hard and the pop quizzes include very specific questions from lectures. He promises to have assignments graded time and time again and ends up grading them last minute. Not a fan.
reviews.rating_tags: Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: horrible. take phil100, not 152, if you want an easy arts credit. just oof.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Tough grader. But he expects students to be understanding when he doesn't return half of the grades until the end of the semester. This leaves students stuck if they do not like a grade they received, because they have no more opportunities to make changes and bring their grade up.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Lecture heavy, good attendance and detailed note taking are mandatory to do well on the weekly quizzes.
