Points are deducted for the most frivolous of reasons, and his TA's are very slow at grading and updating BB. There are three essays and you get to choose which topic to write about, but the final essay is worth the most points.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Get ready for pop quizzes and be specific while answering the pop quizes as he takes points off unfairly. I took his class thinking to boost my GPA because it was 100 level class but it was lot harder than any programming class I took here at UMBC. Avoid him at any cost.
reviews.rating_tags: Test heavy--Beware of pop quizzes--Tough grader

reviews.comment: I'm in my final year at UMBC and Ealick is the worst professor I've had. His pop quizzes are unfair, he uses profanity far too often, and he was rude to students. He snapped at people for simple questions and accused me of plagiarism with no evidence. It's a shame because the material was interesting and he often gave good lectures. Don't take him.

Not an easy A for a 100 Lvl class. Class itself is easy, but grading is arbitrary, with few assignments. Got points taken off final paper for things he didn't mention in instructions. He was mad when I pointed them out. Got points back, but I had to argue and he was toxic about it the whole time. Disappointed, because he was a funny guy. Not worth.

Cool dude; really chill and funny and makes lectures really interesting and you're sure not to doze off. Make sure you do well on the weekly quizzes; there mostly just a few questions on the definitions of the topics covered in class. For essays, make sure to back up your claim and be detailed and straightforward.

You have to go to every class because he lectures without the use of powerpoint or the board, so you have to pay attention. However, that is easy to do because he keeps the lecture interesting and engaging with his stories, amazing humor, and examples. Take lecture notes and you'll do fine on any quiz and exam. He grades fairly and is accessible.

I think hes pretty unprofessional. Not only are his jokes kinda really rude sometimes, but he also just creeps me out. He always wears jeans that he lets sag low and hes also always got sweat stains on his chest even if its 50 degrees out. Definitely wouldnt feel comfortable going to his office hours. Other than that, the class was fine.

He's very knowledgeable and does great at lecturing, but if you need a visual to learn, you're not going to get it. Personally, I don't like him too much, I think he has a bit of an ego, but he's certainly not a bad guy. He's a tough grader, make sure you have all the info you need but not TOO much or he'll complain about that too.
reviews.rating_tags: Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Terrible at getting grades back, never writes anything on the board so lectures are confusing sometimes, tough grader Too hard and too much stress for an intro class, I would not take this again ever
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Ealick is great and makes class fun. He gives lectures from his head instead of presenting slides so writing down important info is on you. The class itself was great and very interesting; I would strongly recommend it. The discussion section is with a TA where you take a quiz each week. Other than that there is two short papers and one long.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Sometimes the lectures were boring, sometimes not! Taking Prof. Ealick again this coming spring. My main issue was the TAs graded our work, and one TA graded much harder than the other. I felt as if there wasn't much communication between the professor and the TAs.

The class had about 20 people in it. You have to delve deep into the readings. Coursework was graded consistently, the criteria is basically that you demonstrate you understand the material for a B, and an A means you demonstrate a philosophical jump onto deeper analysis. Loved the class. He is not intimidating, you just cant BS him.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Professor Ealick is a charismatic individual. He makes lots of jokes, yet some come off as needlessly edgy or crude. Nonetheless, he is very passionate about the material. If you show up and do the readings, you can pass easily. Strict on grading, and exams would have no scores higher than a 92 but none lower than a 70. Randomly gives quizzes.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: I loved his class, he's a great funny guy. Go to lecture, listen and take notes and you'll get an A

Aside from the interesting material, this class was awful. The professor is rather arrogant and is terrible about posting grades when he says he will. I still haven't gotten back my last exam despite him saying that he'd have it up over 2 weeks ago. He's passionate about philosophy but his snapping at students and lack of returning emails ruined it
reviews.rating_tags: BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Professor Ealick is genuinely knowledgable about philosophy. He jumps around a bit when giving lectures, but overall wants to make sure his students understand the material. This class is worth taking, but make sure to read over your notes before each class. Ealick is unfair in terms of pop quizzes and if you aren't prepared, it'll knock your grade
reviews.rating_tags: BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Ealick is really funny and his lectures are interesting. He's disorganized, but he makes up for it in lecture. There are quizzes in discussion, 2 short papers, and 1 long final paper. Never go on your phone or interrupt him (especially when he's about to get to the point). Still participate and ask questions; he's interested in everyone's thoughts.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Seems like a cool professor at first, but was not accessible outside of class at all. His instructions for the assignments are "intentionally vague", but he clearly has a specific expectation of what he wants you to write for the assignments, even though he does not explain them at all. Be careful. I had a pretty bad experience with him.
2 exams and 1 paper. Read the articles and he will discuss them in class. He was slow to grade the exam and paper, but he was fair grader.

This is my first semester at UMBC, and prof. Ealick is one of my favorites! His lectures are always very interesting; never a dull moment. There are easy weekly quizzes in discussion, 2 short writing assignments, and 1 final paper. BE-FRIEND THE TA to get a good grade. His class sparked an interest in philosophy in me that I never thought I had.
Homework was often interesting.  Fair.  Maybe a little flighty but knowledgeable.

Your grade consists of weekly reading quizzes, 2 short writing projects, and 1 longer final paper.  The workload itself isn't difficult.  What is difficult is that there is little clarity on what we are being graded on in our papers.   I think As on papers are hard to come by in this class.

He is smart, funny, easy going, and hippie-like. He is one of my favorite professors that I have had since starting school. He's also really laid back. He doesn't or rarely ever writes anything on the board so you'll have to listen to him carefully when taking notes.  He also doesn't structure his lecture to a tee but that's fine. Awesome class :)

For all of you out there that want an easy A for a humanity, don't take him. He isn't clear about what is need to get an A and didn't pass back the last test (there are 3) or the final paper. Didn't feel like arguing over my grades with him but will never think about taking another class with him. He's a really smart guy though.

If you take Phil 150, the morality class, BEFRIEND THE TA! Heshe will grade all your quizzes, papers, and even the final paper. The TA control's your grade! You can show up and listen to the amusing lectures, but reading the book before the quiz may be fine as well. Overall easy class- do the work and have TA make corrections and you'll get an A.

Pretty simple clear cut class. For 150, Contemporary Moral Issues, you show up to lecture, take some light notes and do readings for homework (10 pagesweek, interesting to me). Quizzes are short and simple. I think he lectures well and is pretty funnyinteresting.  For 152, Intro to Moral Theory, same stuff basically. I enjoyed the class overall

Professor Ealick's course is mainly Socratic and the discussions are interesting. However, Ealick himself is not very helpful and is often rude and unsympathetic when approached with questions or concerns. He was not very helpful, and was quite intimidating. I found myself worried to ask questions out of fear that he would be rude to me.
Awesome class to take, lots of fun, not too hard.

Attendance isn't mandatory, but he flips a coin at the beginning of every class to tell if we will have a quiz based on reading- so you have to go to class. He clearly likes the subject, but I found him rude and unhelpful. He made you feel dumb for asking questions. I don't recommend him at all. I really disliked him! Hard grader, too!

Funny guy and knows his stuff. But when it comes to grading things he gets lazy, which has its pros and cons. He wasn't clear on the final paper which was a pain to deal with, and is easily irritated when you ask him to repeat something.

The funniest professor I've ever had. His humor is a bit dark, but it's not too bad. I would retake his class if I didn't have to pay for it. DO NOT BE LATE TO CLASS. I had a quiz every Friday during discussion, so it wasn't random. I really didn't read a whole lot from the book, but sometimes the quizzes were on the readings.

Interesting man.  Class was interesting but do not play with your phone, computer, etc. in class, and DO NOT fall asleep. He will get mad. Also, takes a long time to grade assignments and curses regularly in class.

This class was really boring. Attendance is not mandatory but he flips a coin every class to see if you have a quiz so you pretty much have to go. Not very helpful and didn't repeat if you missed something. I would recommend taking PHIL100 with Jim Thomas. If his class is already full, wait a semester!

By far the worst professor I have ever had. He was very unwilling to help students when they asked for assistance and his examples were extremely disturbing and inappropriate. Extremely sarcastic and automatically assumed that if a student did not understand something it was because they did not do the readings.
Very interesting class and lectures.

To be honest, I was looking forward to this class and thought it would be an easy "A" but it wasn't. You actually have to work hard. He lectures the whole entire time and most of the time, it's difficult to pay attention or stay awake. He doesn't grade anything. That's what the TAs are for and they kinda suck. Not the best professor. Try to avoid.

Ealick has no idea what he is doing. Most of his lectures are just random information thrown at you with no focus or direction related to the material. Honestly, how do you know what you're going to be tested on if the lectures aren't clear. Not an easy A. Avoid.

Very knowledgeable man. Requires 3 short papers (3-4 pages), and 1 final paper (6-10 pages). If you are a philosophy major and have written philosophical papers before, take his 454 course; easy 'A'. If not, it will be a struggle, but a solid 'B' is reasonable. He talks the entire time, so staying awake is a struggle. Assigns interesting readings.

Not a very good philosophy teacher at all. When he lectures he goes very fast. If you ask him to repeat something he can't remember what he just said. Must read textbook and take notes in class as best as you can.

As a nonphil major, I only take this class for my gen ed credits. Its not that bad of a class. You must go to class and take good notes and don't fall asleep while I do sometimes...Exams are not that hard. Read some of the book, the most useful material are class notes.
Nice guy but definitively didnt sense the energy or humor mentioned in all the previous feedback. Dry chuckles at most and potential quiz for every class.

He's such a stranger person. Some people found his lectures funny but I thought some of the stuff he mentioned was messed up and inappropriate even for college kids. Every class he flipped a coin on whether there would be a quiz so you have to keep up with the readings and go to class. I thought it would be an easy class but it wasnt

Excellent. He is hilarious, just pay attention. His exams are easy, just take a while. Everyone gets a low A or a high B on the exams, the key is to do well on the quizzes. He curves your grade up if he thinks you deserve it, so participate. He is awesome, just go to class and you have an A.

Awesome teacher, just be sure to be involved in discussion (which is often hilarious).  He presents the material clearly and is straightforward, just take notes when you aren't laughing at his crazy jokes.

He is fantastic! Totally hilarious, very helpful, write down everything he says and you'll  fine. Although, you can tell he gets annoyed when people aren't getting him and they keep making stupid examples but as long as its not you it's pretty funny.
Great Guy, Great Professor.
Ealick is the man. However, I would recommend going to each lecture and taking good notes. dont bother reading the text book

I did not use the textbook, waste of 80 bucks. He covers everything during lecture so just take notes and you ll be fine. He helps with the papers during office hour and the TA was really helpful. This was one of my favorite classes. I mean, the lecture is actually very thought provoking and exciting.

I LOVED Phil of Bio with Prof. Ealick. He is, by far, one of the most knowledgable profs. I have had, and is very well read. His lectures can be a bit circular though, and he doesn't make any notes on the board, so learn to take notes FAST! He grades VERY harshly, so be prepared to work at your essays. Very approachable.

Ever since I have been at UMBC, I prefer Ealick's class more than any other professors within the Philosophy department. During Ealick's lecture, his material is easy to understand, cleverly humorous, and just downright charismatic where you just cannot wait to go to his next lecture. Outside of class, he's AWESOME. He is willing to help anytime!

Ealick is an awesome professor! He is hilarious and he makes the class really fun and interesting. There is a textbook, but he knows that most people don't read it, and you could get by just going to lectures and taking some notes. Attendance isn't mandatory. And there are pop quizzes, but he almost always drops hints the class before the quiz.

Extremely interesting as a person and as a teacher.  His lectures are a bit unfocused, and he suffers fools a little too leniently, but that's forgivable.  Has obviously read widely in the relevant literature, and knows the terrain backward and forward.  Very funny guy, as well.  Recommended, if you can deal with the lack of overall organization.
Awesome professor. made the concepts very easy to understand if you attend lectures and pay attention. He's hilarious which made the lectures fun to go to. Best class I've taken thus far

I took the Philosophy of Science Fiction this summer and it was a really great class.  Prof. Ealick gives good, everyday examples to explain philosophical concepts.  I would recommend taking Ealick's class if you have the opportunity.
Ealick really made philosophy easy to understand - at least the parts that he covered in lectures.  If you attend the lectures and take good notes, you will do well in Ealick's classes.

this class is not 'mandatory', but there are a few surprise quizzes & yes go to class. mostly lecture. he is a VERY funny teacher that likes to use sarcasm, but in the most positive way. I had a hard time understanding the material because I'm not a philosophy major. He is approachable :)

Do not buy the book. I wasted money on it. Never used it. Just listen to his lectures. Hard part is lectures can be boring. The quizzes he gives are on the lectures. Everything is free response. I think it is impossible to get an A in his class. Tried my hardest ended up with a high B. I hear Jim Thomas is way cooler.

This review will sound conflicting: The class material and his lectures are interesting(if you are a philosophy student), however, he is the laziest professor I have ran into. He does not have a set rubric for papers, and he arbitrarily throws in grades on papers. If the class is graded on papers, dont even think about an A.

I thought the class would be easy and somewhat interesting. But he pretty much sucks. The class is boring and you leanr nothing. I don't pay much attention and you could still get by. There are some pop quizzes but he tells you when they are. There pretty easy. Tests are easy as well if you prepare. He is unprofessional. Doesn't give  note at all!!
loved him as a teacher, i actually LIKED waking up to go to this class... best teacher, made me interested in philosophy

Take Notes. There is a quiz once a week about what was gone over  in lecture (reading the book can be subsituted for class depending on the TA you get), two short essays you need to write and one long essay. None of the essays have set due dates and you can write about a variety of subjects discussed in class. He's very interested in philosophy.
An overall great teacher!  Incredibly interesting, clear to understand, and knowledgeable in the material covered.  Highly recommended.

I came in ready for some fundamentalist beyond reach or insane liberal.  Ealick kept a tight grasp on the class, which was amazing.  The focus wasn't the inflammatory topics or opinions, but the formal logic and rhetorical skill behind the argumentation presented.  Provides a good preview of what other phil classes will expect.

Great professor. Taught epistemology from a modern viewpoint so the material was somewhat unfamiliar and more difficult. Grades based on three short (4-page) papers and a 10-15 pager. His comments are very helpful. Very helpful professor in general. Class is all discussion of material from the readings, so definitely read ahead to do well.

He has pop quizzes that are very confusing and he grades them very hard. But he makes it obvious when the pop-quizzes are. You REALLY have to work HARD for his class. I am an engineering major and i signed up "thinking" Phil 100 would be easy but it really isn't. On top of all my coursework PHIL 100 also was there to make things much harder.

I didn't really like this class. I mean, I thought the debates on the subjects (abortion, euthanasia, capital punishment) were interesting, but I felt he just shot down anything anyone (philosophers in the book and students, alike) said about the topics. I thought he could be funny, but, honestly, I just thought of him as a huge elitist.

He's a nice guy with a lot of fun in him but he doesn't like psychology much (my major...) so don't mention it.  His tests and paper can sneak up on you but they are ultimately fair and he is relatively understanding.  Keep up with the book.  This is not a guaranteed easy class, period.
Great and interesting teacher. Everything you need to know for the exams he says in lecture, so come to class always and take notes. He's very helpful and tries to explain things clearly.

the material was boring, but he did his best to make it more interesting. exams were all essay format so you must know how to write effectively, he can be a bit picky about wording. show up to class, the book isn't that helpful so getting the notes is a must!
Brilliant man! Thanx for the knowledge. You will love his yipee boots
good teach. delivers material well. May the gnomes be with you GE

Excellent teacher! If you go to class and take notes you will be fine. He is really helpful and you will never be bored in class. He gives great examples and makes sure you undersatnd the material. Loved him!
Has great examples and stories to back everything up, makes all concepts crystal clear.  He is the stereotypical awesome "Dead Poet Society" cool college professor, and thats a good thing.

Ealick is one of the most interesting professors you will ever have. When he gets excited he talks like Macho Man Randy Savage. "Snap into a Slim Jim!" If that isn't convincing enough he kind of looks like a pirate. You should definitely take class with this guy.

Best teacher I've had at UMBC thus far. Very logical, organized in lecture but also engaging. I learned a lot and the work load was not bad at all; he gives very fair quizzes and tests. Great class, great teacher: definitely recommend.
He's a good teacher and makes the class interesting.  He practically teaches right out of the book.  I regret spending that $60.

He's an excellent teacher who always has an intersting little tangent to tell the class to keep them engaged. Is very reasonable in grading, and doesn't make tests that try to trick you. If you want to be intelectually stimulated, take have this teacher.
No Comments
He is great.  One of the smartest people I've ever met.  Just ask him about debate stories.  Expect to learn a lot.

A really great professor, he manages to engage the class in interesting information and ideas.  He's willingly to help you out if you have any questions at all, and is very down-to-Earth, in and out of the classroom.  Very good at getting the class thinking about things while leaving it open for input from him and other people.

(ANTH 320) She is a super sweet and caring professor who will work with you. Just know that this is not a side quest elective. Prepare to READ. These weekly annotated bibliographies are hard to get through. Prepare to read like 40+ pages of wordy and ancient readings and then write an annotated bibliography every week. Exams are open note.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Lectures were so boring but work was manageable as long as you do the 4 weekly readings that are 60 pages long. Allows index cards for 2 in-person exams. Does not enter grades until after finals.

Estabrook is a great professor, and this is a pretty easy class. Attendance is mandatory and graded. You don't really have to pay attention or take notes to be successful. There's a homework assignment every week; they're easy, but need to be handwritten/printed out. Everything on the exams is literally homework questions verbatim.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment:
Estabrook is a good and passionate professor, if you like the subject, she is good.

If taking for Elective credits, it has a fairly large amount of work for a 100 level, and has mandatory attendance, still not a bad option.

She's very eager to teach students, but also to make sure that they are learning and understand the material. Her lectures were hilarious—they had me chuckling a lot, even if the rest of the class was silent. Her syllabus scared me a little when I read it before the first class, but she's very nice and cares a lot about her work and her students.
She gives too much homework considering we are taking this class as an elective and the lecture is extremely boring there is no participation
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Estabrook is friendly and upbeat. Her lectures are easy to understand and her slides are very helpful. Her study guides are fantastic for preparing students for the three exams. Sometimes, her classes run a few minutes past the end time. The weekly homework assignments are easy but quite tedious as she has students handwrite them.

Class is pretty easy, she basically tells us exactly what topics are going to be on exam. Homework is ridiculous though, as it takes hours to hand write each week (not allowed to type) which is a complete waste of time.
Professor Estabrook was very well-rounded, giving good lectures and giving content outside of lectures that wasn't required but helped with homework, tests, etc.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Dr. Estabrook is a great professor. Class is made up of 3 exams, and there's 12 homework assignments. Attendance is mandatory, with 3 "sick days" allowed in the semester. Don't email her outside class hours, if you need anything ask a TA (if applicable) or go to office hours.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Great professor, clear in understanding, and is very passionate about what she is teaching. I would say the workload of the homework is a bit heavy and the homework takes around 3-4 hours to complete since it is handwritten. Very interesting class and insightful in general, but if you are just taking it for the credit do be ready for some work.

I honestly wish I could take every social work class with Dr. Evans. She is very straightforward with her grading criteria and breaks down a difficult semester-long assignment into shorter, more digestible parts. She gives good feedback and genuinely wants her students to succeed.
She gives assignments which encourage critical thinking amongst her students and which come in handy when they eventually become social workers

Dr. Evans is a really great, passionate professor. I enjoy her class and find it to be very manageable. She provides you with clear rubrics for papers and gives good feedback on your policy essay. The class consists of 2 papers and weekly quizzes along with some randomly sprinkled assignments. Her class is definitely one of my favorites.

This course is a lot of work, but Dr. Evans does a great job of working with you! You can tell she cares about her students and attempts to keep everyone engaged during lectures. Be prepared to write a lot, but its doable, and she gives you good feedback on your bill analysis. She also has opportunities for extra credit.

Good mix of lecture, video, class/small group discussion. Each week there is a decent amount of support material to read, watch, or listen to, and you should always count on having to report out on it in class discussions. This was one of the best classes I've ever taken. Papers spaced out well, but the standards are high, so use the time wisely.

Prof Evans is great, she's very kind and supportive and is passionate about social work. I enjoy going to her class, she is lenient about personal circumstances and cares about her students. I took the class for a GEP but it became my favorite class. She will also occasionally bring treats for the class too, which is pretty cool.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Lots of students struggle with this class. It very well may be the toughest in the SW dept. Dr. Evans does take her job seriously, that is true. The work SWers do when we graduate is serious and having a prof that pushes us and makes us better prepared for that work is important. She will help you if you ask for it and gives lots of feedback.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: The worst professor I have had by far. I think she assigns work out of pure enjoyment. If you can avoid her at all cost.
Lectures didnt have useful information needed to pass the quizzes/exams. Needs improvement on lectures. Asks for student feedback but does nothing with it. Not helpful towards class content concerns.
Dr. Evans is an amazing teacher. Her SOWK-360 is pretty writing intensive, but her guidelines are clear and she is a fair grader.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: DON'T take her class unless you're prepared for constant stress, frustration, and a genuinely miserable experience. She shows little to no concern for her students' success. Overall, an incredibly disappointing and exhausting experience. If you have any choice at all avoid her class. Instead, I highly recommend Dr. Hughes who is outstanding.

Nursing school was easier than her classes. If you can take Dr. Hughes, do it. She does not care about your time nor well being. Don't waste your time trying to talk with her either, she does not care.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: DO NOT TAKE HER unless you want a mental problem. she don't provide powerpoint. Test are heavily graded.

This course completely ruined me. She yelled at me for not understanding content one time! The other bio department professors talk bad behind her back and she grades papers subjectively! I lost many friends and dropped clubs because of how deep in depression i was due to this class. Her humor is a bit dark but she is extremely smart. you'll learn.

0 powerpoints. 0 grades posted online. 0 support. you will feel extremely isolated from your friends and family. the majority of your grade relies on your exams & quizzes, which has little to no multiple choice. pick a religion and pray honestly. on the bright side, she answers emails quick!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Nah don't...

I could not have had a more positive experience with Dr. Fleischmann. I first met her on an airplane and somehow a conversation started where we figured out that she is going to be professor in the future. She is so sweet, but her class is difficult. I absolutely worked by butt off for my A, but it was worth every second for the knowledge I gained.

There is way too much hearsay about this professor. She is the most supportive, sweet, and caring professor I have taken thus far. Yes her class is difficult and she was a difficult grader. However, her students will go on to know A&P like the back of their hand, as they should if they want to be healthcare professionals.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Very sweet, caring, and intelligent professor teaching a hard class. Knows what she's talking about and will go above and beyond to help, you just need to show her that you're putting in the effort. No online slides or grades posted does suck, but she replies very quickly to questions about content and grades. You'll be prepared for nursing school

You will have to study a lot but she is a great prof, so sweet, nice and passionate about the class! There are a lot of exams and quizzes, but if you come to every class, take good notes and study, you will be fine! She tells you everything you need to know in lecture. Lab is tougher but she is still a great prof!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Her ONLY grades are test and quizzes! She lectures without any PowerPoints. Nothing is in BB including grades. I took Dr. Hughes' class and the difference of teaching is amazing! I noticed this most in lab since Fleishmann basically has you learn all lab material on your own with no guidance, Hughes will explain every detail till you understand!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: If you don't pay attention or attend lectures you will fail. She doesn't cover everything in the book, only certain topics. She really cares about you and your schedule. She can be scary but is actually super nice and fun to talk to. Class isn't hard if you pay attention and just study your notes.

Pros: Clear with what she's testing in lecture, accessible outside of class, responds quickly to emails, grades fairly, knows what she's teaching, supportive as long as you show dedication 

Cons: doesn't post grades on blackboard, no lecture slides, lab material doesn't align with lecture sometimes

Overall she's a good professor in a hard class
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: For your mental health DO NOT DO IT. I read the reviews thinking I would be different as I get straight A's every semester even in Orgo and this was worse. DO NOT TAKE HER

She does give a lot of tests and quizzes, but if you take the lab at the same time it actually makes it easier because a lot of them are repeats. She does give a ton of detailed information in her lectures, but if you attend every lecture, take good notes, study hard, and ask questions when needed, you will be just fine. She is a very sweet lady.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Fleischmann's lab was pretty disorganized and old-school. She lays out anatomical structures and has her students look at them for the entire 3 hours of lab with lectures on the side. Practicals are insanely difficult, but I'd say the quizzes are pretty fair.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: her lecture exams are very clear cut with what she goes over in lecture. she doesnt try to pull any tricks and if you truly study itll be reflected in your grade. lab on the other hand feels much harder and disorganized. it can easily feel like ur constantly falling behind, but hey pre nursing

Although she expects a lot out of us, the class is doable IF you put in the work. It is not easy in the slightest and if given the chance I would've taken Hughes but one thing about her is you WILL be prepared for nursing school. Her lectures are thorough but lab is very disorganized and most of it needs to be self taught. Know your limits...
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: She is very old school and her lectures are only her speaking and writing on the white board in very small handwriting. The lab portion of A&P is extremely difficult because of the way she structures the tests and practical. She expects you to memorize every little part of the body. Her know it all attitude is also annoying.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Do you know what its like to think you did so good on an exam and turns out you failed it? If not take this professor

She is a little crazy. Her lectures are all over the place so it is hard to stay on track. If you don't attend lecture you will be very confused. I have her for lab as well and her TA's don't know what she is teaching so they will give incorrect info. She doesnt upload grades to blackboard so you have to guess grades. She gives out lots of papers
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--So many papers

reviews.comment: Took her class in Fall 2022 semester, got a C in her lecture, & D in lab so I had to retake the class with Dr. Hughes and the difference between the two professor is astronomical. In Dr. Fleich class there's no multiple choice, everything is written so prepare yourself, she's not tech savvy at all. If you can take Dr. Hughes for your mental health.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Pompous. talked down to people who had questions. Just read off slides. Later Learned in grad school how anatomy should actually be taught.

You do not need to buy the manual bc you barely use it, just find a free version online (even if its the wrong year) if you need to use. They make you learn everything on your own and you must sit in lab for three straight hours teaching yourself the material. Quizzes and practicals are impossible to pass unless you study for weeks.

must memorize everything to have a chance at passing tests, does not believe in tech so you MUST show up to class, PICKY GRADER, no sympathy for students failing. if you are in this class, its bc you have no choice so try to not take it w other hard classes bc all your time will be spent studying here

Nursing cohort students, I strongly consider taking AP1 over the summer after fresh. year and AP2 during the fall soph. year with Dr. Hughes. Prof. F was honestly the worst teacher I've EVER had. I met with her on mult. times to try and figure out how I could improve but to no avail. Dr. Hughes is amazing! Avoid Dr. F. You will have no social life!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I am at a lost for words of how bad this professor is. If you have her for lecture and lab good luck to you honestly because you won't have a life at all. It feels as though every week you have a quiz or exam to prepare for and there just so much material to go over. If you have the opportunity do not take her as your AP1 professor.

Honestly the worst professor I have ever had in my life. She's so picky with her answers and even if you get the question partially right you will get a zero for that question. There's just too much material to cover to which she expects you to know for the quiz and exams. There is no study guides, or worksheets so it's basically a self study class
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Do not take this class with this professor. There is no reason why the grading should be as harsh as it is. She in unfair about grading and is very particular about wording. Just in comparison a majority of people in my class are failing taking it with this prof but with the other one pass the class by a significant margin.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Tip: look a grade distribution on other sites to see how other anatomy professors compare. She is unorganized and all over the place. She's old school and only uses whiteboard and writes super small. She takes points off of tests even if you get the answer right(clearly trying to reduce amount of A's earned in the class)

Its clear that switching online due to covid was difficult for everyone, which really shows from looking at past reviews of Dr. F. She is so passionate and expects her students to put in a lot of effort since we'll 'be her healthcare providers one day' so it makes sense to want us to be proficient in A&P. She will work with you if you ask for help.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring

reviews.comment: I never speak badly about professors but this was necessary. DO NOT and I mean DO NOT take A&P with Fleischmann. She is an extremely hard professor and thrives on strict grading. Be prepared to memorize the entire textbook and quote everything she says for quizzes/exams. If you think you wrote the right answer down, somehow it'll still be wrong.
Horrible. Super Hard Professor and even throws in Lockdown Browser during online classes while being unable to lecture properly on the material provided.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Avoid her if possible! Dr. Fleischman revels in making the class more difficult. She is on a power trip. Teaching is not her goal. She would often test us over material she never covered. She would take class time to tell long personal stories. Her tests were impossible to complete in the time allotted and the grading was often subjective.

She is very passionate about AP and knows stuff well, but she did not know how to teach! She just throws as much material as she can at you. She grades things wayyyy to slow.(it took her 1.5 months to post one single quiz grade). Not much resources outside the classroom. It is the hardest class I've ever taken.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Dr. Fleischmann is probably my favorite professor on UMBC. I took A/P 1+2 and the labs with her. The class was very challenging l, probably the most challenging class Ive ever taken. She recognized when I was struggling and showed a real interest in my success. Now that the class is over, I visit on a regular bases to catch up. Shes the best!
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Accessible outside class--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Dr. Fleischmann is one of the hardest teachers I have had, but what she asks of you as a student isn't out of the ordinary. She is very passionate about A&P and knows what she's talking about. Her tests are very hard but she makes it clear in class what she expects you to know for the test. Take detailed notes and make sure you go to every class!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Dr. Fleischmann is the best professor I have had. She is passionate about her class, and she will take the time to walk you through things individually. Expect to study at least 5 hours a week. Definitely more info than any class I have taken.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Dr. Fleischmann is an amazing professor, and if you are genuinely interested in a career in healthcare, her A+P classes are worth it. The lab is harder than the actual class, but they are both difficult. If you want an easy class, dont even bother. If you want to be knowledgable and confident in healthcare, take this class. Ive learned so much!

Dr. Fleischmann is an amazing but extremely difficult professor. She knows A&P like the back of her hand. Expect at least one quiz or exam every week, especially if taken with the lab. She is tough and will not spoon-feed you anything, but her quizzes and exams are extremely fair if and only if you COME TO CLASS AND TAKE GOOD NOTES!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: She is very smart and a great teacher but she throws out a lot of content at you that you need to memorize. If you take lab at the same time, be prepared to have at least one quiz/exam a week, and they're not easy. Make sure to take good notes in class and study the class notes. None of her exams are multiple choice except the final is partially.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: She knows her stuff, but is in no way lenient about grading. She throws as much material as she can at you and makes the class far more difficult than it needs to be. She could really be a great professor if she provided more resources such as videos, labeling packets, and review sheets that could help with go along with her cluttered lectures.

Dr. Fleischmann is tough but if you show up to every class, pay attention, take notes, and study hard, you will get an A. Everything she says during lecture is fair game but questions on tests can be found in your notes word for word. She is funny but also serious. Dr. Fleischmann is one of the best professors I have ever had. Highly recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Awesome professor you just have to work super hard
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tests are tough

reviews.comment: Hard class BUT I learned a ton. Working in healthcare her class gave me a huge leg up, NOW working in science education I can answer the craziest student questions with ease because of Fleischmann. If you want the easy A take someone else. If you're going into healthcare and be excellent at what you do, take her class. Then work your butt off.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Gives good feedback--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: She gives you a test EVERY WEEK for A&P1. They're so difficult like you have to waste so much time just memorizing every detail. You're not learning. Do not recommend this professor; shes too extra with the tests. THANK ME LATER AND TAKE AP1+2 WITH HUGHES! For some reason I believe Hughes teaches AP1 in the spring so plan ahead of time.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: Dr. Fleischmann is an awesome teacher. She is very knowledgable about A&P material and super enthusiastic as well, which makes her lectures interesting. She tries very hard to get to know her students well especially if you are in the lab. Look over notes and diagrams from the lectures to prepare for quizzes/tests.

Prepare to study! She tells you everything you need to know for all the tests and quizzes given during lecture. Be prepares for fill in the blanks & free response questions. She is willing to answer any & all questions, Do not be afraid to ask! She seems intimidating at first but she is really passionate about anatomy. Take good notes & read!

Everyone told me not to take her, but I had no choice. She is definitely tough. If you don't attend class and take notes, it will guarantee you a failing grade. The first exam is the hardest because it's very different. There are generally three parts: Matching (large word bank), multiple-choice, and a lot of short answer (be VERY specific).
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Honestly if you're looking for an easy A, take Hughes. She will make you work hard for your grade. Very detail oriented (especially for exams and quizzes). Exams were half written which were very difficult unless you studied a lot, even then she will be very nit picky. I recommend recording her lectures. Expect a quiz every week. And STUDY.

she is an awesome professor because you can tell that she is very passionate about what she teaches. during labs, she will come around and quiz you on small things so you can understand better. go to lectures and take notes meticulously. a lot of the things she tests are from her lectures. even the smallest details. understand each concepts

Professor Fleischmann is extremely knowledgable in A&P and really loves what she is doing. She's very willing to help and wants to get to know her students, even though she has hundreds of them. You definitely need to study hard, and you never get a break from studying for her class. Wish that I had more time to study for her class last semester

Very passionate about A&P. Do not understand material, get help ASAP all the content builds on itself. Her personality gives an off putting  vibe but if you show up to her office hours she's willing to help 100%. Will MAKE YOU WORK for grade.  MUST STUDY to pass, quizzes are somewhat easier, tests ARE TOUGH. VERY PARTICULAR GRADER.

She is a great lecturer and professor. However, she tests very specifically. Her exams are given in all forms (multiple choice, short answer, T/F, etc.) so you must study well. As long as you attend class, take notes, and put the time and effort to study, it is possible to do very well in the class. I learned so much to take with me in this class.

This class is hard, but a good grade is possible if you study really hard. Plan ahead and put the majority of your study time into this class. She is very nice and willing to help, but you have to put in effort yourself. She is one of the best professors I've had. B's are easily attainable if you study.
Marks down wrong for each and everything. Avoid if possible.
Terrible

Professor Fleischmann is a great lecturer - I didn't read anything out of the textbook after exam 1 and did fine. However, this is not an easy class. She's a tough grader and will mark you wrong for almost anything. Exams and quizzes are very difficult. Way harder than I expected for a 200 level class. I would say try to take it w/ Leupen instead.

Awesome lady! So enthusiastic about teaching and the content of the course. Very clear on what you need to know for exams. Used the book minimally, just to look over diagrams shown in class. Study her lecture notes and make flashcards. FLASHCARDS ARE YOUR BEST FRIEND. Especially for the bones and muscles!

I love love LOVE Dr. Fleischmann. She is enthusiastic and quirky, as well as very knowledgeable about anatomy. It's A & P, so people who wine about it being hard are lame, of course it's hard.You don't actually have to read the chapters to do well, but study any figures she shows you, & go to class. I will seriously miss her next semester

She's a great teacher and you end up learning so much from her. She's a fair person and her exams/quizzes aren't so bad IF you study. If you don't read, attend lecture, and study...you're screwed. You're lucky to pass. Only complaint is that she has favorites and it really shows--i hate that about her. She's kind of intimidating but she's not bad.
DO NOT get on her bad side.

Dr. Fleischmann is a very enthusiastic and passionate professor. She often relates the subject matter to the lifestyles of her students as examples throughout the course, which can make a difficult concept easier to grasp. Her exams are straightforward and are heavily weighted towards the notes given in class. I recommend making flashcards :)

I recommend taking one other class at most, reading the textbook & paying attention in class. I liked her teaching b/c she's really enthusiastic & seems to know the material very well, but in person, she might seem a little rude. Overall, I think this is one of my best classes.

She is FAIR. If you study for all the exams and NOT Cram, then its an easy A. My favorite subject is Anatomy and Physiology so I enjoyed it and wouldnt have wanted to take it with any other professor! But I do wish she curved a little..b/c i did cram for some of my exams..:( 88% is a B...
She's a tough teacher but a damn good one.

This teacher is enthusiastic about anatomy and teaches it well. But she has drawbacks in the way she talks to people one on one. I have seen on mutiple instances where she mocks people if she thinks the question was bad. Handwriting is worse than the doctors that I intern for which is saying alot. Expect to learn most of the things on your own.

Had her for both bio 251, 252. She's an amazing professor, clear on what we should learn, and she breaks it down so it is simpler. She will answer your questions, but only if they are relevant to subject matter. Study hard because there is a LOT of material. If you slack, you are screwed. An A is absolutely possible.

One of the best professors I've had. Lets you know right off the bat that you have to study A LOT! the material is basically all memorization if you're good at that you'll do great in this class. Make sure you start studying day 1 of class and don't stop till final. Great class A's just require lots of study time.
You will either be a favorite or not. If you are not a favorite you better make this class your life!

If you have to take this class make sure you do not take any more difficult classes it requires alot of time. I recommend taking the class somewhere else. Do not even try to ask questions either in class or outside of class b/c you will get a sarastic response!!

very good professor. hard course but an A is definitely possible. my suggestion is to take it during a full semester (fall/spring), and not summer or winter because it is a LOT to memorize and learn and you need time. study hard!
great professor, very clear. study hard for the bone/muscle tests. fair unit exams. the subject is difficult- you must study..cannot blame Fleischmann if you don't study hard enough and don't do well

not someone you want to go to if you have a question about your grade. i liked her though, her lectures were clear and her tests didn't have hidden tricks. make sure to keep track of your own grade because she refuses to learn to use blackboard, but overall a good teacher
If you go talk to her about your grade she will accuse you of not studying. Avoid her at all costs!!
Take the class somewhere else!! It will save you alot of sleepless nights.
She is the worst teacher I have ever had at UMBC. She critizes students and acts like she's GOD. Her class is BS!

The class is EXTREMELY hard. You WILL fail if you don't put work in. She is rude to some people and def. has favortie students. I talked to her once and she immediatley accused me of not studying. She is enthusiastic and funny at times, but intimidating to. She wasn't in my lab class which I liked becuase i'd be scared havign her there. I dont like

Great teacher, she loves the material, she loves the lecture, ans she almost always lets out early. She is extremely helpful outside of class, and she explains everything very clearly. couldn't have passed it with out her.

She is very enthusiastic about anatomy topics which rubs off on you during class. Go to all of her lectures and read the textbook if you need further clarification. Quizzes are mainly based on the lectures and end of chapter quizzes in the textbook. But read the book for the exams since they cover more in depth material.

Prof. Fleischmann is THE BEST professor in the bio department.  I had her for both 251 and 252  she is funny, enthusiastic, and very approachable. The course is terribly difficult, but she does a great job of explaining it, and exams are fair if you study. I took the class for nursing school, and I am completely prepared for my nursing courses.
No Comments

LOVE HER! she's def one of the best lecturers i've ever had! really wants all her students to do well and you know she enjoys teaching the subject. her lectures are interesting and the labs are very hands-on. go to class, take notes, and go to open labs!
Great professor who wants her students to do well. Subject is hard, but she will help you at any cost! Likes to get to know her students and is very straight up about what she expects.

really good professor.  extremely challenging material, but she can explain it in a way to make you understand.  if you still dont get it she will go over it again and again untill you understand.  she wants her students to do well
Dr. Fleischmann is an awesome teacher and very helpful.  Anatomy is a hard subject, but she was very nice and always willing to take the time to make you understand the material.
No Comments

Definitely the best professor I've had @ UMBC.  The content is enormous, holds students responsible for EVERYTHING.  Material may seem rushed but do text review questions and you will do well on quizzes and exams.  Exams are fair, but very difficult if you don't know your stuff! DON'T SKIP A CLASS!  Approachable, helpful, enthusiastic.

the best teacher i've had in college. gets to know her students and will go out of her way to help anyone. class is very interesting, although challenging. the material is explained clearly and she lets you know what she expects. she's really funny too

Amazing teacher. She is extremely excited and enthusiatic about the material. Also she is always willing to meet with students for help. Quizes are straight from the notes however, exams are hard. You must read and understand the material in the book. I loved this class!!!
Good teacher but test are very hard and she does not let you know what will be covered on them.

very good teacher, passionate and knowledgeable about the subject. very willing to help students outside of class. before each exam she lets you know ALL of the material that you will be tested on. gives good clues on what to focus on extra while studying
No Comments

Took Prof. Enis for CMSC 203 as well as CMSC 202. Great lecturer, goes beyond reading off the slides. Caring and reachable outside of class. Exams can be heavy (in terms of how much they weigh on your grade for both courses). He seems to be a by-the rules kind of guy which I can only knock him for because he didn't round my 89.4% up to an A.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I took him for CMSC203 last semester and loved it! He was amazing at teaching the content and really engaged with his students. Overall I definitely would take a class with him again.

I took Mr. Enis for CMSC 426 and absolutely loved it! He cares about computer security, and it shows in his engaging and original lectures. He makes each concept relatable and easy to understand with examples both real and imaginary. He responds quickly to messages and is always ready to help with the homework. I highly recommend him for 426!
Engaging lectures and seems to care about every student.

Teachers such as Enis are the backbone of UMBC's CS department. Coherent, passionate, and relatable. One of my favorite lectures on the campus. Clearly breaks down concepts and engages the class to ensure understanding and is readily available to provide support both in term of class and career. This man should be considered for a tenure track.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Super easy professor, the tests were just like the homeworks. Only like 1 hw set a week and they're usually pretty chill. Lecture notes are online too, skipped like a month of class and still got over 100 final avg cuz the final exam had extra credit.

I highly recommend Professor Enis; he is a really kind individual who genuinely wants you to learn. He is a very relaxed prof; as long as you have a genuine want to study, he will help you. He is also friendly and knows his stuff. He's just very courteous.   And don't be afraid to approach and communicate to him if you need assistance.
Amazing Professor, explains things super well and makes the exam similar to the practice ones. Super chill dude and really helps their students

Enis is a great teacher. He is new which means he is flexible and understanding to students. I took him for CMSC 203 so I have no clue how he will do for CMSC 202 but I would trust him. He is very gracious with grading and his true intentions in the class are to help students as much as possible. I would definitely recommend having him for CMSC 203

Good at explaining the topics and Very helpful. Fun lectures, attendance is not mandatory but I would suggest you to go anyway. One of the best professors out there, I definitely recommend him to anyone taking this course.

Honestly I had about a 92% until recently, it's now the end of the semester and I have a high B around 87%. She's just an incredibly harsh grader for no apparent reason, this class was meant to be one of those "easy A" type courses, and yet it wasn't. Now I have a B in a course that I don't even need for my major as a pre-health student, bummed.

Kelly is an less that stellar professor, who teaches a waste of a class. Assignments are a waste of your time and energy, and she grades unnecessarily harshly for a class that I don't think a single person who enrolled actually wants to take. Weird due dates, and annoying assignments. Pretends that students have a good time doing her busy work.

I did not enjoy the class. Class was based on WHO articles.Her questions were all  very difficult and answers were mostly, percentages, numbers, and name of countries. I did get the concept and the personal connection of the topics. It was a waste of time for me and I would never recommend her to another student. I regret taking her class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Test heavy

reviews.comment: This professors course load is very manageable the course work is relatively easy, However like a lot of people have stated the professor is very difficult when it comes to reasoning and managing personal issues. As long as you do the very light work it isn't that bad however if you recieve a poor grade reasoning with her is close to impossible.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Fitzgerald really cares about the Aging Population and it shows. The assignments and research are interesting. However, she is a hard grader, the assignments give you little room for error, with some single T or F questions being worth an an eighth of a quiz grade. I wouldn't recommend taking this class unless required... or at least with her.
I actually really liked this class. Honestly, there isnt that much work. The professor is really good with Blackboard and grades in a timely manner.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: Tough grader and flags documents as ai work. Then the onus is on the student to prove that they did not use ai. I do not recommend taking this course and I regret taking it.

This class was a waste of my time. Honestly, I don't recommend any IS student to take this class if you're not required to. Her grading doesn't make sense at all. You can't even go back to check your answers for exams and midterms and that's so messed up! And they have you do these writing assignments...y'all this class is a stretch. Don't take it!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: the worst part was the exams, she had them in a way that you cannot go back once you answer a question and review your work. the final exam had less time to complete than the midterm even though it covered like 2 more chapters of the book.

I really don't understand people hate on him. I took pre-calc my senior year and it didn't even help me much for this course. I swear math 155 is the easiest math I've ever taken in my life on god. Its actually just 70% algebra, and 30% calculus. Fortney quite literally made this class a piece of cake, and deserves a lot more praise in my opinion.

Professor Fortney has a complex over his students. He will berate a student for forgetting an old rule from algebra or making a mistake when factoring. And proceed to teach from his notes and make dozens of mistakes, confusing the entire class. He also is obsessed with fear mongering his students about material.

The homeworks are very long and tedious. Pay attention to the lectures. He posts them online as well. Exams/quizzes are similar to problems done in class and on the homework. Overall the class is very doable

Professor Fortney would often claim he has "made this class as easy as possible" and I believe that is half true. He is very straightforward with the topics and does examples in class that are very similar to worksheets and quizzes. Previously taking a calculus course is a MAJOR advantage in this class. But, no study guides/preparation for tests.

Exam heavy. You pretty much have quizzes and worksheets every week but they dont stand a chance against the exams. Very strict grading on the exams, you could get everything correct on them and you could still get a 85% on it if the work is not shown in the way he wants it. Class is what you make of it but its hard. Prof is nice but not helpful.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I will be honest with you guys. If you struggle with math, don't take this professor. He doesn't let students know what will be on the quiz. The worst part about all this is he doesn't give points for showing work, meaning you only get points for each question if you have the answer correct.

If i were you I would just find a different professor to take this class. You can do well on homeworks, quizzes and worksheets and still fail from the tests alone. Multiple choice q's are worth half the points and you have to show work to get credit with no possibility of partial credit (wth?!). The exams are very flawed. Listen to the reviews!!!

The professor is rigorous; he does not know how to teach, and even his notes are wrong during the lecture. This is a no-calculator math class. The Exams make or break your grades, regardless of what you get on quizzes or worksheets—no study guide besides him having a quick overview of what you are expected to know during lectures.

He did not give us any resources, practice exams, etc. anything to use to prep for exams. All we had were our notes. The homework is too complicated. He only gives us the lecture time (50 min) which is not enough time for exams.

If you have a background in pre calc or any calc class, you'll be just fine. If not, then you might struggle a little bit, in class he doesn't fully go over certain topics but if you approach him during office hours about any questions/concerns he was always generally pretty kind. Be sure to review graded tests, he gets things wrong sometimes.

If you have a pretty strong math background this class will be easy. I got a C in AP calc in high school and easily got an A in this class. I think he explains the material well during lectures and if you know what you're doing, you will understand it. A lot of people fail this class but don't let that scare you, it's pretty easy.

He's average at teaching and sometimes he'll be too lazy to teach a certain part of a topic but still put it on the upcoming quiz. The TA for the class will take off points for any little thing and his help during quizzes are scams, he'll say its okay then mark it wrong later. Jon also will let his TA's make mistakes on grading and not correct it.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: This professor is a good teacher as his lectures are easy to understand and helpful if you go for office hours.
no partial credit on exam at all

He's a really nice guy, but I can see how he's not everyone's cup of tea. HW and quizzes alternate weekly, with 3 exams per semester. MATH215 is a weird course, and even he admits it's not his favorite to teach. You don't really get too in depth with any one technique, so if you struggle with one week, the other week is a new topic all together.

I had to retake this class. Its not easy, but if you study and practice the problems from notes and old exams, you'll be fine. You need to put a lot of time into this class. I took him online the 2nd time, and it was better than spring. Even though it was rushed, I still took time to study his class outside his online lectures (final was in person)

Fortney was a good prof if you acc attend lecture, quizzes and exams were very easy if you understood the material in class. He is willing to help you understand as long as you put in the effort. The TAs were a bit confusing but the SIPASS was good. For the most part the class is an easy A if you do the bare minimum that's required.

Nice and approachable guy but not the most organized. Quizzes don't always reflect what's on the class schedule, so be prepared. Exams are okay if you lock in; review packets and Organic Chem Tutor is a must though.

The hardest part about this class was understanding the material because it's challenging if you don't love math like me. However, Professor Fortney's lectures and slides really helped. Prioritizing those will definitely help you with the exams and quizzes during the discussion. He's very wholesome and funny at times.

He can't work his iPad, he's not transparent at all about what's on exams, quizzes, and homework, you can't call how he'll grade work on tests, he skims through notes, and attendance is required. 
Even with studying and previous Calc experience, it'll be extremely difficult to pass. Go to tutoring and hope for a good TA.

This man cannot work an iPad for his life. He doesn't explain concepts well and gets confused when students do poorly on worksheets, quizzes, or exams. He smiles creepily and is hard to access outside of class. He made attendance mandatory midway through the course because students were skipping lecture. Pray for a good TA.

extra credit? NOPE!
cancels lectures/attendance because he doesnt know how to work an ipad? YES!
isn't transparent with students regarding what will be on exams or quizzes? YES!
insanely late emails? YES!
smiles creepily at you? YES!
Be wary hes a newer teacher to this school but cmon, if I had one piece of advice take the other professor. srsly

if you arent locked in from day one then youre cooked. okay guy but even worse prof, he wont teach certain things but put them on exams?? he doesnt even teach, he explains things like hes trying to jog ur memory but theres nothing to remember because ur here to learn? i gotta retake cause i need a C or better but i couldnt change profs :(

Review packets didn't always match up with the test materials. Discussion is way easier then the actual class. If you have a good TA you will be fine. You have to study to pass this class. He would skip parts of the packet he would use for lecture. A lot of online homework that didn't really match with the class.

Used material from prior institutions requiring calculators (which are prohibited). Partial credit grading felt arbitrary. Struggled with his iPad too often. Spent ¼ of lecture urging attendance or returning tests. Required discussions weren't helpful. Seemed impatient at times. Homework was graded for both online and submitted written assignments.

nice person, not that great of a professor but has potential if he figures out how to use his iPad and apple pencil correctly and acc covers a good amount of the material in the classes. only went to a few classes, discussions are mandatory not becuz attendance is taken but becuz thats when u submit and receive hw and take quizzes.

The material for this class can definitely be easy for some and hard for others depending on what kind of math is easier for you. Professor Fortney is fairly good at explaining the material clearly and seems to care about his students. He is nice and approachable, however the course itself is not structured well, but that's not his fault.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This professor is unapproachable, rude, and dismissive in emails. He rarely replies, assigns zeroes without reason, and doesn't give credit for showing math processes. He refuses to make helpful reviews, uses irrelevant finance problems in notes, and mocks students for pointing out inconsistencies. His strictness and attitude hindered my learning.

He's great person, but not a great professor. This is a business calculus, but he doesn't go over business questions and has them on quizzes/exams. No matter how much studying I did I averaged a 70% on the quizzes and had low grades on the exams. You either get it or you don't, he's not a big help. SI pass taught me more than he has.

Is nice but very disorganized. He'll run behind on topics we discussed in class, and isn't very caught up on the syllabus. He isn't a tough grader, and he generally explain things clearly. As long as you read the texts throughly and take notes during the lectures his classes are easy.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: The class was incredibly arduous. We had surprise quizzes, but they randomly never counted. A final that was in class, while all the other professors gave us take home finals. And, if he disagreed with your interpretation, he would shame you. Oh, also, randomly calling on people? Who does that. As wonderful as he could be, he just isnt.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Professor Falco is a wonderful professor. Some people dont like him because he is not afraid to tell someone that they are wrong (I actually heard this as a reason from another student). But he cares about his students success and pushes them to try. He does give quizzes, but he tells you about them in advance. Do the readings and youll be fine.

He will randomly change the syllabus in the middle of semester, assign homework and then randomly decide it doesn't count, require you to purchase every textbook but then doesn't even get to half of them throughout the semester, requires you to print out 70+ page readings, isn't accommodating to differing opinions and will argue you into silence.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Beware of pop quizzes--So many papers

reviews.comment: dont do it its not worth it if you have to, i'll pray for you

Boring, is not clear about the requirements and how much they count, assigns an undoable amount of work, has incredibly petty rules, seems unsure about the material, presents the material in a confused way, and does not involve the students.

Professor Falco is probably one of the most challenging teachers I have ever had, but this wasn't a bad thing at all. He is intimidating only because of how brilliant he is and how he makes you step outside your comfort zone. He really made us think about things. He is not an easy professor, but if you're up for the challenge, take his class.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Clear grading criteria--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Hardest class/prof I've ever taken. Do not take unless you love lit. He has an abundance of knowledge, but when it comes to opinions about a topic/book he will disagree with you and tell you, you're wrong unless your opinion lines up with his. If you show up to class and meet with him outside of class, he will help you as much as possible.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: I had some mental health issues throughout the semester and Prof Falco was extremely accommodating and understanding. He has a wealth of knowledge to offer his students.

Very intelligent, very well read professor with lots of life experience. Will question you on your interpretations, and isn't afraid to ask you to expound on your ideas or disagree with you if he thinks you're wrong. Respect him and he will respect you. He has only ever been polite to me even what I disagreed. A shining example of a Professor.

Professor Falco is very intelligent and wants to help his students succeed, but he has no tolerance for incorrect answers/discussions. He is quick to tell you if you are wrong, very abrupt about it and does not believe that he can ever be wrong. I will not be taking a class with him again.

Brilliant professor who has no time for idiocy or laziness. If you can't follow direction or if you aren't interested in being a diligent student, don't take the class. If you respect him, he'll respect you. If you make the extra effort he is more than willing to give you feedback and help you out with anything. Easily maintaining an A.

An amazing professor. Yes, he rambles, yes, he sometimes gets sidetracked, but that is irrelevant in light of his erudite scholarly status and amazing intelligence. Plus he is COOL and has a ton of life experience. The BEST Prof. I've ever had!

He did tend to drift off, but on the first day, he warned us about it and told us to call him back to the subject if he did so. The exam was a little tough, but it turned out okay. As for papers, his grading is not that difficult...as long as you don't write make sense-even a little, you will be fine.

Loved Falco. Took 3 classes with him when I was at UMBC. The 2 exams I ever had with him were pretty difficult but I did very well on his papers. Come up with original and interesting paper topics, talk to him about your ideas, sources, etc and you wont have any problems getting an A.

Falco went on tangents more often than he discussed the subject material. Although he read us the riot act on the first day (for at least half the class), all of the rules he set up were eventually loosened or abandoned. I was really looking forward to taking this class but the professor let me down.

Probably one of the best professors I've ever taken. He is not easy at all but he's fun and interesting. All you have to do is show a little interest and participate in discussion and he'll give you a lot of leeway. Take him!

Awesome teacher, goes on awesome tangents, but gives no homework, takehome exams, and will only cover what we want to cover book wise.  We may be behind schedule but it does not matter because everything is interesting.  Did I mention he gives out paper extensions like it does not matter.

Despite his nerdy "Woody Allen" appearance and voice, the man is as intense as a laser beam. He's brilliant, exacting, fierce, and absolutely dedicated to his studies. He expects a great deal from his students, and you shouldn't let him down.  His classes are always fascinating. He wants you to learn, to get culture. Don't disappoint him!

Big favoritist. Demands and grades heavily on participation, but instead keeps talking about his personal opinions CONSTANTLY. We were always 1-2 months behind schedule, didn't finish a single book, but he blamed this on the students, saying that they didn't read up. Assignments given+graded late.Grading criteria given 2 days before end of classes!
Great class. Great teacher.

This is a great class and i loved Prof Falco. You definitely have to do work in this class and its not easy, but it is interesting and Falco always finds a way to relate it to something else. good sense of humor and doesn't take anything too seriously. BE ON TIME! gives excellent study guides for exam and offers help for paper writing.

I LOVE professor falco. this is the third class ive had with him and i think hes fantastic. his exams are definetely not impossible, if you do the reading and attend class. hes extrememely helpful if you need it and he is VERY knowledgeable definetely take a class with him. it's totally worth it!
Funny and engaging. Enjoyable class.

This class has to be the one of the most difficult classes I took because not onl is the topic difficult in itself, but Falco makes it so much more difficult. He has so much knowledge, and it baffles him that the students don't.  "I can't believe that you don't know this," was one of his fav. lines.  However, he is a really interesting professor!

Great guy, great sense of humor!  Hardest professor I've ever had, but I learned so much in his class.  Just keep up with the readings and write down every word he says in lectures.  Don't let him scare you; I highly recommend him!

Falco is an excellent teacher! I don't understand why he has poor ratings. He's funny, engaging, knows his stuff, and is helpful outside of class. Study for exams, but they're fair.  He's not a hard grader.  He offers to help with rough drafts any student who comes to his office.  Take advantage of his help and you'll do well.  My favorite class!

Can't remember class number, but it was a Lit class with Beaowulf, Chaucer, etc. He is very knowledgeable, speaks fluect Old English, but is arrogant, doesn't value student opinions, and exams are IMPOSSIBLE! You're only hope is to write a stellar paper to up your grade.

i thought my head was going to explode..  how many tagents can one man go on!? then he expects us to know tons of history**** that he never went over during lecture.. his essays were hard as hell too.. vague topics

Falco is a jerk. Class is somewhat entertaining, but he digresses so much and then still expects you to learn all of the things he did not have a chance to get to in class...along with quite a few other things that aren't even relevant. He is smart, yes, but he is overall an unsensitive jerk who wants to dork his classes up so he can make a friend.
He knows which students don't care about the material--and he treats them accordingly.  If you work hard, you'll earn his respect and his help with your graduate school career.
No Comments
Tests were impossible.  Paper topics were very obscure and impossible to BS.  You have your work cut out for you in this class.
he is really well read and is so much fun in class and he is really helpful on papers. I would not be afraid to take a course with him if I were you

I just finished a semester with him and i must say he has got to be one of the most engaging and adorable professors. His classes are challenging for those who are afraid of independent thought, not so much for the serious student though. :)
