His arrogance and tendency to belittle his students is funny and makes class entertaining, but the rest of it is awful. Currently, half our grade is dependent on a seven-page essay we've had two days to write bc he can't plan well enough, apparently.
No Comments
Very Engaging.
No Comments
Professor Falco is awsome. He knows everything about everything. He is challenging, so be prepared.
A truly great professor.  The man knows more about literature (within and outside of his specialty) than I thought possible.  He is challenging, but you will learn, and it's worth it.
No Comments
Best beatnik professor ever!

I think this in-person class is one of the best ways to learn ASL!! You'll catch on quick and start having conversations with your peers early on. There's a good bit of homework, but it's manageable. However, there's lots of technical stuff you can get points off on, and you'll probably have to redo a lot of assignments. Classes are fun though!
Professor frame is a good asl professor. As long as you attend the classes, do the assignments and turn them in on time you'll do good in the class!

Professor Frame is awesome! He is hilarious and a great teacher. He is patient if you don't know what you're trying to sign.  There is a LOT of work if you take the hybrid 201, but you don't have to come to class (however I highly suggest you do, there are fun games and it's really good practice).

Very blunt and responds late to emails, class materials are extremely disorganized, no clear feedback nor clear directions. The instructional lessons and homeworks take more time than all of my STEM classes combined. He also made us redo all of our homeworks one week because of a mistake on his behalf. Do not take the hybrid version of this class!

Daniel may be the greatest Deaf ASL teacher that UMBC has ever had. He created a brilliant online platform that makes life easier for students who don't have to attend ASL 201 class, as attendance is not mandatory. Students who attend all the classes will receive a 5% bonus. I have always attended his class, and there are a lot of fun activities!

Professor Frame is a wonderful ASL professor!! I highly suggest that you take his class for ASL if you're considering learning sign language. WARNING  he does sign a little fast sometimes, but he repeats what he is signing if you ask him.  Professor frame is funny as well!

He really cares about teaching, is very friendly, and is absolutely hilarious. Once we could hardly focus because we were laughing so hard. He teaches in a way that shows that he wants us to understand, and is always willing to explain for students who are confused. He has a dynamic and energetic teaching style and encourages student participation.

Very funny guy, he uses a lot of humor in his lessons and his in person classes. Class is asynchronous with one optional lecture once a week. Class is EXTREMELY TIME CONSUMING, you will spend hours on doing the instructional lessons and homework assignments, prob more than you will for a lot of stem classes
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Frame was excellent! He really engages with students and is so passionate about teaching ASL. Going to class is extremely important (he excuses one absence then takes 5% off the overall grade each one after that). He is one of the best and funniest professors, makes coming to class fun. Kind of a tough grader but instruction is very clear
He didn't grade my final grade properly, forces you to buy over $130 worth of textbook materials that you can't find anywhere else. Not lenient whatsoever.

If you can keep up with his signs early on, this class is a breeze. He's very funny and spends a good amount of time visually acting out terms to the class to help you remember different words. The online homework is really easy too. You must come to class though or you will fall behind.

You pretty much get what you put into this class. If you try and stay on top of your work, you can easily get through the class with an A or B. The mistake I kept making was not checking the rubric. If you follow it exactly, you're almost guarenteed an A. He is a very kind and nice teacher but will not let you get away with being lazy.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Loved this class so much, I HIGHLY recommend this professor. He is super funny and engaging. Very light work outside of class. Learned so much from him and truly enjoyed it!
Professor Frame is an amazing teacher. Expection are clear and what is taught is what is tested on. He made learning ASL feel less intimidating.

Funny professor, in a dad sort of way lol. Gives criticism nicely, but can feel a little condescending at times. This course hadn't been offered in a few years, so there were some bumps, but being an active listener and asking him questions definitely helped. Some lab instructions were unclear but manageable. Responds to emails relatively fast.

This is a hard class dont get me wrong but he genuinely cares about the class succeeding. Mistakes made on his/TAs fault are compensated by points going to you. This course has a lot of light physics so be prepared but as long as you go to every lecture and read explanations of things in labs, you will be fine. He makes sure no one gets left behind
Down to earth guy, actually cares about where you are in the course, His class is tough but fair

He doesn't really teach you how to use ArcGIS. He really wants you to figure it out yourself but that realistically takes an excessive amount of time. Unrealistic amount of information he expects us to understand and learn from lectures/readings. The labs take forever but each are only worth 4 points of your grade.

teaches junk, expects you to learn everything on your own, lectures are actually meaningless cant ask for help because he wants you to figure it out on your own, or he says to google it, trash class trash software trash labs
Great professor, is very understanding and always willing to help out. Tests aren't too hard, but he gives random pop quizzes. They don't really impact your grade though.
He is an awesome teacher for philosophy, you can Tell that he wants all students to succeed and understand the topics he teaches. Would take again!!
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: A truly kind and passionate professor. Cares about students and what he teaches. He takes all feedback into consideration. Assignments are easy and there's lots of extra credit opportunities.

Dr. Francis is truly passionate about climate change and that can clearly be seen when he teaches this class. He's very nice and a pretty quick grader. You do need to attend class and lectures because it's much easier to understand the content that way.

Great professor, very informative, and passionate about what he teaches. One assignment per week and the given study guide is literally the exam. Readings are not required for this class, despite being assigned, and not needed at all for an A.  Recommend very highly, will learn a lot and get a good grade while you're at it. Attendance is mandatory.

Super easy class. The lectures were not boring. Honestly, just show up and even half listen and you will do good. You need to do some reading but it's not bad. One little homework assignment a week. He gives exam questions ahead of time so you can prepare. He is a super reasonable and nice guy, I definitely recommend.

Dr. Francis was an amazing professor! He gives you advice on how to make your essay better which you can take advantage of for your next essay. There wasn't a lot of work you're graded on and attendance is mandatory. This class is based on your own opinion and he is very respectful for what you think.
He's a very nice professor. Caring and feels responsible for his students. Even though the class was kinda hard he made it so much easier. Make sure you read before class and you'll be fine

Solid professor, gave useful materials to study for exams and office hours were quite helpful. Lectures can be a bit dry but he records them all and posts them so rewatching on your own time can be beneficial. Do not hesitate to ask questions about stata cause it can get confusing fairly quickly.

His class is a bit boring, but make sure to come to class for the random assignments or quizzes he gives out. He wants you to succeed though, he is great with extra credit and truly wants his students to understand what's being taught.

He is a great professor to get the stat credit out of the way. He does in person exams but everything is multiple choice and study guides so your not lost and does heavy curves to make sure everybody does well in the class. The bad part is his lecture slides are sometimes 40 slides for a certain chapter but he provides a lot of help and extra cred
Very lenient grader - Professor was very light on homework in this class, therefore MUST study intensively on your own with the materials provided, because the subject gets extremely intense.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Attendance was not mandatory, but his lectures explained everything extremely well and thoroughly. The later projects were nigh-incomprehensibly complicated for the short amount of time, but all the regular work was very clear.

Easiest A in history. He curves everything a considerable amount because most people bomb the exams, but those that do still get a C or B. Very caring person, is extremely knowledgeable when it comes to the course content. Course is heavily predicated on use of Stata, which is not fun to use, get a good group to the problem sets you're good.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Group projects

reviews.comment: Nice guy who answers questions but doesn't explain very well for a pretty loaded class that can make for some pretty stressful assignments

Prof. Firsin is not the best teacher because he's not engaging at all. best thing about his class was that it was recorded and you can rewatch the lectures, pause, and then follow along to do the hw easily. A lot of hw, group proj is kinda intensive & He does curve exams (open book. TBH I hated this class but still got an A so it's kinda worth it

Prof. Firsin's lectures are extremely unengaging and it is poorly structured. He zooms through difficult processes on Excel and expects you to learn from it. There was two take home exams that are fairly difficult but he does give partial credit. And there is a group project that had NO structure or clear expectations. Overall a mediocre teacher.

I've taken Pr. Oleg a couple of times before. He is a very nice person and he encourages students to ask questions. Lectures may be difficult but he is willing to help students and to make accommodations to the grading criteria if it will benefit the class. He also is known to curve test and is usually my first choice when picking classes

Probly your best interest not to skip because you do half the hw in class. That being said theres alot of it. Not necessarily his fault though because excel is an extensive subject. Get through the gauntlet of hw and you'll be set for a good grade. The exams are basically the homework. Hes a nice guy though, just talk to him if you got any gripes
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Firsin is a fairly new professor, so he's still learning. That said, the lectures were extremely boring and unhelpful. Doing in-class problems and problem sets are the only teaching method that works. Open-note exams and pop-quizzes. Class averages for the two exams were still around 50%, but he gives a decent curve. Overall nice guy.
The lectures are straightforward and the teaching style is good.

Very respectable in terms of knowledge, how he leads his lectures and his passion for the material, but can be a bit arrogant and displeasing with people one-on-one. If your body language during lecture makes it seem like you're not engaged, he won't hold much respect for you.

Such a wonderful guy! He shows clear passion and interest in what he teaches, so his lectures are very entertaining (as someone who only had a loose interest in ancient Greece before this). He's very kind and makes an effort to remember all of his students.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: pretty chill intro class. It helps if you actually try working through the homeworks(they're super hard), because the exams are actually way easier. Exams resemble discussion problems. Be careful to attend most of your discussions for the free points. The pre-lectures are actually a big help

Provides past exams (amazing study resource, just spam them and you will get an A.) Has a partial worst exam drop policy with the final which got me the A in the end. Go to lectures, they're actually quality. Very nice guy and understanding if you need to contact him.

Good guy. He cares about the students. The class is extremely time-consuming if you aren't familiar with the concepts. There are 6 mid terms in total a final so your grade is pretty much dependent on your exam scores.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--So many papers--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Be ready for a lot of exams, especially if you're like me who is not used to biweekly tests. If you are not an exam person all I can say is study a lot, and learn from your past mistakes.

Lectures could be hard to follow, but he worked many practice problems while explaining the concepts. His exams were extremely straight forward and pretty easy. The practice exams (previous semester exams) he posted were very similar to the exams given which made getting an A more than doable.

Took this class Spring '25, it was good. There's 6 exams, making up 65% of your grade, and anything above 80% ON HW gets rounded to a 100. He's a good lecturer and goes through problems well most of the time. He posts old semesters' exams, so studying is straightforward. There's no reason to fail if you actually dedicate the time for hw and tests
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Test heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Well organized, understands the material well. Very classy. The class is gonna be hard but he makes it feel fair. Good professor.

Really difficult hw (not by prof); 60% is exam and he changes it up each semester (practise exams available); discussions are graded by participation; really important you grind hw & discussions; no extra credit; nice professor, but difficult class; if not done physics before, will be hard. 15% is final exam;10% hw; 10% disc. FRQ graded leniently.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Professor Anderson keeps the class engaging with helpful resources and a supportive approach. Attendance is mandatory, but that's part of what makes this physics course manageable. Unstuck AI is great for prepping alongside the textbook-free lectures.

Overall great teacher, passionate about what he does, explains clearly and conisely, you will learn during the lectures. He uploads pre-lectures for us to learn before class, then we have the lectures, homework, and the discussions. Anything above 80% rounds to a 100%.

Anderson is a cool guy. His lectures aren't super helpful imo, but the practice exams are very similar to the actual exams and he's an easy grader. He's the only prof. whose office hours I've been to and he was very down to earth and helpful. As long as you do the homework and go to discussion you'll do fine.

Very down to Earth guy who clearly wants his students to learn. Lectures are very helpful for learning the content, discussion is rather tedious as it's just a packet you have to complete as a group once a week. Overall a good professor who makes Physics quite manageable.

If you're great at cramming, this class will be a breeze. We have biweekly exams and he posts past exams for each of them. Lots of repeated questions, so if you can cram study those the night before, you'll be good for the exam. Besides that, lots of homework, and just gotta attend the weekly discussion for that participation grade.
An absolutely amazing professor who is supportive and helpful for a class that would typically be difficult.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: he explained really well in the lectures and the clicker was just for participation thankfully, he also gave us past exams for review and it helped a lot with the actual exams, the TA/LAs were reliable with both homework help and during discussion, i think the class is easy to pass if you study and use the resources he gives you
The class was great and easy to get by. the grading criteria were clear and the TAs (in my section at least) ere very hepful

Great professor. Had some good lectures and provided plenty of ways to earn points throughout the semester. You'll miss participation points if you don't come to class and do clicker questions. Physics can get a little difficult but if you do the work it's an easy pass.

Probably the best lecturer at UMBC. Anderson is hard to beat and if you can adapt to his style you'll pass with flying colors. Exams and especially homework are hard if you don't fully understand the material so there is a big time commitment. He is very nice and approachable and wants everyone to pass, so take him if you get the chance.

I took this course for the accelerated summer session. Anderson made the workload manageable and kept his lectures engaging. Be prepared for a lot of quizzes and exams with hardly any dropped grades. Time management is key.

Eric Anderson is great! The class itself requires a lot of time, and can be bad for commuters. My discussion session was at 7pm. But I digress. Anderson himself is very encouraging and provides an abundance of material for students to succeed. Sometimes, his lectures would drag on. But that's my only criticism of him. Wish I could take him for 122!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Anderson is a great professor, he is very good at lecturing, although the material and tests are just hard. Test averages were always C's. 8am Friday exams were tough, no extra credit offered, and no drops, so you need to study a lot for the exams. Homework was not too hard, show up to lecture or you might not pass.

This is a hard curriculum, but that has nothing to do w Dr. Anderson.  This is about the best, most accessible, & effective kind of teacher you'll find in college.  Dont go in expecting this to be like hs, but do the work and youll receive tons of help/resources, a well organized class, and a caring, dynamic, and effective professor.

Dr. Anderson is an amazing professor! He was incredibly organized, his lectures were clear, and he really cares about his students. The class had 6 exams, which sounds stressful, but it actually worked better than having 3 midterms. His lecture notes and the homework prepare you for the exams, so if you attend class and study hard, you'll be good
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: I don't know why Prof A doesn't have a higher rating. Seriously cares about his students, generous attendance policy, lenient grading. Extra exam so that the total weight per test is lower. Yes, the content was a little difficult; it's physics. Ask TAs questions during discussion and you'll do fine. Didn't use textbook at all.

This class wasn't easy. Either you have previous knowledge of physics, or you really need to study and get well acquainted with physics. I personally love physics so this class was not too awful for me, but if you aren't either A. willing to put in 8-12 hours a week of just studying not including HW, or B. have prior physics knowledge, good luck.

If you're a physics major, hope you've taken physics before. If not, take ANY other science course. Lectures assume you already know the material from useless pre-lectures. Homework is near impossible without online resources or prior knowledge. Discussions are long packets without any "Discussion". There are 6 tests worth 10% each and a 15% final.

Lectures were rarely thorough enough to cover the homework material but pretty much everything is online anyways. Quizzes are at 8am on Fridays and the discussion is the only place you really learn the material. I wouldn't recommend him if you're not strong in math/science.

by far a horrible teacher. lectures are time consuming and boring only scrapping the surface of a topic and he makes his Friday 8AM quizzes nothing like homework or lecture. really just a horrible teachers who just needs to change his quizzes, especially if his class average is below a C. honestly just needs to be fired.

Doesnt teach anything beyond the bare basics in very short lectures so homework is hours longer than it needs to be and extremely frustrating. Fri quizzes are worth 60% of your grade and are so short each question is about .5% of your final grade. Both teachers are like this just do a transfer credit.

I really enjoyed the online format and believe it was def better than the in person. Weekly quizzes were based on the homework and the discussion section so as long as you know how to do both, you were fine. Make sure to get the conceptual basis down. I used orgo tutor and khan academy which were very solid resources. Make sure to go to OH too!
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: If you want to teach yourself physics, this will be a great class for you. FlipIt Physics is useless and the professor's lectures are incredibly dull. You can get a B without really learning anything though. Also, I hope you like waking up early in the morning on Fridays, because the weekly quizzes are at 8 AM. Textbook wasn't used once, don't buy.

Anderson was a really good lecturer and his lecture slides were clear and easy to follow. The class was hell b/c we had a total of 6 exams and 1 final. It was a ton of work, but he was easy to go to outside of class. He was really good one on one and in lecture as well. He honestly seemed excited to teach physics too, which was nice to see.

Doesn't explain concepts too well. Homework is pretty different from the lectures, but if you understand the homework then you should be fine. Be prepared for a lot of work. He also makes you wake up before 8 on fridays to take a weekly quiz. This class will take a lot of time out out of your week.

Hes one of the best professors Ive had so far. He makes grading for free responses incredibly clear, and goes thru almost every kind of problem. Practice exams are super similar to the exams. Avoid using chegg and go thru the all the practice and hw yourself an A is not out of reach.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria--Group projects

reviews.comment: Dr. Anderson's explanations are clear and his lectures are useful. Make sure to emphasize the homeworks and do them well. Exams are extremely easy, but make sure you follow the problem solving guidelines or you will lose many points on the big problem at the end of every exam. The final exam is also super easy. I would take more classes with him.

Anderson is a pretty decent professor, he explains concepts quite well but you have to practice to really understand it. For his class there were 6 exams, one on each unit but the last due to time. Each exam had an individual part and a group part (group was from your discussion). Lots of homework, and this class makes you work but you should be ok
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Anderson really knows his stuff and is good at answering questions that you may ask. He gives a lot of wiggle room with grading on everything but exams so come to class to get your participation points, come take the group quizzes, and come to discussion. I had a low C exam average and still got a B in the class!

Approachable. Very nice and easygoing person. It's very clear how this class is graded from the get-go, and depending on your discussion section he seems to ensure the TAs reflect that clarity. DO ALL THE LITTLE THINGS. I've got a 54% exam grade and still have a B average from all the homework. Exams are difficult; make sure you study for them.

I'd be able to better rate this professor if I ever paid attention in his class. You honestly didn't need to to do well. I had never taken physics before but he makes it super super easy. Exams were verbatim the same as practice exams/wikis. Only downside was TONS of busy work outside class and labs were a pain but overall very doable.

Exams are extremely easy as long as you do the practice exams and wikis. (They are almost the same). Quizzes in class can be done w friends. Anderson doesn't care much about what students are doing during lecture and is very easygoing. Easy A class.

This is a hard class, but Anderson makes it a little easier. Because he grades based on total points earned the whole semester, you can have bad test scores and still get a B. The highest exam score I had was a 78. DO ALL THE LITTLE THINGS! All the hw's, quizes, checkpoints, discussion and use that to boost your grade. Don't skimp out on things.

Probably the best professor in umbc. Lectures are clear and he's super friendly. Posts solutions to all exams and quizzes right afterwards. Posts sample exams with solutions. If you study the quizzes, sample exams and wikis, you'll get an A. Homework is harder than exams, don't sweat it. Use Walid Hamarneh physics youtube channel. He solves them.
His teaching style was mediocre at best most topics were not explained very well. Did not follow any text book only flipitphysics which limited the material you could learn from
Dr. Anderson is a great professor! Lectures are great, the syllabus is clear, and the tests are fair (I am someone who is very bad at physics). I would definitely recommend taking his class.

He's not that great at answering questions, but he is good at explaining concepts. His tests are straightforward. Do the wikis and practice tests the week of the test. If you genuinely try them and understand them, you'll probably get an A or B on the tests. You can work with other people on quizzes. This class was not hard, and he's a nice person.

For a UMBC professor, many of those who don't teach well, he's amazing! He provides lecture outlines prior to class and then goes through them during class so you can go home and look over what was taught in class. He does lecture, but you are expected to do some self-teach on your own. Exams aren't that hard. You can do well if you put in time in.

Anderson is very approachable outside of class. If you bring the handouts, follow along, and go back over them in your own time or with him in office hours after lecture, it is SUPER helpful. Reading the book definitely helps, and there are before-class quizzes to do before each week. Overall, an easy class if everything is kept organized.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: He's terrible at responding to emails regarding any questions. Don't bother asking questions in lecture since he does a poor job explaining. Save questions for the TAs. He'll let you ask questions about your exam grade, but won't have a solutions guide to let you see in his office to know where you made mistakes. Avoid taking him if possible.

His lectures aren't the best but it is sometimes useful. He never uses the textbook so only buy it if you need it. Exams are super easy. He gives quizzes once every week which are also very easy. Overall an easy class. I didn't buy the book and learned everything from FlyptPhysics lectures. (Yes that is pretty enough)

Really nice and intelligent guy. He teaches the conceptual side  more than the mathematical side of physics. Goes over concepts and does practice problems in lecture. I recommend printing the lecture outlines out rather than trying to jot down everything in a notebook. Exams were really easy (B avg)  just do the provided wikis for practice.

Eh, he's okay I guess. I found that he actually teaches very little of the mathematical side of physics. He's not bad with teaching the conceptual, I guess. I wouldn't recommend him, but I see why people like him.

Physics 121/122 profs use Smartphysics as a supplement to doing their job. His lectures(confusing & unstructured), in previous semesters were very good, but as usual are ruined because he thinks the student learns from smartphysics. Exams are pretty simple if you happen to go over the material on your own time. Don't expect sample exams/questions

He changed his style of lectures for the worse when the curriculum changed. Previous semesters said had really great lectures and I had seen a few of them online but they were nothing like his current lectures. He just goes over questions from the online homework but the website gives you a better explanation. He is a nice guy overall though

One of the best professors at UMBC! He greatly emphasizes on concepts rather than the dry math aspect of physics. He genuinely wants everyone to do well in the class. I loved how the course is organized; the pre-lecture in smart physics prepares you for what is covered in lecture. Do the practice exams and show up to class prepared and consistently

Poor grasp of subject matter. Lectures are lifted from smartphysics pre-readings. Only lectures on the bare basics of the topic. Exams range from cruel to cake walk, and he doesn't seem to care when they drop everyone's overall grade by a whole letter. Class average for second exam was 50%, no curve. Can't control a large classroom.
Could not ask for a more patient, enthusiastic, crystal clear teacher.

Anderson was the best!  Clickers did not count against you if you were wrong and his lectures centered on core concepts/practice problems rather than theory.  Quizzes and exams were similar to the old ones that he posted.  If you do the work, read the book, and show up to class, it's not hard to get a good grade.

Great teacher! Seems more like a friend than a professor,  which is more than any student could ask for. Made a few mistakes during lecture, but he's very fair and he really wants all his students to pass and get good grades. He's been one of my favorite teachers over my near 7 semesters of schooling.
Assigns genuinely helpful assignments while giving well-thought lectures. Highly recommend.
His powerpoint slides are 1 clicker Question. If you miss a day of class and try to look back you'll see one question that does not even have an answer.

Easy physics course because of previous exams he posts online. He explains his material very well in class. The homework is the only tough thing about the class but if you listen during his lectures, you will do well on them. Also, if you have an A by the end of the year, you can skip the cumulative final altogether.

One of my favorite professors of all time. I hated Physics before taking this class, but Anderson makes every effort to keep class as interesting as possible, provides every resource you could ask for, and really cares about his students. He's a chill dude who provides tough-but-fair exams and all the tools you need to pass. TAKE HIM!

Anderson is a pretty good professor! He's very thorough when going over problems and examples and brings in visual aid and demonstrations to help you understand the information. Posts sample tests before an exam and pretty much tests right off of it. If you have questions, he's more than happy to help.

This class was SUPER boring. Exams were easy retrospectively. Simple mistakes cost you several points. Not a bad class. Be sure to do MasteringPhysics (most answers are google-able). Labs are easy enough. Scattered clicker points throughout the semester. Take notes on the process of deriving answers. WIKIS ARE YOUR BFF!

Excellent professor! Small things like going to class, doing well on weekly quizzes, and completing homework add up and do wonders for your grade. No final if you have an A average. Highly recommend!!!

Dr. Anderson is one chill dude! He's funny and fairly lenient, although I thought the exams were tough (but I'm also not an engineer or anything). I really enjoyed having him as a professor, and I think most people do too. A word of advice: do all the homework and all the discussion work, he gives bonus points at the end of the semester!

To get an A in this class, you have to consistently perform very well on his exams (nothing lower than a very high B). Your homework and lab grades need to be high as well. His exams are generally pretty easy,  but be careful not to make too many mistakes because one slight mistake can cost you a letter grade. But he's still a decent teacher.

Consistently received an A average in HW, Lab, and class participation. Made one math mistake on last question on test an it screwed up entire grade. Received an 89.3, refused to bump it up. Don't make dumb mistakes and do all the work and you'll be fine. Tutoring center helps a lot.

Incredible professor. Not super serious during lecture, often funny, and very clearly explains topics that seemed confusing in the book. Also a pretty lax grader; you pretty much get a free 50% of your grade just by attending discussion / lecture, and doing homework. Very similar to PHYS 121.
A pooload of homework but exams are a joke

Dr Anderson is the best physics professor for 111 and 112. His exams are super easy. He helps you if you ask and is brilliant and super nice. He won't try to trick you with questions and is very clear. If there is an option DEFINITELY pick him

You will end up teaching yourself the material.  He goes over powerpoint questions but none are related to what's on the exam, nor is the online homework.  His practice tests are going to be your only tool.  Hard to pay attention in class because of his lack of enthusiasm and delivery of material. Unless you're previously good at physics,don't take

Excellent professor. I learned a lot from him. When webassign crashed he apologized for "the waste of [our] time." Good person, good professor. Reads and responds to blackboard discussions and truly cares if the students learn.

Good prof. that explains concepts and uses real life examples to deepen understanding. A dynamic lecturer. Clear expectations and exams are just like old exams and class examples. Online hw can be a little challenging at times, but manageable due to multiple attempts. Use book to ace lab hw. Attendance enforced with clickers; easy points.

He's fair. His exams are clear and if you understand the general gist of the topics you will do well. Lab is a bit pointless if you have a bad TA. His lectures get off topic sometimes but he does go by the syllabus. Make sure to review the mathematics of each topic on your own.

Good Professor. I was afraid how I do in this class but it was really fairly doable. The most important thing is to do your homework and understand all the material legit or else you'll make stupid mistakes on the exam. Make sure to attend class!! and Write everything from the board.

Dr. Anderson is a clear lecturer. If you have an A average at the end of the semester, the final is optional. If you attend class, you'll never be surprised by anything on the exams. Discussion questions are most difficult, followed by homework, then exams. There are extra credit opportunities on homework assignments. Highly recommend.

Dr. Anderson is fair, consistent, and very clear in all respects - lecturing, homework, discussions, and exams. You will never be surprised by anything you see on exams. He's the best professor to have for PHYS 122.

Dr. Anderson is, by far, one of the best profs. at UMBC. I hated physics before I took his class; I love it now. He is VERY approachable, his lectures are clear, and his tests are fair, reflecting the types of problems done in class. I don't know if he still teaches 111, but if you can choose between him and Jacobson, take Anderson!!!
One of the better physics professors at UMBC. Fair, easy exams, totally prepares you and doesn't throw any curveballs. If you have an A average before the final then you don't have to take it.

Very good professor. From time to time he will use simple props to help teach, which makes it interesting. He is clear and can also be amusing. The homework is sometimes difficult but it is not too hard. Exams aren't hard. Overall great professor and I hope to get him again.

Dr. Anderson is one of the best professors at UMBC.  He simplifies difficult concepts and is always available for help or just to chat.  His practice exams are very similar to the actual exams so if you study those, review the key concepts,and do a lot of practice problems then you're guaranteed an A or B.

I took Dr. Anderson's 111 and 112 courses and loved both. He does the best he can to explain the topics in the time he's given. He's ALWAYS willing to talk to students outside of class. He's also said that the material he focuses on and the way he approaches the material is based on MCAT expectations. I definitely recommend taking Phys with him!

I really enjoyed this class. Dr. Anderson was very nice and approachable and had a sense of humor. He tried his best to get the class to understand the material by doing a lot of practice problems, most of which were similar to those on the tests. He also gives practice tests from previous semesters and they really help when studying for the tests.
He teaches the material well! Use past exams and tutors at physics tutorial center for help, they are great! Studying required me about 8-10 hrs per week.

I had Anderson for 111 and 112, and there was definitely a difference in the complexity of the material.  Physics 112 is much more difficult, and he does not always do the best job of explaining it.  But the past exams are really helpful, as are the tutors.

Not an easy professor, but you will get an A as long as you're prepared. You should go to class and take notes. Absolutely study the past exams cuz he generally uses the same questions, changing the format a little. textbook doesn't rele help cuz he kinda simplifies the concepts. just know the basic physics and study a bit more = "A"
Loved Dr. Anderson! His tests were great. I feel they really reflected the material taught in lecture. Take him!

This is a fantastic professor- I disagree with some comments on here in which students feel he confuses the class with derivations. He establishes a basis for learning the material and applies several disciplines in the lectures to keep you glued. Mastering Physics is difficult at times but is very helpful. Je has plenty of tutoring hours to help.

Not very articulate, but his exams are easy. He's always calm and will never insult you for asking even the dumbest question. Hw (MP)SUCKS, if you have no friends you'll cry during it everytime. He has a hard time explaining what's in his head, but read the book and you + redo probs and stuff from lecture notes, old exams and MP before exams = A.

Had Anderson for both phys 111, 112. i hate physics. he is a decent professor but goes on telling you how to derive eqns that are already on the eqn sheet so it just confuses you. plan accordingly bc there is a lot of time devoted to the course. online physics, wkbk hw, studying, and pre/post labs. i'm glad i'm done

He's a very helpful professor and super approachable. Keeps lectures interesting with a mix of problems, conceptual, and live demonstrations time to time. HW is due every day, but it's 2-4 problems so it's do-able. Definently form a study group, it pays off! Recommend him as a professor, he is a knowledgable and is great at explaining!

I had him in 2008.His exams model the practice exams. Don't forget to look over old exams because he uses some old questions too.He has endless patience when answering questions.His lectures are very clear. Mastering physics homework is EXTREMELY difficult so you need to work in groups and google helps too. The textbook is nearly useless.
He is very clear at explaining concepts. Good professor for such a low level class.

Takes a hard class and makes it harder. Honestly, as a Bio major I don't think I should take physics, but at least 111 should be doable. He isn't helpful with his office hours and doesn't give you a straight answer when you have a question. Yes hes nice, but nice won't get you an A. Take it at community college if you have the option.

A good professor, tries to make the class interesting. Gives a lot of homework. He wants his student to pass. Exams are easy if you do all the Mastering Physics, text book and discussion problems. The exam questions are some variant of those problems. He also has a useful pre-exam review session. Overall, he is an average teacher with decent exams.

He is a good teacher. 122 is much easier than 121 and the discussions are more interesting. The only real complaint I have about him is that he doesnt give the answers to the old exams so while studying you can think that you are doing it right but then take the test and fail it. He does what he can to help you pass. i shouldve failed 121 but didnt

He is one of the best professors I have ever had at UMBC!  His lectures may be a bit long at times, and the classes are early, but he usually makes them interesting, and at his office hours he answers he is very nice and patient to answer all of your questions.  I highly recommend you go to the review sessions- he tells you whats on the exams.

I had him for 121 last semester and 122 this semester. Seeing as he's your only option for this class, here are some tips: -go to class and TAKE NOTES -do the mastering physics with a friend; don't save it until the night before -use his office hours He is a fair, helpful teacher.  If you fail, it will be because you didn't put in enough effort

Took 121/122 with him. I would have done better if I had paid more attention in lectures. Old exams are very useful study aids for the exams, so are his review sessions and the Mastering Physics review questions (which I should have done).

**First impressions only, may improve later on** Lost several points with me for forcing an 8 AM lecture three days a week. Clickers are cool, but don't use them if you don't know how to work them. Class starting out too simple - I learned all the one-dimensional kinetics in 9th grade. TA is condescending, class insulting to my intelligence so far.

Breaks it down pretty well for people new to physics, but people who did well in HS physics will still get it.  Very approachable, and willing to help 1-on-1 if you come to him.  Discussion is a little boring, but the HW piles up.  Do your mastering physics, too, or it'll bite you in the end.
he is not good teacher, HW is hard as hell, you better get a study group , with out that you wont be able to pass this class. TA's are weird
Really Good Physics teacher, lectures are really informative but do lack demos

The discussian portion of this class is worthless, in which you get these stupid long boring, repetitive packets that nobody does. The lecture is ok. This class starts out easy, but then gets alot of more difficult. And the online masteringphysics hw sucks balls. I aced the first test, got a D+ on the second, and probbaly completely failed the thir

Dr. Anderson is a great teacher. Physics is going to be hard no matter what, but go to class, study your notes and really try on the Mastering Physics. Old Exams are a great way to test yourself before the actual exam, and time yourself too!! Dr. Anderson is funny and very willing to help all of his students. Stay after class and make a new friend!

An insane amount of work for one class; don't take it when you have other hard classes.  Do his practice exams.  He's extremely helpful if you need it.  The trick is to never get behind the material.  He started using CPS for lectures to make attendance mandatory, but gave everyone a perfect score anyway regardless of how many they answered.
blah
He is great at lectures.  The problems he does assign help make sure that you get a least a passing score on the exams.  However you have to put a bit more effort to get the grade you want.

Easiest Class in the university.  Came to class just for CPS and went straight to sleep every day, got a 97% exam average.  Do mastering physics legit and figure out what each equation on the help sheet is for and it will be a breeze.

Probably the most intense class I've ever had to take. His exams are tough as nails. Go to all the lectures and all the discussions, and take massive notes. It also helps to go to his end of week reviews on Fridays. He is very willing to help during his office hours for the homework. It's almost critical to have at least three study buddies.

Entered this class having taken physics in HS and was blown away at how different it was. Does NOT move from his curve, 7 points away from a B. Useless textbook. Had a 4.0 before taking this class in sophomore year. Received the highest exam grades in my calc1 class, but tragically crashed and burned in physics. Good luck.
good teacher, covers material well. the class isnt too hard, i received a B with only having a basic physics course in high school

Had him for 121/122. Lots of work but no way can ppl say his lectures r bad. They're off da hook! Makes material interesting + easy 2 understand. Very witty + charming dude. Injects lots of humor (sometimes unwittingly) into lectures. Probably the ONE class I never fell asleep in. I'm HORRID at physics but gained much knowledge thanks to the prof.

There is a lot of difficult material in this course, but Anderson does a decent job of trying to simplify it in lecture.  His exams are very straightforward and predictable if you study over the old exams.  Getting a B is very possible even with no background...read the book, don't copy the online homework, and study old exams.
Very good professor who did a very good job covering the material in a clear, concise manner.

Seems like a pretty nice guy. Class is easy for the first couple weeks....until you can't withdrawal. Then he doubles the pace and throws in much harder course material. Final grade is based on 3 exams, Final exam, homework assignments (done online), and weekly quizzes in the discussion section where TA's are useless and completely incompetent.

I loved this guys teachin.. I took PHYS122 and got an A. I've taken that class w/ kramer and he made me suffer to barely pass the class... guys, if ya wanna pass  PHYS122, take with this guys.. no ambiguos questions.. go to his reviews just before the exams.. believe me.. some problems are exactly like examples
MUCH MUCH MUCH easier than any other physics professor in the history of physics

Think that just because you did well in calc will mean that you'll do well in this class? Think again. I had the highest grade in my class but STRUGGLED in phys 121. If you never took phys before, you will suffer. NOT an easy class, NOT a good professor. This class made me hate college.

Well above average.  He's a nice guy to talk to outside of class, and will help you when and if he can.  Homework is usually difficult (make sure you form a study group early), but the tests and final are always really fair and not too hard.  Be prepared to do some work on your own, because he doesn't cover everything.

I don't think Physics 121 was that bad and I'm no genius. I think its all about how much work you put into it and whether or not you do all that you can do to understand the material. I wouldn't say that his tests are hard but the questions are often connected so if you mess up on one question, you could really mess up. Homework is difficult but if

Dr. Anderson is a really good teacher.  The class is really hard and you have to read the book.  If you have never had a Physics class in high school or had a good teacher in high school, you will not do well in this class.  The only people that got above a C were the ones that had already had AP Physics and knew what was going on before.
Tests are easy in this class (easier than you would expect though still difficult). All you need to know is how to manipulate equations.

this class was hard. theres a lot of work u need to do on your own. if u understnad the readings in the book theres really no point to show up at 8am for class cuz you dont learn much. u have to teach urself how to apply the concepts which is the hard part. hw is very tough but exams are easier. do the practice exams b/c they help a lot.

Very good at teaching the material.  Makes it easy to understand, puts it in very accessible terms.  The exams are fairly difficult, and there is a LOT of homework, including some pretty pointless "Reading Quizzes" which are due an hour before class, almost every class.  Good teacher, but the class isn't very fun to take because of all the work...

Professor Anderson might be the best teacher I've ever had.  He explains concepts very clearly and it's obvious that he really cares that his students learn the material.  He's very generous when it comes to help outside of class, and he knows the material very well.  His sense of humor is excellent.  I really don't have anything negative to say.

Anderson is the man. The HW is tough, but his tests are much easier than the HW, so just go to every discussion class, get the HW solutions and make sure you understand the concepts, and you'll be fine. I slept in class for most of the second half of the semester and got a high B. Final exam was very simple and straightforward.

Mr. Anderson is a great teacher. He explains concepts very well and if you go to lectures all the time it shouldn't be too hard for you to understand them. But don't slack off in this class cause it's hard catching up. If you have questions he's always willing to help and he offers review and study sessions. Work hard and you'll get a good grade.
The homework is due at 9am and is not accepted late, no exam make up, u get a zero for them if not done on the test day. And they are to confuse you not test you.

Not a bad teacher. Just make sure u study and understand the concepts. This class is not really that hard as long as u pay attention. I did not spend that much time on this class and got a high B in the class. Just don;t slack off. Do your homework and get help if you need it.

Lectures are sometimes boring and not very helpful.  Smart guy though, can answer any questions you have.  Homeworks are very tough and require lots of time (or just get solutions from the internet).  Tests are fair and not too difficult.  Final was also fair and not amazingly hard.  Don't know if he curves or not.
class is a lot harder than it needs to be.  main problem is TA grading homework too tough.  one word: DC++
his tests are pretty straight forward if you study. Anderson is nice and offers extra help sessions to students who need it. He's new to UMBC and teaching large classes, but has done well.

He's the best 122 professor there is.  Keep up with the reading, hw, and talk to him about concepts at his review sessions.  It takes effort but I think his ease through the class makes it interesting and not overbearing.
class was to early to stay awake
He cannot teach!!! The class is hard and you would need extra help to understand it as it is. If you can, take it at CCBC and transfer the credit cause it is not worth to get a bad grade at UMBC.

This class is ungodly hard. I suggest getting a tutor as soon as you can a dedicate at least 3 hours for the weekly homework assignments. He doesn't teach all to well and class alone won't suffice in learning the material. You could easily miss ever class and only come to test days and receive a grade as most people.

He's really laid back and his lectures are kind of pointless sometimes, but all I know is that everyone usually says that 122 is a difficult class, and it's easy with Anderson. Tests are simple and straightforward. Cool prof.
No Comments
nice enough until you try to rechedule a test, i had to email the department head to get a makeup exam. maybe he's trying to be a hard ass since this is his first year
Nice guy, but the lectures are useless and boring.

He is ungodly boring.  Otherwise the class is ok.  Occasional quizzes on blackboard on the reading assigments, but they are easy and he only grades you on the answers that you give to the question, "what did you find confusing about the reading?"  I can't say much more, we haven't had enough classes yet.
He looks like the prince from Ella Enchanted

I enjoyed it. Wasn't there a lot. Sometimes this aggressive guy would come in to kick us out of class and then yell at him about his sanity? My main problem was that he mumbled a lot about the Chesapeake ripper. It wasn't a class on the ripper, so it was weird. He was nice though. Showed us pictures of his dogs :)

Cool guy. Showed us pictures of his dogs if we did good on exams. He had this friend who would always hang out in the back during his lectures for some reason? Gave really good lectures though, his class was like listening to a podcast.

One time I walked by his lecture hall on my way to another class and he was in there alone, standing in complete darkness, staring straight ahead, and muttering to himself. He also sweats a clinically insane amount and never makes eye contact with anyone. Not that that matters, since he's almost never there. Somehow not the worst professor here.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: Stared off into space a lot. Cute dogs. Would often ramble about nothing. Sweats a LOT. Gave us homework even while he was in the hospital. Stopped midlesson and stood in the corner of the room for 30 mins supposedly teaching someone how to fish. Gets giddy while talking about the Chesapeake Ripper. Gave us good grades if we listened to him..?
would stare off into space a lot and talked weirdly specifically about the subject matter, left mid-term and still gave me a C+ :/ cute dogs though
he was literally never there
Professor himself is fun, I just think the material is very boring. More textbook heavy-ish, lecture goes over what we read in textbook in a general basis.
such an amazing professor! encourages student participation and makes it very clear what he expects from you. i would 100% take again.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Dr. Kissel was a great professor to take for PSYC 210. I just had problems with the material because I did not find it interesting. Attendance is not mandatory but he does in class quizzes every class that do contribute to your grade. The three tests are for only the new content areas covered and the final is cumulative and optional.

Class felt more like hanging out than being taught at(in a good way). Classwork is very straightforward and so are exams(with optional final). He had fun activities that people could participate in if they wanted. I heard from others this class taught by other profs can be boring, but taking it with him was pretty fun.

Amazing for students who are new to a college setting. Accommodating of students needs and to makes sure his students are maximizing their grades. Many opportunities to raise your grade and make it the highest possible. Applies the psychological principles of learning to ensure his students are able to learn the material correctly and effectively.

Awesome professor!! He was very engaging and included activities during the lectures. It is not hard to get a good grade in this class, as long as you put in the effort and get the assignments done you will be fine. There are three exams (along with an optional final exam), but they are very fair and as long as you study, you will pass your exams.
Very smart professor, doesn't teach you anything.  Everything he says during the lectures he says as though you already know all the content in and out.  He's nice, but can't teach.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: For those looking and thinking "he can't be that bad," you're wrong. Lectures make no sense, are his English speaking skills are broken at best. If you don't exclusively read/study from the textbook, you will fail. Quizzes and exams are designed for you to fail, and there's no homework to help pick up your grades. Please take it with Kalman Nanes.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Guler is very intellectual but he is a bad instructor. His lectures are boring and teach you nothing. You can hardly understand him and he expects you to know the proofs. If you study hard, you will understand the concepts. Just memorize the definitions. He rarely gave partial credit so you have write and solve everything perfect.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The class is already hard and with this prof it got even harder lmaoo
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I have no clue how I passed his class. I somehow held a straight 57% until the final exam and only got a 60 on it. Guler is quite possibly the worst professor I've had. He doesn't teach well and uses AI to not only make quizzes but to grade them too (which he has admitted to my class). He gets his own notes wrong during class and overall is a pain.
Please whatever u do DO NOT take the morning class with him. If you're forced to choose this class then please choose an afternoon/evening class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Never in my 15 years of education have I had a professor as bad as this one. I implore anyone who takes this class, to please avoid this teacher. Tests often include unfair criteria and points are taken off for occasionally no reason.

Normally I'm not all too worried about the rating a professor gets, but this one is entirely necessary. DO NOT TAKE THIS PROFESSOR! If you're the kind of person who says "I'll ride it out", this is not the guy you want to do that with. His lectures are barely comprehensible, writing indiscernable, and he was so bad I'm writing this a semester later

Are you taking this crazy insane guy class? You will hate yourself for your decision. He seems care his students but NO. reviews.comment: I got an A in the class but I honestly do not like her.  She never gives heads up that assignments are due even when class is cancelled. There were numerous presentations and she barely taught.  She's also quite rude when responding to emails which made me so uncomfortable emailing her.  The class was easy to pass,  but I wouldn't recommend .
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: worst professor I have ever had. She would make students feel stupid when they asked a question that she thought was obvious, or if they didn't agree with her opinion. She expects us to take pages of notes on readings and movies that we watch but will only put ONE QUESTION it. dont take if u want a professor who will take ur questions seriously.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: she gets mad when we do not understand the reading. she is alway right even when she is wrong. makes us read and talk the whole class. slow grader and its boring
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--SO MANY PAPERS

reviews.comment: I love this class. she a bad grader because she is so slow at it but you have to read to know what your talking about. its a fun class things can get heated. hat the group work.

Overall our entire class pretty much hated her, for FYS 102 we had to read about 20 - 40 pages for each class (two classes a week) and writing app. 5 pages of work a week, the class is not marked as writing intensive and only a 3 credit course.  I would not take it or one of her courses again.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: Such an amazing professor! I enjoyed having her and would take another class with her. She's very intelligent and makes the class interesting. Just do your work, come to class and make an effort.

Only 3 quizzes, a midterm, and a final. There are a lot of group work opportunities throughout the semester. 2-12 page readings  per class (no official textbook), plus a series of films. This isn't a class you can take lightly.

I heard she's hard during the school year but I took her for a summer course and she was amazing. The setting is a lot more laid back, we had readings but not too many, and class discussions were interesting every class. Most people in the class were older though so the material was easy for us.

Worst teacher alive. Expects students to interpret the reading on her level. Takes simple films and looks too much into them and making things deeper than it is. & her tests are the worst. She made 1 question worth 60 points!! Avoid this teacher if you like passing.

She doesn't answer her emails, you have to email her TA. You have 20 plus readings 2 to 12 pages long and a novel. You have a mandatory group project. Her lectures were empty and uninteresting. She had a bit of an attitude and expected everybody to be above her level (she has a PhD). She can be cool at times but mostly was a bish.

do NOT take her class! she is rude and will interrupt you if you don't have the same views as her. she takes herself ENTIRELY too seriously to be teaching a 100 level class. the readings are ridiculously long and the tests are all short answeressay. and if you miss 3 classes, pray she won't fail you. this class is a headache!! NOT WORTH IT!!!
She never posts grades online so your grade and the end of the semester is a mystery and she assigns way too much work

She is the slowest grader ever. Assigns 12 pages paper as final exam during final week n expects to have it back 4 days later.Thinks her class is all that.100 level considered as a 400 level class. If AFST is not ur major, please don't take this class cuz she assigns too much work when u have  other things to worry about.
Assigns way too much work for a 100 level course and expects way too much.

She asks for a lot for a 100 level class. This is a history class, yet the papers you write in the class are all based on opinion. If you study VERY hard, and keep up with the readings, you can get an A. Very, very challenging class. She is very funny, but can sometimes get a bit of an attitude.

Nice, funny lady, but has very strict rules. Make sure you go to class, she has a very strict attendance policy. (miss 3 classes = automatic 'F') Not an easy A, but if you keep up with the readings, you could get an A. She's sometimes unclear with what she wants on the essays and the presentation you'll have to do, so be sure to ask questions.

AFST are classes about the history of African American people, aka things that actually happened so I don't understand how you can "teach based on opinion. " But anyways she's a really good teacher, she can be moody though. You can literally get an A or B with skimming the readings. All the "essays" are just 1 page reactions to what you learned.
Would not recommend this professor. Bases class on personal opinions. Lectures are inaccurate at times. Bad attitude.

Not teaches, using students' presentations to make quiz and exam, just wants to take off students' points, handle her class like a 400 level class. You will need to spend Ton of time and won't be care your major courses b/c of this class.
Great proffessor, as long as you do your work you will be fine...dont assume that because  its AFST you dont have to try, talk to her after class and let her know you

She is ridiculous! She is very unorganized and never knows what she wants. She has these ridiculous pop quizzes that don't make any sense. And her projects are very stupid and senseless I would not recommend anyone to take this course.

This class was really stressful until I got the hang of it. The professor expects a lot from you, and it can sometimes be frustrating, but she wants her students to do well, which counts. Not an easy A course, and a TON of reading is required although there is no textbook
Worst teacher ever! she gives too many readings to do. Exams and quizes are hard. If you're looking for an easy A, this is not the teacher! She is funny in class but worst teacher

Not an easy A class. Lots of readings (a book included). All you have to study from are the notes you take. She gives 5 pop quizzes, 5 journals, and 2 exams. She's pretty strict with grading and tends not to give study guides unless asked.

She is super nice and soft spoken. Although her lectures can get kind of dull, she is VERY open to questions (she asks if we have any every 3 minutes). There is a lot of group work which will impact your grade, so choose wisely.Very lenient grader, and a kind lady.The course itself is a bit boring, but not her fault. Make sure you know some diff eq

Long-suffering, kind, and ammenable. Grading was generous, yet fair. Maybe could've covered more material but overall fantastic. Homeworks can be annoying but I got a 60% average on them and still got an A in the class so it's chill

Prof. Kang is one of the most kind and fair professors you will encounter at this university. She graded very fairly and made sure everyone was ready for the exams. Do the homework early and go to class, and you will get an A for sure. Also had a pretty simple group project that wasn't too bad.

Dr. Kang is one from the best professors. She is nice and patient and makes my semester great. Her lecture is amazing and can extend the due date for the homework. She is helpful inside and outside the class. She also gives more hints and explanations by email. The class is interesting and I learned something valuable with her. 10/10 recommend her.

Her lectures hard to get (thank god she got outlines). Her tests were heavy since the problems she gives for 1 hour and 15 minutes exam is too much. Her grades on blackboard are way off to the students' final grades, which is not mentioned until the last day which is totally misleading. Only worth taking it if you have study buddies to work with.

I had Kang for two classes this semester and she made my semester great. She is so helpful and really cares about her students. I would take her for as many classes as you can! Group project at the end of the semester but not difficult.

Kang is an awesome professor and very willing to listen to student feedback, on multiple occasions she moved due dates back because we asked. She offers a few extra credit opportunities and is always helpful in and outside of class. Go to her office hours, it helps so much! I thought I was going to fail this class going in but came out with an A.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Clear grading criteria--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: Dr. Kang is a very good professor who cares more about student learning and success than showing off her knowledge or covering every aspect of the textbook. She is also very approachable and happy to answer questions. If you come to class, do the work, and see her when you need help, you should get a good grade.

One of the best math professors at UMBC, Dr. Kang is genuinely interested in student success and very friendly. She takes constructive criticism EXTREMELY well and goes out of her way to improve the course throughout the semester based on said feedback.
Probably the nicest teacher in the world, take her if you can. Super helpful outside of (and in) class. Very very friendly and sweet.

I had Dr A for 301 and 446 and she is a tough grader but her lectures and classes are interesting. I find her classes to be super enlightening and you learn a lot of valuable information, but you definitely have to work for your A in that class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Amazing lectures --Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: She seems like a good person, but Im not sure if I say she is a great prof. Too many papers with strict requirements. She opened up the prompt for the final paper way too late. It just felt like paper after paper. Class meets twice a week and before class there are journal prompts based on article she assigns. Its writing intensive but too much.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--So many papers

reviews.comment: Dr. A is extremely kind and understanding!

Dr. Antkowiak has a reputation as a tough grader - but she's fair. She pushes you to be a more critical thinker and consumer of information and is particular about your writing with the intent to strengthen your ability to formulate arguments. Go to her office hours and send her your essays in advance for feedback. Seriously. Thank me later.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: mm... well.. she was not good at explaining political backgrounds to students who are not in the political field. Well she seems like a good professor for students in politics
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: She does not provide enough background for understanding politics. It's not a good course for people who is not political people.
Smart and caring professor still a hard grader tho

I took PUB150H with Hussey, which is an introductory public policy class for Sondheim Scholars. This course is somewhat demanding - not the hardest class I've ever taken, but definitely not an easy A. If your a Sondheim, you don't really have a choice. Overall, I love Dr. Hussey. She's incredibly insightful and very approachable.

Hussey is really awesome. She loves policy and politics - and you can really tell when she lectures.  She's a tough grader and you definitely have to work for it but the class is nowhere near impossible. Theres a LOT of reading. She's definitely awkward and strange when you're 1 on 1, but she's great in class.

There are no actually requirements for poli 446, but you want to take poli 301 first. If you want to understand her suggestions about research and sources I highly recommend taking poli 301 before taking this class. If you take poli 301 first, you and her will speak the same language. Tough class but you're guaranteed to learn something.

Make sure you are credible and site first hand sources! Use MLA format or you will get points deducted. Make sure everything is on point and you are sure to walk away with at least a "B". That being said, she is very smart and passionate about this topic. The class is worth taking you will learn a lot. Bear in mind you have to put in serious effort

If you're still at the stage where anti-intellectualism is your mode of thought, the English department is across campus buddy. I don't meet many professors that strike me as all that sane, but Laura does. She doesn't like to fail her students, but Laura holds off on giving A's Dont be afraid to learn from a C in her class, and get the A next time.

Dr. Hussey is wonderful. She is very passionate about what she teaches and she knows exactly what she is talking about. She is always willing to work with you and does what she can to make sure you succeed. Definitely a superior professor.

She's overall a terrible professor. I still have yet to understand how she grades. I was in EVERY single class and participated frequently.. I STILL got an 85% on my attendance&participation! She's not helpful- and it doesn't even seem like she cares to be helpful. She's very dry. and most of all, she's not worth your time or your money.

she's a great teacher! She's very eager to help students out whenever she can. She is a bit awkward, but she's very intelligent. Lectures can get a bit boring, but like I said she'll help you out with anything, just ASK.

Good speaker, though was far to much student participation. Student "speeches" would sometimes take up over half of the total class time and were easy to zone out during. Attendance/participating unfortunately part of grade.
She is extremely awkward, her test are difficult, and she sometimes takes attendance, but sometimes doesn't! Class is pretty boring, but her paper is easy.

She's a great professor. Very well organized with her teaching and extremely fair in her grading. She is educated in the subject she's teaching and is always willing to help out her students. I loved her.
This is the worst professor I have ever had.

I am an engineering major but took this class for a GFR. Dr. Hussey made everything easy to understand and taught everything in a very organized way. She grades fairly and if you apply even a little bit of effort you'll do well. Only one paper for the whole semester and it wasn't long or heavily weighted.
Took her Fall '24 - Fall '25. Very chill and funny professor. A lot of work but as long as you put in effort you're fine.
Nice professor but grades Harsh, And I'm not the best in Spanish, so this class was very hard for me. She also makes you participate a lot.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: She is a funny and hilarious teacher, brings that energy to class every time! Her class is HEAVY on participation and will randomly call on you. There are also a few readings in the class and just know you're going to be talking to your classmates A LOT. She has many mini group assignments in class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Took her in the Fall of '24. She was great! A bit disorganized, so try to remind her of things and ask her to clarify if you're confused (this happened a lot). She's very sweet and entertaining lectures. Participation is crucial! She WILL randomly call on you. Try to finish the assignments on time, they are pretty simple, so don't stress too much.

milvia is hilarious however you have quizzes and homework with a few projects. she is a tough grader tho. i thought just cause im latina and already know spanish I would get an A but it is very difficult to get an A with her. you will most likely end up with a B unless you put your all into this class. she also forces you to read and participate.

The class was enjoyable. Professor Hernandez would continuously try to keep each student engaged by calling on them to read or answer questions, but as long as you are paying attention, participation is not hard at all. She grades attendance each class, so make sure to be there. Homework and projects are not hard, but make sure to study for exams.

Very good professor. She gives you an extra chance to get more points on an exam when handed back to you. At most there is just paper/packet Hw assignment each class. We had one project for the whole semester but that was super easy to do. Do the hw assignments well and study good for the exams, everything on them is what she posts on blackboard.

I had Dr. Hernández for SPAN 202, and she is amazing. She cares about her students and wants them to understand the material, offering lots of help and humor in every lecture. The workload is heavy-ish, but to be expected for a language. I was worried about this class since I hadn't taken Spanish for a year, but I had no problem picking it back up.

I had Spanish 202, but honestly she was quite good. She's always got a lot of energy in the class, almost makes me feel like I'm in primary school again. She can give a lot of homework sometimes but it's not for fun, with language you need a lot of repetition. I would definitely take the class again.

(Span 202, not 201) I genuinely don't know why she has the ratings she does, but after seeing the grades of the raters it makes sense. I dislike learning language a lot. That being said, Ms. Hernandez was a fine teacher. She's knowledgeable and she tries to bring energy to the class. You're learning a language...manage your expectations.
Terrible professor. would never take her class again
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Class was asynchronous. She grades harshly and assigns too much work. 3-4 assignments due per week. 2 cultural projects, 1 individual and the other is a group project. Pace yourself and start assignments early.
She is very rude and acts like you should know everything. Don't know why she teaches if she's going to have that attitude.

Might be my worst experience in a class at UMBC. Left assignments ungraded for a very long time, so quizzes would be marked as an F until she'd manually grade them (almost 2 months in, and still nothing). So almost 0 clarity on your current grade.

Assignments were all online and harshly graded by the online system.

Just take someone else dude.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Lectures and assignments were generally good. Heavy amount of assignments. But assignments remained ungraded for months.

Way more work than 101/102 with a much worse (and harshly automatically graded) online system. >4 hours per week of homework. She did a terrible job with the Blackboard setup- submitted work showed as late, work would be marked as zero until graded, and she took forever to grade anything. She was nice enough in person, but the class was awful.

Horrible horrible class design. You will have 9 diff assignments in one week that are long & tedious to get thru, & these are separate from the quiz, readings and other busy work. The online book used for this class is chaotic & each section can take up 1 hour to complete. I am an A student and I had to drop this class. I had a migraine first week
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--So many papers--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Awful class. No lectures or guidance. She expects the textbook to teach students everything and is pretty irate if they're confused. The textbook is also really particular and the tests and quizzes are hard. No one in my class has a good grade, and I'm not about to destroy my GPA.

This was a horrible class. All of the students were stressed out and didn't feel like they had the information needed to succeed. She provides averages for exams and often the average was in the 60s. She's aggressive in video calls and does not respond well to student questions. 2 group projects during the semester were okay but tedious.

Entertaining, funny, and helpful prof. Class load was pretty easy, midterm and final were ridiculously easy. Midterm you get a full sized paper for notes, and final you litterally just give a basic explanation for a couple easy topics from the class. Projects can be difficult, especially the last one, but overall great prof and good lass.
He is the goat.

W teacher, cares about learning over grades. Pretty forgiving grader as long as you try. 313 is hard if you have 0 background info, but he knows and structures his class so you have a good chance at passing if you attend class and do your best in lecture/hw. Although, i seriously hate flipped classes. But would take again. He's pretty silly too.

6 HWs; 1 Midterm (10% of grade); 4 projects (can be done solo/group & 1st two build upon each other and the last 2 build upon each other).
