Midterm is ridiculously easy (you get cheat sheet one page one side), "Final" is video about you talking about topics from class; the last project is VERY difficult (start early for that one). Flipped classroom.

4 group projects. First two build on each other and the last two build on each other. Flipped classroom so the material is on blackboard and he goes over examples in class but doesn't post them so you have to go. Midterm had like 20 people get A's. Understands external circumstances and gives generous extensions if needed. Great Prof. ~Easy Grader

Took Ivan for CMSC 411 Summer 2024 (4WK1). Even though the class was listed as online synchronous, we were given straight to the point asynchronous lectures we could watch and complete weekly assignments on. Final project was toughhhh and I didn't even finish but luckily he graded really leniently, as it was a 4 week summer course.

He s not funny, hard to reach outside of class, does not teach. Projects were hard to complete considering you have to figure everything yourself. Yes he is lenient on grading but rightfully so bc he doesn't teach. If you don't come to class to watch him solve problems that pertain to your project you will be screwed.

Ivan is the best CS professor I've had. He is funny and lenient on grading. Just make sure that you keep up with the assignments and pre-recorded videos. The video quizzes have unlimited attempts, and the homework are fairly spread out. Also, there are class activities which are graded on effort/completion. Ivan should be your #1 choice for 313.

Attendance is mandatory but very lenient. He is a great guy and makes a hard subject really easy to understand. His class is mainly watching his old videos and then doing activities in class, but the bad comments are from people who didn't do the activities, to be honest. If you do exactly what he tells you to do, which isn't hard, you will succeed

Not my type of professor, not necessarily bad. Posts old lecture vids, expected to watch before class. first 15-30 mins spent on example, rest of time is spent on participation activity. Lenient grading on exam. Personally didn't feel like structure was conducive to learning material compared to regular lectures in class and feel prepared for proj
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: One of the best teachers i have ever taken I wish i could take him for all my classes. TAKE HIM YOU WON'T REGRET IT. He's also funny.

Knows his stuff, 4 group projects, weekly video quizzes and homework, midterm, and final.
Not a hard professor, grades leniently midterm was very, very hard but he ended up just giving partial points on MC questions and other random stuff.

Really cooly guy, very easy, and is caring about his students, choose to use a very obscure software the first half of the class (Xilinx) and does get a little annoying sometimes but besides that the class is really organized,  would recommend taking the class with him, one of the best cmsc prof at umbc

He does a flipped classroom format so watch lectures first (it will def. help) and then come to class to work on class assignments (group but also, solo is ok). He just cares that you walk away learning something and I guess that mindset kind of alleviated pressure for me...which also makes it easier to learn the material. Goated!

Very helpful in and outside of class to learn the material.  Group projects and discussions help alleviate the typical stress of a computer science class, and make the class more enjoyable.  Overall very chill professor and good person.  Always has some quality memes screensavers to look at before class begins.

Nice, chill, laid back professor. Posts lecture videos you can watch and goes over them in class. Plenty of opportunity to earn points, and the assignments were pretty easy too. Also had a few extra credit opportunities during the semester. Definitely one of the good ones.

Totally awesome dude. Sekyonda is seriously amazing. He's understanding, he grades in a way that makes you feel like you got a grade you deserved, his projects are hard but they really make you learn, and he tries very hard to make sure everyone understands the material. He is seriously a gem and if I could have him for every class I would.

Ivan is an amazing professor, I recommend you try to have him at least once. I had him for 313 and then 411 this semester. He made this class super relaxed and hard to fail. He let us make a cheat sheet for the midterm (it was 4 questions with a freebie extra cred) and graded it so leniently. He's super helpful and answers emails timely.

I thought everything about the class was very fair. The projects were challenging but not impossible. He indirectly explained everything you needed to know in order to be successful on each of the projects, quizzes and exam. If my partner and I got stuck, he was very willing to help guide in the right direction. Put the work in and you will do well

Uncle Ivan is a great professor. I forgot to do one of the assignments that were worth 10% but there was an optional final. He told me to make sure to study for the final I review HW, quizzes, n the lecture. The final was easy. I messed up and work with someone for project 4 I told him n he said its fine. Talk to him He will explain ps not my uncle

Ivan was a great Professor! You could tell he really knew his stuff, and conveyed the information in class well. He wasn't super enthusiastic during lectures, which made his videos pretty boring to watch, but if you can get through those he's a great professor and a great guy. There were plenty of Extra credit opportunities as well.

Ivan was solid! Group projs were graded leniently. Videos explained exactly what you needed. Wasn't a walk in the park, gotta put in the work for an A. Attend class (even if its review of vids) since activities he gives are for attendance. If you kill the projs + midterm you won't need to take his optional final. HWs felt a bit pointless at times.

Ivan truly knows how to teach concepts well. No respondus lockdown. The class consisted of HWs, 4 group projects, a (hard) midterm, and an optional final. He was really lenient in grading the projects, especially the ones written in assembly bc he genuinely wants you to learn. Also gives multiple attempts for the video quizzes/HWs. Responds fast.
He is a great lecturer. His videos were incredibly helpful to understand the material. I learned so much, and learning was not difficult. I suggest taking CMSC 411 with him.

Not a bad professor. Offers many resources to study for quizzes and prepare for homework assignments. Just brace yourself for the midterm and the final, which are relatively difficult if you don't know the material by heart.

Ivan is knowledgeable and knows how to explain the concepts well. The class consisted of homeworks, 4 group projects, a midterm, and an optional fiinal.I found the midterm extremely challenging and almost half the students failed. The key to doing well in the course is working hard to understand the homeworks and to do the projects.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--Group projects

reviews.comment: People dont like Ivan because he uses respondus lockdown. Get over it. We are online and its a way to stop cheating. If you actually try and study the content you will be fine. His tests are questions basically from the hws and class. You get 2 attempts on the hw. Participation matters. Big project at the end was not that hard. Very hard to fail.

He will make sure you understand the concept if you email him or post on Piazza. His lectures were on Panopto and those videos were recorded in Spring 2020 so he's just basically reusing them. 1 midterm 15% and 1 (OPTIONAL) final on Respondus Monitor can be replaced for hw/quiz/exam. The HW,QUIZ,Group Projects,Group rating,Participation is 85%.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: The slides he uses for his lectures are explained in a way that you'll feel sleepy after 5mins. The final and midterm will make or break you. The questions are from the class activities so make sure to attend classes. 6 HW's, 15 weekly quizzes, 4 projects and 2 exams on LockDown with WebCam recording ON. Do NOT take 313/411 with him!!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Group projects

reviews.comment: Ivan is a great guy, makes lectures funny (some jokes miss but that makes it even funnier). He really cares about helping you and will spend as much time as you need and even check up on you the next day to make sure you got it. Attendance isnt really mandatory but he gives random exercises after some classes that count as participation.

Great professor, very reachable and friendly. Must go to class as there are examples that he does in front of you that are carbon-copies of exam material. There is a project due at the end but it is not difficult and he let us use the language of our choice. Prepare to laugh. He has some fire memes.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Nice guy and he expalins concepts really well. He emails back really fast as well. He helps you through the projects. You have to put in the work for an A but you have to do nothing to get fail. Class is not easy but he makes it easier. His ppts make you go to class as he does in class examples and does not put the examples on Blackboard.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Group projects--Hilarious

reviews.comment: Ivan is a hilarious guy. He is also really good at explaining concepts and if you don't understand something, he will help you through it. Work is hard though. He said on the first day "You have to try to get an A, but you also have to try to get an F." Definitely taking him again in the future.

Really great professor. He is clear about what he expects from his students and is very approachable. He will go through what you need thoroughly if you email or talk to him and is considerate of any difficulties you might have. Exams were easy as he prepares you well (you must put in the effort). It was an absolute pleasure to be in his class.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: He is an awesome professor, his sarcasm is always on point. It is not an easy class, but he is fair. As long as you attend class, takes notes, and seek help when you need it, you should be ok. The subject itself is hard, but he knows his stuff and is a good teacher.

Ivan is easily the best cmsc 313 teacher at umbc. The exams and homework assignments are fair. The projects take a lot of time and you must start early. You have to show up to class because he solves many example problems there that will not be posted online.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring

reviews.comment: Prof Ivan is overall great for teaching the course CMSC313. Please make use of his office hours.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Make sure you are listening in class!! The sides weren't as helpful. Annoying projects only because he didn't prepare us enough for them and there weren't enough resources to complete the project by your own... you had to go to his office hours. Great Professor, clear explanation, approachable, cool guy. Overall I'd recommend him DON'T MISS CLASS!
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: This is his first semester here at UMBC so he is a little disorganized but well prepared. He definitely knows his stuff and is always willing to explain something a second or third time. Very laid back and approachable, good sense of humor. First half of semester has been assembly programming, now into digital logic. I'll be taking him for CS411.
A pretty good professor. I enjoyed his lectures and he's funny. Test grading can be a bit tough but if you can pull a few examples for the topics you'll be fine.

An enthusiastic professor, relies completely on lectures to educate. Little to no grading criteria or material available, had to rely on previous knowledge. Basically no feedback, lecture slides gave little to work off of. Lectures can be confusing, but generally is understandable.

I like him as a professor - you can tell he cares and he's pretty funny during lectures. However, tests are super important in this class and they are not easy. They are all essay questions and are graded very hard. I almost failed both of them. If you just need a GEP or credit and want something easy, don't take this class.
Majority of class is exam, you NEED to focus in class, do not take if you just need a social credit, many people who do and just sit on their phone fail at the first exam.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: No rubric was provided for discussions or exams, and requests for clarification were met with vague responses and no guidance. Weekly discussion posts were graded poorly without explanation, regardless of effort. The final exam was also poorly organized, leaving many students unable to finish on time.

Great professor, lectures are engaging and well paced. However, grading is unclear and no rubrics are given for exams. I got an 89 and a 67 on two similarly structured exams with factually correct info that answered the question clearly and concisely, but no feedback was given at all to explain the grade.

Took this class on a whim but honestly not a bad class. All grades come from the exams which are relatively easy to complete if you take notes. The exams are online and are pretty consistent with the material learned in class. Overall, the class is incredibly lecture heavy with little room for participation, but it is not a requirement for grading.

The content of the class can mostly be learned through the textbook, but Professor Smead has a lot of interesting comments in the class slides and lectures. He's also very kind and will work with you if  you have any problems.

Smead is a passionate professor who is great at lecturing on the topics in 102. The workload is light, and the lectures are interesting. However, the downside of the light workload is that exams are weighted very heavily (70% of the grade), making it easy to drop a letter grade. Overall though, the class wasn't hard and the exams were online.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment:
This professor and class were so disorganized, most classes were overtaken with off topic discussions of military powers. This class was supposed to go from 1945-2021, we barely ended up touching on the 2000s. 
Gives absolutely no feedback, and when asked for feedback is extremely rude. Wildly disappointed with my experience in this class

The exams are not multiple choice and the time given is not enough to answer well. For an asynchronous course only opening the exams from 12pm-8pm on fridays makes no sense, I took the class for schedule flexibility and this was contradictory. Overall it was not too bad just do the discussions and try your best on the exams, write VERY quickly
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I attended this class a total of four times and got a B. When I did go, the lectures were interesting. I read the assigned portion of the (free) textbook each week and completed the weekly responses without needing to be present. 2 exams throughout the semester, and 1 final exam. No multiple choice, all essay or ID format, all were online.

Unclear assignments and unclear feedback. I just got an essay back with only one sentence of feed back. Not only was it kind of a confusing sentence, he didn't tell me what to do differently next time. He is definitely knowledgeable about the subject material, but when it comes to the writing the class is just a mess.

You are only graded by exams which makes the class more difficult, especially since he is a tough grader. However, he posts all of the lectures online and if you write the important points that he reiterates, you will do well on the exam. He knows a lot about history and you will learn a lot in the class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Tough grader

reviews.comment: All he does in class is lecture, which you can get online once he posts the slides. The only grades in the class are from 3 exams, all essay format. He is very knowledgeable and passionate, but he is a tough grader .. and the classes can be hard to sit through without falling asleep.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: If you take Professor Smead's class, basically those next weeks will be nothing. He lectures, and that's about it. The syllabus tells you what day each topic will be, and that basically tells you that you don't need to come to lecture at all. The only time people show up are for the exams, and sometimes those dates are subject to change.

The class is quite easy. Professor Smead's lectures are very informative and i would recommend going to class. The book helps but is not really necessary. He also posts the slides and does lecture podcasts so you can hear everything he says. There were only 3 exams so make sure you study for them. Pretty easy A if you study for the exams
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Very lecture heavy, puts all of his lectures in the form of podcasts online as well as his power points therefore attendance is not a necessity but keeping up is. Not a class on memorization but rather on synthesis of the big picture ideas because the grades for this class are the 3 exams only and they are essay questions only.

I LOVED Prof. Smead. Super knowledgeable about his field and I actually enjoyed every lecture because I love learning about History. He is really funny too and overall a VERY nice guy. He makes you work for the grade though, since exams are all essay question style and for an A you have to go really into detail and memorize all your dates & names
reviews.rating_tags: TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Smead is a great professor. Although politics can get in the way of his lectures just sit through it. If you're comfortable with your writing you and are fine with GOING to the lectures you'll be good. And by going I mean just sitting through the lectures hungover and somewhat listening. Got a 69.5% in HS english, 85% avg. on his exams.

This class was honestly my favorite history class ever. Dr. Smead's podcast had an abundance of information, was very interesting to hear, as well as entertaining. His syllabus is very clear and organized. His powerpoints match his lectures. The required book and the assigned reading of it gives a brief, yet detailed summary of the topics.

Loved his class, despite it being at 8:30am. Hilarious, sarcastic guy who knew his stuff, and encouraged participation. If you want to learn the truth about the civil war, World War II, Watergate, he's the man. Only graded by 3 exams, the third which is your final. Just do the readings and you can get a B, more effort and the A is yours

Your grade in the class is based on 2 exams and 1 final cumulative exam so you really need to know the material for the exams. The professor was alright, he knew what he was talking about but was boring. He was funny though but the class just dragged on and wasn't very engaging.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: He does a pretty good job of explaining content, but his expectations for what you need to know are pretty vague. His lecture slides contain an outline of content. In order to get everything you need for the test, you need to come to class and take notes. There are 3 exams, each is 2 essays and definitions. 1 of the essays is based off of a book.

Decent teacher, very liberal though so he can get annoying. Your final grade is based on 3 exams 100 points each. Hes a tough grader so you have to know your material really well. Its almost impossible to get an A so study hard for that B.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Professor Smead makes class interesting; which is important at an 8:30am. I loved learning from him and his knowledge and passion for the subject radiated when he gave his lectures. Unfortunately, his exams are the only grades in class, and it's very difficult to receive an A, no matter how much/how long you study. Read the assigned readings!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: Professor Smead is very knowledgeable, which helps the course tremendously, but politics can get in the way of class material, this semester being especially bad.  His grading methods are a mystery.  Grades were based on three essays with no rubric or even a length guideline.  A somewhat below average professor when all is said and done.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: He is a good professor and knows the subject but he has a hard time keeping liberal politics and his opinions out of the classroom. This can be a huge deterrent to coming to class. Your grade is based on three tests so be prepared to read if you want an A or at least show up to all of the classes.

Professor Snead is super smart about American history, and it shows through his lectures. Only three tests define your grade, so make sure you do well. he does get off topic and falls behind very easily and since we fell behind he gave us our tests as take home exams, but they're not easy. The syllabus readings showed up on test 2 but that's it.

Professor Smead is a tough grader but if you attend every class and follow the syllabus you won't have a problem getting a good grade. Completing the outside readings is a must. His lectures are among the best I have sat in as he is very energetic and enthusiastic about history.
Took as winter session class - easy 3 credits. Lectures (recorded - not always good sound quality) more important than reading. On tests, give it back EXACTLY the way he gave to you.

Dr. Smead is a brilliant professor. His lectures are very impassioned and informative. Go to class because you learn from his lectures! The grade is made up of two "hour" exams and a final exam, all written. Read, read, read! Write as much as you can and you'll do well in his class. Dr. Smead-If you're reading this, I'll see you sometime @ UMD!

Could probably get a B without reading the text book, but other readings a must if you want to pass. Good lectures but can get off topic. 3 exams, all short essay. Nice guy, adds some humor and unique insight to lectures. Do the reading an you should be able to get an A in class.

Your grade is three exams, 30%30%40%, and you better study hard and at least skim the assigned readings if you want to do well. He puts up helpful study guides. Lecture is really, really good and interesting, he knows everything there is to know about this stuff and makes it entertaining. Really recommended for gen ed credits.
the only grades he gives are on 3 tests, so you need to do well on them, but he makes it crystal clear what is required for the tests so its not too difficult. pretty funny guy too

By far the worst professor I've ever had. Had 4 essays two exams and 4 discussion boards and he is very biased and opinionated which was quite evident in his lecture which are 10 hrs at least for each week. Don't take him unless you are very liberal and follow his viewpoints. Quite ridiculous for a HIST 347 online class. I'm an A or B person.

He is a polite professor. However, he talks too much, he goes over the class time limit all the time. His exams are all essays and short answers and he is not a lenient grader. You have to read 3 novels plus the textbook outside of class. That is too much for an entry level course.

Dr. Smead's online class is made up of all of his lectures recorded from the previous semester. I listened to every lecture and took notes. The textbook was good for specific examples and helped for quick reference on the exams. Easy class if you are willing to listen to all of the lectures and put some effort into learning the material.

Class was literally  based entirely upon 3 essay based exams, 2 of which had a small BCR section worth 20%. The study guides weren't very helpful at all and had you studying a lot of stuff that wasn't on the exam.
He is a fun teacher. He really cares about your success. This is a good teacher to know. He promised me a stop in his class in the Spring semester after it already filled up.

A couple of points: Firstly, read the syllabus, check Blackboard, and check your e-mail. You'll know what to do & why to do it. Secondly, while Dr. Smead is liberal, he does agree to disagree as long as you can be clear that you disagree and about why you disagree with him. Thirdly, do the reading and pay attention to the lectures & Powerpoints.

He is very well versed in American history, particularly anything political. I would recommend this class or another class he specializes in. Quite passionate about the topic. Very good about utilizing Blackboard.
this guys awesome. 3 tests. not mandatory attendance- however- show up, take notes, study a little and you're golden. highly recommend.

Easy Professor! He really knows his material. Very easy to follow. Posts Lectures and Powerpoints on Blackboard. Attendence may not be mandatory but his teaching style makes you want to attend class. After taking him,I plan on taking hm again. Textbooks seldom used but they actually aren't a bad read if you're interested. Overall Great Professor!

Pretty good teacher, knows his stuff but doesn't seem to care and shows up 20 minutes late everyday if at all. You have to attend class to do well, even though he puts all his powerpoints online. Don't expect to get an A, TA's grade like its a 300 level class and expect you to be an expert on everything.

Doesn't seem like he cares. Shows up 5-30 minutes late EVERY single lecture and sometimes he doesn't even show up. With that said, he's a pretty good teacher and easy to follow. You only get graded on 3 exams so make sure to study. Also don't follow for his trick of making it seem like you have to purchase his book that he wrote. you don't.

A truly talented teacher, his lectures are interesting and he makes sure to draw in the students. He knows the answer to any question you could possibly ask and he records the lectures and puts them on blackboard. He is truly a talented teacher.

My favorite class in college so far. He was a great and very interesting teacher. His exams were very easy if you just paid attention in class. Also, just skim the text of the books for each exam so that you can come up with some examples to put in your essay. Such an easy A.
history of civil rights- incessant rambler, at least 5 minutes late everyday, but a good teacher. offers perspectives backed up with primary sources. easy grader.

Always late by at least 15 min. Goes on historical tangents (including his own opinion of course) He's not clear at all on what he expects you to learn for the exams. There is only 2 essay exams and a final. So there is no room for mistakes on the first exam (never expect higher than B)The exams were 2 prompts and a some vocab.

Just come to class everyday so you don't have to read the assignments, except for the novels he gives out. For the exams I usually was left with 1-2 blank pages left and i got 90% on them. For the final I was writing on the back cover to add more in.

A good prof, knows his stuff.  Very, very liberal, however if you challenge him (respectfully) he usually backs down.    Class is extremely lecture oriented, with 3 books to read (one his own).  Not an easy A if you don't come to class, but definitely an easy B.  If you have a morning class he is usually late.  Otherwise a fair teacher.

Amazing professor! Loves history, so he makes the lectures really interesting. If you go to class, you don't have to read the textbook. He does assign novels, but they're pretty interesting and on the exams.
Never arrives on time. easy grader, no need to read the textbook for the exams. You should read the other books becuase they are on the exams.

Never arrives on time, but definitely crams as much info into every lecture as he can. Take notes. You'll need them. Read the books that aren't the text. They are on the exams. Not an easy A, but a very attainable B.

I agree with the comment below. Smead was probably a great professor once, but now he's running off fumes. He teaches at College Park too, so maybe the Terp kids get his best. He requires one research paper, easy right? Watch out, you MUST not disagree with lecture arguments in your paper. If he says down is up, you better write it that way.

He is coasting, it's obvious that he is bored with teaching. Easy class to do okay in - not many assignments, but hard to get an A in due to his apathetic attitude which results in lame feedback. Likes to write "not germain" when grading essays. Good lectures - was probably a great professor once...
AMAZING PROFESSOR!! Take when possible especially for GFR classes... goes off on interesting historical tangents. 3 tests, 1 paper
No Comments
No Comments
No Comments
Tests are pretty simple but there are no assignments otherwise.  Hes cool.
AWESOME lecturer! He really knows his history!  Take every class you can take of his!  He might not be PC all the time but he's real funny and interesting.
Smead is THE MAN!
Good class.  Learned a lot.  I'm not a lecture kind of guy myself, but I loved his lectures.  If you hate novels, this isn't the class for you, but it's a damn good class.
During the lectures he can get a little off topic and at times, glosses over the material in a not-so-detailed way.  Makes the class feel comfortable.

makes history  come alive  in lectures, easy, little out of class work.  Nice person and highly reccommended, however, quite anti-Bush/anti-Iraq war, (but then again - most History Profs are leftists)

cool ass teacher, keeps it relavant to current times, makes it entertaining, I'm not one for lectures, but his are really good, makes you totally unaware of the time, definately take Smead if you are taking history
Funny guy.  Tests a lil **** b/c 40% of all tests based on a 1 of 3 novels.
Cool teacher....adds humor to his class...easy going
Awesome class! Super easy!
good prof, talks about stuff you won't hear anywhere else

I took this course at the suggestion of a professor I had (turns out they're friends) at the idea that "it's the winter semester so it's a lot less heavy". This was easily one of the most loaded-with-busy-work classes I have ever taken. I get that it was a winter semester, but if that was "less" I don't want to see a normal semester.

The class is pretty easy as long as you participate and do the work. She can be difficult. For someone who teaches "Intercultural Communication" she sort of sucks at it? If any issues were affecting your ability to do the homework, she always made sure you knew it was YOUR fault. It was a weird tic. If it was accidental that's not a great look.

Dr. Golubeva is amazing. I just took MLL305 over the winter and she is very understanding and accessible through email if you need some sort of help. Easy A, just show up and do the work. Her classes are very insightful and will definitely be useful in day to day experiences.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: One of the best professors are UMBC. She answers to her emails fast & always willing to help. The class itself is super flexible. If you want a flexible, easy class, then take MLL 305 with her!

Had her spring 2020 semester (half in person, half crazy transition to online). She recently went up for review for promotion so figured I'd chime in here. Easiest A I had in college and the class was fun. She had a good sense of humor and is very caring so long as you show up and give a little effort.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Group projects--Hilarious

reviews.comment: SO EASY She doesn't care about grading but more the learning experience. Be nice and participate or at least look like you're listening. Easy, easy, easy A. Good culture general ed. requirement class. Attendance is important though because it's a bulk of your grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--Caring

reviews.comment: took online. a full blown research paper is a lot to get done in 4 weeks, but I made it. Take in the summer if you don't plan on going into a research heavy field, instead of the normal 15 week course
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --So many papers--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: My favorite professor! You can tell he loves what he teaches, and he's always willing to help.

if you need to take POLI409, do yourself a favor and take it with Professor Anson. He is incredibly understanding and will make time to help you no matter how far behind you are. He is extremely flexible and genuinely wants you to learn (even if it's at your own pace). I would take this class again because of how great he was. Choose Anson!!!

Professor Anson is surely the best professor in the POLI Department. He is an engaging lecturer and incorporates humor into all of his classes. He also is really flexible in answering questions via email and office hours, and gives grace if you need some extra time to turn in assignments.

Absolutely loved professor Anson's class! I was a bit worried walking into a political science class but he made everything really interesting and clear. The textbook helps significantly with the writing assignments and final exam, so keep up with them! He is a very great and caring professor.

Dr. Anson's lectures are engaging and informational, and I would love to have him again. His lecturing style can be tricky to grasp at first, but the class is a breeze once you get it. There are only a few assignments; the book is a great resource but challenging to take notes from. I suggest skimming it and writing down important facts.

Prof Anson is a great professor! He's very nice and enthusiastic about the course. His lectures are pretty interesting and interactive. There's 2 writing assignments, weekly course journals, a written (inperson) midterm and at-home written final. He takes attendance so make sure to come to class. Overall the class isn't too hard just apply effort.
He's great!

Dr. Anson is a great prof! If you are able to take a class with him please do! He is easily accessible via email and responds quickly. The classes are interesting and the coursework itself isn't difficult either. Just make sure to keep up on the readings, and pay attention in class and you'll be good to go

I've taken 3 classes with Dr. Anson and I've had a wonderful experience in all of them. He is easy to reach and is always willing and able to help out his students. The assignments provide you with skills that are applicable to other classes and the workplace. Highly recommend taking his POLI 301 class as well.

Genuinely one of the best profs at UMBC. He's super fun, caring, and makes a boring class as interesting as possible. He gives great feedback and is always willing to work with you or help in any way possible. Workload is relatively light, the pre-recorded lectures are long and kinda dense but if you watch them all & take good notes it's an easy A.
10/10 would recommend! Easily one of the greatest professors at UMBC.

One of the best professors at UMBC. Engaging and interesting lectures, exams are fair and are easy as long as you pay attention in class. Gives great feedback and is generally a super fun professor. Is also very willing to work with you if you are having personal issues and cant focus on school.

Professor Anson was great. For POLI 100 online, the hardest thing we had to do was 2 writing assignments throughout the semester, which we are given a couple weeks prior to work on. Lectures were engaging, and he was very friendly and joked with students a lot. Great experience

Dr. Anson was probably my favorite professor thus far in my poli sci major at UMBC. Gives thoughtful feedback on papers, and has reasonable/lenient expectations of students. I walked out of this class feeling so much more knowledgable and he really made me feel like what I was doing was special. Dr. Anson, if you're reading this, thank you!

I took this class not knowing very much about political science. I assumed the class would be quite dull but was surprised to find-out that he was able to make the class surpringly fun! He is very easy to talk to and will give you extra help outside of the classroom if you ask.

Take Anson!! Hands down the best professor I've had at UMBC. He's super passionate about what he teaches and is always available for questions and concerns outside of class. He puts a ton of effort into class and grades fairly - no one is ever surprised by their grade. I got a lot out of POLI301, and that had a lot to do with Anson.

Dr. Anson is a great professor for introductory Political Science. I sadly realized that Poli Sci is not for me after taking the class but he was very enjoyable for such dull material. He makes the dull material lectures worth sitting through as he adds humor and such to it. I would recommend. Though I would recommend studying the theories a bit.

Great professor. He's very knowledgeable about all the subjects he teaches and it shows. He's very good at explaining things and always makes you feel welcome to participate in class. You had to work to do well in the class, but overall it wasn't too bad because he made it interesting.

Seriously one of my favorite professors. The class is lecture based but he makes it so engaging and interesting. He also genuinely cares about his students and wants them to succeed and that's very evident with all of the support and resources he offers. So nice, wish I could take him again :/
Awesome prof

Anson goes way out of his way to help you if you need it. There's extra credit and review sessions for exams, which is good because exams are a big part of the grade. Exams are IDs and essays, but for each exam there is a word bank so you don't have to know everything.

Proff. Anson is a very sweet caring person, however he is very disorganized in his teaching jumps around a lot. PowerPoints don't really have much information nor make sense. When you ask questions, he doesn't necessarily answer the questions he just comments on it. Although this class is an easy A, I don't feel like I learned much and wasted time
reviews.rating_tags: ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--Caring

reviews.comment: Great lectures and class discussions. He is one of the few professors that I honestly don't want to skip class for
Anson is one of the best POLI professors at UMBC. His courses may be semi-reading and lecture heavy but he is so understanding and really respects his students.

Anson is obviously really passionate about what he teaches. It is really refreshing to see someone so clearly excited about their own field of work. He is not a harsh grader by any means, but works hard to make sure students are engaged.

By far the best professor I've had. Poli-301 is an extremely challenging class, but Dr. Anson makes it manageable. Don't expect to slide by because he doesn't hand out good grades unless you've earned it. It takes hard work to succeed in poli-301, no matter who is teaching the class, but Dr. Anson really makes it a rewarding experience.

One of my favorite professors on campus! He's always there to help and gives great video feedback on papers with very specific corrections and ways to improve. He's very enthusiastic and I would definitely take him again

Great class. There were three exams with some short writing assignments, and participation which mostly comes from attendance. Some of the things we did in class were a lot of fun. The study guides are really helpful for exams. And oh by the way GO TO THE REVIEW SESSIONS.

Professor Anson was a great professor. The class was straightforward and consisted of 3 sections: Institutions, Citizens, and Public Opinion. There were 7 grades totaling 1000 pts: 3 reflective writing assignments (2 pgs each) (50 pts each), 2 midterms (200&250 points), 1 cumulative final (300 points), and participation (100 pts.) Anson was helpful

Great Professor, explains all topics well. He has reviews sessions before the exam. His exams are not normal multiple choice, you define words he's gone over and write a paragraph. As long as you read, study his review guide, and go to the review sessions you will do great. The reviews sessions really helped me!

The class consists of short papers and blue book exams which he gives you a study guide for. If you keep up with the material and come to class it's pretty easy. Nice guy who tries hard to be unbiased.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Great class

This class is heavy on academic reading - about 3 different journal articles a week and 3 different news articles for a total of 60-80 pages of reading a week. You don't need to read to discuss but you'll need it for exams so you may as well keep on pace. Most of the grade is based on a full length paper which he walks you through. And he's hoooot!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: I expected an intro course in poly sci to be really boring but prof Anson made it really interesting and made me actually look forward to coming to class. Young guy with a lot of energy/def. a lot of caffeine. Tests were pretty straight forward and no major curveballs or pop quiz.
Very nice professor who is clearly interested in what he is teaching. I would defintely recommend him for a course introducing political science.

Super nice guy, loves cats. You can tell he is really into what he teaches, and it definitely comes through in his lectures. The class itself isn't very hard, but be prepared to read a lot, participate and write some pretty long papers.

Wasn't sure what my grade would be until the very end of the semester because it took two months to fix a grade that I was told would be fixed. Not good with Blackboard and not great at answering emails either. Such a lack of communication and didn't hold up his end of the work. Stressful.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--So many papers--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Lectures were very difficult to take notes on. Easy to get a good grade, if he bothers to grade your paper. He lost my papers 3 different times. Inconsistent places to turn in the papers. Hard to find assignment sheets. I don't think he really understands how to use blackboard, which is a problem since that's where assignments are supposed to be
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--So many papers--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Eshel was amazing. He truly cares about his students succeeding in class and gives good and timely feedback. Attendance is mandatory but he makes his classes very enjoyable. He is an easy grader but do stay up to date with class readings.

Dr. Eshel is one of the loveliest professors I've ever had. He's from Israel himself, and provides a lot of interesting insights into Jewish history. He isn't so much concerned with grades as he is about students being interested in the topics. The tests were open notes, and he took us to The Holocaust Museum. All around a wonderful prof and class.

Very contradictory and unclear on her rules and will go back and change them as she pleases, especially during "memory games." She is often condescending & doesn't know what she is talking about. Prepare to memorize EVERYTHING no matter how much she says she wants you to just remember the concepts and not the dates. Once came in with Covid.

She makes art tedious.
She asks for creative exercise, then uses criteria that she forgets to explain to judge pieces.
She ignores artistic intent in her evaluation.
I don't doubt her skill, but she is not effective as a teacher.

At least give us a creatively open final project to work with!

Be ready to spend money on this course. She will ask you to buy things that are not necessary I ended up spending $100+ on this 4-week class . She once gave me critique on a project for things that we never discussed in class. Attendance is mandatory and participation too. She only sees what she wants to see and that sucks since art is subjective.

She is very strict about attendance and how long you stay. If it's a studio day and I leave 20 minutes early because I am all done with my work, she takes points off. I guess she wants us to sit around and look productive until she says we can leave. Be ready to spend weekends and overnight silk screening. Boring long lectures. But fun projects.

everyone who is saying here that she is tuff they lying she is the most sweetest person she is so nice she is my advisor too and i love taking class with her she never make you feel dumb and will answer you until you feel comfortable about the work
I heard so many bad comments about her but I honestly love her shes so nice and always ready to help i am about to take another class with her and I am so excited about it

Be warned: she will ask you to buy more things than the course fee includes. Have some money saved up in prep for this. In some cases she needs specific products, so make sure you buy the right thing the first time. Some of the books she asks you to buy are available for free online, so check first before you buy.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: What a mistake I did by taking this class as an elective. If you are not a printmaking major and do not have to take this class with this professor. Do yourself a big favor and take something else. Tests are hard. Exam 1 curved 18 points, exam 2 curved 20 points. After the final exam, she took us back to class to give us another lecture.

Professor Chan is a very nice, enthusiastic person. You will also be doing so much work, and she absolutely expects that you will get an A if you put all of your effort into achieving one. As previously stated, she's very nice, but she really does teach as if she's the only class you're taking.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Caring

reviews.comment: Irene Chan is a very nice person and means well. She is very upbeat. However, her grading and expectations are drastic and unreasonable. Most of her classes consist of her rambling endlessly, resulting in decreased amount of time and understanding to complete the work. Expect to do several hours of work outside of class to get an A or B.
DO NOT TAKE! I HAD TO DROP OUT 2 WEEKS BEFORE THE SEMESTER WAS OVER.

Art 370 Silkscreen. She takes way too long to get through her lectures. She was grading old projects and returning them while we were working on the final project. She demands way to much on the final project / amount of work wise. We have other classes. Does not do any mid project followups to see if you are following her guidelines to the tee.

At times felt like she tried to hard to find negatives about an assignment during critique.  Some lectures lasted all class when only a few examples would have sufficed.  Very particular craftsmanship wise, ie if it's an 18 of an inch off, redo it all.  Rather than re-wording explanations, she would just repeat them as if it would help.

terrible at teaching the book arts class; unclear directions, confusing and grading is unclear, constantly criticizes work without giving a clear explanation on how to improve it, demands a lot and teaches as if you only have her class, if  you can avoid taking her class - do so!

She was my advisor, as I was a Print Media major. Strict and demanding, but your work and drive improves because of it. She wants you to surpass your own expectations and push yourself. Don't take her classes if you're lazy and want an easy grade. She praises where it's due. Independent Study with her was great: good at guiding the student.
Great teacher. Very knowledgeable of print making and shows alot of examples. Shes very picky on craftsmanship however. Had her for other classes & will keep retaking her classes

I had Irene for three classes while I was at UMBC. I didn't like them at first, but I realize now that's because I was just lazy. She's looking for more than just the bare minimum in your work, so don't be surprised when she doesn't praise something you clearly didn't put any effort into.
Gist of the class and her as a professor is bad. Things are to look as she visions them and not the artist producing them. Very strict, and unnecessarily demanding.

ONE OF THE WORST PROFESSORS EVER. Had a bad vibe from her since the beginning. Very picky and demanding. Her projects are very time consuming and there is one due every two weeks! Definition of a female dog...wait can I even say this on here? Anyway if you're not up to par with her she'll make sure you know. Do not recommend at ALL.
Projects are time consuming! Don't turn in late projects. Tricky quiz questions. Class attendance is mandatory. She's a nice person tho.

Good teacher with a fun personality. Very difficult art problems to solve for projects compared to what I heard the other class was doing. Have to read one very short book and do short exersizes in a book. The reading and book work is very easy. Projects are very time consuming if you let them be.

I hate drawing class. But of course it's a core course... but it's pretty boring, tedious, and easy.. If you don't get A's, something's wrong with you. Cnage majors. She's pretty QUIRKY/weird but she's really nice & laughs a lot =) Take attendance.. critiques are a bit too laid back? Relaxed class & atmosphere
Very nice, but she's picky about your work.

I think Prof Erill is one of the better professors at UMBC. He really does know his stuff and is very understanding if a topic needs to be explained in more detail to the class. He is also very helpful outside of class by having a voicethread for each assignment where you can post questions. Extra credit is given at the end, which is a plus.
Explains things quickly, but will go over in depth if you are confused. Really wants everyone to understand. Will ask in depth questions,  not trick you, as a learning tool. Very friendly and warm.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: This course is really interesting, especially with the guest lecturers toward the end of the semester. He posts videos of the slides with audio attached, which is really convenient for reviewing before an exam. Wording on homework and exams can be confusing at times. Up to 5% in extra credit opportunities.

This guy is almost too smart for his own good. He frequently glazes over or completely skips things because he doesn't realize they need to be explained. If you get confused though he'll happily stop the whole class and explain it in detail until he's sure you understand. Funny and approachable, but still a challenging class.

I am a CS sophomore and I could not recommend this course more to CS majors. Taking it after 341 (Data Structures) will give you a more proper appreciation for the algorithms covered in this class. The course is a great introduction to applied CS problems & algorithms that I confidently think will help in higher level CS courses. As for coursework-

This class is misleadingly hard. Be prepared to spend hours on homework and lab assignments. The material is interesting at times, but he could explain it better I think. He definitely does in person after class. Just not so much in lecture. I didn't spend the time I should have in this class. Don't make the same mistake.

You come and sit for lecture, and it seems interesting. Then you get the exam, and it has nothing to do with the stuff you talked about. There's so much vague fluff in this course, and no concrete science, that anticipating how to study for an exam is nigh upon impossible. Approach with caution.

Very fun lecturer given it's a science course. Gives out potato chips for answering hard questions. Great sense of humor. Obviously knows his stuff. The course was a more BIO and less CS toward the end, making it tougher for us CS majors. Very difficult tests, so study hard! Oh, and don't bother going to the TA; he does the bare minimum to help.

Dresses like a teenager. Easy to understand despite his accent. There were aspects of the computational techniques covered that he  failed to explain because they were obvious to him. I had no trouble as a CS major, but many of the BIO majors were left scratching their heads. No textbook. Attendance is graded.
The great professor explained everything well. Had weekly zoom meeting for like 3 hours and had to listen and summarize a podcast once a week. Had 3 exams which were from the PowerPoint.
Germaine is a cool professor, like she's actually cool. Lectures are just class discussions, the tests are pretty easy. This class is the bomb . com. Take 425 with her you won't regret it!
Great teacher! Just be involved and ask questions if you are uncertain of any work and you will be fine

Germaine Irwin loves IT. She loves new ideas and practices associated. She gives good feedback, and as long as you are engaged and CW ontime she typically sympathizes. She likes to see improvement and handles issues by policy. The class is a little undef. which makes papers hard, and CM is out of order. This is no fault the teacher. I had fun!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Teacher is very lazy! A nice person but a horrible teacher.  Signed up late for the class and was the only instructor available.  I found out why.  Teaching skills needs a lot of work.  I still passed with flying colors.  However would have been better off teaching myself.

HORRIBLE instructor.  When giving lectures the information is unclear.  She doesn't respond to emails in a timely fashion.  Not a good instructor, I learned absolutely nothing and wouldn't recommend this class to anyone.  You're better off teaching yourself because she's no help.  Don't waste your time with this instructor.

Professor Irwin is awesome. She does assign readings but rarely do you have to actually read them.  The material from the exams are on her slide shows. There are four major grades: two group projects and two exams. She does give small assignments in class but they aren't worth much. She knows who comes to class and will give you the BoD if you do!

Great professor! Exams are easy and straight from the material covered in class. 2 projects were fun and not at all daunting. Great lecturer, keeps you engaged and uses tons of great real world examples. Would definitely take another class with her!

She is a confused person.  It says on the syllabus there is not homework or assignments and guess what, there are.  I am not sure how did she grade our assignments and HW.  There are two things I don't like in this class, her grading policy and how she grade them.

Mrs. Irwin spoke more often of her son than she did of the textbook readings. She didn't really care if you skipped class. You learn more from doing the textbook assignments and the end-of-semester project. The material is really interesting and useful for the IS web certificate. Class usually ended 1.5+ hours early, which was nice.

HORRIBLE PROFESSOR! you teach yourself from the textbook, she does not answer your emails, cancels class all the time. The tests and lectures are IRRELEVANT to what you are teaching yourself from the textbook.  Minus well save your money and take another professor who actually teaches.
Cool professor, talks about GPT and AI way too much for how little it comes up in the curriculum.  TA was also really good and was able to do some lectures.

Dr. Schumacher spent very little time actually discussing in class lectures the things that would be on the homework and exams. Instead he spent an exorbitant amount of time talking about and playing around with ChatGPT in ways that were irrelevant to class content. Study guides were not indicative of what would be on the exam. Not engaging.

Highly recommend this professor!! The textbook is important for assignments, but it isn't a bad read! I found it interesting. He gives feedback on every assignment, even small ones. I thought his grading was a little loose, and sometimes I felt I got a higher grade than I deserved. If you're thinking about this class, take it!
John was one of the first professors I had at UMBC after transferring and he was so kind and honestly made me love UMBC he truly cares
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: He was an awesome professor both before and after COVID-19 sent us all home for the semester. He was understanding the entire time and was still always available although we had to switch to an online format. The class is really interesting and gave me a new appreciation for Sociology and its different aspects.

I took this class online during the summer session. I found this class interesting because it is related to medicine. I am a mathematics major and this class made me to add a minor in Sociology to fulfill my upper lever credits. 5 discussion posts, 4 homeworks, 3 to 4 single spaced research paper and 2 exams.

Very nice and understanding professor but he's a little bit of a mess. his in-class lectures are scattered and nonspecific, and he doesn't write anything down. He assigns a chapter a week but the material is so dense. The exams are hard with no study guide, he says to just memorize everything you can and they're worth a LOT of points! :(
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: SOCY 300 was a tad bit boring, but prof. Schumacher does try and live things up with his jokes. His exams are pretty tough, but ATTENDING review sessions is VERY helpful. He also give study guides so doing them will help. Its not a hard class but it also isn't easy, just take plenty of notes, do study guides and review sessions and u should b fine
GREAT TEACHER HE WAS AWESOME

Best teacher for SOCY 300! He was simply awesome. Really tried to make an 8:30am class as fun as possible. He really engages with his students and works with them. He is always asking if things need to be clarified. His HW's, Quizzes and Labs are easy. Pretty much anything that he goes over in class, is on the quiz. Take!!!

Nice and he really tries to engage his students in discussion. He has a lot of HW, labs, and quizzes but pay attention in class and you will get 100% on everything. The exams are a bit harder, but if you read the chapters you will be fine. Easy and fast grader not too particular. Class is fun considering it's  research methods (not a fun topic).

I was initially intimidated when at the first class after receiving the syllabus.  Stuck with the class because I needed it, glad I did!   He's very caring & helpful.   Just keep up with the readings and you'll do fine.  The research paper is a bit of a drag, but he gives plenty of time & guidance to check it over.  Great professor.

Great Professor. Very kind and helpful. Exams are decent. YOu have to study lecture notes, read the textbook, and all the handouts on blackboard. Exam consists of multiple choice and essays. Quizzes are easy. 10 true/false questions based on weekly readings from the textbook. One group presentation at the end of the semester. One 8-10 page essay.

I took SOCY 351, 411 & 431 from Dr. S. because I appreciate his knowledge, style and genuine interest in student learning.  He'll make you work for it, but you'll come out learning immense amounts in the end.  Multimedia and blackboard use only add to the total positive experiences in his class.

His lectures are a bit boring, but that again depends on whether you like the subject matter. Nice guy, a bit dry at times, but definitely a fair teacher.  Lots of work, but I learned a lot and it was a fair class.
Did minimal work and got an A. Very easy class. Quizzes are extremely easy.  Exams cover major topics discussed.

Boring, boring, boring, but not difficult.  Quizzes every day on the reading are straight foward, assuming you read.  Similarly, tests are fair but you will have to study to do well.  There are essays involved in the tests, but usually you have to pick one from a couple choices.  He's very approachable, helpful, and friendly.

Very approachable, makes class interesting.  Fan of videos & movies.  Readings are relevant and easy to read.  He encourages interaction b/w students and material.  Semester-long paper on topic of your choice.

Dr. S. makes an interesting class out of a potentially boring subject.  He uses blackboard well, making it easy to keep up if you miss a class.  Weekly 10 question quizzes force you to keep up on readings.

Boring class, boring readings, but he goes over them in class so quiz's and exams arent bad. One 8-10pg paper, material is mostely common sense and analytical(bull****ting is a must)he is kind of funny in a dorky sort of way.

If there's another prof available avoid him! quizzes were oddly specific to a bullet point on his slides or a comment he made and relied almost entirely on the lecture so if you miss smtg good luck. The exams were a little better if you read the textbook, a lot of the questions were taken directly from there. hes somewhat approachable but snarky
If you're thinking of taking his class, stop thinking.
start praying to a God because its bad

His slides were unorganized and don't make sense without reading the textbook. If you take this class, read the chapter before lectures to make sense of his slides for the most part.

Exam and weekly quizzes has random questions from lecture slides, super random. Lectures basically make no sense, unorganized and scattered. Most of the learning will come from the textbook chapters if you put in the time to read all of it you'll be fine. Hard to get an A.

Passionate professor butnclass is graded by a very little amount of grades (online weekly quizzes and exams). Questions in the weekly quiz are often irrelevant to the concepts needed to understand in biology.

Class graded on ONLY weekly quizzes and exams. No opportunity for extra credit. His lectures are EXTREMELY fast, if you are a slower learner, good luck. reviews.comment: DO NOT take this class. ESPECIALLY if you're an allied health major. He is an absolutely horrible professor and will have you change your whole entire trajectory for your future career path. His weekly quizzes have nothing to do with his lectures, and his exams have nothing to do with the text book or lectures. He comes off as very snobby too.

I had Dr Guzman for biol303 which I barely passed and 303L which I easily passed. His questions are specific and there's a lot of information but he will help you if you ask. He's big on respect, participation and speaking up if you need help. He's very no nonsense but I learned more in 6 weeks than I did in 4 years at umbc.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Very disrespectful, cannot keep his cool during lab. Expectations are not made clear for each assignment. Every quiz, report, and homework question is highly specific with no regard for broad or overarching concepts. Class is essentially an eye-spy book, but in quiz format. Honestly embodies everything that makes a bad professor.

Does not communicate through email. Quizzes are okay, but weirdly specific. Verbose lectures during lab. We spent an hour going over how to use a microscope. If I put in the (Required) time outside of class prepping for a lab, it should pay off. This is the case with every other lab I've taken in the bio sequence, including organic 1 & 2.
One of those classes that will give you a headache but you always gain something out of it

This prof is straight-up terrible. His lectures are a complete mess,no structure, no clarity, just pure confusion. I learned nothing, and honestly, I wouldn't wish this class on my worst enemy. If you care about passing, avoid him at all costs. pick literally anyone else if you wanna succeed, waste of time and money.

FOR BIOL 470- Dr. Guzman is a very caring and sincere professor. He is very passionate in teaching and lectures in class while incorporating class discussions. You will do well in the course if you participate and take notes after each lecture. Pay attention to small details and make flashcards throughout for active recall!

For BIOL 470- Very unclear about expectations around exams/quizzes. Weekly proctored one-chance quizzes tended to nitpick specifics about anything on either of his two packed 35+ slide presentations he uploads AFTER the related lecture. Condescending attitude around questions.  "Study guides" for exams were too broad to reflect the questions asked.

This was my second attempt after the summer with Feeser. Cell bio is very hard and requires a lot of reading and memorization. I didn't fid Guzman to be mean but he didn't seem approachable. He also moved too quickly for my pace. I would suggest taking cell bio at a community college. I barely scraped by with a C and that's after extra credit.

reviews.comment: Not a good professor. Don't take any lecture-based course with him. Terrible experience.

Guzman's lectures were packed with an insane amount of information. There were tons of misspellings and grammar errors making it hard to understand. He had a very negative attitude and was not accessible outside of class (ignored all my emails). Exams focused on the most hyper acute details from lecture. Worst professor I've had, Avoid at all costs

Javier teaching was disorganized and unclear, making the material hard to follow. He struggled to explain concepts effectively, His lack of engagement and dismissive responses to questions frustrated the class. Deadlines and grading felt inconsistent, adding to the stress the experience was poor, and I wouldn't recommend taking a class with him.

I would rather have taken the orgo sequence again than deal with this man. His attitude, tone, and demeanor are awful. Avoid him at all costs. After completing the entire Biology sequence, I can confidently say he is the worst professor. He acts like he's being forced to do this. Dr. Legates should have taught this class alone.

He belittles his students for getting bad scores w/o realizing its bc the qsns on exams ARE SO SPECIFIC. Not only are they difficult but they're UNFAIR! The questions differ for everybody; they're 100% randomized with some people getting easier questions than others, avoid him for the sake of your well-being!

Guzman talks really fast and rambles. This makes lecture useless. He doesn't give you a heads up on what the exam is going to be like at all. HW is helpful for conceptualization - but it's not tested. Exams are like a game of memorizing every vocabulary on the slides - 0 comprehension questions.

You got back what you put into this course. Lab report grading was fair, but I can't say the same for pre- or post-lab quizzes. There were always questions not covered in the material or lecture, with no way to study for them. 39% of your final grade was determined on the last day of class. Professor NEVER responded to emails in a timely manner.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Gives good feedback--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Really enjoyed taking this class, the lectures are more intensive than other courses I've had at UMBC simply due to the amount of material that is covered, but Dr. Guzman does a great job breaking down concepts and is very receptive to any questions. Immunology was definitely one of my favorite bio courses I took at UMBC, highly recommend!

reviews.comment: honestly guys i recommend reading your textbooks before class, taking good notes , and really being attentive in class because alot of things in your exams and quizzes are based on things he says in lecture. Also go to office hours , that really helps to clarify things, i promise you can succeed in this class despite what others may say.

Super harsh grading and 60% of your grade is based on tests, quizzes, and the final. Extremely detailed questions like "at minute 1 of link 3, what did this person say" specific. Extremely stressful but learned a lot
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Very kind person. Passionate about immunology and microbiology. It's a 2 credit course with the work of a 4 credit course. Some quizzes had questions made to trip you up. Hard to reach via email. Clear instructions and expectations. Overall, it's a hard class but it's a good class, & I enjoy what I learned. Great TA & great feedback on lab reports.

Professor Guzman is rough im ngl. He seems like a nice enough guy (even with the ego), but overall I can see why people have problems with him. He did not give a clear designated time for office hours if people needed them, was hard to reach via Email and moved through the lecture very fast. Grading feedback was also nonexistent, so beware of that.

The amount of prepatory work isn't parallel for a 2-credit course. He'll assign multiple readings & videos prior to lab and it's too much. On top of that, his directions are SO unclear and it's ridiculous the way he phrases quiz questions. Too confusing and designed to be incorrect. I agree with him having an ego/power trip. Not recommended.

He moves way too fast during lectures so you're struggling to keep up then says you don't need to write everything. The weekly quizzes are very specific so you DO need to write it all down yet. He has also put students on the spot before for no reason other than a power trip. One student was smiling and he stopped the lecture to question why.

For BIOL470: He's passionate no doubt. But he really expected students in a 6 WEEK COURSE to do the amount of a graduate level PROGRAM. He has a massive power trip, gets irritated when no one knows the answer to incredibly advanced topics. Harsh grader, gives way too much work, will condescendingly answer your questions with more questions. AVOID.

Easily the worst lab I've taken in UMBC. We're expected to read through several pages of instructions, watch multiple videos, watch a lecture, take notes on all of those, take a pre lab quiz that asks specific questions to all of that, AND take a closed note post quiz with questions that are based off the former things and requires a camera. AVOID!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He shows extreme passive-aggressiveness that makes asking questions or help during labs very difficult. You should not have to study irrelevant and specific details for a quiz of a lab that you already successfully completed.

reviews.comment: The quizzes and exams are all multiple choice but, the questions are very detailed oriented. He tends to be extra for no reason his only grades for his lecture are exams and end of chapter quizzes.

I have no idea why his rating is so low. Go to his lectures and follow along, and you will be great. Re-read the powerpoints and study his powerpoints, and you will pass the tests with no problem. Reading the chapters gives an extra advantage but just know the ppts, and you will pass easily. I would take his class again in a heartbeat.

I personally do not think Dr.Guzman was as bad as his ratings sad. This class made me struggle a whole lot. Be sure to get the textbook and read ahead. His lectures are fast and I highly recommend writing out the notes.
