We learned terms and concepts, but it was hard to apply them (no applicable hw). Next classes depend on 313 building C knowledge, which Kidd didn't.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The professor tends to ramble in the lecture and goes on tangents about unrelated things so you don't actually learn anything. The homeworks and coding assignments have very unclear requirements and instructions. He also does not seem to have a rubric when it comes to grading so the grading was pretty inconsistent among students.

Do not take this professor if you want to learn anything. Doesn't teach the curriculum at all. You will not learn anything in this course. Lectures are useless and doesn't stay on topic or explain anything at all. If you actually want to learn assembly or C then take another prof. I am ashamed I spent money to take this course to learn nothing

Worst professor I've had at UMBC. He reads slides directly, loses his train of thought, gets lost in his own explanations and makes assignments with very unclear descriptions. In addition, he is impossible to get in touch promptly. We even had assignments due during finals week, and he does not teach you anything about actually coding assembly.

Professor doesn't stay on topic during lectures and doesn't teach what is actually on the homework and exams. Homework assignments have unclear instructions, yet the professor is a tough grader. Was very unhelpful, would often ignore emails asking for clarification on homework assignments. Just stay away from this guy.

This Professor is horrible at teaching he spends way more than half the class Yapping and clearly did not know what class he was teaching at the beginning of the semester. the professor teaches outside the curriculum and made no effort to teach us the C language or ASM but however expects us to know how to do it on Homeworks and Exams.

Dr. Ka is one of the nicest people I've met in my life. The material itself is somewhat difficult for all the Wolof courses, but he isn't a tough grader and is accommodating. There are a couple of presentations, homework is given somewhat often but is not difficult, and there are a few exams and speaking exams.

He's super nice and funny, but we almost never finished the content within the class period because he talked a lot and almost always showed up late to class. He also didn't put in a single grade until WEEKS into the semester. This class was not real. Pretty easy though, if you independently reinforce what you were trying to learn in class.

if you don't come to class, you're cooked. doesn't tell you when homework is due unless you come to class, gives random quizzes not outlined in the syllabus. if he yaps more abt a topic and pushes it to the next lecture, will push out the due dates for homework, but won't tell you unless you came to class that day (NEVER USES BLACKBOARD/EMAIL).

great prof! for this class, there were two group projects and he graded them easy since they were just summaries of a chapter in the book. the final paper wasnt bad either as it was based on a topic u chose. the only complaint i hav is that the tests werent in the og syllabus and he randomly announced them a week before (they were easy tho).
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Fairly easy A (2 presentations, 3 tests, one ~10pg paper), but don't expect to learn a lot. Ka makes students do about half of the lecturing, and even if students don't know what they're talking about, he won't correct them. He also seems to hate technology; nothing is ever in Blackboard. Says attendance is mandatory but doesn't grade it.
reviews.rating_tags: Caring--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I took this class online, but Professor Ka is the nicest professor I've ever had. You can tell he loves teaching Wolof. Although this class was an easy A I would say make sure you attend class. You miss one class and you've missed a WHOLE lot of material.
He is a tough grader. Using the study guide to prepare for the exam is useless.

Nicks legit a legend. He offers 2 buy coffee ' & has really insightful things 2 say bout the field as hes been in - videos hames, music, ads - u name it, hes done it! He has a unique way of explain concepts & is very theatrical w his movements-he'll dance around the classroom - its engaging, Plus, he sounds like Ryan Reynold! :)

Discussions were student-driven and Dr. Ka facilitated discussions, offering feedback and keeping the discussion on track. At first, I was dreading the two group presentations required, but the way they were assigned allowed students to be put into groups of people with shared interests and I thoroughly enjoyed preparing both presentations.
Great Professor!!! Take him!! There are group projects and presentations but overall the class was really interesting. Make sure you study for the tests!! Grades easy on the presentations.

Dr. Ka is a really great professor. He is very friendly and outgoing, very approachable. His class requires you to do group presentations and the final project is a 10-page paper, but it is not really that difficult. He is worth it!
This class was mostly led by students but his feedback is honest and knowledgeable. Seemed fair.

Ka loves the subject, and makes it easy for non-majors. This class is treated as a true "intro" to applied linguistics, but topics are interesting. He's sweet and funny, and genuinely caring. Slight senegalese accent, but not hard to understand. Talk to him 1-1, you'll have better conversations and he appreciates it. Great person overall.

I had Dr. Ka for LING 290, FREN 302, and FREN 315, and did a research assistantship with him for his Wolof Project. He is Senegalese, but knows a lot about the rest of the world as well. He is very intelligent and very helpful. There are times when he can be a bit dry when lecturing, but I still really enjoyed learning from him.

I decided to take Dr. Ka's class based on the other reviews about him on this website.  I was in the 6-week summer version of MLL-190 and really enjoyed the course.  Dr. Ka covered a lot of material during our class, but he made sure that important points were thoroughly explained before moving on to the next item.  He is a great instructor!

Two short powerpoint presentations based on textbook#1, two quizzes, two one-page homework assignments from textbook#2, final 10 page project double-spaced, all graded very magnanimously. Excellent professor with a genuine care for his students. Attendance sheet randomly distributed. Mild Kenyan accent. A very easy A with no linguistic interest.
OMG I LOVE DR. KA!!! All he wants is for his students to get what he's teaching and do well in class. He cares so much..he believes that all his students have the potential to do well....he is great!

Professor Ka is my FAVORITE professor at UMBC. I just love him. His MLL 210 class really raised my interest in Africa, and even though his 10-15 page annotated bibliography was a bit difficult to do, I actually enjoyed learning about my topic and got an A on it. Definitely an easy class, lots of videos. I recommend taking any class with him.

Probably the easiest class I've ever taken.  Dr. Ka is very enthusiastic about the material and always open to class discussions.  The material was interesting and varied.  Two presentations and one project that allow you to pursue your research interests.  No exams; easy to study for announced "pop" quizzes.  Very chill class and professor.

Dr Ka is incredibly nice. He didn't give any exams, just a couple quizzes that he graded very easily. We had to give two presentations (easy) and write a 10 page paper on basically any topic. Not a difficult class.

This class is complete B.S. and Ka knows it. He makes this class so easy. No exams. A couple of "pop" quizzes which don't require studying really. Other than that, 2 short presentations and one research paper. This class doesn't cover anything, but Ka enthusiastically talks about all kinds of stuff. Nice and very knowledgable.

Professor Ka is so enthusiastic, he can even make French phonetics interesting. He is a wonderful, likeable man, and I can't say enough good things about his personality. The course follows the syllabus, and heavy use is made of the text in class and at home. 1 hr. a week required at the IMC (hated that), but otherwise a very easy, reasonable class

If you're looking for an easy A... run away! Dr. Ka really makes you work for an A. Homework not required to do, but recommended. Exams are tricky because you don't know what to expect on them, and grades them pretty tough. If you want easy A, take McCray. Despite this, he is very friendly and like-able.

Professor Katenkamp is really nice, loves hearing our thoughts and participation. Attendance technically isn't mandatory however there are group work that's done in class so you should really attend the lectures. Textbook required because lectures definitely don't go over everything. Weekly exam is also technically open notes. Great class overall.

Modules for each week consist of reading, video clips, knowledge checks, exams and sometimes written assignments. Professor Katenkamp is really understanding and has an extension policy, which is pretty helpful. It's important to come to lectures as she has in class group assignments that need to be done. Overall, really cool prof :)

Professor Katenkamp's class is pretty boring. Attendance is not particularly important, as all the materials are available on Blackboard. Other than that, she was not very interesting, and I could tell most students weren't into the material and lectures given by her.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Beware of pop quizzes--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: She genuinely cared about her students and wanted them to do well. The lectures could be done by yourself though - just read the book and do the assignments and you will pass this class easily.

Professor Katenkamp is good overall. She's nothing extraordinary, but she gets the job done and is pretty hassle free. The class itself is kinda boring but honestly you don't need to pay much attention. You'll have group work almost every class, it's free points. Her grading isn't harsh and a lot of the work is free points, focus on exams.

Class is super easy, and the prof is very helpful and lenient. Homework is due every Sunday night (super quick, 1 hr max), and a small, easy assignment is due on Wednesday. Attendance is not technically mandatory, but there is an easy group assignment in each class that "counts" as attendance. Highly recommend if you need psych credit.

Dr. K's class was super interesting but super easy. Assignments are not difficult at all. Only 2 "big" writing assignments in the semester but she gives a ton of time to do them. Definitely recommend Dr. K!
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: Very easy; quizzes are open note except for final (lockdown browser). She does small group work in class so show up. She is nice, but I thought her teaching method wasn't very good; talks very fast and doesn't cover everything you need to know for the quizzes. Reading textbook before class and taking notes from lecture/textbook helps.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Most work is online asynchronous. Met once a week for 75 minutes. Very kind and knowledgeable professor

shes a great professor. My suggestion is to take her online! she responds to emails fast and is willing to help you on papers and homework. theres alot of work in this class but it just helps you get an A. Theres 3 possible extra credit assignments. There also is a soft and hard deadline.

Cares about her students a lot. Assignments are pretty straightforward but there are a lot of them. There are in-class assignments that make attendance mandatory, but other than that lectures are pretty pointless.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Professor Katenkamp is a lively teacher who you can tell is passionate about her work. Her in-person lectures are pointless, and I feel as though they should have just been online. Do the assignments on time and use that second attempt. Her online quizzes were somewhat difficult. The most annoying part of this class was the writing fellow meetings.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Gives good feedback--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Dr. Katenkamp is an amazing professor. Her passion for her job is obvious and is deeply caring towards each of her students. As long as you communicate with her and let her know what's going on, she is very understandable and flexible. The work in class is clearly related to what is on exams and quizzes, and she offers a lot of help with reviewing!

Dr. Katenkamp is a great professor! There's a lot of homework (1-2 per week) but it's fairly simple and not too time consuming. Theres weekly online quiz based on material from the books. There's no midterm and the final is multiple choice. The class is pretty easy, participation isn't mandatory but she does count points for in class assignments.

This class is ok. Her lectures are very easy to sit through. Lots of reading and assignments to do for this course, but she allows for you to turn assignments in late if you are having issues. She is generous with extra credit and easy to talk to during her office hours.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I appreciate her passion and clear lectures. Just be diligent.

Dont pay for CMI, we didnt use ours. She required a different textbook and you should be able to find it online for free(yes the older version). The homework is a lot but straightforward, dont wait until last minute w/o knowing what it is. Good teacher but the final caught me off guard, 80 questions short answer??? Luckily it wasnt timed.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Professor K is really kind. She is a bubbly woman and cares about her students. The class consists of two papers and a BUNCH of weekly assignments. She offers so much extra credit that can bump you up a letter grade. She does not grade harsh as long as you get everything on the rubric. She genuinely cares about her students. Accessibl out of class.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Incomprehensible gradebook, as another student noted. I still have no idea what my grade is. A lot of the homework is really just useless busywork. I'd appreciate it as a break from harder homework, but it doesn't even serve that purpose. Doesn't seem particularly put-together.

Really easy A! Lots of online homework which was easy to look up the answers to. 10 class attendances mandatory to do group activities which don't even need to be completed and I never paid attention in class. As long as you follow the rubric for her projects and have decent writing skills, you'll get a good grade on them. Final was easy

Your grade in this class would represent your understanding of the material better if the class were fully online-the two sole assignments of her own design are what got me the B: she graded them extremely harshly. Additionally, her grading page on BB is an unreadable mess: I thought I had an A until my transcript told me otherwise.
Great professor! Very easy class, all tests are online and all homework is online. Only thing is the final is in person but it was easy and just everything in the study guide :)
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Very easy. All tests are online except for the final. I didn't read once and got a high A. (I took psych AP in high school so it might've helped a bit?). almost everyone fails the final and there is a big curve for it. There is a lot of extra credit offered (easy extra credit). Easiest course so far.

Tons of assignments: Grp work, hmwk, raising a child, exams online and in person, 2 quizzes/wk, projects, etc. Easy work just a lot of it. She doesn't really teach so much as opens up a discussion. Makes the students do all the talking. No point showing up to class, you won't get anything out of it (only grp). Nice lady, talks ab her kids too much.

She was super easy. She has lots of extra credit and she is very helpful. Responds to emails back within couple hours and very excited to teach the course. Super easy. Would take her again for upper level classes.

The class itself was not difficult.  I took the hybrid class. There was lots of reading, 2 short papers, and chapter tests.  She responds very quickly to your questions. The only downside of this class was the final exam.  We were given a study guide and practice exam questions.   The final exam was all over the place.

Katenkamp is a good teacher but the way she teaches this class is kinda weird. You only meet every 3 weeks and its a review of the unit. Its really annoying and a waste of time. I went to the first and the last review and I still passed the class.
The review session are dumb, the work is easy (online), but tedious. Read the textbook and you should be fine.

The online class requires you to make your own schedule to read and do the work. The tests are also online so you can easily get help when in doubt. She's a sweetheart, but not much help. The review sessions are a joke. I skimmed throughout the readings, and skipped one class meeting (there are 5) and still got an A. The class is easy/not stressful

This is an online course, but we have to meet 5 times throughout the semester. Attendance is mandatory, you dont want to miss out on 5% of your grades. Unlike many college professors, she is very helpful and replies back to your email very quickly, answering all your questions in very clearly.

I took this class as a hybrid and it was okay. The lectures were completely useless. She tried to come up with "fun games" and "activities" for us to do, but they all ended up a confusing mess, and they didn't seem to help anyone. Online portion is SUPER easy. It's a lot of work, but as long as you stay on top of everything, you should get an A

This class was ok, I learned more from the book than the professor. However she is very sweet and really does try to help students understand the material. If you read the book and do good on the labs you should pass the exams and the final will be optional. I only went to class to get clicker points and group work credit

Very nice teacher, very laid back. Her tests are so easy if you skim through the text. Don't miss class because the things she talks about are pretty neat and the movies she shows are really funny. Very easy A for Psyc and non-Psyc people alike =)

I love her!  she was a great teacher, lectures were pretty interesting, and shes very nice and sweet.  You can print outlines online, and then during the notes fill in blanks so you dont have to write as much.  she really helps people study for the tests, and she is just an overall awesome teacher.  i got an a.  but i AM a psych major...

Very easy and nice teacher. Her test are really easy and she gives bonus points. She puts lecture outlines online,which I really like because all the important information is there, and I don't have to read the book at all :)
really nice and really easy.   go to lecture, she gives away lots of test questions then.

The class is not that hard but she can be difficult to explain things sometimes. She is an fair-grader but is very smart-mouth. Sometimes when you ask a question, she seems to look at you like your stupid. I would recommend taking the class with her but go to lecture! Also read the book! Most questions from the exams are from lecture and the book.

There is no actual syllabus, she flies by the seat of her pants. I can't fault her for wanting to try "new" methods in her teaching, but all she has proven is her disdain for teaching and disdain for students. This class was a waste of my time and not because it was hard (it wasn't) but because she is using AI to substitute actual work on her part.

Class is VERY disorganized sometimes I'm not sure if she understands what the plan is. There is a weird grading system which limits creativity/growth. Class discussions are often not discussions as we rarely have time to properly talk about the prompts. Shes very passive aggressive and snobby. An A is possible but not worth the mental turmoil.
Class is a relatively easy A but you wont enjoy it

speedran unlikability. vague syllabus. arbitrary contract-based grading system. 3 massive assignments due on one day. multiple graded assignments based on AI generated prompts. made fun of a student on day 1. made a race joke on day 2. all assignments are based in google forms, which means the due dates don't appear on blackboard.

Professor Vetter can be unpredictable. Some days she's nice; others she's snappy and passive-aggressive. For 210, an A requires completing the hours-long Capstone Project. Even if you do all the work, get A's on everything, and attend all classes, you still need the project for an A. She mentions this early on, but I think it's an unfair policy.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: You WILL get an A if you put in the time and energy. She can be a nice person sometimes, but the class is overall so weirdly structured (e.g. grade contracts) and can get an attitude. She is absolutely bearable, but if there's a better class/prof then go there. P.S. Do not be fooled by the single review that is "shocked" by the others like I was
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Dr. Vetter begins this class by sharing you will sign a contract for the grade you want (so weird) I signed the B. DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS. Dr. Vetter is a nice person but she does not teach this class well. It is an excessive amount of work, unorganized and unprepared in class. Don't waste your time with this class. Find a better professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Vetter seems nice when you first meet her but she is incredibly difficult to deal with and grades based on a convoluted and confusing system. She also failed to respect my university-approved disability accommodations, claiming that the way her class is set up already accounts for them, but this is not true. She is one of the worst professors.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: never knew how to run discussions, either contributing way too much or way too little and was really inflexible and somewhat passive aggressive over email when trying to sort out technical issues; the content itself was interesting though, so if you enjoy political philosophy then still worth considering this class

I'm shocked by these reviews. I loved her class and I loved her! Although the texts were a bit difficult to understand bc of how old the texts were, her presentations/lectures clearly explained them. Her quizzes were quick and easy and she gives you 2 chances for each. Exams are just past exam questions. Try your best and you will do just fine!

As opposed to lectures, she'd assign us two or three videos that would sometimes go up to an hour and a half long (each!) that I had to watch on 2x speed because of slow she'd speak. The audio on them was also terribly quiet, her quizzes were often confusing and she took ages to grade anything (we didn't have any grades in for the several weeks)

Dr. Vetters grading is bizarre, she is typically very unprepared, and assigns a lot of work. She only gives full credit on assignments that go 'above and beyond,' took 9 weeks to submit any grades for a weekly assignment, and in the last 2 weeks of class we had due 2 12 slide voicethreads, an 8 page and a 5 page paper.

I agree with the views of Professor Vetter. She is not very good with technology. Her quizzes are very confusing. Her lecture videos are boring and long, but helpful. However, her audio is terrible. She responds to emails late and waits until after the semester to grade everything. To those who'll be taking her class, I wish you the best of luck!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Confusing class because Prof Vetter is not very tech savvy. She forgets to upload assignments and then is confused. She also takes forever to grade so you will not know your grade until after the semester. She uploads videos explaining the readings but her monotone voice makes it a very hard watch. She is nice but her teaching style is boring.

A lot of readings; all the lectures are pre-recorded. The volume is horrible, and she yawns through them constantly. Quizzes associated with every reading/lecture; question wording is not very clear. Three VoiceThreads; feedback is right before due dates and vague. Responds to emails late, very few announcements. Do in-person or not at all.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Test heavy

reviews.comment: To start off she is really disappointing. When to try to ask for help on an assignment all she has to say is "We're all doing the best we can" and makes random jokes "Hehehe". Can't believe she assigned a whole project of 8 pages on top of a final exam essay (2 pages) that includes a voice thread all during finals week. Dont take her.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--So many papers

reviews.comment: This class was time consuming for an asynchronous class. We had to watch videos and it was always very difficult to hear what she said and the quizzes we were given would be worded so strangely and would confuse everyone. We had VoiceThread activities and a lot of the feedback we got was very vague. The final exam MC part are old quiz questions

The reviews here are TRUE. She grades very late and responds to emails late. Not sure what she does in her free time but it isn't grading. She is assigning a whole analysis project ON TOP OF A FINAL EXAM THAT VERY WEEK. She posts assignments late minute. There are weekly writing prompts and lectures due each week. Won't take her again ever.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--So many papers

reviews.comment: A lot of reading and her video lectures go in circles like theorists do, extensive weekly journals. Boring and very discussion heavy. you get points for everything and the exams are extremely demanding, she asks for a lot of precision which is extremely difficult considering how abstracts the theories are. Tends to push her own narrative at times.

She is an ok professor, her recorded lectures are boring and lengthy. The quizzes are a bit hard since there is only one right answer. I'm taking her again because her exams are online so it saves the anxiety. She responds to emails late and her teaching is inconsistent. Wish there was a better professor in this department but I don't know any.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Dr. Vetter is a great as a person going to her office hours will help a lot. My class was not in person. most of the work was at my own pace. The issue is that I didnt know my final grade until the end of the year when final grades were posted. I was worried because I was right the boarder between and A and a B so deal with that at your risk.

The class is good to take if you are a Poli Sci major. However, the readings and the lectures were so vague and hard to understand. The quizzes style: are all good answers but there is ONE best answer. there would be assign. due the same week. felt like a 300/400 lev.course. thought I was doing good in this course. there goes the dean's list.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: The course was asynchronous and the pre-recorded lectures were very helpful but she constantly yawned in them which was distracting. The weekly quizzes were way more difficult than they could have been and I would suggest watching lectures before reading as the language is very difficult. You will need the textbook to pass the course.

Dr Vetter is a really caring person who will bend over backwards to help students. If you try to do the few readings she assigns a week, do the minimal assignment requirements per week and at least try to keep notes going throughout the semester you'll be prepared for exams. Easy grader if you prepare to put in minimal effort. Easy A.

Im actually sad to give her this rating because she's a nice person and the subject matter was interesting. But she was so disorganized and inefficient. Posted assignments at an untimely basis. Her exams are ridiculous: timed long essays and a 10 page paper due at the same time. So much reading. Never responds to emails. Grades very late.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: The readings are really long & difficult so you're better off just watching the lectures instead where she guides you through them, the lectures are dense but extremely helpful. Her powerpoints are disorganized though so you NEED to use the reading guide and fill it out with detailed notes throughout the lecture-exams are heavily based off of them.

Honestly I was really disappointed with this class. Prof Vetter is kind and knowledgable but her midterm and final were so hard and she assigned a 10 pg paper on top of the final with barely any heads up. Our discussions were short and we always ran out of time. You teach yourself most of the material.. wouldn't recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Nice professor but she talks extremely quiet and is nearly impossible to understand during lectures. Unnecessary amount of reading assigned each week and the assignments are often posted late. The readings are difficult to understand and very boring to follow. Exams are online but questions are timed and very lengthy. Not worth the headache.

This professor was a bit all over the place for me. She was very disorganized with her notes as she would put random key words all over the board with no explanation. The textbook is a definite must have. The way to get through this class is taking notes on literally everything she says in class, even if you didnt read. All the exams are online.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Nice woman but probably didn't have much business teaching this class at least. Basically every class was a structure-less lecture. She would have a power-point up but it was just small little notes only she would understand to guide her through her "lecture". The TA Gracie Bradford was much more knowledgeable. Everyone learns from the textbook.

Great discussions of different political theorists. Application papers (graded for completion only) make you think about each reading to formulate your thoughts on each author. Unit papers let you choose the theorist you want to write about. Final paper totally open ended - you choose the topic AND relevant theorists.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Lisa Vetter is by far the best professor I have ever had. She encourages discussion and is totally open to listening to you as long as you can back up your points. This is a great starting point for anyone who wants to learn more about Political Philosophy.

Small class, made for great discussions. Highly interactive, participation important. Projects tie theories to actual issues. Variety of authors who often disagree presents multiple points of view. Learned a lot! Great prof.

The theories may be old but you learn to apply them to modern day issues - that's the basis for her graded group application activities and the FINAL EXAM. 3 unit exams deal with the theories only. No papers to write, but a 5-minute reaction writing every class. Is there to help - but YOU have to ASK. Lectures interesting & fun, but can run long.

She is funny, witty and a wonderful woman. She's great teacher and I would take another class with her. This class isn't tough but it's not the easiest either. Reading is essential because she assigns a quiz (online) for each new philosopher.  Lectures are useful especially when it comes time to her tests which are okay. Do you work and you'll pass

I learned a lot in this class about many mental disorders I wouldn't have otherwised learned. Class does go full length, and sometimes she goes on tangents, but I found the information interesting to learn. Grading is appropriate for a 400-level course. Small class structure helps facilitate discussion even if you're more timid.

I felt obligated to warn students about this class.

-SO BORING
-2.5 hours of straight up rambling
-Does not let out early
-Class divided in 2 parts a discussion ab weekly readings(v long)
-Grade is heavily based on participating
-1.5 hours of useless info on the same topic that could've been covered in 30 mins
-Tough grader

Please save yourself.

Great professor! I learned about so many different research topics in psychopathology. Each class there is a lecture portion and a discussion portion, attendance and participation are mandatory but it is not too bad because you get participation points through the class discussions. I recommend this class if you are going to pursue clinical psych.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Professor Yoon was good, caring and provided clear feedback on assignments. Graded by weekly discussion posts, class participation, being a discussion leader, and a research paper (annotated bio, first draft, and final). Get ready to read a lot of research articles and make a discussion post about it. READ RUBRIC for discussion posts and others.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: This class was pretty cool. Its lecture and then a class discussion about the readings/lecture. The discussions were interesting. I usually dont participate much in other classes but I found it easy for this class. Just one paper that you write in chunks throughout the semester. Most grades were for completion and feedback was given.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Very outgoing and kind professor who wants to make sure everyone succeeds in the class. Promotes class participation for an active lecture environment, which makes actual classes more interesting. There are a few big group projects, but as long as you are willing to do the relatively few assignments and come to class, you will do well.

The kindest professor Ive ever had. There's a textbook but you don't need to read, he will teach everything during his lectures. He's really kind and cares for his students. He has 4 pop quizzes but they aren't hard it's a pass or fail grade. The exams are essays that are really easy to get points on too. Overall an easy class but really liked it.

Dr. Lee is very knowledgeable and nice, but his style of teaching is very textbook and you won't understand anything if you aren't diligently paying attention at all times. Its very easy to get lost in this class. Assignments are very easy and he is lenient about deadlines. Offers comprehensive feedback.

reviews.comment: love her shes so sweet and cares about student success, but i would say for a class like psyc309 the amount of work assigned is a little unnecessary. i was not expecting the class to be assignment-heavy because the concepts are easy, but most weeks we have had more than two assignment due. overall, i would take her again, but she does assign a lot.

reviews.comment: 90 questions and 90 mins on the final is evil

She's a really nice professor and her assignments aren't super hard at all. Some are a bit tedious though, like the graphic organizers. Made me feel like I'm in high school again. Sometimes lecture was boring though, but other than that great professor.

Professor Rose is a great teacher, she is clear and passionate about her work. She is overall a good vibe. I would def recommend her, she is understanding and as long as you complete the work you will succeed. Everything is open note
Easy class but veryyyy tedious. Up to 40 points extra credit 800 total points, 720+ for an A.

reviews.comment: Easiest social science credit you can get. Guaranteed A. Class is almost entirely asynchronous, with a few online meetings before every exam. Makes a 4 credit class feel like a cakewalk.
this was a very easy A. Just make sure you do the work before its due and tests and exams are open note. She is also very nice!
Easy A, material is not difficult just a lot of reading. Exams are open note/internet. Attendance is apart of grade.

reviews.comment: A couple synchronous online classes, most were asynchronous. If you're not a test taker, you still should be able to pass. Lots of reading. Homework- you were able to do some of it till you got 100%. Uses online homework software and quizzes. Do the homework and you'll pass. When the Prof would lecture, she was pretty straight forward and nice.

I did her online class and it was super easy. The course work is not that bad as long as you complete it before the deadlines your good and having a good schedule is important too. Her lectures are pretty nice too and you have to join the class in order to get your attendance points. Exams are online too and its open note. 10/10 class
Very straightforward class and easy going class. The prof is very helpful through email and class. Once you understand the format of the work during unit 1 then it's as simple as can be for the rest.

A lot of work however she is very kind and makes the work easy and accessible online. She gives clear deadlines and clear work instructions which makes the class easy. Exams are open notes and the classwork is fairly easy. Prepare for a lot of notes.

Very enthusiastic and made online meetings the best possible. Exam after each unit, but they are not too difficult as long as you take notes/study. Has extra credit opportunities and gives a grade for participating in meetings (which were only before each exam). Easy to reach out of class and the assignments themselves were easy.

Very kind and enthusiastic. She made all the difference (engaged well) because paying attention in an online class is already hard enough. SO much reading though, but you can work on assignments for each unit at your own pace so I guess just manage your time responsibly. 3% extra credit to your final grade, open note exams and no final :)
Participation matters and she's extremely judged and almost fake as an individual towards her students.

She is rigorous with grading and very condescending.Selfish and honestly narcissistic because she will tell you she understands your situation but will not compromise with you. For a class that's about caring for students with disabilities she should be more empathetic with her students' success.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Group projects

reviews.comment: Dr. Rose is clearly passionate about psychology & you can see that through her lectures/lecture videos. She is energetic, helpful & provides plenty of resources to help you succeed. Tests are conceptual & requires you to analyze situations rather than reciting definitions. They are difficult but she allows you to take the exams open note. No final!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Fully online except for a couple of synchronous lessons. A lot of information though.

Easiest class yet. Mandatory attendance; only a participation grade from poll questions. Exams cover exactly what's in the textbook- be prepared to read! Every unit's hw is 3 chapters, 3 mini video quizzes, 100% on 3 Inquizitives, and sometimes a lab(s). Exams are open note + multiple choice so you're always guaranteed to pass.
Professor Rose was an amazing teacher. The class met once before every 5 exams. Those are the times mandatory for a grade. All of our assignments were simple and to the point.

This class was perfect for me. You do everything on your own time. Rose is super sweet, great at teaching, and you can tell she really enjoys it. She's got the enthusiasm of a real teacher, not just a professor at a research university. Everything was easy, there's just a lot of content to cover.

Class was fully online. Assigned 5 units with 3 chapters in each one. Super easy as long as you do all the work she assigns and the material isn't difficult. Extra credit opportunities were available to raise grade by 3%. Professor responds to emails pretty quick. Overall a great professor.

I freaking lovee Dr. Rose! Not only is she extremely relatable, she helps you to fully understand what you are trying to digest! She offers great feedback and genuinely cares about your education, wellbeing and if your fully understanding the content at hand! Beautiful spirit! She responds to emails in a timely manner and will take time with you!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Caring

reviews.comment: Extremely tough grader, I highly doubt anyone in the class got an A. I heard she's not like this for other courses but I took a WI PSYC400 with her. She's very kind and knowledgeable about her topics but I can't recommend her because of my experience. Take this course and prepare to WORK.
Absolutely the most amazing professor ever! She answers all her emails within a day. The readings are little intense, but she has unit reviews and peer mentors to help you throughout the semester.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: PYSC100 was suppose to be an easy A but they switched up the format mid semester which I did not like. This brought a lot of averages of people down so be aware. reviews.comment: PSYC100 is a pretty heavy class in terms of content and material, but she made Unit deadlines, as opposed to weekly deadlines, which was great. reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: I loved this class. Very easy. Also, she cares about her students and will further explain if there are questions. Make sure you go to class though. Lots of online work, but it's easy and fun. I highly recommend this for a GEP which is what I did. Tests are also fairly easy.

Overall easy hybrid class. Meet once a week to take a group quiz and listen to her lecture. Most of the time there were guest speakers in-class. She's very knowledgable and a great resourceful person in the psych department. She gives very good feedback on each online assignment and is always eager to remind students on upcoming assignments.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Dr. Rose was a wonderful professor and I would take her courses in the future. She is very knowledgable and delivers material in an understandable format. Group quizzes are given so it is important to show up to class. It was easy to get in contact with her through email.

She is by far, the fastest emailer east of the Mississippi. She clearly lays out what she expects, reminds the class of due dates and issues, kind and respectful. She will likely respond to any question/concern you have within a hour.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Easy and straight forward class. Study the resources she gives you.

Dr. Rose was a pretty good teacher in my opinion, she explained the material well and expectations were very clear. As long as you turn in all the work, it shouldn't be too hard to get an A. Assignments were always straight forward, never took me more than an hour and always got an A. The paper's requirements were also well laid out.

I could have taught this course. She had one essay and four short discussions. The rest of the work came to a total of (no joke) over 1,000 multiple choice, matching, etc, questions. These questions were generated by the online textbook and from online exams. This was a time-consuming, joke of a course.

Great professor! The structure of class was go over the chapter with slides, take notes, group activity that you would turn in, more notes, and then we'd leave. I had it as a hybrid course, and we had a chapter test every week along with a few other assignments due that week online. Read the textbook and listen to the lecture, and you'll get an A.

Hybrid class. Do online work and complete in-class activities to the best of your ability. Study for final, it coves a lot of information. The teacher is great and knows a lot about child psych. She wants students to succeed.
Overall very easy course. Make sure to do all online work as it is 60% of final grade. Lots of extra credit possible.
Took this class online which chapter exams and the final (an essay) were duable without technically having to read that much, if at all. Easy A.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: Kind person

Rose is very good and passionate in this class about the material. Have one big paper about a movie relating to people with exceptionalities. She gives a list of movie to choose from. 4 exams total which you need to study for. Various formats of the test. Lectures were good through PowerPoints. Lot of note taking. Would take her again. Interesting

reviews.comment: Rose is extremely knowledgeable and nice. Content of class is a bit boring but she does the best she can with it. Have a midterm and final exam and 2 papers. reviews.comment: Psych 200 is hybrid with lecture once a week. Lots of online work. Come to class to get points. Only 1 test final (cumulative), 3 little papers (not hard) and online work. reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Hybrid class. Submit work on time and get an A.

While this course was my only 8:30 class,  I surprisingly enjoyed this class. She was the most engaging professor I've ever had and I genuinely looked forward to going to class. Please do the extra credit- it helps so much. While this class was a hybrid, she explained material so well in lecture. She is possibly my favorite psychology professor.
Hot, friendly, amazing lecturer, gives fun activities in class, easy grader, enthusiastic about the subject and encouraging!!

Dr. Rose is very passionate about Psychology and you can tell by her vocal tone during lectures. She's willing to help! Go to lecture because there are clicker points and you actually learn a lot! Do extra credit because it adds 3% to your grade. 5 tests including final (drop one), labs, and online exams. Read and do everything on time to do well.
I loved Dr. Rose! Her lectures were very on-topic and clear. It's easy to learn in her class as long as you show up for lecture.

Taking this class with Dr. Rose was great! Even though it was at 830, the lectures were always interesting and fun. Dr. Rose really cares about your understanding of the courses and will be happy to help answer any questions. I'm really glad I took it with her and I'm thinking of now adding Psychology as a minor
Great class.

I have her now and she's an awesome professor in the sense that she is very nice and she really strives for class participation.  Exams aren't too hard at all but only a small portion of the material is covered in class. Online labs and practice exams are your best friend for this course.  She'll randomly throw in clicker questions so go to class
She is really nice. although she can be strict, I enjoyed her teaching style.

Ms. Rose was an awesome professor. She is very nice and tried her best to make everyone understand what is going on in the course. I had her for both PSYC 331 and PSYC 332. PSYC 331 was tough with the stats but she help us understand the formulas while PSYC 332 was great. NO EXAMS, just a Final Paper. Make sure to go to lab to get easy points.

I had her in the spring. The course was challenging but she tries to keep things simple and interesting. Dr. Rose was very helpful both in class and during office hours. She also provided lots of extra credit opportunities. I highly recommend her for this course.

Amazing professor. She is honestly a breathe of fresh air, material can be intimidating sometimes but she has so much patience and likes to make sure everyone is on the same page. I would not recommend taking these classes with anyone else! I wish she taught each class that I need, I truly miss her!

The class itself is INCREDIBLY boring but she seems to try her hardest to keep students interested. Lecture/lab could be incredibly irrelevant and repetitive at times but they provided easy points. Final project was pretty easy.

While the material itself is pretty easy, she's actually one of the worst professors I've ever had here. For 331 she's not awful, but 332 is one of the most frustratingly confusing classes. She doesn't tell her TAs things, won't put important information online and is overall incredibly obtuse to deal with.

Took 331 with Ms. Rose, couldn't have been more pleased! PSYC 332 with her is the opposite. Lecture is 331 all over again, and a waste of time, other than a few formulas you'll need for SPSS. There is a big research project due at the end of the semester, they will not let you get ahead on it or give you the info. needed. Back to back due dates.
She is patient, and encourages us to raise questions all the time. Most importantly, she is the the hottest teacher ever. Everyone should take her class.

PSYC 331 is easily the most hectic and stressful psychology class a student can take. However, it's also probably the most helpful with its implementation of statistical formulas when it comes to performing experiments. Rose helps make such a dull class interesting. However, the TA (Julian) was very bad which can make or break this class.

I took PSYC 331 with Laura several semesters ago and she was still just as fantastic as everyone else described. She is sweet, encouraging, and pretty. Her lectures are thorough, clear, and straight forward. She teaches very well as a grad student. The TAs Barb Sara and Krista were great as well. Very good class.

Great teacher. Lectures with power points. Online worksheets, lecture material, and section over view. Very clear on what you'll need but exams are still challenging. Getting an A isn't hard, if you put the work in. Helpful TA as well.

Awesome teacher. Lectures are accompanied by a power point and she makes it very clear what you need to know for exams. Labs are extra credit and can be very helpful, but they are taught by the TA (who may not be the best...) Exams are very easy if you pay attention. Offers study guides and a lot of extra credit opportunities.
Super cute teacher and very smart, you will have to work for a good grade but she makes it very easy to obtain

i had never taken a physics class before this one, and I am honestly heavily unmotivated and living on a prayer in this class. she always rushes through the lectures so it is hard to fully understand most of the time. i wish i would've taken this class at a CC and transferred the credit over. also 8am quizzes every friday are very annoying (online)
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I've never taken physics prior to this class so I was extremely worried but it ended up being one of my favorite classes and Dr.Lili is one of my favorite professors! She really wants you to succeed and the only way you will is with PRACTICE. Do all of the homeworks, REDO them, and you'll get As on exams.

She seems like a nice person but she's hard to understand/communicate with. I haven't taken physics since high school, and this class was really tough. I barely passed. Save yourself the trouble and just take it at community college. I found organic chemistry easier than this class. The exams were at 8am, and it was really tough if you commute >1hr

Honestly, the class is pretty straightforward. The class had a lot of work involved with it, but the lectures helped you with the homework, the homework helped you with the weekly quizzes, and the weekly quizzes helped you with the Exams. Ultimately, Cui was a good professor and explained things pretty well.

I took this class with knowledge of physics already from high school. She teaches very terribly and will look down on you if you ask questions. reviews.comment: Lecture is similar 4 hw quizzes + exams.When you ask something, she makes you feel dumb for asking. You have 2 exams + final. Hw 3x/week, not bad, just do it in time. Quizzes 30 minutes 4 10-12 questions is insane! worth 30% big chunk of your grade 2 drops 4 the quizzes but if there is a class-wide technical issue those will be a part of your drops

She makes sure to integrate practice materials for students, which is helpful. The homework, exams, and quizzes are fair and representative of her lecture slides. I appreciated this and recommend her physics classes. The lectures and the textbook are good resources. She is passionate about her students' success and understanding.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Dr. Lili makes physics digestible with clear lectures. While the frequent 8am quizzes and heavy homework load can be stressful, it all helps you learn. Studying with unstuckstudy alongside the textbook and practice problems is a huge lifesaver.

Her time management skills are horrible. She'll rush material at the end of lecture, so it ends up being poorly explained. Quizzes are also 30 min, which isn't enough time. HW is 3x/week. She can also can be very condensing. If you have a strong foundation in physics, then you'll do fine. If not, I recommend taking this course at another university

Dr. Cui gives a lot of homework, 3 per week and they are each 20 questions. Plus 1 quiz per week. Her lectures rarely line up to the homework and she moves really fast. Basically her class is difficult unless you have a very good background. She was very nice but the lectures seem more like a refresher course compared to a lesson.

Dr. Cui was the best professor I have had at UMBC, she is very kind and is accessible outside of class. She does a great job explaining things but it really helps if you actually show up to class. If you do, I don't think that you should struggle in this class.

Dr. Lili is by far one of the best professors I've ever met. She gives you the roadmap to succeed! The lectures relate to the HW, which translates directly to the quizzes which translate directly to her exams, and you get a formula sheet. I don't understand how anyone can fail this class. She is amazing!!

Dr. Lili is a great professor who cares about her students and she makes it clear what you need to know to do well on weekly quizzes and 2 midterms with a final that are pretty straightforward. You can also use one piece of paper to write anything for exam. very helpful! As long as you pay attention in class and do the homework you  will be fine!

Lili is honestly great. I had her for both PHYS 111 and 112 and her lectures are great. Her lectures directly reflect what she expects and the examples she does in class are very helpful for homework. The quizzes are exactly like the homework and the exams are like the quizzes. It is NOT hard to do well in her class imo.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Lecture slides are critical and HW is heavy/hard. Grading incl. weekly reading quizzes + weekly concept quizzes. Attendance/participation by live app in lectures. Comprehensive exams - no curves. Lab isn't very exciting, but is required (TA taught). Final is heavy (20%). Get ready to study a lot! She does allow a note page (both sides) for exams.

Very straightforward class, mostly algebra and trigonometry. Attendance is only 5% of your grade so missing class is fine. Lab was not enjoyable for me at all, mandatory 2 hours of filling out a word document with unengaging carts and sensors. Not the best communicator but don't take it personally and ask for help when needed and you'll be fine.

Dr. Lili explains well how to do the problems in class which reflect the homework and weekly online quizzes but she would go through them way too quickly. All the exams reflected the material but the cumulative final was brutal because these questions must have been randomly generated with no practice exam so you don't really know what to expect.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I love Dr. Lili. She is one of my favorite professors I've ever had. She is clear on where she pulls material from on exams and quizzes, which makes this class incredibly easy. The material is tolerable because her best quality is her ability to teach. I enjoyed her lectures, the material, and her presence. I will miss not having her anymore.

She was a great professor.  Her lectures were great and taught everything you need to know for tests.  She gave examples in class and they were basically the same problems that would be on homework and exams just with some numbers changed.  She explains everything pretty clearly, so if you come to class often and take notes, you can't go wrong.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: The assignments and exams are good but her teaching style is awful. When you go to office hours she scrutinizes you for not knowing how to solve something.

She is great at lecturing so attend all of her lectures. most of the questions on the exam will be similar to practice problems in lecture and the online quizzes. Only negative really was that every friday there is a online that has to be done at 8 am, and you can not miss them unless you want a zero.

A typical intro STEM class at UMBC; a lot of busy work and takes a lot of effort. However, going to lecture, attempting the homework, and asking questions makes it difficult to fail this class. She pretty much tells you everything you need to know in class. She does go through things quickly though.

Dr. Cui is a great professor! She makes Physics easy to learn and study. I recommend following her study plan and reviewing previous quizzes and homework for the exams.  Dr.Cui is very organized and accessible outside of class. Although she can be strict, her teaching method was very helpful.

Dr. Cui specializes not only in Physics, but in Teaching Physics, and it shows. A potentially difficult topic is broken up into easily digestible chunks and the in-class questions keep people engaged. I wish every class was taught the way Lily taught.

The Professor explains the material somewhat well and the homework is based on the previous lecture. The 8am quizzes are simple and you have to understand all the questions on the homework to do well on the exam. Overall the class isn't that hard as long as you keep up with the material
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Beware of pop quizzes--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Dr. Cui is one of my favorite professors, despite her being a bit strict and assigning frequent homework. In comparison to other stem courses I've taken, this one isn't challenging. Go to class, try on the homework and quizzes, and you'll be fine. She states clearly where she gets her exam material from which makes it a lot easier to study for.

Amazing professor. Great and straightforward lectures. She makes physics so easy to learn and she knows it very well too. The only thing stressful about this class is the 8 am quizzes every Friday and the immense amount of homework she gives u. I ain't gonna lie, even though it's a lot, they're very helpful. Her exams are super easy too!

reviews.comment: There's work every other day, quizzes on Friday and the lowest scores are dropped but don't slack off. This is a fairly easy class if you keep up with the textbook and lecture. The Professor teaches well and attendance is mandatory for clicker questions.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: 8am quizzes every single week was a pain, homework 3 times a week, but the quizzes had the same questions as the ones on the homework, just different numbers. Lectures were kind of boring to go to but you need to for clickers. other than that she was great. I don't understand the other reviews saying she is arrogant and condescending, she is not.

Lectures taught exactly what you need to know for the homework. Homework was just like the quizzes. Allowed a cheat sheet on the exams. Class is pretty straightforward. 3 homework per week which can be annoying. Plenty of resources for the class. Reading the textbook is not necessary.

reviews.comment: if you get an answer wrong in class and she doesn't respond by being condescending, go buy a lotto ticket.

She makes a lot of mistakes, is arrogant, and extremely strict . Even if her mistake is screwing up your grade. She does not care and will not fix it. 

The only professor/teacher in my life I've genuinely disliked as a person.  College is hard enough, Cui will make it way harder than it has to be. Especially for a 100 level course lol.

she's a good professor, she knows her material and teaches well. lots of homework, 3 a week, weekly reading quiz and weekly 8am tests. but if you do the hw and study there is no way you will not pass. attend her office hours and on your own time do practice problems. she also allows you to make cheat sheets for midterm and final which helps a lot
So so arrogant. My god. She definitely knows her stuff though.

As a professor she is not the best, if you could take someone else do it. She speaks in a condescending tone when you ask questions or need clarification. She does not respond to emails so you would need to find her.  The class itself is easy but having her as the lecturer makes it harder than it needs to be, YouTube will be your friend.

Not a hard class if you're willing to put effort. Dr.Lili is very helpful and she has 2-3 office hours per week to help so please take that opportunity. Definitely a lot of hw but they're very helpful to study for the weekly quizzes. Seriously, her quizzes are very straightforward. Amazing and funny professor!!

Dr. Lili is very nice and gives you many opportunities every week for help sessions. It's honestly a LOT of homework though, due 3 times a week. The labs get a bit annoying too. Uses clickers, only grades for participation though. Midterm and final, and you have to do well on each Friday quiz in order to pass the class.

reviews.comment: Dr. Lili is a great professor! She has a strong accent, but she's really easy to understand nonetheless. She's super nice and gives great lectures. She's wonderful!
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I don't know why she has a bad rating, she's such an awesome prof. Her BB is so organized, lectures are interesting and quizzes are all based on the hw and lectures (expect the same type of Qs). Recorded lectures, slides posted after but clicker questions used for attendance. Quizzes are open-note, cheat sheet can be used on final and "midterm".

reviews.comment: Completely understanding when emailing her about an accident when submitting an assignment. One thing to note is that she does often rush through the slides end.

reviews.comment: Best professor Ive had this semester! Lots of homework but 3 attempts are given and it really helps you understand the content. Textbook only needed for reading quizzes, lectures are super important to understand for passing the class.

It's easy to get an A if you put in the work and do the HW, all quizzes are drawn from lecture and HW. Lectures were also entertaining, you can tell she loves physics and wants everyone to participate in clicker questions. Make a study group, go to office hour, SI pass and you'll pass. Don't fall behind on anything bc theres a quiz every week.

reviews.comment: She was not accommodating at all, through communication barely responded to emails and if she did it was a very condescending tone. The material isn't hard it's really the professor that makes the class worse; get a group of friends and create a study group you'll receive more information that way instead of actually learning something in the class

reviews.comment: Professor Cui is very clear in her expectations and straightforward in her lectures. Just about all the material you need to know can be found in her lectures, and the quizzes and homework were just variations of problems that had been taught. Solid class, would recommend.

Dr. Cui is very knowledgeable and a good lecturer. Participation in class is necessary to pass. This is a hard course, so make sure to take advantage of any and all SI PASS/OH sessions. The quizzes draw from hw and discussion problems, and the final exam draws heavily from the quizzes. Start hw early or you won't finish it.

reviews.comment: Phys112 is already an easy class, but this course became stupid easy online. Just know the formulas and how to use the right hand rule. The final was basically the same questions as the quizzes (and the quizzes were basically the same as the lecture-follow ups/clickers and labs)

For her online class, you will have a reading test, two chapter tests, a quiz, a lab, and homework on Pearson every week. It might sound like a lot of work, but I would say it really is not as bad as it sounds. In fact, there is only one exam, final, that counts only 10% of your grade. If you do well on your weekly assignments, you will be fine.

10/10. She breaks down concepts flawlessly and if you are confused, she is really helpful in office hours. Workload is heavy but I can say besides the lab, the extra work is super helpful. Reading is only necessary for the prequiz bc lectures are thorough and explanatory. Maybe she was different in person but virtually 10/10 and a sweetheart!!
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Lili is an amazing teacher. I took physics with her because I needed the credits to graduate and I would have never given physics another glance but she has a way of breaking down everything that makes so much sense. Especially for someone with no physics background prior to taking her class. Overall the sweetest. An amazing professor
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures--Caring

reviews.comment: Took Lili for 111&112 - was amazing for both! 1 of my fave profs I've had at UMBC. Fair amount of work to do, but do it all, its an easy A. Redo the lecture notes, weekly quizzes, & old exams & you'll ace every test. Cares about her students & wants everyone to succeed. Holds office hours & review sessions. Lab can be annoying. Overall 10/10.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Great professor. She's very reasonable and communicative. She makes sure that you know the material and provides great resources and support for you to succeed. Lots of HW, labs, exams, quizzes, etc though. She may go fast in her lectures, and not finish everything in one class. However, class isn't hard if you put in a little effort.
She explains the material but can be so mean. I went in for office hours to ask for help but she like scolded me because I didn't draw the graph neatly. It really made me upset and sad the whole day.

Overall, she was not a bad teacher! Very calm, and as long as just show up, use the clicker, she gives full credit for that. It was definitely hard to understand her. Had to do a lot of independent studying. I did not do very well on my 2nd and 3rd exam. Final was in the 60s range. I still got a C in the class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Dr. Cui is a very hardworking prof who will literally spend hours w you outside of class explaining a concept. She gets a bad rap sometimes because she is hard on her students and wants them to put forth as much effort as she does. Not afraid to yell, thats for sure. Labs/HW are a pain, but tests are very doable if you do the practice exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Very rude and condescending, does not curve even an 89.8%, bad professor. Outside of that the material is easy and her exams are similar to past exams. She's also not very bright as she re-uses EXACT questions from two years ago, unaware that a good portion of students have old exams. Get yourself 2 year old exams and you're golden Bad professor

Prof Lili is very energetic and knows a lot about Physics. She expects a lot of work from us, with weekly quizzes, online homework, and lab work. She goes quickly through her lectures, with a lot of material to cover, but she makes sure you understand the concepts. She also brought in Dr. Leupen to further explain physics to us using biology.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: In order to pass her class, you need to go to it everyday and write down everything. The material is not easy but she give great explanations in class. Her tests are easy if you GO TO CLASS because they are based on the power points. The great thing about her class is the little amount of time she take to grade the exams.
Shes awesome! Her explanations are super clear, shes far more helpful than the textbook. She really makes an effort to help you pass. I very much enjoyed this class.
reviews.rating_tags: ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Lili is awesome!! She lays everything out really clearly, and takes time to explain more complicated concepts. She really cares about her students and wants everyone to pass. She gives you all the tools you will need to do well. Her exams are very straightforward and if you have paid attention and done your homework you will pass.

Her lectures were pretty difficult to understand, so I had to review her lecture notes. Her exams aren't hard if you studied. Her final exams aren't anything extremely difficult. If you work hard, you will get an A in this class,just depends how much effort you put into this class.I will only take her again personally since I know how she works now
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: She is probably the most degrading instructor I have ever had. Makes you feel dumb and does not a good job of explaining concepts. Exams are difficult. Does not curve or give any type of extra credit.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Lili is a genuinely sweet professor who wants to see you succeed. Yes, she can be loud at times but that's just how she is. She is a very kind person who is willing to explain concepts again to you (not that you will need it because she's very clear in lectures). She encourages questions and participation and admires students who work hard.

Cui is the real deal. She gave me the best advice a teacher has ever given me - "This is supposed to be a struggle." It helped me realize I'm not dumb or incapable, but that learning is SUPPOSED to be uncomfortable and challenging. Her class is a real charcter-builder. It will feel like pure suffering but stick it out and you'll be better for it!

I'm pretty sure the three good reviews on here are written by Dr. Cui, herself XD She's probably the worst teacher I've ever had at UMBC. She gets extremely offensive if you question her during her lectures and her tests are way too difficult. When the average test score is a 65% then you know it's not the students but the teacher that's the issue
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: Dr. Cui is my favorite teacher so far at UMBC! I don't see how anyone could find her to be rude, she extremely sweet and really cares about your success. If you participate in class, this course is a breeze. Her exams are easy; they are pretty much straight from the lecture slides but with different numbers. I can't wait to take 112 with her!
Good at explaining concepts but exams are very hard. Exam averages are in D range. If you approach her with questions, she will just say, "You should already know this". Don't recommend her.
If I have to hear her make the same Swimming analogy one more time I am going to jump from the top of the Library. Class is easy but do yourself a favor and find a different prof.

I had her this semester for 111, and I don't know what people are talking about when they say she is rude. She is a very sweet professor, and genuinely wants you to succeed. You can tell because she makes her exams very straightforward. If you understand every lecture slide, you will get 100 on the exam - that simple. You can talk during quizzes.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: I don't usually post stuff on teachers like this but somethin she said in class today rubbed me the wrong way. Some girl asked her a question and her response was "This is a waste of time" I don't know what kinda teacher says something like that.
reviews.rating_tags: TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: She is extremely unprofessional and even condescending when students ask her questions in class. Stay away from this rude woman at all cost
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Every other word she says is "YAAS?" It is literally the most annoying thing in the world. Lady, expand your vocabulary, you're a professor for God's sake.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: This class requires a large time commitment between the weekly discussions, quizzes, and homework assignments. Attendance is mandatory due to clicker grades. She does not curve anything, but there won't be anything on the exams that wasn't on the lecture slides or in a homework problem. A single note card is allowed on exams, which is a godsend.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: PHYS121 with her is cut and dried. Do the online prelectures before every class and the homeworks every week. Lecture clarifies the online content. The exams are exactly like questions she goes over in class. The only thing that's sort of difficult about this class is the volume and and frequency of homework activities.

Did not use the textbook. Prelectures and homework online . Her lectures are helpful, she puts up lecture outlines. Open neighbor quizzes every Friday. 3 exams and final. She does not curve at all. This class also had discussion which is conceptual but helpful.

This class requires a lot of your time and energy. If you slack on things, then you wont learn and you wont do well. I found that the best way to study was to go over old quizzes and exams. She puts the hard questions on the exams and really tests you knowledge. So make sure to study hard! Great and cute personality.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: Physics is a challenging course that requires a lot of effort from both the student and professor.  Dr. Cui understands this and is strongly devoted to holding up her end of the bargain while encouraging us to hold up our end.  This class is not easy, but if you go to the lectures, get help, and do the work, you will be just fine in this class.

Good teacher, if you put in the work and do the homework and come to class prepared, you are set up to do well. Dr. Cui understands that Physics is a subject where you can often fool yourself into thinking that you are prepared when you are not. She stresses the importance of solo practice to understand the concepts. The discussion material is good
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: I'm a biology major and absolutely hate physics. She made me somewhat enjoy it. She was an amazing professor and always explained everything. She gave you all the materials and more to succeed and learn the material. The exams are straight forward with no tricks. Homework didn't help me but it helps your grade. I would highly recommend to anyone.

Take the class with the intention of actually learning the material instead of relying on a curve people! This is basic physics, not rocket science so just put in the hours, show up to class,read the book and ask for help when you need it and you are fine. If you take pride/interest in what you do it all works out. Great Professor!

Exams are only hard if you let them be. Dr. Lili actively encourages use of study groups, S.I. sessions, TAs,  and office hours. Her exam questions are very similar to the past exams and the homework/quizzes she assigns. As long as you read the book and actually do the homework you should be fine.  I liked her humor and approachable personality.

Literally the worst professor ever. She doesn't explain anything clearly. Unfortunately her accent is a barrier and she is even harder to understand when she's yelling at us for not being able to immediately grasp concepts. Ridicules students who do not understand things. Be prepared to teach yourself.
I don't think she was a very good teacher. She's nice but hard to understand. Tough grader too. Wouldn't recommend

Dr. Cui is nice and her lectures are somewhat helpful, but attendance is mandatory due to clickers, and occasionally she'll yell at people for talking. I wish she made lectures optional. However, she does try to make the class fun and cares about everyone. The final is insanely hard, though, and she refuses to curve it.

Dr. Cui's accent makes it difficult to understand her at times. However, if you read ahead of class and put a decent amount of effort, the class is not hard at all. You're even allowed to have note cards with formulas on it. There's no reason to be getting lower than a B in this class unless you didn't put the effort/time needed.

Lecture is completely useless. She doesn't give examples to questions assigned for homework, and neither does the textbook. Some of homework questions are plug and chug, but the harder ones are impossible to figure out by yourself. Hard class already, she just makes it 10x harder.

Take the negative reviews with a grain of salt. I really liked Dr. Cui. There is a large volume of information to absorb, but she explains what she wants you to know, and she stays on topic and does a lot to try and prepare you for her exams. The questions on the exams follow from the type of questions you receive from the homework assigned.
She has an accent but eventually it becomes easy to understand, make sure you understand every question from the reading quiz because she might not bring any of the questions up again until the test
