She is impossible to understand. Its hard to concentrate on the material when you're too busy deciphering her English. Exams are far more difficult than anything problems she goes over in lecture. Tough grader.  Unless you're the best world's best independent learner, do not take this class.

I loved Dr. Cui; she was so nice and always so happy!  I thought she did a pretty good job of explaining things.  I also thought she was funny, in her own special way.  The exams were challenging, but fair (the average was almost always a 75).  She has a heavy Chinese accent which some people hate, but I thought it made things more interesting.

Terrible professor. As a  terrible accent making it hard to understand her. Also, she skips over key concepts. You have to look at the book and learn on your own. She also makes the homework 10x harder than what is in the book, often leaving you with no idea on what to do.

Attendance is mandatory. Prof. is not clear on what exactly to expect on actual exams and does not cover some important concepts in class thoroughly. Hard on grade; there is no curve even with two exam averages in the 60s. Study using the learning goals and the book to understand the concepts fully and do well on exams.

Cute. She's great! I hated physics before her! She made it very tangible. Exams are kinda a crunch.make sure and read the questions properly! Do the past exams. She's really down to earth. Clicker quizzes every Friday you can do with friends. Pay attention in class you'll be fine. Would recommend her! Good luck!

Awful professor for 112. Doesn't curve, even though the average for one of our exams was a 63% (the other exams weren't much better). Explains basic concepts pretty well, but the exam questions are about 10x harder than anything she explains. Also talks down to her students regularly. Avoid this professor like the plague.
too hard on grade

She's pretty nice and helpful. Has this positive attitude most of the time. Like she always say in the class, you'll have to work for your grades. This is not that bad of a class. If you work hard enough, you'll earn a good grade. For exams, study everything esp past exams. IMPORTANT TO SHOW UP IN CLASS

Lili has a strong accent but it is understandable. Her teaching is all over the place—even if you pay attention in class and take down everything said, she will undoubtedly have left out a few key pieces of information that you will probably need for the homework and exams. Sweet woman but not great at teaching physics.

She's very enthusiastic in class and I can understand her at times. But I feel like the way she teaches is different than that of the book and when doing the homework it's more related to the book than what she teaches.

Dr. Cui is without a doubt one of my favorite professors at UMBC! She's very enthusiastic, extremely approachable, kind, and even funny! I had her for 121, and although her class was hard, it was very doable. Dr. Cui is a great person and an amazing professor! I would wholeheartedly recommend her to prospective students!

Dr. Cui is one of the loveliest people I have met at UMBC. She is brilliant and enthusiastic, and will do as much as she can to help you. I enjoyed both 121H and 122. I giggle at her silliness all the time; her English isn't great, but this doesn't affect her teaching effectiveness, but rather makes her highly amusing. My favorite professor so far!

Love this professor. She is every nice and helpful. Very smart and knows what she is talking about. Go to class, pay attention, and study and you will get a good grade. I got an A in 121 and a B in 122. Highly recommend her.

Dr. Cui is the most amazing Physics professor I have ever had. She is adorable, interesting, and loves interacting with her students. I wish I could have her again for 122H. I'm not even a Physics major, and I still loved the class.

Let me start off by saying I got an A in her PHYS 121 class. She is a below average professor and probably the worst one I've had at UMBC. She is unclear and akward. She regularly asks a 300 seated lecture questions expecting a response. She often pauses and asks (in a 300 seated lecture hall) why someone is talking. Thankfully I studied hard.

She is not good at teaching physics. You will have to learn the majority of the subject by reading the text and by using the discussion board for online homework. She is not a very approachable professor and often seems to be temperamental. Although she mentions that she is willing to help you, it sure doesn't seem that way when you talk to her.
She doesn't understand the nature of physics, and will fail you on an exam for no reason.  She also likes to yell at her students in the classroom.
Thick accent, very hard to understand, and she relies heavily on the book. As long as you can learn by yourself you will be fine, the book is helpful, she is not.

I am baffled in all honesty that she is a doctor of our discipline. At times when she can simply answer the question she'll tell you she already talked about it. She doesn't cover material that you get tested on. She expects you to read on your own. Turned the class completely online last minute and told people to drop if if they didn't like that.
In any case where a student makes a mistake, sometimes not even their fault, she says oh well and you just have to take a chunk out of your grade.

This prof is about as bad as they get. Her instructions are so ambiguous, she will never clarify and then will take off points for literally every little thing, even when it's clearly her fault. She quite literally will take points off for the ENTIRE class when her instructions are wrong, rather than clarify that she was unclear or made a mistake

Much easier for 421; 3 projects, 5 exams. The last exam is very easy; projects are super easy; professor nice. Lectures were going through textbook; lots of hints of what's on exam. Won't allow pictures in class, so get ready to write! Grading criteria unclear. Behavior also graded. Sometimes, we did stuff like paging & banker's algo on board.
no clear grading criteria made (projects) r. Lectures are okay. Prepared to read a lot
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Course consisted of four tests, and 3-4 projects. The projects had many little requirements and you're forced to start it way before it's due or you lose 10-15% on it. The tests were relatively easy, attendance was 20% of the grade and the lectures taught me nothing.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Test heavy

reviews.comment: The biggest issues are with the project. They are documents that are filled with information that is spread out. Requirements are buried deep in there that will make you lost a lot of points if you don't read carefully. She FORCES you to start the projects early or you lose a lot of points. Grading for projects takes forever.

attendance mandatory. Explains projs. in the beginning of class and ans. questions as well. Easier 421 course layout compared to other profs. for sure. Has couple of tests in class on lockdown browser. Projs are lengthy but if instructions are followed then its fine. She does calls out students if instructions not followed. Can explai slides more.

Dr. Larson did not have intense lectures, just covered the essential ethics/writing skills. Not a tough grader, she knows this is a writing class for CS. If you put a little time/care into the hw/proj you can easily get an A. Larson's class is laid back, but that also means you learn less about the subject than other 304 classes.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: listen to rate my professor. If you can afford to take it another semester with a different teacher it will be far more worth your time. Project instructions are a joke. Attendance is mandatory, However lectures are her reading off of the homework. Doesn't enroll in CMI meaning you MUST purchase the ZyBook instead of it being included in tuition.

Very kind lady and very lenient grader which makes getting an A easy but she doesn't know the course material as well as she should in my opinion. Still overall it was an interesting class with ample opportunities for extra credit. I personally think the only thing missing was just a bit more knowledge on the subject since I felt lost a lot.

Larson is very generous, giving extensions on projects and open to regrades. The only problem I can say is her lectures. Usually, you leave lectures knowing you're gonna need to look more into the material later. One more thing, that's unrelated to Larson, if you're gonna take 421, don't take it with a M-chip Mac Laptop. SO many complications.

She is a great professor. I took 3 comp-sci courses with Professor Larson and I learned a lot. She allows us to be able to understand what we are learning and effort does have to be put in for a good grade. But at this point taking 300-400 level courses, you shouldn't expect easy. I recommend 481 if she is teaching.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Her ethics class was pretty easy. Only had two writing assignments, one research paper, four tests, and a group presentation. She does allow extra credit if you need it. Grading is lenient. However, she is a little disorganized and lectures are not that useful other than for tests. She is a nice person and understanding. Good class with her.

Professor Larson is a great professor for CMSC 304. I would recommend her for this writing intensive course, especially since she is a very lenient grader. Keep in mind that attendance is not mandatory, but there are in-class graded assignments that you must be present to receive credit for.

Professor Larson seems nice at first, but doesn't know how to teach well, and struggles a lot with technology. She doesn't seem very knowledgeable about her subject matter, and seems to not care much about the class and the students.

This is a great class, but Larson is not the right professor to be teaching it. During lectures, it was clear that she did not fully understand the concepts herself and was learning at the same time as us. The projects are not impossible if you have good programming skills with C and Linux, and they don't have a lot to do with the (poor) lectures.

The lecture itself is boring. In terms of a breakdown 10% attendance, 10% exercises, 40% projects, 40% exams. exams are all on quizlet. Every professor gives the same projects which are hard, and the reason for the high difficulty. If you show up and kinda pay attention you will get at least a B. Neso academy is your friend.

If you know C, and know how to read an API, you should be reasonably set for the projects. Tests were a complete joke in comparison, and weighted equally. Lectures were lifeless - she reads straight off the book. I don't think I, nor anyone else, retained any of the material. Somewhat excusable for an elective, not so much for OPERATING SYSTEMS!

Wanted to wait til the near end of the semester to write a review. She structured the class very well and in such a way it took away a lot of the stress of online classes. 5 smaller tests rather than the typical 3 large exams and she wasn't responsible for the projects which were the worst part. Class time mostly felt like a waste though.

Lectures consist of her reading off the optional zybook for about 30 mins, and then a 'breakout activity' with minimal context - rinse and repeat. Tests aren't bad, but they're biweekly. Treat them like quizzes. Projects are insane in comparison. She'll cover locks for 1 lecture, and then say "Write an IPC kernel module from scratch!" Avoid.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: This is not a professor you want to take. Class consisted of her reading the book to us. Not even the required textbook, but an optional one. At this point, I am not sure she even knows how to code. She either won't or can't give you details about specifics of examples. The breakout activities usually have nothing to do with the projects.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Has absolutely no idea how to teach. This class has fully made me realize I really pay UMBC just for them to pay professors to tell me to teach myself. Takes very little time to explain very complex concepts, is blind to the situation of her students and overall just shouldn't be teaching. Seems like a nice lady, not a good professor.

Terrible. She placed us in breakout rooms today and my groupmate cried. She thinks she's teaching and just doesn't. She gives you maybe 5 minutes of her basically telling you to google and then shoves you in a breakout room to do an activity you don't know how to do. Very few people are keeping up, she simply just cannot teach. Avoid if possible.

Maybe it's the CMSC department's fault for teaching students C++ and python and then all of a sudden we're expected to know C beforehand to complete projects but this is the worst thing ever. pointless group activities during class and we haven't learned anything in relation to our assignments. Do yourself a favor and look elsewhere

I am less than a month into a class with her. I can already tell you the other review was not written by a student, in fact it mentions easy grading but was posted when we had no grades. She lectures with no slides, and any breakout activities are irrelevant to assignments. We've learned basically nothing related to the current project. Avoid.

She is an amazing professor. OS is a hard class, but she puts herself out there to really give a fighting chance to her students. She uses an online learning service with visuals that is great for learning topics and she is an easier grader that takes joy in students passing. Projects that are the same for all sections may break backs though...

I had Dr. Lane in fall '25 and I loved his lectures! I took his class for the gen-ed credit and because I was very interested in the course (compsci major lol). Def look over the powerpoints, all of the test questions come from that and the group wksts. The extra credit was very generous and helps a bunch if you get points off on tests/wksts. 10/10
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS UNLESS YOU MUST. Professor Lane assumes every student is as insanely interested in the content of the course as he is and creates his exams as such. Participating in class basically guarantees you a C but prepare to fail every exam unless you spend an obscene amount of time reading the textbook and preparing for the exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Group projects

reviews.comment: I took professor Lanes ARCH 200 class and I liked it. While I barely got by with a C, the class is interesting and professor Lane is a nice, smart guy. He jokes around a bit in class and is an overall pretty decent professor. He is kinda strict on grading and his lectures are dense. The class itself is hard, so I think his rating is a littleee low.

GOAT, so passionate bro, love him, wish I could go to Greece with him for the digs and I'm not even doing anything for archaeology, art, or culture like that bro... he is genuinely the goat idk what to tell you
I lowkey didn't do the readings and still did amazing cuz his lectures are so interesting, go to his class bro, he is just the best

I took this class as a gen ed and had absolutely no interest in the topic. Prof understands that most students feel the same way in this class and adds a lot of humor to lectures. He is very approachable and even 2 years after I took the class we still say hi and chat when we cross paths. Only complaint is that his handwriting is difficult to read.

Overall, decent guy. He Makes the class fun due to his high energy and enthusiasm for his work. HOWEVER, get ready to read, in ARCH 100 there are so many terms you need to memorize in order to be successful. He provides enough resources for Exams but no study guide... rather you must look over past PowerPoints.

unless you like reading, hard tests, and critical thinking, do NOT take this class. he's an absolute a-hole to his students and answers questions with a question. stopped reading stuff after week 2 because I was in 3 other classes and still passed with an A (barely). he's a tough grader and just likes to hear himself talk. awful do not take
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Test heavy

reviews.comment: This course is ideal for archaeology majors. The energetic professor loves teaching Greek and genuinely wants students to succeed. While passing the class isn't hard, many fail. Instead of curving grades, he assigns extra work to balance scores. If you need a culture credit, consider another course. But if you like challenges this class is perfect.

I found his class very interesting, and it's one of the classes where you can really tell the Professor is enthusiastic about their field. I took this class for the culture credit, but it's not a good choice if you're looking for an easy A. 
We had about one homework per week, and the final paper is a easy way to bring your grade up at the end.

A lot of people may have not liked this class, but I enjoyed it. The lectures had a lot of information, but Mr. Lane highlighted the important stuff and even had slides with main idea questions and vocabulary, both of which I used to study for exams. It also helped that for each exam, we got to use an index card as a cheat sheet.

The exams can be tough, it was especially tough for me since I'm bad with memorizing information like this however just like all classes you get better after the first exam if you study back on them and use your cheat sheet that he lets you use to your advantage. His final cumulative exam was extremely easy which bumped up my grade from a C to B.

This class is not an easy gen ed to take for your arts and humanities credit. Do not take if you want it just for a credit. You have to study and memorize slides and understand the content. He is also a yapper he yaps a lot. Tests are hard. very hard. Also there's homework every week. You can't miss a class at all.

I will say this once, and once only. If you choose to take this class… you better be super smart and able to retain A LOT of information because the lectures and material that is required is insanely challenging. As someone who does great in classes like this, this was by far one of, if not the hardest class i've ever taken. proceed with caution.

I see a lot of reviews complaining about this class's difficulty as a 100lvl. To pass this class you literally just need to listen and do brief readings. Most of the material needed for tests is *very* clearly labeled on lecture slides. He constantly tells you in lecture if something will be important for exams. Just don't try to cram.

Dr Lane is great guy y but as a teacher he is the worst, he is so trapped in his own bubble he does not understand the burden he puts on his students in his world this is the only class were taking his course load is egregious and test are impossible anyone saying this class is for majors is wrong i'm a major and the others  with me are struggling

If you really read these ratings, they are mostly about his PERSONALITY and not his TEACHING style. This class is meant for ancient studies majors and not just for an easy A, there are easier culture credits you can take. The course name/ work is very misleading and nothing like what you think. Please take my warning.

Nice person, NOT a good professor! Test are extremely difficult and he always rambles while you're taking exams which is annoying and if you're thinking of taking this class as a Arts and Humanities requirement, DON'T. It WILL tank your grade. Only thing good was that homework assignments were graded on completion. Attendance was required.

Fantastic Professor, lots of energy, good at teaching, however the tests are HARD, for a 100 class the difficulty is high, and requires lots of studying and memorizing. If you want to take this class for your GPA I wouldn't suggest it, but you will enjoy the professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Dr.Lane is an amazing professor. I sat in the front, recorded every lecture, did all the homework, took detailed notes, and still failed. . Dr.Lane is extremely kind and intelligent and the fact that I failed says more about me then him. I will say, it is the hardest class I've ever taken and it is a 100 level. I will be retaking this class!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Test heavy

reviews.comment: Great professor, extremely enthusiastic, flexible and all around great lecture. Professor taught material well and demonstrated knowledge of material.
For a 100 level course, it is WAY too hard. Extremely passive agressive person.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Lane is an amazing professor! He's really fun to talk to and is incredibly smart and well-spoken. He's always very passionate when teaching but be sure to memorize for tests and pay attention during lectures or you may miss something. Offers extra credit opportunities and makes you earn your grade. Would def take again.

Professor Lane is a very knowledgeable professor. He's very passionate about archaeology and is very lax. I would say that this course isn't geared well toward people not majoring in Archaeology. It definitely takes some prior knowledge and/or heavy research and studying to completely understand everything. Attending lectures is the most important.

He's a great teacher, easygoing, funny, and wicked smart. Best professor I expect to have. This course is an information load that includes a lot of work and memorization. Stay on top of the lecture material, do the homeworks thoroughly and review them well before tests. Tough course, but with hard work you'll do fine.

You can tell he cares, but he gives a lot lot LOT of homework and classwork. Your homework are the answers to quizzes, but doesn't give personal feedback nor direct feedback. The info he does give is in riddles and not very useful. MAKE SURE YOU BUY THE BOOK! Overall, he cares, but doesn't have my style of learning.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Inspirational

reviews.comment: Prof. Lane is great! He will make you work for your grade, and expect a lot of readings and weekly lectures. Attendance is also mandatory but he is really flexible and willing to work with you as long as you talk to him. Would take again
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Lane makes archaeology fun and interesting. I am an engineering major who usually has professors with very minimal verbal communication skills so he was a breath of fresh air. He obviously cares about his students and emphasizes the important material. Overall I was excited to attend lectures, even in pandemic end-times. :)

I needed an elective as I am a MechE major. Loved Prof. Lane as a person! But he was a terrible lecturer. He often went on tangents explaining his experience in X country, the tests were INSANE. If you are NOT A HISTORY PERSON DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS. The class is scrambled and you wont pass if you skip lecture. Take a SOCY or something else.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Amazing professor! Super kind and funny, really knowledgeable and passionate about his field of study. Only 1 4-5 page essay. Takes attendance and there are classwork grades, so come to class. Gives really helpful study guides before exams, fill them out and study them and you'll be good

He's a really cool guy who's very knowledgable in his field. It didn't feel like a 100 level course at times because of the material/concepts but he color codes what you need to know for the test and his study guides are really helpful. A challenging class but if you come to class and take notes on the lecture you will be fine!

His power points are worthless. There is not enough information on them to help you study for the exams. However, he is a very nice guy and he tries to make his class as exciting as possible but its hard to because pottery is not an exciting topic.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Gives good feedback--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: I love Dr. Lane as a person. As a prof, he caters to future archeologists and grades toughly due to that. He gives extra credit and wants his students to do well, but his tests are a bear. Scour your textbook and notes to memorize details and even then knowing all the info to get an A might be difficult. Take him if you want to be an archeologist.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Pros: Ivy league quality. Cons: Ivy league difficulty.

Prof. Lane is an amazing lecturer. Class is mandatory because he does group work and you get the credit by being there, not by completing the work. His powerpoints and the stuff he puts online are basically the tests, he color codes what is important. Easy A if you study and pay attention. He is just a classy guy.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Intro to archeology. Fantastic lectures, didn't really use the book. Come to lecture & listen or take notes. Test questions underlined in powerpoints and posted online. Very approachable and friendly with students. Had a crush, sat in the front, listened to everything, would have been an easy A if I hadn't forgotten about a test.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: As long as you keep up with posted readings for discussion and use your book to study you'll be fine. Dr. Lane can be intimidating since he seems to know everything there is to know, but he grades pretty generously. Take advantage of activities outside of class as well as his office hours. You'll learn a lot. And he's a great connection to have.

I absolutely loved this class. Attendance isn't mandatory but he's a great lecturer. If you don't attend you're just making the class that much more difficult for yourself. I never read the book, but if you pay attention to lecture and review the powerpoints he posts you'll excel. I only got a B because I forgot about a test and didn't review.

Michael Lane is very good at projecting his voice( to the point where he doesn't even use a mic ), he makes jokes, and even though he knows students won't respond, he is always happily exclaiming good afternoon when he enters the lecture hall. He is willing to help any who approach, and is overall very friendly. Would take his class again.

Dr. Lane is extremely well spoken , and his lectures are absolutely necessary for whatever course you're taking. Enthusiastic and helpful, Dr. Lane gives extremely helpful resources in order to pass his tests and assignments. Would not recommend for non-majors, unless you are good at memorization.

great instructor if your major is archaeology, but he is extremely enthusiastic about the topic and gives wayyyyyy too much work if you're just taking it for your general art credit. wouldn't recommend taking this

He's a good professor. He's very into what he does. His tests are very difficult. He even admitted this to the class after the semester was over, and admitted that the grading data was similar to an upper level class. He promptly curved the class. He's tough, lots of reading, but good.

Dr. Lanes Arch 100 class is one of the tougher 100 level course because of the amount of memorization and detail on the test. If you, at the very least, skim the reading, go over his PowerPoint notes and glance over his optional reading questions, you can easily pass his tests. If you expect this class to be a breeze, you are sadly mistaken.
Great teacher. Really loves what he teaches. Projects his voice loud and clear. Don't take this class for a gen ed because his test are extremely difficult.

Dr. Lane is a very knowledgeable professor. However, his lectures are extremely overly-complicated and can really disinterest you real quickly. If you have interest in Archaeology, then this is the class for you, otherwise, find a different class for Arts & Humanities or you will hate this class to death. Lots of random information thrown at you.

I honestly do not know HOW he has such a high rating. Maybe he's a better professor in his upper level classes, but he expects WAY too much out of a 100-level course. He expects you to remember every tiny detail that comes out of his mouth - it's more of a HISTORY course than an archaeology course. Do yourself a favor and don't take ARCH100.

DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS if you want an easy A for a general requirement. He expects you to memorize the slightest details of what he says in class. He gives study guides, but they are very vague considering the amount of details he expects you to memorize for the test. I wasted so much time studying for this class which isn't even part of my major.

Although this course had a lot of memorization and note taking, Professor Lane was so sweet! He is very caring towards his students and wants everyone to do well! Don't take this class if you don't want to work, however it's very easy to pass if you try!

Dr Lane is a fantastic lecturer and a great teacher for UMBC to have. He is passionate in his archaeology and very professional. I went to his office hours before every test, and he helped me clarify ideas. He was everything you can ask for from a professor. The class Arch 100 itself is a memory test, be aware!

Professor Lane is an awesome professor! However, his tests and the class itself is very hard. You must go to class and pay attention and take notes on everything he says to do well. Tests are all short answer, no multiple choice. Lane is very knowledgeable and interesting!

I loved him! He was very knowledgable and seemed passionate about what he was teaching. He gave extra points on the tests to help improve grades, and he always made study guides. I found the classes interesting even though he sometimes spoke a little too quickly. Overall, I thought he was a reasonable professor.

Professor Lane is extremely knowledgeable.  He throws a lot of information at you in class, but it's not too hard to keep up with if you take notes and pay attention.  He is EXTREMELY helpful during his office hours and wants to see you succeed. He even gave me an essay question that would be on the test, just because I came to his office for help.
Professor Lane is awesome, he is extremely knowledable in his craft and will give you alot of good bar travia too but he expects alot so don't be that guy.

Professor Lane is extremely knowledgeable and helpful.  He's charismatic and wants the students to do well, but he also expects you to put effort into class too.  You can't get by without taking notes in this class, or you will fail, though if you can't find something in your notes or his powerpoints, he's very helpful during office hours.

Hands down the most charismatic professor at this school. In his class, no cell phones are present; 50 people crammed into a room are spellbound by his flawless diction and well prepared lectures. Dr Lane has been to all of the locations of Greek lore, and his no nonsense style of teaching ensures an effective learning environment. Also gnarly tats

Hard professor, but knowledgeable. Do not take this class if you want an easy A, though an A can be achieved with hard effort. Some material is interesting, some is very dry. Nice guy, but hard tests. His study guides are sometimes not so consistent with his tests, and he has a love for details, so you have to memorize to the heart. Use the guides.

Not the sort of intro class I had in mind. Very detailed and the tests are incredibly hard, he talks down to you because he's an archaeologist and you're not. Do yourself a favor a skip this class if you don't have hours and hours to study for an INTRO class...so annoying.

This is not an easy A class. The material is very hard to understand. He goes over the material too quickly in class. Gives a study guide before the exam. Do the study guide and you will get a B on the exam. He expects the student to write in excessive details on the exam for the essay questions.However, he is very helpful if you are having trouble
Not easy, difficult to concentrate in class because of the rambling. From now on always check ratemyprofessor.com to get the best professors.

Professor Lane was a great professor but the material is a little dry. He provides study guides that are basically the test. The one problem is he expects certain things in each exam answer. So if you miss one part that the question really didn't ask, you will lose some points. Still was a slightly interesting  class.

He gives you everything you need, exams come from questions on handouts, which he gives answers to in lecture. He does go off on a lot of linguistic tangents, but some of them are interesting. Study a little and get an A, or do nothing (but whine and complain) like the others and get a B. The one textbook is painful to read, art book is good.
He's hard to follow and talks too fast. Its hard to take notes. Class is boring.
he gives the hand-outs of the powerpoints so the students could take notes as he goes through the slides in class. the class is boring but the professor is nice not to mention pretty cute.

Seriously if you're thinking oh he's tough, but I'm an academic weapon, or he's tough but ill learn. Really don't take him it snot worth it at all the class copes and makes jokes of it, but it's not funny he's not a good teacher or p[professor. really just avoid muchedere. -former 4.0 MechE RIP

Nice guy, doesn't look out for his students though. I'm doing well but not because of him. Do not recommend. Said he wants engineers to average a C on exams. He wants you to know the theory behind things, I'm not a math major bro.

Look, he's a very nice guy. He would do great in a podcast of some sort. But his class is VERY disorganized. Exams are brutal, he will barely prepare you, and his lectures are pretty much meaningless. His exams are FAR harder than the quiz and homeworks. Do not I repeat DO NOT fall behind. This is an unforgiving class, you'd rather take it at CC.

Lecture is completely worthless, but he posts online lectures (about 3hours online for every 1hour of in person lecture) that are more thorough and basically mandatory since in person wont be enough. About once every 3 lectures he gives out a helpful hint for the upcoming quiz/exam. Doesn't do examples, he just points to a prefilled out note shell.

If you don't attend the lectures it's your funeral. Conceptual focus, memorization heavy, some short algebraic proofs expected. Tough tests and quizzes just from how much is on them -- even when I didn't get stuck I never had time to go back and check my answers. Illuminated lin alg for me, but I found it hard to keep up. Rounded me up to an A.

He expects you to watch MULTIPLE 70+ min lecture videos before class and then proceeds to yap during his supposed "lectures". He doesn't give you time to process what he's teaching or break it down for you in class, he runs through practice problems at lightning speed and says "good enough." No practice exams, it's just you and the book.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: unreasonably difficult exams not like the quizzes. Very unpredictable. got a 94 on his first midterm. then studied 12+ hours for the second one. I'm PRAYING I got a 65. Only reason I'm not dropping is bc I had lenient TA quiz graders. and I did well on the first exam. Completely ruined my chance for an A. Might even get a C.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: My dog would have taught calc 3 better than him. If you need practice exam to study there none as the only thing is the textbook and his lecture. His exam are multi choice but no partial credit and there hard as he LOVE put in trig in. Did I also mention he love his own voice. Before the exam he yap for 10-20 min and the question are long too.
Just no a good professor

I can't stress enough how misleading the very small pool of reviews are. I assume there are only this many because everyone else who might've left one refused at the thought of seeing his name alone. Take any other professor, only then can you "visualize" a decent lecture and course.

Words don't describe how bad he is when people say 0 practice, literally 0 practice. Like, I kid you not, it's like learning to swim and the instructor says, "Dude, just read how to swim." Like, did I not pay you to teach that????
So slow think's he's funny and kind of mean.
Worst experience of my life

I've never seen a more disorganized professor. Practice exams Nope. Practice quizzes Nope. Decent lecture notes Absolutely not. He posts videos, not even lecture notes.

You will be examined and quizzed on the book, not his teachings, because he doesn't even no what he's doing; he's just talking, and he loves his own voice.

I had never taken a college math class before since I was in my first semester, and this was not the easiest class to start with. Muscedere spends a lot of time on some things and not enough on others and it makes for confusion, but as long as you study and work ahead of the class in the text book, you will understand his lectures.

Pretty good professor for a pretty hard class. Exams are ~1/2 multiple choice, so credit is all or nothing for that section. TA's were very helpful. Best way to study for exams is doing the recommend textbook practice problems. Lectures can be kinda fast paced, but uploads video lectures where he goes slower and more in-depth. STUDY!Calc 3 is hard

If you're not a good test-taker I would avoid this class, tests & quizzes are about 80% of your grade. Prof Muscedere is good, but he often runs through practice problems and just says "good enough". The TA's are somewhat helpful, but get ready to learn a lot of the material outside of class. If you're good at math you might be fine.

Do NOT take this prof, or this class at UMBC. You will fight for your life just to get a 70% in the class. Half the class is currently failing (exam 3 is coming up soon), and everyone is teaching themselves. TA's are trying to salvage the situation but prof does not heed their recommendations. This 4 credit class turned into 8 credits of work.

Fantastic guy, and extremely passionate about what he teaches. He wants you to succeed. His lectures are fast-paced and it can be easy to fall behind, but if you put in the work and go to class, you should be fine. If you have a good TA, they'll be a lifesaver. Check WebAssign weekly; he sometimes forgets to put the homework on Blackboard.

I think he's a nice/funny professor but I just couldn't learn from him. He would fly by lectures pretty fast and he won't even take the time to explain it. I heard more than half of the students withdrew from his class because everyone was failing. I would not recommend taking him if math isn't your strong suit.

He isn't hard, I just couldn't learn from him. Nice guy, but I was thoroughly confused. Pay attention to and practice class problems because they'll show up on quizzes and tests. DO THE PREREQ EXAM because it's basically free points. He changes grading in favor of students and will feed you out of his hand. I just didn't understand his lectures.

Doesn't lecture that well and the study material he provides was never of any help, ever. I was practically teaching myself the concepts the entire semester. Also had hour long video lectures in addition to the in person lectures that he wanted you to watch.
My main concern with him is that he does not respond to him emails. He barely gives you anything to help you study. You might as well learn the material on your own.

He seemed like a nice guy that tried to relate to the class and keep it upbeat but I found the lectures did not teach the material as he just went over example problems and skipped a lot of them. The discussion sections required with the class were the most helpful to me as long as you have a good TA. I would say he was average compared to others.

Was already going to leave a good review before I missed my final and he was gracious enough to let me make it up. Tough class but if you read and put the work in beforehand, lectures are very helpful/engaging & you get out what you put in. Hard teacher but I have a ton of respect for him, would absolutely take him again. Made me enjoy math again

Great guy, friendly and willing to help you if necessary. Also lenient with grading if you talk to him about it. The learning curve gets a little steep midway through but he's willing to help if necessary. Highly recommend, but lord is the homework an incarnation from hell. You will never experience a class with homework as awful as this one's.
kNOWLEDGEABLE BUT TOUGH TO UNDERSTANDE

Amazing Breadth of information, and shows how powerful Linear Algebra is. He emphasizes from the beginning that He wants you to pass. Please, take him up on that offer. His Quizzes are great, exams more than fair. and all he asks is that you attend class. Be a good student do your homework and come to class and you will pass with flying colors.

Very friendly and teaches the material in a very clear manner. Explains what will be on the quizzes and exams and guides you through the questions after passing them out. That being said, his homework is straight from the textbook and is incredibly frustrating and time consuming, especially with problems having you jump to older sections.
If you show up to class, do the work you'll get an A. He helps students with assignments too. Easy A for me.

I took math 155 in the summer. I have difficulty in math classes and  I  usually end up with D or F.  Because  the class was taught during the summer, materials were taught a bit fast pace. Make sure you study, do your homework and ask questions, go to tutors then you should be fine. Today, I am happy/proud to say that I passed the class.

100% great guy, who will do his best to make sure you pass. He get so excited about the subject and really engages the class. Stayed after class for hours to tutor students who still wanted help. He understands the textbook isn't very helpful, and he helps a lot on quizzes. BEWARE: He assigns more homework than you've ever known.

Nice introductory course. Eight lectures based on very thorough notes which are helpful to refer to after class. Homework assignments based off lecture are fair and reinforce concepts. Helpful professor, readily answers student questions and grades fairly. Great course, I recommend it to any math major!
If you attend class he really does his best to make sure you pass.
He is simply the worst I've ever had.  Take Riley instead if you must take 106
Good teacher, tough class
Very lenient and understanding. Corny at times but still fun. Helps you on quizzes and tests. He wants "all his students to pass his class".

Overall a very challenging class but learned a lot.  A bit fast paced, and had to race thru quizes/exams in order to complete on time, at the same time getting bogged down in row reduction.  Learn to do it FAST and ACCURATE.  Not sure about some previous comments.. grad students??  Reviews were interesting, but similar problems really not on exams.

Hard Class but Good professor. I think he can do much better on handling the material that is provided so he can avoid the want to be smart grad students. I believe they are the once who make the class harder. As far as for the professor, he is good and very helpful. His final is basically similar to previous cls exams but long.G2 his review sessio

Class is set up for you to do well.  If you do the homework and actually digest the work, you'll be fine in the class.  Helped out with grades as he wants you to do well.  Funny guy, enjoyable to go to class.

A good teacher, can help if you ask. Gives a lot of extra credit. The class is hard. The test average was around 44. but if you study hard, or at least do better than others, you will be rewarded. Got an A!!!

Muscedere is a great guy and always willing to help a student during his time before class. The class is hard and you will need to put in the effort to do well. HW was a lot, exams were OK and quizzes were not too bad. He does tend to fly through the material fairly quickly but his PowerPoints help reinforce that. Be repaired to put some time in!!

he is a great teacher. A little bit hard, but at the end curves according to student's standing in the class. SO you may do not very good, but later you will get an A or B. Always helps if you ask. Hard work is rewarded.

Muscedere is an interesting man, weird but interesting, he tries to help his students as best as he can but the class is still very hard. The average is like a 65, exams are tough, quizzes are bogus but overall he is a nice guy, but being a nice guy doesn't help you pass the class.
UGH... AVOID HIM. He's helpful... but can't teach.
No Comments

Teaches the class like everyone is a graduate student in Mathematics and expects people to understand it as fast as he can teach it.  Does not give clear lectures, only rewrites on the board what is in the textbook.  Even with a curve at the end half the class failed.  Unless you want to learn the information on your own avoid him.
Avoiding this guy is the key to passing Math251. DO NOT TAKE.

The instructor is suppose to do the exams him self and give the students three times the time it took him. The final was long and I am sure if given to any instructor who was not part of the creation it would take them more that 40 minutes to do the exam. The final exam consisted of 12 full problems with sub parts. Get ready for Flux calculations.
No Comments

Amazing teacher, he actually cares about his students and he really tries hard to get across extremely difficult concepts.  And there is apparently an adjusted grading scale that isn't on the syllabus, so if you think you're failing, you're probably not.

I've never gotten lower than an A in any math class I've ever taken... and because of this guys final exam, I will probably get a C. Most professors allow you to have an equation sheet for exams and this guy doesn't, so unless you want to memorize like 50 equations for 1 test avoid this guy.

Hmm.I think when u are at this level of math, the stuff is not easy at all.This professor i think has done an excellent job in trying to explain mind blowing concepts. He was always avaiable for help before and after class. Homework was lengthy but exam questions were similar to homework. One of the best professor for MAth 251 if u want to learn.

ok.. Muscedere is a special teacher. Everything he teaches is STRAIGHT out of the book ( same numbers, same examples..) and the way he teaches is not the best. The only way to pass this class with an A is to get the old exams!!!! trust me on that..

I always tried to get help and he told me he dint have office hours but apparently he did. He was a good teacher but his grading is very questionable and really punishes you even if you understand the concepts or even get teh answers right. I ended up with a B because the curve saved me.

He's tough, that is for sure. HOWEVER, he is one of the best professors I have ever had. He is fair and actually cares about the students. He WANTS you to learn, which is a very fare thing for professors. His homeworks are a bit lengthy...but, you will never be surprised on exams. He makes sure you have the knowledge you will actually need.

Some of the grading methods were questionable, like a small detail being worth a large percentage of the problem value. There were only 2 quizzes all semester, wish there were a few more to get a feel for the material and for preperation for exams. The teacher was really interested in the material, but seemed to focus on theEEparts attheendofclass

overall he is a nice guy.  even though his lectures are straight from the book, he adds in a few extra helpful notes once in a while.  the high intensity of the exams was not expected at first due to the laid back nature of the class lectures.  he is very generous with the curve.

Mr. Muscedere genuinely cares about his students and their success in his class. His main downfall was his negative self-talk, which started on the very first day. When he talks bad about himself he looses the respect of his students. I would give him a C+. If he didn’t talk bad about himself so much, I’d give him a B+.

He's a good professor.  Explains much better than most math professors.  He is extremely helpful.  He wants his students to succeed and understand the material.  His exam reviews are really helpful.  The material was very difficult, he really takes the time and tries to make it clear to everyone - most math professors don't do this.
over all, hes a pretty good teacher, he knows what is to be taught and what students have to learn. he tells exactly what question will be on the exam. funny guy too lol

He was an excellent professor and did a wonderful job. Whenever anyone needs help he is always available and makes a conscious effort to help the students pass. He practically gives everyone the exam and quiz questions prior to the dates and is just a great professor all around.

Would not recommend taking him.  Reads stright from the book, which anyone can do by themselves.  His lectures are absoulutly no help whatsoever.  He "tell's" you what's on exams, which can focus study time, but has extremely questionable grading.  Get a different proffessor or wait to take the class if you can!!!

boring to sit through, but it's just the subject. He teaches out of the book making it easier to do the homework problems he assigns us. He tells you what's on the exam so if u study u'll get a decent grade. Nice guy... not a bad class

seems like a nice guy but isnt a good teacher. reads word for word from the book. helpful reviews yet his grading is very questionable... you may get the right answer but if u dont do it exactly as they do in the book, he wont understand and therefore you are wrong. be prepared to teach urself the material b/c he simply recites the book to u.

Look..the bottom line is that he wants you to know Calc 3! Dont expect to memorize things and fly through the class. He is a GREAT person with positive intentions. I never liked him until I visited his office hours after failing 3 exams due to my own problems. He curves remakably b/c I have a C. Dont take this class unless ur ready to learn Calc 3!
this guy is a moron.  he knows less than you do about calc.  without the textbook he is lost and hopeless. exams are intense.
He's a good guy, tests are easy and he spells out exactly whats going to be on them. Lectures aren't the best, and hw is alittle long, but overall not bad.

rookie teacher. does evrything str8 outof the book. first exam is hell. rest get better only b/c evry1 fails the 1st 1 and for rest of the exams he tells u exactly wats on it. DO NOT miss the review sessions. I got an A, i thougt i had a C...curves big time (he has to, otherwise evry1 would fail.Be prepared 2 READ the book on u'r own. good luck
Horrible. Everything everyone above has said is true. I dropped the class for the exact same reasons. He is a horrific teacher. Don't take him; If you are taking him, Drop the class now!!!
No Comments
Nice guy, very friendly. Lectures are a litte boring, but he'll answer anything you ask him. Will tell you exactly what you need to know for tests. Not my first choice, but not too bad.
tests are nightmares, not a bad guy though
He is pretty frenetic for the first month or so. After the first mid-term he tones it down a lot. Ends up being pretty good.
I ended up with a B in his class. He's very downgrading and reads slides word for word with no examples.

If you have him drop him. THis is not only a very hard math class, but very useless to take with him. He reads straight from the book, which is horrible, and his test are crazy. Not to mention he is the worst personality professor i have ever had.
He must be the worst teacher...ever.  If you already added this, drop it before it's too late.  I cannot stress to you how bad of a teacher he is.

Horrible teacher, I had to drop this class because it was so difficult, homework is very easy as is everything in class then come the tests and quizzes that completly screw you. The class average was in the mid 60's when I dropped.

horrible... condescending and rude, thinks everything should be "obvious", says "See? That's easy, right!?" when it isn't. Quizzes/Tests 10x harder than homework. Expects mastery of calculus concepts.  My Class Avg = 64%

Horrible horrible teacher.  Completely unclear, even for someone who's always liked math.  Homework and quiz questions much harder than what we learned in class.  May as well just read the book...and even that isn't great...

Dr. Narock leads a very manageable class that mixes lecture and labs well. You get to actually see the data you use in real world situations and you don't feel alone while doing it. He's very personable and I will miss taking his class as I pursue my major! Super kind guy.

Tom is a very kind and helpful professor that is available in and outside of class for help. His DMC 106 class at Goucher College was discussion and lecture based, and he made sure that you were able to do the work, not just struggle with it. I am very grateful to have had him as my professor- I'm not particularly skilled at math!

Great guy, the class was pretty easy as long as you read and do the HW. Quiz and exams are based on what is on the power points and some from the text. I find the exams were a lot easier when you do the practice quizzes that are online(from liang textbook) but trust me they are straight forward questions.

Overall, Dr. Narock is a really nice guy and he really wants his students to learn java. Java isn't a easy thing to learn nor is it an easy thing to teach. Some quizzes were open note, which was nice, and some weren't. Three exams, all multiple choice, couple of easy hws, and a final programming project. Not too bad if you just go to class

Expected perfection and will take off for things that she has not stated that you were supposed to do.  Make sure you practice and keep up and memorize all spelling and grammar. Not very welcoming or inspiring.
Her lectures are basically built up on the homework/textbook, so as long as you stay up to date you should be good. Tests weren't too bad either, again just do the homework and attend lectures.

does not teach much, and you need to basically learn on your own or else you are cooked on all of the tests for the class (which i was, except the final), luckily grade is mostly determined by VHL assignments otherwise i would've failed
Not even worth it, just go take spanish.

Professor Tannan is a great professor. It was her first time at UMBC. She is kind, but a word of advice; I took high school french and had a gap year before college, I would suggest you know the basics of french before coming into 101. It is fast-paced. Make sure you do the homework on time, participate/attend class, and do the extra credit.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: This man might be the Goat. whomever says he is bad is just coping and seething. Textbook has many practice problems to prepare you for the exam. Lock in twin.

Don't just "review" problems/hw. Do everything that they recommend to you ESPECIALLY EXTRA PRACTICE PROBLEMS AND EXAMS. REVIEW 1 WEEK AHEAD. DO THEM SEVERAL TIMES. Understand the HOW and the WHY. Although attendance isn't mandatory, GO. The participation + hw grade HELPS A LOT. DO ALL OF THE HW. READ CAREFULLY. LA's help but make sure YOU get it.

Before taking this class, have: 1) Know how to do CHEM 101/102 calculations, 2) Attention to detail, 3) A good, non-graphing calculator. Prof. Perks is really knowledgeable. As long as you do practice problems for the final and understand the experiment's main concepts, you'll be fine. Do your work, communicate, and SUBMIT IT ON TIME. A is possible
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: I think that many people give Perks a bad score due to the fact that the class is simply just super difficult! Generally, I think that he is a good professor and will spend the time helping you during office hours if needed. Super specific with grading on the exam free responses though, so be extremely precise

The way Perks formats his lectures is that he expects you to understand the material somewhat coming into class through reading the book. If you don't take the proper time beforehand you will definitely be lost in lecture but when you come prepared his lectures help reinforce and patch holes from what you read. His exams aren't bad if you practice

DO NOT TAKE THIS PROFESSOR. I do not care if you have to extend your degree by a semester to avoid him. He is the only professor I have ever earned a C from and I have had him for both 102 and 351. He expects you to learn the content from pre-lecture assignments and the textbook without him teaching and is dismissive when you ask for help.

Dr.Perks is a great professor! He really does care about the students. PRE READ the textbook or you wouldn't understand the lectures( HE WOULD TELL YOU WHAT TO EXPECT ON THE EXAMS)Lectures are practice problems and very similar to the exam questions. Practice, Practice and it is not that hard. He really does help out in office hours as well.

Love Dr. Perks! I had him for 102 and he rocks 351. He is an enthusiastic and respectful chemist. There is so much to learn from him. Pay attention to every detail he says, do all the pre-lecture work, come to class with high understanding, ask questions and practice all the time until the exam. If you live in this course you have this!
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: He's actually an average professor but organic chemistry is a difficult subject. I think he got too much hate for doing his job and it's more of a problem that the subject has too much material and is complex. The lectures were kind of useless if you didn't learn the material beforehand. It would have been nicer to learn in class imo. Lock in.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Test heavy

reviews.comment: He's a good professor, that's about all I can say. His lectures and notes are accessible, he mainly just tells you what the textbook will, but in my opinion hearing him explain it is much better than reading the textbook. He cracks the occasional joke and he tries to immerse his students well in the class. Overall a good class experience.

Dr. Perks isn't the best professor, but he gives a lot of ways outside of tests to get good grades. I found the midterms to be representative of the materials covered in the book and online videos. Chem 102 is difficult if you aren't good at math or didn't fully understand 101, but that isn't the professor's fault.

Lectures focused on example problems with minimal content. Knowledgeable and experienced but had high expectations. Required videos were hard to follow, and he wasn't tech-savvy. Strong proficiency in prior material is essential. You must grasp concepts quickly, as falling behind can significantly impact your grade. HW/tests are intense and broad.

Didn't respond to my email about being sick before the final. I had to take it while sick. Failed the class because of it. 

Don't take perks.

This man DOES NOT TEACH. You will learn entirely from the textbook. His exams are horrible but not as horrible as his attitude and extremely strict personality. Let me emphasize that HE DOES NOT TEACH. He only goes over practice problems in class, no background no nothing. Organic chem isn't even that bad, it's just the prof

I wish I could have avoided him after 102....but here we are. He has all the same problems (if not more) as he did in 102, his exam questions are abs wild and isn't very helpful inside or outside of lecture. this class' only saving grace imo was gierasch was also teaching it and the textbook was actually useful. Perks, I am BEGGING you, pls retire.

Dr. Perks is a nice person and all, but his issue is with his exams. The exams are so hard, the material isn't that much of helping, and so is the univ's aid for learning. The extra credit is a joke and isn't helpful in any way except if you need few points for a letter change. There is a survey and students are blamed in it greatly.

Perks can be a bit quirky, but if you engage with his teaching methods, the class is manageable. Textbook is helpful, and Unstuck study is a great supplement for study prep. Stay focused, and you'll get through it.

Worst professor (if you can even call him that) to roam the earth. Doesn't teach in lecture, just does polling problems, expects you to learn and understand just from pre-reading (you learn more from the reading that this guy). Will belittle & single you out, minorities beware, will speak condescendingly. Explanations to questions are useless.

Throughout my entire school career, I've never had a professor I genuinely wished would quit. I'd rather be without a professor than have him. He doesn't teach; he expects you to learn beforehand, and we just do practice problems in class. I wish this guy would retire and go enjoy his life or something rather than torture us as a professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Belittles students for not understanding "simple" concepts but refuses to explain them differently. The class was at 9 am and over the semester, students would stop showing up to lecture. The class is consistently half full by mid-semester, so don't worry about not getting a seat. He is petty and will remember little things to bring up later.

It was really weird how he would approach you in lab in regards to not showing up to lecture or selecting the wrong poll answer. He questioned my validity in attendance because I selected a different poll answer and I offered to show him my notes as proof that I was in class. He has a way of making you feel small.

He's oddly confrontational. And I mean it in a respectful way. He goes up to you in ways that are questionable. And that's him personally. Viewing him as just a professor, I'd say he's got things to work on. I, myself, and a good amount of my peers discussed how much work we put in to prepare for his exams; and you can never be prepared. Womp womp
man only wants to see you fail. there's no such thing as success with him being the professor. class is very hard and his exams are undoable. beware and please drop the class!

The content for the class wasn't hard, in my opinion. I studied it as much as I could and understood what was going on in the class and for the most part, did well in the hw, poll during lecture, and discussion. The only problems were the exams and the prof. Exams didnt reflect what we learned and the prof was no help either in what 'help' he gave.

If you are taking CHEM102 with him - DONT. He made the class a lot harder than it was. He didn't answer any questions I had when in office hours (he'd be like, oh we covered that in class and then move on) and when I asked for other resources to learn, HE DIDNT HAV ANY. He felt like he was very unprepared to help students and it sucks.

Dr. Perks was a great professor for me. You may have to be flexible with your learning to understand his lecturing, but if you do that and can learn independently you are all good. Read everything given, do tons of practice problems, ask plenty of questions, and don't cram (the course is mainly tests). He is so sweet and hilarious. Be nice to him!
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: If you're on your own, you're a person. Lectures consisted of AKTIV polling questions that were closed before you could even answer. This class covered 31 topics, and each was worse than the last. In class, polling is what you may need to save you're grade. The chemistry department needs help.
horrible professor. Instead of teaching the material in class, all he does is post poll questions and give minimal info about them. He's merciless when it comes to grades too

In 352L now and miss Perks from 351L. He gives you everything you need to succed. He provided videos from the years prior during COVID which set you up for an easy smoother procedure. He also made it very clear what he expects from you. The final was bizarre..but I like him. He's the type of guy that will roast you on spot but tough love.

Try not to be too intimidated by chem351, at the end of the day its just like any other class and the amount of time you put in will directly affect how well you do in the class. Textbook is a really great resource and try your best not to fall behind.

This is the worst professor ever. He came into lab and asked someone why they scored below average on an exam and everyone heard it. He is absurdly rude and mean. He makes exams so hard for no reason and lead offs were completely useless, he instead talks about random chemistry stuff he likes. He also doesn't know how technology works.

Lab manual is made just for UMBC so ask older students for their copy. Lab was pretty standard. Pre-lab quiz, in-lab quiz, and TA grade your work in the lab and write-up. "Lead off" is the Friday class before the labs, which was only sometimes helpful.

Heard from others that he was rude directly to students. Class lecture was okay. Made harder exam questions than the other professor. Okay overall, but was manageable because the class was split with another professor.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I took him for orgo and lab. He was pretty bad at the lab teachings, it seemed like he was just talking about random chemistry he found interesting. He also likes to stare at you in lab and is just weird. Overall seems friendly, but can be condescending. I was always annoyed when it was his turn to teach orgo lecture.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Inspirational--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: One word describes this guy, awful. The way he talks in the lecture is as if you should already understand organic chemistry at the level he does. He is also very rude and dismissive.

Perks was nicer in lab than lecture, but is super dry either way. Takes attendance with clicker questions and only one is dropped so don't skip. Found his lectures a bit hard to understand and would have to go over material on my own, but he's available after class to answer questions. Final is good but make sure you remember/understand experiments

Perks isn't a hard professor, he just isn't too nice a person. Once the class was using the chat to ask about lab during his lecture and he left refusing to answer any questions. He often lectures too fast so it's hard to understand what he's teaching. He also had a lot of assignments, imo. Stuff due before class, after class + regular hw. 5/10
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Dr. Perks doesn't answer questions during class. He leaves that to his TAs. Sometimes he also confuses himself and takes a couple minutes to get situated again. Has easier exams compared to the other Ochem professor, but it takes more self study. Links a lot of good videos to watch, so you don't have to look yourself. Homework due once a week.

Didn't explain concepts clearly in class. The book explains it okay, as did the khan academy videos, but even with that, his class was hard to understand. He didn't pay attention to student questions in chat, didn't spend enough time on explaining the problems. If you didn't understand it & he moved on then you probably would have to find it alone.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: It's a lab so you definitely need to show up to do well but he also taught 351 lecture and I really preferred Gierasch over him. He's nice in person but not the best teacher.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Honestly he improved a lot from the fall sem. As long as you do your readings and reach out to LAs and listen to the ICAs he does in class (live), youll do well. Exams are tough since each question are worth 4 pts. Failed pretty much 3/4 of my exams but pulled As on ICA,HW, PCA and still got a B.

I had Perks for Lab and Lecture for organic CHEM. Overall, the lectures seem a little confusing because I was not used to his teaching style, however, he is the SWEETEST person ever and very understanding. He is fun to talk to and knows his information.
Extremely bad at explaining and teaching. He makes it much more confusing than it needs to be which makes learning hard. Can also be disorganized and gives unclear instructions.
Not a good professor. Very dry lecturer.

Mark is a very disorganized and disaster professor as he moves randomly through different topics. Homework assigned for lab is very vague & relies on the universal lab textbook that was made for all organic chemistry lab students across the nation. Sorting through the myriad of information in the textbook trying to prepare for lab is very tedious.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Perks is great. By now you should realize every science class at UMBC is a beast. The class in itself is hard but he breaks it down well. The key is to use the learning objectives to study (very important). Then solve a lot of questions and a bunch of practice exams. At least a B will be guaranteed. Also do your flash cards ASAP
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Caring

reviews.comment: very straightforward
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: Hes a great guy and knows his stuff and can be funny sometimes. His exams are not bad at all they're just like the practice exams he provides. If you come to class, read before class and do the recommended problems you will be fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: His exams are insane (average is usually around a 65), but there's a small curve at the end of the course. Take notes (textbook + lecture), go to office hours, SI/PASS, and CTC, and make flashcards ASAP when you start getting into mechanisms and synthesis. I'd definitely recommend covering every practice exam, too. Good luck!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: I really enjoyed the class. Dr. Perks' tests were straightforward and he clearly enjoys the material
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: He co-taught CHEM351 with Gierasch in Fall 17 and I honestly don't understand why he gets such a bad rap. Very solid professor, teaches the material in a logical way, and will push you to the limit by requiring you to have understood the material and apply it in new scenarios. Exams might be a little rough, but nobody said Orgo was easy.

Clicker questions for 3/4 of lecture, meaning that you have to be there and you have to learn the material by yourself before going to lecture. There is online homework every class and they help you learn. For me, gap between 101 and 102 were huge, so I had to put so much effort on final exam(101 and 102 cumulative).
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: Boy, did Gierasch and Perks try to ruin Orgo 1 for a lot of people. The lectures were decent, but the exams were quite difficult, and by far the largest portion of the grade. The average for 3 out of 4 of the exams was 68-69%. That low an average does not speak well to the exams' fairness. My advice: take orgo elsewhere and transfer the credits.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: He's a pretty chill dude. He enjoys teaching and he cares about everyone's grade. he's a touch grader and the exams can be hard but as long as you keep up with the readings and aleks, attend every class and attend SI/Pass you should be fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Perks cares so much, so really take advantage of all the opportunities given to ask questions because he'll really take the time to do it well. He is a tough grader, but he's super chill, and his lectures are great. I thought I wouldn't get an A in orgo, but i did by doing the recommended problems, going to SI/PASS, and having a tutor at the CTC.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Perks is a good professor. His lectures are okay. Sometimes, I get confused in class and his answers are not always helpful. He is approachable though. The class was not too bad. I felt that everything on the exams were pretty fair. There was nothing we had not seen before. The content for chem351 is harder than that of chem101 but exams are easier
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Dr. Perks is a good professor. If you actually talk to him and show him your concern, he will try to help. There are lots of opportunities for help on campus like SI Pass, Math Lab, Tutorial Center, etc. Do recommended textbook problems, the readings before every class, and go through practice exams and you will do fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: He is a bit difficult to understand him, but when you understand the material and concepts clearly, his reading quizzes and exams will be more or less straightforward. His exams are tough though and he will try to trick you, quite like the ACS. READ THE TEXT BOOK BEFORE EVERY CLASS. If you don't understand what you read, you wont be able to answer.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Clickers are used in every class so be there. He takes the time to learn your name even though there are more than 200 students. He's super anal about copying/cheating/etc.... so don't do it. His exams are next level in my opinion
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Perks is a great lecturer. He makes the topic easy to understand and the lectures are fun. He is not too approachable. Whenever I would see him for class-related questions I would always have the feeling that he is annoyed, and does not answer emails very quickly. He is an okay professor.

Dr Perks makes you work for your grade, no question. But its clear he cares about his students and puts a lot of effort into making the lab match up with 351 lecture. He makes a point of knowing students names. Even in a 200 plus lecture hall!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Decent lecturer. Exams were fair for organic chemistry 1. I'd recommend doing the Wiley practice problems to help with studying for the exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: He is nice and has a passion for chemistry. He is not too difficult. a Lot thought chem 102 was easier than 101. If you got an A in 101, you will be fine. He curved the final. The final was super easy (90% chem 101 stuff).

ALEKS was rough this semester with a lot more knowledge checks. There was only a curve on the final, so even scoring way above the average may not get you an A. He tends to jump around a lot in the slides and skip a lot of the math so if you don't know how to do it don't expect to learn in class. I had it with Ms. Bass helping.

Dr. Perks is one of the best professors at UMBC! Yes, the material is difficult, but it's ORGO... it's very hard. He's clear cut with what he expects you to know (w/ learning objectives for the readings), and emphasized doing practice problems. He is a bit of a mess, but he's also very funny at times. If you work hard, your grade will reflect it.
Took him for lab and lecture and he is a nice person but he will put you on the spot to answer questions, is mainly trying to help you.

Dr Perks is a nice guy and really knows his stuff; also really helpful during office hours. Orgo itself is a nightmare. You are going to need to do practice problems outside of class if you want a good grade. Exams (multiple choice + free response) were tough as class averages were in the 60's70s. There was a giant curve at the end.

Really smart guy, you can tell he loves Orgo. He's really helpful during office hours. Lecture is only clicker questions so make sure you do the reading + hw before class. Exams were tough, but as long as you do the practice problems you'll be fine; exam is  multiple choice + free response. Giant curve at the end.

Extremely smart, almost too smart to teach students. He has high expectations of his students, but still makes an A achievable with hard work. Personally I fell behind in the beginning of the semester and never really recovered. DO NOT FALL BEHIND in the readings, you will be screwed by exam time if you do.

Dr. Perks is the best professor I have ever had.  He is passionate about organic chemistry and is brilliant intellectually, as well as being pretty funny.  The class isn't easy.  Its organic chemistry--tough is what you sign up for.  Its not his fault.  Ask for help.  Dont be intimidated.  If you fail, its on you.  He does his job.

Great guy. He's really nice and is genuinely interested in chemistry.  His lectures were a bit confusing, but he really tried. If you attend every lecture, and make sure you understand the labs you should be fine.

Dr. Perks is a professor who cares a lot about the subject he is teaching, and an intelligent man. His lectures are helpful, but only if you have done the assigned readings. He is very upfront about what an orgo student needs to do to succeed at the beginning of the semester. Be prepared to work and find a study group!

Very intelligent guy. Despite what others may have said, he pays attention to his students. In certain he enjoys teaching, but he will not sure that by making it easy for you. took his class in the summer from another university. He made enough of an impression for me to remember him years later and rate him. Study, pay attention, and ask questions
He knows the material, but does not have an effective way of teaching. He starts teaching something and jumps to a different thing so quickly.  He was not helpful when I visited him at his office.

Dr. Perks is brilliant!  Take the class seriously and ask questions. He teaches using the socratic method, so be ready to do a boat load of questions in class.
