The reading is a must to be able to do well in his class. Also he gives tough exams. They are do-able but give yourself ample time to study everything.

Not all smart people make great teachers. Very confusing guy. Stutters over himself alot. Does not post powerpoints prior to lecture, so you waste alot of time copying everything down and then try to play catchup to what hes talking about. Exams are rather difficult. If you can, get tutoring ASAP. Form study groups! TAs are better teachers than he.

Prepare to teach yourself orgo! Perks does not lecture at all. The entire class is full of clicker questions. Publisher used for online homework/quizzes is not the same publisher as the text that you will be required. GO OVER PREVIOUS EXAMS when studying for an exam. Clicker questions do NOT reflect exam material. Nothing does.

He knows every person - as in he was able to tell each (of 139) student their full names on the last day of lecture, and he truly is great at remembering who is what major etc. He's funny in class, knows A LOT, and loves orgo. He holds the class to high standards. It's HARD but he's a phenomenal teacher and is very smart, well-prepared, etc.
Knows all of students' names! Very cool and funny guy. Labs are definitely less interesting than 102L. Pre labs, post labs, and lab quizzes can be tricky so ask questions!

Perks is a strange teacher, I don't feel that he really likes teaching 102. He isn't very helpful if you ask him a question and his lectures are very haphazard. I don't think he knows what a conceptual framework is or any real methods to teaching, very smart guy though for what he does know. Pretty descent curve as well which surprised me.

Nice guy, but doesn't like teaching the class, so he just doesn't. Lecture consists of fast-paced clicker questions(5%) of your grade and him running through "examples" on his ipad with a projector. Get used to teaching yourself and always do the practice problems in the book. The exams are harder than they should be so ALWAYS do the old exams.
not helpful at all.

For 351L, Dr. Perks is very unorganized, and not very clear with assignments and class materials.  However, he is much better for lecture classes such as 102 or 351.  He's a really funny person and will pick on people who aren't paying attention and embarrass them (it's great).  He's also incredibly intelligent and sometimes forgets that you arent.

Doesn't present material in lecture. Assigns homework due day of exam on material that isn't on exam. Vindictively asks a ton of graded clicker questions on day of exam because he knows many students skip the class (on material not on the exam) in favor of preping for the exam. When connect was not working he told the class to "call McGraw-Hill"...

Doesn't present material in lecture. Assigns homework due day of exam on material that isn't on exam. Vindictively asks a ton of graded clicker questions on day of exam because he knows many students skip the class (on material not on the exam) in favor of preping for the exam. When connect was not working he told the class to "call McGraw-Hill"...

Great professor! I hated Orgo coming into it, but I've really grown to appreciate the subject. Kind of dorky, but he really spends time explaining the concepts you need to understand to move forward. Exams are, of course, tough, and homework + readings are pretty time-consuming, but if you work hard, you'll do well. Try to take Perks! :)

Dr Perks is great but he definitely is hard. His lectures are helpful IF you read the book first. They are not there to teach you the material, but to help you understand it. You are supposed to read before lecture, and then you go over it to conquer what was in the book. He knows who does well and who doesn't and is great with answering questions.

His exams do not relate in any way what so ever to the practice exams on blackboard.  Lectures are usless, discussion sucks, and he is by far a barking mad loon.  Looks like Larry Kings brother, and his only redeeming quality is that he swears when he makes mistakes and it provides a minor chuckle.  Don't take him for 102...don't do it.

I had Dr. Perks the second time I took 102 and for 352.  I LOVE THIS HIPPIE.  His mandals are the best.  But really, this man lives and breathes organic chemistry and was always very helpful.  I went in dreading organic chemistry and now I'm an organic chem grad student because of Dr. Perks.

Dr. Perks is a great teacher.  His exams are tough but fair.  Organic chemistry is hard; that's not his fault.  He cares about the chemistry and his students, and makes an effort to know you.  Knows organic chemistry like the back of his hand.  I thought his exams reflected the lectures; you don't have to teach yourself from the textbook alone.
Be prepared to teach yourself.

Go to class for clicker questions. Suffer through discussion. Lectures are boring but Perks is pretty good at making them a little interesting. He makes a lot of mistakes in the lecture notes. Also, teach yourself everything from the book. Tests cover all information in each chapter, not the stuff in the lectures. Tests are very difficult. Beware.

Boring, clicker points enforced. Go to lecture to help understand a bit of procedure. Uses TAs for labs. Pre and post labs are somewhat hard but mostly 3 questions long.Book is helpful for lab notebook. Follow lab notebook procedures.

Dr. Perks knows a ton about chemistry but his lectures are very poor. They are organized in a strange way and he messes up on 80% of the problems. The exams are extremely difficult with the average being around a 60%. Definitely read the book and do all of the recommended problems. Know every definition and concept from the book.

He seems to really like chem, but not as a teacher. It sometimes seems like he's not interested in teaching us. He does pretty cool demonstrations but he screws up his note ALL THE TIME. So confusing. He also stumbles over his words which also is confusing. Read the book, it helps. Or take another professor.

It seems that the professor is really interested in chemistry...but not chem 102. All he talks about is orgo. He screws up on a lot of problems in class and doesn't teach very well at all. For those who plan to do well in the class, read the textbook

Dr. Perks is a gifted Professor that truly loves Chemistry and has a true gift for teaching. He takes a lot of tough material and makes it really understandable. I would recommend him over any of the other Organic Chem Professors here.

Had him for chem lecture and lab. He's more at chill in lab then lecture. He sorta of impatient. Its helpful if you read the textbook before class because when he teaches I usually would not know what was going on.

he was not interested in teaching our class, he is a great lab teacher, but not lecturer.  the class is extremely curved, which is good because it is close to impossible to get an A without it.  when you take tests you will walk out thinking you did awesome, then you will see your grade, and your friend's grades, and be confused.

At first when I took Chem 102. It was definitely a bad experience with this teacher because it was his first time teaching it. However, when I took chem 352, he wasn't that bad of a teacher. At times it is hard to understand him. you are required to know material before class and do practice problems.

It really seems as though they could care less about the student. The professors really act like the class is a burden to them and they are not interested  the material. They could care less about your grade or class performance.

The class is definitely a weed out class despite what they claim. The material is not hard, but you go through it at really fast If you are involved with research and internships be prepared to do a lot of teaching yourself. I am really good at chem and do not get A's on all the exams they are really tricky, few questions, and nothing like lecture.

I was really scared of taking orgo 2 with him.However, he really changed my expectations in orgo 2. He is very knowledgeable and passionate about orgo, so he does his best to explain to students. The only problem is that he expects students to read the material before class, so he assumes you have some idea of what he's talking about.

This class if difficult no matter who is teaching it. To do well in the class, you must know nearly every single fact in the lecture notes, every fact in the textbook chapters, and EVERY formula. The tests had 25-28 questions, so you can only get two wrong to get an A. Don't expect many A's on exams. Go to office hours but don't walk in unprepared.
He was a very good professor and funny too. He is very helpful. Tied in organic with real life uses (made it interesting for me) and was very willing to help students.

Much better for orgo than he was for gen chem. The exams are difficult, but fair. He will answer your questions during class or office hours. He tries to give free points with clicker questions. Make sure you keep up with the reading, as he sometimes skips the details.
Awesome. Very knowledgeable about organic chemistry. Very charming personality.

It took a year to understand his teaching style. Dr.Perks is absolutely a fair professor. This is an orgo, of course it is hard. Don't expect the professor to tell you what to study. He just outlines the concepts so you study by yourself after class. Study the textbook, never get behind; then you can pull out "A" even w/out a curve. Use the textboo

Really nice guy and overall a great teacher. He is very smart and teaches assuming you already know what he is talking about, but if you read material b4 going to class you will be fine. His exams are not too difficult. Will curve them a lot.

Dr. Perks is so awesome! None of the classes that he teaches are easy, but it's chemistry. It's not going to be easy no matter who is teaching. But he's always willing to help if you ask for it, and he is genuinely a really good person!
he messes up on the example problems during class and doesnt realize it till he's finished a whole page of the problem and still not solved it. RELY ON TEXTBOOK

He is very excited about chemistry, but that doesn't always translate into being a good professor. His lectures were sometimes confusing. Reading the book is a necessity! Clickers count for accuracy, so try to really learn the subject.
Perks is a great teacher, and his exams were all fair. He really tries to get to know his students, which is rare in science classes.

Perks is crazy. He says not to memorize things or that words arn't important, but doesn't give formulas and asks for definitions on exams, so don't listen to him. He should be teaching organic. He tries to help but I get the feeling he judges. Curved just enough to get the B(.05%), so don't expect too much help.

If you're not good at chem like me, you shouldn't expect to get an A in his class instead of studying chem really hard. Study everyday and don't rely on his powerpoints for studying. Use the textbook, this is the only way you could survive this class. The exams are not that tricky if you STUDIED... he drops one exam..
He's a very nice person, but the class itself isn't. It starts out pretty easy and then just keeps going down from there. It goes down and down and down...and under. Good luck.

I love Perks! He's such a nice guy and he makes an effort to get to know his students. He's very willing to give help but you need to ask! Perks' lectures REQUIRE prior reading. Or else you're lost. Personally, the main use for his lecture notes was to follow along the examples to get the CPS questions right (they count for accuracy).

When it comes to teaching he expects that you know the concept before attending class. He provides lecture notes yet they are not congruent with his teaching method. In order to get an A you would have to study the textbook. He has a lot tricky questions on his exam.
exams are extremely hard

His exams start out really easy (especially during the beginning of the semester), and then get ridiculously hard. The lectures don't really do anything for you, but you have to go for attendence. Basically, you just have to teach yourself the entire course. If you can't, you're screwed.

Nice guy. His tests are easy, but only if you read the textbook. Otherwise, you're pretty much guaranteed to fail. He lectures as if it is a review, so read before lecture. If you learn well on your own, you'll do great. If not, I'd recommend someone else. He drops one exam. And he knows his stuff.

This guy has the uncanny ability to confuse himself. Every once in a while he'll post a clicker question and then realize that there's more than one answer, or the right answer's not on the screen. He uses notes a lot, but skips over ones he doesn't like, so you need to keep up. You may get by if you cram for tests 5 hours before, Just be careful.
Not a bad teacher, just can be hard. Is a very nice guy.

Scattered brain. Cannot stay on one topic to save his life or ours. His lecture notes are unorganized and are mostly pictures that come straight from the text book. Read the text book before/after lecture or else you'll be completely confused. Beware, he likes to throw in a little more "physics" than actually chemistry.
The worst professor I had in college....probably the only one I would ever speak bad about.  Just trust me, and avoid him at all costs.

Perks helps make the ACS practice finals. His tests are abnormally difficult. He is a poor lecturer, as he basically skims the book poorly. His notes are incomprehensible, and are mostly strange pictures. Smith apparently had easier tests and good notes. Only take Perks if you enjoy learning on your own and gaining nothing from lecture.
Not bad I guess.. pretty average.
Not a good prof. Lectures are hard to follow. I wish I took it with Dr. Smith instead.

Perks is a very nice man and he seems to be a good person. Still, he is a very difficult teacher. His notes are incomprehensible and it is very difficult to get anything out of class. In addition, his tests are incredibly difficult and well made, explicitly designed to trip you up and punish you for not knowing something entirely. Avoid.

He is a really good teacher, and if you actually come to class and do the work you will learn it.  He does explain things pretty clearly and is very helpful.  If you take the lab with him, he comes to all the labs and helps you if you need it.  He also does group work in lecture which is very helpful, and he knows everyone by name.

He honestly DOES try to teach, and if you go to his office hours he is extremely helpful and make you understand.  However, his tests don't reflect the material that you learned (or he stressed) in class.  Although he earns points for being very nice, I would suggest taking the class with another teacher.

I had him for Chem 351-352. Very articulate man who loves what he teaches. He is an amazing teacher for the material he has to teach, no one better so far. His only draw back is that he makes the exams very tough (but fair). Take him if you want to learn something, dont take him if you want an easy A (even though curve is ~80% = A).

Absolutely the worst Chemistry professor I have ever had. He takes a difficult subject and makes it near impossible to understand. Going off on tangents and already expecting his students to understand all the material doesn't help. He is also a complete arrogant jerk when you ask him questions. Take is with anyone else, except him!

This professor is great! If I had to choose between him and Hogsmane again, I would choose Perks. He teaches very by the book. As long as you read the book, do the problems, and do the homework, you will get an A. I'm not saying he is easy. The work is hard and time consuming, but it is not impossible. not for slackers.

I have taken CHEM102, 351, and 352 with him. For 102 DO NOT TAKE IT WITH HIM. He is terrible at teaching it. For organic he is great. He only tests on things he has covered in class. Read the book, do problems and you should be fine. He takes a significant amount of questions from the ACS Organic Chemistry Practice Guide, WORD FOR WORD.

This class was hard because the material is hard. I really think Perks could have done a better job helping students to understand. He is not a bad guy, but he belongs in Organic Chem. He wastes A LOT of class time with experiment that don't even work and going off on tangents about how the material relates to Organic Chem, which I didn't even need

If you're serious about chem, take professor perks. SLACKERS BEWARE. I didn't do much studying except a few days before the exam where I did ALL the probs in the chapters (about 400+ in 2 days) and pulled an A out of my ass. Do ALL the problems and you will do well in his class.

If you can help it, you shouldnt take him, he goes off subject all the time. He will do an example in class that will take 30 minutes and it will not even be right . perks really knows his stuff and is a nice guy. his curves are generous and he follows the textbook very well. I recommend him for serious chem. students who can dedicate the time to his problem solving oriented teaching style. also good to take for lab section

I could not adjust to his teaching style so fast- mainly he likes focusing on problem solving in order to understand the concepts (and not vice versa). If you like word problems then you will do fine, but if you are more of a conceptual person it might be a little bit difficult. Do a lot of practice problems and you could probably pass.

By far the WORST teacher I have EVER had. He doesn't use the book, hes arrogant and his demonstrations seldom work. Dr. Perks will know your name, know how well you're doing in the class and will make himself available to help you as much as possible. His tests are harder than they seem but still not bad considering its organic

He's not that horrible. He doesn't go by the book so you really have to pay attention in class and take notes. Since u get 15% for just showing up, u can pull off a C in the class if u get aroud 40% on exams. 50+ is a C. The worst chemistry teacher I've had so far (they've really made an effort to get bad chemistry teachers) his exams are incredibly hard, and he doesn't teach AT ALL. Very helpful. One of few professors who know what he is talking about. Also very nice, will draw strucures and explain reasoing. seems easy, but you really do gotta put in the work otherwise u'll end up with a B like me -__- study for the quizzes, they affect ur grade alot, and as long as u study for the quizzes you'll b fine for the final.

One of the best teachers Ive ever had.  Always helpful and friendly.  I had Dr. John Smith for Chem 101 and 102, and he was horrible.  Dr. Perks was great.  I wish I would have had him for all my Chem classes.

His group work and lectures are entirely relevent to the exams that he gives out, his explanations are well done, and he's always prepared for class. Points are given for attendence. And, in general, he's a nice guy.
I do not like his so-called group participation.  It does not make any sense.  I can learn everything from the book and without going to class. I did not like him as a teacher, but he is a nice guy.
Hard lectures, hard tests.  He comes well prepared for the lectures and usually has time after class - very good office hours.  Nice guy, but hard teacher.

Some people knock this dude, but I think he has a great way of teaching. He layed out a good fundamental track for the ACS final in 352. I liked his teaching style better than Smith's, but that's just me. Says hi and actually remembers my name.

ok, I know some people like hime, and some don't. This course will be very easy of you know his style (lecture, exam). So, first of all, try to find HIS STYLE, then you will have no problem. His lecture will be very clear only when you know how he teach.

Very organized lectures with lots of visuals and examples. Another good thing is his use of groupwork problems. Tests are inpossibly hard (class average was ~45%) and sometimes not approachable. Overall, is nice guy and cares whether or not youre learning

Biggest waste of my time ever. Even when I did go to class, I either couldnt follow  anything he said, or fell asleep. Good chemistry teachers should be able to make a boring, difficult topic fun and interesting, not MORE BORING
I know that this course is hard itself. However, he is well prepared for every lecture, and very helpful when you go his office to ask some problems. Very Good Teacher to prepare MCAT/PCAT/DAT.

Her lectures were easy and interesting at most times. She is very passionate with what she teaches, and It made the class much more enjoyable! She is super super friendly, and is overall a really well rounded professor. Class/lab assignments aren't hard or super time consuming and there are only two exams (midterm and final).

Really easy class, take this class for easy science lab credit. Professor McAllister does go off topic in some lectures but overall really nice and kind, no textbooks so exams are solely on lectures and labs. Labs also is fun, for lab reports just follow the guidelines and you should get a decent grade on it.

I love when professors care about teaching and want their students to learn. She is so passionate about what she does, and that always makes me want to put even more effort into any class. The class itself was pretty easy, and it was nice to see how much she cared about the material and the students.

Professor McAllister is very passionate and cares about her students. The class itself is easy; certain components (mainly the labs) are somewhat tedious but not hard. A great choice for a GEP course.

Good prof. Theres a lot of extra credit that no matter how you score on the midterm or final you should be at a A or a B. You are graded on attendance & participation so make sure to show up but besides that the class is easy. Their is a lot of work, but easy enough for a A so just pay attention.

Professor McAllister really does care for all her students and is insanely sweet; very understanding of circumstances and in any case, offers lots of extra credit opportunities. She's super passionate about what she teaches, and is also passionate on getting to know her students well. Please take her class!

Very passionate about the class even relating material to her own experiences. She truly wishes students to understand the fundamentals of science so even if they don't major in it they can still be educated enough to ask questions and understand others view points.

Class is easy overall. Professor is very passionate about what she teaches. Just go to lectures and study and the exams will be fine. Gives extra credit opportunities and participation points in class. Labs were not too hard and feedback is given on assignments

Lectures were very informative. Extra credit was a great boost to my grade. The workload was not crazy and most of the labs were quite simple. As long as you do the work before it is due and attend lecture, this class should be an easy A.
shes rly sweet .exams are hard study lectures. atendence is optional
shes so sweet. exams are hard so study and go to labs!!!!!!

I adore this professor so much! Her lectures are very reminiscent of secondary school lectures, which I really enjoyed. Has a great sense of humor and often told her own stories that connected back to the topic. Grading can be a bit tough, but she follows the rubric strictly on lab reports. Labs required groups, so be ready to work with others.
She is an extremely nice professor who is clearly passionate about teaching and the subjects she covers. Would highly recommend taking a course from her, whether it's required or not.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: This was my second time taking Professor McAllister and I just adore her. She's so caring, funny, and genuine. She really wants her students to pass and she gives us so many opportunities for points. I skipped her final exam and still had an A. My favorite professor thus far.

A very nice and enthusiastic professor! Please do extra credit, it will save you and boost your grade in the end!! The only thing I would complain about is the amount of work that is expected to be completed by non-science majors. It's a lot. The assignments aren't difficult, but they're tedious.
Amazing Prof, she cares about her student and want everyone to succeed

Professor McAllister is enthusiastic & she made the class enjoyable. Come to class because she takes attendance most days. There are three exams and a final and she drops the lowest exam, one quiz every week, and two projects (one group, one individual). The class is an easy A if you come to class, and read the slides. Also, no need to buy the book

reviews.comment: Professor McAllister, is very enthusiastic about the topics that she teaches. But be prepared for the exams bc sometimes she doesn't give study guides, also go to class or you'll miss out on important information that could potentially be on the exam. She genuinely wants you to succeed, in her class. She is very accessible outside of class.

reviews.comment: She is very passionate about what she does and you can appreciate that. She puts a lot of effort into her classes and her course doesn't feel like other typical college courses. Great professor overall and wants you to do well.

Overall an easy class if you go to lecture. Professor McAllister is very passionate about topics in class and cares about students. I struggled a bit with exams but did well on quizzes so good grade overall. Mainly a note taking class with one group project and one individual project. Attendance matters so go to lecture!

This professor is good overall! She does try her best to explain everything BUT SHE IS VERY TOUGH GRADER FOR JUST WATER SCI.I had done my best to the lab reports and still got below grade and my group members somehow got better grade despite the fact our lab reports were similar when they gave us back to look at the grade we received.

This professor, is wonderful/ amazing. She is very enthusiastic about environmental science! Be prepared to read because she does have sometimes very long google slides. Also don't just use the slides to study for exams use the text book and case studies she gives you to prepare for exams. She is also very accessible outside the classroom.

I'm not sure why her rating is high.Teaching wise she is a horrible teacher. Do not get me wrong she is a nice person but she can not teach nor does she teach on a college level. Her exams are hard to pass b/c her teaching is NOT on the same level. She needs to teach like that. There are 3 labs reports, 2 exams, weekly journal and extra credits.

This class is an easy A if you are good with time management. Bit strict with lab reports but work on it ahead of time, and you'll get a A or B. Lots of extra credit, so go to the lectures and look out for announcements! The exams are a harder than what the content seems. If you use Quizlet and study a week before the exam, you will be just fine!
she was average tbh not that understanding when it came to the fact that i literally couldn't take the final because i was flying out of the country

She is a wonderful professor, I attended like 2 of her lectures and they were informative, but I stopped going because the content is easy enough that I could do without. Do powerpoint to pdf, summarize pdf, memorize. Did great on both exams. The most tiring part of this class is showing up to lab and doing the 3 lab reports.

reviews.comment: genuinely loves teaching and wants everyone to succeed. she understands that ppl take the class to meet their GEP, so she's very lenient on due dates and lab reports. class is not hard just alot of busy work. Lab reports are easy but can take some time. gives lots of extra credit. Exams are easy and come from her ppt.
great professor! you get what you put in

Professor McAllister is one of the best professors at UMBC! She is so sweet and genuinely cares about students. This course isn't difficult at all, it is just a lot of work. Do all of the extra credit, and it will be a buffer for your exam scores. PLEASE attend her lectures; they are not only interesting but can give extra credit and test answers!

This is more of a rating for the SCI 100 class in general. IT IS RIDICULOUS. This class had the most work out of all my classes and it's a LEVEL 100 GEN ED. Nancy is OVERLY enthusiastic. She consistently forgets that if we are in this class - We are not science majors, and we are taking this class because we are forced to, not because we care.

Very well paced class! Only a chapter or so per week, textbook chapters are short and digestible. The topic can be depressing at times, but the professor's such a kind, warm, and enthusiastic teacher that it makes it a lot easier to take, especially when she often emphasizes more hopeful developments in environmental science. The perfect teacher.

Great professor. Personally very uninterested in science but I still enjoyed her lectures because she was so engaged and  kind. You can tell she really cares about the material and wants her students to be successful. Didn't have to take the final exam because I was happy with my other exam grades. Definitely recommend.

LOVED this professor! So enthusiastic about the subject and so caring for students! Lectures were so fun and engaging. Must participate for points. There are weekly quizzes (but 1 is dropped), 3 exams (there is also a final that is optional and cumulative, but can be substituted for lowest exam grade), and 2 projects. Really easy A, take her!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: She really cares about the students and will give you every opportunity to pass the class. Just show up to class to get points and read the textbooks since the quizzes and exams are based on that. She also makes the final an optional exam if you complete the first 3 exams and you are satisfied with your grade.

She is incredibly quick and thorough when responding to emails and is a very kind professor. Much of the tests and quizzes will be on material straight from the textbook but her power points during lecture help to break that down for you.

I took this class thinking it was an easy A and not really caring about the class. And now, thanks to Prof. McAllister's enthusiasm for the course, I'm getting a minor in GES. She's hands down the best Professor I've ever had at UMBC. The textbook helps with the quizzes that are every week. Exams and the two projects were pretty easy as well.
Great Professor. Do the work and you pass it's as easy as that.

McAllister is a great professor, she really cares about her students and is very enthusiastic when it comes to teaching the material. You need to read the textbook and her exams are like the quizzes and study guide. Take GES120 with her!

reviews.comment: she really cares about this topic, and you can tell. She's the best professor I have this year.

Easy class with an optional final and great lectures. As long as you pay attention youre good to go on exams. The textbook isnt really needed for passing. Some questions are pulled from lectures and guest lecturers. All multiple choice so even if you dont remember its usually pretty easy to guess.

Really great professor and enjoyable lecturer. Many opportunities for extra credit, few and relatively easy assignments. Exams will test you on reading and lecture;y you don't have to read the book to pass, but you have to read if you really want a secure A in the class and pass the exams. Syllabus, grading, and schedule are clear and organized.

Hands down fantastic professor. Easy course if you attend class and take good notes. Her grading criteria are very clear and she offers extra credit opportunities. reviews.comment: Dr. Mcallister is a good teacher. She makes her requirements very clear and allows you to take an optional final if you aren't satisfied with your grade. She is very nice and understanding.

Very passionate and has field experience. Lectures are fun and informative. Don't have to go to class, but the extra credit is worth it. Optional final, if you did well on the 3 exams, you can choose not to go. I highly recommend taking her class. Easy projects

Ms. McAllister is excellent! She explains exactly what you need to know in order to get A's on your tests. She's super nice, and very passionate. GO TO CLASS!!! reviews.comment: Dr. McAllister is extremely passionate about Env Science. She's knowledgeable, eager to help, and available by email easily. 3 exams, 2 easy projects, online quizzes. Study from book for exams. Come to class 4 highlights. Don't blow off going to class b/c she gives participation credit. Great course for a science non lab credit. Recommended highly.

Professor King is very passionate about what she teaches. The class itself is easy, but it is discussion based, but participating is not difficult. There are no exams but there is a final project presentation based on a topic of your choice which was actually fun to do. There isn't a lot of homework but there are a lot of readings.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Group projects

reviews.comment: Professor King is amazing! Her class was kind of boring in the beginning but it really starts getting interesting once you start working on your personal project which counts as the final in this class. There is a lot of presentations, group work, and public speaking required so be prepared to share. She is super chill

I like Dr. Nicole King as a person but the course itself did not interest me and the only reason I took it was for a GEP credit. If you are not interested in public humanities I would not recommend. If you need to take this course for a GEP credit just be prepared to participate a lot.

She is unresponsive to emails and seems difficult to reach.  Not very personable, and can even be rude or judgmental or condescending towards students.  Be prepared to complete every homework assignment, attend every class, and ace the exams (which are a mix of multiple choice and written, btw).  Overall, I would avoid this professor if you can.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Nkiru Nnawulezi is really strict and harsh, and her grading is quite arbitrary and difficult to understand.  She provides little to no feedback and does not allow students to look over exams with her.  She usually does not reply to emails either, so best to catch her right before or after class if you have a question.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Professor Nnawulezi is the most unpredictable, harsh, and cold professor I have ever had. She seems uninterested in letting students connect with her or share personal experiences that are pertinent to the class. She is an incredibly tough grader and a lot of it seems arbitrary. Her tests are usually a mixture of short answers and multiple choice.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Her class is quite easy material wise. I am not a great writer but I still got a 24/25 on every paper, however, she doesnt allow late work for any reason and if you miss one assignment you will not get an A. Her main issue is SHE DOES NOT REPLY TO EMAILS. It took her over a month to reply to one of my emails and multiple people have the same issue

I have never experienced so much stress before. DO NOT TAKE. Remove it from your cart I beg you. She is amazing, but her teaching methods are by far the worst that I have ever experienced. She takes at least 25 days to get back with grades, DOES NOT respond to emails, and is a harsh grader. She takes off points, and doesn't even explain why. RUN.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--So many papers--Tough grader

reviews.comment: DONT DO IT. She literally waited until the last week of class to grade everyones papers and its impossible to pass her class. Such a harsh grader. Ive NEVER received a D on paper until her class and Im a junior. This class was a huge mistake. Also she doesnt respond to emails.

Dr. Nnawulezi is the most unpredictable and juvenile professor Ive ever had. The course is 3 quizzes, and 4 papers, making the entire class 160 points. Each paper is 25 points, which gives you very little wiggle space for error. She grades extremely harsh for a course that is so little in points. The quizzes are easy-ish. DONT TAKE THIS CLASS.

Prof is incredibly split in my opinion; the lectures have been some of the most engaging and well-presented material I've seen in a classroom, but her policies are ruthless. If you miss an assignment, you will not get an A. Communication was really sparse as well. Unfortunately, a great professor with really frustrating practices.

Horrible professor. Boring and uninspiring, and doesn't know how to teach. Our entire grade was four exams which she never really told us what to expect. She had to tell the class to stop complaining to the TA about how awful she was. It was something she actually had to address. She's not easily accessible, she doesn't curve, she shouldn't teach.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: This Professor is knowledgeable; however she makes students study too much just to pass any of the exans. She did NOT tell us what to expect on the exams and only gave us the questions on the next two exams after so many people failed the first two exams. She takes weeks to grade exams including the first one. Exams are the bulk of the grade!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: One of the most useless classes I have ever taken. I learned nothing from this instructor. She is not a good professor. At all. Super rude. Intimidating. Totally disrespectful towards MOST of her students. 0/10, would NEVER take her again for anything. Ended up with a 89.7% and received a B.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Homework assigned EVERY class ontop of lengthy chapter readings. Vague powerpoints and tedious in-class assignments EVERY class. I ended the class with a 79.8% in which I asked in advance if I can improve an assignment to improve my final grade, she never replied to my email and of course would not round up. NOT WORTH IT!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: One of the best classes that I have taken. There was a lot of reading and a big group project that spans the entire semester. Great discussions. Tests are very specific to the reading. If you read, show up to class, and do well on the group project you should do well.

Very work heavy class, but the Professor N. will help you if needed. She will also take the time to schedule appointments with you and sit one-on-one to explain things. Hard class, but very good professor.
Hard class, requires a lot of reading. Sometimes the quiz questions were unclear or extremely specific, attempting to pull from up to 40 pages of text. Lot of work for what you get out of it.

Unreasonable. I usually get A's, never struggled so hard in a class. I was told no and also you cannot have extra credit when I asked for a two day extension two weeks before the due date (I was out of state). Most of his assignments took me about 40 hours, so just don't have a life/job I guess. And he had a 5% assignment due before class day 1.

Took Olano in Graphics for Games, and he was honestly one of the best professors I've had at UMBC. While he was occasionally hard to follow in lectures, he cares deeply about the success of his students and is ALWAYS available on Discord with timely responses to ANY question about the projects. If you like video games I highly recommend 438/491.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Great professor, gives good feedback but doesn't really teach game development, it's mostly just a semester-long a group project where everyone is left to their own devices for the majority of the class. Grades very fairly, and takes note of individual effort of each group member, so make sure you contribute above and beyond to the group work.

This class is difficult but eye-opening especially if you want to get into game dev. Lectures consist of learning about UE5 and other computer graphics topics. Super smart guy who grades difficult projects leniently. Just put effort and utilize office hours and you will be okay :)

The 491 game development is a "tough" class that requires significant effort. But that shouldn't discourage anyone from taking it. The assignments are graded based on attempt, so as long as you put in time and effort, there should be no problem at all. Marc Olano is a very passionate professor, and taking his class is valuable for learning UE4.

Professor Olano is incredibly smart, but he knows way too much to be an effective teacher. Lectures consist of him scrolling through Unreal Engine code. Expect to put in 15 hours per assignment, they are INCREDIBLY difficult. Some easy grades are presentations (10%) and presentation feedback (15%), although this requires constant attendance.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: Excellent lecturer.  Gives a lot of examples/content that augments the slides.  I took advantage of his office hours and he was always very helpful.    You can't pass if you just listen to the class.  You need to read about the material outside of class and independently do the HW.

Olano made this class pretty fun. His tests were hard, but were always on topics discussed in lecture. He gives you a good chunk if his code for the projects, which makes some of the programming trivial.  Lectures were always exciting, full of graphics examples and demos. If you're going to take graphics, Olano is a great person to take it with.

Assignments were largely tedious (eg. ridiculously long strings of multiplying and adding things) that you have to be careful, not clever to complete. I thought the lecture was pretty uninspiring too. I had the impression that the professor didn't want to really be there teaching this class and it made me not want to be in the class too.
The architecture class was difficult, but there are also plenty of extra-credit questions in each homework. Helpful professor, treats everyone fairly. Exams are challenging. But I aced it anyway.
In general he's one of the better teachers in my opinion, but not the best.  He's tough but fair.  Knows his stuff, and has a good attitude 99% of the time, just watch out for that 1% :)

This guy loves two things, graphics and performance. He will twist and turn every architecture concept to a problem in graphics domain. His classes are boring and sleepy and assignments are all 'assumptions and justifications'.He will not teach anything but you will learn everything because of his hard assignments. His exams are very challenging.Av

Dr Olano is very intelligent but not capable of passing knowledge to students.  His explanations often include erroneous statements that he later realizes and corrects.  This is frustrating when the material covered is difficult and confusing to begin with.  He is unwilling to offer necessary help even during office hours.  Avoid this professor.

Very bright teacher.  Knows a lot about what he is doing.  Very helpful after class and during his office hours.  I didn't use the book too much, but I would have liked it near the end.  Like most comp sci classes, all the information is available on the internet.  Projects can be time consuming, but if you like graphics you will like this class.

I first came hoping to learn something new, and ended up learning that this is a class for people who knew prior the material to be covered. I would ask for help, and still be left in the dark as to how to complete the several insanely difficult projects he assigned. Office hours were during my other classes and the TA's accent was incomprehensible
Second class with professor, liked IS634 more. Class was good overall. Most assignments are writings. Wasn't too bad. Group project semester writing needed more instructions

This class was 60% group project, 40% individual assignments. It was a lot of work to do in the group project but it wasn't that bad cause the work was more "fun" for being school. The professor opens the content every week & the syllabus due dates are a little hard to understand but she puts the due dates on the actual assignments too. Not too bad
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Gives good feedback--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Great professor - accessible by email, she will take the time to explain any doubts. Work is fairly easy to complete with weekly assignments and only two major papers - one midterm and one group final paper. Only thing is instructions are sometimes unclear and she's also little bit of a picky grader. Pay attention to deadlines, but enjoyable class.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: To get an A in this class, you have to read a lot. You have to do good in your quiz, participate in weekly discussions and the final paper. Good professor, I would take it if she teaches a different course.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--So many papers

reviews.comment: He never responds to e-mails/messages and is EXTREMELY unfriendly. If you write something he disagrees with he will penalize you for it. Avoid this teacher at all costs.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. O's lectures and stories about working in the field were my favorite parts about this course. Being an immigrant himself, and experienced working with immigrant communities, he has a great deal of insight and is the perfect person to teach this course. The main assignment of interviewing someone to hear their immigration story was great.

This is one of the best SOWK professors at UMBC. His class is easy and you learn a lot from the readings. Few quizzes, a mid term and a final and a final paper 10-12 pages long but definitely you will have time enough to complete it and is a great grader unlike some of the other professors in the same department.

Dr. O is super knowledgeable about social work and uses real-world examples to enhance your understanding of the subject matter. He responds to emails quickly and is very down to earth and understanding. I bought the textbook but didn't use it once and it didn't affect my grades at all.

I never even touched my textbook for this class and it didn't matter. All grading stuff was super easy, I almost feel like he gave everyone an A. I fought the urge to fall asleep every class. Despite this, I did enjoy taking the class because he gave good information about grad school and how to find success in my field. He was very knowledgeable.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. O is funny and carefree. Assignment due dates might get pushed back. He might get your class confused w/ another one. Technical problems may arise. Class may get canceled. Do the reading. Good review of Human Development class material. Tests are easy. Pay attention in class as he randomly calls on people. He's better w/ interaction than email.

Dr. O is a great professor that cares about his students and wants them to strive to do great things. He is accessible outside of class despite his busy schedule at times. He is a real gem and answers students questions if there are any. He also mentions in class background knowledge from being a therapist on different topics.

Great professor. Put good effort in and you will pass. He does lecturer by sitting in a chair and relaying his points verbally without demonstration. He knows how to explain information and answer questions in a way everyone understands. He encourages questions and gives reasonable assignments. You learn a lot in his classes.

The class overall was easy (exams and quizzes were online and open note/book) but Dr. O was always late and would ramble during lecture. I learned a lot but not from him specifically - more from the book.

Took 374 early this summer & it was great. Dr. O is a great professor and uses his own experiences and makes up scenarios to help his students understand. Attendance was mandatory because it was summer. Would have gotten an A, but didn't study as much as I should have. All in all, a great professor in the Social Work dept.

I had Dr. O for SOWK 388 & 374, he is very thorough, he offer's extra credit and his availability is always flexible if you need to see him. Everything he talks about in class he uploads to blackboard, gives great feedback on papers. The class is very enthusiast not boring at all. Just show up, pay attn & read you will get easy A. Best Prof ever!!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: I LOVE Dr. O!!! I will be taking his class next semester as well. A lot of students find him to be disorganized and don't like that he goes off on tangents. I happen to like his type of eccentricity, and I take to it well. The exams are easy as long as you read and have your notes and book by your side as you take them. Def recommend!!!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring

reviews.comment: Okay so I am not the biggest fan of Dr. O but he isn't a difficult professor, I just don't like how disorganized he can be and how for every class we spend 20 or 30 minutes (in a 75 min class period) talking about random things... it's unnecessary! BUT exams are open book open note (Ctrl F is your friend)dont wait to do the papers-use the rubric
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Took 389 as a hybrid. Some online quizzes/exams & some in-class, but neither were very hard as he made them open note/book. Dr. O assigns two 10 pg. papers, but they're straightforward as long as you answer all questions, follow rubrics, and maintain page limits. Funny guy, very passionate, asked him to be my adviser I loved is classes that much!

He's alright. Nice enough. He does not use powerpoint, which is fine but his lectures can be very disorganized which is frustrating. He really overemphasizes spirituality and religion, making those who are non spiritual or religious uncomfortable. Class is easy, just a few assignments, lots of extra credit BUT he is really strict about attendance.

Nice,considerate professor who is ALWAYS willing to help& clarify.Impossible to fail;just attend class &he'll tell you EXACTLY what you need to know to pass the course&succeed in the field.Very knowledgable&prepares students for the future not just this one class. Definitely one of the best professors at UMBC!

Awful professor... He was frequently late and ill-prepared. His exams were full of obscure facts/statistics from the text. His lectures consisted of him reading from a study guide in the book. Nice guy, awful professor.

Interesting class material but did not have a clear structure for lectures. No powerpoints and over specific tests. Interesting guy but difficult to know if you are meeting his expectations on papers or on tests.

Dr. O really knows his stuff. He is also very personable and down to earth. I would say that it is sometimes hard to follow his lectures because he does not use powerpoint, but overall, I learned a lot in his class.
Great Teacher!

Dr. O is a great professor. He is very passionate about the profession and has experience in many different areas of social work. He comes from a more clinical/medical mindset which was helpful for those of us interested in medical/mental health/private practice.

The professor is very helpful to his students. His philosophy of class is to prepare students for practice (their career). The information he teaches is very practical. The professor does everything possible to help his student obtain excellent grades. His study guides are extremely helpful - study them for an A on his tests.

Great Professor. Instead of finding devious ways of tripping up his students, the professor finds ways to make the class material clear, practical, and applicable. One of the best teachers I have had.
Great teacher, really makes it interesting. I actually became a Social Work major because of on of his human behavior classes.
awesome, good class. love it
Class is fairly easy if you come to all classes and do all the assignments.. Very nice and funny guy.. I got a B but I could have gotten an A

One of the best professors I have ever had. Great personality, very easy to relate to, you can tell he cares and he makes learning fun. I would recommend anyone take a class with him. He is very insightful and just an overall great professor and person.
Awesome teacher, incredibly informative, helpful and understanding. Very fair grading, loved his class

Dr. O is a great professor! He is always willing to help students with papers, issues with the class, etc. There is a lot of psych in the class so brush up on your old psych notes. Awesome professor, cannot wait to have him for another class!
Very nice Professor.  Really wants you to do well.  Make sure to use the writing labs on papers, otherwise as long as you follow instructions you will do well.
He is a great professor. I really enjoyed his classes!
Awesome.

Dr. O is an awesome teacher and wants all of his students to do well. At first it was hard for me to understand him but after the 1st 2 classes I had pretty much picked up on his accent. He is very knowledgeable and has a lot of experience in the field.
GREAT!
Took him for 388 & 389. Great guy. Incredibly smart but teaching really isn't his forte. If you read and write decent papers you will receive a good grade.

This class was nearly identical to psych100, but even easier. His first exam was hard, but the second one was a breeze. He grades his papers very easily, so long as you follow the guidelines. At first he was frustrating, but he got better.
Dr. O is really funny...he tends to be a little unclear about exams and papers but overall its not a difficult class...i actually enjoyed it.

At first it was kind of annoying but he works with students. Compromises often, don't make annoy him. He is funny, cares about students. SOWK majors take this class with him. Best SOWK class I took thus far.
Dr O is very good I would recommend taking him if you can
Dr. O is great, once you get the rythem of his accent he is easy to understand.  He brings a ton of clinical and research exp. to his class discussion. Highly recommend him.

I took him for both human behavior classes! He is so much fun! I little boring at times because he lectures straight from the book but it makes it easy to follow along, he also cracks jokes every now and ok which are pretty funny, he also some how knows everything! very good guy highly recomendable

Very knowledgable man with good insights.  Class feels like an expanded PSYCH 101 class though.  They tried out a new text book (author: Schriver) that is ABSOLUTELY AWFUL. But Dr. O is very good, very accessible and (mostly) comprehesible.
He has a wonderful personality, very funny. He made the class very interesting. He was always willing to help me when I needed him to. His accent was not a problem for me at all. I enjoyed this class
He is a very helpful teacher.  This class is easy to take in because of his good personality.  He is funny.  His class is a class that I enjoyed.
Mr. Okundaye is a very nice teacher. Its a little hard to understand him sometimes due to his accent. But he's ok. He grades a little hard but he's very funny and keeps the class intresting.
Great teacher, make sure you pay attention though.

Dr. Oyen is very nice and clearly has a lot of passion for the field of Asian studies. Course was graded on in-class participation which could be made up online through discussion posts if you weren't in class, and 5 unit tests (no mid-term or final), along with a final project and a paper.

-Very few assignments: 10 in-class, midterm, final project (whole semester to write 6 pages), final
-Lenient grading, just need to show you understood general diasporic trends and events
-Primarily lectures, but I found them very engaging with interesting stories
-20 pages of reading per week, all provided on Blackboard

You can tell Dr. Oyen is really excited to talk about her area of study. The lectures were all very fun and concise, and there were many opportunities for us to chime in and discuss the topic at hand. There's a handful of quizzes and essays, but they are a piece of cake if you take notes during the lectures. Overall, loved the class!
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Nice prof and enjoys what she teaches. Very knowledgeable and will help you through your papers. The first paper i wrote got a B but her notes made me realize what i had done wrong and the second paper i got a 97. There are group discussions and the class material was quite intriguing.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Group projects

reviews.comment: Dr. Oyen includes interesting informations on her slides, and it will be helpful to jot some notes during lectures. She will give out study guide for mid term and final, so make sure to prepare the outline for the essay portion. The class overall was not hard as long as you come to lecture; however, pay attention to the lessons, not your phone!!

She is a very nice person and truly passionate about her field however, her teaching structure wasn't good and she was a pretty harsh grader. As long as you go to class, and do well on the midterm and final you should be good.

She graded a level 100 class like a 400 level. I have taken level 600 classes at UMBC and got A's on essays fairly easily. However, I was shocked to see how tough she grades for a level 100 class. I wouldn't reccomend taking a class with her if you care about your GPA like I do. Kissing my 4.0 goodbye, I guess. Preparing for her final is hell.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: take any class you can with dr oyen! she uses clear rubrics, is pretty easy to reach via email or office hours, and gives helpful advice. she's open to students asking questions or challenging her lectures. not too much reading for a 400-level class. three papers, 'reading response' homework checks, and some in-class activities. phenomenal.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Hilarious

reviews.comment: clear rubrics and helpful advice. her passion for her subject is infectious; never thought i'd have so much fun learning historiography. as long as you genuinely apply yourself, you can succeed! the only class i've had where the lectures are informative AND involve memes and also the princess bride. looking forward to taking more classes with her!
She makes history fun to learn, and she's extremely helpful and willing to talk to you about any concerns you have. Just make sure you attend class on time and you're fine.

By far one of the worst classes I took at UMBC. I wrote the final paper & I did not get the grade I deserved. If I did not need this class for my major I would have never taken it. She is a very hard grader and won't tell you what you did wrong. Her lectures are nothing but a PowerPoint without any notes. Don't take this class if you don't have to.

Dr. Oyen is easily one of my favorite teachers at UMBC. She's  approachable and helpful, and her 201 class last semester shaped the way I write and study history. I hope I can take another class with her!

This course is an easy A.  The only required reading is online, you don't really need to use the textbook. Attendance is mandatory. A 15 page paper is required along with blackboard postings throughout the semester. Overall a great professor.

She just started teaching the class and she should stop after this year. She's uptight, passively condescending on a regular basis. Her mouth says one thing but her grading says another. She made a class that  basically is the 100 level in a history major a 400 level class. She made the paper more difficult that what it really needed to be

He is very passionate about teaching which makes his lectures more interesting and easy to listen to without getting bored. He is willing to work with students if they have issues, and exams can be difficult content wise but he tells you what to study to do well. He also allows a note sheet for every exam.

Dr. Omland was a great professor and I really enjoyed his section of the class. He was very easy to talk to and very personable so I did not feel intimidated going to his office hours. Really sweet guy, the key to getting A's on his exams (like I did) is simply just to write as much as you can from the slides onto your note sheet lol
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: shows bias and is rude. very unfair
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Good professor. I did better on the exams with Dr. Omland, they were more conceptual or application based whereas Dr. Leips had some math which I wasn't great at(even if it was easy). For the most part I would agree that the material we learned during LECTURES were in the exams. Take advantage of the few extra credit opportunities you get!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Respected

reviews.comment: lectures were long but he makes a good job implementing practice problems during lectures to work on and gives full credit for participation as long as you come to class, tests problems were a bit tricky but overall easy class.

His lectures were very helpful and prepared me for the exams. But some of the exam questions were a little annoying for example a question asked about which reptiles are native to Maryland, which is irrelevant to my understanding of evolutionary biology. Besides questions like that exams weren't too hard.

Omland was an amazing professor. He was very understanding and easy to work with. He cares for his students and wants them to succeed. His lectures are amazing and he tries to make them entertaining and engaging. I would take him a million times over. One of the best bio professors I have ever seen. Pay attention to lectures and you will be set.

Dr. Omland's section is better organized than Leips's. The tests are not easy, but the reading quizzes and in-class questions prepare you for them, and most people in my class did better on his tests than Leips. He is very passionate about his work and easy to talk to! Would have gotten an A if he taught the entire course. Amazing Professor!

Go to lecture, tests will be easy. Go to office hours, get guaranteed As on tests. All lectures translates well into discussion. Reading quizzes before class are reasonable and can be done in under 20 mintues.

Professor Omland was great. Tests were super easy, since many of them used answers found in the reading quizzes, which we did before every class. If you do the reading quizzes and take note of the answers, you'll do fine. Lectures were engaging with polls and energy, although professor was technologically challenged at times. Overall, Great prof.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Get ready to read--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: half the semester is omland, part 2 is leips. on omland: listen to the lectures & understand them. take note of the wordings and definitions. the tests were open note but timed, BUT you have to understand the minute details to really ace them. lectures were based on the textbook, so read the book. not everything was in the book; listen to lectures.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Doctor Omland's tests are so bad. The questions are basically more "have you come to my lectures?" and not "do you understand the concepts of biology?" He will tell you you need to understand the fundamentals to pass, but in reality, you just need to memorize the massive Tree of Life and all the phylogenies, and record his lecture verbatim.

Dr. Omland is a very good professor. His tests arent that bad if you study and make sure to read before class like every other course. He is funny at times and passionate about his work and past research. The only thing that I wish he would do is provide more than one sample exam and be just a little more specific about exam content.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Dr. Omland is a great professor and the class is extremely easy as long as you are willing to both understand concepts and memorize some material. If you pay attention during the lectures and study the information he emphasizes, then the class should be an easy A.

He has minimal clicker questions and his exams aren't that bad. When I took the class, he taught the evolution portion which was very easy if you memorize content on his slides (misconceptions about evolution, phylogenies of chordates, amphibians, reptiles) and how to answer his questions - the man LOVES "all of the above/none of the above" choices

Dr. Omland explains concepts well and is enthusiastic about his subject. He is very opinionated about certain topics. He loves talking about his research and himself in general. He is extremely proud of his accomplishments and wants you to be too. Be prepared to memorize lectures and trees. The only required reading was a book chapter he wrote.

Do not get me wrong he is a good Professor, but him teaching with Professor Leips is complete hell. Do not take them together at all. Do yourself a favor and avoid this class if they teach it. And I am a biochemistry major and this class was too much and it could all be so simple.

Dr. Omland was THE BEST! He was very punctual about responding to emails and was so funny!! He really loves what he does and his enthusiasm is contagious! Go to lecture because not everything he says goes on the powerpoints. Nicest professor ever

He co-taught this class with Dr. Leips.  Dr. Omland taught the evolution part, which most of the time, was sheer memorization.  I didn't really care for the subject and I thought Dr. Omland was a bit narrow minded.  His class was fairly boring aside from him using strange emphasis which was funny.  That might be what I remember most from the class.

This class is less about learning and all about memorization. Even then, Dr. Omland makes memorizing information difficult. On several occasions he gave the class dates in lecture and on the test there would be completely different ones. Sometimes the right answer would be OVER A MILLION YEARS off of what he had told us before.

"Learning the process of biology" and "understanding the fundamental concepts" - no, his class is about memorization, and specifically memorizing phylogenetic trees. Has an obsession with "everyone's reading the trees wrong!" and will literally hammer trees into your skull until you want nothing to do with him, BIO 142, or biology in general.

My least favorite professor of the three. His lectures were dull and his huge ego and constantly bringing up his own papers/research made it worse. Annoying guy, but you can do well on his portion of the exams if you read and go over the relevant chapters and MEMORIZE THE TREES.

Loved him! Made evolution very easy. Understand the basic rules/facts/contradictions of evolution and you'll do well. Also, understanding phylogeny trees is important! Out of the 3 profs, he was the easiest & had the most straightforward exams. Study tip: Listen to ALL old lectures AGAIN & take notes to do well on the exam!!!!

boring and teaches difficult subjects. a lot of memorization and uses old fashioned projector when he wants to write notes or draw phylogenic trees rather than using the board. it is difficult to see what is being written and annoying.

Honestly, I hated learning about trees. I don't know if that makes this sound bias but he used the whiteboard a lot of the times so goto lecture (most likely not on powerpoint). Hard exams because you don't know what to  specifically study. You're on your own. Ask the TAs for help and pay attention in discussion for this part of the course.

Dr. Omland is the 2nd Eco/Evo prof. and he covers phylogentic trees. He is EXTREMELY intelligent and is the first bio prof. I have had who has gone into the philosophy of biology. I have great respect for him, but he is generally unapproachable, and very egotistical. 8% of the 2nd exam asked questions specifically on his research. Tests are hard.

Terrible. Really confusing and unorganized. Didn't make it clear what information would be on the exam, besides tons of confusing, overly detailed phylogeny trees. Ugh. And he's kind of a prick.. he thinks he's right about everything. I guess this part of the course is doable, but its everyone's least favorite.

Nerdy and knowledgeable. He's very interactive with the class, which is a plus. He expects you to know EVERYTHING he says + what's in the book. Tests are very hard, impossible to be prepared for them. Pay attention to his random bird facts, they'll show up again.

He's such a dork (with sense of humor)!  Before I took this class I didn't care for evolution or whatever, but the material he presented ended up being very interesting!  I admit some material made me go "wha...?" but he's pretty approachable if you got a question for him.
i thought it was an easy class. good professor, went over what skills we needed many times.... trees were cool!!

The 2nd teacher for the class. He is a bit crazy and expected you to know dates and all of the seemingly random relationships and trees that he draws. His exams are pretty much all trees. Does CPS early in the class so get there on time.

Dr. Omland's section of the course was my favorite. He is a rather goofy guy, but very nice and helpful. You really have to study the phylogeny trees and do all the readings, but for me, his section was so worth the work. Attendence is mandatory, though. He has CPS questions during the first five minutes of class. Pretty easy on the eyes, too.

He's very nice and knows a lot about his field of study, but his tests will screw up your grade in that class. Basically, you must know how to read those darn phylogeny trees; he bases almost his whole test on them. Also, he likes to do clickers as soon as class starts and if you miss it, he doesn't care.
Not a fan.
I liked dr.Omland alot. He is a little crazy but he gets his point accross and is very interesting. To study just write all the notes onto notecards and memorize them and you will be fine

Hard. Exams are hard. Avergaes are 20 to 30 out of 40. Expects you to memorize the deuterostomia ranks and others too; and his lectures tiny details. Don't procrastinate on the readings. Good at mimicking animal sounds. Kinda strange, but approachable. I disagree with the other ratings, no way he is the best teacher. The notes are def not easy
he was the 2nd teacher of this class , yes he is a gigantic nerd and needs to go do his bird watching --- exams sucked class average would be in the 30's / 20's

He is so ridiculously excited and positive about speciation. it's great. and his notes are very easy to take because there are so few. but don't get too confident about how easy everything may seem. you still need to study
What a gigantic nerd.  But he's cool as heck and if you show up and remain awake, you will do great in his class.
Good guy, OK teacher, passionate about what he is doing though, which is a good quality.

One of the best lecturers at UMBC. This subject could easily be tedious but he makes it fascinating. And he doesn't mind telling rude students to cut it out. His enthusiasm for the subject is contagious, I highly recommend this class!
No Comments

The Birdman will drive you coo coo with his tests.  Other than that, exams are off the notes which pretty much the class will make up as they answer questions as the class goes along.  Average professor since phylogenies are pretty boring in my mind.
Nerdy, dorky, cute in his own way. Birdman is on top of his game. fair man
His part of the class isn't as easy as Freeland's, but it isn't so bad.  Very approachable guy, though the material didn't interest me too much.
Pretty weird and quirky, and makes you participate. His exams will require you to study. He's alright.
very good teacher, explains very well, keeps you entertained and wanting to go to class, besides the notes are not all online and you'll need participation! funny guy!

Very interesting professor, can even make a bird brain understand evolution. I would recommend Omland anytime. Compared to all the other professors, Omland is very clear in what he is talking about. Tests are mostly from old exams.
He is V.E.R.Y. good at imitating animal and bird sounds, class was interesting aswell.

Memorize the notes and old exam questions you'll be fine. Has a tendency to break out into random frog, crow, oriole, and various other animals' mating calls. He is really good at them though! He'll throw stuff at people when they don't pay attention...mostly pens and occasionally a tennis ball.
Nice guy but tests are very hard. Grades completely based on tests. The lectures are rather interesting. He DOES offer a curve.

Has problems communicating clearly with students, but otherwise a good teacher. Will break out with a very loud, very accurate animal call at the drop of a hat - not just birds, either. Ask him about waking up in Borneo.
HIS EXAMS ARE HARD
boring, mean.

HORRIBLE! he's boring, doesn't know how to get the material across and tries to make jokes for the class to like him.  He's very rude to students, so if you are unclear about something...he's not the person to clarify it!

Does his best to teach, but utterly pretty disengaging in terms of the material.  Probably the more boring section of the course to be tested on and yes, his exams are a bag of fun, but not in the good way.
no direction to lectures, not very detailed.

Not a bad professor at all.  lectures are interesting, but make sure u take notes and study the past exams, cuz he takes stuff DIRECTLY from that (sometimes word for word).  dont have much choice with ecology professors, but hes a good one.

Great lecturer, but his exams were so damned confusing!!! He had some good stories and asked students to give examples.  It was at 9 in the morning, which made it sort of hard for me to get enthusiastic about the material.  The Statistics part is BORING.

Decent teacher but expects you to have your notes completely memorized word for word to do really good on his exams.  Like the last person wrote, hes a teacher that has a multiple choice test with 6-7 choices for each answer, so its hard to guess, lol

Some of the lectures left something to be desired.  But most of them were really interesting and engaging.  he loves nature.  he always talks about his trip to borneo, it gets old but some of the stories are funny. class is really easy if you study hard

Tests are confusing because he uses the whole A, A & B, A B & C, None of the above thing. I did a lot worse than I thought on tests. Knows his stuff, though. Don't come in late or leave your cell phone on or he'll single you out.
Great Professor

Asynchronous over winter semester. Homework was very similar to 103 which was fine. Had some other assignments each week (speaking, culture). On a speaking activity, prof got mad b/c everyone did it wrong (spoiler: his instructions were not clear at all). Reused questions from homework on quizzes/tests. Feedback was rare, and unhelpful when given.

Decent professor. Homework assignments primary way to learn content. In-class lectures review of homework. Sometimes felt like he was reaching for student participation too hard. Quizzes and tests not particularly difficult. Listen in class because sometimes he doesn't post details about projects, quizzes, etc. Clearly says what will be on quiz
Great prof.

had him again last semester. indeed one of the best prof on campus..I have a conflict with his course this semester but am looking forward to take his course next semester. I learned a lot from his last couple courses. Samir is an Excellent prof easy going and willing to explain and help.. he wants his students to learn PERIOD!

He isn't the best or most informative prof but he's really nice and an easy grader. He does tend to ramble and go a bit over time but it isn't too bad. You do a lot of work online and he tells you to do smaller textbook based assignments but he never collects them or grades them. He is very easy to please and nice.
reviews.rating_tags: Tests? Not many--GROUP PROJECTS--Would take again

reviews.comment: He is a nice enough guy, but he will tell you things are due a few days before their due dates. Very unclear with directions. Lenient grader on tests. Expect to spend a lot of time (and money) on the online work for this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: He's has a really nice personality and is lenient with grading tests but he is EXTREMELY unclear on assignments and only gives you details for huge assignments a week beforehand. A lot of the students were asking each other about the assignments afterwards and even then, everyone heard something different from him. Unclear & unorganized. See tags.
He is a fun professor and the tests are really fair and easy if you do homework. I enjoy his classes.
Professor Omari means well and has great intentions, but he is very disorganized and know it because he has too much on his plate. Fortunately he knows this and adjusts his grading accordingly.
one of the best I have had on campus

Although Samir is well-intentioned, his lack of clarity and plethora of assignments overshadow this trait. I often found myself not knowing what or when an assignment was due. Due to how many assignments were given, it felt like a 300 level course. Oftentimes, the large amount of assignments felt unnecessary. Despite this, he was a lenient grader.

Samir can be a little unclear at times, but he is more than willing to help you understand. He said something the other day like "I want you to learn; I'm not here to punish you." There is a TON of homework, but it is essential. Beware, he can get very distracted very quickly. Do the homework and come to class, and you will do well.
best professor i've ever had, well rounded and culturally rich. very approachable friendly and helpful

I LOVED Samir! He is a really nice guy. I was dreading taking a French course, but he made it bearable. The classes were pretty disorganized and I found that I had to do alot of learning independantly, but I think that is just the nature of the course. He had lots of funny stories and was very forgiving in his grading.
VERY GOOD
So nice! Great guy and really wants his students to do well! There is a lot of online work to do, but it is very easy. I highly recommend taking a class with him!
