Hands down, the best professor at UMBC. One must take one of his French or Arabic classes at least once during their time at UMBC.
This class was easier than highschool french in my opinion. My lowest grade on anything in the class was a 79% Samir is a very very nice man! I highly recommend him!

Such a nice guy. Has a LOT on his plate; sometimes lectures can feel a bit rushed. If you don't do the workbook exercises on your own time, you'll fall behind easily. Don't leave the binder work til the last day. Everything on the tests is covered in class. Be prepared to move pretty fast 102-onwards. Love this man.

He has such a sweet & cute personality. He's always happy to answer questions and help. He's a busy guy teaching a lot of classes and he's also an academic adviser. He will always answer your questions during or after class. DO YOUR WORKBOOK work & all other homework and you will do great. Takes attendance but I'm not sure if it's part of the grade
Had Samir for French 103 and 202. Very sweet and helpful. EXCELLENT teacher despite the poor French curriculum. Moroccan, but knows a lot about many Francophone countries.

Samir is a very nice man and takes care to explain vocabulary and grammar that his students do not understand. He grades easily--do the C-Hour, homework, and tests, and you're guaranteed an A. Hampered by the inane 202 curriculum, but otherwise a great guy.
He's a nice guy. Pretty absent minded about the quizzes. Doesn't fllow the syllabus, gets sidtracked easily, is not clear about what homework is to be done. class is not very interactive.

A really sweet guy. He was very helpful, and took time to thoroughly explain a concept if the students were having trouble understanding it. He likes to learn from the students, too, regarding English idioms and expressions. It was a really fun class, and easy, too (at least I thought so, but then again I really love French).

Arabic. Samir is the best professor I've had at UMBC. He is incredibly helpful, and since his class sizes are small, he gets to know all his students, which may or may not help when the final grade is decided. His accent can get in the way sometimes, but  attend class, and do the homework, and you will surely get an A. Samir is an amazing professor

I love Samir. I wish I had been able to take 201 with him. He is one of the easiest professors to understand and very nice. He only canceled class when he had to leave the country because his father was sick and passed away.

A really nice person who goes out of his way to help his students. Relatively easy class, just a lot of homework. Sometimes unclear on explanation, but at least his exams are really easy. Had him for three consecutive semesters. I highly recommend him.

I really liked this professor, it is obvious that he cares about his students and really does what he can to help them. I took the class over summer and it was a lot of work, but I learned more than I ever thought I would. Definitely recommend him!!!

This guy is the best. If you have any questions, at all, he will explain it very well. Sometimes he explains so well he gives actual answers on exams. He gives a lot of extra work but they are very easy and helpful. I seriously reccomend him for every student especially those that are not that good in french. I guarentee you that you will have an A

Nice guy, but a little unclear. He expects very much from his Arabic students and moves extremely fast. I took his class during winter session, so it may not be accurate, but I found the class very hard and didn't learn much. Take his class if you must, but he is not ideal.
Great Professor!  He really wants you to learn the language.  His exams are fair and are graded fairly.  I love Samir...he really cares about each student.
He was very kind.  The class was easy.  He's almost too easy on exams.  I liked the compositions he gave us to do.  Good at explaining things and making you learn.
He is incredibly nice and hot in an odd, awkward, shy way. Really makes the class easy and is very approachable! SEKSAYYYY BEAST

This professor usually teaches french from what I hear but I had him for Arabic and he is without a doubt one of the most caring teachers I have ever met. He is extremely sensitive to students and his class is very easy to understand. If not, ask and he will make time to explain it to you.

AMAZING professor take him! He ends class early most of the time, 7 quizzes, 3 exams (same questions as quizzes), and a project. The whole class is very manageable and he works with you to learn the sql and diagrams. Slides aren't long either like 20-25 slides per class.
Love this guy, he made IS 147 so easy. If your not a programming person you don't have to stress at all, he focuses more on concepts and the final exam was take home.

Best professor I ever had. 3 exams, 1 project, and quizzes. The quizzes are from the slides, really easy. The exams are just the quizzes' questions. He explained everything well, making the class enjoyable.
Amazing proff and the work is easy just make sure to get the work done on time.

Professor by far one of the best professors I have had at UMBC, The lectures are clear, he has a sense of humor. Study the Quiz's, because they will help you pass the exam. Exams uses quiz questions(do with that what you will). Learned Oracle SQL , Making EER diagrams, Schemas,etc at a slow pace (so you should be able to get it).

Professor Ostrow is such a good professor. He made SQL very fun and easy to learn. His quizzes are very helpful, they are based off of slides and nothing else. Then the exams are only based off of what was on the quizzes so you aren't completely drenched in studying. He will make sure to help you understand something no matter how long it takes.

Online textbook and lecture slides were great for learning quiz material. HW was easy, quizzes were easy enough. Exams used old quiz questions. Programming was taught a slow pace. He answers all questions with good explanations, small class size. No final.

Ostrow is amazing. The online HWs are kind of annoying but mostly because of Pearson. There are in-person lock down quizzes every week but they are pretty simple if u pay attention. Exams are simple. Multiple choice are like the quizzes and the coding portion is open note which is amazing. Love this professor and 1000/10 recommend for any IS class!

BEST PROF! 2 parts of the exam- online MCQ which is theory questions. 2 part is coding- can you use your notes! there will be quizzes before every class from previous lectures to make sure you understand the concepts. Recommendation: read/look over slides before class for quizzes, the book is not needed & for exams review past quizzes its the same!
Very good professor! This is an easy class to not only learn basic programming but also to pass if you give it some effort.
Easy to understand lectures that are available on slides online. As long as your attending each class it'll be an easy class. Don't forget to do the homeworks.

Honestly he really is one of the best professors PLEASE take him for IS410!! He makes the material very simple if you pay attention in lecture. Gives great feedback if you patriciate in in-class exercises. All his quizzes come directly from his lecture slides and all his exams come from his quizzes so make sure to review those! Easiest A ever 100%.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Very understanding teacher. Actually knows what he's talking about and is able to explain instead of just lecture. Doesn't make the course too hard. W teacher 10/10 recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Beginner friendly, short quick lectures and lots of in class practice. Easy weekly quizzes and exams are easy as well.

Great prof and beginner friendly. Textbook was good for extra help. Weekly quiz, which go over the lecture slides. Exams are mc + programming. The only issue I would complain about is that the software used in class and the hw, make it hard to see your code and errors.

There are weekly quizzes so retaining all of the information from lecture is very important. He explains the content very well and walks the class through practical exercises that help a lot. There is no graded homework. Only complaint is that the class is graded by few things. Ostrow is an exceptional teacher.

This professor was one of my favorites. We had 7 quizzes and they were straightforward. He has slideshows that cover what is important for the quizzes and the tests are straight from the quizzes. The final project is well covered and he makes sure to prepare you for everything he throws at you. There was no homework though, so study for the quizzes
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Respected--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The class was pretty easy. Go to class, review the previous presentation for the quizzes, and study the quizzes for the exams. The only part of the class I didn't like was the homework. I felt like it was redundant HOWEVER the homework grade is like half of your grade. It is unlimited attempts so it was an easy way to secure half of your grade.

Short concise lectures, extremely helpful, weekly quizzes, 3 exams, no final. Lectures are extremely short bc he uses the majority of class time to practice what we learned during the lecture. Highly recommend his class.

Prof is nice and laidback. Lectures were boring but straight forward. You can get away with not reading the txtbook but I found it helpful. quiz at the start of class each on lockdown browser. 3 exams with programming section; questions come straight from slides. Project at the end of semester; no final exam. overall very chill and easy.
I took him for IS 147. He was very straight forward with his grading. This class with him was pretty easy. Would definitely take him again
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Weekly quizzes, 3 exams, and a project. You should not rely on the lectures and would absolutely need to spend some time studying outside of the class. But most of the exams come from the slides, so as long as you study them, you should do fine.

Great professor for IS 410. Took in person for fall. Had weekly quizzes but he dropped the lowest 2. Exams were based of powerpoints and he was always willing to answer questions and help you understand the material.
He is an easy professor. However, prepare to take weekly quizzes. There are 3 exams throughout the semester and an individual project. Use the slides to study for the quizzes and the exams.
Professor Ostrow is a great man and a great teacher. He was straightforward and efficient in his lectures. He was also very understanding of his students.

His lectures were fairly useful, though you could probably get by reviewing the powerpoints. The group project was very easy for me, though I have worked with SQL in the past. My only issue was that the project description was a bit limited and vague.

Coolest 425 teacher ever! He gives out really easy hw assignments. He gives lectures on only important topics relevant to the class. He gives out study guides study guides for every exam so you know what to exactly study for. No final exam just a final team project so make sure your team does well on it. For 425 I have to say he's the best one.
Jeff is cool. He doesn't make you waste your time on things that are not important. He makes the class fun by encouraging class participation. It is a chill class.
he is cool guy. his exam comes from the study guide and he will curve your exam grades. I

Ostrow is one chill mofo. He actually listens to feedback from the class as well. It was his first semester when I took him. He adjusted to our class and made it a great learning experience. I would definitely recommend him to anyone. Classes are pretty easy as well. He does fun class activities as well.

LOVE JEFF!! He is an amazing professor. He really cuts down on the crap and only gives you content you actually need to know (10 slides per chapter at MOST). Really great, really funny. Super amazing professor. I wish he taught other classes so I could take him again.

Asynchronous class with him. He is very kind and understanding. His exams are not bad as long as you study with the material he provides, he does give extra credit opportunities. He is easy to reach through email as well and grades with time. I highly recommend if you need the domain/extra credit course on the Psych track.

Dr. Piccin is a wonderful professor. This was an online course, but when I was having issues and reached out to him, he responded immediately and was incredibly kind. His exams are closed book but he ensures that you will do well. Even in a virtual setting his lectures are engaging and I learned a lot. I would absolutely recommend him!
Tough grader, but managed to get an A. I learned a lot in this class.

I love Dr. Piccin! He is an amazing professor/human and this is a great course. His setup lectures HW and exams were enjoyable allowing you to really learn with no pressure. He posts everything at the start of the semester making it easy/accessible to do everything on time. Don't fall behind and do everything recommended you will ace this course!
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I took him for PSYC 316 online. Class was very easy and straight to the point. 5 reflection questions each week and one exam each unit that are timed, but not proctored. He responded to emails quickly and I enjoyed his lectures and videos. He provided a lot of useful class handouts. I would definitely take him again! Easy A, just put in the work!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Would not recommend it, class is way to hard to be 3 credits. Tough grader too

Professor Piccin is a good teacher. When he can he will help you and meet you if you need that. There are four exams and the final. If you follow the lecture slides and take notes you will get a good grade. The class was asynchronous, so you could work on your own. Weekly homework assignments.

Professor Piccin was amazing for explaining well his lectures. He is willing to help you if you need the extra support. The class exams weighed a lot so make sure to study well for them as they are closed-book. Overall, the class was great.

I really loved going to Piccin's lectures. He was funny and a great professor who found ways to make presentations interesting despite teaching being an online course. There were many students, yet he would interact with us very often and would answer almost every question in the chat. Tests are textbook heavy which helps you know what to expect.

I thought i could pass without ever reading the textbook but nah. I recommend studying for his tests by going through study guides using the textbook and watching lectures afterwards. He gives extra credit, lectures are clear and make material easier to understand and grade is based on weekly reflections and exams. Book can be overwhelming though
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Peatross is an amazing professor. He genuinely cares about your future and helps with CPA, resume, and business skills. You will do well if you memorize his PPTs, MCQs, and HWs. No textbook. He tells you what is on the exams exactly. Personality is straightforward, funny, and real.

John was the best professor I've had at umbc. Homework due every week, 2 quizzes, semester long project, a midterm, and final. He tells you exactly what will be on the quizzes and exams. The bad reviews he gets are from sensitive people who can't take a joke, he is absolutely hilarious. Do not turn in final project late.
I've certainly had worse classes but this professor is extremely hot headed and not any real help if you don't understand course material. DO NOT TAKE.
This professor is perhaps the worst I've ever had, he was often extremely frustrated for seemingly little to no reason and took it out on our class. Which often amounted to many dropping it.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Amazing professor, basically goes through the example problems that will be on the exams the class before. Just attend all the lectures and you'll be fine.

Extremely responsive and willing to help students with course material and career/job concerns. He is a UMBC alum so he relates well to students. There is a semester-long project but he makes it manageable by making pieces of the project due each week. In addition to cost accounting, you learn many important professional skills. Take this class!

This course is definitely very student focused than the professor just rambling on lectures. Grading is pretty clear, a discussion post for each chapter reading along with a small quiz, and a final (group) presentation. Overall not hard, just read textbook outside of class, participation in discussion boards. Field experience isn't hard as well.

Professor Young is very wise and kind. Her grading is very straightforward: a discussion each week based on the textbook, quizzes worth 2 pts each, 4 field placements for this class (online or in-person), and a final presentation. I really enjoyed attending her class each day; she was extremely welcoming and understanding. Take her if you can!!

I think Dr. Young is a classic college professor. She expects you to do the readings outside of class and understand the material. There are a lot of written assignments, but they're all under 2 pages and fairly simple, but she is a tough grader. I learned a lot of the material covered in class and felt as though Dr. Young has really helped me.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Gives good feedback--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Dr. Young is not interested in teaching undergraduate students. I am surprised she ever worked in public schools because she always talked about how you can't care about the kids. She really uses about the text and makes redundant busy work, for what seems like the only purpose is to have a grade, and then grades strictly, with no concrete rubric.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: She constantly made it obvious she did not want to teach the course and just gave unneeded busy work.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: This course keeps you busy! Lots of reading, but you learn a lot. Short papers and online assignments required weekly. One midterm, one final, both papers. Don't slack on the Blackboard assignments, easy points. Follow her grading rubric for the papers to a T. Most people lost points for not following the directions!!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--SO MANY PAPERS--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: There is only a midterm and final. Extremely difficult. Hard grader and her feedback isn't always helpful. Expect to read ALOT and write short papers on everything that you read. You really have to understanding everything on your own to pass her class.

Tough class, a lot of readings in the course, assignments everyday. The feedback from assignments are really helpful. If you do all the readings then the assignments are easy. Don't wait to the last minute to read. Midterm & Final is difficult if you don't understand the readings. Overall, she is a good professor. Can't be lazy in this class
Awful. Changes criteria for grades all the time. Not efficient. Huge amount of readings each week plus short papers each week. Midterm paper was a nightmare. Unwilling to help.

Somewhat difficult class compounded by the fact that the material is very, very dry. You'll learn a lot, however, it's just not the most pleasant class to get through! Bring an extra folder because this class is handout-heavy.

Professor Young was nice. So far she was the best professor I had thus far. You will do a LOT of reading and writing in her courses. But you will see that what you learn and the work you do will be helpful in other classes. I recommend her for 607 & 650.

I was really looking forward to this class, but it was terrible.  Everything I learned, I learned by myself in a desperate attempt to do well in the class.  I learned NOTHING from her.  Grades did not reflect my work at all, and she was not clear about anything.  Did not get out of it what I was hoping to get out of it.  Very disappointed!

Dr. Young is a professor that expects her students to learn the material.  She expects her students to write well and grade accordingly.  She expects a lot and in return the preservice teacher is better prepated to enter the classroom.  My eyes were opened to concepts that I had not previously considered.  A class well worth taking.
Although this class is not the most fun. Professor Young is really nice and a fair grader. As long as you follow directions well, you should ace the class.

Dr. Young is a nice person and really wants for her students to get the information that she teaches. There is not as much work in this class as there is in 417 she is the only person that teaches both of theses classes. Just do your work and you will come out with either an A or B but when she give you a rubric follow that verbatim

Horrible Professor. It is depressing that she is a teacher teaching teachers. She changes grading critera based on favoritism. Contradicted herself in grading on a regular basis. Be prepared to read at least 150 pages a week. Paper due on these readings EVERY week. That is 15 papers people, not including midterm,final, teaching manual, and lesson!

Prof. Young is very nice, and her class is interesting, but you will work and read your textbook frequently. She is not an easy grader, you will have to work your butt off for an "A". A lot of work and reading!

Dr Mayer is a hilarious guy who has a blunt and honest attitude towards teaching students. Many people misunderstand his character because he's unfiltered and ready to discuss the taboo, but the conversation is justified by its relation to the course material. Very love-it-or-hate-it kind of style. If you want a fun Phil class, this is for you.
Too much reading + rude/cruel in general
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Test heavy

reviews.comment: One of the best professors I've ever had. I took him as a GEP req and I had a blast. He keeps your attention with silly stories and will answer any and all questions. He's changed his policies to have "pop-quizzes" meaning you wont be told which day of the week the quiz is on so you HAVE TO GO TO CLASS!!! Spent class time learning Gen Z slang too.

Knew the content very well but his lectures were mostly ramblings so you weren't sure what was important and what wasn't. This was my only non-major class and I had to spend the most time on it.  Definitely don't take him if you want an easy A.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: his teaching style is scribbling stuff on the chalkboard and lecturing about what if questions. then he assigns reads and has a quiz on them. the readings are hard and the lecture doesn't cover anything in the quiz yet attendance is mandatory. i don't recommend.

Dr. Mayer is very funny and his lectures are interesting, but if you're looking for an easy A, this is not the class for you. The readings are long and difficult, the quizzes and exams are way too specific, and there are very little opportunities to get grades. I can only recommend him if you're actually interested in philosophy.

you miss one quiz and it's over. u don't know ur grade because he puts them in at the very end..it's funny when he tells you about how he got his wife from stealing his roommate's gf. but when ur genuinely failing and he jokes about not putting in grades and how it's our fault for being so nervous, it sucks. u can not a miss a day for this class.

This class is well-suited for students genuinely interested in the subject, those majoring in philosophy. However, if you are taking it simply to fulfill an arts and humanities requirement, be aware that it requires significant preparation and engagement, more than other general requirement courses. Also, less portion to get your grades up.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Took him for 350: Ethical Theory. I like his lectures, he has a way with making sometimes boring papers make sense and explains in a fun way. He's edgy, some called him unhinged which I can see, but I think he's mostly "hinged". Makes him refreshing. But, no papers, 2 exams are most of grade. That's subject to change, and gave tons of extra cred op
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: A fantastic professor. Really engaging discussions. Great stories. Would retake this course just to sit in his class again. Assignments were difficult, but they were difficult to motivate you to do your best and genuinely learn.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Lectures are so funny and went by super quickly. He makes class interesting by talking about himself, but always relates it back to the content. Weekly "pop" quizzes on the readings are not too bad, but you do have to study/read for them. I took it as a GEP and studied for the quizzes in classes for my major lol.

Prof Mayer's class is one of the only classes I look forward to attending and I love talking in his class. His hilariously absurd stories nearly always connect back to the topic in a way that draws and keeps your attention. We had weekly quizzes, which he states are meant to be (mostly) easy, as long as you read the texts & a lot of them are LONG.
Awful!! Just awful! I give up
He wasn't a bad professor but attendance is mandatory but he also doesn't care if you're sick or anything. Class wasn't given many opportunities for a grade and wasn't taught well in my opinion.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: lectures are not mandatory.he gives out hw assignments once about every 2 weeks and are pretty straight forward.honestly almost never did the readings and did pretty good on all the assignments. 1 mditerm and1 final, he gives the questions a week before so you can practice before the exam. overall pretty interesting class and not that stressful

Super funny. Seems disorganized but he is. Kind of hard to take notes bc he uses a lot of personal examples/ stories, but he's accessible through office hours for more detailed breakdowns. Lectures aren't boring, but exams are hard. He doesn't give much feedback on the exam so it's hard to know how to improve, but overall great professor.
maybe an evil grader but so funny and knows the material super well.  go to the classes and do the reading it's a guaranteed B or C but an A probably won't happen.

Probably one of the most time consuming classes I have taken (bc of the readings). Not sure if he has lightened up on the work load, but be wary. Almost weekly quizzes and lengthy midterm and final exam questions. But he has videos up on the concepts and can answer almost any question you have about the texts. Guaranteed B if you do the work.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Beware of pop quizzes--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: great dude. classes are a bit hard but he tries his best to make sure everyone understands

Funny but conceited, often came to class unprepared and spent lots of time referring to the class as "youths". The quizzes were based on the readings and he does not go over the readings until after the quiz, so if you are looking for an easy A class, look elsewhere.

If you have looking for an easy A don't take him. He's going to say his quizzes are going to focus on the main concepts of the readings but they're not. Be prepared for questions like what is the counterargument against Descartes idea of free will. And the answer would be based off one sentence on page 12 of 15 of the reading. Overall fun class.

Do not take if you think this will be an easy A. I am not good at reading comprehension quizzes, which is what the majority of your grade depends on. The things on the quizzes are not related to what is being lectured and are barely what is in the reading, so you should really love Ethics if you plan on taking this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Dr. Mayer is very funny and makes a lot of comparisons to real life events to make the material easier to understand. There is a Lot of reading and the weekly quizzes can be fairly specific, so it is important to be thorough. Not the easiest GEP choice, but it is rewarding to understand the concepts in the class.

Professor Mayer was fantastic. He's hilarious, very knowledgeable about the material, and tries his best to make lectures engaging. There is quite a bit of reading, but he also posts YouTube videos of the topics if you don't feel like reading. Great Professor though, and I would highly recommend him.

This review is for PHIL 100. Professor is very funny and a nice guy but lectures are useless and mandatory. Readings are important, quizzes are very specific randomly picked from the readings. Grade is only made up of quizzes once a week, midterm, and final so it is impossible to bring up your grade if you do bad on those. Very hard for intro level

I had him for phil 101 in person (won't let me choose that as the course)
He would often forget to bring our wuizzes the day of class and would just delete that off the syllabus. He has a quiz every week that is difficult and is a big part of your grade. His lectures are very useless- he's a funny guy but does not really teach.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Mayer is so funny and the lectures are hilarious. However, learning the material is extremely difficult. He posts lots of articles to read which most people, including myself, don't get around to reading. If this class is not required for you, do not take unless you like the topic. Prof. Mayer is so funny but hard to learn from.

Honestly one of the best professors I've ever had. Lectures might be long, but the length is justified as they explore the material in an engaging, funny way. Uses analogies to real world events, life experiences, or other disciplines very well, which makes the material much easier to understand and remember. Expectations of students are very fair.

Professor try to make class enjoyable, yet he does talk a bit more than you might think. But it's all good since he always go back into the topic he want to discuss for the day. There is no exam but few quizzes that are important since it will change your grade letter.

The class was interesting. You will get 4 major quizzes and you'll have to read the books before answering the question. If you have a question, go to office hours. Take a note in class or watch the videos posted on Bb. I have learned a lot and you'll too.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Accessible outside class--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: He's funny, but not the best teacher tbh. I had him my first semester here and the lectures were boring since all he did was talk. If you take notes you need to either listen very closely to his lectures or just read the texts assigned to you. The quizzes are a lot harder than you expect and no you can't find them on quizlet. I didn't learn a thing

Makes every part of the class interesting and attractive to learn. While he goes very in depth on every area of study, he clearly conveys the main takeaways of lectures and posts the lecture slides for every class. You will be successful in the class as long as you are willing to come to lecture and do the work.

Dr. Phin is an amazing professor, and somehow manages to make even the most dull myths much more interesting. His grading is lenient and fair. He is quite lecture heavy, and his class requires attendance to really grasp the material, but his personality and storytelling ability makes the incentive to go to class even stronger.

Took classical myth over the winter; super interesting lectures and he's an fun guy so even though the class was an asynchronous I was very engaged. You get to write your own myth at the end of the course, so if that interests you I definitely recommend!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Took the class over the winter; as long as you do the work, it's easy.
great class, great professor.

Professor Phin is one of the best educators at UMBC. The course was completely Asynchronous and it is a great class to take to fulfill GEP credits, raise your GPA, and just to explore something you truly enjoy such as classical mythology. He cares about students and is very flexible and open to communication. 10/10.

Professor Phin is incredibly kind, an excellent lecturer, and deeply supportive of his students. He presents material clearly and engagingly, making even complex events easy to follow. What really sets him apart is how much he values his students' work and opinions. I highly recommend taking a class with him if you have the chance!
Awesome professor and class for winter

Professor Phin, is a very kind and caring professor. He genuinely wants you to succeed in his class. As long as you do the weekly readings for the class and do what you're supposed to do for the assignments you will pass. Just a heads up Professor Phin, can be a bit slow when it comes to grading assignments.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Caring--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Professor Phin is an amzingggg professor, he is not only caring but very understanding. I had to miss a day and I made sure to let him know and he was so nice about it. He also offered to help me with everything in case I didn't understand. He replies to emails fast. Would highly recommend taking him. His class is extremely fun to take.

I liked Dr. Phin. He's extremely passionate about what he teaches, and it shines through when he lectures. The class structure was a bit unorganized in my opinion, but he was lenient and generous with assignment deadlines. He has a great voice for teaching and his storytelling is quite entertaining! Would definitely recommend if you need a gen ed.

Hands down one of my favorite professors! Took this class as a GEP (stem major) and loved every second. He was very understanding when problems came up, and even though we had a lot of technical difficulties, he restructured the class so it wouldn't suck for everybody. You can tell he is very passionate about what he teaches :))
This guys is awesome! Very passionate about what he does, and he makes you want to learn.
Dr. Phin is kind, personable, and really cares about what he teaches, but he grades extremely slowly and gives few assignments with little direction throughout the semester.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Caring--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: An amazing professor. Very passionate, and all the assigments/exams were open-note and very easy. You are graded by 10 quizzes, 10 reading journals, midterm, Analysis reading, making a myth, and final exam. Would take again!

So passionate and it shows. He makes the lectures interesting to sit through. I will say there's A LOT of reading to do and all the quizzes are short answer responses but they are not difficult if you put in the bare minimum.
Attendance not graded, but lectures went into more detail than one gets from the online slides. Everything graded was online, open note, and given large windows for completion, so not challenging.

Best class I've taken here. Easy to get the grade you want but the material and his way of speaking will make you want to learn more. Was totally asynchronous and taken over summer, couldn't recommend him more.

HIST 456 is actually the course #. I had a wonderful time attending his Roman history lecture and I am glad I have taken at least one of his classes before I transfer. I also know why now, he's one of the most talked about professors, and believe that he truly deserves all the compliments. Grading can be a bit slow, but it's alright!

Professor Phin is one of the kindest professors at UMBC! He really cares about his students, and is a quick responder when it comes to emails. He also asks for your opinion on the materials and he's very accommodating. He really cares and it shows!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Caring--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Professor Phin is great. His class is discussion-based which is a nice change of pace. He also cares a lot about his students.

Professor Phin's lectures were always interesting and funny, and the RPG was fun. He is out sick often, though, so if you're actually trying to learn, it sucks. He is also an extremely slow grader; I had no idea what my final grade was going to be because he didn't grade 80% of our assignments until after the semester ended.

Very, very, very slow with grading. Semester is almost ending and I have three grades in and no midterm grade yet. Lectures are interesting and he is good at teaching but is very inconsistent with updates and grading.
Prof. Phin is great. I took this over the winter and its a very easy culture or arts and humanities credit. Asynchronous with a do it at your own pace format.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: I took this class winter 2020 online, and he is an amazing professor. He let me in when the class was waitlisted. There were a good amount of assignments but they were super easy and I got them done quickly. There are 2 projects that were also very easy. I pretty much got 100s on everything, and his lectures were fun, so it's easily my fave class.
The most amazing professor I ever had.

One of the best professors I've had at UMBC. He's a little disorganized with blackboard an assignments, but he is hands down the best lecturer I've ever had. He is also very friendly and accessible, and gives plenty of extra credit. You can sparknotes all of the readings and still pass. The final is just writing your own myth.

+ He's very passionate about mythology - Too many BlackBoard assignments - Poor communicator of due dates - Far too much reading for three weeks Don't take this class if you have anything going on in the winter. The readings alone take too much time. If you're just looking for an elective, LOOK ELSEWHERE!

participation is only important during the role playing game we play for two weeks of class, even if you don't know what's going on, the directions for the assignments are so specific and clear, you will just have to look where he tells you to and answer the prompts. he is so nice, fun in class, and understanding if you need an extension. easy A.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Dr. Phin is one of my favorite professors. There's no attendance for lectures but they're so entertaining that very few people skip (it also helps that this class isn't in the early morning hours, but still). I learned so much throughout the semester and even his midterm/final papers have a "fun" theme

Professor Phin is one of the friendliest people I have ever met. He is very calm and relaxed and sometimes makes jokes in class. He very easy to reach outside of class and bends over backwards to help students pass, if you let him. He is very generous grader. He has interests in all sorts of things and is very approachable.
Probably the best professor I've ever had! This guy has it all. He is funny, smart, and runs a very fun classroom. Take him, you won't regret it.

I took this class in Winter 2018, very crammed but with proper time management, It is possible. Phin's class and homework schedule was straightforward. Lectures were interesting and he gave the class a laugh. Expect to read A LOT and grasp the material for the quizzes. He is accessible outside of class and he will help you succeed in this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Cool professor. Hes really easy. We originally had 2 papers, 2 exams, 10 weekly readings/postings. At the end of the semester he dropped one paper and made us only do 5 postings. And we played a senatus game: a rpg of the Roman senate which was dope. My only critique is that I dont feel i learned a whole lot.

Prof Phin is awesome, he's super caring and understanding. He has great knowledge of the material he teaches and is a bit silly. Class is not boring, you learn interesting things. Read the odyssey and Iliad, along with a few stories...a lot to read but super easy class.

Incredible professor, incredible class.  His lectures are super engaging and he is passionate, understanding, and hilarious.  Absolutely one of my favorite professors and easily one of the best classes I've had
Professor Phin is a great teacher, and is very easy going. I would recommend reading the material listed on the syllabus, because that is what the course revolves around.
Take him!! I had no interest or knew mythology at all before I took this class but his class taught me so much that i can spot mythology any place I go to. He is amazing, everything is doable.

This was his first semester teaching Classical Mythology online! He's a great professor. Unfortunately, I only had the chance to meet him in person once. Is pretty lenient with online homework/assignment deadlines as long as you turn it in 24 hours after the deadline. I enjoyed this class and it was an easy and fun elective!!

Amazing! Took him summer16 session. Lectures were never boring, content wise and how he delivered them. He is passionate about the subject and we know he loves his field. I only read the sparknotes version of epic poems (Odyssey,Illiad) and got an A. Maybe b/c it was summer and less in depth? Easy online portion, blog and journal short response

His lectures were fantastic because he is so interested in, and excited by, his subject. When he talked I felt like he was narrating on stage and I got the pleasure of listening in. Class is not mandatory, but I highly recommend going. A note on his papers: he actually prefers less words, so if you can get your point across in 500 don't add more.

This Professor is a true joy to take a class from. He loves hearing his students' opinions and having good discussions in or out of class. He is wonderful at working with students who are having difficulties for any reason, and he allows much leniency for personal matters. Very engaging and fun.

I took this class in the winter and I loved it. All the lectures were so interesting. The class was very easy as I had a lot of prior knowledge. The main writing were blogs and writing a myth both were very enjoyable to write. Quizzes were online and in class and easy. I never dozed off in the class(which I often do). Highly recommend to fulfil GEP

Awesome professor. Really nice and passionate about history. There is quite a bit of reading, but it is a history class after all. If you are taking any of his upper level classes, it would probably be best that you have some background in history. Very lenient grader. TAKE HIM!
Love this teacher!!! So much fun but there's a lot of reading and writing  and research but will help you even if it's not for his class! Ha' loves to laugh n is Avery animated teacher.
Easy A

I took Professor Phin for ANCS210 in the winter session and his lectures were awesome. Going into the class, I thought it was going to be painful, but he is immensely interested in his material and his subtle humor can catch you off guard.
Amazingly interested in the students, very engaging and a fun class coming from someone who barely knew who Zeus was before class, now after a winter session can pick mythology out everywhere

Professor Phin respects students and wants you to succeed. He also has a great passion for his subject. He offers alternative ways to showcase your knowledge which is great. I would take his class again.

INCREDIBLE Professor. The dramatic quality of his voice makes class like being in a living movie. I learned so much about ancient mythology, and it was clear that this was his true end goal (as was evidenced by the lenient grading system and creative assignments). Take this class!!!

One of the best professors at UMBC. Extremely theatrical voice which makes Greek Mythology even more epic. Super lenient with grading. Cracks jokes and is suuuuper understanding. He is has perfected the art at making a class easy AND causing his students to actually learn! TAKE THIS CLASS FOR YOUR CULTURE CREDIT!!

He's enthusiastic, but he didn't follow anything he said we'd do on the syllabus. He grades essays really leniently. I didn't do any of the readings, I just sat there during class. 40% of the grade was supposed to be based on discussion, but I think he just gave everyone full credit for that. I hate history and stuff, but his class was tolerable.
He is an AMAZING prof. He is the reason I am an ancient studies minor. His lectures are interesting which is good because you have to go to class to do well on his tests.

I've had him as a professor a couple times now, and he is definitely my favorite. His classes involve a lot of reading, but as long as you do the work you'll be fine. His lectures are always fun, and he's very nice.

Great guy. Best lecturer I have ever, ever had. Great speaker always extremely helpful and clear. My only issue was his test were so essay heavy. About 4 short answer Q's, maybe 4 or 5 definitions, and then a usually four-ish page essay. I'm sure for some this is wonderful but I was a freshman ANCS major without ENG 100. Not my test style at all.

I had this professor for Classical Mythology. HE LOVES THIS TOPIC. He is very passionate and knowledgeable. Very nice. I thought the course load was extreme for a 200 level course but he is a very easy grader so it balanced out.

Very entertaining lecturer. All of the answers for the "short answer" portion of his exams can be found on Wikipedia (he gives you a review sheet ahead of time). His grading is rather strange, and it is almost too lenient. People that did not ever go to class got better grades on exams and on the book review than did people that went every day...

Take his classes; he's stellar, and I love the way he speaks. He knows like everything about the ancient world. I didnt know anything before this class, and I've been learning a lot. Super supportive, funny, engaging.

Excellent teacher. Extremely knowledgeable about the content he's teaching. His lectures are extremely fun to listen to. I feel disappointed whenever class is cancelled. Tons of reading, but study guides are helpful and can reduce some of the reading load.

AMAZING professor. Very helpful. He's smart, so nice, funny, and you can tell he really loves the material he's teaching, which makes a big difference. I'm a biology major and so I didn't know anything about mythology before his class; I feel like I've truly learned a lot from him. I definitely plan on taking another class with him next semester.

The person who called this guy the poor man's James Lipton is so hilariously right. His oratory style is insane....in a good way. He's super knowledgeable and obviously loves what he's teaching (Roman Republic in my case). So far, the most history professor I've had at UMBC and I'm a history major. Be prepared to read a lot though.

Seriously may be the nicest professor I have ever met in my college tenure. This grading for the class was composed of participation (30%), weekly journals (30%), and a paper (40%). He is incredibly flexible and very interested in the subject matter which makes the class 100x more interesting. Best part, he sounds like a poor man's James Lipton!!!

Dr. Phin is an excellent professor. His style of teaching is incredibly engaging; his passion facilitates the material. He's very approachable and really wants students to succeed; he really understands students. His courses do require effort, but it's very difficult to fail. Overall, he makes you want to attend class--and that's a feat.

Really awesome professor. What makes him stand above the rest is his interest in the subject and his presentation. He really gets into the lectures and you just sit up in your chair and listen. I wish more professor had his energy about their subject material. Would definitely have him as a professor again.

One of the best professors at UMBC I have ever had. Fantastic at teaching Roman history, extremely helpful, funny, and brings out the excitement in class. 2 exams, discussion on Blackboard and 2 papers. EASY A class! To every student out there: GO FOR HIS CLASS. Prof.Phin is the man!!!!! You rock!!

Awesome class. Had no interest in Ancient Rome before, and now I almost want to minor in it. He is very good at telling stories about Rome, and very interested in answering questions you may have. Two exams, two papers, and an easy online discussion board activity. I highly recommend Professor Phin.
Great Professor, very funny and seemed to know everything there is to possibly know about the subject. Test's were very easy.
Theatrical, fluid speaking ability. Got the class to laugh a lot. Required a lot of reading and writing, but was a fairly lenient grader.
He's a great person and intelligent, but exams were extremely hard. He'll meet with you, but there's not much he can say because the overall class isn't curved.
Good at teaching, passionate about the topics, approachable after class, and really cares that you understand. He is a great biology professor. I wish he taught more.

I encourage every Biology major student to take this class. I truly am grateful for him getting me out of my comfort zone and he is super passionate of this area of study. Also he's a fair grader just answer the questions clearly. If I can pass so can you.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Group projects

reviews.comment: Dr. P was amazing!! His lectures were so fascinating and kept you engaged and he conveyed the info in a way that it was easy to understand. I would love to take this class again with Dr. P!
Lots of fun projects. Enjoyed the coding we did!

She was the best and sweetest teachers, even though she did have accents and weren't always clear, she woul explain it to you multiple times with out getting mad! Also, really nice how we didnt need to use a textbook! She was very open based on her grading as wel. Best Teacher EVER!!!

DIDNT learn real OOP. Took this to impress employers, got a job doing java GUI interfaces. DIDNT prepare me for the real world, despite being graduate class. Only scratched the surface of what I needed to be successful in this job. Wish I had gone elsewhere to learn Java OOP. Back to job hunting for entry level bc thats all she taught us: beginners
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--GROUP PROJECTS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: She contradicts herself as far as grading criteria is concerned. Her lectures can be confusing because she's an amateur, at best, at teaching. Her thick accent and tendency to mispronounce words doesn't help. I did not learn enough to justify the cost of this graduate level class. I think I was better off at a community college.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--GROUP PROJECTS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Class is titled "Introduction to OOP Concepts" but had LITTLE to do with OOP. She taught beginners programming. Extremely slow-paced for a graduate class; 14 weeks to do 9 chapters, 8 of which had nothing to do with actual OOP. Ver easy A, but a waste of time and money. Forces group work on project. Terrible accent. Nice personality but boring lec.
She is from a chemical engineering background, she is not good in the technical domain.  She is very tough and makes student life complicated. She never tries to help and puts a lot of pressure.
Good professor.

3 exams, 3 quizzes, few homeworks, one database related technology presentation, and one semester long database design project. Dont spend too much time reading the power points because you actually have to know how to draw ER Diagrams. She is very unclear for the most part in her lectures. Easy to get a B or work a little hard and pull an A
3 homeworks, 3 exams, and a project.. she is unclear at times

3 HW, 3 exams, 1 short group project on database technology, 1 long semester group project on database design. HW is 12% and pretty straightforward. Questions on exams are similar to hw problems. Exams range from moderate to challenging; easy to pull a mid B. Prof. Zhu grades very quickly, responds to emails quickly, shows enthusiasm and is helpful

Nice teacher. Easy grader. She does not really teach because she expects students to learn by themselves. So it is all about learning independently in the class. If you have time to spare, take this class.

Very clear on what she wants you to learn, but does not teach it. It's more of you reading the book on your own and then come to class for clarification. I couldn't learn a lang like that. Nice, but too busy to talk or for makeup work or to change grade book errors on time.
great teacher. very organized. sometimes is a tough grader on homework,but tests are easy. never tests on anything that we didn't go over in class. lots of work, but not hard to keep up with.
Cares about her students, very reasonable about making up missed work, nearly always cheerful and fun to be around.
she is so cuuuuuute!!!
Very cool professor. The class is not that hard, as long as you keep up with the work. She is very talkative, friendly, helpful and an Argentinian cutie.
awesome teacher.  very leaniant when late and very reasonable.  very easy grader.  shes a fun person to be around
She is a nice person.. she dances and sings all the time!!

Dr. Q is a kind, caring professor. It's obvious she tries her best to engage students in the material, but PSYC 370 is an extremely difficult course that's essentially all bio + anatomy. Participation is a huge chunk of your grade and it can be very difficult to earn all the points in class (especially in large lectures) Exams are open note!

Dr. Quiton, while nice, teaches a course that, in essence, should be essential to attend a lecture, but was not that important. Fewer people showed up per week. Most of the lectures are regurgitated from the video lectures she has, which takes up so much time, and some material is only found within these video lectures and not discussed in person.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Attendance not mandatory. Super sweet and is open to helping with content. Units can be difficult to follow but her in class lectures and activities are the best for learning material. All exams and assignments are online. Would absolutely take her again!

Dr. Quiton is a very knowledgeable and intelligent professor. Assignments consist of weekly check-ins and learning quizzes, 2 reflection writings, and the midterm and final exam. She encourages a lot of group work in-class as well. She is a stickler for attendance, so it is probably in your best interest to go to class.

Very organized with how she wanted the class to go. She also gave clear explanations when students felt confused and overall I had a good experience with this class. It is very homework heavy however, and if you turn anything late, she will not hesitate to take away points fast.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Dr. Quiton is such a sweet & knowledgeable professor. She's very open to student input & is very kind. Her online lectures were super helpful for me, class was used to discuss and clarify. She's very dedicated to teaching-her car broke down on the way here, so she held class virtually from her car. Material will be challenging w/o a bio background.

Prof Quiton was an exceptional professor. She had online recorded lectures and in person lectures (only once a week). Homeworks, quizzes, and exams were online. She gave out extra credit and she challenges your knowledge of the material! If you need anything just contact her, she's very understanding and easily accesible outside of class.

Class is very tough and I wish I took a different class for the requirement. The content and class is hard. She tries her best to help but still not enough for the rigor of her exams and materials she gives out. This is a hard Pscyh course unlike others specially with this professor and semester was rough
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Test heavy

reviews.comment: The class is really hard due to the professor and get ready to put a lot of time to this psych class. As nursing major having taken higher biology classes it was still very hard. Exams are tough. Have to work really hard to get a B and most get C. Not a good experience

Very nice and understanding, the course itself is super difficult but if you do the readings and listen to the online lectures you should be able to do well in the course. Do all the quizzes (multiple chances) HWs and assignments. She randomly gives extra credit in class too.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: The class content sucks but she makes it fairly engaging. Good explanations and has fair policies

Dr. Q is a great professor who knows how to teach the material in very effective ways. I'm not a STEM student and this class material was difficult for me, but Dr. Q helped make it fascinating & less painful. Gave us an open notes final which was appreciated during a stressful time. Grades on participation so come to class! Take notes on lectures!

Professor Quiton is very well organized delivers a clear structure. She is lecture heavy and very knowledgeable, you don't really need the textbook tbh. She offers extra credit and (unfortunately) does use lockdown browser but with no camera. Her class was difficult but she is very open to breaking things down and truly cares about each student!
Prof Quiton requires lockdown browsers for exams, which is malware and spyware. That alone is a good enough reason not to take her class.

Amazing, kind, and knowledgeable. Her lectures are clear, detailed, and interesting. This is a tough class, but she makes it very clear what you need to know for the tests. Going to class and the review sessions is key (and she gives extra credit for in class activities). Fill out the study guides for your own benefit, they will really help!

Dr. Q to this day is one of the best professors I've ever had. Amazing lectures. Something about the way she taught made things stick. I don't know. I just loved how organized she was. Everything was set, clear, and precise. You were never under any anxiety and always knew what to expect with her. Come to class and you'll never touch the book + EC
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: For me, the class wasn't bad because I had a strong bio background. If you don't, this class can swamp you so be careful. Study her slides carefully (book isn't needed) and make sure to practice and memorize concepts in detail. She knows her stuff so ask questions. She gives a ton of extra credit so do it early so that you have a cushion.

The tests are very intense, but if you study the study guides exactly and do the practice quizzes, you will be okay. There is a lot of information to know but if you are good at memorization, you will do well. She also offers a lot of extra credit. I never opened the textbook, I regret buying it. Difficult class, but an A is possible.

Dr. Q basically tells you all the material you need to know for exams. Make sure you read the questions carefully because she likes to do T/F questions where part, but not all of the statement is true. Turn in assignments ON TIME. Not even a few minutes late. Go to class because there are lots of opportunities for ec. Solid lecturer.

Dr. Q is a good professor who is very thorough in her slides. She doesn't expect everyone to come to class, but rewards people for coming with EC. Her lectures can get a bit boring, but she's definitely engaged in what she's teaching. Her tests can get hard if you're not looking closely, but not impossible if you've studied the slides.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: I refuse to sugar coat this course and make it god or maybe its the Professor, but I studied everyday and didnt get credit for all the hard work I put in. I took notes, recorded lectures, and studied from the book and I'm failing. This makes me think that the teacher makes it difficult because they dont wan to see others succeed in life; shame

Dr. Q is very into her lectures, but can ebe confusing at time for an exam. Her exams are difficult, because she teaches one way but test you on different things. She refuses to believe that students are right and she is wrong. Extra credit is honored, but worth very little compared to the amount of work it requires.  She doesn't give full credit!

One of the best professors i have taken. she is strict but very organized, has the exam grades out the same day. Come to class on time coz she sometimes gives extra credit. Read the chapters and do the reading quizzes coz she brings stuff from there, she changes the structure a lil bit but you will recognize the questions.

Dr. Q knows her stuff and is a great lecturer. She gives tons of extra credit so it's impossible to fail her class if you try. Her test are tricky but she has a study guide and practice exam on Blackboard for every chapter.

A lot of information in each class period, so make sure to go to lecture. She takes attendance for curving purposes. Finish with a 79 but went to every classB. A lot of extra credit. Make sure to study the textbook for exams.

She is extremely knowledgeable, and a very nice person. Just tests and a few little homework's. I found the material extremely difficult, coming from a non-science background, but she is very clear about what she expects you to know. Tests are all multiple choice. Start studying way in advance, because it is a lot of heavy material to learn.

She is an absolutely amazing professor! My favorite professor by far! She is very clear and she welcomes all to participate in class. Both Sensation and Perception and Physiological Psych were super informational. All of the material can be used outside of the class. There are a bunch of extra credit options and her study guides are very clear.

It's a tough class. Make flashcards- all memorization. However, she explains things very well and is helpful. Gives a lot of extra credit and drops an exam. Take advantage of extra credit if you want an A. Go to class, it's interesting and helpful.
Class is TOUGH and very sciency. She really knows her stuff and the classes are pretty interesting. Tests are really difficult.

Compared to the biology courses I've taken at this school, this class is so much easier but that doesn't mean you don't have to study. The material is pretty interesting, most of it is pretty conceptual. All you need to do is go to lecture and study the book. Don't buy extra stuff like the online material. A lot of extra credit opportunities.
Super tough class and tests are very hard! She really knows her stuff and is interesting to talk to but the lectures are kind of boring.

Such a nice professor, relates physiological processes to psychology very efficiently. Lots of extra credit! Class attendance not necessary, but beneficial as many ec opportunities are given during class.

THIS CLASS IS SO HARD. As a psyc major, a biological psyc is required, and I heard good things about this class. Easier than psyc 390 but still really hard. She is a good teacher and really seems to be passionate, but it's just a hard class. Her grading system is good too- a lot of lowest grades get dropped, but just be prepared!

You cannot understand the lectures, he is very hard to talk too, practice quizzes and exams are nothing like the real ones, takes him forever to put in grades. You'll be better off with any other professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: He's caring, but wants you to learn the theory more than how to solve the problems. You have to basically learn everything outside class. There are a lot of resources on BB though and tutoring definitely helps. The quizzes are much harder than the practice quizzes posted on BB. And his accent does make it more difficult to understand new things.

the thing is a lot of students don't attend his lectures cuz they're a little hard to follow pace wise and with his accent. Other math professors also keep past quizzes and exams posted for study material while he didn't which I didn't really appreciate cuz it was pretty hard to know what to study. use resources posted on bb
very bad, watch professor Leonard instead if you want to pass and understand the material.

This teacher will withhold information from his students if they don't attend his lectures, which are impossible to understand. He changes his syllabus and the way exams are taken. The HW is mostly random times. He should be reported to the school and given an easier job that doesn't involve contact with students at all. He barely tries for his job

This professor doesn't deserve his job. The people rating him good only did bc they got a good grade in his class. I've done well in his class, and he is by far the worst teacher I've ever seen. I have taught myself everything bc you can't learn from him. He tries to make it as hard as possible for students to pass. He's one big emotional baby.
Worst grader
you cant understand him.

His lectures are completely pointless because you can't understand anything he says. His quizzes and exams are insanely hard; barely anyone passes. Don't take him if you do. He is a nice guy, though, but he's just not professor material. None of his study materials help either. I have had an A in every math class before him. DONT take his class

He is very lecture heavy. However, with homeworks, he cares more that you practice the material as opposed to submitting it on time. Beware though that final exam was bit tough. Still managed to get A on it though. His handwriting can be bit sloppy and talks very fast in lecture. Other than that, good prof and caring prof. Go to OH.

Dr. Rasika is kind, easy to talk to, and passionate about his subject, so attend office hours regardless of if you're struggling. His lectures were a bit difficult to follow, but it becomes easier if you go regularly. If you ask questions, he will slow down and re-explain. Just show up and try, and you'll be golden. I'm taking him again for 152.
His lecture are hard to understand but you can lowkey teach yourself everything with all the things he puts on BB. The HW is good to do, all the quizzes and exams are fair

He's not the greatest at lecturing. He cares more about the proof than showing us how to solve. You have to give up time to teach yourself. The online textbook helps, but to an extent. Extra credit is also a little, and the exam/quiz problems are more complex than those of other professors. I'd suggest considering another professor if available.

Save yourself the stress and take Calc with Dr. Dean. Dr. Rasika's teaching style is difficult to understand, and almost all of his quizzes/exams are more complex than Dr. Dean's. His lectures are not engaging either, and he doesn't give extra credit. I honestly learned more from YouTube. You need to really lock in if you want to pass with an A.

He goes over a lot of material pretty fast, usually uses the lectures to prove things to try to get people to understand why things are done a certain way. Has a pretty heavy accent and handwriting is really hard to read sometimes, but he's always willing to clarify anything. Genuinely kind and caring, generous with partial credit

I am currently taking Calculus I, and the professor puts 100% of his energy into teaching. He explains and proves most formulas very clearly and always checks if students understand (“Is it clear, guys?”). Some students may struggle if they don't speak up when confused, but having a solid foundation in previous math courses is very important.
Dont take this professor for calc 1, you will suffer!! He doesn't explain things clearly and just expects everyone to know what he's doing.

Builds student understanding of Calculus in a sensible, linear fashion by showing proofs behind equations. Things taught in this class always seem complex at first until he breaks them down through proofs. He answers questions when asked on the board, or will answer them after class. He will ask "Is it clear?" intermittently, be honest he explains

He is a great professor. I see people dislike him for absolutely no reason but he really gives his 100 percent in class. I got so many extra credit opportunities and his office hours were really helpful.

Rasika replaced Tighe in Calc1, had him for Calc2 also. He put 110% into the classes, w/ tons of office hours and really wants you to understand when you dont get it. Accent's a bit hard to understand. Not exactly a hard grader. He gave tons of practice work. He gave "hints" for quizes. He really does care man. Study more than you think in MATH152.

I had him for 152 this semester, not 151. I don't think he's a great lecturer, he moves way too fast and doesn't really explain concepts sufficiently imo. But in every other aspect, he's a good prof. He gives out a lot of practice that is very similar to exams. He's also nice and gives opportunities for extra credit. Doable if you actually study

It's a bit tough to warm up, but once his personality shows it's a nice experience both ways. He is very kind and wasn't strict about homework, allowing people extra time since he cared more about you getting the practice. His quizzes definitely test you. If you underestimate his exams, you will fail them; they are absolutely loaded. Nice guy!

Class was a bit disorganized and the final was way too hard. However, Prof. Mahwattege is an extremely lenient grader and his lectures are informative. Out of all the 225 profs, he's definitely one of the best and the class is definitely better-- especially since other profs (*cough cough*, Rostamian 👎) don't even bother grading homework.

Took him in the Fall of '24. I struggled a bit with this class. Just relying on the lectures to understand the material is not enough. You have to heavily study the material and textbooks outside of class as well. TA sessions are more useful. Gonna have to teach yourself, but if you're good at math, it isn't that bad. Lectures just aren't the best.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Test heavy

reviews.comment: He's a nice guy and understanding too. Moves pretty quickly through lectures but he goes through many examples and practice problems. Might be a little hard to understand at times so I highly recommend going to office hours, he'll explain the concepts very well.

For resources you can go to office hours, your discussion section, read the online text book, look at the online notes, SI pass, access practice test for mid terms. Lectures cover main material that will be in the test and the reading checks are 4 questions, hw is around 16. If you failed it's your fault tbh he made it so easy.

Overall a decent professor. He speaks very quickly, but went through lots of practice during class and was relatively lenient with grading (he doesn't take off much for arithmetic errors.). It will definitely require a lot of outside work if you've never taken calculus, but he readily offers office hours and can be easily contacted by email.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Math 151 is already hard to begin with so workload will relatively be the same regardless of the professor. He is really fast with his lectures and has a noticeable accent but it wasnt too bad. His grading also seems to me very lenient. Highly suggest doing practice exams he gives out. He does not use technology. He a cool and funny dude though ngl

While people say he lectures fast (I wouldn't know legit watch every video in 2x speed), in my experience, if you read the textbook before lecture and take notes, there should be no problem. Outside of lecture, he is very responsive to emails and does want every student to succeed, just attend office hours and pay attention. Just read the textbook.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: I'll cut him some slack since this prof had to unexpectedly take over in the middle of the semester while the old one quit. Very passionate and engaging when he teaches but is quite fast so pay attention. Also he purposely does not provide any resources/notes online which can be frustrating at times. Very friendly and understandable though.

Although I wouldn't recommend Mr. Rasika to students who are learning calc for the first time, he's a great professor for students like me, who have already taken calc. He's very fast during lectures but always encourages students to ask questions. He responds to emails quickly and has office hours twice a week. He's also friendly and approachable.

I thought he was pretty okay though his lecture style can be frustrating since he moves so fast. He's cool if you ask for help but you have to be very outspoken about needing it. This class requires a lot of work outside of going to lectures. His exams and quizzes were straightforward enough if you study

Do not take Rasika as your Calc 1 professor. While he seems decent, his teaching is tough to comprehend. There were quizzes every Thursday, and while the quizzes weren't as bad as the exams they were still a pain sometimes. The exams are challenging. If you do have Rasika make sure to know everything about calc before coming to class.

If your taking Math 151 DO NOT take Rasika as your professor. It's pretty hard to understand his lectures, the way he teaches is fast paced. But I can say he is a nice person to talk to but that doesn't mean he is a good professor.

Future calc 1 ppl, this class WILL be difficult for many regardless of the teacher. That being said, he is not a terrible teacher. Yes, he speaks quickly but you can ALWAYS interrupt him and ask him to slow down. GO TO OFFICE HOURS they are very helpful and you get to know him personally. Nag him for his own practice quizzes/exams you'll be peachy

He has a pretty strong accent in his lectures so he's pretty hard to understand and he moves fast. It's definitely a lot of self-teaching. But if you go to his office hours when you don't understand something and do all the homework, you'll do fine. He's an understanding dude too, so if you're a decent student dw

I would not recommend. He's nice and can be understanding but the way he lectures is so confusing. He will solve practice problems at an extremely fast pace, figuring them out as he goes, and does not give anyone time to process what he's doing. He will answer questions but most of the time the class is too confused to know what to ask

Do NOT take this class with him! He teaches as if you already know calc, making it extremely hard to follow. I go to class every day confused about past units and leave just as confused about the new ones. I spend 30 hours a week studying since you won't learn much in lecture. It's incredibly draining. Hard to understand and learn with him.

In his class right now and I hate it. He's hard to understand and just explains stuff like we already know it. 
His lectures just don't make sense to me, and I have to teach the topics
 in this class to myself by watching yt vids. So, if you're looking for a teacher that will explain the topics well and help you understand, then don't take him!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: He is nearly impossible to understand, lecture is used not to teach, but to do problems that he expects you to understand from reading the textbook. The class was very fast paced, he gave us at least 3 online quizzes a week, an in person quiz every Wednesday. Even one on one, it's hard to understand him. Tests are very hard to read. Good luck.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Amazing professor. If you have the option to take his class at any point- TAKE ITTTT.

Absolutely love this professor. 100% recommend him. Very funny, bright, inspirational, caring. Workload is normal but he's extremely lenient and accepts late work as long as you submit by the end of the semester.

Ray is awesome! Not only is he super helpful and willing to offer you extra time or help for assignments when you ask, but he's just a great person to talk to. He's got your back whenever you need. I always looked forward to going to class even when I felt exhausted of most other things.

I really enjoyed this class. I am not a very strong student nor am I very strong in English classes but I got a ton from this class and Professor Terhorst was awesome from day one. The class had such a welcoming environment and I would recommend it to anyone. There's a bit of writing but Ray does a great job of simplifying it. 10/10 professor.

He's a good professor but 2 reasons why I won't take him again is because he made students buy expensive books which were never used and decided not to grade my final four assignments because I helped another student with a video editing project for the class which ended up giving me a 'B' and lowered my GPA unnecessarily

Amazing man. Makes a late Monday class fun and teaches you a lot about writing and life. There are a lot of papers (30 pages overall the entire semester) but they are cumulative so the final 15 page paper takes maybe two hours. Very accommodating but please don't take advantage of him. Highly recommended, and will get to know you pretty well.

Ray is the best! Although we had plenty of writing to do, he made this class really fun and I genuinely enjoyed it. He cares about his students and bonds with everyone in a different way. His feedback is really helpful and he wants you to do your best and goes out of his way to always provide help. Would highly recommend any class with him!

Very friendly and helpful teacher. The class is essay heavy. The guidelines are not always straightforward and therefore confusing. Peer editing is a waste of time. But if you email your paper to him he will edit and give feedback which helps. He gives up to 1 extra point for revisions which can really help grades. Takes a while to get essays back.
Ray is a great professor. He really cares about the students, and is enthusiastic and passionate. He could be a bit more timely in returning the assignments, but his comments are really helpful.
Excellent professor. Ray truly cares about his students. He can go a little off-topic sometimes during lectures, but his stories are always entertaining.
Excellent profession, one of the best I've ever had. Great stories!
