reviews.comment: Dr. Kifle is a great all around professor for STAT 355. The lectures are engaging and the lecture slides he provides the class are amazing. There are weekly quizzes for this course when I took it during the fall semester, but they were all very straight forward. I would definitely recommend taking his class for STAT 355.

Kifle made the course material very easy to understand and was also very helpful in office hours. I wouldn't say his class is an easy A because you need to understand the material well enough to perform well in quizzes and exams, but studying the lecture slides is all you need to get good grades. If you're thinking about taking him for 355, do it!

Professor Kifle is really good but you must want to learn the material. He gives you everything you need to be successful and literally tells you exactly how. You must work in this class. If you do, you will learn a lot!

Very thick accent! I do not understand a word out of him. He also assumes everyone should know everything already and does not understand that people have zero knowledge about what he is teaching. 0/10. Save yourself. Do not take class with him.

The power point slides can be slightly confusing, but they are very thorough and explain everything necessary for the course. Rough presenter; honestly this class works well with me skipping class and just reading the lecture slides. Quizzes and exams are consistent with what was given on the homework. Attendance was mandatory only for discussion.

The meta-analysis course was only offered to graduate students before Spring 22. Kifle made a graduate student course seem really easy. Detailed PowerPoints that were extremely helpful to look back on, working through problems in class, easily reachable through email for help on code. Kifle is a harsh person though. He's snappy. Not the nicest!
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: STAT 418 is pretty difficult. But Kifle is a great teacher.
Very good professor. Goes over lengthy proofs in class, but he mainly tests on the concepts and applications. Clear notes which are posted online. One of the best professors in STAT department!

Dr. Kifle is a good professor. His class notes are helpful and clear to follow, he posts them online too. We had 2 quizzes and a few homework assignments, some in R. He did a few random in-class attendance checks that counted as points. We had a midterm and a final group project/presentation. Definitely have to understand the material but doable.

Prof. Kifle is a good teacher, the class is just SO EASY. like read the slide/pay attention during lecture, do the HW (solution are posted before you turn it in), and you will do fine at both quizzes and exam. Discussion are the worst use of my time ever i don't even bother going its not worth the 2% participation points.

He lets you know what the class consists of and with two classes a week, one is for quizzes and the other is only a lecture, however every once in a while he will have an in-class assignment so you should show up. He is a fairly strict professor and isn't the nicest guy.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: He emphasizes the important topics in lecture and provided good examples to further help me understand. For quizzes, focus on the ppt qs, and the homework and you will ace them! As for the midterms, be thorough with all the ppt questions, quizzes and HW. He does leave a few qs blank in his ppt so make sure to come to class to get those answers!

The class consists of three exams (including the final), 12 quizzes, 12 homeworks, and 2 (extremely easy) excel projects. The exams weren't that hard, but sometimes getting a single question wrong would cost so many points. He allows you to have your own formula sheet for the final. Show up to class because sometimes he gives extra points for that.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Really good professor. He lectures a lot and participation isn't very important. His criteria for what he's testing/quizzing you on is clear. Test questions were from class examples and homework. He wants you to succeed. If you like structure and traditional lectures, he's your guy. One of the best statistics professors along with Dr. Stanwyck
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: He taught really well with clear, step-by-step explanations and a good pace. His lectures were organized, and he used helpful examples that made tough ideas easier to understand. He encouraged questions, was patient, and made students feel comfortable asking for help.

Laziest prof ever. Only reads off slides and doesn't elaborate unless asked to. Does 0 live coding. Very hard to reach outside of class. Never gave back our exams. This guy runs the class based off of the leftovers he gets from the course coordinator prof. Unless you have some experience with data structures, don't risk taking this careless prof.
He reads off slides every class but his explanations are not bad. Good guy, answers questions to the best of his ability.

Cares about the class, engages with the students, explains any issues they might have, and is entertaining.

While he reads from the slides (and they sometimes aren't very clear), he does his best to explain and make sure the student understands.

Lectures are not mandatory/actual classwork (not projects/exams) is easy, would recommend.

Don't bother going to his lectures; he's a slide reader. He adds nothing of value to the course. Somehow, a computer science class about data structures does neither programming nor proofs. His entire teaching style is "proof by intimidation." The code works because he said so! The proof is true because he said so! Little to no explanation.

If I wanted someone to read the course coordinator's slides to me, I'd do it myself. I can count on one hand how many times he coded, or put something on the chalkboard.

All of the course material is prepared for him, the guy shows up with his job already done for him and yet he's the laziest faculty member I've ever seen.

Take anyone else.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Mr. Ebrahimi cares for his students and makes sure that everyone understands the material. He will stop the entire class and make sure that you understand a certain concept so that you're prepared for exams. He was available outside of class and would update/fix the outdated slides (and add helpful information). Doesn't create exams/projects/labs.

I had a hybrid course where you only go to class to take quizzes and exams. We had two midterms, three projects, and one final. Homework and quizzes every week. It was pretty easy in my opinion but you definitely need to dedicate some effort to studying. Nothing too crazy. I mostly talked to the TA since he managed the quizzes. Rarely saw the prof

I took this class for the first summer session and it was the biggest mistake. This class is no joke. It is intense! She does not teach you anything in the lectures and 90% of the class is teach yourself/ read a confusing textbook and do a rediculous amout of workload. Understandibly this was a summer course but good god...
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The content itself is not too hard especially if you already have basic statistics background. Huang doesn't really teach or explain concepts well. Everything is graded by the TA, who might or might not be helpful depending on the TA. You have to self-study for most of the class.

I needed an 8% on the final to get an A with solid quiz scores. Studied way harder for the class than I needed to. Lot of extra credit. She does count attendance via extra credit so get someone to send you a code. Copying down the homework solutions is really helpful for studying for quizzes. Don't expect to actually learn any statistics though.

Dr. Huang has easily been one of the worst professors I have had at UMBC in regards to actually teaching the material. A TA teaches during the lecture portion before giving a quiz, every class, and the TA also does all the grading. You have to teach yourself everything in this course, with little to no help in class. Inconsistent grading as well.

Class was very disorganized and communication about assignments was often unclear. She makes a lot of mistakes in class and it's your job to notice them and correct them. That being said, the hybrid coursework was fine. If you put the time into the class you will get an A. 5 hwmk, 5 online quizzes, 5 class quizzes with lowest dropped each. 2 exams.

Her course is fantastic in terms of layout. She has lots of extra credit opportunities to cushion your grade, and is overall a very nice teacher. The only complaint I have is that the TA does most of the teaching, but I suppose with the limited time she has during lecture she can't do much about that. I'd definitely recommend taking this course!!

Easy A. No need to read the textbook, the slides cover everything you need to know. She lets you make your own / use a formula sheet for every quiz and exam, a normal piece of paper, double sided. Offers up to 6% in extra credit. She is a nice person and although the TA does the majority of the grading, is always willing to help. Highly recommend!

Prof. did none of the work and the T.A. did everything (making exams, grading, etc.). She required people to come in to pick up quizzes but then lectured about irrelevant material. Definitely use the math lab tutor bc that's the best place to learn. The material itself is easy, you just need to get the right formulas. The other professor is better.

Really easy class, professor taught well for a hybrid course. Easy 2 projects + extra cred project, 4 quizzes/homework, midterm, and final. A breeze. Take this teacher if you can. Quizzes can be found online and were reused from previous classes taught.

The worst professor I've ever had. TA did all the teaching, graded everything, & was way more reliable. All she had to do was grade the final, & apparently she can't even do that because the whole class has NG for a final grade. Her teaching style is lazy and she's a joke for a teacher. The class is an easy A, but she's awful.

Took the winter session and it's pretty easy to get through, although prepare yourself for a lot of work: 5 homework assignments, two exams are cumulative, 3 in-class quizzes, two projects (one is optional, 50 points for extra credit) and 5 online quizzes. Material isn't hard, read the textbook to supplement the ppt slides.

If you understand her powerpoints and examples, you'll have an easy time in her class. She's extremely generous with extra credit. She posts the solutions to homework prior to when the homework is due. The textbook was basically useless because everything you need to know is on her powerpoints. She allows students to bring a one page formula sheet.

She puts her powerpoints online--and you can get through the class without cracking open the book(except for HWs). The class isn't that rigorous--you get to have a formula sheet for quizzes and exams. The professor tries her best--but it's difficult when she only spends 50 mins a week teaching us--the other 50 mins is a quiz.

The class is easy if you read the book, just learn from there and her lectures will all make sense. Her quizzes and exams are pretty straightforward, knw the material from the book and then her teaching methods won't really even matter. It was an online course so we only met once a week for weekly quizzes and 3 exams.
She needs to learn how to use a whiteboard for teaching. Also, she needs go back to school and learn how to teach. Unless you can teach yourself stat find a different teacher

This is the easiet class that I've never had before. The professor is very nice, but the class is pretty boring. You don't really have to go to class, and all lectures come out directly from the textbook. There are a lot of extra credits. Just do the assinged hws, do average on quizzies and exams, then you'll be fine. This class is a breeze..

very dry lectures had trouble staying focused every day. teacher runs class like a high school. mandatory attendance and must not do anything else except paying attention to lectures or you will be in danger of failing. assignments and exams are laughably easy though.

I have taken two classes with Dr. Zhang so far, and they have both been great! She makes the density and amount of material (still a lot) for 300 and 400 level history courses easy to understand and creates interesting assignments/in-class activities. Looking forward to taking more courses with her!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Class was *ok*. Tests were open book/note with study guides, so very easy. Everyone did poorly on the pop quizzes (multiple choice), but this is her first semester here, so the course is still a work in progress. She's very nice, was open to feedback + gave extra credit opportunities. If you need a 100 lvl history class, this is a good option!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Beware of pop quizzes--Caring

reviews.comment: Does not respond to emails, doesn't enter grades, reads off slides and does not explain stuff in depth enough to prepare you for the style of exams. Tests are hard and the "helpful" study guide she claims is useful is actually just a really long list of subtopics in each chapter. I had to teach myself everything. Choose another prof.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: She's not mean or anything but shes just not good at teaching and is very disorganized. She read from slides and just doesn't explain well stuff well. Doesn't respond to emails and exams are hard with a very unhelpful study guide. If you're fine teaching yourself everything its ok but you're better ofzaf with a more engaging teacher who cares more.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: She was very nice but her organization was not great. Assignments and quizzes were released late so the schedule didn't even matter. She released less quizzes then the syllabus claimed we were supposed to do. Her exams were difficult. Her study guides were somewhat helpful but her exams didn't correlate with the study guide.

Although the course says no coding experience is needed, I think CMSC 201 or an intro programming class with Python should be a prerequisite. If you've worked with code before, you'll be fine. The projects were interesting, but most lectures felt boring. Most grading was done by TAs, though the professor was very approachable and easy to talk to.

If you talk with her one-on-one, she's very down-to-earth and friendly. As a professor, I found her to be highly unorganized and difficult to learn from. She would often forget to post assignments, so her syllabus was pointless by week three. Study guides weren't helpful and lectures were mostly her reading slides, so I had to self-teach a lot.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The course itself was not very beginner-friendly, especially with no coding experience. The workload was not too bad. She pushes students towards the TA rather than herself. I would not take her again as a beginner is coding, would go for someone who aims to have more connection with their students.

The course demands significant time commitment. Homework assignments typically require 1-2 hours or more each. The course includes a group project with deliverables due every week. The professor's expectations are borderline unrealistic given students have multiple courses. There were three exams that were in-person. Avoid if possible.

This was a gateway class, and the workload wasn't too demanding. She takes extremely long to enter grades, so you never know where your grade is at. The assignments aren't too bad, but the exams are hard. She doesn't provide any in depth study guide for the mini tests. She just reads off the slides the entire lecture.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Great class!  I recommend
This professor is genuinely not okay. I believe she is on something because her eyes are always red and talk extra slow.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--So many papers--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Subpar professor, lousy course. Takes centuries to grade anything. Timeframes for group proj deliverables are absurd. Mandatory attendance also sucks; her lectures are dry and last the full 2.5 hours. Unfortunately, 436 is required so there is no avoiding it. You'll have to just thug it out; get a good group for the project.

Personally, she was rude to me. I took from 4:30pm to 7pm so If I HAD TO, I would take her twice a week like a normal class. She is slick at the mouth, once I fell asleep in class (due to it being damn near 2hrs+ and I'm a commuter), instead of asking if I was okay. She said "if you want to sleep get out of class". As if she could throw me out.

AVOID this class with her. She rarely responds to emails and her instructions are vague. The course itself isn't too hard, but she makes it difficult. Grading is done only at the end, and the exam was very tough with little time. She's nice personally but not effective as an IS professor. No grade curve either. My bf had the same issue in IS 448.

Considering the fact that IS 310 is a gateway class, she makes the class pretty simple. We had mini tests, 9 assignments, a couple quizzes that are open textbook, and 2 exams. It's not too difficult, and she gives study guides for each exam and mini test, so study those. Good professor, but she does take a long time to enter grades.

Assignments from first few weeks of class still not graded months in.
Group project deliverables due every week. Most requirements in the group project she just tells you to read the book and figure it out.
Lecture is not that useful she just reads from slides.

She's a decent professor, the material isn't difficult but it does feel rushed since the project is coded from scratch as you learn. Homework can be demanding. She is willing to help if you reach out response times do take a little long and so do grades. It is a passable class but I felt like I really had to work hard to maintain a B.

Prof Zaidi is an excellent teacher! One of the best I've had. you will learn so much about front end development. We had to code from scratch for our group project which was quite interesting, and she is willing to help. It was 3 Homeworks, 2 exams and 1 project...but slow grader. Looking forward to take her IS436 next semester. Good Luck!

She explains things clearly in class - which is extremely helpful for coding. 448 is a lot of concepts at a fast-pace though, so get help from her early if you need it. She's pretty lenient with grading as long as you try. Her exams are straightforward (and she gives a study guide). The group project takes WORK though - so get a good group!

She makes this course hard to fail, easily the best professor for IS310, if she is available please take her. Gives multiple opportunities to keep your grade either at or above the B you need to pass this class, excellently done. She will get you through the gateways as long as you do your work and pay attention in lecture.

Professor Zaidi is excellent; she wants her students to learn and gives an appropriate amount of assignments. The best thing is she makes study guides which you can fill out and are extremely helpful for her quizzes and exams. So show up to class, do the assignments and study guides, and you'll get the 'A' you deserve.

Professor Zaidi is a pretty good professor, she has a deep understanding of course materials and does a great job and explaining to students. Don't skip lectures, take notes in class, study for exams and you will probably get an A.

Easily one of my favorite professors at UMBC and I wish I had taken this class sooner. The content is all very interesting, but there is a lot of material covered during the semester, so missing even one lecture could hurt. She grades very fairly and is very approachable if you have questions or need help. Highly recommend taking her class!

She is a great professor we only had quiz and homework which was very simple. If you read the study guide you will get 100% on quiz. She takes quiz and exam in class though but they were not hard since she provided the study guide.

Professor Zaidi is very helpful and gives you real world knowledge and experience.  She has helped me on work projects as well outside of class, and has so much real world experience, which isn't the case with a lot of professors who are more "book smart" with little to no real world, hands on experience.  You have to do the work!

She has on her syllabus that she will take 14 business days to grade an assignment. She means that for her email as well. Took her class cause she had 4/5 at first but things went down hill. Content isn't very difficult but with the type of professor she is, it doesn't take much to make it "rough" BE AWARE and BE CAREFUL !
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Not what I expected slow grader you dont know what you have in the class. Lectures have nothing to do with exams, rather worded difficult . Assignments were almost impossible to seek help for
i picked the teacher based on the good reviews but she had difficult exams and isnt always available for help. if you want a heavy schedule take someone else.

Tests weighed a lot and be prepared to study. Class became very difficult when transitioned to online and will take up most of your time. Doesn't ever respond to emails so if your group is not helpful for the project, good luck. Doesn't grade until the end.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Semester long project along with quizzes and at most 2 homework assignments. Find reliable group-mates and the semester will be smooth sailing. Doesn't respond back to emails and is a slow grader. However, is reasonable with extending deadlines.

She's easy on the eyes for sure!  If she is available for IS436 take her. I'm not saying she is the best teacher in the world or anything but she has a lot of real world systems analyst experience so she tells you what is important. Tests, HW, Group Project is graded very easily and relaxed. You should get an A if you are competent.

Probably one of the best professors I encountered within the IS major at Umbc. was a student here before so understands the course load of students and makes her exams and assignments doable. Study slides for exams, and use slides for homework assignments as well.

She is slow to post grades and the homework assignments are wordy and confusing. She also provides about 20 files for each chapter and you only use 1 or 2, which is confusing when she makes you download the whole thing. But overall she seems like she is familiar with the material and her lectures are pretty straightforward. Not too much homework.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: Outstanding professor! Loved her class, she's very knowledgeable and loves to get to know her students. My only negative is that it takes forever for her to grade anything, and she's not good at organization. With so few assignments that factor into your grade, she did a really bad job at giving students a heads up.

The only thing I did not like about this professor is, most days she is late to class. She getting into our daily lives and asking about personnel stuff. Other than that, she is a wonderful professor!
Professor Taj is great. She assigns a reasonable amount of work, is not too demanding, and is very accommodating and willing to help students.

Easy course. Went on a field trip to an NGO and gave us breakfast twice throughout the semester. The course consists of 3 reflections, a midterm, and a Case Study paper/presentation. The course was hybrid, Mondays were lectures, and Wednesdays were online with speakers in the field. We sometimes didn't have class on Wednesdays. Would take again!

Shes a good professor, the class is very discussion based, and would talk alot if people dont participate. Very easy class. Graded by 8 or 9 weekly assignments, midterm, and presentation. Would take again.

Zareen Taj is an extremely interesting professor and I never lacked to pay attention in class, BUT she is just as happy to talk you to death if you don't participate. So do the reading, come to class knowledgeable in the subject material, and it will go by much more quickly for you as she is beneficially responsive to high participation.

Easy class, interesting topics/videos. There are 5 quizzes, 2 Unit Tests, and 5 assignments. Overall, good Professor, but group discussions in class was okay. Depending on the class, some weeks you will meet twice a week; others you will meet once a week.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The class contained a decent amount of reading and homework assignments, but the structure of the class was well done. Once you figure out the proper criteria for grading, everything goes smoothly. She is also a very fair grader.

Midterm scores were very low, but the grading seemed heavily curved at the end. You MUST read the text for acronyms, he tests strict definitions, not the lecture stories. CPSA HW is confusing until it clicks. Final reused tough quiz Qs. Recovery is possible, but you must study his specific terminology to pass.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: You have to read dense chapters every week and remember everything. Lectures are way too in-depth and do not really help on projects, assignments, or quizzes. Frequent quizzes that cover chapter content in minute detail. Low class averages across the board. Don't take this class if you don't already know your stuff.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: DONT TAKE 487 WITHOUT 481 AND 426. Content of the class is just hard and theres a lot.  He gives quizzes on chapters but won't announce it over email or ahead of time (you get used to it but it sucks). Makes us use CPSA for projects, but barely explains and theres little/no documentation for the tool. Huge pain - most ppl bomb projects.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Do NOT take this class if you haven't taken Networks or Security. Big emphasis on textbook and conceptual knowledge. Expect this class to take a majority of your time. Not the most encouraging prof, but the assignments and quizzes will make you learn a lot which will help in your career. Relevant information, but if you hate networking, avoid.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Test heavy

reviews.comment: was prepared for a nightmare after reading the other reviews on here, but Ziegler turned out to be a very reasonable prof. very knowledgeable and genuinely wants to help students understand the material (though his bedside manner isnt the fuzziest). you learn a lot! READ THE TEXTBOOK LIKE A BIBLE. projects are tough but grading is very generous
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Beware of pop quizzes--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Ziegler is incredibly smart and is very knowledgeable about the subject. However, he lets you know he's smarter than you and that there are definitely stupid questions. He's incredibly condescending and does not promote an atmosphere for positive learning. He grades fairly and provides good feedback, but is honestly scary to approach.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Zieglar is too smart for his own good. Asks for participation but will laugh at even slightly incorrect answers. Projects requirements are somewhat ambiguous, and use software with almost no online resources. Projects take months to grade. Weekly quizzes pull directly from textbook. Very smart man, but a below average professor.

The professor is awesome. Attendance should be taken seriously given lots of exam questions could be included from things discussed in class that might not be explicitly mentioned in the text book. The course is somewhat challenging but broadens student's understanding of cryptographic algorithms and network protocols.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Amazing lectures --Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: The course consists of reading and memorizing 350 pages of dense net sec specs. The projects are in an obscure language Dr. Z wrote. He is rude. He makes fun of students who do not understand concepts. Quizzes are specific and harshly graded. There was a curve b/c everyone bombed. Still, he is very knowledgeable and responds quickly to emails.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Professor Ziegler was comically bad. Only teacher I've ever had that required a textbook at UMBC and despite making us read the entire thing, he would routinely say that the textbook was incorrect. Homeworks were confusing, extremely time consuming, and unreasonably difficult. This class was a literal bruh moment the whole way through.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Zieglar is by far the worst professor I've had at UMBC. If you read all required material before the lectures & take good notes, you should do well on quizzes. He doesn't make it comfortable to answer questions in class; if any part of your response is incorrect, he will laugh and say "no" 6 times/second. Great material, arrogant professor. Avoid.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Brutal. Dude is way too smart for his own good, when to MIT and works in NSA. Incredibly RUDE, wants people to participate, puts their opinion on BLAST. Could talk all class about any networking topic. Read the book. Assignments are super vague, hard. Read the assignment thoroughly before going for help. Curved midterm because people failed.

Brutal but highly informative class taught by someone whose been in industry (NSA) for more than double the time I've been alive. That being said, I think he sometimes forgets that we're undergrads (and the only prereq for networks is 341!), and the homeworks are obscene, esp. the BBS project. Take if and only if you really want to learn.

Could be better, but he's okay I guess, and there are definitely worse professors than him. If you attend all classes and take notes vigorously, you should be able to pass the class with at least a B. The textbook homework is a little excessive and obnoxious IMO though, just a heads up.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: I took him Spring 2020. He was really accommodating during the online environment and we had fun projects where you learned a lot. Some say the exams are on the harder side, but as long as you read the book and pay attention in class you should be fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Okay so the semester with him was crazy. 100 slide power points. Theres a project but you can get x3 for your grade. The homework, project, and assignments are worth 55% ! Literally the answers can be found online and the questions come from the textbook directly. Now he does give quizzes at the end of each chapter and they are difficult.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Great class, lots of protocols to cover. Requires you read each chapter, then goes through the book slides. Enjoyed the lectures, always gives good answers to questions, ie if you ask something he just explained, he will remind you he just answered that, then rephrase it. HW, quizes and exams right from the book, its theory,if you read, you pass.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Get ready to read--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES

reviews.comment: Doesn't describe concepts well, and conflicting explanations in different classes Take a chunk of your assignment and project points for something minor

Terrible lecturer. He says to read the book, and class is just for asking questions. He does not post a hw/test schedule online to force people to go to class. Tests and quizzes are impossible. Average quiz grades are 10-20%, and midterm average was 50%. He asks that we read 150+ page chapters in a week, then tests on some very small detail.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: Exams are hard but this is by design, he only wants you to read the material and participate in class discussions. I am by no means a genius and I managed to get an A. I would rate this class somewhere under Algorithms, OS and AI. The material ties in well with Algo and OS. Take his class if you want a solid foundation to grow on.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Although he knows a lot about Networks, he definitely does not know how to teach AT ALL. Terrible lectures. Completely unhelpful when asking questions. Everyone failed all the exams, I'm pretty sure the class was curved 99%. He scans the room every day in the beginning like a robot to see who's missing. Got a 1% and passed with a C. AVOID.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: Read ahead and participate in lecture, projects are interesting and fun. Exams are extremely hard
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Unlike the older reviews I never found his lectures dry. He's not the type to jump up and down but he gives some really interesting/passionate lectures and never read off the screen. Lots of cool content to make you think. BUT his las few lectures need polishing. Music lectures very unclear and days where we read from text together were mindnumbing
Dr. Fatih is so nice! The VHL assignments do get very tedious, but they are very helpful if you put full effort into them.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: 3 days into French 102 for the Winter session and I'm hating it.  I understand it's condensed and extremely fast-paced, but this is insane.  I've taken winter courses in the past and haven't seen anything like this. 20-35 VHL assignments every day except for Sunday, quizzes on Saturdays.  Tried to ask a question two days ago, still no response.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: I regret taking French 102 online and async. the class is done entirely through VHL, and it's just not enough to learn off of. Prof didn't go back through the VHL work to give partial credit. he had lectures on Blackboard, but the time was not announced before I registered and I could never attend, and the recordings weren't very helpful.

This teacher was chill. He makes his zoom sessions optional for students. All assignments are done in VHL (Vista Higher Learning) which you have to pay for. Your grade is really dependent on how well you do on quizzes and tests. Go through the modules and you should do fine on the tests. The teacher is also always available to answer questions!
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Friendly but very unorganized and overall confusing class. Literally you can tell he's just winging it sometimes. A bit inconsiderate of student's times and the fact that some students have other classes. One of my least favorite french profs

Overall for a 4 week course, this class is very intensive. This professor does a good job explaining grammar and what we need to know if the optional live lectures and was generally accessible by email at any point in time. Only complaint was he continuously released quizzes and his study guides like 12 hours before they were due.
He's really understanding and patient. He gives wonderful and detailed feedback, would definitely take him again.
I took him for 102 and 201 online and it was pretty easy. Got an A in both. Learned a lot. Take him.
He is a very tough grader but would give you good feedback for what you got wrong. I think he is a great professor for French. I took him over the summer for the 201 sess to meet my grad requirement.

Professor Faith is one of those professor that goes the extra mile to help his students understand the subject. He is very kind, patient and encourages people to ask questions. I took him during the 4 week summer session so although it was all accelerated, it wasn't all that difficult. Just practice using his study guide and you will do fine.

One of the worst professor's I've had at UMBC and definitely the worst in MLLI. Super disorganized and takes off so many points for tiny things. Everything is based off his lectures, which make no sense. Avoid if at all possible!
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: I took this during the four-week session in the summer. It was quick, and all online. We did have to buy a book, but it's relatively cheap if you rent it. We had four quizzes, and three tests, and homework. You don't get feedback on how you did, just your grade. I would advise people to take this class during the summer, online, SUPER EASY.

While the lectures were a bit dry and he read directly from the power point, he made sure we understood the content and appreciated participation to help solidify the concept. He also makes sure students know that he is available for questions outside of class.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: I had him for an online class, so I don't know what he was like in person, but what I do know is he was great at teaching it. So far he has been the only professor at UMBC that actually emails me back and gives great feedback on homework and tests and such.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Great professor and go deeply into details and he makes sure that you understand him. Easy grader, no attendance required but he gives points if you always show up. Just a lot of reading (3 big books) with 40 pages between each class

If you have a strong background in French, he's a good professor to take. He teaches as if all the students in the class are French majors or minors. He's very strict about grammar. He's also an extremely picky grader and will knock off a lot of points over minor errors. Make sure you attend class b/c he goes over a lot of examples.
He is the best Prof you will see at UMBC!
I also took MLL 301 and beg to differ with the previous comment; actually I learned a lot from the course and knowing Dr. Fatih personally I know he taught this course many times before!

Highly disorganized. He openly said he had never taught this class before and had no idea what he was doing. The material was not particularly difficult, but trying to navigate what he wanted was annoying

I enjoyed learning about the psychological aspects of the revolutions in Tunisia and the Maghreb, not just learning facts and current events but trying to understand the deeper motivations and analyzing the situation from that perspective. Combination of lecture, documentaries and news footage was very helpful. Overall, great class, great prof.
The course topic was fascinating and allowed me a different point of view to a contemporary topic. He found lots of good videos that really enhanced the material.
I took 2 french courses at umbc; this one is a French wizard. he goes the extra mile. I got an A but still was annoyed by the attitude of some students.
Terrible. Quizzes and assignments never pertained to what we were supposed to actually learning in class. So awful, I'm avoiding at all costs in the future
Interesting lectures. No nonsense prof, but with a great sense of humor. You really learn something about France's cultures and literature.

This class was very easy. He's super boring which makes the class boring but he's not that bad. The quizzes are easy and I think he let's you drop one. Gives you simple homework from the book but it's mostly for practice. Goes over everything from the book on the board to make sure you understand.

I can't believe what some guys on here said about prof. Fatih. He's one of the best teacher of French at UMBC. He really cares about students. Befre I signed up 4 his class, I checked his UMBC evaluations online; they're outstanding. I took two courses with him and I have been impressed with his skills. I would def. recommend him.

very distracted and neglectful of the class. canceled class once but never made up the quiz we missed. his tests are 10 questions and worth 200 points with 5 MC and 5 short answer. only gave us one quiz when we should have had 4. read straight from the text, and sometimes seemed to interact with certain students only. very frustrating class overall

I thought he was a terrible teacher. I learned almost nothing except a few grammar things. He's also incredibly unorganized. The movie the class was based on was from the 60s, so we virtually learned a ton of ancient vocabulary that isn't even used in France (my French friends could not believe what I was learning). Avoid getting him if you can.

prof fatih can be a bit confusing at times with what he expects from you, however he really tries to cater to the class so he began emailing us what he expected each week to make it easier. he also really tries to make sure we do well on the tests, he's funny and kind, and also relatively flexible abt taking stuff late

A semi-strict prof that moves pretty fast. Usually only went over new stuff once, then a quick review next class. He is pretty lax about the C-hour work and mostly assigns activities from out of the book. A good prof to take if you have had french before or have the basics down well.

He really seems to love his job. Very enthusiastic about litterature and culture. Made me enjoy lit too.The workload was just right. Perfect balance between readings (novels and scholarly articles) and written assignments. I recommend his graduate classes!
Selfish and Bad teacher.
Wonderful and highly interesting lectures; very dynamic and never misses a class.

Goods: had him for an 8oclock class but was ok with people coming late, skipping a few classes, late assignments, easy exams etc. Bads: really overqualified and knows this. Not the best teacher, basically only teaches grammar, not enthusiastic, thinks students are stupid. I forgot most french from even 101 but got an A by memorizing grammar.
I think he is pretty good. He is very helpful and the class is short and sweet.

She was really funny and I really enjoyed taking her. If you take this class over the summer, it's almost impossible to get an a because 60% of your grade is the final and she does give a pretty tough final, but besides that she was very fun to take she explained the material well and she was very caring teacher.

Excellent professor
Be ready to put the work in
It was hard to understand the lectures. Even with open book and open notes in exams, her grading did not make sense. I wish I had taken the class with someone else.
She'll raise her voice and even scream at you if you ask too many questions!
This professor has no patience with students, and if you ask questions she'll cut you off in the middle of a sentence. Stay away from this one.
Not open to discuss or explaining anything outside of class. Has no patience.

Dr. Zhu is so funny and really cares about her students. The lectures were very informative and easy to follow, and she posts good notes online for you to access later. The material she tells you to study is exactly what shows up on her exams. Overall great professor, and I wish the UMBC engineering dept had more faculty like her.

Professor Zhu is always available in her office and is always willing to help you on your HW. She is always making jokes in class to keep your attention. She is definitely a tough grader but a 60% is a C so there is really no one to blame but yourself if you don't pass the class.

Shes the best professor at UMBC. Genuienly cares for her students and presents the material pretty well. If you dont get it in lecture, she is ALWAYS available and will work with you until you get it. Shes also hilarious.
Go to her office.  She is the most helpful and accessible professor I have ever taken.  You have to work for your grade, but she is very fair in her assessments.

She cares about students and wants you to succeed. She's energetic and her lectures are funny sometimes. Exams are open book and based on homework, so as long as you understand the concepts, you are good to go. She's always in her office and ready to help you.

Dr. Zhu is extremely helpful but her lectures are confusing and won't support the material. Also her accent takes a while to get used to. However she is almost always at her office and will usually drop what she is doing to help you. She will flat out tell you what you need to do to get an A on your reports if you JUST ASK.

Dr. Zhu is very helpful and friendly during office hours. She is very passionate about heat transfer (it's one of her research areas). Her lectures can be a little tricky to follow at times, especially because she has a bit of an accent. Once you get used to it, it's not too bad, though.

There are six labs throughout the semester that make up 84% of your final grade.  They are incredibly time-consuming, but they aren't graded too harshly.  The final exam is short answer and multiple choice (only worth 10%), and there is an ethical analysis paper that was worth 6%.  It's only 2 credits, but you put work into it as if it's 4.

The material its self can be difficult, which is only why I rated 'Easiness' a 3. Posts her own notes, for you to print out. She is very helpful both during class and at office hours. Tests are hard, but very fair and they are open book. Looking forward to taking her other classes.
By far one of the best professors in the mechanical engineering department.  I highly recommend taking a class with her.
Prepares notes for you so you dont have to take any in class. Open book/note final. sometimes hard to understand.
Gives you the notes. Pretty straight-forward class.  Final exam was tough but  was open notes/book.  Overall, pretty good teacher.

Zhu is a great professor! The labs are very organized and she explains exactly how to lab the reports. As long as you follow her report you should do well in the class. She will revise your report if you give it to her before it's due. I've heard that Eggleton is extremely difficult in this course.

Do the homework, and you'll do fine on exams, which were always open book/open notes. If you find yourself confused, definitely visit her during office hours because her explanations have helped clarify a lot of concepts.
Good Teacher will help you out. Her accent is very thick so be ready
Amazing professor.  Very accommodating and understanding. His lectures are very clear as well as the discussions. Attend them and you'll know everything you need to.

You will perform well on the assignments and tests if you pay attention during the lectures. Fair grading was applied, and the feedback was very beneficial. The professor answers emails promptly and is readily available for any questions. Anyone interested in taking the course should take because you will learn, and he allows cheat sheet.

Very bland professor. Class is basically 410 pt2. Skip lectures (slides are posted online), and discussions (mandatory attendance) teach you what you need to know. Exams are VERY easy bc A) you can bring a cheat sheet and B) exam problems are based off of the HW. HW problems are based off the discussion examples. Easy class if you put in the work.

The saving grace of 420 with Chen is he lets you bring cheat sheets for the in-person exams. His exams are also pretty straightforward. However, felt the lab sessions were more helpful than the actual lectures, but overall, he teaches decently. Group project takes a decent amount of time - so just stay on top of it.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment:
If you pay attention in the lectures, you will do great in the assignments and the exams. 
Grading was fair and the feedback was really helpful.
The professor is very much available on emails for all doubts and responds quickly. Would definitely recommend him if you want to learn the course.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: The professor is great. teaches good, learned a lot from him.

The homework assignments, exams, and in-class project are all reasonable. Dr. Chen is a good lecturer and it's not at all nerve-wrecking to ask him questions. You're allowed to use two double-sided pages of cheat sheets during the exam. Take anything with Chen!

Awesome professor! He pretty much reads directly off the slides. The homework he assigns are super easy and he actually made databases fun and interesting.  He makes SQL seem like a breeze and he let's you bring 2 pages (double sided) cheat sheets to his exams and his exams aren't hard at all. Highly recommend.

This professor is pretty straightforward.  If you pay a decent amount of attention in class and have a brief SQL background you should have no problem getting an A.  (I took this class as an undergrad, btw.)  You are allowed 2 cheat sheets on each of the exams.
great professor, no doubt... he will let u to bring a 2 page cheet sheet for exams. even though know what u atleast wrote  in the cheet sheet otherwise ...will be in trouble
very easy!! take him for 410 and you dont even need the textbook at all. Everything is posted on blackboard. SQL was a nice addition.
This class is really easy. Sometimes I felt like he thought we were all stupid and he was laughing at our stupidity. However, I definitely recommend taking him.

Take 410 w/ Chen!  His class is extremely easy and he will even let you use a 2 pg. note sheet in exams.  There is a group project that you work on throughout the year but it's nothing very time consuming.  His class can be boring at times so make sure you bring your laptop.  Great prof. overall!

His tests are incredibly easy: allows 2 double-sided pages of notes + a sheet of diagrams. HW is simple too. On top of that his grading is incredibly lenient. Semester long project is quick, easy 100%. Learned some SQL which was nice. Covered most of the text, so I guess i learned some stuff

Fun Class, Learned a lot of SQL. Dr. Chen is really lenient in his grading. If you pay attention in class, everything will be easy. The exams are really easy! All you have to do is study the in-class discussions, and that will be on the exams. There is one big project that may be the hardest part of the class.

The class was great, as long as you do well on the exams you will be fine, i struggled. The quizzes and exams are great when you have the materials to prepare. his lectures were amazing and so helpful. i wish more professors were like him.

Although lectures are long, Dr. Smith does a great job explaining concepts with detail and gives plenty of practice problems during class. I enjoyed how he is enthusiastic about the material and tries to make it engaging.  The think about its and Mini quizzes were very helpful tools for studying for quizzes and exam.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: My favorite professor from UMBC, his lectures were interesting and he offered so much help learning the material. His exams arent quite as difficult as Dr. Tracys but youll still learn a ton! I wish I could take him for every chemistry class.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Dr. Smith taught the second half of online CHEM 437. His pre-recorded lectures were very long and had lots of extra information. He used the book for his lectures, so reading the book was helpful to find which information was important. The class time was used as optional problem sessions because the practice was not covered in the lectures.

I went into his half of the class with virtually no chance for an A. Only missed one point on all his assignments and learned so much about Biochem in the process. First half was HELL while he was super clear and an amazing lecturer. Take this man for anything he teaches and you will not regret your decision. Also, talk to him during office hours.

Dr. Smith is one of THE best professors in the chemistry department. I almost failed this class, the first exam I got a 10/30. The second exam, which is the final exam, I got a 29/30. If Dr. Smith had not taken over the second semester, I would have failed. Please go to his lectures, study what he points out on the slides, look over old quizzes!

I really enjoyed taking Biochemistry with Dr. Smith. He made it clear what we will be tested on, taking exam questions straight from in class problems and past exams. He was always accessible outside of class, and really cared about his students doing well. Although he is a new professor, he was very knowledgeable about the course content
Super great professor!!!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Aaron Smith was an amazing professor--really taught the course well, was very engaging, made difficult topics very easy to understand, and progressed through material in a logical, methodical manner that made sense. Exams were very easy (straight from slides/practice exams) and he was a godsend for a good grade in the class. Strongly recommend.
He is a great professor. This class was a little difficult for me, but Dr. Smith made the material as easy to understand as possible. Plus there was a ton of extra credit
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: Very few grades in this class and the homework is worth 45% of your grade. For the homework you are given the choice of a 4000 word essay or an extremely difficult coding assignment. My CS major roommate who is in his last semester looked at it and stated that it is something that he would do in a 400 level CS class. I do not recommend this class.
The class has a lot of reading involved. Majority of the classes will need you to go back to understand what was said. In-person classes are way better here compared to online.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: 2 Exams, 2 Assignments, 1 Project. Exams are combination of: T/F, MC, Analysis, and Conceptualizing. Assignments: Paper & Coding, Project: Coding or 4k paper. He knows his stuff, slow on grading, doesn't post grades on bb, can be hard to reach outside of class.

1 project, 2 HW assignments, midterm & final. His lectures are engaging. Won't give you the grades back, Doesn't post the grade on BB. You won't know if you are passing or failing until the semester ends. Tests are mostly applying problems to real issues, not that bad. Project and HW are tough, code like a pro or write a 4000-word essay.

Here's the breakdown. The class met once a week, he read off the powerpoint but made it very engaging. He is a very slow grader, very annoying how the semester ends in a few weeks and I don't know if i'm passing. His tests are not conceptual but application. His project is horrible, either you know how to code like a pro or write a 4000 word essay.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Massey was a good teacher and had reasonable grading standards. Lecture should not be skipped, attendance is very important. His grading was pretty thorough, but if you read through his slides and the accompanying textbook chapters it wasn't all that bad. This class may be difficult for those that cannot write well. Somewhat writing intensive.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Good and cool professor. Nice teaching of subject.

Makes you work alot for no purpose. This professor needs to know the meaning of teaching. If you want an A for this course , go ahead. But he is torturous and makes you work a lot! It would be a suggestion not to go for this course under him if you have taken some tough course because all you will doing the whole semester is just writing. A big NO!
So kind; he really care about his students and the class is really engaging.

He was a wonderful teacher and understood that this was a beginner entrepreneurship class, so he didn't go out of his way to make our lives harder. The only thing that was annoying was that we had to supplement every presentation with a paper or two, regurgitating our presentations . Otherwise, I can say I learned and had a good time.

The guy really cares about his class and if you pay attention to him and listen to his lectures, you will learn a good bit. The problem is its a 2+ hr class once a week and most students aren't enthusiastic by the time it comes. He is a good professor and he knows his stuff. He is chill and wants you to be interested in entrepreneurship and succeed

He knows a lot about the business world and how to get a company started and gives great tips . The class was pretty easy you just sit there and can be on your laptop. Only homework is a presentation, a paper, and the final project. Definitely take this class with him

He's nice to look at. I'll give him that. But he was extremely lazy when it came to the class. It's obviously not his top priority. Most of the class time was spent with students giving pointless current event presentations and boring guest speakers. He barely taught us anything. Also the grading system was VERY unclear. Take him because he's hot.

I would take again.  Nice, funny, friendly, you learn as much as you would like.  You can blow it off or not.  Do the questions before class and you can get all of the answers you need for the test.  Test are easy if you just read over the answers to the questions regularly.
Difficult class, test formats change, plenty of reading, need to read material several times to do well, do ALL questions when assigned them.

If you go to class and do the guiding questions you should do fine. I didn't like that he kept "testing" new exam formats on my class so our final exam was impossible. I would've probably gotten an A if it hadn't been for his inconsistency in testing formats.

AWESOME.Professor Smith is one of the greatest I've ever had. He is interesting, charming, funny, conversational, and very helpful. He tells you which questions from your notes will be on the tests and goes over them. You can't do poorly unless you don't study or ask for help when needed. He made me want to take a phil minor. Class is fun, take it

A good professor, no doubt about it. Made me want to change majors. Discussion was very stimulating and he kept you interested in the material. You need to be able to write a lot and want to discuss. He also provided all the reading materials in electronic format so the students didn't have to buy anything. Good class.

Great professor, one of the best I've had. Very interested in the subject matter, and always helpful and funny. Tests are written so your wrist may hurt after, but there's only 3 total and no other assignments, including papers. Easy A as long as you attend class and listen to what he says. Loved his class and taking another by him in Spring :)

For basic philosophy:Understand that many students are there for basic requirements however he also encourages, engages and challenges the logic of the most interested students. He gave a list of possible essay questions that would be on the exam. He gets distracted and off topic often but only temporarily. Very nice and open to opposing views.

He is a great professor that encourages asking questions. He sometimes struggles with answering them, but overall he does a good job. He seems nervous, though, because when he talks about differing viewpoints he keeps reminding the class that he doesn't support the sides considered "bad". Overally, good professor.

Took both 150 & 152 and he is the most helpful professor. If you go to class it is an easy A, depending on how much you actually pay attention. He lectures on what is on the readings and tests only on that. Funny and nice. You might not like Phil, but his class is not hard to motivate yourself to go to. A little random, but he is awesome.

For an intro philosophy class Smith's methods were a bit of a roller coaster ride. Some days his lectures were intriguing and funny, while others were painfully dull. This professor doesn't use a book for THIS class, but makes the student print texts frequently for reading. After a LARGE purchase of ink and paper, prepare yourself to learn in class

Professor Smith was one of the best professors I've had at UMBC so far. He is very funny, keeps his class interested in the material at hand, and is very knowledgeable about the topics. I had the pleasure of talking to him outside of class a few times and he was very eager to answer questions I had. Exams and papers are outlined very clearly.

Uses too advanced books for Philosophy 100. Incomprehensible because he always goes on tangents during class. Would not recommend taking his class if you are interested in Philosophy, wait until you are a Junior or Senior and take Prof. Jim Thomas.

Wonderful Spanish teacher ! I was sad to find out that she wasn't teaching Spanish 102 for spring 2016. She really made Spanish easy and fun to learn. She is compassionate about teaching and the homeworks will help you pass the test . Study everything and you are sure to pass her class. She is very friendly and helpful ! She made Spanish fun!
Nicest Teacher Ever!
No Comments
Great professor! would take class with her again!
Very very easy tests. Very nice lady.  Don't think you can get away without doing homework though..she likes to give pop quizzes to check up on that.
She said she would give extra credit and round up grades at the end of the semester but she never did anything no extra points were given on the exams. Definitely don't recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: she was not  understanding at all especially when you have technical difficulties during HW or exams. I also had to self teach myself on top of that she creates new policies without any notice to inform students.

Lectures were extremely pointless. You self teach and then the exams are extremely different from lecture material. Exams were given on lockdown and your exit times are compared to exam submission times without any notice. Definitely don't recommend. Not understanding at all.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: No curve for any exam, regardless of class average, close to no opportunities for extra credit, no practice exams or study guide given. Lectures were quick and not easy to grasp.
Labs are so boring doesn't make anything interesting. Here lectures are useless u don't learn anything and the exams are so hard no curve and you get no practice exams
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: difficult matching of course content and exams
Wonderful professor! I loved prof Abraham :> highly recommend her for 102 chem lab
Very good teacher, my TAs of this class dragged it down though. She was very good at explaining topics while keeping the class entertaining. Was also very helpful with late labs and sick days.

Dr. Abraham is very sweet. The only difficult part about this course was the in-lab quizzes. Make sure to study the slides and manual for it and write all the important info as a cheat sheet on notebook!! The exams were ok, just study the exam slide she provides and previous in-lab quiz questions. Lectures were mandatory w quiz at the end.
Sweet lady, her lab was easy and exams weren't too bad, just the in lab quizzes were getting me haha. Really depends on LA because LA grades and how you do depends on how lenient they are.

Dr. Abraham is a very good teacher who clearly explains the procedures and expectations for each lab. If you complete all of the assignments, you should get an A. Weekly work is a lecture quiz, prelab quiz, in lab quiz, lab report, and lab manual writing (tedious). Grading depends on TA. Some are helpful in lab and with reports. Some are terrible.

She's a very kind professor who cares a lot about what she teaches. She'll gladly answer questions and she loves forming connections with students. I would love to have her as my professor again, she's a very sweet lady.

Dr. Abraham is an amazing professor and CHEM 102L with her is very easy. She walks around to each lab section during lab and helps you out if you have any questions. My TA was also really chill and helpful.

She was one of the best professors at UMBC. I took this class in fall of 2022 and she's the nicest professor you'll ever have at UMBC. Just listen to what she tells you and you'll get an A in the CHEM102L.

She was amazing!! Answered any questions we had, made the class very easy by giving extra credit and listened to student feedback to make the class as smooth for us as possible! Also shoutout to my TA, mans was super cool! Her exams werent that hard as long as you did the pre- and in-lab quizzes! Just do your work & ur good!

I love Dr. Abraham! She accommodates students making lab about learning and not about grades. Her TAs are wonderful, and her labs were the highlight of my week. She is student-oriented, listening and applying all our feedback. You are all set if you read, do the lab reports well, and attend lectures/labs. I want to take lab all over again with her!

This class was fairly easy. In lab, pre-lab and participation quizzes are what make or break your grade. The labs were graded by TA's, but she always responds to emails. Overall very nice and understanding woman.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I had Professor Abraham for chem 102 lab and the 50 min lectures were boring but she was so sweet and always had a smile, but all grades mostly come from your TA of your assigned lab with only 2 midterms (not cumulative). Pay attention to the PowerPoints in class when studying for lab quizzes and exams. She tells you what to expect in the exams.
great professor! so nice and so helpful!

Easy A if you have a lenient TA for a grader. Dr. Abraham was very clear in giving directions for lab every week. Her lectures were good too. Exams were not bad - don't need to know the procedures in-depth or step-by-step, just know the general ideas, lab instruments, and processes used. There was a significant amount of extra credit offered (3%).

Eric is genuinely interested in his students' success and wants them to make art they can learn from. Discusses individual project ideas in depth with students in order to provide helpful insights before and after critique. Pushes you out of your comfort zone and wants to see the creativity you come up with in each assignment. Very friendly & kind!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: So pretentious. Cares more about his promotion than putting effort to teach or do their administrative tasks - seems terrible that we are learning from someone who is still an undergraduate; makes zero sense.

Awful time with this professor. 4 exams, 3 essays, 30 journal entries, 15 assignments, and a final project for a THEATER class? Citations in Chicago?! Never had this much to do for a subpar class taught by a pretentious white millennial trying to teach about POC experiences. How you make your students feel matters more than what you're teaching.

This class was very simple as far as what we had to do. There was a lot of work, but it was all do-able. Eric was very understanding and loved his job. Just know there are multiple assignments due at once.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: Eric is the best teacher I have taken in 3 years of college. He is so well informed, caring, and passionate. He is a tough (but fair) grader but if you listen to what he wants to see it's an easy class. Just show up and do the work and he'll teach you so much.

Eric is one of the best professors I've ever had. He is very flexible and understanding. As long as you read the plays and engage in class you have this class in the bag. He makes class very enjoyable, and the topics are actually interesting!!

Professor Abele is an awesome teacher whose lectures are engaging and entertaining. This was a summer course, so there were daily assignments and weekly projects, but they were reasonable and fun to complete. I would definitely recommend this class!

Eric wants his students to succeed. All he cares about is that you communicate with him if you are struggling and strives to support you as best he can. It is obvious he cares about all his students and lays out his expectations Very clearly. He expects you to present your work to the class, but is fair in his grades and artistic liberties.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Eric is great and it is clear he has a lot of experience with Fashion, but the class structure is a bit obtuse. The lectures and reading are very vocab heavy but none of the tests have been vocab relevant. The tests also don't really make sense format wise / aren't very forgiving. Also, there's a lot of writing-based HW.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--TEST HEAVY--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Sure, Eric will make you work hard. But if I'm being honest, his classes were some of the only classes that really challenged me at UMBC. He's a tough grader, but he's not unreasonable and if you take the time to talk to him outside of class, his feedback is very thoughtful. He has been known to raise your grade if you talk to him about it.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: It's nice that his syllabus has all the due dates on there so you know exactly what's due when and how to do it. he's a very tough grader, sometimes the criteria is unclear. Make sure you attend all class or you won't pass. Made us read an entire book but spent only two weeks on the material. Sadly due to lack of THTR Profs you'll see Eric often.
The grading is subjective, so you either make what you want to make, or you get the A. Choice is yours.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: Well, if you're a theatre major, you have no choice in professors. I just made this page because he complained about not having one. He's very sassy, but usually that's a good thing.
The professor was a great explainer of all the details and truly cares for his students

Whoever gave Salem a 4, you are DESPICABLE. Salem is the BEST professor in the econ department, and his passion for econ will make you care. Short, easy hws; study these before the 2 exams + cumulative final, and you will succeed; they mirror each other. Bonus pts on exams! The research paper was hard, but a good challenge for senior year!

Professor Abo-Zaid is a top-tier economics professor! His lectures are inspirational, well-explained, engaging, and get you interested in the material. There is one homework per week, which is a piece of cake if you take notes. Exams are nearly identical to lectures, so take good notes, and you should have a great time! 100% recommend.

Took his class this semester, he provided a sheet of equations which covered most of the topics seen on tests and weekly homework assignments came from. Study that sheet, pay attention in lecture, ask questions if you don't understand and you will ace this class. He is a great professor!!! sit up close in class though he is quite soft spoken.
Gave good lectures, was willing to explain things again in office hours when had trouble understanding, grading mostly on weekly online homework and a few tests.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I have taken Professor Abo-Zaid for 3 semesters straight and this course was probably his more complex one. He does not force attendance, but he welcomes questions and is very informative. This course was very useful for real world application, i.e EXCEL. Tests were in relation to lectures.

Professor Abo-Zaid is the best economics professor at UMBC. He is a very smart man and applies his lectures to real world examples. Although attendance is not mandatory, it is highly recommended. His lectures cover everything that will be on quizzes/exams.

If he is available as the professor for a class you need to take, take him without hesitation. He is accessible outside of class and grades work with feedback quickly. He is very kind and presents the material well. One of my favorite professors so far at UMBC. For the class I took, as long as you pay attention and apply yourself you will get an A.
This class was great. Attend lectures and do the HW assignments so you can  easily learn the concepts. He is more than willing to answer any questions and provide constructive feedback when needed.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Caring--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He is a very caring professor. If you need assistance he is willing to help and his homework and practice exams are similar to the actual exam. One can learn most of the class from the powerpoint and paying attention to his lectures.

SAZ is a great person. He is very caring and will answer any and all questions about the material. He is straight forward with expectations and doesn't try and trick you on exams. 2 exams & final (final is worth 40%) with HW thru/out sem. HW is simple and not too time consuming. Just study the prob sets for exam & pay attention to lectures for A

Professor Abo-Zaid is a wonderful professor and he really cares for students. He is really good at explaining the concepts in a very clear way. His lectures are very helpful and the problem sets and practice exams are very helpful as well. I would highly recommend this professor for all courses in Economics.

One of my favorite professors. Lectures are engaging and he is always willing to answer questions. He boils down the material to a level where it is less abstract than other economics courses, and makes models actually applicable to the real world. Practice exams and mathematical derivations are very helpful. Study those& do your homework (1x/week)
Hes a wonderful professor, he gives practice exams which are extremely helpful, explains theories very well, and makes lectures entertaining.

Pr. Abo-Zaid is a really caring person. There is homework is once a week, it is always due before class starts and is almost always multiple choice. Although lectures can be a difficult, his exams are based off the homework and the study guide. Thumbs up!
Great professor. Go to class, take notes, and do the homework and you will be well prepared for the exams and get an A.
Very high quality professor! He was extremely helpful and caring. I would highly recommend taking him for ECON 312.

Professor Abo-Zaid is amazing!! He really cares about his students, and wants you to pass. You go over Excel, Stata, and MatLab, and he simplifies and breaks down the material really well. Easy weekly homework assignments, 2 midterms, final, 1 project. Midterms are open-note, so no reason to fail. Super accessible, one of the best teachers at UMBC.

Professor Abo-Zaid is amazing!! You go over Excel, Stata, and MatLab, and he breaks down and simplifies each software really well. He really cares about his students, and wants to make sure you pass. Easy homework assignments every week, 2 midterms, final, and 1 project. Midterms are open-note so there's no way to fail. Overall, really caring guy.
Professor is very whimsical in her decision making. Often gives misleading or completely incorrect information. Often gives harsh grades after giving contradictory instructions and feedback.

I might be biased because this class is basically my career goal, but I thought Abod had a nice, proactive approach to the class. While it was not super organized, that was met with a similar amount of flexibility. The exams were well structured; actually testing knowledge rather than memorization.

Professor Abod is extremely disorganized but tries her best to make the class interesting with group work and activities. Exams are harder than you'd think, so write a ton even if she says to stay succinct. She's not consistent at grading exams either, obviously creating other problems. Overall, this class kind of sucked.

She makes really unreasonable decisions really last minute and expects you to fall in line. Tests aren't too bad but wording is confusing. She's still a good teacher though. You will definitely learn the subject and in multiple ways like groups, presentations, partners, and lecture.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: Super boring and mandatory lectures filled with useless info (+1). Poor english, and provided no motivation to come to class. Not terribly difficult, just a depressing and unhelpful class to be a required credit.

Dry lectures and difficult tests. We were given a lot of extra points on the tests (your lowest test grade was replaced with the highest test grade), but it still wasn't easy. Homeworks weren't too difficult but usually involved learning a lot of stuff you don't know and wasn't covered in lecture.

I took the summer class for CMSC 426 taught by professor Dutt. The assignments were overall difficult, mostly because of the poor layout and explanations given on them. There were so many questions being asked about topics that should have been taught to help with homeworks to the point where the professor recommended ChatGPT.
Nice guy and helpful in office hours but not the best at teaching material during lectures. Class is extremely dry.

Dutt is a nice guy and cares about the students but he honestly does not fully know what is happening in this class. The group project was not bad as long as you have a good group. The individual assignment we did was a joke as everyone got a 100 no matter what you turned in. His ppts are not in depth and sometimes, decent professor to take with.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Graded by few things--Group projects

reviews.comment: Group Project the whole semester so pick good partners.
Super boring and mandatory lectures filled with useless info. There's no course organization, but he is a nice person. Unfortunately, this course is required.
