Prof. Dutt has no business teaching this class. He hasn't worked in the industry for decades and never implemented Agile/Scrum. More than once he has said he doesn't know the material well. His typical lecture is disorganized. His explanations are usually unclear and most homework/exam questions are vague. Only plus is his somewhat lenient grading.

He is a very flexible professor in terms of grades and assignment due dates. He does not always go into depth on some subjects, but teaches you what you need to know. I liked that he used videos and examples to teach. Available for office hours.

I like him as a person. I would never take another class with him. He knows his material, but not great at teaching it to others. Assignments and Exams are easy. material is an overview so you won't really know details of things. If u want an easy A, take it with him. If you can take it with Oats.

Nice guy, willing to help, not always very clear. He is boring too. Class is fairly straightforward. Assignments graded pretty easy. 1 long project. 2 easy HW. 2 medium tests but graded easy. If you try on the project and get b's or so on the tests (fairly easy) than an A is pretty ez. Project harder than cain but less documentation.

DON'T TAKE THIS PROFESSOR. Easily the worst professor I have ever had. He makes you want to fall asleep as soon as you step foot in the classroom. He doesn't follow his syllabus for the class. Lastly never shows up on time to class. He always has you waiting 10 minutes after the class starts to show up.

Most painful lectures ever, he just runs page by page through the textbook. Is un-organized and does not possess strong technology skills. The grading is super relaxed and leniant, but no feedback is provided.

You will most likely have to teach yourself/learn from other sources, he will either read verbatim out of the textbook or play youtube videos in class, he is so lazy that sometimes he may play the same video and not notice. Lecture is literally useless.

Insists on online learning, but refuses to learn how to use a computer. Will only lecture word-for-word from the textbook, and incredibly hard to follow along. It is much easier to just not go to class and Youtube the material for the class. Avoid at all costs.

Took his class online and was completely unprepared for how difficult and directionless his course was. I got behind pretty quickly and when I asked him for help, he blew me off. Also two weeks into class, he forgot I was his student. Retook it with a better prof in-person and the class is 10x better.

He doesn't teach very well. Lectures are boring and are just him reading through textbook examples. It's not too hard to get an A because the exams and homework weren't very hard but I hardly learned anything from lecture. If you take 225 with him, expect to learn from khan academy, Youtube, and the textbook, not from lecture.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Abrams lectures gave good information on the topics we learned. However, in terms of grading, it is as awful as it gets. The great majority of my assignments were graded at the very end in January, which is after the semester ended.

Agree with everyone on here saying he is a terrible teacher, however I stopped "going" to class (he stayed online this semester) in about mid-october and still managed to secure a B in the class because his homework assignments are incredibly short and easy and so are the two quizzes we took. Super easy to pass if you just need the math requirement

Horrible. Like others said, AVOID AT ALL COSTS. Horrible lectures were boring & monotone (long pauses and then would speed through content). Lectures were literally copying the textbook. Syllabus was messed up and sent out late. Claims online learning is better but not tech-savvy. Only survived by using homework as reteaching. Tests felt too simple

Very monotone and difficult to pay attention to. His exams are no more than 4 questions and extremely easy. You don't have to attend lectures because the assignments will teach you everything. Quizzes are open note and book.

Once uploaded a file called "Exam1." The file type was "textclipping." This immediately created many problems. Essentially, the entire class could not access the exam. Professor is not tech savvy despite preferring online learning. He struggles to effectively use technology to teach. I highly recommend not taking classes with this professor.

Think twice before you take him! I repeat twice (2x), his explanations werent clear, his voice is so low and he makes pauses as he speaks, you might fall asleep and not just any regular naps you will be snoring FS, u will be depended on discussion, text books, YT and OHs. Youll stop going to the class after abt 4 lectures! Stay safe, stay away!
Half of what he says sounds like a question, and he has a habit of doing long pauses multiple times in the middle of a sentence, making it hard to keep track of what he's saying.

Terrible professor. Dont know how effective his teaching is in-person but from an online standpoint he is the worst teacher ive ever had. During his lectures he just goes over the textbook and rarely provides examples. Do not make my mistake and choose a different calc professor because he is horrible

This professor is the worst math professor I've had so far. Lecture covered textbook problems and aren't helpful in understanding the material. Very monotone and easy to lose attention. The only way to learn calc 2 was through homework or discussion. Exams would be based on the homework so it made lecture even more useless.

Lectures were useless, the only way to learn was through homework. The discussion taught more than the professor. Did not adapt well to the online environment, lecture only covered textbook example problems so it was useless. Math is one of my best subjects but I learned so little with this professor. Choose someone else if you want to learn math.
Horrible communication, did not give direction on class guidelines, syllabus did not outline course. I don't know how this professor is in person due to covid-19, but online this instructor is awful.

Worst math professor at UMBC by FAR! Lectures were useless. Watched him write down examples from solutions manual, that was the class. Didn't seem to understand a majority of what he taught (hence copying solutions). Sped through content, making an already hard class unbearable. PLEASE AVOID AT ALL COSTS IF YOU ACTUALLY WANT TO LEARN!!!!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Abrams was a funny and great teacher. If you do all the assignments and complete all the study guides before the exam, you really shouldn't have a problem getting an A.

If you study her slides, use her study guides, and pay attention to her jeopardy, you'll pass her exams. She knows 311 can get very boring but she still manages to make it as interesting as she can. You can tell she's very passionate about what she does which is inspiring. OLAs can get hard but she does have good extra credit via SONA, etc.

Professor Abrams is amazing. It was a group version of 311 she still lectured each unit for you to properly understand the course material. Her personality is infectious and makes you want to smile. Extremely sweet, caring, and wants everyone to do well. Lots of extra credit, exams are fair-just read the book, and she's easy on the eyes (jus sayin)

Abrams was probably one of the nicest and most accommodating profs I've had at UMBC. She knew 311's content was dry, but she pulled examples from her own research exp and I felt like that made the class all the more bearable. I learned things about psych research I otherwise wouldn't have known by just learning content from the textbook.

Dr. Abrams is a down to earth professor that makes learning the material bearable. She is accessible during her office hours and she's goes in-depth with explaining things. The exams are tough, but if you study the powerpoints and her study guides you'll get an A. She lets you earn up to 50 points of extra credit through SONA and events.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: The best professor at UMBC. HANDS DOWN.

Dr. Abrams is great. She cares about her students, she's good about giving examples to explain concepts, especially for such dry material. She's willing to make an appointment with you and is big on explaining how things are in the real word, which makes her a great resource.

Her exams are pretty tough and are not always from the study guide. She is extremely friendly and funny, although her class wasn't very organized. Groups are assigned and she gives group work randomly, which are a large portion of your grade. No cumulative final, 4 exams, and a group project. Extra credit opportunity through SONA, which helps a lot

This professor always seems to be in a world of her own. The exams are quite hard, with the true and false questions being extremely ambiguous. The group work she assigns every so often is pretty important because there aren't that many grades in the course, but they are very sporadic and I don't think she even knows when they will be.

The subject material is incredibly tedious and dull, but she made it worth it! She explains concepts by talking about actual research to get you connected. Breaks the umbc official class format and lectures for you--god bless because the class format is AWFUL and her lectures are amazing. Show up, skim the reading, do the homework, do just fine.

PSYC 311 is incredibly boring, and sometimes Dr. Abrams legitimately just reads off the slides and you question if it's worth it to descend into the void. It's not a difficult class by any means(she sometimes repeats questions from the group quizzes onto exams) at all though. Get the EC though(50 pts max!)- you won't be sure if your group is stupid
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Clear grading criteria--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: PSYC 311 is boring, dry, tedious, and dense.. but Professor Abrams saved us all from a slow and boring semester by bringing her cheery humor and lighthearted nature to class every day. She's young, fun, uses relevant and poignant examples,  demonstrates applications of 311, & inspires us to work hard. She does not dumb it down, just brings us up.
EASY EASY A. Show up and get A. Two exams which are 100% from the study guide she gives 2 days before exam. Group presentations are super easy.
Very easy class; In-class assignments add up so make sure to attend every class; Great and understanding professor; There are no exams, just applied work
Easy class, just make sure you show up for the in-class assignments.

The issue with this course was the messy and non-negotiable environment. The worst part was the perfectionist expectations that the professor held for the students. Students would receive low scores, even when their work was highly detailed. Her standards for what qualifies as perfect are unusually high, almost impossible to reach.

She is uniquely terrible at her job among UMBC's art professors. She is uninterested in teaching more than the bare minimum, directing us to tutorial videos that don't help. She doesnt teach important tools like program shortcuts, yet expects them from us. These are long projects, but she admits to not viewing them fully before giving an F.

She is self obsessed and disorganized. She calls peoples work disturbing, for minor issues and awful at giving people authentic feedback just saying that it looks wong or needs to be changed without any explanation. Her Syllabus is confusing and doesn't match to what she says during class. I dropped out due to her disrespectful attitude.

A good professor and is very knowledgeable about Graphic Design. I have learned a lot about Design that I didn't know before. I think most of the negative reviews are people that would argue just to prove they are right. I will say, her communication is not very good but she still cares about your work, you as a student just need to be respectful.

If this was my first introduction to graphic design, I would've switched majors. Drags lessons on longer than necessary, gives conflicting advice, will not let students record or take notes during lectures, and the designs she teaches are just confusing. If she edits part of your work, she'll critique it the next day not knowing SHE made it. Avoid!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: heavy on attendance, disrespectful, dont get sick because you wont have an excused absence, contradicts her own rubrics, directions, and crits. Will edit your work and then hate it the next day, and then get defensive when you say she did it. Would recommend taking this class with a different professor.
Changes her feedback depending on her mood, refuses to acknowledge when she's wrong, and does not give clear instructions

By far my favorite design prof at UMBC. She can be a tough cookie but intends to better you as a designer. She has plenty of design knowledge to share and brings the heat to critiques. Don't take her words to heart, she means no harm. You'll see your work grow throughout projects and the feedback will pay off!

She is not the best teacher. She gives tough criticism and is sometimes rude about it. She often contradicts herself in the feedback she gives students. Also not very understanding in my own experience of certain situations. She made me feel terrible and hopeless about my work and discouraged my interest in graphic design.

Great designer... Awful professor. She will tear down your design and your soul. While she gives a lot of feedback on how to correct your design, she will also insult your performance (ex: "If I was a design company, I would've fired you by now"). Took away my interest in book design and made me fearful of each critique session I have with her.
I attended her class last year. I had a hard time communicating with her, and the feedback she gave me was not very helpful. She is qualified as an artist, but not a professor.

Gives a ton of feedback but you have to learn how to understand her because she doesn't communicate very well. Impossible to reach outside of class and gives no feedback on submitted assignments. She's an amazing graphic designer but a terrible teacher. I learned nothing about the technical side of graphic design and only background and history.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: She's a designer first and teacher last. Shes very knowledgeable but a terrible explainer. Frequently goes on tangents and if youre not one of her favorites expect little remarks as to what you did right. Contradicts her own critiques and has her own tastes where if you dont meet them expect your grade to drop. She's a good person, but a bad prof
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: MY FAVORITE PROFESSOR! She knows everything there is about graphic design and she really helps you improve your skills. The class is not really hard. She grades based on if you listen to her feedback and fix what needs to be changed. A lot of her criteria is unclear so you should go over it with her to make sure.

Long overdue review, for context I had my class with her during Fall 2019. It was one of my worst experiences at UMBC. I was criticized for every action I did although it was the same as my peers which was approved. Got my first panic attack then. Felt pretty much worthless. She did end class with "Oh, I was a bit hard on you" with a laugh
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Grading criteria and assignment directions are often UNCLEAR. Make sure to ask for clarification or examples if you're confused. Hours of work go down the drain with one misunderstanding. Otherwise, I think she gives honest, direct feedback. She is understanding and often times gives us extra time if we express concerns on a deadline. Good class.

Professor Abraham is very kind and flexible, it was a difficult and busy year but she was very committed to her class despite all the hardships. Take notes on her feedback and participate in lectures, she'll appreciate it. This class breaks down design principles and builds makes you reconsider your process, there's room for failure, & fun projects
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: She clearly has experience in the graphic design field but makes this lower level class more difficult than it should be with unclear directions and critiques. Her critiques can come off quite harshly or rude even though she is trying to help. Though I have never had her in person, online is not the best option for this class or this professor.

Horrible professor, did not like her. Her grading criteria was not clear AT ALL. Show to students once on how she graded but yet did not even follow it. Unclear on how she graded any students assignment. She will grade you on how enthusiastic you are in the course. If you are not then she will give you a bad grade. Worst professor ever. DONT TAKE

Professor Abraham is a highly talented graphic designer and has a strong grasp on the principles of good design. You will learn the most from her feedback, so I recommend you really listen and understand what she is telling you. If you are humble and willing to take her feedback, you will find this an easy class!

-No individual work in the class (no lab), she want everything to be done at home.  -every class, she gives lecture (usually showing other students work) and critique work that you did at home.  - very subjective -Will take your computer to rearrange your designs - instructions are not clear - she doesn't respect students option or work.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: This professor is so knowledgeable about the field. It's refreshing to have a professor who gives real life examples and assigns projects that you can actually put in your portfolio! I loved this teacher. She at times gives directions that are hard to understand and contradictory, but overall she was great. She gives great feedback.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--Caring

reviews.comment: Guenet is a Graphic Designer, not a teacher. Until she learns how to differentiate, you might as well find a random client on the street to teach the class for you because it will practically be the same thing.

She does contradict herself often and really pushes her students which is why she has the poor reputation she does. However she is completely understanding and there to help you if you take the time to get to know her and ask for help. Respect and participation go extremely far and she is known for giving students several design opportunities

Professor Abraham really cares about her students and wants to see you pass the class, but she's really terrible to work with. She is very confusing and clear with what she wants, and flips back and forth of her opinion. Although she has great feedback, she's very picky of what she wants, and she's very criticizing, and gives you C's for no reason.

Guenet is a great professor, however she is a lot of design students first experience with a 'client' so she gets a bad rep. She is honest with her critiques which really pushes you to improve. Despite her flip-flopping, she is extremely helpful and you'll love your work in the end. If you don't, that's not her fault.
So bad! This professor shouldn't be teaching. Anyone  half-decent graphic design teacher giving you the same assignment would do an equal or better job. Nothing special here.
GD 1 as a class was generally easy but she is a horrible professor. You won't learn as much from this professor compared to others in the department. Avoid Guenet if possible.
Learnt alot from her one on one. She is ver frustrating to work with and is very wishy washy with what she wants. She has great knowledge of design and type. If you make an effort she will too.
She has a lot of experience and is knowledgeable about graphic design but she is a terrible professor. She doesn't really teach anything, but rather critiques based on her style preference.

She is horrible! you will pretty much have to take her as a GD Major here at UMBC, but she is so scatterbrained, always flip flops on what she wants you to do, she will tell you to change something, then decided she dosent like it that way.  There are no deadlines until the final crit.

She is an extremely caring and understanding person. She is not clear often and some of her projects seem like busy work rather then something that will actually help you develop your skills. Overall she cares about her students learning and she wants them to be happy. Not a bad teacher at all

Guenet is awesome! Definelty one of my favorite professors at UMBC. She is extremely helpful to anyone who truly wants to learn. She is honest with your work and has tons of experience to back up her opinions. If you don't get a lot out of this class it's because you didn't put enough in it. I can't wait to have her in the future!
Probably the most sincerely nice professor I've ever had at UMBC. She is always willing to help and is always perfectly honest with your work.
she is not very clear with her assignments and also never responds to emails. her homework are not hard but the directions are very vague.

She chooses favorites, forgets who you are if you are not a favorite, and grades arbitrarily. She's also always late. She forgets to mention details about the assignments. She's a nice person and GD majors pretty much have to have her as a teacher, but she's not a very good teacher.

She has a lot of real world experience and knowledge. She's not ridiculous and anal about stupid things either, and doesn't baby-sit. If you do good work, you get a good grade. No stupid gimmicky crap to pointlessly stress you out. I really liked her, and I'm taking her next class next semester.
She's too scatterbrained and has too many other responsibilities to be a good teacher. It was an easy class but I learned nothing.
Very nice, easy going atmosphere in the class, not the easiest grader unless you spend the big bucks printing... don't fall behind cuz she doesn't have weekly deadlines.
Love Guenet! Hard but worth it, You learn a lot and she gets really involved. You should try to learn as much from her as possible.
Great professor, relaxed classes, no deadlines until final crit, helps you improve your work, just really a great sincere person outside of class too.

Alen is an awesome professor for calc 1. I have no idea how he got so many bad reviews. He provides plenty of extra credit, answers emails, is always available for students and is very helpful in his office hours. He does have an accent, but it's not hard to understand - I barely notice it now.

He was my TA for this course, and was extremely helpful to me.  If you go to his office hours, he will sit with you and explain the material, and go over examples.  I would have failed without him after I was out sick and missed two weeks of class.

First, he never really used the textbook, so I felt that I had wasted my money. It also meant that you had to attend every lecture. The examples he gives in class are never as hard as the ones on his tests. Final was a torture for people like me who aren't good at math because he didn't write it. He's also too lazy to give hw probs from the book.
omy lord!

It is true that he (barely) "has as accent," but if you can't understand him, it's probably because you are a sheltered child who has never left MD.  His exams, while challenging, are a fair representation of the material. He grades fairly.  He demonstrates proofs in lectures, which might puzzle some of the dumber students.
I can't understand what he was talking about...he has an accent, average test score in my class is never above 70 even he curved it.
Good Teacher

He is a good instructor and explains math concepts very clearly. He makes it so you never need to read the textbook. If you attend the lectures and do practice problems regularly, the course should be straightforward.

All around, Reddan is a great instructor. The class doesn't feel boring and he engages the classroom well. The biggest downside to him is his tangents. One time, he started talking about the Simpsons and how it's the best show for mathematicians. It was interesting to hear but took away time from instruction. He only teaches in the summer.

Prof. Adali was very effective in teaching the theoretical foundations of the relevant concepts and made clear connections with the applications. The assignments were beneficial for understanding the concepts and prepared us well for the exams.

Not an effective teaching professor. She can laugh or show frustration when students cannot answer questions, which some may find discouraging. Classroom interactions can feel tense. 
Core courses may be better with another professor, and non-core classes often include mostly/only her research lab students.

Dr. Adali is not qualified to be a professor. She may be qualified to work as a research professor but that is all. She gets frustrated or laughs at student's questions. She gives bare minimum material so you have to heavily study the book to prepare for exams. She may ignore you if she feels you are not doing well in class. Very disappointing
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Hard tests, but she teaches all of what you will need from the test in class. She is very knowledgeable, you just have to study her class notes and do the homework many times. Excellent teacher, the best in the department
Woohoo best prof
She knows the subject very well.if you ask a question,she will make sure you undrestand.
She knows the subject very well.

Not very eager to help students with comprehension. Laughed at several students for answering incorrectly in class. Assumes that students have same prior knowledge as she. Gives difficult tests that are not easily finished in time allotted. Does not give take home tests.

Did not teach some of what was in the course description. Test items were fair, but grading was not (i.e. deducted points for x^H = x^T, x = real). Refused to provide notes for days that I had to miss class, and that material was on the test. Changed assignment for a month's work, claimed lack of convergence.  When confonted, admitted convergence.

Took ENME 110 during the summer. Although it was a very fast paced for a 8 week course. Prof B did a very good job at explaining every concept with detail and many different approaches. He genuinely cares for his students to do well. Homework was very similar to the exams. Def recommend.
Took him for ENME 464, not 204. Professor Bridandolph has a long way to go when it comes to teaching, but he's chill fr.

I had a really good experience taking this class. Prof. Bridendolph often correlates some of the course material with personal work and designs he did in the industry which made the lectures extremely engaging.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: It's very obvious he cares a lot about teaching engineering, as he always seemed very interested in everyone's projects. That being said, lecutres were very mundane in my opinion. He tried to spice them up but I could tell they were just recycled. The work for that class isn't super hard if you know CAD, there's just a lot of it.
Great Professor. Extremely personable and always make a point of utilizing office hours for any question related to the course.

Not great lecturer. Just 2 quizzes covered lecture material. Useful stuff (e.g. CAD) learned in the Labs w/ TAs. The group project and reverse engineering project is the majority of the work. Some dates/grading criteria were not clear in the class . Lecture material didn't matter except for lecture quizzes and (scarce) relevance to projects.

Took Dr. B for CMSC 441. He will be the first to admit that he isn't the right prof for everyone, but I loved the class. Algorithms is interesting topic and Dr. B wants you actually learn how to critically think. The lectures are fun and he brings good energy to class. Just make sure to stop him and ask questions because he does talk quickly.

Professor Bargteil is an excellent professor. The only downside is that he has nothing to do with the projects. If you start the projects early and go to office hours the projects aren't too bad. As for lecturing, all you need to do is pay attention and take notes. His tests are the homeworks, but with the numbers changed. Anyone can pass him

He teaches material very fast, just ask him to slow down. His lecture doesn't use power point slides (so if you're used to that, choose a different professor). The homework he assigns is basically the exams, so just keep practicing those. Lastly, his writing can be difficult to read, so ask him/clarify what he wrote.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Lecture heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: AVOID! writes tiny unreadable gibberish on the board. he has never actually coded in front of us and only writes it in his terrible handwriting with 30 errors. he didn't know which proj we were on! and he forgets to assign the hw on time and doesnt change the due date. he doesnt teach the material assigned in the projects so good luck not failing.

Super chill and easygoing. A bit disorganized and bases lectures on what the class wants to focus on. But they are pretty engaging; he'll give advice and tell interesting stories from time to time. Exams are very similar to homeworks so it's easy to do well if you understand those.

Bargteil is a very lax grader with 15% of the grading going towards homework assignments you get full credit on if you turn literally anything in (blank pdf included). Tests were easy as they were based on the homework assignments. However, his lectures were unorganized and I couldn't learn much from him. Easy teacher but not a good one.

Class was very straight-forward. Professor Bargteil was very knowledgeable and, although boring sometimes, lectures were very helpful. Homeworks were basically graded for completion and exams were based off homeworks, so it wasn't too difficult. Very enjoyable semester

Professor Bargteil was a good professor although sometimes lectures were a bit dry. There are 6 projects, midterm and a final, the class was pretty difficult but is manageable and there is lots of extra credit so it's not too hard to get an A.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Clear grading criteria--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Professor Bargteil found a way to make the class enjoyable. He added lots of humor into his lectures as well as fun facts about important people who came up with the different algorithms covered in class. He was not always prepared for class with examples, but clearly knew the material he was talking about. Lots of fun, best CMSC prof at UMBC.

Bargteil was clearly not excited about teaching 341, he was seldom prepared for class and often made mistakes when drawing trees on the board. On the plus side, he was extremely clear about expectations on exams to the point of giving basically the same exam as a practice exam. Nice guy, I feel bad that he was forced to teach 341.

Clearly knows what he's talking about, works in the field and is generally very knowledgeable and intelligent. He heavily focuses on students actually learning and understanding the material. The course mostly follows the book and the book is pretty good. First projects are pretty difficult but they get easier and there's a lot of extra credit.

There are 6 projects worth 60% total. They are difficult and time-consuming. Partial credit is very generous, just get something running. This class covers a lot of difficult material. He is not good at explaining it, but does not expect you to learn all of it. Tests are hard, but curved as much as 40-50%. Work hard and you can get a B.

great prof 
made it easy to understand material

I took his Math 215 class this past summer (Summer 09') because I heard all the bad reviews about Kapoor. Only Kapoor teaches Math 215 during the regular school year, so I definitely wanted to take Vancea, from the good reviews he got. Let me tell you, go to class, pay attention, act like you want 2 learn, and you will pass.  Test are not that hard

I only had Adrian as a TA for my Calculus I class. He was very clear though, and I sure as hell learned a hell of alot more from him than I did from my professor (Wilson). Adrian is a good teacher, and knows what he is talking about.
i thought i was  getting a D in the class but i ended up with a B. just make sure you go to class and look like ur trying. do the homework and participate in class
Def. take this guy, he's the best one teaching this course. Easy A+

BAD teacher, I dont understand whats going on in the class along with the rest of the class.  Unfortunately he was the only professor teaching this class.  The material he goes over in class is not clear at all.
He's friendly and helpful to students if you ask for help but his lectures are mediocre at best.
I am not sure why he has such low ratings, his classes are really easy to get A's in if you read the material and do work.
just rattles off code, does take questions or explain anything!!
He just reads the slides and says um a lot. His quizzes are hard as hell and are focused on small details in comparison to the full chapter. DO NOT TAKE HIM!
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: By far, worst professor ever. The class is very dry and tough. He lectures straight out of the textbook by showing you it and reading it. Even then, he says "um" every 2 words which drove me crazy after one lecture that I never attend them because of it. His quizzes are tough and fast paced and focus on minute details relative to the entire chapter
Ta? A joke. His lectures? A joke. This class was so unnecessarily hard. He never gives a clear grading criteria and will find anything to take point off of.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Engaging professor with a strong emphasis on participation. Lots of in class discussion. They provide detailed feedback on written work and are very accessible outside of class. Concepts are explained clearly and questions (and debate) is welcomed. Definitely opinionated, but creates a respectful environment.

reviews.comment: She is absolutely amazing! Shes caring and understanding towards first year students and only tests on material covered in class. She is clear about the content and is willing to help anyone who needs it. Ill be taking her for chem 124 this spring and I am so excited!

AMAZING professor. Loved her. I gave it a 4 on difficulty because I find chemistry easy, however, some do not. One of the best teachers at UMBC! If you show up to class, take good notes and understand the lectures, you are set for an easy grade!

Real good instructor. Cares a lot about her students. Tests are tough, so studying is a must. Fair grader.  Accessible outside of class. Didn't use the textbook at all, you could probably get away without it.  SI Pass sessions are extremely helpful. Dropped  from a B  in 123 to a C in 124  when SI was  not offered.
Best teacher I have had at UMBC and I am saying this a senior.  There aren't enough words to describe how awesome she is.
She somehow makes the content more understandable and is extremely flexible about meeting with students.

Dr. Tracy is the sweetest! she is smart, caring, and funny! I loved taking 102 with her, she needs to teach 101 and 102 all the time, carpenters' method is not working... Dr. Tracy's exams were challenging but she was always so helpful and never moved on until you understood everything.

Dr. Tracy is a really great professor! Put a 3 on easiness only because CHEM 124 is not easy but she makes it as understandable as possible and she is very approachable if you ever have questions. I'm very glad i had her!! Would definitely recommend! Only teacher to take if you need to take Chem 123 and 124. She is clear about grading and exams
Dr. Tracy was amazing and very sweet. She explains things very clearly and makes chemistry seem soo easy. Take her!

Dr. Tracy is very clear cut and makes the material of CHEM102 seem easier than it is. No clicker questions so lecture is not mandatory. I got away with skipping a few times in the semester but she always has at least one lecture-related question on her exams (which are easier than carpenter's). She loves to answer questions during class.
Doesn't teach that well.. No friendly interaction with students .. Gives out tests suddenly out of nowhere.. Just not motivated to teach
Uses R and teaches quantitative methods. Highly recommended.
Organized course. You know what to expect. Grades on time and answer questions accurately. Sharp guy.

The huge group project dominates the class. Groups are assigned by him, and the project will be difficult if your group members aren't up to it. It's a lot of work. He can be snarky to students who ask questions or answer them incorrectly during class, even though he encourages participation. Tests and quizzes are easy, open book, & taken online.

Dr. Koru is a nice guy.   However I'm not a fan of the timed online quizzes and exams.  On two occasions for quizzes my connection failed which affected my grade.  Luckily he allowed me to take those two quizzes over.   Make sure your group for the project has strong programmers.
Professor is very professional and "clean cut". Class has a ton of work, but isn't really difficult. I found it extremely boring but others may disagree. Overall, good professor.
The course is among the most difficult courses I have ever taken. Having said that, the professor is helpful and he is an expert.

This class was pretty heavy workload-wise. There were weekly readings and online quizzes (open book). Your grade relies primarily on a semester-long group project. Dr. Koru actually provides useful feedback in a timely manner, though he may not seem to be the most approachable person. Ask plenty of questions.
Answered questions to clarify any issues in a timely manner.  Available via email.

Not easy but gives a lot of insight. I was working full time while taking this course. Course project is a real project which is difficult so teamwork is important. Examples given in the class were helpful.

The course was well organized. Weekly readings and project were useful. We learned Ruby programming and I am looking forward to learning Ruby on Rails. The professor is an expert and he has been helpful in programming tasks
gives good guidelines and grades on time.. he knows a lot. he is nice, the course is hard but useful... pleasant experience overall

Such a useful course for my current and future jobs. He is a very helpful, warm, and wonderful person but make no mistake; when it comes to academics he is also an expert and he'll make you work hard. Quizzes are useful and they keep you on track. The project is tough but gives insight.

Course material is interesting  and very useful.  Your grade is based off of online quizzes , an online midterm, participation, and a project.  Project is very time consuming  so don't make your scope too large.  The professor's grading style is strange so you may get low deliverable scores even though you met all of the requirements. Nice but dull

Very professional appearance and presentation, but a normal underneath (don't let the 20pg syllabus fool you). Be professional with your project deliverables.  Reading quizzes every week, but they're easy.  Project deliverables are tough, involved, and the core of your grade, so be prepared.  Compared to the other teachers, he's the one you want.

I am taking the systems analysis and design from him. The expectations are crystal clear. The project is extremely useful. The best organized class among I've taken so far. The professor is very knowledgeable.

Directions for class assignments are vague or contradictory.  He doesn't explain why he considers answers to problems to be correct or not.  His sylabus is innacurrate with regard to project due dates.  Expects 100% class attendance even though he often isn't there when projects are due, so TA's from OTHER CLASSES end up grading your work.

Tied for worst teacher ever.  Very little help on projects. sub/ta gave exams, hard to understand, boring as hell and reads from slides. TA grades all documents after converting them to chinese.  Had class grade quizzes and made up answers as he went and couldn't explain why certain answers were right. would not explain grades when asked

Professor goes over slides with little to no words on them. His explanations are very vague and don't have any actual substance or information. He expects you to be paying attention at all times as well as he will call on students randomly. He clearly does not have enough experience as a teacher and it is a big gamble to stay.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment:
He's making these reviews look at May 8th someone left a review saying “This is the best IS310 professor ever. Amit for life.” for the IS 425 but refers to IS 310 make it make sense.

Also not a coincidence how most of the ratings were posted on the same day.
Please do yourself the service of not taking this man, He is new hopefully he gets better.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I see that people gave him a 1/5 and is saying that these reviews are made by him. Trust me, these 5/5 reviews are not fake. I was there when my classmates made these reviews.I gave him a 4/5 because from the beginning of the class, it seemed pretty boring and hard (ONLY because he's new at UMBC). But towards the end, he was doing pretty good.

Just save yourself the stress and don't take him currently. His inexperience shows and it was just a gamble for me staying in the class. His explanations are vague, his slides are either too many words or pictures with little to no words. His exam structure is vague, can't take constructive criticism and left good fake reviews for himself.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This class was super lecture-heavy, and the professor didn't explain things well. The syllabus didn't match how the class was actually graded, which was confusing. He was slow to grade and hard to reach, but he is a pretty easy grader. The class did get a bit better toward the end, but overall it was hard to stay engaged.

This Professor is horrible, he doesn't respond to emails, can't teach (his explanations are vague) his slides are either completely overly verbose or pictures with little to no words. His exam structure is vague and can't take constructive criticism, leaves good fake reviews for himself. This class is truly a gamble please save yourself the stress.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Some of the ratings about this professor are completely wrong. Take a different professor. He will confuse you throughout the whole semester, and when you email him, he will take weeks to respond to simple questions. The class was in complete confusion learning from this professor.

Worse professor. I usually nvr post on here.  But this professor is posting fake 5 star ratings on here for himself. Please save yourself and take another professor if you care about understanding material.
One of the best Professors I have had in my tenure at UMBC. I truly wish he teaches other high level courses so I can take him again!
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Best IS professor at umbc. Responds to emails on time and for exams you are given a cheat sheet. 100% would retake this course again if I could even if it didn't count for credit.
This class was so good I almost failed on purpose so I could take him again.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: This man is the best lecturer ever to exist. Im graduating, but I don't want to cause I want to take this class again.

Good professor, made IS310 easy, doesn't teach much and is slide heavy. He also takes a while on grading. However, he will help you and he's new to UMBC, so cut him some slack as a beginner professor. Ending with an A because the class work was easy, and the exams shouldn't be hard as long as you study.
such a good professor -- really understands the students esp since its a night lecture course. would take him again since he's chill.
made IS310 much better/easier and got an A in this class which was supposed to be pretty hard. W PROF !!!!
This is the best IS310 professor ever. Amit for life.

I'm going to just put this here as an early warning. Currently taking his 425 class and he really does not teach, does not follow the syllabus, and is very very vague of what content is on the exam. It got so bad that the midterm was delayed because all the students did not know what we were suppose to study. Avoid him like the plague.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Beyond amazing as a professor. Really helps build passion into photography!

A very fun and engaging class. If you remotely like any bit of photography, you will enjoy this class. Most of the assignments are enjoyable and let you get creative your own way, and isn't tough at all. Also very lenient with due dates and is very helpful when you have trouble with assignments!

Professor Voos is an amazing professor. She helped me a lot when I was struggling with personal issues during the semester. She was very flexible with due dates and always willing to help. She is very kind to her students. This class is an easy A as long as you do your work.

Easily the best teacher I ever had! Very flexible with disabilities and assignment deadlines, super kind and understanding, and allows maximum creativity for students. As someone who dislikes videography she made this class interesting and enjoyable! 10/10, favorite professor

she was very nice, understanding, supportive, resourceful, and easy to get in contact with. she showed respect for our individual submissions and projects, even personally complimenting me on one of my projects, saying she was very proud of my work. she brings great energy to the class and made me want to pursue photography more. highly recommend!!

Kindest, most laid back prof I've ever had! She's very communicative & clear on her directions. She wants the best for all her students. She offers valuable help when needed. We really only had class on days when a new project was introduced & crit day, giving us ample time to film & edit our videos! She'd host editing workshops if need be. Easy A!

Amelia is one of the best professors I have had. I didn't know much about photography but she makes the concept easy to grasp. She doesn't care about attendance or extending deadlines as long as you talk to her or email her. If I see her as a professor in any class id lady take it with her.

She's hands down the best and easiest professor you can take. If you need your GEP credit 1000% take her. Course consist of 3 exams (gives the EXACT exam questions the day before), 8 random quizzes (1 question on each quiz, questions like "whos your favorite superhero"). Attendance kinda matters since u need the quizzes. overall ez class, take her.

She's a very sweet old lady and genuinely cares about her students. Definitely attend her lectures they can feel a bit slow if you're not into philosophy, but she's kind, She posts exam questions beforehand, holds review sessions, and gives about 10 super easy quizzes all semester sometimes even fun ones like What's your favorite cartoon?
Super nice and makes the test easy to understand. She loves her job and tries to make the class fun and easy.

I enjoyed how chill and stress free her lectures were. There was no homework, class days for exam reviews, and quizzes were extremely simple. She is super calm and lectures are fairly organized, the content is all laid out on slides but she tends to revisit the same content multiple times. Kinda challenging but it's not normally an issue.
Super easy class. She gives exam questions the class before exam day.

Slides posted on blackboard, lectures ok but I don't think anyone ever went to class cuz she would go over the exam QandA the class before the exam, and there would be a video on blackboard of the review so students could reference it. Basically a free class. She's also really nice.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Respected--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: She was a great professor. The class was an easy 100%. You could skip every class except for the one class before the exam and pass with 100% because she gives you the answers to the T the class period before. Amazing and easy.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Very easy class, goes over all answers before exams. Show up to class during review sessions and you will get an A.
Very chill and laid back professor, goes over all answers before an exam, just show up and you'll get an A.

I loved having Amy for philosophy, she is one of the best profs at UMBC! She puts a lot of subtle humor into her lectures and assignments are incredibly easy if you just show up to class. Awesome class and would absolutely take again.

Ms. Payne is a UMBC gem. I've never felt so relieved or glad to have taken a college class before. She really cares about her students and this class is so easy to pass, as long as you show up. Even if the room is "dry", she will still try to inject humor so the lecture isn't boring. Although easy, the class discussions were a blessing to the mind.

Dr. Payne is one of my favorite teaches til this day. Her quizzes are all written but they are short and you are able to watch her past lectures on her Youtube channel to help. She gives us like 3-5 days to do the tests but it'll probably only take you like 10 minutes max. This class is a must take if you go to UMBC.

Professor Payne is awesome! Shes funny, and actually teaches you the material that she puts on the exam. Before tests, she goes over what questions will be on the test. Also, her attendance isnt mandatory.

The easiest class I've ever taken. Easier than any high school class I took. She makes it easy and digestible and gives exam questions and answers before the exam. You have to put in considerable effort to pass with less than an A. Not only this she's a great person, very knowledgeable, and is there for you if you need it (academically) :)
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Graded by few things--Caring

reviews.comment: Her classes are very interesting!

Take Professor Payne if you want to take PHIL100! She is very laid back and gives very few assignments, and she is not a tough grader. Professor Payne genuinely wants you to learn and doesn't want you to stress about her class. Highly recommend!

Her class was pretty simple. She has readings but you don't have to read them to understand what she's talking about. We have weekly 'quizzes' that are easy as long as you partially listen and extremely easy if you take notes As long as you show up and engage in her content a little, the class won't be a problem.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Graded by few things--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Her lectures might put you to sleep sometimes but if you listen a little bit you can pass the occasional quiz. Also the exams are essay based and she gives you the answers the class before. Literally just memorize it and you should get an easy A. The final paper is not that difficult. One of the easiest courses you will ever take at UMBC

one of the easiest professors at UMBC. Gave us the answers to the exam questions the class before the exam. If you didn't want to go to class, she said "just say your dog ate your keys and its fine." Along with the class being easy, she is actually a really great person and she is so funny. if you participate she'll love you, but sleeping is fine 2

She is a very sweet and funny teacher. The lectures are a little boring but it is very easy to get a 100% on all three exams (which are essays she gives you the answer to the class prior). 3 essay exams and a final research paper that is not very difficult. Class is very easy and do-able. There are quizzes once a week or every other week, easy.

She was pretty good. She seemed a bit disorganized and like she didn't plan much ahead of time, but her lectures were still interesting. She's funny and definitely adds some of her humor to the lectures. Not the best prof at UMBC, but definitely not the worst.

Prof B is extremely approachable outside of class and does his best to answer questions in as much detail as possible. He drew examples of ADTs whenever possible which I found very helpful. Exams and projects were straight to the point and not too bad as long as you pay attention during class. Probably one of the best CS profs at this school!

Simply not a good professor for this course.  Either late to every lecture, or flat out cancels it.  Does not explain concepts all that well, his exams are poorly written, is not in control of the projects, and is overall very disorganized.  It is still possible to do well in this class, but your best bet is to teach yourself the content.

awful paced class. too much time was spent on specificalities so we were unprepared for projects. wasn't in touch with the main professor so couldn't answer questions about the projects beyond general info. was tardy to every class. exam questions had ridiculous point weighting and since he didn't proctor exams he couldn't answer exam questions.

He was friendly and explained the concepts, but he was wishy-washy. He often canceled class or switched the meeting format with same-day warning. He tried to punish the whole class because some students weren't there. He wasn't familiar enough with the projects to be helpful with them. He covered only ~75% of the material we should have learned.

He cares about his students and goes above to present material to help make you understand. This is a hard class, you need to do outside research on your own to have a deeper understanding of these concepts that will repeat again. Attend office hours, he will explain concepts in detail.he is not in charge of projects so cant blame him.

He is a kind professor who can be flexible with due dates if you plan in advance and communicate. But he tried to cancel half of the classes for the semester. Spent 30 minutes on project structures (SPLAY), but 3 days on miscellaneous things. Doesn't know about projects at all. Does not plan for class. I did not learn a single thing this semester.

I am sorry but the reviewer  that said he a good professor is living in a delusion . he is awful , he tries to cut corners and only "teach" us stuff just for exams and reads from the slides instead of giving us practical problems and break it down step by step. he just talks and acts like a TA or tutor instead of a professor. I learn all myself.

I have never had a worse professor. I did very well with the concepts and had no major problems with the projects, but I still struggled on the exams. The second exam, no one finished and he would not take feedback on the length of the exams, instead arguing with us the next class about why we should have been able to finish. DO NOT TAKE PROFESSOR.

I took CMSC 341 over the summer with Prof B. The class was hectic, due to being a 15 week course crammed into an 8 week course.

Prof B was very approachable and personable on discord, which served as a main means of communication. Seemed to be a fair grader, and was open to criticism about poor wording on assignments, often issuing corrections.

All the bad reviews are probably people that either did not understand the class or expected the professor to handhold them through the semester. Very chill professor and is understanding to situations and is very lenient with some due dates. 341 is a tough class and he made the experience easier compared to what I heard from other friends.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Honestly one of the best professors. All the bad grades are from the class being hard, it is very hard but this professor makes it so much easier than it needs to be with how lenient he is. He is also very quick at responding on discord. I would take again!

Everything from the tests was from or derived from the slides. The projects were common for all sections, and they gave 2 weeks per project for a reason. It wasn't particularly hard. People who didn't get a B or higher didn't manage their time on projects or didn't pay attention / attend class.
reviews.rating_tags: Test heavy--Graded by few things--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: Do NOT take this professor. The class itself is challenging, but he made it 10x harder because he is so disorganized. Never responds to email, only communicates on discord. Takes FOREVER to post exam scores. Didn't know barely any of our grades going into the final. Had to curve a bunch just for people to pass. Would recommend anyone but him.

Middle of the road lecture wise, answers project questions during class. His lectures are fine, nothing special. Homework is participation and he gives a 3% "attendance" grade to mainly just boosts your final grade. Exams are a mixed bag, but he will curve them if everybody does terrible. Do well on the projects and study regularly and its EZ.

I would not take this professor. Take ANY other professor. Grading is very unclear and he is impossible to get ahold of. The class itself is not a 5/5 difficulty but dealing with this professor is. All email correspondence was bordering on aggressive or rude. Take anyone else but not him. 5/5 do NOT recommend

Unorganized professor, had to teach myself or go to the TA's for help. Attendance was mandatory but it was pointless going in person. Grades weren't put in until very late so I had no idea what my grade would be which was very misleading. Also, we randomly switched to online lessons which was how it should've been from the start. Disappointing.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Lecture pptx are not made by him, they are made by Donyaee (same as projects). Lectures are worthless, better off self-learning. Exams are hard, there are 2 of them and a final. Nobody finished the second exam, and even though he is NOW potentially doing a curve, it does not excuse an impossible exam. He is nice on occassion, but that is about it.

Professor resists student feedback and seems uninterested in improving. Lectures are unengaging, relying heavily on reading slides. Whiteboard explanations are often confusing and disorganized. I was disappointed, as I initially had high hopes for this class.

This is above all a mandatory class for computer science majors and every option is difficult.
Know going into it that lectures are mandatory, but not his. If you take his class you can still do Dixon's lectures. That is really the only role that the professor has. Because it's the TA's who do the real work, the instructor matters little.

Rambles a lot and live coding in class was rare but it was his first semester teaching. He does care about students and would spend lots of time clarifying project/exam questions and had exam prep outside of class. He's a former student and provides useful info for future classes and topics. Ok for 201 but would not take for more advanced classes.

I didn't learn much from him and most of my studying came from past knowledge and working with TAs. His lectures are essentially useless, he rambles way too much, and wastes half the lecture going over the project? However, you're not out of luck if you get stuck with him; you can always attend another professor's lecture.

His lectures are rambly. He doesn't grade anything in a decent amount of time. Two TAs and he just graded everything on the deadline Jan 2th. Rushed assignments and projects last minute. Assigned a project after the final exam and made it due right before Christmas. Really passive-aggressive and condescending to students asking questions.

Adjunk professor. Seriously the most unprofessional "teacher" at this school. Somehow takes him two months to grade a simple assignment when he has 2 TA's, constantly cancels classes and wont go over material, and attempted to teach python after the final exam because he procrastinated doing his 1 job. Don't take this class with him ever.

To be honest, for this class office hours matter more than anything since all professors used the same course material. I will say though he is really chill for a professor and you can come up to him after class about pretty much anything related to the course. He was late for a couple of lectures but outside of that, he was pretty solid.

Lectures were disorganized rambling, instructions were unclear, grading took forever with little or no productive feedback. Totally unreliable with schedule. Despised communication. Wouldn't provide material online or helpful resources. Barely learned anything for three months then went at 2x speed for the actual topics promised. Worst Ive ever had
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: She's a good professor. Seems very caring and understanding, but such a tough grader on discussion posts. Definitely not an "easy" class, but it's bearable. Graded by participation, weekly discussion posts & reflections, with a fun midterm and final! Midterm was creating your own medieval story, final was cooking a recipe from Middle Ages!

This was my second class with Froide and I loved it.  The readings she chose were really interesting and Froide always leads amazing lectures.  The coursework was minimal.  We didn't have any tests or massively difficult assignments.  Our final was baking something based on historic recipes!  10/10, would take again.

Amazing class and an amazing professor! If you're interested in European history you'll have a good time in her class. Lectures are engaging and she comes up with very fun assignments. She was also very kind to students and was accessible outside of class. If you're a history major or just looking for something fun I would recommend this course.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Tudor/Stuart history was a great class. Prof. Froide is really passionate about the subject and knows a lot. She also made it easy to understand and joked around a lot. Lectures are pretty vital to understanding the subject, so make sure you don't sleep on them. Also, get ready to read, write, and do thorough analysis of assigned readings.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: passionate about the subject and very knowledgeable. open to conversation with students within lectures. not too much reading for a 400-level. tough but fair grader - really expects a lot from papers and test responses (blue books!). we had a feast day at the end of the semester for extra credit. kind, cares about students. clear syllabus/policies.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: She is a decent Professor and knows the subject. However, she is a tough grader and the class was boring to be honest. She also has political leanings that can get frustrating.  Attendance is mandatory and your grade will reflect. If your're going to to be out of town she needs written proof in advance. I've had better at UMBC.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: The course was meh, but Prof. Froide is a good professor.   Three papers and two assignments.  Attendance is "mandatory"-it won't ding your grade too bad for missing more than the 2 "allowed" absences.  The grading is fairly tough for a 200-level course.  Lots of reading, but that's to be expected for a history course.

As a person, Froide is very friendly and helpful. But she is a tough grader. Her two TA's are EXTREMELY tough. There were 2 tests and 3 papers. The papers were difficult to write because the content was tedious and boring.

Prof. Froide could make Mortuary Science seem like a fun subject. Her lectures are upbeat and energetic. She doesn't read verbatim off the PowerPoint or constantly stop to consult her notes.  Despite having almost 100 students, we frequently had class discussions which really made you think. Froide has been my favorite professor at UMBC.
Professor froide is great, but she is a tough grader. You will read 4-5 books since its a history class, but only the chapter that is assigned to you by your last name. No test and one final project.
Professor Froide is one of the best in the History department! She's so helpful and nice and lets you know just what she's looking for on papers and tests. I'd take another class with her for sure.

This teacher was amazing. She provided many resources that you could use during your research. She is very approachable and will help you with anything and everything. She really wants you to be successful. Also, you can write about any topic as long as you can link it to 18th century London. This class was amazing. Definitely take her!

She is one of the best professors in the department. As long as you come to class, take notes, and read you'll do fine. If you do what is listen above you will have no problem getting an A. She is very helpful and entertaining. She is also the nicest person in the department.

Class could be interesting, but it could also be supremely boring and sometimes droned on forever. Although it was a topic I was interested in, she just couldn't seem to grab my attention. The books were very boring and she didn't like my writing style. In general, a good prof, knows her stuff, but not good for a non hist major who needs electives

I'm not a history major and I was real intimidated by the amount of books we were required for this class, but I really enjoyed it. You write a short paper for each book, discuss them in class, and have two longer papers to write on subjects you choose. Participation and attendance count for 25% of your grade, but it's easy if you try. Great prof!

Dr. Froide is AMAZING! Her lectures are like one-on-one conversations! She makes complicated British history seem accessible and understandable. I don't know how she does it, but I get it now! Attendance is optional, but go to EVERY class & you won't regret it! The books and research are interesting too! Uses visuals,discussions and group work.

She is a great teacher! She is very helpful!! This class is quite reading and writing intensive, but is still fun. One of the two research papers is about crime in 18th Century London, and the research you conduct about these criminals is so interesting and enlivens the past!

You don't learn too much general European women's history.  Instead you read books on specific topics.  2 papers and "discussion questions" on the books & no exams.  The class is based around the books & discussing them.  You should probably take a class before this to put everything into context.  There is no real lecture.  The course is lacking.

SHe is a good teacher. She assigned two papers and discussion questions which made up the majority of your grade. She also assigned points for attending class. She made helpful comments on your paper to let you know what you had done wrong. Only bad part was you were graded on your classroom participation so expect to talk alot

HIST 497 this semester was on 18th century London. The class involved researching any aspect of London's history with 18th century English newspapers.  Dr. Froide was truly helpfull in recommending books, answering questions, and commenting on the rough draft for improvements. Overall, an amazing professor!!

Best teacher of the Western Civ teachers.  Classes are lecture based.  Fun, smart, and effective.  3 non-cumulative tests are essay based which turned out to be a great way to be tested on the material.  There's 2 short papers on museum trips, which are easy.  Great teacher, I recommend taking her.

Dr. Froide made learning about European Women's history a fun and enlightening experience. She assigned interesting readings and the class discussions were never dull. This course had 3 male students and 20 female students... as a male student I can say the class was a positive experience and would recommend it to anyone.

Excellent professor! She is really knowledgeable about early modern England. Also, Froide assigns interesting readings about topics like witches and Britain's path to becoming a world power. A fair grader and writes a lot of comments on papers to show what was done well or not so well.
One of the best professors. Made the somewhat boring content fun. Easy grader. Would recommend

I liked Prof. DeVos for most of the semester and found him knowledgeable and caring, but I was very disappointed by a moment in class when a Hispanic student shared he had family members who were undocumented and the professor joked “I'm calling ICE.” It made the room uncomfortable and nobody laughed, I lost a lot of respect for him that day.

Overall, I enjoyed taking class AMST 200 with DeVos would take more classes in the future with him, I enjoyed his lectures, although they can be lengthy; they still held my attention. I'd recommend the professor and also the class if you need a culture credit. Overall, pretty easy but with challenging discussions that I really enjoyed.

Easily the teacher that made me most believe how passionate they were about the subject they teach. Projects are high-effort but enjoyable and students are given a lot of leeway. Final exam is intentionally easy and he actually marks the part of lecture slides we should take notes on. Very funny and interactive before, during, and after class.

He's very passionate about the content he teaches, and he's very open to all perspectives. He tried to engage with the class as much as possible, but he doesn't scrutinize anyone for not participating. The projects were easy, and so was the homework. He laughs a lot lol, and most work you do are group assignments.

He's a very niche person... Very cool and has a lot of interesting interests and perspectives. He's a very easy grader as long as you follow assignment guidelines and attend classes. He's also very passionate about the courses that he teaches, which is very refreshing.

Straightforward class short weekly assignments, 4 projects (1 short essay and 3 audio-visual projects) and one open note final. The projects are not too difficult and can be completed in a day and the final was a no time limit-take home exam. He is also a pretty lenient grader, so if you try you'll receive a decent grade.

This professor is really good at explaining within his lectures. He tries to incorporate a lot of videos so its not just him talking, and I feel like this is the only class that I genuinely can connect to the real life world with. He is really well spoken and makes sure that. everything he says is appropriate, and funny! Super empathetic professor!
This professor is the best professor I have had since my Kindergarten teacher. He is so well thorough, he is really good at explaining

Dr. DeVos is by far the best professor I've had in all my college years! I wish he taught every subject. His teaching style is unique and FUN. I took an accelerated distant learning course and his expectations are very clear! Participate in lectures and complete some assignments. He's not a tough grader as long as you show some critical thinking.

i took AMST200: What is an American and AMST365: The American Horror Film with devos! easily my favorite classes i've ever taken. they were fun, got me excited to go to class everyday, and helped me grow as a person (both academically and emotionally). devos is incredibly kind and chill if you're the same. be open and authentic and you'll do well!!
puts on chill guy persona, not actually chill

The professor is amazing! He is funny and cares about his students. This class was graded by weekly assignments (very very easy), two projects (very easy), and a take-home final exam (easy). Would definitely recommend anyone to take this class and him.

This class taught by him was the coolest class at UMBC that I have ever taken. He is an awesome professor and his lectures are very interesting and keep people watching. He has 4 projects and then a take-home final at the end and every night before class there is a small video to respond to. this was an awesome class!!!
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: I had him for AMST 200 and he was great! My best professor yet. He's funny and very knowledgable. His lectures are captivating and there are a few small projects throughout the semester that he grades lightly! The final is open note, so go to all of the classes!

I made my ratemyprofessor account just to review Professor DeVos, I had him last semester for History of Music and I genuinely think he was the best professor I've ever had. Very casual and easy to talk to, makes jokes, talks about his personal life sometimes in a way that makes you feel very connected to him. I cannot recommend him enough.
Professor DeVos is an amazing professor! If you are interested in music definitely take this class! He cares about his students and is always willing to help them.
An amazing teacher, really fun lectures

I've never said this about anyone else at UMBC, but DeVos is exactly what a professor should be like. He isn't a person who simply hands out grades, he's a lecturer that incorporates everything for a fun and easy (if you put in the work) American studies course. Any music lovers should definitely take this class with him. 11/10 would recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Inspirational--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: He is a solid teacher. His sense of humor is hit or miss, but the class was very interesting and he delivered it in a good way

Took Professor Anchor for MCS 101 Lab, and she was great! Super easy class, just follow her instructions and read the guidelines for the projects, and you will easily get an A. It was fun using editing apps, and she was really helpful if you had any questions. Definitely recommend her if you want an easygoing professor!

Took MCS 101 with her in Spring 2024. Her lectures were pretty engaging and she would ask the students many questions. There are lots of videos we watch later in the semester. The lab section was not hard as long as you paid attention. Even if you struggle with video editing, this class is easy and Professor Anchor is always willing to accommodate.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: This was the second time I have taken a class taught by Professor Anchor and I have greatly enjoyed both. I am not the strongest student but this class was an easy A as long as you turned in the assignments on time. Anchor was very helpful during the assignments and was always very kind to everyone.

If you are into video production or photography , you might like this class. As someone who is into video editing / photography I enjoyed these projects as a break from my usual work , even if they are time consuming. Attendance matters but if you keep up , projects aren't too bad.
Extremely nitpicky when it comes to grading for group projects. Also mandatory attendance is annoying to deal with. Not a horrible person, but I would definitely not take another course with her.

Professor Anchor is a great 101 teacher. She gives relevant information to topics, and the projects and papers that go along with it are based on what was learned in class, especially for Lab. She gives plenty of background for assignments, and plently of time to complete them. Easy course, just sometime lectures are not the most interesting.

Professor Anchor is the only choice for MCS 101 and that's fine. She has structured the class well but there's a lot of work between the lecture and lab. Assignments are easy but require some effort. The textbook is a "required" read before class but you really don't have to. Some weeks you'll need the textbook to do the weekly questions, or not.

Lazy, gives unclear assignments, gives way too many assignments (not little homework assignments, important assignments that will easily mess up your grade), relies on the TA too much (and the TA rarely grades and when she does she does she grades strictly). Another prime example of the average UMBC prof.

Very average professor. Easy class with easy projects and short assignments. She's very nice but her lectures were kind of boring, and sometimes we would just watch online videos for a large portion of the lecture. Not very stimulating, but take it if you want an easy A.

She's a really good professor. I would totally take her again! The projects are super easy, and the work load isn't a lot.  If you ask question she'll happily answer without making you feel like you're  burden.

She's a decent professor, but kind of unclear in assignments. Generally, it's not too difficult taking her publishing class but if you're even slightly unsure about what she expects in an assignment, definitely approach her because there were many times when I thought I did well but actually got a low B or C. Also, come to class!

I read all of the bad reviews on here before taking this class, but it was the only section I could fit in my schedule. If you have any choice at all, do NOT take this class. The amount of homework assigned is ridiculous, and most of it is not  even graded until finals week. I wish I would have just waited and taken it with another professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--SO MANY PAPERS

reviews.comment: This class would have been one of the most useful classes in my professional career and she ruined it. She was unprofessional, a horrible communicator, she looked down her nose at everyone, and she was incredibly boring.
Awful professor
Yes, there are assignments.  You're in school.  Do the work.  I appreciated the work we had to do in class and I feel like I write better because of it.  I would absolutely take her class again.

She takes attendance, so if you skip three classes.. you fail. She gives so much unnecessary, long assignments, but she doesn't grade any of it. Her "lectures" are so long, boring and pointless. You don't learn anything in the class or out of class. I've never taken a class where so much unneeded work was assigned.  This class sucks.

The material learned is pretty easy and useless at the same time. WAY too many useless assignments that takes her forever to grade. Going to class is pretty much a waste of time, but attendance is mandatory and if you miss 3 classes your grade drops 1 letter. Would NOT recommend taking her!
