reviews.comment: You HAVE to read the textbook because he provides 0 notes and lectures will not be comprehensible at all if you haven't read it beforehand. 85% of your grade is 3 exams while the rest of it are frustrating homeworks that'll be up to 25 questions long - other teachers will only have you do like 5 questions.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: if u have a choice take any other professor. your grade is basically what u get on the 3 exams. the avg for my class mightve been a D and he didnt curve. lectures were poorly paced and in my opinion you fare better by learning straight from the textbook. if i could give a 0 i would, disclaimer i am a  4.0 student this guy was not good
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Good lecturer. You have to work for it but you can earn it if you try hard enough.

I really liked him! Tries to connect what we learn in lectures to things that he's done in industry and give "real life" examples. His PhD is in math so he's fairly strict in terms of making sure the proofs are logical and structured the way they should be, so he's a tough grader. That being said I learned a lot. Redo HW problems to review for exam
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Hard, but fair. If you work for it, you should get the grade. He knows what he's talking about and does it well. A+

He's a really good teacher, and keeps class interesting enough. If you take notes and pay attention you'll be fine. Exams can be more difficult and there is a decent amount of homework, however, he's not unreasonable.

He's a nice guy, but he grades like his life depends on it. You don't write the proof the way he wants it.. he'll deduct 10 points. There are 3 exams including the final and they're all really difficult. Half the class failed the first two exams, and I don't know if he's gonna curve the class. DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS WITH HIM. TAKE IT IN SUMMER.

Honestly, he is a good teacher but he grades as if we are flawless humans who cannot possibly make error in life. Will possibly end up gives you a two letter grade curve. Doesn't really care too much about the class.

Although Professor Horta is a lenient grader, his lectures are a nightmare. He wastes your time rambling and giving advanced examples without much explanation. His expectations are incredibly unclear, and each exam is worth 25% of your grade which makes the lack of clarity even more stressful. To succeed with him, you need to be your own teacher.
Class wasn't too difficult, but this was my second time taking it. Not recommended for first time students. Takes a long time to return tests, doesn't have office hours or use Blackboard.
Very annoying. Lectures are boring, incomprehensible, and tests are hard. Don't take.
Boring, unhelpful, and hard. Lectures are very boring, did not learn anything, and tests are very confusing. AVOID.
301 is a hard class. But if you must take it, take it with Arnie. Very good professor and is always willing to help out. Presents the material clearly and makes it clear what you need to know.
Very intelligent and helpful.  It all comes down to your effort.

You have got to be kidding. I walked into the final with a B average and after studying for 2 weeks, I still failed the final which was so hard that 2 people actually got up and left once they saw it.  Not a bad teacher but his final submarined 5 people that I knew in the class including myself. I ended with a D and never retook it.
The best! Best! Best! professor I ever had!  He made  linear algebra really easy and fun!  Instead of hating the homeworks I really enjoy doing them!  A really great professor.  Everyone loves him^_^

Dr. Elisabeth genuinely care about her students. She encourage us to learn from one another and to build bridges that will help us have better communication and to learn problem solving skills that will impact not only our careers but also our personal lives. Easy grading. Course is well organize and she is easy to reach and helpful.

She's very willing to help students, and passionate about what she teaches. She interacts with the class and encourages us to interact with each other. She explains confusing concepts without translating, so we understand the ideas in the context of the language, encouraging us to think in Spanish rather than constantly translating everything.

Fun, engaging, thought-provoking... a great class and teacher! I took the class online in Summer 2024, and she was fast in responding and giving feedback. I learned a lot about the topic, myself and my culture. She is understanding with students and really wants you to succeed. I highly recommend taking the class with her.

Love her! So sweet, incredibly knowledgeable, very fun to be around and always willing to learn. One of my favorite classes I've taken thus far: thought-provoking, useful, and taught super well. It can be a lot (multiple assignments a week) but all very interesting and a great opportunity to learn from other people.
While Dra. Arevalo is very knowledgable, I could hardly understand anything she said. She is hard to understand-- even in English.  She makes her lectures entertaining but the class itself is boring.

Dr. Guerrero is a wonderful professor and the class is fun. You have discussion board posts and blog entries once a week, a presentation where you present something from your culture, and 2 exams that aren't hard. At the end of the semester there is a multi cultural potluck that is lots of fun!
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Inspirational

reviews.comment: The professor did make us read many chapters for the Espana y Sus Culturas class, however, I learned so much! She only has two exams and a paper. She gives study guides for each exam which help whilst studying. A true understanding of the material is needed and in lecture, she clears is up. Lectures seem long and boring if you don't do the reading.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Group projects

reviews.comment: Although she is very friendly in person, I found this class to be very disorganized. I went to her office hours many times during the semester for feedback on my essays and made the changes but she still took points off of random things. Didn't do anything in class besides talk about irrelevant and random things; doesn't teach spanish. bad prof.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: very reasonable workload and grading system. participation and attendance are important

I am taking her class right now and I love it. She is so nice and helpful and I LOVE that she is from Spain so you can learn the correct way to use vosotros. A lot of other professors don't know it or refuse to teach it. I highly recommend.

He's blatantly biased towards certain students. In fact, it's known by many that one student got an exam grade in the 60's on the 1st midterm and online he changed to the 70's. He gives up on ALL the students just because they don't get the grades he expects on exams. He needs to take responsibility for this! Awful professor!!

Exams make up 90% of the final grade so if you mess up on just one of the midterms there's a lot of catching up to do. The grading on the exams have an unclear criteria/rubric and it is very easy to lose points if you don't write exactly what he wants to see. Lectures made the content more confusing than just reading the textbook.

He's constantly making fun of students and blocks the board so students cannot see what he is writing. If you go to ask questions he really doesn't want to help as he thinks he covered it well enough in class. He will laugh at the students and say "it's easy". Unfortunately, you can't take it with anyone else as he's the only choice.

Being a biochemistry major and taking the chem required PCHEM was scary enough, mainly because I had not done calculus is 3 years as well as how hard I heard this class to be. Dr.Arnold however made the subject very approachable and made it easier to understand. He can be a bit passive aggressive but, is a very great professor. GO TO PCHEM CLUB!!

Prof Arnold is not a mean prof (though I wouldn't call him nice). He is however precieved as mean to many students. The course was hard to learn from to the point that going to lecture left people more confused than staying and listening. When 50% of the class is failing exams he points out the one student who got an 98. An anomaly not the standard

Dr. Arnold is a rockstar lecturer, but a bit old school. His lectures are very engaging, if fast-paced, and he takes a lot of time to go through the more complex parts of pchem in "gorey detail," but he also often glosses over whole branches of mathematics that he assumes we're all familar with, but aren't prerequisites (diff eq, lin alg).

Excellent teaching style, but he doesn't stick to the order of the textbook. Write down every example in class - he probably just gave you some great hints for the homework. For more help, go to PChem club. Again, he will help you solve the homework, clarify material, and prepare you for the exams in the most efficient way possible: problem solving

Go to class, go to P. Chem club, and hold on for the wild ride. Dr. Arnold is THE best professor that I've had, and he makes P-chem tolerable. He's helpful and always has answers when you approach him with intelligent questions regarding HW and concepts. You get out what you put into this course.  "P-chem isn't difficult, it's just complicated."

Attend Class, Take notes, Do Homework, Check keys to HW posted, Finals  has atleast 3 HW q's. Doesn't exactly follow the textbook but insists on reading. 4 q's on mid-term exams. Gives an eqn sheet for exam, so no need to memorize the formulae. Overall, one of the best professors in the Uni and trust me I've encountered a lot in the past 3-4 years

Great Professor. very helpful. really cares about student learning. P-chem is a very difficult class. Homework is extremely challenging and time consuming. Exams are almost as difficult. He sets up a "PChem club" each semester. highly recommend participating  or forming your own study group. Course material is almost impossible to grasp without it
extremely good, wish I had professors like him in every class. A tough topic like Pchem is made very interesting and most importantly I've never felt bored during his lecture

Good teacher. Hard subject so it wouldn't matter who teaches it. He tends to make tests questions from homeworks which he doesn't grade at all. He is a fair grader. Tests are 4 questions and generally reflect whatever he has taught. Good teacher.

His class is definitely not easy, but he's straight forward in what he expects of you and students have ample opportunity to learn the material. He is a good lecturer and eager to help students outside of class.

P.chem in general is a very tough subject. Arnold's a nice guy who wants his students to do well, but does not stick close to the book. HW is hard because information could not be found in the textbook, but it is only worth 2 points each. There is not enough resources to get help if you have a question. Very, very tough class, but curve is generous

Although the final exam was really tough in my opinion, the midterms (4 questions each) are relatively straightfoward. Nobody should have a problem getting a B because he curves the final grades by 10%, i.e. 80  is A, 70 B, etc. I wouldn't worry too much about the ACS exam either because I got 20/30 questions right but got a 90% after the curve.
Good professor, clear lecture. His exam are clear, and following closely the homework and example during classes. If it was not for him, PChem would be very boring and hard to get over with/
Makes a terrible subject like PChem tolerable

He is THE professor to take for non-CMSC-majors who would like to learn introductory computer science (through Python). Any difficulty from the class comes from the required materials for all CMSC 201 students (shared Homeworks/shared Project 1). His projects were extremely relevant to nonmajors, and he wealthily-prepares you for exams. The best!!!

I'm a biochem major with no prior coding experience; he broke down Python so easily and made it so that I caught on quick. He has clear office hours, and the class was small, so asking questions was very easy and inconsequential. Exams were open-note, he prioritizes learning above all else. Easily one of my favorite classes.

Arsenault is a passionate professor who clearly loves teaching computer science. Although he's a bit nerdy, he's very friendly and helpful. He taught Python well, and the exams were fairly easy and similar to the practice exams he posts. The only drawback is that some of the homework and projects can be time-consuming and complex.

As someone who has never coded before this class, the content was a little bit difficult for me even in this intro class, but prof is a very nice guy and he'll really help you if you're stuck. He's VERY understanding when it comes to grading and due dates, just email him and give him a heads up. Overall, a really great prof.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Graded by few things--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I had him when taking Computer Science 201, and he was one of the best professors I've had. He answers all questions and will stay after class to help with homework or projects if you need it. He also gives out a word document/pdf on how to do an assignment/project step by step and will help if you do not understand it. I would 100% recommend him.

He was a really nice guy. I took this class with no programming experience but he was very helpful if you directly went to him with questions. Class was graded by labs, projects, and tests but there are TA office hours and professor office hours so as long as you use them you should be alright. Try not to procrastinate the projects!

The test makes up 50% of the grade. The answers were not taught in lectures. You need to know the answer by reading out of course material by yourself. the timed test has so many questions one can't complete and after an hour test is automatically submitted.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: No idea how this dude has a job. The TA carried the class teaching and grading. Coding assignments deviate from the book, video lectures feature obscure random details not on exams. Exams are full of misspellings, grammatical errors, and repeated answer options. Exams are a race against the clock (1 to 2 minutes per question) Avoid at all costs.
Too Hard

Was a horrible professor. His PowerPoint slides did not explain the material well at all. He made no effort to explain things in lecture videos. You cannot understand what he is saying in his videos. His PowerPoint slides were literally gibberish and all over the place. I would not recommend taking this class with him.

Professor was unavailable and uninterested in helping. After questions, told students material was already covered or on the internet. Strong Python skills needed for this course, but are not listed as a prerequisite. Sample code had errors, material not updated in yrs. 40% of the grade was on a final. Syllabus just a list of topics.
Great

Self-paced class consisting of a weekly reading, assignment + quiz.  Self-motivation + independent learning is essential. Prof's email/forum communications are vague/short but class expectations are clearly posted. I wish forum discussions were not discouraged so it would seem more like a classroom instead of indep. study. But a good class overall.

any graduate students who would like a somewhat self-paced class, take this. consisted of: weekly discussion board questions to answer, timed quizzes (you can take multiple times though), a large SQL assignment (~20 questions to write out statements) and a comprehensive take-home final. learned a lot (on my own, but regardless). online = $$$$$$ tho
Easy Going Professor, Explains concepts clearly for a really broad topic. Tries to make the most time to meet with his students. Lenient in grading, very approachable and nice.

Easiest class ever, nicest professor ever. She is a literal angel. The workload feels fairly light compared to other classes, and she is not strict on attendance. If you have a chance to take her class, do it without second guessing. No regrets

One of the best professors at this school. She understands the workload of a college student and just genuinely wants you to do well however that works for you. She is clearly knowledgable about UX/UI design. I plan on taking her again for 431!

A literal angel. She is the only professor who actually realizes the workload she gives and organizes the class on bb so it's really simple and easy to understand the timeline for projects. She gives clear grading criteria and excellent feedback. Highly recommend her as a professor. Also had her for the 333 typography class and she was great.

I absolutely loved prof garcia, she was a gem of a teacher and my favorite so far at umbc. Had her for typography1 and she made sure everything was organized and easy to follow along with, as well as coordinated with other professors to make sure not everything was due the same day. The nicest teacher i've ever had. Highly recommend.

Dr. Blumberg is the best professor I've taken at UMBC. He's very supportive and very flexible with assignments.  We only had to write 3 major essays for the entire semester and they were all based on interesting pop culture topics. He doesn't provide timely assignment feedback unless you email him directly. Besides that, an AMAZING professor!!

This class is an easy A. You will not learn a whole lot, and as far as my experience, you will only be graded for one assignment out of three by the end. Dr. Blumberg has a focus on media as opposed to books, which is what makes this introductory class more engaging. I never watched Star Trek or Night of the Living Dead until this class.

This class wasn't super difficult but it was so frustrating. There were only three assignments the entire semester with extremely unclear directions. We only get one assignment back with basically no feedback. There weren't really lectures or anything so don't expect to learn much. However, this class is fine if you just need the gen-ed credit.

I really liked Prof Blumberg. He did a good job with the online format providing good online lectures. We only had 3 essays through the sem. He gives you a lot of time to craft your essays, I procrastinated a research paper, but was still able to finish in one night. The only issue is he takes a long time to grade so you never know what you have.

This class was so frustrating. We had three major assignments. Only found out the grade of the first one halfway through the class. The other two, still have no idea what I got. He grades so harshly and doesnt have a clear grading criteria. If you actually want to learn how to write, dont take this prof.

Only graded one essay all year and did not give any feedback. I found out I had received a B when the transcript was released. Got mad when I asked what grade I had received one 2 essays which had no grades on it. Do not take this professor, there are better english proffesors on campus

I loved this class. Professor was very chill and class felt welcoming. Class time mainly consisted of short online work or editing your groups papers. Show up, or you cannot make up the work. Class usually ended 20-30 mins early because it's based on how much work you personally need to do. However, very slow grader. Last "essay" is multimedia.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Professor Blumberg was amazing. Loved going to his class as it was really laid back and he didn't bombard you with work. Also, the essays had really interesting topics. Would take again.

We wrote a research paper on zombies and made a presentation on superheroes. He is a pretty tough grader so make sure you have someone check over your work. He didn't provide a rubric of any kind and his TAs do not look over your rough drafts they way that the prof grades them. I thought English would be an easy A. Not so sure anymore.

Horrible professor. Gave me a C on my first paper because it was submitted as a PDF and not a word doc and didnt say anything about submitting as a word doc in the directions. Assignments are very vague and you get no good feedback. Do Not Take This Professor
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: One of the better professors I've had. He has a good sense of humor and is pretty laid back. He grades pretty fair, and is available to help you both in and outside of class. You have to write a few papers on interesting topics, such as zombies. The final was a powerpoint presentation on who is your hero and why. I totally recommend taking him!
never had grades posted, instructions were very vague, prompts were also very vague and didn't include clear or detailed instructions.

This was the easiest college class I've ever taken. He's a really sweet, caring guy and he is very approachable both in and out of class. There were three pop culture essays and a group presentation but he doesn't give a lot of feedback on them unless you ask outside of classJust hit the word count and have good spelling/grammar and it's an easy A.

Blumberg is a chill professor. He was nice and his essays were more pop cultural and interesting than most English classes. The only problem I had with his clas is that out of everything I did, I only received one grade back the entire semester. I got a B In the course and I didnt know what I got on the last 2 essays. He was decent.

Very nice, passionate teacher. Assigns three pop-culture essays and a group presentation project as the final for the semester. Grading criteria is unclear, he puts red lines on the side of your Word doc essay and then a final letter grade with a sentence or two about his opinion. Take him if you want an easy A. Don't take if you want critique
My favorite professor so far, the Essay topics are awesome and actually got me interested in the class.

Very chill professor. Easy grade, and less work than other English classes. Cool papers on zombies and superheroes. However, you don't really learn anything about writing (or English really). Not clear AT ALL on grading. You submit a paper and he will give you a grade with one or two comments.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Awesome professor! Very gentle hearted and very approachable when it comes to questions. Would take again!

If you're going to take Engl 100, take it with Blumberg. This is not a stressful class at all and writing the essays for his class are very doable. The first essay was on Star Trek, second on zombies, and third on superheroes (presentation multimedia). The other tasks are simple and easy to do. He is very nice and approachable.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Easy a but not clear about his grading system and you don't feedback after your first essay
Dr. Blumberg is the best english 100 professor at UMBC. He is so funny, and he's very open minded about writing and POVs. TAKE HIM! Or you'll be missing out.

Blumberg is extremely knowledgeable but very laid back. There are 3 essays including the final with some in class assignments. He gives great feedback if you go and ask him to evaluate your paper and if you have questions he will answer them. The topics of the essays are also quite different which is a nice change from the regular English essays.

If you need to take English 100, take it with Professor Blumberg. He is the most open-minded english teacher I've ever had. He has a very clear grading criteria, and grades VERY fairly. He's always available to help students with their papers and gives so much feedback. Very great teacher!
Dr. Professor Blumberg is honestly one of the most chill guys I have ever met. The second essay was particularly amazing, as it was about zombies. I wish he taught more English classes.

By far one of the best professors you can get for English 100 at UMBC. He doesn't teach it every semester, but if he does, try to take it. He won't waster your time with unnecessary writing assignments, its just 3 papers and in-class assignments. He's kinda nerdy, but that's what makes him awesome. He might give you assignments about zombies.

I cant say enough good things about this professor. He is very passionate about comic books and is respectful of students' opinion. I'm a bad writer, but I got an A- on both papers. Make sure to meet the minimum page numbers and READ HIS PAPER GUIDELINES. He docks a lot of points off if you dont. Read the material, put in effort, and you'll do well

This class was great. The comics were first superheroes, then the material covered some nice stories that had tragedy in them, like Holocaust and other issues. There are 4-5 quizzes throughout, 2-5-7pg papers, and a final 10pg paper or optional comic creation. I had never drawn in my life, but the comic was fun to draw. Cares about grammer 2

Comic book lit was a lot of fun and, in my opinion, an easy A. But you do have to read the books regularly---he gives pop quizzes---and carefully edit your papers. Blumberg is a stickler for correct grammar usage, hates to have his name misspelled, and will dock a letter grade or two from a paper if it fails to meet the min. page length. Funny guy.
Excellent teacher, especially if you like comics, or english for that matter. He is very easy to talk to and understand and has a great sense of humor

good teacher, knows what he's talking about. For a class about comics, it was some work.  3 papers & a bunch of reading quizzes -grades papers hard but reasonably. Was out a lot for his wedding/honeymoon-sub provided was v. good. Fair bit of class discussion, the readings were good, you have to actually read them, but they're comic books! fun class

He seemed to be kind of stuck up about the comic book industry.  He treats Watchmen like the Bible. And I wrote some kickass papers and got B's. He's definitely the hardest grading english professor I've had.

The best. Has a dry sense of humor, is extremely intelligent and tactful, and will hold extensive class discussions about the most interesting things. Very much a stickler for proper grammar and spelling, so be aware of that when writing essays. He's fantastic!
Not that good

very mediocre professor. doesn't keep track of time sometimes, which gives us very minimal time to complete in-class activities.

exams and quizzes are super easy, though

Dr. Jackson is an avg prof but provides more work than avg for an intro class. There're required textbooks/readings but you can get away without them to pass the class. The class was well paced, just bothersome to go the extra mile for this course with her strict grading on your writing skills.

I actually took 370. Awful professor. Gives massive exams that if you fail (which most do), your grade is doomed for the rest of the semester. Add that on top of a bunch of other work, the class has stressed me out more than any other class ever has.

Prof Jackson is a very helpful and knowledgeable. Workload is high, but is manageable. She is willing to discuss topics outside of the curriculum and gives you useful info. Her lectures are not as interesting yet she delivers the message clearly. She teaches something outside of the textbook in her lectures. She is a lenient grader.

reviews.comment: Barely passable. If you're taking this as an elective, Don't. She's a very hard grader. exams are difficult and tricky on purpose. Lectures are very confusing and advanced for a un undergrad. this is not a law school. Overall very disappointed in taking this class and lowering my own GPA.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: She is from the University of Ohio and is a newbie at UMBC. Such a hard grader. Especially the exams, worth 60% of your course!! She teaches like we're in actual law school. Lectures are boring and powerpoints are only one word so good luck reading them on your own. Wish she was on here when I signed up for her class. DONT TAKE HER.

reviews.comment: She's a super nice and fair professor. Pretty easy class if you do the readings. You'll cover the likes of Plato, Socrates, St Anselm, etc. It's a fairly interesting class if you actually pay attention and take it seriously, but it is also an easy A. I would definitely recommend taking this course, I learned a lot more than I thought I would!

reviews.comment: Shes so easy, all the grades are just discussions which are easy if u read the textbook, and there is an annotated bibliography, midterm, and a final exam which are all written. But overall shes a great teacher. But she does randomly pick on students to answer her questions if no one is participating and if u dont answer she'll note it.

So easy. If you need an easy elective credit take this class. Most of the work is discussions but there is a midterm and final which are just essays and super easy. No tests and exams my final grade was 99%.

boring lectures. says atndnc mandatory but canceled class like every week?? late work only accepted if u ask (you can only turn it in late 48 hours after initial due date for only 50%:/)  The format of this class is like 12 online disc posts, there was a midterm based off disc topics ,annotated bib assignment , and a final essay from disc topics.

reviews.comment: Super easy, but just be prepared to read. I found the topics really interesting which made this course great. You essentially just have to write

reviews.comment: Very easy class. Read your textbook chapters by class and youll have no worries.

reviews.comment: She seems intimidating at first, but once you get to know her she is a kind person. Read the texts enough to at least know whats going on, put some effort into the assignments, and you will get an A. She is knowledgeable and passionate about what she teaches. I'd recommend her
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Caring

reviews.comment: She wants us to read about 40-50 pages before class and come in with discussions and answers ready. She also calls on people randomly and takes them off guard. It is a lot of reading and homework. If you are ready to do that, then take her. Annotated bibliography, midterm, and final were not that bad.

reviews.comment: In person this semester. Class sessions are so intimidating for no reason, she randomly calls on people during class and expects you to do all readings before coming to class. Its only PHIL 100 and some of us dont have time to do so much for a GEP class. Shes kind of rude and doesnt let you use the BR during class. HW is pretty easy though.

reviews.comment: There were no lectures (live or recorded) in this class. However, the material was easy enough to understand, and a big chunk of the assignments were discussion posts with other students, which helped students understand the material better. Midterm, final and the annotated bib assignment were not difficult. Grading was lenient with good feedback.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Caring

reviews.comment: LOVED this class. Fall 2020, no lectures, no exams. Only reading, discussion posts, and 2 essays. SUPER EASY and flexible. Prof is very nice and understanding. You will have to read a LOT but it is not bad. take this class with her!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: I took her for Philosophy 100 mid-Coronacation and before Corona the lectures were long and boring and not many people actually read the texts so she'd call on random people but when we switched to online she was super accommodating and understanding and every assignment could be answered through YT crashCourse vids and or google search. Very Easy.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Both the midterm and final are essays that are not that hard if you follow the rubric and her directions. Lecture is just going over the readings and participating. Excellent professor and is easy to communicate with and get help outside of class.

The first semester is all that matters. The group projects are easy A's, you just summarize it in a PowerPoint and she walks through all the points. The midterm is the only real exam, she gives a great study guide. Second semester content doesn't matter too much other than another group project, the final is a take-home paper. Great professor.

Dr. Aufseeser is the best undergraduate professor I've ever had. If you have a passion for the subjects taught in her classes, you will excel. She is extremely knowledgeable and cares deeply about the subjects she teaches.
Her Teaching style is good and she's very educated on the topics she teaches. If a student were to ask any question she answers them perfectly.

She grades harshly on the free response on exams, which brought my overall grade down. The few exams are all online and the multiple choice are alright. You need a clicker to answer questions in class. I didn't read any of the textbook and did fine. The class isn't too much work, but be prepared for the exams!

Dr.Aufseeser is fantastic, I would highly recommend taking any class with her. Keeping up with readings is essential to participate in class discussions and activities. Even though the material can be challenging at times, Aufseeser is clear with her expectations and makes the course engaging and fun. One of the best at UMBC!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: The class was not very hard but the lectures were extremely boring. The exams were easy all multiple choice questions yet some of the material on the exams did not come up in class or on the textbook.
Nice teacher long lectures sometime, make sure you get clicker

Amazing professor, no textbook but assigned readings and discussion assignments are due by class time - you can still turn them in late, Lectures and course content is eye opening and inspiring. I also took GES 443 with Dr.A, I would take any class she is teaching!

Prof. A lectures can be lengthy but I found them to be interesting. She encourages everyone to participate as to get the most out of the class. The exams are fairly easy as long as you pay attention in class, take notes, and read the textbook. Most of the info on the powerpoints are from the textbook, with some more arbitrary info being left out.

Shes an empathetic professor and will definitely give you clear cut advice on how to do well on exams and assignments if you email her. For exams, make sure to take thorough notes on the points she mentions in class, read the necessary tbook chapters and rewatch the videos she played in class and you will get an A in this class. Good luck!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring

reviews.comment: She was very nice and helpful when it came to going over previous exams. The written portion of exam is graded by TA, so get to know the TA. There are 4 exams and you need to score in the high B to A range to get an A in the class. Take your time on the other assignments and do it well because it can boost your grade. I loved the material!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: This class focuses on cities and how they have changed over time. She is very knowledgeable and has extensive powerpoints each class. Midterm and final make up a huge portion of the grade but they are manageable with proper preparation. She is helpful if you go see her during her office hours especially for the papers in the course.

Participation is graded, but includes little assignments, so it's an easy way to boost your grade. Dr. Aufseeser encourages everyone to participate, and is great at facilitating discussion. Exams can be very long and sort of difficult, but as long as you pay attention and participate leading up to, they aren't bad. One of my favorite professors.

This is probably the best professor I've had at UMBC. She is extremely clear in her expectations and as long as you hold up your end of the bargain she does as well. Her content is very interesting and even her readings. I'm always eager to get to her classes.
Go to class - clicker participation does make a difference in your grade Don't procrastinate on papers (easy but she's specific in what she looks for) For the tests/exams - READ THE TEXTBOOK

This class was not at all hard but the lectures are extremely boring. Usually, a good portion of the class falls asleep. It is quite difficult to stay awake and she does not make an effort to liven up the class. There are 4 exams total one of them being the final. 2 country assignments that require some work. Most interesting thing were the movies.
Best teacher ever!!!
Lectures were extremely boring, tests were hard but not unbearable, assignments were really easy
Super easy class.  Just pay close attention on her questions in class and skim read your textbook you will get an A.
tough exams

The nicest teacher I've had at UMBC so far! She's engaging & gets everyone to participate. She's always willing to help & is super understanding. There's pretty much no daily homework (except for 2 projects that were pretty simple  & she gave us plenty of time to complete it). I really do enjoy her teaching & her class!

Wonderful professor and person! Her lectures are engaging and she encourages participation from and among the students. You'll end up hearing some strange opinions from your classmates; the lecture environment is such that you don't feel afraid to disagree with the majority.

Great professor, she cares about her students greatly and taking her in higher level smaller class size courses is definitely worth it. Also i'll be honest. The readings assigned were hit and miss but the in class discussion was always fun. be ready to talk about some heady issues and hear some bizarre opinions from your fellow classmates

She's a nice woman and is very helpful. If the entire class does poorly on a test she will curve it. Only had 4 exams (there was no final) and 2 easy research assignments. She encourages discussion and will often have you watch a documentary pertaining to the chapter being covered. Overall, A nice class to take for a culture credit.

Aufseeser is extremely clear and organized with her teaching style. She encourages engaging discussion and knows how to be part of the class and just "the teacher". She is 100% competent, 100% empathetic, and genuinely enthused. I've found that these traits are what make a great professor and a well rounded learning experience. She's super nice!

Aufseeser is extremely clear and organized with her teaching style. She encourages engaging discussion and knows how to be part of the class and just as "the teacher". She is 100% competent, 100% empathetic, and genuinely enthused. I've found that these traits are what make a great professor and a well rounded learning experience. She's super nice!

She is one of those gem profs at UMBC. I took FINC150 my sem before graduating, figuring it would be useful to know before going into the real world. She turned a potentially dull topic into a fun, informative course that was the highlight of my last semester. We built a finance excel sheet that I still use today. If she returns, take if possible!!

Prof. Hennigan is a great person to take financial literacy with! She teaches it very well and encourages students to express themselves through class participation. The most work you'll do are Excel spreadsheets to learn how to make the most out of your budget. Great class!

2nd time with her but SHE IS WAY BETTER AS A TAX TEACHER. Take her for tax. She knows what she's doing and you will learn a lot. She challenges you but in a good way. If you try, follow directions, and pay attention there is no reason you shouldn't get an A. Projects are tough but well worth the learning.

Hennigan is a great person & wants you to do well. she challenges you &her lectures don't prepare you for the exams. The tests are hard af, so study well in advance and ask lots of questions. The homework is so easy compared to the exams. She uses a point-system so if you do all your work and not get the best grades you still will not fail.

She cares about her students and gives multiple extra credit opportunities if you try hard enough. The tests aren't easy but she teaches so well that they should be if you show up to class. She gives relevant examples and isn't against trying to make accounting fun.

Professor Hennigan has a very upbeat personality, and offers quite a few opportunities for extra credit. A very beneficial resource if you're willing to commit to it is her MyLab assignments and the nonmandatory assignments. Concepts will take practice. If you're disciplined in getting things done and getting proper understanding, you'll do fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Beware of pop quizzes--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: She is very easy, not a hard teacher. Gives a lot of chances to get a good grade and it helps that the content is not hard. Occasional pop quizzes that are very easy if you pay attention. Tests are fair and only on what she teaches in class lectures. Actually cares about you understanding the material and gives tons of examples. She looks good too.

reviews.comment: She is a very nice professor who gives good lectures. The homework takes time but it is mangebale compared to other accounting classes. The projects and exams are tough though. She tries to get her students to think like accountants and consultants. Take her class if you really want to learn accounting, but get ready to work.

Dr. Soller was a very kind and welcoming professor. The class content was interesting, and she let students guide conversation. She's strict about AI and made our class do a writing sample, but her tests were all open-note and asynchronous, with not a lot of writing. Work was balanced and not too hard. She tracks attendance but doesn't grade it.

reviews.comment: Took this class over winter; it was a very concise class that depended a lot on reading and exams. Prof. Aubrey herself is very kind and accessible, I never felt like I was drowning in all the content. Her lectures get to the point, and she knows what she's talking about.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Terrific online class to take alongside others. Didn't require textbook, straightforward homework released on Sunday and due the next week, completed within an hour and done before the week starts.
All online. Exams are easy and open book. Had a 96% in the class and did less than 30 mins of work a weed. Easy credit
very mediocre professor. doesn't keep track of time, which gives us very minimal time to complete in-class activities. exams and quizzes are super easy, though
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This was asynchronous online and 75% of the final grade was based on exams. If you struggle with test-taking I would advise against the course. Also if you want a passing grade or time that isn't spent on 60 pages of reading per week, stay away from this course. This was overall a nightmare, I have never had a more stressful course at UMBC.

Pretty much a "teach yourself" class because all we do in lecture is go over what we read...so if you have a hard time reading text scanned into a Google drive, definitely pay attention in class. There are also no real opportunities to make your grade better if you don't do well on quizzes because there is no extra credit, no projects, no papers.
Class is easy. She gets most of her content from Quizlet. If you want an easy A/credit. Take this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Caring--Gives good feedback--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: She is a ridiculously hard grader for no reason. Doesn't offer extra credit.

reviews.comment: I only interacted with her once and it was very awkward, seems as if she doesn't want to interact with students at all. Exams were super easy and discussion posts had controversial topics. Overall pretty boring but an easy A.

This class was definitely not what I thought it was going to be, subject wise. Our classes were asynchronous, which was nice. There were 3 exams and 3 essays, she gives you a week to do them. We had lectures to watch but they never helped for the exam imo. Professor gives feedback but is kinda boring, the class in general was boring tbh

Her criteria for discussions and criteria are very clear. The lecture videos she posted were very clear as well. Read the textbook and readings and you'll be fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Course was based on the textbook and some articles, which were very engaging. The quizzes weren't graded but were great study material for exams. Fair grader, with two assignments due per week and occasional makeup assignments & extra credit. Prerecorded lectures were nice but unnecessary. Just read the things and you'll do fine. She's really nice.

reviews.comment: Her lectures aren't great or very interesting. She uses a powerpoint to list main ideas, but she usually extrapolates the info while talking so pay attention to what she says and write that down. Exams are okay make sure you know your definitions and concepts to a T if you want an A on exams. There are in class assignments so show up to class!
Attendance not really mandatory. Just write 250 words summarizing the readings which are tough to read at times and do your part in group projects and it's an easy A.

Dr. Reed is an excellent instructor and will provide guidance in reading some difficult to understand texts. The readings can be a lot, but the way that she approaches the material and discusses it helps to decipher some of the more complex topics. Very generous in helping improve writing and citation skills. I would definitely recommend.

Professor Reed, is the best teacher you can take because she is very nice and caring when it comes to talking to her and even by her grading. if you do the work and submit it she will give you a 100 on the assignment. No finals for the class just a chat with her of what you liked about the class that was the final and a final group project.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Dr. Reed is an amazing professor! She helped us students prepare for our future writing intensive courses by having us read passages from the book and online articles, write an argument about them, and gives us good advice as well. Thanks to Dr. Reed, I was also able to write my papers well by using her helpful outline guides.
The class consists of discussion boards & written work. The course is a definite must for first year students!
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Inspirational

reviews.comment: Her teaching style is easy to follow. There's a lot of reading and writing, but she'll go over it the next day. She gives a lot of feedback on writing. She answers her emails pretty quickly. She really cares about her students health and well being, mental and physical, so she understands if you need a break. There will be group projects.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: Assigns a LOT of work but teaching style is really engaging and she's really understanding about the workloadwhen people have problems. I really loved the class and I wish some of the other history classes I've taken were as interesting as this one was. All of the readings, while long, were relevant and pretty interesting in their own right.

Dr. Reed is a great professor and very helpful .The workload at the beginning of the semester was crazy (really long readings and too many online discussions). But she is always willing to take her students opinions into consideration and the workload went significantly down. You' ll learn a lot although, at times the material might seem biased.

It takes so much focus and concentration to understand what is being said in the lecture. When he talks it is very boring and lengthy. Sometimes he can talk about something for 20 minutes and I only need to write down about 4 different ideas. Also no guide for what is on the test, a lot of just guessing and using the slides.

(Actually for ANCS 201, but it wasn't listed)

This guy treats teaching like a 9-5 job. He straight up does not care what you do. Anytime I asked him a question, I got a weird answer. He really doesn't want to answer student questions. Content of the class was interesting since I love history, but he's very boring. Not a super hard class though.

the content itself was interesting enough, but the professor was so boring it made engaging with it impossible, and the quizzes and exams were open-note online which was nice but still had some overly specific questions and it was just too difficult to engage with the class, so i wouldnt recommend unless necessary

I know other reviews say he's a good professor and he seems nice.  The reads are easy and fun but the quizzes are insane because he asks for small details and the quizzes are poorly worded, and hyper specific based on one thing he said during the lectures.  Only graded on 5/10 quizzes, midterm, final, and paper.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Really fun class, with lots of reading but not difficult overall. Weekly reading responses always were easy to understand and consisted of 300 words and quizzes weren't confusing. Prof Kapach responds to emails quickly and cares about students. As long as you read, turn things in on time and watch the lectures + take notes you will do great.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: This class is an interesting and fun course. There is a lot of reading that's very interesting and unique. Weekly writing due with a minimum of 300 words, and he grades fairly. His lectures are great and corresponds with the work given. Responds to email quickly and is a wonderful professor. Always looking to help you and provides good feedback.

I found this class genuinely enjoyable. We read a lot but it was balanced and the reading was interesting. We would have weekly reading responses which he graded clearly.  His lectures were to the point and so were the quizzes and exams. You can't fail if you keep up with the course work. He responds to emails quickly and is overall a good prof.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: She was honestly extremely rude and was always sarcastic or would write with such attitude in her emails when I would simply ask for clarification on things. Doesn't seem to care about her students, and is just overall unprofessional I would NOT recommend her.

If you like participating and creative writing, then this prof is for you. Unfortunately, I don't. However, Prof Avagliano is very passionate and the workload is manageable. If you take this class, know that she hates "boring" summaries, so make sure to always answer the "So what? Why do we care?"

Lectures are very engaging and cover interesting topics. I was never good with English but she made it a breeze and something worth remembering. The book choice she had was very interesting rather than just being a typical classic you were required to read in grade school. Coming to class, participating and getting the work done will suffice.

Okay for lectures, but better to take another prof. Annoying grading approach, and treats ENGL 100 like its the most important class to ever exist, at a STEM school. Somewhat lenient with late work. Also beware, At the end she wants a 3-page reflection for basically a high school class about what you, "learned". Good book choice and topics though.
easier than high school English, very engaging teacher, very fun class.

She is an amazing professor. I never really liked English class but she made the class enjoyable enough that I actually looked forward to being there. It is writing heavy but she gives great feedback and if you aren't happy with your writing at the beginning of the semester then you will be at the end. She makes the class engaging and interesting!

Felt as though I learned a great deal however.

reviews.comment: I took micro during 6wks & professor Madhavi was great!She posts everything that u need for the class ahead of time, so youre able to review b4 class. She was always available after lecture to answer any questions & even let you get more practice in lab if needed. As long as u put time aside to study for the class u will do fine. Highly recommend!

reviews.comment: Shes the coolest professor I have ever known. Shes very knowledgeable and very approachable. I wish she teaches me often

STUDY

reviews.comment: Dr. Baek is fantastic at engaging with students through humor and being welcoming. I personally liked this class.

Class could be easy if the professor was clear and engaging. Lectures were beyond boring and I learned more from youtube than the actual lectures. Also never communciated with the TA so grading was horrible and discussion had no value.

Not a fan of his teaching. He is hard to understand and his notes are bad. But he is accessible via email and office hours. I recommend using the library study tools. Exams were p easy, and short. Homework was worth 20% of grade and was super easy. This class is definitely passable. But be weary of missing class bc his notes suck.

PLEASE DO NOT TAKE THIS PROFESSOR. Expect to fail because his lectures make no sense and asking questions is of no help either. The TA assigned is no help either. Please for the love of your GPA and money beware of this Professor Baek. Please ask around to see what professor is better and it will be worth the effort.

Very dry lectures that were hard to follow and often weren't even applicable to the hw. However, he would prepare us well for the quizzes and the hw's being a large part of the grade made things much easier. Don't expect to learn much, but it's very passable. I don't recc taking it if you don't have to take it tho

Never before have I met a more arrogant, inconsiderate professor. 85% of the stuff we went over in class had nothing to do with the quizzes/exams. He was a terrible lecturer. He would put ppl on the spot then laugh when we were confused (which was all the time). Gave out nearly no partial credit on the exam. Avoid if you can.

VERY demotivating unsure what he wants from us. Unsure if we just want to challenge us or wants us to learn. Lecture is not helpful, just practice problems by yourself for tests. rest should be "easy". Doesn't provide a formula sheet for at least the first exam from what I remember, other professors provide them.

- The lethargic manner of speaking by which this professor delivers his lectures will struggle to capture your attention.
- Exams demand cramming a copious quantity of information into your head in a relatively short time prior to test-taking in order to obtain an adequate score for them.
- Professor provides scarce amounts of hands-on material.

Received first exam back w/over 20 people staying after class to discuss. Got answer right on many questions, majority of points taken off. When asking him, he said he "would take more points off if he could've". Avoid.
dropped the first week..
good
He was passionate about the subject and taught it well.

reviews.comment: Homework assignments are difficult but are graded by completion. Quizzes are typically very easy if you have a basic understanding of the concepts covered. Class participation is graded on a poll posted at some point during the lecture. Grading policy is fairly lax with partial credit if you show your work.
Excellent professor! The content was interesting and I gained new information to learn. The grading is very efficient and quick.

reviews.comment: Textbook is a better teacher than he is, and the textbook isn't even a good one. Lectures are difficult to understand. The worst part: No transparency or clarity with grades. Deducts massive amounts of points from exams with no explanation for anything. Exams covered content he said wouldn't be covered. By far the worst prof I've had at UMBC.
The critiques below are way too harsh. He really knows the material clearly very smart and willing to go over material again.

If you have another class that is on top of his office hours, good luck passing he doesnt help beyond that. Although the prerequisite says you dont need to know R programming, you definitely do! He is a harsh grader who doesnt give personal feedback since you can find it in the book. Expect to learn better on your own then with this professor.
His lectures will not help you at all, terrible professor. Does not give any examples of R code during his lectures. Overall the worst professor I've ever had. Do not recommend.

It was his first time teaching stat 355, it wasn't the best his voice makes me want to take a nap. just thinking about it makes me tired. I suggest you take someone else, he is a nice professor and will help you out. But if you don't have time then don't take him. Your exams are your only grade for the most part, no extra credit unless "pop" quiz.

R is a hard language to learn, but he is really understanding and helpful. There is a lot of opportunity for bonus points. Also, there's pop quizzes in class, usually in groups. For the most part they're ok especially if your group is good. Sometimes at the end of the semester he'll give you the quiz credit just for actually showing up to class.
Very kind teacher, not boring if you like the topic, attendance is important and checked on but projects were simple and fairly easy.

I loved Proff Ball. The exams weren't too bad, and there were a few projects and quizzes that helped keep your grade up. The projects were fun, and the quizzes were open-note. I loved this class, and Ball was a great professor. She was engaging and fun and gave a few opportunities for extra credit, which was really helpful.

Professor Ball is amazing! She is very passionate about what she does, and genuinely wanted us to succeed in the class. She explains everything clearly and is very approaching, and the material is not hard to learn nor hard to remember for exams. Quizzes are online at the end of each week, and class engagements for attendance are easy.

very easy class, show up and do the class engagements if you know someone in the class, they can just send it to you before lecture ends and attendance wouldn't be mandatory in that instance, easy lecture slides that she thoroughly explains each class, and is very enthusiastic and keeps you engaged, and easy to remember for the tests!
She's absolutely amazing, she's extremely accommodating, kind, knowledgeable, and so much more! Professor Banks deserves the world! I don't have much more to say.

A genuine and kind professor. She interacts with other students to get to know them better. She's aware of her own identity and ensures to be diligent and respectful when talking about other identities. She's also incredibly passionate in what she does. Thank you for your authenticity and compassion, Dr. Banks!

She is incredible, I would take every social work class with her if I could. Very helpful and sweet, she's so engaging that I forget how early it is when class starts. The best quality a professor could have is passion about what they're teaching, and Dr Banks cares so much about what she does. I see it in every class.

Classes were lecture based but heavily encouraged discussion. She was very sweet and communicative. Great with accomodations. Midterm, final and weekly journals on Blackboard. Highly encourage taking the class.

CMSC 491 Mobile Computing: Surface-level Android. Demos lacked depth, making HW hard & requiring self-teaching. Outdated libraries suggested. Difficult midterm (avg ~50-60%), easier final. Exams seemed AI-generated, testing content not fully covered. Felt professor was disengaged.

Group project of 2 people, a few programming projects, and 2 exams determine your grade. Programming assignments were relatively easy to understand. Introduces outside topics such as cloud computing with its relation to mobile computing.

Took him for Mobile Computing. Challenging but interesting homework assignments. One Midterm, one final project. Provided opportunities for extra credit with in-class assignments, which really helped the students actively learn the concepts as well. Overall, a nice professor who cares about the students learning the material.

Professor Banerjee was thrown into teaching this class last minute and honestly, I feel like he did a great job! He was very kind and knowledgeable, and he was very lenient with his grading. Although the class was disorganized, as a Professor he was great. The only downfall is that he is slow at responding to emails and piazza posts.

Random Lectures. The course is not difficult, he makes it difficult by giving more quantity of assignments and skipping basics. Incomprehensible TA. You will not be able to do any other graduate course work if you take his course.

The professor is well versed with his concepts but badly fails at communication with students. Students have to beg for his time which I found to be utterly disrespectful. I would NEVER recommend a course/project/research under him.

Advanced OS was a great course, packed with new and useful information. Concentrated on distributed and parallel programming. You need some background in programming to keep up. Dr Banerjee is enthusiastic and helpful in teaching it. You will learn a lot in this course.
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: A very helpful professor. Teaches to his lecture slides, but knows the material well. I highly recommend going to his office hours if you have any issues or confusion with lecture material or projects.

Very nice guy and very good instructor. Slides are very helpful and good study tools. Also not unwilling to curve and help your grade. Attendance is required but the lectures really help. The average on the midterm was low so he gave the midterm again as a take-home test with the potential to boost your test grade by upto 20%. Would take again.
Android Development. Tries to cover most of the topics in android. Must take if you want to do a hands on.

Dr. Banerjee uses a examples a lot in lecture, I learned more in his class in one week than I've learned in other classes for the whole year. He's willing to help and really wants you to think about good design for mobile apps.

He is very good and want to help his students not only pass but understand a class as difficult as OS. GO TO CLASS because if you don't his slides are hard to understand without the in-class examples he gives. Overall, he is a nice guy and a very good professor who happens to teach a very difficult subject.

Dr. Banerjee likes to teach using examples and coding demonstrations which is helpful in the exams and homework. The projects are very difficult but are manageable within the time allocated. He likes to give out candy for participation in the class. Outside of class he will do anything to help his students be successful. If possible take his class!

One of the worse IS professor I have taken. This professor has a poor explanation on his lectures. His study guide does not pair with the exact exam, it will be completely different. DO NOT take this professor
The IS420 course, led by Professor Prakash Bandaru, suffered from unclear instructions, especially in the group project, causing confusion and stress. Other than that, all was good.

The lectures are not too long or boring. Grading criteria sometimes isn't too clear so you may lose points. He doesn't give a study guide for the exams which isn't a big deal but this class has a lot of information so it would be appreciated if there was one. Besides that there's a group project just hope your group actually does their work :)
He wants you to succeed and will help you if you need. Very very nice professor

Makes me really sad to write this because this professor is so great but we were cut short by the pandemic. His lectures were SO engaging, I always looked forward to being there. He said this is the last time UMBC is doing 101... Sad... We moved from lecture to just assignments online. If you have the option to take him, do it!

The class is based on 4 exams and one paper. Overall the exam questions were straight from the slides but I preferred to get the textbook to get a better understanding (although you dont need to in order to pass). Pretty easy class if you study the lecture slides well & attendance is not mandatory.

Professor Ozok is an awesome guy. He is extremely passionate and knowledgeable about everything technology. The content is super easy and as long as you glance over the slides you will be perfectly fine. His exam reviews pretty much give you everything you need to know. Take his class, you will not regret it.

Best professor ever! Easy class. Just study the slides and read the textbook. The exams are based off the slides so it's really easy if you actually study. You don't really need to go to class, attendance isn't mandatory! Overall it was the easiest class i've taken so far. LOVE the prof!

Professor Ozok is an awesome professor! He really does know his stuff about computers and enjoys talking about them and teaching them! He also pretty funny when he explains some of the concepts. The class had 3 exams and they are all based off of slides. Beware of semester long project paper. If you are a tech-savy person then this class is easy

He rushes you on exams and he tells the class his exams are easy but in fact they are difficult. I wish he can give more time on exams and that there were other ways to bring your grade up other than his exams.
He rushes you on exams and he tells the class his exams are easy but in fact they are difficult
He has the greatest accent of all time. Most hilarious and nicest professor at UMBC. Definitely wants you to get an A. Take this class yo

Dr. Ozok is the nicest man I've ever met. He's a big nerd, and clearly loves what he teaches. Don't slack off in this class, you have 3 exams, a paper, and lab assignments. The exams are from directly from the powerpoint, or textbook. Lots of material to memorize!

I don't ever recall looking forward in the week for a class, but with this class I did, every week! The instructor is funny, knowledgeable, dynamic and smart. I never thought I would develop an interest in technology, but he made me develop it! Take a class with Professor Ozok and you will know what I'm talking about! It is too much fun...

Ant is an awesome teacher! He's definitely passionate about his area of study and is willing to help students. The class itself is pretty easy. There are 2 very easy labs, which just involve using Microsoft Office, and 3 exams, plus a final exam and a final paper. And he does take attendance
Awesome professor! So engaged and interested in his courses.
DONT TAKE ANYONE ELSE IF YOURE TAKING IS 101!
Prof. Ozok's great knowledge in what he teaches is only eclipsed by his genuine interest in helping his students.

I didn't have much interest in technology before I took this class, I took it only because it fit my schedule, and boy was it the right decision! I got to know and learn basics of technology thanks to this professor, he really has a keen interest in technology and great knowledge! Now I share this interest too and really want to work in computers!
This guy is GOOD!!!

This professor is responsible for my decision in a career in information technology. He knows how to make classes fun, big time. Brings all kinds of examples (hardware, software demos, videos, news, movies, you name it...) to show us the "fun" side of technology. He knows EVERYTHING going on in technology, and is very fair in exams and projects.

Easy class and very straight forward lectures.  Exams are done in class on blackboard, so you get scores back immediately.  Only two actual homework assignments and a paper,as well as 3 (i think) exams.  Easy A if you pay attention and look over notes for a few minutes, but most people just facebook during class. AND HE DOES NOTICE.

Extremely knowledgeable, passionate teacher and researcher. He genuinely cares about students and their success. Treats students with utter respect and plenty of humor. His technical knowledge is so good he answers any technology question with perfection. Very fair in exams and projects, always open to suggestions for improving class. Great person!
Too much busy work, too many assignments due at the same time.

Very friendly and laid back. Class was really easy, especially for an honors class. Material is almost common knowledge if you are interested in computers at all. Multiple choice exams online. He puts sample exams online as well. You shouldn't have a problem getting an A in this class if you turn in assignments and study for exams.
Nice guy.  Easy class.

Cool professor, very kind person. The material is easy if you have some knowledge and still pretty easy if you are a novice. Tests are very fair. With just a little effort, anyone should be fine in this course.
Very cool teacher, brings lots of examples to class to show you what he's talking about.  Class is very easy, and very fair.  He is always willing to help students out who are having trouble.
very chill

Class is easy if you keep up with homework and quizzes and understand the textbook concepts. There's a quiz and homework almost every week, so stay on top of it to avoid dropping below a B. The professor is interactive and caring but can be strict at times. Exams are weighted a hefty amount, so make sure to understand the topics well.

reviews.comment: hard, can come off passive aggressive but all in all does actually care for students' futures, a little so much so that hes a stickler when it comes to grades, curving, ai. when it comes down to it, if you put your best foot forward, he'll meet you where you are, still a very demanding and heavy class.

FYI on the previous review: He DID curve everyone's exam 1 grades AND dropped quizzes so everyone passed with a minimum B. He's tough on homework and work ethic in general but he is fair and he is understanding. He will work with you if things go sideways and gives you plenty of chances to get back up. For ref, I got a low D in the 1st exam.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Test heavy

reviews.comment: He is really really great! The most engaging IS professor I have taken at UMBC. He really genuinely cares about student success and makes a great effort to get to know every student individually despite it being a larger class. Super accommodating, but still encourages everyone to be on top of their work. Highly recommend.
Great professor with very clear study guides. I enjoyed his lectures and would 100% take this class again if I could.

New IS Professor for UMBC, has been great so far, he's a good lecturer and has some energy. Flexible, but has a higher set standard, which makes the class difficulty a bit higher than another professor, but its not really outside of expectation for a college class. Good overall, easy to talk to, good overall for his first class as a Professor.

Professor Beverley is a great Prof, he made IS 310 much easier to understand with clear explanations and a supportive approach. He was friendly, patient, and always willing to help. His passion for teaching created a positive learning environment. Highly recommend

Dr. Bass is a wonderful lecturer and is always open to questions during and after class. RealChem (used for HW and readings) is not the best platform and frustrating to use, but her actual Blackboard course is very well structured. It is easy to fall behind, but she has many opportunities to catch up and clearly cares about student success.

Incredible information accessibility for the course. REAL Chem is a pain to use at times but manageable. Lectures are consistently too fast to take notes effectively, but as long as you review you will be fine. Tons of out of class opportunities, very friendly professors.

reviews.comment:
Chem is very challenging but Dr. Bass does her best to break down complex topics. Her lectures are clear and provide helpful examples, and are thorough without dragging on too long. 

Attendance is not mandatory but gives bonus points (and I'd highly recommend attending). I found the workload of this class to be the most difficult aspect.
dont take lots of work

reviews.comment: she teaches the content more confusing than it needs to be

She's a really good professor. Always answers her emails, her lectures are very good, they give bonus points if you answer pollev questions in lectures, exams are straightforward and REAL chem is super helpful. I reccomend her and would take her class again!

Honestly, Bass wasn't a horrible teacher at all; Chem is just beyond difficult. For a class like this, a more engaging teacher would've been great, but Bass's voice is enchanted with some sort of sleep spell so that wasn't helpful. However, she always made herself availible outside of class, offered plenty of extra credit, and gave us resources.
