reviews.comment: Chemistry is a hard course on its own so I think that a lot of students blame her for that. HOWEVER Dr. Bass is always willing to help and has great lectures - you just need to come prepared and not be lazy. She teaches in a way that carries off the readings and homework which is super helpful - she tells you exactly what you need to do to succeed
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: dr bass is amazing

lecture attendance was extra cred with pollev. lectures were kinda rushed and not the most helpful. realchem textbook/hw was SO annoying. posted multiple old practice exams for every exam except final. second exam brought me to a B. go to SI PASS/other tutoring, helped more than the lectures. loads of extra cred opportunities.
Great professor, you can tell she puts a lot of time and effort into every aspect of the class. The subject is naturally content heavy, so put the hours in outside of class and you'll do just fine.

everything was fine until the final. we were only given 50 minutes to answer all 40 questions which i think was not enough time. i felt so pressured and rushed on most of them and couldn't even go back and check my answers. i also didn't get to answer like the last 5-10 questions even tho i knew how to do them bc of the time;(

For preface, I took CHEM101 last sem w/Carpenter and failed so I had to retake it this sem w/Bass and I gotta say she is SO MUCH better than Carpenter. I'm honestly confused by the bad reviews from this sem bc she's genuinely so lenient, like she gave us sm bonus/extra credit opportunities through PollE, tokens, etc., which Carpenter doesn't do.

If you are a bad test taker you may fail this course. The exams are 60 percent of your grade even if you do well on discussions and homework it's unlikely you will pass. I don't even blame Professor Bass because she is a nice instructor but chem is inherently difficult.
Trust me, it gets worse. Her lecture is bad, and she doesn't know how to teach.
Boring boring boring boring boring, takes all the fun out of chemistry, but keeps all the hard stuff. Nothing is fun about this class, just question after question.

Amazing professor. She was very clear in her lectures, and the tests/homework were over material taught in class. The slides and blackboard course materials were helpful and accessible. Very friendly environment and she is very easy to talk to when needed.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Bass is a decent professor given a poor curriculum. However, her teaching style is overly fast-paced and lacks depth for true understanding. This course is essentially self-paced due to the heavy reliance on readings and homework assignments from the online textbook, while her lectures are just summarized slides from that same textbook.

Bass is super nice and genuine. She doesn't just read off slides, she explains well, with examples. Reading content isn't too heavy, but lots of assignments each week. Her exams were pretty good: they reflected question styles from assignments. Same with the final which is external: her assignments, notes and exams set you up well for the final.

This class is unnecessarily hard for a chemistry 101 class, even when it is required for most majors and your grade is mainly dependent on exams Just know that this class is a lot of self studying and lectures she just reads off the screen.There are extra credit opportunities for 5% bonuses on exams, but doesn't really help since exams are tough.

Bass is a good teacher! Very well-made slides and great explanations. There is a fair amount of homework, but it's not hard so long as you pay attention in class. Pretty generous with extra credit and exams are manageable with studying! If you put in the time and effort you will do well. She provides tons of resources and opportunities to succeed!

Bass is a good teacher! Very well-made slides and great explanations. There is a fair amount of homework, but it's not hard so long as you pay attention in class. Pretty generous with extra credit! and exams are manageable with studying. If you put in the time and effort you will do well. She provides tons of resources and opportunities to succeed!

She puts thought and care into her lectures, and knows the subject very well. There's so many resources to help you- videos, practice problems, office hours, please utilize all of it. She will gladly explain things if you have questions. Anyone can pass this class if they just stay on top of things.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I enjoyed Bass more than Carpenter because of her genuine care and love for chemistry. But, it is hard to do well in this class unless you self-study and enjoy math, because this course is extremely math-heavy. The quizzes are just like the practice problems she gives out.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Professor Bass is great as she takes the time to explain during lecture and will address individual questions. The course is more of the issue. HW and reading quizzes due 3x a week for each. The exams are generally fair and there is extra credit offered but it takes hours to complete. Would recommend to go to Bass over Carpenter for lectures.

Attendance is mandatory because we do polling questions in class that count towards your final grade. There is a bit of work (smth due everyday) but a lot of resources to practice the concepts are provided which are super helpful! She also gives the opportunity of a 5% bonus on each exam if students complete the extra credit assignments :)

Gives way too much homework, flipped classroom approach, her lectures usually consist of her reading off of copy-pasted textbook slides and practice problems that are unnecessarily hard (and grades those problems for accuracy).

Please do not sign up for this professor. She gives absolutely no resources to complete her math heavy work other than these stupid and useless TA's. Before exams, the resources and tutoring is very pitiful and very limited, AND she gives us more homework and quizzes right before the exams. This one class takes up so much time.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The professor gives virtually no feedback and the grading is horrendous. I get zero grades on assignments that I didn't know we had that were not on the syllabus. Exactly what this class wants from me is incredibly unclear and I can't find what I need on blackboard.
reviews.rating_tags: So many papers--Graded by few things--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: I love her so much; she articulates her class effortlessly and is a great human for chem and life. Stay on top of all the readings, and do and redo all hw and all practice problems you can find; If you are unsure of small things, ask because it will make everything else make sense. Her whole setup was incredible to prepare us for everything.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Lots of homework

reviews.comment: took in the fall and got a D, retook this past semester got a C. each unit goes by super fast so stay on top of material/each topic or you WILL fall behind. didn't learn much from her and depended on online videos (she provided a lot of resources tho). each exam covered around 15 units each (3 exams)+cumulative gets math-heavy after first exam.

I have taken CHEM101 with this professor twice now, to say that she mostly relies on tests to make up the final grade would be an understatement. The exams make up 60 percent of your grade in total, so if you are a lousy test taker, you will fail no matter how well you do on the other assignments given throughout the course.

When I originally signed up for this class, plenty of other students granted hearty endorsements to this professor. To my dismay, she decided to run a "flipped classroom" this semester which meant she didn't teach the material in class, just practice. The worst part is the exams, few of the questions are close to the homeworks or practice problems.

The format is reversed, you learn outside of class with lecture videos, and then practice during lecture. About halfway through the semester, it becomes more efficient to just skip lecture and study for exams rather than actually actually show up and do a meager 3-4 practice problems PER class. Respect for Bass though, helping about 300 students.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Caring

reviews.comment: Great professor. Given the sheer size of the class she really does make an effort to help students. Class content is very straightforward and she was great with communicating any changes in assignments. No office hours but she offers other resources. Lecture was mostly practice problems but she explains stuff if you ask her to.

while she's inaccessible outside of class, she does walk around the hall during lecture and is willing to answer your questions during and after class as well! the material is hard so you need to put in effort to get a good grade and she's provided a lot of good resources to help you learn so make sure you can self study and do lots of practice!
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: You'll have to teach yourself but it's more of a problem with how the curriculum is set up than with the professor herself. Pretty good at explaining the problems we do in class, and ended up rounding up my grade which is great.

You have to teach the material yourself by watching the prerecorded videos, practice questions on Aktiv homework(has 3 attempts). Make sure you know the concept and how do the math problems before class because the lecture summarizes what you read & are just extra practice questions. Tests were much more difficult than practice questions we learned

Great professor, difficult class. Exams reflect hw+discussions and there are always more practice problems on aktiv. Read textbook, watch the lectures, attend class- all will help to learn the content. Only hard work+significant effort will result in a good grade, so be prepared for a challenge! Manageable to do BIOL141 at the same time.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Gives good feedback--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: bass explains chemistry concepts eloquently and clearly in lecture, in which attendance is graded. Aktiv homework usually takes 30 min-1hr to finish. on average, exams are moderately difficult. only problem is that bass is inaccessible-she can't have office hours.

I wish UMBC offered another 101 chemistry professor, she is awful. she taught nothing during lectures it was just 50 minutes of solving problems even if you did not understand it. her 4 exams were completely different from the practice which makes no sense. she overcomplicates exams questions and makes a 101 class so hard.

Don't listen to the people who have given low rating's. They're just a bunch of freshman complaining, that think college is going to be easy like high school. Dr. Bass is an amazing professor whose caring but her class is very hard and requires you to be focused and do all your required work and assignments on time. Also STUDY hard before exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: She doesn't teach at all, whatsoever. You have to teach yourself and then go to lecture so you can get participation points. And all you do in lecture, is complete participation points. Why are we all wasting our time in class and outside of class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Nice and caring teacher. But, it doesn't make up for the lack of "teaching". Entirely way too uptight for a level 100 class where we don't actually learn anything. You have to teach yourself all the material. Most of the test questions contain problems that weren't even reviewed in class, the textbook, or homework. Mentally draining class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Caring instructor. But with the number of students in CHEM101, there isn't much she can do for individual students. Lots of homework, and online tests that are all or nothing for points. Flipped classroom means a lot of time will be spent outside of class. Lectures were mainly there for practice.

Changed in-class participation to require attendance codes and discussion got changed from being online to paper on the 10th week of the semester. Very uptight for a 100 level class. Annoying. Lots of work. Reverse learning style; you learn the material yourself anyways so there is no incentive to attend class other than a few example problems.

There are four online exams and 1 cumulative in person exam, with 2-3 homework's and reading quizzes a week. She expects you to be familiar with the class content before class; lecture is treated as a review and polling questions are used to apply that knowledge and practice the material. LA's help in discussion, ask questions!

Dr. Bass is an amazing and kind professor. Be ready to work with people in lectures to answer clicker questions. There are graded on correctness, but that is about all that is stressful in the class. She goes over material very well, and is very approachable and accessible after and outside of lectures.

I got the opportunity to see Dr. Bass in person, even though this class is online and she is very nice. She genuinely cares about whether you pass, and will offer you solutions to help you succeed in the course. Dr. Bass tries to do her best to provide plenty of practice problems. 
The LCPs can be stressful, SI Pass can help with that. 
Good luck!

Professor Bass is an incredible Professor! She really cares about how well her students perform, and provides so many resources for help and extra practice, which I found really helpful! The only downside is that the lectures were online, but despite that I found Chem Talk to be very useful.

I had her when the exams and lectures were online and discussion was initially in person but they allow us to call in. Never met her, but she was very clear and good at explaining during chem chats. Exams matched the homework questions. Should be easy if you know how to take notes

I took this class twice and know professor Bass wants her students to succeed. Although the material is hard at times, it's easy to pass her exams as long as you read the chapters & go to lectures. The discovery isn't helpful & some exam questions aren't ones that are gone over in lecture. She's always available for questions and helping students.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: I was explaining that as a matter of a few seconds ago: almost two and a half months into the semester, I am keeping track of my grade on blackboard and what I thought was an A dropped to a merely but futile C. I think that is quite the drastic change, and simply just unacceptable and inexcusable. Seriously!? What kind of professor pulls this?!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: What really sucks is for one; how the learning checkpoints are constructed. It truly sets limitations on what can be accomplished in the class efficiently. Secondly, you know how normally a class, when your grade is posted on blackboard, the fraction that is next the the 'My Grade' panel, is actually your grade? Well surprise! It's not.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Worst professor I've taken. CHEM talks were not at all helpful. Lasted at least 30 mins and didn't cover all subjects for the LCPS (exams). Problems on the exams are harder than the homeworks. I've attended tutoring sessions, chem talks, etc. and still got a C in this class. Only take it AT YOUR RISK. She's nice, but I wouldn't recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Test heavy--Beware of pop quizzes--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Dr. Bass gives a lot of chances to make up for the quizzes with the crazy amount of extra credit she gave out. The final was very simple and sometimes she would even throw in a free point here and there in the quizzes. My grade went from a D to a B because of all the extra credit and the final. She also responds to emails very quickly.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Not a lot is required in this class but you need to do a lot of work to pass. It's a tough topic and I think Dr. Bass does a great job of teaching it. She takes time to go over specific questions and gives extra practice and plenty of resources to do well. I would highly recommend attending every Chem Talk you can.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Amazing, down-to-earth professors! Always took the time to explain any questions we had and grading for all assignments was clear. Her lectures were really interesting and helpful and responded fast to emails. Offered extra credit opportunities and really treats you like a human being which is a breath of fresh air :)

If you suck at tests, you're screwed. The 5 exams and then the final are pretty much all that matter. I did horrible for the first few but my grade was saved because I did amazing on the last few and the final (which replaced your lowest exam grade). The chem talks were such a snoozefest and the homeworks were the most helpful in my opinion.

Chemistry isn't my strong suit, but thankfully in Dr. Bass's class you get several learning options that are not mandatory: lectures where you can ask chat questions, learning module videos you can go over and over again, textbooks, teaching assistants (?) who run tutoring sessions, and finally groups of peers you get broken into. Really nice lady

Dr. Bass is truly an amazing person. As a professor, she's okay; I think if the class wasn't online, it would be better. She is approachable and never makes you feel like you're not learning. She knows what is best for the class and goes with that. Plus the CHEM 101 Homework app is amazing and actually makes learning chemistry a lot easier.

Chem 101 was taught by 3 professors (Bass, Hamilton, Carpenter). Dr. Bass is very kind and approachable. Her lectures (CHEM Talk) were practice problems (notes taken ahead of time). Questions about content or tests could be asked on discussion board and answered quickly. Workload was decent but manageable. Answered all questions asked in class

Terrible teacher. Learned nothing from her and shes gives very little time for the exam. 30 minutes we section is fine for the first few exams but should not apply to the multiple step math based problems. Will NEVER recommend her to ANYONE EVER.

Her lectures are not at all helpful (online) and her Chemtalks aren't that useful either. She goes over incredibly easy problems and the hw problems are easy also, but then when you go to take the LCP(exams) they are HARD! I find her to be extremely confusing and I feel like she's genuinely not a quality teacher.
For the ones who are saying CHEM101 is difficult, its not if you read the textbook, do your homework and pay attention to her chem chats. You guys just like to complain when you put no effort in.
She taught chem as best she could. Do not rely on her to follow her own syllabus mainly her grading rubric. she completely nulled out any extra credit I earned and refused to bump up my 89.4.

Dr. Bass is very nice but being nice doesnt make a good instructor. The discussion groups werent useful for learning due to other students wanting to rush and people Not working together cohesively. Dr. Bass also teaches concepts and learning strategies which is fine but they arent useful for the quizzes which make up most of the grade.

Dr. Bass is nice but I wouldnt take her again unless she was my last option. She focused a lot on cheating instead of teaching and went through so much effort to keep an online class from cheating that she made a lot of mistakes on the quizzes she created. She and Dr. Hamilton created their own periodic table which caused more confusion.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Took Professor Carpenter's CHEM101 class and failed. Took Professor Bass's class and got a B. 10/10 recommend taking Professor Bass's class. She is the best!

Classes started as synchronous, but switched to asynchronous halfway through. We went from having group discussions/labs to doing them completely by ourselves. We were told to talk to our fellow classmates which wasnt very helpful when were all trying to learn new material. Lectures were essentially YouTube videos, but with less explanation.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Listen up, chem 101 can be very challenging especially in this pandemic but Dr Bass was such a great teacher! If you truly go to chem talks and si pass review sessions you will find it is doable! She is very supportive and cares about all her students. One of the best Professor hands down.

Dr. Bass was honestly super considerate despite the panoramic. I have never taken chemistry before so this class was insanely difficult for me, but with enough practice problems, taking notes from lectures and the book, and going over practice exams and her 3x a week "Chem Talks" I was able to do well. + She gave extra credit, practice exams, etc.

Chem 101 was definitely hard but Dr. Bass gave you everything you needed to do well. The chem talks, discussion board, CHEM101 assignments and the discovery all help you for the exam. The practice exams is near identical to the real exams and she tests on application not just facts. Overall a great teacher 10/10!

Dr. Bass is excellent. You can tell she's very passionate about chemistry & genuinely enjoys working with students. She was very accommodating for online school. She extended deadlines, gave EC & dropped low test scores for us. That being said, you still have to work for your grade. Do your homework, study for tests, go to CHEM Talk! She's great!!
Chem is not an easy class but she made this so bearable for students! She was very transparent with us and made sure that we were successful in this class!
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: This class was by no means easy but it was clear that Dr. Bass cared about her students' success, even though there were 700+ of us. It was easy enough to get questions answered through the discussion board and/or during "chem talks", which were optional review sessions she held three times a week. Workload wasn't too bad and the tests were fair.

Absolutely Amazing. Accessible anytime. In fall 2020, lectures were pre-recorded due to 727 students being in the class. Prof Bass made the best out of it by having "chem talks" 3 days a week, on the topic of the homework that is due that night. HW is due MWF weekly, but is on Chem101 app/website and not overly hard. Very organized as well.

I had more mental breakdowns than I've ever had during my undergrad, and I'll been in college for four years. Most tutors are terrible, don't listen to any of them. But Prof. Bass makes you work hard for the class through hard work, so do those practice problems!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Super organized and straight to the point. Everything prepares you for the exam

She's a really cool prof. While she wasn't our original professor, she was able to take charge of the class while still ensuring that we were learning despite having two courseloads. Her lectures were information and easy to understand and she's a very nice person who cares about her students.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Pre-corona, she was wonderful! She took the class's feedback, helped us understand the material, cheered us on, listened to us. It made the class easier. Post-corona, she knew it was hard but she also adapted! Yes, the material got harder, but she was accommodating and became a lil more lenient with assignments so that we could learn it thoroughly.
Overall pretty good prof. She gives lots of extra materials to help students. She does not round up. Was stuck with a 89.7 (B). An average professor but very organized.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: The Chemistry Department at UMBC is phenomenal, with people like Prof. Bass here. Her lectures are kept short but straight-to-the-point, and the assignments help us better prepare for the exams better. On top of that, she is extremely generous with extra credit; she basically does not want to see you fail. I would definitely take her class again.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Dr. Bass is amazing. In a class of 300, she actually cares about each individual and wants everyone to do well in the class. She offered extra credit for every exam and she was available for office hours and other out of class help. She even had occasional sessions on Friday's for extra help as well as online office hours.

Dr. Bass saved my grade in CHEM 300. She teaches the lab half in the Fall. The lab sucks and will take a huge chunk of time but is the really easy juxtaposition to the terrible class. She really cares about her students and even tried to help us rectify our problems with the lecture. Go to her office if you have ANY question and you'll be fine.

I had to take this class for my psych B.S. and it was painful. Dr. Bass is nice, but I feel like she would be better if she actually taught instead of giving clicker questions the entire time. The course demands more than your time and money, but your soul. Worship your textbook. Overall, not awful, but would not want her as my professor again.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: CHEM101 has a terrible reputation due to Carpenter. But Dr. Bass is a gem and really cares about her students. She engages with any student with difficulty and thoroughly explains the content. I enjoyed her this summer session. Im bummed she wont be teaching 102!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--Caring

reviews.comment: Chem101 is an extremely difficult course. Now that Bass has completely taken it over, it has improved. Although difficult, it is possible to pass, just be prepared to dedicate your semester to this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: tries to get by on smiles. students like her regardless of how much they hate the class. I don't get it. She IS the course guys. Horrible materials and very mandatory. Nothing but graded HW and quizzes. A true weeder course. "there will be no curve!" then when 40% pass.... ok curve. Chem dept. step back and look at yourself. Miserable

CHEM101 at UMBC is notoriously a very challenging course, but taking it with Sarah Bass was actually somewhat enjoyable. The course is naturally pretty work heavy, between two different online components, additional practice problems, and very tough exams, but you can always go to Bass for help. Overall, take Bass over anyone else.

Bass SERIOUSLY cares for students. If it were her class exclusively, I think more would pass. Her rep is lowered due to Carpenter. Bass helped me with the course but also w/ IRL issues, and had lots of hope in my ability to improve. This is an extremely rigorous course, and while things can be improved (+I failed), she makes it a bit more bearable.

Test heavy. Studied super hard still didn't get good test grades. Not Bass's fault. Dr. Carpenter makes the tests and it is definitely not a 101 level course. Dr. Bass is super nice and cares but it's the tests that count. Despite years of student complaints, UMBC does not care enough to figure out what is wrong with the CHEM 101 and 102 class.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: The course is very rigorous and demanding as it is but Dr. Bass really cares for all of the students and her office hours are great as she is very friendly and explains things thoroughly. If you don't understand a problem, she will go over it and provides many resources and opportunities to get help. Just make sure to do the ALEKS and don't rush!
Her exams are considerably easier than Carpenter's. Know that she's more than willing to help both inside and outside of class. She's more approachable and cares about her students.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Caring

reviews.comment: She hardly lectures. You expected to know a lot on your own. Discussion seems useless too . Bottom line, expect to do lot of work on your own, which is fine, but if you are not going to lecture in class then it defeats the purpose of going to class . Way too much material for 101 level, way more complicated than needs to be. regret taking it.

Her lectures are garbage, but graded. You don't leave with any more information than you entered with. She presents problems, and you know them or you don't. They aren't gone over, at least to any depth. Must be trying a different teaching method than in the past. The other reviews do not match my or my classmates experiences.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: Chooses not to lecture in favor of just doing in class quizzes. Caring maybe, but its an online course with mandatory graded attendance. Tons of at home work. little in class lecture.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES

reviews.comment: She is very nice and easy to follow. She thoroughly explains the examples in class and answers questions. I highly reccommend her. In CHEM101/CHEM102: She does NOT write the exams. The exams are poorly written as some questions are above and beyond the skill level that the book has prepped us for other questions are on target.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Would take again

reviews.comment: A really great professor! Explains the concepts really well. Although, the exams are extremelyyyyy difficult. You really have to work extra hard to know beyond the concepts. Plenty of trick questions, so be sure to read carefully, you will have plenty of time during exams.
Bass is great. She cares about her students, she explains well, Carpenter is ruining Bass's reputation.

Very nice, very smart, and cares about her students. However, she makes the exams MUCH harder than they should be for a 100 level class that most freshman have to take even if they aren't majoring in anything remotely related to chemistry.

Professor Bass is a very kind and intelligent teacher. She cares whether or not we understand the concepts, even though there are 300 of us in a class. However, the Chem 101 exams are extremely difficult. If you want to pass, you must attend all mandatory classes, stay on top of reading, and do practice problems.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring

reviews.comment: This professor's AMAZING. I loved going to his lectures. If you want to succeed: sit in class, listen carefully(he explains to you like ur a baby), and jot down the few notes he mentions that aren't in presentation. For exams, write EVERYTHING on a cheat sheet in small font (like he advises) and you'll be set. By far, my favorite professor at UMBC.
if ur atheist, pick a religion and start praying cause those tests are not easy

His exams are by far the most annoying exams I have ever taken in my life. He tests you on stuff he says in class. Not even application or anything. Actually before an exam, I would pray to die coming to school. I had Feezer and her exams were 100% easier.

THIS GUY! Dr. Lohr is an asset to UMBC - I learned so much in animal behavior (480) and his exams are exactly what he teaches - no tricks. In all seriousness he was 100% in the running for my favorite professor at UMBC - he is caring, respectful, and actually teaches you in a way that is fun and interesting. 10/10 recommend if you need a 400 level.

The wording on his exams isnt the best. He tests a lot from the lectures and minutia of things he says. Relying solely on the allowed cheat sheets will not get you good grades but he also tests largely on topics he spent the most time on. He is passionate about biology and very happy to help students during his office hours.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The only thing going for Dr. Lohr is that he is very approachable. Otherwise his lectures were kind of boring, though the concepts were fairly clear. The exams which counted for 60% of the grade, had almost nothing to do with the lectures. Each exam felt like Trivial Pursuit. the homework was virtually nonexistent but the discussions were horrible.
reviews.rating_tags: Test heavy--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Dr. Lohr is a great professor, extremely knowlegable and gives very interesting lectures. He is however a really tough grader, my class had a 60% average for the first exam and the top grade for class presentations was a 95% (no 100%). This aside, I do not at all regret taking his class as I have learned so much more than any other bio courses.

Dr Lohr made it remarkably easy to pay attention during his classes. He's an excellent teacher, gives fantastic explanations and encourages discussion. Outside of class hours he remained approachable and patient. He designed assignments to test our understanding and communication in a wide range of relevant topics.

His lectures are well prepared and he is one of the knowledgeable professors Ive had at UMBC. I recommend listen to his lectures in class and try to understand and if you can record and listen to take notes later it would be really good. His tests are not easy, but if you study well and understand, A is not that hard. I recommend him as a logical p

Dr. Lohr is very knowledgeable, and his lectures are crystal clear. However, he covers material at lightening speeds, so be sure to record every lecture. The tests he gives don't test on the important concepts and tend to ask for unimportant details of the text. Also he LOVES asking questions on hormones.

This guy is really knowledgeable and he is very clear when describing concepts and answering questions.  Unfortunately, his voice kind of drones and puts me to sleep.  His exams are a little difficult, but fair and there is still a large curve.
He alright. He is the only teacher for 305 who is articulate. What he says in class is mostly from the book but he goes by pretty fast. Gentle and mostly expressionless. Easy on the eyes though! :)

very clear and easy to follow lectures, 12 homework assignments graded on completion with 1 extra credit assignment, exams were tough but I'm also not a good exam taker but if you attend lectures, take notes as they are written on the board, it should be easy.

Attend lectures, take notes, do problem sets the moment the day they are assigned so the material is fresh in your mind. Both exams have 11 multiple choice and 2 long questions based on the problem sets and lecture notes. Final was cumulative, 21 multiple choice and 2 long questions

Attend the lecture, ask questions, and visit office hours. If you do all of those, it's an easy A. He grades on completion, which means you get full credit for everything. 

12 Problem Sets 
2 Exams 
1 Final Exam
He truly cares about his students. Doesn't give an easy A, but it's not unreasonable either. He takes notes on the board during each lecture so taking notes are super easy.

This might be the best professor I have ever gotten, he was so clear during lectures, which made his lectures very important but also interesting, however the tests were a bit hard but if you go to lectures and take notes its an east A

Professor Berkes is superb! This class was highly theoretical, featuring concepts about the urban economy and how cities exist. Only 6 homeworks, graded for completion, and one easy presentation. Engaging lectures. Two exams worth 50%, easy if you studied notes and homework. This course may implement code in the future. Professor is very caring.

I took this Fall 2023. He was great! He is great at explaining concepts and if you have questions, he will do his absolute best to answer them. As long as you attend and pay attention, you'll be perfectly fine. Most of the work is weekly homework assignments based on the lecture materials and the exams. Just take notes and pay attention!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He's a bit dry, but he'll go through the concepts thoroughly. He'll try his best to make things clear to you if you let him know you're confused. There are a good amount of practice problems every week, graded by effort, but it's for your benefit. The exam questions are similar, so if you keep up with the work, you'll do great in the class

Professor Berkes, knew what he was talking about. There are 12 homework assignments graded by participation, 2 midterms and 1 final. If you fail the first two midterms, good luck. This class really requires you to study on your own and memorize the terms. (There are a lot). There's also no extra credit offered. It helps to go to office hours.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Sousedik is a rlly easy grader. Homework, quizzes, and exams are easy A's if you remotely understand the content. Also has a lot of quiz/hw drops. Love this guy, but if you depend on lectures for learning, do not take with diff eq with him. His lectures are boring and his explanations make things seem harder than they are. I recommend tho

The lectures consisted of him just writing the exact example problems that could be found in the textbook. He would teach with his back to the students for the entire lecture, missing students' questions unless they vocally interrupted him. I absolutely do not recommend taking him for 225 there are definitely better professors.

Great professor. You can tell he cares about his students. His lectures consist mostly of problems. So, you will have to do reading on your own to understand some concepts, but the concepts in 225 aren't too difficult to grasp.

Hardest 225 prof @ UMBC but you can tell he cares. Grading dist is rough asf tho and the exams (esp Exam 1 and the Final) were more difficult than they needed to be. He also just copied from the book so there's that.

Sousedik has a pretty dry and quiet delivery at lectures, but he seems to genuinely care about his students' success and encourages to work in groups on hw and to see him in office hours. Sit near the front, read the textbook, STUDY THE HW QUESTIONS for exams (some were copied almost exactly for the midterms and finals), and you'll be fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Terrible, unorganized, doesn't know what he is doing with 50 "uhmm's" each lecture. He did so poorly with teaching that the average student in our class is failing. It is so bad he had to drop A WHOLE EXAM out of the 3 we have! I had to teach my self calc 3 with the book and videos. Hopeless and useless, VERY surprised UMBC hired him for Calc 3.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Extremely difficult to follow lectures. His teaching style is to point at pre-written notes and just say the steps of the notes. Doesnt explain things well and is all over the place with his notes and explanations. Tests and quizzes can be very hard. He stated the tests would be based off the quizzes and homework, but they were nothing like it.
He's a sweet guy, but hes quiet you should sit in the from to hear. Homework is roughly 20%.
reviews.rating_tags: ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Clear grading criteria--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: There is homework, two tests, and a final. His grading on exam is a little rough. Going to class will help, but I had friends who passed and never went. He a sweet guy but you can't hear him if you don't sit in the front of the class.
reviews.rating_tags: ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Clear grading criteria--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: This class was pretty easy. The final grades are very dependent upon exam grades though. Tests aren't too hard; all the problems are straight from the book. Make sure to do homework and practice before exams. He is very quiet, so if you actually want to hear what he's saying make sure to sit in the very front row.

Dr. B is a pretty good teacher but he's quiet. IF you can hear him/understand him, youre golden, but its hard to ask him questions since he gets wrapped up in his lesson. THE BOOK IS YOUR BEST FRIEND. know how to do these problems then your tests should look 80 itll just come down to practice. Lecture is optional but id suggest it. hes a sweet guy

His first semester teaching. Lectures might not be too clear, but read the book and you'll get it. Notes straight from textbook. Attendance - not necessary. He assigns hw weekly and often uses these questions on exams. Exams are straight from the book practice all questions and get an A. Very helpful in office hrs. Sweet guy.
Dr. Sousedik teaches straight out of the book. You really don't have to show up. It's tough though because you only have homeworks and tests. He's a nice guy though.
An easy A if you put in the work. Just finish everything on time. Instructions for assignments are on the syllabus and professor can be reached by email.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: One of the best professors that I have had at UMBC. Wants to get to know you and to succeed in his class. People who end up failing this class are the ones who do not show up to class, it is mandatory!

Professor Beverley is a great instructor! He made ENGL393 much easier to understand with clear explanations and a supportive approach. He was friendly, patient, and always willing to help. His passion for teaching created a positive learning environment. Highly recommend!

SPCH100: Three in-person speeches total. Readings from two books were assigned but not necessary to read and we didn't really talk about them. Laid back class, great practice for public speaking. Don't read from a script, be natural and know your topic. He likes chatting with students about anything from sports to local politics.

Professor Bennett cares about his students. He is kind and understanding. His work is relatively easy, just make sure to do them. We had several papers to do, but nothing we couldn't write about. It was honestly fun. If you need help, ask. He encourages us to ask if we wanted him to proofread or look at our papers and group assignments.

Professor Bennett's class was indeed probably the best class I've ever taken here so far honestly!!!
he is so kind and really care about his students. The course itself is a bit hard but he made it fun and uncomplicated. He is really one of the best! and I would take him again if he is offering any other 300 level courses. Bless him!!!!

Pretty good professor, I just found his lectures to be kind of dragged out and boring (sucked because attendance is mandatory). Couple of biweekly essays, one 10-page essay, and a group project, which is really not bad at all for a technical writing course. He's a very lenient grader and very responsive. Only con is he takes forever to grade.

Professor Bennett's class was probably the best class I've ever taken here. He is very generous when it comes to due dates and wants everyone to get an A. I don't know why everyone is saying the mandatory attendance sucks because it was probably the only class I wanted to attend. The writing can be too much but it's a writing intensive course!
Great professor and overall chill class, just a few papers and a group project. Attendance was sadly mandatory, but show up, do the work, and its an easy A.

Prof Bennett is the coolest prof I've ever had. It is a writing intensive class, so there will be weekly writing assignments. As long as you communicate with the prof and your group and do your work, you will get an easy A.

Professor Bennet is a solid teacher as long as you are fine with mandatory attendance and semi-engaging lectures. He is clear with grading standards and easy to communicate with. He can be a bit stubborn if you want to use software he doesn't know, but can be swayed as long as you deliver good results. I found his class very enjoyable.
one of the best teachers I've had at UMBC. Cares about your work and wants you to become a better writer. Lectures mandatory and kinda long but he makes them go by quickly. take him for eng.

Professor Bennett was really fun and helpful. You'll do quite a few writing but he will not penalize your grade if you are present in every class, doing all assignment on time and participating as he expects you to. He gives you a feedback and let you submit revision as Final portfolio. Its an easy A class if you do all your work and show up.

Professor Bennett is amazing. If you are looking for a relatively easy writing intensive, this is the class for you! The only thing I do have to say is that there were alot of class presentations. Otherwise, if you participate and turn in your assignments, you are guaranteed an A.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: One of the worst profs at UMBC. I can safely say I learned nothing in his class. I doubt if he even reads the papers that he grades. On the bright side, show up, do all the assignments, and you're practically guaranteed an A.  BEWARE! If you miss more than 3 classes (excused or unexcused) you'll lose 10% off your final grade for each class missed.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: One of my favorite teachers. Lots of papers because its a writing intensive courses. Your grades are based on your final portfolio. Just do everything and attend class and you will most likely get an A. The group project you need to go out and get a real client for. Make sure your group members are not lazy or just do all the work that's what I did

NO LECTURE. Class is once a week. Very few class work and/ or homework. Almost everything is group work during the semester. So pick your group members wisely. you have to write a 10-15 page research paper and it is due last day of class. He barely returns graded papers and doesn't post grade. Show up, do your work and get A
Great professor. I had no idea what was going on in the class but I wrote  the papers and showed up to class and got an A.

No exams, didn't discuss grading policy but I am confident that everyone will pass that attended class on a regular basis. Communicate effectively, and turn in all assignments and you should be perfect.

LOTS of writing. you either get A, B or you Fail. just do everything assigned, and you will get A. Attendance is important. very nice professor, sometimes running late. There's no grading system in his class, but he will have a midterm analysis to tell you how you're doing in the class.  Very picky and has his own style that you must follow.
Most of the grade is based on writing and exams and the rest on some presentations. It wasn't so difficult, but wasn't easy either

Prof Ryan is a great professor. All of his grading criteria is highlighted in the syllabus. As long as you read that carefully, you should have no trouble getting a good grade. His exams are also not very complex if you read the book and pay attention to the study guides. Also, his lectures are easy to understand and well planned.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--So many papers--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Had Professor Ryan for my IS300 Summer I session. 6 week compact course...you have to make sure you're on top of your assignments, or else you will fall behind fast. But very doable! Just show up to class, participate in the small group projects, and you should be fine. Tough grader and it's hard to get 100 percent on assignments. But also fair!

i had prof. ryan for both IS 300 and 369. both are writing intensive but it's easy material. the exams in 300 were a little difficult but in 369, there is no exam. prof. ryan is so sweet and funny. he provides good feedback on assignments but he does not allow late submissions. he gives class time to complete assignments which is helpful.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: There are 3 presentations, a few writing assignments, and 3 online quizzes. He is a tough grader, but he likes when you write more and go into good detail. He's pretty lenient with due dates if its a day or two late. This class is significantly easier than the other English WI class. Bill is a good professor and gives good feedback.

Professor Ryan is solid when it comes to teaching the material, and he clearly is passionate about this field. The only problem I would say is that his BB has about 200 random folders, which makes finding assignments very confusing and difficult. He is sort of a tough grader when it comes to the writing assignments as well. mid prof

Great professor! There is 4 article reviews, 4 respondus home exams, and a group project. The article reviews you should write a lot. He is strict on the grades for these cause he wants in-depth stuff. Just write more than you think. The exams were straightforward and he did an exam review in class which is VERY similar to the exam. listen to it.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Test heavy

reviews.comment: IS 300: Prof Ryan was OK. You start getting used to the class by the time it's almost over. There's group work, article reviews, and exams with pretty good study guides. Just put forth a good effort, and a B is certainly possible. Online exams w/ lockdown browser. Attendance was taken every class, that counts towards a participation grade.

Prof. Ryan is a good professor if youd rather read the textbook. Lectures arent mandatory and most of the exam content is stuff from the book. Id recommend just reading the textbook and memorizing the vocabulary for exams. MAKE SURE YOU ASK WHAT HE WANTS FOR PROJECTS. Not a hard grader, just turn in all the work.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Accessible outside class--Group projects

reviews.comment: Class is easy; you are allowed to have 1 sheet of notes for exams. There are a lot of E.C. for each exam.  Lectures aren't usually boring, and Birger is a very nice and caring professor.
Professor Birger was a very kind and accommodating professor. I would recommend taking her courses!

Professor Katie is an amazing professor and I enjoyed all her lectures. the exam questions are based on the study guides she gives and you are allowed to bring a cheat sheet. Overall she teacher why well

This is one of the best professors on campus and I've only been here a semester. She's so understanding and so easy to talk to! She's approachable and so sweet.Assignments don't have hard deadlines just turn it in before the exam.She's doesn't take attendance but don't take that to your advantage because you will miss alot. All exams are open note!

Had this professor for PBHL 100 and PBHL 340, and I enjoyed both classes. 
- Both classes had open-note tests on paper, interactive modules, and in-class activities. 
- 100 had case studies that weren't that hard, and weekly quizzes. 
- 340 had an end-of-semester project with plenty of class time to work on it and two papers.

she is so sweet and amazing during lectures there are group assignments during class, which was ok bc u can also work by yourself but we don't know when we will be having them soo just attend everyday. also extra credit is granted for exams only i believe!

Amazing Professor, very clear and easy to understand requirements. Works with students and not against them, very understanding of circumstances. Explains concepts and assignments in great clarity, and provides feedback on assignments. Somewhat writing intensive, however well worth it if going into a public health focused pathway.
Best professor ever. that's all. taker her class for an easy A

Professor Birger was amazing, her class was fun and interactive. Her assignments and tests are easy if you read the book and look through her slides. Show up to class! She does random in class assignments and the grade for those add up!

She is very sweet and easy to follow in her lectures. It's important to complete the assignments and read the textbook so you don't get lost during class. Her lectures support the assignments and they're connected. She uses examples real-world examples during class to make it more relatable for students.
The best. Tests are open note/open book. Extra Credit opportuinities if needed. Great professor. You'll never be confused in her class

To me, her class was kind of boring. I didn't understand any material in that class but I somehow passed that's all I care about. Exams are open notes and the lectures are always posted on the blackboard. But if you go to class somedays she'll randomly do group participation stuff on google docs. She also posts  exam study guide and that helps too.

Professor Birger's lectures are interesting & informative. The tests are open notes plus EC options. The case studies are probably the hardest part, but not too bad; they just require extra reading and some thinking. I can't remember if attendance is required, but go to get notes for the test, as that is where most answers come from.
awesome professor, easy class IF u find public health interesting and are ready to write case studies almost every other week.

Professor Birger is the best professor I have had so far at UMBC. She is clear and concise and it is obvious that she is an expert on what she teaches. I have so much respect for her because of how much she has taught me in just one semester. She is truly just so knowledgeable and so good at teaching and her lectures are so interesting as well.
for a 100 level class there is a lot of work! she's nice but till a lot of work and kinda fast. easy to get lost! Quizzes are online!

Prof Birger was so kind and wants every student to succeed. Exams are straightforward and open note. Information was interesting and I learned a lot through her lectures. Only con is she doesn't respond to emails and takes a bit to grade but nonetheless she's great. Allows you to redo assignments within a timeframe making it easy to get an A.

Professor Birger is really sweet. Sometimes lectures drag on because she really likes to talk, but you will do well in the class as long as you review her slides for the exam and ask questions you cannot answer for yourself on the study guide. She is a great resource and mentor in continuing your college experience if you are Public Health major.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Birger is so nice and easy to approach, and her lectures are interesting and engaging. I took the class for my major, but PBHL100 with her seems to be a good choice for a GEP. There is a final paper, but if you space the work out over the semester it's definitely doable. I will be looking for more classes to take with her !!
Great professor lets you use notes on exams and is very easy on grading. She really cares about teaching and if you pay attention it is easy to pass.

due dates for everything/organized. allows as many notes as you want for exams. very lenient with turning in assignments, gives good amount of time for them (2-4 due each week). there's a final paper (5-8 pgs req) but gives whole semester to do it. heavy-ish writing intensive course. lectures were eh but she's a great professor!

Such a good professor!! I really enjoyed being in her class and she was flexible with you when it comes to turning assignments in late. She is very understanding and cares for her students. There are a lot of group activities so make sure you attend class. She let us join the class through bb collaborate even though it was an in person class.

Very nice and will let you turn things in past deadline, quizzes and modules are easy, finals are harder and you are not given enough time to complete them so work fast, lectures are really boring, class is only an easy a if you pay attention to lecture, nice grader, class seems hard at first but will get easier, so dont feel overwhelmed

Professor Birger is one of the best! She genuinely cares about her students and wants them to succeed. The first part of this class was a little challenging for me, but it got easier throughout. Will take her again for my upper level PBHL classes.

The sweetest and best professor I've ever had in my three years of college. She's clearly very passionate about her job and she tries to relate to students. She's very understanding and flexible with due dates and I wish I could take all my HAPP courses with her. She deserves a raise. The type of professor they all should aspire to be.

Honestly is one of my favorite professors on campus, she is the reason I decided to switch to a HAPP major. Just do your study guide and youll pass her exam everytime, her final is a retake of one of your exams ( i had her pre covid though)
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: This was the worst class that I have ever taken if your are not planning on going into the health field don't take this it is way too much to work for an elective all these people that give a good rating to this class are try hards who trying to get into the health field do not take this as an elective you will fail.

A lot of professors at UMBC won't budge their grading policies, even in the wake of a pandemic that's forced us to drastically change the way we live and learn. But Katie really understands and cares. Deadlines were not strictly enforced at all and she was always willing to give feedback if you needed it. I'd definitely take her again if I could.

Katie is the best HAPP prof at UMBC. She really cares about our success and comfort. HAPP100 content is easy, but sometimes questions on exams. can be tricky. HAPP340 has no textbook, and assignments are super easy. I had both these during corona, and she was so understanding, never gave us strict due dates, and sometimes extended exam time. BEST!!

honestly my favorite HAPP teacher so far. Class is extremely easy, the reading quizzes dont count as a grade , the writing you unlock from getting a 80% or higher on the reading quizzes is what counts for a grade. unit test is amazingly easy, final is choose one of the 3 to retake. boring lecture but extremely easy, take notes in class, very nice.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Group projects--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: She is the best HAPP professor at UMBC. She assigns fair and helpful work. Her lectures are engaging and you actually learn. I took HAPP 300 and 411 with her, loved her both times!

Professor Birger is one of THE best HAPP professors at UMBC. I wish she taught all of the HAPP courses because then I would actually learn. In all of her classes her lecture slides are information heavy and are very helpful for her exams without necessarily having to read the book. She gives amazing information on not just her class but life.

She's super chill. She definitely talks a lot during her lecture, but she posts them online so if you couldn't keep up in class you can still work at your own pace. She lets people redo assignments if you didn't like the grade you received.

Literally this is the best professor to take this class with. I showed up to class for the first month before I realized that a literal high school drop out who knows that the mitochondria is the powerhouse of the cell can pass this class.

Professor Birger teaches one of the harder classes that HAPP majors have to take and she makes the info heavy class easier to understand. The content is still a bit difficult but she is very easy to talk to whenever you have an issue. Would deff recommend her to anyone since she is one of the more down to earth profs I've had at this school.

Professor Birger is one of my favorite professors in the HAPP department. Although the assigned book for this class was hard to follow, Birger make it so easy to understand. Her lectures are clear and she keeps you engaged. Two exams; Mid-Term and Final, 1 group debate, a couple reading responses, and quizzes each week. I recommend taking her!

She's a pretty good professor. She seems interested in her subject and her students. However, the attendance is nowhere near mandatory. All assignments (tests included) are online. She posts her slides, and it's really easy to complete your assignments using only the slides she posts. I'd recommend taking HAPP 200 with her, it was pretty good.
She is such a great professor, she makes lectures interesting and fun, one of my favorite classes. Quite a bit of writing but just keep track of what is due and she grades fairly. Take her class!!!

I truly enjoyed this class. Mrs. Birger is professional, peppy, courteous and a great teacher. She somehow manages to make the mundane, boring topic of health regulation interesting. I enjoy her lectures and actually learn about the material. Exams are easy if you pay attention in class and take good notes.

Not sure why others say it's hard, but I got 100% on both the midterm and the final and ended with a 99% in the class. It's ridiculously easy if you show up to class and read over the slides once or twice.  Her exams are a joke, as long as you went to class you can easily get 100%. You don't even need to read the book.
She's the best HAPP professor!

Her lectures were always interesting and I picked up a lot of valuable knowledge. Her class is different from other HAPP classes as it does not reiterate the exact same points. You will definitely pick up new information from this class. She is also not an A producing factory. She is tough but fair. If you study, you will do well in the class.

Professor Birger is one of those rare  and enthusiastic professors who is extraordinarily passionate about teaching. It is always apparent from the powerpoint discussions that she is highly knowledgeable about health policy and health care in general.   she is also very attractive!

Had him this past fall for 115 at Towson, class wasn't too difficult as long as you pay attention. The tests and exams aren't difficult as long as you do the homework and do the study guides posted. Allowed a note card for every exam and did a great job of teaching the material in the class. Even cracked a joke or two during most classes.

Although he was sometimes disorganized, I think he was an overall good professor. I had a lot of fun in his class and I found him very funny. Just make sure to do the homework and study for the tests! He was also a very quick grader. His class was very welcoming, and everyone would participate and work together. I would take him again!

Had him for Math 106. He has a rlly hard accent & rlly hard to know what he's saying most of the time. He was alright with teaching math but sometimes idk how I understood what he was saying. theres a lot of hw on a website we did i forgot but omg it was annoying. you basically have teach urself in this class, so beaware its not fun. idk how i pass

He's a pretty chill professor, and allows a note card on exams with anything on them. His lectures are always on time and organized. He posts the lecture notes after class. Overall pretty good math professor.

I don't think I have ever experienced a professor like him... He could be very scatter-brained, indecisive and his lectures were very messy. I want to be fair to him seeing as he is a new professor and I am hopeful that he is knowledgable in his profession; I could not understand him at all, the whole class would have to correct him often.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Lots of homework--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Never have I EVER taken a class like this. The exams are designed to make you second-guess what you know, the lectures fast paced, and the homework barely matches the learning objectives. Even with a final grade curve and an exam drop, people still struggle to earn a good grade—take that as a sign!!
Solid biology professor for UMBC. He's a cool guy, but you can tell he likes to hear himself talk. Pretty good at lecturing and is nice one-on-one as well.

I loved his lectures; he puts a lot of effort into what he teaches, and cracks the occasional joke. People don't give him the same effort he gives them. All his lecture slides are available on Blackboard, so reviewing and studying is easy. Overall a great class.

Passionate professor who taught hard to understand content in a pretty understandable way! I felt like he was rushing a lot of the time, but to be fair there was a lot of content in each lecture and his slides were thorough enough to go back through and read and understand.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Test heavy

reviews.comment: His lectures were passionless and boring unless he was lecturing about cancer. His content wasn't challenging, but there was so much in each lecture, making it hard to remember it all. His exam style was tricky; discussions and homework assignments were hard. The class is curved, so it's not hard to get a B or an A with a little more effort!
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Exams based on lectures so make sure to study those well and probably make flashcards and prepare for discussions. I didnt touch the textbook unless it was for some difficult HW problems. Kind of condescending and tough grader. HWs were long, difficult, and unhelpful and no drops. Barely any time to answer clickers and only drops one of those.

Dr. B is knowledgeable about the material, especially the topics on cancer. His lectures dominated the final exam so make sure to study his slides. Overall clear lectures but somewhat boring, and the material he teaches is heavily memorization-based. Everything on the exams is on the slides so just memorize from those.
Okay at explaining lecture slides but the slides are really heavy. There's homework once a week and discussion is very confusing if you didn't review everything beforehand

Can drop 1 exam (including the final). Homework was difficult and not useful. One time, I mentioned to him that the homework included content we hadn't reviewed yet, and he told me to "read ahead". Felt like he does research and teaches minimally. Lectures were stale and difficult to follow at times. Not the most friendly. Overall grade is curved.

Exams are based on lectures only, not textbook. Dr. Bieberich has very concise lectures, and his slides are easy to study from. He does participation questions at the start of class, meaning if you are late a couple minutes, chances are you already missed the questions. A little condescending but overall not a bad professor. HW due once a week.

Gave a curve where 85 was an A. His exams were tricky and tough but everything from his slides. Covers a lot of info in lectures and tests on details. Explains concepts fairly well. Not lenient at all. If you don't do things according to instructions, you get penalized. I worked very hard and still got a B. Final was brutal.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Bieberich is much less engaging than Dr. Eisenmann. He has more material to get through since he covers all the memorization heavy parts of genetics, but he is slow and gets behind due to taking to many questions. Take this class with him and Eisenmann and you'll be fine. His exams are easy since it's just brute memorizing.

Terrible lectures. He never explains concepts. He literally just reads off the slides in a very monotone voice. He also takes too many questions during lecture so we lose time and fall behind. Genetics is super detail-oriented and Biebs does not make class interesting or engaging at all.
Nice guy, knows his stuff, but he has a lot of information crammed onto his slides, and I found myself falling asleep during his lectures. However he does get the information across. TAKE NOTES.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: He is amazing. Make sure you go through all his slides and understands almost everything. Exams are straight from slides. Memorize if you can.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Dr. B was amazing and so inspirational. He knows all of his stuff, makes exams fairly tricky, you can tell his questions apart from Eisenmann's questions. Had to study a lot harder for Dr. B exams but he tells you what you'll need to know for the exams so  I always got a high B on his exams. one thing, HE NEVER RESPONDS TO EMAILS!!!!

Professor knows A LOT about the field and is able to answer almost any question. That being said, he doesn't go by the syllabus (attendance is graded on scale with lateabsence and he gives everyone e.c, dont need seminars), also he will find just about anything to pick at with your papers/exam. However, if you show up its easy enough to pass.

I was in the combined section of eisenman and Bieberich for 302. It's a tough class. Exam averages were usually in the 60 somethings. I liked him over the other professor because he has a funny way about him and he puts things into jokes so you remember things better. You get 5 exams and they take the 4 highest for your grade.
Amazing and inspirational professor!
I LOVE HIM!!! He's one of the best professors I've ever had.
His lectures are awesome and he is so nice and friendly!!! One of the best professors I've ever had. I would love to take his classes again.

He is so clear on what to study. He posts all the lecture slides and emphesizes on what we should study more. He makes biology easier for me and he is also inspirational. Definitely love to take more of his biology classes.

I have mixed feelings about Dr. Bieberich.  He wasn't incredibly organized in class and often rushed through the material to get it done on time.  Also, like most bio professors, his exams were fairly tricky.  That being said, there are definitely worse professors here in the bio department, so don't stress too much if you're stuck with Biebs.

Great professor!  Very helpful and cares a lot about his students.  His tests are very tricky.  Just work really hard, go over each question AT LEAST twice, and you should be able to come out with the grade that you want.  He's VERY specific so you can't just memorize the big picture stuff... I got an A by memorizing every little detail I could.
Good professor. Hard class

The best class I took at UMBC. Amazing teacher. Best Ever. He rocks ! Never enjoyed classes this much (even though it was at 8 AM !). He is super cool and an extremely nice and helpful person. If you are not interested in science, take this class and you will start loving it ! Highly recommended.

One of the best biology professors out there. Very clear explanations, and while material can be challenging, goes above and beyond to make sure everyone is caught up. Does not patronize you for being wrong or not understanding something. Outstanding knowledge of biological field of research. Would highly recommend any of his classes.
Really good professor. Puts powerpoints online after lectures. Very clear, and good at answering questions.

Must go to lectures as the questions he asks in class appears on the exams.  Only professor to wear American Eagle and still look hot.  Knows Bio really well, will answer questions, is very nice.  Exams are based strongly on the lecture but reading the book will help signifigantly.  Very nice, smart and helpful.  Take this class with him.

Good Professor!  Explicates the material well and only lectures on things you need to know for the exam.  However, you need to take good notes because there are stuff not on his outlines that are most likely on the exam.  His exams are similar to previous exams.  Take  it with him IF you have to...in general the course is difficult

His exams weren't as hard as Eisenmann's and he was very approachable. Must go to class though, because pdf notes aren't specific enough and textbook is too descriptive and will make you learn things you dont need to know. You will do well in the class if you go to it regularly
awesome professor He knows what he is talking about and very cool when it comes to grading. As long as you do your work you should be fine. A guy is nice!
Great teacher... hard class but Dr. Bieberich is very clear and helpful.
Good course
No Comments
Pretty good teacher.. writes everything out.. but can be a freaking hardass..

309 has more or less the same coursework for any professor or section however Billingsley does not prepare you for the assignments that are given. Attendance is mandatory and is graded. The lectures are so boring. The course would've been better off online/asynchronous. Heavy work load that's not too difficult but very time consuming

Dr. Billingsley is an amazing professor! She lays out everything clearly, with class only one day a week for the course. One quiz and assignment due weekly with weekly readings. 2 final papers, and a final exam. Love her teaching style and the way she was so energetic at 8 in the morning!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Dr. Billingsley is a great professor and is super nice! This class is a little hard to get through because of how long the class is but I would take this class again with her. The assignments feel like busy work but are very helpful.

His lectures are extremely good. I was suprised every time because he taught them like it was the first time teaching them. He was always so excited teaching the class. Finally a professor who loves his job and cares for students.

One of the coolest professors at UMBC by far. Always fills his class with anecdotes relating to the course material making it fun to learn. Semester long group project was a drag but as a professor he did everything else as well as possible. Definitely take if you get the chance.

Sweet guy, he really wants everyone to do well in his class. Attendance is mandatory, but he is very reasonable if you do not come a few times. This class is an easy A/B so you could skip at least half the classes and be fine, but I recommend going because his lectures are awesome and you should give him the respect he deserves.
Actually a very easy class. Semester long group project broken down into 4 papers. Expect about an hour or 2 of work a weel very enjoyable class.

Dr. Birrane took this class way too seriously. We are CMSC majors, not English majors. He is a super harsh grader and your grade relies heavily on the group you're assigned. Weekly quizzes were over the top with what he expected us to remember from class (mostly things he just brushed over).

His work consists of a quiz per lecture, a glorified homework assignment, phases/group projects, lengthy homeworks, the midterm and final were online for this semester. We also had the option to attend class in person or online. Feedback can be harsh but I personally didn't mind. I think Birrane is a cool and funny dude.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Group projects--So many papers

reviews.comment: He's a VERY tough grader and will leave harsh feedback. If you are one to take feedback to heart, do not take this class with him. There is a semester long group project, weekly lecture quizzes, two exams, and homework that are of essay lengths. If you want an easy A, look for another professor, cause this class is a lot of work for an A.
Extremely tough grader specifically when it comes to the papers you write. Don't let him be your first choice.

Edward is an okay teacher. His exams had many silly questions and his semester long project was a mess. If you get stuck with 2 group mates who don't care about their grade it's gonna be hard to get an A. He uses a "multiplier" to help boost grades but his algorithm for determining it is ridiculous and many times hurts your grade. Don't recommend.

This professor teaches you HOW to think as opposed to WHAT to think. He teaches not only ethics but critical thinking and writing skills. His lectures are really interesting, He's sort of tough on grading but it's always in the interest of molding students into better thinkers. Be prepared to write a lot, that project is no joke.

Edward has done an amazing job teaching 304 online. He records YouTube videos explaining the PowerPoints. There are 11 weekly quizzes based off entirely from the PowerPoints; 5 homework's; 2 exams on LockDown but without webcam tho! and 1 semester long group project. Would definitely recommend him if you need an easy A and want to up your GPA

First of, the course is labeled as writing intensive so do expect the group essay to take a good chunk of time. Each stage of the group essay was graded individually and the feedback Birrane gave was extensive and thorough which helped immensely with the following stages. Lectures are interesting and solid. Quizzes and exams are more than fair.
Hands down most enjoyable class of my semester

He is an nice and interesting professor but not necessarily an easy A. Expect to do a lot of writing. Tests are also medium difficulty and not a complete joke like others. Also only professor for ethics to give a final. If the schedule is convenient hes not the worst option but think twice if you're taking a tough courseload.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Cool professor, really smart in his field, great lecturer, and very decent on grading. Pay attention at least 75% in class and you'll do great on the quizzes. Put a couple hours of work in on the project and you'll do well. Material is a little tougher than expected, but for a CS class it's definitely a break.

Prof. is really passionate about this class, but it's a slog. Group projects with 7 people yet he wants "one person feel" from papers.
