reviews.comment: Prof. Channel-Ward is nice and humorous, but her exams are not that enjoyable. Her class requires students to spend their time studying out of class. Her exams are super long and pretty hard, but students get several attempts, except the final.

She is a great professor, but sometimes the lecture can get boring. I barely passed the exams because they were hard. The exams and quizzes are through mylabaccounting and they were hard since I was attempted to cheat. She tries to keep the classroom lively and keeps talking about football.

Take Mrs Ward if you need this intermediate accounting class! Read the chapter before class and you'll be fine. Homeworks and Exams were through Connect. She has a good way of picking up the spirit of discussion in the class making Accounting fun to learn!

Really nice. Wants you to learn the subject and is really lenient. Almost all assignments are online. Everything you learn or do in homework is on the test. She is super interactive with the class and wants you to participate in order to gauge your understanding. She only gave out quizzes a couple times and gave enough time to complete assignments

She is a great professor! The homework, quizzes, and exams are all online. Final exam is in person and requires at least a 50% to pass which is very do-able. She keeps lecture interesting, and is willing to bump up your final grade in the end. Takes attendance randomly. Allows you to redo assignments at the end of the semester. Take her!!
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Tests? Not many--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Great teacher! Very intelligent and very understanding! Best History Teacher ever in my opinion. I'd recommend him to anyone!

One of the best teachers I've ever had. Really knows his stuff and has a passion for history. He made me like history even though I never have before. You have to put some work into homework assignments and the one essay he assigns but his 3 exams are online, open source, and multiple choice. Take him.

took his 1st 6 wk course and it was HARD mostly cuz he used ALL the info form a normal class and squeezed it into 6 wks good teacher, REALLY knows his stuff, makes the lectures interesting and posts in pwrpnts online and the tests are online AND open note. can be difficult to sift through the info but over all hes a great teacher. I recommend him.

This professor is really good. I had him for hist355 us enivironmental history. Two exams both where short answer with one essay. Other points where for writing on a blog about assigned reading and showing up for class. Not that hard easy A if you put some study time in.
i found dr b quite hard. her powerpoint slides are not very clear. she says certain things will not be on test and then puts them on. if you read alot, alot, alot you have a chance at succeeding.

NO CURVE < OFTEN GOT CLASS GRADES MIXED UP WITH OTHER STUDENTS NEVER RESPONDS TO EMAILS NEVER HELPS < USES OTHER PROFESSORS SLIDES AND EXAMS PATHETIC GARBAGE UMBC SHOULD HIRE ME I CAN DO A BETTER JOB, WHAT PROFESSOR LEAVES FOR 1 MONTHS DURING CLASS

She is a great professor. I don't know what the other person is saying. He or she must be really un-intelligent. She is a very down to earth person. If you study the lecture slides, go to class and pay attention you're going to get a "C" no matter what. If you ask questions and are attentive you'll give a "B" with some work. She's a great professor

Genetics is a hard subject in general. You have to work hard to get an "A" Dr. B. makes this class a little easier, by making the exams exactly reflect the lectures. She's one of the best science professors at UMBC. She's extremely helpful. I recommend everyone take her class, if you need to take genetics. She's Great.

This professor is for those who want to get an easy A, his attendance level is very poor, so check if he'll show up 3 hours before class to know if you should wait, thick accent, but, who cares? Quizzes are online, and exams are take home.

The class is easy.  Economics is normally boring to me.  However, I admire his style and personality actually which is pretty light, cool.  So that helped a lot in me enduring Economics.  I'd take him again.

At first I thought what kept him from communicating effectively was his accent, but he actually makes no sense at all, even in his problem sets. His tests are exactly like his practice exams so if you memorize them you are golden, just don't expect to learn anything. Professors like him make me lose faith in humanity and the MD education system.

He is very hard to understand and harder to read his handwriting. Attendance is not mandatory but he recognizes faces and will know if you miss a class. His test are basically the practice test he goes over and he does have make-up tests, which he helps walk you through them sometimes. He's a good teacher who knows his stuff. Definitely take him.
dont take him. Save ur energy, Save ur CGPA!
Greatest Prof EVER! Take any class with him!!Easy A and an extremely funny guy.Best class i ever took in UMBC

Ugh. I love econ, I love math. This was a wretched class. Most of the lectures he'd spend showing how to derive one equation from another with no motivation given. When he would discuss theory he would not write, only speak in a thick african-french accent. As a visual learner that was a nightmare. Lectures from book's powerpoints and unprepared.
If you want an easy A in a general education requiriment take his class and thats what you will get. If you are majoring in Econ don't plan to learn much in his class.
take him ! there 's no free ride in the world except his classs

Took Econ 312 and Econ 490 with him. Very funny guy, who will crack some jokes and will be convinced to make exams EASY if whole class says so. Class lectures are very fast and may sound impossible but exam are SUPER easy. Good professor, the best for easy A
Cinyabugama, a short, troll-like creature characterized by a long, streamlined snout and red horn; often seen scouting the long grass areas for treasures. Not to be confused with a Chumbawamba.
I agree with the other reviewers. If you can do the practice exams, you'll do fine on the  actual exams. He's entertaining - probably the best of the bunch for 312.
Great teacher, love to study with it.

I didn't pay attention after the first few classes -- he mostly spends time proving formulas only to test students on the concepts via graphs. Therefore, I recommend reading through the chapters on your own and familiarizing yourself with the content. He gives practice exams, so it's in your best interest to do them; class will be a breeze.
The tests are pretty much the exact same thing as the review. Lectures gat a bit off topic with proofs that you dont need. He has an interesting sense of humor, but he gets the class to laugh.

He's the best!  I love his class!  He tells you pretty much what's on the test and he has an unmatched sense of humor.  Spends an ungodly amount of time in class reviewing, so there's no excuse not to do well!
Very knowledgeble

The man seemed lost many times, and is not very good at getting the material across.  Our Third Exam was supposed to consist of 1-2 chapters of material.  On the last day of class he handed the class a 30 page packet of new material that we were suppose to learn on our own, adding 4 more chapters to the final. Take this course with Mark Thomas.
No Comments

Overall nice guy. his tests are practically like the reviews. you have 2 midterms and a final plus a few quizzes that you can take for extra credit. sometimes i feel like he didn't know what he was doing so i got confused. you don't really learn anything (even though he makes an honest attempt to teach) but you can still get an A.
he teaches in a very mathematical kind of way (barely any graphs) so that complicates things a lot..just go over the practice exams and talk to him during office hours
poor teacher, take it with mark thomas

His accent is French- not African.  Matthias is always willing to help his students (he gave a reasonable curve), and if you make sure you understand the hw you will do fine in the class.  Take advantage of office hours- it will give you some perspective!!

Bad african accent hard to understand during lecture.  Seems to be a nice guy, all you have to do to succeed is have a all right understanding of the subject and make that clear on the exams.  Homeworks as well. Big curve helps a lot

Talks fast. Expert in field and tons of great/relevant stories. Expect to participate. Every week is a group presentation - gives 10/15 mins to work as group. Utilizes jigsaw strategy/method for reading assignments and weekly group presentations. Harsh grader - Easy A if do the reading and follow provided outline for papers. You learn a ton!

Great instructor who clearly is an expert in his field.   He assigns lots of reading but not a lot of other homework.  There were 4 short papers we had to write for class and he gave clear guidance on what he wanted to see in the papers.  There were no tests in the class.  10% participation and the rest was the papers.  Easy A if you do the work.

It's an easy A if you do the reading (moderate) and use his outline to answer papers of various lengths (2 shortest to 8 longest).  Best part is he wants you to take something away from class instead of just a grade, this good to know where law plays with technology.  Prof has worked in NSC, DoD, DHS and ODNI!!

Robert Clark is a great lecturer. He makes a potentially boring and dry topic, law & policy, quite exciting. I always look forward to his classes. There's no quizzes or exams, just six papers. He's not a harsh grader, and he gives a detailed outline of what exactly he's expecting for the papers too, so it's a no-brainer.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--SO MANY PAPERS--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Its a law class so it is expected that you have to talk, not like law school but still different.  Dude has lots of experience working in and around USG
talks really fast and goes on tangents a lot.  calls on students without warning.  but seems laid back.
She is fantastic! The best teacher I have had for Spanish. I have learned a lot in her class and appreciate her enthusiasm.

I enjoyed professor Clay's class a lot. I've learned more Spanish than I ever did throughout my 4 years of high school. Her class isn't too hard, but expect lots of homework with mySpanishLab. Also she is very helpful and making sure you understand the material and has office hours every week.

Professor Clay seems very flustered. She is not very clear about homework at times and leaves students with many questions. For a 100 level class, this class had A LOT of work. She expects a lot from a class full of students who have zero experience in Spanish. My recommendation to you is if you can find a better professor than do not pick this one
Enthusiastic in the way she teaches, but the class seems kind of like a joke sometimes, in some events students will be correcting her Spanish.
does not really teach and very hard grader.

Avoid her if you can. She doesn't really teach, puts questions on tests/quizzes that she didn't really go over. She'll tell you that you have a good idea on a project then proceed to give you a bad grade w/o talking to you about what the issues were. She isn't very approachable.

Only good part of the class was when Dr. Schreier lectured.  Dr. Claassen didn't even give lectures most of the time.  She made us do "In Class Activities" and turn them in for participation points.  It was pointless busy work and reminded me of high school.  Her exam questions always have flaws in them.  Overall awful experience.
If you can help it, do not take any courses with Dr. Claassen. She does not make clear what she expects of her students. The only good part of this course was when Dr. Schreier taught in the middle.

the labs are pretty easy; recitation is pointless as she reads off of her slides; she is unapproachable and has the lab reports graded so you can get the lowest possible points; she is NOT approachable b/c she assumes that u have been skipping lectures if you ask questions;exams are impossible bc most of the material is not taught so it's hopeless

Go to her office hours if you have questions, she is extremely helpful! Some labs can be tiring and annoying, but then some labs are exciting. Exam are very tricky! Study hard for her lab quizzes and do well on the labs and lab reports so if you do average on exams, it won't hurt you much!
dr. classen made me want to be a bio major. shes helpful in office hours if you go and knows her stuff

The teacher has a very simple grading style, where you get to drop one lab and one quiz, and you have 2 comprehensive tests.  However, her anti-plagiarism system can ruin your grade, as she gave one of my friends a 50% on a paper even though he didn't plagiarize and even proved he didn't plagiarize.
Very important to attend her lectures as most of what she says will be on exams. Stick it out though cause her lectures are boring.
SHe doesn't knows her stuff clearly
great teacher, really nice, knows her stuff. just make sure to go to the lectures.
Beware! You're better off taking her class at a community college

An amazing professor and genuinely the best classes I've had were with Conor. Even if he doesn't teach at UMBC anymore, I would take his class at any institution. Bring back Conor and pay him well!!!!!!!

I'm really going to miss Conor as it is his last semester here. His class was one of the most interesting and informative classes I have taken. There's only 3 assignments to be graded on but they are all relatively easy as long as you look over the material and show up to class. Remember to participate as it  counts toward your grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Amazing lectures --Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Donnan is such a gem! If you have the opportunity to take one of his classes you should absolutely jump on it. I took one class of his freshman year almost by accident and he was so amazing that I ended up changing my major to American Studies. His connection with the student body is such a vital resourse for everyone at UMBC.

Overall, Mr. Donnan was a good professor. He was a chill guy and his lectures were interesting. There were only 3 assignments in the class, all of which were pretty simple. Participating in lectures is needed for the participation grade, but just showing up to class helps with that. I would definitely recommend taking this class and professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Awesome guy

Professor Donnan is one of the best professors at UMBC. He has very engaging lectures and he is very funny. I have taken multiple of his classes and they are all very good. He has about 3 projects. almost one a month and they are very manageable.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: This man is AMAZING. I took AMST 317, and was definitely the best decision ever. He only gives three assignments throughout the whole semester and his lectures are actually pretty interesting. He doesn't take attendance so you don't have to worry about having to take a sick day. All around, great professor. A++
Hands down one of the best professors I've ever had! He's extremely flexible and wants everyone to succeed. This class is participation heavy and it will count towards your final grade.

Prof. D was great. He's a really interesting and memorable prof, might be one of the best at the school. He leads lectures but tries not to make them too boring. Grades are from a few midterm assignments, but if you understand the material, you should be able to get an A.

Professor D is very passionate about American studies. There are 3 assignments and a small portion of your grade is bason on participation. His lectures are interesting and the content isn't boring. Highly recommend if you need the credit.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Took AMST 345(in person). The class was very interesting, reading was heavy(but not required), assignments were few and far in between with multiple options for what you would like to do, and last but certainly not least, he is a great professor and a really interesting guy.

MCS 144 not MCS 222. Professor Conroy is an amazing professor, if you need to take MCS 144 then take this class with her! Although she may not take attendance through blackboard right away she will eventually put in your attendance grade. She takes attendance through a QR code.If you show up and put effort into your work you will pass the class!

MCS 144* She's very sweet and straightforward about assignments. The class is group and presentation oriented, gives a lot of asynchronous days, so you can work with your group and presentations, but sometimes wish we had class to keep people accountable for group work. One group presentation, one individual presentation, and a final interview.

Professor Conroy was great! She was really nice and an easy grader. She kept the class was fun with her presentations and it wasn't intense at all. There is a textbook, but she provides it and it's really small. If you want an A take this class.
I took three Military History courses with Dr. Laurie. HE was by far the best professor in the UMBC History department.
Very good professor, sad he will not teach the WWII class next semester.

Very passionate and knowledgable about the subject (the history of U.S. intelligence, ie- CIA, etc.) Lays out what he wants out of papers and tests very clearly, not difficult, just particular. I would take his classes again but I hear he's retiring.

Two essay exams, two papers, and one research project. Not a ton of reading, but a lot of writing. Lectures tend to not make sense, but that's just his style. TA this semester taught the last few weeks, and if you can get her again, do. Good teacher, and hot! TA's are not usually like that. Thanks Dominique.
The Ta is very hot and Dr. LAurie is really fair...win win

A lot of work so far, but I am liking it. He knows his topic well, and lectures are fun. I don't like all the movies, but some of them are OK. The textbook isn't bad, but expensive! This is my first time taking his class, so I can't say much. But I can say the TA is excellent, and she and Dr. Laurie make a good team.

So far, it's an interesting class. Clearly he is passionate about his work. Lots of writing, and exams are semi-hard, but his TA this semester is hot! Hopefully not a hardass, though. Lots of movies scheduled which sucks, but he is a nice guy. Take the class if you need it, but if you hate writing or studying, please stay away. You won't do well.

Dr. Laurie was one of the best teachers I ever had.  I took his WWI, WWII and Vietnam War classes and they were WONDERFUL.  He made the subject matter not only interesting but relatable.  A lot of times classes about war can be overly technical and dry but none of his classes were.

One of the best teachers I've ever had. Definitely responsible for making me so interested in history. If you like military history, Dr. Laurie is the man to speak to. Requires substantial work (and asks you to follow specific guidelines), but if you do what he asks you will get an A.
Best professor at UMBC. If you show up to class and pay attention and put in at some effort outside of class, it is hard to not earn an A or B.

This class is a lot of work but ridiculously easy.  You just have to review the practice exams he posts on BB, do the film notes and make sure your ID's are decent and you're on your way to an easy A.  There are also two papers which are pretty easy as well.  Overall, take HIST 111 with Laurie!
Great class for anyone interested in History. Dr. Laurie is a great professor and makes it a fun class. If you study hard in this class you will do really well.

He's very interested in the subject...I stopped taking notes towards the end though. His tests are exactly the same as the practice test, so if you memorize that, you don't actually have to know the class material.

boring, unorganized, terrible. grading is arbitrary and he uses TA's, who are ridiculous- your grade will depend on which one grades your paper. just avoid him if at all possible. you will not learn anything, and it isnt worth the time or effort.

I have had WWI, WWII, and Vietnam with Dr. Laurie. WWI is definitely the weakest class. A gigantic research project about the Dead Men's Penny is required. Depending on who you get to research it can be a breeze or a nightmare. Doesn't grade too hard. Looks mostly for buzzwords/concepts in exams. For the papers just pay close attention to grammar!

I took both World War II and War in the Modern World with Laurie. His lectures are straightforward (you don't need the textbook), his exams cover precisely what he talks about, and, most importantly, he works for the freaking CIA. Expect lots of stories- if you love military history, take at least one of his classes

Lots of work for a 100 level course, but definitely worth taking for a culture credit. It's easy. You can get a good grade on the exams if you go over the practice exams multiple times. Notes during lectures are kind of scrambled, but the only reason to go to class is because he takes attendance and not showing up will affect your grade in the end.
DON'T BUY THE BOOKS. His tests are based on the online blackboard practice exams. 2 papers, notes on films, and attendance. Easy to earn a B, but you have to study a bit for an A. Good guy.
An incredible teacher. Captivating lecturer. The assignments assigned are not just about facts but call for a nice amount of creativity. Does have some trouble with technology however.

Took this class over the summer, very easy, lost of extra credit by watching videos and writing summaries. Tests are easy, he gives 300 practice questions, 10 0 of those 300 will be on the test. Easy class over the summer. He explains things well, learnt a little bit of History! :)
Great professor.  Knows his stuff and loves to share it with students.  What he doesn't know isn't worth knowing.

The best professor ever, hands down. Loud, funny, very intelligent, and has a very cool voice. Take a class with him if you can. Also, DO NOT BUY THE BOOKS. I never understood why you would buy a book on something you can find for free on Wikipedia!

He is extremely cool to listen to.  You will learn a lot because he makes the material interesting and throws in cool little facts.  He reminds the class of upcoming due dates and tells us to check our email for things.  He responds to email quickly.  He's very approachable, great guy to take a class with.

All you need to do is memorize the questions on his practice exams and ure guaranteed an A. I watched tv shows in class and i dont think i payed any attention partly because i dont care for history. Easy A, enjoyable if you like history but if not, it doesnt matter :)

Awesome teacher. Taken 4 of his classes, all relatively the same (except WW1 has an extra project). Take good notes and your good. I did all of my papers/test studying the night before and got A's. Enjoyable classes.

Dr. Laurie is the epitome of history buff. He knows everything, and is extremely eager to impart his knowledge on his students.  The History of Intel. class is absolutely awesome. There's three papers due during the semester, and two tests. He has very clear guidelines for what he expects on the tests and papers; just follow them and you'll do well
He explains everything that he requires of you in detail and provided a walk through guide for a research project. As long as you did everything on the guide you got at least a B.
Great. Easy exams, easy papers, very accommodating, lots of fun. recommend this class for sure.

Great teacher. Straight forward history and he knows his stuff. Assignments same in each course: 2 tests, 3 papers. All are easy if you study & pay attention. Has some good stories and likes to talk to students. Even if you're not a history major take one of his classes if you like war.

this guy was awesome. he liked his history and knew a lot about everything. if you asked him a question he didnt know, he would actually look it up and get back to you the next class. very clear on grades, only 4 of them, if you study for midterm and final you can easily get an  A. class is mandatory attendance though. Awesome class, take it.
Laurie was great.  his lectures are interesting and his classes never get tedious.  if you get the chance, take his military history class. its the best.

Decent teacher but he shows videos of another professor from another school lecturing rather than doing it himself. When he does talk he is interesting but his notes on the board can be hard to follow. Wouldn't recommend him but wouldn't say avoid him either.

I took 306 (world war I) with him...he definitely knows his stuff, but I could not stay awake in his class, his lectures can get boring really fast, and you MUST read the textbook. He's a likable guy if a bit quirky, he paces around the room, and hes a tad paranoid and loves his cigarettes

He's a great man, but his teaching style is boring and he makes things more difficult than they need to be. There is no need to read in the class, all you need to study for the tests is wikipedia, but they are still very hard. His papers are like middle school book reports. I'd heard great things about him, but I was really disappointed.

If you have a desire to fall asleep in class go ahead and take it. He reads from prepaired notes for at least 10 minutes of each class.  Im sure that since you are in college you can read on your own. He knows his stuff but gets caught up in the details. The midterm is scarier before you take it than it really is. READ the TEXTBOOK! Boring class.

The man is a beast.  He really knows his stuff, and gives you cool anecdotes about history that you can tell your friends or use as a cocktail party snippets later on.  Gotta do a bit of reading on your own, especially for the two 3-page research papers.  The exams are pretty meaty and intense though, so studying the material!

Laurie is as strait laced as any other CIA operative now teaching college courses. He lectures strait from the Christopher Andrew text, so only buy that book. His stories are funny, he gives you a good study guide to go on for the tests, and every other assignment is a 3 page paper. But, learning about intelligence is NOT as cool as you think

47 half hour videos with a paper and 27 chapter tests for the hybrid course. Its a lot of work but an interesting class. You need about 3 hours a day for this class, heavy workload. take the class if youre up for the challenge, youll learn a lot!
Best History teacher I ever had.  Could have done without the annoying videos.  READ THE BOOK

I've taken him twice, for hist 306 and 303.  Dr.  Laurie is awesome!  His lectures are awesome and you'll never fall asleep.  He knows everything about what he's teaching.  He's an okay reader.  There's A LOT of reading, though and there's a lot of writing on the test.  Go to class everyday.  I definitely recommend all his classes, they're great :)

This is the best class I have had at UMBC.  Dr Laurie is friendly and really knows his stuff.  It is like watching the history channel, but more fun.  A lot of reading and writing, but if you do the work, he is a very fair grader.  Teaches you how to think, but not what to think -rare at this university. A MUST TAKE class.

Dr. Laurie is one of the best history teachers at UMBC and the best one I have had so far. He is very approachable and freindly; he always seems to be willing to help no matter what the request. The two exams are tough, but having the essays posted ahead of time is a great benefit. If you can get into the class, take it!

Great professor, knows his stuff, and cracks jokes to keep you awake.  Fair grader and gives out exam questions in advance.  Requires a good deal of reading and writing, plus you need to pay attention.  All in all, a fantastic professor.
Amazing teacher. He makes WWI comprehensible. Take him and this course, or any of his other courses if you can.
He taught my his 100 class as a bit of a weeder class, which i'm bitter about.  That said, he is very interested in the course work, and knows his stuff.
gives you the answers if you listen. sometimes tough grader. awesome lecturer though. even if you disagree with him: he knows the history.

He gives out exams questions so it's always helpful.  The way he talk and the way he teaches made my feel like I was living in the WWII days.  Going to his class is like listening to the news broadcast.  Great lecture, very knowledgeable, easy to talk to and work with, defintely very glad I took his class.  This class was one of the best I ever had

Dr. Laurie is the best professor ever. I had him for HIST 303, HIST 306. He knows everything about the subjects he teaches. He is always willing to help. He is so a good that, I regret not being able to take HIST 304 or any of his other classes.

Dr. Laurie is a remarkably well spoken and intelligent professor. I have taken all four of his classes (WWII, WWI, Vietnam and War in the Modern Wolrd) and he was well informed on all of the topics. His book reviews are easy enough, but beware his tests. Study hard!

You dont need to buy anybooks for WW1 class. All the info is from the lecture notes and is available online. You will have to do 2 book reviews..which also you dont need to pay for and are available at the library. Take as many notes as you can. He wants details in his exams. Pretty easy class.

Dr. Laurie's a wonderful professor~ one of the best at UMBC. His lectures are interesting and he makes it so interesting that even I found that I wanted to change my major to history, with a concentration on military history.  He's THAT good.

I have taken every course Dr. Laurie teaches at UMBC.  His lectures are the most informative, fascinating and entertaining I have ever attended.  His class was always my favorite, each semester.  But most importantly, he truly, genuinely cares about his students and loves teaching. I'll miss him.

I have taken 3 Dr. Laurie classes and gotten As in them all. Hist 100 is SO EASY, exams are the mult. choice in the back of the study guide, 300 levels have 3 book reviews which you can b.s. and he gives you the questions that will be asked on each exam so you can study exactly what will be asked.
relatively easy, if you study before exams and attend class every day
Great Prof. Adds a little humour to the class and knows his stuff.  Covers a lot of information, but if you take notes and do the reading he advises you will be ok.

This prof requires more work for a worthless 100 level class than most 300 and 400 level classes. you have to memorize dates that even he has to read off his notes. do not take this class unless you want to waste your time (or you are a history major)

Great man, knows lots about military history in general. Classes can sometimes drag on because he bombards you with facts, but when he does anyalsis it is excellent. 1 suggestion do you report early and get it revised, it gurantees you an A on the paper.
Very interesting lectures and a great lecturer, very hepful if you have questions or problems. I took a summer class and we even had a field trip.

Best teacher ever. Every other day you watch a movie on western civ.Get points for going to class and writing notes on the movies, 2 papers(pretty simple)and the tests are soley on the mult. choice from the study books and time line or map (answers given)
Brilliant man, knows all his military history, but it's a lot of work-the tests are just 2 essays and IDs, and there're three book reports-4 and 5 pages.

Talks fast and has a lot to say, but it is worth hearing. This Professor knows his stuff and loves to share it with his students.  Very helpful and approachable.  Lots of work and exams aren't easy but if you go to class and do the reading you will be OK.

Talks fast and has a lot to say, but it is worth hearing. This Professor knows his stuff and loves to share it with his students.  Very helpful and approachable.  Lots of work and exams aren't easy but if you go to class and do the reading you will be OK.
One of the best professors I've ever had. The man expects a lot from you, but his class is incredible.
This course is super easy. Nice guy with pretty good lectures. Attendence is required. Just prepare for the exams, and it's an easy A.
Great teacher, and goes all out for his students.  He remembers his students 3 and 4 semesters later.
Lectures too quickly. Simple exams. Overall easy course.
He is a very good professor. Lots of presentations in groups, but everything is explained well. He cares about his students and entrepreneurship. Definitely recommend!

If you are looking for a great prof for this class, this is it. His class is based on a group project for the most part, that you will present as your final. There're several chapters you have to present with your team. He always has snacks and is very willing to help you in any way he can. Learned a lot from him. He loves his students.
The professor wants students to succeed and learn beneficial material. Very approachable and easy to talk to when working through group presentations.

He is genuinely super nice and understanding, the class is 90% group work, so b wary of that, make sure u communicate with ur group. If they all suck at communicating, take lead and assign everyone specific roles, even if ppl say they have no preference. HE ALWAYS PROVIDES SNACKS EVERY CLASS. U can tell he cares about his students. HIGHLY RECCOMEND

Prof Costlow is truly so intelligent and passionate about entrepreneurship. There are no exams this is a presentation-only class so be prepared to present in almost every class. He gives amazing feedback and is always willing to sit down and brainstorm ideas with you. Unfortunately, he doesn't teach ENTR-201 but I would've taken his class if he did

Bill works as an entrepreneur, is very willing to help and give feedback without any condescension. Mostly straightforward group presentations about startups, graded extremely leniently. Book used is The Lean Startup but you only really need to read two chapters to present about throughout the whole semester.
10/10 Professor. Had a lot of knowledge to give as an entrepreneur. All the assignments were group projects which was not bad. Only individual assignment was to interview an entrepreneur.
Terrible professor doesn't actually care if you have a situation if you cant come to class

Professor who is interested in what he is talking about. If you talk about something he does not have knowledge he may be dismissive. Very extensive and informative lectures and easy to do well, all quizzes and tests online

I heard this professor gives less workload than Dr. Swan's GES308, and it's very chill. He cares about attendance (if you miss 20% of classes you fail) but it's simply enforced with his own eyes. Labs are chill and we often get to leave early, sometimes we go outside it's nice.

As a GES major his lectures are actually interesting, just jot down the stuff you didn't know already and have the notes to flip through during the open note tests. He also gives out study guides where many of the questions are on the test/final. NGL you can get away with not touching the online textbook I opted out lol

The class basically consists of dry PowerPoint lectures, so it's really what you make of it and how much you like the content. He seems like a generally nice and smart guy, so if you're interested in environmental science, take him! He creates comprehensive study guides before every exam, which are extremely helpful
Thorough lectures and homeworks closely matched test contents. Very good.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: The exams are exactly like the study guides and online quizzes. The lectures aren't really helpful and sometimes cut short. The Professor barely explains the material but you can mostly just memorize the study guide and quiz questions to do well on the exam

This was probably the worst professor I have ever had. He is very monotone. Not helpful. He constantly makes spelling errors and errors in general and won't own up to when his mistakes affect his students. Would not recommend taking a class of his at all. He seems like a nice guy, just a terrible professor. Tests had questions he never taught us.

Lectures are long but must go to class cause he takes attendance and does clicker points. Exams are just like the review guides. Nice professor and available if emailed, good to take ges110 with Professor Studds
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: One of the easiest A's I've gotten at UMBC. Attendance is required since there are clicker questions and he rounds your grade up if you have good attendance. The study guides are essentially what make up the exams. Highly recommend if you're looking for an easy A or a GEP to take.
His class is easy to get an A. The tests are exactly from the study guide he provides. The lecture is boring, but you'll get through it. I am not an Science major and it was an easy class.

Colin really knows a great deal about birds and he is prepared to tell you all about it which was great. The field assignments we went out and did were really enjoyable as well. Anyone interested in wildlife management should take this class. He has a lot of good research ideas and his research is fascinating and he will gladly tell you about it.

This is the easiest A ever. The hws are all online quizzes and super easy if you read the chapter or use Quizlet. The exams aren't bad either, bc he provides study guides. You have to go to lecture, because he counts attendance and has clicker questions. he's funny and passionate and makes the material fun/easy to understand - loved this class!!!
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: This professor is so passionate about his field that it really does rub off. His lectures are well prepared every day, perfect length and the information is meaningful and fair. I feel like the bad reviews are just people who wanted an easy A. Its not the easiest class in the world but the tests are very fair if you just look over the info.

Dr. Studds is a knowledgeable professor, especially in his expertise; birds. He encourages questions and really took the time to answer the questions he was asked, not one of those professors who make you feel dumb for wanting a more detailed explanation. The only problem is that he grades really slow.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Dr. Studds is one of my favorite  profs. I've taken a few classes with him. He is obviously very passionate about his work and very knowledgeable about his field and conservation biology in general.  He seems to do really groundbreaking and interesting research and is just a really cool guy all around. He's understanding &willing to work w/students

Dr. Studds is a very well intentioned teacher who is very easy to talk to and ask questions, and makes it very easy to pass without having opened the textbook. If that's what you want, take this class. If youre really interested in this subject, take a different class because while he is very nice, hes not very engaging and people would doze off.

His lectures were incredibly long and boring. He overcomplicated everything and I can honestly say I didn't learn much in that class. It was easy to pass because the only things graded are simple reading quizzes and 4 exams. The exams were super easy because all the answers were put online ahead of time so all I had to do was memorize them.

I looked him up on this site before I took the class and was nervous because of what people said - but he has been one of my best professors! He lectures clearly and concisely.  If you have a question he'll take the time in class to answer. The exams are very easy if you go over the study wiki he creates. He's also surprisingly funny!

He is a okay professor, very knowledgeable about the subject he teaches.  He talks a lot about birds. He takes forever to grade. The test are easy if you study hard for them and its only three. You also have to write a long research paper. He can be hard to get in touch with.  Doesn't give feedback on papers. STUDY HARD AND GOOD LUCK!!!

Very hard to get in contact with him outside of class. You have to hassle him to answer your emails. He is a slow grader. Makes you write  a huge end of the semester research paper and gives no feedback. Very disorganized.
I loved this class, Dr. Studds is a great lecturer who really cares about his content. Be ready to pay attention, there's a lot of material!

For a 100 level class, he expected way too much. He is always late to class, and seems the least interested in his own lectures. I would not recommend this professor to someone who enjoys geography, he will ruin it for you.

Dr. Studds was nice, and very helpful 1 on 1. His class was interesting, and exams were fair. There were 3 exams in essay form, a research paper, and a presentation. He was an easy grader. Overall, a decent class!

He is a very nice and chill professor, don't get me wrong a great guy but for a level 100 course, I don't recommend taking this class if you're just trying to get the credit. Take something else because it is challenging. I basically learned nothing from the lectures, but when the test review guide came out, I studied a LOT.

I was used to other professors handing out praise easily so professor Vaporis caught me off guard because he more often will critique you when your writing is wrong/bad and not praise you if it's only mediocre. I felt stupid at first but this teaching style made times where he did praise me feel earned. My complaint: too many textbooks to purchase.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Classes/exams are some of the most challenging but if you complete all of the work you're going to leave with a really deep understanding of the content.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: This was a really difficult gen ed class and the lectures covered a lot but much of that information was not needed for the exams or papers. There were a lot of readings and those are important to do well in this class. Overall, I would say to do well in this class, you would need to devote a lot of time to it.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Vaporis has the student's best interest at heart. That being said this class is not easy.  There's much reading it can get overwhelming at times and there are lots of writing assignments. If you are taking other classes, or if you hate reading, writing, critical thinking, or don't have a strong work ethic (warning) DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: professor knows a lot about the topic and seems to enjoy speaking about it but his lectures are overall monotone and boring making it hard to follow. The exams are super difficult but get easier after the first one you just need to make sure to keep up with the material. much reading in the class good luck. exams are short answer no multiple choice
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Pretty difficult/lots of work for a 100 level class. Recommend if you have an interest in history, but not a great choice for an easy GEP. Vaporis himself is pretty nice and clearly passionate about the subject. Added an Asian Studies minor after taking this class!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: He's nice however during his lectures, most of the slides he goes over, hell talk about random stuf or xtra fax that are completely irrelevant 2 wat u actually need 2 no n learn. There is genuinely 2 much 2 remember, study, and read for a 100 lvl class. Spent days studying 4 the exams and still got D's and C's. You do NOT get rewarded for effort.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment:
He's a good professor.
Makes the best out of a looong subject. 
But class is way harder than a 100 level course needs to be. 
It's gonna be all about how good you are at memorizing stuff. 
Most of your grade is gonna be the exams which just require a lottt of review and cramming. 
Otherwise he makes class fun and is very informed and passionate.

Pretty much was fine up until second exam. Answered the question the way it was asked and the TA grader gave me half points. Followed up and was basically told to screw off. Would not recommend this class if he is teaching.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I enjoyed this professor as a person and lectures were enjoyable to me. However, as a 3 credit course, it's VERY reading heavy. Be prepared to ready 30-40 pages of the textbook in addition to 1-2 course documents before lecture each day. Also, he's a pretty tough grader. Definitely hard to keep up with, but try to focus on enjoying the subject.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: My only gripes w/ Vaporis is he can't make a powerpoint to save his life, garbo required reading scans, and he expects you to cover 6 pieces of work in 3.5 pages max for the Midterm&Final. He wants you to analyze texts not write a summary which many ppl did in discussions. If you don't like reading, writing, or critical thinking, then don't enroll.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I was so excited to take a class on Japanese history, but this professor killed my enthusiasm. He's hard to approach, gives vague directions and an unrealistic workload, especially for a four-week class. I don't usually give professors bad reviews but this was too much. I didn't even leave feeling like I learned a lot either. Would not recommend.

He has a passion in what he teaches, but his lectures are still very tedious and dry. He assigns a ton of readings each night, but you don't have to read any of them to pass. His exams are all short answer and essay-type questions. He expects you to know A LOT for tests, and it'll take a lot of memorizing the night before to pass.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: This class on modern Japanese history was enhanced by use of tons of visual sources like art, photos, and video. There are a lot of writing assignments. Good class to take if you want to get used to churning out a lot of papers after quickly mastering some material and coming up with an argument.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Clear grading criteria--So many papers

reviews.comment: Long and monotone lectures that are riddled with unnecessary tangents that will put to sleep. This course (HIST 103) is required for the Asian Studies major and Prof. Vaporis is the only professor who teaches the course. I would not advise taking this course as an elective. Only take this course and prof. if you have to.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: If you are looking for a History class that is interesting, educating, and enjoyable, I suggest you look for one not taught by this professor. He has an unrealistic amount of reading and the questions he asks are very ambiguous and hard to understand.  The coursework is tough and he is an even tougher grader. I suggest you look elsewhere.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: Constantine Vaporis is passionate and knowledgeable about Japan's language and culture and other parts of Asia. He's a great teacher, outside of a 100 lv class. He will assign a ridiculous amount of work for a entry level class you need. This isn't an easy A - it's an easy C and may cause you to balk or rethink your major.

Up to 350 pages of reading (worthless) and +15 hours of film a week . Prof. is less than clear about what he expects in tests and assignments (his instructions often don't match his expectations). He is rude over email, if he even responds, and exudes self-importance. He is extremely subjective, and it shows in his questions. I do not recommend.

Great professor! He was very helpful & clear. He loved the subject & I knew nothing about Japan prior. Reading was required, but I did none of it & got a B in the class. Document IDs on the midterm, but you go over most of those in class. Attendance wasn't mandatory, but it is helpful to go. Final was in the usual format of IDs & essays.

Absurdly difficult for a 100 level class. You HAVE to do the reading and you WILL read 2 or 3 books cover-to-cover before the end of the semester. Difficult grader. If you are only casually interested in Asian history and are only seeking to satisfy a degree requirement, avoid at all costs. Most students get Cs and work thier asses of earning them.

Tough, but fair grader. Teaches class in lecture style. Makes you work for your grade and I very much like that. Must Read Texts To Pass!! Very Helpful and gives extra credit. If you have a question he will know the answer. Also, do not b.s. in your Term paper, he sees right through it and it will cost you severely. It's college, Show him Respect.

If you're not a history major stay away from this guy. This was the least enjoyable history course that I have ever taken. He teaches in seminar fashion in a very dry tone. Lots of reading required which is ok but he expects you to read 200 pages a week and to absorb all of the info immediately.

I definitely did not enjoy his class. Way too much reading for a low level culture class, and his lectures don't help at all. He speaks in a very boring tone that makes you zone out easily. Hard grader on essays and tests - doesn't really give partial credit and only curved one test. Find another professor if you can

Reading load was a bit much for a entry level class.Exams were not too hard, he gave helpful study guides. the major pitfall of this class is the essay that requires you to read 40 pages on art analysis and find a way to get to a meuseum in baltimore. it can't be done earlier in the semester due to not having enough knowlegde.
Interesting class but crazy amount of reading(well over 100pp some days). Hard grader on essays, I'm an A student but got Cs on papers (B in class)

Writing prompt and participation both worth 25%, midterm worth 120 points (25%), 7-8 pages comparative book review worth 80 points (20%), and final worth 120 points (30%).  midterm or final included 5  identifications, one primary source interpretation, and one essay.  Identifications  (50 points), primary source  (20 points), and essay (50 points)

Knows a lot about Japan.  Lots of reading, random writing prompt. Hesitant when lecture sometimes paused a little bit long during lecture to see if students had comments or questions sometimes just a loss for words.  Used a lot of visual iamges from travel to japan as an illustrative technique in lecture.
He's okay. His exams are the tough part, class averages are around 70% but everyone works their butt off for it.He does gives extra assignments so make sure you are always checking blackboard.
Very interested and enthusiastic about East Asian Civ, if a bit dry when lecturing. Writing assignments were not too difficult, though the reading load was perhaps a bit much for a 100-level class.

Definitely one of my favourite professors. Paying attention during class discussions is extremely helpful as well as reading the assigned readings. Doing journal entries is very helpful in maintaining good grades. The final exam was take home. You can tell that he really knows what he's talking about and feels passionately about the subject :).

Wonderful! He is doing his job... too many students give him grief for making them actually work. Professors like this increase the standing of the university. If you don't want to work, get out of school!

Great Professor. I don't know why everyone screams about the difficulty of his tests. I got a 108 on the first one. Just do the read and take good notes. Not the most exiciting speaker, but has a hard job covering 10,000 years of history in one semester.

This class takes a lot of work for a 100 level class. Vaporis is a nice enough man, but he lectures in a very monotone voice that puts one to sleep. The curve at the beginning tends to be generous but realize that for every test you need to work that much harder to beat the next curve. The few writing assignments he gives are easy.
Very dry, somewhat intimidating. Prescribes busywork, even in upper-level classes. His only redeeming feature is his name, which is awesome ("Constantine Vaporis"?!).

Took his accelerated class over the summer and found it very challenging yet informative. got alot out of the four weeks. Very approachable and really knew his East Asian history. Test are very difficult. Ended up getting a "B" in the class. Alot of reading but if you are a history major the reading only increases as you take more upper level class

So the tests weren't easy and it was a tougher than average 100 level, but history classes do not get easier as you go on. There wasn't really that much to read. If you bothered to do the reading tests weren't so bad! He is a great professor especially considering the task at hand, Asian history from beginning to the 20th century.

I took this class during the summer. all we did was watch japanese movies about hiroshima and the culture of the samurai. He didn't lecture except for in the 1st class but thats about it. There are a lot of readings to do for this class. There are only 2 exams that were 2 questions each. Basically if u got to class you should be ok.

Tests are RIDICUOSLY HARD. there is no reason why his tests incorporate as much detailed and unrelavent material as they do, it's not fair to his students who are now struggling to do well in a 100 level class

Like all the others, I have to say, this class is very demanding and there's a lot of reading involved.  Then, when you're in class, I dunno...  I ADORE history, and to me anyways, he makes it boring.  Talks kind of monitone, doesn't fully engage the class.  And, yeah, the tests are REALLY hard.
The amount of information the students were expected to absorb for tests sucked.
obviously he knew his stuff and was interested in it, but it was too hard
taught a 100 level like it was a 300 level.  very demanding. nice,but hard

She's not awful, she's very passive aggressive but she's an easy grader if you do the work. No textbook but I did have to buy a play. Her expectations are clear, and assignments make sense but in class activities feel juvenile and unnecessary. Just say you like puppets and she'll like you.

This class was subjectively difficult for me due to my social anxiety (acting in front of the class), however, Prof. Searls was very understanding and helpful. The class involves memorizing lines, performing, and analyzing 3 plays to be read outside of class. Note that you have to wear an athletic/studio outfit, so you can't dress up.
this class is all bout being able to analyze plays. Just read the plays and be engaged in the discussions and youll do well. Colette makes it very easy and interesting. Awesome class to take
If you have never been to the theatre or need to fulfill a requirement for your major even if a theatre major - this class rocks!

Assigns lots of reading, but you can tell she's passionate about the material. Wants to engage students in class discussion. Don't take this class if you don't like to read plays or form your own ideas.
I genuinely learn something is his class !!! The way he makes 2 hours class engaged is impressive

Probably one of the best professors that I've had at UMBC. Not only is he knowledgeable but he cares about students very much. Definitely recommend taking him for any classes that you can. The semester did consist of three tests and a group project but he's very clear on what is going to be on the test and the project was straightforward

Prof. Coakley is probably the best professor I've ever had. He's extremely experienced in his field and cares a lot about the success of his students. Your grade is based off 3 exams (he tells you exactly what will be on them, no surprises & if you study you will do well) + 1 group project, which is just a paper, & no homework.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Coakley is very understanding, and cares for his students. Sometimes he can ramble on about things that are not necessary to know for exams. It is very important to take notes during his lectures. Class only had 3 exams and 1 group project. This course was lecture heavy and there's no homework which is great!
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Accessible outside class--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He's an amazing professor. I took him for HAPP 405 during the summer. The material was really easy. I will definitely recommend him.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Group projects--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: He is a real Gem to UMBC! His Marketing class consists of three exams, one group project, and participation. He teaches from the experiences of working in the real world and tells us how to view the two sides of any problem. His class is an easy A! He is very inspiring. I would highly recommend this professor for Marketing 425!
Very chill, very nice, very respectful! Best professor I've had. Easy class. Interesting discussions! Exams are easy! He tells you the topics that will be on there!

He is Amazing! Come to class, pay attention to the lecture and you're guaranteed an A. One group project only but easy if you have good group members. Take him if you have the chance, you will not regret! I loved him!!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Great professor and great class. Definitely recommend

One of my favorite HAPP professors at UMBC! He tells you what is going to be on tests, which is the holy grail to any college course. His lectures are very informative as he has a lot of experience in the health/marketing field!

He is the nicest and friendliest professor I have ever had! You can tell he really cares about his students. There are 3 exams and he will clearly tell you what to know. The lowest grade I received was a high A and I studied for maybe 2-3 hours. One group project and you only need to write about 1.5 per person. Our group got a 100%. Easiest A!

Best HAPP professor ever. He's funny, caring, interesting, and a great teacher. He has a ton of real-life experience in health administration, so he really knows what he's talking about. His tests are tough but you'll get an A if you study. I wish he taught every HAPP class. Definitely take a class with him if you get a chance.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--GROUP PROJECTS--Tests are tough

reviews.comment: He is the nicest professor. He makes everything you need to know on the 3 exams (MC and 2 out of 3 short answers to choose from) clear and there is only one group project that requires each person to write about 1.5-2 pages. EASIET upper level mgmt.

Professor Coakley is the best professor I've ever had in my whole entire life. he is very helpful and he would do no matter what to help his students succeed. I hope that he teaches all my other courses.

Professor Coakley is the modern day Yoda For HAPP majors, He is the best teacher I have ever had at UMBC. I'm taking 3 more classes with him. Highly recommended. Listen and pay attention to his notes, he is extremely fair in his tests.
Best teacher I have had my entire college career hands down.

Take every class you can possibly take with Coakley. He is incredibly smart and will go out of his way to help any student with anything. He says his part time job is writing recommendation letters for students, so he is a great person to know! Not easy material, but definitely an enjoyable class.

Arguably the best instructor within the HAPP program. Immensely knowledgeable and highly qualified. Urges all students to participate, but never puts you on the spot. 3 exams (including final) and 2 case studies. Before every exam, holds a review where he tells you exactly which topics to study. Do that, and you'll do very well every time. Take it!

I see students here saying Paul Comitz should be fired, and I 100% agree. He's rude, unhelpful, and dismissive, and acts like he doesn't care. He just reads off slides, gets annoyed when asked questions, and expects us to already know everything which defeats the purpose of taking the class. Very unprofessional. Seriously, avoid at all costs.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Plz Avoid this class if you can. Paul Comitz is rude, dismissive, and reads straight from the slides. Asks are met with frustration, and he often cuts students off. Grading is harsh, and the environment is unwelcoming. One of the worst teaching experiences I've had. He's makin UMBC IT Dep. image look bad and for that Paul Comitz shud b FIRED !!!

reviews.comment: Tbh idk who made him Prof. he don't deserve this job. Shows up late, reads from slides, never returns grades. Gets annoyed if you ask for help. I met him in person few times, I felt like I was bothering him by being in class. Just don't take him. I met him in person few times, Very Very Rude man. Paul Comitz is By far the WORST person / Instructor.

reviews.comment: Always has an attitude in class. Rude when u ask questions, never replies to emails, and explains things poorly. Class is disorganized and he acts like helping students is a burden. Do yourself a favor never take this prof. Avoid at all costs.

reviews.comment: Paul.C, is very unresponsive to emails and does'nt handle student questions well. When students ask for help or clarification, he often reacts with frustration or sarcasm, which creates an uncomfortable learning environment. It felt very unprofessional, and it made it hard to succeed in the class. I would recommend avoiding this course if you can.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The class was hybrid but we never met in person until the final exam. The group project rubric was so unclear and vague, then he started to take off points because we didn't put comments in the right places. Mind you, we added comments when suitable. I barely learned anything from his lectures. Shout out to Udemy fr.

self-taught class cuz you meet every other week. expects you to code what he barely taught. Very few things in the grade: hws, 3 discussions, 2 exams, and a group project; not much room to struggle. project rubric was unclear. revealed the final date just a week before it occurred. don't have a strong java foundation? expect to struggle
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This class is essentially self taught unless you are extremely proficient in Java I would not recommend this class. Homeworks can take hours, exam are extremely difficult and he is incredibly boring to listen to during the lectures. The final project is also extremely unclear and difficult. Likely one of the worst professors in the entire IS dept.

This class should basically count as a self taught course considering while you do meet virtually he expects a lot from the assignments even if you have barely gone over it in class. I tried to set up an office hours with him because I needed help and he never responded. I went to IS147 tutoring for hw and he still marks it as wrong. Don't take.

tldr: RUN

if yall are struggling and are weak coders, don't take this prof. the set up for this class is alternating asynch and online. he goes through a billion slides, doesnt really teach, makes u code, and expects u to learn. if yall cant learn by yourself (and be honest), look elsewhere

Worst Java Prof. He never reviews anything before a quiz. He piles topics on top of topics and then expects you to do assignments on topics he has not taught. This is not an introductory class, especially with the way this professor teaches. We felt like we were teaching ourselves Java. He takes points for anything! Extremely confusing!

save yourself - passing this class will be a labor of love. Prof seems like a good guy but he's a meh professor because he's hard to get a hold of outside of class and the assignments can be confusing. He's specific about grading.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: He's nice inside class but he is verrryyyy rigid when it comes to grading. Expect a chunk points off on your assignment over miniscule errors or details. It is hard to succeed in his class, but possible if you grind. He will also randomly cancel lecture or do async with little to no update sometimes, but it is to be expected as an older gentleman.
His grading policy isn't clear. he doesn't take attendance but being in class is important. he is okay but  VERY TOUGH GRADER.
The class was okay.

The class and concept are hard if you have no experience in coding but he tries his best to make it understandable. He is very nice and encouraging to have you participate. He is also good at explaining and giving real-life examples. Half of your grade is weekly HWs, the other half is 4 (online and open note) quizzes and one group project.

Great professor for IS 147. I was not familiar with Java before, but he taught this as a great Intro class. Homework was not difficult to complete and hes a lenient grader. Quizzes were short, open book/open note, and fairly easy if you review the material. One final project, but it is not too bad if you have an idea of what you're doing.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Graded by few things--Participation matters

reviews.comment: The class is challenging and you get to hands-on learn Python and PHP, but the professor is an absolute jerk. If you miss one assignment (during a pandemic!), you will be criticized as having a poor approach to graduate school, along with a bunch of other unprofessional "advice." He then makes errors and recycles old material. Nice approach...

Terrible professor for an online class. You learn everything from w3schools and the rest of the internet. Also makes you do a group project despite it being an online class so get used to working with random strangers who will work on a completely different schedule than you since this is an online class and they're traveling.

Weekly assignments are practical and instructive. Course materials are all online and a bit disorganized. It's easy to miss something important. Keep in mind that the two exams (a midterm and a final) account for a large portion of your grade, are very terminology-heavy and don't directly relate to the weekly assignments.

If you're just starting to learn how to code, take this professor. All his quizzes are open note and the project is with a partner. If you need help, he will assist you until you understand. He's an amazing professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: He is the best Java instructor at UMBC. If you have the option, take it with him.

Comitz is one of my favorite profs of all time! He really knows his Java and as long as you complete the homeworks, show up to class and put forth decent effort you will get an A. Exams are online, open book, and pretty short.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Even though the class is really long, Dr. Comitz doesn't usually use up all the time. He teaches all the material thoroughly without feeling like he's rushing it. You can tell how passionate he is about Java and coding in general through his lectures. He is a lenient grader and you will get an A if you show him that you're trying.

Dr. Comitz knows his Java. You will be ahead of other IS 147 students if you take him. If you stay after class to talk to him, he will help you with whatever you are struggling with. As long as you are trying and doing the homework, he will give you credit for it.

He is a great IS147 professor.  Your grade consists of homework assignments, 4 quizzes, and a project. There is no final. Also, all quizzes are open note. He is very knowledgeable and will help you understand concepts if you're struggling. He also emphasizes team work and so you work on all of the homework assignments and the project with a partner

Java intro course. Professor was condescending. Treated less skilled students as if they were wasting his time. Hardly welcoming for a major that accepts undergrads without experience in CS or IS. Felt disrespected at times. Grading was based off of one major project and about 5 or so quizzes. If you can't code, learn quickly.

Prof. Comitz was very knowledgable. The material being taught was also very interesting. However, he is quick to make assumptions and judgments of students and will talk down to them even if it is not deserved.

There are 4 quizzes, weekly homework assignments, & a final project. All are very reasonable. He's a nice guy and a clear lecturer, but he can be kind of boring. There are no surprises on quizzes which are open note & open Internet. This is an interesting class, but if you're not a good programmer, do NOT take it.

He is a good professor. There is no textbook, you learn as you do work on hws. He is very knowledgeable. His exams are short (10 questions) and each question is 1% of your grade. Don't worry though, you are allowed to look at the internet/your notes during exams. I did the hw, attended class, I passed easily that way.

Great professor, very experienced and personable. He actually wants to teach students and have them be successful.  There's no final exam, instead a final project that you work on during the semester.  As long as you don't procrastinate on the project, you will do fine, assuming you have the programming background required for the course.

Nice guy. The class will be hard if you and your partner don't know Java very well. He's a lenient grader, but the assignments will be hard for those who haven't coded in a while or aren't confident in their abilities. Don't overthink the quizzes, because most questions aren't tricky.

Worst teachers I ever had. There are 4 quizzes, homework, and then a final project. Quizzes are a big part of your grade. The quizzes can be hard and tricky even with open book. He knows his java but can not teach very well. If you already know java then go ahead an take it otherwise use a different class for your programing requirement

Great professor, he's a very experienced java programmer and knows his material well.  Attendance is mandatory (graded), the homework assignments aren't bad and the project is reasonable provided you start early.  You do a lot of programming, while the concepts are basic, this is not an intro to java course  (reconsider if you have zero java exp.)

Comitz is such a knowledgeable Java programmer that he fails to realize that his 147 students, for the most part, have never written a line of code in their life. I came into the class with no prior knowledge and I felt like he moved too quickly. He grades fairly, although he said I would get a B, and he gave me a C.

Also you do need to spend 3-4 hours outside of class working on projects every week. You don't have to get them perfect to get full credit, though. You MUST read the chapters before class or the slides and the projects might seem somewhat confusing. Don't let the easy first projects lull you into a false sense of security. Keep reading!

Last poster apparently didn't take into account tests and quizzes. Paul's grading system is weird, but if you show him you're actually trying and stay after class to talk with him about homework, he'll be lenient with grading. Quizzes are open book. He sometimes comes off as cocky, but overall a nice guy and good teacher. Knows his Java.

I worked my butt off in this class. He grades using checks, check pluses and check minuses. I got decent grades on the quizes, and "check pluses" on all the programming projects, which to me is at least a B. I checked my grades when they were posted, and I got a C in the class. I guess a "check plus" means a C and that projects mean NOTHING
The exams can be challenging and a fair amount of work outside the classroom is required. I learned a great deal - but I worked for it.

I took his 310 class a few semesters ago. His tests were hard, you need to read the book and study hard or you're not getting past a C. He assigns a project you need to present in class. Its anoying but it can help your grade. Again, it's not hard to get a C, but you need to work for that B.
Good teacher.  The mid term and final were open note and open book.  The hw is assigned weekly and graded.  It was an easy way to get points.  Group project is assigned and was fairly easy.
Comitz is a good professor and great person. Tests are challenging, but Comitz's interest, knowledge and enthusiasm of the subject make the class worth it.  I def recommend him.
No Comments
This is basically a teach yourself class. Test are hard with multiple answer per problem. I suggest passing him by.

You definitely have to read the book & teach yourself the material if you don't already know this stuff.  The definitions & explanations in the book make a whole lot more sense than his.  He works for Boeing & he knows his stuff, but not that great of a teacher.  However, he doesn't require alot of work (2 tests, 1 paper) & he's better than Redding

If you have the opportunity to pass this guy by, I would do so.  He tests Grad-School style with any number of multiple choice answers being right answers.  This makes easy material relatively difficult.  Class is hideously boring, and he is terribly dorky.  He teaches all 2.5 hours while 1.5 hours is review.  Just don't take anything with this guy

This class was one of the easiest i have ever taken...anyone with a fair amount of computer knowledge will do just fine with a little studying...i have an above average computer knowledge base and i got A's on all of the tests with zero studying done
This is a challenging course. The professor puts his heart and soul into it - this comes through in the lectures. They are enthusiastic and high energy.
This professor is a confuesd man and bit to dramatic and agreek (which he's proud to be) exams are frustrating and class is boring

Paul Comitz has his ups and downs, but overall is a good professor.  He teaches 1 day per week, and goes the entire 3 hours.  He is extremily thorough, and quite knowledgable...but he will force you to participate...it gets old after a while.  Only real bad thing about him is he doesn't give a structured syll. and doesn't respond to e-mails.

Very easy class, don't even need the textbook. Just return it and keep doing the assignments until you get a 100. I finished the whole class by the end of spring break so make sure you don't miss any assignments and you're good for the whole semester.
Somehow takes her forever to upload our final grades when the entire class is automated and she doesnt have to grade anything. Don't email her cuz she doesn't want to hear it

This class is very easy, the professor essentially doesn't exist. Unlimited attempts for every assignment. No actual learning is required. The textbook contains all the assignments and are directly from text. Copy and paste in textbook search bar.

The professor does not want you to contact or email her, but she was very understanding when I had a mid-semester injury. I enjoyed this class because it was entirely online. Everything was super easy. Just take the quizzes and tests until you get a perfect score.  I got this class done by October, and it opened up early in August.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: Just pretend she doesnt exist because she repeats 20 times in the syllabus to not contact her. The class is very easy. You can easily do any assignment without looking at the notes at all.
This professor really does not want you emailing her. Luckily, you don't really need to. Class is super easy and you get unlimited attempts on most stuff. You get out of it what you put into it.

I loved this class because it was all online & you just read the book and grades automatically pull from Cengage (you can do multiple attempts to get a 100). No interaction with the professor, you just learn on your own at your own pace but everything was pretty straightforward.

There will be no interaction with the professor for this class. I found out the name of the professor on the last week of the semester just to leave this rate for her class here... Easy credits and not much learning.

Not much of a professor. Since this class is online, she basically sets it up as asynchronous and gives no extensions whatsoever. She does not seem to care about her students because she directs them to Cenage support if we had any questions at all and basically makes it clear in the syllabus she doesn't want you emailing her.

don't take late work but class was easy and the book is expensive but if you have the book you don't need the lecture but if you don't have the book watch the lectures because she literally paraphrase the book.

It was taught online. If you had any questions about the topic (such as wondering why you got a question wrong), she would tell you to contact Cengage support, and wouldn't answer much. Despite this, the topics were relatively easy, and several assignments had unlimited attempts. Everything is in the textbook, so read that before doing assignments.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Very easy class, just a bunch of busy work, but prof. is passive aggressive. On the first day (and multiple other times) she sent out an email basically saying don't ask her for help on anything bc she doesn't know how to fix it. I don't know why she got paid. There were no lectures and all homework was done through Cengage which was auto-graded.
Literally the easiest A ever. Its all online and all the chapters are very easy. Take this.

Dr. Cronin is an amazing professor. He is passionate in what he does and is an awesome lecturer. Couple small papers and 1 very long review paper. Exams were fully written and really tough. No textbook though, so everything is from his lectures. If you're up for the challenge, take his class!

I want to be like Dr Cronin when I grow up. He's brilliant in his preferred field of research, sharp and enthusiastic even when stepping outside of it. Every lesson with him was engaging and in-depth, less like a class and more like a field trip even though we never left our seats. Discussions always came with a wonderfully dry sense of humor.
