Her feedback always makes me feel better no matter what. She is NOTHING like any other professor I've had before. I learned so much from her class. She is the best of the best!

Prof. Johnson is amazing, she gives individualized feedback and wants you to get an A in the course. the course is not bad at all, theres a discussion everyweek along with reading the txtbook and taking a short quiz. There are 4 major papers and you can get a letter grade bump on each if you choose to do the extra credit.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: You basically read a chapter from the text and then post on the discussion board. She grades the discussion board and you also have a quiz on the chapter. If you read the chapter, you should do fine. There are three papers throughout the semester and a final paper. Her grading isn't too strict, as long as you follow the grading rubric.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--SO MANY PAPERS

reviews.comment: I had Mrs. Johnson for both AGNG 200 + 320. Weekly quizzes and discussion boards, and a few essays-the classes are heavy writing, so if you're not a good writer don't take it! Not difficult unless you slack or wait until last minute to complete the assignments. Mrs. J actually reads all of your posts/essays and provides exceptional feedback.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--SO MANY PAPERS--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: He wants everyone in class to be present/respectful to other classmates as there are a lot of discussions and sharing personal stories and if he sees you distracted he will call you out. He can be passive aggressive but the amount of things you can learn is great. (TA completely dipped so we didn't get grades on time) he's really not that bad

Dr. Knight specializes in orienting sophomore psych students to how humans posture for out-group politics. Show up with course material to discuss about you won't get filtered. He values introspection and places emphasis on recollection in situ.
DO NOT take him, grades harshly, and will be months late to grade all assignments; you will have no feedback to improve. Teaches absolutely nothing in class.

Attendance is required; it is 25% of your grade. Material is self-taught, and the class period is meant for discussion.
Dr. Knight is an excellent professor, very funny. He ain't here to play around; be prepared to be challenged and for in-depth self-reflection. Don't be scared to ask questions and attend his office hours.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Group projects

reviews.comment: He isn't the worst teacher at UMBC, to be clear. He is very passionate and personable outside of class, but is so strict and particular (no late work, no devices, controlling discussions) it ruins the class. Outsourced most grading to the TA, who was AWOL. Again, not a bad person, but runs the class terribly. Avoid if you can 4 a better PSYC class!

Terrible professor! Don't take him! Take any other professor!!

1) Randomly goes off in the middle of class. You can't talk or use your phone/laptop in this class, even if its for taking notes/something important.
2) Takes two months to grade assignments that have a MAJOR impact on your grade.
3) Never responds to emails.
4) So inconsistent.
He was so interesting but very odd. Tends to rant a lot rather than teach. Easy and interesting class if you attend class and participate !

Avoid this psych prof! Belittling, insensitive, and doesn't care about serve personal problems. His ego matches the fat head he has. Find a better class! A professor has never made feel like i'm at the brink of taking my own life like he did. How is he able to teach psychology when he's a psychopath. He needs to check into a mental hospital STAT.

Extremely neurotic and emotional, it took him 2 months to grade a paper I worked rly hard on, just for him to give me a D. He is the kind of professor who will leave you .01 points below the next up letter grade due to his own ego. Not sure why he still has a job here, he lies constantly and all the positive reviews are obviously him (very weird)

Pretty cool classes (if you read). Class engagement is very important, so make sure to contribute. He can get quite emotional, so make sure you choose your words wisely. He misinterprets what students say, and if you try to correct it, good luck. I don't regret taking the class, but the environment can be anxiety-inducing. Still learned a lot!

Dr.Knight can be tough, but the class can also be fun. Great discussions. He is a tough grader and is never really specific about what to do to improve your grade, he often leaves the grading to the TA's. Advice- do the reading, participate in the class, and do NOT pull out your phone.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Everyone must understand the serious nature of interacting with this professor-  highly sensitive to feedback, takes everything personally, leads to emotional reactions (very disruptive and unprofessional) STAY AWAY from his class. If you're put in an uncomfortable situation w/ him avoid escalation and handle the matter privately outside of class.

I joined late due to a death in the family, he gave 0s anyway even with proof. Marked an assignment I submitted correctly as a 0, refused to fix it when I pointed out his mistake. He Ignored all office hour requests so nothing was communicated & resolved. Talks down to students and creates a hostile vibe. I dropped the class- do not recommend.

He has an ego, is passive aggressive, gets frustrated easily, and wastes lots of class time. He hated when people used the chat in an online class… Someone with a speech impediment answered a question using the chat and he got mad at them and ignored it. He got called out for it and double-downed because of his ego and mindset. Bad professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--So many papers

reviews.comment: I loved having Dr. Knight as a professor! I will say he sometimes gets off topic during lecture so make sure to read but his is very knowledgeable about the content and Psychology in general. Definitely go to his office hours the door is always open, I spent countless hours there asking him questions about how to progress in a career for psych!

The classroom environment was anxiety provoking, intense, and sad. He barley teaches and just rants about something random. He is always angry or on edge. Avoid taking a class with him if you can. He makes everything unnecessarily stressful and difficult.

This professor will constantly call out students for either being on their phones or even taking notes. Nothing on the syllabus states that having your phone or laptop in class to take notes during discussion is an issue. Missing one day of class could result in your grade going down by 3 letters. The class environment is depressing and intense.

Worst professor I've ever had by a landslide. Aggressive, insulting, says very little of substance during lecture, has ridiculous grading criteria like having to respond to discussion boards on two different days, and leaves his TA to do all of the grading. Papers are 30% of the grade and are not graded generously at all. Do not take this class.

Would sit in class feeling like I was being hunted for sport.Anything can make him go on an angry rant,will accuse students of cheating for no reason, laugh about making students cry,end a class early because he didnt like our questions.This class is basically self taught because half the lecture is him feeding his ego with no way to ask questions.

From my personal experience Dr. Knight has been a very inspiring professor and makes you think critically about life in general. All you do is read the textbook and do the 5 question quiz and just come in ready to participate in class. Dr. Knight puts in the same effort as you do, if you participate and try he will do his best to help you!

Most egoistical man, calls out students for checking the time. Boasted about making students cry. Will rant about phones/random subjects for 40 mins. 6 years into college, first time I have ever truly despised a professor. Class started with almost 30 students and ended with 13. He reads these ratings and talks about them. Do better Dr. Knight.

I really tried to not take anything he did personal like other students did but he made it extremely impossible.He is always accusing students of cheating, he is extremely hard grader, makes student email both him & TA, makes you feel dumb and question yourself.
absolutely horrible.

I really enjoyed Dr. Knight's Clinical Psychotherapy class! There are definitely lots of papers and a VERY large group project, but he is very knowledgable and is more than happy to answer questions. Just make sure you are  NOT slacking off! Always read the chapters before class because it is a discussion instead of lecture. He wants participation!

I don't write reviews typically, but this time its different. Prof. Knight is short fused, egotistical, and will aggressively talk you down when challenged. His class is easy if you keep your head down. He's willing to fail students based off "interpretations" of cheating he has. I write not in anger. But to warn you all. Avoid him at ALL costs.

reviews.comment: This professor was very difficult to deal with. Don't bother emailing him. Wouldn't recommend asking questions either. He usually ends up giving a condescending response while belittling you. if you ever have this professor... good luck!

I have an open case of harassment against him. Disrespectful, belittling, & condescending. Semester is over & he is still sending class-wide emails complaining about students & accusing us of cheating. I asked him to stop emailing me. He replied with implications of me cheating & said I was being passive aggressive. Literally unbelievable behavior.

Becomes irate from students making a group chat or study sessions
If you need clarification on assignments, don't ask in class or he will become angry; he will tell you to email him instead
It will take him a week to email you back and it will explain very little
Will not get past the opening PowerPoint slide for at least 20 minutes 
Rants

reviews.comment: He is rude and not fair ...he doesnt respond to emails and he is a terrible professet
This class was beyond stressful and triggered feelings of wanting to commit suicide. What a horrible experience.

reviews.comment: Expect to do a lot of self teaching at home. Calls out students in front of the class EVERY week. Very rude when you email him. He won't answer your question and will instead tell you to schedule an appointment, no matter how simple the question is. Literally created this account simply to warn other students to stay away.

His lectures are okay but I do not suggest taking this professor! He has no empathy and can be very rude, he has not been helpful with any issues I have come to him about, when I have had difficulty with the instructions on his syllabus and emailed him about it he has responded very sarcastically. Very difficult teacher to communicate with.

Just plain rude and disrespectful. Attacks viewpoints that differ from his own and calls out students. Very intimidating and impossible to reach via email (he literally replies back basically saying not to email him). Grading criteria is unclear and always changing. Only 4 assignments in the entire class so far have gotten 100%...stay away from him

Has a very condescending attitude and spends most of the class going on random tangents rather than teaching the actual lesson. Calls students out in front of everyone and will threaten to put you out of class if you respond back. Doesn't accept late work and won't assist with any assignments via email. For anyone taking his class - good luck.

Dr. Knight doesn't give clear instructions for assignments, doesn't meet deadlines outlined on the syllabus or set in class, and will never apologize or recognize he has caused any problems. He returned a major paper to me to revise with less than a 24 hour turn around (4 days after the syllabus states) and would not given an extension.

Ratemyprofessors are really lucky I cannot say what I really want to say about this man but never ever take this man as you teacher. This man has lied to me plenty of time and waits until the end of the semester to grade. A lot of hw and other stuff. This man has completely made me lose motivation to keep going in those classes. DON'T TAKE HIM.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Participation matters--So many papers

reviews.comment: I wish this man wasn't a professor, never has clear instructions, literally rude, had a demeaning way of carrying himself and it frankly stands in the way of my education, he is always making excuses and goes on random tangents. Participate, talk! he liked that and try your best

Dr. Knight is very condescending, he talks in circles and does not answer questions directly. Assignments are always due at 5pm, does not answer his email past 5pm. He does not accept any late work at all. He does lecture but does not actually cover material. I disliked everything from his personality to his communication to his teaching method.

Personality- he is unclear, contradicting, he calls out and argues w/ students, on day 2 he quizzed us on the syllabus, thinks he's funny but ._. HES INTIMATING. I was anxious and terrified. I love psych, love to learn, and put as much effort I can, but I dreaded going to class

Dr. Knight was an excellent professor. His classroom setting is very different from the typical class. He uses the textbook, but its for taking tests. This is not a testing class! Its about relating to the material and using it, especially in papers. Read his feedback and use it to get better. I know that I have. Thanks Dr. Knight

Professor Knight was by far the worst professor I have ever had. I really tried to look for the best but he was unprofessional, inaccessible, and honestly incompetent. He changed deadlines multiple times, did not respond to student emails, went on strike mid semester and stopped holding lectures... didn't know that was possible.

Dr. Knight is straight forward & blunt with his classroom expectations. He encourages students to participate. Be prepared to answer his favorite question: How does this resonate with you? Overall, I think Dr. Knight is fair & practical. He is clear on his expectations but if you have questions don't be afraid to reach out! Also, do all assignments

Material's useful but you teach yourself with it. doesn't cover things, 12 tests- 10 MC on the book, websites etc. video worksheets + write papers, teacher is inaccessible, doesn't reply to emails, TA LITERALLY does EVERYTHING his criteria and guidelines aren't clear.

The class material is OK. You learn some things but it is self taught. All the assignments and quizzes are online and the TA grades everything. The worst part about the class is the professor. I had stress and anxiety walking in the classroom because you never know who he is going to put on blast. that day. I feel like he could make a student cry.

He is the worst professor ever!!!! He argues with students, waists class time and it always has to be his way. Do not take his class if you actually want to learn the material. You will have to self teach.

I signed up for his senior seminar class at upstate. Everyone in the class was failing but two people. He doesnt teach & I have yet to learn anything. Hes way too cocky for his own good & decided to argue with me in-front of the entire class b/c I saved my PowerPoint in email. His seminar class is paper & presentation heavy & does not care.

worst professors. He never teaches the material. In fact he waisted the whole semester inviting the library, academic center etc. to show basic skills and finishEd the rest of the class asking what are you taking from this class. He gives points for answering and he asks what are you bring from last class . You will have to self teach to pass
One of the worst professors I've had. He spends a lot of time talking about himself and he is arrogant. He always wants to be right and his TA takes forever to grade assignments.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Worse professor ever! Dont take any of his classes. He is passive agressive and gets mad if you dont answer correct. Im a good student and eager to learn but he made it so hard for me to learn anything.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: great class! great professor!

I really liked Dr. Knight's class! As long as you go to class and actually put in effort it really shouldn't be a problem. He doesn't put up with BS, but it's clear that he cares about his students and wants to see them succeed. He doesn't allow late work though, so be careful to get your assignments in on time.

He doesn't post grades on a timely manner and it's very stressful. You will literally not know what your actual grade is until the very end. Any questions or requests you ask will be denied with the excuse of how he's too busy and has no time for any of that. He is extremely rude and unhelpful. I got an A in the end but was not worth all the hassle
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Don't take class with him if you don't need to. I attended the first 3 classss, after which I stopped b/c going to class was pointless. This professor does not teach. A few students and I worked our way through the book together. He doesn't answer Qs and he is rude. He also cancelled class four times including cutting class short bc we "looked dry"

Dr. Knight is rude to students that disagree &has this demeaning habit of clapping his hands in your face when talking to you. All semester my grade on Blackboard was a B & he assured us that it was accurate. On Dec 22 after the final he changed all our grades by making an assignment that had been worth 50p & worth 15 & my grade dropped to a C.

Ok, its Spring semester and I am taking Professor Knight's PSy 380 class on Personality. Let me just say this is the second class and I see there's going to problem! He basically is not giving any lectures, asking the class to give their opinions and not confirming whether or not its right! Basically we are teaching ourselves! Not happy!!

I will never take a class with him again.  He wasn't able to teach the class the information, and towards the end of the semester basically gave up and had us teach each other.  After the majority of the class went to the program director he ended up making some changes, which is probably the only reason anyone passed.

i would disagree with the post below and its funny how little of valu is actually offered, mmm makes you think. truth is Donald is a nice person who is finishing up his phD so as a teacher he lacks teacher skills, its really that simple at least that was my experience. provides little guidance, puts the blame on you and its his way or the highway.

LOVE! This professor is so funny and a great person :) responds to emails in minutes and keeps class interesting. Not a difficult class at all and taught me valuable life skills. Extremely passionate about psychology and willing to help you. So glad I took this class, what a wonderful person Dr. Knight is. Highly recommend!

the professor is a likable person but sometimes gets too passionate about what he believes or what an ideal student should be. for a 200 level course you will find yourself asking why things are made hard for no reason, at least that was my experience  if you like trial by error learning then he can be a fit  for you otherwise i would NOT recommend

This has been my favorite class at UMBC. Dr. Knight is a great teacher and he makes sure you learn the material. This class was fun and educational (as classes should be)! I would take a class with Dr. Knight again in a heartbeat!
Best class of my semester. He made the text easy to understand. If you are taking the psych 230 class i recommend you take it with Professor Knight!

This was honestly my favorite class of the semester. You don't have to read the book at all as long as you keep up with the online work and pay attention in class. You can get up to 3% on your grade worth of extra credit by participating in psych studies. He's a really down to earth professor.

The way he did his psych100 class was "hybrid" core learning (all learning essentially) outside of class, then real-life applicationsexamples and clarification in class. Basically class is a waste of time unless you're confused, but you have to go to get clicker credit and group participation credit. HW can all be googled. Tests pretty easy. 810.

I loved Dr. Knight. I hated waking up for this class, but he was really funny and he made up for it. The class is a lot of reading, if we had reading guides my life would've been so much easier. The hybrid class makes this class time consuming, but the material is interesting! It's a lot of group work though, so be prepared.

Dr. Knight is a fantastic lecturer. He gets your attention with his charisma that keeps you focused and oriented in class. Decent amount of online work and the extra credit is great, giving you the chance to earn 3% to your grade. That's a huge grade booster and the difference between that A and B. Great professor.

I have this class at 8am, but it wasn't so bad because Dr.Knight is very awake and energetic in the morning. He is hilarious and I'm glad I didn't drop the class! This class is a hybrid course so exams and activities are online. In class we mostly discuss, its easygoing.

Very energetic and funny man. This class was very easy due to exams being administered online, but YMMV. Class discussions are a treat, and he often has activities planned for interacting with other classmates. If you just need this for the culture credit, go for it. There's some genuinely interesting material, and this is not a difficult course.

I really enjoyed taking this course due to the class discussions which cause the entire class to be engaged. I honestly feel that this class should be mandatory for every college student. You really grow as a human being. The professor created an environment that fostered meaningful discussions. The class was engaged and this was an evening course.

HORRIBLE PROFESSOR!!! DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS. The tests are straight from the book yet he gets upset if you skip class or space out. His lectures are completely useless. The final is cumulative on a 400 page book! He quizzes on the smallest, non important details!(BTW I got a "B" in the class, for all those who think i'm just mad about my grade)
Professor's assignments are primarily mindless busywork.

Reader, I have never seen such a condescending man who has no regard or respect for his students. He treats his class like the Hunger Games, classifying students by competency. He demotivates students by asserting that only a handful of students will succeed in the class, only for whom he will provide recommendations and career opportunities.

Makes class unnecessarily tough. Makes his view clear on how your competency on finance is solely related to your test scores. Very smart guy but makes tests unreasonably difficult and overcomplicated. Would avoid taking if you can

reviews.comment: He's just meh. Comes off condescending. Makes the class way harder than it needs to be. No textbook, you gotta study off his notes. They're an image of a PDF so you can't even CTRL+F to search for terms while studying which is annoying. For INTRO to finance, this class is very hard coming from someone who had straight A's in Econ classes until this
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: It was a hyrbid class so you only see him 3 times for exams. Really nice guy though, kinda rambles but he's very nice and encouraging, makes you want to do well in the course. Studying for the exams is as simple as he says: take the practice exams. Take them with notes, then without notes. He doesn't change the exams much at all except for values.

It's a hybrid course, so you'll see him 3 times. First class, midterm, and final. There are practice exams for all of the exams, so you should be fine. Homework and quizzes on the modules each week. He drops the 2 lowest. Read the modules, do your work, and you'll do fine. You get a make a cheat sheet for the exam.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: His time slot of 4:30-7 isn't great if you're trying to pay attention. I believe he's making this class hybrid, which is a great improvement. Always ready to help, and the material isn't too hard. I never attended class and only studied his notes online and the practice exams. Easy A.

Really nice guy and has tons of great career advice. As a professor, his 4:30-7 timeslot isn't in his favor and most of the students aren't paying attention. The best strategy is to study the practice exams, even if you don't go to class. Easy to get a B or C.
Material is very easy. Shows plenty of examples in class. Posts practice exams on blackboard. If you actually do the practice exams, then the actual exams should be no problem. Good professor.
Easy A class if you review all old exams on blackboard. A good teacher and a great person.

He is a good professor. For the exams, make sure you study the old exams; he will provide the old solutions on BB. Even  if you do not know how to answer one, it is very likely that the answer is the same as in the practice exams; he probably played with it to confuse you. Take notes, go to class; know all the ratios, and you will get an A.

Unless you're a Financial Econ major, avoid him at all costs. Says the textbook isn't necessary, however it's good to have to review all that he races through in lecture. No practice problems other than exams which he then proceeds to switch around. Don't bother asking for help understanding the material. He'll tell you no in a roundabout way.

As an FIEC major it is always a joy to have a teacher who is knowledgeable about what he teaches.  Lamdin is one such teacher.  he is genuinely interested in his material and constantly brings his own experiences into class.  If you put effort into the class you will get an A even if you skip on occasion.  Will be taking more classes with him

Textbook is not needed. Exams are exactly like previous exams posted on blackboard. He teaches with overheads, which are hard to read, and he talks very quietly, so make sure you sit in the front if you want to hear/see. Workload is 2 exams, 2 projects (easy, on financial data), and you have to read this book and take 2 quizzes (only worth 10 pts)
Easy if you're good at following directions, exams are just like practice exams (MC).  Highly recommend for many economics courses.

He has his own notes which you can print out from blackboard. No Textbook required. Exams are tough so you have to know your terms, ratios, and equations-which is a hassle since he races through them as if you should already know them. He gives you previous exams to study from which helps a good amount. Be 100% attentive and copy down all notes..
material is ok, just don't like him personally.

Three test one project, test are multiple choice.  Can be tricky, make sure you can do the problems, by front to back back to front.  Will on occasion throw a curve ball or two.  Would definently take him again! Got an A in the class!

Prof. Lamdin breaks down what can be very confusing topics into dumb language.  His exams are fair which consist of 20 multiple choice questions however they are not that easy.  He does give out practice exams with solutions from previous semesters which help ALOT.  I will be looking forward to taking him next semester in his investments class.

Lamdin is pretty easy. If u've had him before u know exactly what 2 expect, no surprises. Quizes on the readings r very easy! Questions straight from text & r MC, T/F, fill in blank. Haven't had a test yet but he gives previous exams from other semesters so u can study from those. He's a great prof I had him for ECON374 so I wanted 2 take him again
flat out sucks and is of no help.  Flys through the material like a nuclear bomb just dropped. If you have even the smallest trouble with math, forget this guy.

Lamdin is cool but his lecture isn't really about teaching as much as it is about copying down what he puts in the over head becaue all he does is read the over head notes. He could just put it on black board and you would be just as well off. Exams are multiple choice but still not easy so study. Nice guy.

There is alot of material to cover so it makes studying for the exams a little more difficult however, he gives you exams from previous semesters which REALLY helps with studying.  Majority of the questions are the same just with different numbers plugged in.  Ur grade consists of 2 exams 1 project and 1 final.  I think Prf Lamdin makes Econ374 fun

The material covered in this class is hard, but he explains everything very clearly. Just follow his notes, you don't even need to buy the book. The exams (2 mid-terms and final)are not bad, learn from old exams. Project(just one) is easy, just follow his instructions. You don't need to show up for class, but it would be better if you did.
He was very nice and helpful. If you use the exams as study tools, you will do well.

his class is supposed to be pretty easy cuz he gives u the old exams but they are never the same as the old exams he changes it up like crazy but if u get an A on the easy project and do good on the final, u will get at least a B in the class

I like Lamdin...he knows his stuff...you can't afford to slack in his class...but if you follow his past exams and stuff...you should be ok...I learned at alot...thats something I can't say for all professors...:(
boring but very easy class. just study the review tests and project is a piece of cake!
Really easy!  Just go to class and study the exam reviews
He sucks big time and very rude too!
Great teacher.  Really easy!!  Project is a joke it is so easy.  Great exam reviews
No Comments
No Comments

The professor was very genuine and caring. He always explained us things and engaged us during lectures with discussion. There were some surprise activities and extra credit opportunities during lecture as well!

Though quizzes and test were closed notes, they were take home. And the professor let us retake a quiz if we explained why we missed.

Honestly, I showed up to maybe 2 lectures the entire semester. You really don't have to go. Professor Dopico seems nice and genuine. The class is a free A. You don't need to do anything. Every week you'll have a test that's take home and open note, same when it comes to exams. I don't understand his low rating, maybe in other classes he isn't great
The professor brought a fresh look to a verybstaightforwd couese on etymology and medical terms with some activities and group work. Very passionate about the material.
Fun class with different activities. Be sure to attend lectures, might get extra credit in doing so
Very nice class try to show up and do well on the weekly tests and exams and you should do well.

I had a great time in the course. The lectures were cool and the teacher taught using his student interests and a down to earth style.

Also the homework was not too bad. 20-30 pages assigned per week for a class that meets once a week is very doable!

heavy, HEAVY reading HW. lectures are not very engaging and hella dense in information. if you have a genuine passion in mythology you can get along with him and will probably enjoy this class but if you are planning to take this class as a free easy credit do not. 

major plus is test are online and can be done on your own time.

He does explain things a bit too fast, however once you communicate with him during after-school hours, he does help in breaking down projects and assignments into smaller and more simplified chunks. Provides good extra credit opportunities, and will extend assignments for students if necessary. Very passionate about the material he teaches.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor was fairly pleasant and seemed to be passionate on the subject. Homework was straight from the textbook and quizzes weren't too far off what was talked about in lecture. All quizzes and both midterm and final have a small amount of extra credit. Should be an easy A.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Boring class but was pretty easy. He was a nice guy, but the syllabus and his idea of the class felt different.
Inconsistent grading and expectations, unclear rubrics, HEAVY weekly homework readings, sent me the wrong final exam and went MIA for the rest of the day
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: +1 for rounding up overall grades of 79/89 & being generous with extensions, but the amount you'll NEED to ask for them is just cruel. Paces lectures horribly, gives weekly readings of 100+ pages, and tests you on stuff he barely mentioned. Assignments are rapid-fire with vague criteria, and some grades take MONTHS to come back. DO NOT TAKE HIM.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Dopico was one of the most unpleasant professors I have taken. I feel he had way too high of expectations for the students for a 200 level class. Most frustrating thing to me was the lack of a rubric or consistent grading at all for the biweekly research papers which were a large chunk of our grades.

reviews.comment: lol. class is ancs210. check gritview to see how had his grade distribution is. unless you have 50h/wk to devote to this class and a deep love of the subject, avoid this prof at all costs. comes across as a good human being tho so dont be too mean to him. Exams arent exaclty the fairest. his questions tend to leave a lot of room for ambiguity
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--So many papers

reviews.comment: i heard that rlst 210 and ancs 201 had different experiences but i took ancs and he was a tough grader and assigned hard papers. he "didnt believe in rubrics" but that led to the papers being confusing as to what he expected and then us getting low grades. he gave too little time on the exams, overall not a mean person but not a good professor

Tests you on material he barely covers, if at all. Doesn't hold office hours. Rubrics have no real distinctions between scores. Some grades take MONTHS to show up, and if you think he'll give you truly constructive feedback on the bad ones... tough luck. Also accused my whole class of cheating on the midterm without evidence. DO NOT TAKE HIM. EVER.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Do not take this class with him. LOTS of long homework and quizzes. Unclear grading criteria that take weeks for results. Do not trust those two good reviews. If an elective's coursework is laid out to where you have to constantly ask for extensions and reach out - it's the professor, not the course.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: While he isn't an easy grader, he is absolutely a fair one. His lectures are interesting and energetic, he clearly cares about the subject. He is very willing to give extensions, work with you, and explain things provided you actually communicate with him, something I am inclined to believe many of the negative reviewers did not do.

While there was a lot of work, all the due dates and assignments were well laid out. I emailed this professor many times about missing assignments and needing extensions, and he was open-minded and understanding every time. As long as you do the work and communicate with him, he is an amazing professor with a great sense of humor.

Frustrating. In my semester, he told us there isn't a textbook for the class, but I just found out his lectures (disjointed, rushed) are based primarily off of one. If he does that in your semester, the textbook is Ancient Greece A Political, Social, and Cultural History (4th edition) by Sarah B. Pomeroy, Stanley M Burstein. Oxford Press.

Pros: This class is VERY good exposure therapy to research papers, if you're able to put in the time and energy. IMO, if you come to him with questions about the material (like I often did), he's really nice and receptive to feedback. There is extra credit.

Cons: VERY inconsistent grading, and rushed over-condensed lectures.

I should have followed my gut and dropped the class in the first week when I felt like this isn't gonna end well, for somebody who claimed this class didn't need initial knowledge, he expects you to know everything, only if I found reviews on him before we signed up but he totally ruined the idea of this class being easy, take it with phin pls.

For an intro arts and humanities class this professor assigns too much work. Students are expected to read 100-200 page myths each week with a reading journal to complete. He often criticizes the class for not understanding the myth and having incorrect interpretations. Mythology can be interpreted in DIFFERENT WAYS.

He berates the whole class for our poor writing skills and when asked how to do better or explain the feedback, he just says that getting bad grades is what will help us in our writing for the future. Assignments often have incorrect descriptions that are not updated making it confusing on what we are writing about.

Though at first it appeared like the class was going to be fun & entertaining, he expects the class to know everything (even though he assured it was just an introductory class.) His attitude during the lectures feels sarcastic to those that are confused. Tough grader with no clear feedback other than berating you for not knowing. Long assignments.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Worst prof Ive had in my 4 years. So much wrong with how he set up the course, but worst part was his attitude. he saw himself as a "good prof" just because he didnt act like his old college profs. He accused of us not knowing how to write, but when we asked how to analyze the text we were to write on, his response was: you'll just have to learn.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Dopico is the worst professor I have ever had in my four years of college. This is an intro course, but he expected us to have strong knowledge of Greek history from day 1. He is nitpicky when it comes to grading. He gave papers to do every other week with no rubric and no feedback. He berated the class for not being smart. Don't take his class.

This class was incredibly difficult. I took a 200 level on classical mythology, and he had us reading about 200 pages per week. The instructions for the paper were incredibly vague. Basically every class started with him angrily ranting about everything he disliked in the reading journals. I took it as an elective, and had to drop it from stress.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Awesome professor. She's very kind and has a great passion for biology. Had no complaints about any part of this class.
Dr. Donohue is extremely helpful. Her enthusiasm for biology was evident and she wanted everyone to succeed
The only reason I even passed this course is because she let me redo an assignment. Great prof!

She was the other prof teaching with Dr. Leupen for this class. She was okay? Like the labs were fine and she explained what she wanted clearly but her in-lab quizzes were a lot harder simply because they just weren't as to the point as Leupen's (imo). When she said anything from the protocol would be tested, she meant it.

Overall, pretty good. Grading for the projects is a bit ambiguous, with different TAs giving different advice, leading to point deductions at times, since project requirements aren't straightforward. Takes a lot of time to do the projects, concepts aren't that hard, just tedious implementation.

He has live coding in lectures which can help solidify the basics of each concept, but beyond that the lectures are standard. TA's grade your projects and exams, which can make or break your semester, there are some serious differences from grader to grader. Professor wasn't very friendly or accessible when I needed help & didn't respond to emails.

Donyaee is very nice and is pretty thorough with his lectures. The majority of your grades is from homeworks and tests. The quizzes were mostly based off lecture notes, focusing on terminology mostly. He's very nice so don't be afraid to ask for help. There was also a curve at the end of the semester.

The resources he posts on Blackboard are practically unintelligible. Everything I have learnt thus far was either from Youtube or other professors' slides I got from my friends. Even those are poorly explained but at least a few things are sensible.
This professor is great. He's always willing to help you out and he actually cares about your learning. Absolutely recommend this class for the summer too!

He's a good professor, you might have to geekforgeeks for some clarifications on some concepts. Projects and homeworks weren't crazy, you should be fine as long as you start as early as possible. More importantly, he's a great person who's willing to help out students when in need, and fun to talk to in general.

I think he's the best prof for data structure he explained things very easily and class is not boring, he likes when student ask question and help you understand what you're confused about. He's very knowledgable.

He's a very knowledgeable professor, but this course I feel wasn't the best organized. His lectures can be quite confusing, and leave us not fully prepared for homeworks or quizzes. Plus, it's hard to prepare for exams. We're given a mock exam, but it's like 50% representative of the actual. Not an easy A or B. Homeworks were graded harshly too.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Great, interesting class, but demands a lot of time. The lectures help a lot and the supplementary videos he provides is essentially broken down portions of the lectures. Be prepared to Google A LOT for this class. Many items and troubleshooting tips will need to be Googled as they aren't covered very well in the lectures/notes.

Lectures were bland. Projects were long and involved, but there wasn't much other homework. Tests were difficult but curved. Solidly middle-of-the-road professor- I don't have anything particularly bad to write about, but also nothing particularly great to write about either.

Donyaee is one of the better teachers in the cmsc department. He takes time in class for students to practice concepts and his quizzes reflect material covered. He is also very gracious with extensions and looking over grades done by the TA
It's easy to pass his class if you put in the effort. Curves the final grade which is amazing.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: bestie. he is such an amazing prof!
reviews.rating_tags: Caring--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Donyaee is a good professor to some extent. I say to some extent because if a professor depends on curves they really aren't that great. His exams are very difficult and will get curved no matter what.
Ver caring professor just pay attention in class

Overall a really lackluster professor. Lectures are extremely hard to follow and do not help with homeworks and exams. The only other option he offers is his overpriced textbook that barely gives a surface level understanding of the content. Prepare to have lots of outside resources and make sure to take the it online if you can.

Nice guy, lenient grading, and flexible on request. He provided very limited context so it was difficult to want to understand the material as opposed to just memorizing steps to pass. The homeworks were easy (40%), activities were for completion (5%), quizzes were a little challenging (5%), midterm and final exams were not easy, study! (50%).

In charge of 341 projects, and they can be pretty difficult. Also a lot of errors and things missing when projects are initially released. Honestly, you'll only be relying on the TA's for help, they're your best bet :)

A decent professor. Lectures were pretty hard to follow but he posts lots of resources on blackboard so you can catch up if you're lost. There's a textbook for this class but you really didn't need it.

He's an okay professor. He says to buy his textbook for $90. I didn't buy it, nor did I need it. If online, watch the lectures at 1.5x speed. Homework was graded for accuracy and activities for completion. Quizzes and exams are fairly straightforward and have similar questions like previous assignments, occasionally weird questions with no guidance
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Due to videos just being posted as a lecture for half the semester it was hard to connect and understand. Easily accessible outside of class, TA's helped a lot. Projects are challenging and difficult.
He is an understanding professor and tries his best to help the students.

He's a very supportive teacher. I got extension in two different projects. I explained my situation to him, and he was very understanding. Everything is pre-recoded and it was a bit tough to get through (2 hours per week), but it was useful. And same for his powerpoints.

His pre-recorded lectures are lifeless. Other than that and having to buy the textbook he wrote for $90 extra instead of the book every class uses, it wasn't terrible. Textbook was pretty useless too. Exams were okay since lots of the problems were from quizzes. Wouldn't take him again though.

I believe Donyaee has really improved since he was first teaching a few semesters ago. Although the homeworks are worth a lot (40%) and there's only 6 of them, he's really quick with responding to emails and helping. He also randomly decides to push dates so that was a plus. His exams are easy if you do well on the quizzes (5% of grade).
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Graded by few things--Caring

reviews.comment: Great professor. Puts effort in explaining content

He makes you buy his own book for a minimum of $90. Don't take him for CMSC331 since you can find the other professors textbook for no charge. He prerecords his lectures, which is the only positive. Dry and boring tone when lecturing. Weekly homework, activities, and quizzes.
Pro tip: if you're taking 331 online, watch the videos at 1.5x speed. It helped me a lot with staying focused. Good professor overall.

Took this class over the summer and it was a breeze. Also prof. is very helpful. He held office hours twice a week and was able to clear up any questions I had. Also homework was 40% of the grade; if you do well on those and actually know your stuff, you'll get a good grade. Very generous grader also :)
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: For CMSC 202, Professor Donyaee was very interactive with students, but I found myself struggling to understand him and was bored in some lectures. The class definitely makes you work for your grade, though.

His lectures are from his book. His book got some wrong answers. The book is not clear how to solve the problem. The solution is not consistent. Thus, no way to know where your point would be taken off. He (or his TA) grades very harsh.

This guy sucks. Hard. He is unclear about what exactly he is trying to teach, grades things far too harshly, and basis his "class participation" grade on things he says multiple times are not graded. Horrible. Avoid.

Dr. Donyaee is a great person! Very open, understanding, and reachable. The curriculum in class is hard, and to find that information online is hard. Nevertheless, as long as you try to do homework, and try, you should pass!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Took him over the summer and he's really improved. He's a good teacher and the material makes sense, just practice it. He wants you to do well. Definitely curved the class.
Dr. Donayaee is an awesome teacher, he really cares about whether his students understand the lessons. He has improved very much from his first semester.

This was Dr. Donyaee's second semester teaching and he has tremendously improved. The class is very heavy regarding how much material you are responsible for, but you will learn a lot. He gave a hard final, but also curved it very fairly. The hw and midterm were also fair. He is also a very nice person and is nice about helping students.

Most of the very low reviews below were posted before final grades when most people expected to fail. Homework is kind of difficult, but if you go to office hours he helps a lot. The tests are very hard. Overall it is a difficult course, but he curved generously to make up for it. As a professor he's very nice and helpful.

The homework was painful and the tests were quite difficult, but ultimately I received an A when I was expecting a C. So you'll have to work, but the final grades are more generous than you'd expect. More importantly, Donyaee posted better review materials as the semester went by. So future semesters should go better for students.

A very nice and caring professor, this was his first semester teaching so he may have been a bit rough around the edges, but I'm sure he will improve in the future. His midterm was impossibly difficult, but he showed the desire to improve and although difficult, the final was more fair.

The course was not hard but this professor made it way harder then expected. The exams are very tough and his grading are very unfair. I would not recommend anyone to take this professor. He will not provide you anything like past exams etc for the help. The exam guide is useless. Lecture notes are just scanned copy of the book.

I don't understand all the iffy ratings people have given him. I'd say it's one of the harder courses I've taken, but comp sci courses aren't supposed to be easy A's. Homework isn't bad & seems to be graded pretty fair and not too harsh. The exam was tough, but he gives you literally the notes for everything we've gone over in class so study those
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Gives good feedback--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: Really nice guy but horrible at teaching. No lecture slides in class, only blackboard notes in paragraphs copied directed from the textbook. Lectures are done on the chalkboard with no clear objective of what hes teaching, not good at explanations. 6 hws with unclear directions, grading is inconsistent. Many students are hoping to pass.

He is an incredibly nice person, but that is about it. He decided to make a course that is supposed to be easy incredibly difficult. The coding HW is worth almost nothing compared to the writing HW. The midterm was one the worst experiences I've ever had, he provided no study guide and was surprised when a lot of people failed.
Awful professor. He writes on the board but never connects each lecture with each other and his exams do not test the material that we learned in class. I would NOT recommend.

Professor Donyaee is a nice guy. However, he assigns lots of homework and the exams are hard and long. He gives heavy lectures and expects you to know everything. Homework is not always from the book. You have to code in python, C, C++, etc. He thinks everyone is proficient coding. Try taking another instructor unless you're great coding.
Took Unruly Bodies in the summer. Interesting class for culture gep!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: I took this class online in the winter session and loved it!! Dr. Kate is my favorite professor by far and I found the readings for this course were really interesting and engaging. She's very accessible outside of class and super understanding about accommodations and deadlines and really makes the class enjoyable. She is also very passionate. :)

Dr. Kate is the best instructor I've ever had. She's amazing to her students, and you can tell she cares about them individually. The class was an easy A, you just have to do the weekly discussion boards. Attendance isn't mandatory, but I always hate to miss her class because it's so enjoyable. She's truly an amazing professor.
Attendance is not counted for, basically one assignment due per week. She is super flexible and super nice!!!
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Graded by few things--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Dr. Kate is probably one of the best professors in the Gender, Women, and Sexuality Studies department, maybe one of the best at the school. She is very understanding and is willing to give you time to make sure your work is the best it can be. Her lectures are engaging and interesting and she makes you care about the class.

Dr. Kate is a real gem and a great professor! She is so funny and gives amazing lectures! There is a lot of reading assigned for each class but it's definitely not necessary that you read *all* of it because it will be discussed in class, but make sure to take notes. This was by far my favorite class this semester, maybe my favorite class at UMBC!

Dr. Kate is a great professor! Her class is so fun to go to. If you need a culture credit for GEP at UMBC, this one is the way to go! Lots of reading, but if you don't do every page no need to sweat, just understand the main points and you will be okay. Exams are written and you have plenty of time to do them, attendance is important, fair grader.

Dr. Kate is an amazing professor! Feminist Activism is a great class too. No tests, one major project, one group project, 4 discussion questions. Her classes are heavily discussion based, super chill and open. Highly recommend!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: A wonderful course that I really enjoyed taking with Dr. Drabinski.  She is very understanding when there are any circumstances related to the exams or grading and the grading criteria is very clear.  This course involves essays and BB discussions related to the material and it is straightforward.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Participation matters--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: Dr. Kate is by far my favorite professor at UMBC. She makes lectures interesting and they are almost always hilarious. She makes learning very easy as she does not give standard exams but has you do essays instead. She's very understanding when life happens and is there to help students with matters even outside of the class.

Taking a Dr. Kate course is one of those invaluable experiences UMBC has to offer.  She engages you with the material through stories of her own life and an extensive knowledge bank and understanding of the world.  I've had her for both GWST 200 and 310 and she was fantastic for both.  Willing to work with students.  Read in order to participate.

Dr. Kate is by far my favorite professor at UMBC. She makes lecture relevant to what's going on today and really knows her stuff. She was the highlight of my Mondays and Wednesdays. Definitely take one of her classes!
She is an amazing teacher. So willing to help, very understanding. Incredibly interesting, loved going to class. Projects were fairly easy and fun to do.
Awesome lady, awesome teacher. Definitely would recommend!
I love her. she's the best!
Best prof I've ever had.

Easily one of the best professors I've ever had. Friendly, knowledgeable, engaging and hilarious. The course material was interesting enough, but having her as a teacher made it just that much better. I highly recommend her.

By far my favorite professor in college so far. Don't blow her class off because it appears to be easy, you'll learn so much if you pay attention, go to class, and do the readings. This class made me pick up a GWST minor.

took this class over the winter. 2 easy group presentations. 1 presentation at the end. a few films. Keep up with the readings. Take notes, this makes the (3)take-home exams easier on you. if you type notes, make sure you reference your notes on what pages your notes come from.
super easy

Professor Bridges is a good professor. His class was very easy and low maintenance, only 6 quizzes and a final, and his friday lecture, the quizzes, and the final are all online. My only problem is that his lectures were boring and not useful, but mandatory.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Bridges is a really funny guy. He keeps class entertaining and students focused. The tests are a combination of the textbook and what we learn in class but more textbook focused in my opinion. Great class and professor.
Overall, great class. Attended was graded but he was leinient if you were sick or such. Grade was based off quizzes and tests, all of which were online. Would recommend!

Loved Professor Bridges. The class has 6 quizzes and a final but the content is easy to understand. Attendance is mandatory and worth 10% of your grade. If you aren't feeling well or had something come up just email explaining and he won't mark you absent. Idk if he reads these but if he does, thank you Professor Bridges you're the best.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Great professor who is very understanding and cares about his students. He has great humor and makes his class really interesting. He is also quite lenient. It's not stressful at all and you learn a lot.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Hilarious--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: one of the best prof. very chill and straightforward class. attendance matters. lectures are very interesting and sometimes funny. all his quizzes are online (no lockdown browser). Only downside is that quizzes are the only things in the grade, but they're straight from ppt and lecture so taking notes helps. take this class with him. easiest A!
Easy course that explained simple, but important concepts.
Truly an icon, multiple days it felt like he didn't feel like teaching so we just watched videos, class is not very vigorous and there are no big projects or tests which was nice
Go to lectures and take notes, pretty much everything on quizzes/exams is discussed in lecture.
He is very easy to follow and everything he goes over is in powerpoints he posts on Blackboard later on.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Respected--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Super easy class, fun lectures, easy quizzes, not much else to say

This class was a breeze. The quizzes were online and honestly super easy. Prof. Bridges' lectures were always entertaining, and he was a really cool person. He was kind to everyone, and genuinely cared about his students. I passed with ease. There is some textbook reading, but its not half bad.

Attendance & participation are mandatory. Just show up and speak at least once everyday. Everything was based on the quizzes and textbook, so just read and take solid notes and you're good to go. Post-corona, he wasn't entirely accessible via email. Took a few days or no response, which was kinda irritating. But he's chill and the class was easy!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Love him. Like a father to us all.
Andy Bridges is a caring and enthusiastic professor who cares about the engagement of the class. Read the textbook before the quizzes and attend class and PHIL 146 should be an easy A.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious

reviews.comment: Very engaging teacher, as a freshman going into college I was very comfortable in his class and he values all opinions and all viewpoints on any topic. Very fun and relaxed professor.

One of the best professors i had freshemen year, his quizzes are hard but fair. Reading the text book is required do to do well in the class. He is a really caring professor knowing i was struggling with his quizzes he offered to create me study guides. I would recommend him to any student interested in philosophy.

Really good professor and class. Class is graded on 6 quizes (all online and open book), and a final (closed book). Andy B is really funny, gives really good lectures and its really great when theres a lot of participation involed. However attendance is mandatory and is part of your grade. Overall really enjoyable class. Wish i could take him again
reviews.rating_tags: GRADED BY FEW THINGS--Amazing lectures--Would take again

reviews.comment: I like him Good dude Good class Happy GPA

Excellent teacher. Great sense of humor, professional but fun. He did an amazing job keeping people interested, except those on their phones or sleeping. By far the best handler of 'class discussions' that I've seen. He kept people from going off on tangents but still let people participate.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Amazing professor with a nice and funny attitude. Class is easy, but interesting. Quizzes will make or break you, but he's willing to help if you don't do so hot. A+ teacher in my book.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: The quizzes are hard. Pay attention in the class coz quizzes are based on in the class materials. Final is not bad. Read all the quizzes before final and you will get 90 above. Hard to get A.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: The online quizzes literally ARE your grade so PLEASE pay attention in class. If you pay attention, participate, and take the quizzes seriously, there's no reason why you can't get an A. Andrew's a perfect referent of the concept "great professor".

Quizzes are pretty hard. Read the chapter and study, or else your grade is gonna take a hit. 100 question final wasn't too bad. Study hard and you'll get a A, or you're probably end up with a B. Cool guy, very likable and approachable.

Professor Bridges is great. Talks about his cats and makes concepts clear to understand. Actually read your notes, though. Had I actually done that, I would have ended up with an A instead of a B. The instructor made waking up early to walk up the hill worth the struggle. 10/10 would recommend.

One of my favorite professors at UMBC. Very fun and clearly explains the material covered.  Class was all based on 12 quizzes which were pretty fair. If you had an average of 93.5% on them, you did not have to take the final exam.  Highly recommend.
While this is a great class with a great professor, do not take the six quizzes lightly. I did and I ended up with a B as a result. Good guy doe.
While this is a great class with a great professor, do not take the six quizzes lightly. I did and I ended up with a B as a result.
One of my favorite teachers at UMBC.  He made the material very easy to learn and used real life examples to help understand it.  The quizzes are very fair as well.

Professor Bridges made logic accessible without being condescending or making the content easier than it ought to be. He has high standards but you'll want to meet them. Definitely one of the coolest, youngest, most down to earth professors I've had.

I loved taking Professor Holladay! I took him during Spring 2024, and even though attendance was optional, I still attended nearly every class, because he has a great demeanor and is very intelligent in his content area. The only thing I'd say is that you need to be open to reading a good amount per week, and the material will likely be quite new.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Genuinely one of the best professors at UMBC. Have taken multiple classes with him and plan to continue taking them with him. Very intelligent about everything he teaches. Super understanding and happy to give extensions, especially if you are vocal in class and generally do your work. Seriously, take ENGL 300 with him!!!

[ENGL 387] - Very easy class but never responds to emails during the semester. He grades very late, so you do not know if you are passing or failing the class until the last day grades are put in. Instructions are misleading at times, and in-person classes aren't informative sometimes.

He is really understanding when it comes to extensions and makes himself available for additional help. Probably the nicest professor at UMBC, he seems to enjoy what he teaches and genuinely wants to help students succeed. 2 discussion posts and readings per week with 3 essays and 1 project.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Caring--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: A very very sweet professor. I learned much from him for class where we discussed disabilities and how people can be treated unfairly because of them. Learned a few things about myself and my own mental health issues while I wrote papers for the class. I'm very happy to have gotten to take a class with Professor Holladay before graduating.
I was in a pretty small class, 7 people including me. But Prof made it easy to hold a discussion. Readings were interesting and relatable. Deadlines were flexible. He was very understanding.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: As a grader and a one-on-one reviewer, he's fine. But he's an awful lecturer. He sounds constantly nervous and his voice puts me to sleep.

reviews.comment: There is a lot of work for this class but Im rating him as a professor. Hes very caring and sweet and is always willing to help or grant an extension. Hes always available on his email and gives wonderful feedback. I would take him again in a heartbeat
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Gives good feedback--So many papers

reviews.comment: Holladay is a great professor. The material is not as boring as people on here make it out to be if you are actually interested in communications. He let us have a lot of creative space with the major assignments which was awesome, and he genuinely wants his students to succeed. Also, his lectures/discussions were often very interesting.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Professor Holladay is truly one of the nicest people, but the class itself is very boring. I think it's the material which is just not fun to listen to or even read about. From what I can remember, attendance didn't seem to matter too much and it was mainly him giving lectures the entire time. Most of the reading material is documents online.

He really is such a sweet guy and seems like he loves teaching and what he teaches but unfortunately the material is extremely boring. We only get graded on the midterm and a paper so that's not ideal. Also, having an actual test in an English class is a little off-putting. A ton of reading and from horrible books, too. Never takes attendance.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: He's a young professor. The course content is extremely boring. Attendance is supposedly mandatory but I never saw him take it. He makes students do a lot of discussion posts on blackboard instead of teaching us the material. Most of class is spent sitting around, but he never releases class early. Hardly any assignments from him and no grades.

Professor Holladay is by far the coolest and nicest professors I've had in awhile. He cares about his students and is willing to listen to reason if any trouble should befall you. I highly recommend taking his class, if you show up, participate, and take notes you'll do fine. Study for midterm, the projects are easy if you put in the effort + time

Dr.Pan undoubtedly has more knowledge in her field, But her way of teaching is totally worst. Most of her classes are just a presentation and you will get boared of it. Apart from very few topics, i dont remember any thing useful from her lectures.

The lectures were lengthy to follow, making it difficult to absorb the information. Additionally, no accommodation regarding missed exams, unless you go to the hospital when sick. While polls were used, only a small percentage of the material covered in class appeared on the quizzes, which were still challenging, even slides were mostly useless.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Great Professor, She cares and Easy grader
Great professor, super clear on what is expected for exams and the project. Gave reviews for each test so you knew what was coming. Highly recommend.

Professor Draganescu did nothing to prepare you for exams, and never uploaded any material for you to practice, and the tests were significantly harder than ANY other class. Avoid for math 300 as you will not get a good understanding of proofs at all.

I saw the reviews here and thought Draganescu would be pretty horrible, but he is not bad. He is pretty funny when lecturing, and the worked examples done during class are relevant to the homework. The only problem is the way he explains the abstract: 3Blue1Brown's Essence of Linear Algebra series on Youtube can help you with that though.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: He is a nice person and does try very hard to teach the class. However, he teaches too abstractly and is really hard to follow. His quizzes are from the book but his exams are really theoretical.

He's a nice person, but he is bad at explaining mathematical concepts in terms that students can understand. He also writes proof-based exams that are not in line with what the homework has you practice. In addition, the first exam was graded too late for me to drop the class and save my GPA. There are FAR better options for MATH 221.
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Try to take a different professor if possible!! He gives computational homework, but the tests are almost entirely theory based. His lectures make little to no sense (go to the lectures anyway - not graded but used to boost your grade if you showed up). Read the book and memorize language/theories. It's not impossible, but it's not fun either.

He is a good teacher, no doubt. He will challenge you to the max with the problems he assigns and tests on. 80% of your grade  comes from 3 tests all of which will be the hardest 3 tests you will ever take. If you are a math person and you know for sure you will pass then sure take him and learn the most. For the average person, take someone else.

He puts the entire burden  on  tests. Its a hard class and many of the other teachers give quizzes and a lot more HW  which help with understand as well as grades. it feels like he does the bare minimum.
hes ok

The people below me sound like people who usually don't get A's in math classes, and are giving him a good rating because they did well. I also received an A, but I usually do so my view is more objective. He isn't hard by any means, but hes certainly not "the man". He is hard to follow in class. Unless your self -taught, lectures will be useless

Dr. Draganescu was friendly and very fair.  Like others said, he likes to prove things,  explain theory, and do hard problems in class.  However, homework (quizzes) and tests covered the core concepts of the course and were not very difficult.  If you read the book, take good notes, do the homework, and pay attention, there is no reason to do bad.

Draganescu is the man, best math professor ive had at UMBC. Grade is made up of quizes exams and final. Quizes are based on HW. Exams somewhat challenging but questions focus on core concepts. He wants his students to succeed and makes that possible with some announcements at the end of the semester. You wont be disappointed,take the class with him

Great Professor.  As long as you did the homework, and came to class and put in a little effort, you will get a good grade.  He explains things very well, and his classes are completely related to the topic.

Sometimes goes above what is necessary in class scaring students.  However, he is very helpful, gives exams that give many to do well.  Homeworks can sometimes be a little difficult but the exams will bring up your grade.
He is a bad teacher, make me start scared math. I don't think he knows how to teach. The things he wrote on blackboard was mass. Terrible
He is not very easy to understand in the lecture but he is very fair in all aspects of teaching. His grading methods allow you to recover even if you don't do well in the  beginning.

One of the better professors at UMBC.  He's new, and I hope more people discover him.  He's willing to work with you as much as you need it.  Tends to do a lot of proofs in class, gears it more towards math majors than engineering students. Sample Exam may or may not strongly resemble the actual exam.  Take him if you want to learn something.

Teaches an intro class the way it should be taught; tests focus on problem solving and not a ton of theory...he tells you what to expect on each test and gives plenty of partial credit.  The project is a pain but most people got good grades.  If you do the homework and practice his sample exams, a B is almost guaranteed and an A is very possible.

Very good professor. Detailed, easy to understand lectures. Although the class is quiz/exam heavy there are many drops and good TAs to help you prepare. Some exams may be difficult but Prof. Listorti is considerate in grading.

Super great professor. Posts notes for each lecture online and lectures are easy to follow. The exams, and quizzes are pretty decent, and he posts tests from previous years which are really helpful when reviewing. He also offers drops for assignments and quizzes, so it's okay if you don't do well on some of them. TAs are also very good.

I couldn't recommend Professor Listorti more. He makes notes available before every lecture, he makes difficult concepts easier to understand, he offers drops for assignments, and he's open to go over concepts before exams if you have any questions! On top of that, he's a high school math teacher, which further shows his passion beyond lectures.

She is amazing!!! the best professor i've taken at umbc and extremely caring, after having a bad experience with another professor ghosting me for my letter of rec she  wrote one for me in 2 days and submitted right away on such short notice please take her she's the best !!!

Professor Ducat is amazing, and she is so passionate about her job and what she is teaching. There are some readings you must complete, but they are fairly easy. The homework is easy, and the quiz is open note. The final project is so fun (you do a case study on a fictional character of your choosing). Take her class, you won't regret it.

I'm taking Community Psychology with Prof. Ducat now and she's super nice. 

We have 3 assignments per week, no final, just a Town Hall. I have an A in the class so far and it's not too hard. If you show up and participate in class she gives you extra credit. She also lets you resubmit late assignments and assignments you want a better grade on.

Dr. Duffy is a great professor who the students can really relate to. He is easy to speak with and very approachable. Standard book hw, exams based on them, and group design project with a presentation at end of sem. Material could be dull at times, but the project was very open ended and good practice for rising engineers. Very positive experience
Duffy is one of the best professors I have had, highly recommend taking any class with him.

A fantastic professor that lets his personality shine through into his lectures. Easy to get a hold of and is very down to earth. Have taken 3 classes with him and not a single one was confusing or unenjoyable.

He is a very considerate and funny dude and the lectures were very engaging and helpful. The homeworks are kinda confusing to navigate, but once you get used to it it'll make sense. Make sure to get started with the assignments early because some of them take some time to do. Overall an amazing guy and a moderately easy class.
Only a week and a half in but he seems like a pretty cool guy, ngl
Took the course over the summer session and had a blast. The material was well explained and Prof is understanding enough to give you assistance when you need it. Also a great conversationalist.

Great experience! Handled remote learning exceptionally well and assigned reasonable amounts of work per week. The quality of the group members you select at the beginning of the semester will determine your grade!
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Group projects--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Great teacher highly recommended. He jokes around making it more fun and interesting to learn. He teaches the material in a clear and easy way. He gives a clear grading rubric of the homework, which can cause it to take longer, but it teaches you the thought process for solving problems. He responds quickly and is very easy to access out of class.

Homework problems are few, but take a long time. He is not the best at teaching undergrads because he is used to teaching grad students, so his lectures can be confusing since he doesn't always know what we do or don't know. It doesn't seem like he reviews his slides beforehand, so he will often be trying to figure out his own diagrams in lecture

Dr. Dusman is one of the best teachers I have ever had. She treats each student with so much respect and thoughtfulness. She is supportive what you want to do with your composition, and is there to help guide and help you get to your best!

Difficulty is more like a 3.5.  If you indicate that you have a drive and desire to work hard, Dr. Dusman will help you achieve things you never thought possible. This is not an exaggeration. She is a phenomenal educator, probably one of the best in the country right now. If you have any opportunity to take one of her classes, jump at it!
Very good professor. Took instrumentation. Geared towards music education majors, not composers. Was an easy class as long as you tried and followed what the book/professor said to do.

One of the best professors at UMBC. Hands down. I adore her and she has been a great help to be as a Music student. She's very approachable and makes concise and creative decisions whenever you have concerns. The class is easy if you are willing to do the work. Be prepared to do a lot of composing for class and always PARTICIPATE in discussions!

She is one of the best professors I've had. ALWAYS DO YOUR WORK, it will help you understand composition better. She is a very talented composer, too. In her administrative aspect, she is very decisive and very creative with solutions to problems. She has helped me out in all of my years here as a Music student.
