Thanks to her, SPAN 201 was my favorite class during my first semester of freshman year. She's so sweet and thoroughly explains something when a student is confused. Also, she speaks a good balance of Spanish and English. Online homework assignments aren't bad if you pay attention during lecture and study the vocabulary in the textbook.

Mary Ely is so sweet and cares so much about her students. Participation is important, but she fosters a forgiving classroom. She's very encouraging and super helpful, and while there's homework at least a couple times a week, as long as you actually try, you can't fail. She's the best Spanish teacher here and she actually wants you to learn.

She is honestly one of the best professors here, cares a lot about her students and is always open to help. There's a fair amount of work, but she is very reasonable about what she assigns. As a person she is very active and personable, and makes coming to class a pleasure. There are a lot of options for 201 professors, make sure you choose her.

Instead of participating by raising hands, she will call on a random person meaning you can get called on 0 times or 10 times in a class, and if she doesn't call on you, she will give you a poor participation score. What she says and what the rubric says don't match up a lot and if you don't understand something she will tell you to just study more
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Spanish class can be intimidating when you do not know the language well and if you do not participate she will not like that. She is a very strict grader and if you miss class she will not help you make up work. The online work is very tedious and is not helpful with the lectures she gives. On top of online work there are a lot of written work.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: She is honestly an amazing teacher! I had her for SPAN101 and then a different teacher for SPAN102 and the differences in their teaching styles were insane. Prof Hernandez is very patient and understanding when it comes to questions. She is a big fan of class participation, which actually helps with her conversational style of teaching.

She is amazing with helping students understand Spanish. Very participation-oriented but she makes sure the discussion is fun and engaging. Assignments are completed online, and while they're a bit tedious they're not difficult. Exams can be tricky. Overall Prof Hernandez challenges her classes but makes sure they succeed if they try.

Elaine is an incredible professor. College is meant to push us to grow and she creates a warm space to learn and experiment with ideas. She won't force you to learn, that's your own responsibility and why you're in college, but if you put in the effort you'll become a more fully formed human:)
I took a class with her back in 2013 and I still remember how great of a professor she was for ENGL100 Composition. Definitely take her class if you get the chance!

Professor MacDougall is such a kind and lovely person. The course was an honors seminar, so it was discussion based and there were projects included but there were no exams. She is so understanding and so genuine, she made the course engaging. I would 100% recommend you take her class!

Elaine is my favorite professor ever. She is so caring and understanding towards students, and doesn't make her classes more difficult than they need to be. If you have the chance to take a class with Elaine, absolutely take it.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Caring

reviews.comment: Not difficult class that helped students understand the course.
Elaine made English digestible.  Is very understanding which made English a breeze with her.  Take English with you if you can, as long as you do everything you will get an A.

Professor MacDougall may the only time in my life where I enjoyed an English class. She had us sign a contract that said if we turned all 5 essays in, participated in class and showed up every week, we would automatically get an A. She cares about her students and is very flexible with due dates. She values student inputs and opinions.

Professor MacDougall is great, she is a caring person and will make sure you succeed. As of Spring 2022, her FYS101 is labor based so as long as you do the work (which isn't even a lot to being with) then you will be fine in her class.

Took the FYS - Truth and Technology, and it was super chill and actually pretty fun! She was a really good professor and very understanding. The assignments we had were all easy and she wasn't too bad about deadlines either. Definitely the easiest A for me for the semester. If I was able to take english with I would've! She's an amazing prof!!!
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: elaine is an absolute gem

One of the nicest professors I've had! She cares about her students and is understanding. The work is not difficult, with minimal homework, and for a writing intensive class, there was not too much work. The longest paper we had was two pages. I would highly recommend

I had Elaine MacDougall for ENGL 101 with my cohort of Sondheim Scholars. Such a gem, very fun and helpful. If you're a Sondheim then you're in for a treat, if not then you should definitely take her class!

The FYS was mainly discussion based, but there are a few short papers that essentially give your thoughts on in class discussions. Watched lots of movies and videos. There was a service-learning component of the class, so she built in days into the schedule where there was no class to make up for the time. Overall, very easy.

I love Prof. MacDougall. She's very sweet and laid back. Her expectations for the class are clear and simple so it isn't hard to follow. You're expected to read only a few novels and write a few papers, not a whole lot. I still send her copies of my papers for other courses so that she can edit them even though she isn't my professor anymore.
Very calm, nice, and understanding lady. Class was not overwhelming or hard. Few readings, mostly discussions and watching movies to later write papers on. Would recommend.
Easy-going and really flexible. Easy grader and a genuinely nice lady.
Shes the best English teacher. Helps you any time you need help, lets you resubmit papers at the end of the semester. Also very easy grader.
She is soooo good. A friend recommended her and I don't regret taking the class

Professor MacDougall is awesome. She's really easy going with her students and let's a lot of stuff slide if you just talk to her about it. Papers were kind of a drag but she made sure you knew what you were doing and gives many opportunities for improvement. Really nice lady.

Prof. MacDougall is great! She helps you out on all your papers and truly cares about your interests. This was a very relaxing class at the end of the day. Homework assignments were short and gives positive comments on your papers along with good constructive criticism.  I would definitely take a class with her again!

AMAZING PROFESSOR!!! I can't even begin to say how great she is. Def recommended for english 101. Super nice and lets you re-do essays at the end of the semester. Just go to class and you'll get an/a A/B.

Professor Macdougall is one of the best intro professors I've had so far.  Makes English very enjoyable for those that are not majoring in it.  Overall her personality is quite pleasant as well willingness to compromise when turning in late assignments.

Professor MacDougall has been one of the best professors/teachers I've ever had.  I have never gotten higher than a B in English until her class; she makes it understandable and actually a pleasure to go to her class. If that does not convince you, she's also extremely easy on the eyes. You will not regret taking her class.

I loved Dr. Stanwyck. Stat is a really hard class in general but she makes it bearable and pretty understandable. She always tries to explain the best she can and is so willing to answer your questions. Super nice and adds 10 points to tests for a little boost.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Prof Stanwyck is an awesome professor. Statistics isn't my strong suit but she was always very understanding and accessible, and had a great sense of humor. She was always very engaging and you can tell she loves what she teaches.

Great professor! It was her first time teaching STAT 350 and she was amazing. I didn't really like the format of the class but her teaching was great. You can tell she really cares and that is something you don't see in a lot of professors at UMBC sadly. I had a great semester with her! Even though she doesn't curve or anything class was still okay

A great professor who is passionate about teaching her students. Class might be a struggle mid-semester if you don't have a strong calculus background but she is willing to take her time to go through each concept

Absolutely an amazing teacher! Accessible outside of class via Discord. Promptly answered questions w/ supporting info/examples to give a better understanding. You can tell she's passionate about the class, making it more inviting and easier to learn. Drops the 3 lowest quiz and hw scores. A difficult class in general but she makes it tolerable.

Loved her! She really made sure everyone knew what was going on in class. She explained concepts well and made it easy to understand. And she's super animated in a way that makes you want to keep learning calculus. There were 3 exams (including the final) and 3 projects. You can skip lecture but attend discussion and seminar because they count!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Inspirational--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: She's a great and motivational teacher. Always listens to questions no matter how simple and explains everything thoroughly. Her exams are weird but can score easily.

-Class was actually English 204-
 It is an English class, there will be reading but most of the semester was poems/short essays and stories so it wasn't over the top. We did finish with a novel but it was a very quick read and a very good book. The reading material Dr. Yoon picked was always interesting and she obviously cares about her students.

Dr Perez is awesome! She gives lots of constructive feedback on papers & writes a personal response to every discussion post, so you can tell she really engages with everyone's work. Classes are discussion-based but she never forces you to speak. She also lets you skip a few discussion weeks which is helpful for when you have a really busy week.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Caring

reviews.comment: Dr. Perez is a wonderful professor and just an all around kind person. She is willing to take time with her students and provide extra help if you ask for it. She is generous with her time and knowledge. We tackle some touchy material in her class and she handled it with the right amount of sensitivity. Recommended.

Absolutely amazing and perfect professor. Accommodating, very reasonable workload, extremely interesting topics, kind, just absolutely everything you want from a professor. She is a bit of a tough grader but she makes her expectations very clear and achieving an A is as easy as showing that you care about your work and showing up everyday.

Prof. Perez can shift gears & be flexible when a lesson isnt working, finding new ways to present material to make sure that every student understands the key concepts. From personal appearance to organizational skills & preparedness for each class, her communication skills are exemplary.

Prof. Perez is an exemplary & visionary educator. I appreciate & treasure everything she has taught me. Enjoyed the class & learned so much from it. Having her encouragement & support even when I wanted to give up was invaluable. Her class was one of the highlights of my week - each one brought something new and exciting to learn & think about.

She makes you work for the writing-intensive requirement. 500-word responses weekly, 3 essays, group project. She's strict on grading but gives you plenty of feedback and workshop. Most classes are discussions on readings each day, participation graded. She does a checkpoint halfway through to let you know how you're doing. Overall good professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Close to if not a perfect professor. Her readings are never excessive, and she gives meaningful feedback to every assignment including the small ones. You'll read new, interesting, and engaging texts, and there is rarely a dull moment in the class. You will not regret taking her. Talk to her too, she is such a lovely person and is super helpful.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Caring

reviews.comment: Quite enjoyable class. It was her first time teaching it, but it was still good. The poetry section is a bit rough unless you really like poetry. Good feedback on the papers, and isn't too strict of a grader. Group project was enjoyable.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Group projects

reviews.comment: truly my goat, funny guy that offers a good, difficult class that teaches a lot of important subjects.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Gives good feedback--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: He's a pretty good teacher. The class is like an open discussion and you help edit and give suggestions to each others work throughout the semester. Lots of homework, but it isn't awful. You'll rarely receive a 20/20 on an assignment, but his feedback is helpful and he wants his students to succeed. I would recommend this class !!

Prof. Keravec is an accomplished writer in the field of writing for media arts. However, he does not do the best job teaching the class. He has a well of knowledge of the industry of writing and developing writing, but he does not explain concepts nor point students into the direction of fully understanding them. He also seldom responds to emails.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I had her for MATH 120, and she was very helpful. Her lectures are clear and easy to understand, and she is always willing to help when someone is confused. She is also not too strict about late work, funny, and very kind to her students.

I had to retake 151! She explained everything very clearly and never tried to overcomplicate the material. She's very caring and is always willing to help students. Office hours were extremely helpful and would help walk through the problem and material with you so you have a full understanding. She doesn't post lecture notes in blackboard.

Professor Galambos is a great lecturer, and it's clear that she understands how difficult the subjects she teaches are. There are a lot of homework and reading quizzes on Webassign, but they aren't particularly difficult to complete. Pay attention during lectures, submit assignments on time, and do not be afraid to reach out for help.
Hard to understand, not well at explaining in depth but rather just completes the problems.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Dr. Galambos was one of my favorite professors during my time at UMBC. The class, although globally structured, was run very fairly. Print out her online notes before class starts. Go to review sessions, and don't fall behind. This class is not an easy A; however, help is readily available.

Yeah i didnt have her for 151, i had her for 120. She's a nice woman but an EXTREMELY harsh grader (if you're 0.0001 off, she marks 0 pts) and sometimes she's just flat out wrong. Had to argue my way into a passing grade multiple times. Really do not recommend

Great professor! Lectures were not attendance mandatory, classwork is assigned in almost every class, and the quizzes and exams are pretty fair. She makes it known that she cares for her students' grades and is accessible outside of class!

She goes through questions way too fast. She does not allow you to turn in ALEKS assignments late. I am very disappointed at the fact that there is no TA for this course. Quizzes every week. but she drops the two lowest grades. Do not take MATH104 with her unless you are good at math.

Lectures were always lined up exactly with quizzes and exams, so it would be helpful to be in class although attendance wasn't mandatory. She is very accessible outside of class and reminds you of homework, quizzes, and exams.
Galambos was a great professor. She explained things clearly and was accessible out of class for extra help. Exams and quizzes were kind of hard but manageable. She's also very nice

Galambos is a good professor yet some of her explanations did not make sense. If you do the homework and practice problems you will be okay. Exams were very difficult and the final was extremely hard. Content is somewhat hard but that is expected.
Took this class during covid and had to download spyware for tests. Listening to this professor is like watching paint dry.

Professor Galambos Is a good teacher. Most times I left class and I was able to solve all the homework problems without help. Don't get me wrong you need to spend time practicing in order to get an A. But that's just how calc 1 is.

She's a pretty good professor, at least on online classes. She explains problems well enough, but the hw on WebAssign explains it better. The pace during live lectures is very fast, so make sure you have your camera open to take a picture of the notes (if you don't want to watch the recorded lecture).

Exams were crazy difficult until she switched to multiple choice questions. Reading quizzes due before each class and a 20 question webassign the night before your first class of the week. Professor Galambos is very friendly in person, but she is pretty difficult.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: One of the most down to earth professors and you didnt need to be buddy-buddy w her to notice. She cared about lectures and to any students who had questions, she would stay late to assist. The ONLY issue I had was that she wasnt flexible w deadlines. I had a doctors note for an emergency w my younger sister and she wouldnt excuse my quiz grade.

Indeed, for exam 2, she did the free-response format. However, after so many people fail to turn them on time, she switches to the online format for the rest of the semester. The exams are not hard, study and you will do well. And remember to do the HWs. Moreover, she gives us a lot of extra credits in the quizzes and exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: During the COVID-19 Quarantine, when universities transitioned online all the other professors had multiple choice exams. Where as professor Galambos elected free-response online exam.

Her lectures were very clear and pace herself to make sure that people understand the lesson. The load of homework is a given. You're required to do them regardless of your teacher. Calculus at UMBC, in general, is hard. Expect to put in the work!

Professor Galambos is not the greatest at giving lectures. But she is very nice, tries to help, and is always pushing for you to come to office hours. Make sure you do online work, I could not log on for the first week and because of that I missed an A. Attendance is mandatory but you will learn the most by going to your TA discussions.
Professor Galambos was pretty entertaining in lectures, yet i feel that the classwork was not super reflective of what would be on the exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Professor Galambos is a great professor; I believe this is her first year teaching. She really cares about her students and makes the material easy to understand. Our exam averages range from 75-80%, which is better than other MATH 151 averages. She is also really nice and funny, an overall good professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Writes in pen but makes a LOT of mistakes. We have to correct her work multiple times a lecture. Can't explain anything too well (2/5). She does a lot of over complicating on simple subjects. The TA's are good though. I wish they taught the class.

Take him for FIN330! Professor Anoruo understands the lives of full-time working students and parents. I know I won't get less than a B in this class because he made it possible for me to really get through this class. His class materials are extremely helpful! he's awesome!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: AVOID this instructor!  I cannot stress this enough. Learned nothing from him.  He posted power points generated from the textbook, assigned homework from MyFinanceLab, and posted a discussion question each week from the book, but he did not interact with the class at all. Deducted points randomly. Had to FIGHT to have assignments graded.
I took the online Macroeconomics class with Dr. Anoruo and it was easy. I totally recommend this class,It's much faster than the semester long classes. If study, you'll get an A

Professor Anouro, is very knowledgeable in fincance and he took the time to help students learn how to use the finc calculator.  Assignments were easy given from the book and exams where not that bad.  Over all I think he was very laid back.

BEST TEACHER EVER! If you fail his class, there must be something seriously wrong with you. He tells you exactly what he wants on his exams (gives you practice exams). He takes attendance so you would want to go. What I love about him is that he explains everything step by step. Best teacher.
Very helpful. Always willing to help his students.
If only every professor were like Prof. Anoruo.  Everyone should take his class.

You can sit in class, do nothing except hang on aim and still get an A without a problem. Included 4 HW assignments, 3 easy exams, and a project that took about 2 minutes to do. Take him for anything if you want to make your life easier but hurry, his classes seem to get full extremely fast J

His class is easy, then he gives you his test. The first test was missing a chapter that he told us to prepare for, and that we spent most of class time going over, and had problems from a section we were not told to prepare for. The second test about 20 people were still there 35 minutes after class was supposed to be over still struggling to end

Dr. Anoruo is a very helpful professor.  Although at times his explanations may be confusing, he does his best to make the class doable.  He assigns and grades homework, and says on the first day of class that he will not try to make anything difficult for the students.  He even gave a take home exam for the class.  He's also a really nice guy.

Econ 312 in itself it a difficult subject to take at UMBC and if you can get an easy A with Anoruo then do it! I will take any class this guy teaches because it leaves more time to study for other more complex classes like Advanced Accounting. Take him with anything if you want an easy A. No thought process was involved in this class at all.

This man gets my vote for "worst professor ever". He  is unable to explain some of the most fundamental economic concepts, and is bad at explaining those he does understand. The best thing about his 312 is the text; Mankiw is excellent. He is very biased, and his lectures consist of reading Mankiw's PPT slides. He takes attendance. Awful.

This class was very straightforward and easy. The prof is incredibly kind and passionate about this subject. All you had to do was discussion posts, simple quizzes, midterm, and final paper. Had no trouble in this class, 10/10 would recommend :)

Loved this class. There's a lot of reading, but it's manageable if you read a little every day. Quizzes come from the Ayers book, and there is a midterm and final paper. Overall straightforward class. If you want to learn more about the greek and Latin roots as well as a sprinkle of mythology, you'll really like this class. The prof is also sweet.

Erickson was a pretty good lecturer. She enjoyed interacting with the student as much as possible, despite it being an online class. The class was incredibly easy. I read the required readings, but I didn't need too. The quizzes and exams were stupid easy and I achieved over an 100% as my final grade.

Professor Erickson is extremely passionate about mythology and it really shows. I took this class as an easy elective but ended up enjoying a lot of the material. Grades come from discussion posts, quizzes, and exams. There is A LOT of reading material, so you want to make sure you keep up with them and know the gist of what is happening.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Caring

reviews.comment: Super easy GEP class. Not any specific textbook, but make sure you have access to several mythology stories. Only about 4 quizzes, and are easy- each one has extra credit. Definitely take if looking for an easy A!!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: attendance is mandatory, this class is reading and lecture heavy so go through the slides and you will ace the the quizzes and the tests. she also puts up weekly discussion boards but they are not hard at all.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Horrible
attendance is graded. Not a hard class overall if you watch her lectures and read the book. Should be an easy A if you pay attention and do the assignments she assigns.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: If you want an easy A, this is the class for you. As long as you watch every lecture (40 minutes avg.) and complete the discussions, you really shouldn't have an issue. Quizzes are easy and extra credit is offered on it, but the "study guide" is really her just telling you the format. Only bad part of the class is all the reading that's required.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Her adaptation to online learning is awful. Shes putting in zero effort, giving us a prerecorded lecture and making us buy SEVEN books, we have so many assignments with NO in class access to her . Zero effort from her side and still expects the students to dedicate their time to her class, yeah no...

Emily was an easy A, need I say more? Class was once a week. Her homework was all based on completion, the midterm was all online, the final writing assignment was a straight-forward opinion essay, and just showing up to class would boost your grade. If you are looking for an easy GEP, then look no further.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Professor Ergun is the BEST professor I have ever had.  Every day I left class more informed and more knowledgeable about the world.  I have learned more from her class than any other class in college so far.  She is an amazing lecturer, and makes every topic fascinating to study.  Because of her I am now minoring in GWST.

Professor Ergun is very friendly, helpful, understanding, and intelligent. She has a bit of an accent but it isn't hard to understand. For GWST there are response papers due every class, and there's a lot of reading. She is very knowledgable in her field.
Wonderful person, really engaging lectures. Does not use powerpoints, which is awesome.

I don't really agree with the comment below. Emek is incredibly open minded and fun to have as a teacher. She talks a lot about her experiences in Turkey, but that is because she is Turkish, and it is what she knows. These experiences are also very relevant! I never got the feeling that she was ****, biased, or intimidating!!

Very judgmental and biased against Americans, Europeans, whites, and the West. Class is "global perspectives on gender and women," but only HER perspective is allowed. Insists that whites don't have the right to help non-white people. Cuts students off; interrupts them, very unclear about grading - totally arbitrary! Inexperienced teacher - AVOID!
Really awesome and engaging professor.  Extremely knowledgeable about the subject matter.  Her papers will make you work, but she is very clear about what she expects.  Very caring.  Take her class!!

I did not know how good it could be until I took this class by Dr. Engel. His lectures are clear and easy to follow, which is a great help on the homework and exams. Grading is extremely fair. Truly cares about his students and gives very good advice.

Best Professor I've had. Took time to prepare slides that were better than the textbook. Very enthusiastic and captivating lectures. Genuinely cares about students succeeding. Very easy to approach during office hours and responds to emails promptly. If you can take multiple classes with Dr. Engel you won't be disappointed.
amazing teacher

Don Engel is a shining star among professors. If you see a chance to get in a class with this professor, TAKE IT! His lectures manage to make something that should be boring, very interesting. Everyone I have talked to about this professor loves him. His grading is fair and he genuinely wants to see every student excel. The class was perfection.

The fact that I'm giving professor Engel a 5 for teaching algorithms is about all anyone would need to know. If you're able to make algo bearable and in my opinion quite interesting, you're quite a good professor. The grading has been quite fair and its not heavy on memorization which I really appreciate.

Dr.Engel is a great professor. Cmsc 441 is a hard subject, but he made it comprehensible and interesting. There is little to no outside resources for this class and the textbook is impossible to understand. Dr. Engel made animated graphic for every lesson in the book. His slides are the only reason I got threw this class. 10/10 class 10/10 prof.

Enszer is a great guy with some humor. He explains chemical engineering introduction the best he can. Don't be bitter if you don't do well because the major is really hard. Be prepared for hard tests but the problem sets are fine
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Cannot say enough good things about Dr. Enszer. ENCH 225 is a difficult course, but he was always available to help, offer encouragement, and he knew exactly what he was doing (even made his own electronic textbook instead of having us buy one). It was an honor to have studied under him.

Dr. Enszer is engaging, invested in the school, great in class, and loved in the department. Teaching itself is really a big love and focus of his and it shows. He's departing for University of Delaware, curse them... and their terrible (y highly respected) Chemical Engineering department.) Our loss will be a fantastic gain for them.

Dr. Enszer is a fantastic lecturer. He is always on time and extremely prepared for class. The best thing about him is that he really cares about what he teaches, so he is always passionate and excited to teach. His doors are almost always open, and even when he is busy, he will listen to his students. UMBC has been extremely fortunate to have him.

He's charming and engaging, and available outside class. But he's also totally a mathematician in how he approaches things - and talks like one. He's put together his own course materials - very economical. And mainly he's clear, but boy does he love matlab and a linear equation. Would take him for future courses. Gotta give love for a gaming geek.

Terrific instructor.  Clear and concise (but we need to get him a new set of dry erase markers).  Do not fall behind in this class or you will falter (especially in the summer)!  Forced to withdraw due to work conflict limiting my available study time; BUT I highly recommend taking this course under his tutelage.

Really great professor with a clear interest in his students. Super organized and prepared. Very engaging when it comes to courses he regularly teaches/designs (i.e. ENCH 225, ENCH 442, ENCH 470). Innovative teacher who knows Matlab inside and out.  If you must learn Matlab (which you will), he is the best instructor for learning this tool.

He is nice and professional. Not very helpful during his office hours though. He is clear in what he wants from you but unfortunately there are no solutions to his in class/text examples. So when preparing for an exam there is no way to check if your answers to the practice problems are correct. Nonetheless, he is  knowledgeable and approachable.
Whoever gave that ENES rating was probably a mechanical engineer.

He's a gem! If you want to learn and understand ChemE concepts, he is your chance at that (you can't escape him at UMBC even if you try). He is clear, concise, always willing to help, and he is very friendly. Go to class, ask questions, study for exams; his finals are usually more difficult. He is a great teacher, but you have to work hard.

He is the worst professor I have ever had at UMBC. He puts the burden of teaching on the TAs and has little relevant info during his lectures. getting answers from him is like pulling teeth from an alligator.

Great professor! He writes very thorough notes and constantly references the textbook. He does examples quickly, so you have to pay attention, but he's very clear about what he expects from you. He's nice, funny but professional and respectful. He's a gamer, insists on earning rather than losing points, is very meticulous and expects you to be too.

Great teacher! He's VERY prepared, always early to class, available for ?s and his notes are exceptionally thorough! He's a nice guy & knew everyone's names (first and last) by the 2nd class. Keep in mind that it was a small summer class, but he really tried to personalize things(eg: made a unique Pandora station based on our class' preferences).

Dr. Enszer is a great professor, and a great person. He will put in as much effort to help you learn as you do to learn. His lectures are extremely clear, and he posts MOST things online. Tests were easy, but the final was very difficult. Quizzes were simple, and homework was moderately hard (but graded differently depending on your TA).

Very strict grader. Most of the stuff in this class you have to teach yourself by doing practice problems/homework. Lectures weren't much help. Put effort in the class and you should get a good grade.
Pretty good teacher. He seems to be almost overly strict and way to shrewd of a grader. You better make sure you study all material, Disc quizzes are easy if you practice. ATTEND EVERY LECTURE.

Great teacher! Very approachable and knowledgeable of course material. Textbook was used to supplement course notes generated by instructor. Heavy empasis on writing, MATLAB coding, and problem solving.  Also, at least 50% of class is devoted to group labs. Attend class, do hw, and ask questions, and you'll be prepared to do well in the course.

Really great. Very clear and helpful about everything but lab reports. A bit soft-spoken - sit up front. Hard grader but very reasonable with what he asks of you. Very young - around 28. Complete dork (which is awesome). Class isn't that hard if you pay attention. Awesome grading system - it's like a video game! (Again, he's a dork.)

This lady is nuts,  she freaked in our class cause we asked her ?too many questions? about things she should have been able to answer.  A normal teacher is supposed to answer you or at least admit that they don?t know something. But this one would rather call you hostile and put the blame on you.

Nice, but down to business. Show her you care and are actually trying, she will cut you some slack and be very willing to help you out, answers email fast. Allows 1 page cheat sheet for exams. Start prog projects early, ask for help, she'll take time to help you. if it still wont work, she'll be lenient Wait til the last minute tho and you'll fail

Grad student teaching IS 147J.  She curved all of the tests we took, programs were really easy, even gave us a bonus test to help our grades out.  Definitely take 147 with her.  Just make sure to be polite and know your stuff...previous programming knowledge will make the first half of the course a breeze.

She's a great teacher who will take the time to break things down and help you in-class or during her office hours.  Even though the class is for people withour prior programming experience, it would definitely be beneficial if you had some.  Some of the homeworks were pretty hard so ask for help.  She will definitely curve the first test.

Greg is a graduate student, so he knows what its like being a student at UMBC. He has clear slides that he goes over, and gives study guides for his exams. He makes it clear what is expected of you. There are only two other assignments, and easy group presentation, and a written paper about a pysch movie. All around super nice guy.
reviews.rating_tags: BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--Caring

reviews.comment: Greg is the coolest professor you'll ever have. He wants to help his students and doesn't make the course too difficult. Definitely one of the (very) few UMBC professors that I can say I actually like.

Great teacher and intro to psych. Read the chapter before class and keep up with your lab work. I followed the schedule ofr the labs iand it helped get it done before the due date. There are licker questions and class and group work so it helps to show up to class to solidfy the info. But if you miss one class you'll be okay.

Honestly one of the best professors at UMBC. If you're new to psych, definitely attend every lecture and read the textbook. He goes over lecture slides pretty quickly so do your best to keep up. Very friendly and understanding.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Gregory Epstien has clearly had a ton of experience in his feild. He brings his own personal experiences in psychology to class which is a nice touch, however he always has clicker questions, his TA are like watch dogs, he always talks the whole hour and fifteen minutes and sometimes even longer. But if you really like the psychology he is great.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: he's one of the best professors in the psych dept. He goes out of his way to help you even in things not related to class. Lots of extra credit. 1 movie paper and 3 exams. He throws in a quiz whenever he wants so make sure to read. Textbook is needed. All in all he's An amazing professor and his class is great! Take him
reviews.rating_tags: ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--Caring

reviews.comment: pretty chill dude. he goes out of his way to help you succeed and has studygroup sessions from his free time. he's a grad student as well so i guess he understands our struggles. cool dude take him.
reviews.rating_tags: BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Interesting class. 3 exams including 1 final, 1 movie paper, multiple in class quizzes at random- to get attendance. If not there get 0. Responds to emails very quickly. Open to suggestions and change. Extra Credit is available. Very clear grading criteria. I would highly recommend and take him again! No issues at all.
reviews.rating_tags: ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Clear grading criteria--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Robyn is by far the worst professor I have had at UMBC. She canceled class 9 times and she didn't cancel until 10 mins before class. never returned grades. I got all A's on my papers , attendance, and participation, while turning in all of my homework, but received a B. The grading scale was unclear. She is very rude and shouldn't be a teacher.

She is a wonderful professor who really knows the topic of Gender and Women's studies! Not only is she very knowledgeable but also explains everything in detail and makes everything very clear. She is very nice and understanding and I recommend her for this course! There are some readings but they are all interesting and helpful with discussions!

Robyn Epstein should not be a professor at this school. She assigns ridiculous readings and shows extreme frustration when students do not know how to comprehend. She cancelled class multiple times and took months to grade papers but expected students to be on their tip toes when assignments are given to them out of the blue. Do not take this class
Cancelled class repeatedly. Uncomfortable talking in this class. terrible at getting grades back.

Prof. Epstein is amazing. She is not a hard grader, as long as you make an attempt to engage with the material. You will read a lot, and she will quiz you if it appears no one has read. She's super friendly and understanding. Just come to class, come prepared, and don't be rude. She will call you out on disrespectful behavior. Great professor!

I would never take a class taught buy her again. She is rude, and if your opinion doesn't match her opinion she shuts down your idea. the class didn't have many grades, and she did not give back any feedback through out the course. Overall she is a horrible teacher.
Takes a long time to grade stuff.  Didn't grade my last paper, it really hurt my course grade. Why? Why do that?  Do I deserve that?  Overall, waste of time.

Assignments were relevant and interesting, but the class contribution to discussion was often frustrating and irrelevant, which she would often do nothing about. Lost her temper in a very unprofessional manner on a couple of occasions. Also, VERY slow grader. Hadn't graded last paper when she assigned an essay final. Resulted in NG on transcript.

Professor Epstein was one of my favorite teachers in college because she really cares about the subjects , and because she wants you to learn. She really pays attention in discussion. She also really cares about students. It's true that she does not forgive plagiarism, but she tells you that from day 1.

She can be rude and disrespectful if she feels as though your contribution to the group discussion isn't good enough. Also, the slightest citation error you make on essays she tries to accuse you of plagiarism and give you an F in the course. DON'T TAKE THIS COURSE WITH ROBYN EPSTEIN.
Don't take her class
Awesome professor! Very passionate about the topics and knows her stuff. Assignments are easy to do. Material used was very interesting as well.

Unclear rules. Changed syllabus several times. Changed grading system. Unwilling to sympathize with students. Does not address theories by name or definition. Final paper is about a theory we don't know but we don't know any theories now. Second time I've left this review. She must be deleting. Poor teacher overall.
In this class now- it's totally amazing! Be sure to take this class with Robyn!

Dr Epstein is a great professor! At first, it seemed like the course is too hard and boring, but then you are learning a lot, especially about media. You learn how to really think about it so you aren't just mad or too into it. You can be conscious. I grew a lot with Dr Epstein.

Recommend. The professor is so cool. Class almost always kept my attention and she will meet with you to help any time. I didn't know talking about race and women could be so great. Cool class. Taking her again this semester for AMST 310.

This class doesn't have exam but 2 papers to pass, one is short and one should be 20 pages long. Class is easy and make me feel like wasting bunch of time. If you want to get easy A, don't take this class

Thoroughly designed curriculum that taught us about sexualities, identities, and the politics of sexuality.  I learned about things I never knew.  This class was so cool and Dr. Epstein is an amazing person that teaches you to be curious and accepting of the world and yourself.  Definitely recommend!

Professor Epstein taught a challenging and enlightening course.  Mostly, I learnd to understand race and gender constructions in media.  Overall, she taught us to be more conscience in how we consume culture. This was one of my very favorite courses at UMBC.

The best thing about Prof Brown is that he engages in open dialogue with students and broadens their understanding and perspective within the flow of class

Course isn't very strictly structured which can be both good or bad because there are many tangents and rambling moments

A fair amount of reading is required but it's mostly interesting stuff

reviews.comment: Class was fun only downside was that he graded nothing in a timely manner. Things that were due in March got graded well after finals. He took points off for no reason and didn't really explain in his comments. I had a horrible semester in this class because of the stress of nothing being graded and not knowing where I stand the entire semester!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: The course is really interesting and he really makes you think. You will not get bored in this class. You cannot write an essay in 5 hours and expect an A. He is a pretty tough grader but gives great feedback and is available outside of class to help you 1 on 1 with papers.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Inspirational

reviews.comment: WAY TOO MUCH WORK for a 100 level course. Expects his students to write papers as if this was a grad level course and the the only course we are taking. He is a hard grader as well and gives points by the decimal. Also not very approachable.

The class can be interesting at times, but it is definitely more difficult than you'd expect for a 100 class. Eric Brown is funny and tries to keep the material entertaining, but don't expect an easy A; the assignments are very time consuming. The readings can be difficult to understand and/or lengthy. Also he's VERY slow with grading.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: If you struggle with writing like me, then good luck in this class. I personallly felt that I didnt learn a thing in writing a term paper. He is hilarious sometimes, but he is a very tough grader, and his teaching assistant isn't any better. He gets pretty disorganized at times and he is super slow at grading.

Not a bad teacher, but he co-teaches with Tatareweicz, who grades extremely terribly and arbitrarily. This is a 100 level class. I have taken 300 and 400 level English classes and earned A's easily. I got a C on the 1st paper. That being said, Brown is a much better professor and grades much more fairly. Knows his stuff but is sometimes unprepared.

It's a pretty easy class and he's a nice guy but it can get boring sometimes. It wasn't bad for a writing intensive class. 4 essays and a few other SMALL assignments. There are a lot of long readings. You don't have to read every single one in depth but at least skim over them because essays are based on readings. No exams, final, or note-taking :)

Frustrating class- Assignments graded weeks/months after turned in, bribed w/candy & extra credit for this. Lots of LONG required readings posted on blackboard only, lots of printing. Lectures not prepared well. Lots of work in last few weeks because he kept pushing things back. Interesting subject though, just a LOT of work for a 100 level class!

Class material was interesting and Professor Brown definitely knows his stuff, but he's really unprepared.  There's a lot of down time in class while he's trying to figure out what he wants to say.  Tests are easy, but he takes FOREVER to grade things.

Awesome professor. Very interested in what he is teaching. The essays are easy and not too long. Offers several chances for extra credit. Very committed to making his students better writers. The class is interesting. It made me think a lot about how science is done.
SO easy an easy A. Just do your short 3 pg papers well.

History of Science Since 1700. Allows you to take exam within a 48 hour period. Not too tough of a grader on exams, you don't really need to come to class if you read, but never gives work back. EVER. Never graded our final paper (which was worth 60% of the grade). Avoid if you can.

Easy prof, is his last semester teaching at UMBC (Spring 2025), gave us all A's on quizzes bc of course evaluations, Was easy and fair when it comes to grading. However, he is strict with electronics, found this bit frustrating.

Ngl bro yaps like the entire lecture. Attendance isn't mandatory but you have to go to class bc he has random quizzes. He also grades hella hard when it comes to essays he can tell when you use chat gpt. The average quiz grade was like a C-D on the last exam.  I DO NOTTT reccomend him if your looking to take an easy GEP.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: A great professor with great potential but poor execution. I'm conflicted about my rating because he was good and bad since he was funny, yet his class was considerably tedious. Reading endless amounts of philosophical pages before class with my other classes was hard to balance. The readings were hard to understand and the pop quizzes... yeesh.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Beware of pop quizzes--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: spectacular. explains in quite simple terms, excellent professor with incredible knowledge about his profession. I would recommend his classes, yet if you don't attend don't expect to do good. The lectures are key to succeeding in the exams.

Professor Campbell is an interesting guy. He jokes around a bit and has some health issues but his lectures are thought-provoking and he is incredibly wise and insightful. He's not great about posting grades (don't expect grades on essays for a month), just warning.
Just put in the effort, do the readings, participate a little, and you'll be fine.

reviews.comment: homework and papers were rough, his criteria is way too specific.

reviews.comment: He is very articulate and good at explaining things. Focus on taking notes on the lectures rather than the readings. I recommend this class and this prof!

reviews.comment: Professor Campbell was by far the best prof I've had during online classes. The content he covers is actually interesting and this was one of the few classes that actually made me think. I took this class as a humanities requirement, and am pleased that I did. Nice to have a class that challenges your brain without using math. Slow grading

Slow grader, but if you've been active in class and on top of your work, it is likely you will get an A. He is a harsh grader on exams which are essays. Even if you follow what he says, he will grade tough. I still ended the class with an A though. His topics are interesting and I genuinely enjoyed the class. He provides the readings
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: I'm slightly conflicted over how to rate Professor Campbell. I loved his lectures and he displayed a great deal of knowledge and insight into the material we covered in class. On the other hand, he never posted grades on blackboard and usually took over a month to grade papers, despite never being more than a few pages in length.

Quite literally the best teacher I've ever had at any university. Succinct about expectations and thorough in feedback. Provides extensive notes on lectures. A professor who seems to actually want students to benefit from the course. Encourages/seems to enjoy open-minded discussion in class. Lectures are intelligently humorous and engaging. 17/10.

Dr. Campbell delivers clear lectures and provides notes online so you can pay closer attention to what he is saying in class rather than having to worry about taking extensive notes. If at any point you find something to be unclear, he is there to answer questions. His lectures and reading assignments are engaging and he gives helpful feedback.

Professor Campbell is definitely one of the best professors I've hat at UMBC. Your grade in this class comes only from papers (8 pages max)  and class participation (10%) so you should definitely go to class. It also helps because he will like you, especially if you ask questions, and therefore probably be more lenient. Definitely recommend!
Took in winter 2025. Easy class
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: The course itself was easy and I found a lot of the material to be straightforward. The only thing is he is a picky grader and a lot of the feedback he gave back to me and some of my friends seemed very vague and it didn't make much sense why I got the grade I did at times.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: prof stokan is very kind and chill! his class consisted of summaries and exams but if you do that and study for the exams you'll be fine. attendance is counted so make sure to go
Stokan was very kind and clearly knew his stuff. 250 is an intro course to public policy, so it was a little repetitive for me, but you will definitely get a lot out of it regardless

Dr. Stokan is a real GEM at UMBC, considering all the other professors in the department are a waste of time. He is easy going and laid back. The class itself is manageable but he is available whenever you need him. I cant tell you how many times the whole class has been thankful he extended our papers to accommodate everyone-who does that!

I enjoyed being in his class so much that it did not even feel like schoolwork. He is available to help and simplifies the class for you to enjoy. His projects are reasonable and will help in improving your knowledge.

Professor Stokan was an amazing professor. From having recorded lectures to cover the content in depth, to live lectures which would provide more modern context to the issue, to pushing students to engage in recent events-- I loved his class and his teaching style helped me not only understand the content, but apply it to understand the country.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Graded by few things--Hilarious

reviews.comment: Dr. Stokan is a wonderful professor. Very passionate and understanding. Easiest guy to talk to and his class is so much fun. You have to read and do well on exams but he's a cool guy. If you're struggling, he's extremely accommodating and supportive. Great guy, 10/10 professor. DRY course material, hence the 4.0, but he makes it interestingish?

The tests in this class are EXTREMELY hard, questions often don't even make logical/grammatical sense. The professor has no idea how to prepare a class for an exam and it shows on his poor exam averages, though he continues to blame students for not studying well enough. Tests take up so much of the grade that other assignments feel meaningless.

The tests had very little to do with the actual material and questions were very difficult. His lectures are very long and he tends to go off on irrelevant tangents. The class is very test heavy, expect tests to make up a good portion of your grade.

I thought that this class would be more understanding to entry level students due to the fact that it's an entry level class. However, this class is extremely and unnecessarily difficult. First of all, make sure you are good at tests because tests are 66% of your final grade! and many questions on the exams aren't even related to what he teaches!!!
There is no home works other than projects(individual/group). grades are test heavy but he does curves the grade base on results. Should pass easily as long as read power points.

reviews.comment: One of the worst professors I've ever taken. First he's arrogant, his power points teach you nothing and his quizzes and exams are harder than theyre supposed to be. This guy is very full of himself. He gets cited in professional journals all the time and it shows. the guy has a massive ego and leaves everything up to the TA who does nothing but sits on her phone all class. Dont even think about trying to email the guy because hell just refer you to the ta who doesnt respond. His grading system is wack

Professor Ellis is very entitled. He is not accepting of feedback from his student and not even the slightest understanding or companionate about his students well beings. This professor does not care about his students. As a class we voiced our concerns and he took no accountability and kept blaming us for our problems. He also was talking down on community colleges as well which is disgusting considering i came from a community college. Hes inconsiderate of others and doesn't realize his teaching is outdated.

Hes a terrible teacher! Our class asked him to create a study guide for tests and he told us to use our notes from his slides that he is never clear about. Literally told us "Study guides are cheat sheets and I do not hand out cheat sheets and neither will life. Figure it out." Absolutely the worst professor, doesn't care about his method of teaching and how it is not useful to his students

Professor Ellis is very knowledgeable. Though quizzes are not easy, they are doable. And you get to learn from the quizzes, which really helps for exams. As long as you skim over the assigned readings before class you will understand what is going on. Professor Ellis does not teach things straight out of the text book. He includes many rl examples.

reviews.comment: This was honestly the worst class I have ever taken at UMBC. There's a textbook but you may as well memorize his lectures bc that all matters on exams.

reviews.comment: Dr Ellis is a really inspiring man who has a lot of interesting things to say. He's endlessly knowledgeable and extremely neutral in how he presents environmental studies. His lectures are very engaging, and I enjoyed going to his class. Hope I can take another class with him in the future.

Dr. Ellis is a good teacher and knows everything there is to know about landscape ecology. Do not take this class if you are not interested in the specifics of landscape ecology. It was not what I expected but I enjoyed the class as it went on. Dr. Ellis is very well known and has a lot of connections in the field.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Gives good feedback--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: I took his class in the fall of 2018 and he is a gem! When I took the class there was a quiz every Friday-the quiz was only graded based off effort. If you tried, at all, then you got a 100% on the quiz. Same goes for the wiki page. For the exams, I never read the book, I took detailed notes and reviewed them once before the exam and got an A.

Do not ever take him as your professor. He is very entitled and does not care about his students. His grading are unclear and will make you feel stupid if you ask him about it. He should not be teaching since he does not demonstrate a good caring teacher. Just because he taught Harvard does not mean anything.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Dr. Ellis is a fantastic professor. I was a little apprehensive going into his Landscape Ecology class, but it is one of my favorite classes that I've taken at UMBC. Also, his exams are completely fair; there are NO surprises. Although they're open response, he's open to a variety of answers. Highly recommend this class for any GES major.

I don't know why Dr. Ellis doesn't have a better rating. In my opinion he is very talented, engaging, passionate, funny, clear and fair. I loved his class and think he is an awesome professor. If you do all of your assignments well and on time, read the book thoroughly and show up to lecture you should have no problem succeeding in his lass.

He's an ok guy but the class was hard for no reason. He had very brief power points and the book was very boring! he was there to help but you'd have to go on his free time or set an appointment. I don't recommend this class at all if your not well with understanding what you read and taking notes.

DO NOT I REPEAT DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS. It is one of the worst classes in the GES department. Between changing the dates around every week and not explaining the material clearly at all, I'm lucky I passed

If you have questions for this guy, I wouldn't bother.  I took this class because the past comments didn't seem extremely bad, but it is seems really apparent that he cares more about his research then he does his students and teaching.  Would litterally walk out of class at the end when students were trying to stay and ask questions.
very good teacher.

He is a nice teacher and is willing to help, but can be rather unclear in answering your questions sometimes and condescending towards an idea that you would feel is sound. This class was a test class to help him write his book, and it wasn't structured well. In all I'm not going to take GES302 b/c of this class.

I got a C but did absolutely NO work and did my quizzes at the last minute with my textbook!! <-- HINT HINT easy!! AND his lectures DO correspond with the exam? you just need to read the book and listen to what he says obviously correlating with the book. Nice guy he's my academic advisor approachable to me

The powerpoints really explain the information, you yourself need to understand what is being said. But it is CLEAR. He is very helpful & likes helping as much as he can. He is approachable by email, but don't be scared to ask in person, he just seems stressed. 3 exams, 60 Q's each. 6 Online quizzes. A lot of reading in the book. Nice teacher!

His lectures are pretty dull and he makes the class harder then it needs to be.  Reading the book is a much better alternative then attending lectures.  He also assumes that the students just happen to know certain vague things, which left me sitting confused.  The difficulty of the test questions does not correspond with the class level.

This guy cannot teach.  Had him for intro to environ. sci.  He's fairly incomprehensible; his slides are nonsense and don't clearly follow with his lectures.  Too pretentious to seem approachable.  His test questions are ambiguous, despite any objections from him, and don't really have much to do with his lectures.  Take with another professor.

If you enroll in a course with Prof. Ellis, ensure you?re well versed in the subject beforehand.  As previous reviewers state, he makes the course more difficult than it needs to be - case in point, his tests.  However, the final grade is based upon additional factors - you can improve your grade and trust me, you'll need to.  I escaped with a C.

BIGGEST ****. don't take it with him, find another class with a different professor if you absolutely have to. It's all common sense but he makes everything much  more difficult than it really is. heartless and shows no remorse for any situation, even if you're practically dying.
The class is made harder than it should be; it's very important to read the book.

I have Erle for GES 120, (intro environmental science). This professor seems very interested in this topic and presents his lectures with an engaging voice and attitude. If you do the reading and practice quizes the exams are way easy. Though we are required to do wiki and discussion board posts online that can be a real pain.

Pretty average teacher. Exams are a bit hard though, you will need to study. Never any homework except to read. I usually waited till a few days before the Exam to read everything i was supposed to and still did fine. Very friendly guy.
No Comments
No Comments

I have never had a teacher so bad it made me want to drop the class. At least until Ellis. His lectures made me fall asleep no matter how much sleep I got. The fact that he just read off his slides didn't help. He might be ok for 120, but don't take him fo landscape Ecology, it will be a mistake.

Umm, the lectures are very interesting, but the exams are difficult!  Online quizes are a plus, and you get to retake them for an A.  other than that, it's just online discussion, but make sure you are there and take good notes in lecture,b/c they're not online, and he's all about taking good notes
Don't do it. He gave me a 67% as a final grade. He is not helpful and exams are worded in a way that causes confusion. Prior knowledge is required!

I think Dr. Ellis is a good teacher. If you go to class and participate as well as take some interest you'll do fine in the class. I'm an Env Science major and I think he does a great job with his Env Science class... Probably easier classes to take but you'll have a good understanding of the environmental topics if you take his class.

This calss was not hard at all, he words some exam questions in a way that is tricky, but if you really think them through you will have no problem. He gives very good notes on powerpoint too, also interesting videos and pictures.
Exams have nothing to do with lecture, don't take the class

DONT TAKE IT WITH HIM!!!Worst teacher...he doesn't know how to teach the information instead he worries about his presentation of power point instead of caring if you actually learned it.  I ended with a 68% and he wouldn't give me a C even though I went to him numerous of times for help.

I did not like taking this class with Hamilton. His lectures didn't make much sense. If you have background in Python, sure you're good. If you rely on his teaching to learn, you'll probably have difficulty. His exams aren't bad. He's just okay. He's very unhelpful during office hours.

Definitely attend the lectures, he does a great job explaining the topics. Do not procrastinate especially on the projects. Start learning python before you take the course because he moves pretty fast, and go to his office hours!

Class is all lectures hearing him geek out about the class content(highly recommend), covers concepts in the form of "how does this algorithm/proof operate, be able to write some psuedocode or result so you can show you understand". Very smart guy, good course.

Hamilton is both a thorough and fun lecturer (downside is he is confusing at times, and fast). The class is hard if you're not used to coding so if you're like me don't expect to get everything the first time. Projects and homework are hard. Do not procrastinate it is painful. Exams are straightforward if you know the content and he's very lenient
Great professor! Explains complex topics clearly and makes class engaging. Super helpful during office hours.
the goattttt
hes so helpful and explains stuff so well!
Such an amazing professor! All the people complaining are just lazy, and 201 is the easiest it'll get if you're a comp sci major.

You can tell Professor Hamilton truly loves teaching. Their passion for computer science makes lectures engaging and fun, even when the topic is like recursion. They're great at breaking down difficult material and making it feel manageable. Highly recommend their classes if you get the chance!
This is a good class. good prof
Without question this is the best comp sci professor at UMBC, its not an easy class, but its worth it
Pretty simple class for beginners
Not sure about these negative ratings, this is for sure who you want to take this class with
Go to lecture and your good.  no textbook needed
This is a very good prof. I took 201 with him a couple semesters ago and he was great. he needs to teach more upper level classes
Very good prof. I went in with little to no coding experience and he really helped
If you go to class, you should be fine. The practice exams are almost identical to the actual exams

For a CS Prof, he's decent. HE TYPES EXSTREAMLY FAST! You actually have to put effort into the class, it's not an easy class. Its frustrating when he'd go through previous exams and there'd be mistakes or he would run out of time or could say that the problem was extremely hard and why did he put it on the exam. Go to the lectures, or you'll fail.

The class was easy for the most part. I would recommend learning the basics of Python before starting to make the class even more easier to the point where you don't need to show up to any lecture. He does try to trick you on the exams sometimes so be careful about that. Overall, easy class.

He likes to go off on random tangents. His lectures are pretty dry, but 201 is so easy you don't need to go unless you want to relearn or have him go over the basics. I would say to go to his class right before the midterms as he gives you the answers for the multiple-choice section and tells you what you need to focus on.

His lectures and dry, confusing, and overall not helpful. He frequently goes on tangents about pop culture, such as spending large amounts of class time talking about Portal 2 or The Fifth Element. Luckily, CMSC201 is extremely easy, so you probably don't need to go to class to pass.

You either like him or you don't. He doesn't bore you with slides and does in-class programming almost 99% of the time. Projects are definitely more difficult than they should be for a introductory class but they are all doable. Tests are difficult-ish.
The man!!! Office hours he is very helpful. Projects are very clear and the rubric is put out for projects.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Entertaining and self deprecating. 202 is rough with anyone and your experience won't be too different between sections, but Hamilton kept class time engaging, at least compared to Dixon

Professor Hamilton is amazing! He's very committed to his students' success, explains difficult concepts well, accessible outside class, and genuinely cares about his students. Lectures can be fast-paced due to extensive material of the course itself. Consider taking 104 first, regardless of professor. Very underrated and deserves more recognition.

As someone who has both been taught by and worked for Professor Hamilton, I can say he is by far the best professor I've ever had. If you're willing to do the work with integrity, you'll have no trouble succeeding in this class. He genuinely cares about his students and he's very approachable in office hours.

Only enroll in Hamilton's 201 class if you have coding experience. His rapid pace requires extensive outside work. I secured an A with prior knowledge but still struggled on projects, but tests are easy if you practice with example tests. Beware: strict policy against code sharing; sharing results in class failure. I would avoid him if you can.

Great professor, just pay attention in lectures and practice what he teaches in class and go over his github slides. Exams are easy. Best to reach out to him via email with screenshots of your code and explain the issue you are having. 6 HW, 10 Labs and 3 Projects. Exams were pretty easy, simple concepts covered MCQs, debugging and 2 coding.
Mr. Hamilton is special, so it's no wonder he spends so much time talking about star wars instead of teaching us how to code. You have to self-teach yourself almost everything.

Good lectures that were easy to understand, textbook referenced but not required to read. He doesn't post any content online so it is definitely required to come to lecture, but he is funny and engaging so it never felt like a slog. All tests and homework graded leniently. As others have said, he is more of a math guy.
They are super nice, make all the assignments clear, and go over some processes with similar questions in class. Super easy class.

really accessible and helpful during office hours and responds to emails within 5 hours or less. he is truly a math dude and many of his examples are math-related. he does go sometimes a bit too fast but dw he posts his notes on Git Hub. attendance isn't mandatory but I suggest you come to class to hear the explanations.

idk wth was going on in his 201 class, but he does seem to be more of a math guy. For 441 I didn't really pay attention in class, but it was like discrete math so it was never too bad and for once in my CMSC life there were actually online sources for the stuff we were learning. the class was easy and the final was optional (for our class at least)

Eric literally bestieeee. Class was hard bc no prior experience. He is knowledgeable about Python, so his personal office hours were more helpful than TAs. Sometimes hes too fast/sidetracks during lectures, but he gave us exam extra credit + would give project hints. Get ready to invest a lot of time into the weekly HW (6) and projects (3)!

Eric's lectures are very useful and everything he demonstrates has a purpose. I can't speak for the 201 students, but I would say that he's a math guy, so 441 is probably his strong suit. Highly recommend.

Not a CS major, but I took this because it was a recommended class for me to know. I hadn't done a bit of python before this class and I felt like it was pretty easy. If you miss a lecture he has an entire semester of lectures from COVID up on his youtube channel which made the in-class lectures not as stressful. His lectures helped a lot. Spring22
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: Prof Hamilton teaches the class by explaining and using whatever he taught in pyCharm w/ energy. I like the unusual information he would share while discussing coding. The worst aspect of his teaching method is that his hands move too quickly, making it difficult to keep up with him later in the semester, although he publishes his notes on GitHub.

Pretty nice professor. Heavy on lecturing with no materials posted online, so you need to go to class to get the information. Lectures are pretty clear though and if you take notes you can get through them. You can tell he's really passionate about computer science though and he'll sidetrack into more complicated stuff as he lectures.

I have never hated a professor more. I had 2 years of coding experience going into the class and still fell behind and was told it was my fault for not doing enough to catch up when I asked for help. He basically refused to clarify any questions I had on projects because 'all the info was in the rubric'

Coming into this class with hardly any solid programming experience was quite difficult at the beginning. Over time it got easier although the homework and projects got harder. The best tip I could give to a student prior to taking this course is to look over the lecture slides before class and to start the homework as soon as possible.

CMSC 201 is an intro to programming but he teaches as if you already know the basics. Hamilton is understanding when asking for extensions. Teaches and codes too fast, I couldn't keep up. As someone who has no coding experience, hws and projects were very difficult and one hw problem took me days to do even with the help of tutors and my TA.

Codes in class, but doesn't properly explain what the code means or why he's writing it. Even though the class is meant for people with no programming experience, there's no way anyone could learn without previous experience with his pacing and poor explanations.

It's like he's trying to put the whole class to sleep every lecture. Doesn't let students help each other or discuss how they solved a certain problem, considers it cheating. Had a book but would be unclear on due dates for assignments on it. Doesn't put the grades in Blackboard, you have to create a whole new account just to see exam grades.

This dude goes so damn fast you cannot even keep up. You know he is bad when everyone is staring at their screen confused in his lecture not even trying to take notes or even attempting to but the dude just goes way too fast. His homeworks and projects are obscene and its so called "beginner" programmer with "no" prior coding experience is terrible

Wonerfully funny and online-savvy guy, but this was the most disorganized and hard to learn class I've ever had.  It was almost impossible to tell what we needed to learn, there were almost no practice/assignments, and lectures were so unfocused the simplest of topics became an overwhelming, confusing mess.  Super easy grader though!

He is a terrible professor who not only doesnt used the text book at all, but his lectures are really useless. His lectures are cringeworthy and are not worth going to. Dont take his class, please. Id rather go to a community college than learn from "Mr Hamilton". Btw, star trek sucks dork

Overall, Professor Hamilton's course on Intro to CompSci 1 was challenging, but rewarding. The assignments in this class are project-based, meaning you use the code you learn over time. This helps solidify an understanding of programming concepts. Topics covered include, conditionals, iteration, recursion. Heavy emphasis placed on array manipulatio
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Whatever bad things people say about him in this class is true. This is not hard class, prof Lupoli and Hamilton made this class harder for new students. Self learning will be your only way.

Even with a little experience programming, this dude was not it. In lecture, he would often go on tangents and did not explain the harder concepts well. Thankfully, I got a good TA but yeah, the later and hws and projs are hard, the projs especially. not the best prof and I will def avoid him when I retake this class.

reviews.comment: If you're thinking of starting with Hamilton on your CMSC journey, don't. If you have taken Comp sci in HS(or prior computer science courses), you should be fine, but if not this will be very hard for you. The Homework's take a while to do / typing, formatting and submitting and that's not including time spent thinking about it. His lectures are all over the place and goes off topic often. I took this in fall 2020. The lectures are extremely disorganized, but somewhere within that mess, there's stuff you're gonna depend on for projects and hw. Pray you get a good TA because mine had a terrible attitude and barely showed up to our meetings, nonetheless responded to my messages. She was blonde. There's such a terrible support system.

I had a similar experience to the person who took the class to decide a major, I ended up dropping as well. reviews.comment: I had to take this class to decide for major but ended up withdrawing. It is very hard for beginners and you dont get much help in this class. Hamilton is excellent. Really smart guy and delivers lectures in an entertaining way.

Eric Hamilton is a really great professor. His lectures were a lot of fun. Professor Hamilton was always very engaging. The lectures can get kind of math-heavy when he goes off on math tangents at the chalk board, but it's fun seeing him get into it. Quizzes and exams aren't too difficult if you follow along with all of the lectures.

Hamilton is just not it. His lectures have little-to-basically nothing to do with the homework and other assignments that he assigns; so there really is no point in going.
