reviews.comment: Unless you have endless time on your hands, this class might not be for you. the amount of time needed to complete the hw and projects is a lot. They aren't crazy difficult, but its basically just trial and error because you are trying to learn the concepts while having to code semi complex projects/homework.
Want even my teaches but he's the only reason I survived my class because my teacher was very incompetent. A cool dude who teaches quite well.

His entirely class structure during COVID college was intensely impersonal and a slog to get through. From youtube livestreams that werent good teaching/review tools, to projects that were always harder & more time consuming than he planned, to just having a condescending attitude throughout it all-- he made sure the class wasnt student friendly

Unusually mean and not very understanding of the online environment. He completely got rid of a lecture time because he didn't feel like repeating himself, so a lot of students couldn't ask questions during lectures and had to just watch a recording. When students would ask questions in class, he would read them outloud, pause and not even answer??

This class ruined by self esteem and my first semester at college. The professor was never available. The TA's had to teach. The TA's are abundant but your chance of getting one that is actually willing to help you is low. Try to get A's on the projects because they will be a big influence on your grade. And it's 100% not a beginner class.

Aside from late homeworks, exams, and slow grading, Prof. Hamilton made this class with several horror stories quite enjoyable imo. His lectures were super helpful as he mostly draws out the concepts and does live coding on those topics. He is super helpful with the projects especially early on, so don't sleep on the projects and ask too late.

CMSC201 for majors with Professor Hamilton was initially easy but became incredibly difficult, even with my prior coding experience. Hamilton handled this online semester poorly, making assignments more difficult than necessary (he acknowledged this himself) and was not helpful at all. He is smart and knows his stuff, but isn't a good professor.

Hamilton is a nice guy, but the class is god awful. During his lectures he goes off on random topics that have nothing to do with the lesson or the upcoming assignments. Tried to set a meeting up to talk about hws/etc but he never showed up. If you dont have background knowledge, dont even bother. TAs are nice but quite harsh and not specific.

reviews.comment: 201 was beyond difficult; nowhere near considered an "introductory course." If you have no prior background in Python, you're going to be spending an immense amount of time and energy on the homeworks/assignments. Hamilton was "nice" and knows his stuff, but goes on random tangents about stuff that doesn't relate to anything. Not recommended.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Prof. Hamilton is great 201, but fell apart in 341. He was always late on the release of homeworks and exams, always late on the grading of said assignments, one time changed a question on the midterm half way through us taking it, and doesn't read the project documentation before helping students thus breaking code. We felt neglected as a class.

Prof. Hamilton offers extension on projects and homework, is very accessible outside of class, gives extra credit on projects and likes to crack a joke or two in lectures and on assignments but he expects a lot for an intro course and made me question whether I wanted to continue CMSC. Hamilton knows his stuff, but I wouldn't recommend him to start

If you think you will, or currently struggle with entry level coding, try turtle programming on CodeHS. This level of coding is below what a college level class is, but will help w/ fundamentals. Prof E does a great job explaining concepts and makes it to where its not just some boring thing where you watch a dude type for an hour.

A lot of bad reviews that I don't think he deserves. This class is obviously a weed-out class. If you can't take the heat, don't be mad at prof E. His lectures are helpful and he is pretty accommodating regarding extensions and all. especially online. This class was probably the most difficult I've taken but I can give credit where it's due.

Eric Hamilton is one of the worst professors at UMBC I have ever taken. Not only are his lectures intensely concept/course heavy, but he does not explain them in a manner in which you as an introductory student, would understand. Unless you have prior background knowledge in Python, you are going to fail. He knows his stuff, but is not a good prof.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Eric is a math whiz, and that routinely shows up in his lectures. He's also funny and likes to crack nerdy jokes when teaching.

Hamilton made sure to keep the class interesting. The best thing to see in a professor is to see them actually caring about students really learning the material. He taught so that people understood, not so they would just do well on the exam. He super available outside of class, and I only went to him for help with code instead of TA office hours.

Since most people are signing up for classes soon, ill write a review. As the other reviews have said, the class is extremely difficult for an introductory class. I've never coded before and I find myself spending hours outside of class trying to understand. Hamilton knows his stuff, but as intro level students, he holds a very high standard.

If you're looking to get into Computer Science, do not start your journey with Hamilton. The class is homework heavy and assignments take between 20-25 hours a week to get a low B. It disappoints me to say that I was really looking forward to my major because of Python, however, it is just ruined for me.

Fantastic guy! Really likes to teach you things. Very easy grader, during one exam he literally helped people on the exam sheet. His lectures were very fun, and I enjoyed being in them. 10/10 would recommend
terrible with lectures. Acts like he actually cares, but in reality, he doesn't. gives the stupidest programs for he and bad exam questions. lots of grammatical errors in his problem sets.

I took comp201 with prior experience, and I would absolutely NOT recommend Mr. Hamilton to anyone who really wants to learn. His assignments forbid students from using the built in features of Python for no reason other than to increase the difficulty. If I hadn't worked as a developer before this class, I would have failed.

I had him for 201 in the Fall 2019. He had very specific slides which helped me better understand the material covered. His live coding does tend to go fast. But he was always happy to help during his office hours when it came to projects and exams. He helps guide you on the projects which is very helpful. Would definitely take him again!

Makes an intro class, which students with no prior programming knowledge should be able to take impossibly difficult. In class, he gives the most basic examples but in the homework & tests, expects you to solve difficult problems even those with programming experience struggle with. He is also cold and aloof when you approach him during office hour

Even before class went online due to Covid-19, his teaching was the most unprofessional, disorganized, and lazy I have EVER encountered in all my years of schooling. When asked about a course plan or help outside of class, he responded with "lol, I don't even know what I am going to be teaching when I walk into class!". Do not take with Hamilton!!!

I am so happy I took Eric for 341. Hes very knowledgeable on the subject and always kept the class interesting. He helped me and others a lot on projects for hours after office hours were supposed to end. He made difficult exams but graded them very leniently. He chose to make our final optional which took a lot of stress off of finals week.

Nice guy but I didnt learn anything from his lectures. UMBC claims you dont need programming experience to pass the class but even people with programming experience struggled the second half of the semester. I withdrew from the class because I was failing.

Professor Hamilton is a decent professor. He def knows the subject and cares about teaching. The class is a little disorganized with the grading but this is an irregular semester. I had no experience with coding before the semester and this class was pretty easy. Just play around with python and you'll do fine.

Hamilton knows his stuff and has been coding for a long time. However, homeworks and projects are way to hard for an introductory course and the expectations are way too high. Do not expect to receive many grades for this course even though you will have assignments weekly.

A lot of the bad reviews here are surprising. Erics lectures are easy to follow and well paced. He goes off on tangents sometimes but it keeps the class fun. I had no experience coding and found that if you just attend the lectures and start the work early, its an easy course. The biggest downside is grading is slow but its a giant class.

Eric Hamilton is by far the worst professor I've had at UMBC. Has a horrible attitude, and acts like he's doing you a favor answering your questions. He ignores emails, grades extremely tough, and takes months to grade assignments.. DO NOT take this class with Eric Hamilton unless you want to suffer for an entire semester. Horrible Prof/Person.

Bruh this professor is trash. He got a cocky attitude and he seem like he don't want to help you or something. He makes the projects and assignments way too hard. TAKES FOREVER TO GRADE. THAT OTHER REVIEW THAT SAYS he explained project 3 very carefully is a burner because proj3 was released 2 weeks after April 13, 2020. DONT TAKE THIS CLASS!!!!!!!!

He definitely knows his stuff and is helpful. However, he makes an intro class impossibly difficult, especially the homeworks . Grading is tough and strict as well. I think he is in charge of the material for this semester and I heard from those that took 201 previously said that this current semester's material seems way more difficult.

reviews.comment: If you do not have people who you can study with or already know the material, be prepared to study individually. When asked for additional help, he uses the "I have other students to worry about" attitude. Takes several weeks to get back returned assignments.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--So many papers--Tough grader

reviews.comment: I retook the class with Hamilton and I found his lectures to be really engaging, he can get a little off topic, which I didn't mind, and actually found very interesting, but for first time learners of the material, it might be a little confusing. For proj3, he gave a very helpful walkthrough, when other profs will avoid talking about projs at all.

DO NOT TAKE HIS COURSE! He doesnt not go by syllabus at all for grading. He changes it mid-semester (50/50)to where youre screwed. You dont get feedback on turned in work like weeks after. He often cancels his office hours and ignores your help emails. One lecture he spent 45 minutes on a topic to then have realized he taught it wrong.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Eric is a great guy, and banters with the class a lot which is very cool and funny. I had him for CMSC 201 and have him now for 203, and my advice would be that while he's a good teacher for 201, he's not great for 203. It may be because this is his first time teaching this class, but the structure is very messy. He's easy for 203, less for 201.
Hamilton is a really good guy, but just goes off on random tangents about math almost every 5 minutes. Hes a mathematician at heart, and it really shows.

Professor Hamilton was by far my favorite professor so far. He kept the lectures entertaining and overall was just very knowledgable. I felt that the Projects were a little on the tougher side, but regardless CMSC 201 was great.

He was poor. I did ASL 101 with him online, and he rarely responded to emails & waited until JAN 5TH to grade 25 assignments from weeks prior. He will ignore you during Zooms and doesn't seem to really care about students. I'm thinking about taking ASL at my local community college & transferring the credit instead of letting ASL drag down my GPA.

Do not take this professor if you want to be happy. He is SO condescending and has kicked someone from our zoom for yawning. He doesn't answer emails and grades everything within the last week of the semester. Group assignments are done each class- if your partner doesn't know what's happening, tough luck- he does NOT care and will call you out.

This professor does not respond to emails or questions via Zoom. I have repeatedly reached out to him, and he has not replied to a single thing. He only bothers responding to you if he thinks you aren't paying attention. The class is fairly easy. He does not grade anything until the last minute, though. I would not recommend him as a professor.

The single worst professor at UMBC. This man will ignore you the entire semester because he doesn't care about his students at all. Grading is completely arbitrary and most of the assignments weren't graded until after the last day of class. Do not take his class under any circumstances, it's crazy to me that this man still has a JOB.

For ASL 101 - Do NOT take this professor if you genuinely want to learn ASL. He does not respond to emails, very disrespectful towards students, instructions on assignments are very unclear, accuses you of using your phone of you're just zoning out, and kicks you from the mandatory Google meet classes without telling you.

This professor does not enter any grades until the day before grades are due to the university, you will never know how you are doing in the class the entire semester. He doesn't bother to respond to emails either, he's extremely unhelpful. The entire class you're paired up with a random person to practice signing you barely know, it's unhelpful

He only sometimes responds to emails, also didn't grade until the class was completed. Nice guy and I think his lectures are helpful in learning ASL but the structure of the class was lacking. Grading was too tough and there's lots of make up opportunities, interesting content
Interesting, fair and give extra credit for participating

Professor Read was okay, yes it was lecture heavy but if you pay attention you'll be fine. The study guilds are great except for the final exam one which most of it wasn't on the quiz. The class was very lecture heavy and you have to attend every class (there is a grade on class attendance). But she is very passionate about her work and just wants us to succeed

dogwater professor, in order to get a good grade you need to come to every single class which shouldnt even matter for some easy A credit class. made way harder than it needed to be. nobody cares about archaelogy

Professor Read is friendly and passionate about her work. Her class is lecture heavy so paying attention to the spoken material is important. Her lecture slides are quite useful and available outside of class. There is a lot of memorization needed for quizzes and exams but the difficulty is manageable.

Very difficult class, only passed b/c I had a previous students work for the class which when followed closely, will guarantee and A in the class. The quizzes and exams are some odd questions which I averaged a C on the quizzes, and a -A on exams. Hard class in general & i'd recommend to avoid unless you know someone who previously took it (exams).

Class was eh. At the start of the semester, she would give straight forward study guides but as the class progressed the study guides she would provide became more convulated and redudant. Very laid back and funny proffesor but at the same time was very petty and strict about attendance. Beware it's not an easy given A.
I wish I dropped this class.

This class was a lot of work for a gen-ed. If you want a gen-ed thats an easy A and will boost your GPA, don't take this class with her. \I became very disinterested in the topic after taking this class. Overall a very great professor that is passionate about what he teaches. His goal is that he wants you to grab concepts or at least be familiar with them to help with future careers. Scope of the course is to learn coding. During the course it felt like we were blazing through every coding language.

As a senior at UMBC, I have to say that Professor Fayyaz has to be one of the best if not the best professor I have ever had. Dr. Fayyaz is an absolutely fantastic professor. He puts a lot of effort into making sure you are able to fully grasp the course material.

He means well and wants us to learn amongst ourselves as wells as in class and his expertise on the subject shows. He moves pretty fast during lecture which makes it follow and understand. Be prepared for very long lectures that you have to patriciate in for their entirety . It's an easy class but a lot of work. Finish the work and you'll do fine.

Alwaus participate!
Impossible to reach outside of class with no kind of grading policy. Still can pass the class if u turn something in. Will not learn anything.

He was very flexible and shows in class examples.
The content is very useful. I actually liked it and Fayyaz was super knowledgeable. In class examples and following along. Explains things super well stepbystep.

Dr. Fayyaz was really patient to explain every single question that students asked, he also gave us a simple and easy example to explain the complex question. Overall, he was an excellent professor at UMBC.

One of my favorite professor. I have learned a lot in his class.
An extremely interesting class that all college students should take. It's a lot of work but as long as you do the assignments, it's very possible to get an A.

Great professor! Very understanding. His exams are very easy and the coding part of it is open book/computer. Also the final project is extremely easy. Definitely take him for IS420. Easy A

I took IS410, IS448. He is caring professor, however skiping a class not an option.
very helpful.

heavy lecturers, technical terms and too many concepts. Good class to learn dss.

Very knowledgeable. It was very easy and straightforward and he is also fair in dealing with grades.
Awesome teacher, really knows his material and is clear in explaining everything. Very helpful and cares for the students.
Great professor! Love the way how he explains. Very helpful, can talk about anything and very encouraging!

Really good professor, he is nice and he offers you help if you need it, I would totally retake it. The final project was very challenging and the exams as well, but he gives study guides so you can see what's going to be in the exam.
He is a shining example of how most professors should be. He is extremely helpful. One of the best professors. He makes you work a lot for the class, but it is worthy all that you learn for life.

Let me start out by saying this is truly one of the best of professors. His lectures were long but well structured. He made sure you learn the topic and understand the concepts not just memorize stuff. Test are hard, 2 exams, 1 project and 1 presentation. super Easy, but also easy to fail if don't take it seriously.
It was a about coding and application development.  It was hard but I have learned a lot.

Worst professor I've had at UMBC. Lectures consisted of copy-pasting code he sent to us via e-mail, but half the time would not work. Excellent learning, long classes. Learned a lot about application development.

I would not recommend his class to anyone. I took him because he made it seem a good learning session the first class. Everything went down the hill after the first two weeks. He is not clear at all what he is teaching and keeps changing things. The last day you have to take thr final and do presentation. Not clear lectures or explanation.

Never have I EVER taken a class like this. The exams are designed to make you second-guess what you know, the lectures fast paced, and the homework barely matches the learning objectives. Even with a final grade curve and an exam drop, people still struggle to earn a good grade—take that as a sign!!

Nice guy but terrible prof. Very unorganized and scattered slides which makes it really hard to study. His lectures consist of heavy breathing and just reading the slides at x2 speed. Took the class with him and Bierberich, who was a really good professor with super neat and easy to follow slides and good lectures in contrast to this dude.

Dr. Vonhoff is very knowledgeable and passionate about teaching and wants his students to succeed. He is a nice man. But his exams are all on slide material but he goes through 90 slides in such a short time every lecture so you have to make time outside of class to understand the material. He goes too quick and the exams are worded weird.

Study lecture slides before and after lectures and the class won't be as bad as people say it is.
The Professor rushed through the slides during lecture so it was very hard to understand. The textbook wasn't really helpful and the exams were based on the slides. The curve is high though

Can drop 1 exam. Lecture powerpoints were difficult to follow during class at times. A caring and kind person when you ask for help. Exams could be tough as lecture content was not the most dynamic all the time. Definitely tried to make the class more engaging.

Professor Vonhoff is one of the nicest I've had at UMBC. His powerpoints have a lot of information on them but that is helpful when you need to review for exams. His exams did require a good bit of studying, which is typical for an upper-level BIO course. It's clear he cares about students and he is always happy to answer any questions you have.

I am taking BIO302 this semester with Prof. Vonhoff and I would not recommend any other student to take this class with him because he spends more times reading information off the slides instead of actually explaining them. The exams are heavily based on his slides and each of his lecture consists of 90-100 slides.

For someone who teaches genetics, he should be able to explain the topics clearly and slowly. Dr. Vonhoffs lectures are too much and he only spends a very small amount of time explaining something that needs a deep explanation. Other than that he's chill

Vonhoff as a lecturer was just all over the place. I don't think he should have taught the classical genetics portion of the course since the textbook questions were not really reflective of what would be on the test and lectures were very dense. Do well on the first 4 exams so you can drop the final. The final was 73 questions (as a reference).

reviews.comment: Probably his first semester teaching genetics. Very sweet but lecture slides were repetitive and not well organized. Tests are difficult so you have to study a lot to even get an 80. reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Class under Professor Vonhoff was intense. Each Lecture covered around 80-130 slides and his exams were brutal. Poorly written, and sometimes based on 1 specific detail on a single slide. He's a great person, but a bad lecturer. Exams are worth 60% of the final grade and with his bad lecturing and difficult exams, earning a high grade is tough.

I think he is a new teacher for genetics this semester. He has a lot of slides and some of them are filler. He does not go into depth on certain topics he teaches. This class was so chill. Mostly it was reading ~30 page chapter each week and two online lectures. 3 tests total and a few other projects, but nothing too hard. Tests were graded a bit harshly imo but they are open-book. Technically attendance isn't mandatory, but participation is a grade.

There were very few assignments.

Incredibly intelligent and inspirational.

Brazilian born with a unique and passionate expertise regarding the area of immigration policy and Latin American politics. Participation and staying on top of due dates are important. Ask questions in class or outside class. He's great with email also. His immigration research seems very interesting and he does't mind sharing info about it if you ask. Fair professor and recognizes when students are actually putting in effort .

Dr. Filomeno is a great professor. While his lectures can be a bit boring if people don't participate, he does a good job of explaining concepts clearly. Some of the texts are confusing, but just do the reading and ask questions in class, and you'll be fine. He's a pretty easy grader and if you go to his office hours, he's really helpful.
Good if you like the subject

Filomeno is extremely competent & knowledgeable in the course matter. The class isn't easy but it's not difficult so as long as you pay attention and occasionally read the book. Would reccomend
She cares about students. I asked her for extra office hours, she was pretty flexible in time and put effort to make sure that I learned.

Best professor in the dept hands down. I feel so much more prepared as an educator because of her. THE BEST, take her classes!!

Probably best or 2nd best Stats355 teacher here besides maybe klement.

This class and the professor suck, first of all, I already work as a developer and have still not seen any use for this class in years, UMBC just does this to piss people off and keep you in college longer. As for the professor, he sucks, horrible at explaining and the worst grader

She also grades quite easily.

reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--LECTURE HEAVY--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: The subject matter in this class was tough, and I think she did a decent job teaching it. The problem was she just wasn't always clear. She did a good job explaining the theories, but didn't spend a lot of time on getting us to learn to actually apply the theories which we had to do for the papers. If you asked for help she'd try to help though.

Fernandez is far and away the worst professor I've ever had. This is my 3rd class with her and she has only gotten worse. She is constantly rude and disrespectful towards her students. She has no respect for students' time, and has mentioned that she believes students should only take 3 classes a semester. Utterly poor educator.

As my academic advisor, Dr. Fernandez was cold and rude, but she's become one of my favorite professors now that she personally knows me through 2 classes. She's INCREDIBLY intelligent and can bring tremendous insight to texts which often feel inaccessible. Her grading isn't difficult or unclear; just take good notes and listen carefully.

Makes it very clear that she doesn't value your opinion by constantly cutting you off in the middle of discussion, yet she tells you to "hurry up" and answer her question.  She arrives to class late, embarrasses students for using the bathroom, and has no idea of how to "teach".  Very smart but her only teaching method is "I talk, you listen"

Fernandez loves hearing herself talk, so she rambles on all class, without pausing for even a breath. Sometimes has drool dripping down her mouth, and looks at you like she just saw a ghost. Arrives to class 6 minutes late, and appears out of breath, red face and all. Very boring, stands in one spot all class, and her accent is inconsistent.

Fernandez is very rude and does not seem to care or understand the needs of her students. She claimed that students should only take 2 classes per semester, a clear indication that she does not understand contemporary university education. She is often unclear in what she desires for her students to retain from her lectures. Very poor professor.

She is a very rude teacher, to be honest. She gets angry when student do not answer, but when they try to answer she will cut them off in the middle of speaking and go to someone else. She did this 4 times in one convo. Does not let you use the bathroom either. Can be helpful but is too distanced from youth to know how to handle them.

The instructions for all assignments are complex and the professor does not provide sufficient clarity. The professor lectures consist of complex and disorganized questions. She does not provide a study guide to help students maneuver through her train of thought. She is an intelligent person but she needs training as an educator.

Do not take this professors course. Dr. Fernandez does not treat students with respect and she rambles on during lectures.  She expects students to write her thoughts and specific wording on assignments before she will issue a grade.  Good luck.

She is a very knowledgeable professor and very enthused with the material. She talks a lot and can be intimidating however she is an easy grader. You will get yelled at if you don't bring books to class but so long as you take good notes its an easy A.

The material is hard and confusing, but she is a fair grader. As long as you actually study and read, you can earn a B. Earning an A seems pretty difficult. The material is not something you can BS with any professor. But Fernandez uses real life examples to relate to you. I enjoyed her, some don't like her- but she isn't unreasonable

Probably one of the most intelligent professors I've had. The class can get tedious, but it's usually interesting. My favorite part was the examples she gave when illustrating her points. She'd go from "Beowulf" to "America's Next Top Model" to NCLB.
If your a lit major take 401 with Fernandez and no one else! Its the most interesting ENGL class I've ever taken and everyone else who teaches it is sub-par at best. Do yourself a favor.

Professor Fernandez's classes are some of the best I've ever taken.  Complainers are usually those who don't care about literature anyway.  If you're interested, really interested, her classes are invaluable.  And if you have half a brain you should be able to know what she's looking for in her assignments.  She all but spells it out for you.

Worst teacher I've ever had.  She tells you to write one thing for your paper, yet she expects something entirely different so she gives you a bad grade. Never uses Bb. Hard to contact. Doesn't give her office. Hard to follow. TAKE SOMEONE ELSE!!!! I wish I had.

I grew to like this class once I realized she really knows her subject. But the lectures were often long and pedantic. She's not very approachable, and she took weeks to return the few graded papers we were assigned. Also, we got so far behind schedule (spent too much time on each work) that we had to skip about 1/4 of the works on the syllabus.

I had Professor Fernandez for Womens Perspectives in Victorian Lit. Class subject wasn't all that interesting to me, but Dr. Fernandez was very passionate about the subject and knew what she was talking about. Lots of readings but the class was pretty much all discussion so if you didn't read, it's ok. No quizzes, 2 papers, midterm and final.

She dives very deep into the subject, which some people can find annoying, I however loved it. She can go on about detail about the work without any notes. I would suggest her to anyone who really likes to dive deep into lit. If youn get bored with long analysis, then you'll probably find youreself out of place in the class.

Easy grader? Hmm, yes. But her class was boring. Did not tell you office hours. As soon as class ended, went out faster than the students so you couldn't even ask her a question. and she was always late to class even though the class started at like 3, and let us out late as well!
Good teacher, learned a lot from her, am taking again for victorian seminar.
you learn a lot from her, but she grades papers really slowly.it takes weeks sometimes.  also, a lot of feminism. a bit too much for me.

Ethnically Indian professor (christian indian); so her teaching style is different from your usual profs. Over all ok teacher. She, for one, talks a great deal about the social background of the work (actually she seems to only choose works that will illustrate the times in which it took place). This is both illuminating and boring. You get to unde

Good teacher, knowledgeable, always wiling to help. Participation counts a lot. She gives you the themes for  papers you write, and mostly they focus on spirtituality or genderisms, so people who are bored by that should probably stay away. Very detailed al beit slow coverage of material. Heavt emphasis on context.

Boringest class. Felt like I was becoming stupider and stupider. Treats you like a middle schooler; evidence= tiny reading list ofChristmas Carol, Mill on the Floss, Animal Farm and Mrs. Dalloway. Most eng majors have read these before highschool, and CC in middle! Lectures involve heavy science bashing and feminist rants. Dumb, annoying teacher.
Good prof, interesting, would take again.

Prof. Fernandez is a relatively new professor, but don't start thinking this means she doesn't know what she is doing.  She is incredibly bright and has such a passion for what she is teaching.  You can't help but get lost in the materials with her.  She i

She is so nice.  she will let you turn assignments in late, as long as you contact her.  her final was easy!  this class was an easy A!!!!  the class can get boring, the poetry section more so.  a very easy grader.
She is a very fair grader and is always gives students the benefit of the doubt.

Obviously well-versed in her subject matter. Her selection of books played to her strengths. Her accent is at first hard to follow, but you get used to it. She has a tendency to be unorganized, but any new professor would. Come to class with an openminded attitude and give her a chance.
I recommend a different professor for ENGL 301 if you can manage it.

Absolutely horrible professor. All he does is read off the slides and doesn't go very in depth with the material. He grades and gives back assignments very late. He rambles on and on and it's extremely difficult to get an A.  You really have to read a lot of the textbook to pass. Definitely wouldn't recommend him and take someone else if you can.

Professor Fiedelholtz really knows his stuff when it comes to computer networking, the only complaint I would have is that his lectures are death by power point. Although this course covers an insane amount of topics so I cant blame him entirely. There is a Group project for the midterm and he gives great feedback and help if you are struggling.

Dude was chill, but grade scaling was so stupid. you're graded on like 3 things in this class, and the final is 50% of your grade. hard to fail the class cause the final is easy, but also kind of difficult to snag an A if you have anything lower than an 85% before the final. Everything else was graded frivolously, but he was cool tho I can't lie

Actually literally doesn't know what he's talking about. If a word has multiple meanings he will always use the wrong one. Constantly tries to tie everything back to getting a job and then never tests you on it. His tests are poorly written and confusing, his lectures make no sense, and your grade is decided by a total of six things. Do not take.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: I've had this guy for 430 and 451. Both were incredibly easy A's, he curves very accommodatingly, lets you complete homeworks and labs in groups, and posts all his lecture slides. You just have to show up and try, the material might be hard, but you get what you put into the class. It's almost impossible to get lower than a C with him.

I truly think that a lot of people here are just lazy. Literally this professor is super nice and laid back. His exams are poor worded because he does take a lot of questions and try to change them around. He is very helpful if you ask for help.

He is a cool guy, but not a very good professor. Our entire grade is just 3 tests, and there is always content on the tests that he didn't cover. Also, the test questions are very poorly worded to the point where you might get the answer wrong even if you know the content. It was nice having a class without any homework though.

I would not recommend this class. Tests questions are badly worded or from a CISSP book which he does not teach from. So when you take the test you will have no idea what he is talking about. Project and Labs are supposed to help your grade but he refuses to give 100% on either. Don't ask for help because he doesn't know the answers either

Had Glenn for IS 310 and 430. Great guy, really knows his stuff. Grades are solely on tests and a project (and a lab in 430) but grade heavily relies on project and he grades easy on it. Awesome guy, recommend him to anyone.
Great pfofessor. Fairly an easy class if you read and understand the security questions.

Professor Fiedelholtz is friendly, encouraging, helpful, and also very knowledgeable in his field. His classs consists of 3 MC exams and a project. Although his class is overall fairly easy, his exam questions are a little ambiguous bc they are standardized questions. He'll also work with your final grade, if he sees you that you attend his class

He is an easy going professor i highly suggest taking him, the key is to show interest in the cyber security field even if you are taking him for is 310. overall he is super chill and very understanding
He is always there to help students  and he explain everything very well.

This was his first semester teaching apparently and he previously worked for the NSA. Lectures are a joke, just bullet points ripped from the book on PP, however he will give hints as to what will be on the exam. His exams are 50 question vocab quizzes, and are riddled with grammatical errors and cloudy ?'s. You will get 70-90 every exam.
She is a strict grader, sometimes she does not follow the syllabus due dates, and rubrics are seldom posted
Harshest grader and makes no sense, easily confused, rude, and acts like a know it all. I have gotten praise and 100% in essays for other classes but with her it's a complete 180; Fire her.
People who cheat will pass and those who are honest will fail. The odds are set up against honesty. Unfair class. Awful experience.
Grading doesn't even make sense. Very tough grader, you could miss one word or even add too much and get -6, hello?!?
She is a great professor and very friendly

Thought this class was going to be easy since it's a 100 class but I was so wrong. She is pretty hard with the way she grades and when she gives you back your essays most of the comments don't make much sense and often aren't very helpful. Btw she doesn't use blackboard so don't assume your grade on their is the actual grade your going to get.

She does not like being corrected by students, any argument or questioning was met with extreme condescension. Even when she would make mistakes, it was always the fault of the students. Also her exams are graded harshly and answers do not align with explanations provided in class. Exams and quizzes felt like a guessing game based on her mood.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I thought this class was going to be easy but I feel like she made it so much harder than it was supposed to be. She was very disorganized and expected long readings to be done in a short amount of time. Also, her grading was quite harsh with little to explanation for why you received the grade.

Pretty easy class, especially if you already have a good understanding or even just a good intuitive sense for grammar. Wouldn't recommend if you really struggle with grammar. Prof doesn't answer questions well, is judgey when students get things wrong, and gives bad/incorrect writing advice. All quizzes/exams are take-home. Go to class, it helps.

Mrs. Fitzpatrick is an excellent instructor who works to make her students better and more efficient writers. If you're a good writer with reasonable HS experience, this class should be easy. Grading is tough especially for a 100 course. Lots of reading but it isn't bad if you have decent writing skills. Don't take her if you just want a free A.

-Unclear grading policy
-hard grader
-worst professor ever
-horrible.

She's a great professor to have and improves your writing abilities. My argumentative papers improved my writing skills, and the grading was fair. However, it's a little unclear sometimes. There are lots of useless readings. But if you come from AP Lit/Lang, it's much easier when compared! Recommend. Able to balance with other tougher courses.

Not very tech savvy. Most of her exams and readings are poorly formatted PDF scans. She is funny and understanding but unclear. Most of the definitions she defines are example-based. She appears to structure her lectures around a textbook different than the assigned one.

Some of the older ratings don't seem very accurate. I took Prof. Fitzpatrick's class in the Fall 2021 semester. She had no exams and a few small quizzes. There were 3 papers and one group project. At least half of the class got a 100% for the group project. Participate in the class. She really appreciates it and it will be reflected in your grade.

Fitzpatrick's syllabus and material is very outdated but she is a wonderful professor and person, at least in upper-level courses. She was kind, helpful, and very accommodating for my classmate's and I's mental health issues. Her grading was a bit tough, but she is very lenient later in the semester. Very lovely professor but I wouldn't recommend.

Class is 2 quizzes, 4 tests (including final), and 1 paper. Open book & she recorded class lectures. Old ratings dont seem that accurate to meshes organized, clear on grading/weight, and after every quiz/test she went over all the answers. Also very helpful when I had a family emergency: excused me from class and granted extension.

Starts off not too bad, if you study and review the beginning tests are a breeze, after that... no thank you. She reuses the same content every year. The test's feel outdated, she'll focus on one subject for days saying it'll be important on the exam, then it turns out it's barely there and the content is nothing you remember doing in class
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Very unclear grading criteria, no rubrics, would give examples to follow but then once she grades your paper she'll say you missed certain things when they were never clearly asked for in the first place. Lots of unnecessary reading. Also you don't know your grade until the end of the semester bc she doesn't use blackboard? lol
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Professor Fitzpatrick is a very nice person. That being said, she probably shouldnt be teaching. Firstly, she is very scattered, disorganized, and is rarely on time. There was no breakdown of how assignments were weighted or graded. She announced a project that was not in the syllabus. I still have no idea how the grade was calculated. DO NOT TAKE
Assigns wayyy too much reading material and barely goes over it
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Not a good Professor. Speaks too fast making it difficult to understand her speech. Difficult course with way too much information to retain and be tested on. Confusing lectures and useless textbooks. She gets annoyed when you ask her to repeat something because she talks too fast.

Hard class. She seems to know a lot but grammar is hard and she could have been more helpful so more students would succeed. She would say things once and expect us to remember what she said for a specific question on quizzes/tests, which were very hard. She was inconsistent and confusing when answering questions. Work very hard to be successful.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tests are tough

reviews.comment: -Unclear grading policy -Very tolerant and encouraging of opinions -Great for a summer session class
She's a great professor, but as with many english classes, there is a lot of reading and a lot of writing.

While I understand that this is a literature class, the course load was ridiculous. There was so much reading involved (even more than my bios and chems). It was not necessarily Professor Fitzpatrick that was the problem, but the material. She is absolutely a sweetheart. I just wouldn't recommend taking her for this specific class.

Prof. Fitzpatrick was one of my favorite English teachers. She is very open to others opinions and grades based on your effort level and revision efficiency. She is also very learned in grammar, however she will not dock your paper too heavily if your content is good. I learned A LOT about grammar in this class as well as composition TAKE HER!

I thought she was a good teacher. She has a very sweet disposition, and was very helpful. Each class was on topic. There was a lot of reading (it was a lit class after all) and she was pretty understanding that it was a heavy work load.

Dr. Fitzpatrick is a great teacher. As long as you do the work and read the material you will do fine. I was surprised at her grading, it was easier than I thought it would be. She knows her stuff and expects you to do the work. She was eager to help you with any questions and will even proof read papers before you turn them in for final grading!

I did not mind Dr. Fitzpatrick. While she was not my most favorite professor, I preferred her over Dr. Hickernell for 395. She seems a bit scatterbrained at times, but knows her stuff and is very friendly. She also seems to be a nicer grader than Dr. Hickernell.

Professor Fitzpatrick is the only professor I've ever had a problem with. Her grading is all over the place because she focuses on grammar and proper citation, giving little attention to the content itself. She WILL cry plagiarism. She gives vague rules, then docks random points for everything. I just hope I never have to deal with her again.

She is absolutely awful. She shows up late to class every single day and then we always have to stay late so she can fit everything in. She demands our respect but doesn't respect our personal time. She literally laughs at you if you ask a question that she thinks you should know. DO NOT TAKE HER CLASS...It was a huge mistake signing up for this.

I had her for grammar and she was so wacky. Just so scattered and all over the place. But she was very nice and eager to help. I barely prepared for her class quizes but I would usually pass. Plus she would throw in a huge curve. If you try even slightly, you'll get a B. Just attend class regularly and make sure she knows your name. Recomended.

it is a hard course if you haven't taken 226 before. Pay attention, take good notes are keys to success in the course. It is hard to ask her for help as well. She does not really repond to your questions well.

Watch out for Frizzy, she gives you handouts that completely contrast one another. AND if you try and say something to her, she WILL be bias on her grading. She is an unfair, lazy, incomprehensible teacher. Doesn't explain anything clearly and then gets angry when you don't understand. Take 226 instead. If you have to take her, god be with you.

Professor Fitzpatrick co-teaches ENGL 395 with Professor Hickernell. Since the course is intended to prepare students to be Writing Center tutors, I wish they had developed a more hands-on curriculum rather than a textbook-based one. She does convey new information in her lectures not found in the textbooks.

She barely lectures! She goes over the material as if you already know it, shes always late, even if you don't understand material she moves on. LAZY!! Instead of actually trying to teach us, she has us work in groups which does NOT help. Her horrible teaching style makes her awful! The book will become your bible.
Easy to understand when only listening to her. Asking questions will make things worse. Not a hard teacher if paying attention.

Her pace is a bit fast for the reading material. She'll tell you what book she wants you to read and expect it finished the following week, probably not realizing that we have other classes to worry about. Also, she tends to be dismissive toward students whose opinions differ from her own, which causes her to quickly change topic when countered.

Neither the best nor the worst teacher.  She's flexible in terms of scheduling, but she's always late for class-- sometimes as much as 20 minutes.  She's very stuck in her ways, and generally espouses her opinions as facts and your opinions as "possibilities."  Not the worst grader ever, but she can be picky.  Overall, she's so-so.

DO NOT TAKE HER, especially if you are a senior.  she is the type to fail you and keep you from graduating. She makes courses harder than they need to be and she is not sympathetic towards those who have difficulty.  She may help you somewhat but she can be disrespectful towards those who are struggling.

I don't know what people are complaining about, she is very nice--however, there were some students who didn't know what a direct object was by the 8THE WEEK, and then she did get a little sarcastic. Her exams and paper grading is fair and it is totally possible to get an A. I didn't buy the book b/c everything is from her notes and handouts.

I've had her class twice--the first time I left feeling that she did not think outside of the box which is terrible in the field of literature. However, I took her class a second time which was a horrible mistake. She is narrow minded and can be condescending to students who think differently than her.

I didn't find this class very hard, i suggest that you read the books since it is a literature class. she moves swiftly though, and sometimes I found it difficult to read the books as quickly as she wanted them to be read, but honestly, if you even glanced at it and listened to her you'd do fine.

Grammar is not easy. Knowing what looks correct will not get you past this class. Attendance is important in understanding what she tries to teach, because there is NO other way to get the material. I skipped a lot and got a C. I cant say it was the professors fault because she taught the material to those present. She was clear enough and helpful.

She is nice and helpful, however she is a hard professor.  I do not know of anyone who ever got an A on their paper.  Very difficult teacher.  Take her only if you are an extremely good writer or if you do not mind settling for a B or a C.

Do not take her class!  She was late everyday for class and sometimes she didn't come at all.  She requires you to read ten novels.  She expects them read in two days. Some are 300 pages.  She picks apart your papers too.  She is never pleased!

Fitzpatrick is a very nice lady, but some people find her style of teaching condescending. Don't take her comments to heart. However, ENGL 226 is a VERY difficult class. You can't go into this class expecting an "easy A," I've worked my butt off and I was able to bring my D up to a 79%. She's very willing to help students, but she is challenging.

Class is hard & she is really sarcastic toward people who have trouble. She contradicts herself all the time. Tests have questions that everybody thought were unfair. She doesn't answer questions because she misunderstands them.

I've taken two of her classes. Basicly she will give you a B if you show up and listen. Take a few notes, look at them before an exam, and you are bound to get at least a B. As for papers, write whatever you think she'd like to hear (what she talks about in class) and she'll love you for it. Originality might get you a C.
No Comments
she makes me feel stupid!  she's condescending.
I took many of her classes and learned a great deal. She was a wonderful teacher with an excellent teaching method.  She is one of the reasons I have my degree today.

Needless to say, I dropped her class. I lost respect for her after she allowed students to berate others because they did not enter the classroom with a warehouse of previous knowledge about the subject. Isn't that why you take a course? To learn? Completely and utterly frustrating.
she's good

Aww, cut her some slack. I agree she can be tough to get; sometimes I wish I could raise my hand and offer an explanation that actually EXPLAINED another student's question. Honestly, I recommend this class most for science majors who need an English class.

She was a decent professor who was outright rude to some students (especially those who didn't catch on right away).  I noticed her roll her eyes and even snicker on several occasions in response to student questions.  Keep up with the reading/exercises and you should get an A.  Bad personality.

NEVER.  I repeat, NEVER take her.  She is a hard professor who is so caught up in her own world that she fails to notice anyone who's not in tune with her particular wavelength.  She gave me a D on the midterm because I had the right answers, but not in her exact words.  AVOID HER LIKE THE PLAGUE!!!
Never....Again... Hard grader, not fun, not particularly nice either- Do not take this woman!

I found her to be a good professor, but she was occasionally lacking in some knowledge areas.  Of course, it was sort of an introductory course.  I also felt she was unacknowledging of some student's thoughts and somewhat rude to others. Not a bad teacher
No Comments

I loved her discussions then only thing is that we didn't get to talk about it in class. She was really nice but the work was a bit difficult and if you don't have the book that cost an arm and leg then you will fall behind. I fell behind and when trying to ketch up and still was confused but this class is definitely easy if you keep up.

This professor is pleasant; most of your work will be mini group work during class, and a bit of writing outside of class in terms of the stories you have to write. Not the best presentational skills, but nice to be around and does care about the subject. Really focus on grammar and try your best to be creative with the guidelines given.

I did not really appreciate her feedback on my stories nor did I find any of her lectures or her presentation skills enjoyable. However, she really loves the subject and is just the sweetest person out there. If you take the class seriously then you'll have a good time. She's very good at the more technical things like grammar than creative though.

Grade was basically 2 large stories that you have to make with 0 feedback from the instructor to improve it. You have discussions with classmates to critique your story to improve it but the actual grade resides on what she deems acceptable in her own mind with 0 chance of redeeming yourself. VERY UNCLEAR EXPECTATIONS.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things--Tough grader

reviews.comment: As far as English/Language courses go, I've had much better. A little step down from high school honestly. It was quite boring to sit through the lectures. I think there are better options, but she is a nice person who does care about the subject.

As far as English classes go it's your run of the mill. You get essays and journals and are expected to do some writing while in class but they're usually short response and not difficult at all. She's not a super tough grader but you should definitely try in this class. She was very nice and pretty likable so I recommend this class for everyone.

Very heavy into reactions and test heavy.  Would not recommend.  Had to change major because of this professor.  He was intimidating if you asked a question that he thinks you should know.  Retook class and passed with Perks.
This man's CHEM438 is the reason I had to stay in school an extra year. Currently a medical student so I would argue I wasn't the problem... This class is harder than medical school.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: The chemistry involved in this class isn't difficult to understand, but the sheer amount of information you have to retain makes it very difficult. Fishbein will bluntly ask you to recite extensive reaction mechanisms on exams from memory. Come prepared. Study 2 weeks in advance. Tough guy for a tough subject. Coming to EVERY class is paramount.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: I took Fishbein in Fall 2017 for Toxicology. This man is tough, very straightforward and gives out alot of case studies. Even though he gives out alot of readings, everything he gives you, you WILL see on the test. But beware, he will test you on the SMALLEST DETAIL, so pay attention and attend ALL the lectures!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: The WORST professor/teacher I have ever experienced. He has tenure, which no doubt contributes to his attitude. He is very unclear on what he expects on tests, wont make his materials available online, and displays LIMITED INTEREST. The teacher from the other half is MUCH more helpful/dedicated. (Had to repeat solely due to this half)
Brutal AF. 10/10 would take again.  Very interesting.  Extremely attractive - makes it easy to want to come to class.

For once I felt respected as a student who is capable of doing chemistry. He's brutal and you have to memorize a lot, but you will end up learning a ton and the curve is huge. His exams are very similar to sample exams and HW. I really respect this guy, I love his teaching style and sense of humor. You take him seriously, he takes you seriously.

No BS. You ask stupid questions easily answered by readings in the text, he will call you out. Don't BS him. He's clear, concise, and hilarious. You might not get it at first, but pay attention because he brings it all into the picture at the end. Exams and homework are tough, but nothing you can't handle with hard work. Loved this class.

Take very detailed in class notes as his exams are completely based off the notes.  He is much more approachable than he seems so don't be afraid to swing by his office and ask for help.  Just make sure you preview the material and pay attention rather than asking pointless questions.

Great teacher if you enjoy chemistry. He's funny, down to the point, and skips the fluff. He lets you know when you're doing something wrong will put you on the right track. You're not going to pass this class if you don't care, you have to do the work but well worth it, he's extremely knowledgeable and made me love organic chemistry more.

Best prof ever! Such an engaging and funny guy! Really makes you love Chemistry! I love his hair. Easy grader, I thought, although most other people seem to disagree. Overall I thought he was helpful, very responsive to questions. He really emphasizes that there is no such thing as a stupid question! He also has good style.

He taught 1st half of bio-chem II. It was all about mechanisms, so you have to attend every class and take notes. He thinks most question are stupid, he makes you feel stupid if you ask him questions. so not too fun to talk too. To get good grade, you have to learn the mechanisms and write them over and over. There are alot of them.

He is a good teacher overall. He is strait to the point, no BS kind of guy. Most people have a problem with him because they ask him questions like "How long should I boil ___" or "What color should it be?"... You are there to learn people not have your hand held! Beware of his tests though, they are graded very harshly (tho curved well at end)

Well, it's obvious that he hates teaching 352l, maybe he thinks it's below him or something. The TAs are out of control and if you get poor grades I suggest you go up to them and talk otherwise they will try to screw you. Lectures are him rapidly jotting mechanisms on the board then letting class out. You learn very little.

I guess he is the WORST lab professor. Everyone should be awarded for what he/she has done. Wish he taught all my classes.

Favorite class ever. He is modest about how smart he is, you would never know he had a MBA from Wharton. He is funny and really cares about everyone.  But you do need to participate.  Also attendance is mandatory and will greatly lower grade if you do not go to class. But after a few lectures you will definetly want to go to class.
Funny professor. I showed up to every class and realized I was wasting my time in class. EAsy A
One of the easiest teachers at UMBC. Not the best, mind you, just easiest. I've learned absolutely zilch in this class, but I got 100 on both the first two exams without studying so...

Mr. Fleischmann brings quite the expertise to class each and every day.  His humor lights up the room while still setting the appropriate tone.  Not only do the students learn a ton but he is genuinely one of the cooler guys to ever teach at UMBC.
Cares a lot about his students. Will go out of his way to help them out. Professor was genuinely nice and carrying. Definitely would recommend.
Professor is one of d best have taking so far.
Great teacher! He is always helpful and very approachable in and outside of the classroom. His real life experiece of the business world helps bring industry best practice to the classroom.

Good Professor , works in the loves when students participate during the class, it makes the class more fun and easier to learn . Has a business background so he knows what he is talking about.Highly Recommended
He's not a bad teacher.  All his tests are from textbook material.  He gives you a nice helpful study guide so you'll be fine.  He's a nice guy.
Takes everything out of the book. But he gives you a 25 page study guide for exams. exams are 6-7 chapters. wish he would give a few quizes in between test to retain knowledege
very easy A as long as you show up to class... exams are easy, no project

Not a bad teacher. Kind of comes off as pompous at times, but he's not overly obnoxious. The material is fairly easy. The exam questions come entirely out of the book, the true/false can be worded incredibly tricky at times, but he says its all out the book. Attendance is mandatory as there are participation points, and the HW is fairly simple.
One of the best teachers I've ever had.

Amazing professor although he's adjunct so he might not be around for anyone else to enjoy. Definitely one of the best professors I've had. He has so many insightful things to say and he can be pretty funny too. Every single day, my mind was blown by some new bit information I gained. This is one of the few classes that's worth the money.

EASY no tests but class consists of 5 3pg essays where you workshop 1 essay. a few quizzes from textbook readings and each person is assigned a reading from 2nd book to discuss in class. portfolio of 3 rewritten essays including workshopped essay. okay class except 3 hours long got boring really quick. last semester at umbc though

He's really laid back, as long as you make sure that all your essays meet the minimum page requirement and MLA is perfect then you'll guaranteed an A. A big thing is that during the peer edit and workshops, you HAVE to participate or else even if you do everything else right, you'll get a B. He's pretty funny as well. I definitely had a great time!

One of the best professors I ever had in my entire college career. He made an intro level creative writing class so enjoyable. To succeed, you need to do all your readings and go to class. Attendance, class participation, and preparedness are what counts the most towards your grade.
Funny, knowledgeable, helpful, attractive... greatest professor I've ever had.  He really does need to teach a mid-level nonfiction course.

He is one of the best professors that I've had as an undergrad; he helps you with emphasizing voices, helping the readers with clarity, and building solid structure that can strengthen your writings. Yes, you do need to attend the 2.5-hour lectures at night, and yes, you have to put your best effort - the class can tell if the essays are rushed.

This class is not hard! The essays he assigns are edited then given back for us to fix and then at the end of the semester we turn in three of our best papers for a grade. Class IS long but the way it is set you it is NOT boring. Many are intimidated by how straight forward he/class is but go to class, be vocal, do the work; get an A. It's simple.

Professor Flanigan is great. He knows a lot about creative writing and literature in general. He makes English and the class fun. Be prepared to speak during workshops. As long as you make a conscious effort to really improve your writing and participate, there is no reason you can't get an A. Do the readings and pay attention.
Best professor I've ever had.
great teacher. grades hard. knows his stuff. needs to teach more higher level courses. always looked forward to his classes.

Prof. Flanigan is truly one of my favorite professors. Funny and down-to-earth, a lot of things he taught me have resonated since I completed the class. Yes, it is difficult, but an A is manageable if you sincerely try.
Good teacher. I'd recommend him.

This is a really hard class, and the professor is insane about grammar. He's pretty strict about all the papers you turn in, and grades them hard too. It is impossible to do perfectly on them, but he is available for help usually. Also, the class was 2.5 hrs long, so it got really tedious sometimes.

I wasn't interested in the class when I signed up, but had to take it. However, I'm glad I took it with this professor. He knows how to teach, is extremely helpful, professional, and sincere. It is a hard class, and he is hard on students, but I enjoyed having him for a professor. I'll miss the class. "There are lies, damned lies, and statistics!"

Not the most enthusiastic teacher, but very down to earth. Encouraged personal voices in essays, and was okay with curse words and slang in papers as long as it fit with the topic. Very cool guy, probably the most relaxed english100 professor at UMBC. Ask for help, you won't get an A unless you try.
Truly, a wonderful teacher and person. I'll miss his class.

Mr. Flanigan is the best English teacher I have ever had.  I had no interest in English going into class but I came out loving it.  He is a stickler for grammar, but he is kind and funny, which makes class very enjoyable.
this teacher was great. definitely recommend, but the class does require work. Go to the writing center for help on papers, but don't rely on the writing center to fix every problem last minute.
i think he made the class harder then it needed to be. tried to simplify too much and i dont think he taught very well. oh well....

I don't think he liked teaching english comp. He was nice and stuff, but he had no enthusiasm. I felt like he didn't really want to teach our class but only did so because he did not have a choice. He probably couldn't stand us and thought we were really stupid - we definitely amused him a lot. But he's not a bad teacher; a lot of people liked him.
Wayyy too much poetry here!! I guess its good if you like it, but to me, none of those poems ever made ANY sense! The class itself was alright, but it was at night so that sort of sucked.

I don't know what the heck is wrong with the people who typed the preceding comments, but Flanigan is a HARD teacher. He grades hard, and has really high expectations. He really likes poetry too. You do a lot of poetry if you're in his class. Beware!!
Needs to stop smoking so much; its bad for him.

He's nice...kind of uptight though, and never gets off task. You can only talk to him ABOUT English, but he's passionate about what he teaches. Still, a good teacher even though he is always tired. Lol. I'd recommand taking his classes.
Yeah, Sean's a good teacher. Very easy class. Fun too.
Awesome! Grades pretty fairly, his assignments are fun, and his lectures are good too. He will really help you learn and become a better student :)

Down to earth, approachable, and always ready to help! Really helps you learn and become a better writer. His classes are never boring - always makes everything interesting and fun. Great professor! Needs to teach more classes here!!

She taught AMST 357, but it wasn't listed. Professor Fouts is easily one of the best professors I've had. She's an amazing person, and the workload wasn't heavy or bad. There were some readings throughout the course, and we even went on some field trips! She's understanding and willing to work with you. Participation is really important for grades.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Literally the most amazing professor. HUM was such an amazing class to have taken, and Professor Fouts's overall vibe is a huge motivator in general to complete work. There are reading assignments due once a week in class, but they are super quick and easy to do. Participation is key! The material they lecture as well can be applied outside class.

Amazing professor. They're passionate and meant to teach, constantly going above and beyond (field trip/lunch, guest visitors, extra credit opportunities at community events). Dr. Fouts gives meaningful assignments that apply directly to the lectures. Clear grading criteria and organization, provides opportunities for growth academically & overall.

Was good at first, but as the semester went on, became extremely disrespectful and belittling. I emailed her about my grade, and she literally told me to stop emailing her. Extremely rude and unprofessional professor I ever had. Very demeaning. Will pick on you and and call you out if she doesnt like you. Avoid her at all costs.

Prof. Fouts was great. She made the class interesting, and all she asks for is participation. You have a HW assignment due before every class, but the readings aren't too difficult, just try to understand the material the best you can. I would definitely take her again and would recommend to any student.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: There was a lot of reading, such as articles, newspapers, academic journals, but they also gave us three movies to watch. BB post 200-300 words, two papers 700-1000 words, and final was optional. All BB posts were due before class. Partication matters.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Really nice teacher. A couple BB posts a week and a couple papers for the whole semester. Participation and attendance was important. Readings can be long sometimes but its not too bad.

Great professor, lectures are fun and the professor is funny and engaging at the same time. I only took this class for a gen ed credit but I will be lying if I said I didn't enjoy my time here, participation matters and you do have weekly written assignments but she makes it fun instead of it being a chore. Final is optional too.
Back-to-back projects can feel stressful, but the amount of time allotted to do them is fair. Ask questions. Participation is key.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Her lectures are pretty planned and very engaging! She tries to make jokes, so make sure to laugh at them. Be prepared to talk in class at least once per lecture, since a HUGE portion of the class grade depends on that. Otherwise, as long as you engage in the work and do the weekly assignments, you don't have to do the final.

TAKE HER! Prof. Fouts is the best. NO EXAMS. class was graded by a handful of essays that were not hard whatsoever, but fair warning, there is a LOTT of reading. 20% of your grade is participation so if you enjoy doing class discussions, this is the class for you. Material was pretty interesting, I would def recommend for an easy A&H.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Caring

reviews.comment: She is amazing professor. Attend each class. Attendance is the part of the grade about 20%. 2 Critical Responses, 2 presentation and 1 final project. No exams. Easy A

She is a professor who grades heavily on participation and attendance. For her methods course, it was her first time teaching it. Dr. Fouts can give contradicting instructions on her assignments. Once she learns to give proper and thorough instructions this class would not have been confusing at 1st. She makes it very easy for you to ask questions
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Dr. Fouts gives great lectures. Gives out easy assignments, she takes awhile to grade things which is fine with me but others were unhappy about it.
reviews.rating_tags: Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: This was a super easy, chill class. She gives clear instructions and very detailed, helpful feedback, and is a pretty easy grader. There were three 1 page assignments, two fairly short papers, a presentation and a final. Attendance and participation was supposedly 20% of your grade but I barely ever participated or went to class and got an A.

Explains assignments well and is an easy grader. Participate, turn in the three short writing assignments (super easy), put in some effort when writing your 2 major papers, read the assigned articles, and just show up to class! This class is an easy A. May seem boring at first, but it gets really interesting. Class goes by so so fast!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Easy A and such an interesting course. I don't regret taking this course at all. You have to do some reading before every class in order to contribute to class discussions. Participation matters, but don't worry, this is an easy class to participate in, she gives so many opportunities and the topics of discussions are super interesting. Take this!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Insanely passionate about course content. Well thought out powerpoints, very knowledgeable on her subject. Takes a very liberal stance on most things, however is lively in discussion. Insanely easy class, relatively easy grader, 50 minute class flies by, heavily into bashing Trump and Republicans, some warranted some just because.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Caring

reviews.comment: I never saw a professor like him. So rude, helpless. Whenever I emailed for some help, I received an automatic reply, he was never straightforward. He won't even review the draft papers. It's just the pass or fail. waste of time and money for sure, if you ever take a class with him.
Rude Teacher, he get very mad if you stop by to his office and he doesn't give you a time to ask him

Do your work, you'll get an A!! Good teacher. He takes Ethics very seriously, and he has A LOT of experience in the CyberSecurity field. Discussion based course, no 'real' lecture and all group work, 3 papers and a midterm. Class participation is 30% show up and you basically get the full 30%. Awkward at times, but most of the CMSC professors are.

I took her in a hybrid format. The online lectures were super well laid out and effective, but in-class felt like a repeat of the online but forcing people to talk. Still cares a lot about the students and is very kind. However, exams are a huge part of your grade. There is a fun project, but it feels so small because it's much less than the tests.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Graded by few things--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Dr. Fountain genuinely cares about her students and takes time out of her day to be available to students outside of class. Reach out to her if you need help; the course material can be a little challenging but she is very caring and helpful. Her lectures draw from her research experience in the field which is cool. Go to her class and participate!

Super caring and knowledgeable about what she teaches. Aware of students mental health. Theres Quizzes each week but as long as you go to lectures and view her PowerPoints youll be fine! Quizlet is a good resource too! 6 Quizzes, 2 Papers and 3 Exams. If you have issues with assignments you can always feel comfortable reaching out to her. 100/10

Material covered in the class is very challenging, but the grading criteria takes that into account. No exams. There were weekly quizzes (don't bother trying to study for them) but they won't hinder your grade. The labs were challenging, and usually involved the professor doing most of the time. Make an effort on the lab reports, get an A.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES

reviews.comment: nice person
He knows his stuff but can't teach worth a damn. He can't explain anything very well or at all so don't bother asking questions. Pretty much teach yourself from the book. He is useless.

Terrible, terrible, teacher.  Makes this class much harder than it has to be.  He is not clear in his explanations and reads straight from slides.  When he does write on the board its illegible. This class will make you hate computer engineering.  Based on my experience in this class, I switched majors.  Wait and take it with LeBerge
No Comments

Very long and boring lectures.  Bother your TA for help.  Definitely study the homework before tests.  Just about all his test problems were straight from the homework.  Since he's here for the research he doesn't really care about the grades, seems like most of us got B's even with how bad we did on the tests.

Choa is like most grad. profs who get assigned this course: not very helpful.  Very nice guy, though.  This is basic circuit theory so it doesn't much matter.  Homeworks are extremely hard and time consuming; exams are killer but he puts some HW problems on them.  Choa curves so study your ass off and do good on labs & HW and you can swing a B.
The guitar is a hard instrument to play.  The professor made it accessible.

obvious that mr. forshee writes his own review. as a teacher he is mediocre squared. in fact forshee is a square. thinks he's a stud genius and is really a careless depressingly boring teacher.. i wish i could give a good review but i really cant
He is awesome! So funny and really really cute. And super easy.
Professor Valchar is very kind and sweet, the class material is interesting and his grading rubrics aren't strict!

Professor Valchar is a really caring professor. He encourages reflection on your teenage years and there are only 3 assignments (submitted by email) in the semester. Attendance is not mandatory, but it helps to get an idea of what's going on. Really enjoyable and relaxed class, the only thing is that he can be hard to reach outside of class.
easy, take if you can

Amazing prof, so kind and super chill. Very approachable and understanding. Class included 3 very doable assignments: midterm, case study (which is an interview and an analysis) and a final exam. All take home and ask you about term topics and how to apply them introspectively. Love him!!!! Take him if you can!!!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Caring--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Valchar seems a bit confused by what he is doing. I feel like he is a longtime substitute; however, he is very sweet and understanding, and from what I remember as far as my midterm, he grades easily.
