There is a class once a week in person; however, attendance was not mandatory, so I did not go. Easy A

This class is rough because it's writing INTENSIVE, but Prof F is nice and straightforward. The instructions for everything are clear in her textbook, and for everything else, she'll tell you. The worst part about this class is starting. There is a LOT of work, but it's easy. It just takes a while to understand everything. Class is fun and useful.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Caring--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Forestiere is like a PoliSci Energizer bunny and actually cares. Poli301 is mandatory for PoliSci majors and it's actually a really good course regardless. The final paper is around 25-30 pages long, but you write it incrementally through the semester and the textbook is literally an instruction manual on how to do it.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: She is a fantastic professor and really cares about her students. This was my first time taking her course and she is impressive. I really enjoyed her teaching style, and she is able to break down tougher concepts into easier ones to understand. Make sure to read the chapters and use the T.A. for assistance! Looking forward to taking her again.

If you are interested in doing research in political science, DON'T BE AFRAID TO TAKE THIS CLASS!! Dr. Forestiere is such an AMAZING educator, UMBC is lucky to have her as a professor so don't miss your opportunity to learn from her. With that said, DO NOT PROCRASTINATE ON THE FINAL PAPER if you want to get an A and maintain your sanity.

Dr. Forestiere is an extremely approachable teacher who seeks to help every student in the writing and data analysis process. She makes clear that POLI 301 is a fast-paced class, and that there is a lot of material to cover, but she also helps students immensely through her feedback, office hours, individual help days, and built in time in class!
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback--So many papers

reviews.comment: 301 is required for political science students at UMBC. This whole online environment she kept pushing with her lectures even with the world around us crumbling down. You work towards this huge research paper due at the end. Is there when you have questions but is intimidating.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Forestiere is an eminent professor at the department of political science. Even though her class is in somewhat difficult but it interesting what you can learned. I took poli301 because it requires for a poli major. And also, I would suggest that to put more effort in out class study. But overall, I found the class very relevant for Poli major.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Dr. Forestiere is an awesome professor. This class (301) definitely has its reputation for a reason; it's tough. But she did everything she possibly could to explain things in a clear and concise way, and her expectations are reasonable. She also provides plenty of opportunities for extra credit. It's a hard class but she helps you get through it.

Took this class as a summer class in Europe, the class was very content and vocab heavy, but Dr. F made sure everyone was understanding and comfortable with the information. You can tell that she loves what she teaches and if you pay attention, some of that love for learning will rub off on you.
She is the worst and tough professor ever. Avoid her classes at all cost.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--SO MANY PAPERS

reviews.comment: A lot of work, need to put in the effort to pass and have time management if taking her online classes, but she explains everything very clearly.
She's good

This class is a lot of work, but Dr. F makes it enjoyable. A lot of the skills she teaches in this class are really important to know. Though this class is a lot of work if you put your best foot forward she's always willing to help.

This is just one of those classes you have to take if you are a poli major. This class is hard. Unless you have a mind for formal research and can crunch out and "A" paper in a night then you're going to need to put a lot of outside class time into this course. Many students fail this course at least once because of its difficulty. Be prepared.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: In regular semesters the grade is based on 2 full length research papers and reading quizzes - both are very manageable because she walks you through the research process. The only problem is if you are not motivated / have other obligations and no interest in research; if you pace yourself and keep up with work it is difficult to not do well.
There is no playing around in this class; however, she is very willing to give her time. Very good professor.

Good professor. I didn't pass the course, but the course isn't super hard. She tries to make it as easy as possible, but sometimes it takes a little hindsight to get it right. Will have to take again. It is VITAL to passing that you read her chapters, no matter how boring they may seem.
Made the class less complicated
Awesome prof
Amazing

Probably one of the best professors I've ever had. What I really appreciated about her class is that she treats you like an adult - no mandatory attendance (though you will miss a lot of tips and instruction you'll need for the papers) and class days dedicated to individual researchpaper writing. She is also kind of hilarious. Would take again.

She is one of the best professors at UMBC, especially at the PoliSci department. She takes the time to help her students, clearly explains the content of her requests when it comes to papers, and she is a wonderful adviser as well. HIGHLY RECOMMENDED!!!!!

Dr.Forestiere is easily the best professor at UMBC. Class requires two large papers, but she makes them easy by breaking them down and stating exactly what she wants. The essays are graded on content and not poetics or style. Very helpful inside and outside of class. Highly recommend.

Very intense workload, but she is the greatest at helping out and if you are in class and not some slouch, she's eager to make life easier, though perhaps not super easy. She loves to teach and you can't help but love her class.

By far one of the best professors I have ever had. Took her for POLI 301 in the Fall and I learned a lot. Whenever I asked her for help, or an extension, she was always available to help. Professor Forestiere is also very friendly and approachable.

Hands down the most intelligent and engaging professor at UMBC. As previously rated, do not take her class for an easy grade. It may be challenging, but you will learn a lot. She is knowledgeable and very passionate to teach and is always willing to help. She is also very easy on the eyes.

I cannot say enough wonderful things about Prof. Forestiere. She is a wonderful woman, extremely intelligent and is arguably one of the best Professors at UMBC. If you want to learn more than you have ever learned before, and be left with skills to last a lifetime TAKE HER CLASS!

Dr. Forestiere is an overall great professor who was very interested in the subject matter. I've had two classes with her and the only problem I have with her is that she gives very vague directions regarding assignments and papers. This can make it incredibly frustrating to know exactly what she wants and can come back to haunt you later.
She very knowledgeable. One of the best professors I have ever had. The work is hard but it is worth it. I promise you will learn a lot.
She's generally awesome.  You are lucky if you have her.

For those of you who need somebody to walk you through your difficulties and restore your confidence, she is the bottom line. However, please do not take this upon yourself that the class is going to be an easy A, you still need to do the work. If you do, you will be okay.

She is so awesome! She's very clear, fair, and you know what to expect from her. Grade is composed of weekly 2 page papers, one research paper/presentation, and a final. Don't take her lightly though, she isn't an easy grader and you should participate. You will learn a lot.

One of the best professors I've had at UMBC. There is a lot of reading, but she is good at explaining it all. She's very nice and pretty fair when it comes to grading. I definitely recommend taking her if you have even a remote interest in Political Science.

This professor's creativity, originality, and intelligence were outstanding. Discussions were always interesting and included something for everyone. Paying attention was easy and I gained some valuable insights. Wonderful class and professor!

Extremely helpful, fun to listen to and always kept my attention. Class format was four multiple choice exams for 60%, and the final was worth 40%. Highly recommended, and will be taking more classes with her!

Very enthusiastic.  It doesn't hurt that she has an extremely pleasant speaking voice (easy to pay attention to).  I don't think you get much choice at UMBC as to who will be teaching 301 during a given semester, but if you get "stuck" with this professor, good for you!
Incredibly smart, energetic, fun and attractive. Sometimes, may throw out too much info. Exams are short essay. (I took her during a winter mini-mester.

Absolutely loved this teacher. I was inspired to catch up on current events, read the newspaper, and watch CNN which I never do. She really does bounce when she lectures because she has so much enthusiasm. I have never once fallen asleep in her class.
Good teacher

The first class I thought she was super nice so I blew off the readings until the night before the first test. BIG MISTAKE! I stayed up all night and got a B. After I started doing the readings on time, I got As on the exams and she gives extra credit. Plan on taking her for 301 in the spring.

Very straight forward about what needed to be done, and willing to talk to you and help you as many times with assignments until they get done.  Had a tendency to be late to class quite often, but when you have a young kid like her, I won't hold it against her.  Very attractive and down to earth, and all in all a great person to talk with.

very hot, very interested in teaching but not the best at it.  her tests can be a tad random but after the first one it shouldnt be too bad.  she is cool and gets to know ALL of her students by a first name basis. i would take her again if i could...

One of the best teachers I've had here. She is very energetic when she teaches and is a great joy to have for a teacher. She loves what she teaches and hopes that everyone else will have the same excitement for comparative politics as she does. Her tests aren't too difficult if you go to the lectures and read the textbook.

This class was actually too easy, so much so that I didn't really learn that much. She was a great teacher though. I don't understand how people could have done so badly on the first few tests -- I guess they didn't take her seriously.

Excellent teacher, loves the subject so much she almost bounces when she teaches.The exams are not too difficult if you read and study and the final is a take-home paper that is pretty simple.Enjoyable class and easy A if you pay attention.
I would love to take another class with her, she has loads of energy and loves comp. poli. passionately. Study for the tests and know the vocab, she likes to quiz that. Final paper is not too hard.

Awesome teacher, she is very friendly, has tons of energy, I would take another class with her if I could...just make sure you really study for her tests! She has no problem answering emails quickly, and will accomodate you if need be. Great professor!

Excellent and energetic professor.  Knows her stuff but is still with the times and remembers what it was like to be an undergrad.  Very helpful and lovely person.  Not to mention for any of the guys out there this professor is good on the eyes as well.

If she ever asks the class to vote if they want a take-home final and says the take-home final will be just about like the midterm be careful- she very well may be LYING and will give you a 6-10 page paper that you have to complete in two weeks instead of an actual take-home final. That sucked.

The final project is a pain and she nit-picks on the summaries, but the class is fairly easy overall.  I don't recommend missing class early on, she covers a lot.  It gets easier as the semester goes along.

Great new teacher, so interesting and helpful, fair exams. I loved this class and would take more classes with her. This was my favorite class this semester, makes participation fun and easy. Learned a lot.

Sadly, Dr. Freet has passed away. He was one of the most caring, kind, and passionate professors I ever had the pleasure of taking and I do not feel like I would be where I am today without him.
R.I.P Dr. Freet, you helped to shape my career. Going to your lectures made my weekdays better.

Unfortunately Dr. Freet passed away in Jan 2025. He was incredibly understanding of a personal situation I was in and allowed me to turn things in late.

I will always respect him for his understanding and his genuine interest in the topic of Computer Science and Cybersecurity.

RIP Dr. Freet

Freet clearly doesn't put in as much work as the students do, often simply leaving inaccurate information on Blackboard for students to deal with. Also very open about his right-wing politics, if you are LGBTQ stay away. Project instructions are unclear and tedious, but not difficult.
dude he's so chill

Really easy class, labs were just following some steps and taking screenshots, and the tests were on blackboard. Unfortunately, he's some sort of right-wing conspiracy nut and can't keep that shit to himself, so lectures frequently go off-topic and are instead about the "plandemic", the FBI stealing his gold, or his ex-wives.

Freet revived my Computer Science cybersecurity career.  One of the most interesting and fun class.  Emphasis on the labs which are basically step by step tutorial and super easy.  Exams are super easy if you pay attention, he asks questions at the beginning of class which you should pay attention of.
Very easy A. Freet makes online lecture enjoyable and has very interesting things to say about cybersecurity. Good CS elective to take with harder core CS classes. Take Computer Security with Freet!
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Group projects--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Loved Professor Freet! He is a real genius when it comes to learning about Computer Security principles. He even addresses what could be possible interview questions during lecture presentations.

Easiest CMSC class at UMBC. His 'labs' are a step by step tutorial of what to do. Really nice guy and genuinely interested in the subject though, so I really appreciate that. However, I'd argue if you want to pursue cybersecurity as a profession, he's the person to talk to but you're better off taking Active Cyber Defense in the Fall. (CMSC491)
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Dr Freet restored my faith in the CMSC department of UMBC. His lectures make me want to attend class. The subject matter is incredibly interesting, and his real work experience makes every much more tangible. He's knowledgeable in the subject matter as well. Projects/HWs are actually fun, and exams are very fair.

Dr Freet makes class fly by. His projects are actually fun, and super informative. It's been a REALLY long time since I've actually been able to say I've enjoyed a CMSC class. I would probably show up to lectures even if it wasn't for credit. 10/10 would definitely recommend.

My mans David Freet is a legend. This guy is really easy but his assignments are hands on and give security experience. Class is pretty fun to go too. He isn't the most experienced at teaching but he's a really nice guy and relates things to examples. He's also a meme lol. He told us he got stuck under a cave while scuba diving the first class.

When you approach him to ask a specific question about the concepts you should be learning or a project he often doesn't know the answer or he gives one that isn't accurate, as if he doesn't know what was planned for the course. Does share project code if you attend class, otherwise not worth. Talk to TAs, other profs and friends to get by.

class was mandatory in person and literal torture for 3 hrs BUT gives online retakeable quizzes and MULTIPLE bonus/extra credit opportunities. doesnt post notes so you have to pay attention. overall very chill but not all that helpful if you need accommodations. exams were in person and moderately difficult.

She clearly outlines the structure of the class. Slides are not available to you but there are guided notes where you fill in the blanks to get all the information. You'll do well on the exam if you go over the guided notes. Several quizzes based on the textbook but you can retake it as many times as you need until the due date.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: She made her classes really understandable and she was easily accessible outside of class. Her exams are pretty straightforward if you attend classes and read the guided notes. About the notes, if you let her know before class she would print out copies for you. Her quizzes are unlimited trials also which helps a lot as it carries weight.

Very few professors have blown me away like Dr Crawford. She is incredibly smart and a great speaker and you never get the sense she does not know what she is talking about. She is also a kind professor. I got the sense she actually remembered who I was from class to class despite there being many other students. She also gives out lecture notes.
Lectures can be dense, but are recorded so you can rewatch.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Test heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Dr. Frey is a UMBC treasure. He's a world class separations expert, and a hilarious guy. He gives youtube tutorials that are very helpful. He gives great examples for separations, lots of interesting trivia facts, and does a great job of answering questions. He loves to give hints and extensions on homework. His generosity knows no bounds.
Great!

He is one of the smartest professors I have ever had, really knowledgeable and great at transferring that knowledge to the students. If you really want to learn and understand transport  phenomena then do not hesitate to take this course !
good prof
Frey is a very good teacher.  He explains things very clearly and if you go to class he gives extra credit.  Also, gives hints on homework assignments a lot!!  :)

His lectures are dry, and being early in the morning only further the soporific effect.  However he's a very intelligent man and at times shares interesting facts and trivia (that later find their way onto exams, so go to class).  If you go to his office he is very helpful, and if you are able to do his homework his exams are straightforward.  Nice
BORING! BORING! BORING!

Professor Frock is amazing. She's a little old school when it comes to her classes. Phones have to be off and in front of you and she doesn't like laptops for notes. There is no final or exams. The group project & article presentation are easy and she's there to help you if you need it. Attendance is mandatory but she usually ends class early.

Highly recommend taking her. All assignments, quizzes, and tests are through MindTap, which you can complete early. There's one group presentation and one individual presentation. She doesn't require you to turn your camera on. She encourages participation, but you can use the chat box if you prefer not to speak.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Old school professor, doesn't like laptops/phones out during lectures but very kind and respected. Lectures are slightly boring and mandatory. In-class discussions are a requirement (I still got an A without ever participating in them). Presentations make up most of the grade. Lastly, don't forget to do the easy online tests/assignments on time!

Your grade is based on assignments, quizzes, and tests done through mindtap, one group project, and one article project. Not a tough grader. Doesn't like technology. Something weird about the class is that you read, turn in assignments and quizzes before you're given lecture on the chapter. Only would take again because I found the class easy.

Professor Frock is a very old School and by-the-book professor. By the third lecture she knew everyone in my class by name. Course material is easy (All of the Homework and tests are online). The lectures are mandatory and participation is part of your grade. There is a group project/presentation that accounts for a large portion of your grade.

All homeworks, quizzes and tests are done online, very easy and no exams. Only two projects due during the semester one solo and one group. Very easy to follow along, all she asks is that you stay off your phone and participate during lecture. Attendance is graded too. One of the easiest professors to take here at UMBC 1000/10!!

Took her over the summer. Very easy going and kind. Reminds me of an old lady you can have a nice chat with. There's 1 individual and 1 group presentation. Hw's are very easy. You need to read the textbook for your presentations, but after that, it's not needed. No tests or exams. Lectures are very boring tho. Easiest A ever. Would take again
Professor Frock is really a gem. I took 210 with her and I'm taking 410 with her this semester. The class is set up pretty nicely. No EXAMS, 2 PRESENTATIONS, and tests + quiz on cengage.

A great professor, she is understanding and nice. Easy weekly homework assignments, article presentations, and a group project and paper. The class is very common sense and her lectures are nice. Definitely  take MGMT 210 with her if you have the opportunity.

Easiest. A. Ever. Aside from 2 projects you have to present, there is just HW which is very easy to do. As a very laid back student who just goes into the online class and treats it as a podcast I found no difficulty with this class at all and sometimes forget I'm even in this class. Just be a active student keeping up with assignments and your set
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: AMAZING professor. She is really sweet, but she does expect you to attend class, communicate, and participate. Homework, quizzes, and tests are all on Mindtap, which were fairly easy to complete. She assigns one group essay/presentation and one individual presentation for the semester. Easy A with nice professor!
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Get ready to read--Group projects

reviews.comment: Very easy, easiest A ever. Take her, shes great. Learned a ton without a lot of work.

Professor Frock is very sweet. She actually cares about all her students and her class is fairly easy. You have quizzes and homework every week and they're all on mind tap. You will have to do one group presentation and one article presentation. She will assign you a group and a chapter for your article presentation.

There is not much to say, she is a good professor. Class is a tad boring but she tends to finish early. Class has a lot of discussion elements she incorporates. Class moved online for pandemic. She handled that very well with weekly meetings. Online material is Cengage... It is unclear, you know the drill already, that is on the department.

Frock is a fantastic professor. She is extremely kind and well informative. Class is made up of a couple weekly online assignments, an individual presentation, and a group presentation. Definitely highly recommended class and professor.

She's a great professor. She's so sweet and class is easy. Homework, quizzes, chapter tests are all online. There is a group presentation and an individual presentation. No pop quizzes. If you ask the prof. to end class earlier she'll say yes if you can give her a legitimate reason like a UMBC party for UMBC kids that never go outside.

I feel like i learned little to nothing in this class. Almost all of the work is online, minus 2 presentations. Her lectures were very boring and she basically just read from the book. Each class had multiple presentations on random topics by students. Only take if required, not if you are genuinely interested in management.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: 14 online exams, lots of pop quizzes, and a couple of presentations, and class discussions happen in this class. You can get an A in this course but be ready to do lots of reading. She knows who read the material or not based off of the pop quizzes and class discussions.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Test heavy--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: TAKE HER!! She's the best professor and is always there to help you out!!! Very easy A! Make sure to do all the work she gives you!

Professor Frock is a wonderful professor. The quizzes and exams for this class are administered online through MindTap. Attendance is mandatory but you wont regret it - lectures were always interesting and she only focuses on the important details. She taught many great life lessons and is very experienced. You can tell she cares about students
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Group projects--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: She may seem a bit intimidating at first, but Professor Frock is actually very lenient and caring about her students. Almost all the work for this class is online. Make sure to pay attention to her syllabus; she will assign an assignment or two and will not notify students to verify that they are reading the syllabus.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--Caring

reviews.comment: She is a very inspirational professor. She cares about students on how they will do in the real world than just in the classroom. Four take home exams, few homework assignments, random pop quizzes, and attendance and participation. Easy A! Highly Recommend!

I feel like this class is simple, and this professor makes it even simpler. Assignments and presentations are very clear, lectures is often fun, and she listens. She listens! It's a great class to get management skills, and an easy A, but just don't be on your phone in class

Professor Frock is a classic professor with a modern, real-world approach. Less theory, more application. With an extensive history in the business industry, she provides expert advice to take on this ever-changing, competitive world. Yes, she's an easy "A", so long as you try, do your readings, and actively participate in the classroom setting.

She was not the best teacher. She was kind of lazy and her grading was unclear. Her lectures were very short and she basically said out loud what the textbook said. She did not upload any grades to blackboard so there was no way to tell what grade you had until the semester was over. The class required a lot of online work.

It's impossible for you to not get an A in this course. All exams are take home. She is very lenient if you stay on her good side and show her you care about this course. In fact, I did that and I had bad time mgmt and forgot to do 3 chapter tests (which is a huge part of your grade) and she gave me an exception and extended my deadline. So awesome
Management 210 is not bad at all with Ms. Frock. Treat her with respect and she will do the same to you.  Do the small amounts of work she gives and you should get an A.
Very enjoyable class. Online quizzes due every week, 1 presentation, online tests, 1 final group project. Great professor.
I took MGMT 210 with her as well. Very good professor, easy grader and knows the subject well. Defiantly recommend her.
Great professor!
Take as a summer course. 3 exams with questions directly from the textbook. 1 presentation. 1 group project. very to the point and easy to pass. go to class and participate, she really likes that.

Took Mgmt 210  Show up to class  READ THE BOOK  Not a lot of hw, mostly reading VERY IMPORTANT If you want to pass Exams READ Group Project is decently stressful  Individual Project is easy Trust me this class has a decent amount of work, but you will get an A if you work hard
One of the coolest professors I have ever had. Very easy going. You must be a fool to not get an A in her class.
Reviews don't lie. Amazing prof. Enjoyed her class.
Very good teacher. Just show up to class and do the simple work, and you will get an A.

She's one of the best UMBC professor I've ever had. She's awesome, and funny. She explains everything very well, and the study guides are really helpful! Make sure you pay attention on what she wants on the case studies, because she reads all of them.

AMAZING professor. Crystal clear on her expectations, and definitely makes class hilariously fun with the jokes and diminutives for all the students :D You'll learn a lot. Don't bother with the study guide, just get the textbook :)

One of the easiest classes I've ever taken.  There's a lot to remember for the exams but so much of it is common sense, there's no need to panic. Plus there's a ton of extra credit. I didn't even need to take the final to get an A. She's pretty nice, and makes class fun.
Great professor, helps you with anything that you could possibly need in the course, I would recommend to anyone having to take management 110 to take it with professor Frock 100%.

Class is made up of 3 exams, 5 case analysis' and 1 presentation. Just read the chapters and your good for the exams (a lot of extra credit on exams). case analysis' are just 1-2 page papers, very easy, takes like an hour. And presentation is simple, 5-10 min and your good. Very nice lady, wants to make class as easy as possible. Easy A.
very easy and helpful!! Strongly recommended.

After our midterms, of which the average was about a 14/25, he asked what had gone wrong because none of his previous classes had done so poorly. We gave him ways to help us do better on the final exam (study guide, practice problems, etc.) but he shrugged them off and claimed that he had "tried those before" and "they didn't work".

Down to earth older guy, clear presenter. Sometimes a little short, but overall he has a kind personality. Makes lab procedure modifications and concepts necessary to know clear in lecture. Grading criteria clear. Caveat: One mostly interacts with their TA during the actual lab, so the quality of the course is heavily contingent on that too.

Tyminski was an engaging professor in lectures and brought demonstrations to class when it was possible. The test material is well-covered in pre-lab quizzes as well as in lecture. He will walk around and visit you during your actual lab period, but you will most likely only interact directly with your TA. Just hope that your TA is an easy grader.

Lectures were so boring I decided to not go to them anymore halfway through the semester and I fared just fine. Exam questions were pulled from the quizzes or the lab notebooks so if you studied, you did well.

Professor Tyminski is really sweet and amazing. I was lucky that I had a good TA, but a LOT of other students complained about their TA. Professor Tyminski doesn't really do much; it all depends on TAs. I liked the class overall, but the tests were weighed too much for a 2 credit lab and some questions were difficult too. Take over summer instead!
Skipped/cancelled over half of the semesters lectures. When he did hold lecture it wasnt engaging, just reading off of slides. Frequently went off topic. He should retire

I only really saw him in lecture on Fridays. He overviews the lab for the next week along with his funny anecdotes. The lab experience and the lab grades will majorly rely on your TA. He pops into lab every now and then. The labs were confusing initially, but you get into a weekly rythmn.

Would lead lectures while TAs led lab periods. Lectures were often funny but sometimes a waste of time. Had to write the lab procedure down in a notebook before class which could be annoying (modifications to the original protocol could get confusing). Your experience depends on your TA. Worried about COVID and then walks around with his mask off.

This professor is interesting. Seems nice at first but is just super cranky. Class is run by his tech assistant who is thankfully nice and approachable. Lectures are pointless since all material is posted, labs are easy and straight forward. Exams are difficult. There were no lectures at least every other week this semester.
Labs were okay, but exam is actually difficult. We never got a final review day kinda just gave us bullet point list of things to know.

Kind and passionate professor. He has accommodated lab very well in the midst of a pandemic. Sometimes the lab instructions can be confusing but he and the TAs help out a lot. Very solid choice for a professor.

I did not see this man once the entire semester. Lab was in person with no lecture just readings/PowerPoints. The entire semester I only got 1 lab grade back so my final grade was a surprise. Labs were relatively easy tho, as were the lab reports so I still ended with an A. They just do not make anything explicit everything was a guessing game.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He made a lab lecture class on a Friday the most fun it could be. He's a charming man who always shared some life stories in the free time that we had in class. I highly recommend taking him for your CHEM lab.

Prof. Tyminski lives up to the hype of being 'the fun professor'. He tries to make his lectures short, simple, and interesting as possible by adding a joke or a story every now and then. The labs, on the other hand, will be difficult, as one time many people had to redo a lab halfway through because of misinformation.

Tyminski is a very nice man and you can tell he really is passionate about Chemistry and teaching. The labs can be confusing sometimes, but the TAs help out so much. It would be an easy A if the final was not weighed so heavily.

I really loved this class. The labs were pretty easy for the most part and the grading criteria and expectations were straightforward. I would definitely recommend attending the lectures for this class because he has the class copy a list of modifications for the lab and you will lose points if you don't have those modifications.
knows his stuff and cares for students, the class is easy if you pay attention and do everything on time.

Really nice and funny guy! He made the lectures very fun. You should definitely go to those as he does make changes to the lab that you otherwise wouldn't know about. He's easygoing but serious when it comes to lab work so pay attention, ask questions when you need to. Great guy.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: He is funny and very friendly. Lab is pretty easy (but that also depends on your TA and his or her grading style). The quizzes were the most difficult but they do not count for a large chunk of your final grade. The final was very easy. Just go to the final review lecture and they will pretty much tell you everything that's going to be on it. EasyA

He's a really cool guy. It's a shame you only really see him for the lectures, and not for the duration of the actual labs. The TA and lab partner you end up with makes more of a difference to your lab experience, but he makes the lectures fun. Also be sure to attend the final review session, since he basically tells you exactly what's on it.

Frank is awesome! Of course you have to put in some work to do well in the class, but it is not too difficult. (This also depends on you lab partner and lab TA) However, Dr. Tyminski's lectures were helpful and he is a cool guy. You can still do very well in the class if you miss them, since he posts the PPs online. But still go! He is great!

Tyminski was such a great professor. He knows his stuff and has been in the field for a long time. You can tell he loves what he does. Would definitely take again. Not a hard class, but you do have semi-time consuming pre-labpost-lab activities. Super helpful, labs were fun. If you show up, participate, & put effort into the class, you'll get an A
My man! Frank is awesome. He jokes around a lot and in general tries to keep the lectures entertaining. The final for 102L isn't bad, and I found the course overall to be fun.

Dr. Tyminski was just plain awesome!  He was super funny and the class wasn't too challenging, plus he made the final easy (at least I thought so).  My only regret is that I didn't get to know him better, he's a great guy!

Very nice professor. Loved his class. It was hard so review notes everytime before you come to class. First day it seems like alot of work, but it really isn't you have fun in lab and work with a partner. Tests are fair, but all comes from notes.
Super friendly and very approachable!
Very respectful and quite generous.
:) Best/Funniest teacher I've ever had.
He's nice but very unclear about material on tests. Many of the questions aren't even from the textbook or his lectures.

He's currently just assisting the main professor but I think his lectures are more helpful. He does excellent demonstrations that give you a good understanding of exactly what you'll be doing in the lab so you can focus on learning from the experiments rather than get hung up about doing the procedures correctly. Really nice and open to questions.

Mr. Tyminski is really nice and funny. Tends to go on tangents that are not really helpful but wants you to learn and be excited about Chemistry just like he is. Nice about correcting mistakes but will correct them.

I don't know about Mr. Tyminski having a 'supple bottom', but he is definitely an excellent teacher. He goes out of his way to help students in both the Lab and Lab Lecture, he is very clear about what he expects from you, and he is always cracking jokes about himself. Very great Chemistry professor. It's an honor to have him as a professor.

he was one of the best professors i've ever had. he's very professional and his experience with covergirl helps a lot. just keep up with the writeups because they take forever to do, but overall i thought he was a great professor
Good professor. Knows his stuff and is filled with stories. Will help you out with anything you need. His TA isn't that great, so keep an eye on your grades from her.
Prof Tyminski is one of best prof. I've had @ UMBC. He is soo nice and will do anything to help the students. If you do your work you will be fine.
One of the chillest professors on campus.  Very NICE and easy going.  Quizzes and tests are short and easy if you read the text.  Labs were fun as well.  One of my best professsors!
One of the best teachers I've ever had.  Cares a lot about his students' success and loves to teach.  He is very straightforward, never tricky.  Class is easy if you take it seriously.

Here to clear up some ratings. It's a lot of presentations based on textbooks then your own info. 2 chapter presentations, 1 solo, 1 final group presentation. You get a lot better at public speaking, I know its scary but your not being judged, make sure to know your content. Group work makes up the class, be an adult do your part and your fine.

Lots of presenting. You would think this was a public speaking course. Multiple group presentations throughout the semester and an individual interview an entrepreneur paper and presentation. He doesn't understand presentation anxiety and pretty much says to get over it. He's nice overall though.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: super condescending, doesn't grade by his own rubrics/grades by "vibes", says "that's how things are in the real world" when you have group members that don't do any work, arbitrarily decides to give pop quizzes if he thinks you aren't reading, will keep you for the entire 2.5hr lecture, picks favorites, lots of writing assignments
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Group projects--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Can be intimidating at first, but chill once you get to know him. Strict with classroom procedures, picky grader, and expects attendance & participation. Lots of presentations with assigned teams, individual writing assignments, weekly reading, but no exams at least. Not a bad class overall, but LONG - you'll be there the full 2.5 hours.
Really cares about his students and wants them to succeed! Is serious about participation but only because he has high expectations for his students.

Professor cares a lot about the students and their grades. He grades quick and gives good feedback. He also encorporates a lot of cool aspects to help better understand the material. He is really great and prepares you with what the business making environment would be like. Super cool guy would definately recommend taking

Everyone has to read and present, regurgitating it for others. Then he'll complain he already knows what you presented. Rest of lecture consists of Top 10 Entrepreneur Tips on Youtube. He has some anecdotes on Amazon, Apple, but has no knowledge of other companies. One lecture he personally does is going to Africa to like find himself. Don't bother

Worst part about this class is all the group projects. He's not that understanding he wants you to be at every class. Attendance is mandatory or it will affect your grade. Easy grader, but long lectures. Books were boring and repetitive.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Rude professor that expects way too much from students in an intro level course. He grades harshly on group presentations and acts entitled and narcissistic. One of the worst non-stem professors at UMBC; 10/10 do NOT recommend
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Tough grader

reviews.comment: It's a self-help book club. Easy but boring. Prof is ok guy, but terrible at fairness. If your partner doesn't bother doing work, he'll expect you to let yourself be taken advantage of for the good of the team. "You need to be empathetic about your partner" and "That's the real world," while your actually doing work and your partner isn't. lmfao
Not good to take this professor as an online class, demands alot from you and is very critical of the work hes gives.
Very nice & helpful.  Def knew his material.  Def take him.
terrific guy, knows the subject by heart. taught us DB designing and SQL in 2 hours with easy to follow directions and rules. recommend him to anyone...
great guy, recommend him to anyone. Learned a lot in his visual basic class...
This guy is cool, lets leave it at that
very approachable, always willing to help, sometimes he can be fun.

I think this is the same course as IS 101. Anyway, he was great. I learned a lot in his class and I would take whatever class he teaches. I believe he is now teaching Visual Basic, but not sure. He can sometimes be monotonous but that’s ok. He knows his stuff very well and conveys his knowledge very effectively. Ah, he is also very cute!

play with his rules and your A is guaranteed. He is a great teacher, he taught relational databases and SQL all in one 90min course, unbelievable. I've seen many professionals not knowing when and how to use the group by and having clauses and he made it perfectly clear and yet simple how to use them. Recommend him to anyone.

great teacher, enthusiastic on the topics. Willing to help in any occasion. Understanding and very knowledgable. Easy to approach. Even though it is an introductory course, I learned more stuff in his class than in any other IS courses offered. Will take any other class he teaches.

This class is super interesting and well organized. Prof Williams gives great feedback on discussion boards and hw's, but the final paper being 45% of your grade can be scary. The textbook is not free which is kind of inconvenient ($10-20 used) so beware. Williams is really good at communication and will answer any questions clearly. Great class!!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: If you are doing well in his class, he will be very rude to you.
This class is all on your own. There is little chance for failure as long as you keep up with the due dates. Super interesting class too!

The class is completely online and very simple. Do the assignments on time and ahead of time, and you will be fine. There are three actual papers that I found very irritating that he graded hard on, but other than that, he is a good professor with good communication. He allows for redos on homework and just truly gives you the grade you deserve.

Professor Gary will take his time to help you understand anything you may be confused on. The class is difficult and time consuming, I definitely recommend office hours, but overall he is a wonderful professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Caring

reviews.comment: I am taking his EMT course and he is the best. Grades are clear and he does everything he can to help out. He is very funny and makes class fun. When you are in class you are doing hands on activity. Everything else is online.

Very interesting class thats useful to anyone really, especially those going into healthcare. Weekly discussion posts to engage, one homework assignment, and 10 page essay. Professor was available but not needed, you'll primarily interact with your classmates. If you need upper level credits, this is a good one!
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Completely asynchronous class with just weekly homework assignments and discussion posts which were easy, but I was not prepared for the 10-page essay due at the end of the semester which was not fun but he is an easy grader. I recommend going to the writing center to help with the essay.

Great class if you still need upper level credits. The material of the class is very interesting, there were a lot of things that I had never thought about previously. Most of the class involves DB posts between students. The professor does not interact with the class very much. The two exams are pretty easy, the final paper is a bit of a challenge
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Professor is very knowledgeable and cares if students succeed. The lectures are extremely helpful and the test are fair. You have to study for the course and devote a lot of time to get the content down, but it is worth it.

Professor Williams assigns discussion boards every week, which I hate to do honestly. Other than that, there is a mid term and final exam, along with research paper. The exams use lock down browser, and material on the tests is not on the study guide. I would not take him again for that reason only. The material taught in this course is interesting
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Prof Williams is laid back and well respected. I would describe his teaching style as very direct and to the point. My only complaint would be that we spent more time reviewing things we didn't necessarily need for the NREMT exam. The final exam for 203 is meant to mirror the NREMT psychomotor but I failed the NREMT after passing his exam...
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring

reviews.comment: Professor Williams made everything clear and do able. You really dont need to communicate with him much but when you do he is super kind and responsive!

If you tell this man you were in the hospital dying, he would say "that is no excuse". The class itself is very easy, however, you can not expect any sympathy from him which is not ideal considering the situation our society is in right now.

Gary is an amazing professor. He is so kind and truly cares about his students. Tests were taken with lockdown camera but honestly the content was not hard at all. One big paper at the end but he's very kind about grading
Williams is a great and understanding guy. Class itself is extremely easy, just a matter of completing the work by the due dates. Highly recommended class.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Easy A

Great Prof would take again. There are 4 total exams no final. Lots of small assignments during the week 1-4 homework assignments. 6 programming labs and he grades the hardest on those and they're the heaviest assignments other than exams. Overall, he is a super understanding guy and wants you to do well. Curves grades at the end of the semester.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Professor Ganapthy is one of the best at UMBC! I was nervous about IS 247 because I heard it was hard, but he made it manageable and cares about his students. He explains concepts well and is very approachable. Attendance is mandatory, with weekly exit tickets, class exercises, Sunday quizzes, and 2 exams. Lenient if you communicate!

Currently taking IS 247 with Mr. V. Attendance is mandatory, with roll at the end of the 7:10-9:40pm lecture. He adjusts assignment deadlines to suit students' needs and is flexible with extensions if you email him. Lectures are long but informative. Quizzes/assignments are straightforward, based on slides. Highly recommend.

Most confusing course I've taken. Instructions were so overexplained/hard to follow and mtgs with the professor made me more confused. His explanations contradicted module directions and even his past videos. He'd say we had freedom on project, then insist we follow his exact method.Learned nothing, disliked every module and gained no useful skills

He clearly has a lot of experience in the web design/coding field and its very helpful for context to the class. The materials used for the class are really great for learning code as well. He is also very understanding to your circumstances, I had a major life change during his class and he allowed me to continue at my own pace to pass.
Super chill guy and very funny. He is funny without even knowing it. Projects take a while to do but they are not very hard. just tedious at times.

Professor Rozanc is an excellent prof, with lots of knowledge, experience, and great insight. Very kind and cares a lot. The video tutorials were so long and the class pace was so slow and flexible that I couldn't focus on class work and it got pushed aside to focus on higher priority classes. This class structure was a nightmare for me!

This guy gave me more chances that I would like to admit, I was at a very difficult point in my life, I moved out of the country and started to live alone while holding a job. I was late to so many assignment and had trouble understanding code. Regardless he always understood my circumstances and gave me time until the very end. Plus over all nice.

I love professor R , he us very easy going but make sure you do his projects and show him that you are really working and is A for you. Is not a easy A class but if you put in the work you should be good

I really like Gary he seems a little hard and harsh at first but once you get to know him , he is actually really cool. Just make sure you work hard so that he feels that you are taking his class seriously.

Gary is a web designer outside UMBC, so he incorporates info that is applicable for real world design jobs. I learned so much, and he takes time to share lots of good links & resources. Plus, he gives good honest feedback, LISTEN TO HIM, he knows what he's doing. If you are not a fan of Lynda tutorials, he does assign a lot. Highly recommend.

Taught 2nd half of microbio with Dr. Schrier. Study guides were not as detailed as Dr. Schrier's and his exams were more difficult imo. You need to use the textbook as supplementary info since the lecture ppt doesn't give enough details for exams. Final is questions from previous exams, don't delete your akindi sheets (answer keys not posted on bb)
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: His tests are extremely hard but I'm glad I I was able to take such a hard class with as good of a professor as him. He's very good at explaining and generalizing concepts so that it's easier to understand. For someone who came in with little to none of the prereqs he suggested, I think I did better than I expected thanks to his lectures.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I have Jeffrey for the remaining section of bio375. Its an online class with in person exams. 90% of your grade is based off 4 exams and a final. he gives no study guide, SI pass, or practice exams, if you ask for help hell say "you should have scheduled office hours".
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The entire grade is 3 tests, no extra credit, no curve. These tests are HARD, as in usually less than 10% of the class gets A's on any of them. Having said that, he is one of the most knowledgeable, prepared, and articulate professors I have ever had. My GPA suffered a bit, but this class made me a vastly better scientist and analyst
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: I took Dr. Gardner on my final semester of 2019 spring. He is literally one of the greatest teachers, mentors and human beings ever. He inspired me so much and I was able to make a huge comeback at the end. He's a very well rounded guy. Taught me to believe in myself. Best biology teacher ever! Made me proud to wear my Labcoat everyday.

Assigned several papers to read each week with guiding questions and in-class group activities. Homework was a single-page critique of 1 paper each week with clear guidelines. Great about providing exposure to new material, explaining things in class and providing room for discussion. Infectiously passionate. Would take this class again.
Good lecturer. Exams are not that easy. He explains everything but then expects as much. Make sure you know your mistakes after each exam, since exact questions might show up in final exam.

He is the best! Interesting person and Very understanding. He includes all the important points in his powerpoints. He brings up very interesting and up-to-date topics in class. I would love to take his other classes! 3  He is a rather young biology professor but he knows what he does and he is good in giving lectures!
He is a tough grader and not easy to deal with.

Awesome professor. I wish he was teaching more courses. By far the best biological sciences professor at UMBC. Actually a professor that helps you during office hours, amazing! Recommend him!! AWESOME

Best bio professor I've had at UMBC. I learned so much about Systems Biology and research technique. Theres lots of scientific reading in this class but his lectures are so thorough and clear that you get a good grasp of each paper. Fair grader and exams are straightfoward. Again, great professor.

Dr. Gdovin, is by far one of the best professors at UMBC. It's sad to see her leave. Her lectures were easy to follow and I learned so much in the course. This class made me want to pursue a Ph.D in Virology and I feel very comfortable doing so with the skills and knowledge she gave to me.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Inspirational--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: She is awesome. Probably the best professor on campus
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: A lot of my classmates kept on saying that she's super nice. Personally, I'm not sure about that, but she does have a kind character. Make sure that you do well on the practicals (once you put oil on your smear, DON'T wipe it off!!!) and the group project. Choose an easy topic for your group project to get an A easier (

Great professor. Willing to work with students and help them learn microbiology lab topics. Class involves weekly assignments and involvement in lab activities. Learned so much about the essential techniques and basic experiments to be successful in other labs.

Dr. Gdovin was awesome! She was always available whenever I needed help. Wasn't very interested in the class at first, but her lectures were great and always left you wanting to learn more about viruses. I highly recommend this course!

Very good professor and is there for the students. Class was pretty tough and took a lot of hard work, but Dr. G was there whenever you had questions. Interesting class and one of the best professors i've ever had at UMBC.

Dr. Gdovin was by far my favorite bio professor;  amiable and knows the material well. When asking her about a question she will try to push you so that you can answer it.  Easy class; just don't slack on the notebook and lab reports! There is quiz every class based off of material from the previous lab.  Group project at the end of the semester.

She  knows her stuff  but do not bother asking her for help during office hours or in Lab. She will make a mockery of your mistakes or questions in front of other students. The only good thing about the lab are the TA's . Skip asking Prof Gdovin questions and ask the TA's they are open to help you without being sarcastic
One of the best professors I had!! Very nice lady!!
Overall a pretty good professor, nice woman. Recommend you go to all the classes, material was pretty hard for me to grasp but others seem to understand. Pretty hot as well.
took the microbiology lab, its so much work for a 2 credit course!
She is the best!

Write down what she says in class, material will show up on tests.Few assignments and discussion-heavy class.Goes too fast over difficult material and doesn't always make the material understandable.Too much material on tests.Book optional.>89% was an A.
The best Bio professor at UMBC. She knows her stuff very well. I loved the class and her teachings!!! Her name should be listed on the "To be cloned" list for the future!

Great teacher. Class is extremely interesting but hard. Notes are powerpoints but I would recommend recording lectures because what she says will be tested on exams. 4 exams, 1 group project, and few assignments. Very approachable. Book was hardly used. Loved the class and teacher!
One of my favorite teachers at UMBC! She's always excited to teach and gives real world examples. Very friendly and extremely helpful. Very down to earth. Also very stylish. :)

Don't underestimate this class. We had 3 different lecturers but Gdovin was the best. Her slides are specific so take notes in class or record. Exams are very hard and specific. But she is very friendly and personable.

I loved taking this class with Dr. Gdovin! She made sure to incorporate real-world applications to what we were learning, which was a first for any Bio class I'd taken at UMBC so far. Definitely not a super easy class, but if you study hard, it's awesome.
she seems more like a soccer mom than a professor, she has a lot of personality, which is a rarity amongst professors. yeah, she can use some work on her lecturing though

Yes, her exams are very hard and she is an extremely nice lady. She was always staying after to help students in her office. She is always willing to help and made the material seem very simple although it was tough. I would recommend taking her but only if you really want to learn alot. Its not an easy grade but it will pay off. Shes awesome!

most students failed or dropped, she is too specific, test on too much material and yet no multiples choices, she wants specific written answers!!!!! the way she said it in class, so make sure you attend and note everything, very nice lady but too much material from her mouth not  her slides and not from the book so you need to memorize a lot

I took this class during the semester that Genetics was co-taught with Eisenmann. It's nearly impossible to adjust to their very different teaching styles. Her lectures are overly-specific, boring, and practically useless. Exam questions are very difficult. She's a sweet lady but not a great professor, overall. Avoid if possible.

Understand what other students went through with this professor.  Definitely he is condescending, rude, and sarcastic man.  Sad that this course did nothing to advance my academic and professional career.   Happy to have transferred to University of Maryland at College Park where professors were total opposite of Mr. German Westphal.

Worst class I ever took. Mocked students, and several people came out of lectures or tests crying. The oral tests are bizarre- its not a phonetics test, and the material involved diagrams. You have to sit in his office alone and describe stuff that could be drawn. Uncomfortable and discouraging, even if you love the subject.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Don't take this class. Well it's all your choice, 90% of your grade is exams. 10% Spanish lab. He does give out packet that is like replica of Spanish lab, but it's pointless. Exams are multiple choice, but doesn't matter. All you do in the class is random HW and go over it. Nothing else, wish I would have switched the first week. It's exhausting.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: This guy has a very thick accent that can sometimes be difficult to understand, and his humor is, while funny, dry and very ill-timed and frequently demeaning. He's difficult to ask questions and he clearly doesn't like teaching and hated half the curriculum of the class... didn't mean he didn't test us on it. He rambles unintelligibly ALL THE TIME

he is a terrible teacher- he does not know how to teach at all. He will try to make jokes but it is honestly super annoying and rude. He WILL discourage you if you are not doing good in that class ( C or below) and he will tell you that you are in danger of failing the course. He does NOT offer extra credit nor does he upload your grades into BB

Three oral exams. You have to go to his office to take them face to face.  Want to pass? -Go to class.  -Write down the examples he gives; he WILL use them on the oral exams. -Understand things conceptually, and know the names for the concepts; see the end of the chapters in the book for the terminology and brief explanations.  Help? Google.

Vague and somewhat confusing. You can take the three tests (only three grades) and pass the course by keeping up with the reading. You will want to run out after 15 minutes of class. He's a good guy, just none of this material stuck. Spent too much time trying to pass the test and learn what I didn't learn from his boring lectures.
Unintelligible. Tests are based on his personal opinions regarding linguistics, NOT from the textbook. Rude and degrading of students.
Worst Professor I've ever had. Avoid at all costs.

I have no idea how I passed this class. In class, He reads whatever handout he gives you or rambles forever. He used 75% of the book material on the test and the questions were vague with alot of "a and b" or "all of the above". I wouldn't mind him if he hadn't sent a failure alert to the entire class in order to boost attendance. Skip him please!!

German Westphal should not be a teacher at any institution. His class is virtually do it yourself he''ll assigned homework on material that hasn''t been introduced yet and then use the next class to go over it to teach it. If you are a failing student he will announce it to the class a violation of student-teacher privacy. How is he employed

Avoid him at all cost! He does not teach anything. He only gave us worksheets and textbook and online exercises. He does not review anything, and then he blames us for failing his tests. So if you hadn't taken Spanish in forever, too bad and good luck on passing his class.

His class was really easy; our only grade was on 3 papers, and he gave blanket A's. However, he's extremely condescending and doesn't respect opinions that differ from his own. He doesn't seem to care about teaching at all, and his lectures are boring and confusing. Take Ling classes with someone else - everyone else in the department is awesome.
AVOID AVOID AVOID AT ALL COSTS. WASTE OF MONEY, WASTE OF TIME. DON'T EVEN BOTHER TO TAKE HIM! WORST DECISION EVER!

the WORST professor I have taken. boring class, boring professor. he kept calling us "hopeless". didn't bother to help us out at all. exams were all multiple choice (doesn't even contain information from the handouts). every class, all he did was read the handouts. STAY AWAY AS MUCH AS POSSIBLE if you value your grade. retaking in summer. =\

Has weird sense of humor, but nice person, just not as professor. Spends classes reading handouts, not lecturing, and rambling. Not clear at all in explanations--even harder to understand with his accent. Grade solely based on 3 multiple choice tests. Questions as vague as he is; debatable ones not according to textbook, but personal opinion.

This professor refused to allow me to test in the testing center, despite disability and being required to do so.  Also, he's incredibly boring and rude. Also, he does not post his classes on Blackboard so grades are unable to be monitored.
Boring boring and boring, he read handouts the entire class and reviewed pointless material. Taking the class again with a different professor.
Great Prof.

What a guy. Hilarious if his humor isn't directed at you- don't be late, read before class, do NOT ask questions that can be answered using the textbook. Tests are based on what he says in class- he doesn't agree with a lot of material in the book so you can't rely on solely textbook studying. If you're self-teaching inclined you'll be better off.

I dropped the class because it was not working for me. He would go over hw all class which was so boring. He wouldn't correct anyone's pronunciation. He didn't know vosotros form at all so he couldn't teach it. And he refused to use the internet to email or anything. He deducted points if you emailed him! Ridiculous!

He can come off as a bit of a jerk at first, but give him a chance. He knows his stuff and is deep down a kind and insightful, if sarcastic, man. He grades fairly as long as you give the class your all; i.e. read, go to class, ask questions, and take his cracks in stride. If you are truly interested in linguistics, there are few better professors.
If you go to class, study a bit and have the work in front of you with added humor you'll do just fine. Though he seems to pick on certain students that's just his way of joking with you.

The fact that anyone can sit here and call this man a good professor is absolutely beyond me. I have dropped the class to retake it next semester with Dr. Field, who is brilliant and I know will teach me something worth learning. Don't take a class with Westphal if you value your GPA.

I agree with the last poster. At first, I thought he was intimidating and at times rude, but eventually I came to realize that he just has a unique sense of humor.  What I sensed was that beneath the surface he really cares that his students learn and succeed. In general if you do the work, he's pretty laid back and will help you if you need it.

Had him for MLL 190 and 320. He is sarcastic, blunt, difficult, and can be MEAN. But I learned a lot from him and he is a really good teacher despite this. I both love and dread his classes, and got As in both. He really wants you to try, and even though he may be harsh in class, he can be really fun and easier if you take it in stride and TRY.

One of the worst professors I've ever had.  Only teaches the theory of language that he subscribes to and is surprisingly biased.  Very slow talker and loves to hear himself talk. Don't take this class if you want to learn anything.

He is a syntax-man. He knows what he is talking about, but wants students to fumble through the material themselves. He will let a student ramble on about stuff even if they are wrong, mostly to force them to come to a logical reasoning themselves. He hates giving out answers and refuses to do so. Participate in class or he won't want to help you.

His accent can be difficult to deal with at first, but once you sit through a class I didn't have any problems understanding him.  The tests are all multiple choice and are only difficult if you don't study well, and he's a funny guy.  Not the easiest class in the world, but not one that you'll fail if you put some effort in.

Westphal is an awesome professor. He cares about his students. If you read your book, go to class every time, and show that you are trying (participate in class) he will help you out. I am going out of my way to take another one of his classes.

Avoid this class: His tests are not worded very well so they are hard to understand and they are tricky. (every point on the test is worth 1% of ur final grade)He makes the class a lot harder than it should be. Take it with another teacher if possible!

Dr. Westphal is a really sweet man. He does get annoyed when students with no interest in linguistics take the class. I liked the material; a lot of it was common sense but some of it really made me think. It is a bit challenging at times but overall it's an easy A if you like linguistics.

A really fun guy. His sense of humor is dry, so not a lot of people get it (and it leads to semi-awkward moments). I took him during Winter, so no one cared to ask a lot of questions; he will explain things until you get them though, you just have to ask! His tests are worded a little weird, so watch out - other than that, he's a cool dude.

Dr. Westphaul was the best Spanish teacher I have ever had.  He doesn't bother with the online chats, quizzes every week, or oral evaluations...simply 4 exams (no final).  Attendance is mandatory but he provides a fun class!  Take his class in the winter/summer if possible!

Difficult to understand with a thick accent, but if you talk to him afterwards about the material, he's really gracious about talking until you get it.  If you're pleasant and show up engaged, having read the material (which.. I am old fashioned..you should be doing anyway) he's very sweet.  Catch him during a cig and amusing conversation will ensu

His class can be a little tricky but his TAs do a lot of the teaching, but normally he is sitting in class to add more to the explanations the TAs give. My class is confused by the material, but they never ask questions! Ask when you're confused, he's not impatient or mean, just a strange little man with a corny sense of humor.

The class is difficult, but that is a function of the material--not the professor.  Three exams, one review paper (which he will give you full credit on if you just does as he asks).  Westphal truly cares about his students, and has a great (but not always obvious) sense of humor.  These negative ratings truly boggle my mind.  A fine professional.
The worst professor UMBC has to offer.....I never had as much trouble with a class as I had with him....do not take MLL 190 with him, it's horrible.
his class was not easy but he allowed extra credit papers if you were on the verge of failing.
No Comments

I took both Ling 190 and Span 201 with him in the winter semester and I thought he was REALLY EASY.  Half the time we scheduled class at a later time and he basically had a really laid back class.  Nobody seems to like him in the reg. semesters, but I say TAKE HIM during the winter...so easy!

I thought this class was very easy, but I saw that many others struggled with the class.  He was/is very opinionated and you have to follow the logic of his lectures in order to do well on the tests.  But it was probably my easiest class yet at UMBC.

This class is torture...I can barely stay awake in his class..he lectures the whole time but I don't see where he's going with the material, and find myself glancing at my watch often to see how many minutes of torture are left.

A most dedicated educator, actually.  He made time to tutor me personally & arrange a project for me.  "Old school" in the fact that his classes *are* lecture-based, and he doesnt curse or joke around a lot in class (bet this 'crime' earns him the bad reviews). He is a sweet, caring professional.
This guy is the worse. If you want to be bored out of your mind, and struggle to answer questions on a test then this is the class for you. But don't waste your time, pick another class.

I HATE this class!!  His lectures are boring and not helpful.  I can't understand him because of his accent. I have to drink coffee before I go to class just so I can stay awake, but it never works.  His test are designed to confuse you, not to test your knowledge.  He takes pride in failing people!
i hate this class.  i can't understand what he says from his accent and he makes the class hard.  im not sure what to study for the exams and the exam questions are so tricky.

He gives boring lectures and never seems to make things make sense (already understood the material from previous classes though so maybe that's biased).  His test questions are riddled with all sorts of traps... not really easy.  Won't admit he's wrong.
He will put you on the spot in class, but is *extremely* knowledgeable, and is willing to question the status quo. Highly recommended.
super easy class, he's kinda funny too
This man won't admit when he is wrong about ANYTHING. He is kind of boring too. If you write a term paper, he won't read it. Definitely not a dedicated educator.
Easy A.
No Comments

I don't care what other people say about him, he's an awesome professor. Had him for French 102 and genuinely wants to see us succeed. Late penalty is extremely minimal on homework. He does have an accent but you need to understand the french accent to pass this course anyway.  Expect to participate if you attend lectures but he's fun to talk to.
Has an accent that makes him hard to understand

He really isn't as bad as people say. He's picky about pronunciation but it really will help with speaking. There are so many opportunities for ec! (French Hour, French games, etc) Stay on top of VHL and you'll do just fine. It can be hard to get him to understand your questions so try to be as straightforward as possible.

He really doesn't deserve all the bad reviews. He genuinely cares about his students succeeding. His class is very interactive and fun. Attend French hour for EC at least a couple times, it's a major help. Put effort into class and he'll notice. As someone else said, you give what you get. Stay on top of VHL!

My least favorite professor so far at UMBC. His homework does not line up with the course, so you'll be doing homework the night before the test that has nothing to do with the test material. Laughs at students for not being able to pronounce words. Says tests are “simple” and doesn't like questions. Talks for 10-15 min. after handing out test. BAD

If you are not already a French speaker and/or struggle to pronounce some words, don't take this class thinking you'll be learning anything. Take this professor only if you have the sole interest in being in a class with the most biased, unreasonable, bully of a professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: One of the worse professor at UMBC, he is extremely rude to his students. He will be rude to you if say a word incorrectly. You will not be able to ask questions on a test if you need clarifcations, his response would be "No need to ask questions, the quiz is simple"  he will make fun of you in front of everybody to make you feel bad.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Extremely Disorganized, was lost everyday.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Extremely helpful and disorganize

My advice for someone rusty on French would be to go to his French hour(ez EC btw) and he'll say the vhl videos as well, though I don't think that's necessary to get at B . Quizzes are straight from the book exercises and readings, so you can literally memorize those and ace them, exams are similar so it's not difficult to study for in my opinion.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: N/A

Professor Mushayuma is one of the worst professors I have had at UMBC. Even though I attend class every day, I observe him picking on people for no reason when they are trying their best to pronounce words. He is an extremely disorganized professor who doesn't know what he is doing. Do not take him, you have been warn.

Professor Mashayama is a terrible professor. He doesn't respect his students    and he enjoys humiliating students in front of the whole class. He will be rude to you if you mispronounce a word. This professor shouldn't be teaching french if he expect us to say the word correctly in a snap! DO NOT TAKE THIS PROFESSOR!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Great professor, very funny, engages the class. I learned a lot being in the classroom, even if sometimes he can humiliate students a bit. He is a little bit out of touch with UMBC and some students, but a great guy and a good educator.

An extremely terrible professor who does not respect his students. He enjoys picking on students and disrespecting them. If you mispronounce a word, he would disrespect you as many time you try to say it correctly. Don't bother going to office hour, he will just be plain rude. I feel like he is rasict to certain individual.

I walked into his class thinking I was going to hate it, but by the time the semester was over, I wished I could have him next spring. Once you get the hang of the way he teaches and the material on the quizzes, his class is not hard. Just remember to participate and show up to French Hour and you will pass.
Professor Mushayuma genuinely loves the French language and he truly cares about his students success. As long as you stay in your textbook and do your homework you will be successful in this class.

His confusing communication with students was incredibly frustrating. About half of his course was just asynchronously filing through an online textbook course similar to Khan Academy. Due dates, specific assignment isntructions, and feedback are often unclear. If you have to take his class, try to make sure it's all in-person.

I'm not sure why he has bad reviews I've had a good experience. He's caring and fun too, it's clear he wants the students to do really well. You have homework online, 4-5 quizzes, a midterm and final. Participate in class, you get points. Only time he gets frustrated is if someone asks stupid questions that he's already went over so pay attention

I took his course in the Summer and genuinely thought he was hilarious and helped me so much with pronunciation by getting me to slow down and focus.
