I think something that overwhelmed some more reserved students was that attendance was graded depending on participation so it was beneficial to work ahead in class in order to answer questions.

He is a great Professor but there may be some pitfalls depending on whether you a reasonably good foundation for FREN 101. He has some trouble with English so if you also have trouble with English, this may be an issue for you. I and some people generally enjoyed and performed well in the class

He's an alright professor, he's a little messy with lectures and he's pretty forgetful, but some of the critiques I've seen about him on this website are a little exaggerated. If you go to class and do the homework, you'll pass. He's just an old man, so of course he won't be the best French professor in the world.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: French was/is difficult for me, but this class was not that bad. Keeping up with the online textbook is extremely important, honestly it probably saved my grade. Quizzes were straight from practice problems used in class, if you were paying attention you should know the answer.

He is a great professor. It is sometimes difficult to keep up with what he is saying but he is extremely caring about students and helps them as much as he can so everyone can pass. He is very accommodating and explains concepts over and over again until you get it. If you pay attention and ask for extra help when you need it, he will help you.

English language barrier, better to communicate in French. If you ask "Why?", he says because it's wrong with no further explanation. Tough grader on pronunciation. If you don't have a strong FREN102 background, not the professor for you. You will not pass just by doing the bare minimum. Has office hours and tries to work with schedule conflicts.

The professor is helpful to you if you show that you are actually trying. Its important you memorize the gender of nouns, extremely important! There are lots of assignments and are heavily weighted; easy way to get grade. Gives study guide for quizes/exam. Language is hard to learn specially french, only take if you are ready to commit. Good luck!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: He's a nice guy but when you ask him questions he goes on forever and doesn't explain very well. Goes on tangents about random things. Ask for help during quizzes and he'll help a lot. Make sure to read the text book.

He is one of the worst professors I have ever had, he is sexist and is disrespectful to female students. grades his quizzes ridiculously. will not help his students, consistently talks down to students. Constantly says "Don't worry my students it's easy" Avoid this professor at all costs!!!

The professor is late half of the time and usually blames the traffic. Lectures can be confusing - the book is much easier to understand and much more useful for quizzes. He talks down if you don't understand right away. He also doesn't keep track of what he already taught, so you can spend too many days doing the exact same thing.

Taking this guy right now. He can be flexible but it's not worth it. The book teaches better and will help you with the quizzes. His lectures are sub-par and attendance is taken. He is very condescending. He grades harshly and will not hesitate to express disappointment. Ver y unclear and gets upset when you don't understand... help :(

This man is abrasive. I had second semester French with him, and he literally taught the class entirely in French. Really? He often gives students an attitude when they ask for help or pronounce something incorrectly. His lectures do not even remotely prepare you for his quizzes, which are graded harshly by the way. Also his English is sub-par.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: NICE TO HIS STUDENTS, AND HE GOES OUT OF HIS WAY TO MAKE SURE YOU UNDERSTAND THE MATERIAL. GREAT PROFESSOR

If you can avoid taking him you should I would recommend anyone else but him. He is unclear at times and expects you to already be a french speaker. I am taking the class to learn not to already know. He will humiliate you if you do not know the answer to an activity. Honestly one of the worst teachers I have ever had.
I'm a senior in Computer Science and French is my hardest class.  Avoid at all costs.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Horribly unclear, very demeaning to most students in the classroom. From my experience he's the worst teacher I've ever had. This was my fourth year in college and the first time I've ever done badly in a class. I would never take his class again. If you're taking French at UMBC I recommend Anne Bengochea. Great teacher, strict but clear.
Good guy, but not great at explaining actual concepts within the language. Will give you extra time on assignments if needed.

Prof. Mushayuma is a wonderful person who truly cares about his students.  He gives us every opportunity to succeed, and tries very hard to ensure each of us can better understand the language.  He wants us all to pass, but he does make you work for it.  If you want a great learning experience, go with professor Mushayuma!

Take notes and show up for class and you'll do fine! Make sure you ask questions if you're confused. Professor Mushayuma is one of the kindest people I have ever met. He's just a really freaking good person. It's awesome he happens to be a professor.
Awesome man, extremely helpful tried everything to make sure you passed with an A. Totally recommend!

Prof. Mushayuma is a very personable, approachable man who makes every effort to see his students succeed. He'll extend deadlines, give re-tests, and sit with you until you figure it out. He's from Congo and has some hilarious stories about marriage, family, and goats. Just read a little bit every night and you should have no problem in his class.

This professor is the most helpful one I have ever had. He is always willing to give extra help and extend homework deadlines. He really cares about his students and wants them all to do well. If you have a chance to take him for a class, do it!

Georges is the best!! There is a lot of clapping in class so be warned. He his energetic, fun, passionate about the language, super helpful and an overall pleasure. Wish I could take him for 102 and 201! He helps you learn a lot w/o stressing you out. Languages are tough but Georges makes it  easier and fun

Georges is an amazing teacher & wants everyone to succeed. He will do his best to help you do that.If you show up & do the work you'll get an A. He will tell you exactly what he expects you to know for quizzes/tests/exams and if you have questions you need only ask. I would take this professor for 102 & 201 if I could.

Horrific slides with info straight off Wikipedia. No additional knowledge gained from class. At times even spread misinformation (talked about seed oils, called a shark a mammal, and stated experts aren't sure if global warming is happening). Luckily the curve is huge and 78% counted as an A. Don't go to class. Lectures are just him rambling.

Chris is by no means a good professor. He likes to tout that he enjoys teaching in an associative learning-like style, bringing real-world examples into lectures. While this style is effective for many professors, he tends to ramble about topics unrelated to the class and spouts misinformation during his tangents—a Dunning-Kruger effect professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The class grade was based completely on exams, but most were just multiple choice questions that were similar to ungraded assignment problems or examples in the lecture slides. Lecture slides were VERY dense. Dr. Geddes was always approachable and helped as much as possible.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Ppt slides were dense, taken straight off wikipedia, had unclear calculations, and didn't provide a good basis for exam review. Simple concepts explained in the most drawn-out and complicated way.  Final was in different format than we had been prepared for throughout the semester. Very few materials to practice with and no access to graded exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment:
-PPT slides with many mistakes
-Misinformation spread in class
-Condescending attitude
-Unsympathetic to student struggles
-Incomplete derivations
-Unclear test expectations
-Text-heavy PPT, info from Wikipedia
-Confusing tangents
-We couldn't see exam equation sheets beforehand or take our completed exams home
-Minimal examples/practice problems

Exams based on content not covered in class to the extent it was tested on. He was rude to students.Textbook not used, only wikipedia. Formulas derived in class incomplete and unclear. Lectures included long stories of world applications that were not tested on. Hundreds of slides with unclear direction for examination.

He doesn't seem to like teaching and doesn't put in very much extra effort to ensure organic student success. The large curve on the final grade attempts to makeup for poor teaching style, inaccessible office hours (typically early in the morning and hard for commuters), and no present TA. Simple concepts are overcomplicated and not explained well.

Class grade is only reliant on exams, and lecture slides are heavy in content. We only get a couple assignments a semester (not-graded), and they inefficiently prepare you for examinations. He is sometimes accessible over email, but there are no TAs or office hours. Exam feedback is nonexistent and unhelpful, and cannot be taken home.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Easily the best Chemistry professor I have had. The way he teaches keeps you engaged and awake. He loves to tell stories that go along with what you are learning about, which helps you learn about the material. The 3 exams were hard, but they felt fair and reasonable. He is very approachable and easy to talk to if you have questions.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Great class! It wasn't overwhelming, extremely reasonable. Interesting topics and even more interesting tangents:)
Had a very good experience in this class, very interesting and Dr Geddes is very approachable, unlike several other ProfessorS I have had at UMBC.

Not a hard class. He lectures off powerpoints and tells you which slides have exam content. His lectures are interesting but the class fosters memorization rather than comprehension. If you memorize the wrong things you won't do well. Your grade is based on 3 exams and a comprehensive final. There's no graded homework and he curves.

I have thoroughly enjoyed this class. Dr Geddes is an amazing professor. His lectures are clear and he explains concepts several times. He relates life to his classes, placing everything in context. I strongly recommend this course. The assignments are not compulsory. The exams are multi choice and from the lecture slides, straight forward.

An excellent course. He spends a lot of time going through content and even repeats the last class concepts at the beginning of the next class. Exams are multi choice and straight from the lecture notes, very fair. This is the best class I have taken at UMBC so far.

The exams are all multi-choice but as he says many times he spends more time coming up with the wrong answers than the right ones, ie. they're almost all trick questions. This is a very ineffective way of gauging student knowledge. I've learned an immense amount in this course but have done very poorly in it, he has a poor assessment style.

Took Chem 303 this year and "A"ced it !,  Its a great class. Dr Geddes has a very rounded grasp of science and can relate real world situations to science. He teaches very clearly and always had time to meet and answer questions. Not too many homework assignments, which suited me fine.

Dr Geddes is one of the most inspirational professors I have ever had. He is able to teach content of chem 303 and relate it to real life science in such a way that makes it very interesting. The downside to the class, is that there is a lot of slides, hundreds. This was the best class I took at UMBC.
Very much enjoyed this class.
Great class, I enjoyed lots, would do again

I took P 303 a  year back and enjoyed immensely. Dr Geddes was very helpful and he too h tie to answer questions and go through the exams in detail. I would take the course again. He has a very cool English accent.

He teaches main concepts and little bit of details. His lecture slides are mainly from Wikipedia. Interesting lectures, he talks about snow on mars, dust levitation on moon, Nazi trying to use deuterium water to destroy England.No HW.3 tests (multiple choice)and final worth 40% of grade. If you study and do problems he puts up, then easy A or B.
Very ineffective teacher. Nice man, but not skilled as an educator. Participation grade was determined by a most absurd method.

Gerrad is very cool and funny, but when he's serious take him serious. He is so talented and deserves respect. If you aren't a theatre person, don't take his vocal classes, you're going to think their weird, but I  love it.

Attendance is very important and is graded. You also never know when there's gonna be a pop quiz. The class can feel boring, but it's super easy. The work is super minimal and as long as you participate and do what is asked of you you'll get an A. A great class for an AH requirement.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Gerrad is one of the best acting profs I have ever had. He is kind and gives amazing feedback, and he is not afraid to tell you how it is. I wish I could take all my acting classes with him.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Graded by few things--Caring

reviews.comment: This subject is incredibly important, but unfortunately, the way it is being taught does not do it justice. The instructor struggles to deliver the material effectively, making it difficult for students to grasp key concepts. Additionally, the group project is poorly managed, which negatively impacts students' grades.

Econ 477 course seemed hard but trust me, get that textbook.He doesn't require it but it's very useful and it's free to download.If you use youtube and that textbook and the lectures he posts in bb, you should be able to solve everything.Easy A.The prof is the sweetest person ever and will respond to emails asap.If you got questions, just ask him!

He is a great prof, but the material is very difficult. Skip class wont pass is real here, you need to attend to ask questions and understand material. There are only three items that are graded, mid, final, & project. There are problem sets which are extra credit, up to 12 points, out of 125. He cares a lot about the students, online sucks tho

His entire class is based on 4 pre-recorded lectures which SUCK. The problem sets are incredibly difficult and the lectures do not provide the necessary information to do well in the class. There is one exam the entire semester, and it's the final exam worth the majority of your grade. This guy is god awful. Don't torture yourself like I did.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Group projects--Tough grader

reviews.comment: His classes are the hardest things you'll ever do, but I learned more from his courses (ECON477 and ECON478) than I did in the rest of my degree program (FIEC). He gets his test question/group project ideas by reading through actual news about the economy from the Fed and news outlets. If you devote the time, it's great. We love him.

Darryl Getter is the best professor I have had at UMBC. He is an actual practitioner, great teacher and honestly just cares about your success. Tests are open book, but they are difficult if you don't study before hand. The way the class works, if you understand the material you will do fine. If you don't show up or take notes, good luck.

Darryl Getter is an awesome professor and uses humor to get through the late night classes. The material is hard and you need to write down everything he does. His exams are very difficult and you need to think beyond the material to do well. Do not miss a class because, you will miss a lot. He is great but get ready to study.
reviews.rating_tags: GRADED BY FEW THINGS--Amazing lectures--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: Favorite Econ professor! Great sense of humor. Chill and genuinely caring.  Pro & con: No textbook to fall back on so you absolutely need the class notes. Best tip: make sure you read all notes up to that point prior to each class. Make sure you understand them all otherwise you'll need clarification. Don't rely on the open-notes, you MUST STUDY!!!
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: He is a very nice professor but yo is the hardest professor i have taken yet. Okay there are open note exams but you still have to study and know the material or else you will fail. Exams are very tough and there are only two and one group project. Recommend do not take if you want an A.

Getter is an amazing and caring professor. His exams take a bit of time to get used to because he tests your ability to analyze/ critically think about the problem. He's exams are mostly written so you have to explain your thinking carefully  and accurately as possible. 2 exams (35% each) and 1 group project (30%).

Darryl Getter is the man. Take his classes if you actually want to learn and apply economics to the real world. Exams are open notes but they are difficult, you have to understand the concepts of the material so make sure you take good notes. Very helpful, always willing to stick around to answer any questions you have. Great professor.

HE can teach for real but he's the worst teacher i have ever had. He teaches easy stuff in class and gives homeworks and problem sets that he says are supposed to be harder than exams but that's wrong. His exams are things that you have never experienced in life, never seen in class. it's like he's at UMBC to fail people in purpose. avoid him.

He is one of the better professors at UMBC because of his work experience. Not to mention, he's awesome. The tests are tough because he wants you to think conceptually. The way he word things are weird, but he will explain things clearly if you ask. Two exams and a term project. Do not come into this class expecting a easy A.
Nice guy but incompetent. I got an A but don't know and forecasting. I'll have to learn it on my own for my capstone project.

Go to every class and take notes. The book is not used but instead as a reference. The exams questions can be unexpected. It is open note but you had better know the material before the exam if you are to do well. He is also very helpful and will respond to e-mail questions on the weekends and at later hours than most professors.

Excellent lecturer with wonderful real world experience. However it is impossible to know what types of questions will be on his tests. Hopefully his exams from his other econ classes (477 and 423) are much more straightforward. Get a good nights rest the day before, study the practice exams and hold on. Grade consists of 2 Exams, 1 Group Project.

One of the best prof at UMBC. He is very clear in his classes and very helpful. It is open book and if you come to class, there is no way to fail his classes. I took 3 of his classes and passed them both.

Man what can I say....dude is the hardest Mofo alive....he is a nice chill dude but he doesnt use his textbooks....tests are open notes but its a trap he almost uses nothing from the notes....instead you have to derive an answer from the notes you have by thinking creatively but he is a tough grader so you have to be specific....Too much pain lol

Professor Getter is a straight up G, he is the best professor I have ever had at UMBC. You don't need the book but WRITE DOWN EVERYTHING HE SAYS IN CLASS and make sure you understand it, not just memorize it. Incredibly helpful and clear in his teaching. Would have liked to have him teach all of my Econ/Finance classes.

NO textbook needed.  Show up, take good notes (tests are open notes!!) and use Getter if needed, as he is VERY helpful!  Getter is very interested in the subject, wants everyone to do well and has a great sense of humor.  Take this class WITH Getter!!
I love this guy and will take him in the future. DO NOT leave UMBC without taking at least one of his classes. Yea its hard but the subject is very interesting.

Professor Getter is the best econ professor I've ever had. He raises the roof of knowledge all day and is always happy to help. He wants you to learn so he doesn't take any BS answers but he makes sure that you understand. He's the man!

One of the best Econ professors I ever had. If you like economics and you think you are smart, take his class. You will learn a lot in his class. I think his class is very easy and interesting. I got an A in his class.

Best teacher ever. If you are looking to sit on your hands, he might not be the best fit. If you want to learn real world applications, he is the best. I graduated in 2005 and I still rely on his advice. I am glad UMBC has teacher like him.
this teacher sucks , u should not take his class......he will fail everybody if he can...for all those seniors just look into other classes otherwise u will have to take another class later...

one of the worst teachers on the planet, he doesn't allow any BS on his exams... it's open book and if you get a question wrong he usually crosses out everything you write with huge X all over your paper and write comments like "are you serious?" or "did u really just write this?" that not only embarrasses you and then he gives you an F on the exam

Hard class, I may have only gotten a C, but I feel like I learned more in this class that I could apply in the real world, than in most of my other classes put together.  He's got a very laid back sense of humor, don't be afraid to go up and talk to him if you're having a problem.
No Comments

He's a jokester. You'll definitely here something about raising the ruff but during the test you'll feel like the ruff is falling on ur head eventhough it's open book. He tested on things not even covered in the course and you're expected to do you're own research.Nice guy but no the best professor.
Easy class. He gives open book / notes exams. Just make sure you understand the material and show up in class. There is a group term paper. Take him if you can. Most people got A or B.
One of the hardest teacher I ever had but he is a very nice person.
I took this class online over the summer and it was the easiest course ever. Professor Ray was very helpful and was caring about his students. I would definitely take him again.
He's both an easy grader and he's a good teach who you can learn from. Win-win.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Group projects--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Cool professor. I took databases with him, pretty easy class, but it's not like one of those classes where it's easy and the professor doesn't know anything. Dr. Ray is very smart, having worked for Microsoft and a variety of other places, so people still show up for class to hear what he has to lecture even though they could probably stay home
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Graded by few things--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Prof. Ray is an absolute joy to have as a professor. Super chill, attendance not mandatory but people still want to go to class. Easy A, midterm took 15 mins max, projects are group projects but can easily be done individually. If you're sick of getting C's in your CMSC courses and having unnecessarily tough profs, take this guy.

Every project is group project which we can finish it in hour if you come to class do the classwork. Exams are pretty much what its on the study guide. Looking for easy A? take this class and show minimum effort.

Easy teacher, but still has a way of making you want to work hard. He loves what he does and very thoroughly enjoys teaching. the best part of the class had to be his in class handouts.  He walks you through programming an example of what he just showed and makes sure you have a working version of the code before you leave. I wish everyone did this

It's the end of the semester and I feel sad because of this class. Professor Ray is such a good instructor. Super organized, super reasonable with grading, super knowledgeable on the topic, and just a pleasant all around human being. Take this class if you truly want to learn and not stress over a grade.

With a resume like Dr. Ray, I was very excited to take this course with him. Very straight forward class. He is not there to trick his students. Also really enjoyed his connections to Computer Science.

One of the easiest CS classes I've taken, especially for a 400-level. Not much work, and it is really easy. Dr. Ray is very nice and will help if you ever have a question about anything. He reviews the core concepts over and over, which is helpful at first, but then gets boring. Expect boring lecures but an easy A.

George Ray is an amazing person. He truly cares for his students, and weighs all of his assignments equally. There are three projects, three labs, and three exams(including the final, which is not cumulative) which are each  worth 10% of your grade. Then there are three home-works, each worth 3.3% of your grade. All of it is very easy. Easy "A."

The Professor is very good at what he does and has this course down to a science. He speaks slowly and eloquently which lends itself well to teaching PL/SQL. The project was good work and if you show up and attend labs you will have no problems. Don't slack in taking notes and doing the HW and you will have an easy semester.

Prof Karabatis is passionate in teaching his course and he knows what he's talking about. This class definitely requires lots of time for self-study and practice. This is class TEST-HEAVY. You will have two exams, each weighing 25% of your grade, and another 25% for a group project. So, no need to be stressed out too much about labs and homework.
Not a good teacher.. His methods are old, his exams are old-fashioned. He may have 100 years of experience but his teaching style is 100 years old.. He wants students to memorize programs and syntax
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Beware of pop quizzes--Test heavy

reviews.comment: he will not give you a cheat sheet of syntax in exams... you have been teaching for 30 years and not to question that, these things are fine but your methods of teaching and examination are primitive.

Waxes philosophical, and gives you the sense that "you should know that already". Prepare for ambiguous assignments and one to three word replies via email. Will forget to grade your materials for long periods of time. Favors lockdown browser with timer on exams. You just survive his class as best you can.

Its honestly not that bad, its a difficult class with heavy material just in general and he does his best to give you lots of resources to help learn it. He is still very lenient on the project. Like Ill admit I did the bare minimum and just simply got it to work and still got a 100%

I learned a lot in this class, but not from George. If you have lab separate that will be where you learn the most. But I don't think he knows what he's doing. His assignments are full of contradictions, and his exams dont reflect what you've learned. He's also really bad at time management, running out of time in lectures and giving exams too soon
The exams are not that hard and he grades very leniently. The group project was not outlined very well and most groups did not get theirs to work but still got an A . Overall great professor
reviews.rating_tags: ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--GROUP PROJECTS--Tests are tough

reviews.comment: Karabatis is a good professor. The midterm was pretty difficult, but if you study you can do perfectly fine. There were no A's, but B's were achievable. He is an extremely lenient grader, where for the group projects, a lot of people got 100's even though their parts didn't work properly. You need to pay attention, but you can do fine in the class.

This was by far my hardest and most time-consuming class to date. The group project is extremely involved and takes a lot of time to complete. He was very unclear about what was expected for group deliverables and did clarify well when asked about it. That being said, you will learn how to use SQL and PL/SQL very well.

Dr. Karabatis' reputation is that he is strict, but he really wants the students to learn and become independent ready for the workplace. He cares about teaching. His group project had allowed many students earn jobs once graduated.

Attend all classes and don't be lazy.  You must learn how to use SQL to get an A in this class. He's an easy grader. Do all your homework it will help with the project. The project is great don't rely too heavy on your group because there are a lot of bums at UMBC who are lazy and don't care.  If you are somewhat smart and motivated its an Easy A
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Inspirational--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: Good professor don't be scared about what you hear. His grading is very lenient. Labs will help you if you attend and ask question. HW are easy just look at what you did in labs. Group project will require dedication and teamwork. Project requirements were vague in some aspects so press the prof. on what it means. Exams weren't bad.

You will learn a lot from this class. Lectures are dry but straightforward. Workload is overexaggerated. The group project will take time but is not particularly difficult, just requires a good group. Let me repeat: your group project grade will be HEAVILY dependent on how good your group is. The group project requirements are also a bit vague.

This class was hell under this guy. Do not take this class if you are full-time because there is ALOT of work involved in this class. You have lab, homework assignments, weekly quizzes, 2 exams along with a huge group project which is heavily reliant on teamwork and cooperation. The professor himself has no clue on how to help you with the project.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: 10/10, would take again and again, but not a fourth time because UMBC only allows 3 attempts for a course.

He is a good professor when it comes to teaching but doesn't give grades easily. Think before you take course under him , he won't help you much with project but explain you the concepts when needed. To get an A under him you will have to work really hard in group project and do something out of the box. Start with the project as early as possible.

Very unrealistic workload. HUGE final project. For my project, 2 of my group members dropped out and he didn't care to reflect that in the project grade. So naturally, me and my 1 other group member didn't do so hot. Make sure to complain a lot about bad group members if you dont want to be punished for them, otherwise ur screwed

Overall smart guy and good lecturer but not the best teacher. The workload he gives is unrealistic for students with busy schedules. You will have to write multiple codes weekly for both lab and hw on top of a hugeeeeee project he gives. Manage your time wisely and brush up on SQL a lot.

Dr. Karabatis really cared about teaching his students.  His style of teaching always creates an environment of learning.  One has to understand that he is teaching seniors who are getting ready and graduate, hopefully work maturely.  I learned a lot from his class, though it was difficult.  His projects are industry level.  Great professor.

The class is very unstructured and unorganized. The material that's supposed to be taught earlier in the semester, is presented the last. Not enough time to finish the group project. So you're better off studying the textbook on your own and completing the project throughout a semester in properly timed deliverables.

Dr. K is an awesome professor. He is very knowledgeable in the subj and very helpful.The semester long project & 2 exams were a direct reflection of everything that was taught in class and the lab assignments. If you do the work and attend class and labs, you will DEFINITELY learn a lot from this class & do well. I would CERTAINLY take Dr. K again!
Teacher read off the slides, was not very helpful since we only met once a week since we also had a lab session. The TA was much more helpful in explaining SQL and what we were expected to learn.

I've never referred to a professor as horrible before but that absolutely describes Dr. Karabatis.  It was a regular occurrence to not receive grades back for 1-2 months after submitting.  Professor never resolved Blackboard issues after weekly student complaints.  Exams are medium-hard difficulty and projects can be challenging for non-SQL experts

Worthless. Explains how to use software with a slide show and no computers in the room. Very difficult way to learn. I don't think this guy even uses a computer. Very unhelpful, and if you can't use the textbook to figure out how to do assignments you're screwed.
This guy is ridiculous.

Dr. Karabatis is a really cool guy and has a sense of humor.  He responds to emails fast and is always willing to help.  He doesn't give much guidance on the project, but its not too bad.  Exams aren't bad as long as you study.  My lab teacher left a lot to be desired, but i think that was the luck of the semester.  All in all, I'd reccomend him.

There is a semester long project that he doesn't give much guidance for. The labs and exams are pretty easy but make sure you put in time for the project, it's worth 30% of the grade and it takes a while no matter what you're doing your project on. He is a cool guy and is there for help if you ask for it.

This was the best history class I have ever taken! Dr. Musgrove is extremely intelligent and caring, and he truly wants you to succeed. Very approachable and happy to help you if you need it. His lectures were engaging and full of information. I learned so much from this class!

I took Dr. Musgrove for the Post-WWII history class and although he does assign a lot of reading, if you're there to learn you'll find this helpful. He's funny and super passionate about history and he makes the class enjoyable. He doesn't put text on his powerpoints which forces you to pay attention; some students don't like this.

Go to his office hours. The class was better after I did. He's a good guy, and, though he won't give copies of his notes out if you're absent, it's a pretty easy class.  It's a good class, but I wish the papers were longer and more in depth.

Get ready to read a whole bunch of blah that you will NEVER understand in the first place. He tries to be funny and relatable, but is really just extremely boring. His lectures are long winded and my hands cant write it all down before he is on to the next. Only pictures on powerpoints, so you have to pull from what he says which is impossible.

Very tough grader. Did not give very many assignments and had to write more in this class than I did in my writing intensive course.  Also assigns way too much reading homework. He is helpful outside of class.

Awesome class. Dude's the man. Super passionate and clearly has mastered the subject. Also hilarious if you can catch the jokes, but they're pretty subtle. Only problem with the course isn't in depth enough, he should be teaching this class at the 200 or 300 level. Terrible at computers though

Been in class every day, and I am still having a tough time. Grades are pretty much based on 3 tests and a paper. He requires participation which is 10% of ones grades. I am not really big on history so participation is tough for me. And he requires a lot of reading, which is some-what  covered in class.

I went into this class with very high hopes because I find 20th century American history very interesting.  But Musgrove insisted on teaching political affairs rather than the major domestic and foreign issues.  He should be teaching a polisci class.  He is also extremely poor at using technology.  The tech guy was basically there every week

Projects were designed extremely poorly. ZERO communication via email when changes made to the project documentation. Changes to the documentation made HOURS before the project was due and TA's spreading misinformation constantly. The most stressful and horrible class I have ever taken at UMBC. Graders not doing their job made it so much worse.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: One of the most cruel and unforgiving people I've ever had the pleasure of knowing. He makes no effort to understand students beyond their numerical grade and offers no sympathy for any obligation outside of his class. He puts himself on a pedestal and expects his students to march around it. I wish he would learn to interact w/ students positively

This class was super hard but I managed an A somehow thanks to how it's all weighted. The exams were fairly easy and since it's open note I think you're guaranteed at least a 50% in the class. Project concepts are extremely niche and vague though, it is not just regular C programming,  so it's super hard to find sources outside of him and the TAs
He is a great professor. Tests and Projects are 50 50 which I appreciate since I am not a very good test taker. His explanation is great. I recommend taking his classes if you can.

He's perfectly fine, though this isn't an easy course with any professor. Only work for the class was 4 tests (not cumulative) and 4 projects. Tests were multiple choice only. Projects were fairly difficult, and they didn't give us rubrics for them until *after* grading them. You can probably get away with skipping lectures.

Professor Tompkins is a great choice for CMSC421. The class is inherently difficult, but Prof. Tompkins is really sympathetic and always available outside of class. If you are struggling, talk to him and he will happily help you! I wouldn't have passed this course without his support. Further, his lectures are interesting and tests are easy.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment:
(For CMSC 626 -- Won't let me select different from 421)
After working a job related to comp security, I can't speak highly enough of this class w/him. He's retired NSA so he knows these concepts VERY well and explains them VERY well. 11/10 would recommend for any class. Every CS grad student should look at this class, regardless of your research.

Tompkins was an interesting professor.  The class is one of the hardest in the Computer Science pathway but Tompkins made it some what barrable.  Class grades was 50/50 with between projects and tests.  Which if you don't do well is sort of hard to make up points.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Respected--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Tompkins is based

#1 choice for OS. Great, entertaining, accessible lectures. Very helpful in & out of class, loves when students ask questions. Easy exams if you pay attention to lecture. Your grade is weighted towards projects (unlike other profs) which is where youll learn the most. TA help this semester was chaotic, shoutout Enis for keeping things afloat.

Honestly, Tompkins is a great choice for 421. He's down to Earth and teaches you what is necessary. Multiple times he's just said "Eh, this is boring" and skipped slides. This would be a problem if his tests were hard, but they're really easy and open-note. The projects are the hardest part. Dedicate time to those.

Tompkins is a good professor, however in terms of his lectures he's mostly just reading off of slides. His tests went beyond the scope of the lectures but he allowed for a test to be dropped and gave free extra credit on two exams. 421 is a really disorganized class as TA's are completely in charge of projects which isn't Tompkin's fault

Tompkins makes this class enjoyable. This course is difficult. The TAs made the projects, Tompkins made exams. His exams were pretty straightforward and you could easily snag a B at least. These boost your grade. The projects are what make this class hard. Study, and start the projects EARLY.

Tompkins is great in lecture and does not make the class/exams any harder than they need to be. The only hard part about this class when taken with Tompkins are the projects, but they are still manageable if you actually put in a decent amount of time and effort. Hardest CS class in terms of projects
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Tompkins is a very caring and thoughtful professor. He makes the exams and homework very straightforward and no harder than they need to be. Questions are straight from the lectures so be sure to pay attention. Lectures are a bit dry but he tries to insert humor here and there. Projects aren't easy but not as hard as people make it out to be.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Respected--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Very easy-going professor. His office hours are always open for help and resume reviews. The projects can be challenging, but he provides resources. His lectures are interesting and he plays videos and does activities to teach some topics. Would definitely recommend.

Very nice professor. LEctures focus on fundamentals. Exams test those. He grades leniently. Projects are pretty hard but it is graded very easily. Got A in this compared to C in 341. Considering my projects were half broken and failing some tests and last minuted like in 341 the fact that I got A's instead of D's should tell you it's graded easy.

Prof. Tompkins is a great professor, his lectures are clear and easy to follow. He encourages you to ask questions and gives good feedback. If you attend all of his classes you will know what to expect from the exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--Hilarious

reviews.comment: He realized the projects are very challenging, so he does not make the lecture portion harder than it needs to be. One way or another, he covers every question that will be on the exam (when he says "that would make a good exam question" he never lies). Nicest guy, office hours are invaluable.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--Caring

reviews.comment: Attendance is not mandatory. But, if you miss many classes there are high chances of getting poor grades in the exam. He ask questions in class which will 99.99% be on midterm or final. Projects are tough start on the very first day. Homeworks are not that bad. Grading is fair enough. Tompkins should/must be your first choice for CMSC421.

Professor Tompkins is absolutely hands down the most amazing professor I have ever had. He cares about students and wants them to learn, rather than playing that points game like other professors do. He works in the industry so is straight forward in telling you what you need to know. Projects are super hard, but its OS. They all are.
reviews.rating_tags: ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Amazing lectures--Would take again

reviews.comment: Fantastic prof! His exams were relatively easy, especially if you go to class and pay attention. The projects will always be hard, but he does his best to help your grade (he doesn't make the projects). Extremely knowledgeable and incorporates cyber security into his class to make it more interesting! One of the best I've had at UMBC.

He would attend study groups on Sunday prior to exam week to help students study. Projects make you work for it, exams aren't that hard if you study for them. One of the best professors out there. Attendance is expected, but not mandatory.
Uses Pearsons for everything. No blackboard announcements and only announces in class. Attendance not mandatory but needed if you want a good grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The concepts were not difficult to understand because the lectures were well-presented. Always receptive to questions and made sure to explain homework problems. Grading is based primarily on "homework"-types of assignments and 3 big exams (final included). Attendance not mandatory but helps greatly. Textbook is important for understanding material
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Great lectures, the concepts were not that complicated that you would NEED to read the textbook before class. Although I would heavily recommend reading the textbook. Exams were kind of tough because there were only old practice exams, and you would just need to know the material. Attendance was not mandatory, although work would be due in lecture.

I have taken two classes with Professor Gindling this past year, ECON 102 and 387. I highly recommend him if you show up to class and pay attention, but if your lazy I do not recommend because you will fail badly without going to class. He is kind and forgiving(to a certain extent) and always has office hours especially during exam weeks. 9.5/10
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: He is a great professor and his in class lecture relate to the exams and also provides a very good study guide for them. The only issue is there are only two exams both 37% of your grade and are all free write. So you have to study hard on memorizing a lot of terms and essay questions. The other work/hw are weekly reports which are easy.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment:
I took ECON385 and was a TA for his econ102 class.

Very clear lecturer, good info, knows his stuff, overall a great econ prof!
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Professor Gindling was great! I enjoyed his lectures and found them helpful for the exams. Reviewing old exams he gives from past years for reference is also helpful for the exams. His teaching style and class setup are straightforward and clear. If you do the work and listen during lectures you will do good in his class.
the class will be easy if you attend the lectures, For exams just review the old exam and you will find multiple questions from the old exam in the exam.

His lectures can be boring but he's good at explaining. Information he goes over in lectures can be on the test, and old exam questions will pop up in the new exam. He's a nice prof, and it's easy to go to his office hours. I'd just say pay attention in lecture and you'll be fine.

Professor G knows his stuff when it comes to econ. Do not skip his class as it is very lecture heavy ad he hands out assignments on paper. The course materials are easy definitely takes some effort if its your first time taking econ. Lectures tend to get dry.
Class is EXTREMELY BORING. No interaction in class the guy just talks for the entire class period nonstop. He is very organized and grading is very clear. Problem sets are graded by attempt.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The class is basically a few weeks of lecture with a few homework assignments mixed in. Gindling makes the chapters interesting but the lectures tend to drag. We had 2 Exams, 6 Problem sets, and Online homework. Old exams are on his website which make for a great study guide. Grading is unclear... he doesn't use Blackboard like other professors.

It shows the professor was passionate about economics. the lectures could be dry at times, but if you pay attention, take notes, and read the textbook, the class is very easy. and he would often make jokes to make the lecture more entertaining. BTW he loves milky way bars.
reviews.rating_tags: ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: If you're interested in learning something new, this is the class to take. Dr. Gindling is also very passionate about his field. Unfortunately, he does not use blackboard and his grading is unclear and tough. Still, it's not a very difficult course. Grade is based on 2 exams, 6 brief essays, and "participation" (he just gives an A for that).

Lectures are interesting but the pacing is so slow it gets dry. The midterms and exams arent difficult as long as you attend classes and review notes. The averages are usually Bs. Hw is light and is either problem sets, which are graded for completion, or myeconlab, where you get many attempts.

He was pretty good and offered quite a few opportunities for office hours, especially with his multitude of TA. He is very knowledgeable and passionate. He does have a fascination with Milky Way Bars. He does have practice exams on his personal website. His website is a little weird and outdated however, I wish he just put it on black board.

Great guy. He is really passionate about Economics and that comes through in his lectures. He tries to keep the lectures as interesting and current as possible. He made the content easy to understand and was a fair grader. The old exams posted online REALLY help so study them.

This class isn't too easy to put it flat out. As long as you pay attention to the lectures or read the chapters you'll be fine. Go over the old exams he has on his website because his exams are close to his old ones with similar questions. He loves the topic and he explains it well. If your lost ask questions because he'll explain it. Great dude.

By far, one of the most valuable Economic professor out there! He is very intelligent, helpful, and clear. It might be hard to stay focused during the lectures, but don't miss out on his notes! You will need them for the exams. If you show up in class, participate, and take good notes, you will be fine. Come to him for you need advising too!

awesome prof, very helpful. I was preparing frantically for the class by reading the textbook because I thought I wouldn't do well without microeconomics. I was wrong. He makes everything easy for you so don't worry. Just pay attention cuz it gets boring sometimes, but other wise, he's an excellent professor!!!

If you attend his lectures then you don't have to buy a textbook! He's a really good professor. Cares a lot about his students. 3 Exams (2 Tests, and 1 Final). Final is cumulative. 6 Problem sets, he checks them for completion. 6 Online Quizzes. Use his previous exams uploaded on BlackBoard to study for the exams.Really helps! Milky way bars FTW!

really nice guy, fair, curves final grades, gives practice exams without answers but if you go to his office hours he's really nice and helpful. it's difficult to read his writing so sit towards the front. 6 quizzes and 6 problem sets (PS are graded for completeness)

Clear, Honest, intelligent, and patient. He cares a lot about his students. I changed my major to economics after hearing him explain economic principles using snicker bars. I have a very high respect for Prof. Gindling who is an outstanding teacher in my opinion.

He is a great teacher. Gives great examples on the material and ensures that you understand the material. 3 tests (last one is the final, cumulative) , 3 online quizzes, 6 problem sets (he just checks for completion not correctness).
Best teacher I have ever had in my 2 years that I've been here! He is very clear and makes the class so interesting. If you attend regularly and read over your notes, you'll do fine, A or B.

Awesome, two test, and a weekly one page paper.  Gives you an extensive review sheet before each exam.  Do the review properly, and you will get at least a B.  Very helpful if you go to his office with questions.
Really nice guy.  He always tries to answer questions no matter how stupid and obvious they are.  His lectures are all written on the board which I find extremely helpful.

Loved the professor! Loved his milky-way bar scenarios, loved how he went beyond the scope of the book to get his points across about current real-world issues. My only issue is my dyslexia with math, which is what kept me from doing as well as possible, but Gindling, you are hot because you know current events, and I find that sexy!

Seems to be a genuinely nice man. Exams are heavily based off of notes, problem sets, aplia questions, and past exams. Reasonable grading, and not my toughest class at all. I am an Econ major and feel like Gindling was a great choice for my Macro class.
He's nice and pretty cool, has a strong passion about Milkyway Bars, lol.
He is a cool dude.  He explains all the notes very well and even if you're still confused, he's very approachable, cool dude!
You will learn a lot and he's also very nice/confrontational. He can be little picky with the grading though.
Boring class, but he tried to make it interesting.  His exams were a little tough and his grading seemed a little picky.  3 exams worth 30, 30, ad 34% with 6 homework problem sets each worth 1%.

Great professor + lecturer. Highly knowledgeable. Very boring material, but his lectures were clear and concise, and I had no problems staying awake. My tip: come to class everyday, and you'll never have to read the book. He nails home in 5 minutes, topics that would take you half an hour to read and understand on your own. Easy exams.

Took the Macro Class. Impossible to get less than a C. Attendance is not mandatory but he does go over alot in class. He gives out problem sets once in a while Which are super easy. Good Teacher. Very Boring material.

I loved the class, it was very interesting.  It's also easy if you pay attention and do the work.  I actually enjoyed the class so much I looked into getting an econ minor, but calc is a prereq for the upper level classes, so that isnt going to happen.  Also, they say you should take Micro before macro, but I didnt and had no problems getting an A.
i dont think he knows it, but he is hot.  sorry if i was staring but he looks good.  and the reviews that say he is boring - they are wrong.

soooo bad....... he teaches you what the textbook says, so just dont waste ur time goin to class, just read.  oh and did i mention that he is probably the most boring person on this planet.  his class is actually naptime, not econ. overall not that hot....

EXTREMEMLY BORING! I don't normally fall asleep in class, but I did in his - and I was sitting in the front too! Relatively easy class - if you can stay awake during his lectures, you don't need to read the book, otherwise read the book. Hands out a few easy problem sets also.

His exams are straight-forward and pretty much come straight out of his practice quizzes and lectures. I know many people who never showed up to class and did fairly well, but he does cover material that is not found in the book. He has done extensive research and is very knowledgable about economic

He is a great teacher... I can't wait to take him again.  His class can be a little boring, but they help A LOT. His tests are not bad either, they are usually the same format as previous exams which he does give you. : )
Had a hard time staying awake, but the material itself is not exciting. Exams are alright, nothing tricky.  Provides previous exams for study which are very helpfull.
Mr. Gindling is so sweet! He is very understanding and he always explains everything! His tests are kind of hard but if you pay attention, you will do very well!
GREAT TEACHER! NO BOOK READING IF YOU GO TO CLASS!
Get on his good side early
No Comments
very good professor.  does not require too much book reading if you go to class.

Professor McCann's class was pretty easy; he's also very understanding. You just have to make sure to stay on top of your work, show up to class on time because he does take attendance. There are a lot of essays, but if you manage your time properly, you will be okay.
Very great professor! He is very sweet and understanding! Grading is taken lightly. Just make sure to do your work and you will have an easy A!

This proffessor was very accomadating, and allowed for a lot of creative liberty. The projects and problems we had to solve were thought provoking, and gave us a basic understanding of english concepts. For a STEM major just looking to knock out an english credit this is the one.

Professor McCann is really accommodating and understanding, especially if english isnt your best subject. Its a fairly basic class in terms of english composition material, so its not too challenging. There is a lot of activities in class and two essays, but its nothing to worry about if you took english in high school or before.

He is a very mellow, and laid back guy who does care, usually sending an email after class saying thanks and what due next class. Class can be a bit boring at times but later in the semester he did more interesting activity's He's a very light grade and so long as you try and communicate with him this class will be an easy A.

He was a pretty mellow and easy-going guy from my experience. There are about 3 essays, but he makes sure you're prepared and ready to write them smoothly. I'd take him again. Make sure you participate.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Boring highschool- like class. You won't learn anything, but if you do the assignments you will get an A. If you came to class and want to learn something about writing or english, change professors. Class will be random and boring. He is a pretty weird guy who does not follow lesson plans. If you have basic writing skills you can get an A.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--So many papers

reviews.comment: Very good, humorous, easy to understand, and thorough lectures, as well as manageable homework assignments and projects and lab assignments.

It wasn't until I took other classes later on at UMBC until I realized how good Professor Gibson actually is. Her slides are well structured and easy to learn from. Projects were super fun, although I didn't enjoy having multiple VMs open on a low RAM machine. Still, definitely learnt a lot and would recommend taking her (she left though..)

I don't recall a single class I've taken with Gibson that wasn't informative, entertaining, and overall understandable and worth the time. For some lectures, you feel as if you're not learning or that the lesson is not applicable in the real world. I felt that each lecture was worth the while and the tidbits of extra knowledge was appreciated.
Dr. Gibson is a professor that truly connects with her students. I took her for 201 and now again for 426 and she did not disappoint. She makes learning fun. One of the best professors I've ever had.

Gibson was great, the class is to teach algorithmic thinking. Exams are difficult. Practice. Do HW. GO TO OFFICE HOURS. Even with exp, Ican't this stress enough. However I thought the final was extremely difficult, asking questions on topics mentioned only brief at the start of the sem but never practically applied during class. Felt a bit sneaky.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Dr. Gibson is an amazing professor with hilarious lectures. I loved this class because of her. The only downside was the toughness of homework/projects. But otherwise this class was great and Dr. Gibson was better. :)

Professor Gibson is truly an amazing professor. Having just switched my major to Cs with no prior programming experience, I was a bit overwhelmed at first. However, Professor Gibson made the class really fun which made me enjoy learning. Her lectures are like a stand-up comedy show sometimes. Just make sure you start your projects early.

If you want a good start on being a comp sci major take her!!. Shes interactive and she explains everything you need. Relates work to real life, and answers all your questions. Very animated and fun. She loves dogs, so everything you learn will be somewhat dog based. Homework is not based off her, its based off the whole CMSC Department.

Rude and Condescending - verbally and in writing. Teaches by reading strictly off slides. Youll get better help from TAs. Two exams are half your grade, which would be fine if grading overall wasn't extremely unforgivable and study guides/review sessions actually gave decent material and ANSWERS. Good luck finishing exams comfortably and on time.
One of the best professors I've ever had. She makes the lectures very entertaining and engages the entire class. Has office hours for extra help and is always enthusiastic about teaching.

She's a really great professor. She genuinely cares about students, and she's really helpful. This is an intro to coding course, so she's a little strict about coding standards, but there's no busy work and everything we do in class has a purpose. She LOVES dogs!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Amazing lady, she teaches you about computer science in all the ways imaginable. Loved her class. But the subject is rigorous. The projects will trip you up if you aren't careful. And the midterm and final are the big grade sinkers, so STUDY WELL AND HARD.

Very Good, Funny, understanding. A lot, A lot of HW but then again it is a comp sci class. Two tests count for almost half your grade so study for those. Lectures are important so you can ask questions but she honestly just kind of read off the slides. She also loves dogs>
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Tests are tough--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Dr. Gibson is a great teacher and explains concepts in depth. She is a great teacher for students who have never coded before because her lectures are detailed. The class is challenging but the professor is very helpful.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Professor Gibson is the best teacher I have ever had, hands down. Her lectures are very funny and engaging. This is the best course possible for someone new to Computer Science, but if you're already experienced, then you probably won't get much out of it. The homework and project assignments are long, but very doable if you get started early.

She's a good lecturer. She makes lecture funny and actually engages with students. But, she's not a good teacher. She just reads off the powerpoints, there's literally no point in going to lecture. The class itself is actually challenging. The homeworks are long and challenging, they are graded hard and the projects are challenging too.

Dr. Gibson teaches the material in a way that is very engaging and informative and she genuinely cares about her students. I cannot recommend her enough. I would advise students to start working on projects early, especially the last one. As long as you come to class and discussion and do all your assignments, it should be a relatively easy A.

Professor Gibson is a great teacher, her lectures are simple enough to understand the content at a good level. She starts off with the basics and and uses many examples so you don't get lost. She loves to answer questions, a hard thing to find in professors these days.
shes cool
By far, she is most entertaining, engaging, and efficient teacher I have taken a course with. I definitely encourage taking a class with her if possible.

I LOVED Gibson. She is one of my favorite professors that I've had. She consistently makes sure that students are engaged during lecture and she is actually concerned if no one understands whats going. If she sees lost faces, she will stop lecture and ask if everyone understands what's going on. Overall, she did a great job at explaining content

Amazing professor. Definitely able to connect with our level of expertise in the field. Doable class whether or not you have prior programming experience. Homework can get challenging in the later half of the semester, so be prepared to allot some time. Also, be prepared for dogs. She loves dogs, and it shows in the multitude of examples she gives.

I don't know why I found her assignments really tough, but conceptually wise, she was very approachable and would always answer questions. However, during lectures, she bases her livecoding samples off dogs too much. Otherwise, she was awesome.
Very enjoyable course. There for you if you need help. I would really recommend her.
Best teacher I've had yet at UMBC.  Only problem, while she is the one teaching and creating the tests, she is not the one creating the projects.
Easily the best prof at UMBC if you are considering computer science as your major take Dr Gibson for as many classes as possible

Dr. Gibson IS THE BEST!! Her lectures are entertaining, and she covers the material perfectly. I always tried to drag my friends along just to show them how cool she is. The class is easy, so if you show up, and pay attention, and do all the assignment, anyone can get an A. (Also, don't buy the book. And I always buy the book.)
Fun, knowledgeable, and great. I only wish she was the one actually creating the course material, projects in this class are very hard.
Very enthusiastic, strong grasp of the material, and overall very entertaining. Loves dogs.

I can't count the number of times I've come back from lecture with Gibson and told my friends that she is my favorite professor I've ever had. She is super engaging and lectures are fairly interactive and she explains everything very well.   Also, if you like dogs then you'll enjoy Professor Gibson.
She's very enthusiastic, has a strong grasp of the subject matter, and knows how to teach it. Eager to help too. Talks about dogs all the time, and uses dogs in examples.

As someone who already had a lot of experience in CS coming into college, I worried that this class would be boring. Gibson literally managed to make any redundant topic fun and very interactive with 'LIVE CODING!'. She is just as educational and she is entertaining (which is saying a lot). Also read her paper! Excited for CMSC 202 with her!

Ms Gibson is a good instructor, but the feedback at the end of the semester was very poor.  The scores for final homeworks, labs, project, and the final itself, were not posted until weeks after the semester ended.
The best teacher I have ever had.
If she was my professor for all of my classes, I would probably have a 4.0 GPA now.

I skipped lectures alot in this class, never had any coding experience before but i learned the most from TAs and the professor during office hours. She is very helpful and when available explain any questions you have very well. IF YOU ARE STRUGGLING GO TO THE COMP SCI LAB I ITE!!!!!!!!!! WILL MAKE A HUGE DIFFERANCE

Super enthusiastic and clearly loves what she teaches. She's fun to listen to and be around and she makes going to class pretty fun. Lots of labs and homeworks but her office hours or "party hours" means help is available. Love this woman and cannot recommend highly enough!

Really great lady and really good at lecturing. The work itself is somewhat difficult as the curriculum assigns a ton of homework and labs. Gibson is great with helping students understand topics so make sure you're there in class to follow what she has to say. If you don't follow coding standards used in class you will fail.

After taking Beck's class, I'm sure most of the bad reviews are due to people advertising the class as an "easy A". Three exams make your whole grade for the semester, which are VERY easy ONLY if you spend a few hours memorizing the terms on Quizlet. While the content itself is easy, I wouldn't call it an "easy A" due to the time spent studying.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Gina Beck is the most putrid, nauseating, imbecilic sorry excuse for a music "professor" at UMBC. Her teaching is incredibly ineffective and she lacks basic empathy.

reviews.comment: what was supposed to be an easy A culture credit turned out to be so sucky. wish i never took this class . disappointing professor, disappointing lectures, disappointing everything

reviews.comment: Taking this class is something I regret. So much work for a 3 credit 200 level music class. The question sets have to be THOROUGH and extensive, otherwise you will get a failing grade. The exams ask you to recall VERY specific details of these cultures, and it is not open book. Do not take this class for a culture credit. She's not very nice.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Literally the worst culture credit available at UMBC. Don't take. Horrible professor. Useless character. Awful teaching. Cruel responses. Hands down the worst instructor that I have ever encountered at UMBC. Do not waste your time with this terrible excuse for a human being. She will never amount to anything and life will never be kind to her.

This class is not an easy class to makeup a few credits. If its not required for your major dont take it. Its very paper and test heavy. You are required to remember very obscure instruments and people by heart then have an opinion on them. Truth is, this class has made me think of music as stressful. That shouldnt be.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--So many papers

reviews.comment: She is very friendly and hard to get on the bad side of. Her teaching is a bit canned, but you learn a lot from it if you take notes. She brings out real instruments and lets you play them.

She was a great professor. Her class is very interesting and it is also very easy. Just be sure you go to every class to take down the notes. You don't need to study at all. Just go to her office an hour before the exam and she gives you a great review.

I was so excited to take this class when I came to UMBC, but it turned out to be such a disappointment. The class is basically one big lecture and the tests are based solely on an incomprehensible amount of vocabulary combined with essays on the history of world music. I was sick of this class three weeks into the semester. Find another AH/C class.
Nice professor! She really knows her stuff and very dedicated. The Test are pretty average if you attend every class and take good notes than you should be fine.
Really great professor. She encourages self-exploration and will meet with you if you need help (even on weekends). She's a fair grader. Really interesting class. Learned a lot

she is amazing, tons of assignments and discussions but it is expected for a 600 level class, she give tons of feed back in the after action report and she work a lot with us to make sure everyone succeed. the hardest and the best class that i took so far 
I would take her again
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Very fair. Answers you within hours usually.  Great lectures.
She is a professor that really cares about her students. Gives good feedback on labs and discussions. Gives extensions on labs so that students can learn the concepts.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring

reviews.comment: He is a wonderful teacher who truly cares about the thoughts and opinions of his students. Often plays music as students are coming in and loves to have open discussions. We did group presentations every week and fun exercises at the end of class. Outstanding Professor Overall!

Gib is one of the best professors you'll ever have here at UMBC. Really knowledgeable about everything dealing with business and entrepreneurship. He won't hand you all the answers though, you gotta figure out that part on your own. His classes are only difficult for those who don't have trust in themselves and their work. I learned a lot from him.

Gib Mason is one of the greatest people I have ever had the chance to meet. He is a very knowledgeable and caring professor. He makes it easy for you to succeed in his class but prioritizes your learning and growth as entrepreneurs and also as students. He helped me become a much more confident communicator and presenter in just one semester.

Passionate/brilliant/excellent teacher. 1st 2 semesters I studied w/her mostly spent chain-smoking/talking but it was what I needed & totally worth it. +A+ memories. Philosopher & musician. Caring, open, intelligent. Approaches each student individually with great insight into their psyche & into music. Cannot recommend her strongly enough.
Lessons with Gita make my day! She is so positive and has so much experience as a cellist in performance throughout the world.
No Comments

Gita is one of the best teachers there is. She is passionate about music, an amazing and experienced cellist, and she is wonderful at relaying techniques. She is kind and understanding, and wants the student to get the most out of the lessons she teaches. I have only ever heard good things about her.

Gibson is a true historian. His passion of legal history come across in his lectures. He requires outside research that prepares you for in-class discussion. He is humorous and make sure each class is engaging and informative. Gibson is a pillar of the UMB community and is a great person to know.
honestly, the worst class i've taken in my life.  the fact that the school still employs him makes me embarrassed to say that i have graduated from there

Professor Gibson is a warmhearted man who cares about his students.  He is a great person.  Unfortunately, he asks questions without giving answers.  The book we use asks questions without giving answers as well. Don't expect help from either.  You're going to have to pick up a supplement for this one.

Easily one of the best professors at UMBC. It's one thing to know the content, it's another thing entirely to know how to teach; she understands students like no one else. She made a year of orgo so easy to where I questioned why anyone found it hard at all. I hope my future professors can compare to just how incredible she is.

Gierasch is a fantastic lecturer and an inspiring chemist. Her lectures are informative, and she gives you all the tools to succeed. Do all the work before class, come to class with questions and a good foundation, and keep practicing as much as possible until the exam. Learn the content instead of the exam and you will appreciate Orgo even more!

reviews.comment: Everyone knows Orgo is hard, but I went into the class thinking it would be the class that ruined my GPA. Dr. Gierasch made Orgo easy to understand and so interesting that it quickly became my favorite class at UMBC. Highly Recommend. 10/10

Orgo is a very difficult class; she made it so easy for me to understand and digest the material. You could see peoples' faces in lecture light up as they started to understand what she was saying. Just reading the textbook is numbing, please make sure to go to lecture. Her teaching style makes this class so much easier.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Pleasant lecturer who cares about students. Encourages setting time aside for HW, reading, and practice problems. Grades rely heavily on exams. Videos are manageable, and she uses tech well. Lectures focus more on examples than on new content. Start using flashcards early, as the material is cumulative. Must keep up with all material consistently.

I learned solely form the textbook. The lectures were all review she didn't even teach anything. Her personality one on one is unnecessarily rude. Just bc your a prof doesn't give you the right to be stuck up. Mark perks is the same if not worse but comparitvielt she's not as horrible at teaching as him

You learn solely form the textbook and her videos on blackboard are useless and so difficult to understand. Lectures are just review questions. 0/10 would not recommend bc it's all self study but she's better than mark perks

Dr. Gierasch was a very nice/friendly person and made a challenging class a little less intimidating. I learned mostly from the textbook though, which were required before each class and then the lectures just ended up being in class questions/polls which didn't really teach us much. Exams were pretty tough too.

reviews.comment: Prof. Gierasch makes organic chemistry more manageable. Her lectures are engaging, but the class is still challenging. Using resources like the textbook, Khan Academy, and unstuck ai really helped me grasp the material.

Had her for orgo 1&2. The amount of work you put in reflects your grade. If you read the textbook carefully and understand the concepts, the exams aren't bad. Sometimes couldn't follow her logic during lectures but would go back and review all questions covered in class, after reading the textbook. Understand the chemistry instead of memorizing!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Test heavy

reviews.comment: I had Dr. Gierasch in 2013 for Organic chemistry 1. She was an interesting professor. She is nice; however, I feel as if her class is a bit deceptive. I remember our second exam well. Everyone did well, the class average was a 78% percent. She was not happy about that. So much so that our third exam was unreasonably difficult.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: The class was split between Prof Gierasch and Prof Perks. Her lectures were definitely better and made the problems easier to understand. However, this class in itself is challenging and she would often lecture us about not knowing the material after the average for an exam was in the 60s. Good luck!

Dr. Gierasch co-taught with Dr. Perks and she was much more thorough and creative in the way she presented the material so you can actually understand it. You have to be able to sit down for a long period of time and do a ton of practice questions to fully understand what you are learning because studying for Orgo is not the same as gen chem.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I loved taking both Orgo 1 and Orgo 2 with her. She explained things really well and made clear what the expectations were going into the course.
