reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: After taking orgo 1 with her, I thought this class would be easy. However, the exams are 80% of your total grade and there are 3 exams with ACS (orgo 1 + orgo 2 combined) final, not made by Gierasch. It only takes 2-3 wrong multiple choice on an exam to drop down to B. I would suggest to not take any other 300-400 level class along with this.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I had her for both Chem 351 and 352. She is super nice and available for one on one help all the time. Her exams are pretty reasonable. My biggest issue is most of the class is learning on your own and then coming to lecture for review of materials. She explains things well and enjoys teaching chemistry!
Dr. Gierasch co-taught Organic Chemistry I with Dr. Perks. She was a much better lecturer than Dr. Perks. She made the material digestible, which was nice.

Super dynamic and energetic lectures. Very helpful and friendly in answering questions. Makes organic chemistry much more approachable. You definitely need to keep up with the course, but then it flows really well.

She's not the worst at teaching orgo. I learned mostly from the textbook and Kahn academy, however. I've heard she can be rude to students but she seems pretty nice. She's available to answer questions.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Did not learn a lot from the class and you have to keep up in general with orgo. Exams were very hard so make sure to understand the concepts

Personally the WORST prof I have ever had here and single handedly killed any joy for chem. Doesn't teach jack and just does clickers the entire class 3 days a week instead of teaching content. Also refuses to acknowledge that her lack of teaching is the reason majority of her class is borderline failing. She was also extremely condescending.

She was my anchor even though I failed. I took her with Perks and Gierasch is so sweet and made up for all I didn't understand with him. Retook the class with just Perks but still watched her linked videos because she makes sense. Really makes an effort to know students and is accessible outside of class. Class is hard, but she helps make it better

If you get the chance, take orgo with Dr. Gierasch. She genuinely cares about her students and the class. The class will be difficult but that is to be expected anywhere cause it's orgo. Be prepared to read the textbook and do a bunch of practice problems.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Caring--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Dr. Gierasch is the best professor I've had the pleasure of learn from. She gives good lectures and assigns work that keeps you practicing. Orgo 1 isn't very hard as long as you make sure you understand the practice exams. She also takes student feedback seriously and will implement it mid semester. Class was really fun and I wish I took it sooner.

I had Dr Gierasch for CHEM 351 and 352. She is an amazing professor who knows her stuff and genuinely wants her students to succeed. If you ever need more individualized help, she has weekly office hours which are super helpful. Success in Orgo comes from doing your own practice. If you consistently put in your own work/time, you'll be successful

Prof Giearasch was very nice and taught/ explained well, unlike Perks. This class is probably the hardest I have taken at UMBC so far.

Gierasch might seem rigid, but the point is to make sure that we really understand the material. I can for sure say that the depth of my knowledge in chemistry has certainly increased after this semester. Drops homework, ICAs, and PCAs. reviews.comment: B in 351 and an A in 352. Her classes are structure amazingly. Maybe it's because chem 101 and chem 102 got me accustomed to this style of learning, but I would learn things almost immediately in this class. reviews.comment: Love her to death!! Best prof on campus!! :)

Do NOT take over summer unless you are mentally and physically ready to work on orgo everyday and use up all your weekends for 6 weeks. Lot of info in little time. Tests were ok. One of my favorite professors, hands down. Dr. G makes it easy for those who follow her advice. reviews.comment: The other reviews are mostly reflective of my experience. A pretty good professor overall. Exams are fair, MC is very difficult but FR is easy. reviews.comment: Dr. Gierasch is by far the best teacher I've had at UMBC and probably my school career. If you actually read before class and pay attention to her lectures, it'll be a swift, if not, you can still get an A ( i read once b4 class)

The fact that Dr. Gierasch has such a high rating for such a hard class should speak to her efficacy as a teacher. In class she works through problems very logically, then helps you do harder and harder problems by applying the same basic principles. Out of class the book is very good. Exams can be hard, but a good work ethic will see you through.

reviews.comment: Gierasch is an amazing professor! You can tell she really cares about her students and wants everyone to succeed. Tests are fair and homework/clickers are almost free points if you put in the work.

reviews.comment: Great professor. She does an exceptional job at making organic chemistry somewhat enjoyable, and she cares about the success of her students. She provides the pieces necessary to succeed, but it's your job to put them together. Work smart and work hard to get an A in her class.

I don't write reviews often, and I rarely give 5's, but Dr. Gierasch deserves it. Organic chemistry will always be a difficult class, so you need a professor who is organized, experienced, and fair. Her class was the most well organized and balanced of any STEM course I have taken.

Your final grade is made up of 3 components: Pre-Class Assignments (PCA), In-Class Clicker Questions, and Exams. The PCAs are only 3 questions that you complete on Blackboard. You get 2 chances, so your PCA overall grade shouldn't be bad. Plus, she drops the 4 lowest PCA grades. For the in-class clickers, you can work with people.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Respected--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: She is the best orgo professor at UMBC. Smith's exams are all free response and perks exams are written weird. Go to lecture, she gives a good idea of what is going to be the free response. for the MC do a lot of book problems

reviews.comment: Gierasch is a much more lenient professor than Perks. Perks adds random difficult questions that look like they came from a 50s typewriter. Having Gierasch for 352 was a blessing. Her exams are challenging, but she gives you reading guides, learning objectives, practice exams, and partial credit. She is really sweet, and great at teaching.

Boy, did Gierasch and Perks try to ruin Orgo 1 for a lot of people. The lectures were decent, but the exams were quite difficult, and by far the largest portion of the grade. The average for 3 out of 4 of the exams was 68-69%. That low an average does not speak well to the exams' fairness. My advice: take orgo elsewhere and transfer the credits.

reviews.comment: She kinda hands you off to the TAs or assistane. This class isnt hard. Its the TEST. they make it very dificult. Honestly, I would get some things right because I KNEW they were trying to trick me. So I would pick what I wouldve never guessed..

Though many stem professors at UMBC are proficient, Dr. Gierasch really knows her stuff. She implements well her knowledge of the material in a way that is exciting and easy to understand. reviews.comment: Dr. Gierasch is very nice! Everything in the syllabus is clear and executed well. Orgo is hard, but she makes the lectures interesting. She answers emails in a timely manner and is very approachable. She is a fair grader.
SHE IS DA BEST, literally. You cannot find a better, more knowledgeable, caring and funny chem professor than her. She is everything 3
She is the best chemistry professor ever. Though I am struggling through the course, she has helped me and worked with me so the experience is less painful. TAKE HER FOR ORGO I and ORGO II.

reviews.comment: Dr. Gierasch has helped me out countless times. I don't even think I'll have my current love for chemistry if it wasn't for her Orgo I & II classes. The passion tho!

reviews.comment: As an instructor in Organic Chemistry, Dr. Gierasch is super hot!!  She is smooth, smart, calm, patient, and a highly skilled teacher, while also making one work hard for one's grade.  She is an ideal professor to teach this course! She does not seem to be getting enough recognition as other instructors  in the department who are really not as good

Dr. Gierasch is really inspirational, nice, and always willing to help you-pushes you to work hard!  Lectures are mainly clickers, so get yourself into a study group. Exams were really tough (mult choice + free resp), so don't wait until the day before to start cramming. Had to memorize around 20-30 different reagents used for synthesis per exam.
Excellent but hard professor.  Makes you work hard and earn your grade.

By far the best chemistry professor I have had at UMBC and elsewhere!  Love to see her teach a senior or graduate level course, and I shall be the first one to seek admission into her class!  She is thorough, tough, and fair. She is an asset to UMBC!
She is very nice and willing to help. Her exams are pretty difficult and organic chemistry is already a pretty difficult concept. Helps you try and learn ways you'll remember.

Very helpful and patient to explain things. She really wants people to do well. She puts a lot of time into her lectures and models, and ochem was actually kind of interesting thanks to her. Would take again (except it was pretty hard).

She's the best lecturer. Very funny and enthusiastic about her job, makes everyone like the subject; even though, orgo gets challenging sometimes. I loved her classes. Definitely one of the best profs.
Amazing professor! She's so passionate about chemistry and makes me more eagar to study organic chemistry!!!
I LOVE HER! SHE IS SO FUNNY AND AMAZING PROFESSOR!!!!!!!!!!!!!!
Great professor by any standard.

Wow! She knows the material very well. Honored to be her student. She is way too much for UMBC. I loved her class. Whatever she taught and assigned to read is on the exam. If you pay attention and study, you will get a good grade.

Dr. Gierasch cares about both the subject matter and her students. Her lectures are helpful as long as you read the book ahead of time. She is very willing to help students that are struggling and she is often in the Chemistry Tutorial Center. Make sure you go to lecture and form a study group!

Organic Chem. with Dr. Gierasch isn't easy but she does everything to make it easier. There is a tutorial center to help outside of class and if you read and keep up with the pre-class assignments you will do fine. Definitely not an easy class but if you put in the time you'll get an A.
Simply amazing! Passionate, fun, understandable, knowledgeable, and cute.

Felt in love with orgo when I took her. The best professor ever. Attend class, take notes, do problems from the back of the book and you should be fine. The exams are fair and not that difficult. She is very helpful.

Very enthusiastic,  passionate, and extremely knowledgeable; actually makes you want to learn Orgo (you can tell she 3 Orgo). Office hours were helpful. Class is all clickers and her going over them; no "official" lecturing. This class will require a lot of time outside class. Exams were extremely difficult and detail oriented.
she is very good. try to take her if you can.

Take her! There is no other professor that teaches orgo like her at UMBC. I took orgo 1 with perks and ended up not learning the fundamentals. It is just I didn't like the way perks teaches. However, Dr. Gierasch has different style of teaching. To do well in her class, study everyday and REMEMBER, pay attention to the DISCUSSION QUESTIONS!

I fell in love with Orgo after taking her class and I'm a Math Major! That being said; her exams are not easy and you need to prepare at least a good 3 days before each exam. Got to her for help and practice, practice, practice! She's the best person for the job!
If you are a student who cram one day before the exam, you will be history! Dr. Gierasch is truly the best professor I have ever had during my college years.

Dr. Gierasch is a really good teacher, she is very knowledgeable about organic chemistry. She requires A LOT of out of class work, which is fine by me. The one thing I found is that some times she can be very condescending and that can be a turn off in her class. Her curves are max 2% in general.

Dr. Gierasch is a really good teacher, she is very knowledgeable about organic chemistry. She requires A LOT of out of class work, which is fine by me. The one thing I found is that some times she can be very condescending and that can be a turn off in her class. In my opinion, Dr. Perks is more approachable. Her curves are max 2% in general.
She is the best!

I personally don't mind Orgo as a subject. and Gierasch is a good teacher. But this was difficult. I had a lot going on the first exam, got a C. Then, had a 93% going into third exam and after the final ended up with an %82. she gives lots extra credit but doesn't compensate. I'm a straight A student but first time in my life I was pleased with a B

This professor is not for everyone. Her class requires dozens of hours of work each week and a level of understanding that most students just don't have. Her exams are really tough, there is no curve, and she expects a lot. That being said, she is passionate and knowledgeable about organic chemistry. Most people get a C.

Impossible exams, and nothing relates to the lecture. Her lectures are very clear, and she makes you actually understand; however, she tricks you in the exam so much that it makes it impossible. you might be prepared to retake the class but an A or B is impossible to get.

I really respect Dr. Gierasch since she perfectly teaches her class the real organic chemistry. Only one complaint however is that She should have never allowed other professors to cover the spectroscopy section which was on exam one. That killed most of the students chance of getting an "A" including me. So heart braking and SAD.

Dr. Gierasch is an excellent liaison between the textbook and the students. Be sure to do all of the in/end of chapter problems! Be sure to go to the chem tutorial center for help, or office hours. Exams are hard; however, they can be easy when you over-prepare, starting about a week out from the exam. Final exams are ACS. Curve was 1-1.5%, 3% MAX.

I had another lady professor for CHEM351, who often boasted about herself and some fellowship she got from Govt. She skipped all difficult topics, e.g.  atomic & molecular orbital theory. I took Dr. Gierasch for CHEM352, and what a difference it was! Although she was much harder, but very helpful and fair. Wish I had Gierasch for CHEM351 as well!
Phenomenal Professor! She beats every other professor hands down in teaching this course!! It is a privilege and honor to be in her class!

I had Dr. Gierasch for both 351 and 352, and I cannot say enough good things about her!  She is friendly, approachable, and has a passion for what she does.  She is incredibly helpful and will do anything she can to help you as long as you meet her halfway.  Her tests are incredibly hard though, so be prepared to work for your grade.

Dr. Gierasch is a fantastic teacher! She is extremely organized, helfpul, and fair. Her passion for chemistry is contagious, and her enthusium for teaching really makes her approachable and helps make the material much easier to understand. If you have to take orgo, take it with her. One of the best professors I've encountered at UMBC!
She is a really good teacher, she made orgo actually interesting even though I had no prior interest in the subject. Study hard the tests aren't easy but she doesn't try to trick you either.

After her classes, I LOVE organic chemistry. Most people got D's on exams, but I always got A's. Go in with a good attitude and you will see that organic chemistry is BEAUTIFUL! Dr. Gierasch is really enthusiastic and SO nice. These were my favorite classes I have ever taken. If you had Carpenter for 101/102, Gierasch is really similar, but better.

I love classes that are rigorous to a certain extent. She's literally a professor that expects you to be on your A game every class, let alone exam days. She tests concepts that aren't specific to the chapters being tested! Other than her class bringing down your GPA (as most get Cs), she does know a lot-and expects the same. Take with someone else

Can't do her justice in this textbox. Strives to know any of her students that approach her or volunteer an answer. Not only is she brilliant in chemistry, she is brilliant in knowing how students absorb the material, can't overstate that. This makes her literally one of the best professors out there, and certainly the best I've had in all my years

That woman is a force of nature. She's full of energy, obsessed with Orgo, and speaks chemistry like it's her first language. If you're thinking about taking Orgo, you know you're in for a world of hurt, but she presents the material in a way that's easy to process. This course is a greater challenge for your work ethic than your mental ability.

One of the best science professors in general. I honestly believe she makes organic chemistry seem like the easiest thing ever. Her tests might not be EASY, but they are by no means over-the-top. Plus, as long as you pay attention in class, that is what you will see on the test. A really great chemistry teacher!!
Best Organic Chemistry Teacher there is. You definitely need to work very hard but she is a great teacher and has an extremely organized class.
You will definitely need to put time into the class, its really as hard as you make it. The book is your key to understanding everything. Khan Academy is useful too.

if you read before class,ask questions, memorize/study the material every week, and do lots of practice problems, you can do well. the problem is that that is not practical. its hard to do well in this class because there is way too little time for the tests, and it makes it very hard to show your understanding. its sad b/c the material isnt hard..

Showed me that Orgo gets a bad rap and isn't as hard as people make it seem. If you put in the work and know your stuff, it really pays off. Gierasch pulls some tricks sometimes but it helped me. She has a great attitude about class, is genuinely concerned about how students are learning, and tries to make it as easy as possible. Def recommended!
This Prof is extrememly hard!!! Class test average was a 60% and she would not curve.  Very little extra credit.  Her exams were 60% multiple choice ( a lot of trick questions) and 40% free response.

One of the best professors I've ever had, I hated general chemistry and basically failed 102, but Gierasch turned that all around with an upbeat attitude and energy, its like she transfers the energy onto you. Easy B, exams are EASY if you study, I was shocked, made me realize how smart I am and how much potential I have.

Professor Gierasch is far by the best professor I've had so far at UMBC (third year student). She explains the material very thoroughly. She's full of energy and is genuinely passionate about what she teaches, which makes learning all the more easier. Exams are not easy, but if you do the assigned textbook problems and go to class, you can get a C

Difficult exams but she does give you a learning objective sheet so at least you're guided. Clicker questions are really important! Overall, I think she's one of the best chemistry teachers I've had so far. She's very smart -- went to Harvard!

Go to class, clicker points count.Don't cheat,she will catch you.She is nice,go to her and tutor asap.Read book. Do practice book problems she assigns.Do ACE Organic earlier than day before it's due.Do practice exams.

Definitely read the chapters and take notes on them to understand what you are doing. She kind of expects you to read ahead, and ofcourse no one does, but make sure you take notes in class and review, since she picks up certain points from the chapter that she would test you on specifically. Overall she is quite nice and peppy.

Dr. Gierasch is very smart.  Went to Harvard and is very willing to help.  She wants to make sure you really understand the material. She also is careful to not criticize when you get the answer wrong and that's important when actively learning.

Attendance thru clickers which cushion the grade, yes, BUT does not tolerate malfunctions which hurt my grade and it wasnt my fault.Exams are 60% MC which is not helpful. My advice seek her attention and help early on bc later in semester shes a bit rude to students. NEVER question her tests or time given for them. she gets snappy.

If you must take Orgo II, take it with Gierasch. She is extremely approachable, her lectures are crystal clear, and she provides you with plenty of grade cushion and extra credit opportunities. Her tests were hard---after all, its orgo---but they were fair. Nicest prof. at UMBC, and I am not a fan of orgo.
Gierash was more clearer than Perks but at times she would get confused or mess up on a problem. Go to to her office hours or the chem tutorial center and you'll do find in the class

Dr. Gierasch is very easy and understandable professor and she tries to help out students as much as she can even outside of her office hours as long as you put your efforts into it, I don't think this class is hard at all. Although exams are sometime contains 2-3 tricky questions, if you think about it, you will get it.

Class requires work, but that should go without saying. Dr. G makes it a lot easier, consider yourself lucky if you get to take this class with her instead of other professors. Very helpful, you ace exams if you PUT THE WORK IN, which most people don't want to do. She made me want to minor in chemistry (which I'm now doing).

She is the best professor I ever took at UMBC. I wish she can teach all my chemistry related classes throughout my entire college career. She is definitely good at explaining and her lecture is very friendly and interactive. As long as you print out all the prenotes before class and take notes+do wileyplus ungraded hw, you'll ace the class for sure
Tries to explain thinks in lecture.

Useless professor.  Can't teach straight and consistently messes up equations in lecture then says you can figure it out on your own.  Tests contain material not covered or conveniently skipped over.  Practice exams ~2-3 times easier than actual exam.  Highly inconsiderate and even rude to non-chemistry majors.
Tough teacher but explains very well. Tests sometimes have concepts that are not exactly gone over in class. Exam average for one exam was a 54% hahaha...

She is definitely 'better than average' professor. She is very willing to help students even when students come to see her outside of her office hour schedule. Lectures, however, a little boring and monotonous.
She is one of the best teachers for orgo. She is clear and tells you what you need to know. She doesn't make it unnecessarily hard but its orgo so its going to be a little bit hard.

She's awesome! I expected a difficult class but she made orgo so easy to understand! Exams are straight fwd and have a free response section too! She knows what she's talking about and can explain it all very clearly. I learned tons and did well at the same time :) Take her for Chemistry!!

Pros: great teacher, highly articulate, exams test on essential stuff instead of crazy puzzles and are just like old exams, tons of office hours, easy to follow during lecture. Cons: sometimes standoffish/cold when approached at office.

BEST TEACHER I HAVE EVER HAD. Her exams are not easy but they are very fair and based only on what is taught in class. She is head of the chem tutorial center. Provides previous exams, online homework, homework problems in the book, and flexible office hours. Her grading policy is more than fair, at times I think she is too nice. Amazing teacher!=]

Gierash is the best teacher I've ever had in college. Especially for chemistry she really knows how to explain and simplify everything. I'm actually looking forward to taking organic chemistry because she is teaching it!
She's a good professor and her tests are pretty fair.. She can be kind of rude though.

Very friendly and charming personality.I enjoyed learning in this class alot, she actually does the prblms in class and explains concepts along the way. Instead of pure conceptualization like Carpenter does.CPS used in class, but just for attendance, not for grades. Just follow along in class and you should be ok for the exams.Discussion sucks tho.
She is really good at explaining concepts, although there is not a great curve, and when approached her was very stand-offish and misleading

She is the best professor at UMBC.She is extremely helpful.She wants everyone to pass the class.She has most office hours than any other professor at UMBC.Organic is a hard class to understand, but she available to help you everyday.Not an easy A, with the help of Pro. Gierasch its possible.Class curve is not huge,possibly one exam can be dropped.

Tiff is pleasant but she teaches the easiest problems in class. Everything makes sense then but the exams really test what you know.  I just wish she had taught harder stuff in class instead of expecting you to learn it all from the book's problems. Very helpful during office hours.
wonderful teacher!! attend class, she has group work for credit. very helpful

Orgo is HARD and Gierasch does an excellent job teaching. Her exam are fairly straight forward and her lectures are actually informative.  However, the actual material is really tough and requires a lot of outside study time.
super nice prof. no tricks on exams. strait forward. orgos requires alot of work but shes one of the easier professors you can take it with.
Best Professor I've ever had.  Extremely helpful in class and during office hours.
Very nice Professor, curves a lot at the end. If you do all the homework and study the notes, you will get an A. Very helpful, definitely recommend her class.

Its a chem class. of course youre going to need to put in the extra work! But shes a great teacher, always happy to be there and teach. Study from the book, come to class, do all the groupwork, tests are difficult. I wish someone would have told me to pay more attention to the stuff in the beginning of the semester..it never goes away!
too fast

New at teaching, very obvious.  Makes several mistakes while teaching, and doesn’t catch on to them until the end of class.  Had her twice once for 123 and again for 124, she was the only teacher teaching it.  Huge curve in both classes, even though she claimed there wasn’t going to be one.  Try to avoid her, if you can.

I was in her class, dropped it because I decided not to do the BS but instead the BA in psychology...her class is HARD as any chem class will be, she tries to explan things, her test are KILLERS!! study like its your life, all the answers on the tests are possibilities if you make small errors, tricky tricky tricky!...gives group work & hmwk weekly

Excellent teacher! Highly recommend!! Don't know why the bad comments. I am in her class now & she's great! Chem, esp.orgo, is difficult, but she is the best! Loves what she's teaching, enthusiastic, VERY VERY helpful, answers any questions, doesn't try 2 trick u. Just Pay attention, study hard & use the resources available 2 u, & you'll do well.

I'm taking her now and I HATE her  class....she gives tests with every answer that you could possible get if a mistake was made in her pool of answers on the multiple choice tests which is kinda mean and tricky, she's not very clear in class and isn't around much to help- tells you to go to the tutoring lab! you will use your book to teach yourself

She is an excellent professor. Class is insanely difficult. Study like its your life, because you will think your ready for the exam...but your not, and never will be. Exams are tricky. Not like exactly like the problems in the book. However, she is good and will help. Go to the tutorial lab. It's really really helpful. it's hard, but take with her

Lecture is pretty boring. She tries her best to explain everything but Chemistry is not an easy subject. I don't think she's a good teacher- heard the old teacher Carpenter was really good, take her if you can!

Started off the semester saying that she will not curve. After the first two exams had a class average of around 50% (all exams were like that), she changed her mind. Chemistry is hard no matter which professor you take. I worked extremely hard for this course and pulled off an A. I've seen people who study last minute and fail. Study hard.

She's not a bad teacher. She tries to explain things the best she can, but unless you pay very close attention (which nobody does) or are actually interested in chemistry (which you could be, but the large majority aren't)it will be difficult. CHEM101 is not going to be easy no matter who the teacher is, so don't expect a good grade. she's just meh

Worst teacher I have ever encountered, and very unfair about grades. I failed by a point, and failed due to her error in grading, and she wouldn't let the extra credit I did in class help at any cost. Avoid if at all possible!
very good prof

this class was a nightmare. Teacher is VERY unfair about material on tests. tests more on math problems than course content.  3 hard midterms and weekly quizzes and NO curve.  avoid this teacher at all costs
No Comments

Lectures are long and boring. Three exams and a final, all are very difficult with weekly online quizes that allow you to only get 1 wrong before failing. Study hard and keep up with all homework or you will struggle severely. Good luck

Her class is really boring and she is not very clear on what you need to know for exams. Her exams are extremely hard and nothing we went over in class for review was on the exam and there is no curve! Good luck

All exams are from the homework. The material is boring, but he does his best to be interesting. Show up to class, go through the slides and the homework and you will get an A. The textbooks are irrelevant, don't bother buying one. I would recommend talking Calc 2 and linear algebra and cmsc201 before this

He is one of the good professor who teaches CMSC 203. He also teaches necessary content required to know by students and expect the same. Just prepare before the exam and Get A if you understand the subject.
I had very good experience with this class. Classes are super cool, very inspirational professor, and would take it again.

Was hard to understand and read off slides for almost all of his lectures. He seemed to know what he was doing but couldn't figure out how to make his students understand it as well. Do the homework he assigns, although its not graded the problems were essential what each exam was. Only 3 exams  including the final.

Giuseppe is a visiting professor at UMBC. He is teaching one of the most dry courses in the CMSC curriculum, so I can't really dock him for that. He seems like a nice person, but his lectures are difficult to understand and he is not one for partial credit. The course grades are only 3 exams, each a third of your grade and only 6 problems. No EC.

Professor Glyshaw created an incredibly positive environment throughout the semester. Deadlines were relaxed and she prioritized student wellbeing consistently. Sometimes things were unclear, but you just had to make sure to double check with readings and powerpoints. She brought candy, donuts, and cute bird bookmarks at the end of the semester!
The Professor is extremely kind and caring and the coursework is extremely easy. All assignments can be done when it's convenient for you, she does not believe in hard deadlines.

Cozy class atmosphere, got to work with classmates a lot. Professor is extremely kind and genuinely wants you to succeed, class is interesting and easy to follow, and blackboard content is exceptionally well organized with her integrated syllabus. Class's topic teaches valuable skills for both counseling and the workforce overall. AMAZING class!

There's an Interview Project. Very time-consuming and tedious, but easy. Many assignments, and quizzes but fairly easy. If you have an A on the Interview project and overall, you don't have to do the Final exam. Overall, fairly easy but takes a lot of time.

I loved how the class was structured, and she is so insanely kind and understanding. I had a blast with the class, getting fairly close to the people at the table while also getting practical knowledge. Slightly disorganized but she is very open to feedback.

I think of her as a fun aunt. She's a little quirky and a little bit older and she really seems to care about each individual student. If you get the chance, TAKE HER! Organized, super easy, and I feel you learn quite a bit about the interview process. I only wish she taught more courses. --Also expect lots and lots of easy groupwork.

If you get her, just know that as long as you do the assignments you will be PERFECTLY fine. She is so understanding, caring, and an amazing person. Her lectures aren't boring, they start to feel more like a class conversation. Many of the stuff we learn stems from our own experiences. This class WILL improve your communication.

This was one of the best courses I could have EVER taken. I admire and love Dr. Glyshaw - she really listened to her students and had assignments that kept us engaged and reinforced what we were learning. She was very understanding and I learned a lot of valuable information about interviewing techniques that I'll carry with me.

If enough students argued to let us take the final in crayon, she'd have not only let us, but also offered extra credit for initially marginalizing a writing utensil. Friendly? Yes. Extra credit? Sure. Organization? Absolutely not. Several quizzes, classworks and homeworks throughout class have been misplaced completely. Entirely inexcusable

Really sweet professor who loves birds. She gives good feedback if you ask for it. Take advantage of the interview practice in class. Assignments are straightforward. She actually memorizes every student's names and takes attendence each morning. There are plenty of extra credit options. Easy A.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Dr. Glyshaw disagreed with UMBC on how to teach this course, which resulted in some confusion for us. Papers weren't clear about what to write, and she wasn't able to clarify. Her TA graded everything. She grazed over statistics; STAT is not a prereq, so... good luck. Despite all this, she was a sweet, giggly prof who I could tell tried her best.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Caring

reviews.comment: Dr. Glyshaw is so friendly, and really makes class fun and interactive. There is almost always an in-class activity, and she always takes attendance. But, I found every class genuinely enjoyable! I felt like I was learning useful stuff. She can be a bit of a scatterbrain, but she is very easy to talk to.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring

reviews.comment: She doesn't give clear and precise directions but overall the class is easy A. She gives eggs for extra credit. Everything you learn is easy and makes sense. You don't need to buy the book, rent it from the library. You only have 4 quizzes, 1 midterm, 1 final and 1 interview paper. She's understanding, just show up to class and you'll pass.
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Tests? Not many--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: CW's are mostly group work, HW from each chapter, that are super easy. Two interviews, and lots of extra credit "eggs". Dr. Glyshaw gets overwhelmed at times and is a bit disorganized. But she is super nice and caring, she will work with you and help you in any way.

She is a really caring professor. She took the first few classes to learn ALL our names and remembered them. The class is really easy; kind of like a communications class. You have HW for just about every chapter and two group projects. Also, she loves birds so she incorporates them into everything. Lots of extra credit, too.

Prof. Glyshaw was so adorable. She would crack herself up. She really cares about her students personally and in class. You will have class participation points. There is also homework and quizzes from the book. She will work with you. She's a great professor.

You can miss class only 3 times and then you start losing points. There is 10pt classwork(group work) EVERY class. 2 tests, which are super easy. 2 interviewing projects(u interview ur classmate) which are annoying but easy. Homework due every other class which is straight from the book(she reserves a copy in the library, so don't buy it.) *EASY A*
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--EXTRA CREDIT--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: Professor Glyshaw is a very nice woman! There are two projects during the semester.  Both of which are very easy.  Assigns homework straight from the book- Very easy questions. As others have said there is group classwork (worth 10 points)  Although it was an easy A, I have learned a lot.  Highly recommend !

I love Kathy Glyshaw almost as much as she loves birds! Lots of little homework straight from the book (can find most answers in the glossary). We do 2 interviews, but she is a very understanding grader.  Easy tests, she lets you defend your answers. LOTS of class group activities. Look out for her hidden "eggs" - aka Extra Credit to show listening

This is the easiest class ever. It was basically a waste of time because the entire class is like random group interviewing projects that you have to record during class, and like 2 tests but the tests were so easy and this professor is really dumb so you can get away with anything, grading and attendance wise. Just go and you'll get an A.

Yes, she's a little disorganized and class can be annoying but she's extremely nice and helpful. Class projects can get disorganized too, but everything always worked out great in the end. An easy A if you do the work, which isn't hard. She gives GREAT study guides for exams too. Really enjoyed this class and learned a lot more than I expected.

Nice lady. Super easy class. She's so disorganized and it makes it confusing. Class was like being in a middle school class- crazy easy group work every day. takes her FOREVER to respond to emails. gives out a phone number, but she never answers or returns calls. gets overwhelmed easily. but an easy A if you can deal with the frustration

Very nice, like the other comment said, disorganized, class is very interactive so if you are shy, probably dont want to take it. Have to do interviewing with classmates, kind of awkward but I would recommend the class

She's a sweetheart, but a little unorganized which makes it frustrating at first. The good thing is that since she's unorganized, she's willing to work with you on deadlines. Give her a chance, the class is an easy A as long as you do the work. :]

She's nice. Extremely easy class. BUT she's very disorganized. We had 2 projects at 1 time but she said she won't do it to future classes. Only allowed to miss 2 classes without penalties.  Very easy A but she and the class can get VERY annoying. Way too much group work.

The instructor struggles with tech (20 mins to pull up slides), shares bullet points slides (no extra info included), and gives incorrect info that is corrected by students. Grading is bizarre (requires citations within citations?). I've really seen nothing like it before. Prioritize your mental wellbeing before taking this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--So many papers--Graded by few things

reviews.comment:
Does not give good feedback 
Obnoxious grader 
Her own info isn't accurate but the second u use a source she doesn't like, ure practically done for 
Her lectures aren't good either, don't understand the purpose of them & why she requires them so much 
Didn't learn anything , would not recommend & try to avoid if possible
Dr.Chuku is very knowledgeable. The class is heavy in lecture but she does look for class participation. READ, Participate, show up for class and you'll succeed.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: She is without a doubt very knowledgeable. Her approach is rather stern and is not very flexible nor welcoming. Do take notes and ask pertinent questions only.

Dr Chuku is serious! If you want to learn serious about obtaining sound knowledge take her class. She teach with the style of African professors where she grew up. She lectures, you take notes. If you have questions ask during office hours and you will have her undivided attention.Take good notes. Everything she says is important to pass the class.

First off, I can definitively say she does NOT show favoritism to African students. The class is pretty straightforward right up to the end of the semester where the take-home exam responses had to be at least 10 pages long. She only gave us a week! We have other classes Dr Chuku.
Participation is a must. A few debates, a paper, an individual presentation, and a group presentation.
This is a literature and debate based course. If you don't like talking or engaging in discussion, you will not have an easy time. She is a very reasonable person, but beware of her bad side.

Dr Chuku is extremely knowledgeable on the topic of Africana Studies. I had to take her class for two semesters and I learned a lot from her. A student who follow her guideline would do well in her class. Don't arrive too late she will send you back home!

Professor Chuku can be nice; however, her grading system is horrible. She is not clear on instructions, and you are never sure what grade you are going to receive. She does not have a clear grading system, and is impossible to reason with. DO NOT TAKE IF POSSIBLE

She is a great prof, follow the syllabus strictly, show up to class and take notes coz she has the chapter outline that she carefully elaborates on, participate in debates and other class activities coz people usually forget that they are worth points. Its only people that underestimate the class and do not participate that do not do well.

Dr. Chuku is excellent! she is very knowledgable and thorough! who ever has negative things to say about her i would understand. They have to be the students that come extremely late to class or are not prepared during debates and presentation. Other than that, she is experienced and expects your work to be a university level.

Not a great professor at UMBC. She doesn't like to repeat herself even though her accent is so thick we can't understand what she is saying. Special treatment to African students compared others. Many of my fellow students have noticed the same. Only take if you are straight from Africa!

Do your work, show up to class, pay attention, participate in class discussion and you will do just fine. She can be a hag if you piss her off, but if you show up to class on time and do what you are supposed to, you will not have a problem with her. Her accent is pretty thick, but she will repeat herself and write words on the board if you ask.
Extremely hard to understand. Miss alot of information because she is incomprehensible. She hates repeating herself so you better get it right the first time. Avoid her if possible.

Dr. Chuku is a great teacher. She is passionate about her work. If you read the assignment you will understand her thick accent. She is specific advice as to what she wants. Her lecture will help you answer every question on the test. She made interested in West African History!
She was rude and it's hard to understand her accent.  Like the previous reviewer she is biased towards African students and has favorites very unprofessional and she states opinions not facts.

Pay very close attention in her class, he quizzes can be quite difficult. However, if you follow the syllabus closely, you should get an A. It is not an easy class, but with hard work, you will do fine.

Honestly, in my entire educational career I didn't think I would dislike a professor as much as I do Professor Chuku. She does not make any effort to help students, she states opinions as facts, and clearly fosters a bias amongst students. Honestly, worst use of my time!

THE WORST PROFESSOR EVER! If you want to learn another culture and take an unforgettable good experience while doing it. Look in another department. Better yet try another institution. With this professor you are sure to find a high level of injustice, inhumanity, discrimination, disrespect, unfairness, stereotyping and worse. Sad but true warning!

The text used was written in a pedantic way, and was difficult to focus on. My suggestion also is to pay VERY close attention to the lectures. Write everything down; nothing is off limits on your little quizzes. The most difficult part is differentiating names and places, since these combinations of letters aren't typically seen in English.

One of the worst teachers I've ever had. Takes her class WAY too seriously and she's so rude. Only nice to African/black students and embarrasses people in class. If you're going to take AFST212, take it with someone else.

Never mention the word "tribe" in her class or in any of the papers. She'll go off on you. She takes attendance at the beginning of each class. I personally think there is way too much writing for a 200 level class. Take very very detailed lecture notes. Make use of her office hours, she's more approachable one-on-one.

Omg I literally love him. Hes the best teacher Ive ever had in college. Hes so relatable and is very clear as to what the expectations are. He grades as if hes grading himself on his test making, so if the whole class gets the question wrong hes going to remove the question. Hes literally amazing. Very approachable outside of the classroom.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: Kowalczyk is a great professor. He drops the 2 lowest quiz grades and lowest exam grade. All you have to do to pass this class is read the book, the articles, look at the slides he posts on BB and do the coglabs. Also, use the study guides! They are very helpful. He gives you everything you need to pass this class with an A.
Read the textbook, attend lecture, do the coglabs, and you'll pass. It's that simple.

Great professor-- passionate and very knowledgeable about his field. He's also very human in that he understands that "life happens" and gives reasonable assignments with reasonable expectations. Lectures are once a week, but class gets let out early. Lots of extra credit opportunities. Exams are easy and you can basically use process of eliminatio

Dr. Kowalczyk is a great professor. Gives study guides for every exam, use them.  A lot of reading but it's pretty interesting. You will have to read research articles and you will be quizzed on them. Drops your lowest quiz and exam grade, which makes your final optional if you are happy with your grade. Overall, awesome class and professor.

Professor Kowalczyk is fantastic. Classes are long, but that is because he only comes once a week, but classes are interesting. Tests were not had as long as you paid attention in class and read the assigned research papers (even is you don't, he emphasizes what's important during lectures). Also tons of extra creit opportunities.

Dr. Kowalczyk is an excellent professor. Incredibly knowledgeable, fair and lucid in his grading, approachable, and a funny lecturer too. His exams are kind of hard, but the content is straight from the lectures. He tells you everything that will be on them, so there aren't any surprises. I'd definitely recommend taking his course.

Prof. Doug is awesome, he really is there for the student. He make sure you understand and gives great feedback. If you really want to learn Spanish, take it with him. He's very down to earth and really wants every student to succeed. I wish he would have taught my 103 course instead of Daybert Linerez. Definitely recommend him to anyone he's good.
He's incredibly easy, but don't expect to learn anything from him. He strongly favors the boys and the attractive girls in class. He's kind of an ass.
Very funny guy, makes class interesting.  Beware though, he doesn't take Spanish as a joke if you miss class or do not do well.

prof doug is a great teacher. although he is more of the joker type you can tell he has a serious approach to whats expected of his students and has high expectations out of everyone. he will help you if you dont understand anything. just ask
He's a **** pig, but he's pretty. Pretty gorgeous. If you want to actually learn something, don't take spanish with him.
No Comments

Prov. Doug! If you fall into the category of someone who enjoys Spanish but doesn't plan on going past 201, take him. This guy is a great professor. He's funny, he's very clear, uses enough English to be clear, and his class is very easy if you put decent effort into it. If you have decent Spanish skills and a decent work ethic, its an easy A.

My, Boooooooooy!! Yeah He is A Beast, I Loved that Class forreal, Funnest part of My Day was in that class, Sometimes he just sitts around tells jokes, he is so funny, youll love this class....Best Of all He Can Teach You will learn, and he makes  it so easy....so you will half to dedicate yourslef and really really hard to try to even fail... A+++

My Dawg, homie to the end!!!! Ill ride for that dude, the funniest teacher of all time. He is so cool, never gets mad guarnteed to pass his class, even if you don't know squat...All you gotta do is show up and do the chats, debates and your good!!!!!!

This is not an easy class for winter, but Dr Glezen tried his best to explain everything and worked on a lot of examples and hw problems. His exams are directly from hw, so make sure you memorize them.
Fair grader, tons of homework- and grades only 3 (random) out of 30 assigned. Exams are mostly from homework problems. Nice guy.

Dr. Glezen is a really nice guy, and might just be one of the smartest people I've ever met.  However, he can't teach calculus to save his life.  He claimed he wouldn't curve but had no other choice after he saw how bad the first exam grades were.  The common final for 152 (written by someone else) was a cake walk compared to Glezen's exams.

Dr. Glezen has years of experience with the material he teaches and actually loves to teach to students at the university level. As a teacher, he's patient and eager to help when listening to questions and he applies what he learns on the job in the defense industry to the abstract calculus being taught. As a grader, he's very generous, but be forewarned: his office hours are difficult to make. Highly recommended regardless.

He is a part-time professor that also works at Northrup Grumman, so a lot of his example problems revolve around aerospace. This class is pretty much just your typical high school statistics class, except with calculus. He is a very nice guy, and he grades very leniently. The exams aren't too bad, and they're based off of homework problems.

Lots of homework that then comes up on the exam. Wants to be helpful, so ask questions - although often he doesn't understand the question. Office hours are good. Projects are well described. Discussion is totally unrelated, he leaves it entirely up to the TA.

The entire course pretty much boils down to homework memorization, which is NO WAY TO TEACH. He goes over sample questions in class then gives you a metric ton of homework. Don't do it, and you fail. Otherwise, very funny and helpful.

He is a great and nice teacher. He goes over all homework problems before you turn them in, so you pretty much get a 100. Also, he goes over the projects and pretty much just helps you. Exams and quizzes aren't that bad. Exams and quizzes are closely related to the homework. He grades leniently.

A good teacher; definitely knowledgeable in the field. Moves very quickly in class. Nonenforcement of homework assignments was problematic for me (no motivation to do homework over other class' assignments). Lenient on grading.

Great teacher overall.Homework assignments were not part of the grade. This may seem good, but it doomed many students who tried to do all problems a day before the exam. The professor will tell you to "know your homeworks". If you know how to do every homework problem, then you will get an A.Helpful and polite in office hours unlike most teachers.
Easily the best professor I've had at UMBC. Homework isn't mandatory, but it incredibly helpful for quizzes and exams, JUST LIKE IN REAL LIFE. No curve, but if you do your work you won't need one.

Although he's not the best professor I've had, he really knows his stuff. I just don't think he's sure how to effectively teach students all the ridiculous amount of material required for biochem. If you want to get the most out of this class, go to his office hours. If you want the A, you REALLY have to work for it.
If you can, avoid this teacher for biochem! This is hard material and needs a more serious teacher. Good luck!

He's like a big kid. If you're into immature humor and the like you might dig this guy. Know his slides and read the book. He's all multiple choice but does give some extra credit. You get to drop one exam but the final is mandatory and comprehensive. He's not my favorite.

IS 450: class was a nice 450 experience. HW every week, not too hard. 3 exams, non-cumulative final. She reviews your study guide and gives suggestions if you send it early enough. Lectures are pretty boring. Wireshark labs weren't too hard. In-class exercise every once in a while, that is graded, so don't skip too many lectures. She's very nice.

Pretty fun class. You get to configure Windows servers and create an Active Directory domain. The labs are pretty straightforward, but they can sometimes be weird. Exams are the only downside. You are allowed one double-sided cheat sheet, but the questions are pretty tough. I still think its worth taking though.

Very engaging lecture and she gives great examples. 9 homeworks that total 40% of your grade but the lowest one is dropped (online and mc). 3 exams that total 60% of your grade, they are straight forward with no trick questions. It is a lot of content but as long as you pay attention you will do fine.

Solid prof. 3 non-cumulative in-person tests, ~9 HWs (on blackboard & timed, 1 dropped). Lectures are ok, slides posted online with some extra readings. HWs are straightforward as long as you review the slides/readings. Exams are so-so; can easily catch you off guard if you don't prep; lets you send in your study guide and will give feedback on it.

On her class there are 3 exams and 9 homework's she drops the lowest 1. She is passionate about teaching, the tests are from lectures. The exam is very hard you need to memorize the concept from the reading. Missing class affect the grades since she go over important stuff on class that actually not on the slides.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Test heavy

reviews.comment: This class is straightforward. As long as you read the materials she shares and review weekly, you will be fine in this class.
One of the best professors I've ever had, great material prepared for the class and really good explanations of tough concepts. She will work to make sure you get it if you show effort

She knows what she is talking about but you have to take lots of notes during class. The slides don't have much information on them, but she explains them during class. Lots of labs in mindtap that can be tedious and time consuming, but straightforward instructions.

Is451M was easy with Professor Glazer, she did amazing explaining the slides. The only thing is the Exams were tough because they were scenarios. buts the exams didn't weight a lot the labs did. the labs aren't tough but the labs Virtual Machines kept freezing. also if you did bad on the labs you can re-do them for full credit. she is very GREAT.

She is an awesome professor, who really knows her stuff. They are 3 exams and I think 15 homework's She drops the lowest homework. she is really caring and does really well explain her slides, the tests are from articles and from lecture so make sure to read them and pay attention in class and you will be fine.

Not sure why her ratings aren't higher. Her class is relatively straightforward. Grade is mostly based on weekly HW quizzes and exams. Content is not too hard to understand, and she does a good job at lecturing and responding to emails. Lectures are not mandatory and she records them. She's also a very nice person. Overall, a solid choice.

Ms. Glazer is hands down one my best prof. at UMBX, took 451 with her also. This class is set up easier compare to 451. 3 exams, pretty straightforward if you are attending lecture and reading, and rest are lab which are all completed in class. Don't miss labs, read her slides/book, do review questions, you'll be solid. Again, She is awesome.

One of the hardest class I have ever taken at UMBC. There are three exams, 4 quizzes, and one case study. The exams are 75% of the grade while quizzes are only 5 % each, and 10% for case study. The lowest quiz grade gets dropped. She is a very tough grader and sometimes rude to students. She relates networking to real life. Would not recommend her!
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Exams are extremely hard, nothing from her notes help. Boring lectures
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Entire grade is exams

A lot of material is covered. There are quizzes between the tests, so you get an idea of what you are expected to know. Lecture ends early most days but feels like it went the distance. Not the most exciting delivery from a professor, but I learned a lot. The "OIT" tour was fun.

No textbook, all material publicly accessible online (articles). All powerpoint lectures are based off those materials, you will do much much better if you actually read them. Great lecturer, wants you to ask questions and succeed. Material isn't even difficult... Class does not require any actual networking... Just broad concepts...

Study and do the required readings and you will do well. I am surprised to see the poor ratings, the professor is more than willing to help after class and the networking knowledge (mainly concepts in 451)  is very valuable. The IS people who complain the technology classes are too hard (We have it easy compared to comp sci) should switch to BTA.

Worst class you'll ever take. Terrible lecturer, difficult tests, and tough grader. The lecture is dry, boring, and not at all engaging. The tests are out of 35 (take no less than 32 for an A) and the quizzes are out of 15 (take no less than 14 for an A). If you want to excel, you need to be dreaming and eating networking. The material is huge

One of the Worst Professors in UMBC. She teaches , but she is really mean when coming to exams. She would talk all through the class which makes boring. Her exams are tough as hell only people who know networking can easily handle it. She would on purpose make it harder for students to pass. Also, she will take points off for no purpose. DONT TAKE

Horrible Professor- If you do not have a background in Networking her tests are impossible. She will not help you study for material that is going to be on it. She is not helpful when you ask outside of class. DO NOT TAKE THIS UNLESS YOU HAVE A STRONG NETWORKING BACKGROUND.
good professor

Very Clear! 3 exams and 5 pop quizzes, so you need to make sure you do well in all of those. Quizzes are all multiple choice; However, the exams have multiple choice and short answers. She grades the multiple choice very easy tho. Make sure you know the section that you have not been quizzed on before the exam Last exam will be 80 percent caching.
Overall great professor. She is very clear and straight-forward. Her lectures slides outline everything you need to know for the exams.

Easily best networking professor I've ever had. 3 pop quizzes, 3 exams, no cumulative. We don't even have homework. Just make sure you go to all the classes, she gives you hints about when the pop qizzes are (she pretty much tells you). She uses relevant articles and Cisco webpages to teach, no textbook usage! She's super nice and really clear

Great instructor, one of the best in IS department. She likes what she does and she does it right. Lectures are straight forward and exams are easy if you know the material. She seams like a really nice person and she cute too. Great professor!
She is an amazing teacher! Loves what she teaches, responds promptly to emails, and super cute. DEFINITELY TAKE HER! EASY A!!

All of Glazer's classes are great.  She's very familiar with all of the topics and makes it fairly easy for students to understand.  This class was lab based using the textbook, and exams were easily studied for by taking notes in class and by using class slides, available on BlackBoard.  Grade is solely based participation, three exams and a quiz.

GREAT professor, horrible lecturer. Class isn't mandatory so don't worry about skipping now and then. She gives pop quizzes at random (but you can kinda guess when to expect them). Wording on exams is tricky in places so you MUST read carefully. 3 exams = 90% of the grade. 10% = quizzes. Do not underestimate the exams it is very easy to lose an A.

The best advice I can give you is to take the hw seriously since it's worth 40% of your grade.  The exams come from her lectures and online readings so if you pay attention you should be able to get an A no problem.  The professor is really nice and knows her stuff!

You have 3 exams, 10 HW assignments and thats it.  Exams (25 multiple choice) are based off of HW assignments (10-20 multiple choice), so study those questions and related topics.  HW questions are a bit tricky, so the slides and wikipedia will be your friends.  Class attendance is optional.  Half is online (free day) and half is in class lecture.

great teacher.. beautiful too..try to do good in home works all the time.. if u do that u will be fine in exam as well as in overall grade.. do not compare 450 and 451 451 is way too easy for people who took martens
No textbook required, everything on blackboard....only meets once per week. Although her wordings on exams/quizzes are pretty much  close to impossible to understand....
Great teacher, really easy course. Class only meets once a week. Online quizzes are pretty hard but exams are pretty easy. I didn't try very hard and I got a B.

I think she is easy, but try to do good on all h.w on blackboard because it will help you out in the end of class.  Other then that she is cool.  Test are comes from h.w assignments SAVED ALL OF THEM.  BEST OF LUCK

She's a nice person and seems interested with the course material. Class is once a week, mostly (unless it is a "study for exam Thursday"). There are Blackboard assignments each week, and while these are easy, they  are at least 4-5 questions that are so vague that the "best" possible answer is a mystery. She's too stubborn to make them clearer.

This was a very easy class.  We were assigned weekly HW that she answered nearly all the questions during the weekly lecture.  Although the schedule says the class meets twice a week we only met once a week.
She's very knowledgable, fair & teaches well.  This class gave us a lot of good info with enough hands-on activities to keep it interesting.  I would take any IS class with her.
class was easy. very thorough in her lectures and everything taught in class was on the test. the end of chapter multiple choice really helps on the pop quizzes.

I felt this class was very straight forward.  Glazer was very helpful and as long as you studied the questions at the end of each chapter you can easily pull a B on all her quizes and exams. I got an A without much difficulty. HINT: Use the books website for answers to the end of chapter questions.
No Comments

He's nice and you can tell he has a passion for math. That problem lies in his teaching though. Just b/c you're good at something doesn't mean you are good at teaching it. Spends time on talking and explaining theorems rather than doing problems. He expects everyone to "reflect" on math all the time like him. Tests can be very tricky.

I took him over the summer. He talks way too much about theory, especially for a class like MAT251. I worked very hard and got a B but I taught myself most of the info and going to class was a waste of time. He's a smart and nice guy, but he can't teach. If you want to waste your time in class and then teach yourself take him, otherwise don't!!

Way to smart to be teaching. Absolutely can not dumb it down for the students to learn. Thinks we understand what he's saying but goes way to fast to even realize we are all stuck. If you get him..drop him asap.

I loved Gloor! I think he's so cute and funny. He made me fall in love with Calculus. Albeit it was kinda hard. I aced the quizzes and homework but failed 2 out of 3 exams. I don't really understand why. After the tests I'd look at them and see that I could've done better. His tests could be easier. I suggested that. But he's so cute!
Taught myself everything. TOTALLY ruined my GPA basically with his hard tests and unstructured lectures. Final? Hard. Loves math though... i'll give him that. I'm retaking this :(

I went to lectures for a few weeks and found them extremely dull, yet confusing. He explained things that we didn't care about and skipped things that we did care about. I have taken Calc before and still found him confusing. Also not very helpful outside class. Very bad with technology. I have done much better since switching to another professor.

The class isn't easy. You need to work hard and actually understand concepts and how to apply them. That being said, he's an excellent professor. His lectures do help you understand the material, and he's always willing to explain things multiple times. You might not get an A, but you will actually understand Calc by the time his class is done.

Gloor is an interesting professor because while you can tell he enjoys math, his teaching skills aren't helpful. Lectures are composed of him talking for a good hour straight with examples here and there. Don't take the class if you're trying to get a good passing grade (C or higher)

He talked more about theories rather than the math and gave history on how formulas were discovered.  He also goes into why the derivatives work, writing up proofs that take up the whole wipe board.  Horrible teacher that uses roundabout ways of figuring out how to solve a problems and the examples he uses are so difficult and jumps steps.
Without my T.A. I would have absolutely no idea what is going on in that class.
I have him for 251 this semester and he is really a good prof I think he does a good job explaining.  His test was hard but I think I did ok.

I had him this summer.  He was really good.  I think the only people who don't like him are the lazy ones.  That last commnebt about him hurting your GPA is bull.  You earn your own grades and he is fair.

Psh I agree! all the positive comments have the same tone. I dno what that person was on to think that calc is so much fun with gloor. He is a good/cool guy but he will take a dump on your gpa folks! His lectures have absolutely nothing to do with the tests soooo good luck.

After a careful read, nearly all of the positive comments here are nearly identical in form, tone, and content.  I suspect serious ballot stuffing, especially considering the even tone of the complainers and the saccharine tone of (what I suspect are the professors) positive comments.

Dr. Gloor is a fantastic Professor. He teaches a lot of theory with which you can approach any problem presented if you truly understand the concept behind it. I would highly recommend him for any math.

Prof Gloor is awesome!  Before I took this class I had really no interest in math but now I am thinking about being a math major.  He put all the ideas together.  I had to work hard but I feel like I really understand it now.
The most fantastic calc teacher i've ever had. As long as you are willing to put into the work you walk away from that class a calc king
He really did a great job of explaining the conceps of statitics.  This was my third try at this class and i finly understood it.  He is nice guy and very helpful.
I know a lot of people think he is too hard but i think he was great.  you have to go to class and do the work but if you do you will really undersand.

Gloor does a very poor job explaining the course material, taking all of the class time to divulge in theory rather than practice. The exams are very hard, and I think there are much better options for a calc teacher.
Brutally hard tests, with no curve. Besides that, he's a nice guy.
Great lectures, very clear. The tests are murder. Even the TA had a hard time figuring out how to do some questions. They are both long and complex. He does not curve them either.
One of the worst professors Ive ever had, exams are extremely difficult and has the worst discussion sessions
don't waste your time and money find another professor. He got too many students and the exams were extremely hard.

Focuses too much on mathematical theory rather teaching how to solve problems. He needs to take into account that this is a general freshman class and that most of us are not math majors. I don't feel like I am learning calculus skills in such a way that I can better apply math in other classes like chem or physics (which is why I'm in this class).

i came into this class not interested in math for my entire life! prof gloor changed that: he made me LOOOOOVE math!!! this is the first time i have ever enjoyed math at all, and i am not majoring in mathematics/engineering. i am half indian, half indonesian. i have always been a little more indian, but boy did he bring out the inner asian in me XD

he saved my first semester gpa, taking 18 credits sure takes its tole -.- but i got E's and D's in all my classes, but Gloor was the only professor that gave me a B. currently taking him for Calc 2 (while taking 16 credits) and i have an A. so nice :)
woooweee did gloor change into a great professor. i had him 2 years ago and he was just so-so, but coming back to have him teach me Calc 2 was a privilege.
very interesting lecturer; knows a lot about the theories of calculus. gives you a good understanding that will guarantee you an A or B on every test/exam.

i meant the previous comment right below to be for MATH 151, not 155. anyway to reiterate, take him over tighe! he's great :D i promise you will not regret it- besides, he has the best discussion sections. he teaches you the complete theories of calc and you will leave the class with a full understanding of calc and fully prepared for CALC 152!!!

as of right now, philip gloor is a changed man. he attended a math class for selected professors and teaches material in a brand new way. i highly recommend him over tighe because this will be like the only chance you can take him: easy A- he will give you study guides and the material on the exams from now on :) he is also incredibly nice/sweet <3

This professor teaches Calculus I. He spends all his time teaching theories and emphasizes them as if you should memorize them. But when it comes to exams, all the problems are super hard and you feel very under prepared. Be prepared to teach yourself. What's also frustrating are those unannounced quizzes
Hes probably a real cool guy, but the teaching is not great at all. I failed. This semester with a new professor seems to have a better outlook.
Waste of time & money.
AVOID AT ALL COSTS! We asked him to do complicated questions and his reply was, "Lets save those for the exams!" enough said

Gloor teaches theory, not how to do problems. The problem is, his exams are on the problems, not on the theory, so you fail. Our exam averages were all around 60% and there's no curve. I have a D and I pray that I'll get a C in the class. Also, his TA's suck; they don't speak English well.
HW every week, 2 Exams and the Final. I hate math, but he explains really well. Nice guy, but you really have to put in the work. Small curve at the end of the semester.

many people don't like gloor because tighe is little better at clarity, however tighe's tests and quizes are very tricky and tight on time so more studying/practice is required. Gloor's tests are a less tricky

this is the second class i took from him.  i think he is a really good prof.  this is a boring subject but he explains things very well.  you just have to do a huge amount of practice problems and you will be fine on the tests and will get a good grade.  i asked him for more problems i could do for practice and he gave them and helped me.

It took a while to realize he was talking about theory to give big picture we can't get in the book and we should work problems on our own.  After the first exam I started doing a lot more problems and studying. I also went to his office hours with questions. I must of spent 10 hours a week doing problems.  I got an A and chose him for my math152.
Not my favorite professor for sure

Ok if you are cornered during scheduling and he is your last option, wait until next semester otherwise you will regret it. I'm currently failing his class not because I suck at math, I study a lot. HE CANNOT TEACH. He goes into theory too much, also take into account that anybody who wanted to be a math major would have gotten AP cred.in HS prior.

One of the worst professors I've ever had.  Many of my classmates also hated him.  Puts you to sleep and only teaches theory.  Then goes off tangent.  Tests are darn near impossible and little to no curve at all.  Would be great for higher level math course, but not Calc 2.  He's too theoretical

really bad professor. exams are hard, does not teach material well. goes into theory a lot, which is great, but does not teach how to solve the problems well. TAs are much more helpful than he is. take another professor if you can.
Very good prof, you can tell he cares a lot about his students. The class was a lot of work at times but as long as you do the work and listen to grading feedback it's not that hard to get an A.

One of my favorite professors in the physics department! He cares deeply about his students and is ALWAYS there for help. I found the lectures were extremely useful for completing the lab reports. Also, even though lab is 3 hours, it never actually takes that long. You can tell he genuinely enjoys what he does and wants to see his students thrive.

He is very understanding to students and clearly loves what he does. He enables you to succeed and is very accessible & approachable. As with all lab classes, the lab reports take time, and it's never something to procrastinate on as you will not have enough time otherwise. But he gives the most digestible & pleasant experience for such a class.
Solid professor. There is a ton of writing associated with his class. However, I am sure that the skills I have gained in his class will be extremely handy some day.

Lectures are skippable if you know your statistics and physics 2. Labs are pretty interesting and usually we finished with 2 hours to spare, you must do a report for every lab but you get two weeks to do them. Very lenient grader on the final project and he brought snacks on presentation day. He's awesome and I love him. Makes a lab class fun.

One of the best professors in UMBC. I've been in this university for quite a while and can with confidence say that Dr. Gonzales is one of the most kind, caring, and smart professors out there. He always listens to student feedback and gladly helps with things unrelated to his class, be it other homework or life advice. Everyone I know loves him:)

A kind guy who wants you to learn physics. Be prepared for a lab report/analysis each week with difficult questions. There is an independent lab at the end where you work with 2-3 people. If you reach out to him, he is always willing to help. Gives extra credit sometimes.

Strenuous, stressful course-load and class environment. I do think she means well, but I have never felt more overwhelmed by a class in my life. Not an ideal class for beginners or slow learners. Also, she requires you to have your camera on for online lectures while her own camera is off?
If you miss one question on one assignment she takes half of your points. Gives a lot of homework and is very strict. This class is stressful, if you are a beginner do not take her class.

This had to be the most stressful class I've ever been in; the constant shouting and overall distrust the professor had in students left me walking on eggshells. During my midterm, I suffered a panic attack and cried so hard in the bathroom that I vomited. The overwhelming humiliation and stress of being in this class has left me with nightmares.

LOTS OF HOMEWORK. Other than that, the feedback for your Spanish she gives during class is very good as long as you keep up with the loads of homework you will be doing. Quizzes are all online and the tests were pretty easy.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Gives good feedback--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Now while this class was a bit more rigorous than some of my others, and the Professor was stern with us, I believe she means well and intends for her students to succeed. Will this course be heavy in term of work? Yes! If you study, reach out for help you'll live!
Horrendous. Does not make her expectations clear and is very confrontational with students. Expects far too much, especially for an introductory course and is awful at giving feedback.

The amount of work given out for a beginner level class is ridiculous. You have to make sure you stay on top of ALL of your work or you will get marked absent. Late work is not accepted at all and you are given course work on holidays. You are expected to learn Spanish in an impossible amount of time. The language credit at UMBC is a joke.

Holy, avoid this woman if you can. She will take the concept absences and turn them completely against you, even though you can be present in class. On some assignments you receive a ZERO if you miss a question or a section REGARDLESS of how much of the assignment you completed, and you're reported for cheating? She will chastise you constantly.

I don't have anything personal against the teacher, but her teaching style is not ideal, and does a lot of correcting in class. Conversifis are pretty stressful for me and wasn't comfortable for me to talk to random people in a language I have no experience with. For a 101 class theres a lot of expectation, would not take her again.

Professor Gomez truly doesnt have bad intentions, however if youre a freshman or your course load is large be careful taking this class. Any not turned in work=absence.
