Long winded homework, and the final project youre expected to do a full presentation in spanish without looking at notes. So take this class with a grain of salt.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Group projects

reviews.comment: She is the worst language teacher at UMBC. Her instructions are never clear and her class is far to difficult for a "beginner" course. She wants us to learn the material in a week and expects everyone to be fast learners. I never understood why she thinks that learning a language can be an easy process that we would have conjugations down in a week
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Gomez is an very nice person and I believe her intentions are pure, but she falls short on many aspects of teaching. Her course is very difficult for a 101 class. She expects you to know the material very quickly and wants you to have full blown conversations. Just take another language...
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: This is the absolutely worst professor I have ever had. I suggest if there is another teacher take them instead. She is beyond unreasonable, she's the type of teacher to assign something to you and not understand herself and the call you out for not understanding. UMBC should do a better job in auditing their professors.

She expects us to make our whole life around her class. For example if you work on the weekend as almost every college student does, it will not work with her class as we have projects, quizzes, coversifis due all in one week. And for conversifi we have to spend so much money or spend alot of time to get a token which rarely happens. DO NOT TAKE.

Professor Gomez is a tough professor, I won't lie about that. There are a lot of assignments due in a week and it is expected you keep up on them but you know about them far in advance. Attendance was HW, participation, and the discussion board after class. She corrects you out loud yes, but it is to help you learn. You will learn a lot from her!!
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Quite literally the worst professor this entire country has ever seen. I wanted to blow my head off every MWF sitting in a 50 minute class. Her attendance policy is quite the worst, have 9 absences and your grade drops by an entire letter grade, this may seem bad until you see that causes an "absence" , eg. not doing 1/1000 weekly assignments
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Avoid her if you can. She expects constant in class participation for attendance but will yell at you if your Spanish is not perfect. Will change guidelines for assignments often, sometimes hours before said assignment is due. Lots of work and very condescending.

Awful class. Shes gives way to much qork for a beginner class, expects you to know everything, and changes rubrics/grading criteria last minute or after the assignment has already been turned in. You cant get anything wrong or she will call you out in front of the entire class and is so condescending.

DO NOT TAKE HER CLASSES. After having dealt with a semester of her buffoonery I cannot fathom how she is still trusted as an educator. She expects every student to have mastered the content PRIOR to lecturing rather than actually teaching us. The amount of work she assigns, attendance policy, attitude towards students and so much more. Good luck.

The study plan each week can be extensive on top of other work so there is lots of homework/studying. Professor Gomez is always available by email and willing to let you make up on work you may have missed but only under certain circumstances.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Professor Gomez makes her expectations very clear from the beginning. She is very accessible and responds to emails very quickly. She expects a lot but does her best to accommodate students with extenuating life circumstances that may get in the way of their education. I recommend anyone to take this class but be prepared to work hard.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I transferred to UMBC and noted the language requirement. But Professor Rubio has been the worst professor I've ever seen. She makes up reasons to mark you absent from class, even if you sit through her entire lecture. For a 101 class, she expects you to know so much in just 1-day intervals! I couldn't imagine taking her again. Avoid it honestly.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Professor Gomez-Rubio was completely unprepared, posed assignments with less than 24 hours notice for completion, expected classes on national holidays to be made up, and extremely impatient. She counts people absent for tons of reasons out of the student's control, and drops a letter grade for absences that she creates.

Professor Gomez is one of the best teachers I had at UMBC. She is indeed a tough grader, however, if you do all the assigned work and you participate during class it will make everything easier. She is always willing to meet with students whenever they have questions or concerns.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Gives good feedback--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Profe Gomez-Rubio is such a great help when learning a foreign language. She expects vocabulary to be at least somewhat memorized before class, then in class she focuses on conjugating and using vocabulary in practical examples. The Conversifi section of the course is intimidating at first, but I never had a bad experience with any of the coaches.

Professor Gomez has really thorough slides that are on Blackboard & gone over in class. The weekly Study Plans helps a lot too. Orals are via Conversifi so we get to practice with someone in a Hispanic country through video call. If you really want to learn Spanish, take her class. She cares a lot & is very helpful and generous with her students.
Worst teacher ever taken. Very rude. Not flexible whatsoever. Very unrealistic.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: DO NOT take her if you want to pass your class. Her carelessness regarding grading resulted the difference between a letter grade for me.

If you take 102, be prepared to work like never before. Tremendous amount of online homework with short period of time, writing, conversation with spanish speakers, exams. But dont be scared, just study hard and do all those on time, you be alright.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Tough grader even for winter classes, and I know spanish

Spanish at UMBC is demanding but it is expected. The assignments were awkward, such as video-chatting with a native Spanish speaker and the exams can be tough if you don't study. Professor Gomez is sweet but she can be abrasive. Study hard and attend every class and you can definitely pass. She is very lenient on grades at the end of the semester.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: First, do yourself the favor and DO NOT take Spanish with her. She is unreasonable for a 101 level class and expects you to know 200 material pretty fast. Test are hard and all free answer, so you have to know your stuff. Attendance is basically mandatory and you work with a partner also very class. Also required to do assignments due on weekends.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: She wasnt particularly hard, but I did not enjoy her class. She doesnt have a very organize system of learning and everything is basically work from the textbook. Theres so much partner work and its basically what you do all class.

Only 4 extra credit opportunities always on Wednesdays. Attendance is mandatory, online homework is super easy and you can do as much as you wants as early as you want. She expects you to learn the material outside of class and come in and review it in class. Must be prepared for the journals with the pre-writing.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: Her class is easy if you do your work. I spent an hour or two a week doing the homework and reviewing the vocabulary. I see why people complain about her, but they complain because they don't want to work for a grade. Not how college works.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: I have taken 300's classes that are easier than Professor Gomez class. She makes the class unnecessary hard for no real benefit. Unless you're looking for a really hard and challenging Spanish class, don't take her.

Is not clear while lecturing. Goes over material once and if you ask a question or if you dont understand, she acts irritated. I have learned more from the book and internet videos than I have from her. Her English isn't great, which makes understanding her answers difficult. In short, SHE DOES NOT MAKE SENSE.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: She doesn't really teach.  Profe Gomez just hands out a bunch of pieces of classwork and makes you do them without ever teaching the content. Plus, you cannot use the book either. This leaves you constantly confused. Also, she is a very subjective grader. Honestly I have learned nearly nothing in this class, which is far from the standard at UMBC.

Please do not take her class. She has terrible English, doesn't teach, changes due dates, grades harshly, and is just generally a horrible professor. She makes the course so much more difficult and confusing than it needs to be.
- Attendance was taken every class - Attendance and Participation was 10% of the grade   - Participation is required.

She is plain and simply a bad teacher. I absolutely would avoid taking spanish with this woman. I explained to her I was confused and having trouble and she told me to drop the class. Do not take class with her.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: Professor Gomez is really dub honestly. This class is literally an extension of 102, so if you took that you know EXACTLY what you expect. Same kind of lectures, group/ partner work, unnecessary homework, etc. But you can get away with anything with Gomez and she always makes you dance to Pitbull or something so good luck with that...

I LOVE Profesora Maria! She's hilarious, plus really wants you to leave her class with the fundamentals and cares if you actually learn. I took her class at AACC, and literally wanted to follow her to UMBC! She's great! Buy and READ your text, pay attention and participate in class. STUDY the material when she gives it and you'll surely get an A!

Took her class at AACC- Absolutely loved Profesora Maria. She is absolutely hilarious and really tries to make learning another language easy and fun.  She is a tough grader, but only because she expects you to really try in her course. If I decide to continue Spanish, I will definitely be taking her again!

She's got a lot of personality! Be prepared for lots of homework, and be sure to participate. Not uncommon for several important assignments to be due at once, and deadlines can be pretty random change without much notice. She's usually very sweet and funny, but rarely might jump down your throat  for little reason. Also, she makes you dance!

I could have gotten an A had I turned one of my homework in on time. She's ok though. Has an accent but we could all basically understand her. Has these discussion boards though where you have to work in groups and those SUCK. Exams  are straight forward. Show up to class and you'll get a C, do the discussion boards and score ok on exams its a B.

Profesora Gomez definitely expects a lot out of her students, and I worked a lot harder in this class than I expected to. She can definitely be hard to understand at times but is happy to answer questions. Sort of crazy but in a good way- she keeps things interesting. She even tried to make everyone dance during the final!

Took this class as a condensed summer class. If you really study, it's not difficult. Profesora is as helpful as a person can be. She is a native speaker and does have an accent, but if you PAY ATTENTION she is very easy to understand. We had some HW before going over the topic in class which meant more effort to read the book and figure it out.

Hands down, the BEST Spanish teacher I have ever had! Lots of class activities and partner work. She is very good with introducing new concepts and gives a lot of hand outs for practice.We review before EVERY quiz and exams are super easy. Lots of online work involved, but if you show up every day, participate, and do the work, you will have an A:)

Profesora Gomez is a great teacher. She expects a lot from you. One thing others did not note was that she is told to give assignments and projects by the MLL department. It is not her choice. As long as you do the assignments in the manner she requests and show up to every class, you will be fine. I have a 97%. Work hard and you will be rewarded.

Profesora Gomez is hard on those when it comes to late work, missing a class, and when you need information relayed to you cause of it. DONT MISS CLASS. She explains everything thoroughly and the class in general isnt that hard. But there is a lot of tedious work you need to do. its not hard its TEDIOUS

Maria Gomez-Rubio expects you to work and work HARD. The department wants you to do a lot in a 201 course but Gomez-Rubio does nothing to help except pile on more work. She was great and really funny the first day and then awful the rest of the semester. She has a good heart, but I would highly recommend that you avoid her at any cost possible.

Unrealistic expectations and course load.Try hard for a C, probably get a D. Told class she will fail people that dont understand even if you try. Youre here to teach not threaten. Fix the problem dont just fail people because your entire department is inept. Got a B –I tried so hard I struggled in my real major classes and didnt have time for them
Worst Spanish Professor EVER. Spends tons of times to speak herself about trivial things. NOT TEACHES. Unfair grader. Explains NOT clearly. DO NOT TAKE HER.

Worst class I have ever taken. I hope you're not planning on taking ANY other classes along with Spanish 201. She barely understands English and assigns more homework and activities than some of the upper level BIO or PSYCH courses I have taken. She has no concept of what a reasonable course load should look like relative to the level of the class.
Terrible teacher and very hard to understand. Avoid this class.

She is very nice and makes the class exciting. She's funny and optimistic but she does expect a lot from you. She gives out A LOT of work mainly becuase she wants you to take the class seriously. Do the work and participate and you will be fine.

Professor Gomez is great! She really cares about her students, and you have to do a lot of work. Learning another language is tough, and Professor Gomez made Spanish very exciting. TAKE HER COURSE if you really want to learn Spanish. Take someone else if you are only looking for an underserved A. You have to earn your grade is her class.

There's a LOT of work assigned in this class, but DONT WORRY it's still pretty easy. She explains and sometimes even has the entire class go through it. It's a pretty nice class and sometimes she is funny. I'd recommend. All the Spanish teachers in this school have been a blast!

I really enjoyed having senora Gomez as my spanish profesor! She is a very sweet lady if you work hard in her class. Attendance is VERY important. I took this class only for the GEP requirement. There is a lot of work and projects to do, but if you try your best she will likely give you a good grade.

I have never written reviews for an instructor in my four years of college, but I feel it's my obligation to warn students about her. In short, disorganized and a poor English speaker. Communication is difficult, and she IS NOT willing to work with students that struggle with the language. If at all possible avoid this professors classes.

There is a lot of busy work in this class, but it's meant to help you understand the material. There is a bit of a language barrier, but she is sweet and helpful and definitely wants to see all of her students pass. Make sure to attend class and participate.

She is a very good professor and an incredible person.  Talk to her outside of class because she has an amazing journey to where she is now.  The class has a LOT assigned material and you will not pass if you miss too many classes (but thats MLL policy).  She wants you to do well and will help you even when it is not convinient for her.

Always very nice and energetic. Honestly, it's not that much work. A good amount ends up counting as extra credit. If you are an active participator, she will be more likely to let you turn things in late/accept extra absences (and really, just raise your hand 3-5 times a class to answer questions). She's really a sweetheart and wants you to pass.

I love Profesora Gomez! I'm going to miss her so much. This class is a lot of work, but as with most language classes that's the only way you learn. She is a wonderful teacher and person. If you participate and are nice, she will love you and let you off the hook easier if you mess something up. She wants everyone to get As. Extremely fun and kind.

Idk why everyone is giving her such bad reviews. She is a really nice teacher and tries to make class very interesting. This is my favorite class this semester. She is from Mexico, so sometimes she messes up in English, but that also means that she knows her Spanish. There is some work but if you try you will be fine. Funny lady.
Her English is terrible. She assigns a good bit of work, but can be unclear sometimes. Show up to class, participate, and put in a reasonable amount of effort and you should earn a reasonable grade.

there is allot of assignments in this class. make sure u go by how she wants the disscussion board,chats and other assignments or you will loose points.Must attend classes or it will substanially affect ur grade. She is not very compramising with things unless u have a good reason. the syallbus will probably be updated at least a couple times.

She assigns a TON of work, but it helps your grade.  You'll probably get a B if you make a modestly honest attempt to do everything.  But her English is not the best so she often gets confused and refer you to the syllabus or "NO!".  Also, ignore anything she says about assignments in class, follow the syllabus! Again, her bad English confuses her.

SO MUCH WORK! The assingments did help to keep my grade up, yet she is very strict about keeping with the "plan de trabajo". If you attend class and do everything she asks, you can probably end up with a B. It is just annoying because it is like she assumes that spanish is the only class you are taking.

An adorably sweet lady..So nice and tried to make the class enjoyable(videos, dancing, etc.) She told us at the beginning of the semester attendance was necessary yet people didn't understand why they were failing when they never came. She gave us many many extra opportunities to make up work. Sweet lady!
This professor is very passionate about her job and culture. If you do all of the assigned homework, it should be easy to get a good grade. Somewhat of a language barrier, but great teacher overall.

If you are going past 201, seriously avoid. She is from Mexico, and can't understand what students say when they ask or answer a question. All you do is go over homework the entire class, which sounds easy but is soo boring. Go to class for quizzes though. Not sure how you can't get a good grade, but if you want to go on, she doesn't teach anything

She is a great teacher if you just want to get 201 behind you. She is very clear with what she is going to test you on. She assigns homework, we go over it, and then we are quizzed on that concept at the end of class. It makes it easier that way! If you go to class and pay attention you will get a good grade. Homework isn't graded but recommended.

She's hispanic, and sometime's its hard to understand her, but usually its harder for her to understand the students' english accents, which is annoying. Overall she's really easy. The classes are pointless, but still go to take the quizzes and she takes attendance. If you're going past 201, don't take her

Great prof and T/A. Despite outside circumstances, the class was fun and supportive. Prof made class fun and provides practice exams/quizzes—though problems may vary. So don't just study them for quizzes/exams (though his exams/quizzes are similar format-wise to practice exams/quizzes). Highly recommend MATH 300 and this prof.
His lectures are very-well equipped. His quizzes and exams are not bad if you study and do the homeworks fairly well. He explains things well and his class isn't too serious. Pretty good.
Class was relatively simple, but prof made it fun. Wish there was more to do and less in Math301. Super recommend going to office hours, he's fun to talk to and will give lots of good advice.

Dr. Gowda is one of the best math professors that UMBC has to offer. He is very lecture heavy, so don't skip class unless you want to miss important information. He is kind, and very obviously passionate about what he does. I would take him again in a heartbeat!
Hands down the best professor I ever had.

I loved Dr. Gowda's class. The class I took was combined with the graduate class. It was 490/602, so basically, it was a special topics class. Complex Analysis is one of my favorite topics in all of mathematics. Dr. Gowda taught the course very well and I enjoyed every single lecture by him.

Dr. Gowda is an excellent prof and among the best I've taken as an undergrad. He does a great job conveying the essential insights to a subject during lecture, and also sprinkles in historical context. His homework is typically short and relatively easy, and his exams are of similar difficulty. He's also very kind.

Do not take if you struggle with lecture-based professors. Should you get stuck, his resources outside of class are very scattered and hard-to-follow. In addition, the class is only graded on very few assignments and there's less guided practice to know you're doing it all correctly. I really wish he would implement these in the future.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He is VERY specific with what he wants on almost everything. Ive gotten points taken off for wrongly drawn arrows. Im telling you guys that this is a difficult class to pass and he is even more of a difficult teacher to please. He really is a nice guy buts thats it.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: The entire class is graded out of 180 points so if you get two on your 40 point exam you lose 1.2% on your final grade. Makes it so you are mathematically barred from certain grades from making small mistakes on exams

Dr. Gowda is probably the best math professor at UMBC. His lectures were very easy to follow. I'm not sure if it was the content or him but 302 seemed easier than 301. He always had office hours right after class, which always helped with any questions we had on content from the lecture or in the homework. A1 professor and person

Gowda is the man. It might take a minute to get used to his accent, but he is very smart and really good at explaining complicated topics. Sometimes lecture can be a bit boring, and while it's not mandatory to go, you still should if you want to understand the material. Homeworks aren't too bad. Tests are average.

He is not only a brilliant mathematician, but also a wonderful teacher.  Very engaging during lectures, willing to help outside class. If you take good notes and pay attention in every class then you won't need the textbook.   This class is supposed to be one of the most difficult math courses, but because of Gowda it was my easiest this semester.
The best math professor at UMBC,  the best math teacher I've had, and perhaps the best professor I've had in general. He's that good.
Do everything in your power to take Dr. Gowda's class. He exceeds even the highest of expectations.
The one, the only, the legend Gowda, is the best professor at UMBC. Zat's it.
Gowda is a thoughtful professor who was very good at lecturing. An easy A if you do the homework and learn how to do basic proofs.

First A in an upper level math class (and I mean almost aced it, very atypical for me). Didn't buy the text book, did all homework, copied his lecture notes verbatim. Aced every exam. His lectures made me actually like mathematical analysis. He cracks funny little jokes, is excited to teach. Best teacher at UMBC BY FAR.

He is fantastic super clear for both Math 302 and 411. He teaches both courses completely from memory. Just take notes in class,because your notes become your textbook. The material is super clear and homework and exams are very straight forward. Also, he is very helpful in office hours.
outstanding clarity

I've never had a better professor than Gowda. He teaches beyond the course material in lecture, wraps concepts from higher level math into the context of the course, ties on a nice little bow and sends you on your path to enlightenment. Truly the best.

Coming into this class, I had no prior experience with proofs. Through his lectures, he sets up multiple proofs for you so you understand the structure, and he also answers most of the homework he assigns in his lectures. So if you go to the lecture and pay attention, you will be perfectly fine. Also he loves to use questions from old exams.
Gowda is Love. Gowda is life.
One of my favorite math professors. He is fair and always makes class enjoyable. He also knows when you are not in class, but his class is fun.... so don't skip class.
Best math professor at UMBC. Period.
Boring class.  Complete waste of my time.  Useless material that won't help me get a job.

Gowda is great, clearly explains the material in lecture and gives 5 homework problems a week to reinforce the problems. Exams and quizzes are fair and sample exams help you prepare. Great at answering questions during office hours and ensuring students understand the material. Definitely take Gowda for this class, you will learn a lot & enjoy it!

Dr. Gowda is great! He managed to make difficult material interesting and his passion for mathematics showed through in his lectures. Homework, quizzes and exams were fair with practices exams given. Definitely take 301 with Gowda if you have to take it. I dropped 301 with another professor but excelled with Dr. Gowda's guidance and clear lectures.

Excellent explainer, very willing to help over email and during office hours, and a fair tester and grader. To do well in 301, I recommend recopying every lecture's notes, starting assignments early, and taking advantage of office hours. Redo all homework and practice problems before tests and quizzes and you will do fine and learn a lot.

I am a math major and definitely one of my favorite professors. He does not use the text for math 301 except to occasionally assign hwk problems. Hwk is a good chunk of the overall grade. Offers a LOT of bonus opportunities on tests and quizzes. Tests are manageable and based off of practice exams, notes, and prior quizzes. Overall great professor!
Absolute best professor that I've ever had.
Plain and simple, one of the best professors' in UMBC.

Best math teacher I've had so far at UMBC (I'm a junior).  Very clear, with decent homework and exams that are very passable as long as you study.  Expects hard work but works hard for you to succeed and stops at nothing to help you.  Makes the subject enjoyable.

Gowda is by far the best math teacher at UMBC. He is always willing to help and if you pay attention in class and study you will get a good grade. Definitely not an easy class but he explains things very well.

Very good teacher, he explains everything very well, test expect you to be able to recall a lot of information but it is not anything you have not been taught, overall he is a great teacher you actually learn in his class

He is a nice teacher. He can explains this topic very well and he makes this class easy for you to understand. His exams are a little hard and TRICKY. He grades harshly. If you want to understand this class then take it with him. Otherwise take the class with Draganescu, his exams are a little easy and does not grade as harsh as Gowda.

My absolute favorite professor!  He doesn't rely on the textbook at all, which forces you to go to class, but he keeps it very interesting. He likes to make little jokes, and obviously loves every second he's teaching.  He creates a great learning environment.  I highly recommend Dr. Gowda!
Fantastic teacher.  Complex analysis is a massive waste of time and thinking.  Yet somehow Gowda made me want to attend.

Excellent professor.  Approaches topics almost always differently than the text, which is only used for homework.  Your notes from his classes will be notes to keep.  He loves his little jokes too.  "That is the test for conservative vector fields.  There is no test to see if they are liberal."  Cheery and helpful.

I took this class over the summer, Dr. Gowda is really nice and really tries to help you out, he just knows his math down PAT so watch out for his consistent writing on the board. He will go back over material and make crazy analogies which are rather adorable, but he REALLY knows his stuff. STUDY PROOFS!
His class was the biggest waste of time and life.
He makes funny jokes relating to animal and their habitat. It was easy in the beginning, but gets harder, and sometime clarity is needed after class. But overall, it is enjoyable class

He knows basic topology well. He is excited about the class and subject. Uses silly sayings to clarify and lighten up the class. Very nice, and not too hard. Homework was mostly straightforward, and both tests were easy take-homes.  Highly recommended, but you need to be able to write proofs clearly.
I took the class my freshman year with him. I've had tons of math professors since, and none has topped him. I still remember Green's Theorem.
Best Math teacher i've ever had.  I think almost everone in the class would have agreed with me.  He made me enjoy calculus.
Dr. Gowda is an excellent professor.  He teaches the material straight forward with no tricks and his exams are easy to pass.  If you put in the time, you will get the grade.
He is an excellent professor. He teaches extremely well. He's funny and smart. Always ready to help.
Good professor who really cares about how you apply what you've learned beyond the classroom. He wants you to succeed not just in the course, but after you graduate too.

This person is just awful and does'nt have respect to others. Attending his classes are a total nightmare. Doesnt ask clear questions in assignment and assign a ton of work to do. Stupidest to the core, asks all his students to use a stupid latex software to do assignments.

Overall, really chill guy. One of my most favorite classes I've taken at UMBC. Almost everything is myLab (tests and quizzes). If you study myLab, easy A.

But I would not recommend this professor if you don't like math, as he did deduct points on Chapter 4 and 5 quizzes for those who didn't watch the recorded lectures.

his videos are very helpful

If you want to actually learn the material, not the professor to take at all. If you just want to pass the class? Take this guy right here. Group work for quizzes and open book, I passed the class with a B without spending a single minute outside of class doing any work or studying.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Not as bad as others say, awkward guy but generally well meaning. Group quizzes each class with occasional individual pop quizzes. Exams can be a bit of a curveball (keep old quizzes), but not impossibly hard. Make sure you understand each topic thoroughly before progressing, it will bite you later. Quality of team correlates with class experience.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Clear grading criteria--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Save yourself the time and misery. Thank you professor goofy gobbert. 0/5.
Bro is definitely every student's worst nightmare. Rude, condescending, please I am begging, choose another professor. Avoid this man at all costs. God bless

Simple: this guy is the most condescending person I have ever dealt with in my entire life. He was rude and belittled everything that came out my mouth. I am a very easy person and give people the benefit of the doubt, I always showed him respect while he didn't. He humiliated me various times. Such a BAD rep for UMBC. Reeks so much ego I PITY him.

He made 75% of our grade just tests and each one had 4-5 questions on it. I'm a bad test taker so this is my worst nightmare. I got 5/10 on most of the homework because he graded for accuracy and I didn't want to cheat. Bad teacher.

Very smart professor who knows what he is talking about, however, he comes across as rude and or condescending. I took the class and we worked as groups when he would ask about questions no one asked for help due to the several times anyone asked for help he would be upset about any questions or clarifications asked.
He's rude
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I had him for Math 225 last fall, he is legitimately one of the worst professors I've ever had. His recorded lectures spend 95% of the time on proofs and no actual examples. He is condescending and rude when you ask questions. He puts absolutely no effort into teaching you, I recommend watching the math sorcerer on youtube. Avoid at all costs.

This class is relatively easy (it's linear algebra. simple stuff rly), but there are better professors to choose from unless you're stuck with Gobbert being the only professor. MyLab is horrible and he never emails anything important which makes the class such a mess. Sure, it's online, but that's the only positive. Avoid this prof for another prof
this class was pretty fair. There were some tech difficulties and adjustments with is expected with an online class

The class material isn't that hard, sometimes the format can make it hard to get good scores. 15-minute quizzes for 5-6 questions don't leave you much time to think. He offered retakes for quizzes and allowed the two midterm grades to be substituted for your quiz averages for the period which was nice. Talked about policy more than course material

Old RMP states non-mandatory attendance and the newer RMP say otherwise. This is due to a random policy change in the middle of the semester and your knowledge of the topic does not matter as much due to his way of managing the course that benefits cheaters in such a heavy manner. I know some smart people who watch YT for learning instead. Useless.

On the first day of the semester, Professor Gobbert introduced his structure as a "flipped classroom" where a student watches lecture videos and reads the textbook then practices in class. The videos were of poor quality, and the classes, which required attendance, was always about class policy. He also could not give any real world applications.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The most recent review for his current 221 online course is laughably off the mark. This dude does not teach. At all. Abysmal recorded lectures sound as though they were recorded in a wind tunnel during the Great War. Does not listen to feedback re: quizzes. Avoid, avoid, avoid.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: I am currently taking the course and will update after the semester but so far he is so niceee. He always asks for feedback and he goes over every little detail for homework and quizzes to make sure everyone understands how it works and is able to complete everything. There are a lot of examples and lectures recorded, you can work on them anytime.

Just one of the most awful people to ask for help from. He rarely answers questions without being condescending. He yells at you for wrong answers, and he yells at you when you ask for help fixing them. Do not make any careless mistakes ever or you'll be sorry. He's a good mathematician, but an extremely harsh teacher.

His class may be online, but that's where the honeymoon ends. Extremely rude, refuses to help students, and easily gets mad at students. He is not worth your time and money and you will not learn anything from him. His online class is so horribly organized that you are better off taking this class in person anyways.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Very condescending. Was unclear of how he wanted your HW answers to be. HW's were also long and took away the time needed to practice each of the problems. Refuses to help students and easily gets mad when students ask the simplest questions. Lectures were not useful and his notes were very hard to read.

Horrible! The worst lectures I've attended. Upon finding out what kind of condescending weird jerk this guy is, 3-5 lectures were enough to convince me his class is not worth the time. He will create rocket science out of simple stuff. He is unclear on HWs/Projects. Avoid at all cost! He is a boring and unmotivating prof. Beware.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: He is a solid prof, could be worse. Other reviews are coping; the blackboard is organized differently than most professors but it is affective and easy to navigate. A lot of homework (3-4hrs). The exams are quite literally slightly easier homework problems so it works well. Can be a little rude although. Lectures are in a very readable cursive.

Never answered emails, never answered a question clearly, insisted on using an old IDE for R, and used an ancient textbook that wasn't up to date with the current R code or the current package code. Incredibly unhelpful, incredibly boring lectures, not worth the stress of taking an already hard course with a bad professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: A very nice and gentle introduction to MATLAB, from IO to 3D Graphics to Numerical Methods. No quizzes or exams, and 8 homeworks, of which he'll count the best 7. The first ~hour of class is spent with him giving a lecture and live demo over the tutorial, next 2 are to do the hws, in which he'll answer any questions. Would rec. + take again.

Homework was long. Pre-recorded lectures were hard to navigate (bad handwriting, makes things more complicated). He wanted class to be group work but usually, it was just silence. Says he's accessible via email and then takes days to get back to you. Can be condescending to students if they are struggling. Blackboard is organized strangely.

This man is condescending and not nice to be around. Asks us "why aren't we asking questions", when he has an attitude if you do. Class is afraid to even speak up because it feels like you're punished for being wrong. The material is interesting and generally, it is not hard. It would be 10x better with someone else teaching it who likes people.

Solid professor, I won't say he was the best but he was effective in my opinion. Weekly homework (expect to take 3-4 hours to complete) and 3 midterms and a final. Pay attention in class, and do the homeworks with care and attention and you'll be fine. Exams are very much like the homework assignments. I would take a class with him again.

Gobbert's winter class would decide whether I would graduate, and let's just say that I definitely do not regret taking this class with him. :) Be prepared to work hard for your grade though. Your HW grades are determined by how well you follow previous feedback. On the other hand, there is no midterm or final.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Doctor Gobbert's lectures were very boring. For a class like 225 I felt that he delved too much in to proofs and not enough practice. His lectures didn't feel like they helped me as I would end up reading the textbook for clarification anyway. His homeworks were lengthy but proved to be very helpful in preparing for the exams.

The instructor has the worst handwriting ever. Hard to argue with things while you clear your point. He is really trying to give you more information and guidance but it overwhelmed you some time when that reading material is not well organized. So trying to understand what he wants in the hw is harder the hw itself.

He is an alright teacher. He can seem mean, but he is always fair. All his exam questions are very similar to ones he asked either in homework or in quizzes.  There is a participation component to your grade, 10%. He is very tough on this, like not using the discussion board will knock you 2% off your total, so be sure to participate in everything.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: I will start off by saying he may be the most pretentious professor I have had. Though slightly condescending, he does give you exactly the information you need. Homeworks ar every long and do not help you on exams (besides the first problems on homework). You need to be familiar with Matlab.

His lectures are really boring, most of the class are just on their phones. He doesn't speak loudly so it is hard to hear him. He doesn't explain the homework that well. He will do practice problems in class, but the homework is 10 times harder. The exams are not bad if you do the homework! Would not take again.

The class is something new to learn and it will get a little challenging at times, especially with the Homework, so plan ahead in time to complete it. Starbucks is the way to win her heart.

I'm not a fan of statics, but Professor Gurganus made the subject interesting, was incredibly approachable, and overall provided a very enjoyable experience for the semester. I would definitely recommend her.

Prof. G is my favorite professor so far.  She has very clear lectures and holds lots of office hours.  I sometimes go to office hours just to hang out and she provides lots of insight into engineering beyond her statics class. It seems like she believes everyone can be an engineer and is willing to spend time with anyone to help them get there.
LOVE HER!

She is most likely the most caring professor at UMBC. Very helpful if you go to her office hours and will spend a lot of time going through things if necessary. One of the best freshmen teachers at the whole university.
Great and helpful.

She's nice and a little bit over-energetic.  Not a very good teacher in the lecture setting.  Speeds through material and needs to walk through examples a little slower.  The course is also really unorganized and the grading system is a complete mess.

Sometimes she may seem a bit too excited for school and makes some lame jokes, but she's definitely one of the nicer teachers around. She does go a bit fast during lecture and it can get frustrating because your notes always seem halfway done, but she will definitely help you out if you go to her office hours. A pretty good professor overall.

Ms. Gurvich was an awesome instructor for this course. It is lecture heavy so if you take notes you should understand the material because she teaches it very well. There is homework pretty much each week, she is nice enough to give extensions when you need it. You do need the textbook for HW. She is approachable and laid back! 10/10 recommend.

Literally in love with this Professor! She's so down to earth and truly wants to help students do their best. I've been a silent admirer for the past semester and actually fell in love with math, she's really passionate about it and I can't help but recommend her for future students because she's an amazing person :) Textbooks are a must!!!!!!!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: I liked this class a lot more than previous math classes. Ellie's office hours were very helpful, and every test had opportunities for extra credit. Classes were almost entirely lecturing and the handwriting was a little hard to read. The homework problems and some of the material could be confusing, but they were very good at explaining it.

She is a great professor. She explains things clearly and is very helpful. If you can go to her during office hours, please do.
One advice is you'll have to use the textbook. You can't do some of the hw problems without it. But, you can email her if you have questions and her explanations are very clear. I definitely recommend taking her class.

Ellie is a solid lecturer who takes care to prepare her students for the exams.  Homeworks are relevant to the test material, and she drops (blatant) hints about what will be on exams if you attend class.  Extra credit has been available on each exam.

Gurvich has been more helpful than the one I actually have (Potra).  She got her students to join my 221 discord I was advertising unprompted and has provides resources and specific help.  They also offered to leave said discord because (paraphrasing) "I respect the right of students to shittalk profs". 10/10 wish i had them for this class

I am not big on straight lectures and thats basically all that happens during class time. She bases the homeworks off of practice questions in the book. The problem with that is that there are questions that are on the homeworks and in the book that are not explained in her lectures or in the book. I constantly have to seek outside resources Beware
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Ellie was the best TA i have experience thus far at UMBC, she took a difficult class and made it manageable for the undergrads in her discussion section, and set the bar for consistency despite one hell of a semester where the professors were swapped more than once and class was not always consistent.

I took MLL 191, which isn't listed here for some reason. She's knowledgeable about the topics, and encouraged participation and discussion. She's friendly and pretty funny, and the course load is pretty standard, not bad at all.

Prof. Jang's very understanding and clear about her expectations, wanting students to succeed. There are small quizzes + a test at the end of each lesson, but she uses class time to review and prepare for it. She allows us to choose partners for projects and homework is graded based on accuracy. Just consistently practice and do HW!

She is a wonderful professor, who has personality, and cares for each student that participates. She grades fairly and wants everyone to pass each quiz. Is relatable in terms of outside of school, makes jokes every now and then to lighten the mood, and keeps a lighthearted energy everyday she teaches.

Took her class last semester and her face was too expressive so if she didn't like something, you would know, whether it be the idea of your presentation or you're struggling to speak Korean. Too much discrepencies in her syllabus and her assignments, when we confronted her about her, she wouldn't admit that she was wrong.

She can speak Korean but can't teach it. Syllabus isn't written clearly- no way to know which assignments have deliverables. Blackboard has broken links she found like a Quizlet full of typos and mistranslations. She spent 1st class threatening to fail anyone who can already read the alphabet. Treats students like children with a 5 min late rule.

I cannot stop telling my friends my experience with Dr. Slaughter. She is the best professor that I had at UMBC. The materials are tough, drought, and hard, but with this professor, you will understand everything. Exams are easy, expect Lecture exercise every lecture -> they are helpful for studying and understanding the materials. Love :)
Dr. Slaughter is the BEST professor. She genuinely wants her students to succeed. While the course was difficult and dry, she is very caring and you will walk away at the end of the semester smarter.
Excellent Professor. Great teaching skills.

Hard class. Unrealistic abt the difficulty of projects & didn't even teach the information necessary to complete them. Tests were mostly reasonable(but so hard to study 4)- many questions copied straight from exam review booklet. Talks really quickly in lecture. 1st half of the semester, didn't explain info clearly AT ALL. Getting an A is possible.

She doesn't seem particularly interested in the material of the class, but that wasn't a problem. The exams, projects, and homework were all a reasonable level of difficulty. The class was challenging but at that same time very manageable. TAs were not particularly useful so labs and projects were very hard, but that isn't the instructors fault.

She expects you to dedicate all your time to ONLY her class. We were forced to do our final project demo on the "Finals study day", labs would run 2+ hours over allotted time sometimes. she can teach very well, but is VERY UNFAIR in regards to workload. Going into the final, only 2 students had Cs, after the final, more than half the class failed.
She is confusing and cannot teach. I would not recommend  her to anyone that wants to learn (or learn assembly before taking this class).
She wasnt as bad as some comments are suggesting. Just a hard grader!!!
Most unorganized unclear professor

Many reviews on here I feel are biased since this is an intro to Computer Engineering course.  Most freshman want grades handed to them. She makes you work and earn your grade. The class has been the same ( both exams and projects) since she started teaching it. Learn the material, don't just memorize it! She wants you to think outside the box.

Makes an easy class conceptually impossible to comprehend.  Never keeps study material online, so if you want to even remotely prepare for exams you need to save everything she posts of everything, EVEN LABS  Homework doesn't prepare you for exams. So you do a week of binary to see and get a hamming code question on the exam and just fail. AVOID.

Absolute worst professor I've ever had at UMBC.  Gives a RAT (Readiness Assurance Test) every other Friday. Which is graded off of effort so you'll never really know if you get the concepts until the exams which are inconsistent, unclear and test esoteric concepts you'd never experience.  AVOID

Confusing teacher. Lectures are generally read verbatim from a set of slides. The primary issue is that her exams are poorly written and vague and projects are extremely difficult. She often tells us how engineers will never use some of the difficult, abstract concepts she teaches in class and then proceeds to lecture and test us on them. AVOID.
Her expectations are unclear and exam questions are vague. Average on first exam was a 59%. Refused to curve or go back over the material. Avoid if possible.

Her lecture slides, and especially exams, are riddled with vague, confusing wording and grammar that always leads to confusion. This gets annoying because the TAs often don't understand what she meant on the tests either. Then she leaves the TAs alone in class to review exams, naturally... I don't get the feeling she cares much about this course.
I you want to pass 310 do not take this class with this professor, though she is very helpful and approachable the class is extremely demanding. She gives biweekly quizzes and they are exams.

She was really nice, but she can be very unclear. English isn't her first language, so her quiz/test questions can be vague. She often further confuses the question while explaining. Advice: If confused, ask. If you understand, then DON'T LISTEN to her explanation. Even if she says "You'll never use this info," she will still test you on it.

She gets mixed up which mixes you up. Says she wants to foster an environment for learning, but will not allow you to take notes on devices of any kind and if further clarification is needed she debases the class by exclaiming "Come on guys. This is easy" and lets out a frustrated sigh. Overall if you can avoid her, you'll do yourself a favor.
This class is a lot of work. Learn assembly before taking it.

She was an incredible professor and I enjoyed being challenged in class. She kept me engaged in class. Excited to step into class and discuss the reading as a class. I highly recommend her if you want a good challenge.

Gives very unclear directions on assignments. Never prepared for lectures despite course being lecture heavy. Extremely unresponsive to questions from students and even if she does answer, her responses are dismissive: either giving a vague answer or say "we'll talk about that in next class" only to never talk about it. DO NOT take her classes!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Professor is fair and thorough and gives helpful feedback. She has made me love policy, which I had not idea I'd like.

Professor Harmon-Darrow is pretty strict and organized. She expects a lot of her students (nothing unreasonable) but the positive is that you'll learn a lot. Lectures were sooo boring, though. Multiple hours of sitting and listening to her speak with little emphasis or excitement. Great teacher, just needs to work on lectures!
Had a great experience in this class! Knowledgeable of the material and passionate about the field of Social Work! Would definitely take a class again!

One girl in my class STILL didn't have her midterm graded even by the time of the final. Read straight off the powerpoint, rarely answered emails about questions on the material. ALSO doesn't believe in study guides. I got As on the paper, would've had an A in the class if she had provided some form of a study guide.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: Gave us a list of content to study for exams, but none of it was on the exam. After being confronted about it by multiple students, it did not change. Unclear grading criteria and difficult material. Reads word for word from the powerpoints. Boring
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES

reviews.comment: grading was rough.

Understand that this course is a bit rigorous with constant papers because it is an English course, and you are required to hand in a hard copy of each paper. However, professor Turney gives really good feedback on the writings, and you are allowed to revise on some. She genuinely cares about each student, and is also very lenient and kind.

Prof Turney was probably my favorite professor my first year at UMBC. She is super nice and caring and she gives really good feedbacks. As long as you do your work and attend class you can easily get an A. She doesn't make you read a whole book either it's mainly just little chapters throughout. Highly recommend you take her class.

Professor Turney is a really nice and thoughtful teacher. She cares about the students and their opinions. As long as you show up, pay attention in class and turn in the assignments you should do well in the class. I am glad I chose her as my teacher and I would recommend everyone to take her as well!

A great teacher to take for English 100. She takes the time to give helpful feedback on papers and is respectful and kind towards her students. You will most definitely receive a solid grade in the class if you listen in class and work hard on a couple of essays.

She is an amazing professor! I had so much fun in her class! She is such an amazing person and always ready for students to reach out and ask questions. You will have to write a lot as it is an english class ,but she is so open minded and always encourages her students to step outside the box and write about new creative topics!

Very discussion based but he gives you a lot of opportunities to speak on various topics. Very open to different interpretations of the readings and breaks down books by their construction and content. GO TO CLASS.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: It's never too late to change your major. How much do you want to work at Starbucks after graduation?????

participation matters, however if you don't skip any class and just sit silently (paying attention) you're better off than someone who participates and skips class frequently. hes a nice teacher but my advice is that you go for office hours if you need help with your papers because that's what this class is about.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Perhaps he's not the best professor teacher in the world, but I enjoyed his class. If you are good at writing the types of papers he wants to read, you'll get a very easy A. If not, it might take a bit more work. One major upside: he's willing to read and help with papers before you turn them in.

hes very brilliant but omggg.... there's a lot of work to do. i took  him for 308 and he was pretty interesting. he wants everyone to participate and he also wants us to give presentations. hes not a walk in the park but if you want to challenge yourself, you can take him... as for me, nahh..

Sooo,  he's my advisor and I took him for eng 308  he's pretty nice but you have to work for your grade..  I might take him again not quite sure about it  be ready to give presentations  I'll advise you to just stick it out or run..   He likes participation but if you don't want to talk just show up,  take notes quite attractive too!

Passionate about what he teaches, but a tough grader who can be rather unclear about his expectations from assignments.  Will give absolute zeros on papers if student misinterpreted unclear criteria, despite effort and care in writing it (but sometimes allows for re-writes).  This happened to multiple students in my section. Be sure to read.
Stay away from him. His grading system is tough. This is undergraduate.

He is very interested in his classes and you can tell he spends a lot of time preparing. The topics and the students really matter to him. His assignments are challenging and he doesn't just hand out a good grade. This class is definitely worth taking, and if you're willing to work you will learn a lot. He's an amazing professor.

Stay away from this man. He grades paper too hard as if it is a Graduate paper. He is a mean grader.I do not recommend except you want to fail. I'm sure people dnt know they need to come here and rate him down

Very easy to get an A. Attend every class, highly discussion-based, so participate. He hates when people don't participate (only time he might've raised his voice slightly). But he's a very nice, smart, funny man and an easy grader. Pretty hard to fail this class. I highly recommend this to anyone wanting an easy English course. :)

He is such an amazing professor!  I think this was the first time for him teaching a lower level class, but thankfully he was not very hard on us.  He loves participation and discussion so participate alot.  He talks the majority of the class but its okay b/c he knows alot and has an awesome accent!  If you have the chance to take him, go for it!
Extremely intelligent and insightful. Is an accomplished writer and scholar offering noteworthy perspectives to materials...sounds like dracula..wudnt mind a bite.

He loves to talk, but he knows what he's talking about. I had Gwiazda as a freshman for 308 and I'm happy to be ending my major with his seminar. He brought in poets to speak, which was great. No exams, but lots of writing (of course). He is willing to look at drafts! Definitely worth taking while you're at UMBC

I found his class to be somewhat easy -- but be careful, if you don't participate, then you're probably not going to get an A. He says he will only give A's to students he thinks are "memorable." So, if you're not planning on writing stellar essays and participating a lot, then maybe stay away.

The previous reviewer prob. has a penchant for dead white males, but Engl308 can't be taught like other surveys  because of the american diversity principle (his other classes DO contain a lot more DWMs). Different groups prefer different cannons. One valid complaint is however that sadly he DOES dumb his classes down for the poorer students.
Easy grader and the class.. basically just show up and sit there, so it's pretty dull.  Easy A though!

He's probably the best professor I've had yet.  Knows the subject material very well.  He is kind of tough on grading papers, but his comments are very helpful.  If you get a chance, take any of his classes.

HOT!  But also a very good professor...knows his stuff and you can learn alot.  As long as you put a little effort into the class you should do well.  We had a lot of great class discussions.  Just try not to be too distracted by his amazing looks and hot accent...

I took this class as a freshman and got "A"s on the first two assignments. He is, by far, the best professor I've had so far. I always left his class with a passion for the subject. Really got me into my major. Don't let his lectures intimidate you! He does talk a lot which can get boring but it's all relevant material. DEFINITELY take this prof!

He's a pretty cool guy, i guess.  Sometimes, he can be strict or very serious, but overall, he seems like a nice person.    He doesn't seem to like it when you talk too much in class and he definitely takes his classes pretty seriously.    Watch out on some of the papers.  He has some very stringent guidelines which can seem unclear.  So, I def

WOW!!  Defintely one of the hottest professors I ever had.  However, I feel that he has a bit too much to say. He has loads of information about authors and their works, but sometimes I feel that he doesn't know when to stop talking!  Resulting in about 15 min of class discussion. And he's a bit flirty too, just email him.  Not that i'm complaining

Rating Dr. Gwiazda here exposes to me the flaws in this ratings system.  Where's the ranking for "knowledge of subject material" or "teaching ability"???  Dr. Gwiazda is hands down the best lecturer whose class I ever attended in my 4 years at UMBC.  He is the smartest prof. I've ever met there (next to Dr. Loviglio) as well.  If you're the kind of student who can really appreciate and open themselves up to the ideas a qualified teacher can put forth in a class, you'll love him.

Piotr is not only quite attractive, but intelligent to boot!  I had a lot of fun in his class and it seemed like he took the time to get to know everyone on a personal level, which is always great.  He is a nice guy who is always out to help students with
He's adorable...his accent is hot...and for a man who isn't from the US, he sure knows a massive amount about American Lit.  I'd recommend him to anyone.
He's adorable...his accent is hot...and for a man who isn't from the US, he sure knows a massive amount about American Lit.  I'd recommend him to anyone.
I love Gwiazda!!!! He is the best teacher in the English Dept.  301 opened my eyes to so many things,and it is all because he taught it the way that he did.
Gwiazda is the man!!!!  308 is the best class I've had in the English department, it was really fun and we did learn some things.

I had him this spring for Engl 308, and the class was so great.  Class discussions are really good, and he always has a lot of info. about the authors & their lives.  He was very understanding when I had some difficulty this semester.

This guy is good for nothing but looking at.  Is getting on in years, so appeal will be lowered soon, but until then, he is a metrosexual-looking hotty with blue frames. Too thin, though, needs to relaize this is not communist Poland and he can get food.

very interested in the literature, he brings out the historical significance of everything--he's a walking book.  wonderful professor; accent was at first hard to follow, but you get used to it.  great for english major class; a plus:he's very attractive.

Extremely intelligent and articulate...  specializes in poetry, knowledgeable in all areas (hist, mus, phil)... has high expectations for class discussions and writes reasonable exams... friendly but introverted, I think... a great professor.

Wow.  I could listen to this man talk all day, such a sexy accent.  and not only is he hot, but he also teaches wonderful, is extremely nice, and knows everything about what he's teaching!  I wish I didn't have to graduate so soon...I'll miss him!
Such a hotty! My whole class, at least the females, bonded over how adorable he was.  Sometimes you can get lost in his accent, but he is very easy to look at and pretend you are listening!

He called us all lazy for not participating in class lectures when we didn't know the answers, which is funny considering he made us watch all of his covid lectures from 3 years prior and he never actually lectured during class time, he literally just sat there and critiqued. He was extremely rude the entire semester to be honest.

Professor knows the material like the back of his hand. If you try to bs your assignments he will see right through. Good teacher but it's a lot of reading, weekly hw's, and lectures. It's a class where you will work and he ensures you know by putting it in the syllabus as well.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Respected

reviews.comment: Really good, I actually enjoyed the class prepare to read, discussion posts weekly, with at least two replies, and two exams with a final. Basically, pay attention, take notes, review before taking exams. You will pass with an A! All the best.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Amazing lectures --Get ready to read

reviews.comment: L prof. didnt answer my questions through email and often talked about non-material things during class, dont know how he expected us to do well

attended all lectures until out of nowhere he practically called students who did not participate "shameful" and "sad". i understand wanting to have everyone talk, but bringing them down was just weird for me, stopped going after that, tough and weird grader, often insulted my work in his comments and had no respect, thinks he's the best.

wrote what he wrote on the board in my work, yet he continued to question my phrases. my work was based off his teachings, so confused why he was confused. did not teach material he asked questions on, insensitive towards others and thinks he is above all, stay away.

dont understand his high ratings. man practically degraded people's knowledge and expected them to be philosophical wizards, kids dropped like flies in lectures and he was the one upset/rather than looking at himself in the mirror. gives no feedback and has no respect for students, stay away if you're not a lover of philosophy.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I had the chance of having Prof. Harding at Johns Hopkins in the MLA program. Amazing professor that can make philosophy interesting instead of boring. Makes one question on human conditions. This man is certainly going to have a stellar academic career. He is very knowledgeable about his field and an excellent communicator and professor!

I took this class thinking itd be an easy A to fulfill my A&H but it wasnt. Your grade consists of discussion posts, 3 exams & annotated bibliography. Discussion posts every week are easy but the exams are lecture heavy (very long and boring) and about the books (which he expects you to buy). Hes also terrible at responding and gives no feedback
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Prof. Harding really goes in depth in his lectures on the concepts covered in the readings. He is a pretty easy-going professor, and often makes the lectures interesting by telling stories here and there. The class is only graded on a few things; 3 exams and an annotated bibliography. Pay attention and the assignments should not be too difficult.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: In this class he grades 3 exams and one annotated bibliography. I never touched a book but got an A just off of his explanations of the materials in class. He does really notice when people miss continuously and does not feel bad for you if you skip class. All his exams are online and outside of class and you have about a week to do them.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: Dr. Harding is a nice guy. He expects a lot of reading to be done but he goes over everything in class as well. Keeps it interesting with lots of personal stories. Grades were two ONLINE exams, an annotated bibliography, and a final paper. Take notes on everything he says and you'll be okay.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: Dr. Halem is one of the sweetest professors. He's very knowledgeable and passionate about his work, his students, cares deeply about his course. 1000% would recomend taking a course taught by him.
Very knowledgeable and helpful professor. Not hard on grading.

This is a good subject as they're is only one project to be implemented and it is peer rated for most part. Only those who are genuinely interested in Software oriented computing should take it and you can expect Dr. Halem to be there to help you.

Dr. Halverson is a great professor, you can tell he's passionate about teaching. engaging lectures most of the time. there are some classes you just come and take notes on a documentary. i only got a C because I missed a few quizzes online. there is no homework so be sure to do the quizzes, your grade relies heavely on them.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Nice guy overall, and super passionate about his field. Lecture heavy, but it could also be because I took his class during the summer. Exams were about average, but he does give out study guides. He let us sit through a video conference with the National Weather Service prior to an extreme storm hitting us, which was super cool to see in person!

this class was very test heavy but extra credit was offered! lecture is just him reading off the PP.. just make sure for your exams study the study guide and do all the NOVA quizzes and you will be good! but his lectures had me falling asleep.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This guy and clearly loves what he does. I found his lectures interesting. He gives study guides which are very similar to the actual exam. Exams are usually about 50 m/c questions. My biggest grip is exams are about 3/4 of your grade. I wish there was more content to offset those exam grades.

Halverson is passionate about what he teaches, lectures are engaging. I recommend taking notes in lecture, exam questions are pulled from lecture & study guides are exactly like the exam. Novas are easy and engaging with 2 attempts & lots of time. Honestly the easiest class I've taken. Pay attention to his lectures, and you'll find it interesting.

Doesn't even put the answers in the study guide , literally what a study guide is for !!!!!!!!!!! Never hands back test . 
Doesn't post all the slides !!!!! So if you can't write fast or don't take all the pictures you're screwed !
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Prof. Halverson gives great lectures with relevant examples and visuals. He's a wonderful speaker and never makes anyone feel dumb for asking questions during his lectures. Even if you are generally not very good at math or science, there is absolutely no math involved and he makes the science seem very simple.

Incredible professor! Lectures were straightforward and I learned so much. Still important to do the weekly readings. The TA was amazing and made study guides and held study sessions for everything that was going to be on the exams. Genuinely enjoyed his classes and would 100% would take again!
I enjoyed this class. Study for exams well. The TA he had during the semester I took this (Spring 22) was very helpful and held study sessions for exams.
The professors lectures are interesting and held my interest through humor. Tests and assignments are based off lecture and group projects. Overall, Professor Halverson is a great professor.

If you have the opportunity to take a class with Prof Halverson, do it. He loves the material he teaches, wants students to succeed, he gives challenging/ brilliant lectures, and he posts his powerpoints on blackboard. He's a super sweet guy who has so much knowledge in his field. He loves Earth Science so much, he will inspire you to love it too.

Jeffery Halverson is a delight. I find him very amusing and approachable, and the material is relatively easy. Lectures are fascinating, and every once in a while he will make you laugh so hard you almost fall out of your chair. Final questions are just taken from the 3 midterms, so if you study those you absolutely can get 100%.

Overall just a great teacher. Makes the class interesting and involves you by having all or most of the notes handwritten on the board. I would suggest his class to anyone who was thinking of taking the class

Professor Halverson was a good teacher, very enthusiastic about his field. There is a lot of reading with this course, and you need to be diligent with it since the study guides aren't a huge help. He gives quite a few chances for good extra credit.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Final exams based directly on his midterm exams, gives a lot of extra credit assignments, drops lowest exam scores. His class was a breeze.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Great professor and really easy class. If you're looking for an easy lab science this is your move, you only have to really show up to get an A.

I realized that going to class was basically pointless. The book will teach you more than Professor Halverson ever could. He's a smart man, but unfortunately a mediocre teacher, at best. He stands at the front of the room teaching from a white board (that nobody can see) and teaches things that aren't on the exam.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: According to most of the good reviews on this page, Professor Halverson seems pretty amazing. Unfortunately, I had a rude awakening. You can tell he knows much about this subject, but I don't think that he recognizes that nobody knows what he's talking about. The study guides have nothing to do with the exams. It's useless trying to study. AVOID.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Halverson is one of the best professors at UMBC- his lectures and powerpoints are engaging and humorous, and his grading and overall conduct of the course in terms of assignments/etc. is very laid back.  I wish he taught more classes than just two or three.

Nice guy, but he made lots of mistakes. His syllabus claimed that we did not have to complete one of two problems sets. However, we informed us in class and via email that we did in fact have to do it. This was around finals week, and he only gave us two extra days to do it, and did not offer any help for those who decided not to do the first set.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: He's a really nice professor and has really good lecture slides that he puts online. As long as you do the readings you know what he's going to talk about during lecture. He doesn't take attendance so if you miss lecture it's no big deal. Tests are easy if you at least kind of payed attention to material and they're all online (smartbook).

He's a really nice professor and offers help if you ask for it. His lectures are kinda boring and he just goes through powerpoint slides that are in the textbook. Since you have to the smartbook assignments with the readings, as long as you read, you don't even need to go to class. His lectures are boring and he puts his slides on blackboard

One of the best professors I've had at UMBC. He kept class interesting by explaining things clearly, and providing real-life examples. There were 5 exams and a 10 page paper. I'd say the exams were easy to fair- some were trickier than others. If you have a chance to take a class with him, do it!!
Awesome, in every way

For a science class, you can't get much easier than matching questions on all of the exams. Just make sure to study from the study questions he posts and you should get an A. There's also extra credit.

He was very boring and redundant in my opinion. Many of his lectures started with a forecast unrelated to the given lecture. He also seemed to have a tendency to become distract by student questions, meaning he would answer it but continue to talk about it. Laptops aren't allowed in his class and about half of the semester wasn't in the book.

This class was awful. Not worth your time.The man is all over the place with his subject and youll never know what was actually going to be on the test because the tests consists of real world problems and equations...leaving everyone guessing.The Final was BS,it was 100 definitions and you must use a guide you create in order to guess the answers.

Not a great class. Tons of information to learn.  Exams are very hard.  He is a nice guy, but he is all over the place with the material.  Lots of annoying labs due everyday as well.  Constantly revising the syllabus, it got pretty confusing.  DONT TAKE IF YOU DONT NEED TO.
one of my favorite professors at umbc. lectures are well prepared, informative and are presented in a fun way. exams can be hard. definitely recommend taking his classes.

He is very nice and is very interested in the topic he's teaching. He uses alot of real life examples, which keeps me interested. Quizes once a week on vocab, easy if you have looked over the words. Study guides for exams show exactly what will be on it so tests are pretty easy if u do the guide. Pay attention in class and you'll be fine!
easy going
Really chill professor, took some assignments away when we didn't really need them towards the final. Not a harsh grader, lectures are fun and you should take him for a relatively easy A.
For a class that I deemed as less important, it somehow became my favorite class for my entire semester. Hes funny and chill, take him fs.

Funny and understanding, but disorganized. Changes assignment instructions frequently, so there's no incentive to start early.
