Grading and feedback can be harsh, since it's not clear what he's looking for. Said our midterm would be a crossword puzzle, and ended up being short essay (which we found out the day of the exam).

The structure of grades changed like three times during the semester but they were all to help us students. Tried getting rid of the major paper for weekly discussion posts but the school wouldn't let him. Tried getting rid of the final but opted for an easy assignment you could do if your grade was on the cusp. Wants best for students. Take him.

I think my semester in particular, Heiss slightly ramped up the workload, so take this review with a grain of salt. Mostly graded by two assignments besides exams, a 2500 word paper and a group presentation. He has a lot of passion but also expects the same passion from the students. If you're just taking 304 cause it's required, not recommended.
reviews.rating_tags: So many papers--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Such a fun prof! He's a wonderful speaker, commands attention well, and has great charisma. You will need to present in class so if you're an anxious person maybe avoid this class. Not too many assignments & always keeps it fun. This class is fun if you're a yapper (me).
He's a great lecturer and good guy but he takes forever to grade and isn't clear on what he wants for the assignments.

Professor Heiss is an amazing lecturer; his topics are very interesting and reflects the current events. There's no clear grading criteria (no rubric), yet he grades the assignments based on certain standards. Grades given to you are based on comparison to how others are doing (so there's a distribution??). He takes a while to reply to emails.

Heiss is without a doubt, one of the professors of all time. His lectures are amazing. However, grading assignments are his downfall. He never gives any rubric for his assignments and takes off points heavily. He will make you email him to resolve issues, and then proceed to never respond.His grading will truly frustrate you. INCONSISTENT
He's the best and he's funny. TAKE HIM

Amazing professor. Want you to learn how to present well and learn ethical frameworks in the process. Understand that we are busy and is lenient if you talk to him about extending deadlines ahead of time. You will have to show up to class every day because participation matters, but its a fun class. You choose your groups. take him if you can!

Funny, doesn't take himself too seriously, and gets class discussing the different topics. Very laid back, only 3 papers throughout the semester which are graded leniently, occasional homework, and a final group presentation. Tests/quizzes are online and very easy.

Super chill guy, is super relatable, and knows what is happening in the world. Is forced to assign 3 Papers by the department but still graded lenient, homework is easy, one group project and midterm, and the final are online and super easy, with no right or wrong answer on them, just your stance on topics. Easy A if you just go to class.
Professor Heiss is awesome. He made me really care about certain issues in the world and made me grow as a person. I would definitely take him again in another class. I would 100% recommend.
Easy and fun class with a funny professor! Super chill since we can look at the slide lecture notes outside of class.

Interesting class. Covered many, many topics. Exams were straightforward from the slides. Two long papers and a group project.  Do all the assignments and you will get a B. Work a little bit harder and you can get an A.
Best Professor I Ever Had! TAKE HIM!!!!!  Also, No Textbook for the course!

If you go to class and do the work you'll get an A or B. He's a good teacher but obviously it's up to you to put in the time for a better grade. He gave us some real world work experience like public speaking and advice on making it. Keeping it real professor Heiss!
light workload, lenient grader. The class is required attendance for all sections but he made it interesting.

Weekly homework thats basically read an article or two and then write about it. two big papers that arent too bad, but the rubric was hard to understand for hte first one. Grades pretty leniently and theres no final
Helpful teacher, easily approachable. Grades fairly and as long as you go to class you'll be fine.

In his lectures, he uses equations coming from thin air, which is "all in the book," and generally unhelpful. He will take time to explain things if you ask, but you will do most of your learning on your own anyways. Luckily, he's not a crazy grader, but you'll probably be well off by just reading the book.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: To be blunt, his lectures suck. The fact that he follows the book closely is a weakness since he doesn't provide much value in his lectures, but it's good since you can easily reference what he says in the book. And, he is very kind and caring to his students, and he definitely gives you a chance to succeed, which helps balance his lesser aspects.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Caring--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: His lecture style is just copying his notes, which are straight from the book, down to a T. If you have the drive to self-learn, you're better off just reading the textbook. You'll have to do that anyways, since his lectures aren't very coherent to begin with. He's not a bad guy: just not a good lecturer. Grading is simple and fair.

Prof. H was a really good professor. The grades were pretty much all textbook HW and exams, which aren't too difficult if you understand the material. The lectures are kind of boring, but he is passionate about the material and you can ask questions for good answers.

To anyone giving Professor Henriksen a poor grade is wrong. I have never had a professor so passionate about a subject; it is very admirable. Professor Henriksen is also the smartest professor I have had at UMBC, he is literally a living book. 10/10 professor.

The class has a lot of material so he teaches a bit fast and tends to gloss over some more important derivations. If you are active in class and as questions though he will start to loosen up and provide clearer examples. Also is a fairly lenient grader and gives a lot of credit for showing your work.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: This is a tough one; you see the mix of good and bad reviews he has? Theyre both right. He can be boring sometimes, exciting others. Comes alive when students start participating, which is awesome. But glosses over hardcore derivations which is unnerving sometimes. You get the feeling like you dont really know what youre doing, but overall not bad.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Caring--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Super chill class & professor. Focus on the study guides when studying for the midterms/finals, a majority of his questions are the exact same as they are on the study guides he gives you. Homework is super easy but is weighted as heavily as your final so make sure you're turning that in every week and you should get a good grade.

Lectures were pretty boring, but very informative. Since it was online all the lectures were recorded but you should still watch them or attend lectures. He only gave us 1 homework assignment a week so he was pretty flexible. Test content reflects notes from lectures and textbook. He was ok fr.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Astrobiology was a great class. Thank you professor! I appreciate how flexible you were with homework and lectures. Have a good summer!

Professor Henriksen went the extra mile when the course went online. I got behind on homework and he let me make all of them up. His multiple choice tests were fair. There were practice tests for all of the exams. I loved the class.
Professor Henriksen is very student centered. He even helped me with another physics class. Knows a lot about the subject.

Truthfully, this class was a remedial course. It is honestly a set up. There is no help at the Math and Science Tutoring center or the Physics tutorial center. The teacher himself is barely a resource unless you are trying to bring your grade up at the end of the semester. The only thing good about this class is the curve at the end of the year.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: His lectures were pretty interesting. Homework is math heavy. Be there for the exam reviews!

Very knowledgeable on the subject it's just he's not very good at teaching the information. He's a caring professor and wants students to understand, but unfortunately he's not aware of how boring he can be. You have to find your own way to connect with him and I guarantee the class will be doable. Study/ review each chapter and you should be fine.

I really enjoyed Modern Physics with Professor Henriksen. He covers interesting topics from the book, but not all of the book. He is very clear and well organized. He likes students to participate in class and asks us questions. I am definitely taking another class with him as he also teaches higher level astronomy classes.

Henriksen's lectures are absolutely terrible. His numerous mistakes and frequent omission of necessary information make it impossible to take anything useful away from this class. To make things worse, the textbook he uses is a typo ridden mess that fails to provide basic explanations for almost every topic. He offers no advice on exam prep. 0/5

Lectures were impossible to follow being so scatter-brained but the book didn't reflect the problems asked in quiz's and exams, which are the only graded assignments. nothing is online so nothing was learned and nothing was taken from this course except for pages of the worst notes I've ever taken. Don't waste your money/time people.

Professor Henriksen is very knowledgeable about astrobiology. The lectures are interesting and he is a good lecturer. If you come to class and take notes its pretty easy to get an A or B in this class. I would definitely recommend this class if you need a science elective.

Although he is a nice guy, this prof. can't teach. DO NOT TAKE THIS COURSE IF YOU ARE NOT A PHYSICS MAJOR-your chances of doing well in this class would be very low. Quizzes are beast in his class. He has the worst handwriting ever. He doesn't follow the text as close as you want him to. You really don't catch the important things he says in class.

Prof. Henrikson knows alot about the course material. His lectures have alot of details but it makes it much easier to understand the concepts. I would say he is by far one of the most intellectual professors I've had. Really made stellar physics interesting to me.

Can't read his handwriting, which is essential for all of the derivations which he writes on the board.  Talks to the board.  Doesn't see if your hand is up.  Assumes that you know everything about physics, calc, and astronomy before taking his intro class.  Way too hard.  Beware!

The most horrible teacher i've had. Does not think before he talks, does not know the material. He stops frequently and asks for our book to figure out how to finish a derivation. If you ask a simple question he will beat around the bush for 5 minutes and in the end not answer what you asked. I wouldnt trust him to teach even high school.
this professor didn't make physics easy for me but he made it understandable. his lecture style is clear and easy to follow, if you can read his handwritting. one of the best professors at umbc.
I think this guy is a great teacher if you like physics. His lectures aren't bad and he likes to help students. Definitely one of the best I've had in science.

I got a B, and I had to work for it! If you want multiple choice take someone else, he expects you to be able to work problems. Can't complain tho cause he is very clear and  spends alot of time helping students outside of class.
I got a lot out of this course. The prof LOVES astronomy and explains it well.
Enjoys working with students...a bright guy
This guy singlehandedly discourages anyone who might have had a slight interest in astronomy from ever following through.
No Comments

He was one of the worst professors I've ever had.  He made people look stupid when they asked questions, solved things incorrectly in class, didn't follow the syllabus and gave horrible exams.  He even told my friend she wasn't smart enough to be a physics major.  Avoid him if you can.

Dr. Kamal is a great researcher/professor. He explained well but the content was narrow not showing the essence of the concept but specifics. Study hard independently do problems but ask him questions. He is really fair in his tests and grading (if you argue for points he is willing to give them back). He wants you to do well but it's more on you.

Dr. Herana is a mediocre professor. He gives minimal direction for what to study on exams despite being 60% of your grade. However, he leniently grades on exams (so long as you go to his office hours) and the actual exam content is not too difficult. Exams aside, his lecture slides are straight from the textbook and irrelevant information is added.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This professor is quite literally the WORST professor i have seen at this school. Does nothing for students its like he hates teaching and is only doing it because he has to. Very boring lectures and he rips the slides straight from the textbook. It takes so little effort to be a good person and yet this professor does his best to be inconsiderate.

RMP needs to allow 0 for a rating as that would be mine. He's horrible! I have never had a professor NOT teach material that we need for our future, not to mention lab. He uses the textbook for slides which is close to plagiarism except he cites it. No homework practice problems so no guidance for tests. He obviously hates teaching and we lose out.

Don't take if unless you want to learn everything yourself. Slides literally word-for-word from the textbook and didn't explain how to do any practice problems. Actively dodges answering questions or straight up tells people to read the textbook. Will never have any idea what the exams are about. Luckily other than ACS final they were easy.

Final grades are  60% from the lecture course and 40% from the lab course. Of the lecture course, grading is 15% for each of two free response midterms, 25% the ACS multiple choice final exam, and 5% class participation. This guy reads his slides that are ripped from the textbook word for word and he talks to the board. Doesn't answer questions.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Lecture: reading through slides ripped from the textbook. Worse, he could never answer students' questions- he always blew them off, telling them to read the textbook before class, thus no one engaged during lecture. Exams weren't that difficult, but trying to find out what we would be tested on was like pulling teeth. No learning objectives.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Great teacher! I would love to take a class with her again. I learned and understood more of the topics that I found difficult than ever before. Fantastic. She gives lots of chances for extra credit, take them!
DO NOT TAKE A CLASS WITH HER IT IS AWFUL AND SHE IS RUDE

Professor Hemmis is hilarious and can easily navigate very tricky discussions and topics. She makes sure to be available for students to ask questions after class or during office hours. You do sign an attendance sheet, but it doesn't count for anything except for her knowing who regularly shows up in case they need a grade bump at the end.

This class is very discussion-based, but she will never call on you to speak; it is strictly voluntary. There are some interesting/difficult topics to have cordial discussions about, but she navigates these well. She is always willing to talk to students after class or during office hours about grades or other topics which is nice.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Professor Hemmis is great. She is so in touch with the real world and has a great awareness of social issues. Assignments are easy as long as you are paying attention in class. She delivers lectures very well and is so funny! Would absolutely take another class with her.

Professor Hemmis made a dreadful and difficult course much less stressful and taxing. Grading criteria is clear and lectures/labs helped so much, not to mention she explains things super great and is really funny! Very accessible as well as the TA is accessible, this course was an awesome choice for a research requirement and Hemmis is awesome!
Don't really get why she has bad ratings. Professor Hemmis's class had such a fun atmosphere and the discussions are fun. Easy A if you are an attentive student and getting work done on time.

*Fall semester* Love the professor. Amazing lectures. Very easy class if you do all the assignments, a lot of small writing assignments, and one big essay with a big project. Attendance doesn't matter but still does it to help boost a grade if you have an 89% or something.

Prof Hemmis is the best professor I've ever had. If you do the work and come to class you WILL get a good grade. She offers LOTS of help with labs. Great communication, absolutely hilarious. TA does the grading. She's very flexible with late assignments. If you do the practice on the mindtaps you get extra credit. Testing is in person on paper.
Not a great class. It was not formatting well on Blackboard making it all feel claustrophobic, overwhelming and unorganized. I had to drop out because of one assignment.

I honestly don't understand why her rating is so low. It's pretty hard to get anything below a C in her class. She gives students extra credit opportunities, offers exam reviews, and helps students during labs. Her exams are a bit difficult, but if you study you'll be fine. She's very caring and genuinely wants her students to succeed.

She seems a nice person but her class is boring. She talks a lot of extra stuff more than the class materials. This class is an easy A if you are an attentive student. The grading is done by the TA's, which makes it inconvenient because some of the grades were not posted on time. You have to do Lots of MindTap and labs each week that's annoying.

Professor Hemmis is a great instructor. Between her and the TA's, there was no confusion on how to succeed in the course. Prof. Hemmis was very accommodating for students and their requests. She also has unique and clear ways of explaining concepts. Glad to take this core course with her and her TA's. I learned a lot and really enjoyed the labs.

Professor Hemmis is a reasonable professor, although communicating with her and the TAs was rather difficult. All of the grading in this class was left up to the TAs and by the week of finals, we are still missing 40% of our grades in the gradebook. The class itself is fair, but would be better in person.

Professor Hemmis is very passionate about the material taught in this class. I loved watching the short films and videos during lecture. This course was super interesting and made you empathetic for drug addicts. Take home quizzes, in class assignments, three exams, all but the paper assignment, and a film analysis is required for this.

Unfortunately professor Hemmis didn't finish the semester with my class and I dropped the class (through no fault of her own, covid learning and math simply did not agree with my brain), but for the time I knew her she was a lovely teacher who really wanted to make things as easy for us as possible. She all but let us google answers sometimes, too.

Originally had an adjunct professor before Professor Hemmis took over in the middle of the semester, so that was an adjustment. She seemed all over the place honestly, she didnt really explain things very well. The labs were annoying and this class was SO boring but I needed it for my major. Luckily we got some extra credit from the aides.

This class was actually very difficult and there were many assignments. Professor Hemmis also took a while to grade assignments and we didnt get feedback until the end of the semester. I would not recommend taking a course taught by professor Hemmis
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The grading criteria wasnt clear and we assigned somewhat irrelevant assignments at times
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Test heavy--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: I love sociology but hated this class. I'm not sure if it's because the entire thing was political science or the way the professor taught but either way I would never take a class again with this professor
This was supposed to be a sociology class yet the entire thing was political science

I really did not like professor hemmis' method of teaching. She talked about a lot of material that wasn't quite relevant to the course and she made us watch a film that contained very little relevance. I definitely will not be taking a future course with her
She took points off my papers for literally nothing and feedback was terrible. I do not recommend this professor

Well first of all I always get A's so it was no surprise that I received an A in this class however I had to work harder than I ever had despite this class being an elective. If you are looking for an easy A this is not the class!
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: She's super sweet and passionate about what she teaches! Always wants to hear your thoughts and provides PowerPoints that are easy to follow. Exams are easy and based off the study guides/Powerpoints!

I love her. She is compassionate and the assignments are fairly easy, you just need to make time for them. She is funny, there are weekly quizes, attendance is mandatory though, but youll actually want to come to class.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious

reviews.comment: Highly recommend taking her class! Shes super easy! We have weekly quizzes, but it's online! On tuesdays, its lectures and I usually didnt come to class! On Thursdays, we usually did group discussions and had in-class assignments! Her exams were honestly the most easiest exams I've ever taken!

I took Hemmis for SOCY 300, 330, 353, and 374. She is one of my favorite professors at UMBC. Her exams are based off of her study guides and she does not try to trick you at all. You have to go to class to do her in-class assignments which are super easy and worth a lot of your grade. We have quizzes every week and they are super easy.

Mrs. Hemmis is a GREAT teacher, I will have taken 3 classes with by the end of this semester. She tells you EXACTLY what is due & when it is due. She wants you to do well, & doesn't trick. She can seem very strict on the first day of class, but don't let that deter you, she is fabulous; print off the schedule she gives you and just give effort!

Super nice professor. You will learn a lot. HW are online, you just need to use the readings or textbooks to find the answers. Memorize the study guide she gives you. It is literally the test. And she will give you one of the questions for the exam.

I would love to have this professor for all my classes- she's the best! And this class helps you become more open-minded and respectful to all people. She gives everything you need in her ppts and there's no cumulative final. Straightforward, a little behind on grading, but amazing. You can only fail the class if you don't pay attention.

Prof. Hemmis is a great lecturer and her study guides are very helpful. Exams are straight forward. You have to write short essays on her exams and multiple choice questions. Essay part may be a little difficult. She will help you when you need it so go to her office hours. I recommend taking her class.
There are specific days you have to come in to do the classwork and the rest you can skip but her class is interesting.

There are quizzes everyday for each reading, but the couple lowest are dropped at end of the semester. Quizzes are easy, not multiple choice though, and you're allowed to use notes taken. Other assignments were using readings and relating them to certain outside sources, and she gave good study guides for exams (multiple choice, T/F, short & long )
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Prof. Hemmis is a great professor! We have weekly quizzes on the chapters we are going to go over that whole week. We only had 2 exams: midterm and final. One group project and two papers to write. She gives great feedback to your essays and really cares about her students. I definitely recommend taking her class!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: This professor was my favorite for my Fall Semester. She was one of the most interesting, thought-provoking, and eye-opening professors I have had. Lectures were not boring at all. Really understanding when it comes to personal issues. Open-minded. Very passionate about the topics she teaches. Exams are straightforward. Open-note quizzes.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: The class material is pretty easy. Your grade is basically comprised of weekly quizzes based of the readings, a few easy projects, and 2 exams. She also gives multiple opportunities for extra credit, though if you go to class regularly you won't even need the extra credit. Lectures are interesting and so are the readings. Take Hemmis she's great!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Ton of reading on hundreds of cases. Clearly knows what she is talking about, but material is incredibly dry. Wouldn't recommend this course to anyone who isn't planning on going to Law School, unless you're fascinated by Constitutional case law.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Dr. Hinkle is very well educated and knows what she is talking about. She's really into the subject matter and made class interesting and understandable. She is very nice and approachable. Everything on the midterm and exam was basically straight from the lectures. Take a class with her! She's the best!
great professor, lectures are actually detailed with the majority of the information given on exams. very enthusiastic and negotiates with students. take any class with her.
One of the hardest professors I've ever taken a course with, but he makes it rigorous so that you can learn a lot. Very knowledgeable and really wants students to be engaged in class.

He is one of the best if not the best professor UMBC has. He is an excellent teacher who does not believe in spoon feeding students. He makes them work and expects more from them which usually does not settle well with undergrad crowd enhance bad reviews. He is an absolute guru of his field. He can be strict at time but for legitimate reasons.

I successfully avoided this professor for 4 semesters but he was the only one teaching databases this semester. One of the WORST professors I ever had. Not helpful at all, very vague in class, homework was very difficult and did not relate to what was on the exams AT ALL. If possible, do not take him and if you have no choice, I'm sorry.

Smart man, horrible teacher. Always very ambiguous and likes reiterating theories and definitions rather than explaining them. Wouldn't give partial credit on homework, and if so, not much. Tests were kind of hard. The final project was the worst. Gives no explanation of what it is or what we need to do. Avoid him.

His tests were hard but were purely on material covered fully in class. Class average for both midterms was about 25/50. Homework is not directly from the book but can be easily solved by referencing the book. Good lecturer but he can get quite annoyed if people dont know what they are doing. Hard but not terrible

I had an A for 441 with Dr. White, but had to drop Kargupta's class after the midterm.  He tested on stuff that he didn't really cover in class, but briefly referenced in 2 minutes some time.  He doesn't care about his students at all, so there's no point talking to him outside of class either.

Nitpickiest grader I've ever encountered. Reads the first sentence to your answer then stops and writes "unclear" and gives you no credit. Doesn't bother to read the rest of your answer which explains the first part. I studied my butt off for the exams, but always got C's. I had a 4.0 until I took this jerks class.

This is by far the worst teacher I have ever taken. He is rude, he isn't smart, he hates his students, he lies to you about what is on his tests, and he has better things to do than show up for class. First test, nobody got an A. Second test, nobody got an A or a B. He says he will curve, but he's lying. Don't trust him!! AVOID AT ALL COSTS!!!

We get homework every class + two projects; one final video project and one group project with a student from Japan (COIL). The projects are very heavily weighted, and half of lecture is the warmup (which is conversation practise). The other half is going over a worksheet/reading. Assignments graded on completion (apart from projects).

I took a lot of classes with her and wish umbc had other profs to choose from for these classes. She ranges from being nice to being rude a lot. Slow grader. Classes are super disorganized and you have to hunt for the easter eggs that are your due dates and assignments. Directions always left most of the class confused.

A 2.5. I had her from 301-309. Your Japanese will improve if you are active and speak up, but it can be hard if you aren't the best as she will poke fun at you a bit. If you vibe her style of humor and the topics she picks it's fine, but if you don't you're just kind of stuck with her for all 4 300-level classes since there are no other teachers.

Interesting and informative class w/ understanding and knowledgeable prof. Each class we had a discussion based on hw readings, then Dr Hoogenboom would give us more information on the topic. Grades were based on a variety of assignments (movie reflections, discussions, final paper and project, small group discussion collab w/ Japanese students)
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: My Japanese has improved so much because of Hoogenboom Sensei and her methods. From 301-309, I noticed a major improvement in my oral, reading, and writing comprehension skills. If you're serious about Japanese, take 301, 302, 319, and 309. I promise if you show up, speak up, and put effort in, you will see major results.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious

reviews.comment: I also took her for JPNS319 &JPNS301, as well as MLL316&MLL333. If you are serious about Japanese, I highly suggest taking her courses. Yes they are tough, but participation and showing up will make it easy. Most of the class involves speaking about various topics in Japanese so showing up is key if you want to pass and improve.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: If you want to learn Japanese and are serious about it, she is 100% worth it. 301& up, her lectures are in Japanese and she enforces Japanese only speaking environment. It's hard at first but of you show up, study and participate, you WILL improve on oral communication and listening skills. My Japanese has improved drastically thanks to her.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: She grades pretty harsh. She isn't clear on what she expects for the writing assignments. So, trying to get a perfect score seems unlikely. She picks favorites and grades like a snail. I will avoid her for future classes. She doesn't submit grades until months after the assignments have been submitted, so you have no idea what your grade is.

If you are really into learning Japanese for your future career or having a strong desire for learning Japanese as a foreign language. You should go with her until the end of your undergrad year. You may think, she just gives you hard time and lots of assignment, but seriously if you can concentrate on what you've been doing. You will get the 'A'

Good introduction to translating Japanese, I think all the students gained insight into the issues involved and found out if they liked it. Many genres, including manga and video. Most feedback was through peer review. Not a hard grader.
Super sweet lady. Extremely easy class but lots of readings. On average 3 readings a week but all are easy. Would totally take it again with her!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: She is the best Japanese teacher I have ever had. Attendance is like 12% of your grade so be sure to show up. She also groups quizzes and homework together to try to buffer your score and tries to not make the final have much weight on your grade. She's always willing to help after class but it is DIFFICULT. This is a 300 level language.

Yeah, just don't take her. While I passed with an A, she's extremely passive aggressive and expects you to finish her (mostly rhetorical) questions and sentences. Just lots of awkward sitting in a circle staring at each other. Taught us from a syllabus that dated back to the early 90s. Out of touch professor.
She is an alright professor. I had to work hard to get an A in her class but if you talk to her or go to the writing center you should be fine!

Despite the fact that she comes off as sweet, she can be a very intimidating professor. She is a very harsh grader on papers. However, I have gotten through the class with an A without doing the readings. The class is mostly just BORING to sit through, and mostly unnecessary for learning how to tutor after the first 2 weeks.
Very easy class as long as you put a little bit of time into it and come to class on a semi regular basis.  All her papers are pretty short and simple, and she is helpful when going over the,.

She is a weird grader in the sense that she doesn't give out many A's and she doesn't give out many C's, either. Most of her grades are B's. Her class is the most boring class I've had. She doesn't actually teach you anything about how to write. She just makes you read something and she talks about it. The essays have nothing to do with the reading

Pretty boring - I often fell asleep in class. Seems to expect low-level writing, but grades harshly anyway, with little justification. Indecipherable cursive, making her few notes on the blackboard and her paragraph-long notes at the end of your essays pretty frustrating.
This was not a very hard class, but her teaching style is extraordinarily boring.  She doesn't talk with much enthusiasm and chuckles a bit when nobody responds to a question.

There is a perscriptive element to this class, and a lot of readings.  Some of the assignments are long, but you can usually choose your own topic.  Revisions on essays are sometimes allowed, and the final exam is a short out-of-class reflection essay.  Warning: only take this class if you are fine with working in the 80 degree writing center.

Professor Hickernell co-teaches ENGL 395 with Professor Fitzpatrick, which is a class on how to tutor in the Writing Center. I wish they had developed a more hands-on curriculum rather than a textbook-based one. There are a few large writing assignments, but stay on top of the tutor memos and you will be fine.

Hickernell is not a bad professor at all. She is very nice and not a hard grader. I usually did my papers the night before they were due and got a B on most of them. Grade consists of 5 essays which are pretty easy. The seminar portion is worth 15% of your grade and is definitly worth taking for an extra credit! I wouldn't mind taking her again.

Garbage. That's what this professor is. She grades absurdly hard. She is always unclear. I have no idea what my grade is. I have learned absolutely nothing from coming to this class. You are better off being a human crash dummy than taking this class, as it is less painful, more enjoying, and a million times more rewarding.

Very nice older woman. I hate english and got a B for the semester. Read the required Novel, you will spend 2-3 weeks discussing it. Grades are based on 5 essays throughout the semester and a Final Out-of-class Essay. Semester essays are given a second chance for revision to bring up your grade. The Y sect counts as 15% and is easy. TAKE THIS CLASS

Took her last semester for Technical Writing. We were ditto-ed to death. It was an easy class if you did things her way but impossible if you differed. She makes student hand in outlines and more for assignments. She was rude, and condescending if students asked questions. My resume ,which she berated, got me a job that I am very pleased with.

OMG I still don't know my grade for the class and it is the end of the semester!!! I have no clue, she does not use blackboard, and assignments are usually sent via e-mail at 8pm the night before they are due. She is also quite boring....VERY BORING!!!! AVOID HER LIKE THE PLAGUE!!! But she is a nice person.

Yes, she does give lots of handouts. And most of them are useless. I have a hard time keeping track of papers due to the sheer amount of random handouts in my binder.  She is a harsh grader and never gives a good reason as to why she gives you a bad grade.  None of what she says makes sense, and her class is boring.
lots of work and handouts. very helpful. she knows her stuff. i would take another class with her

UUUUGH! It's so not worth it. Expect at least a 3 inch binder full of handouts that you never use. But, unfortunately, in order to tutor in the Writing Center you have to endure this class! There is a ton of work. Expect to write at least two huge papers that require about 20 hours of work to complete to standard. Field Work too.

I got more handouts from her than I got total from 4 other classes combined. The assignments are extremely time consuming, demanding and boring. What's worse is that she thinks everyone should write a certain formulaic way (outlines, forcasting etc). To top it off, this class is co-taught Ms. Fitzpatrick, the resident grammar nut. Not Fun!

I got more handouts from her than I got total from 4 other classes combined. The assignments are extremely time consuming, demanding and boring. What's worse is that she thinks everyone should write a certain formulaic way (outlines, forcasting etc). To top it off, this class is co-taught Ms. Fitzpatrick, the resident grammar nut. Not Fun!

Too much busywork and so many handouts I needed 2 binders. Some of it is helpful, but lots of it is just repetition. She's easy to approach, but sometimes seems condescending. The class isn't too hard, its just a lot of time spent on unecessary stuff. Not the most fun class, but pretty easy to pass.
She runs over the time a lot. There's a class time limit and I don't like staying late.
Completely boring class topics... She said I was the best person in my section and I still got a B. Lot of meaningless busy work and "journaling".

she give out sooooooooooo many handouts, and a lot of readings to do. you basically can skip most of the readings. cept sometimes she'll test you on then but no prob cause u can read it as ur testing. theres a paper due about every 2 weeks or so. class is tooooo boring, and if ur falling asleep she'll call on u. class doesnt seem that hard, as long as you come to class mostly and just do the work.

Very disorganized and would make you feel like your an idiot even when you knew what was going on. Class wasnt too hard to get through. Just make sure that you papers are solid. She is in charge of the Writting Center in the Library and is nit-picky about every little detail.

She is bad. she knows the course stuff, but she repeats her self.this was an arugumentative writing class,and we had to answer to "what makes an argument?" so many times she is unorganized,and has killed many trees with her many handouts.she is a very difficult grader, and absolutely buthcers a paper.dont get papers back on time to know our errors.

She's not THAT bad. But she can be a bit confusing for some people, and is a pretty harsh grader. I had her for a few classes, and my writing definitely improved in her classes... but those were some of the hardest classes I took at UMBC. Think of how hard a UMBC science class is, and that's how hard her English classes are.
She means well, but her lecture style is so dry.  Her assignments are often unclear and I found her unapproachable.
No Comments

If you think English is an easy A, do not take this class. Hickernell is very tough and challenging. She will tear all you papers apart for futile mistakes. She will also kill a forest with all the handouts you get.
EASY grader. Requires a ~2 page reading every week and exams are written format. There is an easy research paper at the very end. Everything is sent through email, so PAY ATTENTION to EMAIL.
Took him freshman year and by far one of the best professors on this campus. I had him virtually and wish I could have had him in person. Very engaging and interesting class.

A great professor! The readings he provided were insightful and thought-provoking. I learned a lot from his class and the final paper allowed me to express my ideas and perspectives on such an interesting topic. You can easily do well if you pay attention. The reflections on the readings will help you in the long run; take good notes!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Respected--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Very sweet man, lectures were very interesting and he was an overall very friendly and caring professor. Easily one of the best I have had at UMBC. There was a weekly reading and paper due, with a midterm, final, and a 10 page research paper too. I do not recommend this class with another writing heavy class as I was overwhelmed.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--So many papers--Caring

reviews.comment: He's a very great down to earth professor. Very easy grader with VERY interesting lectures. You do have to read and submit a page reflection each week which are completion. There's two free response midterms and one research paper, again easy grader. Entirely relies off emails

He is a very sweet guy and he was a pleasure to listen to every week. He opens the class up for discussion and answers any questions. He assigns work by email and the class is VERY writing-heavy. There's a reflection every week, the midterm and final are both 2 papers each AND there is a 10-pg research paper. And make sure you participate in class.

Professor Hochberg is so king and easygoing. Weekly/biweekly reflections on readings that he puts on Bb. Midterm essay, research essay, and final essay. Once a week online meetings. Overall, very easy class and kind professor.

One of the best professors at UMBC. I took him twice. He is very easy-going, respectful, and cares about his students. Professor Hoch is a wealth of knowledge in the History department. Only assigns 1-2 page reaction papers for HW. One mid-term paper and one final.

Prof Hochberg is a very nice professor! Cares about his students and their grades by providing feedback. Weekly 1-2 page reaction papers & 1 research paper. Has a midterm and final exam. It's an easy class. He posts some articles online but some readings are in the textbook(s). Again, easy class! I'm also taking him for HIST 355
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: hochberg runs all of his classes the same way. a weekly reading and essay, one take home midterm and one take home final. as long as you listen to what he says during the lecture and complete the weekly essays you won't have trouble getting an A.

Okay class, but the professor is super sweet! Honestly didn't get that much out of going to lectures, but they added a bit of context to the reading. Feedback he gives is really well thought out and he's extremely encouraging and personal.
great professor, interesting lectures and engages class a lot. not that difficult but a lot of writing
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--SO MANY PAPERS

reviews.comment: professor is very nice and caring. He is hilarious and tries his best to assist students. If you do your work, you should be fine.

One of my absolute favorite professors ever.  I took him twice. This guy is a wealth of knowledge and gives fascinating lectures. He is kind of old-school in his teaching methods, but he is funny and interesting and really encourages students to think critically. If you are at all interested in the Holocaust or history, you should really take him.

By far my favorite professor i've had at UMBC. Super understanding and helpful during lecture. Come to class, pay attention, do her (few) assignments and you'll pass. She posts pics of the text book so i didnt need it, but its nice to have it to follow along. I wish i could take her for all of my social work courses!!

One of the BEST professors I ever had! T.B. is required but I didn't need it because PPT and notes were enough. Easy quizzes and papers. As long as you put in effort, you get good grades. 1 grp ppt and class grp activities. Offers extra credit. Very caring and available outside of the classroom.

The best professor. Professor Hoover is an amazing professor. He classes are very much engaging. She gives good feedback and is very helpful. Long as you do the work, you get a good grade. Took her for both 481 and 483
She is an amazing professor, she is always there to help students during office hours, I learned so much from her lectures.

First of all go to class, I had her for 386 & 388, attendance is MANDATORY. As long as you come and pay attention you'll be fine. Her tests are easy and come right from the material You would have to try to fail. She's really sweet and she'll bring her dog in for one class period. Definitely would recommend
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Professor Hoover makes what might be a long and boring class, fun and engaging. She has a quirky sense of humor and truly has her students' best interests at heart. Her grading criteria could not be more clear, making it very easy to do well. Her papers seem daunting at first sight, but they're not. Tests easy as well! I love her

Very good professor. I believed I learned a lot about the subject and inspired me to want to know more about it. is very accessible and give an opportunity for extra credit. She truly cares about her student and makes sure you excel. her class is not boring is very interactive and makes you participate.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: She's very passionate about what she teaches, but it is by far the most boring lecture i've ever had to attend. She's super sweet and gives extra credit, but the class itself is really boring. There are some random exit tickets which aren't bad and then the tests can be challenging if you don't pay attention.

Really boring course to be totally honest. Professor is super passionate, so I'm sure her upper-level courses are great, but this one isn't it. She grades attendance at random through class participation but it's not super serious, so I honestly wouldn't go to class, or would at least do other work during. I'd recommend the bare minimum effort.

Great professor. Do the work and you'll do great. She genuinely means well and her interest in the topics is fascinating. The reflections are easy. Quizzes are easy. The videos are super interesting. Tests are easy, just study.

This class is fairly easy, but really boring. Prof. Holland is nice and I can see her passion for her field, however, when it comes to exams and quizzes, you need to study by yourself with her PowerPoints uploaded on BB. So, basically, there is no point of going to class.

Dr. Holland was amazing. She posted everything on BB so don't worry if you can't get everything written down. She incorporated a lot of current events- made the class more interesting. If someone asked a question and she didn't know the answer, she would find out and get back to you. Even though it was a large class, she engaged in discussions.

Great Class. Every week we focused on content that was extremely relevant to current events. The chapter on human population was really cool and a learned a LOT of really awesome things in the class. If you come to class and do the assignments you will easily get an A. Two extra credit assignments can boost your grade almost 10%. Highly Recommend.

Material is presented in a way that is easy to understand. Very nice but a little boring. Very little homework. Posts lecture slides on Blackboard, so you can still do well if you skip class (which I did a fair amount). Three exams throughout the semester and the content matches what you learn in the class

Attendance is not mandatory and she puts her slides on blackboards, but it was so interesting everyone came anyways. Her exams can get pretty specific but if you pay attention and do the assignments you should be fine. She was super nice and passionate about her field.

Her class is pretty straight forward. Go to class. do online work. Make sure you pet effort into your response and you can pass. I failed all test but i did well on online assignments and did one extra credit. Test is mostly vocab and certain stories on powerpoints. I recommend

Dr. Holland seems very knowledgeable and passionate about Latin America. The class included reading assignments, weekly writing assignments, and group projects. You are expected to participate. Overall, the workload is not too overwhelming as long as you stay on top of it. If you are looking for a smaller discussion based class, this is it.

Dr. Holland is obviously very passionate about the subject, but I don't prefer her teaching style. She is a very sweet woman though; I'd recommend her! There are quite a few short writing assignments, but they're spaced out evenly. Keep up with the work and you'll do just fine!
Just reads off the VAGUE powerpoints, doesn't use the book, and then expects you to know the tiniest details on the exam. One of the worst professors at UMBC.

Never uses textbook, reads a lot from powerpoints. But she is really passionate about her subject and is willing to help. Isn't always responsive to emails, but gives all semester to do an extra credit assignment. Lectures can be dry and poor grading system. Some assignments seemed pointless and you had to really know the material for tests
All she does is read from the power point, very bad grading system, very shady about what is going to be on the test, and the $120 textbook is never used. Don't take this class.

She reads from the powerpoints pretty much word for word, and the powerpoints are on blackboard. Coming to class is pointless. The way she distributes points is stupid. The textbook isn't even really used.
not very knowledgable, just reads off of slides or reiterates previous points.
Tough grading only because the fact that nothing seems to be worth over 10 points.  If you attend class regularly and actually do the projects and homework then an A is easily earned.

Great Professor! She really is passionate about her subject. She is REALLY REALLY NICE, however, be prepared to really work hard on your projects. There are no tests or exams, if you put in effort you can easily come out with a B but to get an A you really have to do GREAT and/or AMAZING on your projects. Highly recommended!

I had her for an elective course and she is not clear of what she want.  No exams, however projects are very hard (not an easy grader).  There are outside of class activities(mandatory). Do not take her.
Overall if you attend class when needed and skim the textbook then you should come out of the class with a B.  She also gave the whole semester to complete an extra credit assignment.

Instead of teaching, this whole course just felt like a semester long exam. He thinks that his students have way more pre requisite knowledge of java than they actually do. If you are not a elite  programmer this course will be difficult and time consuming.

After reading the reviews, I wasn't going to take this prof but had no choice since I was on the waitlist. So glad I took this class w this prof. He's very flexible, straight to the point, willing to help & lenient in his lectures and assignments. Course consisted of weekly quizzes, exams, hw, and semester long project. Would def take him again.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Very energetic during his long lectures, blunt but clear, a bit repetitive but its understandable. Explains everything very thoroughly, helps if asked, flexible in terms of class structure, allows late submissions with a penalty. IS147 is a pretty easy class if you come to lectures, and do all the labs and hws. Assigns groups and a group project.

He's definitely knowledgeable, but spends too much time rambling on unrelated topics. Disorganized. Kept changing the schedule and forgetting to post quizzes and assignments on blackboard. There's a semester long group project which requires you to plan out a bunch of features for a program in the second week of class, which makes zero sense.

Do yourself a favor and don't take this dude.  He hardly allows questions to be asked and expects too much out of students.  I firmly believe no matter what kind of student you are and what you are looking to get out of the class, you would be better off taking another professor.

Jumping from 147 to 247 was pretty rough with Houdeshell, he flew through lectures and didnt really give us good understanding of concepts. The programming exam prompts were also infinitely harder than whatever you learned in class or on HWs and Quizzes. Great prof but didnt handle this course well enough in my opinion. Glad I passed though.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor H is not the best professor if you are looking to increase your skills in java. I could tell that the class didn't really learn much by the end of the semester. The exams consist of coding an entire program in an hour so be prepared before hand. He fly's through lectures and expects his students to be coding wizards.

Was usually a good prof, however, he seems to think the jump from 147 to 247 makes us automatically expert developers. gives minimal practice and goes into unnecessary detail on ''industry'' but then tests us on things way more difficult than the work that has been assigned. expect to flunk/not finish the coding portions of his exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I think these ratings are way too harsh. This professor wants everyone to learn and is always willing to help. His lectures consist of slides and inclass labs (graded based on completion and is very lenient with grading). Theres 2 exams, weekly quizzes, 5 hw assignments, and group project. Exam has 2 parts- multiple choice and programming question.
He thinks that all of his students are coding prodigies even though most have little experience. He speeds through lectures. Useless study guides.

Really not great. Does more highlighting and showing code than explaining concepts or fundamentals. Tests were easy enough but very specific phrases from textbook so you're better off just reading then actually paying attention in lecture. Easy A, but don't expect to actually learn anything other than keywords. Textbook is very outdated and simple.
He's awesome and really cares about his students. The course work is simple and straight forward and directly related to the lecture each week. He's always willing to help a struggling student.

Yes, his class is easy but I feel cheated out of actually learning. Cares very little about teaching. Avoids grading at all costs (didn't grade a single assignment, everything was by completion). In lectures, he talks to you like you already know the stuff. He literally forgot what day it was once and tried to assign HW after semester was over

Hes super disorganized and doesnt teach. He reads slides and shows examples but doesnt explain anything. Hes a nice person and very knowledgeable, but I wouldnt recommend taking this class with him unless you want to teach yourself. He is a very lenient grader, which is helpful but he isnt the best at teaching.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I think his rating is TOO HARSH. Most are honest but his class is no where that bad. Lecture heavy but you can really skip them, as long as you do the hw's, which the answers r on the book. Grades VERY leniently on projects and exams, all which are based off the hw's. Do your hw's, in class exercises, and put it normal work, and it's an A.

His lectures are extremely boring as he just mainly reads from the slides. If you want to take this course with him, you better be prepared to learn everything yourself. He's a nice guy and has experience in the field, but his teaching leaves a lot to be desired.

Pretty decent professor, if your not invested in the class, actively participate and show a good amount of effort you may not pass. He was very lenient with grading and gave lots of opportunities for extra credit if you showed up to class but attendance is not mandatory.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: He reads the slides very fast and goes, "Any questions??". At this point, we are not even sure how to ask questions because we haven't gotten a clue about anything. He replies e-mails in 2 weeks, and often cancels office hours. He posts homework and quizzes right before the due date. In two words I would describe him as disorganized and careless.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: This class was disorganized at best. The tests are very hard. If you know your way around Java, you'll do fine on the programming but still do poorly on the tests. This is a class where you don't learn a whole lot, you're confused throughout, you expect to fail, but things turn out alright in the end if you stick it out.

His a positive guy. Tries to "help". His way of helping is basically reading the slides and the examples. He does not give clear reasoning on how the program is working. There's really no teaching in his class. I wouldn't attend a university if I was going to teach myself programming with a textbook. Youtube  this guy.
reviews.rating_tags: GRADED BY FEW THINGS--GROUP PROJECTS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Nice-ish guy, but too busy to teach this class.Tells to read slides "and we'll get it". Not resourceful/knowledgeable. Only good thing is the grading of HWs/labs, by completion not accuracy =40% of grade. Android project = 20% (presentation + paper) 4 Exams, 10/each=40%, people average D and C bc word by word ?s but open note so print everything!

He doesn't explain anything, just reads through slides. Disorganized, it is spring break still no grades posted. Lot of HW and readings. Assumes we know all the material and never explains anything in detail. Has a hard time understanding students questions. I was excited to be instructed and learn Android, but this guy is a major fail at teaching.

Freeman is the BEST President UMBC has ever had. Yes, he has his flaws, like not allowing us to have a football team, but he truly wants us to succeed as UMBC students and will do anything to make sure that that happens. He is always kind and all over campus. Overall, he is a phenomenal president and I wish he gave me a hug and never let go.

President Freeman Hrabowski is THE best president that UMBC has had in recent memory. He's always accessible outside of class and willing to sit down with you and have a chat. He is extremely kind and professional and is willing to work with you to make sure that you succeed. He is pro-black women in STEM. I trust Freeman with my life.

Freeman is one of the most ingenious men I've met in my life. He is out and about on campus often and is more than willing to sit down and talk with you when you see him around. Always smiling, always something nice to say. He is really leading the University in the right direction. WE LOVE YOU, FREEMAN!!!
Met me twice (officially). Still remembers my name, jobs, and struggles. Lauded my accomplishments to visiting people from the Social Security Administration. I trust this man with my life.

The old saying that "The only time you ever see the school president is at graduation" is something that will never be said about Freeman.I would argue that his historical and turmid upbringing shapes his leadership qualities and the way he approaches the advancement of this University. Renowned and Succesfull, now mentioned with the ivy leagues.

He's not a professor so I dont know why he is on this site but he is an amazing president. He is very nice and greets everyone when he walks past you.He really makes you feel like you are important. He's gotten many awards and honors such as top 10 college presidents by Time magazine.

Probably one of the brightest minds in academia today; mathematician par excellent.  I knew him while a student @UMBC when he was provost back in the 1990's. Shortly after ****'s retirement, He became president. Without question, he made UMBC into the school it is recognized as today.  The H-man is good peoples.

Extremely charismatic. Promotes UMBC as an "honors university in MD," even though you wouldn't think so if you saw the grades of the students transferring into UMBC. The motto is a marketing tool, NOTHING ELSE! Ask the advisors in Academic Services. He pushes that motto too much.--Very attentive to students when speaking to them.

As a former UMBC student(class of 2006) I remember President Hrabowski as a man who really cares about the direction of UMBC. As I was a commuter student during my two years there,I almost always saw him walking around campus talking to the students and any parents who happened to be waiting on their kids. He is one of the most engaging presidents.

I have seen him all around campus, very active for a President and so pleasant! Went to his house for scholar's dinner over his pool and he welcomed the students to UMBC. Great speaker and extremely supportive of student affairs. My last sighting of him was at the FA 2005 honors recital, which meant a lot to me to see him there after I performed.

He is very supportive of all aspects of a students life. I see him all the time around campus and I am glad that he is actively dealing with the campus. The last time I saw him was at the Music Department's Honors recital which meant a lot to me because it shows how much he cares about not only the academic subjects, but also the arts and humanitie
Watch out for that giant bling he wears. It's crazey! (P.S go to him to complain about stuff, because that's fun)
If you want to see "Free," take the stairs!
No Comments

This man is a shadow! I've only ever seen him at speeches, where he promptly dissapears back to the elusive 9th floor of the administration building, which is his office.  At any rate, he shall hence forth be refered to as "Bling Dog", because of his blinged out scholar's robe he wears to graduations. Have you seen that thing??

He's against football because he's into education. He's not in charge of making school fun, he's in charge of making it effective. Big on diversity, and that definitely comes through at UMBC - it's our school's strength! Very cool person, extremely intelligent, amazing life, fantastic sense of humor. He is a role model to everyone but slackers.
Freeman Rocks!
constant tuition increases, against football, bad or lack of events, no connection to student body, not trying to make the school more enjoyable
I don't know if anyone's gone to UMBC without at least having one brief personal conversation with Freeman.
No Comments
Go Freeman! This man is AMAZING and has turned this university around. Props.
FREEMAN IS THE MAN! Funny, chill guy...  PRES HRABOWSKI RULES!!
he is a hot hunk of man with a passion for education.  gotta love that guy.
i love 'im!!!! he's spicyhot! and he's got all the smarts! mmm!!!
No Comments
GO HRABOWSKI!!!!! YOUR NUMBER 1!!!!!!!1
He's amazing!  And understanding too... :)

Dr. Hu should have a higher rating. He isn't the easiest professor I've had, but he's certainly better than others. He's flexible with missed work and will spend extra time making sure you understand something in lecture but you HAVE TO SPEAK UP ABOUT IT!!! Lots of homework, but it's to help you understand and doing it will help you pass the class.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Dr. Hu definitely deserves a higher rating. He makes it clear during syllabus week that success depends on your drive and time management. The curriculum is straightforward, and he provides plenty of resources to reinforce material on your own. Attending office hours was especially helpful for getting unstuck and clarifying difficult concepts.
