I had this professor for both BIOL251 and BIOL252. She is extremely clear about her expectations and very thorough in making sure that all of her class materials are available online via Blackboard. If you use all of your resources effectively, including the teacher herself for any questions you may have, you should be able to get an A.

She is one of the best professors at UMBC. It was an awesome and great class. She is really helpful, and she cares about her students a lot. I wish I could take another class with her. For the exams, if you do the study guide and understand it, you will do great in exams

Dr. Hughes is one of the best teachers I've ever had. She is friendly, competent and well-prepared. She tries every possible way to help her students; for example, she makes anatomy lab videos that you can watch before the lab, and she posts vocal recording of the class in case you miss it.

I was terrified to take Anatomy & Physiology but Dr. Hughes makes a tough class seem easy. She gives so many resources that you can use to study. I'm in the lab with her as well and she has videos of every model that you can use to study for the test. In open labs, she will work with you until you get it. Love Dr. Hughes, looking forward to A & P 2

Dr. Hughes  knows anatomy like the back of her hand.  She's really nice and always willing to help.. Lecture is optional, but there are clicker points that will help you out in the long run, and worksheets that reinforce concept. She posts her video lectures and slides online. Exams were easy; just do the study guide. Don't bother getting the book.

Dr. Hughes is an excellent professor. I took BIO101 for my science credit (English major). I had to put in the time to study for exams, but she was extremely willing to help out with anything. She posts EVERYTHING on blackboard, and responds to questions via e-mail or blackboard discussion. She makes complicated concepts very simple to understand.
You could basically never go to class because she posts everything online. Pretty easy class.

Compared to IB and AP Bio in HS, Bio 101 was easy. If you haven't taken more than one bio in HS, or it's been a while since you've taken bio, buy the textbook-otherwise, go without it. Her lectures and powerpoints are very thorough, and everything is on blackboard, including worksheets and study guides. Listentake notes and you'll get at least a B
Dr. Hughes is an amazing professor.  Her power points are clear and easy to follow.  She can make the hardest concepts easy to understand.  If you need to take bio 101, take it with Dr. Hughes!
Great teacher.
Good professor

One of the best professors I've ever had. Her lecture power points are clear and detailed which was very helpful when it comes to study for tests. Very responsible professor that actually cares about her students. Class is not hard as long as you study.
Study the powerpoints and read the worksheets she gives and you will learn a lot and get an A. She is fair but keep in mind the only grades are tests so don't slack off.

She is really clear in her lectures, and you can tell she loves what she teaches and enjoys teaching. She's very helpful. Exams are pretty easy, lecture material is easy to understand. She records lectures and puts them on blackboard which is extremely useful if you missed a class and want to catch up. she's a great prof.

Absolutely loved her. Her lectures were very clear and she gave many study guides and review sheets that help a lot. The tests are mainly memorization so as long as you study and memorize, the class is not too bad.
Just 4 exams (the lowest of the first three will be dropped) and not much work. Do clicker and pay attention to the lecture and you must be fine
She's super helpful. Just make sure you attend class and pay attention to guarantee you're A in the class.
Easy A class.

There were only 4 exams, including the final, and she drops the worst grade out of the 3 (final can't be dropped). She gives detailed study guides that include EXACTLY what you need to know for the tests. Don't bother buying the book, all info comes from the class lectures which she also posts on Bb.

I would definitely recommend Mrs. Hughes. She doesn't give much work just 4 exams and a final exam. She drops the lowest grade for you, and gives you 1% extra credit for just using a clicker during class. If you miss a class, don't worry, she posts mostly EVERYTHING on BB including recorded lectures. She is very helpful and cool.
Coooool
Show up, do the clickers, do the study guides seriously and you will be fine.

I was absolutely terrified to take this class, but Prof Hughes does an amazing job with her lectures, powerpoints, and clicker questions to help students understand and enjoy the material. Exams go a long with the study guides she provides, and she drops the lowest exam grade out of 4! Def recommend her as a professor! No textbook

This class is super easy. No textbook, just simple powerpoints. Professor Hughes is really nice and even though this class is a lecture, it is actually interesting biology material so you won't be bored. Only 4 tests and a final and your lowest test grade is dropped (but the tests are already so easy...) Love Professor Hughes!
Professor Hughes is a great professor, I wish more professors were like her. Highly recommend her.

She explains topics thoroughly, and uses worksheets & clicker questions as reinforcements. Showing up to class is not essential, but completely understanding the topic is easier with her lecturing than just reading the slides. She is quick to answer emails and will do just about anything to help a student grasp the information. She's wonderful!

I am that person who is terrified of Bio and I have been putting off this class for 4 semesters However, Dr. Hughes is making me love Bio. She explains everything clearly and explains why this stuff is relevant. My only complaint is that we are not following a textbook. Instead we are reading articles she provides.

Dr. Lu is a very kind lady who loves what she teaches. She might stumble with her words occasionally, but English isn't her first language. She's very good at getting a point across, and she will gladly answer any questions. I don't understand the negative reviews, she's a perfectly fine professor and I needed no outside help in this course.

I liked Professor Lu as a person, but her lectures were stuffed with so much content that wasn't even compiled in a cohesive manner. It was hard to know what to actually study since in class we would skip over many slides. All exam content comes from the slides, which is annoying because the slides are not detailed enough to really rely on.

I do not take anything out of Hua Lu's lectures. She's a sweet lady who obviously loves what she teaches but it's the way that that she does that threw me off. outside resources will be your best friends (I also used an AI tool) for you to fully understand everything. Also, exams are a true test of your knowledge on the content, they are not easy!

Nothing except Khan academy and erin green the other professor got me through this class. Hua Lu is very kind but she is distracting in her lectures because she sounds confused at times. Overall the class is manageable but only if you spend an absurd amount of time studying her lectures because she doesn't teach them very well.

Dr. Lu goes by 80-90 slides per lecture and uses visual imagery and examples to relate to us in order to grasp the material. She uses humor and explains hard concepts in a simple way for us to fully understand. She really cares about her students and is always open to answering any concerns or questions during her office hours.

Textbook isn't necessary, just refer to it if you're confused on a topic. She's lively and knowledgeable, but not the best at explanations. This class isn't too bad if you take notes BEFORE lecture and remember bio141 (first half of course is basically stuff from that). Exams are exactly like in class questions, just know the material thoroughly.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Lu is an amazing professor and very passionate about plants! Her lectures are very active and engaging and there are lots of times where she will ask questions. Her quizzes and exams are straight from the lecture content so if you understand the material and study before the class you're good to go! She's also super sweet and easy to talk to.

during lectures she often skips around slides which makes it confusing to take notes and such. thankfully she posts the lecture slides beforehand, but it's hard if you didn't take notes then. does not explain clearly as i had trouble understanding her thought process, but she is very kind when answering questions before and after class.

dr. lu is very sweet and likely a great geneticist in her field, but her ability to relay that knowledge is not very strong. she is lecture heavy and mostly reads from the slides. i would recommend you go through them and take your own notes. she does clickers at end of class graded on accuracy. she split the semester with dr. e

I feel like I am an international student, alone in the country, stranded, trying to understand her. The amount of mental stress I bear every class in order to comprehend what is being spoken is astronomical. If you don't have a problem understanding accents, I guess you will be okay...or will you?
reviews.rating_tags: Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Lu is one of the most caring professors I have met! Her lectures cover all the important aspects of the reading. She usually includes a question or two in lecture for you to discuss with others and check your understand. As long as you spend time going over the slides, practice questions and previous quizzes/exams, you should have no problem!

Honestly I never paid attention during her lectures but she is super sweet and emphasizes wanting the best for her students. Personally, this class was pretty easy if you read the lectures and do the practice exams. Don't bother reading the book, it won't help and doesn't cover some of the topics she mentions in detail. The best genetics prof here

Professor Lu definitely cares about her students but her teaching style is pretty difficult. There was a disconnect between what we learned in class, the clickers and the exams. Students often felt frustrated after they asked a question and got a somewhat unrelated and complicated answer. She is a great person, very enthusiastic and passionate.

Dr. Lu's a caring person and wishes her students to do their best. Her lecture covered all the important topics. 
There're clicker questions for every lecture, which you should keep up with. Go over her slides, clicker questions, homework, and past exam questions and you'll do great. Put effort into this course to see the result you want.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Professor Lu is a good person and cares about her students, but her lectures are often long and complex, and she often goes on tangents and glosses over on harder topics. Many students feel confused or frustrated after lectures. There is often a disconnect when a student asks a question and her response.

Pretty much all of your grade comes from the quizzes and exams, there are a few other assignments but they make up a negligible portion of the over all grade. As others said her exams are very hard, but her study guide is pretty much the EXACT SAME as the actual exam questions. Memorize the study guide back to front and its an easy A for the exam.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: A very nice person but makes her exams and quizzes impossible. Her exams and quizzes consist of true and false, very precise fill in the blanks with no key, and those multiple choice questions that are like which of the above are right. Very difficult

Her lectures are very heavy in terms of information. Her slides are very long, almost 100 slides per day. She is considerate and cares about students, but a bad professor for this class. She curves generously, but not equally. The range for a C is much larger than the range for an A or B, which is kind of unfair.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: First, Dr. Lu is a great person. She co-taught with Dr. Tracy Smith, and clearly cares about her students. As far as teaching the course goes, her lecture slides are devoid of necessary information, and the learning objectives are too vague to be objectively helpful. It was her first time teaching the course, so there's room for improvement.

Dr. Lu is not very clear at explaining the function of certain proteins in the formation of a product. Combined with the 48-100+ slide lectures makes this class very time consuming. Outside of lecture, Dr. Lu is a kind person with true concern for you and your goals of the future. Dr. Lu and the class just do not go well together unfortunate.

Very long lectures in comparison to the amount of content you need to know. Our other prof for this class gave clear learning objectives, but Dr Lu's were too broad. Half the class stopped showing up when she started teaching, probably because it was impossible to pay attention. Makes her exams too precise in comparison to her objectives.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Took Plant Molecular Bio with Dr. Lu. Most classes were only lecture. Other classes are presentations. We read at least 20 papers, no textbook. You will not pass her quizzes if you skip class. Lecture slides are not helpful. Feedback is not helpful.

Worst teacher. She was nice at times but a very harsh grader. Essay drafts were pointless because she did not give constructive feedback for you to get a decent grade. Also there was no schedule for exams so they were whenever. The final was horrible and required a lot of detail unlike previous quizzes. Also she does not grade timely at all.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: Nice woman.  Not good teacher. Explains things very vaguely. Expects all students to understand every article inside out. Organization of the course is absolutely terrible, doesn't follow syllabus. There are graduate students in the class, and she expects the undergrad students to have the same understanding as them, and the same performance.

This professor will make you feel like crap. She calls students out in front of the class, makes no sense when she talks, but expects us to remember every word she says. She wishes we were plant researchers, not students. Even if you go in for office hours and follow the rubrics, she will still find a way to give you a C. Grades are subjective.

This class is a must!! I came into this class thinking it would be really boring but I fell in love with this course! She is also a great professor she is willing to help when you don't understand something. Although there were times I didn't clearly understand in class, but if you email her she will reply back quick with an answer!

The Exams are mostly what makes up of your grade in the class. That sounds intimidating but the tests aren't so bad compared to the exams in cell. She'll make a curve at the end. Mostly, go to class and take good notes. Book is optional but recommended.

Absolutely horrible at teaching. I took plant with this professor and she was so I decided to take BIO456 with her and that was the worst decision in the world. Her criteria is unclear, she is a VERY slow grader, her grades make absolutely no sense. Don't bother trying to argue for a higher grade, she won't even listen to you.

I just want to say only one thing. This lady made me cry and I would never forget that. No one wants to fake problems when they are in university. Only fools would do that but some professors are way too mean. Sadly, one cold person I have ever come across.

An excellent teacher who really cares. You can tell she puts a lot of effort into the class. HOWEVER, if you are taking Devo with Plant, dont expect to party for that semester. It is a bad combination, but it is possible. Nevertheless, without devo, it is an easy A.

This professor likes to review previous material at the beginning of lecture by asking questions to the 200+ students.  While it is helpful to know what material she emphasizes, it hinders progress through newer material and takes time from answering a CPS question at the end of class.  Will answer questions after class and shows related videos.
Great Proffessor, with clear explanations and aid for students

He is a new professor and this is first time teaching it seems. He was okay, but he was very unorganized. He was quick going over problems and would actually get answers wrong during the lecture. I would take Calc 151 with Tighe.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: I took AP Calc I still found it sometimes difficult to follow along with what he would do. Sometimes he does tend to skip problems during lecture and not have enough time to go through things thoroughly enough. Don't skip lecture, it still helps. He gives you practice exams that are crazy similar to the real ones. No curveballs. PRACTICE PROBLEMS!!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: This is his first time lecturing this course. I think he overall does a pretty good job, although sometimes he goes a bit fast with the content, skips problems, or talks too much about other stuff at the beginning of class before actually getting into the material, but if you pay attention and use your resources like the Math Lab, you will pass.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Great professor. I took his class during the winter (writing this review late) and I truly enjoyed it. The assignments were straightforward and easy to complete.

Hummel is a super enthusiastic professor and honestly just wants people to learn. If you ask for an extension he'll give it to you just make sure to communicate. The quizzes are kinda tough, just make sure to pay attention in class and you should be fine. If you try you should be fine to get an A just make sure not to miss any assignments.

AMST 320 was such a fun and chill class. You do have to read and pay attention to the lectures (or watch the powerpoints later), but this class should not be difficult at all. about 4 discussion boards throughout the semester, two papers, and one group project.

Michael Hummel is a great professor. AMST 320, despite its high number, is not a difficult class. A few quizzes, discussion boards, 2 essays, and 1 group project is all we did. My only complaint is that the textbooks were never really used. Lastly, attendance is mandatory, so make sure to show up to each class. It's free points.

Cool professor easy class. Most textbooks were useless & the few articles used could be found online, but he uploaded VoiceThread PPTs which helped a lot. Keep in mind this was a 6 wk-long summer class: 2 papers, 1 group project (paper + presentation, weekly short answer quizzes & discussion boards. Not bad at all.

Prof. Hummel is really organized so you'll know everything that's due from the get go. He's pretty straightforward and not a tough grader. There are readings and discussions, I'd say it's an easy A as long as you submit your assignments on time and show effort
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: He was a great professor! We wrote several papers but they were usually short, he's tough with grammar but other than that very fair and gives awesome feedback on your papers. The class was lecture based but the material was interesting and he always made dad jokes which were entertaining and there's a final group project at the end of the semester

Professor Hummel is an extremely nice guy. He can be a little awkward at times. He talks about his kids a lot & tries to infuse his dad humor into the lectures. The class has a few quizzes, 2 papers w/1 requiring a presentation, & 1 final group project. Hes a tough grader, but he gives great feedback and really knows what hes talking about.
reviews.rating_tags: GROUP PROJECTS--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Did not pay attention in class at all and received an A. He has a couple of quizzes and he gives you the questions ahead of time. No tests, just papers, and they are all pretty easy. He does not seem like a tough grader, but definitely put in some effort. My friends who wrote their papers the night before still got Cs while I would get As.

good professor, everything you need for quizzes and exams is on the power points he shows in class. If you cannot take notes fast enough he always puts them up online. The essays were graded very fairly, mainly grammar. No final, just a midterm. Class is not an easy A, but with Professor Hummel it's not hard either. Would take this professor again!
I would not recommend this professor. Boring lectures, harsh grader, and somehow you have to read his mind on what he wants on the written exam.
He's a very hard grader grammar wise. He's very awkward but if you just do your work, show up to class and have conversations with him you will get an A.

Very nice, dorky guy. Goes off on a lot of tangents about his family and cracks a lot of jokes. (Sweet sometimes, annoying other times). A little scatterbrained, but definitely an overall competent professor and an enjoyable class.
Really good teacher. Makes the class fun. Easy work. He used to be a stand up comedian, so his joke are pretty funny.
Great teacher. The class was interesting. 2 papers, 3 quizzes, and a midterm exam. No Final exam. I recommend this class. I got an A

He's...weird, in a cute way. Totally a nerd, and constantly talks about his daughters. It's cute at first, then it gets really annoying. He says he doesnt grade hard, but dont let that mess with your head because he takes off points for the dumbest things. Other than that, he's a pretty chill, funny professor. Always cracking jokes.

Prof Hummel is a very good, caring professor.   The class material is fun & entertaining.  You do have to write 3 papers, but they are easy as long as you follow his guidelines.  Piece of cake.   Wish all upper level courses were this easy, fun, & stress-free!   Take this class!

Hummel is a tight prof. It's an easy course with easy material. His quizzes are pretty easy as well and its kind of a chill upper level class, you just watch a bunch of clips from TV shows and talk about them. Write whatever he writes on the board and just be familiar with the terms and theres no way to get any lower than a B+. There are papers..

A pretty easy and interesting class.  There were three papers altogether, one group paper and two on your own.  You have to present one paper and you also have a group presentation.  I definitely recommend this class and this professor!  Good way to get 3 upper level credits done.

I really loved this class. The papers took some work, but he tells you EXACTLY what he wants from you for each. I really learned a lot! He talks about his daughter a lot, which is really cute. I like him so much that I'm talking a sitcom course this summer with him.
Fairly easy going.  Very understanding when it comes to late work and absences.  Take his class in the winter to knock out three upper level credits.

Fun professor, very easy class.    Loves to teach this subject and has a great knowledge for the subject.  Alot of writing is required, plus presentations.  You watch alot of TV programs and videos.  Make sure your grammar is perfect because he deducts points on papers for errors.

I love this man. Made it fun to read articles and encouraged open discussions. His Culture in TV class if REALLY popular. If you have the chance senior year and want a fun one, take him for that class.  Plus he's a Beatles fan, so that's a plus 1 already!
very nice guy, good class, a little hard on grading papers. Grades more like an english teacher at times, but its not too bad. Hes very considerate and willing to help you out so you do well.
One of my all time favorite professors!  His classes are interesting and informative, and he is a funny and nice guy.  Definitely take AMST Pop Culture, AMST Television, or AMST Intro with him!

He is so nice. Class is not hard, just take notes on what he writes on the board, and that is not a lot of notes. 3 short and easy papers, quizzes, 1 group project, short presentation of 1 paper. No useless pain-in-the-neck busy work. I learned a lot.
He is great and interesting! I think if you read his notes on the board and some of the readings you should be just fine. There is no reason why you would get anything lower than a B.
Wonderful professor, wonderful class.  Even if it was an easy A, I still learned a ton.
A good guy and a good teacher.  Knows his material, a few quizzes, mostly writing/essay assignments.  You'll learn a WHOLE lot.
I think he's really nice. Some people find his constant talking about his personal issues, but I really liked the class. You can get an A with minimal effort
Such a nice, funny professor! His classes are interesting, his assignments are fairly easy, but as with all American Studies classes, you'll get something out of it.
Keeps things fun and interesting. Has a very dry sense of humor that helps to break things up. Really knows the material too.
Really nice guy. Makes class fun with video clips from various things. A few quizzes and a few papers, but both are fairly easy

Genuinely is the most amazing and sweetest professor I've ever had at UMBC. She takes her time getting to know each students name, likes, etc. No exams or quizzes, just a group project and a final paper! I can't stress enough how amazing of a teacher she is and how much I recommend taking her; This was the one class I truly looked forward to go to.

LOVE LOVE LOOOVE THIS PROFESSOR! She's so nice and caring, always understands her students. There's no quizzes or exams so that's a plus! Her lectures are very clear and I learned a lot. This is definitely a stress free class, I highly recommend taking her.
Awesome professor. Super caring and understanding. She's clearly passionate about what she teaches and wants students to succeed.

One of the best professors I've ever had. She really care about her students. She is very organized, and is not hard grading. We had group presentations and she built the rapport in the classroom. Do the assigned readings, work with your group, and don't procrastinate for your final paper, and take advantage of the extra credits, you will get an A.

Professor Hwang is hands down the best professor I've had at UMBC! Her teaching style is very engaging and she is very clear about her goals for us in the class. Attendance is mandatory but I did not mind it at all because each class was so interesting. I loved this class and highly recommend taking it!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: I LOVE DR.HWANG! She is possibly the best professor I have every had and I would definitely take her again! Her class was so fun and engaging.  One of the most understanding and caring professors ever! I would suggest for this class is to participate and show up since that is a major part and its honestly so easy! Great class! Great Professor!

Dr.Hylton is lecture heavy, but very informative. He answers questions and is easily accessible via text. It does take a while for him to grade but if you text him in regard to your grade he will respond. Great class, I'd definitely take him again if possible.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: He turns some of the most depressing topics into informative lectures. I really enjoy his classes I have taken him 2x & will probably do a 3rd semester. His class is fairly easy as long as you show up to the classes that happen once a month and do the discussion boards which are easy if you do your work. His syllabus is nicely organized & uniform.

This semester I took SOCY310 and SOCY351 with Professor Hylton, and prior to this semester, I took 2 other classes with him in the past. He's a relatively easy professor to take classes with, as he only gives out discussions and short quizzes every week, but he doesn't answer his emails/texts and does not update grades consistently.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Our class was a hybrid course. Whenever we would meet up, he'd go over what we'd learn from the last time we met & before class is over, he'd explain the upcoming assignments and etc. Only thing that I didn't like was that he does not check his email and didn't update the assignment dates from the previous years which made the due dates confusing.
Such a sweet professor, easy grader, gave great feedback. Would def. take again!
Very fun, easy class. You learn a lot and she's very friendly, too. Easily one of the best teachers at UMBC. Take her for 101/102 if you can.

I have her for discussion and she's amazing. She uses Korean in the classroom to immerse us and she also gives us more chances to speak Korean as opposed to just listening. If she were to teach my next level I'd definitely take her for lecture. Overall much more interactive, and she's also very sweet.
you will pass in his class even if hes boring

Will make you hate being an engineering major if you think this is what you'd be doing for the rest of your life. If he had one of those TV shows, i would put it on at night to get sleep. I completely agree with the user below that a solution manual would help A LOT.

Boring. Reads off of slides and isnt interested in the material. The examples he goes over on the board are confusing. Theres lots of hard homework too. The book sucks examples dont help much.   GET THE SOL. MANUAL IF YOU CAN! Exams are OK. The material's pretty easy once you understand but that happened to me when finals came so i have to retake.
Horrible teacher, reads off slides, does not seem interested in material at all.  Tests and quizzes are ridiculous, does not give enough time.
I really caught up on my reading of the school's newspaper during this class.
This class is boring as hell.  The material seems pointless.  The exams are OK.  The lab was the biggest waste of my life.

Decent professor, lectures are a tad on the boring side. Provides Powerpoint slides that are fairly comprehensive. Exams are easy. Homewrok is doable for the majority of the semester with just a few weird questions. Lab portion was a joke- programming MATLAB's built-in functions is REDUNDANT and POINTLESS.

Lectures were pretty boring and powerpoint slides had material taken directly taken from the book. Attendence is mandatory for both the lab and lecture. Lab is pointless as you have to program in matlab and you will never use it again (we programmed functions which matlab already has). Tests are rather easy as you get to use your own equation sheet

A rather boring professor, although the subject itself is quite interesting.  He was not always the most clear on some subjects, and often placed too much emphasis on the simpler concepts.  But overall, I learned statics, which was the main goal.

Great professor. Hard to understand but if you fail quizzes you can at least learn and pass and get a decent grade on the Exams. At least few questions on exams are from quizzes. Homework was hard. Overall a decent class and a decent professor.

exams are so easy, hw is hard since he only gives stared problems, but his exams are straight forward, just read the sections he assigns and you will get a B at the least, hes really boring but hey, you want to pass right?

Avoid this class, especially with the Thorpe and Garcin combo by all means possible.  Your GPA will suffer greatly!! Everything got screwed up for me because of this class.  I agree with the person before, he is not helpful at all.  AVOID AT ALL COSTS!!!

So matter how much I studied, prepared and asked for help, I always ended up failing every single exam.  I wished I dropped out of this class. The material taught in class has no relevance to the content given on the exams.  There's no way I'm going to get into med school now because of what this class did to my gpa.

He definitely Knows what he is talking about but, has some trouble communicating exactly what he wants to say. If you can be patient with this professor, you will learn a lot. Tests are not too easy and book is not an easy read. If you have any trouble with the material, asking questions after class is the best way to get clarification on material

This is one of the most difficult classes offered, and Dr. Thorpe did a good job in explaining the material. The slides were provided by the publisher, but edited to fit class content. A lot of material was explained further during class discussion. Seems unapproachable, but really does care about students. Fair in grading and regrades.
Not interested in the material, basically reads off of the lecture slides provided by the publisher. Unpleasant outside of class and isn't typically able to answer questions during class. Boring.

Teacher is useless. It's always unclear as to what hethe students should be doing and he constantly changes plans. He grades different than he claims & is incapable of facilitating a decent discussion. Narcissistic and constantly talks about himself, which cuts into class time. He complains about his grading load, yet piles you high with work.
Good lectures and in-class activities. A lot of writing
Fun and interesting class with many in class and peer to peer discussion.

Literally horrible. Nice guy but bad prof. He skips class so much and expects students to somehow know information that was never covered. "study guides" for exams consist of student made questions that make absolutely no sense and are extremely vague. So boring and drones on for 50 minutes about absolutely nothing. Covers maybe 3 slides max . lazy
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Dr. George is a great cultural import from the UK. He's very kind and knowledgeable about the material and presents it in a very easy to understand way. His tests are essentially everything he discusses in class. He provides some readings but is always willing to discuss anything. In all honesty, you have to be very lazy to not get an A his class.

Very nice. Exams are kinda dumb, some of it isn't covered in class or wasn't covered enough. Study guide aren't very useful, only used them to find out what to study. Slow grader. Very approachable. Very chill class.

Dr. Ian George was a fun professor with a good heart. He brought humor to the classroom as well as his extensive knowledge of the subject matter. Astrobiology was an energetic class with an in-depth look at the potential of life outside of Earth, as well as a detailed look our own planet's life on an atomic scale. Take your seat up front!
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: He's a hilarious professor that makes the class worthwhile and interesting. He doesn't give many homework assignments, so exams are everything. Also, his grading system is a bit weird. Other than that, I recommend him and his class if you want a simple science credit for GEPs.
reviews.rating_tags: Hilarious--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--Would take again

reviews.comment: I took both PHYS 105 & 106 with Dr. George. This man is full of British character and his lectures are always entertaining. He's clearly very passionate about the subjects and cares about his students. I highly reccomend both classes with Dr. George as they are fairly easy and very interesting.

Dr. G is really passionate and loves having people engaged in discussions. He takes a while to post grades and gives few homework assignments, making your grade rely on the 3 exams. He spends a ton of time talking about interesting current events. Even if you're not fond of the class, go to it; he gave students who showed up extra credit points.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Every single class was him reading from a PowerPoint. He ended up only giving 6 homework assignments and 3 tests, although he said he would give more. He didn't update grades pretty much the entire semester. He's passionate about the class, but that passion did not translate into good teaching.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Pretty good. His lectures are really fun, he's very passionate about his subject, and he loves when the students are engaged. But he also takes forever to post grades, doesn't hold my attention, personally, and gave WAY fewer assignments than he said he would. I enjoyed the class, but didn't do especially well, but I'm not really a STEM person.
One of the easiest professors. Very hilarious and personable. Teaches the material well and you'll pass whether you choose to go nuts with it or not

Dr. George is a wonderful professor who is willing to answer any and all questions students have. He is willing to work with you if you are willing to put in effort. It is crucial to regularly attend class and also read the book for the tests! His class was very insightful and I feel like I learned a lot with him! Highly recommend!!

If you skip lectures, you will miss key things critical to passing the exams/quizzes. The tests themselves are not hard, but you need to be able to study the material and APPLY it. It's a physics course for this reason. Not many equations but concepts are key to your success. He is a great teacher and is willing to put in as much time as you are.

Never responds to any of your emails and I have sent over 10 without a response. Class is also pretty straight forward, boring unhelpful lecture so get ready to read text book and learn by yourself. Study guide for exams are also rubbish and exams are somewhat complicated.
Dr. George is an amazing prof. He's very passionate and knowledgeable about the subject, and interested in sharing this with students. He also works with NASA, and has an awesome English accent.

Took his course on astrobiology. Great topic! He made it easy for science and non-science majors to understand. Homework once a week or so and then 3 exams. He's an easy grader. He's obviously passionate about the subject. The only down side was that it took so long before we got to the good stuff (but that's college I guess)

Ian George is not the best professor by any means.  He did not bring anything to the lectures all he did was basically make a power point of pages from the book.  He did not do many examples at all, and he would post multiple choice questions but never tell you what the answer was. He is a nice guy but a horrible phys 1 teacher. His curve did help.
Dr. George is awesome! We had very few assignments but learned a lot.  I get why he may not be the best for a 100 level course, but if you're an Astronomy minor he is great!

first of all he has an english accent, quite easy to understand. did not seem to know how to teach the class, every example he does is "trivial". You'll hate the word by the end of the semester. you learn nothing from the class, discussion was better. the best thing though was that he curved a lot.

He is a good/nice person but not the best professor for a 100 level course. He does not go over problems and makes his tests somewhat complicated. He is a nice person but not the best professor to take for a 100 level course. Hopefully he has a good curve

Dr. George seems a little out of place teaching a 100 level physics course. He never really showed us how to do problems, only skimmed over them on slides and assumed that we knew how to set them up and solve them. I learned a lot more from discussion than from lecture. Which is a pity because he is a likable person, but not too good at teaching :/

Very entertaining lecturer, though he is a little disorganized at times (he forgot his powerpoints a couple of times and had to wing it). He hates the dry and boring parts of the course too but once you get to the fascinating stuff (especially his research area) he can talk for hours (in a good way). Easy grader, but takes a while to return things.
Entertaining. A little scattered. Pretty easy. Has a tendency to get a black smudge from the white board marker dust on his forehead.
Great teacher. Very easy going and always willing to help!

You'll get out of this class what you put in. The homework is hard sometimes but he will answer your questions on it. He gives alot of partial credit on quizes and exams but he is an honest grader too, if you didnt get it you dont get credit.

He only has about 5 problems on quizzes and they're worth a many points each.  He quizzes you on problems that have not been gone over during class. He expects you to read ahead and know the material.  Taught pretty well, but he his testing system was horrible.  TA's graded very strictly also.

I have never met any professor like Dr. George.  He goes to every single lab each week personally giving back our quizzes/labs and discusses our grades with us separately, giving us motivational talks. He's constantly regrading our quizzes, giving us extra points if we've done badly. Dr George rocks
Treat all with respect. My strong accent from Africa did not discourage her from listening and helping out. She reads everything and provides very effective feedback with alacrity.

Coming from an undergrad program where professors treat students like kids,    Ms. Izenberg treats students as equals and very respectful. Her class participation strategy help bring out something in me that I didn't know I had - communication. I left her class six years ago in 2009 and still credit her teachings to some of my success at work.
Awesome teacher who's very upbeat. One of those classes in which you can't get drowsy. Learned quite a bit. Take her!
Very nice, very good.  Clearly knows what's she's talking about.  Really learned a lot, pretty much all the work was applicable to the classroom lessons.  Will seek her out for other classes.
Really good teacher, very nice.  Seemed to care about the students.  Very approachable.  Quick to get graded materials back.  Really great teacher.
No Comments

This course was super hard. She sucks! I had no help from the professor what so ever and her grading sucks ! She's terrible I don't think I'll ever take another course like this one. Especially online. If you want to fail take her. Besides that's what happened to me after taking her "easy" final. I would never recommend her. Good luck passing

There is a good amount of reading.  I really enjoyed the discussion leader assignment and the final project.  There were only a few 3-5 pape papers required.  The final exam was  a take-home exam consisting of 20 essays which could be as long or as short as you wanted.  I really enjoyed this class.  You will too!

very interesting class. professor is great. a lot of readings; no exams. a few 3-5 page papers. final was a bunch of take home essays. community action project was tedious, but not that bad. overall if you do the work you should be able to pass easily

The class is small and the grades are based on attendance and blackboard discussions. Not hard to get a good grade because the professor cares more about the students having meaningful discussions. He is a great professor and it is obvious that he cares about his students.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring

reviews.comment: One of the worst classes ever. You won't understand anything he teaches. He does theory a lot which you don't understand at all. When he does questions, he only writes equations that are going to be used and explain the process a bit, but never solve the question. Lectures are very useless I learned everything just by reading the book.(A85)

Lectures can be confusing, but he is a very kind soul. You can tell that he is very interested in the course and enjoys it a lot. Curves the class substantially, which is needed. If you attend his TAs review sessions before test you will do fine in the class.

Took for First Year Seminar course (can take as a freshman or transfer student). Super easy arts and humanities credit.  Each class you get 2 points. 1 for showing up, and 1 for posting a discussion question before class. No exams, no quizzes, no final. Just show up and talk about the reading. And Dr. Irvine is a pretty chill/funny guy.

Dr Irvine has this quirky personality that will make him more approachable from the start. His lectures get harder to follow once the class gets to Rigid Bodies, but he's more than willing to work problems out if you go to his office. BUY AND READ THE TEXTBOOK.

As long as you do the readings, go to class and participate, you will get an A. Super easy. 2-3 random easy reading quizzes but if the class participates enough, there won't be any. Bring your book to class. He is such a humble & open professor. Totally someone to ask for a recommendation if you develop a good relationship with him. One of my favs!

Great professor! He's a very humble guy, very nice, and isn't afraid to work problems cold when asked (but doesn't try to pretend like he knows everything!). He holds helpful reviews before exams and has an exceptionally merciful curve. It's interesting material and good that fear of a bad grade (thx to curve) didn't get in the way of enjoying it.
Dr Irvine is very nice and funny. He's good at explaining things well using calculus and makes class time fun. His exams are fair and easier than the online hw.

Really dedicated to teaching. His lectures are easier to pay attention to than anyone else I've had, also much more useful. He believes in fair grading and curves a lot. The grade needed for an A in Dynamics was a 80%. I would definitively take him again if I taught more courses.

This was Irvine's first time teaching Thermo.  While his lectures are occasionally hard to follow, all you have to do is ask a question and he is happy to explain.  He invests A TON of time into understanding every aspect of what he is teaching so that you can as well.  Definitely worth taking - one of the top 3 professors I have had at UMBC.

He has a mildly sadistic character, feeding his huge ego. He solves problems using variables alone, making lectures hard to follow.He firmly believes that students understand what he is saying even though nearly all of them leave the lecture hall feeling bewildered and lost.He respects some students, disrespects others, but the reason is masked.

A funny, likable guy, but his lecture style is very scattered and he often goes off on tangents while working problems and gets lost in his notes trying to figure out his own algebra if you ask him a question. Much better 1 on 1 or in a smaller review-session atmosphere. Sadly, I learned as much from the online tutoring problems as I did from him.

He is so bad at lecturing. He doesn't even do examples in class, he just talks about them. And he acts like the whole class understands everything about engineering when they don't at all. He is the sole reason why I switched out of Mechanical Engineering

Has a beard that hasn't been shaved (just trimmed) since 1976 or so. Is very humorous, but I get the feeling that people are afraid to ask questions for fear of being embarassed (he's not mean, just saying). Is friendly and seems wise, but he's a philosophy professor. He's not playing on his home turf. However, his tests are relatively easy.
Great professor! Teaches many subjects, and explains things in great detail. Works with the class, and is generally aware of and willing to help with specific problems.

Irvine's a mixed bag. He's very into the material, but doesn't present it very clearly. He flails a lot to try and help you understand 3D coordinates, which is fun to watch but not the least bit helpful. Test are tough, review sessions are useless. Very helpful in smaller summer classes though, a lot easier to understand. He's funny too.

Very helpful and fun teacher. Really tried to get everyone involved and know everyone. When I took the class he was co-teaching the course with another teacher and Dr. Irvine's parts of the test were much clearer and easier, which should be an indication when he teaches alone. I'm looking forward to having him again this semester.
No Comments
Very tough grader. For someone who says she wants everyone to get an A dhe sure doesn't act on it.

Really passionate about the subject and encourages discussions, which are interesting, but can get awkward and off-topic. A lot of busy work to go with the readings, but they're easy grades. Tests are pretty easy, as she tells you what to study for. Offers a lot of extra credit opportunities. Overall, a pretty interesting, easy and laid-back class.

She's very passionate about this class and I got an A easy. Kids complain about the tests, but every one has the same exact format and she tells you everything you need to know for it the class before. I never got below a 90 on one and she gives lots of chances for extra credit if you need it. You just have to actually show up and take good notes.

She's a nice lady, but her teaching style is definitely not for everyone. Also, It helps if you have a TA that isn't in his feelings all of the time. She is very interesting to listen to when not talking about STAT. I would recommend you build a relationship with her or you probably will fail.

This professor is the best SOCY Statistics professor ever. She loves what she does and will help you every step of the way. I entered this course expecting a C because I am terrible at Math but I recieved an A. This course is A LOT of work but a definitely recommend this professor.

Best SOCY Statistics professor ever. I took this class expecting a C because I am terrible with math and have no interest in statistics. However, this professor loves what she does and will help you with every step. I definitely recommend taking this class if it fulfills your statistic requirement. It is A LOT of work though, but you will love it.

This class isn't that hard but it's hard listening to her for an hour and 45 min. She goes on rants about sex and republicans and doesn't teach the material. I would not take one of her classes again. She does tell you everything that will be on the test and there are no papers, just a lot of math.

She's hilarious! Absolutely love her to death - one of the best classes I have ever had. Everyone says her exams are hard, but if you go to class and actually listen/read the material as well as participate, you'll do good. She literally tells you what will be on the test and what is important to know - just read what she says.

Lottes is a very fun professor and extremely approachable and nice. She's very political and her disparagement of republicans is irritating, but she encourages students to challenge her ideas and make up their own minds. The exams are ridiculously hard but she does curve and offers extra credit. If the TA offers study sessions ATTEND THEM!

Ilsa is one of the best. She's very passionate about what she does, she's pretty liberal and may offend anyone who's super conservative, but she encourages students to think for themselves and disagree with her if they want. A lot of work/reading, and exams are hard but she really wants you to pass and will help you out a lot. super nice, take her!

Dr. Lottes is one of my favorite teachers. She is hilarious and always tries to get students involved in discussion. Her class is not easy and the tests are crazy hard but she offers tons of extra credit and other ways to get points. Definitely recommend her!

FYS 103G or something like that: Sexuality, Health, and Human Rights. She was AWESOME and I love her so much. She's really sweet and understanding, really wants what's best for her students. It's easy to pass her class if you actually try. Tests are difficult but not too bad if you study.

Thee worst! I agree with comment below.. She gives extremely hard tests and tries to make people kiss up to her so that people can attempt to get a good grade.. extra credit is available but it is a class I wouldn't recommend with her.

Avoid this class! Tests are impossible unless you memorize every study done in the book. Tests you on random statistics she gives in class, not general ideas of the course. If you don't do all the h/w and E.C. you will likely fail. Don't waste your time.

I think this class was fair enough. Her exam questions are hard & you have to read about 100+ pgs a week; she warns you about this in the beginning. She gives a lot of extra credit & assingments to make up for the difficult exams. Attend all classes, do all assignments (including e.c)& average a 70% on exams, you will get an A. 60% on exams is a B.

this was the worst class i have ever taken. I am a transfer student in my first year therefore i was already stressed with my grades. Everyone in this class, besides suck up from her other ones, failed. She is not helpful at all and her tests make no sense. I would recommend not to take any Lottes classes unless you want to fail.
AVOID THIS CLASS!!!! I am a Biology Major, Socy Minor and a senior and this was the hardest class I've taken at UMBC. Not helpful at all. Do ALL extra credit as you may need it to get a C!

Dr. Lottes is a lot of fun! Attendance is mandatory, but the class is 100% easy. If you complete all the homework, you WILL have an A. There is homework every night and a large research project on a topic of your choosing. I loved mine! One of the best professors I've ever had!

Dr. Lottes' tests are unreal, more than 1/2 the class scored less than a 60 not sure how anyone deals with this professor. She writes her own book and boy is it boring. Statistically I don't know how she is still teaching.

The class could be quite disturbing at times and varied from interesting to boring. She wrote her own text book which is horribly boring. She tends to talk about Finland more than the US. She gives you ton of hints to help on her tests (which are hard). A ton of Extra Credit point are available. DO THEM ALL!
Worst Prof every, her exams her had and not very straight forword.  I wouldnt take this class if i were you.

Class sounded interesting since I had a small sociology background, bottom line is it is not easy/fun/or even possible. It's a dual class between women studies and sociology, if you have a **** it will be ten times harder (no pun) to pass this class. I recommend staying clear of this class and Mrs. Lottes!

Literally the best professor I've had in college thus far! The only thing you have to do is show up for class and do ALL the assignments, and an A is a very real possibility :) She cares about her students, and will work with you if you have any problems. Definitely a fun/easy class you should have when your schedule seems to be a bit overloaded.
Great teacher,she obviously loves what she does. The topics could get a bit controversial, but always stayed fun. I would totally take her again and probably will.

I loved her. But you Have to be in her FYS to really get to know her and enjoy the class, since its made of maybe 15 students. If youre in her 333 class with a lot more people you probably wont like it. But i loved going to class everyday, we got to talk about very personal things and learned a lot about sexuality. If your a Freshman, TAKE HER FYS
Worst professor ever!!!Lectures are all over the place. Never clear. You feel you know everything on the exam and end up failing the exam. Please do not take her!

Thought this would be an interesting class about sexuality in the world today turned out to be more of a history lesson. Makes you do alot of reading online about things written 50yrs ago. She hates Bush with a passion and won't shut up about it, a feminist too. wish there was a better teacher, i feel this class could've been very interesting.

Loved her!  Very nice, super enthusiastic, and passionate about class discussions.  Attendance is mandatory, but worth it anyway because she gives in-class assignments and basically tells you what the test questions are.  The only downside: a ton of readings that weren't always relevant (or, sometimes even brought up in class).

I really like Dr. Lottes but she is a little whacky.  Her lectures are all over the place and her tests are extremely difficult.  You really should go to every class because she gives random facts that are not in the book and also has in-class writings.  Tests are based on readings and class lectures.  Don't take her if you need organization!!

Terrible! I am a poli sci major and didnt think that Human sexuality would give me the hardest time compared to my other classes. Lottes is very unclear, her tests are ridiculous, and she is not interesting. Instead of making the class hard like she wants to, she makes it uninteresting . I can't believe she is teaching, UMBC needs to say Bye Bye.

This class turned into group therapy more than anything. The tests are extremely hard, but the homework is fair if you do the readings. There is a lot of reading though!! Dr. Lottes gets off topic a lot, but makes us laugh. The class is very open to discussion and opinions. I liked it, and I got to make a lot of new friends in this class!
No Comments
No Comments

This is also one of the worst professors I've had.  Her lectures are not clear and seldom have anything to do with the material being tested. FREQUENTLY shares situations about her sex life even in her non-sexuality classes.  I was really looking forward to this class but was let down completely.  Do not take any classes with her.

The worst professor I have had at UMBC.  If you want to learn in the class you must get past her major attitude and frequent political tirades.  The subject matter was interesting.  Tests reflected more what you didn't know (facts and percentages) than general teachings of the course which is one of the worst approaches to learning I've encountered
what a nutcase... would never take a class she taught again.
She is so passionate! Interresting lectures and very easy to talk with! Take a class with her!!
No Comments

She assigns a LOT of reading.  Some do well without ever reading in the class.  She gives a lot of extra credit to make up for poor exam grades.  She gives random classwork sometimes, so you must go to class.  She's pretty liberal and provative. Don't take her if you're conservative.

She gives a lot of extra credit to make up for the somewhat hard exams.  The exams are only hard if you don't memorize little facts and percents she gives you.  The concepts are easy to understand.  At times, she can be very political.  If you can't handle politics, don't take the class.
Contradicts herself more than any other professor I've ever had. She is passionate about her statements, even when they don't make any sense. A nice person, just not too good of a professor.

I really wanted to take this class and it was really fun for the first week.  Dr.Lottes is very nice and esily approachable but she contradicts herself a lot and is really trying to push her views on everyone else.  Even though I agree with her many times, I don't think that's what teaching is about

Great teacher, very nice, loved her lectures. If you are very conservative u might not like being in the class all that much. I loved going to class!! Tests are difficult but not if you study and work with her.
she'sso funny and nice!
Great teacher!! Her tests are hard, but I was in her office a lot to clarify things and she helped me out. I got a B. YAY for Dr. Lottes!!! :)

I thought Dr. Kramer was the best & toughest professor when taking any physic course.  He would lecture on and on, class after class. At a point I was so lost and frustrated. After 1 office visit I realized the problem was not Dr. Kramer but me and everyone else in the class for NOT asking questions. Student & Professor together produce learning.

Long ago Dr Kramer Kicked the I can't out of me. I started his class and I would give up after 15 minutes of not being able to solve a problem. I passed his class on the second try, and have never again felt like there was a problem that could whip me.  He was the toughest professor I ever had, and a lot of my success in life is owed to him.

Dr. Kramer is an excellent professor. He teaches like an old school MIT professor; because he is. His class is extremely challenging. He will expect you to derive and integrate everything fully with out a trig table. He explains everything clearly. And is open to questions. He does lots of examples and expects you to recreate similar ones on exams.

I needed to pass a course in physics in order to stay on task with my engineering studies and boy did I waste my money and my time attending this class, so vague and he/his TA's all have a different method of teaching you the subject so you get confused quickly.

His tests do not reflect his teaching style from class, making it remarkably difficult to study for them. No wonder his students have a hard time trying to figure out his vague exam questions. If you can avoid taking his class, please do so. It will be near impossible to receive an A.

Insane, when grades come out i wouldnt be surprised if this is the second class ive failed with him as professor. Exam questions are vague so you dont know how to answer them. Doesnt explain situations or give many examples.

Not helpful, he tries to get you out of his office as quickly as possible as if his office hours were simply for show. His grading is without mercy. If physics profs were reqired to push an old lady down the steps in order to teach, Dr Kramer would have brought his own grandmother. Only take him if there is no other option and forget about an A.
Extreamly hard, I failed completely. He doesnt give any examples and works only in variables.

I liked that he does not collect any homework. He gives quizzes every week, but those does not really count as  a grade.  i did not even attend the classes, but I still got B.  So, you just have to do the best on the exams.  If you don't wanna go to every class, this is the teacher you are looking for.  Good Luck.

Had him for both 121, and 122, his grading is brutal on the tests even though the test questions are generally easier than the homework.  He doesn't collect hw, but rather gives quizzes on it and uses the quizzes as a saftey net (get 7/10 or > on each one guarantees a C).  His grading scale is very subjective but you do better than you think.

To tell the truth, his tests arenot not that hard, the homeworks are much harder. His grading is brutal but OK, I still get 100 twice and an A too. He is definitely a good teacher for students who want to major in Physics.
His grading is brutal, which tends to defeat any confidence which you have in your Physics ability. Study for the quizzes like they are your only chance to pass the course, because they may well be.

I really can't agree with his teaching style.  He gives really hard exams and rarely hands out any partial credit.  This leads to absurdly low test scores.  What's worse is that he dosn't actually teach the subject matter well.
His tests are EXTREMELY difficult... however, he never collects homework, and his quizzes are fairly easy. Just watch out for those tests...
Class average on tests 20-30%, no curves, no partial credit. 12 Quizes, one each week with problems from the HW. You get 7 or above on each you get a C in class.

Very hard to understand, especially when he moves fast. Again what he teaches in class is not used in the homework at all. Spends alot of time deriving the formula in variables and not enough in telling you what the equation means.
you've already failed.

Dr. Kramer is clearly a very good physicist, however, sometimes he moves a little fast and in-depth for an intro course.  He is very helpful during office hours but his exams bite hard!  You shouldnt worry if u've had physics b4 in HS or with another prof.  THERE IS NO PARTIAL CREDIT.

All the above reviews are correct, he is a hard teacher. Very few people i know pass this class especially with him on their first try. The only reason to take him is so you can tell everyone, ah i've had krammer this professor can't be that bad.
Ok. He is probably the hardest teacher on campus. But if you can study your homework you are guaranteed a C. Its not that hard really its not!

Tough grader.  Partial credit almost doesn't exist with him.  Very hardcore about the subject, and expects the same from his students.  His lectures were a waste of time, as he tends to devote it to problem solving, and not actually teaching.

First, this class is extremely hard to begin with.  Second, what he gives for homework/quizzes has nothing to do with the exams or lectures.  He makes you derive equations they have in the book on exams. Need a STRONG calc background. Avoid

My grades on his 4 tests went in this order: 30%, 95%, 20%, 95% - and I haven't a clue what I got on the final. I wound up with a C, and so did my friend with a test avg. in the high 80's. Take him if you have to, it's an experience you'll never forget.

He's a notoriously difficult teacher and spends most of class deriving proofs instead of teaching material,so his teaching style's difficult to learn from. BUT he's always willing to help you out. Tough but fair grader

This class was the easiest class I have taken. He is super nice and helpful if you need but watching the lectures tells you everything you need to know. Start research paper early though if you don't want to stress over it.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: He is the best professor i ever had.
Provided useful study guides and pulled his test questions directly from lecture slides. Final exam was replaced with a term paper of any EMS related topic.
He's an amazing teacher, easy to understand the material, and extremely accessible out of class if you have questions.
Great teacher, lecture were engaging. Quizzes are open note but exam are lockdown browser. Clear exam study guides are given.

1 big paper, easy grader, works 3 jobs so lectures were never synchronous and he was busy, easy grader, quizzes are easy if you use notes, finals are tricker but still doable, does like to do trick questions but just use notes, easy class

Very creative with class content, and very adaptive with the pandemic. The pandemic hit in the middle of the semester when I was taking this class and he solved problems quickly and was able to use resources to make project and group discussions work.

Overall great prof! The class is what you would expect for an intro course and he tries to be flexible with any student issues. The class isnt super hard as long as you show up to the classes and complete all the assignments. Easy to talk to!

Hes the man! The tests are based on his PowerPoints and the stories he tell in lecture are interesting but mostly funny. There is a research paper but its not as rough as the ones you do in English class about a random topic and you get to choose what youre writing about (based on EHS). Overall great guy and the class is an easy dub.
Best professor I've had, answers emails quickly, fair grader, and a great guy overall.

He is the most chillest professor I have met. 2 exams, 4 quizzes (3 highest), attendance (just look over ppt) and weekly discussions. As long as you put in the effort, you can get that A. If you go over ppt, you are in good shape for the exams.

Where do I even begin with this professor? He's the best thing that has ever happened to my life. He's given my life meaning. His enlightening methods has been nothing short of a blessing to me and my aspirations for success. Without him I wouldn't have made it through the darkness which we call school.

Not only did he teach me what and how to be a good paramedic, but, in doing so, he has taught me what it means to be a good person. As a direct result of professor Yang challenging me to learn about EMS, I gained a deeper insight into who I am as a person. I only hope my children are fortunate to have a teacher with half his talent.
Literally best professor of my undergrad career
I have no idea what I learned in this class. But had a blast doing it.
Great instructor. Cares about students and always willing to help you understand class material

Very knowledgable paramedic. He will work with you to make sure you're proficient and confident in your skills. Will go out of his way to help you understand complex topics that you may have difficulty with.
love him :)
