I took this class because the name sounded interesting, but I am not a PoliSci major/minor. The content turned out to be a lot more dry and difficult than I expected, and there were long readings and few assignments--including open note quizzes, but the prof was very understanding about it, especially towards non-majors/minors.

I really enjoyed the subject matter of this course, however, do not expect to do well or be respected unless you adopt his views. Also, if you are in a group project and your partner drops the class, expect to do the whole thing on your own. His quizzes are open-note, but he is definitely trying to trick you, and again, you need to adopt his views.
Inspirational class - if you do the reading you'll do well and get a lot out of it.

If you read the cases, and show up for class, you should be able to get an A or B in this class.  The prof is clear about what's required and how to understand the cases.  If you work hard he will help you out.
The material in this class could be pretty dry but the prof made it very interesting and relevant to what's going on today.  If you do the work, and show up, he will help out a lot.
This was an awesome class dealing with issues that are really important today.  Davis made the cases come alive and taught me how to analyze war and conflict.
This was a great class.  We covered some tough topics and the class discussions were really interesting.  The professor is willing to help if you do the work.

Good professor, no doubt. Love his classes. But I have one problem with him he doesn't respond to emails. Like who are we supposed to ask for help?  If you are reading this, please respond to emails. You ask us to email for questions, but you don't respond...
Not a good law course. Professor isn't bad but he isn't open minded enough sometimes and is very picky with your argument... it is often easy to see his bias. I would not recommend this class.

con law- not easy, not terrible but you definately have to work for that A.  if you don;t wanna be a lawyer- stay away. if you do wanna be a lawyer- proceed with caution. it may end your career aspirations.
One of my better teachers. He enjoys the law but is very aware of its short comings. Read and participate in class. Being silent will not help you in any of his classes
Ugh, its very difficult to understand what exactly you need to know. Quizzes are irrelevant to the cases and you need to adopt his point of view. Great class but I was not happy with his teaching.
Interesting class. Can be boring, but he's a great professor.
Took him for con law. Hard and boring - worst combination! Couldn't stay awake in class. Studied very hard/did all the briefs - still got a B. Final Paper was a drugery to write.

International Law. Was pretty boring, had to drag myself to class every week. Wanted to study IL until I took this class. Hope your class participates cause he gave ours a random pop quiz one day. Not a bad professor, should just think of better methods to engage student interest other than asking "What happened in this case?" every day.

Teaches a very slanted version of the "law." If you followed his methods to law school his style and paradigm would ruin you. Kind of a joke. Some hypotheticals work but others seem like he makes them up at the last minute. Definitely does not grade consistently. Unremarkable and easily a professor not worth having.

Dr. Davis is a great professor. He really is interested in his subject and will help you a lot. He also is very understanding and if you have a problem or need help, he'll be more than happy to help you out.
Perfect teacher!  Will expand your brain and you won't even know it!!
The class wasn't too hard, but his quizzes could be challenging. There's a paper to write at the end, but don't expect much help from him on it. I asked for my grade on it and never got a response.

I did not particularly like Const Law. It took up every ounce of my time to complete the readings, and going to class did not help me at all. I got the best grade on a quiz when I gave up at the end and didn't study at all, and when I studied my butt off I got a D on the quiz before.  Tons of trick questions and confusing hypotheticals.

Incredibly liberal.  Recruited for amnesty international during class.  Lecture oriented, but he barely helps your understanding of the cases.  Do the case briefs, use the book and the web.  5 quizzes and one paper.  An A is not hard, a B is easy even if you skip.  Posts notes and review on his blog, which is usually more helpful than not.
I got my first B from him. I was not amused but I got over it. Hes not very helpful but if you do the readings and get a study buddy, you should be fine.
No Comments

The class part of this was very easy. He has you do one assignment (research paper), a moot court argument and a final paper. Class attendance is optional, but you should really go. The internship part is great-he works hard to make sure you get place with a good place and really enjoy it. Take the class if you can.
You have to read the material and attend class, pay attention to the hypotheticals. The questions on the quiz can be tricky, but you don't stand a chance just trying to wing it.
Good class, do the case briefs and you'll do fine

Overall a good class.  On paper you think Con Law will be hard, but Dr. Davis makes it interesting and worth hearing.  Quizes are pretty fair, if you study.  Uses a lot of Simpson references for hypotheticals.  Nice guy, good class overall, a decent class to take.

I went to this teacher with an almost "A" a week before the paper was due and asked him if i was doing mine alright.  He said I was going in the right direction and was doing fine.Studied hard for the final quiz and ended up with a "B".Not always clear, does teach well, but not the most helpful.Nice teacher however and good class on the whole.
read the cases and do the briefs and you will do well.  Tests are fair.

Dr. Davis is helpful, but can come off as not caring at times. Definately enjoys the subject and tries to get you to as well. Nice teacher and if you read the material you should do well. Alot of reading and case study.

I'm not a Poli Sci student by any means and found myself having trouble in this class. Good, funny teacher. But don't do what I did... read the material. And read it until you understand it. Then you'll like the class.
Great teacher. Liberal...but I can over look it. Lectures are entertaining and the exams are fair.

Professor Davis is great!  Not only is he friendly and funny, he also knows his materials well.  Moreover, he's extremely helpful to students.  He's an easy-going guy who would not hesitate to answer your questions or assist you in any way.  I definitely
really great.  really funny.  one of the best!
Kewl guy.........Extremely liberal, like me.  Classes was pretty easy.  Mostly discussion. hardly no papers and very little reading

Lectures consist of him reading off the slides for 90 minutes, so have fun teaching yourself for the semester. Discussions are basically the same thing along with quizzes with lots of questions and a very small time limit. It's a boring class overall, and poorly structured IMO. The SQL part of the class was pretty interesting. Final was curved.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: His lectures are convoluting because of his accent. Nevertheless, he's really smart and gives instant replies to student e-mails. Take him for 651.
nice teaching.

Dr Wang is a extremely helpful and intelligent.  He responds to emails quickly and is helpful in kind during the classroom labs.  In my opinion the lectures are kind of rushed so concepts are not completely clear.  But he is teaching Dr. Canfield's lectures and using his online textbook which has many typos.   Exams are very very difficult.

Don't take this class if you don't have to! Very disorganized when it comes to everything: assignments, readings, deadlines, even if class is being held on a certain day or not. Everyone is usually guaranteed a failure on exams as we have to remember very specific information in order to do well. Lectures are not engaging, makes it hard to learn.

I do not recommend this class. I took this class online and maybe that has impacted the quality of this course. Extremely writing intensive and lectures are not entertaining. Briefly explains the subjects over lectures, but then requires us to remember specific details about the textbook material. She seems like a kind lady, but wouldnt recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Discussions, quizzes and papers were never due at the same time/day each week. Some assignments were not for a grade, but this was never specified. The class was abruptly told to buy tickets for a performance that was also not in the syllabus and told we would come together later and talk about it as a class. Sweet lady but not the most orginized
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Group projects

reviews.comment: Class is ridiculously boring. material is interesting but she finds a way to make it feel like hell. class is extremely writing intensive, which is insane for a 100 lvl class. Textbook readings are extremely long, boring, and you must remember specific details for the test. Would not recommend this class to my worst enemy.

This has been the funnest and one of the most unique classes Ive taken at UMBC. DANC201 Dance History was really fascinating if you are fan a of history and enjoy learning about very cool looking dance spectacles. The studio class session were super fun with practice while also breaking down the details and elements of all sort of old style dances.

Professor Vasbinder was is very specific about her grading. Participation is the most important part of your grade and there are 4 to 5 other papers which are 2 to 4 pages long. but she is very specific abut grading and grammar like English or writing class. if you are a good writer and participate in all class, it is really easy and fun class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Does more essay in this class than my actual writing intensive class. Very particular in grading paper if you're not good at essay look elsewhere. Few actual dance class. More of a lecture and writing intensive class than anything. Quiz looks like a test.
No tests, just a couple of papers which are butts easy. Participation is a thing but it's hard to not get points for it. Great fashion sense.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Tests? Not many--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment:
Really smart guy; gave very informative/compact lectures with good organization, verbal style, and chalkboard writing organization. Pay attention in class, you will learn for sure.
Homeworks were reasonably challenging (but doable) and covered discussed topics; same with exams.

Terrible professor. He lectures way too fast, and it is almost impossible to understand with his accent. His homeworks are nothing like the things he teaches in class, and tests are absolutely impossible. Avoid at all costs!

You won't need the book if you go to class. Shen's lectures are incredibly organized, and he is very prompt with test grades (always a week after). Be forewarned, though: this man is a machine. Expect homework every week including on exam weeks. Overall, a nice guy and a very knowledgeable professor.

Dr. Shen is a very good teacher. He explains what you need to know for exams while also covering harder material that will not necessarily be on an exam. Homework was sometimes difficult but if you go to office hours he's very helpful in guiding you towards the answer. Exams were straightforward and covered the exact material he said they would.

Dr. Shen is amazing. But MATH301 is very hard and he's a tough teacher. You're going to have to work very hard for a good grade. However, Dr. Shen is very approachable and  helpful outside of class. If you put in the effort, he'll help you do well.

Great guy and a decent professor. Class lectures were long and most proofs he did in class were straight from the book so the lectures didn't help much. However, he is very approachable and helpful outside of class. Very generous with partial credits on exams as well. Take him if you can but be prepared to crack open the book as well.

I'd say hes a very fair professor. His tests pretty much cover everything we learn without the intention of tricking students up. He does have an accent but he teaches the class at a very reasonable pace. I would definitely take his class.

Dr. Shen is an easy grader, and with attendance not being mandatory, it is quite easy to get a good grade. He is a little difficult to understand from time to time, but that does not detract much from the lectures. His tests are not bad if you know the notes. A decent professor, overall.
very helpful, crystal clear to understand, good example problems. very straightforward
Good teacher. Bit of an accent but just sit in the first row and you'll be fine. Material is easy and he is straightforward.
Good teacher. He tries really hard to make it understandable. Exams are easy HW easy. class easy
Extremely nice guy, extremely helpful.  Very clear handwriting and lectures.  Tests very fair.

It's hard to understand his Chinese accent in the beginning however, throughout the course, I started to understand him better.  Conceptually on the material, I still have no frickin' clue what's going on and I think I'm still managing to get an A.  Just make sure you go to class, turn in HW, and try to pick on patterns like any other math class.

I had a hard time understanding his lecture so i barely went to class except to turn in hw. But the material isnt hard  and his quizzes and examz are very fair .Very quick grader and he is not too picky either. Do the hw w/ good understanding u'll b fine ..
No Comments

Nice guy. His accent was not bad, but he was terrible at answering questions. All work was graded by the next class, and he was especially generous on exams. The lectures were painfully slow though; he would take 5 minutes to show that 2 * 3 = 6.
Nice dude and fast grader. English could be better, but very helpful if go to him
Nice & helpful

Not the greatest but probably not the worst.  Hard to understand but you get used to the accent.  Didn't answer questions very well but offered office hours.  Quickest grader ever and very fair with partial credit.
Can't understand him! Heavy Accent! Nice guy but can't understand him!
Nice prof. Gives lot of partial credits on exams. Will do well if you look at this examples problems he shows in class.

Awesome professor! Very sweet is a generous grader and gives good feedback. (Doesn't give free points but will help you actually learn). Allows you to revise your work for partial credit if you mess up. Took her class in Fall 2019 don't regret it. Easy if you're good at Spanish.

If you ever have the chance to take a class with Profesora Jiron - DO IT. She is funny, understanding of students, and also engaging. I always looked forward to her classes. The best part I appreciate about her is that she makes you *EXCITED* about learning Spanish! I went from just doing it for the requirement to being invested in it! 10/10!!

Profesora Jiron was the best teacher to take spanish 102 with. I struggle with the class and she was very helpful and offered the class extra credit oppurtunities. She is a very nice person and would take a class with her again.

Profe Jiron has been one of the best language teachers I have had. She is very helpful to students learning Spanish for the first time and cares about the well being of all of her students. She starts every class with some good Latin music and tries to engage all students to actively learn (as a language should be taught). 10/10 would take again.

I have always disliked Spanish because of my teachers, however, Professor Jiron is the nicest, most caring, and most helpful professor I have ever met. She really cares about the success of her students and will help you with anything. She is very relatable, easy, and fun to talk to, and you will have a blast in her class because of how fun she is!

Listen to the reviews here, avoid this guy if you can. Don't think he's teaching anymore tho because he has no interest in anything other than his research. Makes no effort to teach the material, just rambles about unrelated stuff and makes students teach the class. But hey, you might have a 1% chance of winning a fraction of a $15 amazon gift card

Quizzes for every chapter, case writeups that can be done in groups, rapidminer. Final were split into 2: online (use quiz questions) and written (probability, matrix, etc). He's a bit all over the place, way he does group presentation doesnt make sense. He makes the students teach the class on new subject which make no senses.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--So many papers

reviews.comment: Based on how his grading system is set up, as long as you do your work in this class, you are guaranteed at least a B. All of his quizzes are online, the case writeups are graded leniently and he gives you an outline of what to expect from the final. He has real world experience that he shares it with the class during each lecture.

He said he won't be teaching the class next semester. SUPER boring class, I wish it wasn't a requirement for IS majors, as I have not learned anything from his class and it was a total waste of time. The class consisted of case write ups(graded on completion), online quizzes, class participation/presentation, final.

Lectures can be boring. But he does talk about applications of data science (cool part) Grades case write ups hard. And the Final Exam is on concepts not taught or practiced in class. Uses a whiteboard but you cant read it at all, because the whiteboard is small and the classroom is large
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Class was heavily disorganized and the structure of the class kept changes throughout the semester. We were assigned extra work during holidays and a late assignment during finals. What should've been an easy class became frustrating.

Professor Gong is a friendly guy. He likes it when you call him by his first name. This was his first semester teaching at UMBC, so the course was a bit disorganized and hard to follow. The class had online weekly quizzes which were difficult. I learned a lot from reading the book more than his lectures.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--SO MANY PAPERS

reviews.comment: As other reviewers said, RJ is a great prof. I would actually take the time to meet him during his office hours whenever you have questions! I ended up talking to him about future CS classes and his recommended profs.

I'm taking CMSC 313 with RJ, and he's doing a wonderful job in his first semester teaching it. He explains concepts clearly using slides and his iPad, offers extra credit, and makes sure we know what's on the midterm and final. He's funny, engaging, and highly recommended!

Cannot recommend RJ enough. Awesome understanding guy. Took both 449 and 426 with him and they were awesome. If you review the slides on your own, no need to come to class. Participation activities REALLY help with understanding and applying the course content. He makes everything really intriguing - and he is very knowledgeable

Bro is the professor you want for all your classes and that bum gave 1 star cuz the class itself is hard. I have no interest in cyber and hearing the class "Malware Analysis" I thought would be the hardest of all my classes, but RJ made it understandable AND fun even with me still having no interest in this topic. Lectures always help with hw
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: Very down to earth and very helpful. I'm ngl I didn't have much of an interest in cyber security but he made lectures pretty interesting for me so that was a pleasant surprise. His homework's are also very hands on and he usually provides resources to help you complete it
Very worst prof kindly avoid him and take another course instead of this. Tough assignments

RJ is by far one of the best, if not the best professor I have ever had. He engages with the students, is always available on Discord, and is super helpful when it comes to homeworks and assignments. He is very passionate about what he does and is a must have for 426. Homeworks and exams were challenging (not overly difficult) and super engaging!
Great lectures, homework was reasonably challenging but engaging and informative. Only tests are midterm and final, which pull directly from lectures and homework. Cool guy all around.

Greatt professor that is super available outside of class. Gives demonstrations and helps with the homework, provides lecture notes and recordings, very friendly. He also bought snacks for the class multiple times. Not much more you could ask for in a 400 level class.

RJ was pretty cool. He's relatively young so he's very relatable, while also being experienced enough to be knowledgeable on the subject matter. I felt as though his grading criteria was very fair and anytime I got points off for something I felt like it was entirely justified. Definitely recommend.
He's just extremely epic all around, nothing bad to say. Worth taking for electives even if you're not interested in the course material.

RJ's currently a PhD student, and is super knowledgeable about most things cyber. The class is pretty easy as long as you attend lectures and pay attention. I didn't really take any notes and still did well. The midterm was rough on grading, but he doesn't write them. The labs are enjoyable and you're given more than enough time to finish them.

Tough course but Webster makes it super interesting, digestible, and is extremely helpful in understanding the content. Highly recommend him as a professor. No midterm exams but homework is hefty to account for this.

Standard math class with a great professor. He works the course around the students to make their learning experience as good as possible. There's a normal amount of homework, and you should study for exams and tests. He makes the course very enjoyable and understandable whether you love math or not. Great at office hours, very compassionate.

Weekly HWs; lectures were in-depth and provided explanations for each topic (did not expect you to know stuff beforehand); great person overall and had entertaining lectures; half the quizzes were take-home; exam 1 was difficult and did not have enough time; I studied mostly through textbook; two exams (exam1 20%, exam2 30%, quiz 30%, hw 20%)
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Genuinely the best professor I've had here. Had a teaching style that did exactly what I've been needing other math professors to do. Course content was taught in an engaging, accessible way. The work that I needed to do outside of class was so much easier because the lectures were focused on conceptualizing ideas, than endlessly doing examples.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: If you are just looking to "get by" a class with an A, don't take a class with Dr. Webster. He makes you work like hell on his homeworks. He is made for the students who want the absolute-best understanding of the content he teaches, and are WILLING TO PUT THE WORK IN!!! He offers TONS of extra credit, so if you fail that's almost definitely on you

He is among the best lecturers not just in math, but the university. His class are all intellectually stimulating. It is impossible for you to come out of his classes without learning something. That being said, his class will be your full-time job (a bit inconsiderately) with homework regularly taking multiple days. Plan your schedules wisely!!!

Had him for 221. Webster is the goat, he is incredibly intelligent and great to learn from. I absolutely loved his lectures, they're entertaining, and he focuses on making students understand concepts, making time for lots of questions. Go to class, he gives extra credit for those there. Not a difficult teacher, just teaches difficult subjects.

Was he a good lecturer? One of the best I've ever had. Was he a tough grader, had mandatory attendance, and would get verbally annoyed if students came in more than 5 minutes late or frustrated with you in emails? Also yes. Don't get me wrong, he teaches amazingly, but things can be worse outside of classtime than in it. Good overall though.

This professor is helpful but his teaching skills was not for me. There are only 2 tests that carry 45% of your grade so if you fail one, you are at the level where you cannot reach A. Taking it at HCC was so much easier and understood the material better.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Absolutely amazing mathematics professor! I love how he goes in depth with the topics and uses real world examples mixed with a good dose of humor to keep students learning and engaged. When online, he used a flipped classroom approach which proved very effective.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: He is very knowledgeable about his field and focuses on the conceptual concepts of differential equations more rather than solving problems. He is entertaining and encourages questions. However, he does little to no examples in class or in his recorded videos. Also, during quarantine, I would have preferred live lectures instead of recorded ones.

One of the best math professors at UMBC! This guy is so friendly and serious at the same time. Very helpful during class and office hours. The class is difficult but lectures are not boring. If you want to take this class he's the one you want to take it with!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: He enjoys his work and is a great teacher, taking care to help anyone who seeks it. Missed many classes early, but attending each of his lectures afterwards, and going to his office hours for homework/subject help allowed me to easily catch up. Lectures are great and he was the most helpful prof in office hours I've had. Hands down favorite prof.
very chill prof best one for english& very understanding

Dr. Justice was my favorite professor at UMBC so far. He's really funny and super knowledgeable. His class is very low maintenance and his lectures are him reading from a power point on his phone. His class has 4 easy projects. He is very helpful too and always happy to talk about literally anything. You also don't really need the textbook.

Prof Justice is a funny and good professor. Some lectures can be a little boring, but overall it's a good class. The assignments were innovative, and if you show up to class and participate, you're golden. There is a lot of reading, and attendance is enforced. He sometimes goes on funny tangents about jujitsu or fish but I didn't mind. I recommend.

One of my most interesting profs ever. He was a little scattered in terms of due dates early in the semester, but we found a good system. He does draw out lecture sometimes, with stories that are funny enough to keep you engaged. Assignments are kind of fun, and he's not too tough of a grader. 10-ish small papers, with 4-5 larger projects.

Took him in Spring 2024. Prof. Justice is probably one of the best professors I have ever had. The class itself is very participation-based and you are graded on attendance/participation, four 3-4 page papers, and weekly discussion posts typically based on assigned readings. He explains concepts clearly and is very entertaining. Highly recommend!!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Hilarious--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Justice is a great Professor! He really cares about his students and extremely funny! He talks a lot about fishing!

Honestly very intriguing class and Professor Justice is very engaging with his students. The workload in the class is mainly discussions and essays. The discussion topics are very interesting and the essay workload is light. Overall would recommend this class.

He's a great professor; he makes dad jokes every day. Everything was online—the quizzes, the exams, and the in-class activities—but you did have to work in a group for them. On the quizzes he makes sure you're not able to use chatgpt and itll give the wrong answer but anything other than that he was great.
Take him you won't regret it, The best professor I had at UMBC, he is really kind, funny and very understanding, if you do the work, participate and show up you will pass

He was a really great professor, one of my favorite PBHL class professor. He genuinely wants students to understand the lectures and is very understanding. Exams were take home, and quizzes and class activities were easy to complete. He also encourages students to succeed if you get a low grade, he offers extra points for class participation.

Great professor who really cares about his students. He is willing to help you get the grade you want if you put in the work. You don't need the textbook as long as you attend class for the lectures, but he almost always releases you early. I had weekly in-class activities and quizzes, but they weren't hard, 3 papers, and 3 tests.

Dr. Chu is one of my favorite professors at UMBC! PBHL 300 is a boring class but he made it as fun as he could with dad jokes!  I 100% recommend, super easy and straightforward professor, show up to class its worth it since you can get extra credit, and as long as you do all the assignments you'll get an A!

Super down-to-earth and relatable professor. He is very Gen Z coded. He has in-class assignments and quizzes so attendance is recommended but they are insanely easy. His exams were given online, take-home and super easy. If you attend class, you'll be okay, but it's also not mandatory! He was also very understanding, unlike other professors.

Such an amazing teacher. He has in class assignments and quizzes so attendance is recommended but they are insanely easy. His exams were given online, take-home and super easy. I took PBHL 316 with him and he's able to take boring content and make it fascinating with this lecture style and personality. Definitely recommend him!!

Chu is a great guy and one of the best professors at UMBC. His lectures are entertaining and very useful. Homework isn't hard; he gives you 2 weeks to complete an assignment. The exams are also pretty easy if you pay attention in class. He gives a lot of opportunities to receive extra credit. take his class if you want understanding professor

My favorite prof of all time. Really cares deeply about all of his students and makes an effort to get to know you. Very chill guy! Lots of extra credit opportunities and the course work was very manageable. Difficult because its all application based but if you study for the exams and just follow the rubrics he gives you will do fine. 10/10!!!!!!!
The chillest guy ever

The GOAT. I skipped all his lectures and feel bad lol, probably would have had a higher grade but still came out with an A. Very nice guy and all the assignments are slight. I barely paid attention to the textbook and did some of the learning myself since I would skip lectures and still was able to do good in the class, and I'm not even smart
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Graded by few things--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: Pretty easy class with him. There were only two tests, about six short assignments, and four projects. He walked through how to do each project and was lenient in grading. Lectures are useful for understanding what the projects are about. He is also a pretty nice guy and has interesting stories to tell. Some concepts are hard to understand at first

Great guy. He was always very friendly, genuine, and caring towards me. I respect his work and I would recommend him. The class was at least very easy and he helped a lot with the assignments, projects, and homework. One of the easiest classes I've taken. Just show up to class.

Professor Jungwirth is awesome! He's a genuinely great person and truly cares about his students. He makes a difficult class easy to understand with minimal stress. He has a nerdy sense of humor that he always manages to utilize during class. One of the best profs at UMBC. If you did fine in 313, you'll do great in his course.

Excellent educator. Taught hybrid class with in-class and online students together. Some technical glitches with campus system that he quickly fixed. Prof took a dry, boring subject and made it interesting. If you took 311 before this class you’ll do well in this one. Accessible outside of class for help and good at quickly responding. -EH

This teacher for the most part was not terrible. He was disorganized probably because that was his first time teaching online. The deadlines were extremely flexible and he is very understanding. Their are multiple lectures you would have to read and he would base a lot of the projects on the lectures but if you understood 313 you good
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: There is about 6 projects and 4-6 hw. The professor is very understanding with time to complete assignments. Class was not too difficult if you reach out for help. The assignments align with the lectures and if you took assembly you will be fine.

He's a good professor who makes lectures interesting, and he actually ties in the lecture material into a project. There're alot of assignments but if you reach out to him he'll work with you. Overall he's a really nice guy and does a good job at teaching a boring class and making it interesting. Would take again
Amazing professor. If you have to take 411, I highly suggest you take it with him. He's knowledgable and always willing to help. Made my semester a whole lot easier.

If you want to pass CMSC 411 easily, this class is your best bet. If you want to learn something about the course material, you're better off looking elsewhere. I will never look at popcorn the same way.

Great class to take before graduating. Waited 1.5 year to take. Had two guest lecturers. Learned a lot from professor. Awesome text. Current experience and technology. Recommend to other grad students. Would take again. A+ class.

Professional professor: book author, numerous patents, Dept Army ARL, experienced, lecturer of several classes both undergrad and grad. Taught real world knowledge. Challenged class. Thinks outside the box. Helpful. Gives extensions if needed. Taught on all levels for the variety of students from different programs. Would definitely take again!
Enjoyed class very much. Popcorn example best summarized lesson. Full class every time. Would take again. Recommend to other friends. One smart guy.

As far as 411, hes an easy A. Minimal effort but you wont learn much. I suppose that doesnt really matter though since the class isnt a pre req for anything. Not the best at communicating but is open to extensions if you ask. No syllabus but hes getting better at class structure every semester so your mileage may vary. 2 take home exams.

Semester consists of a multi-part popcorn project to optimize higher-level code for RISC architectures, but were never really taught anything about making said optimizations so it was just face-value 'convert C to MIPS'. Jungwirth is cool n nice n all, but if you wanna learn anything about computer architecture look elsewhere.

Professor Jungwirth was the best thing that could've happened to me. Every single one of his projects had a purpose. After all, I rather be learning about how to apply hysteresis to a popcorn machine than learn how to make a 16-bit ALU. Best professor, highly recommended, will dissapoint.

Assignments were very ambiguous, there was no syllabus so I had no idea what my grade would be. I didn't really learn anything, the exams were take home and assignment deadlines were always pushed. He was a nice guy, just not the best as a professor.

Class was a joke. Lecture was supposed to be 75 minutes but barely lasted 20. We didn't even have a syllabus this semester, that's how unorganized he is. Taught us the same 3 MIPS Architecture commands every single class. Didn't grade a single assignment all semester. Speaks at a whisper level in a lecture hall. Take for easy A and to learn nothing
Helpful feedback to my assignments. Responsive to inquiries. The textbook can be chosen to be more carefully. A useful class for my foundation in information systems domains.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Respected

reviews.comment: Careful grading, extra credit for extra efforts. learned much.
carefully read all homeworks and papers with useful feedback. will recopmmend this professor for future students.

reviews.comment: I attended this class due to the degree requirements. Dr. Jeng provided guidelines with ample examples from variety of sources. The burden of reading was heavy. Difficult for people who had not any experiences in programing and IT experiences. I have benefited from this class by exposing myself to the fundamental knpwledge of computer networking.
Feedbacks are well done and timely.
Detailed feedbacks Professional. Well-prepared.

reviews.comment: The content is well prepared. The group project is inspiring and I appreciate my teammates. Nice experience!

reviews.comment: I like the way being orgznized for the course content. The lectures were good.
I learned much from this course. The group project is helpful. The feedbacks are timely.
I am new to technology and this course is probably over my head. I appreciate Dr.'s help me going through this tough process.

reviews.comment: I did not need this course for credits yet I think it is a good choice to take as needed for future technical work.
The content is not super difficult yet the details required attention. The lectures are well-prepared. The feedbacks are fair.
I havfe received detailed feedback on my work. I appreciate the efforts made by Dr. Jeng
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Inspirational--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Dr. Jeng is a hard working and inspiring professor.

Ineffective and unclear communication. Takes time to respond to emails. Takes 2 weeks, and two emails to receive an initial submission feedback. Lengthy and confusing feedbacks. Templates do not align with the learning objectives. Overall, my experience was frustrating, stressful, and confusing, and it led to a decrease in my motivation.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--So many papers

reviews.comment: Dr. Jeng is an industry expert and longtime teacher in the domain of computer networking. He is very good at helping me to understand the content of network technology. It helps me greatly as I am a refresher in the computer network. The test and the content are organized in a way that fits a person like me. Appreciated Dr. Jeng very much!
Wonderful teacher and considerate professor. Very responsive to my questions. Always listener and an expert in the field.

Disorganized. Feedback is unclear. No real live examples. The problem sets are not clearly written and are tricky. Excessive work for a 3 unit class, 12 timed problem sets, 12 conferences where one large contribution with references and 2 explanatory comments to other postings are required. A midterm, a comprehensive final, and a research paper.

Not very organized.  Changed the syllabus half way through the course to included a group term paper.  Had no grades on discussions through the first half of the course.  The material is the class wasn't too bad - but the professor was very confusing.

I took the honors section. If you have to take a certain class and a section with Dr. Oakes is available, definitely go for it. Saw other reviews saying she was disorganized but I never felt that. Great at engaging lectures and a balanced workload. Take notes on lectures and do the readings and you'll be fine. I studied my notes before the exams.

Dr. Oakes is great! Sometimes a tiny bit unorganized, but who isn't? She is super flexible with deadlines and gives great feedback! My one issue is that some of the assignments are more media literacy focused rather than history focused.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Dr. Oakes is truly one of the nicest professors ever. Occasionally she is a bit disorganized, but is VERY open to extensions if you make it clear that this hindered your learning. She is such an expert in this subject and so valuable as an instructor. I would take every class she offers if I could!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: A genuinely kind and caring Woman. If you talk to her, and let her help you pass, you WILL pass. This is a hard class, but she is a good lecturer and deeply invested in the topic, which does make it easier, believe me.

This was a six-week online summer class. She struggled with some of the technology. Lectures were disorganized. She walks you through everything the class prior to a test or essay, just take notes and you'll be fine. Tons of writing for a 100-level. Lots of group work in class. Easy to reach by email if you have questions.

Dr. Oakes is one of the nicest and most-caring professors I have had at UMBC, very accessible and easy to talk to. I took HIST 103 for a culture credit, however, I was not expecting the level of work we do for a 100 level class. 3 exams @ 60%, all short answer, and essay. 30% on 3 papers, 10% attendance. Great class, just expect to put in the work.

I love Dr. Oakes. She is so kind and an amazing professor. History 201 in itself is a difficult class but she's the reason I got through it and understood what I was doing. I don't specialize in Asian history but plan on taking more courses about it just to have her again!

She is one of the best Professors I've had at UMBC, also one of the sweetest people I've ever met. Truly cares about students and is very lenient. It is not an easy A but she is worth it. You won't regret taking her.  I've had her for two, once a week, 2.5 hour classes, and she makes the time go by.

I've taken every class Prof. Oakes teaches at UMBC and I'm a bit bummed that I can't take any more this year. She's so sweet and really cares about the subject matter so her classes are really interesting and the lectures are engaging and easy to pay attention to. The reading load is pretty sizeable but I've always skipped it and done fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: She was so nice! She would give me feedback when I needed it or if something came up she would accommodate my situation.

Professor Oakes is probably one of, if not the nicest professor at UMBC. She's very knowledgeable when it comes to East Asian Civ, and her lectures are where most of the info comes from. I barely opened my book, just relied on the notes she gave in class and did fine. You have a 5 pg paper at the end, but it's not that bad. She's great.

One of the best teachers. She lectures very well, and clearly knows the topic. But if you don't take notes, LEARN, otherwise you will flounder when it comes to the tests. But if you take good notes (As in, at least 2-3 pages, back and front, a class) then tests are easy As.

She is an awesome professor! One of the best classes I have taken so far. She takes attendance every class/going to class really helps, so don't skip! Lots of reading, but you can pass without them. There is one paper due on a book that is assigned. She gives you a study guide for every exam and even tells you the essay question. Easy A!

Prof. Oakes is very god at discussing the topics in this course; she knows how to hit all the important points in history. Tests are easy IF you study your notes. There is always chances for extra credit, but through more obscure history q's. Study. Paper at end was challenging but worth it. Very kind, works with students, approachable.

Prof.s preparation for the course needs to improve. Felt like she was winging it for most assignments.  Guidance for one paper came 2 weeks before it was due, and after we had read the 1st book, so had no clue what I was supposed to be looking for in the book. Tons of reading, almost as if she doesnt think you have any other courses to read for.

Great professor, would love to take history with her again! She knows the subject and very helpful! She does a grading system based off the +-, Don't worry, there's extra credit, and few quizzes. Come to lecture and you don't need your book. There's 3 exams (both essayshort answer),  a 5 page paper, and no cumulative final. Great lectures :)!

Julie Oakes knows the culture of Japan like no one's business! She's a free spirit to boot which sometimes works for and against your favor. She's super knowledgeable and very well read but sometimes her instructions are a little unclear. She is a busy woman who is also at times difficult to nail down, but once you do she'll help you out.

If you like east Asia and need a GEP this is a must. Perfect balance of easy and interesting. She assigns a lot of reading but most of it isn't necessary, except for the documents book and the online documents she assigns. If you attend lecture and take good notes you'll get an A, if you miss lecture be sure to get the notes from somebody.
Lectures are great but often long. ATTEND THE CLASS OR YOU WILL FAIL.

Extremely knowledgeable and  passionate on the subject. Lectures were really refreshing and interesting; if you're not into art history  and writing don't take this class; there's a 10 pg essay on topic of your choice. Very open to student ideas + interpretations. Exams are mini comparison essays. Grades fairly and offers really good feedback.

Good teacher, she know her stuff! Need to read a lot. She is a really hard grader. I thought her class was really interesting but it is very challenging. I think she needs to remember not all her students are history majors and she should not be that hard of grader on minor details for those who are not used to her system.
She's amazing. If you're planning on taking this class definitely choose her as your professor.

She's great! I'm purposely taking her 380 class next semester just so I can have her again!!! Although the reading from the textbook is boring you don't actually need to read it, only really need to read the documents book, which she goes over the documents in class. 3 test (short essayessay) and 1 paper (plus 1 page papers randomly). Super Fun!!

She is so nice! She is my favorite professor i have ever had. Simply read the text, participate in class, and take good notes to do well. She does not hesitate to help any student in need, and she is an extremely fair grader, not to mention how passionate she is about her subject and how well she teaches. Class is never boring!

She is extremely nice and very approachable; she's also very chill . Really passionate about Asian history and definitely knows what she's talking about. There are a few essays, that are pretty decent. Tests are short answers and an essay. I totally recommend her.
She is one of the best professors at UMBC. She does assign a couple papers but she will try her hardest to understand your points and give you a better grade.

Super nice and passionate about Asian history. No homework to turn in, but many readings and a couple of short essays. Can get away with not doing most readings as long as you take notes from lectures.  Tests are fair and prepares you well for them. Mostly short answer and essays. Managed to make Chinese history during Communism era bearable for me

Super nice and passionate about Asian history. No homework to turn in, but many readings and a couple of short essays. Can get away with not doing most readings as long as you take notes from lectures. Tests are fair and prepares you well for them. Mostly short answer and essay (which I prefer). Will continue to take other classes taught by her.

Prof. Oakes is a fantastic teacher and very knowledgeable about so many Asian topics!She's a tough grader on essays but she gives many opportunities to improve not only your grades (extra credit) but your writing. She is also very personable and makes herself available to her students.

Professor Oakes is a great teacher. I loved the class and I wasn't even interested in the subject to begin with.There is midterm and a final tests, no quizzes, and a one 10-12 pg paper. There is a lot of reading but if you go to class and take notes you will get a good grade.

Exams are a mix of short answer and essays. The saving grace? She gives you a list of names  of every person or event that might be asked about on the exam. If you want an A in the class, Wikipedia search every single name she gives you, read the summary paragraphs and make study guide for yourself. MUCH more efficient than reading a 500pg textbook

A great professor for this class. She is very knowledgeable about Asian history, but also has a knack for teaching gender studies. She was easy to listen to, was well prepared for lectures, and she made the class interesting. I really learned a lot and did well (for a psych major). I would recommend Professor Oakes.
Very passionate professor. Loves material concerning japan and wants the students to succeed

She's passionate about Japan, but it never really bothered me because I love Japan. Her exams are very very fair, as long as you pay attention to the pictures that she goes over in class and you know everything on the study guide. Exams consist of an essay and explaining and identifying the significance of images that she gives you.

Dr. Oakes is a newbie, but she's awesome. She really loves Asia--especially Japan--and it's evident in her teaching. The course requires a fair amount of work for a 100-level, but she thoroughly explains everything. She's an adjunct, so if a student really needs help, I'd recommend contacting the TA directly.

Worst professor ever. Tests are composed of essay/short answer/analyzing images and there are 2 essays and she grade it really harshly. IF you are going to take this as an elective, then take something else and try avoid her. Also there are LOTS and LOTTTTS of reading and are really boring unless you are history person.
She's a wonderful professor! Super sweet and extremely passionate. Keep up with the readings, come to class at least once a week, and pay attention to the slides: you'll do fine!

Good professor. Very passionate about the subject. However, I found the class boring and continually found myself falling asleep. But again, she was a good professor and her exams were easy since her review sheets covered everything that would be on the test. She graded fairly and her essays were well-graded as well. I recommend taking her.

I have heard a lot of complaints about Prof.Saraswat, but to be honest, she is one of the best math professors I have ever met. I hated the lecture so much because it didn't make much sense to me, but I started to visit her during her office hours and she clarified everything for me. Challenging course, but you will learn a ton

Pretty good professor. Fairly dull lectures but incredibly helpful during office hours and always willing to provide resources/help both in class and out of class. Her tests are difficult though, so you will likely need to study. However if you need to take calc 2 highly recommend as she will prepare you and give you solid foundations.

Yes, she has an accent. Yep, shes tough. and YES, her exams are mad challenging. However, I walked out of this class confident that I learned the concepts. She prepares you well for the final. Look over old exams, they help a lot. She is very interactive with students, I appreciated that. I consider her a very good prof. -study hard and reach out!

She enjoys teaching and is very interested in helping students who seek help. She wants to get to know all her students personally even though it is a big lecture class. Her tests can be challenging so if you find yourself struggling I suggest you get know her well and she'll be more than happy to help. She also curves a lot.
Skips over many steps which makes it confusing. Indian Accent makes her somewhat hard to understand. Class average was very low because she expects us to spend 10+ hours a week on Math.

Take this class if you want to learn on your own time. She skips so many steps on problems it is hard to know where she is. Also her hand writing is terrible. The class average for the first test was a 56, the second average was a 65 and so many people have dropped. she says its our fault.  She does gives extra credit so that helps.

horribly structured class. you will have to dig through lecture slides, announcements, and the syllabus to find directions for a singular assignment. She makes directions very confusing and projects are badly structured as well. Her class isn't impossible, but it's one of those classes that is so rough it will make you re-think your major.

She isn't a bad professor at all. However, this class is heavily group-project based. Most of the solo work is only homework. For exams, it was lockdown browser and in person. Exams were majority portion of your grade. If you study the slideshows VERY WELL, you will pass this class. Her slides are literally the same on exams, all multiple choice.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: AVOID HER AT ALL COST!!

I was nervous for this class after seeing the reviews on here but it ended up being my highest grade this semester. All you need is minimal effort to do well. Tests were straightforward and fully multiple choice, the answers lined up well with the powerpoints. Group project can be rough with others, so take charge. Very little and easy homework.

Class is incredibly difficult to focus on and actually attend, she spends a full hour and 15 mins explaining something that could be explained in maybe 20 mins. Assignments are incredibly confusing to complete, expectations are unclear, you will hunt through five different files to piece together the expectations for a basic homework assignment.

The majority of your grade is earned on three exams; the rest is the group project. The hardest part of this class is finding companies to work with to get the needed information for your semester-long project.  As long as you can find the companies needed and study for the exams, you should be ok.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: She is horrible. You can read the book and attend every class and still fail exams. Her power points are useless and exam questions don't even match them. If you're BTA it's honestly one of the hardest courses you'll take, try to read the book to semi understand what is going on in the class

Honestly the worst Information Systems professor I have ever had. Everyone fails her exams. She is horrible at putting grades in. You never know what your grades are because she doesn't input them in. The whole class fails exams but she curves them. If you have to take this class for your major beware and know it's going to be awful for IS 202

All graded at the end of the semester, even after the semester ends. Rubric is kinda vague and impossible to gain points back. Don't know what your grade is. The project determines the whole thing. Hard to get useful feedback on each part of the project before the grading is done, so theres no way to fix it.

reviews.comment: truly a shame that a fascinating class is being taught by an arrogant professor. I was very excited to take this class but from the very beginning, she was very passive-aggressive and made herself unapproachable. I would have better luck teaching myself the content than going to her office hours just to be met with such a condescending demeanor.

Professor Kahl is not a good professor. She is passive-aggressive and her teaching style will not help you learn anything. Some exams contained information that we had not learned which made the exams difficult. She grades the group project deliverables harshly and doesn't submit grades until the end of the semester. Don't recommend her.

Her teaching style is boring and confusing. She never explains anything clearly including lecture, group project, and exams. You have to basically memorize her incoherent lectures in order to pass the exams (1st exam was 100 q/1 hr). Please choose another professor if you can for this class.

I had her for IS 202 in the fall of 2022, She was and is hands down the worse professor I have ever dealt with. She would have a "Study session" for the exams that would go over the PPT and then have completely different questions on the exam DO NOT TAKE, AVOID AT ALL COST, if you value your mental health.

Please do not take her class. She is a very mean-spirited teacher who will not help you at all. Lectures are all over the place. Will lecture about everything but what you need to pass the test. If it is between her and not taking the course. Plan to take it next semester or during the summer.

I think she's an okay professor, personally not my favorite. There's 3 exams and a group project that lasts throughout the whole semester. Exams are hard so make sure you take the time to study!!! She will call you on the spot to participate and if you don't know the answer, she'll make it seem like your stupid for not knowing.

3 Exams worth 60% of your grades / Group project was 30%
The rest is just showing up and doing small assignments. If there was a different professor, I wouldve taken them instead.
It's just not worth it.

I took her class virtually in Spr2020. I had a hard time finding out who my groupmates were via BlackBoard and email. Then when I found out, the "leader" kicked me out of the group instead of trying to reach out to me in the first place! Prof didn't help at all, was unresponsive to emails, and didn't even grade my deliverables without a team!

Lectures are unnecessarily complicated but the textbook/material is usually pretty easy to understand and not bad. Her powerpoints will let you know which sections to skip. Hope you get a good group for the group project. She teaches like we already know what she's talking about (even though we haven't learned it yet) but is a nice person.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Group projects

reviews.comment: Professor Kahl would try her best to explain your questions if you ask. The way she set up this class is very hard to get good grades. Pray for that you have nice teammates, if they dont work, and you dont want to do everything all yourself, you fail the project. Study the slides for the Exams. Grading system is a mess.

Kahls teaching style can be described as seamlessly switching between speeding through very brief notes and ranting in an attempt to teach material, but falling short of successful. She says there wont be trick questions, but there will be. She includes new info on tests and is also poor at responding to emails. Her grade book is never correct.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: This was my experience in her online class. Material is easy, but don't try to wing it. You have to attend lecture; sometimes she rambles and sometimes there's actual information. Hope for a good group that works and talks to each other, for the project, so it isn't on a single person to do the entire project. Good luck, you're on your own.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Group projects

reviews.comment: she made it the most difficult class i've taken at umbc. avoid her if you do not want to have to retake the class again or have a bad experience with online classes. i was taking about 26 credits and i passed all 23 except hers, despite everything being online, & some having the same reqs. as her class. i dont recommend.

I had Professor Kahl for both IS 202 and IS 440. I really like her as a Professor and as a person. Very nice and enjoyable to talk to. Group projects was really difficult because group members were never on the same page. The course is basically a capstone course, so the material itself is not difficult, the group projects make the course difficult

The class is similar to IS 300. Stay away from the 3 hr lectures, they're just a drag. The prof tries to make it entertaining with a few stories and real-world examples. The 2nd exam is normally the hardest but was changed due to COVID. The virus also made the group project harder. You'll need to interview & find improvements for a real business.

So the class isn't that difficult, but Professor Kahl made it a lot harder than it needed to be. The group project is a systems analysis and technical proposal of a real company - requiring you to meet with managers and observe the company - but this was made difficult with Covid. She's not very lenient and lectures are boring. Read the book!
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Group projects--Tough grader

reviews.comment: You got to pay attention in lectures. You got to attended it can boost your grade at the end. You have a group project, which sucks, but make sure you organize the group and take charge for a good grade Three test, ten homeworks, paper, group proposal-project. Theres deadlines for the group project so its not the bad just stay on top. Good class
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Margaret Kahl is hands down one of the rudest professors you will have the displeasure of attending class with at UMBC. She does not curve exams or final grades, late submissions are not allowed, be prepared to get hit with her constant sarcasm, do not miss any homework/assignments, and use textbook as a studyguide bc her Powerpoints are worthless.

reviews.comment: DO NOT TAKE! SHE LITERALLY DOESN'T UPLOAD GRADES AT ALL SO BE PREPARED TO BE IN THE UNTIL IT'S POSTED NY THE END OF THE SEMESTER ON YOUR TRANSCRIPT.

reviews.comment: This course was not designed to be an easy A however Prof. Kahl will help you out if you truly put the effort in your studies for this class. Ask as many questions as needed because the group project is pretty much like a final exam. Choose your group members wisely. Prof. Kahl knows who is a good student or not. Study well and you'll pass.

reviews.comment: Dont take her class. She thinks that students are only taking her class in the school and give them a lot of work to do. During test if you move your to stretch she will fail you. She also checks your hats, shoes, clothes to make sure you are not cheating. You want to fail so definitely take this class.

FEW examples of materials taught, that end up being on the test. Powerpoint uses detail to a minimum. I suggest communicating with her after class for extra help AND using your group for studying. PAY ATTENTION and stay on track. You'll need to do research on the side for all the topics on the powerpoint to learn it all.
reviews.rating_tags: TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: she is a very challenging teacher, she is old and petty, she checks your hats, arms, book bags before exams. she is a very tough teacher, and will fail for 1% if needed too. don't take her and you will thank me. take her and you will regret it
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: She is an okay professor, goes off topic too much. Exam reviews are pointless, they will not help. A lot of work and grades aren't posted online so good luck staying the in the dark till they are submitted to the office. You will have to buy a book and read it, her ppts are just bullets, which she just simply repeats during exam reviews :)
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--SO MANY PAPERS

reviews.comment: Lots of work. Take the group project seriously because is 20% of your grade. She is not a bad professor but she is not the best either. Make sure you read the book and take notes.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: This class is much easier than her 202 class. Whatever she has on the board will be the free response on the exams. Make sure you read the textbook if you want an A. Take the group project work very seriously because she is a tough grader. Also, chose a good group because you will be working with them a lot throughout the whole semester.

Most challenging class for BTA majors. I received an A but had to work very hard. The exams consists of MC, T/F, and a max of 3 open response questions. The diagrams she works through on the board are always the free response questions. If you want to get an A, go to every single class, understand the diagrams, and READ THE BOOK.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tests are tough

reviews.comment: I think she's a great teacher, nothing like the reviews I initially read. People are paying so much for college that I think they want to be handed a grade these days, but she simply expects you to give her class a fair amount of effort and her expectations aren't unreasonable. The book helped me, I aced the last two test. Just study & give a care.

After reading the reviews on here, I was tempted to drop her class after the first day. Ms Kahl is not a hard professor but you have do your work. She is really nice and easy going. I am glad I didn't  drop her class because the class is easy if you do your work. You have to read the book to do well on the tests. pick good group members. NO FINAL.

It's so ironic how she is so strict on plagiarism when  she copies the PPT slides online. Overall, she is a great professor. Very boring class, you cannot use electronics at all in class- she will call you out for it.  lecture heavy and tough grader. Study and do your work, getting A is very attainable. Choose group members wisely as well.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Course materials include 3 exams, which mostly consist of free responses that of potential ones will be given in class, 2 projects, and 5 assignments. She gives lectures only for chapters 1-4. Remaining chapter lectures are given by the groups of students through presentations, as part of their current event projects. Grade A is fairly attainable.
Worst professor ever. DO NOT TAKE!!!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: 3 exams, everything is off of the ppts. MEMORIZE the ppt, she loves lists. All her exams are just list stuff & compare to a real topic, so if there is a list make sure you know it. Shes a strict grader & there is group work so make sure you have a good group. Avoid if possible-doesnt teach, just reads off ppts. Attendance is mandatory, but useless.
I didn't pay to have students in the class lecture me about course materials.
her exams too hard and everyone failed the first exam because she does give a study guide. i managed to get a B by getting a 75 on first exam and A on the second exam.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: She reads directly from the slides and does not input anything meaningful.  She makes the class much harder than it has to be.  Read the book yourself in order to do well on test, her lectures do not prepare students for whats on the test.  Do well on the group project,it will help your grade. It sucks that shes the only teacher for IS 202,440.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Kahl is a very boring professor, She does not use blackboard(strictly email only), her lectures are all just reading the power points, she doesn't add any input besides stupid stories. Always takes attendance so definitely show up. Overall, she's not that bad in comparison to the other professors. just go to class, study for the exams and your good

Avoid at all costs, seriously. Her lectures are about 20 slides long each, and she makes it take up the whole 2.5 hour class period. Her lectures are her talking without actually saying or explaining anything. Tests are insanely hard and the group project is graded like a grad level class. Thinks she's God's gift to the Earth.

Lecture slides and whatever little actual "teaching" she does will not help with tests.  Be ready to actually look (read: READ) at the book for specific details on lecture slides, they were on the tests.  Very anal personality,  but a necessary evil to BTA majors as the only professor for IS 202 and IS 440 during Fall and Spring semesters.

Terrible professor. She only reads off the slides. Expects students to read the chapters but exams are 100% based off her slides. She does give points back for any questions that majority of the class gets wrong on.
Do not take her. Very hard grader. Barely teaches. All lectures are from powerpoint...

She obviously doesnt care about this class. If she was a good professor she would know the material. Instead she reads word for word notes that she has straight from the book. Drones and boring. Will tell you words and concepts, but will not define or go in depth. She said exams wont be tricky. I studied very hard as a 3.4 student.I found it tricky

Do yourself a favor. DO NOT TAKE HER CLASS. On the day of the exam she decides to send an email out to everyone to bring a folder to class as a divider to ensure nobody cheats! Are we in middle school?? This is ridiculous!

I am an average B student and this class is honestly not that bad, but the professor makes it harder than it really is. For exam we weren't even allowed to look up because she would assume we were cheating... Is it wrong for me to look up just to think. Just because you look up doesn't mean you're cheating... Avoid her at all cost. Not worth it.

Professor Kahl is a very difficult professor. Either you have it her way or its the highway. Teaches directly from slides and slides are directly from book... Basically paying her to read the book to you. She is insanely strict for no reason and honestly seems like she hates her job. Most likely because she is an adjunct professor.

Be prepare if you take her class. She reads directly from the slides. There are three tests and make up the major portion of the grades. The test is quite hard but if you are study and well prepare then you should be ok. Just the reminder, good luck :)

Tests are a major portion of the grade. It you want an A or B don't screw up on the tests. For group projects divide it up and make sure everyone actively participates, you will have  better deliverable if everyone participates. No extra credit. Attendance matters if your grade is borderline. Class is boring so bring a pillow, jk.

Review materials for tests are not consistent with actual tests.  Some material that is on reviews are not on tests, and material not discussed in review are on tests.  Be ready to actually look at the book for specific details on lectures from now on, they were on the tests.  If you even look up from your test, she will give you a warning.

Didn't learn anything in this class. Would not take a class with her again. Do not use your phone in class or she will yell at you, and she is looking. Don't buy the book, it's all from the powerpoints. Her tests have you apply what you learned to real-life examples, so you have to make sure you understand everything or can BS pretty well.

She's not the best but she's not the worst. You don't really need the book. The info on the tests come straight from the PowerPoint's and class discussions. Make sure you ask any questions that you have in class because she's really bad about responding to emails. Overall, she's not a bad professor. I would recommend her.

Professor Kahl is very nice. She reads directly from the slides, and you need to ask her questions to clarify. No need for the book. She also either takes forever to answer emails or doesn't reply at all.

Very simple instruction. Class instruction is somewhat boring when she's only teaching from the PowerPoints. Study the PowerPoints PRIMARILY, but still read the book. The tests are EASY. 20 MC and 2 essay questions (usually). The semester long project requires WORK! Make sure you have a good team and you got an easy A. I ashamed I didn't. Good luck
THE VERY BEST PROFESSOR THERE IS IN Info Sys. This is the 2nd time I had her (IS303) and she is awesome. Easy A if you study the slides for the exams because the book isn't needed.
The silver fox is the easiest teacher i have ever had at umbc. take the easy a.

This professor is awesome. She is the easiest professor ever. You don't need the book! Don't buy it. Also, you can A's the exams by studying the slides and the notes taken in class of things she write on the board. I hope she is the same way for IS440.

She takes a bit of getting used to. She likes to do pointless activities sometimes but sometimes they help (quite a few are things you do directly on the exam!). The exams themselves are from from her lectures/slides. If you are a borderline grade like me, she'll bump you up for attending! DO NOT BUY THE BOOK IF YOU ATTEND CLASS AND TAKE NOTES.

I have had Prof.Kahl for IS 202 and MGMT 210. This teacher is very clueless. She reads straight from the slides and usually has alot of time left. So she makes up dumb activities to do. The project is very boring and is basically a time filler. Honestly she needs some new teaching techniques and a new curriculum.

no need to buy the book even though she tells you that you'll need it. the format of the tests changed, but either way you need to memorize a lot. She is very helpful and just study the power points. our last test was all multiple choice and T/F so i don't know if she'll keep it that way.

Prof. Kahl is a sweet lady, and will tell you exactly what to do to get an A. The course consists of 3 exams and a group project. The exams are directly based off of her lecture slides so DO NOT BUY THE BOOK! You'll never open it. She is a list person, so be prepared for some heavy memorization for the tests. Overall, not too hard for the 400 level

This class required more studying than any other class I took this semester, but was by far the least useful. She's a nice teacher, but her tests are really hard considering the essay questions are random and are about 60% of the grade. Her classes consist of taking notes from her notes. It's very important to write down everything.

prof Kahl is the worst instructor i've ever had. She didnt even bother showing up 4 class half the time, and when she did she was usually late. Didnt learn anything. Subjective grader. Lazy. Makes mistakes on her tests. Lies about having posted stuff online and sending us emails. Unreachable by phone/email. Completely unproffesional.
One of the worst IS teacher.

very easy course! She hands out all of the notes for the course, just read them and you're golden. Do not buy the book, you will never open it. She gives easy exams, and no final. There is a group project that she assigns at the beg of semester. It is VERY easy. She is funny and really helpful too
No need for text book. Really wants students to succeed. Tests are rather easy. Attendance is extremely helpful. One semester long group project- kind of sucks but plenty of time is given

She knows her stuff but she is a very boring lecturer and does not bring much fun to the class. Tests are hard, there are only 2 of them and both contain about 10 chapters of information, be prepared to study your butt off if taking this course.
The class is Very boring :( hated the group project and homeworks are pretty dumb.
She gives very boring lectures and a pretty stupid project, which she said a lot of students enjoyed but that was absolutely not the truth. Not helpful at all.
Very boring teacher, needs to be teaching high school rather than college. Handwriting is hard to read, pay close attention when she gives notes - otherwise you'll get lost.
A very fair grader. The class contains a lot of opinions and group project is easy and fun. Go to class and you will do well.
Great Teacher, Different teaching skills but knows her stuff. Very polite and helpful.
very easy, very clear group projects ,

All she does is read her notes & draw diagrams.  The class is easy and she is a VERY lenient grader on the tests (30% and 45% of your grade).  Not as bad as you may think at first.  Please get into a GOOD group for the project!

She's an "OK teacher."  It seems like she's just making up stuff at times, but she CURVES both of the tests (30% & 45% of your grade) so most people get Bs on each.  The class is pretty boring, but it's not hard.  Make sure you get into a "good group" for the group project (25% of your grade).

I took both her sys analysis classes. It seems like BS, but trust me, it's not. I've been a programmer/analyst for a few years. It comes in handy. Half of IFSM is learning how to problem solve. Her teaching seems like a bunch of retarded buzz words and theory, but that's what it's like in the real world. Get ready for it SUCKAZ!

This teacher does not do her job. She scrawls illegible handwriting on the board but if you don't get every detail you won't do well on the all-essay test. She tries to be helpful but unsuccessfully. A good third of the class dropped in the first week. The only good thing is I somehow swung a B, despite C's on both tests so there must be a curve.

Tries to be intimidating at first. If material is new to you then you learn a lot. I absolutely hated the sememster group project (due to bad group) but admittedly I learned a bit from it. Lectures can be fun. An OK teacher.

Took both classes with her and could not tell the difference between them.She gives identical information and identical examples on both classes.Didn't learn anything in 300!Test stupid unless work in field and can add beyond class level stuff!

I've had better professors...she brings across the materials well...just make sure you jot down what she teaches and you will be fine for the exam...the project is also a no brainer...Overall I give her a B.

Wonderful teacher.  Nice person, and knows what she's talking about.  Very clear about what she teachs and what she expects you to know.  As long as you come to class and take good notes (and study them), you will pass the class.
Very unorganized teacher. Seems like she is making stuff up on the fly sometimes. Didn't learn a thing even though I went to every class.
Doesnt exactly give you the most clearly explained test questions.  Taking notes is important, but doesnt mean you're getting the information that will be on the test.
Assigns a group project the first day of class which is due the following class. Each class consists of a group presentation. Where is the teaching? I pay to be taught....
No Comments

I took night class and her notes were helpful.  Get on her good side early and she'll take care of you.  Exams are essays and PERT Charts, and working out diagrams. Easy, just go to class to learn examples and get in a responsible group for the project.
