Take Tighe or someone more experienced if you can. Also his lectures are just him re-writing and re-doing all the examples in the textbook. Not really all that helpful.
The class was easy. His quizzes are not hard, just show your work.

His lectures are engaging, explains content and encourages questions. Appears friendly, but has a tone of he's god and you're an idiot. Tests are graded and written to try to fail students, even said they're intentionally extra hard. 1st exam class average 62% and whole class was left at the time limit. Tests like students are math professionals.

Nanes is friendly one on one.  It's evident he likes math, but he goes 100 miles an hour without clearly explaining the details of what he is doing.  He thinks we are at his level, so he teaches at his level and not at ours.  His tests are deliberately much harder than anything we do in class. I guess this class is supposed to build character.

i can't blame him for my bad grades but the quizzes and exams are near impossible. the fact that my korean TA sucks at teaching and then follows up with strict grading is not rubbing me the right way. great professor, horrible class

Wow, I have never seen a prof at UMBC be this clear and upbeat. Even though the semester just started, I am glad I took his class. His lectures are clear, homeworks are straight from the book(with the answer at the back, just show work) and he helps very well when you visit his office. I am hoping his exams are easy too. If they are, he is perfect!

I enjoyed this class, I don't prefer her teaching style though. There wasn't enough immersion, the curriculum confused me (ex. we know how to say our major but not our age or interests), she put a lot of emphasis on some topics but not enough on others, and there wasn't enough spelling practice.

Had for both 101&102. Such a wonderful professor who's great at teaching the language! She is native Korean and able to give helpful feedback on pronunciation and writing. Gives lots of opportunities to practice speaking in class. Homework was easy and graded based on completion. Will ask for students to practice with each other in class.

Prof. Kim is super sweet! She gives a lot of homework and there is a lot of speaking/social engagement during the classes which can be kind of draining at times if you are an introvert, but it's very clear that she cares deeply about her students and wants them to succeed. She is great at her job and listens to her students if they have any issues.

I loved Prof. Kim! She was super nice, and easygoing, and made Korean very easy to learn. Attendance + participation was graded and you get lots of homework that helps you learn the material. Quizzes weren't hard. You will have to practice writing and memorize lots of vocabulary though not to mess up your spelling. Great course and teacher!

very nice and down to earth guy!! his critiques can be really tough but as long as you do what he says you'll be fine. even if you're a talented drawer, throw out anything you've learned before and go into your drawings exactlyyy the way he says. he doesnt put in grades until the end of the semester tho which can be frustrating.

Mr. Kissack may be THE most interesting guy. I have never had an art teacher so passionate about art.
At the start of the semester I thought I'd hate it. But I stopped taking myself too seriously and ended up enjoying the class a lot. 
It's easy to do well if you're trying to improve. He can be rude, but he's genuinely proud of his students too :)

Passionate about art, His teaching revolves around onomatopoeias, which, if you're taking this course as a fun credit and aren't as artistically minded, makes it incredibly difficult to understand what he means when he gives feedback. Many people seemly dropped the course, but if you ask questions about what he means you'll be fine. Sometimes rude.

Most of class is spent listening to him talk. His critiques are very strong worded and he can be overly harsh at times. Grading is strict to his standards, and no grades will be put in blackboard until the end of the semester. He knows what he is doing art wise and is very good at it, but he expects a lot for an introductory drawing course.

He yaps a lot during class and is overall pretty dramatic imo. His lectures are beneficial and does give advice on how you can improve. He is pretty particular with grading, which makes sense; you just have to draw something weekly and a final drawing. I found him kind of rude at times to other students or to myself when he would give critiques.

Similar to what other reviews say, his instructions, particularly for homework, may not be very clear. Apart from that, his lectures are captivating and engaging! He's the first art prof. I've had who provided me with genuinely helpful critiques. Overall, he is a laid-back individual passionate about his craft. Def my favorite teacher by far.

As the other reviews say, his instructions aren't as clear so sometimes I had to ask him after class for clarity but other than that, his lectures are interesting and he's friendly. He makes these sound effects while he's describing an illustration so the lectures are comical sometimes! Overall, it was a great experience to take his class!
He is incredibleeeeeee. The comments on my work were so detailed and well thought out, made me do better.

Genuinely the best art teacher I've had! Mr. K is really great at what he does, and as long as you don't procrastinate on assignments and put in the effort, it's pretty easy to do well in this class. I only wish he would post his assignments on bb with a description of what he wants, but he usually does go over assignments in class!

Very skilled at what he does; his demonstration sketches are clear and for the most part illustrate what he wants us to learn. However, his lectures and assignments are presented in a confusing way and instructions are never written down. Make sure you have at least three people's numbers in the class. Mostly does not grade below a B.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Graded by few things--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Spends a majority of the class ranting on about his own personal opinions and beliefs, has ZERO written explanations on how to do well in his class, will grade poorly for doing anything outside of what he demands but wont tell you all his demands, insulted every member of class no matter skill with no instruction on how to do better. Condescending.

I learned so much not just about drawing, but life from Prof K's class. what a classy guy. as long as you put in an effort and challenge yourself a bit, you'll do fine. usually just one homework drawing a week. nothing too crazy. no midterm or final. just some one-on-one crits. COMPOSITION, QUALITY OF LINE, and PLAY OF LIGHT. that's it. rock on.

Best teacher I have ever had. He is very nice, and all the work I did in his class really helped me become better at drawing. His lectures are very engaging. I can tell that he is passionate about art, and he really cares about his students. His class is the only class I was actually excited to be in. I enjoyed everything about him as a teacher.

Mr. K was fantastic! You can tell he is passionate about art, drawing, and composition. His lectures are filled with rich descriptions of textures or moods to inspire us as we draw. His feedback is thoughtful, honest, and encouraging. If you are someone who's just there for the grade and you don't care about the spirit of art, he may annoy you.

This professor expects so much and he puts out very little. Makes crazy sounds and tells pointless stories. He is extremely judgemental. Favors students who kiss up to him. Also isn't clear when homework instructions and harsh when giving his critiques, especially if he isn't a fan of your work. Not encouraging at all. Do not take his class!!
Great guy, active in arts scene in baltimore city. Super down to earth and encourages personal drawing style choices while still promoting technique.

He's a great professor. He always explains what you can do better in your drawings, and will understand if you speak to him about any problems you have. Classes are very entertaining and he fully explains what we need to do for each assignment. Dont be afraid to ask questions. He grades you based on your improvement in drawing, not how good u are.

Professor K is great. He grades based on your skill level and he understand that everybody is not a great drawer but still tries to bring out each student's greatness. He's very entertaining and passionate about art. I really enjoyed his class.

Prof. K is absolutely an entertaining and helpful teacher. He focuses on composition, and if you focus your art work on composition, you will get an A. As long as you try, he will see that. I thought he was hilarious, and his class was fun to attend. Overall, he's a great professor, I wish he taught more classes at UMBC. He is brilliant

Ok so idk about the person under me, but  I'm taking it right now and Mr K is a great guy. You can tell he's passionate about art just by the way he talks about it and makes his sounds. He takes the time to  go around and physically correct your drawing if needed. Its a complete joy to take his class. If you dont take it serious, you wont do well.

Completely useless teacher. I came out of the class with the same level of drawing skill that I had going in. He will state that he dislikes your drawings without actually telling you what specifically is wrong with them or how to improve them. I received back one graded drawing that just said "This is problematic"  on top of it and nothing else.

I have to say that Mr. K was one of my favorite drawing teachers ever. I took this class because it was a requirement for my major, but ended up having a blast. He was charismatic and fun and made getting up at 10 to draw an absolute pleasure. His witty comments and helpful critiques make him a wonderful professor and I would recommend him highly!

I had him for a visual concepts course and I swear that was a trial. He was so particular when grading but explained nothing when giving the assignment. It was so annoying. I almost wanted to quit the art program. I mean, I got a B. But no matter how much I pestered him I could never get a clear answer on how to get an A.

Nice guy, fun class, just don't expect an A unless you already knew how to draw before you stepped in the door. Don't expect him to explain the reasons for your final grade in a coherent manner either, but if you just want to learn/practice drawing and don't care about the grade you'll have a blast!I only recommend the class under those conditions.

This is a science with a lab class. Professor Kirvan, is a really awesome science professor. She is very understanding and willing to help you with an assignment if needed. The assignments aren't hard but their not easy either. But as long as you come to class, turn in the assignments and put effort into doing your work you will pass the class

I took this class for my Science w/ Lab credit. I would absolutely recommend if you are taking it for the same reason. Course content was super easy, even though work load was a little tedious at times. There were about 3 assignments each week relating to a lab. As long as you keep up with assignments (which is not hard to do) you'll do great!
I ended the class with over an 100%. She's funny, nice, and understanding. Lab reports get exhausting and dragging but topics are super easy.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--So many papers

reviews.comment:
Ms. Kirvan is such a great professor; she's caring, funny, and easy-going. Everything in this class is super easy too, I took this class for Science plus Lab. But there are a lot of things in this class too;
 I was overwhelmed, tbh. Professor Kirvan, I love you but I wouldn't take you again :(

She made topics easy to digest, encouraged students to ask questions, and make helpful connections between math topics and the real world. The mid term and final have built in extra credit, she gives extra credit on some of the worksheets in lecture, and is heavy on partial credit for quizzes and exams. I finished the class with a grade over 100%

lectures weren't mandatory but i still went, and she notices who comes every time and who doesn't. offered 1-2 bonus worksheets in lecture. easy material, provided old quizzes/exams to look at before every quiz/exam with almost identical questions. always encourages people visit office hours. really nice put pics of her cat in lectures lol. easy A.

I recommend this class if you need a lab credit. Rebecca Kirvan is amazing and there's no midterm and final. She gives lots of extra credit opportunities, and she can excuse anyone who has missed one lab. She gives group quizzes like the T-RAT, and she gives really good feedback on lab reports. Even if anyone is tired she spends time outside.

I took this class as my lab credit, and she was great! She was very refreshing, and honestly made me feel like I was back in high school (in a good way). The content is painfully easy, and labs are a lot of fun. If you try even in the slightest, you're guaranteed an A

Such a great professor, especially if you are a beginner to pre-calc. Lectures are easy to follow, provides notes to go along with, and provides old exams/quizzes which are very similar to the ones you'll take. Lots of extra credit throughout semester.

I took her for Fall 2024. Its a good class overall and you'll definitely pass if you do your work and study a good amount. Lectures were not very helpful but it gives u a broad idea of the topic, the work is more complicated but not very hard to understand. Math is not my strongest subject but this has been by far my best math class.

She was a really good professor but her lectures were a little bit fast for me. She gives a chance for extra credit and will also drop your lowest exam grade and replace it with what you get for the final exam. She also drops a few or your lowest homeworks and quizzes. Overall she was a really good professor but get ready to study by yourself a lot

She is so nice and you can tell that she cares about her students. I love her teaching style because it's very easy to follow and it's similar to how my high school math teacher taught. There's weekly hw/quizzes and about 4 exams, but she is an easy grader and drops your 3 lowest grades/gives out extra credit opportunities. Would def recommend her!
so easy, great professor, almost impossible to fail
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Great professor that is all that needs be said.
I really enjoyed her class! Her lectures are very easy to follow, and there are several opportunities for extra credit that you hear about if you come to lecture often.
She teaches very well over lectures and uses effective metaphors to explain certain concepts. If you attend her lectures, you may learn how to get some extra credit too!

I adore Professor Kirvan. She has a lot of availability outside of lecture and doesn't mind if students pop into her office outside of established office hours for extra help. She's great at explaining concepts in a way that is easy to understand. She's easily my favorite math professor.

She teaches like a K-12 teacher, which as a freshman was very familiar. HW was on Cengage, due Thursday nights. Replied to my emails in a few hours on weekdays. Flexible office hours. Those that aren't good at math would gain much from taking her class, so long as they use the resources available. Grading depends on the TA, but usually it's fair.
I really enjoyed having her as a professor. I love the way she explains things and it isn't as difficult of a class as I thought it would be. I would love to have her as my professor again.

Kirvan is so nice! I'm not passing the class right now due to mental health reasons, but she's been very understanding and has let me come to her office hours for help. She explains things well and encourages students to come to her office hours if they have questions! Take MATH 150 with her, it's a hard class in itself for sure, but she def helps
She's a great professor. She taught in a way that made the work so easy to understand. She's also super chill and nice. Definitely take her!!
Easy course if you attend lectures and take notes. She gives in EC if you attend class.

Professor Kirvan is not bad and gives a lot of opportunities for extra credit along with study guides for all exams and quizzes. But, she is extremely irritating and short-tempered. If you ask her a question she will give you a condescending response. There are no opportunities to make up tests or quizzes, if you miss it you get a 0.

Really good professor, lectures help a lot. She drops a lot of low grades or zeros which helps. She's easily accessibly outside of class and just wants to see her students succeed. The way she explains can sometimes be confusing, but it's math so it's bound to happen. Overall, she's a good professor and the class is easy if you put in the effort.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: She's a very strict grader - pay attention to all the details that she wants you to include in your assignments and projects. Lectures are average. Manageable to get an A, but she expects a lot of work from you.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment:
The lectures weren't really that great in terms of knowledge gained but since the subject is a fundamental subject so I guess it is basic and easy. So even if you lose focus, it is fine. Just finish up the homework on time and study for the exams, you will get an A. 
The grading was generous I would say.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: One of the worst professors I've ever had in my life. Loses her train of thought very often and mixes up terminology equally often. Does not follow her own grading rubric. Makes lecture slides directly from text book.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Lectures are a pain to get through. It seems like she's seeing her powerpoint slides for the first time and does her best to try and understand the slides on the spot. Despite saying she won't ask trick questions, she asks nothing but trick questions. The class itself is easy, but she somehow makes it hard. Just study the slides and you'll be fine.

Professor knows her stuff and does care about the students. Book was kinda used but can def. get an A without using the book. A lot of homework but it is all broken up with your group members. Come to lecture because quizzes will be given, easy quiz using clickers. Exams are pretty straight forward, read power points slides and you should be good.

This was my first master's course and I found the topic and the teacher to be amazing. If my undergrad work had been like this, I would have been set very early on. Definitely recommend. Lectures and weekly assignments are important. Grading criteria is clear and exams aren't too bad. Looking forward to more of her courses.

She was a very funny and engaging teacher. She has many opportunities for extra credit just have to participate in class! Work isn't even that hard you just have to keep up with the mini readings answer a few questions. She has only one “big” assignment which is her research paper but as long as you follow the directions an stay on topic your fine.

Her lectures are 2.5hrs long but she is super fun and engaging, I feel like I learned so much more than my previous art history class because of this. There are plenty of options for extra credit (for one class we got extra credit points if we dressed up like we were going to the ren faire)

Very easy course. Do hw, paper, quizzes and you'll be fine. I didn't participate at all and still got enough points to skip the final. Follow the exam reviews 100% and you'll score 100% in the tests. Also do extra credits.

Very knowledgeable professor and passionate about art history. Can be difficult to talk to at times due to her way of speaking and her emails answering questions can be vague sometimes. Lectures are wonderfully detailed and cited. Research paper grading isn't harsh as long as you follow the rubric tightly, use correct information, and cite sources.

Pretty rude and condescending. Have taken two classes with her, Emailed her a basic question once, received a strangely rude and condescending response. She frequently calls on students in class and if you ask to repeat the question or for context she usually just moves on with no explanation. Presentation slides are uninspired and dry.

Great professor! There are definitely some significant class expectations, but as long as you participate and complete all assigned work on time you'll be fine. She is incredibly knowledgable and her lectures are very energetic! Definitely a higher work load, but lots of extra credit!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Very fun and interesting class. Explains concepts in a way that's very easily digestible. As long as you do your weekly quizzes and study for your exams you'll do great. Overall a really sweet and personable Professor!
She was great. One of the best at UMBC.

Very strict about attendance and will haunt you with it if you've missed too many (Even if you had good exusable reasons for it). She is a bit passive-aggressive, pretty rude. Be prepared to be called on randomly. There are readings and quizzes every week. She grades easy on the final research paper. Make sure to really study for exams!

Energetic and passionate about what she teaches. Do the weekly online REVEL quizzes, they help your grade at the end of the semester. Study exam reviews a few days before the midterm/final. The research paper is the most difficult part of the class, but she grades easily. She often speaks to the class as if we're kids, but she's nice overall.

Love Professor Anderson! Shes so nice and so funny during our lectures, she definitely makes class more enjoyable. You can tell shes passionate about art and art history by the way she explains things in class. Would love to have her again!

She is really fun! Took during the covid so lectures were on BB collaborate. Not a lot of course work, 2 major exams and a paper. I honestly loved her because of her personality: easy going, very patient to students (I rolled my eyes on my classmates so many times with my cam turned off), gives very good feedback to help succeed on the final paper.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Professor Anderson has a great attitude and is really knowledgeable, seems like a great travel partner. Do the homework and the readings so you can participate during the discussion. She provides study guides which make for good prep, cool class. Don't forget about your research paper
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Anderson is very intimidating. She will call you out for sitting in the back, being quiet, or not taking notes. She will require you to buy her ebook, but I suggest sharing a login with other classmates. All hw answers are online. I wouldnt bother taking notes in class either, just use the study guide before exams. She brings cookies to exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Pay attention, show up, do the homework and you will pass! Lots of reading for homework. If it looks like you are trying, it will pay off for your grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: everyone I talk to loves Kimberly. she's so brilliant and has so much information to share. just one quiz a week on the reading and a research paper ( and a presentation on your paper). she got rid of mid-terms and finals- but they weren't even that bad. she's hilarious and her lectures are so interesting. I will take every class she's teaching.

Professor Anderson is literally one of my favorite professors. I picked up an art history minor because of her class and I wish I had time for the major. She gives so much extra credit that it's kind of difficult not to do well. DO THE READINGS. She's absolutely hilarious and obviously loves what she does. I always looked forward to her lectures :)
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Professor Anderson clearly loves what she teaches and brings that enthusiasm to the classroom. There's so much reading and her lectures are so long and full of things I doubt I'll ever need to remember. There's quizzes at the beginning of each class so you really can't miss class ever, but hey at least it's only once a week.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: I loved Kimberly's class so much, I declared an Art History minor! She can be tough on you if she knows you're not paying attention, but she definitely knows what she's talking about & offers tons of extra credit. She's delightfully sassy and a fair grader. All of the people giving her poor ratings can meet me in the Denny's parking lot for a duel.

There were several instances where she was really rude or condescending to students--especially those in the back! I felt bad for people back there because it seemed like she mocked them, so sit in the front. Her powerpoints remind me of high school--long, text-heavy but somehow simplistic. She brought food to tests though, so that was cool.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Professor Anderson makes it  clear that she loves what she teaches. She may come across as quirky or even downright weird at times, but you really can learn a lot from this class. The course includes a five-question quiz before each class, so weekly readings are essentially required for success. She offers ample extra credit opportunities.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Be aware that this teacher gives weekly quizzes in which you MUST read the assigned reading. The tests were direct lifts from her notes (she told us this ahead of time as well), so they were not hard at all. I liked this teacher so much, I opted to take another class taught by her. She was very nice and knowledgeable.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--Hilarious

reviews.comment: Do yourself a favor and don't take her class! Anderson's lectures are horrible. Not only are each of her power-point slides an essay long, but she gives you very little time writing it down. It gets to the point whether you choose to listen and participate or get all your notes down because you can't do both. Quizzes and the test are nonsense.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Decent professor, teaches via slides so prepare for notes. Book is required and you take a quiz at the beginning of each class, however they aren't difficult if you read. Her tests and final are difficult so definitely study for the. There is one group project but it was pretty tame. Shes not the best but shes passable.
lectures are not what i expect at university level. limited understanding of the world in general.

So the paper part is where this class got me. The Chicago style format usually isn't used in my experience at UMBC but it's used here. And there's no examples for using the style or formatting an outline. She gave us a necessary extension but then gave an ambiguous due date and when she was asked to clarify, she got pretty rude.

AWFUL I never understood her teaching methods. I took the class as a gen ed and for someone who has no experience in art, she didn't explain well enough what is expected of the class and expected everyone to be upper level art history majors. You have to be very self-sufficient in the class in order to do well and PARTICIPATE

Great sense of humor; Enjoyed her lectures Wants you to do well  Lots to read & remember  Offers an exam study guide with   potential exam questions to help you focus on  before exam what's important prepare you for the real

Could probably learn more from Wikipedia, and trust the validity of the information more. Every ppt in soul killing, eye-burning fonts like comic sans and papyrus.  Doesn't understand what critical writing entails or what is appropriate for that context. Middle school atmosphere to the point of physical pain. Technologically impaired.

Welcome back to high school. You will have to sit in a assigned seat, even if the spot sucks for you. Can't make it to class? "Make sure you have an excused note" You heard it in high school. Lots of information and you must be interested in the class to do well.  Doesn't matter if you don't like speaking, you will be picked involuntarily. Avoid it

OH MY GOD I had to add her to this site. Kimberly Anderson is possibly one of the best teachers I have ever encountered. She is the most non-boring teacher ever, and that says a lot considering she teaches art history. As long as you participate, you will definitely do well. She was helpful and very approachable Kim, here is the pepper as promised!

Klement is one of the best professors I have had at this school. He doesn't care about making your life hard, he wants you to actually learn stuff you can use in your career. Makes quizzes open note because again, he is replicating the real world for us. Midterm questions are similar every year and straight from the quizzes. Class is an easy A.

Mr. K teaches STAT355 for fun. He's very passionate about what he teaches & makes sure we know what we need to know future classes/jobs. His slides are only available in-class; he moves relatively fast and often goes off on a tangent about some story. The book is available online, but he doesn't require you to read it. Just pay attention in class.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: The best STEM professor I've taken. He doesn't care about making the class hard, he wants you to learn statistics that you will use for the rest of your career. His tests and quizzes resemble real life problems, and are taken from his lectures, so you know exactly what to expect. Actively wants students to do well. Wish I could take every class.

Good professor to take STAT 355 with, the exams are usually 4 questions, homework are from the textbook but he gives the questions. He doesn't post notes online but does explain things well and actually understand the topic. Show up to class, pay attention, and open note quizzes every Thursday but he drops some.

Not much to say, he's a good professor. Show up to class to know how to do everything. Exams are a bit harder only because other professors contribute to them and they go over other content. Still fairly easy if you go to class, and grading is extremely lenient. If you're going to take STAT355, take it with him.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Quizzes may be easy, but the midterms he gives is 10x more difficult!

Klement was always confused during his lectures and students who hadnt learned the material had to correct him. Since too many people in his class were getting A's he had to made the class harder and the quizzes were too much. His lectures were too late at night and he was boring. His attitude was rude and he acted like he didnt really care.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: First math class I looked forward to. His lectures were hilarious and he actually taught everything you needed to know. Had to cancel office hours sometimes since he was busy, but overall a solid professor.

Very well organized and entertaining class. The professor is accessible outside of class in case you need help. Regardless, you always know what to expect from the course and with enough effort, you can get an A.

Mr. Klement is a solid professor. Lectures help solidify an understanding of the material and give a good sense of what will be on exams and quizzes. Homework is graded on completion and quizzes are open note. If you can complete these assignments without worry, you should find exams relatively straightforward.

Klement is a good guy who tries his best to give students the opportunity to succeed. Open note quizzes every Thursday and homework due on Tuesdays. Two exams and a final. He teaches in a way that makes the class actually relate to "the real world."
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: He is not always clear with his explanations. Since he is a part time professor he barely has office hours. Lecture is boring, homework's are short. You don't need the textbook because he gives you all the homework questions. Quizzes every Thursday that are open note. 3 exams total are closed note. Homework's due on Tuesdays. Can't just show & pass

I rate him highly even though I didn't do well in the class. I took the "Easy A" notes from people here too literally. He is a good teacher, explains well, and also tells funny anecdotes in class. But he just changed the schedule on us without announcing it on Blackboard which annoyed me

Don't know why the person below gave a poor mark on Mr. Klement. He is an approachable professor is actually cares if his students do well in his course; didn't get the narcissistic vib... If you have to take this class, totally take it with Mr. Klement. The other options for this course don't produce results that come close.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: He isnt a bad professor but all he does is recite the textbook. he is a bit narcissistic. overall some people like him some dont

Don't buy book, it's free online.  Klement is very passionate about stat. He will get sidetracked, but still gets through the material. Always answers questions and helps you understand. Homework is optional, but I would do it since he sometimes reuses the questions on quizzes. (Hw answers are in the back of the book.) Open note quizzes/tests!

Klements teaches Stat because he wants to, not because he needs to; he loves to teach. Your grade consists of ten quizzes, two exams, and a final. Quizzes and exams are typically open note. There is homework but it is optional. He is very kind and keeps lectures entertaining. Do yourself a favor and take this class with him, you won't regret it.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--Caring

reviews.comment: not good at public speaking, he focused a lot on using R, all the hws are based on R, but the hws have nothing to do with the exam
Prof Klein has no defined structure and has high expectations without giving instruction. I do not recommend him.
Martin is the best STAT professor I've ever had.  His writing and explanations are so clear it's unbelievable.

Professor Klein is not good at  public speaking skills but he is a good teacher. He goes over what will be on quizzes and exams (both are very easy) in discussion so it helps if you don't understand something. No graded HW, just HW probs he gives for you to practice before quizzes. I am glad I had him for my STAT class!! He is pretty cool haha
No Comments

His class was pretty easy, however he's not a very good teacher.  He's fairly young, and doesn't have too many public speaking skills.  He tries to help, but doesnt always.  His tests are easy.  He will make a review if you aks him, and normaily the review is very close to the exam.

Dr. KMA is an amazing professor. If you are truly passionate about learning AI/ML, he is the perfect choice. He clearly loves what he does and is also a comedian, which makes lectures fun and engaging. His exams are hard, but homework weighs more. If you score 80 to 100 on HW, you can pass.

Old reviews are not a good representation of his class now. It's changed quite a bit since then and his lectures are not that bad. Tests are important and midterm is harder than final. Assignments pretty much every week and are kind of annoying but they are useful. He knows a lot on the topic and can be quite random during lectures = fun.

I'd say his 471 class is overall a bit better than his 478. The 478 was pretty tough, homework assignments could be inconsistent or confusing at times, and his exams were pretty tough, he tested some of the mathematical theory so watch out for that. However he's helpful and did curve our grades a bit at the end of the semester. Solid professor

Great professor. He might've been bad in previously semester but it seems like he took the criticisms into consideration with this past semester. Assignments and exams are straight forward. As long as you keep up with the slides, you'll be chilling.

If you're looking to understand how KMA's class is going forward, I would look to the more recent reviews. His lectures are engaging, and he's pretty straightforward with his expectations. Do your homework and use the materials he gives you to prepare for the exams, and you'll do well.

Does not deserve the rating he has. His lectures are overall solid, and he will stop and take questions if students are confused, and his slides are great. Fair exams, open note but if you know the material well you won't need it. Also provides past exams. My only gripe is that his assignment formats are inconsistent. Final was tough though.

It was honestly a fun class and learned a lot. His teaching style might not be for everyone but his assignments are fair, and he wouldn't test you on anything he didn't teach. HWs, midterm/final, and programming assignments(basically projects) were all straightforward. And he's funny imo.

Machine learning is challenging in itself but professor Solaiman does his best to make it easier. 
Pros: Interesting class and topics, professor listens and answer questions, funny, no attendance, no quizzes just HW a midterm and final
Cons: Uses the white board a lot, everything isn't in the slides

Don't let past review stop you from taking him

I have taken 478 last semester, and I am taking 471 with him currently. He was very unorganized last semester but has improved a lot this semester. His grading criteria for homework are clear and he provides steps to request a regrade. In addition, the practice exams given were similar to our mid-term. He is an approachable person too.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Withdrew-- I saw the writing on the wall with this class. Poor lecture quality and homework that causes needless confusion. Tests are exceedingly difficult because they cover so much at a time. Students don't have much of a chance to apply what's being taught in order to truly grasp it or use the concepts practically. Avoid like the plague.

Of all the classes I've taken in my college career this one was likely the worst. The guy explains mathematical concepts very poorly and seems to have major issues planning out lectures and organizing his thoughts. Furthermore the class material did not prepare me for the homework AT ALL sometimes and did more to confuse me than help. Avoid.

Do NOT take 471 or 478 with this professor. He's terrible at lecturing and give exams that are pretty much impossible. He'd ask students if we were understanding the content during lectures, some would nod and afterwards he'd laugh at them and say that even he doesn't understand the content he's teaching.

While this professor is usually nice to students during class and tries to keep us engaged with humor, he can not teach so save his life. He gets frustrated as us when we don't understand the concepts that he can not explain and usually says "this is not a hard concept. why are you all struggling with this". Lots of students will fail.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: This professor is not a very good teacher. Often you are more confused about a topic after lecture than you were before lecture. His slides were not very clear and equation notation never seemed to be consistent. Often times your homework is going to have you solving a math/statistics problem which looks completely foreign. Nice guy bad teacher.

Wow, where do I even start with this professor? This professor has seriously made me question whether it was all worth the tuition fees. From the outset, it was clear that his teaching approach was deeply flawed. You'd think a professor would be more supportive, right? Nope, not this one. Ask a simple question, and get ready for some eye-rolling.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--So many papers--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: HWs with difficulty on topics that was way beyond what was taught in class. That's saying you were able to learn from his lectures. He tries to keep students engaged with humor but his teaching method just doesn't work. He uses Stanford slides with zero explanation and just expects us to understand just by him reading and rewriting it on a board.

one of the worst profs, if not the worst prof i have had. midterm was open note, but that didn't even help because of how confusing he made the material. questions for the midterm were from 671 courses, the graduate level of AI. dont take him its not worth it.

TERRIBLE DO NOT TAKE. Midterm and Final were EXTREMELY hard when he said it would be easy. Lectures are him reading off another professor's slide. In each lecture, he reads around 100 slides and expects everyone to understand. Very rude person who laughs at students. Gives study guide 2 days before exams. HWs are ok but Exams are really hard.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: ABSOLUTE WORST PROFESSOR. He is absolutely AWFUL at teaching. Half the semester is rushing through AI material and the other half is rushing through an introduction to ML. All his exams are unfinishable, the least taught subjects, and the reviews he gives out for exams are misguiding. He also mocks the class and gets into fights w/ students.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Class seemed more difficult than it should have been. Harder than my core CMSC classes. I enjoyed the first half but the second half of the class I got lost. I don't recommend taking AI with him unless u want a challenge. The only thing is he hates if you ever leave his class mid lecture, I went to go pee lol. Tough grading. Exam was unfinishable.

I wouldn't take this professor again. One of my hardest classes, and as said before, rushing through 100 slides, and expected to know everything (every detail, differences). Midterm was insanely long... people were not able to finish. The professor is nice, although inept with helping students understand. Look else-where for your AI interests.

This professor cannot teach. He forces us to use an obscure website called Campuswire to communicate instead of a discord server like everyone else. He is regularly late to class and cancels class with little warning. He is rude to his students and to his TA. He is a bad teacher and reads quickly from slides. HWs are difficult and poorly graded.

4 years at UMBC and only 2 professors are under 4 stars.  Professor is bad at lecturing, and content within AI class was mostly ML and Search algos. He would often move on when the entire class made it clear they were lost. The textbook does a much better job then him.  Going to class was a waste of time, but he gives you 5% participation grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Genuinely the worst professor I have had at UMBC.  He cares so little about being understood.  He will recognize when the class doesn't understand something, and then move right on.  He managed to get through his entire first semester teaching without improving any aspect of his lectures.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He is physically unable to teach clearly it seems. Most of the class ended up just teaching themselves the content. Half of our class failed the midterm and he didn't care at all. He has been described as teaching the class as if he is "trolling" the students, which is accurate.

CMSC471, this prof seems new to teaching. He rushes through 200 slides each class and expects students to remember everything. Hws are created with poor guidelines which are challenging and graded harshly. Has a very rude attitude and feels like he's indirectly attacking you sometimes. Hard exams with short time, low-class avgs. Choose other profs!

Teaches undergraduate course like a graduate course. Unrealistic expectations for students and rude in responses. Literally makes students compete for scores (best code gets no points reduced, next best gets 2 points reduced, etc.) How that is even allowed is beyond me. He is very confusing and terrible at teaching. Does not care about students.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Honestly she was super sweet, alot of the times she didn't force us to talk so I really enjoyed her initative and actually engaging with us. She's super understadning and a great communicator.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Caring

reviews.comment: Overall not a bad professor. She's very kind and understanding. I took her this past semester (Spring 2024) for SOCY 201 and it was a hybrid class. 50 minutes twice a week we would spend sitting there and listening to her ramble. Often times students would do homework from other classes. She often cancelled class last minute, wasting student time.

She is a very confusing prof. I'm taking her class for a GEP cred and it's absurdly easy, she also seems very nice, but her syllabus has not lined up with how she's actually grading us and she's missed so many classes that I've stopped going (at week 10 I calculated her attendance at 66%). She also does a poor job at engaging the class.

I had Professor Knisley for Socy 220 but it was not an option. They are a very kind professor but they are very often canceling classes and if not canceling classes they are showing up late. This would not be terrible if the class was not 50 minutes and they spent a lot of it explaining why they were late or rambling about something else.
Professor Knisley is easily the best professor I've had at UMBC so far. The workload was very manageable the class itself was very interesting. I would love to take Professor Knisley again!

I actually took SOCY 301, but Prof. Knisley was awesome. She's easy to contact and is willing to help with everything. She does ramble quite often, but I personally appreciated it. She also grades on a curve with just about everything.

Very chill professor. The final was a small paper that was quite easy. The midterm was online and multiple choice with open notes (easy). There are a few books that are read weekly, but I didn't even get one of them and was fine. There are weekly journal entries based on the readings that are easy homework! The class isn't graded on much.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Caring

reviews.comment: Prof Knisley is a great professor. As a member of the Cherokee Nation, she gives a lot of insight and makes the class very interesting. There's 4 books, but by skimming them you'll be fine. There's a group project that spans over the semester. Offers extra credit. No exams except for the final. Only critic is that she is a slow grader.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Group projects

reviews.comment: Professor Knisley was an incredible professor. She handled the pandemic really well and was understanding towards students. Her exams and quizzes were fair and reflected ervrything we learned. The material is based on her lectures and PowerPoint. She tried to make the class engaging. There are weekly reading assignments, but they are easy. Easy A.
Dr. Knisleys SOCY-409 class involves a lot of reading and writing, but she is a fair grader and offers plenty of extra-credit.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Prof reads straight from slides which can get boring. Class was super interesting and not hard but she cancelled so many times I ended up having to teach myself more than half of the class. You need the textbooks so definitely get them
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I give everyone the benefit of the doubt given I had her for the first semester where we transitioned to online-only because of covid, but she really wasn't the best. I don't think she responded to a single email I sent, even ones that asked questions about important assignments. Still passed though.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Group projects--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Knisley is one of the nicest professors Ive ever had. The class also isnt too hard.

I took Professor Knisleys American Indian Cultures class because it seemed interesting and I needed one more anthro class for the semester. Shes real sweet and genuinely cares about her students. Shes also very accommodating with assignments & attendance. The class itself was okay, kind of boring at times with all the reading we had to do.

Professor Knisley is a good professor with a clear criteria for the class. Get ready to read there are two books you cant go without! The discussion boards are interesting and conversations in class. There is no paper except for two quizzes which is a shortened paper.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Caring

reviews.comment: Prof Knisleys lectures are so gooooooood. It is not boring at all if you participate the discussions and ask questions. Prof Knisley gives rl accounts and examples which are very applicable to the course (social problems in America). I love how open and multi-perspective she is. Youll learn a lot from her if youre proactive.

She's a nice person, but is not accommodating enough. You need to be explicit and continuously demanding about your needs all for just a little leeway. All the assignments have been papers that require reading (and rereading) the course materials.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--So many papers

reviews.comment: i agree that she cares about students. very nice and accommodating but this class is a lot. 3 exams (8+ pg essays), 2pg papers due weekly and material is dense. LOTS of reading. this was harder/required more than my writing intensive classes. I would take another class with her to see if the issue was the topic or the teaching style though.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Caring--So many papers

reviews.comment: I feel like her heart is there and she cares about her students, but I always feel like what we are learning in class isn't on the test. Many students in my class feel like we are being set up to fail with the way the class is structured. I want to like her, but the way she teaches and this class is not worth your time or stress. Don't take it!

I don't really understand the poor reviews. I had no trouble getting good grades in her class and her discussions always increased my understanding of the content. She definitely has a more laid back style, but that made it easier to have open and hones conversations.

The course is graded almost entirely based on weekly homework discussions/online quizzes. The lectures were not necessary, although attendance is graded for 10% of your overall grade, so you can't miss too much. Knisley is an ok professor with a good heart. I enjoyed the content but many students didn't interact during class discussions.

She is a nice woman but is disorganized. Went off syllabus a few times and people get confused about the class schedule. All assignments are papers. Three exams range from 6-12 pages. The end includes philosophy which is really difficult. She is willing to work with students about deadlines so that helped
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--SO MANY PAPERS

reviews.comment: She's a nice woman but she is completely disorganized. Her syllabus had the wrong dates on it and her Blackboard homework links had no due dates so it was difficult to turn the right thing in on the right date. We had 3 take-home exams. The first 2 had no clear due dates.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: She is extremely unorganized and expects the students to know a lot of stuff that she BARELY, if that, teaches.   I would recommend NOT taking this professor if you actually want to learn the material. She is also very opinionated and wants everyone to agree with her.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: By far the most chaotic, and least helpful teacher I've ever had the displeasure of taking. You can do well on quizzes, read and comprehend the material, and give it your best effort, and the best you can hope to come away with in this class is a C. I had 300 level classes where I received A's, and this was an easy class and I received a poor grade
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--SO MANY PAPERS

reviews.comment: Her favorite grade must be a 5/10 because every blog assignement I received that while receiving 9-10/10 on the quizzes... She makes no sense grading wise as I cover the material and still am penalized. Avoid to save your GPA.

Professor Knisley was great. Took her for this past Spring semester and had a good time. The discussions are interesting but beware of emotional individuals that may be in the class, seriously.  Her tests are pretty much straight forward and you may have a paper every week but it's not too bad. Show up and do your work and you should do fine.

This professor is one of the worst ever at UMBC. Her grading system is chaotic. Attendance for her is like the end of the world, if you do not show up you might fail. Which is kind of weird because my sixth grade teacher took attendance that seriously. No one ever talk during her discussion because no one cares about the topics she brings in.
Professor Knisley is a wonderful person. She truly cares about her students. The only way you can do bad in her class is if you really do not try. Please take her! It is worth the experience !

She is a wonderful professor who really knows Sociology. The discussions held in class are wonderful and she is very good at answering questions. She is willing to help her students. Her lectures are wonderful and relevant and this is a good class. I would recommend her and this class!

I took 273 lecture and lab with her & she was great! Both lectures are extremely boring because it's based off slides but during class I would upload the lectures to Quizlet and spam it until I knew everything and I got easy As on the exams.

The overall material was OK. As long as you know BASIC BIO and AnaPhys, you'll survive. Study her slides, but add notes from the book where possible. Can be disorganized so pay attention to due dates for projs. Study guides help a lot. There is some memorization, but she also let us bring cheat sheets to exam (don't rely on them too much tho).

She is VERY nice, but her teaching style is very disorganized. It's taken her 3 months to grade 5+ things, and she's pretty bad at answering emails. she's more helpful in person. she also likes to change due dates around so stay on top of her schedule.. i took her for both microbio & nutrition and the content is amazing but it's all over the place
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Group projects--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Dr. PK is very kind but her labs were often confusing. Many students made mistakes due to the lack of clear explanations for lab procedures, but she is happy to help if you have questions.

If you do Monday lab, she's there & there are TA's as well but Pushpa teaches what we're doing in lab. There are prelab quizzes; make sure to do those. Sometimes she doesn't explain the lab well, so it's confusing. She also does nutrition 233, don't take her, take Caitlyn if u can! I had to W her since she does that class too much over nutrition.

The lab was insanely easy. Mostly taught by our TA. Prof. K rarely showed up to the labs, and her lectures were pretty boring. As long as you study active recall and watch videos on youtube of what you'll be doing for the day (like gram stain) you will pass. Everything is very straight forward, the final is an "unknown project" (unknown bacteria)
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: was barely in lab and mostly relied on TA. questions for exams did not correlate to materials we covered and wording can be confusing. prelab quizzes and guided notes rely on textbook reading!!! honestly just hope your groupmates are smart and chill. hand everything in and make sure to attend class cuz attendance is mandatory
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Test heavy

reviews.comment: I think I saw her show up to lab like 4 times the whole semester. She relied a lot on our TA, who also graded everything She was supposed to keep our lab stocked and ready and it never was. Wrote confusing questions for quizzes and just disorganized. She was nice when she was around, though.

He's good, but can get carried away when presenting. Assignments are fine, but may take some time. 5 research proposal assignments, 2 presentations, 1 book review, and 1 final summary. Not your regular grading style. Reading heavy. Very fun class, and also challenges your worldview. Regarding a previous comment, he's not anti-God. He's Jewish.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Kobren is a very sweet professor. The reason why I rate his teaching of POLI 406 a 2 is because he bases the class on the premise of evolution. He flat out states he doesn't believe God could have created humans. If your personal views differ from the view of evolution, the class may be frustrating. I thought others should know if considering.

There are about a half a dozen readings per week, but the assignment is participation. The few assignments he does have are presentations and essays. He's a very lenient grader since he simply wants you to learn from this, but there is a lot to do for that. I enjoy his lectures, but I wouldn't take this class if I didn't want to read a lot per week
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: I would take another one of his classes just to listen to him talk & teach. He was an easy grader (just wanted us to learn as much as possible), & the only big assignments were the group presentation & paper at the end. He doesn't want to make the class a burden, and his teaching style reflects it well. The readings were very diverse & informative.

Prof. Marty is an amazing professor, at he beginning of class he states his intention for the class and he expects a statement of intention from you as well (graded). He is very straightforward, he also assigns newspaper assignments and expects a detailed discussion and paper on it. In class participation is advised. He is just a sweet grandpa.

Professor Kobren is an amazing professor! He doesn't give out any tests/quizzes; grades are based on papers and small assignments which are fairly easy. Lectures are quite boring but tolerable. Attendance is mandatory but he uses quickwy where you type in a code to check-in so ask a friend for the code when you can't come.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: So when I took this class, he stated that instead of tests and quizzes, he changed the course so that you had a total of 5-6 writing assignments for the entire semester and if you did those and showed up to class for the most part + participated, you'd get an A. He's also pretty lenient with deadlines too, just put in the work, show up and you pass
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Hated this class. He had good intentions, but his way of encouraging participation was very uncomfortable. He calls on you and if you say you don't know the answer he waits for you to say something. Not my type of learning. Also, tests are extremely difficult and don't really make sense. But extra credit will help your grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Professor Kobren is an POLI 100 professor which is an introductory course. In the beginning of the semester he talks about curving the system to a median score of 82%. Then you get your first tests which everyone fails. I took a 3 200 level classes and 1 300 level class that i passed and somehow could not pass a 100 level class. Never updates grade
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Horrible. Never again. A 100 level class should not be this hard. Exams are bias. The only grades in the class are two exams and a current event hot seat presentation that goes with a paper. Says he gives extra credit but wont accept most things you try to submit.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Dr. Kobren is by far my favorite professor. He strives to create a welcoming learning environment and wants to see his students succeed. Discussions are encouraged and very interesting in class. You should make sure you do the readings and truly understand the material. You need to be able to apply what you learn to real problems and discussions.

He's not a bad lecturer but he gives horrible online quizzes and probably the worst exams I have ever seen in a college-level course. The class scored so poorly on the midterm that he allowed for a retake of the same exam. Shows questionable teaching methods and lack of foresight. All in all, his class requires more work than upper-level classes...
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Prof. Kobren is very passionate about what he does, which I admired greatly from him. His lectures are often more like discussions, so participation is a big part of the class. That being said, the tests are extremely difficult, to the point where a bunch of people failed the midterm - but he does give extra credit and emphasizes effort.

Professor Kobren is a great professor whose lectures are actually interesting; he engages the class for discussion on current events. However, his midterm is designed to be difficult. Most people failed, so he allowed everyone to retake it. Also, he assigns way too much reading (takes hours), and gives quizzes on it. I  usually skimmed and did well

Honestly I think Professor Kobren shouldn't be teaching undergrad. The class is harder than some 300 level classes that i've taken. Many people failed his midterm & when asked about the exam he said it was based on critical thinking more than what you read.. Also his quizzes were fill in the black (hard) & 100 pages readings/wk.

Dr. Kobren is really inspiring. Theres only two exams, and the first one is really hard but he offers extra credit which he adds directly onto your first exam score. If you're at all interested in politics, take this class because you learn a lot. He goes over everything in class, so make an effort to go to each one.

Kobren is awesome and super inspiring, but the class sucks. The structure is 2 tests, a midterm and a final. He does offer 15 extra credit points but that doesn't do much if you fail the first exam. Really loved his a professor but stay away from the class.

He is a good professor. The lectures are not mandatory, but I advise showing up for class because he goes over the readings very well. He also encourages participation and class discussions become very interesting at times. I barely missed the A because I messed up a little bit on the final. If you have any interest in politics take the course.

Learned a lot.  Hard test.  Liked his teaching style but not his test.  Offered opportunity for extra credit which was needed by most.  Cares about his students learning.  I'd recommend if your looking to learn but not if you want an easy A.  Do all outside readings!

Asynchronous class, very easy. Just do your work and follow the instructions thoroughly and you will get an A. Some assignments need you to reply to others people's posts. Just stay respectful and have fun learning about different cultures and communication!
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: Great Professor!

Easiest class ever: lots of self-cultural discussion posts. Main challenge is managing numerous due dates and responding to 4 peers. final is a group presentation on personal experiences, no external research needed. very approachable and easy to reach outside of class. not the most interesting class but an easy A and culture credit.

She is an amazing easy professor. Alot of disussion board involvement, but its all talking about you and your experiences. Very easy class. You dont have a final or midterm exam. Your "final" is a group project presenation. SOOOOOO easy!!! Would take again!

literally the only class I've ever taken which Id consider fun. It's all just discussion posts and the questions are either about you or just generally philosophical, to the point where it's actually enjoyable to go through and read other people's responses. Very little effort is required, this class is 100% the best GPA booster you can wish for

I liked this professor but the lectures would sometimes be boring. She teaches in a roundabout way so it was hard to focus. Attendance was 35% of my grade so you better make sure you attend. The homeworks had no wrong answers but were a decent amount of writing. My only gripe was that we had to write 4 replies to peers in every discussion post.
All around good professor. Workload is pretty easy despite being a little long winded sometimes. Lots of discussion board work though, which could get a little tedious

On days when you meet online, it can be a little boring... There is A LOT of work to do each week but it's all about you, so there is no right answer. She is such a sweet lady and will give extensions if needed. There was one group project to write about how you and your group members are different and or the same. TAKE THIS CLASS, fun & easy

Professor Kohler herself is a great professor. She's extremely knowledgeable about intercultural communication and is very enthusiastic about hearing everyone's experiences.The course itself is hell, there are so many assignments and discussions board posts to be done every week. If you want to not do work this isn't the class for you

This is a very simple asynchronous class. You will be doing something different everyday but the assignment directions are always clear and will be given to you. It is an accelerated course so there will be a ton of work to do in a short time. None of the work is hard though and there really aren't any wrong answers. Overall a fun laid back class.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: You listen to pre-recorded slides w/ lecture, textbook, discussions, short essay-responses, watch videos, do 2 interviews, then you got an A. Staggeringly easy for a 300-level course (accelerated is fast-paced tho), professor just there to administrate it, however delivers the lecture effectively & concisely. Always open to help outside of class.

MLL 305 is relatively easy. Just show up and/or do some short assignments online and you will pass. Loves to facilitate discussion in class. She is very nice and responds to emails promptly. Only one final exam. For online lectures, she has both synchronous and asynchronous options, so you don't exactly have to come to class.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--Caring

reviews.comment: Attendance counts as a LOT for this class. The class meetings are very long but do not skip, it really hurts your grade. Very easy class as well. Sometimes extraordinarily boring on days where she does not involve much group work or activities, but besides that I loved it.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Group projects--Caring

reviews.comment: Professor Kohler is the best professor I've had. If the science dept. had professors like her, being a bio major would actually be enjoyable! If you get a chance to take an MLL course with her you should do it, she is so sweet and makes class fun and interactive. The syllabus is very clear, if you show up to every class you'll easily get an A.
Great professor. Very caring and realistic about how much work students can get done within a small timeframe. Very flexible as well. Loved her relaxed teaching style. Gets you ready for final! :)

Great class. Dont skip any, attendance is something like 50% of your grade. If you pay attention in class, the 5 papers are easy (they are 2 pgs double-spaced), and the 2 tests are easy. And you know at the beginning of the semester when everything is due, so you can easily do assignments ahead of time.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: She is a very sweet and kind professor. Class is interesting and fun, she does a lot of class activities. The class is easy if you show up, attendance is mandatory , it is 50% of the class grade. 5 online discussions and 2 exams. This is a good, easy upper level and culture course. Definitely take her!
Great class, great professor

This class is so pointless honestly don't waste your time. It is an easy upper level and the professor is super nice but i find myself irritated in this course and i feel like im wasting my life away sitting in this classroom.

Professor Katie is amazing! Shes my favorite professor at UMBC. She wants all of her students to get As so she makes attendance a huge part of your final grade. Her lectures are super engaging and she prepares lots of fun activities for students! Shes a sweet woman with a great sense of humor. I really enjoyed her class!

Professor Kohler is one of the best and easiest professor to take. More than half of your grade is attendance. There is no reason for someone to not get an A. Fun group activities in almost every class. No projects. Just attendance, 5 discussions, and 2 exams which are fairly easy. She offers a lot of extra credit towards the end of the semester.

She is one of the best professors I have ever had at UMBC. The class is super chill and as long as you show up and engage to a certain extent, 60% of your grade is guaranteed. The exams aren't hard and if you just go over her study guide and know the terms there, you'll do great.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Would take again

reviews.comment: One of the BEST and EASIEST 300 level classes without prerequisites. Attendance counts more than 50% of the final grade. No papers, easy exams, and easy activities. Quizzes are based on readings, be prepared for that but her grading is very easy and flexible. HIGHLY RECOMMEND!!!

One of the best and NICEST professors ever! Huge percentage of your grade is based on attendance. There's a quiz every class but she gives you topic hints from before. Final exam is a take home and there are no other exams or papers due. Love that she focuses more on learning than testing. Really interesting class w/ great prof! HIGHLY RECOMMEND.

Exam-heavy, 75%, with no clear guidelines on what would be on the 2 exams. The semester-long project was graded leniently, but the amount of work put in does not match how much it's worth. Avoid him if you can; he goes on tangents in lecture and makes following along difficult. His exams are hard, and difficult to study for, very SQL heavy.

We had a semester long project that is worth only 20% of the grade. We also had 5 homeworks each only worth 1%. The other 75% of the grade was the midterm and final. Multiple choice exams but several trick questions and heavily SQL based.

Don't take. Homework and Projects are not correlated in line with lecture material. Reads off slides, doesn't help with learning. Exams are worth 70% of your overall grade, and does not provide study guides. Frustrating, and provides no motivation to come to class.

Good professor, super nice and caring. One of the few CS profs who is passionate about what they teach. Office hours are huge help. 5-6 homeworks, semester long project, and two heavily weighted exams. Exams are the only negative; they are poorly structured and heavily based on SQL (not good for an intro to SQL class). Class avg on midterm was 59

Dr. Kalpakis is very passionate about teaching SQL and takes the time to explain topics in detail to students. You don't have to come to class, as all of the notes/PPTs are posted online. The projects and homework are graded really easy, so as long as you do turn those in and do average on exams, you should get a decent grade in 461.
reviews.rating_tags: Test heavy--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I graduated 5 years ago now, but felt compelled to review Kalpakis. He was, by far, the best professor I had at UMBC. He was also, by far, the hardest professor I ever had at UMBC. I took CMSC 441 Design & Analysis of Algorithms with him in 2016. Do NOT skip class. He is very unforgiving, but very informative.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Amazing lectures--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Understanding & takes feedback, his passionate lecs get heavy once you hit SQL. Learned tons from leniently graded HWs/proj, but clearer instr. & feedback would've helped. Wished we went into tougher concepts more as exams were hard, take them seriously, they're worth a lot. Go to OH! He's nice and wants to students to pass. 461 is worth enduring!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Graded by few things--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Kalpakis is one of the few professors I've had who actually seems to take interest in the topic they lecture about. HWs are pretty long, but these assignments pretty much taught me SQL--don't half ass em (despite lenient TA grading). Project instructions/feedback were the lowpoint of this class.

AVOID AT ANY COST! He makes no sense and is difficult to understand. There are 5 hws, 1 big project, midterm, and final. The project is very long and tough, it takes forever just to understand what he actually wants you to do. Exams are very unfair. He is rude and inconsistent. He will put you through stressful situations. DO NOT TAKE WITH HIM!

it's one of the worst professor in UMBC. the instructions of the project are complex, you don't how to start even though you know the materials. it's not on time for online office hours. His exams are really hard/tricky. it's pretty hard to get A in this class. I do not advice anyone to take him, otherwise you may have unexpected situations.

His lectures were entertaining, I just wish he would have to more hands-on SQL. I learned a lot about database design. I would have liked to have more time to finish the second part of the project. Overall he was decent, but you won't know what your final grade is until the deadline.
Best computer science lectures I've listened to. You need to practice SQL on your own time or else the exams will not go well. Very thankful for the curve.

Theres 5 homeowners two test and a project. The project is large, he doesnt not expect everyone to get everything completed. The test are hard, he doesnt expect great grades. Its rumored he curves I have not got my final grade yet but stay tuned. Overall do not take this class with more than 5 other classes. Take it as a third or fourth.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: DO NOT take the class with him. The worst professor I have had in 400 level classes. The TA is bad and does not know what he is doing. The exams are so hard and avg is around is 40-50. The homework is the only thing that will pull your grade up. The projects start early. If you get a 100 on the projects and homeworks you can pass the class.
Amazing

He killed the interest that I had in databases and SQL with 4 homeworks that had multiple parts and many questions which took a really long time, and really hard exam questions. The lectures didn't really hold my interest, but at least the exams were multiple choice. He expects you to read the book and play around with databases outside of class.

Lectures are absolutely useless. He tests on things that you would only know from reading the book, he just does examples in lecture. Goes on tangents, whispers to the front row so you can't hear what he's saying otherwise. If you read the book, take notes, and teach yourself the material, you'll be fine. 5 homeworks, 2 projects, 1 final, 1 midterm

Very knowledgeable professor and good adviser. Discusses the math and logic behind all algorithms and methods discussed in class. Lectures may be heavy for most, you really need to be attentive and not zone out.

One of my favorite lecturers at UMBC. He'll explain something as many times as necessary until you understand, and he's always ready to help you after class or during office hours.  Tests are incredibly difficult. You can't do well without closely reading the book and attending class. Luckily he'll curve generously if you show effort or interest.

So here's the thing -- he's an amusing lecturer, and I did learn useful information from this class. That's a win. This is UMBC we are talking about here, I don't think you can ask for much more. The class is insanely tough. But he does EPIC CURVES (60%+ avg seemed to be an A). But you will not have any clue what your grade is until the end.

Class required work, project was difficult and there were issues with the project architecture as put together by the TA. But professor was understanding and helpful. Tests closely followed homework, if you do it and review it, you should expect a good grade. Is a very animated teacher, very interested in subject. Felt I learned a lot.

Easily the worst professor I have had in my entire college career. First exam average was 27%. Learned nothing the entire semester. I ended up with a C with a final score of 31%. Highest grade in class was 65%. I would have avoided, but it was the only section offered this semester which was my last. Plan ahead to take this with someone else.
Avoid his class altogether

Terrible. Most difficult exams I've ever taken, problems on obscure topics way harder than hw. 1st midterm class avg 27%,  asked for suggestions and ignored all of them for final. Grade breakdown 20HW, 35/45 mid/final exam. Can't follow lectures, goes very quickly and doesn't really answer most questions you ask - like he's teaching to himself.
