First, I'm a Math/CMSC major. Kalpakis is extremely difficult, in part because his proofs for are not rigorous at all. The other part is that the hws and exams expect different skills from you, so don't look to the hw to study. The exams have no partial credit; writing an alg gets no points if you don't answer the accompanied questions.

He doesn't care about his course. He acts as if he cares, but the TA shoulders the entire thing. TA decides on the project specifications, deadlines. TA makes the questions for the exams. You ask him something, he says he has to ask the TA. Final exam had the exam same q's as the midterm so remember the midterm! Happily, grades very easy.

An entertaining lecturer and knows the material well. Exams are very hard. Homeworks are from the book, so if you read the book theoretically you should do fine on those. The semester project wasn't terribly involved, but extremely tedious. He said he would make changes for future semesters. Definitely expects students to read the book.

Others say he is a great professor -- I have to disagree. Yes, he is engaging as a lecturer, but he is a very unfair prof. Tests are multiple choice which doesn't make sense for this subject. Questions on tests had multiple right answers, which was not revealed until later. I'd avoid taking him, even though he's a good lecturer.

Projects were difficult but very feasable if you allowed the necessary time. The tests however were very hard but come from the book, which he expects you to fully read and remember the assigned chapters. Most hw comes from the book and answers can be found in the previous edition solution manual

Great Professor! You will learn tons of interesting things. He will make your programming HWs be like projects and your projects will take you days, but you will say thank you in the end. I think all classes should be taught like this. If you have a little extra time during your semester take it with Kalpakis.

His lectures were interesting, and he is very smart. I enjoyed operating systems up until I got my final grade. The TAs didn't grade half of my projects and homework(even though he promised we would see all of our grades before the final) so I got a C in the class. I emailed him several times to see if I could get a regrade. He he responded after a

Overrated in both difficulty and approachability. Expects no more from you than many other profs. If you're a CMPE or MATH major, you won't flinch over workload. Also seems a bit bipolar: sometimes very friendly + engaging, but other times very cold + impatient. Never replies to emails. lol. Lectures are definitely top notch though: A+++ there.
He curves at the end of the semester

Projects? Hard. Homework? Lots. Exams? Very Hard. Lecture style? Superb! Very knowledgeable; really wants to see students succeed. Be prepared to work very hard and learn lots of really useful stuff; recruiters were very interested in this class and the projects.
He is a very knowledgeable guy.  I learned a lot in his class.  Tests are based on homework, which there's little of, but if you do sample exercises you'll be fine.

Kalpakis is ONE of few professors that actually teach at UMBC.  Plain and simple.  I was pleased that I was able to attend a lecture that was engaging for once.  This is a MAJOR aspect that I think UMBC lacks and that I've been utterly dispointed with.  THEIR FACULTY SUCKS.  Not all, obviously, due to people like Kalpakis.

Great for people that are willing to ask questions and discussion. I enjoyed being in his class. For those that want an easy prof don't take him. He will make you learn something when you come out of his class.

Nice guy, gets very animated during class. Class always runs 5 minutes over. Homework gets graded easily by the TA. The tests are hard, don't expect to get old exams from friends. The project was huge but grading was lenient. Tough professor but I learned a lot! Go to office hours, don't email. Makes you think he doesn't curve, but a 75% was a B.

Kalpakis = great teacher, his HW is hard but the tests are an easier version of the HW. This is how you should teach, if you need an ex just ask. Go visit him in office hours he will like you better if you show him you are working. He is extremely leanient in grading the final project, but its huge so start early I got 100% but it took me 50+ hours
Horrible teacher .... Stay away from. Never received a reply for my emails to him. I agree with the call to fire this professor ... Anybody listening .... FIRE HIM.

4 Words: SEE YOU NEXT SEMESTER!! Don't ask him questions, he will laugh at you and try and make you look dumb. Made a project for our class: Make a new linux scheduling algorithm. No links, no sources or instructions as to how. Horrible teacher. Needs to be fired!! Nasty attitude toward students!

Korossy is truly a great teacher. Lectures are sometimes long winded and there are not enough breaks but he is very lax and open to extensions. If you can sit through long classes than it is okay. Only a couple grades though.

Dr. Korossy is an incredible professor! He was so chill but still taught us the ins and outs of Chinese Politics and made it so fun. Such an understanding and flexible professor. He engages with his students on a friendly level and shares great stories. 100% would take again!

He is an awesome professor! Makes the lectures very entertaining! I was taking five classes and working full time and thankfully he made this class very manageable. He appreciates attendance, honestly the ones who complained are probably the ones who never went to class. Very generous with extensions on assignments.

HE IS THE BEST PROFESSOR AT UMBC!!!! He really knows his stuff but also knows how to teach it. He teaches very well and during his lectures he gives us notes and writes things down which personally that helps me learn. He also shows examples so we can have a clear understanding. His personality is also AMAZING!! wish he teached all poli classes.

Laszlo was hands down my favorite professor at UMBC. Had him for Chinese Politics and Urban Politics. His lectures were amazing and his grading was extremely fair. Wish I could've been able to take more than just two of his courses. Will not be disappointed by taking any class he teaches.

Fantastic professor. A very good man and a very good lecturer. Highly recommend any and all courses taught by him. I have laughed harder than I have ever expected to in a class. I have been inspired to learn more than I have in any course previously. Truly a wonderful course. Come to class every, day it will make your bad week good again.

Great professor, super funny, kind of weird. Lecture heavy, prepare to take notes. The classes he teaches are usually late/at night so he does his best to keep us awake. two papers, weekly discussion posts, final presentation. Take him, cool guy.

He is very cool and easygoing, not a tough grader, although writing intensive. From what Iv'e heard he usually only grades 2 assignments total. (a midterm paper that is 8-10 pages, and a final paper+presentation that is also 8-10 pages). He also doesnt allow more than 2 missed days so if you're a habitual skipper, I would avoid taking his class.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: don't take this professor. super boring. overly strict attendance policy, not understanding or reasonable at all

Entertaining and eccentric. All he cares about is that you walk away with some basic knowledge. He likes class discussions so expect to put in your two cents on the topics. Not many assignments so they must be done well if you want a good grade. Big on attendance. Kind of a history nerd. He's not very tech savvy.
Great professor! Lectures are long but very entertaining. Requires two papers and a group presentation at the end of the course based on the second paper.

AMAZING PROFESSOR, it was honestly one of the best professors to have. He loves what he does and it is shown through his teachings. As long as you do your part in the discussions and papers you'll pass

Took his Urban Politics class. He is very passionate about cities and it is a great class if you fell likewise. There are papers only, no midterms or tests. A lot rides on it so if you are a good writer and attend ALL classes you can do well. Be prepared to take part in discussions.

Best professor at UMBC, really proves that the best professors are snazzy Hungarians. Loves his subjects and can make even the most dry of ideas seem fun and interesting. Will look over your papers and gives good feedback, as long as you care you will not fail.

Caitlin is great and makes learning really easy with her teaching style. Exams are not weighted very much so don't worry if you fail the first one you can still easily pass. She likes to put bonus questions on the exams so thats an easy point. Make sure you come to class on time it is graded.

On an in-class assignment day, she said that she was taking attendance based on the assignment submission so I started working on it with my group instead of signing in and submitted it when we finished. She gave me a zero for the assignment, which brought me down to a 89.2%.I didn't miss a single lecture all semester, but she refused to change it.

The class is not that hard as long as you come to class having read the readings and assigned video. Regardless she still goes over them in class so you don't need to worry too much make sure you pay attention though the final you need to identify an unknown and use all the skills she taught you.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Cares about how you do in the class and will support you with how many study sessions she holds. She clearly goes over the major ideas of each topic so you won't be very surprised on test day

Definitely not an easy A, but she does all that she can to help you succeed in the class. She holds many study sessions before exams, gives good study tips, and all of her lectures are available online. We didn't use the textbook at all, just the lecture videos and slides were enough.

One of the best professors I have taken at UMBC. She makes you very interested in what you are learning both in the lab and lecture. She is very supportive and is extremely tech savvy. Be prepared for lots of memorization and difficult exams, just because the professor is good does not mean you should under estimate the class.

Attendance is mandatory (6% of your grade) and there's lots of homework, so keep up and stay on track or you'll fall behind to study for exams. Do your best on the first exams, the final exam is the hardest and not worth risking to fail. Overall great prof, hard class, but you'll learn a lot.

The microbiology lab that I took with this professor was very easy and understanding. I was rarely in there for the full 3 hours, and everything was very straightforward. It was probably my favorite class I have ever taken. It was so interesting and fun, and the professor made sure you knew what you were doing and prepared you well for the final.

A very nice professor but definitely makes you work for your grade. She does her job very well and makes sure you are well educated before going off to nursing school. She does a lot of review and holds a lot of study sessions, and is very caring and makes sure you understand everything you need help with. 10/10 recommend.
Really great teacher and not too challenging of a course, but it's definitely not an easy A.

This class was so organized and the prof was very straightforward. If you watch the lecture videos and use the guided notes, you're set with an A for the class. She is very passionate about biology and explains concepts very well. Quizzes and exams were not difficult at all. My fave class this semester, 10/10!

Microbiology is a very hard subject, but she simplifies and makes it so basic. She told us exactly what to study, and when the class was struggling she recognized it and gave out multiple extra credit opportunities. Very sweet and always willing to help. Still have to work for an A, but she makes the material easier to understand.

I took her class for microbiology to fulfill my credits for the pre-nursing program, she's an amazing professor for microbiology. Teaches the most important material you need for exams and applications to allied health careers. Group projects every week with lectures and quizzes however everything is organized wonderfully. I'd definitely recommend!

*Enrolled under HIT-658 and not IS-436 as mentioned on top of the review (there was no option for HIT-658)*

I would definitely enroll under her again. She is considerate of personal issues and has given extensions when I had genuine issues. Good grader and did not face issues in her course. Mine was a completely online asynchronous class.

I took Data Mining Class with her and her knowledge in this domain is simply terrific. She uses very simple language to explain the Machine Learning algorithms which is the best part of her class. She is always willing to provide extensions to the students if the student reaches out to her. That makes her the kindest professor at univ.

This professor basically did not exist for our class. The TA taught the class and was the one at office hours. On the final project my group had a member leave so we met with her to discuss what we should do. We did what she said and gave us a C on the grade which dropped me from an A to a B. We tried to email her and she just ducked us lol. Crazy

She is an amazing professor. She was very flexible during the pandemic , she is easy to work with and understand everything. Her lectures are long but as long as you pay attention you will pass. the exams are easy just terms, as long as you review her slides you will pass your exams. Easy A, amazing professor. She needs to be full time.

She is terrific. Accessible outside the class. Her lectures are great as well. Unlike others, she does not read from the slides. I took this class during the pandemic and I found her very understanding and flexible. Super responsive with emails and gives good feedback to the assignments.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Group projects

reviews.comment: Had group projects the whole semester. No final and no midterm. Amazing, just land a good group that'll work hard and you'll get an A. Quizzes were there but they were also very easy to do. Very flexible professor.
He was awesome. One of the best!
Take this class and you will be a better person and student. He's brilliant, but be sure to engage and ask questions.

Worst professor I have ever had. Please only take him if you HAVE to. He does nothing but stand on his soap box preaching, not teaching. You will teach yourself the material. He critiques harshly, you will never get a perfect grade. He is rude in class when someone speaks their opinion. Slow grader and confusing in his expectations.

He is not clear in lectures. His exams are not based on his lectures and he asks very vague multiple choice questions. Expect a regular homework on top of readings, exams and projects. If you do not have to, try to stay away from taking his class. Same material can be learned from the book if you are really interested in the subject.

Worst teacher ever! No one got an A in the class. My grade came down to a difference of 0.30 to get the next grade up and he doesn't round. On top of that he lost my last hw we turned in and refused to look for it and blamed me. He hates students and has no patience for questions. Boring class with only one powerpoint slide. DON'T TAKE

While the work load isn't too ridiculous this professor is one tough grader. If your interested in having someone nit pick every single word you type into a discussion board then this is the class for you. As mentioned below he definitely does take his sweet time grading everything. He also does not allow quoting, which can somewhat be a pain.

Take this course only if you absolutely have to. Professor is  ambiguous about all assignment instructions, drags his feet with grading (so you don't know if you did the assignments correctly or not), and bends over backwards finding criticism of students' work. All said and done, it wasn't too hard, but it was hell while it lasted...12 WEEKS!!!

I think the course material was fairly easy to comprehend. The instructions and the evaluations were not. Evaluations did not reflect what students were asked to do; they factored in more than was stated in the original questions. Also, it seemed odd that we were not allowed to use quotes, even if we cited them. I do not recommend this professor.

Not gonna lie, he was fired during this semester so for the last 3 weeks we had a new professor. While we was there, his class was just practice problems we worked through together, no structured lecture, and there were 3 tests the whole year. He allowed a study sheet for the tests and had an optional final so didn't learn much but was easy.
The reason it's hard is because he doesn't really teach but see what we know when he asks us questions.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Take this professor at your own risk. His lectures do not help; he's too slow and barely gets through any material in a single class. We didn't get our Quiz 2 grades back until after the withdrawal date, more than a month after we took it. Only 3 quizzes and a final that's worth 55% of your grade. If you have the opportunity, take Nanes instead.

Kogan's not a good teacher. He explains everything in a very proof-heavy, math-guru way that doesn't prepare you to apply the content on the exams. BUT, his grading policy almost makes up for this. Skippable final, reference sheet for exams, has 20 more possible points than needed for a 100 on each exam, and he bumped me up from a 79 to a B.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: One of the most entertaining classes I've taken. The professor is hilarious and a decent lecturer. Dif EQ is heavily based on equations and processes, and you're allowed an equation sheet during the exams. The class consists of 4 midterms that are equally weighted. Do well on the midterms, as the optional final will be worth 50% of your grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Clear grading criteria--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: This guy! If you want to know the definition of a difficult grader, take this professor. Our exams had four questions, 25 points each where you can only get 0 or 25. The material is already difficult and then he teaches like we are all math gurus. He'll be frank with you that you're going to fail though, so that's something.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: You'll have to teach yourself pretty much everything, but with the cheat sheet and optional final the man is just TRYING to give you an A.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Accent is hard to understand until you get used to it. I highly recommend watching 3Blue1Brown's Essence of Linear Algebra series on Youtube if you're in his 221 class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: It was going so well until the very last exam, which Kogan graded. He grades so harshly! It's literally either all or nothing! Plus, your final grade in this class is based on only three exams. So, even bombing one will bring your grade down significantly. I relied solely on the textbook, didn't learn a single thing from lecture.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Find the chalk that is soft enough to show up on the board otherwise there really is no point for the students to arrive to class. Also lecture yourself - 30 minutes of students working problems on the board is a snoozer. I would also suggest not to cancel class so often if only it were more interesting.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: The class has no graded homework. The only grades are 3 quizzes and one exam. If you like your grade at the end of all three exams you do not have to take the final. All quizzes are 30 points and the final is 100 points. So, you can do a Hail Mary for your grade if you're up for that.
Grader looks for only specific patterns in problems to determine credit. Failure of a single of the only four grades ensures a terrible overall grade.

As a professor, he's okay, but he is absolutely the worst grader I have ever had the misfortune of coming across. In every exam question, it is either you get 25, 10 or 0 points and there are only 4 questions!! Unless you are Stephen Hawking and have a strong heart for his sarcasm and non-response to questions, don't take him!!!

Dr. Kogan is an interesting professor. The class is confusing at first but if you follow along in class and read the book to figure out how to do the problems, then his lectures will make sense. The exams are pretty much all or nothing (there's no partial credit). Practice from the textbook and don't make small numerical mistakes.
All I want to say is DO NOT TAKE HIM ! TERRIBLE PROFESSOR

Tough grader, even though I answered every answer correct on every exam I still only got 70's.  You need very specific answers that align only with his explanations in class.  Doesn't know the contents of the book he has you read and grades against you if you use methods from the book.  Avoid if possible.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: Terrible grader.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Dr. Kogan is an interesting professor: Positives: 1) Works through understandable examples in lecture 2)  Gives good explanations with an aim at developing intuition 3) Has a droll sense of humor Negatives: 1) Grades super tough 2) Doesn't give entire class time to take tests  3)  Hmwk counts for nothing 4)  Total grade  3 tests + final
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: If you're a math genius and can teach yourself from a book, then this class is for you. The homework is optional. But if you're a mere mortal who needs a teacher to teach, pick another. The grade depends on 3 exams and the final. No partial credit. The lectures are a mess, and he doesn't even know what's in the textbook. He laughs at questions.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Lets you have a cheat sheet for every test, 4 tests  total, optional final, weekly homework. He grades really harsh on  tests, especially for his true or false questions, i always got every "math" problem right on his quizzes, but even though many times i had the right answer for the T/F problems, he didn't like my explanations and gave me 0/20s
PRACTICE! PRACTICE! PRACTICE!

You get to make your own cheat sheet for every exam, the final is optional, he recycles a lot of questions from old exams, and you get a free ebook. His lectures are only good to show you what sections of the book to read, and his exam questions are a lot of work, answers longer as the page is wide. Not hard but expect to teach yourself.

Not horrible, but certainly not one of the better professors at UMBC. His lectures are boring and pointless, but his quizzes are nothing like the bookwork he gives you. He lets you bring a cheat sheet to all quizzes and offers an extra credit problem, but they are hard. I highly recommend watching khan academy youtube videos in addition to reading.

I have had kogan before for Diff EQ. It was super easy. The TA graded fairly and the textbook was helpful. Then I took him for Matrix Analysis and OMG! His proofs in lecture was straight out of the book word for word, the TA would not give any partial credit and the quizes (Exams) did not accurately test on what we learned in class. DO NOT TAKE!

He has a number of metaphors he uses that can confuse people and likes to try to be funny, which he can be sometimes.  Somewhat strong russian accent and has difficulty explaining how to understand something if you don't get what he means. All tests are scored on the first 100 out of 120 points (20 EC) Drops low exams and hws. Optional final

If you find yourself at UMBC and needing to take this upper level class.. Instead of forking over your hard earn money to have him as instructor, give your money. I will hand you a text book, tease you when you raise your hand, talk randomly about about math in general, not formally prove anything, and then grade you without any partial credit.

If you really are interested in mathematics, why the ideas you will learn are true, and you aren't a cry baby, this professor is the best you can ever have for a mathematics class in the whole university. If you just want to bs your way through this class or you are just taking it for a requirement, then take someone else.
Often times it's hard to understand him b/c of his accent, but he's a nice guy who tries hard. I only passed b/c I had an extraordinary TA.

When you go to office hours he is is not very willing to help. He does not teach the required materials in lectures--you will be teaching yourself. His tests are short but do not compare to the final that all students in Math 151. If you haven't taken calc 1 before you will have no idea what is going on so switch to a different professor.

While he may not be the easiest professor, Dr. Kogan wants his students to do well. The quizzes are simple enough, but the tests are quite difficult. Study the textbook and actually do extra problems in the textbook to do well. Also,  if you ask him for help, he will really try to help you do better. Also, take advantage of any offered extra credit

Do not take him for 151, exams are only 6 questions with no partial credit and no curve. Very hard to understand and is more worried about proving how smart he is instead of actually teaching material.

This class contained a lot of theory, so it was confusing for me. Dr. Kogan is always willing to answer questions though. His homework and quizzes are reasonable (he lets you bring a cheat sheet) and the final is completely optional. There are extra credit opportunities on the quizzes.

This guy is so funny and too nice. I miss this class. Very laid back. I admit he is very hard to understand. I am good at math but an art major so this class was extremely easy for me. The way he explains things does not get through to most students. If you are lost in math, be careful; I would not recommend this teacher.

Nice teacher, but not very clear. Class seemed somewhat pointless since I had to teach myself from the book. One time his test had material we were never assigned for homework, but despite all of that, the class was easy. He lets you have note sheets for tests, plus he gives you like 120 pts in problems out of 100 pts. And the final is optional.

Great guy.  Class was sometimes a waste of time, a lot of time was spent rehashing previous lectures.  Quizes were extemely easy, with a significant amount of extra credit.  He also allowed a cheat sheet for very simple math, allowing you to put all the formulas and anything else you would need to get 100%.  Final exam was optional.  Take his class

Somewhat engaging, but not very clear. In all fairness though, linear algebra is filled with concepts that can make your head spin. Often jokes with and teases students, which sometimes makes it worth coming to class. Tests are concept based, although he allows you to have a cheat sheet. Copy down the theorems in each chapter, and you'll do fine.

Lectures are useless, so rely on the book. Nice enough guy, but often teases & randomly calls on people. Doesn't always understand the questions asked. Weekly HW from book. Quizzes are often concept-based and are hard, even though he allows a cheat sheet. But I didn't attend all classes, so maybe if I went to more I would have fared better.

Great professor.  Made class fun to come to.  If you pay attention and come to class you'll get an "a-b".  His tests are not terrible plus we could use 1 page of notes as a cheat sheet.  I typically don't enjoy Math, but this class was interesting.

He is a really good professor. Is always late to his class, but lets u go on time.  His exams are concept based.  His quizzes are doable. The best part of this course was that you didn't have to take the final if you did well in class.  So its helpful if you go to class regularly.  :)

I would AVOID this prof. His lectures leave you without a better understanding of the material, the quizzes test your knowledge of the concepts rather than actual problems (which makes it 10x harder), and he is bad at explaining things. Depend heavily on the textbook and if you're good, you wont every have to attend lectures.
Not a terribly hard class, do all homeworks and study a little and you'll get an A. Plus his final is optional.

Nice guy. Has a sense of humor, always seems happy to speak with students. His "quizzes" take the whole class period and count for most of your grade, but he doesn't call them tests so he doesn't have to grade them himself. Despite that, he seems to know what level of understanding of the material each student has and grades the course fairly.

He was an okay professor. He makes things more harder than it needs to be but his exams are EXTREMELY EASY! They're all based off the homeworks that he gives so all you need to do is study the homework (he also puts the answers to the homework online after they're submitted) and you'll be fine. I found him to be okay. Not great but manageable. I di

Very dedicated to rigor.  This is not a class to skip or sleep through, he will get 90% of every proof by asking the class.  He is VERY lenient with partial credit, but his exams are pretty tough.  Be prepared to read the book and reconcile the material there with his lecture.

Math 115 is a substitute if you do not want to take Math150, take Stat 351 if you don't want to deal with him.  He will help you if you need help, and he assumes you know more than you should because its only a 100 level math course. Just come to class, do the homework, and study/come to his office hours. Basic probablility and matrices taught.

Do not take this class. It was the worst experience of my life. The majority of the class was failing..did not understand the work and received no help from him. Got the run around between him and the grader and there was also a disconnect between the two. I repeat..DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS.

I didn't think he was a great professor. He was difficult to understand, and didn't explain concepts well at all. I would not recommend his class. Quizzes weren't too bad though; a lot of them focus on conceptual stuff as opposed to just problem solving. Def. possible to get an A in his class.

throughout the semester you may think that hes hard to understand. but just read the book, he lets you use one page of notes on the quizzes. and if you do well throughout the semester the final is optional what more could you ask for!!

I was uncertain to take this class with him, but all is well. More than willing to reiterate points in class or go over course material outside of class. He has feasible office hours and a dry humor. Goes into great theory depth, which I love for understanding purposes. As long as you attend class, you won't have any problems getting a good grade!

One of the best teachers I've had. Has a great sense of humor, and while he is hard to understand at times, he is more than willing to repeat and spend extra time on something. Cares about students, and while his grader is strict, he allows partial credit and will curve if needed. At least 5 min. late to every class, but always lets out on time.

He has no idea of what he is doing, he comes in puts things on the board that are all wrong. Says stupid phrases like He is lost and this is America you can do whatever you want. If you dont like math dont take this class.

Extremely hard grader, but not unreasonable.  I can only guess that that's the explanation for his low ratings, because I thought he was one of the best professors I've had.  Teaches very well, & a really cool person.  However, in this class understanding the material isn't always enough to get by, as proofs can be hard to produce if youre a novice

Never take this class. He is horrible at explaining -- he assumes you know it. Constantly makes mistakes that are pointed out by the class. I dropped this class weeks ago and I am sure I made the right move.

Jacob Kogan is one of the coolest teachers I have ever had.  This guy is awesome.  He's got a sense of humor about himself, is willing to joke with the class and will repeat anything if you ask him too.  This class is hard, and he does not give much partial credit, but there is a curve and if you understand the material, he'll know and you'll pass.

I took him over the summer.  His quizzes weren't hard, they were completely doable but I never had enough time to complete them and his grader was the stingiest mofo i've ever had grade a quiz.  For instance, if you found the wrong values for X and you finished the problem and did everything else correct, you still got maybe 5/20.

He only proved the theorems in the book (which are already in the book) and never explained how to use the theorems in proofs.  He also failed to give the first test before the very last day to drop the class (3 or 4 weeks before the final.)
No Comments

Never ever take his class.  You will defenitely get D unless you get an F.  Dont even know how to teach except knows how to COOK VECTOR.  In our class, 75% dropped out right after the mid-term and rest, most of them failed except couple of them passed with C.  Exams are really hard.

Dr Haerian  is one of the best professors I have ever had-very knowledgeable in the subject matter, amazing at explaining difficult concepts in a more easy to understand fashion, and a true inspiration for her students. All this, and a wonderful person. Do not hesitate to take her classes.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Inspirational

reviews.comment: Good sense of humor. Lots of graded assignments

She is a lenient grader. She is cool and her class is totally stress free. Learning her subject requires more than 80% of your OWN effort. Her classes are interactive. On the contrary, reaching her is a big problem. She is a very busy person and email response time is very long.
Alan is one of the worst teachers I have ever had. His instructions for homework and tests and projects are all vague and his grading is absolutely arbitrary.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Pr. Alan's class was fun! He is very big on class participation and his class is one of few classes that make feel engaged on a personal level. He is pretty lenient when it comes to grading, he is very caring and this was the easiest class I have ever taken. Thumbs up.

The class itself was great fun (Craft of Acting, mostly for theatre majors) but I still don't know anything about why I was given the grade I got. No indication of what my grade would be, he said I was doing fine, and I ended with a B. I'm not upset by the grade, just bothered that it was a surprise. Craft of Acting was very physical. Beware.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: He might seem scary at first but he is super nice. This feels like a PE class because we do a lot of physical activities. He makes you grow a lot as an actor. He is willing to help and give you advice if needed.
Awesome Professor!!! I highly recommend him. Straight forward and will let you know what exactly to study
Alan is a great professor. He's very passionate about the topics he teaches, and never minces his words when giving his opinion on matters. Really encourages us to think.

Craft of Acting 1 is basically the most emotional workout you will ever do. I cried and sweated more this semester than any other time of my life. It was hard physically, mentally, and emotionally, but I feel like I'm a better person after taking this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Alan was great. Class was a reading, quiz on that reading, and discussion. Sometimes would give away answers. Some plays were boring and some weren't. Overall, it was an easy class. Great Professor.
This class is open to non-majors, and every one will learn some really amazing life lessons from Alan.

Alan's one of the best professors I've ever had. He's very nice, and knows his stuff. On more than one occasion he has stopped me outside of class to just chat with me, and he does that to many students. He remembers seemingly unimportant details about his students and connects to them with how likeable he is. Definitely worth taking this class.
More than willing to explain questions about the readings, explains in an easy to understand way. Simple class, just do the readings, take a test, and discuss it. Very easy to get along with.

I struggled with this professor a lot at the beginning because I did not really understand much and she can definitely come off as rough. I took 101,102 with her and am taking 201with her next semester. I think that she definitely cares a lot and wants to help. Be present during class, get extra help if you need and you'll be perfectly fine.

Krippes was a caring professor who filled each day of class with quirks that I had never seen. Throughout my time with her, I noticed that she did have a bit of favoritism as well as a short-temper. Nonetheless,  I enjoyed my time with her. Very easy grader. Cares more about learning than scores.

Do not take Krippes, she is the worst at giving instructions, and when you try to say something, she'll say "oh no you got it wrong" in front of the whole class. I recommend taking Jee Park, instead of this professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Participation matters--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: She isn't as bad as people say she is, granted that this is 102 so I'm not sure how she was in 101. I think the class is pretty manageable. She DOES come off rough especially to those having more trouble, but I honestly think that she just wants you to do your best. However, I understand that she can be seen as mean by those who are more sensitive

Just a hard no unless you're Korean and have prior knowledge of the language. And I don't mean Koreaboo level, I mean grewup speaking it at home with your Korean family. Other than that you are in for a tough course. She is hard to communicate with and is very strict. She's sweet but definetly is a tough woman. NO issues regarding that on my end.
absolutely awful teacher. not patient, incredibly rude, constantly yelling, and unwilling to help.

She is the most frustrating teacher I've ever met! I do NOT recommend her!!!! She gaslight and is just completely rude when you have a genuine question! She grades you low for the absolute minor things and she is just horrible... avoid her if possible

Took her for 101 and taking her again for 201. Rude and passive aggressive but also kind of nice. I like the way she structures her class. Grades are always up to date, but she's a tough grader; would take off 0.1 points for no reason. a minute late to class? you get a 50% for attendance. Gaslights students for asking certain questions.

This is the worst language teacher i have ever had in my life I have learned three different languages in a school setting This is the first time i have had a teacher blame everyone else for the fact that she does not care she barely gives you enough time when you are taking an online class very passive aggressive and give attitude for no reason
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Straight up rude!! Makes insults to students and is not helpful in any way. If you plan on taking this class I recommend you already knowing a good bit of korean if not you will be lost.
Horribly passive aggressive. Never want to hear her voice again.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: The class was fairly easy if you paid attention in class. The only thing I will agree on is that she is a bit aggressive at times. However, I think it's due to students not meeting her expectations to participate. If you participate, read the book, and practice you'll get an easy A. She does have a lot of quizzes but they all cover previous lessons
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Thorough in her lessons (take notes) & will review entire lessons or give us time to correct ourselves. Her affinity w/ technology is poor, but improving. She sounds intimidating, but she's actually forgiving w/ beginners (my past teachers were belligerent). Practice more outside of class & you will meet her goals of making a proper Korean speaker.

Marks you late if your lagging computer is unlucky to finally load at 10:01. Asks you why you haven't participated when you already did. Is very rude and misunderstands the students often. Speaks to us as children than adults. And also wouldn't give enough time on the test until someone brought it up to the dean. She's better in person than online
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: During test she manages them so poorly. Leaves like 10 minutes for a whole class to do an Oral presentation one at a time. So naturally with only 10 minutes, a good chunk of students don't get to go so she tells them to meet her in her office at a different time, and when that time conflicted with other classes you straight up just got a 0 for that
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: She is by far the worst Korean language professor at UMBC. I've had her for KORE102 and 201, the latter being online. Don't ask her questions. Be prepared to never know what to do. Horrible time management for tests. And if you take an online class with her then be prepared to lose points for things outside of your control. She's funny at least
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Beware of pop quizzes--Tough grader

reviews.comment: So in KORE101 where you literally have no idea about the language and want to learn it you are expected to understand everything she says in that foreign language at a SUPER fast pace. When you stop to ask a question she gets all agitated that you don't fluently understand the language already. Plus the pop quizzes she gives everyday, verystressful
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: One of the WORST professors I've ever had. She honestly made me hate learning Korean. When we ask a question she just points to the board saying "see? it's here look" which wasn't helpful at ALL. Also her final had information that was on a completely different lesson that's not for 201. She was also disorganized with tests.. just terrible
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Beware of pop quizzes--Tough grader

reviews.comment: completely disorganized. There was even one incident over winter break where she didn't assign the homework until a night before it was due at 11:45 pm and expected everyone to turn it in the next day. She also does daily "pop quizzes" which are annoying and speak way too fast to be understood. assigns in-class homework 10 mins before class ends.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Beware of pop quizzes--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Professor Krippes was very hard to work with. She gives pop quizzes on things you just learned so memorize new vocab instantly or you will struggle. Don't ask questions in class because she will just belittle you for not understanding. If you're sick and miss class, even with a doctor's note, she won't care and will punish your grades.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: I like her, my only problem was that it is very hard to communicate with her the issues you are having. Otherwise, she has been very helpful but beyond level 1 I wouldn't necessarily recommend her. Not only that but she herself will get passive agressive at the class if she makes a mistake and doesn't realize it so please speak up if u notice

I have to disagree with the comment below me, Krippes is one of the most open-minded, organized professors I've had my entire college career. Her 'various outbursts and passions' are one of the many things that make her more endearing as a language teacher, and they give the class an energy that's otherwise hard to find in a normal college class.

Don't get me wrong. Krippes is good person. She's funny, very outspoken, and teaches more than just Korean. These three points are also exactly why she's not a great teacher. She wastes a lot of class time with her various outbursts and passions. She's also very disorganized, and expects you to see things from her perspective. Great personality tho

I loved having Professor Krippes! She's hilarious and really approachable and always keeps the class interesting! I'm taking 102 with her this coming Spring and I can't wait! The homework load can be a bit heavy at times but I mean, it's a LANGUAGE. You have to practice! She always makes sure everyone is up to par. Really great overall!

One of my favorite professors! It helps if you come to the first class with some background information on Hangul. Always something to laugh about in her class, and I learned a lot.  If a project is due next class but she says it isnt/you dont have to worry about it, its safer to do it as she strictly follows the syllabus. Lots of partner work also

Learned a lot from her, but, at times it was hard to keep up because she talks fast and goes fast. I spent roughly 2 hours a night doing homework. It's a lot of homework but if you want an A you have to do it. Do all the homework, attend class, try to understand and you will get an A.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: I like professor Krippes a lot, but studying abroad forced me to realize that she's not a great teacher. I spend the last year studying in Korea and when I got there I - and everyone else from UMBC, who by that point had been taking Korean for two full years - was placed into Advanced Level One, the class for people who only know the alphabet.
I love Krippes. She's really funny. She can be a little confusing at times and the tests got harder as the semester went by, but I would love to have her again as a teacher.

Fantastic teacher! She's there for you. She's so kind. If you want to learn Korean even in the slightest, she will take that want and turn it into a love. She's amazing! Will help you whenever you need it. Homework every class but is marked by completion. Wonderful teacher. Would recommend!

Professor Krippes is a very enthusiastic and quirky professor who constantly keeps students engaged and tries to get them as interested in learning Korean as possible. Assignments and exams aren't very difficult as long as you do the homework. If you give your best effort, you will get no lower than a "B," although getting an "A" should be easy.

She's a bit quirky, but super funny and nice. Many tests but easy if you're Korean or have previous knowledge, and not hard if you review a little--no need to study too hard. May be hard to understand, but will try best to help you. Hw is super easy and light. Allows test corrections and offers extra credit opportunities. Will miss her after 202...

I love Professor Krippes she's so sweet and very silly.  She's occasionally a bit hard to understand but if you ask her she'll explain very throughly (after a bit of "Wah! Ya! Weren't you here? Wah. How can you not know this? Wah!" in a kind, blustery sort of way).  She's really fantastic and the class isn't hard if you study the flash cards.
She's really helpful if you care and do the work, and the work isn't even that hard.
Incredibly helpful and kind. The class isn't hard, but if you struggle at all she will help you. She's awesome!
She is nice and is also very helpful! I like her.

Contrary to at least one classmate who posted below me, I found Professor Krippes to be accomodating and helpful.  She holds more office hours than most other professors and is proactively concerned with rectifying any weaknesses her students may have.  The academically active student will appreciate Professor Krippes.

I had her for 101 and 102.  She failed me even after I did all the work and did the best work I could.  She barely helped me when I had time and refused to help as all other teachers usually do.  If you want to learn Korean, I suggest taking it anywhere else, but not with her.

Very nice and always willing to help. Quirky but funny and makes the class interesting. There are a LOT of vocab quizzes but if you study they're not hard. Do all the work she assigns and you'll be fine. Also, she usually lets you redo work for a better grade.
very energetic and fun to learn in her classes, very caring
Extremely helpful, energetic and inspiring. Cares about her students and gives every opportunity to learn and pass

A good teacher. Although she is the only professor who teaches 100-200 level, I would recommend her. She cares about her students and is funny as well. Her assignments are easy and she sometimes lets you re-do the quizzes and tests. Attendance is mandatory though. TAKE HER CLASS

Ms. Krippes is very friendly, energetic, and engaging... but I'm finding it hard to learn from her.  Her assignments tend to either be so easy that you learn nothing, or so difficult that a non-native speaker will have trouble completing them.  There is very little direct translation.  She's a wonderful person, just not the most efficient teacher.

Awesome professor! Incredibly helpful and super nice. She REALLY cares about her students.  Always willing to help and difficult NOT to pass her class. Awesome, I love her. Waiting for her to teach 301 so I can be with her again! :):):)

this is such an easy class, just make sure you go to every class! i missed 2 quizes, and i still have a chance of getting an A. and she is the only teacher that lets u take home the graded quizes/tests to recorrect them and turn it in the next day for full credit. take it!
Energetic and interesting =^-^=

Speaks softly but overall explains things pretty well. Projects were rough, but a different professor came up with them. His exams were very memorisation heavy, but he told us what was on them so aslong as you studied you were fine. Curved generously at the end
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Group projects

reviews.comment: Very knowledgeable on the subject and it shows in the lectures and office hours. His lectures are absolutely packed with info, uses cli tools to go into great detail, like opening up obj files/ examining addresses and registers. Projects are easy/straightfoward, 5 total, one of them took <2hr. Very friendly to go to for help in office hours.
He was a decent professor. Lectures were a bit boring and it was difficult to hear him at times due to his low tone. He's very helpful in office hours and curved exams when the results were poor.

Prof Deepak is a good professor. he speaks soft in class and kinda hard to hear but he is available monday-thursday for office hours help. i struggled in assembly but he helps you out. there's 2 exams, 4 hw, and 8 projects.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: He seems to be an ok prof.
I found her teaching to be Awful would not take her again.

No textbook. Class can be boring (she explains how to use commas), but definatly helps you research. Attendence is mando but she's a fair teacher and VERY helpful. We wrote one 12 page paper. Quizzes were for attendence purposes only. Take Her!!!

Great class, did well even though I didn't show up much. Low textbook use, everything you need to know can be found in her lectures which are posted online. Online quizzes can be a little tough but she offers extra credit. Relies on the TA a lot but he was great too.
Very understanding

I took this class last semester and have to say that this was by far my favorite class and i'm an engineering major.  Lectures are very interesting and she is the only professor that I know that can show Monty Python in a class and make it relevant.  Also lets you watch the HBO series John Adams during lecture but definitely do the readings.

Great class and great teacher. Her lectures are very interesting and she makes an effort to learn the names of her students. She is very personable and a fair grader. I hated history in high school, but this class has been great with her.

Great Professor! Always willing to help. Read all three novels, they will have questions on the tests. 2 midterms and a final. weekly online multiple choice 10 question quizzes. drops lowest 2 scores. Exams 20% multiple choice, 30% Identifications, and 50% 1 question Essay. Very interesting lectures.

Great teacher. Very glad she's the head of the History Dept., she helped me out a lot. I haven't had any of her high level courses but when I did she was a very easy teacher. Offers a lot of extra credit.
She is the best teacher I've had here at umbc. she is extremely helpful on the paper. she taught me how to research

I LOVE this professor...she's my favorite.  Her class is actually fun to go to.  I don't fall asleep in her class.  Before I took her class I wasn't all that into history.  Now I'm adding a history minor to my political science/pre-law major.  TAKE THIS CLASS!  It's NOT hard.

One of the best courses and best professors I've encountered. Very helpful, you will not go to sleep in this class and if miss any classes, it will be your loss. If you're a history major take this course before you take any other history course if possible.

Dr. Lindenmeyer is extremely helpful in writing the 12 page paper. She gives students all the tools they need and is willing to assist in the process. The class itself, the method of history, is not all that interesting, but it is helpful and Dr. Lindenmeyer tries to make it more interesting and relevant. Great Prof
Very good teacher. She is very nice and will always explain things to you a few ways so that you know what's going on. Also has a sense of humor which is a plus, it means you won't fall asleep.
She's great and very helpful in class and outside of class.  Highly recommended, and she's hot!!
Dr. Kusmaul is phenomenal. She engages with her students and helps them if they are struggling. Her assignments are both challenging and fun at the same time as well.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: With this being an online class, I was nervous about it being boring, but it was surprisingly engaging.many class discussions in class and a generally healthy atmosphere over difficult topics. There is a quiz almost every week over each chapter and a few big exams.

For a social work introduction class, this class was ridiculously hard, especially when it came to the exams. I got really good grades in my upper-level social work classes but struggled to keep a decent grade in this introduction course. Gives study guides, but hardly anything on the stud guide will show up on the exam.

Dr. Kusmaul is an amazing teacher. Her writing assignments, as well as her class in general, encourage students to draw on both knowledge learned both inside and outside of class, and are very applicable to the social work profession.

Professor was very understanding with attendance and the syllabus is so clear and easy to follow. However she needs to come up with more than just reading from the ppt, it can get very tiresome. Not a difficult course and it was much more interesting once discussion gets going so try and participate

Great class and engaging teacher. Very understanding with attendance and Covid. Easy to reach outside of class and reasonable grader. Gives weekly quizzes/discussion posts. Possible to pass without reading because of slides, but would recommend getting the textbook to help with studying. Gives clear instructions and plenty of time for papers.

One of my least favorite Social Work Professors. She is a nice lady and will help you if you ask for help, but in class she basically just reads straight off the power point and has students discuss amongst themselves instead of actually teaching us. The quizzes are tricky and you really have to follow the rubrics if you want good grades on papers

He's the professor you want to take if you already know CS202. He's funny and young. His one "problem"(I dont see it as one) is that he does go on tangents/rambles a lot, but these tangents are about real life. If you're a transfer or have a knack for coding take him. The projects make you think, but u can do em in a weekend.

Brilliant individual. Has a great awareness of what's going on in the computer and technology world. The only critique is that it took a long time to receive grades on tests and homework assignment. Tests are fair.

Professor Kukla is incredibly knowledgeable about all things Comp sci and has a lot of real world experience in the industry. If youre looking to actually learn something, and not just memorize stuff, take him.

Prof. Kukla made me fall in love with Comp Sci. His lectures are interesting and engaging and it is great to learn Computer Science from someone who clearly has lots of experiences working in the industry. I have gone to him outside of class and asked for help in becoming a better programmer and he has always been helpful.

Hard class, but that's not the professor's fault. Kukla is very good at answering questions you have, and has a great sense of humor. He tends to ramble off topic at times, but will snap right back to it. You can argue test answers with him and he'll very much consider changing them if your answer was correct and mis-graded. Good luck!
10/10 professor. Really cares about his students and tries to teach for understanding rather than just memorization.

Had a horrible experience with Kukla! What others have said about him is true. He really is not in charge of the class. If you ask him any questions, his usual response is go ask or email Professor Dixon. He also will start typing the email like we can't type it ourselves. He is also not good at explaining things and goes of topic. Don't take him!!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: Prof. Kukla is not meant for a beginner programmer. He doesn't follow the timeline on the syllabus and doesn't cover necessary topics before an exam. His lectures are hard to follow. He does not seem to have knowledge about the projects or lab assignments. Avoid him at any cost.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: I do think he is a good professor. I would recommend finding another professor if you don't have that much background in programming. He made me hate C++, He is very well experienced for years and  he sometimes doesn't explain what he is doing because he doesn't remember what it does exactly. Puts question on exams that is not martial related
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: The issue with Dr. Kukla is really only one. He isn't really in charge of the class. He just lectures. So he often had to email the other lecturer for info on the assignments. That being said, he's awesome. Smart, funny and experienced.
Just awesome. "my fingers never leave my hands" "It's turtles all the way down"  He will remove the mystery from computer science, If you ask questions you will get great answers.

Hardest grader ever, will assign problems on stuff you covered in class for a whole 5 minutes. Doesn't sympathize if you know what you're doing, only if you've memorized what he's said, though you can easily get an A if you know what you're doing.
Very entertaining and fun. Explains thing clearly, brings a lot of examples, asks questions  and respects your opinion. Laid back and always willing to help. As a lecturer, he is pretty good.
His lectures were fairly boring, but he was a cool guy. He was easy to talk to and get help from. Sometimes he could be a little bit too casual, as in walking around class barefooted.

Explains the material very well for both beginner coders and more experienced students. He clearly still codes a lot (unlike some older professors). The class itself is difficult if you're new to object-oriented programming, but Kukla is very helpful if you ask questions. Bonus points for funny and interesting tangents during lecture.
Very cool and funny guy! Explains things clearly, always willing to help. He's very understanding and encouraging, which is really nice especially if you're an amateur programmer.

His online lectures are straight forward and easy to follow. Working with a partner is required for a lot of the content in this course. The exams are heavily weighed but a lot of the content come from the weekly deliverables & quizzes. Overall, he was understanding and his office hours are helpful.

He's a very caring and knowledgeable professor. He speaks very slowly in recorded lectures, so I sped him up. His course is extremely groupwork oriented. There's a lot of terms to memorize but if you do, it's an easy A. He is a very easy grader, just do your own work.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Group projects--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Honestly for an intro level management class, he is pretty sucky. Does not believe in extra credit and is such a stickler for plagiarism when all his quiz qs are on quizlet. ironic. Decided mid-semester to make final exam monitored. Final exam worth 25% of grade so the loads of other work he makes you do, BARELY counts
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: So the class is basically a UI design class for websites, which isn't what I expected at all but I guess there are very few ways to teach it online. You need photoshop or any good photo editing program in order to do the assignments, unless you find a way to scheme them otherwise. Class isn't awful but nothing special either.

Out of all the IS courses, I cannot understand why a discussion is necessary for this course. Discussions were basically busy work. I am not a graphic design major, so why is the course so graphic design heavy? You will redesign a new website every week based upon principles learned in the Panopto lectures and it's not easy to do without photoshop.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: He's a nice and polite professor, but very monotone. If he was alittle more energetic maybe the classes won't seem so boring. Show up to class because attendance is mandatory and there are clicker questions. You have lab assignments each week that you do with group members they assign you with. But if you listen you can pass for sure with A or B
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: A very nice, polite teacher, will not be rude to you unless you give him a reason to.  Take your time to study ALL lecture material, not just review, and you should do fine on tests.

BRITISH! Great professor, really young, so he knows a lot about real-life applications in HCI and usability. Projects were kind of tedious, but not hard. He will call out students who skip his class though. Exams are short answer, pretty much all from the slides. Really good resource to have, and is extremely helpful if you ever have any questions
Very interesting course and well presented.  I'd take it again.
Easy teacher. Grade consists of attention/participation, essays, and two tests. Long lectures but very thorough and the assignments are a piece of cake. Study the powerpoints and you'll be fine.
Dr. Kuber clearly puts in a lot of effort in his lectures.  He's very helpful and knows his stuff.  Definitely worth taking his class.

Really good teacher, very nice.  Seemed to care about the students.  Very approachable.  Tests were easy as long as you study.  Only negative, it took some time to get graded materials back.  But still work taking.

Kuber is a good guy, he's nice, understands the material he is teaching, and is always willing to help you during office hours. Takes a personal interest in students and will help you out if you are not doing well, even provide recommendations. Tests and Projects can be time consuming, but interesting. Take IS303 with him, you'll learn a lot!
Dr. Kuber is very helpful.  He provides good quality notes and is always happy to answer questions.  His asignments take time but you learn a lot. Kuber rocks!

Dr. Kuber is a great teacher.  His lectures aren't the most interesting in the world, but he does his best to make the fun and involving.  His tests require a lot of writing, but the review lectures cover everything you need to know, no surprises.  Assignments are a bit ambiguous sometimes, but he'll clarify no problem. Kuber is awesome for IS303.

The slides & syllabus weren't even hers. WOULD'T recommend this class for beginners/ non comp majors. It's extremely hard & she is a tough grader: No redos, no reviewing answers in class (b/c she's paranoid about cheating). There's no study guides, the slides are useless & her answer is often to Google it. She gives up if the students don't get it

Terrible teacher, treats the course like it's your 3rd computer science. Syllabus said no prior programming experience required, but the lecture slides should be more directional for beginners. Expect a lot of frustration and sarcastic comments from the professor when you ask questions, she does a good job of making you feel stupid.

No textbook is required, but her lecture slides do not help AT ALL. When she assigns you homework, the slides give you no help. When you email her questions, she doesn't help you and will rather ask you questions that leave you even more confused than before you asked. She does not have the teaching skills.

Literally took an entire class period and had everybody work on the homework and come up to her with questions. Everybody walked out with at least most of it done. Did 2 lectures in one class to make sure she had time to do this. Homework is very similar to lecture slides.

She does not help at all. Her lecture slides rarely match with the homework that she assigns. If you want to do well in the class, sign up for a tutor immediately, or better yet, do not take the class with her. She googles how to do certain codes during the lecture because she does not know how to do them herself. Avoid her!

She is a terrible teacher. She usually searches google in the middle of her lectures because she doesn't know how to do some things. Also, she rarely responds to email inquiries about homework, which she makes harder than those assigned in cmsc 201.
Didn't explain things clearly. Homeworks did not connect to the powerpoints. Tests were hard. She had a clear lack of teaching ability.

First of all, if you're a physics major with ANY programming experience, take 201 instead of this course for your core.  That said, Kuss is pretty dull.  He's been teaching for 10+ years, but he hasn't mastered teaching.  Nervous, stammers a lot, but easy to understand. If you know your stuff, skip class except for tests, do the projects online.

Very bad teacher. as someone said earlier... takes time with easy subject, but when the topic is hard, he rushed through it and doesnt give time to ask questions... he goes extremely fast and act nervous.. as if he doesnt know how to explain better. take someone else. it doesnt matter much but... he has a very boring/geeky personality.

Great intro class if you are into computer programming (C, linux), but I imagine it wouldn't be fun taking this if you're not majoring in a computer field. You program 8 projects during the semester, take 3 exams, and write 1 paper. Kuss talks very fast but he really know's his stuff, he lectures all class while showing powerpoint slides.

He does know his stuff and if you are looking for an instructor who knows what's what in the computer science instrusty then he is the one for you.  But if you are beginner in the field and you require  a lot of additional assistance then he not for you. Overall, I would recommed fast pace learned for this course only.
Sometimes confuses himself while teaching.

Fred is a nice guy, but a very boring, typical "geek" like teacher.  You can tell he knows his stuff, but he doesn't teach it in a very interesting way.  If you ask him for help, he will help you... but if you are taking this class and don't put in a lot of effort...you will not do well.

At the very beginning of the year, his class scared me to death.  I didn't know much about computers, and he just seemed to assume that everyone did.  But as the year went on, the material covered got easier and easier.  Exams are very easy.  The final questions come DIRECTLY from the study guide.
Not a bad instructor at all.  All CMSC 104 instructors will read from slides, but Fred adds to it.  Better than most, and nice to boot.
Not helpful goes too fast shows no visuals and is an all around boring ass little dork. spends no time helpin you out and teaches through slides only.
Not helful. Selfish little devil
Spends hours on basic concepts and seconds on complicated ones.

Her lectures were horrible, waste of time. You had to teach yourself everything. Chat GPT was more helpful. she laughs more than she teaches its so annoying. and her exams were okay... lab was good but honestly, youre mainly graded on exams and the final was ACS.

She's really kind and caring. Her lectures were pretty useless, since she just reads off of her slides (15/60 ppl showed up every lecture. But, she uploads them online and it makes studying for tests very nice. Tests are exactly what her slides cover so if you know your stuff it's easy

Dr. Kyoung is (along with Dr. V) the kindest most caring professors in the Chemistry department. I wish she taught the lecture as well as the lab. Always available, understanding and great at explaining. She makes Analytical Lab a smooth experience. For sure take any class with her. Not heartless like most profs in the department.

his section got put online and she shortened the exam times from 75 min (usual class time) to 60 min., and the questions did not change in difficulty. Imagine trying to complete long pH questions without a chance to check your work, or for partial credit. This speaks volumes for type of teaching style. Horrible and unhelpful.

reviews.comment: I highly recommend to take achem with this professor! A lot of people struggled in the class. However, all you need to do is study the lecture slides and you will be solid. 3 exams and ACS final. Try to get a B avg or higher on the exams to get A. Curve is huge, my dude!!!

Dr. Kyoung literally tells you what will be on her exams at the start of the semester. You don't even have to go to class, just pay attention in the first lecture and you'll know exactly what to study. A-chem is a tough class and the trick is to study smart, not hard.

I disagree with prior comments in that Dr. Kyoung is a good teacher and gives us all of the info we need to pass. You should come to every class! She carefully explains every slide and what you need to know. My only issues were that I did not find the textbook/homework helpful at all, and we had no guidance on how to study for the ACS final.

She needs more teaching experience. Her lectures are just reading off of Power Points and doing only one example problem from each topic but only shows slides instead of actually showing by hand. No clarity, just making you do practice after rushing a chapter. This class is not an exciting chemistry course and she won't make it make it any better.

Should just read book and go to class only on test days. He is hard to follow in lecture, and distracting even if you try to pay attention.

That would be the best thing you could ever do for yourself.

reviews.comment: Would give assignments due next chapter on the day of the exam, would overload you with assignments, and was obsessed with making exams "more difficult" to "prepare" us for harder chem. He's a good lecturer and you will learn but he'll make you work far more than you'd probably enjoy doing.

He always forget to give our exams back. He is so unorganized and he changes syllabus so many times, so you will be confuse. he is not a good professor. Take this class with another professor, if you can select anyone else.
He gives extremely hard tests and tries to trick you on them. 70% of your grade is based off of these hard tests. There were 4 tests and none of the class averages were above a 60% on them.

I really felt like he didnt want his students get good grades. He Tries to help when u ask him somethin but thats not enough for him to be a good prof. too much homework and no point for it. He doesnt even go over them so u dont really learn anything!

reviews.comment: Kyle's awesome, nuff said.  I had a good regular teacher when i took from him, but he'll get you through no matter what.  Go to office hours!
Kyle Stern is a pretty cool guy. He will make you work for your grade, but if you come to his office hours, everything will be fine
kyle stern for president

Very nice prof, but can be really particular about grades and doesn't provide much detail on feedback. Class was mandatory for attendance and was discussion based. Fairly easy assignments: 3 film reports, 3 film reviews and a final paper.

Professor was nice and cared about students but was difficult to contact online. Every homework had errors and whenever students needed to contact her, she would either take a week to reply to emails or not reply at all. She also would sometimes simply forget to post assignments and then would complain when students didn't understand material

She's really passionate about the subjects covered in lecture, therefore I can see why she loves to have discussions and groups share their thoughts during lecture. However, since most of the stuff she graded had nothing to do with what was covered in lectures, it felt like I only went to lectures for attendance points.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--So many papers

reviews.comment: Professor Yoon is definitely my favorite professor & the best I've had in a while. She knows what she's doing & is very organized with her materials & contents we learn & is lenient on mistakes & encourages them so we improve. She cares for students & while she may seem strict on things that's what makes her good. Don't hesitate to take her class!
A solid professor who cares for the subject she teaches and for her students. The class materials are dynamic and interesting.

Dr. Yoon is an awesome prof. I've learned so much about South Korea that I never would've otherwise. Her lectures are engaging & interesting. The assigned readings are as well, although there too many. I would absolutely take this class again, and if you're considering taking it you absolutely should. I'm a spanish student and got by fine.

I loved every second of class with Professor Yoon. She is an amazing person and every minute in her class is worthwhile. While her assignments are daunting, the instructions are very clear and she does not grade hard at all. All the movies and lectures in the class are interesting, and you won't dread going to her class at all. Superb teacher.

She may scare you a lot in the beginning, but as long as you can show some dedication for her class. You won't fail her class, and if you can answer her question crystal clear you'll get at least B. She is a tough grader.

reviews.comment: Watch a movie, read a book, write a short paper. Not a hard class. There is a lot of Korean history and references in the class.
