reviews.comment: She is very understanding. The class has many oral activities in addition to written quizzes and writing activities. They are all helpful.

She is very friendly and gives good feedback on your work. I thought she was really picky on what she looks for in her student's paper. I found her grading to be very strange at times. She seems more like an English teacher because she grades on grammar, cohesiveness,etc. Overall, she is very knowledgeable and I learned a lot.

She is a really great professor! Very kind and understanding but she is one tough grader! It was incredibly informative and insightful overall. I sincerely enjoyed this course from start to finish. This is a class where you really gotta put in your A-Game but it's totally worth it.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Gives good feedback--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: I am Korean American and had some background knowledge before taking KOR 301 and MLL 311, but it didn't make the courses any easier for me than other people. Actually, other people who didn't know about Korea or didn't speak Korean before seemed to do better on the exams. I needed to study hard and she was always willing to help. I learned a lot.
shes really helpful but you have to be ready to put the work in  in order to do well, unless you're of course really korean and know the material already.

should not take it if you are not very good at korean. this class needs a lot of background knowledge. if you are korean she would make you do more work and put you in advance group. lots of HW and quizzes and oral presentations. attendance and participation matters. she always penalizes for everything, late work, late to class...

She is such a nice person and a good teacher. Her class is pretty hard though. Especially If you are not familiar with Korean history or customs like myself. I did pretty bad on the 2 Tests, but I did all my homework and had a good final presentation and paper so my grade ended up being a 'B'.
She is just okay.

I don't think KORE 310 class is easy at all. You have to study a lot. However, she tries her best to help out everybody get the contents. She always asks us to "think" about the language and culture, which is sometimes hard. But I guess we learn from it.
easy.... period

If you are Korean already it's super easy. If you are just learning or not Korean it's not as hard if you are really interested in Korean culture. Hang out with a lot of Korean friends to help you with your homework and your pronunciation! She's a very nice teacher :D

The class is easy if you read the assignments.  You just need to study a bit for the exams because everything is covered, and stuff you don't expect to be on there is.  She's always willing to help you if you don't understand something.  To get a good grade it's pretty clear, and she tries to help you succeed.  Many extra credit events too.

She's excellent at explaining her materials&makes sure that students understands the material. KORE 309 (Business Korean) was required a little bit of studying but I learned so much. KORE309 (Korean Culture&society) was a little difficult because there were some presentations and readings, but I learned a lot. MLL 315 (Movie) is very fun and easy!

she also teaches 302, 309, 310. like the commenter below, she knows how to teach. she likes to see students be interested in the class. if you are worried about your grade or struggling, she will do all she can to help you as long as you talk to her.

Amazing Professor, knows how to explain her material for easy comprehension.  Very fun class to be in.  Not too difficult, not a class you can just sleep through.  Have to work for it, but she definitely does her best to help you out.

He would force people to move to the front if there was an empty seat in front of them. Stopped class to single me out for not singing when 5 other people around me weren't and a few even had headphones in. There is always new steps to learn. He is kind

Professor Kwame is an interesting character. He is passionate about his country, Africa, which is why he is a good African studies professor at UMBC. You really just have to show up to class to get an A. We have weekly summaries that are basic- you are in college, you should be okay with doing the bare minimum to get an easy A.
You have to try hard to not get an A. Interesting class, easy chapter summaries, exams are basically question from the summaries. Would def recommend to get your gen eds out the way.

reviews.comment: Interesting and funny. Not a hard class but I felt like I learned a lot. I really enjoyed it.
Easy class
Really nice teacher. Lectures are interesting and easy to understand. Not a lot of homework at all.

His grading system may seem a bit off, but if you do all the work, you should have no problem getting an A. Lectures varied in length, but if you participate, it whizzes by much faster. I actually learned a lot about African Religion in this class.
His style of teaching emphasizes on hands on learning. He's one of the greatest teachers I've had @ umbc
This teacher's class is the most hands-on learning experience I have ever had in any class. The class doesn't list practical as part of it but the format was very hands on. He's extremely helpful

Kwame is the man!! anybody that says anything negative is ridiculous. his classes are so easy and hes the nicest man on the planet and super understanding. ppl get pissed because he can be spacey but seriously its a guaranteed A so stop complaining!

The course is Black Music but it really is African Music. You learn about music and instruments in Africa. He gives attendence at the end of class. He is never on point with the assignments. He reminds me of a substitute teacher in high school who does not know what he is doing.

SUPER EASY TEACHER. Easy class. Fun class. Very popular class. Very long though. Also an African studies credit. AFST215 or Dance260. Great exercise.teachers are trying to make it a culture credit. Once a week. 2 and a half hours.

Class is VERY lecture-heavy. Missing a lecture definitely puts you in a tough position. Lectures only consist of pictures and titles, which makes studying unconventional. Exams were easy, a lot of E.C. was given too. She canceled a few times, but adjusted the schedule & exam fairly. Whilst studying, you NEED to browse the internet and photos, etc.

Professor Poolman was definitely something. Her classes are lecture heavy and only have titles and pictures on her slides. You have to be very attentive and also give pop quizzes out of nowhere. Her class is respectfully a mess I would say but you just have to acclimate. I'm thankful she cancelled classes sometime

reviews.comment: She is a nice professor, but her course structure is terrible. There are no homework assignments, just readings before every class. If you miss a lecture your done for.

reviews.comment: She made the class very enjoyable and taught in a way that I was able to understand and retain Spanish. I highly recommend her!
She's supportive, always understanding and will see you through till the very end. Make sure you work and she will work with you.
She is so kind and always willing to help. her quizzes are easy and she's funny young and doesn't require you to speak Spanish throughout class like the other professors at umbc. Take her!!

Simply one of the best professors I've had. I took spanish 101 already speaking spanish to get an easy A, and expected to be bored to sleep by the class, but she actually made it worthwhile to pay attention and continue attending class. Seriously, if you take spanish, take it with her.

Best professor i've had. She's a lovely person inside and out. She is in touch with her students and her attitude makes you actually want to attend class. Makes the material relatable and turned an otherwise dry subject into something worth your tuition. I wouldn't recommend anyone else as highly.

She's a great professor who really wants her students to learn. She answers questions when asked and moves at a pace where everybody can understand. She made the lessons fun so it was more of a discussion rather than lecture. Definitely recommend this professor.
Awesome Spanish professor.

Professor Liptak is a great Spanish teacher! Her expectations are clear and her teaching techniques make Spanish easy to learn. I really enjoyed her class and I would recommend her for students who need clear instruction in class (like I did). She's amazing!

Took his new HONR 300 Food and Society course (not a course option here yet).
Some either love or hate this professor; to ME, he was super annoying & never prepared. 
Always changed his mind on the syllabus, never knew what he assigned, lectures were so bare, had a SO unnecessary verbal final, doesn't know bb AT ALL. I did not enjoy his "teaching."

Prof. Lansing is great. Attend the lectures and succeeding in the course is simple; his lectures are very helpful and held my attention. Instructions, course objectives and deadlines are very clear and organized. He is transparent with his expectations and wants to see everyone pass.
Engaging guy, super easy to follow lecture. If you show up to lecture you'll pass the class easily.

You must attend lectures because that is where the exam information comes from. He does not seem to know his stuff for a professor. He is very odd, and he never provides clear grading guidelines. His grading is unreliable. He asks condescending questions to every student in the class by going around to them. He is not someone to wake up for.

Awesome professor who is genuinely one of the smartest professors I have had. His examples and energy regarding the material make lecture interesting. The term paper is only as hard as you make it, don't save the paper for the week of, and then you can submit a revision. Lots of readings with few points in the class so must be serious from day 1.

reviews.comment: Attend the lectures and do the reading quizzes and you are pretty much guaranteed to pass. Dr. Lansing's lectures were very engaging and interesting. I took this class as a Culture GEP and it was easy. I recommend attending all his lectures because tests are mostly about lecture & uses the lecture quiz questions on exam. I believe there are multiple components to look in to decide to take this professor or not. 1st, he does not post any slides on black board to go back and study. 2nd, he does not write a single word on the white board to take a note. 3rd, he talks 6 sentences in 2 seconds that you have to take a note!
he is the one human geo teacher that is not boring so take him and he is easy 2 multiple choice exams and a final exam it's not that hard

Lansing is a really funny teacher and has interesting lectures even though he doesn't always fully comprehend what he is talking about. He knows a good deal about policy however it does not always correlate to the information in this course. He is not always super clear about how he grades assignments but I learned a lot in his class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Hilarious--Would take again

reviews.comment: He is a super chill and funny guy but he grades surprisingly hard. It's a writing intensive class. Tests are open notes. He doesn't seem to know a lot about what he's talking sometimes, but it's a fun and interesting class. I would definitely recommend.

He wrote on the syllabus that he almost never replies to student emails. that it very true! Hes impossible to get a hold of outside of class. The class has quizzes every week & 3 papers + 2 revisions. He NEVER gives out clear grading rubrics. He grades how he feels like it. In class he goes around to each one asking questions, its patronizing.

reviews.comment: This guy is one of my favorite profs at UMBC so far. His lectures are great, the class isn't too hard but I feel like I learned a lot. It is sometimes hard to kno exactly what his expectations are for assignments but overall he's a great prof and its a good class

only + is that he's a funny guy. but I really question Lansing's knowledge of human geo bc he was awful at answering questions in class. he's not great at replying to emails. Exams are ok as long as you spend a day or two rlly studying your lecture notes. Highly recommend attending lecture (even tho it's boring)bc exam q's r lecture based

Dr. Lansing is a really great professor. Skimming through the textbook should be good enough but if you really wanted to, you could prob get away without it. It helped to take notes fill in the skeleton notes because most of the exam Qs are pulled from the lectures. Exams were all multiple choice. The project was easy if you put the time into it.
Gave the greatest lectures I've ever witnessed. Attendance is not mandatory, but attending class with help with the 3 exams. Exams were fairly easy, and lots of free points were given.

A lot of people say"best teacher ever", this teacher definitely is!He blends a very funny sense of humor into his teaching method, is brilliant and passionate about Hu. Geo. I highly HIGHLY recommend this class. He wants you to succeed, he practically gives you 12 the easy tests to study from. Don't miss out! Register ASAP! You won't regret it! :D
Really funny guy, but doesn't always seem prepared for lecture, bounces around slides a lot and checks notes a lot, class is easy and material is pretty straight forward.
would definitely take this class again, love the professor, makes class entertaining, pretty easy class as long as you show up to the lectures

he seems to have very little in-depth knowledge about his material. he is always looking down at his notes and he would often be not too sure and don't know. He's very articulate and SEEMS passionate in what he talks about but he only has little knowledge considering he is a professor. Tests are from lecture quizzes and lectures. 1st exam was tough

Lansing is very passionate about the subject. He gives very good lectures. He can get lost sometimes, but I find it to be very interesting. There was a midterm, one paper assignment, and a final. If you keep up with the reading, you should have no problem

He is a great Professor. His lectures always keep the class interested and involved. His exams were straight from the notes and he was always available to help with whatever you did not understand. Easily one of my favorite classes/professors since attending college.
This prof is very chill. He gives out 20 freebiee test questions.  Exams were not hard. Take him!!

By far one of the best teachers at UMBC. Despite being held in a large lecture hall, he manages to keep the class awake with animated and interesting lectures. Tests come straight from the lectures and he even posts a review quiz before each with roughly 20 of the questions/answers. You actually spend time LEARNING rather than stressing. Love him!

Best teacher I've had at UMBC, and for a class I just took for a requirement. Gave us 20 of the 45 questions on any exam in practice exams on blackboard, and was fun to listen to. Lectures are entertaining, and even more so if you stay involved with the content. Just show up, take notes, do your practice exams, and you'll get an easy A!

very good teacher. like the course and its contents. group project was good. quizes on readings can be confusing but not hard. can be somewhat hard of a grader on project components of the final paper you write in this course. interesting teacher, very passionate about the subjects he teaches.

Lansing is really passionate about the topic but gets lost a lot while he teaches. He is the definition of the absent minded professor which can be good or bad. Overall, if you take his class you get what you put into it.
Great teacher. Very helpful. There are two papers you must write and two tests. The tests are open note. He makes note pages for you the night before class.
Like the way he teach the class. Exams were easy. Taking note is very important to get a good grade in this class.

Class is easy. I didn't even buy a text book but this required me to attend almost all classes and get notes. He makes topic interesting and easy to understand.  Lansing did tend to mumble the most important pieces of information. He did not answer emails had to speak to him after class. He seemed like to see people sweat but helped in the end.
awsome teacher. a must take

Very good teacher because he makes the topic interesting, makes jokes and class, and lectures in a way that makes you stay awake and listen.  There are a few simple assignments, the tests are all multiple choice, and he is really nice if you take advantage of his office hours.  I would highly recommend him.

He's definitely a good teacher. There was reading every night & a short 2-3 question quiz once a week to make sure you keep up with it. There was no exams and one 15-page paper due at the end that you work on throughout the semester so it's really not that bad. Good class! I'd take more with him!

Laberge constantly makes sexist and racist comments, making generalizations about immigrants and women. He also doesn't take suggestions very well. Constantly interrupts everyone, including his fellow professors. Other than that, not bad. He's been doing this for a while. He knows what he's doing and is good at it.
This guy's a ray of sunshine.

reviews.comment: Lectures were not helpful. final had questions with content that was never taught.  discussions were the most useful thing in this course. all they gave us to study were the discussion slides and a practice quiz that was 10 questions long

Only thing useful about the course was learning MATLAB, which the professor never even taught. Wasted lectures telling stories about his career instead. Made sexist comments at the beginning of the semester about girls in the class only choosing engineering because their dad or boyfriend told them to, which rubbed me the wrong way from the start.
His class was great! A little difficult and very wide ranged but he was a great teacher and very leanient.

Definitely a rough semester for ENES101, but most of those factors that made this semester rough was mainly out of LaBerge's control. He's a professor that is always willing to help students and ensures that there are a high number of resources outside of class to help students succeed in this class. His management of post-midterm panic was great.

lectures are useless, most of the content taught by TA's in discussion. It's an easy class with easy content, but it's often unclear what we were even learning, what's on the exam, and when stuff was due. Most of class is a group project which was poorly handled. The professors themselves though are nice and approachable and very helpful.
Definitely a great teacher. Pretty lecture heavy but makes it up with Projects that you work on. Very helpful with any questions and is available often outside of class.

Dr. Laberge is an excellent lecturer, and gets straight to the point. Ask questions, he's intent on helping students succeed. Doesn't have a warm personality, but it actually works for him; again, ask questions.
The content of the course is broad (from basic programming to a project) but it actually is a fair workload with good grading.
He's a gem, such a knowledgeable and wonderful guy. Very glad I will see him again in my CMPE education. Lectures can get a little boring, but he is there to help. Go to his office hours.

Lectures were pretty normal, and the grading criteria is clear from the start. As long as put some effort in, you can easily pass and get an A. There's a decent amount of assignments but none of them are really that challenging. Group work is also a big part of the class.

Dr. LaBerge is the best prof you will take at UMBC. cmpe 306 is hard but I've never wanted to make a professor proud so bad. he makes it clear that he really wants you to do well. you can ask the same questions over and over and he will keep explaining without making you feel bad. his office hours are a godsend, don't be afraid to go, he is awesome
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Inspirational--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Dr. Laberge is extremely nice and helpful. If you have any problem you just have to talk to him and he'll make your life a lot easier. It doesn't even have to be about his class and he will still go above and beyond to try and help you. Great person and very knowledgeable. He's not fake, you can tell he really knows his stuff.
Dr. LaBerge was an amazing professor. He was way too advanced for this level class but he brought so much wisdom with him. By far the best ENES101 professor I had.

Supremely knowledgeable and wants to see his students succeed, even if he is stressed/stretched thin at times. Incredibly helpful mentor that has been in industry and wants to help create good engineers. Unlike many profs, he knows there's life outside academia and he teaches toward that. I owe all of my professional knowledge to this man

LaBerge was a good prof, as well as Prof G and Prof Hennigan. The class can seem a bit disorganized at times but they do try to make lectures interesting and relevant to UROS. Learn Matlab early on and make friends with your TA and you'll be fine.

The class was time-consuming, but the grading was very relaxed. If you make any attempt you'll pass. There was a lot of curving/criteria bending which meant a lot of students ended up with As. The class was heavy on MATLAB (pro or con depending on the type of learner you are). Dr. Laberge is very knowledgeable in the material.

Take him for any Engineering class you can. He made ENES seem like it was going to be really hard, the class turned out to be extremely easy. Can't tell you how many lectures I skipped, still got a 102 on the final, which is extremely curved apparently. Would recommend to everyone.
Makes the really boring lectures interesting. Head of computer engineering, and helps us navigate the major. Great teacher, great orator

Such a helpful, understanding, nice, clear teacher. Gives his free time to help students. Tons of extra points available on the test. Textbook problems are helpful for doing the homework, which is counted for participation only. This class is not easy, but Dr. LaBerge will make you feel like you can do it. Take classes with him if you can.
Extremely compassionate and sympathetic. He has no ego which is very rare trait among professors. I feel sorry for future students because rumor is he wasn't be teaching the course in the future.

I went to all the lectures during the year, did the homework, asked questions, and payed attention. Some people can get along fine without attending lecture if they took AP Physics in high school, but otherwise, you're screwed if you skip. Do yourself a favor and earn a good grade on UROS. The people that got less than a B+ didn't apply themselves.

Class was interesting in the beginning, but became less and less organized as time went on. The class was not well managed and the assignments and homework requirements and especially due dates constantly shifted. This may not be specific to the professor, but may just be poor management from the TAs and other professors managing this class.

He teaches all of the hard stuff at the end. Going to lecture in the beginning is not necessary but towards the end you should go. As long as you learn heat transfer, statics, and circuits then you are guaranteed a B on the exam.  You only need the textbook maybe 2 times for homework, if you can get it form someone else doit because it was a waste
The test are not the hardest, they are just very long exams.

LaBerge is probably the best professor I've had at UMBC. He understands that his material is difficult and allows for lots of extra credit on his tests. He really wants people to learn and will change his teaching style to best suit the class. If LaBerge is an option, take him.

He does assume that we know things that we do not actually know but that's what office hours are for. GO to his office hours he loves to help and chat. Go to lectures because on the final there's a bunch of questions about what happened during lecture which are easy points to get. There is no curve but does have point buffers on exams.

Assumes you're already familiar with most of the material. I didn't really learn anything from the lectures, but they're posted online. Assigned really hard homework that I wasn't taught how to do by myself. TAs retaught everything in week before final, which helped a lot. Final was curved a lot. Don't need the textbooks at all.
The class lacked structure and the final is filled with questions on things that were never lectured on. But LaBerge is a great lecturer and an even greater human being.

He is a very good lecturer, makes funny jokes, and explains the information well. Each test is graded out of 100 points but you can earn up to usually 120-130. Do not study prior exams, he switches up problems and you will fail if you memorize solutions. Homework is for completion. A lot of work, but an easy B.

Laberge is awesome. He teaches well, and he is entertaining, too. His exams are long and can be a little difficult, but there's usually 120+ points on it, and you are only graded out of 100. His lectures are mostly clear, and he usually gives good examples. He's also quite approachable and ready to help.

After taking more engineering classes, I figure that so many things that we learn from this class are 100% right. His quizes and hw are really hard. But he curves A LOT. If you can't pass this class with at least a B, just change your major. Harder things are coming later.

Sufficient preparation for the course content? Are you kidding me?  TA’s are useless as were your lectures. You were right about the class being about ambiguity.Realize that this class is a gateway for all engineering majors. I don't recommend this class to anyone and I feel bad for those who do have to take it. Switching my major.

The class was a good introduction to the engineering industry. Lectures were well put together and well communicated. The homeworks and the quizzes proved to be a challenge occasionally, but if you put in the effort (which people have trouble doing these days) then it wasn't so bad. Be prepared to do a lot of MatLab. Overall good instructor!

He is very clear and is always willing to help. The homework and exam was difficult but he curved the final grades in light of this. Very approachable and knowledgeable. He is also pretty funny. Would recommend.

He is very helpful one on one; however, I found the course content and assignments very complicated compared to what we were taught in lecture. Killed my GPA and matlab goes from being simple to extremely complex in the span of a week. The course content jumps around all over the place as well.
Like a grand father

Format of the class was awful. Taught very basic MATLAB at beginning, had a month long stretch where nothing involved MATLAB, then gave out an incredibly challenging MATLAB exam. Content covered in lecture is nowhere near the difficulty of the exams or homework. However, is always available to meet with students and is extremely knowledgable

He is helpful and god at teaching. However, the course was very challenging for an intro level class. Be prepared to do tasks that you are not prepared for. Though, this is good engineering practice it is really a killer on the GPA.

Very good professor, one of the best I've had. He is easy to understand, the lectures are very well prepared, and he definitely knows what he's talking about. I would very much recommend this professor.
He is very fair, very helpful, and lectures are clear and interesting. Definitely, one of the best professors I've ever had.
The course material was confusing at times. But Professor Laberge makes a clear effort have available times for students to seek help and ask lots of questions on confusing concepts.

I learned a lot in the class, but it was really challenging.  The material is tough, but he makes it clear that you can ask him for help during his office hours every day.  He's a nice guy and is very knowledgeable.

He is an awful teacher. I have been taking this class all semester, and he leaves all of the hard assignments until the end. Unfortunately he is our only option for 101. Good luck to whoever has to take him.
One of the better teachers in the CMPE program.  Students complaining about the workload should reconsider an engineering degree.

He is a very good professor. If you can, take him for circuits. He teaches you everything you need to know, and the exams are basically a revision of the homework. If you are having trouble with the class he is extremely approachable during his office hours. He cares that his students succeed, unlike many other professors. Overall one of the best.

He is the terrible at teaching this course!! He expects too much from his students and the exams are reallyyy hard! I'm sure he would be a better upper level professor but he is terrible at this course. HARDEST CLASS EVER! it was his first year teaching this course and the whole class was struggling

I'm sure that LaBerge is a good professor for upper level courses, but he is not very well suited for a freshmen level courses. He expects more than the students are capable of, even the TAs have expressed this. He does keep things interesting at least, but his exams and some homework are ridiculous. He is not a bad prof just isnt suited for course

His exams are the longest and no one had finished the first exam in the allotted class time. To quote him "I'm still trudging through Wednesday's exam and it isn't pretty." He does know the content quite well and is not hard to listen to in fact he is interesting.

Dr. LaBerge IS the best professor at UMBC. Lectures are very well prepared. The homework problems always reflect the lecture concepts. He is very approachable. Tests are challenging, but always reflect the well-stated expectations. His grading system is explicitly defined by well-planned rubrics.

What can I say?  He's one of the best professors at UMBC.  If you have the opportunity, take a class with him.  He is more that fair and genuinely wants all of his students to succeed.  His exams can be a little tough, but he offers a comprehensive note sheet and additional extra credit questions.  His door is always open to discuss the material.

Possibly the best professor I have ever had. He is always prepared and exceptionally interested in student performance. Go talk to him during his plethora of office hours and review sessions; he appreciates student input and likes to know that you are trying to learn.

He is the best engineering professor at UMBC. He has weekly review sessions and you can come to his office hours at almost any hour of the day. The exams are challenging but they have extra credit problems. 29 people got over 100% on the final exam but you will need to study hard to get an A.

He is one of the BEST professors at UMBC. He is very helpful. Just go to his office hours if you are not clear. It'll help you a lot. Exams are not that hard if you do the hws and go to his weekly review sessions. Try to get old exams from people, they are good reviews for the exams. Labs are OK. Highly recommend this professor.

One of the best professors I've had at UMBC. He expects a lot out of his students, but he gives just as much back in additional help and accessibility. His door is almost always open for assistance when he isn't actively lecturing.  The course itself is hard, though the lab work is mostly a waste of time.

Dr. Laberge is my favorite professor in CMPE (so far at least). Extremely accessible and cares that he helps people grasp the concepts. The exams are hard, but the hw is harder and if you do hw and go to review sessions, you should get A's. I got an A w/o using the book. The labs are useless and the reports are a waste of ink, paper, and time.
Great professor.  Very accessible.  He takes a lot of time out to help students understand the material.  Love his grading system.

Exams are really hard and long, He actually has no idea how hard the exams are. To him the exams are completely fair. Averages are in 50's. LEctures are okay, but the class is so boring its hard to pay attention. Labs are useless and reports take too much time. Overall pretty bad class.
Excellent professor! I would highly recommend taking him for vibrations. Makes complicated problems into the simplest ones! Exams are very similar to the class examples and homework problems.
Overall a good professor. Lectures were well prepared and the project was fun.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Lots of homework--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: 10 homeworks (20%), once a week, 2 exams + 1 final (75% total). The grade breakdown sucks but he's a solid professor. he knows his stuff and to me, the lectures made sense. he always tries to go back and clear up confusion. He does seem to get annoyed when students ask the same question. He responds to emails pretty quick.

Dr. Lee is a pretty solid professor. The class is 75% exams but the exams are graded very fairly based on your process of solving. The homework problems are a good gauge for what will be on exams so be sure to practice them plenty. Class feels like a mix of dynamics and Diff-EQ, definitely challenging if you don't put in the work.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Good speaker; kind Professor. Homework and exam content is all covered in lectures and well explained; fairly graded. The first 2/3 of the class is basically MATH225@UMBC (ODEs), but more symbolic. Very easy course; this the `get well' course among the MechEs junior year. I wish there was more content to cover, because he was a very good teacher.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Failed me by .6%

Dr. Lee's class was easy in some ways but not in others. Exams are straightforward, although he doesn't always allocate enough time for them. Homework can be difficult but the TAs were a big help. By biggest gripe with Dr. Lee is that he doesn't really seem to care about his students. He's pretty inflexible.

Dr. Lee is a strict but fair grader. I enjoyed his lectures even though some might've found it boring. Exam was fine as long as you pay attention and study the slides he tells you will be on the exam. NO FINAL. Don't slack off because there is no curve but as long as you do your stuff, there's no reason for anything less than an A or B

If you have friends who previously took this class you will do fine, if not it will be a bit more difficult but very doable. A lot of students will do well and as long as you pay some attention in class and discussion you will do fine. You're pretty much guaranteed to get a B at the least

Does not curve at all. Was less than 0.5% from the A and I got a B. Got points off a presentation for not being enthusiastic enough. When he tells you what will be on the exam, just memorize every lecture slide he says to look at.

Overall he's a good professor. And he pretty much tells you everything that's gonna be on the lecture exam. If you study the slides he mentioned, it shouldn't be too bad. the course load is reasonable. TAs grade things leniently which is a good thing.

This guy's lectures are pretty bad. He reads off of slides (and not very well). Very thick accent so he can be hard to understand too. We don't use any of the things he says in lecture in the class itself so that made studying for the one and only exam very hard to do. ENME 204 is mostly groupwork based so get ready for a big project.
Overall a good professor. The midterm is mostly memorization. However, lectures were well prepared and the project was fun.
Useless lectures. Must memorize slides for exam. He follows a grading rubric but arbitrarily decides how to apportion weights.

I love this guy. It was a cool introduction to campus. Easy class, I wrote my final paper relating to my major, on the Family Guy Theme Song. Very lax, I would come to class just to listen, even if I did not understand all of what he was saying. This is just a FYS class so don't take it too seriously. He's a really sweet guy and likes chemistry.

Sweet elderly professor. Homework seemed optional and he had a gentle grading system for the final essay. It seemed he just wanted students to come in and be present. Would mention the occasional chemistry concept during his lectures. Gave many opportunities for students to come to the board and participate in the conversation. Easy A!

It's no hyperbole when I say he only talks in circles. I'm a heavy notetaker and I struggled to gather anything from his 2-hour anecdotal tangents. Wanted him clarify what the HW was after class, he forced me and another student make small talk for 15 mins til we had to interrupt him. Friendly guy, doesn't get to the point, you will learn nothing.

We are only a few weeks into class and he is already behind on our chapter discussions. Even though this is supposed to be an introduction course, it seems like he expects you to have a certain amount of knowledge about this course. Thankfully as long as you participate in group meetings and do your homework you will receive a good grade

Rabbi Levine is not good at following the syllabus or pacing the class, for example we only made it halfway through the book we were supposed to read in its entirety. He really struggles with technology, causing lots of problems with the only parts of the class that are interactive. Lectures are long, boring, and basically irrelevant to the test.

Professor Levine is a nice man who is willing to work with you. There are only four total grades in the class (including class participation/attendance, 2 essays, and the final) so if you do poorly on one thing it may affect the rest of your grade. Classes are all lecture, and the class is long so it can get tedious. Makes you read passages aloud.

While one of the hardest courses at UMSON, Dr.Legambi is extremely organized and leads a well structured course. Her course structure requires you to prep prior to coming to class, as most of class time focuses on case studies to apply the material. If you do your prework, you are able to follow along and can fill in where you may be unsure!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Not a good professor. The class is not structured well, so succeeding is very difficult.  Had to utilize a lot of online outside resources to prepare.  She is a micro manager who details a ton of things to do, which she says will make you succeed.  Unfortunately, everyone has different learning styles, her style tends to overwhelm and distract.

For the most important class in nursing school and we have the worst professor teaching it. She does not lecture or teach, period. Rather, class time is based on cases study discussions where answers are never really given or given vaguely and with a condescending attitude. Worse, she speaks extremely softly and refuses to get a microphone system.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: She made no changes as she thinks it's appropriate that the average grade in her class be a C. This class is hard enough without her teaching it. She's clearly incredibly knowledgeable but doesn't do relate her wisdom well with students personally.
Glad to be done with the class.

She is highly organized and smart, BUT If majority of the class is failing or testing below expected standards, then re-evaluation of teaching methods needs to be priority. Any solution for redemption during a pandemic is supposedly a "disservice" . PPT's are non- existent and she has told the clinical instructors that no one should get 100.
Horrible lecturer. I barely passed and the exam averages were so low. She even refused to curve like how does that affect her

Legates was better compared to her co instructor Guzman, but was still hard to follow. She focused on concepts while most of the semester was memorization and taught by Guzman. She was also hard to reach and wasn't the most understanding. After the extra credit and post it note “cheat sheet” I ended up with a C. Try to take cell somewhere else.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Horrible attitude. The exam averages were in the 50's and yet she doesn't want to give curves and blames the students for her poorteaching style

she is in fact better than Guzman but the information she presents is an overload. Plus she has a horrible attitude and doesn't respond well to emails. Most disrespectful worst prof out there. If I could give a negative I would

I know a lot of students complained this semester about this course but tbh Dr. LeGates did a great job lecturing. The stuff she emphasized in class was what showed up on the exams. She was also responsive to emails.
Just study it's not that hard maybe you don't like biology

She co-taught with Guzman, but she was the MUCH better professor and lecturer. Her lectures were very manageable and I found to learn a lot from her teaching style. She does not answer any emails though. Exams were still very hard, but the averages went up whenever she taught and gave exams compared to Guzman.

If you have to take a cell, for the love of god don't take it with her OR Guzman. Just delay it by a semester. She has the worst attitude, cant teach for the life of her. UMBC NEEDS TO STOP FORCING THESE "PROFESSORS" TO TEACH LIKE THEY ARE HERE FOR RESEARCH LET EM DO THAT.

final exam is worth 25% of your grade. doesn't know how to teach, exams are from space, content is so hard, and she skips over most slides. to add to all of that the class avergae was in the 50's and she doesn't want to curve
Grading criteria a bit unclear and wasn't as available outside of class.
Very nice professor. Class was definitely hard and lecture heavy. Would take her again.

Very kind professor and you can tell she enjoys teaching. However, the exams are graded very strictly. She says they follow the learning goals, but the tests often feel more detailed than what is emphasized in class. Lectures can sometimes feel a bit scattered, so expect to spend a lot of time reviewing and studying outside of class.
A good teacher with a complex lesson plan
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Don't let the B fool you. Hefty part of the grade is group work. Grading is subjective. Sometimes has an attitude when you ask questions. Unclear rubric. Does not hold class members accountable but their feedback is the same weight as people who do the work. Unclear guidelines. Very specific and subjective in what she wants in an answer
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dynamic professor, fast paced class that covers a lot of interesting material. Detailed exams with MCQ and (long) FRQ, but everything is included under the learning objectives. She uses funny metaphors to make complex topics easier to understand, and posts previous exams to study from. Be prepared to spend a lot of time with the textbook!

Dr. Leupen was AMAZING!!! When it was her turn to teach lab, she explained the background knowledge and lab protocol clearly to ensure everyone was on the same page. Her in-lab quizzes were easy and straight to the point, all you really needed was study the lab protocol objectives and you'd be good to go! Def take her if you have to take this lab!
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Exams had FRQ and MCQs. They were tough but not impossible, and she gives a study guide which contains all concepts on the exams. Groups were assigned at the beginning but they're for discussion, not for grade. Overall amazing and enthusiastic professor... an effective, charismatic teacher who is a fair grader. This was such a fun, rewarding class!
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Test heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Forced groups throughout the entire semester and a large portion of your grade relied on how your group did on their tests which wasnt great. Very unclear when it came to free response, would not take with her

She is one of the best professors I have ever had.  There were no surprises on tests, the learning goals literally tell you exactly what will be on there.  She makes lectures interesting and engaging as you are seated in discussion groups.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: She was very passionate about nutrition. If you go to class everyday you get bonus points added to your lowest exam grade. There its 4 exams which is a lot but they are very straightforward and easy. If you go to class and review before the exams, you will do well.

Dr. Leupen wants you to succeed. All you have to do is follow the goal sheets, ask questions, do the practice questions, and you're guaranteed a B. Attendance isn't mandatory but every class is 0.5 points to your lowest exam score
She is an amazing professor. Class was fairly easy if you follow her goal sheets, and super easy to go to with questions

This is my 3rd course with her. She is seriously the best. It is impossible to not do well if you pay attention, read, and THOROUGHLY complete her study guides. her study guides are the only thing you need to take notes on and study off of. basically no hw except easy diet analysis assignments. this is one of my fave courses I've taken at UMBC.

Dr. Leupen makes things so much more understandable. She really wants you to learn and her enthusiasm about it is makes you want to learn more. The textbook and learning objectives will be your best friend but overall this was an interesting and fairly easy class.

I by far learned the most in the entirety of college from her. Her direction for the course is clear, what you have to know is clear and defined, and as long as you follow the learning objectives and put in a little bit of effort. Boom 10/10. If you have any questions, she is always more than willing to answer and explain questions. Kind and Great
Easily the best biology professor at UMBC. She is so caring and honestly works hard to make class interesting and digestable. 10/10

The reading guides are a life-saver. Using those as I read the textbook and took notes was definitely the best way for me to prepare for the exams. Exams are not too bad if you pay attention in class and actually understand the material. Be prepared to memorize though!
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: I walked away from Dr. Leupen's nutrition class with a ton of useful life information. She was an engaging informative teacher. If you read the book and go to class you will pass the tests. She tests over actual information. I highly recommend this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Professor Leupen has very interesting lectures and she ties everyone one of her lectures back into a relatable way to help the material easier to understand. The iRAT's are easy if you pay attention to her goal sheets. The tests are somewhat difficult but are easier if you study and do the goal sheets. 15/10 would take the class again.

Dr. Leupen was a breath of fresh air during this time of virtual learning. She was able to deliver amazing lectures that made you eager to log onto Blackboard. Her way of teaching easily cleared up any confusion. My only regret was not getting to experience this class in person. You need to study for exams! Thoroughly use the chapter goals.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Easily the BEST professor at UMBC. The exams are basically based off the chapter unit goals, so do those thoroughly. No tricky questions, everything is straightforward. It is a lot of content so manage your time wisely to study. You will learn to succeed in this class, not just learn to pass. 100% recommend!

Easily the best bio professor I had in my college career. Enthusiastic, great at answering questions, available, clear expectations, and gives extremely engaging lectures. She single-handedly restored my faith in biology and gave me a passion for the subject that had been ruthlessly stripped of me in previous bio classes

I liked Leupen as a person. She was amazing and compassionate and kind, especially during a pandemic. But SHE GRADES HARSHLY ON SHORT ANSWER on exams. The exams are multiple choice correct and a lot of free response. You HAVE to do the learning objectives because she pulls her questions straight from there. She really makes you work for your grade.
Such an amazing professor, caring professor. Truly a gem.

Dr. Leupen is one of the best teachers I have had at UMBC. She is energetic, intelligent, and really cares about what she's teaching. She is conscious of a students schedule, and will change her schedule/assignment accordingly. She holds online review sessions where she answers questions. I would definitely take any class she taught. 305L is easy

Took nutrition with her, wasn't interested about the subject at all going in but now it's my favorite class. Hilarious, engaging, and fair grader. Go through the posted goal sheets for each chapter and you'll be golden, though she also has review sessions before exams which are helpful for clarification. Wish I could take her again!

Leupen is one of the best profs I've had at UMBC. Her exams definitely need preparation, but they are fair and cover topics discussed in the book/ class. She cares about her students and is great at explaining topics and offering help outside of class.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: There is a lot of work and the class is group-based. Dr. Leupen is really passionate about what she teachers and makes lecture funny/enjoyable. She truly cares about her students passing and is always willing to help. Her quizzes/exams can be tough but are not too difficult if you do all the learning goals. She is a harsh grader on free response.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: She has a ridiculous method of grading, if only she spent half as much time teaching the material as she did quizzing us maybe the students would actually learn something. When the class average for every quiz and exam is in the 60's to 70's you know there's something wrong with the teaching method and/or grading system of the instructor.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: The version I took was hybrid. Only meet in person once a week. There is a lot of work. Every week you have discussion boards (write and reply), taking notes on the chapter for the in class meeting on Friday. Usually a quiz every week. Quizzes arent that bad just study. But you really do learn a lot in the activities and discussions of class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Hilarious

reviews.comment: She needs to learn how to focus her course material to better fit the class schedule. There were weeks when we had two quizzes and an exam in the same week. Also she shouldn't take criticism to heart, she gets personally offended if you correct her.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Honestly, I'm going against the grain here but she is not the best professor, in fact I wouldn't even list her in my top 10 professors at UMBC. Her lectures are extremely quick paced and we have quizzes before we even discuss the chapters. You are expected to know the material to a high degree without even coming to class, it's ridiculous.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: one of the best. seriously. truly.

Professor Leupen was one of the best I've ever had. I don't generally rate professors but I'm making an exception here. She genuinely cares about students and is very happy to answer questions and explain concepts. She is an excellent teacher and makes all the material super clear. Highly recommend!!

Awesome professor in general. If you ever want to learn about human physiology, this class is probably the most exciting way to do that. Dr. Leupen makes science seem more appealing than any other subject you'd have to take in college. I would take this class over again just cause she's such an amazing lecturer.

She is such a phenomenal professor and I wish I could take more of her classes. She's great at explanations of difficult material. She has great energy and will encourage you to learn. She's super patient with students and will never make you feel as if your question is stupid. She's clear with what she wants you to know on exams/quizzes.

"Good times!" Dr. Leupen is such a great professor! She's enthusiastic and presents tough information in a fun and exciting way so that if you're paying attention and are engaged, your grade will greatly benefit. Reading the textbook and doing the learning goals are essential, and they make tests and quizzes straight forward and relatively easy.
Best teacher I have ever had. She filled the class with energy even at 10 in the morning. Definitely recommend her course.

I had Dr. Leupen for both Biology 101 and Biology 233. She's an amazing professor who makes lecture fun and interesting with her very obvious charisma and passion for the subject. She very clearly outlines test material.  I wish she taught more of the classes i'm required to take because I would love to have her again and again.
She is AWESOME! The group work really helps you remember important concepts, the exams are a little difficult but there are weekly quizzes to help your grade.

Just do her goal sheets, read the chapter and you will be fine! There's a short quiz every week and it's only the italicized goals. Her midterm and final for Bio 101 were all the questions mentioned on the goal sheets.

does not teach material on hw;hw qstns unrelated to test.has disorg.teaching style.slide not helpful and contain error and almost no text.test qstns are very ambiguous and wording can be misleading/confusing.try to force learning thru teamwork.hard grader;lack of part'l credit and little curving to make up for it.use caution if take w/her.

Amazing prof! Leupen has a great teaching style and always keeps students engaged in the classroom. I'd totally recommend her for any class - knows her biology through and through and is able to explain it in a way that students understand. One the best professors I have ever had.  Always willing to answer questions and discuss extra material not covered in the class. I had her for 251 and 251L. Let me just say that I have never been the type to love a class before. She makes class so enjoyable and is completely fair with her exams. You can tell she really cares about her students and wants to help you. Read the goals sheet and you'll be set! No tricks, ever!

Dr. Leupen is a great professor. Definitely one of the best here. She is very passionate about what she does, which makes learning fun and less chore-like. She's a very understanding and realistic professor. I definitely recommend you to take any bio class you can with her.

best professor i have ever had.  she makes class very interesting because she isn't the typical professor who simply reads from powerpoint slides.  she is very helpful in answering any questions you have. i would highly recommend her.. great personality, excellent teaching skills.

Dr. Leupen is by far the best teacher at UMBC. I always thought that Jim Thomas won this category but Dr. Leupen wins by a mile. Dr. Leupen is the Jim Thomas of the Biology department. Dr. Leupen is the BEST teacher I have had at UMBC by far! It is obvious she is passionate about teaching and her students. Her methods are unique, yet they really help you learn. Best teacher I've had in my 4 years at UMBC. So friendly! Class is easy as long as you prepare and read the goal sheets

Prof. Locke is really kind and funny! She gives good feedback and genuinely cares about students. She allows a study guide for her two exams. You will have to work and learn in this class, but she makes it easy and is a good lecturer. She is a great professor to take.

Super sweet professor! We were graded based on three reflections, two exams, and a group project (proposal, pamphlet and presentation). Very understanding when things come up and very willing to provide extensions if needed. I've taken her two semesters in a row and would 100% take her again.
Professor Locke is an amazing teacher. She is engaging and also very kind. She allows a notes sheet during exams to help you.

Danielle Locke is a AWESOME professor! She is very kind and her lectures are very easy to follow. She is always willing to answer questions during lectures and during her office hours. If you are thinking of taking a class with her, I highly recommend her! She's great! (She's also very pretty. 😊)

Professor Locke was an awesome professor. Assignments were super easy and tests are based directly off homework and lectures. Lectures easy to follow and go back and review. She's very nice and accommodating as well.

If I can give him above 5 I would. One of the best profs at UMBC, he is so sweet and funny! Homework isn't too bad. Definitely will recommend him for this class, you won't regret it!!

Professor Lomonaco is very knowledgeable and super nice. reviews.comment: You literally don't need to attend class. Ever. Requires no effort to get an A. Simply do the homework and the exams and you will get 90-100% on every assignment.

Algorithms with lomonaco is a must take if offered. Class is easier than 341 and only has 5 easy hw's and 2 tests with optional final. No projects or any of that either. Just be familliar with Big O, master theorem, heaps and BFS, DFS and you're good for an A.
His lectures were very enjoyable since he has a great personality. He makes mistakes every now and then, but usually fixes them. Assignments/exams aren't terrible.
Very nice professor, Exams are somewhat difficult but, he grades them easily. Go to class and do the homework and you should do well.

Lomonaco is a good professor for 442. Clearly teaches the material without overwhelming students. Tests are straightforward. This is a good class to take as a CS elective as it is taught well and not too stressful. Good to take as a 6th class/ 18th credit. 1 HW dropped and 1 test can be skipped.

Very sweet, caring, and understanding. A bit disorganized at times, but he teaches you everything he wants you to know for homeworks and tests. The concepts are not too easy but if you pay attention, the class is very manageable. And he is great!

He does not make the material harder than it needs to be. Says exactly what will be on tests. Averages two tests in place of final if you want. Always explains things in detail (sometimes ad-nauseum, but you definitely understand it in the end). Overall a nice, approachable guy and a good teacher.

I really like Dr. Lomonaco. He does make mistakes fairly often, and his sense of humor is definitely different. Nevertheless, his funny not-so-funny jokes do make lecture more interesting, and he does a decent good job explaining topics. I would take him again if I needed to repeat the course!

Dr. Lomonaco makes lectures more interesting by making jokes every once in a while. Lectures can get confusing because he makes a lot of mistakes, but as long as you do the homework it's an easy class. Pretty lenient grader on exams (if a T/F question is worth 3 points, he just deducted 1 if you got it wrong) and drops the lowest 2 homework grades.

He is terrible, condescending & makes too many mistakes. In class he tends to make many mistakes and then says he did them on purpose. Class is very easy compared to the other 203 professors     His Exams are straight to the point nothing to confuse or trick and gives partial credit for attempting problems

This was my second time taking cmsc 203 and I believe Lomonaco is one of the better 203 professors at umbc! Homework and exams are really straightforward with only one proof for an exam written the whole semester. Lomonaco is also always willing to help on homework. Very easy class if you know somebody who has taken the class before.

He give out a homework from the book almost every week. The final is optional, if you choose not to take it, your grade will be the average of Exam 1, Exam 2, and homework. He reuse question on previous Exam.

Dr. Lomonaco has a strange sense of humor, but that's what I love about the guy. Not really sure what to say. He's a nice person, but he can be confusing at times because he makes tons of little mistakes. He is pretty stingy with points and regrading, but the class isn't hard. He does talk about the history of mathematics at times which I enjoyed.

Lectures were clear cut, and many examples reviewed in class showed up on the exams. This is an easy class to pass if you pay attention, and complete the homework assignments. Great professor!
Outstanding

material than what would probably be covered otherwise.Which personally I like better than teachers who don't spend enough time on stuff and just satisfy whats listed on the syllabus.If you have to take any of the more math heavy courses crypto, algorithms, information theory  etc.and Lamonaco is teaching he is a MUST TAKE period.

easy lecturer, wont try to trick you with hard questions AT ALL, do the HW and u can tackle the tests easily, though tends to deduct grades sometimes for really no reason, and he is stubborn wont give the grade back, and you gotta be carefull, makes mistakes during his lecture tooo often
He goes completely off topic many time and spend more than half of class time with it. By the end of semester I realize that I wasted time and money by taking his class.

He don't know how to teach!!! No power-point and makes a lots of mistakes while writing on the board!! His exams are completely off tangent then what he teaches in the class!!! I would not recommend this professor...
Not a great professor!!! Can't tech this class!!! His Teaching style is worst and made lots of mistakes. Exams are not what he taught in the class!!! I would not recommend this professor....

supposed to be one of the hardest courses for comp sci..but this class was the opposite...if this guy teaches this class or any other..take it..weekly homeworks, 3* exams

He's a friendly professor and usually pretty good at explaining things. He is a very nice teacher and is good at explaining. He loves it if you ask questions and doesn't mind slowing down. His test are not that hard but you have to study. The final exam is optional. Dr. Lomonaco is Amazing! He reviews every class. If you go to his office hours he really helps, you can ask questions in class(he loves that). Homework for the most part isn't that hard, he wants you to understand the material and get 100%. I recommend him for any course.

One of the most boring classes I've sat through. He can go on for hours because he's so interested in the topic. I felt like that class was 5 hours long. I like his grading system. You can either average the 3 exams and thats your grade or you can take the final and average 4 exams. HW boosts grade up too.

Very knowledgable.  Can sometimes talk over students heads, but just ask him to clarify and he will.  Homeworks can be difficult, tests are very simplified versions of the homeworks.  They test basic knowledge to see if you understand the concepts he is teaching.  If you have an A in the class before the final, you don't have to take the final.

Took him in the Fall of '24. I enjoyed his class! Very reading heavy, so make sure to read them before class. Most of the class was us teaching each other; divided into groups and they led discussions about the readings, along with two papers and a project. Participate as much as you can. It's very straightforward and he is a good lecturer.

reviews.comment: Professor Loviglio is truly exceptional! His classes are incredibly engaging, filled with insightful tangents and dad jokes. It is evident that he genuinely cares about the success of every student. He gives excellent feedback on essays and is flexible to meet outside of class for extra help. If you participate, you will have an amazing experience.

Loviglio is a very funny and understanding professor. If you're passionate about media and its connection to modern issues, you'll really enjoy this class. If you do the readings and at least listen to the class discussions, as well as do the assignments, you should be fine.

Loviglio is the most fresh and funky prof out there. Every class is a trip and if you put in the effort, you can get so much from this class. 333 w loviglio made my mcs major worthwhile. He's super passionate about media theory and genuinely cares about his students. make sure you do the readings they're actually really interesting

This guy only talks the entire class. You sit in a circle everyday and talk about random crap that doesnt even relate to the topics. I only took this class because its part of my major but this guy is horrible. He brings his political views into the classroom far too much and grades on a very difficult level. He hates athletes too so good luck.

Dr. Loviglio is an amazing professor who truly loves his job. He is ALWAYS there if you need to discuss anything with him, he sincerely wants to see his students succeed and it shows in how he runs his classes. You need to read and put effort into the projects, but do that and the class is a cinch.

Dr. Loviglio is an awesome professor, very funny and just a nice person to be around. His lectures tend to only scratch the surface of the topics however if you go to office hours he will further explain the topics. Also, he'll talk about non-class stuff too. So if you're considering taking his class TAKE IT!  FYI MCS101 is project based!

This guy is amazing. Loves what he teaches and can explain media communication to anyone. He's very humorous, you don't feel like you're going to class. He puts on a show everytime and gets everyone to participate.

What a fun professor! Very friendly, in-touch, and approachable. The discussions are fun, so be sure to stay engaged with those. No tests, but frequent activities that were really pretty easy. If you keep up with the activities, it's an easy A and you;ll even have a fun time! Always looked forward to class. Great professor to know.

As far as engaging, passionate, and fair college professors go Loviglio is easily the best I've had at UMBC. He's fair to everyone, but participate in class and put some effort in and he'll go out of his way to help you out. He grades a bit hard but so do all good teachers. Make sure you do the readings, they're all interesting too.

This man is truly a joy to have for a teacher. Hes funny, his lectures are amazing and I really felt like I grasped the material due to his teaching methods. Had I not have slacked off this class would have been the EASIEST A anyone could get.

This class is discussion based; he'll come into class with a topic to teach and a point to make, and reach it through class discussion. So, participation  brownie points. No tests, just papers and media-production projects over the semester. Really fun, engaging, interesting teacher. Knows his history and his pop culture. Funny and informed.

Looked forward to his class. Really gets you thinking critically about relevant information in the news. Very approachable and really cares about his students. Has a great sense of humor, hope to take him again!

Awesome professor/guy, stupid humor but hilarious - will make you laugh. in touch with pop culture & other technologies. Challenges your ideas, makes you think. No attendance but randomly gives in-class writings which are brief summary's of the readings. MUST DO THE READINGS! Very easy tho, actually enjoyed/looked forward to attending class.

Great professor. I'd taken the course based on great reviews about him. I really did enjoy it and learned alot. He is a great guy outside of the class as well. I definitely see myself staying in touch with him for insight later on in my academic career. Grand experience. I would recommend the course to anyone.

He wasn't anything special. He makes you think, but he expects you to think what he tells you to think.  If you love hearing other peoples opinions, take his class.  if you like to think for yourself,  maybe not.

great guy! this class with really make you re-evaluate how you think in regards to the media, and participation is easy. he makes you want to get involved and will inspire you with his wealth of knowledge.

Lovigliio is a funny guy- but WOO he is a liberal! Sometimes he takes half the class to spout off his political opinions. He assigns a ton of work, but grades fairly easy. If you don't like listening to someone's political diatribe every class, this is not for you!Oh, and be prepared for three 10 page papers.

Pop Culture is one of the best classes offered @UMBC. He makes you think about everyday life in a totally new way. Be forewarned- this class is tough! Thinking about life in a new way is not easy, but it's worth it.
What can I say one of the greatest teachers and mentors!
No Comments

One of the best professors in American Studies!  He really makes you think during class and he doesn't hand you the answers.  This makes for some really good learning experiences.  Take any of his classes if you get a chance, especially Media Studies!

very hard, writing-intensive class!  the final paper is exhausting and hard and he isn't always clear about his grading for it or the abstract.  take his class with caution, but he is an excellent, witty professor-- just a bit on the tough side.

great guy, great class-- wonderful, approachable, and caring teacher.  he really puts things into perspective!  be careful about grades though, the BIG paper is a huge pain and he is a real stickler on it.  come to class and youll WANT to participate!

Dr.Loviglio is very nice and very passionate about the subject.  There's a lot of reading and in class discussions and if you can follow his thoughts it will be a piece of cake.  He's very smart and very friendly.

I took this class as my senior seminar on comic books and American culture during WWII.  He was very approachable and helpful and did everything he could to make sure I got the most out of it as possible!  GREAT, great guy!  Lots of hard, hard work, but worth it-- I learned a ton!

BEST class I've taken.He's very articulate and eloquent.Grades are based on participation and papers.Papers are easy if you take the time to really think about them-you can't pound it out the night before and expect to get a good grade.Very fair grader.

He doesn't hand our prompts til right before the papers are due, and then the day before, he tells you what it is he wants on them. He's not very organized and his papers are extremely hard. I changed my major b/c of how much I hated him and this class
He's a great teacher.  If you read the assignments and write the papers you'll be fine.
Interesting and witty, his classes allow for a lot of student input

I am an aging minor, so to me the class was wonderful. Make sure you read, and try to connect the book to real world situations. The more notes you take, the better off youll be for finals. The lectures arent hard in the slightest.

I have very rarely felt so vindictive towards an individual. The lectures are fine honestly, it is not relevant to the issue at hand which is: she sucks at asking questions and grading them. Professor is caring and will give extension if asked. Great updates for class and cares about the content she teaches. W class

You will be fine as long as you communicate with her, read the textbook, attend class, and be thorough with the grading rubric she provides for assignments. If you can understand what she expects off of you, you should get an A.

Dr. Murray is one of the nicest professors i've had! She is a bit of a tough grader, and there is not a ton of writing for this being a writing intensive class. Most of the information is straight forward and easy to understand. Highly recommend this class if you need a writing intensive credit!
