Great Prof. Would def take again. The class is super easy if you do the work especially the readings. But you could probably get away with not doing them if you come to class but its strongly recommended. Meghan is super cool and down to Earth, explains things so well and is super relatable.
Just a good teacher and a better person

Meghan is a greater professor especially for a first time professor. She gives great feedback on essays and writing assignments. She's not a harsh grader, but she does provide personalized feedback. She's very accommodating when it comes to external factors. She was overall very sweet and she was passionate about what she was teaching!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Prof Lupoli keeps the class engaging with hands-on demos and a good sense of humor. Homework and projects require solid Python skills, but Unstuck study is a great study aid. Definitely worth taking if you're up for the challenge.

He is the best CMSC professor I've ever had. He makes lectures worth going to and breaks concepts down so well. The tests are hard but they are not written by him so just try to study the concepts as much as possible. Lectures are very useful for exams. Take his class because the entire upper level cmsc prof department is cooked.

Do not take him for 331. Prerecorded recycled lectures, group labs every week on things not covered in lectures, Misspelled his own name on multiple documents as well as numerous syntax errors, and the final project/exam was a out of nowhere advanced java crash course that left the whole class failing with an overall curve, never responds even once

Shawn Lupoli is the last guy you want to be stuck with on an elevator. His final exam was an absolute curveball for no reason and screwed over the grades of many students with borderline grades. And he will straight up not answer emails ever. you learn nothing of value in his class, take literally anyone else.

He gives solid lectures on topics and I personally liked the way he explained comp sci concepts (physical demonstrations), he has a sense of humor and lightens up the class by engaging with students, the homeworks and labs are very standard and well organized, projects can be confusing at times but theres plenty of ppl thatll help u in the discord

Most of the work was a timed weekly group lab. We found it difficult to complete them within the time limit. Tests were in class and written, not a great choice for a coding class. Final project was completely nonsensical. I didn't find it hard, but I have prior experience. This would be very rough for someone who was learning from scratch.

Lupoli is not a good 331 Professor. The class was asynchronous, with poor recycled lectures from Texas A&M. He was hard to reach outside of class as he all but quit responding to emails after the midterm. The final project had vague instructions and the code provided was in c++. Midterm had an average below 50. Labs give you barely enough time.

I am Lupoli's biggest fan. This class was so fun and well-taught and I honestly have 0 complaints. If you are taking CMSC201, do everything you can to take it with Lupoli. His lectures are super engaging and enjoyable and as long as you pay attention and turn things in on time, this class is very easy. 5 stars.

If u take 331 be prepared to have 40% of your total grade in the hands of your lab partners. All labs in this class is with a group which can heavily impact your lab score when 1 or 2 of your members don't understand the material. Midterm was on some subjects not covered and the avg was below 50% with Lupoli refusing to curve. Take with anyone else

Asynchronous class, he contradicts himself constantly in both labs and tests. His midterm had an average grade of ~50% due to him giving questions that were not gone over in class, as well as not giving adequate time to finish said questions. Most of his actual work is labs, and it's often a 50/50 on whether his weekly lab matches the material.
Great lecturer, and in a fully coordinated course, this is the only thing that really matters.

Took him over the summer. Lectures were async and decent. But in office hours, the guy could be pretty rude and condescending. He also didn't respond to my emails on two separate occasions. Exams were okay. Projects were fine, but the third one was a doozy. Also the first couple of homework assignments were kinda BS. All around a pretty meh class.

Lupoli expects way too much from his students. Excessively large assignments, especially group labs, are impossible to complete on time. Be prepared to learn Java to a greater degree than you already understand C++.

I am not a cmsc major, so I struggled a bit with this class. Lupoli is funny and interacts with the students during lecture, but he seems intimidating to approach for help. He seems to be more willing to help the students who have experience in coding. People like me were left to fend for ourselves. Also this class is 100% planning. Use time wisely
Prof. Lupoli slaps. Very entertaining and hands on with the course material. I've heard he sucks to work under and is bad w responding emails, but aside from that, you won't go wrong.
A nice guy who knows what he is talking about!

I had a great time in lecture with Professor Lupoli! He was entertaining to keep our attention in lecture and generally make it all worthwhile! Although his lectures are mandatory by having it affecting our grades, it should be mentioned that you need to attend to know what's going on. HW and projects will go in DEEP with Python basics, beware!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Prof. Lupoli is a great lecturer who utilizes humor to keep the class engaged and attentive. Notes are documented online, but expect to spend a lot of time working and coding in this class. Class has clear grading criteria so you know what you need to work for. Be prepared to reach out to TA's for help since you'll have to talk to them a lot.

He is not a good teacher, never reply back to email, often times rude if you meet his office hours. This class was online but the lab and hw was in person. Lab's are fine, if you are lucky with a good TA. Class will not help you with HW and Projects, you need to have basic python knowledge to pass. The class could be better if prof were helpful.

He is almost inaccessible with emails and if he does respond he is very rude. Even when i had covid and was extremely sick he had no sympathy. He doesnt have alot of coding skill and cannot help you with any questionable in class. Overall stay away from this professor and his lectures are terrible.

This was my first computer science class, and I would go to him for help to make sure I was understanding things. He told me that if I didn't understand certain concepts, then I would have even more difficulty with the major in the future. Very discouraging. I now work as a software engineer, so don't let his discouragement stick.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Lupoli is really fun and cares about his students. His lecturers are engaging and tests are not bad at all. He is very organized with this course EXCEPT the projects. Watch out for these and do not procrastinate! You have to work for your A but it is achievable. Watch out for projects and don't procrastinate! GET HELP!

You will learn a lot from him, he teaches you how real life works, the way is bitter but the aftertaste is surprise. Students who hate him because they lose faith on themselves, yes his classes can destroy you in the middle of the semester but making a comeback is highly possible. He is a professor who would offer as much knowledge as he can.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: He'll try to give assignments in more 8 languages (Even he can't code in all those lang). There'll be flipped labs which holds majority points of the final grade. 2 projects and 2 exams (all coding). Prof and students will learn together all those languages and students would get graded harshly.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: Class assignments are flipped labs, which are usually ok except his videos are very unclear and if  you ask him questions about it, he will talk down to you. Grades are based off of being able to do group work based on these videos and two group projects, which very little to no guidance is offered. The final exam expectations were too high.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Lupoli never taught in my class -- it is all on the students to watch unclear videos at home to learn the material. If you ask him a question, he just talks down to you. Grades are based off of two group projects which he offers no guidance for, and the final exam expectations were ridiculous. Worst comp sci professor I have had at UMBC.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: You will hate him, hes a super narcissistic person.  At first you may think hes kinda funny, but after a few weeks you'll grow to just hate the man.  But he teaches the course pretty well, I definitely felt like lectures were helpful.  Worth taking for sure, but don't expect to like him...

Mr. Lupoli is honestly one of the best professors I've ever had. The material he teaches in 331 is the whole reason I got an internship. His notes are great and the project was super helpful in learning web development. Take a class with him and you won't regret it. He makes it difficult, but in the end you learn a lot.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Awful, always returns papers late, often loses things and is late for class. Will not hear any opinion other than his own so close to tenure. Teaches the same recycled material every semester with his youtube videos and exactly identical "flipped labs", "projects", and exams. Does not respond to emails, don't take his classes, there's many others.
reviews.rating_tags: GRADED BY FEW THINGS--GROUP PROJECTS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Pay attention and participate and he'll quickly learn your name and be very willing to help you. Class attendance is a must if you want a good grade, but he makes lectures interesting and provides good visualizations for difficult conceptions. He hates tardiness so don't show up late consistently.
I won't recommend anyone to take course with him, he's the worst professor you could find and you won't learn anything from him and they way he grade is awful.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: This class is basically a web development course. You learn HTML, CSS, PHP, SQL, Javascript and Bash. Every class is a graded lab based on the reading, with an online quiz. You will be in a group for labs and 2 group projects. It can be a lot of work to keep up with, but you learn a lot and it's good for your resume. Grading is lenient in the end.

341 is tough no matter what, but Lupoli made it bearable. May seem harsh sometimes, but that's just his sense of humor. Don't be afraid to go to his office hours if you don't understand something - he's actually really nice and helpful. Projects are time consuming, but not too bad if you pay attention in class and use Piazza.

Best CS professor at UMBC. Not easy, but fair. You will know your stuff after a class with Lupoli, that is if you put in the effort. Better yet, the stuff you will know actually matters and will get you hired because of it. Tests are hard, study for them.
Very unclear assignments that did not match the material we were being taught.

Good guy. I've had him for 3 classes. You'll have to do work, but nothing too difficult. He makes mistakes and sometimes his TAs mess up but I still recommend taking a class with him. Makes jokes; don't take it personally. What I've gained from his classes has helped me land a solid internship.

Lupoli is a tough teacher that can come off as a bit rude but he actually cares about the material and structures his classes so that you LEARN. I have landed a great internship based solely off of the database material he taught in CMSC 331 and have done well on interviews because of the material he covered in CMSC 341. I would take his class.

I thoroughly enjoyed Mr. Lupoli's humor in class and I think he is a great lecture-er. Class was tough but I sure learned a lot. His exams are fair to what he asks of you to study. His final was really hard but I got a 99, and he gives a lot of partial credit as long as you explained the process. I love a teacher that you can sass back!

331 with Lupoli is very, very hard. The in-class labs are hard to complete, and a great portion of the grade hinges on it. The project during my semester was to develop a webstite for advising scheduling using php and html, which we were expected to learn on our own. Very stressful semester, barely got a B. 331 is supposed to be easier imo.

My favorite thing about Mr. Lupoli is that he actually cared about our success; he would be hard on us to make us better. When I submitted a project that I know I didn't do well on, it felt like I was really letting him down, and it made me want to do better. Do be aware that he does poke fun sometimes, and just don't take it personally.

Amazing lectures, he provides lots of notes, and is genuinely interested in our well being. he takes time to help us and when there's a problem. it was easy to resolve grading issues. better read the book; his lectures cleared up everything that was unclear, and he did this intentionally. i learned a lot

He was the course coordinator for the class I took with a different instructor. Managed to screw up something on every project and changedclarified 3-4 times per project. Comes across as arrogant and grading can sometimes be suspect.

Lupoli clearly is interested in and understands the course material, but sometimes has trouble conveying it to students. His lectures were pretty entertaining, but projects were a nightmare- the descriptions would change while we were supposed to be working on them, because students had to point out that requirements did not make sense.

Lupoli is overall an awesome person; listen in his lectures, and MAKE SURE to ask him questions. He has an interesting sense of humor (dry and slapstick), so beware if you are a sensitive soul, because he likes to poke fun harmlessly.

He was Rude. The lectures are helpful but he doesn't even go over the slides and expects you to know them already. Doesn't respond to emails. His TA's were really helpful and nice. Some people find him funny but I thought he was really rude and he liked insulting people a lot. Gets really angry if you're even a second late to class.

Good professor overall, manages to keep lectures entertaining with a blunt humor style(which some might take offense to but I found it funny). I already had plenty of experience with Python so I mostly showed up for the tidbits/tricks that might appear on the tests(2 worth 50% of your grade programming class!) and he covered those well.

Lupoli has that "football coach" vibe to him, however he is not intimidating. He cares for his students, is well-prepared, and is a great choice if you have to take 201. Class is easy with prior programming experience, difficult without it. CMSC201 is work, and that is unavoidable, regardless of professor. I am glad that I took 201 with Lupoli.

His notes are worthless, he talks to you as if you are a window licking mouth breather; very condescending. 2 exams, 2 projects. If you really want to learn basics of coding, take it with some one more competent and professional.

Hard class.  His notes were not easy to read... However I did have very minimal programming knowledge.  The only students that knew seemed to know what was going on were the students who were  experienced.

May have had a sufficient understanding of java and Data Structures, but failed to demonstrate so. Loopy Lecturer: Notes that he wrote himself give you the impression that he rarely programs professionally. Data structures is too important a class. Don't take it with him. That said: Nice guy, Very approachable, funny.
Good guy, very helpful and understanding in person. Gives interesting lectures, but they sometimes lack context and the class can be hard to follow for someone with no programming experience.
Good teacher, somewhat rude. Taught half the material in the last two classes of the semester(searching and sorting).

Can be loud and rude, but really knows how to get your attention, unlike Sadeghian and Radka. Means well and really wants to help you. Homeworks and exams are the same for all sections and are challenging. Be careful on the midterm, full of trick questions and the average grade was a 70.

Great professor!!! Uses his voice to keep the class engaged, which is a good thing! My only critique is the projects. He assigned a super long project at the end of semester which was overwhelming with other classes consistent with engineering majors.
Really enjoyed having Mr. Lupoli as a professor.

I never got the sense that Lupoli really knew what he was talking about. When I asked him questions about Python features he would rarely know the answer. He also really doesn't take criticism well. I pointed out an issue, and he went berzerk. Crappy professor, but the assignments are pretty easy, they've been the same for years.

I think the reason people who have a problem with Mr.Lupoli on this site is mainly because they do not show up. He explains everything very clearly, and if you ask him to, he will even further explain. He obviously cares about what he is teaching and does his best to incorporate visuals and examples to help us learn.
He's really good at explaining things.
Attend class for the criteria to do the codes homework and for specific cases of code that will help for midterm. Class is easier if you have previous coding experience.
Very good at keeping the lecture interesting. Helpful when you have questions. This class would be challenging if you have no prior coding experience.
He yells instead of teaching but can explain things clearly sometimes
He tends to yell a lot, but he tries his best to make the subject matter clear.  Don't be offended when he comes up with a nickname for you.

The class is relatively easy if you have had programming experience. If you have not you really need to pay attention and study to stay ahead. The class moves through topics quickly. He can be intimidating but don't act like an idiot and you'll be fine.
Great professor! Great guy definitely would take this class again!!!!!

Good professor with a great sense of humor and a good attitude. Wants to see his students succeed. Assignments are challenging (especially if you don't have prior programming experience), but help after class is available on weekdays.

A lot of students think he is rude. They are pretty lame. He is funny and makes Computer Science interesting every day even though I already know a lot about Python. Plus, why the hell are people using Python 3 instead of Python 2.7.
Lupoli explains things really well. He's pretty funny. You have to put the work in and do things like he asks you too and you'll be fine.
Great professor, never a dull moment in class.  Only real complaint is he can sometimes move too quickly, or be unclear at times.  Carries my complete recommendation.
Has anyone ever been so far as to decide if not?

This is a tough class, it's meant to weed students out of the CMSC and Engineering majors. But Lupoli makes the class really easy to understand. I hardly used the textbook because his notes are so good that I just didn't need it. He's always at office hours and answers emails quickly. There are even periods in class for "Dumb Questions Answered."
Overall my favorite professor, very funny and engaging and makes the topic fun to learn. If you pay attention in lecture you should do fine in the class.

posts on blackboard whole semester's notes. happy to explain anything when needed but very sarcastic behavior, to the point it's a bit rude. How assignments are graded is mysterious and often changed by what is said in class rather then the posted rubric in the beginning of the semester

Very engaging and pretty funny in class. Can get mean if disrespected, but genuinely cares about his students and their grades. Teaches in a way that the material can be learned even by beginners (such as myself) in a successful way. Tricky midterm and final
I feel the professor did a fine job.  I would not mind having this professor for higher level CMSC courses.

Great guy. His dyslexia strikes often but it is comical. Didn't think class was that helpful but homeworks and projects are very helpful. Attention to detail is key in this class. Only points off for me were detail oriented stuff.
Easy class
very intimidating, seems unfriendly, but very good at what he does
Very rude individual.  Does not respond to emails.

Good guy.  Okay Professor. He was often unclear about what was expected.  Quizzes would regularly have material that was not covered.  Overall, though, quite knowledgeable.  Would probably recommend, but would advise you to pay close attention and ask for clarification regularly.
Great guy!

Horrible professor!  Notes were hard to follow & so colorful that they prevented me from understanding the material.  I bombed the 1st midterm cuz he asked minute details on it (e.g. 4 Qs about random #s, a topic barely discussed in class).  Homework grading was redic.  No rubric given in advance.  Wouldn't give my roommate (who did well) a rec.

Shady grading, forgot about the extra credits he promised earlier, forgets everything, but funny and engages everyone, motivated and motivating , nice person, tests and quizes just made no sense, lost me a lot of points, projects extremely helpful, wants you to have fun, not a good grader

He knows a lot about computer science, and the course is well designed. HOWEVER, he's a very rude individual, rarely responds to an email in less than a week, and there is no better way to describe his grading other than "sketchy". Nobody likes taking exams on blackboard either...not the worst prof in the world, but there’s better ones out there.

I learned ALOT in this class, but it was ALOT of work (most work I have ever done for a computer science course...and I took a few upper level ones). There is ALOT to learn here, especially with Mr. Lupoli, but beware the workload follows. Also his grading is VERY shady...I still have not received points back on a few midterm questions.

I thought it was a pretty interesting class, but I felt we could have learned more in class about the programming languages used for projects. But he is fairly helpful at most of the languages he knows.
Lectures were very well prepared. Classes consisted of interactive labs that were very hands-on. Receptive of student input/criticism. Very forgetful, must remind him to update grades constantly.

One of the better instructors I've had at UMBC. Not because he's a great lecturer, it's just the way the class is designed. I've learned more in this class than any other class I've taken. You'll do A LOT of work, especially on projects, but it's not hard. Just be prepared to spend a lot of time on assignments. Totes worth taking his class.

Directions on projects and homework can sometimes be a little ambiguous.Great Personality, and very engaging teacher, does great inclass examples, flipped class quizzes had some ambiguous answers, or answers that weren't discusses fully in the video lectures. Overall, a fun professor who is committed to teaching and being engaging.

Great guy, but average professor. Skimmed over word documents without really clarifying or explaining material. Homeworks were challenging, but doable. Final project was a nightmare just because of the time constraints and learning a new language. Tests were alright...the first test he used student submitted questions, but it was tough.

I had him for 104 and 201 in concurrent semesters. Got As in both classes. His class isn't easy, and he expects you to put in the work. That being said, he is so helpful, especially in office hours and you can tell (despite the snarkiness) that he really cares for his students. Great teacher.

While he seems to be a great guy (though a bit snarky at people), this class was a major pain. Slides are only mildly helpful and what we were supposed to study for the midterm and final was completely unclear. The projects asked for too much, with no guidance but Google. Time was also a major factor for the second project, in a bad way.

If you go to him he helps you a lot. Very understandable, likes to make fun of his students. The class was tough, and I worked very hard for my A, but at the end of it I really learned, and it makes all other computer classes a cakewalk.

Great Guy. Great Teacher. GO TO HIS OFFICE HOURS AND FORM A RELATIONSHIP!!! Very important!! Lectures are informative and helpful!! Homeworks aren't bad and labs are posted prior to sessions and students can do them prior! Take advantage and definitely take his class!

He was a cool teacher for 104 but his class was difficult. It is an intro to comp sci class, and on the first day he told us that if you have no experience you should be in the class. DO NOT take the class if you have no prior experience because you will be lost
New but good professor who knows the material. Always available for questions. Lectures are funny and exams are based on material covered in class

The entire class is online using Pearson Software. Would not recommend this professor if you are trying to retain the information taught in this course. The homework and even tests just feel like busy work with the way it is assigned.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The entire course is outlined on the syllabus, and she only meets once a week. Overall not a stressful professor, but not necessarily as engaging.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I'll update at the end of the semester but I was really disappointed with the way this class is set up. Maybe it was because we have her once a week(lectures are optional), but she really just throws assignments at us and relies on the book to teach us. Doesn't give us much time for exams. If you have the option take this class 3x a week.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: The Hw is a pretty good indicator of what will be on the test.

Professor Brown only does hybrid classes now, so all the HW is on Pearson which can take hours to complete. Her lectures are precorded and are posted on BlackBoard. The exams are in person but they are similar to the HW questions on Pearson. Had her for ECON121/122, shes great. She's a short little lady, very caring and hilarious.

Great professor that really knows her stuff. Make sure you read the book before class and it will help you a lot. Exams are all online but don't be tempted to cheat, otherwise all the definitions, formulas, and concepts will catch up to you for the final exam. (You need a 50% or higher on the final to pass the class and is still worth a lot).
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: Prof. Brown is a very smart and caring lady, and her accomplishments speak for themselves. She does not give any extra credit however, and the midterms are all on the Pearson lab which can be difficult, and come at bad times. She does move pretty quickly during lecture, so you may get out early. Overall, she is a good professor, but subject is dry

This teacher is the best one you will ever have on French Im not even kidding she will always make sure you understand and will drop your lowest test grade, but you cant use phones in class that's a no, but please take her, you will understand the class and have a good time

Mme. Nelson is very nice and knowledgeable. For the most part you actually learn French from the homework and reinforce the vocab and grammar in lecture. you must participate in class but is very forgiving so as long as you try she will appreciate your participation. Also forgiving on accents, so mostly graded on written french.

Personally, I was frustrated beyond belief with her. She took ages to answer emails, and docked points over incredibly small mistakes. I felt like I would have learned more if I had simply gone through the textbook and done the Portails homework on my own, without her lectures at all. She had an attitude towards students sometimes, too.

Mme Nelson is a nice French teacher. She is caring, interactive, and wants you to learn! Truly! She enjoys learning about her students and desires that everyone participates, and also, she checks in with all her students! She genuinely is worried about how every student performs in her class, but she doesn't like disrespect! Please TEACH 201 Prof!

Professor Nelson is extremely caring, patient, and concerned that you do well. No tolerance for cell phones in class, you have to be paying attention, but I can understand that. An easy A if you do the homework and study for a few minutes each week.
Great teacher, great class, my only complaint is that the online homeworks are often glitchy and there are too many of them but she is very understanding

She can be really mean during critiques. It comes across like she's taking everything that students don't do to her specifications as a personal attack. I can't imagine that that's how she intends it, but it can get hurtful when she's directing it at senior projects.

Worst professor at UMBC.  Teaches subject matter she has no knowledge or skill set of.  Uses the term "conceptual" not in its intended form, but more an excuse to justify bad teaching skills.  Single handedly ruing UMBC photo program.  If you want to learn art/photography, I would avoid her.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Lynn is a great professor! She knows what she's talking about, gives great feedback, and expects you to know what you're talking about with you photos. Critiques are always thought-provoking and interesting with Lynn. She's an awesome person and a awesome professor!

Assignments are easy to accomplish if you have taken a previous photo class or just enjoy taking photos in your free time. Projects are not that time consuming (unlike ART 210) and are enjoyable. Only five projects throughout the semester. Requires reading but then gives lecture on what is read so doing the reading isn't necessary.

AVOID THIS CLASS! No matter the teacher! Installation is a waist of time! It is not art, it is a waist of everyones time and energy! Poor Lynn had to put up with teaching this class she means well and tries her hardest to get the class interested but honestly everyone hates this class and its shouldn't be mandatory! Lynn can be boring but is nice

Class is fun and easy but you spend a lot of time coming up with creative concepts and using the dark room. You will get cancer if you are a photography major because you inhale a lo of fumes. The teacher is nice and willing to help--- but please do expect to spend 4-5 hours at a time in one day in the dark room.

I loved this professor. I think she was a grad student? (very young and nice) Nice sense of humour; I learned a lot about manual photography. We also used the computer which for me was the fun part. 4 projects, 1 paper, participation points, many opportunities to redo work and extra credit. Overall I enjoyed this class!

I have had Lynn for multiple classes. Her teaching style is pretty much the same across all disciplines. If you show that you are trying and you don't goof off in class you will get an A. She gives really good feedback without criticizing you. While her classes are not hard, she can tell when you come to her class ill prepared.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Lynn's focus is usually in vocal and movement, so it was kind of strange having her for an Acting-based class, but I still learned a great deal of stuff with her. She introduced us to breathing techniques and given circumstances and their give and take for each other.

She is good at teaching how to use your voice, but horrible at instilling mechanical acting in her students.  Take the healthy habits she teaches and ignore the rest.  Get the rest of your acting skills from the actual acting teachers.  They on the other hand are excellent.
In terms of an acting class these were the best I ever had.  She is clear and upfront with what you need to do in order to do well.  As an actor I grew a great deal with the work in these classes.

If it's one thing about Lynn, she will tell it to you like it is.  If you suck, she'll tell you.  If you're good, she won't lie.  Practice and give it your all.  The only downside to her is that ultimately you're going to have to give her what she wants instead of what you want.  Overall she knows her stuff though.
Great course.  If you do what you are asked and practice you will do fine.

What a wretched teacher.  So unclear, so unhelpful, always talks about how she worked with kelsey grammar, doesn't make any sense, wouldn't recommend her to anyone, reason she has no reviews is probably because they were all nasty. hated this class!!!!!!!

One of my favorite people I have met at UMBC, in and out of class. Cares about her students. She may be confusing, but devotes all of her time to help you so just ask. Tells you everything that will be on exams, drops quizzes, gives extra credit if you ask, is willing to preview your work before you turn it in, etc. What more could you ask for?
She is very easy to talk to and willing to help everyone individually and outside of class. Learn to roll with the punches and you'll do great!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Participation matters--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: Sparling is fantastic. Don't be fooled by what is written here--she DEFINITELY knows her stuff and is one of the tops in her field... but I can see her getting frustrated teaching 121. She likes to help you one on one. She is remarkably kind and helpful, but can be tough. If you put up the effort, she'll do her best to meet you halfway.

Great teacher! She is always ready to help you in any way she can. She makes exams very predictable and not difficult at all. She basically goes by the book. Though this is difficult material to understand, she breaks it down as best she can.
It was a hard class, but she gave everyone as much help as possible.

Very good Prof. and very nice.  Have had her for 2 classes, and if you go to her, she will help you in any way she can.  Lectures sometimes get a little confusing, but if you follow along with the textbook, you will have no problems.  If I had a choice, I would definitely choose her for a prof.
nice person...bad teacher

She makes a hard subject even more confusing with her lectures. She seems very disorganized, but I can tell she knows her stuff, just her teaching style needs a lot of improvement. She tries her best to help the students though. If you can, get Worchesky instead.
bad! dont take this class with her

She is a great teacher if you pay attention.  And she is EXTREMELY helpful and will do everything to help you succeed.  You do have to learn the material, but 121 is a hard class no matter who you take it with.
Horrible teacher, not fair at all
No Comments
WORST prof ever!!!  don't ever try emailing her...she won't reply.  doesn't know her material well - so cannot teach AT ALL!!!
Oh my goodness! The tests are crazy impossible. The lectures were so confusing I stopped going and tried the text, which is also horrible! Egrade sucks.

She is impossible! She could take her her test in an hour and have a hard time. She is very nice, but often gets lost in her own explanation. It should be calc based physics, not a problem that involves a spring with about 15 diff prob substitutions in it
Great person, not the best teacher. But if you actually go to her for help, she is great. And she's willing to help you with anything, regardless of if it's physics-related or not.
She scared me, a 4.0 GPA student, away. Beware!
SHE SUCKS!
Sparling doesn't have a clue!

amazing. love her! She tends to give more consistent assignments so that your grade is based on much more than just a couple of exams. super nice person, always willing to help! Very interactive classes, she loves when you participate. She is also pretty organized. your attendance matters!

This class was a writing-intensive class. The class was boring and students are forced to talk for a participation grade! Participation/Discussion was worth 40% of the final grade. The TA is annoying when it comes to grading and takes forever!
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Dahlquist is a great professor and shes really funny and nice. I have her for intro to interviewing and both of our interview projects have been great. Quizzes ask specific questions from text so make sure to read.

I enjoyed her class a lot. Get ready to take a lot of notes, every class. She makes the class very interesting. She is willing to help her students. Her tests are very hard and she does not post her powerpoints on Blackboard so if you don't go class you will miss A LOT of information. Her tests are very hard and long, so study !!!!!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: A few tests, regular case study assessments. Tests really tough, if you are not a good test taker/quick writer this is not going to be the class for you. She has hilarious stories and is a really nice person, but she grades based on what she wants in an answer word for word. Test questions are taken from the textbook, wording hard to understand.

Dr. Dahlquist is an okay professor, makes you memorize DSM criteria for an essay on the exams. Most of the multiple choice questions are from the text so coming to class doesn't really matter. Most of her lectures turned into a therapy session for students to talk about their problems.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Dr. Dahlquist is awesome. She's super passionate about her lectures and has a TON of stories that help you relate to what she is teaching. Her class was really interesting! Just go to class and take notes, and do the homework! I would recommend to anyone!

Very fair professor. She is willing to go above and beyond for her students, and she really knows her stuff. Easily one of the most caring, intelligent, and professional professors I've had. 10/10 would recommend.

Not the easiest professor, but her presentation of the material in class in addition to some independent study makes this course manageable. Has tons of experience in this field, so her stories make it easier to memorize disorders. Attendance isn't mandatory, but it's a good move to attend. Only uses Blackboard to post announcements and grades.

Everyone was making her sound like an amazing teacher but I wasn't very impressed, nice lady, way to much material to know on the test. She has good real life stories but even though my major aims to work with people with mental disorders, besides learning about disorders, class wasn't great.Wouldn't recommend her but she isnt terrible

This class is easy if you study. You must study from the book in order to pass.  Attendance isn't mandatory, but she does mention things that aren't in the book that's on the test. Case studies are do-able if you memorized the criteria. All of the class points come 4 exams. Her questions are fair.

The class itself was interesting w/the amount of interest she showed in the subject&all the examples she gives in class,but exams are hard.The case studies are pretty straight forward,but the material on the exam is very detailed&specific.Some mult. choice questions were tricky where you eliminated it to 2 answers and it was hard to choose from.

Dahlquist is a great professor! She makes it very clear what you need to know and what she will test you on so there are so surprises. Her lectures are interesting with all the stories she shared - she definitely has a lot of knowledge about abnormal psychology. Be prepared to take a boatload of notes and study your butt off for her exams.

She is absolutely amazing. I got into grad school and I feel so prepared because of her. You definitely need to study and work hard. But nothing comes easy in life anyway. You do not need a DSMIV manual, just read your book!!!

She gives amazing lecture, and is extremely helpful and understanding outside of class. I actually requested to change my academic adviser to her after the semester and feel really good about it. I would recommend everybody to take her class if they can!
She is AWESOME!!!

Terrific Lecturer, always was able to keep the class engaged. She also offers good extra credit. Only problem was with my final grade she did a miscalculation and refused to believe that it was her fault. I earned a B but she refused to change it.My grade was never changed and I got  C.

This class can be pretty hard, if you don't know what she wants you to learn.  make sure that you get a copy of the quick reference DSM-IV.  And study the disorders that she talks about in class.  She is very kind to her students and was very polite about waking me up the one time i fell asleep in her class :)

She is a great professor and very clear on what you need to know. You MUST study for exam, You really need to know those cases. You can get by with skimming the book for information not covered in class. She is very clear and helpful on the subject. A great overall professor!

Excellent professor!  She always relates the material to everyday life.  The best thing is that she takes the time to let students discuss and ask questions.  The bad part is that all the histrionic and otherwise personality-disordered ones ask all the questions.  Highly recommend Dr. Dahlquist!
She is one of the most helpful professors I have ever had but her exams are tough have essays on them, definetly need to read the book to do well in the class, and attend all lectures.

She may not be the easiest teacher but she is definitely good at what she does.  She is compassionate about issues you might have and helpful when you get stuck.  The subject is fasinating if its your thing and at least clarifying if its not.  You have to read the book but its very VERY well written and clear.  Don't skimp on studying for the tests

although her tests were straight fwd but still kinda hard. wayyy too much info on her tests they are long and very little time to finish. she gives case studies. she doesn't really like to help and choses her favorites.

Tests were pretty straight forward and easy, with a lot of the information being simple common sense. Reading helps, but it's not incredibly necessary. Notes are very clear, and she likes to tell a lot of stories that help you to remember disorders. She's kind of anal about cheating on exams, but it's not really a problem..unless you're cheating
Excellent professor.  Tests are difficult, but fair, so study hard.  Also offers an easy extra credit assignment.

Very uncaring teacher. Picks pets early on, and ignores the rest of the students. Wrongly accused me of cheating on the final because my friend and I sat next to each other every class. Was also extremely difficult to go over her head, and talk directly with the department dean. I barely made it out of the class with a grade. My friend did not.
Interesting professor, try and take one of her classes if you are a psyc. major.

Now, this is coming from someone who had ZERO interest in the class, never paid attention, and took all his willpower to get through a lecture--She's good. She always knows what she is talking about, and the fact that she's a practicing psychologist off campus offers some real-world examples for the material.
Relatively easy. I didn't have the book or study for our first test and I got a B.
I dont know what i was thinking taking her , she is un caring about students she only likes teachers pet's -- she has problems at home and takes it out on the students
Good argument against nepotism.
best professor i have ever had. she is demanding but helpful. she gets to know you and cares about each person. she has great stories and lectures are very interesting.

Wonderful class, wonderful teacher.  She knows her psychology, and you've gotta take this class.  She is paranoid about cheating though, so get on her good side and she'll love you.   Interesting sidenote... she seems to have dated a guy for every disorder out there.  Very weird.  You want 285 with her.  Work hard, and you will not regret a good A

Great professor, probably top 3 I've ever had.  You is always willing to help.  She answers e-mails almost immediately.  If she gets to know who you are,  and that you are trying hard, it's a big plus.  First exam was very difficult but it gets a little easier from there.  Keep up with the reaing...
interesting class but a very hard grader- not easy to pull off an A or B

Great professor, she really wants the students to understand the material.  Answers emails promptly, and she is always willing to help you outside of class.  Her tests can be difficult.  Study hard and go to lecture and you should be fine.  Easy extra credit, too!
Knows what she's talking about, always ready to talk about research oportunities and classes. Take her class, it's not that easy, but it's fun.
Knowledgeable and great teacher.  Classes were alright, but exams are pretty hard.  the study guide helps a lot!  Reading does too of course.  easy extra credit project tho.  Not bad at all.

Dr. Dahlquist is an amazing teacher.  She makes the class difficult enough to challenge you, but easy enough to pull an A in the class.  Attend every class, read all of the chapters, and do the extra credit if she assigns any.  The class is very interesting!

I won't lie...this is a HARD class.  Dr. Dahlquist is AMAZING.  She used to be a Clinical Psychologist, and uses real life examples to help explain the material.  Go to class, and READ the book.  You may have trouble passing the exams if you don't.  One of the BEST professors I have EVER had.
Abnormal psyc is a difficult class and she is a tough grader, but you will learn SO much from her. She is always there if you have questions and is very nice and extremely personable.
Extremely hard. Had trouble staying awake.  Take Dr. Anderson instead
No Comments
No Comments

SHe is very Hard and so are her tests, it took me two times to make it through her class but she tries to make every understand. she gives real life examples. but i would not recommend taking her abnormal psyc class
Difficult class but she makes an effort so that everyone understands

His accent is very thick, his handwriting is not very good, and he teaches straight from the book. I would recommend reading the book, and if you do, you'll be fine. Exams are based off of homework problems and examples in the book. The final is tough, but that's because it is mostly on line integrals. In general, he's an excellent professor.

Professor is not very good.  He basically writes the book on the board. The only need for class is to get the homework assignments.  He faces the board the entire time and is hard to understand.  I taught myself the class!

The tests weren't terrible. They definitely reflect the homework. But his grader is ridiculous. You lose some mayny points on both exams and homework for little mistakes. Also, just go to class for exams since he usually does the odd problems. This helps with homework. He is hard to understand and blocks the board so its difficult to see.

HORRIBLE TEACHER! Had for calc 3 and had to teach myself through the whole course only to fail and have to withdraw. Awful teacher and shouldn't be teaching anymore. Whether you have a choice or not, don't take it with him. You're better off being behind schedule than to take any class with him. Very small illegible writing and hard to understand.

DO NOT. I REPEAT DO NOT TAKE THIS PROFESSOR. You will teach yourself the entire course, and waste your time doing so b/c his tests are NOT fair. Read the rest of the posts...it's all true, he's impatient, grades unfairly, speaks softly, writes lightly, he doesn't know how to use email/computers...AVOID AT ALL COSTS.

By far the worst professor I have ever had. I have gotten straight A's my entire life until this class. I have never earned a grade lower than 96% in any Math class before taking a class with Yen-Mow Lynn. Speaks terrible English, is absolutely no help when it comes to learning the material, and his test are very unfair. AVOID AT ALL COSTS!!!
This professor is horrible.  I spent the semester teaching myself.  This highest 3 grades on the first exam were 87, 87, 86.  Avoid him if you can.

DO NOT TAKE THIS PROFESSOR! The worst professor I have had at UMBC. He writes the examples directly from the book and mumbles incomprehensible narration. He literally never once turns around to face the class during the hour and fifty minute period so asking questions is impossible. Taught myself everything I learned from the book

Be prepared to teach yourself entirely from the book.  First test avg was 50's.  Said he was going to curve @ the end and never did, so half the class failed and I got a C.  Writes HW on board 5 mins before class and erases it 5 mins after class starts.  No BB or online resources.  I'm a senior now - he's still the worst prof. I've ever had. Avoid.

Lynn assigns extensive homework, and expects a certain amount of studying outside class.  If you do not keep up, his lectures will be difficult to follow, especially because of his emphasis on proofs.  However, with test questions practically identical to homework ones and a one page formula sheet for all tests, work = A.

He teaches straight out of the book in fragmented English and faces the board the entire class. He writes very lightly on the board which is dirty and dusty to begin with so only the first row can actually read what he's writing.Exams are EXTREMELY difficult with failing averages. This is more of a study place than a class.
...Just don't take him.

WHY IS HE STILL TEACHING!???  He writes in perfect penmanship on the board, but often erases it before you can copy it down.  I'm not joking --- the ENTIRE class is either sleeping or daydreaming; he talks extremely slowly and softly and has absolutely no enthusiasm.  He'll help you if you need it, but try to get someone else.

I saw that he was the teacher for Calc 3 this summer and I thought I was going to be in trouble.  However, his tests were straight forward if you did the homework problems.  He let us use a one page formula sheet which was really efficient if you wrote down how to do the homework problems on them.

was the worst math teacher i have ever taken. beats arround questions without answering them. lectures are imposible to understand. you have to teach everything to yourself. my advice is dont take this teacher at all costs. try to take Rostamian instead.

HORRIBLE!! Makes completely no sense and makes a joke about the fail rate in his class. I took this class with him and had an F average by mid semester so I dropped it. Retook with another teacher and got a B. That really says something about his teaching ability.
worst professor i have had.  Speaks to the chalk board, doesnt answer questions clearly, and does not help when you go outside of class to him for help.

worst teacher I have ever had. Lectures are unbearable and completely useless. I can see how the material can be easy if you have someone teaching you other than yourself. You can study all you want for his tests but they are a lot harder than the homework. He shouldn't be a teacher.

Terrible professor. Talks to the board the whole class, skips steps, difficult to understand him. Exams are difficult and he does not curve. Avoid him at all costs. Stopped going to class after half the classes and taught myself the course. You will do the same if you take it with him, if you can't teach yourself, then get another professor.
Absolutely the worst teacher ever. I never had a problem with math in my life until I had him. Avoid him at ALL costs. If you don't you will be forced to teach yourself the material.
WORST TEACHER I HAVE EVER HAD.  GOES WAYYYY TOO FAST.  AVOIDDDDD

omg! dun understand wt the heck is he talking about, writing is horrible too..cannot drop any test nor exam grades..the TA is helpful tho..in helping students wif hw probelms

reviews.comment: She is the best English professor she is very kind and understanding, there are only a few essays for this class and they are all open-ended prompts, so they were interesting to write

She is genuinely the nicest person i have met since I have been here. Love her class. Guided us through our assignments and offered great advice. TAKE ENGLISH WITH DR. CARTER!! she's actually the sweetest professor ever, super easy-going, brings candy to class, and has these cute little activities as writing prep for major assignments. you can tell she really cares about her students and gets very involved in your writing process if you ask! 100% recommend!!

I think she was one of the best professors I've had in college. You can write about what you like and so there's a lot of room for creativity. Definitely an easy A.

She is so nice and caring! There isn't a lot of heavy homework until the last couple weeks. But those assignments were a part of one big assignment and help to do the final paper. She was a great teacher for English 100. Her lectures were very easy to understand and we did a lot of group discussions and group feedback. i love prof carter! all the reviews are accurate shes one of the best at UMBC! so so sweet she truly cares about her students and what they have to say. u can write about topics u want! def would take her again if i could!!!

She is such a sweet teacher. She clearly cares about her students. She gives candy too! Love her!!
One of the best ENGL teachers. She is so nice and sweet.

Honestly she's one of the best English professors at umbc, she's very lenient and understanding. The class was fun because she let us mostly write about topics we were interested in. I would take her again if I could, 10/10 recommend.

Very nice professor! She gives us extra days to submit our papers and is lenient with grading.

Very kind teacher! I felt bad not going to office hours since they were so early, I would've loved to talk to her more. One of the nicest professors at UMBC. Understands that students are busy with major-related courses and does her best to accommodate the workload accordingly. Lenient with grading and helpful.

Professor Carter is such a lovely person, she truly cares about her students and wants them to succeed. I would totally recommend her for any student that wants a hands on instructor that will focus of them individually.

He has funny jokes that he says every once in a while the funniest joke is his teaching. He teaches the class straight out of the book reading every line word for word. reviews.comment: Prof. McAlpine is one of THE best teachers I have ever been able to work with. He is very inclusive in class participation, but that in itself can sometimes feel scary. The only thing I would warn is that he does ask you to express your creativity which can be scary if you have social anxiety, but he makes it very welcoming and inclusive.

The most passionate professor I've had.  Expects you to show up and be respectful because it's a small class.  It was a long class but he let us have breaks and even run to starbucks.  Lots of movies.  Such a cool guy with contagious enthusiasm.  Definitely take this class.

Professor McAlpine is one of the best! I am not an INDS major, but  I absolutely loved his class. His lectures are lively and involve a lot of discussion. Incredibly friendly- he tries to make class as fun as he possibly can. Can be a tough grader, but not overly difficult. Great adviser too!

Great professor.  He wants the students to succeed and will work with you as much as possible to make that happen.  He's very interesting and full of stories.  Probably the best professor I've ever had, can't recommend him enough. I hope to take more of his classes, whether I need them or not.

Best professor I've had. Makes class fun and really tries to help students. Has a lot of knowledge on a lot of different things. Great class and even better professor

McAlpine is very helpful. He can come across as intimidating at first but as you get to know him he is very personable and helpful. Assignments can seem hard at first wile you gain an understanding. Text is life raft in the class while you can skim it you need to know the foundational principal of each chapter.

Prof. McAlpine is probably the coolest professor (and person) at UMBC- extremely talented teacher and great friend! Class was so much fun and we learned oodles of really useful tools and strategies. I can't say enough about Prof Mcalpine, he's my advisor now because of this class. Best class @ umbc, best prof hands down!

reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: She's tough and I didn't appreciate all of her humor, but she cares deeply about both the subject and her students. She let me go off on my own interests in papers as long as they were well researched and on the texts. She's interesting and tries to connect students to the material with creative assignments. It's not an easy class, but worth it.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--Caring

reviews.comment: When I first took McKinley for 302 I didn't like her but she's grown on me a lot over the past year. She cares about her students a lot. She gives good feedback and really wants everyone to succeed. If you develop a good relationship with her, she will do everything she can to make sure you do well even outsider her class. She's a peach i love her

I adore Prof. McKinley. She also happens to be my advisor, which is a plus. She's super sweet and helpful; just a little wacky sometimes. Super organized and responsive. She really wants her students to succeed.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES

reviews.comment: After a full semester with Prof. McKinley, I'm still not 100% sure how I feel about her. In the beginning of the class, I couldn't stand her. She seemed strict and rather obnoxious. However, as class went on, and I had more face-to-face meetings with her, I realized she is actually really generous and kind, just stressed. Give her a chance.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: Professor McKinley is a great professor who knows her material and is passionate about it, but she can give long lectures. Don't forget to read, she gives lots of pop quizzes and don't forget your material. Take lots of notes, do the reading and you'll be golden.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: This is coming from someone who likes Mckinley as a person and gets good grades in her class. I really find her lectures interestingShe is so strict: don't expect to come in late, go to the bathroom, or forget your bool. It will be held against you. Her expectations are really high and there's too many pop quizzes. If you can avoid it, don't do it.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES

reviews.comment: Mckinley is a seemingly nice lady but very very strict. The class was a total bore and very intensive, you have to listen and read everything she tells you. If you think youre going to get through the class by going on your phone or doing other work forget about it, she yells at people for just going to the bathroom. Would think an easy A but no.

Overall, Eng 206 was very interesting and I learned a lot over the course of the semester.  The tests were difficult.  Having to write 4 essays over the course of 70-80 minutes was no joke.  Take down notes for everything she says in class, and make sure to read the passages.   She is understanding and willing to help if you go to her and ask.

Professor McKinley is a great teacher and knows her material, but she requires participation and constant presence in her class. You have to be ready to read the material and read it on time. She gives pop quizzes and the only way you'll pass them is if you READ THE MATERIAL. I cannot stress this enough. If you need help, reach out, she's there.

Okay, she has a problem with students leaving class to use the bathroom, ebooks and expected 112 pages to be read Tuesday to Thursday so in like 2 days. It says its an English class but she is the head of the Ancient Studies minor, so it REALLY is a history class. Just run. Seriously. Nice lady, but with so many options TAKE SOMETHING ELSE.

McKinley is the most helpful professor I've ever had. She will give you all of the resources you need and more to be able to really excel in the course. She is always available to give advice without judgement or harsh criticism, and her enthusiasm about your ideas is contagious. Her period specialty is 14th century.

Professor McKinley is a very unique and interesting individual. She really is quirky, but it makes her classes fun. If you attend class, read the books, and listen during class discussions, you'll get an A, no prob. For the tests, you just repeat information from the reading discussions and you'll be good. She offers lots of help for the paper.

I missed 5 classes, 3 of which I showed her doctors notes for, and she said she had no choice but to fail me. There's a lot of reading and studying needed to do well on tests. Bring your book to every class. And take it seriously or else you'll fail. Other than her strictness, she's a very clear and helpful teacher who can also joke around in class

Huge stickler for attendance. Claimed I had missed a higher number of classes than I had, and when I tried to dispute it, she said it was non-negotiable and seemed unwilling to even see me. I liked the class as a whole, but ended up failing because of this.

McKinley is obsessed with control within her classroom to the point where she treats the class like children rather than college students. You cannot leave her class without permission emailed to her prior to class. She will cause a scene as you exit the room. Her quirky personality can be charming and you will learn a lot about medieval text.

Deducts grades significantly for just about everything. Odd and quirky. Don't get on her bad side, go to the bathroom, forget to silence your phone, rumple your papers, turn your pages too loudly or you'll fail.

Absurdly strict grader. Treats you like a child. Leave to use the bathroom? Grade deduction. Forget your text? Grade deduction. Provide "negative contributions" - which apparently means speaking up in class in a way she disagrees with - grade deduction. McKinley does not facilitate learning or discussion, she demands obedience.

She is extremely vague and fake. She has an odd sense of humor and is very unhelpful. Don't take this class if not comfortable with medieval style literature. She'll leave you in the dust and not look back.

To get an A, take the papers seriously, miss 1-2 classes max, and familiarize yourself w/texts for the exams. Quizzes don't really affect your grade, just how she looks at you as a student. Quirky sense of humor, really interested in topic, great lectures, interesting texts. Had no previous interest in medieval lit, but really enjoyed this class.

New teacher. Used to teach in Miami or somewhere in Florida. Obsessed with Chaucer, makes you read the middle English texts aloud in class. Really great about reading students papers beforehand if you email them to her. Likes original paper topics, new ideas, and creative (but reliable sources).

Helpful, kind, funny. Great professor. 4 papers, 1 mid term exam, and 4 pop quizzes. She canceled the final exam. She drops the lowest quiz score. You can still pass the class if you fail the quizzes and the exam. She might not cancel the final in future semesters, so be careful. The content was dull, but the professor was interesting.
No Comments

I say hes a tough grader but hes actually not, he is a roll of the dice grader. I took this class for an easy A and I got a B. I honestly tried my hardest and made my speeches and final paper interesting and engaging. Mind you I had a 4.0 so for this to be the class I lost it in, is crazy. He gave me a B on every assignment, for no reason.

Nice old man but he did not know how to use blackboard. He didn't post the syllabus until a month+ after the class started. We had 3 main talks and didn't receive any feedback on any of them. All his lectures were literally just him talking; no slides, no videos, just him talking! Not responsive/accessible AT ALL! Just don't take this class.

Lack of tech ability is super frustrating. Didn't upload syllabus for weeks, didn't have any grades in until 2 weeks left in the semester. Forget emailing him. Should be an easy A. Also, I have no issue with expressing a political opinion, but it gets to a point where it's embarrassing for him. Clearly coasting on tenure, deserves to be fired.

professor yaps A LOT. You only have to write 2 papers in MLA, and write an outline so u can do ur speech (optional but aint nobody is remembering their entire speech) Speeches have 2 be roughly 5 minutes. He is terrible with tech, syllabus wasnt released till a few weeks in, + u wont see grade updates, doesnt check emails.VERY EASY A+ CLASS THOUGH.

If you think the Trump stuff was bad, imagine taking him during the semester of a presidential election. Complete waste of time, but laughably easy. No one respects him and just do homework in class. Two papers during the whole class. Attendance is a big part of the grade though, so make sure you show up.

ATTENDANCE IS MANDATORY. He says in the beginning of the year that it isn't but I failed his classes because I only showed up to class 5 times. He is boring too, you'll end up watching a movie or playing games in the class.

This class was easy to obtain an A in, even if you don't know how to write a speech. During the class, he would only cover the material about social issues and how to write a speech, so you don't even need to buy the books required to pass. I liked the professor's attitude and humor during the class, which made the class more enjoyable.

The most boring professor ever. Insanely easy grader who doesn't know how to use technology messes up his submission portals all the time. Doesn't answer emails, spews tons of outdated information when it comes to news and history, and is a heavily left-leaning professor. Go to class, chill on your computer, it's a simple 9th grade English class.

Professor McGurrin is a good lecturer however, he is not accessible outside class, if you want to send him an email to ask him something, he is not responding. Otherwise, he is a good teacher, good to talk to but just remember that if you take a class with him, ask all of your questions in class as there is a chance you might not get an answer.

No exams or quizzes just papers on different speech topics. The speeches are recorded on voicethread and don't have to be given in front of the class. Overall pretty easy class and a fun professor to talk to.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Online (covid). He doesn't respond to emails but does answer questions before class. He talks about topics but they aren't really related to assignments. Six speeches total for the class- turn in the script and do a voicethread. Felt like a waste of time & I didn't learn much. It's probably better to take his class in person. Textbook wasn't used.

Professor McGurrin talked a lot about stuff like politics (especially Trump), religion, and marriage. We didn't learn anything about public speaking, but we were assigned speeches (5 --> 3 because of his ramblings). It's an easy A, but I personally don't think it was worth my time. If you don't care about course content, this class is for you!

Professor McGurrin is incredibly chill; you really only have to write 4-5 speeches in the entire semester (about 3 pgs, double spaced). However, he doesn't post anything on Blackboard, so the only way you're getting information about the class is in lecture or if you reach out to him by email. Some of his lectures can feel pretty repetitive though.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Hilarious

reviews.comment: He is the worst! All he does is talking about nonsense and Trump hating speeches. If it wasn't for Trump, this guy would not have anything to talk about. It is ridiculous that he is teaching us considering he probably does not have a clue about the class. It's such a shame that I have to sit in the class, listen to this clown talking and pay for it

The worst professor I have ever had. Easy A, but learned absolutely nothing. He demands that your speeches have a thesis and purpose, and yet his lectures are purposeless, unguided messes that drone on for at least ten minutes past time that class should send. You will get an A, and you will learn absolutely nothing.

Take this class! Prof never unlocked the Blackboard, or gave a syllabus, and never gave out a single rubric, but I received an A. He's super laid back, just do what he asks and it will be an easy, enjoyable class.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Inspirational--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: If you are looking for an easy A, take this class. All you have to do is give a couple of speeches and you will get an A in the class. His lectures are useless, but entertaining because he is a funny guy.

Get this, I'm 47 now, I graduated UMBC in 1993. I took four classes with Tony. He is laid back and lectures with no direct plan for any class. The thing is though he tackles any topic and works it back into how to understand people and communicate. Of all the professors I have ever had in any subject he stands out. Take any class he teaches.

He was actually really interesting to talk to, and to listen to. I normally only came to class to turn in my papers or to get papers back. Other times I just sat in class to do other homework. If you need to take this class and don't want to put in the extra work for an A, TAKE HIM! He is very understanding and his lectures aren't course related.

If you have room in your schedule, take this class for free credits. Attendance is not mandatory, and lectures are mostly him talking about random stuff and most of that stuff repeats over and over, so you can pretty much study or do work for other classes while in his class. I don't see how you can get a B for the class, and don't buy the textbook

He is an amazing professor. It's a total of 3 papers you have to do throughout the semester. He told us more towards the end of the year we're only doing 2 papers. He doesn't give due dates you just turn them in when you want too, no rubric. No rules. Just write on any topic you want. He lets you turn the papers in as many times as you want.

DO NOT BUY THE TEXTBOOKS unless you would like a real reference to public speaking, it won't help you much for the class. Attendance is now mandatory, although I have skipped quite a few classes and still managed an A. He LOVES talking about whatever he wants to talk about (not related to speech really). We ended up making 3 speeches instead of 5

The class was extremely easy. Most people showed up late and he didn't care as long  as you got your speeches in at some point. He never gave us a syllabus or told us how many points anything was worth. He also never handed us anything back or gave feedback. I don't recommend him as a professor (although he's very nice), but still a very easy class

Really nice, down to earth guy. Easy class, 3 speeches total and he grades very liberally-as long as you show you put some effort in he'll give you an A.  Will collect speeches, but doesn't hand it back. Takes attendance, but not much people show up regardless. Bought the books, and never opened them. Also never received a syllabus.
reviews.rating_tags: SO MANY PAPERS--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: He talks about politics for an hour and thirty minutes two days a week. Show up if you want to, but you're not going to learn anything. Write a few essays, show up if you don't have anything else to do, and get an A.

Good professor. Technologically illiterate and very disorganized, but he will is a solid funny guy. I never got below a b- on a paper and I could turn it in as many times as I wanted to bring it up. He grades tough but will always give you chances. If you need a chill class that will help you take a break from crazy classes this is it.

McGurrin was great. Yes, he rambles immensely, but I always went to class because of how interesting he was. Ask him random questions to get him talking. Essays are graded hard, but he looks for your improvement through the semester. He helped my technical writing a lot. Attendance isn't mandatory, but I recommend showing up and connecting with him

Actually the worst class I've ever taken.  By the end, a 25 student class had turned to 7.  We had three papers and the prompts were unclear and grading was arbitrary based on whether or not he agreed with you.  Lectures were literally him talking about unrelated stuff the whole time.  Love yourself and don't take this class.

I'm not sure why McGurrin's rating is so low. He may be a little disorganized, and he's definitely technologically illiterate, but he's fantastic. Loads of great stories and advice and jokes. I've even spent a lot of time outside of class just chatting with him. He always provides great feedback on assignments. Turn in the work, you'll get an A.

Taking a class with Tony is all about what you make of it. Yes, he rambles a little. Yes, he repeats himself every class. But if you take time to talk to him and ask him questions he will help you out a lot. Get him to like you. Attendance isn't mandatory and you only need the book so that you can include quotes from the essays in your papers.

Attend class, pretend to pay attention, do your work (put some effort into it), and you should get an A. Each lecture was just a political rant. I spent most of the semester worrying about how I was to pull an A when my all of my sets of poems earned Cs. We didn't get the syllabus until the third to last class... Somehow I got an A.

I ended up dropping after 2 classes. He spent the first class rambling about stuff that had nothing to do with the course materials, and the second class was a repeat & expansion of the first. He really wasn't living up to the reputation of UMBC as an "honors college." Your time & money are too valuable to waste in McGurrin's class.
Awful teacher, but a nice guy. Lectures are utterly pointless.

I didn't learn anything I was supposed to after hearing what other 391 sections were like. We just wrote personal essays. Class discussions were pointless - he just rambled and none of it was on topic. That being said, he seemed to grade easy, attendance wasn't necessary, and he let you revise any papers.

make yourself know and go to class. Going is useless though, but it helps him know you. He rambles all class about lots of random insignificant topics. WONT GIVE YOU BACK YOUR PAPERS UNTIL THE LAST WEEK OF CLASS, yet he expects you to do multiple revisions without getting your papers back. You never know what your grade is. Gives out lots of Cs.

By far the worst professor I have ever had in terms of what I learned. Which is nothing. I learned nothing. He seems like a nice guy, but he's painfully awkward. This leads to uncomfortable and often genderist jokes. I attended every class, but that was unnecessary. Don't worry too much about the work during the semester. Just turn in the final.
One of the nicest guys. Full of wisdom.

Easiest and most useless class I've ever taken. Easy A. No textbook use. He'll help you revise everything if needed. Class discussion was useless. Attendance is a waste of time. Didn't get work back until the last three weeks which was a bit frustrating. I didn't learn anything, but if you want credit w/out work take Mcgurrin. He's a very nice man

Very easy class but it was nerve-wracking having NO idea the grade you would receive. Don't expect a syllabus and don't bother buying the books "required". Go to the class at least most of the time, make yourself known, turn in your poems. That's how I got my A. Lecture consists of repetitive rants that can drive you nuts. Expect to hear cursing.
Teacher is very repectative, he likes to talk about the same things for several weeks, there is a portfolio that he makes you complete for the final. Could be a good Arts and Hummanities class

Recommended for non English majors. Very nice guy but do not take this course for anything but an easy A. You will not learn anything and his rants can be insufferable depending on your persuasion. You can skip class a lot but stay on top of your grade because he tends to lose papers a lot.

He rambled about politics, sex, religion, and baseball. ALL CLASS, EVERY CLASS. I am not exaggerating. Absolutely no guidance on our papers, I think he threw darts to determine which paper received an A and which didnt. If you are happy with a B or a C, then by all means take his class. There is really nothing you can do to control your grade.

SUCH AN EASY CLASS. I highly recommend this class. I attended basically one of the three classes per week. He is very redundant with his lectures so it really doesn't matter. There are 4 papers for your grade but you can do as many re-writes as you need. I highly recommend taking this class if you do not plan on majoring in English.

I think he's one of my easier Prof.'s. His class is enjoyable and if you miss any that's ok, it's easy to catch up. Very helpful on what he comments on. Class discussions get off topic, but if your fine with that then it's an easy class. Some topics are offensive, but he means no harm, get's you thinking.

I don't understand why everyone is hating on McGurrin. HIs rambling is somewhat interesting and this class is an easy A. Not only that, he doesn't seem to care about everyone facebooking during class, much less attendance. I would definitely take another class with him.

very nice professor. he is willing to work with students and give them as much time as they need. his instructions are not crystal clear and leave room for creative interpretation on purpose, so if you're anal and need strict direction, don't take this class. he has a lot to say and he's very intelligent. overall, great, very laid back class.
