I took him for Creative Writing, Poetry. If you enjoy writing poetry, don't take this class. If you enjoy talking politics, it's the class for you. You can't be easily offended in this class, because he can be offensive. Not much else to say; I don't recommend it to anyone.

Don't expect to learn much, but the class is very easy, and you won't have to do much thinking or participating while in it.  There are a few papers, but the topics are open-ended and well spread out.  He likes to talk about a lot of random things that seem irrelevant.

Absolutely no english was taught. He talked politics, baseball, politics, sex, and more politics. No textbooks just reading. No exams just papers. No notes to take. Most people that came to class surfed the web or starred blankly.  I think most people got an A or B

boring as anything. This class was a waste of my time. We didn't learn anything about poetry, instead he repeated the same crap everyday for 15 weeks. It's uncertain to know what your grade is and he's not very helpful when you ask questions. Very broad and confusing... if you want a class to sleep through then take this one.

Personally I thought he was an amazing professor. The texts he chose I thought were extremely good, I even decided to keep one of them after the end of the semester for myself. He does procrastinate and he doesn't say much about what you need to do other than remind you of things. Still if you make an effort to talk to him he will go the extra mile
He's AWESOME!
I hated the book and his lectures were boring, but he was realitively easy on grading and deadlines. Perhaps the best thing I can say about him is that he procrastinates A LOT.

There were no in-class writings, no exams, and only 3 short papers with re-writes. Never got a syllabus, papers never really had a due date, and we only got the first paper back. After the first month, his 50 minute lectures became 5 minute reminders to continue reading Gravity's Rainbow, which most students thought was extremely difficult reading.

He's certainly a nice man. Very friendly. Unfortunately, I learned nothing from him. Classes (when they weren't cancelled) were mostly just ramblings about politics and baseball. He's an easy A. If that's what you need, go for it. Otherwise, don't take courses with him.

His classes are the hardest to sit through, and he will make you read Gravity's Rainbow, which is without a doubt the worst I've ever read.  We never got a syllabus, or rubrics for our papers.  He's a real pain to deal with.  I'd rather do a bit more work rather than put up with this guy.

Should be called McGurrin's Commentaries. Each class was a lecture about politics, society, culture, religion, university life, occaisionally touching on literature. He says that he hates politicians; what becomes clear is that he hates Republicans,  especially conservatives. Papers were self-guided, with revisions encouraged for better grades.

HORRIBLE.  Cancels class often, most of the time without notice.  The impersonalized grading makes you feel like he is randomly assigning you grades.  Doesn't stick to the syllabus so you end up doing 3 papers rather than 5+.  Just do the papers, go to the writing lab for show and you will get an A.

Easy coursework. Initially assigned 5 papers, but that was reduced to 3. Didn't show up MANY times. Talks about assignments vaguely. You could ask him a question, spend 30 minutes talking about it and never have the question answered. Paper deadlines were pushed back many times and frankly were never established.

He's crazy.  papers were never turned in on time, nor handed back.  He rambles on about NOTHING in class, never ever talks about english, just politics and baseball.  almost never comes to class either.  i dont understand his grading system.

If you want an easy A take this professor.  He won't show up to class half of the time (every person who has taken him has said so as well as my own experiences) and he'll push back paper deadlines almost on a regular basis.  You won't learn much but you won't have to write about the "First Year Experience" book that freshman must read.

I took him for "Writing Creative Essays." All hyperbole aside, Anthony McGurrin is the worst teacher/ professor/ person I paid tuition to teach me that I've ever had. Don't, DON'T take him. He hardly showed up and when he did it was only long enough to **** for an hour then leave. We never used the readings. Grades were random. He's awful.

VERY easy on people. NO exams, just 3 papers with lots of chance to rewrite and revise. Read the book, write the paper with some efforts, you got an A. Very clear on what to do to get an A, not a clue on what he's talking about in class.

He's an interesting speaker and a nice guy, but not the best teacher.  If you take him early in the morning, don't be surprised if he's late all the time.  Didn't give much constructive criticism, the class didn't improve my writing any.  Didn't give grades until the very end; it seemed like he graded arbitrarily.

A nice guy, but not a great teacher.  His comments on my work didn't help with anything.  If you take his class, don't even bother buying the books (unless you want to read them on your own) because he doesn't use them at all.
Not the most structured of courses. He's an easy professor.

Extremely easygoing teacher. His intentions are to teach but does not always project them with clarity. He accepts rewrites and is flexible regarding due dates. Putting in a little effort will guarantee you an A. Take this class strictly for its easiness.

Don't bother going to class unless you like listening to someone talk about random stuff that has nothing to do with the material. Not very punctual, misses classes without posting notices, but is a nice guy and will let you do rewrites. Our class didn't have a midterm or final! Just 3 papers!

Horrible teacher! His syllabus (handwritten and barely readible) was vague, he spent the classes going off onto  tangents and offered few actually helpful comments. Told me to be more concrete, but offered no explanation. Beware- Grades poetry based purely on what he likes.

He's a nice guy and the class was extremely easy. He was very flexible with assignments and even cancelled our last paper so we only had 3 papers for the whole semester in instead of 4. My only problem was that this guy has an extremely liberal political agenda that he presses upon you in class.

As an English major, I have taken two courses with him. I think hes great. Its true he isnt always specific with his instructions, but he is very flexible and willing to listen. I would recommend him to anyone, English major or not.

A very easy class, but do not take if you want to learn something. The lectures had nothing to do with the papers he expected you to write but he was an easy grader so it balanced out. You can do re-writes on the papers.

Incredibly easy class! But not everyone may enjoy it. There isn't much of a syllabus and it can be hard to know what he wants in a paper. But he is a pretty flexible grader, and he will accept rewrites of papers. Take his class for its easiness!

Very nice guy, I'll give him that.  The syllabus was given to us two months into the semester.  He doesn't like computers and won't answer emails, so don't bother.  Very lax on grading papers.  Only went to class every other week.  Hit or Miss
This professor WAS TERRIBLE. no syllabus, didn't hand first paper back til the second to the last week of school. total of THREE papers.  dont need to even go to class.

One of the worst teachers I've had...extremely unclear with the syllabus, vague deadlines, and sometimes he wouldn't even show up to class!  I was highly disappointed with this teacher and do not recommend him to anyone.

One of the nicest professors on campus, will work with you for hours on end after class.  all you have to do to get the most out of him is ask questions.  doesn't like to restrict students' creativity with a syllabus or with very structured assignments.

You all are insane. For the real English majors out there: word of warning. He has no syllabus. He is very unclear and very negative about student work. He tells you to have concrete poetry but never tells you what that is. Good luck to those who take him
easy class- very independent- i only had to go to class about once every week- no real deadlines for papers- is very flexible
Well, this was an easy class but the instructor doesnt really play a huge part in the class. Its more of an independent work. But he is helpful to you in improving your papers.

Prof McDonough really knows what she's talking about. Not only is she an engaging lecturer, she is really caring and works with you personally to ensure that you're meeting your goals for the class. She is open-minded and loves to share her knowledge with her students.

Professor McDonough is very well-verse in the topic and tries her best to engage the class into discussions. The readings are numerous and thick and some of the readings you had to purchase were expensive. There are three essays that require multiple readings, but she grades extremely easy. Recommended, but be prepared to find ways to keep up.

there is a TON of reading, most of which winds up being good background for in-class lectures. grading is tough but fair and she's super helpful during office hours. it's obvious that this subject is her wheelhouse: her lectures are detailed and engaging, though she sometimes gets off-track. it can be tough to reach her via email.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: One of the most competent and knowledgeable professors I've ever met, seriously. I'm an Environmental Sciences major, and her class was one of my favorites by far. Awesome lectures, and cultivates enthusiasm and curiosity, which is so lacking in history departments.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: There is a lot of reading but it is all relevant. Grading criteria is clear and she gives excellent feed back. Strict with deadlines but is also understanding and will work with you. One of my favorite classes and professors.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: One of my favorite classes. I am not a history major, but I took the course for my diversity requirement and loved it. Professor McDonough is extremely knowledgeable and her in-class discussions are fascinating. You will be doing A LOT of reading, but all of it is relevant.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Susan McDonough is a smart, knowledgeable resource. She is great, outside of the classroom. Inside of the class she is tough and hard to approach. She picks out good and valuable readings, but she assigns a lot of it. She is a tough grader and expects expert material, no matter your level of writing. Your grade rides on harshly graded papers.

This woman was the bane of my existence. I am a history major, and have never had a harder class than this one- even my undergraduate thesis was easier. She is unfair in her reading assignments, expects you to memorize primary sources, and gives the worst exams. The midterm was so awful she had to curve it 35%. Prepare to work hard for no reward.

Okay, McDonough is FAR AND AWAY the absolute WORST professor I have ever had. She is extremely demeaning and belittling when she speaks to you and the entire class revolves around primary sources, which would be great except I have literally learned no history. Her exams are total crap; she is one of those takes-questions-out-of-the-footnotes. UGH!

Dr. McDonough is a very committed professor for this course, and is very interested in teaching students to write history papers. She does a good job telling the students how to improve their papers and emphasizes classroom discussion. She was a much tougher grader than the TA, but that is probably expected. Overall she is not too challenging.

It's an interesting class, but I only took it to have a 300-400 level course. The readings are a bit much, and sometimes I don't get to complete them, resulting in bad quiz grades, but there's alot more to make up for in papers, etc. Difficult class, but I don't regret taking it. Very helpful teacher and interesting topic.

Expects a lot from you in this class. Keep up with the primary source readings! Papers are easy but the midterm and final are a bit much so prepare to study. I wouldn't recommend this class unless you have a burning desire to learn about Medieval Europe. She's super helpful and nice though.
Not too bad. Considering that the course is mandatory for history majors, Dr. McDonough made the class bearable. Follow the rubrics posted on Blackboard!

Very knowledgeable about what she teaches, though she doesn't really know HOW to teach. Nice, but this class is only for those who have had her before and don't mind memorizing large sections of text for class. Papers are easy though.
pretty good, had her more than once

Dr. McDonough always seemed very happy and passionate to be teaching. Her class was very interesting and she was always very clear about her expectations. She knows her stuff and is a very good lecturer! Not necessarily an easy class, but I feel I learned a lot. I would definitely recommend taking a course with her.

Clearly very passionate about the subject and her students. Offered lots of advice on how the research and writing skills we were learning would help us in the real world as historians. Occasionally a harsh grader, but her comments on my assignments generally made sense, and when I asked for help she was accessible and friendly. Great teacher.

Gave good feedback for class discussions. Did not answer email in a timely fashiom, if at all. Did offer help, but had that fresh-out-of-grad-school lack of sympathy. Essentially used Dr. Lindenmeyer's HIST 201 syllabus with some changes. The poor editing on the paper can probably be laid at the feet of the graduate students.

Great professor--very passionate about her craft, always excited to lecture even about stuff that she will tell you is "boring as****". 201 has a lot of busy work, yes, but it makes the final paper that much easier; her feedback is really helpful and she works with you to develop a good topic.
Definitely knows her stuff.  Pretty demanding, but will take another class with her.  Learned a lot.  Good sense of humor, too.

I took her for Medieval Europe & Medieval Gender studies. Take her courses seriously and you will do well. Must attend class, be willing to discuss topics, do the outside reading. Very understanding, genuine concern for her students, always available to help. Extremely clear expectations. Brilliant scholar yet down to earth. Witty , stylish, cute.
Great Teacher, Always looks good during classes kind of eye candy. She knows her stuff as well and shows it fluently through her powerpoints.
Expect to do a LOT of outside reading.

Great teacher.  She really knows her stuff about medieval Europe and she goes out of her way to give students every chance to succeed.  Expect a lot of Primary source reading and papers.  There's also a midterm and final but if you go to class and do the readings there's no reason for you not to pass.

It is virtually impossible to please Mejdulene, and her expectations for the course are rather confusing.  The material is interesting, but be expected to read several books, write multiple essays, and discuss weekly readings during class.  She is an extremely harsh grader and if you miss a single homework, you cannot get an A.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: Completely boring and a waste of time

I took this class before covid so it has been awhile. However just avoid this professor because she is really nit picky about everything. It is a lot of reading and writing which I think which is over kill for this course.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--So many papers

reviews.comment: I took a graduate-level GWST class as an English grad student and I was nervous that I would fall behind, but Dr. Shomali's lectures made even the most difficult readings accessible to me. I still look at my notes from her class as a researcher today. She gives constructive feedback and pushes her students to work hard. I can't recommend her enough

Anyone saying Dr. Shomali is difficult is most likely trying to coast. She tells you exactly what is needed.  PLEASANT. HELPFUL Answers emails quickly.She pushes you to do your best and that's what college is supposed to be.GWST students will tell you what an asset she is. She is a researcher so no you cant coast on her. . She knows her work. WELL!

Interesting class content but she was very nit picky about certain things. Way too writing heavy. Gets offended if you bring up an opinion other than her own and passively tells you youre wrong. The papers she made us write about were way too long and hard to read. Not worth it.

Dr. Shomali is amazing. She may not be everyone's favorite but she is one of mine. She made this research class/senior capstone doable and fun while still trying to survive this COVID-10 pandemic. She is very smart and a true researcher so lazy students beware. Keep things real with her and she'll help you to the finish line. Class was chill.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: This lady is SCARY. She's rude, judgmental, and hates anyone questioning her. At one point she straight up told us that our opinions don't matter so she doesn't want to hear them. She's clearly very knowledgeable about her field, but she expected way too much for a 100 level class and her way of talking down to people is very off putting.
Extremely rude and hard to talk to. Does not care about the students. Just assigns work and forgets about it. Always trying to push her own opinion.

Her course is VERY writing intensive and you wont be allowed to have an opinion during her discussions. She is clearly upset whenever someone disagrees with her viewpoint. If you want someone to keep forcing their narrative on to you then this is the class to take.
She sucks. DO NOT take her for gen eds (trust me).

By far the worst teacher I've had at UMBC. She is rude, unapproachable, and does not seem to care about her students at all. The amount of work for a 100 level class is RIDICULOUS. She does not give good feedback and flat out ignored me multiple times when I tried to ask for help. Definitely will never take her again.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: Probably one of the worst professor I've ever had for a general education credit. She is a tough grader, extremely judgmental, and does not act like she wants her students to succeed. Gives terrible feedback, unapproachable, gives a lot of work for a course that isn't even writing intensive. Would not recommend this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--SO MANY PAPERS

reviews.comment: She expects way too much for a 100 level course. She knows what she is talking about, but gives way too much work that is very writing intensive. Gives judgy looks when she hears something that she does not agree with and everyone in the class can tell. She lets u miss a few classes and is understanding about requesting extensions.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--SO MANY PAPERS

reviews.comment: Professor Shomali is the best! She is so down to earth and the way she teaches, you want to know more and ask questions. This was a very easy going class, she's not strict about too many things. There are a lot of readings and writings with them, but as long as you do those and participate you should be fine!

Dr. Mej was incredible! She's incredibly passionate, and it shows within her lectures, as she's very articulate and makes even the most complicated aspects of femininity easy to grasp/understand. The assigned readings could be dense at times, but you want to come prepared to the class discussions. (Her outfits were on point every single day, too!)
great professor
Easiest class in all of UMBC. If it's a potential elective requirement of you just need to fill 3 credits with the most stressless class ever? Take this class

Going to this class at 7:10 pm is pretty brutal because of how boring it is, but it will let out at least an hour early every time. In class, you just watch videos or read a text, then go home and write a couple paragraphs about it. Sometimes she takes attendance for a grade. Small projects that are easy. Add this to your schedule for an easy A.

Perfect class to add to your schedule if you are looking for an easy A. Attendance is not mandatory, but sometimes she takes attendance, which is graded. Group work is in most classes, and these projects make up most of your grade. Easy final case study.

Tax is not scary with Medicus! Few assignments that are all easy A's! Going to class felt like a waste of time, but sometimes she takes attendance, and it hurts your grade severely if you are not there for it. The class let out early every time. One easy project. Overall, if you are looking for a light class with minimal effort, this is the one.

Class is one of the easiest that you can take on campus! everything is opinionated so there is not a real wrong answer. Great weekly discussions based off of the topics that you go over.  A weekly homework assignment and one final paper at the end of the semester.

She's a great professor with engaging lectures. Even though attendance isn't mandatory, her classes are genuinely enjoyable especially if you enjoy participating in discussions. 

You have 1-2 paragraph essays due at the end of each week and try to attend class because there is group activity on a random day. no final, no exams, just essays

I have taken her twice. She is a good professor that seems to care about her students. She might seem harsh at the start but once test role around you realize she is a kind person. She wants students to succeed, but wants them to put the work in. You are likely to pass her class if you stick through it.
She is a great and funny professor, I would recommend her for IS317.

Professor Medicus is my least favorite professor. While this course was an easy A, during lectures she would not answer questions and would be passive-aggressive. Homework would be unannounced, and not enough time would be given for exams. If you are looking for an easy A, take Medicus. If you would like to learn, I cannot recommend her.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment:
Hands down this is probably the worst online class I've ever taken. Lectures consist of her reading off the slides. Group work is randomly given out, and you better hope she even posts the problems. 90% of test questions have zero relation to the homework.
If you do not enjoy accounting and/or don't like teaching yourself, do NOT take this class.

First week in, the class is purely online, thru Blackboard Collaborate. She reads the content on slides. A lot of idle time of just empty staring, and not really tech savvy unfortunately, a lot of time is wasted and not really learning anything, just feels like a robot spitting facts.

Great person, not a great professor.

Easy A. There were only a couple homework assignments and 2 take home exams, that's it. Lectures are extremely tedious and I never saw her take attendance. Assignments are based mostly on opinion and backing your reasoning.

She is a wonderful professor. Very chill and you do end up learning a lot of information by just listening to her speak. She plays a lot of videos to help with the topics. Just ask questions and answer hers and it's an easy A class but if you don't engage with her you will have a harder time. Great Professor 10/10

She basically read the slides even though she said she wouldn't. I once asked for help on hw I did to get ahead and all she said was we'll learn about it next week but I needed help because the question was worded weird. I also did the review too fast for her liking and she took off 25% and dropped my final grade to 89%
Very chill, easy going professor. Lots of group work, 2 take home exams and a project. I had her for MGMT 385, same exact structure. Show up to class, participate and u will easily get a good grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Graded by few things--Group projects

reviews.comment: Nice professor. There are 3 exams, and the lowest exam is dropped, and a final exam. There is homework through accounting lab and a final review guide which is graded for completion. She goes through PowerPoints quickly during the lectures so make sure you ask questions and also read the chapter in the book to better understand the concepts.

For her class, you will have three exams and a final. She is a nice person, but not an effective teacher. She goes over materials super fast and is not very good at explaining. Be prepared to become an independent learner.

Literally learned nothing from this course but it was extremely easy to get an A. She is caring and will work with you. Lectures are boring and it seems as though she does not prepare at all. If you are looking to boost your grade and need this credit take it with Medicus!

Professor Medicus is a super nice person. Someone that you can tell has a genuinely kind soul. That being said, Ive learned NOTHING from her class. Her lectures are extremely unorganized and lack meaning. I often ask myself in class, what are we talking about?? Super easy a, but if you enjoy learning I wouldnt recommend.
lots of group work, mundane lectures but respectable, nice, and fair professor

3 Exams (lowest one dropped), gives random extra credit, attendance req., gives a final review packet (worth 15% of grade, based on completion). Overall an easy class , not a fan of her class reverse setting with the whole group work. If you study the check-list of end chapters and the review packet answers she gives you'll be set to pass.

Nice lady. She cares for her students, always ready to help. The class has 3 online take-home exams (drops the lowest one) and a common final. Attendance is mandatory. She gives worksheet to work in groups. There are online HW. She reads from the slides, so lectures can be boring and hard to understand sometimes. Take her if you want to get an A.

Professor Medicus is a adjunct professor. She lectures at the beginning of the week then gives out work the end of the week. She often just sits in the front of class staring at her phone or computer. She doesn't do a good job of ensuring student understanding. She is rarely available outside of class. Her lectured are just reading powerpoints.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--EXTRA CREDIT--So many papers

reviews.comment: very nice professor and very easy going. take her class for mgmt 385 and you will learn alot about ethics. easy A. take home exams and there is only 2

She is a interesting professor who is baffled by her own planning of lectures. An example, hands out a single worksheet to be done in 3-4 lectures while for those exact ones shes on her phone. Acts like she knows what shes doing toward the end of each class but honestly doesnt know what the next lecture going to be. Lets you redo exams!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: In my experience with Accounting professors at UMBC, she is one of the better ones. She encourages asking questions and I feel like doing questions in groups helps us understand better. Yes, she just reads off the slides but which accounting professor doesn't? Choose her and get your good grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: Professor Medicus is one of the best professors you can have at UMBC. She's caring, thoughtful, and always happy to help. You should have no problems passing (most get As and Bs) as long as you come to class and participate in the group activities and group project. You must take her!

Hands out doobie points that decides whether she will curve your final grade or not. All exams are online (except final) and she doesn't hand out homework every week like other professors. Classes are an even mix between her lecturing and group work. Allows us to work out problems in class together instead of listening to her talk all the time.
NO exams. Just 2 papers and that's it.

Professor Medicus is a very good accounting professor.  She's actively participating in the field, which means she is able to give you the book version and the real-life version.  The only detriment is the department-mandated grade threshold on the final exam to pass the course, but that's not her fault.  Great prof, looking forward to 122.

Professor Medicus really makes accounting interesting! She also has her CPA so she teaches you what the book says and what really happens in real accounting life. You do the homework, take the 2 online exams, and attend class everyday then you'll do well. Unfortunately, the final exam is by the department and you must get a 50% to pass the class

Attend every class. Do every homework. Ace the two exams. Study study and study. Ask questions. Look at YouTube tutorials. Note each formula as you progress through the course, will be helpful for the final exam. She is an amazing professor and she really cares about her students. Definitely recommended.

Lots of online hw which was easy, 2 online exams that were also kind of easy, and extra credit is offered to cushion your grade. She goes extremely fast during class and reads off PPTs. The final review packet really helps you understand (or memorize) the material to pass the hard final. Just do the HW, study the review materials, and you'll pass!

Medicus was an ok professor. I had her for ECON 121 and again for ECON 122. She only reads off the slides and makes you do pointless group work. Tests are online and easy. But if you fail the final you fail the class. Like someone else said if you want to learn something don't take her, but if you want an easy A go for it.
BEST I'VE EVER MEET

Accounting is not an easy subject but she has a positive attitude that is encouraging. She speeds through powerpoints created by the book publisher. READ THE BOOK before every class! Group work was extremely helpful. As an adjunct, she does not have scheduled office hours but is willing to arrange meetings before and after class.
Boring class, but goes extremely easy on tests. Take this if you want an easy Accounting class. She's also a very sweet grandmotherly-type woman.

Easily one of the better accounting instructors. The class isn't difficult and the group work helps, but she flies through the lecture when working out problems. Attendance isn't mandatory, but helps w/ final grade. You must pass final with >50% in order to pass the class. Homework & exams are online and require an accounting lab subscription.

Had her for accounting 2 over the summer. Overall, an easy class. Tests are online and she gives you 4 hours to complete them (you can start and stop as many times as you want). The final study guide really helps for the departmental final.

The whole class she reads off of powerpoints and makes you do useless group work, all assignments are on online. It doesnt matter if you have a A in the class, if you fail the final you fail the class "/

Useless professor. Just straight powerpoint reading. Had her for accounting 122 and got an A in that class also. If you want an easy A, sign up for Medicus, but if you want to learn I would avoid her. The auditing class has take home exams (the only time I used my book), a group presentation, and a few homeworks but she never collected them.

She is very helpful and tries to work with every student. The course is not easy so studying is key. Having most of the course online helps keep your grade a float but the final is a doozy. Good luck!

Really good teacher that cares about her students. The exams are hard but if you come to class and study you will be fine. The departmental final is super hard, but it's not her fault. Does multiple examples in class while going thought the chapter. Probably one of the best professors at umbc.

Shes a great professor for someone starting out acctng class. 2 exams plus a hard departmental finals. exams are easy. come to class, you'll do fine. grp work and exercises is a must to master the exams!
She clearly knows the material very well. Easy class IF you read ahead of time plus do the homework. Her exams are ok, departmental final is hard!

Knows material, but ineffective teaching it - textbook replaces rapid-fire and unhelpful PowerPoint lectures. On-line work tedious and picky with answers. Shouts while teaching as if in lecture hall; irritating. No good 121 instructors exist; sadly, she's a better instructor than most. Depend on textbook for final exam. Offers extra credit - DO IT.
Attendance is mandatory for a class that could be entirely online.  Group work is pointless and exams are terrible preparation for the accounting final.

attendance mandatory. Doesn't give out much online homework. Group work on random days. She teaches by basically going over powerpoint and doing some problems in class. Exams aren't too bad, just study. Her exams don't really compare to the departmental final which is a lot harder so be prepared for that.

Make sure you read the book, because that will help you understand what she's talking about more. She talks from powerpoints most days, which is not helpful. Her tests are multiple choice and fill in the blank. The second one is harder and the final is ridiculously hard, so study. Idk if theres a better prof for acct 1 but if there is, take them

She basically teaches straight from the book and you do problems out of it sometimes in groups. Group isn't bad, actually helps more than she does. She reads off a powerpoint with is useless. Make sure you bring the book to every class, and she takes attendance which you'll need for participation credit.
All the tests are multiple choice so it makes it harder (but curves).

If you want to know the material, she is NOT an effective teacher.  The class is boring, because personally, powerpoint is not the way to teach it.  She is a passive teacher, who appears as if she is only there because it pays the bills.  If you just want an A, she is the one.  Her tests are so easy, they are stupid- but the common final is not!
Half the class is her quickly going over powerpoint slides and the other half doing problems from the book. She takes attendance, but offers extra credit and curves exams.
Very flexible. I love her. I've had her for 2 classes.

Really nice prof. But all over the place. Not clear in her teaching if accounting isn't your thing. 2nd exam she had to curve 15 points because most of the class failed it. Then gave 30 points extra credit assignment extremely difficult to help offset the grade. If Acct isn't ur thing, take with another prof.
great teacher!
Cool Professor, exams are easy, but she goes through the powerpoint really fast

Although all ECON courses are based on PowerPoints, she did a good job explaining, relating to real life events.  We used the textbook just for reading, but with PowerPoints, you don't really need to read.  She is now my boss, and she's so chill, laid back!
Dude if you get her, may God be with you. She is too scattered and expects you to be composed and organized

I enjoyed this class and the professor. The class can be boring if you don't like learning about policy and the government but it's not too hard. Midterm and finals are written assignments, a two-part paper, and weekly quizzes; you must participate in class. She cares about her students and will help you outside of class if needed!

The most unaccommodating and condescending Professor I've ever had at UMBC. I only took this class out of personal interest and boy do i regret it. Exams are quite simple while, ironically, attendance and participation is heavy and worth too many points. I only took this class out of personal interest and boy do i regret it
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: I would advise against taking a class with her for your own well-being. Despite my enjoyment of writing, she made me feel like I was a terrible writer. She is a tough grader without clear reasons, often giving bad grades simply because your paper doesn't align with her specific expectations. I hope to never have her as a proessor  again.

Dr. Mellinger is by far my favorite professor at UMBC. If you are a social work major, take her class. She is super knowledgable and passionate about policy/ advocacy. She is also really kind and willing to meet with students about their work and will try to support you in any way. She is a tough grader but she prepares you with specified rubrics.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: I love Dr.Mellinger. I took her for SOWK 260, 360, and 376. She is a tough grader but mostly on her writing assignments but she gives a clear rubric so as long as you follow it you should be fine. Her exams are not bad, all the information comes directly from her power points and from discussions we had in class. She wants her students to succeed.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Dr. Mellinger is great as a person first. She also is quite harsh about her grading however she is really passionate about IPV and she really challenged us. We did do some fun activities and she tried to be as positive as she could considering the topic. Overall, she's a tough professor but if you can make it good for you.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Dr mellinger is a great lecturer and very knowledgeable but a very harsh grader and will find faults with your work. Lots of work in this course, readings, podcasts, news. Attendance is mandatory and the size of the class is much smaller since so many have dropped it at this point. Passing is not impossible, if you are up for the challenge take her
really hard grader would not take her again
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: One of the harder graders I've had. She doesn't just give you an easy A, she expects you to participate for a participation grade so you have to read all of the material she gives you. She also made us listen to the news to participate. Papers were graded kind of tough, and I fought hard for my grade. There were lots of group discussions as well.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Dr Mellinger is an incredible professor who demonstrates the ability to lead a class better than most professors I have encountered online. While she is very strict with her writing expectations and APA format, she is an amazing professor in the SOWK program. Writing intensive, and reading is definitely beneficial. Stay current on the news!

If you don't know APA, you will learn it. Writing & reading heavy w/ weekly chapter quizzes from text, podcasts, Voicethreads, & articles. Discussion-open lectures; participation counts. You need to do the readings & elaborate on them for discussion board entries & writing assignments. Text is used for 260 & 360; free online PDF.
She's really sweet and WANTS to help so take advantage of this!! She is a tough grader but overall shes an amazing professor!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Tough grader

reviews.comment: She's a great lecturer but also the toughest grader you will ever have. If you have her be prepared to do A LOT of research. If you don't follow every direction to the T and have a source for every claim in your paper you won't have a good time. If you can't handle a tough grader maybe don't have her as a first option if you can help it.

Professor Mellinger is a great professor and is very passionate about the subject. However, her class is fairly challenging and she is a very tough grader. With this being said, she gives good feedback and she does want all her students to succeed in her class.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Do not take this Professor. She is unaccommodating and grades so harshly. The amount of assignments she gives is uncalled for. She seems to forget that we have other classes and responsibilities. Awful.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--So many papers--Tough grader

reviews.comment: I'm sure she could be a great professor for a lot of people. Unfortunately, she's incredibly, incredibly rulebound and inflexible--which can be really tough when combined with even small miscommunications. This is the kind of professor who would fail you for turning in a paper five minutes after midnight unless you were in the hospital.

Professor Mellinger is a good teacher. She wants her students to do well and gives good feedback on essays. There are 4 essays -- book critique, policy paper, and poster, midterm and final. Don't expect her to lecture on the powerpoints! There are two group work activities which were nice. It allows students to get to know one another.

Dr. Mellinger is intelligent and passionate about her work. She is knowledgable and available and really wants her students to succeed. Attendance and participation are required, but she balances lecture with homework very well. If you have an option between her and another professor, I recommend her.

Professor Mellinger is one of the BEST professors at UMBC. She may be on the difficult side as a professor but she is open to help you on your assignments if it is needed. She gives good feedback. Participation matters in her class. I would definitely recommend her to anyone.
Dr. Mellinger might just be the best professor at UMBC. Her classes are challenging yet rewarding! She gives amazing feedback, and shes always around-ready to help students! She is a true gem.
Nice teacher, Great lectures, AMAZINGLY harsh grader. Nothing less than perfect grammar is acceptable for her papers.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Great professor, great lectures! Easy to reach outside of class, really cares about the subject. Has a lot of experience outside the field. Be sure you check your APA style for papers!
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: As long as you participate in class and do not miss more than two days you will be fine.  She is very strict on APA grammar so be sure to cite things properly. She goes out of her way to help you with any concerns or questions you may have. She does not give extra credit so be prepared to ace her exams and papers. TAKE HER!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Gives good feedback--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: Awesome professor, great class!

She's a wonderful teacher! She will discuss anything with anyone and will listen with an unbiased opinion. My lecture was once a week for 2.5 hours and I wish it was longer! One exam, one final, two papers (3-5pg and 8-10pg). She is so willing to help her students out in any way she can. Though, if you miss two classes, your grade drops by a letter
Great teacher- make sure to take part in the class as you are graded for your participation.

Dr. Mellinger is happy to explain anything that is not clear. She is willing to take time after class or in her office to sit down to help with whatever you need. If you're taking her class, you better know APA style writing to the tee because she is like the APA police and will pick your papers apart.
xxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxx

The material is difficult, there is nothing the professor can do about that. He does a great job at explaining the material, and was helpful during office hours. The workload was pretty heavy for a 3 credit class, but it isn't the professors fault we have so much to go over. Quizzes were difficult, and grades were not regularly posted.
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: He's passionate but doesn't teach well. He does not go through any examples and his slides are copy pasted from the book - which he just regurgitates. He expects you to know the material before he teaches it and grades homework very harshly . Exams have very specific questions that are impossible to answer unless you knew beforehand.

Awesome Professor! He is probably the most intelligent professor in the CSEE department  within Electromagnetics, and has a passion for teaching. He is very clear, and is very organized. If you truly do your homework, the exams will be easy. Enjoy this class, you will never have a CMPE class this organized ever again

Flat out the worst professor I've had the misfortune of having. He takes shorthand notes from the textbook and transcribes them onto the black board. You're better off staying in the dorm and reading the textbook.

Great professor! He obviously has a passion for what he's teaching. The lectures are straight out of the book and he doubles back to make sure students understand. When you go to his office he is very approachable. Tests and pop quizzes aren't easy, but if you understand the lectures and homework,it's an A. He also gives you the past exams to study

He's out to destroy you, if you're in Mechanical Engineering. He took over from Bourner during the beginning of the semester, and turned the class into a test anxiety nightmare. His notes are on Blackboard, but don't expect to learn anything; his explanation of Bode diagrams is useless. The class average for the final was 22%.

one of the few professors who actually gives enough credit for hw assignments. they are long but worth a good part of your grade. very knowledgable and wants you to learn but the material can be difficult
complete waste of time... he talks abt how great he is n thats about it... very bad person to teach... he throws incredibly hard problems in exams
Grading is extremely arbitrary, he does fail people but gives people with 5 points higher final scores Bs. Relies heavily on powerpoint slides.

graet guy. has lot of enthusiasm about the material. he tries to help you out as much as he can and he gives a grade that you deserve. NOBODY FAILS IN HIS CLASS unless you dont do anything. Go to his lectures and go to his office hours. I got a D with Dr. Yan but I got an A with Menyuk. Exam questions are staright from text's examples.
class is hard.but he gives your grade that you deserved.In my class nobody got fail. but you have to do his HW and Assigment even Assigment are not going to effect in your final grade.

AVOID-> take Artola. If you are forced into this, prepare to kiss ass, he plays super favorites and gives your grade based on who you are. "I'm not here to teach, I'm here to supplement the book" - direct quote, no lie, my jaw dropped when he

The topic is already difficult, not to mention the professor doesn't help.  He writes notes on the board directly out of the text word for word. He might as well tell the students to sit down for an hour and read the book.  Would not recommend!

Very hard to understand, makes an already boring, difficult topic unbearable! He's very quirky in a way that makes him hard to understand.You HAVE to read the material before class to get an idea of whats goin on.

Very interesting class, exams are overly difficult to the point where almost the whole class complained about exam 1. Was over 8 pages and contained material that wasn't dived into deeply. Professor quotes assignments will be graded in a week, mind you it has been a month and semester is almost over, the only graded assignment is project 0.

Professor Mironov has high expectations for her students and that is always a good thing if you're serious about taking the class. Projects and tests may seem quite too much to handle but they will help you learn and grow immensely. She will always lend a helping hand if you need it. Another thing about her class is that her TAs are top-notch.

She has good intentions, but her priorities are not teaching. She is always busy doing something else and her TA picks up the slack. Lectures are underprepared textbook slides. She does lectures in a fast monotone voice (bad for notes) and doesn't take criticism well. She hasn't dealt with the material hands on in years, tough to learn from.

Professor Mironov makes OS fun and challenging! She is friendly and kind and makes every effort to engage students and prepare them for careers. The projects are great opportunities to practice low-level programming and independent thinking. They also come with clear, reasonable rubrics and amazing TA support. This class was a wonderful experience!
Most chill professor, super caring, and super understanding. If you get the chance to take a class with her, definitely do so.

The best OS professor at UMBC. Projects were hard, but support from her and (some) TAs will help you tons. Cares about all of her students, and notes those who comes to class, though attendance was not mandatory. This is the only professor with which you will actually learn something for this class. Would take again, and any other classes with her.

Knowledgeable and accessible outside of class. Expects a lot from students, but adjusts grading to reflect what people can do. Projects are a moving target, so you never know what is really required. Two of them will make you cry. Tries to structure projects to prepare you for jobs. Gives great career advice, funny, and cares about students

Projects are extremely disorganized, project requirements are confusing and changes often. Don't start the project early since parts of the document might change in a few days meaning you have to restart. Every time you get your project grades you have to fight for you points you lost like you're trying to win back custody of your child.

couldn't even bring myself to selecting a tag for this course....as a child i thought i only had to worry about monsters under my bed, didn't know that this class would be my biggest nightmare. so incredibly disorganized, its insane.

Projects are insanely disorganized and unclear. When the prof asked for feedback in class, we had to convince her to add a rubric so we could have an understanding of what is expected of the project. Lectures are heavy but bearable. These projects are just way too much thrown at you at once.

About 3 weeks in & this professor does not know how to keep project 0 organized. Gives "pop exams" (1 week notice only) and no where on the syllabus does it give us a date for the 5 exams/tests we have. TA's flat out say they can't help or "don't know what's going on" for the introductory project, which is unreasonable.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Amazing Professor! Highly Recommend. The class has exams but they are not grade heavy at all. She will stay up late at night answering project questions on discord. She responds to emails fast and overall truly cares about wanting to see her students succeed.

Overall, Prof. Mironov was a great professor. In her lectures, she used analogies and drawings to help students understand complex topics. Projects were challenging, but she took the time after class to help me understand what was being asked. Prof. was very responsive to students and adjusted projects and deadlines to benefit us.

Professor Mironov is one of the most caring professors I've ever had. She is very friendly and understanding. She cares about her students and gives extensions if the courseload is overwhelming She is even supportive during exams often giving extensions for assignments during exam week. She is just amazing. It's like having a friend as a teacher.

Hands down the best OS professor. She's new, but she knows her stuff and how to teach it. The projects are SUPER hard, but gives you so many resources including her own videos. She's on Discord every day answering questions.  When I stopped showing up, she reached out to check on me. She actually cares and wants you to succeed, but its OS.

Professor Sanaa Mironov was a great professor to be teaching about this topic. Operating systems contain a lot of crucial information, but her lecturing style and being able to speak to her about the class content helped a lot with working on the projects and taking the exams. Taking the course with her made the class really enjoyable.

Literally the easiest class and I got a 99%. Low effort needed and she made it even easier with the easy grading. There was however a final group paper that was 6-8 pages long and a couple other essays but rarely any homework besides that.

Professor Mironov was very disorganized and frustrating to keep up with. Projects are often unfinished close to deadlines, her lectures are mostly reading from slides, and announcements/schedule changes are always late. While I first enjoyed the class structure, it soon fell apart leading to constant confusion from the whole class at times.
This is one of the best class I have ever taken.

She was a very kind teacher and took the time to get to know everyone. This class is difficult but she made learning the concepts easy by going through everything and putting all the material on blackboard. The tests were easy but the projects were tough. She does not assign homework and you only have to do the projects. JOIN THE CLASS DISCORD!!!!!

Sanaa is very nice.  Project organization was iffy at times but she was very accommodating.  4 exams and projects which is all you're graded on.  She is very open to feedback to help her be a better professor, so assume that what you hear from reviews will get better over time.
reviews.rating_tags: Caring--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Most difficult CMSC class at UMBC, Prof and Tompkins were very helpful and kind for SP24 semester. No final exam, 4 tests and 4 projects only. While I'd rate both Tompkins and Mironov as 4-4.5/5, the project organization was pretty rough and unclear at times. Regardless, Prof. Mironov went above and beyond when possible. Definitely harder than 341

Lectures were dense, and exams were multiple choice with no curve. Class was difficult, but I thought Dr. Starz-Gaiano was good. Make sure you don't miss the lectures, you get points for participation in in-class polls. Plays music related to the topic before class starts, which is fun.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: She was very nice but her tests were extremely hard and there is no rounding at the end!
Exams are extremely difficult and lectures are very slide heavy meaning there's soooo much information you could be tested on.
Exams are impossible and will determine your whole grade
TERRIBLE EXAMS

knowledgable professor. she is good at explaining topics. however her slides are terrible, they are just pictures. you need to go to lecture if you want to know what's going on in class. her exams are pretty tough as well
Different topics, papers, one presentation, good quizzes.

Great professor. Clearly explains literature papers and helps you understand difficult findings. Makes a huge effort to make the class fun, and clearly enjoys teaching. If I wasn't graduating this year I would try to take another elective with this professor. Exams are fair and reasonable.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Class is extremely hard because of the extensive memorization the class topic requires. However, Dr. Starz-Gaiano a at least makes it enjoyable to go to class and comes up with great didactic ways to help us remember difficult processes. She is very good at explaining and really understanding.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: This class is hard and you really have to pay attention in their lectures. Their lectures were very heavy but overall good class and professor.

One of the most caring and kind professors I have ever had. An incredibly smart woman that just wants her students to do well. Exams are more than fair if you pay attention to the lectures and homework. So accesible and helpful in such a hard class. Would definitely take again.

Dr. SG was a great teacher, she took time to answer questions in class and clicker questions modeled what would be on the test pretty well. Exams were hard, but if you use lectures as a guide for review textbook material it isn't too bad. Her questions were very application based as well, so if you know the material well it shouldn't be too hard.

Dr. Starz-Gaiano is amazing. She really cares about her students and wants them to learn. Explains material very well, in a way that is easy to understand (even though cell bio is very tough). Very clear about what she expects you to know, and makes a big emphasis on understanding, rather than memorizing. The lectures and her laugh are hilarious

You can tell she really cares about her students. There were a lot of paper readings for this class, followed by a big term paper. Good feedback on writing. Her goal in this class is really just to make her students scientifically literate and prepare them for the field. Nice Prof, would take again.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Respected--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: She is an excellent professor but her exams are really hard, one of those kinds that you will expect on the MCAT Biology section. Her exam questions are mostly application based with their application in real laboratory settings.

Expect lots of reading from the textbook. We covered about 18 chapters in the course. Her lectures consist of PP slides that bounce from various topics so it can get confusing. Her exam questions were multiple choice but very complex. Avg class grade on exams were around 60%.
Super fun professor! She's very sweet and encouraging!! I would definitely take her other classes!

One of the best professors I 've ever had. One warning, she goes over the lecture material really fast so it's best to read before class to follow her. Despite that. she takes time to get you to think about the material deeply even though the class is like 300 people.  I think she is an amazing human being and a role model.
She is an incredibly intelligent, kind, and helpful professor.  The kind of person you would want to stay in touch with long after finishing college.

She is a nice person, but this course is not easy and it is one of the famous tough courses of Bio major. Her lectures are basically reading over slides, but she is clear about the information she needs you to learn and understand. Her exams are fair. Sometimes, she uses an acitivity to teach you a specific topic which makes you remember forever.

Her slides aren't super well organized but I really appreciated Dr. Starz-Gaiano's energy and enthusiasm for cell biology. Her questions made sense and weren't nearly as tricky as Rosenberg's. Overall, a really great professor!

ridiculous. to do well, you need to memorize every single detail or everything handed out and given to you. I couldn't do it, given my other classes.she doesn't guide your studying and she expects us to remember sizes of molecules and asks a lot of experimental/ graph analysis questions that dont test our understanding of the material/interest us.

She's intelligent, kind, and tries to make class interesting. That said, cell bio is HARD. I was very overwhelmed with the amount of information expected in this class. She reads off her slides and loves talking about experiments and scales. Be ready or run far away.

This class is difficult because it involves too much memorization, and most of the exam questions are tricky. If you like memorizing every single detail, this class will probably be easy for you. However, this class does not give you any skills that can be applied further, most of what you learn will be forgotten very soon.

She's a kind, helpful and resourceful professor who takes care of answering any questions and always willing to help.  The material is tough and she goes really really really fast in lecture.  Covers lots.  I can't stress how fast she goes! Read the book, go to discussion and ask questions.  Do not fall behind.
Amazing!

Everyone makes her out to be horrible, but she really is not that bad.  I think she is way better than the other prof.  She is very intelligent and knows a lot about cell bio. Her lectures are very straightforward.  Study her slides and read in the book to get the most out of the class. Exams are not that bad if you study.

Fantastic professor; one of the few that actually cares about students. Extremely intelligent but does not utilize this in an intimidating way.  She is extremely helpful and always willing to explain things to clarity (one just has to ask questions and try..which is a major lacking in people that may do poorly in her class). Very fair with grading.

i love this professor! i took her for cell bio last semester, and she really helped me understand the material as best I could. While this class is difficult because of the content, she is very helpful and explains it well. tests are fairly straightforward after studying, far better than other cell bio profs. highly recommend!
I lost hair, time, sanity and almost dropped out of UMBC because of her. She needs to be removed from the school.  University needs to rethink their hiring policy.

Her course was very disorganized and her instructions were always unclear, and when asked to clarify she would just make things more confusing. Her rubrics were not specific and she graded assignments extremely late. Genuinely the worst professor I have had.

Very disorganized. Gave us an unfinished syllabus. Makes a lot of grammar mistakes in her emails and announcements despite being an English professor. Deducts points if you don't write something the way she wants it, even if it's correct by English standards. Only good thing is that there are a lot of extra credit opportunities

She is by far the WORST teacher I have EVER encountered. Classes are unbelievably disorganized, she very clearly does not plan, consistently gets confused about what is happening in class, and EVERY class is a waste of time. I cannot begin to describe how poor of an experience her class was, and would NEVER recommend ANYONE to take her class.

Worst professor ever. Awful, disorganized and provides no help. Anytime you need help, her response is "sorry not my job". 
She will penalize you for everything she has an opportunity to penalize you for. 
If you don't want your grade to tank along with your mental health then I would NOT recommend.

Her class isn't hard and is very manageable if you put in the effort. Her instructions were a little hard to understand, but if you are confused, don't be afraid to ask questions because she'll happily answer them. She's pretty flexible if you need extra time on an assignment. Overall, an understanding professor and an achievable A.

If you value your sanity and your gpa, DO NOT take this class PLEASE. She is not flexible at all to the slightest and it's like she really has no regard for the students grades. She grades things late, she won't allow you to redo an assignment off a mistake and she's disorganized. AVOID THIS PROFESSOR AT ALL COST.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Professor Raj is an incredible instructor who genuinely cares about her students. Her assignments may seem tough at first, but with effort, you'll earn full credit. She offers extra credit opportunities and is always approachable and willing to help. Put in the work, and an easy A is within reach!

I swear by the Almighty this is the worst prof/teacher I ever had in my life. Lectures in slow motion, docks for attendance points, rubric is super broad and unclear. She shows examples of a job presentation. The example is a blank slide with text that reads "show your skills". Rubric is unclear and she's hard to understand. Super picky grader to.

The professor is very hard to understand during class and is never thorough with her work. Usually you have to figure out what you're doing in class by yourself. There is also no way of understanding the teacher during class. She does not speak clearly and you can barely hear her while she's speaking.

Difficult to talk with and such a hard grader. Makes directions unclear when in class but attendance is mandatory and is part of your grade. It is hard to understand her because of her accent and her directions for things are even more unclear. It took forever to get through one essay which caused us to be behind the syllabus every week.

WORST PROFESSOR EVER. She is unorganized and makes an easy course in rocket science. Deduct points for tardiness even though she is late. Dates are set for things and we never do them. The grade is deducted even if you followed her rubric. Do not put in a grade till the end of the semester. AVOID THIS PROFESSOR AT ALL COST!!!!!!!!!!!!
Course materials isn't very clear
Very confusing teacher. Her advice would always go in circles and she was never flexible with students about how to handle certain topics. Do not take her class AT ALL

Such an awful professor. It is a miracle of god that this professor has been able to teach at all. She is an embarrassment to UMBC and is so simple-minded. Yet everything she does has to have a layer of complexity beyond what her 3 brain cells can handle causing her not even to understand what she is grading on herself. Switch classes ASAP

Yeah no dont take her course, she is incredibly awful. She talks a lot but says absolutely nothing. When you ask for help or advice she talks in circles and when you finish youre left more confused than you were. She waits until the end of the semester to grade assignments and she grades harsh. I am genuinely surprised how she became a professor.

this guy is amazing. look I know you've seen all the reviews about how good he is. and I have to agree he's amazing. as long as you actually show up to class and read a sentence or 2 when he asks you, you'll pass 100% guaranteed. what an amazing professor. truly a 10/10. I will say Tho please dont take his class around 5-7. I was fasting @ the time

bit of a harsh grader. you have to review each assignment with him to make sure that it is exactly to his liking. but, he is nice and lenient in terms of due dates. plenty of extra credit opportunities

This dude was a great professor. Very lenient with grading and interactive in lectures. Easily approachable and willing to help whenever you have confusions. Assignments were pretty straightforward as well, putting any decent amount of effort should earn you a B. That being said I don't know what I have yet but I definitely know I didn't fail.

Professor Shane helped me not only learn how to be a better writer and reader, but made my first semester of college enjoyable by assigning the right amount of work!

He responds to emails extremely quick (weekends and evenings, too)!

He shows up to every class prepared and always radiating positivity!

A professor who really cares about his kids.
All around pretty good
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--EXTRA CREDIT--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: One of the most genuine professors I've had. Cared about each student, always gave feedback, always in his office, always ready to smile. Held great conversations, and any disputes you had he would settle directly in front of you. Very easy grader as well so long as you but effort into your work.

I struggled with writing in high school, but found my joy in Prof. Moritz's class. He is funny, encouraging, and explains concepts well. He is regularly available during office hours, even helping me during his lunchtime well past his designated hours, showing a genuine care for his students. 

He is not only a good professor but also a good man.
Great guy and an understanding professor who really cares. The only downside is he picks students at random to answer or read, which can catch you off guard.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: When I remember Prof Moritz, I first think about how kind he is and how much he shows that he values every student. I would especially recommend this class to a first-year student who is maybe nervous about entering college.

for this being ENGL 100 it has a LOT of work. prof moritz is HILARIOUS, hes just like sikowitz from victorious. you have to really try hard to get an A. you will need to revise your papers a lot and make sure he likes it.

Moritz, though friendly, makes ENGL100 harder than it should be. His grading standards are too subjective (students have to "surprise" him in order to get a 10/10). He deducts points w/o explanation and is reluctant to give anyone a 100. If you take him, be sure to take advantage of every extra-credit opportunity. And be prepared to hear profanity.

If you want to get a good grade in this class then be prepared to genuinely put in the work for the assignments. Passionate guy, but VERY particular abt what he looks for when grading. His feedback isn't always clear along w explanations to it. He will assign a new essay 1.5 weeks before the previous essay is due, and expects u to have finished
He's the sweetest! He makes class so much fun and creates an enjoyable environment that makes you want to come to class.
He is genuinely a good guy, and as long as you complete the assignments with effort, you should get an A. Participation matters, and you can tell he cares about his students. Would highly reccommend.

He has been a wonderful professor that is always available outside of class. Always provided clear instructions to projects and is very passionate about what he is teaching. 10/10 would def recommend.
Professor Shane Moritz is so interesting. His classes are so fun. And he is so quirky, which is so endearing. He is clearly passionate about what he teaches.

His class is amazing. Took it for my english credit. There are a couple papers w peer review thats very helpful. There is a fun group presentation and single presentation, very quick tho, nothing to worry abt. No tests. never had a teacher like this before. very fun!! Enthusiastic

Very enthusiastic and passionate. Sometimes he can be confusing because he can be a little jumpy but a great teacher. Also a lot of peer reviewing which was very helpful and made it easier to get closer to classmates. Mr. Shane gives a lot of feedback on papers and it is always very helpful. I loved taking his class! Also don't but the books.

Beware of peer reviews, they do not give you much so it is worse when he swoops in and tells you that your essay is terrible. I have had to rewrite two essays because he made me scrap my thesis. Semi-entertaining in class, a very particular guy. Only 5 essays which was kind of a lot
Very outgoing and made class interesting.

One of my favorites at UMBC. I really enjoyed this class and I looked forward to it. The essays that we did felt unique and fun, so there was at least 1 essay you would enjoy during this class. I wish I needed another english credit so I could take it again

I would NOT take him again. He was very nice, but his grading criteria is not clear at all. He takes random points off without explanation. He is an extremely tough grader. If you are taking his class good luck.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--So many papers--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: It's an easy A as long as you manage your time well and put in the effort, because the papers can be pretty time consuming. He does offer extra credit for a lot of them though. He's very eccentric and engaging, and he gives good feedback on your papers. I really enjoyed his class
Great teacher
If you are taking ENGL 100, take it with Moritz. If you put in the work you will do well, he will give you thoughtful feedback, and his assignments are creative and fun to write.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I really enjoyed this class. He makes class interesting and engaging. His grading criteria are clear because he also provides a sample of papers that got an A from previous years. There are two creative projects to boost your grade. He also offers extra credit. Use his feedback to improve your paper to get a good grade. Highly recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Professor was vey kind and lively. He was a harsh grader and took off points randomly sometimes but it was pretty easy to just get back with extra credit since he offered it for most assignments. Papers were fun and included different literary structures.

He helps a lot with the 5 major papers that we do and sometimes gives extra credit. Make sure you follow his feedback because that will boost your grade. The assignments require a lot of effort and time. Lectures are pretty fun and he is lenient. The assignments are not extremely difficult but he is a tough grader. Easy to pass.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: I am very conflicted with Mr. Shane. His classes are anything but boring, which I respect greatly. However, his policies on attendance and attitude towards student frustration, infuriated me at times. He gives a lot of homework, usually with vague instructions. However, the structure of his class and the group work, allowed me to excel and learn
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He's really cool! Is very understanding if you have and mental health things going on and is willing to help you stay on track! He also gives good feedback on papers and does have a lot of peer review/editing before turning in the major papers. Has precise grading criteria & if you follow his instruction ==> good grades on the papers and the class!

Professor Moritz is the best prof I've ever had! Papers are reviewed like three times before the final paper deadline so, there are a lot of chances to improve essays. Really funny and responds to emails super fast.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: For Mr. Moritz, attendance is important, but his lectures are pretty engaging. He's very witty but a pretty funny professor. He provides examples and feedback for most of the major papers. He appreciates student feedback and works on helping to establish a good writing foundation for his students.

Attendance is important, but his lectures are pretty engaging. He's pretty clear about his expectations for papers and provides examples that show the structure that he's looking for. He also gives feedback before you turn in the paper so if you listen to that you're golden.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Clear grading criteria--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Best professor I ever had. Gives you a good feedback on essays etc. He is very respectful and it is such a fun class. Gives you fun activities to do. Definitely recommend anyone to take this class.

It's an English class so obviously, there's gonna be 3-4 papers, but he was an easy grader and was so fun to be around. I loved being in his class and actually waited for class to start bc I loved it so much. DEFINITELY take this class if you can

Professor Moritz was an amazing teacher! The writing projects he assigned were varied and he kept his lectures entertaining. He was open to requests for extensions on papers as long as you made a real effort to do your best in his class. Definitely my favorite professor that semester!
Really good professor, just make sure your not sleeping and active during class and its an A. Dont listen to the dude at the bottom, he was probably one of the ones sleeping during class...
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring

reviews.comment: Mr. Moritz is a great English teacher, I enjoyed going to his class a lot. He is funny, caring and will make you participate in class. However, he does give a lot of assignments, they are long and you have to put effort into the class and work hard if you want an A. In the end, you will 100% improve and develop your writing skills.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Participation matters--SO MANY PAPERS

reviews.comment: Best English professor I have ever had. I was not good at English in high school but it is totally making sense now. The notes on your drafts are actually helpful and not just like circling a spelling error or something like that. I thought he was kind of weird at first but in a good way. The book is only used like 4 times, so get an old edition.

Worse professor I have ever had in my entire college career. I know people who take him during the Fall seem to have a better experience, but his Spring class is absolute h*ll. Don't know why this varies. Take anyone else. Please. He is terrible and unprofessional. He brings in politics, has inappropriate assignments, and more. Avoid.

One of the best classes I have taken at UMBC. Attendance not required but extra credit will be given if you show up to majority of the classes. Exams are all take home and 75% of your grade, but you are expected to be in depth and source the class readings. The rest are assignments revolving around the shields you make. Do the work and you'll pass!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Test heavy

reviews.comment: I have so much fun in Dr. Jones-Lewis' classes. They're not easy but she offers so much insight into ancient Rome beyond just having students read the Latin texts. If you're on the fence about intermediate Latin, I highly recommend going for it, her classes are so delightful. Be mindful of declensions, cases, etc. and prepare properly before class.
Dr. JL is very kind and accommodating. It's an easy class but is pretty interesting.

she is super knowledgeable and her grading criteria is pretty easy. you have 3 or 4 exams they are open note and you have an entire week to do them half the exam is multiple choice and then the other half is essay questions. There aren't many other grades in the course and she does expect you to be pretty knowledgeable for the exam.

Lectures were intersting and it's very obvious she is super passionate about ancient Rome and history in general. All of the assignments are very straight forward and as long as you pay attention in class and read the required readings they're all very easy. Assignments can take a while to be graded, but she'll grade yours sooner if you ask nicely.

Amazing Professor! She's so caring and understanding. We are graded by 3 Quizzes, a midterm, and a Final. Very easy course with playback recordings. Everything in the Lectures are in the quizzes. The quizzes are very short (roughly 10 Q's). Also! OPENNOTE/OPENBOOK! But wait, there's more! All the tests are untimed. Would take the Professor again!
Very very nice. Really cares about her students and about the subjects she teaches. I took the class as a non-history and non-premed student and I had a blast and learned so much.
