This was my first semester taking a course from Dr. JL, and I am now regretting not taking a course from her sooner. She is a delight! I love taking her class. She's very passionate and enthusiastic about what she teaches. Probably one of the most relatable and easy going professors I had at UMBC.
Dr Jones-Lewis is an extremely caring and kind professor. This is my third time being taught by her and i once again love her class.

Dr JL is super understanding & an amazing person. She understands life gets in the way sometimes, and while she does expect you to get work done, she's also willing to work with you if you can't submit something on time. Her lectures are super fun to attend, and you learn a lot of neat stuff! Her assignments were content heavy, but straightforward.

LOVE this professor. She was so understanding of extraneous circumstances and she is passionate about what she teaches. You have to share your part out loud with the class which made me nervous at first but she is super supportive if you get it wrong. She is easy to talk to and her assignments aren't too much as long as you keep up with them.

The KINDEST professor i have ever had. Extremely caring and understanding. Teaches at a good pace for everyone and is willing to help at all times. Always makes you feel welcome to ask for help and questions. I learned so much in this course because of how helpful and accommodating the professor is.

Fantastic professor who genuinely cares about students.  Dr. Jones-Lewis is an expert in the subject and gives engaging and entertaining lectures (with closed captions!).  This class is genuinely fun, and Dr. Jones-Lewis is the most understanding professor I've ever met.
Great Professor, Exams/quizzes are similar, there is usually extra credit and she gives review slides that have some of the answers which you can use for the tests/quizzes.

Dr. Jones-Lewis is a simply brilliant professor. Ancient medicine is her specialty, so she is ridiculously knowledgeable in this area. Her online lectures are like podcasts. She is also so understanding and her policies about late work and extensions are the most generous I have ever encountered. Take one of her classes - you won't regret it.

Dr. JL is a phenomenal professor. Her policies are flexible, and she prioritizes student well-being over deadlines. Her lectures are like podcasts, and she is the most approachable person ever. She is so knowledgeable and the assignments are fun. Even if you aren't an ANCS student, you should still take one of her classes. Best professor ever!

A truly incredible professor. I've taken several courses from her. She's very knowledgeable about the subject matter, and always willing to answer questions and grant extensions. Extremely kind and understanding-- during the pandemic, she's really recognized the human behind the screen for a lot of students. Best professor at UMBC, easily.

10/10. Wish I could put more describers for her. Honesty and communication with her are all you need, and if you pay attention and actually participate in the class for readings and direct translation you are very likely to pass with a very high grade. Even if you slip up on correct definitions and exact translations she mainly focuses on effort.

The class was online and fully asynchronous with weekly assignments, but due dates were extremely lax as long as you emailed her asking for extensions (no reasons needed, and a few times she still graded things full credit when I didn't ask!). Video lectures posted were actually insanely entertaining and insightful. 10/10 you'll learn and get an A.

Took her class online this past semester and she is by far one of the best professors I've had here at UMBC. She is very flexible and willing to give you more time if you need it. Her lectures are intriguing because she has a lot of energy and passion for the subject. Tests and quizzes are directly based on the lectures so they are not hard at all.

You have to do quizzes each week and the answers were in her lecture videos, which were quite long and we had 3 essays to do. She will give u an extension no matter what the reason is and will also give extra credits for the quizzes and the essays. She's very sweet, lenient, considerate and amazing. BEST TEACHER AT UMBC. TAKE HER CLASS IF YOU CAN.

Dr. Jones-Lewis shows real enthusiasm for her subject. Several of her class have been recommended to me by peers. Meeting with her outside of class makes a huge difference.

reviews.comment: Perhaps I caught her on an off semester. She was very behind on her grading, and there was little feedback due to the fact that multiple things were not graded until after the semester ended.
Dr. Jones- Lewis is passionate about her line of work and her students. She is extremely understanding and always has the student's best interest at heart. UMBC is truly blessed to have her.

Highly Recommend. The kindest individuals to have graced my life. Very dedicated to her field, shows true interest in her students & does everything she can to help her students succeed. Dr. Jones-Lewis is compassionate about the issues she teaches & dedicated to her duties as an educator. I have the utmost respect and admiration for her.

This class was kind of stressful because you gotta read in front of your entire class and sometimes embarrass yourself if you're awful at learning languages, but it seemed like whatever i have trouble with Dr. MJL is ready to help me through it. reviews.comment: Dr. Jones-Lewis is one of the best profs I have ever had. If you want to take a life-changing class, that will actually help you be a better adult. Favorite professor by far. I wasn't really interested in the subject, but she makes class fun and is very passionate about what she teaches. Easy to get along with, totally awesome. Pretty cool projects that atleast if you do well in them you will do well in the class

Dr. J-L is so passionate about what she's teaching and it shows in every lecture. She always has a smile on her face, and keeps lecture interesting. All the tests and quizzes are online (midterm and final included), making it fairly easy. She takes attendance seriously, but also offers extra credit.

MJL is extremely passionate about the subject and very good at explaining things. She provides many opportunities for extra credit and is encouraging and helpful to students. I am considering an Ancient Studies minor because of how interesting her class was.

Dr. JL is by far my favorite professor I've had at UMBC. She is very helpful and answers questions with extreme clarity. Professor Jones-Lewis is one of my favorite professors! She is amazing, her lectures are so interesting and very detailed. She is hilarious! If you can, take her!

She assigned a good bit of reading and has mini-essays (about 600 words) due every so often. Bottom line, I would take the class again and I will take anything else she teaches.
Dr Jones is honestly the best professor I've ever had. She clearly loves her subject and her lectures show it. She's really helpful and always returns emails promptly. 1010 would recommend
She's awesome. I seriously debated adding an Ancient Studies minor just so that I could take more of her classes, even though I'm terrible at history. That's how awesome she is.

Probably the best professor I've ever had. Extremely smart and loves what she does, which shows through. Always willing to explain and go over things if asked. Generous grader. Wants you to do well. Tests are mainly essay format and are easier than expected considering all the stuff you cover. Read, listen and take the time to study. RECOMMENDED!

Best Professor I've had. She gives amazing lectures and is actually interesting to listen to. Sooooo helpful too, will answer any questions you have clearly and concisely. He is the definition of a model teacher. The material by itself can be difficult to fully comprehend, but he goes through with easy to understand examples. Dr. Rose is one of the best professors I've had. His lectures are a bit tedious, but everything he writes down will most likely (in some shape or form) be on the exam, so there are no surprises there. Study the notes nd do da prac. exams!

He writes so much on the board you have no time to understand the information. Just rambled through pages on pages of notes. Was not very helpful. Kind of unapproachable honestly. I didn't know what his problem was anytime I asked a question because he has a bad attitude always

Remember Andy Bernard from the Office? Imagine a really intelligent, better looking version of him. Prof. Rose the most organized teaching style Iv'e ever seen. He is very helpful! there is online homework that is kind of tough but if you go to his office hours he will help explain the material to you. we have only had one test so far, if you do the old test he provides, it helps alot. I had Dr. Murphy for psych 312. He's such a good professor and he really enjoys teaching. He is super sweet and makes the lectures fun !

He taught most of the educational parts of FYS. During lectures, it was often difficult for students in my class to maintain their focus. When students were distracted, Murphy would call students out or passive-aggressively call them. However, he was a good professor to have and gave some funny jokes. Was patient with class.

Murphy is an incredibly caring and passionate prof! FYS104 was heavily discussion-based so he did SUCH an amazing job facilitating meaningful conversations about vulnerable topics where everyone could share their individual experiences/opinions. Easy weekly readings/videos, 4 ~2-page reflections, and then one group project for the final.

Had him for my first year seminar class, which was heavily discussion based. He is very understanding, relaxed, and makes a comfortable atmosphere for students to share their opinion/experience. Posts all power points on Black Board so W Professor>>

Definitely take this class with Murphy.  He's very articulate and knowledgeable about the field. Your grade only consists of four exams, but they are so easy.  There's no trick questions and only four answer choices for each question.  As long as you read the chapter summaries and study his powerpoints you are guaranteed an A.
Can be boring while lecturing, but is passionate about his teaching. All the ppt slides are online, so you dont really have to go to class, but I would still recommend it.
Awesome professor!
oops, the bottom comment was from me. I rated the easiness backwards- correction: 4/5 not a 2. :)

He's Awesome!! Very kind with a good heart. He is funny and makes class interesting. Study the slides(most on test) and read textbook and you'll do great! He is understanding and a nice professor. Loved psychology after this class.
Funny!!!
Awesome professor! Relaxed and confident and very attractive.
attend class and pay attention. the material is hard but if you pay attention you will do fine
Very clear and uses power point which contains all the information you need to take notes on.

Nice man who is not at all up to date with technology...  Laid-back teaching style, not a tremendous amount of notes to copy but you need to study for his exams.  There are 4 exams and a final only but without putting too much time into the class I'm probably going to end up with an A or B in the course.  A little dry but a good professor to take.
nice and nice-looking
he makes the class interesting and has a sense of humor. be sure to read the articles though.
horrrible man.  boring.
He is very nice, but his course isn't too easy.  Very disorganized, just walk into his office.  But very sweet when attempts to make class laugh.

Very nice man. He's always well-prepared for his lectures, presents the information clearly, and is very easy to talk to. You'll do well if you study, go to all the classes, and read your articles. You have to photocopy all the articles yourself, though.
Very kind and ammenable. Actively tries to prevent students from failing. Can be a bit boring but a true charm all around. Excellent!

I have had 3 classes with Dr. Rathinam and he is the best professor and he makes my semester great. His lecture is amazing and I love math more than before with him. He is nice, patient, and helpful in and outside the class and we were encouraged to answer. The class is interesting and I learned something invaluable with him. 10/10 recommend him.

Dr. Rathinam is the best professor that I have ever had. His lecture is amazing and he is very patient and nice with us. He is so helpful during his office hours and by email. He makes sure students are following and can extend the due date for the homework. He gives us advance notice for the exams. His exams are reasonable. Highly recommended him

Doctor Rathinam's class was not easy but I found it very rewarding. He is extremely patient with those who have never dealt with proof writing before. He genuinely wants his students to succeed, and will help you plenty outside of class if needed. My favorite professor at UMBC so far.

Prof. Rathinam's homeworks can be a bit hard, but he's incredibly helpful during office hours and really cares about the students. I've had him for two classes so far, and he taught both incredibly well

This is supposedly the hardest class for math majors and minors, but it was easier with Rathinam because the problems on quizzes and tests were usually variations of the homework of examples in class. Good sense of humor, very nice, seemed to care about the students. Helpful at office hours.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Avoid if possible, he is a nice professor, but the quizzes and exams were hard. The averages were 50%, first quiz average was a 2.5%. He curved the class for a 65% to be a C. I went to almost every office hour and did not help me pass the class. Not sure how many students passed the class since the averages were so low.

A good professor; grading system will change in your favor more than likely. Class attendance isn't mandatory, but highly recommended -his tests are his notes. Helpful during office hours, so use them. Very quick to reply to emails, textbook use is for homework only usually.

Lectures were almost always prepared, and were very helpful in that he proved most of the theorems and lemmas he introduced. During office hours, however, he was very condescending, unhelpful sometimes, and made you feel stupid.
He gave very clear and powerful lectures from which I learned a great deal.

class was very boring. i had a lot of trouble paying attention. lots of notes, most of them you won't use. spent a lot of time in his office w/ questions about the hw. generously gave extensions. only 2 exams and the final was a take home. often assigned hw ?s w/o attempting them 1st and then dropped them when they were too hard.

By far the best professor i've ever had. He's very patient and will ensure that everyone understands every aspect of the topic being taught. Exams/quizzes can be slightly difficult sometimes but you have plenty of opportunities to ask him or read the book.

DR. RATHINAM IS THE BEST PROFESSOR EVER!!!!!!! He really cares that the students understand and he cares about their individual academic goals also.  His tests and quizzes are fair.  He's funny and the way he dresses is so cute lol.  Take him for everything, you won't regret it!

Dr. Rathinam is amazingly patient and very clear--he really understands the material, so he anticipates where people might misunderstand.  The exams are straightforward--know definitions!  He has a great sense of humor, and his tendency to wear sweaters with lots of holes is endearing.  You won't regret taking a class with him.

I heard lots of horror stories about 301 before taking it, but there were no worries with Rathinam. His exams were long but very straightforward - he doesn't try to kill you with the material. Very helpful in his office, also. He can be funny sometimes, although never intentionally.

301 is going to be hard no matter what prof you have, but Dr. Rathinam made the class as easy as possible.  His tests/quizzes were fair and reflected what was done in class.  He did not curve individual tests/quizzes but gave a curve at the end (after half the class had already dropped lol) but dr. rathinam is HIGHLY RECOMMENDED! he rocks!

Prepare to do a lot of homework for this class. Nothing too difficult as you get many attempts at the homework but definitely very tedious. She seems a little disorganized and grades a bit slow. Two essays and two exams.
One of the worst Spanish teacher ever came across. Speaks spanish all the time and when she speaks English its very difficult to understand. Would not recommend taking this class at all.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Lots of online assignments and they kinda get hard to keep up with. She doesn't always tell you about them so you have to check all the time. On top of that she speaks spanish all the time and doesn't let up even if the class is confused. Overall not too bad of a class though, you can do alright if you work hard.

There were a lot of online assignments, and sometimes she does not tell you about them. So constantly check for due dates online and make sure to do these assignments because they add up. She cares for her students and tries to have conversations with everyone in the classroom. Tests are difficult and she is a tough grader.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: One of the best professors I have ever had. Took her for both 201 and 202. She will speak in spanish for most of the class and expects that you will try to speak mostly spanish. More than enough time to complete assignments. Fair grader. Teaches you about culture and often has spanish songs to show you. Organized and clear grading structure.

Gives quizzes on things she has not gone over. Contradicts herself, yet does not explain her reasoning. Not very friendly. Gives way too many assignments. Very short amount of time for quizzes. Its hard to even think about answers when she is calling out every minute rapido rapido! un minuto! Can I think???!
This class is easy. It's a lot of work, but that's the department's fault. She's kind of harsh and annoying at times, but you'll find she can be nice enough and that the class is quite easy.

There's a lot of time consuming work in this class that cannot be avoided but after a while you get used to the pace. Online homework was difficult and online exams were a headache. But in general, she's funny and very understanding. She explains things well and answers emails. 202 wasn't easy but she made the course bearable.

Extremely nice and understanding prof. Very enthusiastic and engaging. Sometimes you will struggle because of the sheer number of assignments. Assignments are usually quick and easy, but there are often two or three due, so it's hard to keep track of them. Tests are pretty easy, and you might be exempted from the final with an A and no absences.
I enjoyed her class. she is helpful and fun and makes learning interesting.

Really great teacher! She's energetic and funny. All of her deadlines are announced up to a week in advance and she is always willing to answer your questions. Easily one of the best professors I've ever had. If you have to take a Spanish class, take one with her.

She will be late for class sometimes and she gives a lot of assignments, but overall, a good professor. She's an upbeat morning person and she will expect you to participate in class, so be prepared for that.

Awesome and energetic teacher.  Super easy grader.  Granted, the class is review, but she makes sure everyone understands the material.  A lot of class participation.  Easy tests with some busy work make for an easy A.  Definitely recommended if you are just trying to get done language requirements.
Difficult but very nice teacher.  Gives a ton of work but it usually helps in the end.
Kept all lectures in Spanish which could be confusing, but she gave a ton of extra work to boost my grade. Very friendly and helpful. As a student who barely tried and hates Spanish, I recommend her.

Not a good teacher. Will never extend deadlines. Attendance is mandatory and will only explain everything in Spanish. If you don't know Spanish, then you are screwed. She's rude if you don't understand the work. Takes off points for everything. Requires perfection.
This is my 3rd semester taking Spanish and I can honestly say it's the first time I feel like I'm learning something! If you can, you NEED to take this lady for Spanish, she is excellent.
Awesome teacher.  She is very helpful.  She makes sure everyone understands before moving on to the next subject.  I highly recommend her.

She's a really good teacher; she actually teaches. She's also very helpful.She's glad to clear up any confusion before going on to the next material. She gives out a pretty good amount of work, but they all help for your understanding. Language courses require a lot of practice and she gives you the opportunity with all the homework and classwork.

Professor Hernandez was very cool.  She's a solid professor, who's not out to kill you.  She's very clear in her lectures and really cares if you learn.  No need to fear Spanish if she's your professor.

Natalie Panfile is a hilarious and interesting professor who aims to provide her students with a true studio class experience. The drawing class is 4 hours long, and she gives excellent feedback to help her students improve. Her assignments leave a lot to interpretation, but she grades with this in mind. My art improved a lot in her class.

Natalia gives pretty vague guidelines for what she wants with her assignments, so it's a lot of trial and error in the brainstorming phase until she likes one of your ideas. But once you figure out something she likes, it's not too hard. A lot of the class is repetitive and I didn't learn too much, but it's overall not bad.

Natalia is hard to read, because you never know what she wants from you. Art itself is supposed to be subjective, and you're judged on everything. She also considers this a studio class, and expects multiple hours to be spent on pieces a day, even though its just an intro class. And don't even get me started on her online portfolio...

HE WAS AMAZING!!! online class so everything was open note, exams reflected problems done in the hws and lecture. very easy to get thru cuz we used StatCrunch ($15) and he skipped the formulas in favor of telling us what to do in a simple way! also go to class and take notes! 9/10 those class problems could be on the exams or hws!
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: The best professor I've ever had! His class is so easy and he explains the material in such a chill way. Great for bio majors that don't want to do math. Only need to pay for Stat Crunch which is $15, compared to a $100 textbook, that's pretty good. Weekly discussion (super easy) and hw's, exams, and project.
Super easy, explains things well. Really cool guy. I definitely recommend this professor.

One of the best professors at UMBC. Funny, straightforward, caring, professional, and made me want to learn the material. There were no surprises and he outlined exactly what to study for exams, no trick questions. If you put in the effort you will get an A and learn a lot of useful things. I genuinely enjoyed taking his course. The best.
One of the most understanding and considerate profs. He makes his courses interesting and digestible love him! 100% recommend to anyone that needs to take STAT!
This is the model professor! I was LOATHING the idea of taking STAT 355 over the winter. Prof. Myers made it an actual enjoyable experience! Such a great person, would recommend any class they teach!
Great professor, and he's hilarious.

Was the easiest class I have ever taken. He is a great teacher and tried to make this course as easy as possible. I took it online over the winter which was the best decision. Would highly recommend him.
Amazing Professor for STAT 355!

This Stat class was extremely easy, with short readings and homework that goes with it. attendance is not mandatory, but extra credit is given during discussion. projects are easy but require some effort. Used stat crunch so formulas weren't required for memorization.

Professor Myers is the chillest professor out there. Lectures are self-explanatory and TA sessions help your understanding. If you have taken AP Stat, this is much easier as all calculations are done on StatCrunch ($15). At the end of the course, you can even jump a whole letter grade if you give him a good reason. I 100% recommend him.

Great professor all around, very funny and seems to really care about his students. Just make sure you do the homeworks and discussions, study adequately for the tests, and attend class and TA sessions. If he knows your name, there's a good chance he'll bump up your grade at the end of the semester if you make a good case for yourself.

Easiest class ever, about 20% of the effort of AP stats. Everything is online, including exams (max 20 ques). Literally got 100% in the course, almost everything was done with StatCrunch (although I fully support learning stuff by hand too). Best course for a heavy semester. Didn't love how a each multiple choice question was like 8 points tho.
Such a great professor. Classes aren't too hard. very clear on assignments. also a friendly flexible professor!

Dr. Myers is a great professor. Even though his class was online, he tried his best to make sure we understood the material and tried to get us to get us to participate. He makes his expectations clear and the class itself is very easy. Statcrunch saved my life in this class.
Amazing professor, would take him again! If you need STAT351 YOU HAVE TO TAKE HIM! He makes the class so much fun with the games and he has never had anyone fail his class.
Professor Myers is one of the nicest you'll have, and his class was not too difficult. You learn but don't feel overworked at any point. If you need a math credit and STAT350 covers it, take him!

I am taking Stat350 with Prof. Myers and he is honestly one of the best professors to take if you have a tough semester. The class itself is fairly easy and his lectures are very enjoyable with kahoots and other interactive games with class.

Absolutely amazing professor. Statistics tends to spook a lot of people, but professor Myers makes the topic incredibly easy to understand. Make sure to stay on top of assignments, and go to the lectures before tests (you will thank me later).

Great professor! Definitely go to discussions with the TA and participate in the chat during class to pass the course! Very engaging even though the class is virtual and cares about his students! He clearly states what is due: 3 exams, 1 final, a weekly discussion and response, 1 project, and a couple of homework assignments comprise the grade.
Very nice professor. Makes it easy to get an A.

Best math professor at UMBC, hands down. Took it as a 6-week. He explains the concepts so well, super organized, works with students, takes feedback, offers so much extra credit. He encourages attendance, but worth going to class. Assignments and exams were online, but super easy. Weekly discussion posts and one project. Easy A, take it with him!

His teaching style is really good, you could pass just by going to his lectures and not do any reading. He's really nice and will attempt to make students be engaged by asking questions that arent class related. Only thing I didn't like are the stuck up know it all students in my class discord. God were they annoying.

A fun and engaging professor that is very approachable. He makes the subject very easy and will not bury you with work, even his exams are at most 20 questions which makes his class very stress free. Be sure to go to discussions as he looks at your attendance when determining whether to curve you or not.

It's really hard to not do well in his class if you really try. He provides you with all the resources you need to pass. He does exam reviews which has similar questions to exams. Due dates are fixed, you have discussion posts, hw, and a pre reading quiz due every week. exams are open for a three days and are open note. easy a if you put in effort

It seems that he knew stats would be scary subject for most people so he took an engaging and welcoming approach to the class. Lectures weren't mandatory but it was in your best interest to attend. Each lecture was fresh and interactive and was even fun at times. The classwork is an application what is covered during lecture and the text.

Tricky class for someone with no coding background. Provided code was often outdated/deprecated and materials were frustrating to use. TA would take off random points on worksheets and not explain why. Hard to learn R asynchronously but manageable with the help of outside sources/AI. Professor was available through weekly office hours.
Overall, a nice person but a very bad course structure and unavailable.

Very hard course if you don't have a background in stats or coding (me!). No lectures, only stats-dense slides and textbook. Zero communication from the professors and EVERYTHING is posted late. Assessments on Saturdays, with audio, visual, and screen recordings. Final grade is 50% assignments 50% assessments. Nice professors, bad class. AVOID!

Very disorganized class and the professors who run it are radio silent for most of the semester. I've had emails go unanswered for days or just completely ignored. Grading criteria is unclear and it can take weeks before you get any grades back.
I only took this class for a degree requirement. If you have other options, take them. Avoid this class.

The exam requirements are ridiculous; he asks you to record your screen with a webcam and administers the exams on Saturdays. On top of that, it's 3 pm on Saturday, and he hasn't uploaded the exam yet. Also, it's currently Easter weekend, and he expects us to wait around for the exam when people have to go home and do family things.

Really ugly coding interface and package. Textbook is relatively up to date and has most of the answers but you have to try a bit to get an A. Professor is alright and very animated during lectures, but lectures aren't mandatory to succeed. Make a class discord and you're chillin'.

you will probably need to take his class for your major (if it's at all stem related), since he's the only option all I can say is good luck. He's a pretty funny guy when he's talking, and would probably be cool to talk to outside of anything math-related, but he's horrible at lecturing, and you'll be teaching yourself for this whole class.

Bare minimum kind of professor. Lectures put you to sleep, but if you put effort into it you can get an A. Only reason I did not was because I literally did not sleep the night prior to the final exam, which was worth 30% of the grade. I was doing so well otherwise that it only knocked me down to a B, and if you try harder than me, you can succeed.

Lectures are pretty bad. Lecture notes are disorganized and illegible. Discussion took place before class, so we would be expected to complete a worksheet on unit 6 before having learned unit 6 in class at all. Final exam was "comprehensive" but 4/4 FRQs were from the last 2 weeks. Multiple choice included maybe 4/15 from the first half semester

I cannot understand 75% of what he says. He rushes through things and expects you to already know what he's teaching. First day of class, u know what he said to us? "I don't teach, you learn" and proceeded to make a bunch of excuses and how we shouldn't blame him should we do bad. No surprise this guy has such a low rating....

Dr. Neerchal is funny and charismatic but his lecturing is subpar. You learn 99% of the information from the homework so lectures are really only for participation worksheets, quizzes, exams, and reinforcing the information from the homework. Tries to help by posting all his lecture notes online but his handwriting is barely legible.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: went to every lecture just to hear "I dont believe in teaching". and got midterm grades back when its time for the final. Learn everything on your own or avoid taking a class with this professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Not sure why this is called environmental stat. This was literally all coding with R. This professor is never clear with lectures, homework, or exams. Expects you to come to office hours if you want a grade, BUT cant tolerate a student making mistakes. Easily just gives 0s for assignments you work hard on just due to the tiniest mistakes. Avoid him
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: He gave us a take-home midterm that left at least 3 in tears, and was assigned 2 weeks before finals. Very disorganized, unclear on grading. One week he says: "Why do you take so long on quizzes? I am here, ask me questions." the next week: "Why are you asking so many questions? I give you quiz questions you don't know so you'll have to struggle!".
reviews.rating_tags: BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: Both the midterm and final were take-home. His lectures are confusing, but I recommend going as it's sometimes helpful for homeworks. Quizzes are impossible and nobody in the class was able to finish them in time, the good news is they're MOSTLY graded on participation. He's a softy and will usually cave if the whole class asks for extensions.
reviews.rating_tags: BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: It's not "Environmental Stat" as labeled, it's "Stat using R". Bio majors avoid!  He's so bad. Quizzes on book material that he doesn't cover in class, homeworks are on using R which he doesn't teach in class (answers in book, but still hard), and exam questions are on formulas that he breezes through. It's like studying for 3 different classes!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: I thought the other reviews were exaggerated/rude (towson and umbc ones), I was wrong. She's always very lost and confused and doesn't know basic computer skills and always ends up snapping at us if we tried to help/ask questions. She always yelled during class and would either teach us the wrong thing or doesn't know how to do it so we were lost.

Never had a class so disorganized and unclear. Everything, especially Blackboard page was an absolute mess from the start. Prof is not helpful or responsive, gives very unclear instruction. Talks for whole 2 hour class session about unrelated topics/assignments. So disorganized. Prof is technologically inept. Frustrating class altogether.

She is nice and willing to assist you whenever you need it. Although she is not a strict grader, she does expect you to participate in class discussions and critiques. For the first half of the semester, she was a little disorganized with Blackboard; however, she is extremely accessible outside of the classroom and via email.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: She made the content very digestible. However, reading the book is a must. Tests are not easy, but make sure to take a look at past exams. Take your time to do the homework. Office hours are a great resource.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Best professor ever especially given how difficult this major is! Wish I could take all of my classes with her! Funny, good teacher and super caring as long as you put in the work you'll be fine!
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring

reviews.comment: She is a goddess from above fam.

I've had Dr. Raikar for 3 semesters now, fluid mechanics, and now for Safety and Controls. neither of these are easy courses in their own nature, but she does a good job of teaching them. she regularly passes through the TA office hours to answer questions. Her exams are hard, but she gives a review packet that will cover anything you need to pass.
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: This class has three major themes to it. Each one can be an upper level class of its own. She is great one on one and she knows her stuff. She is readily available outside of class and will gladly help you. She is awesome.

Dr. Raikar is new to instructing so one can not expect her to be able to communicate as well as a more experienced instructor. That being said, she is definitely one of the smartest professors I have ever had. Any question you go to her with she will give you an answer and is much better explaining the material in a one on one setting.

Dr. Raikar is a decent professor. Most of her lectures can be found from the textbook; however, she does her best to be accommodating and clearly cares about her students. Not sure if I would take again but if you put in effort and participate, you should do fine. Don't get behind--Fluids is a tricky class.
Great professor. Do your homework and study for the tests.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring

reviews.comment: I had him for calc 1 at AACC and he was just awesome. He was a tough teacher but very fair and wanted all his students to be successful. He worked in one of the tutoring labs full time while I was taking his class so he was almost always available for help if you needed it and made his students a priority. I would definitely recommend!!

Isn't very clear on giving lectures. Can tend to jump around and doesn't seem to sure on what to teach next. May be able to understand what is going on if you are a math major, and you might want to avoid him teaching you if you are not great with math.

He's a really confusing lecturer, and changes his instructions like 10 different times for each assignment. But he is totally willing to help you out, and will even give you feedback on resumes and such that you use outside of class. Class has a lot of downtime and involves a ton of groupwork, take this with friends and you will have a ball.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: Professor Nelson was really nice and flexible with due dates. The assignments were not difficult and he give many chances to work on them in class and ask for help. Overall, I would take it with him again!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Graded by few things--Group projects

reviews.comment: chapter summaries weekly, 2 or 3 presentations, 3 papers. very very very easy grader and is really helpful. deadlines are flexible, can really turn in all assignments whenever as long as they are all in. will give a bunch of feedback. one of my favorite professors.

Nice guy & very positive attitude, but SO confusing. Due dates and assignment expectations always changing. Each time he mentions an assignment, he tells you something different. Off topic a lot, but he's just trying to make students laugh. Doesn't really work, but I credit him for trying. Assignments are simple, but it's hard to know what he wants
Sense of humor, Easy going, makes students feel comfortable. Gives projects relating to course material to help gain a better understanding. No quizzes or exams. Great Professor!

The Best Professor Ever. Very Helpful and Easy going .  All i'm gonna say is that TAKE HIM and you won't regret. Amazing instructor.  Text book will be required and it will be helpful doing the assignments.

Professor Nguyen, is really kind and sweet. She genuinely wants you to succeed in this course, and she will help you if you are willing to put in the work. Also don't miss more than 4 classes or you will fail the course. Even if you have a good grade in her class you will fail if you miss more than four classes.
Make sure to participate in class and do the assignments on time and you're chilling. The assignments are pretty easy consisting of discussions and a couple essays.

Take this class! It won't let me put ENGL 271 but thats the course. We wrote two short stories about whatever we wanted and it was so fun, and she doesn't give HW besides reading short stories, and she is so nice and funny. No exams or quizzes either. And no textbook, you do have to print 22 copies of your short stories which kills your printer tho
Made the class easy to follow and will help out anybody who needs it. As long as you participate in either class discussion and revise your essays well you will get a good grade.
Similar problems are used from homework and lecture on the quizzes and exams. Her notes are very clear and extremely helpful, she prints them out for everyone too.

The quizzes were one question and tests were five, so she gave very little room for error. Her lectures were boring and dry and homework was graded on accuracy, so if you got a couple questions wrong it could tank your grade. Also there was graded attendance. However the class wasn't that hard if you put in the necessary time.

Very caring/understanding professor. Easy to reach, encourages students to come to office hours and to ask questions, and her class criteria was pretty straightforward. If you can do the homework without looking at the solutions you very well can get an A in the class. Most of the exam/quiz questions are just variations of the homework questions.

I absolutely loved having Dr. Welcome as my prof, and I thoroughly enjoyed his class. He is super flexible, very passionate, gives lots of hw but has clear grading criteria (doesn't always give feedback though).

Dr. Welcome is a great professor, this was my second class with him and I thoroughly enjoyed it. Although he gives a lot of readings and the lectures can be a lot, he was overall very passionate and graded fairly. The class consisted of 10 discussion posts, 1 online test, and 2 very long papers with multiple parts.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: i hated his exams, there was sm writing & felt like my answers weren't good enough for him which we're jus extended versions of my discussion posts WHICH always got 10/10 sooooooo. my discussion posts & papers helped me pass

Urban Anthropology 

 Most organized professor I have ever had and is not a tough grader in my experience. Lectures very well and is passionate and knowledgeable in his field. Grades only consisted of attendance, discussion posts and papers. Provides all texts in an organized format. No buying of materials required.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: Dr. Welcome is a very nice professor, however this is a very lecture and reading heavy class. He will take points off for missing class. There isn't too much homework and the exams are partly based on what we discuss in class. The content is pretty easy to understand and he clearly cares about what he is teaching but sometimes he has an attitude.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Welcome is a great professor, he is super nice. This is a low maintenance class. His lectures definitely can be boring but the content is easy to understand. 10 discussion posts, 2 essays, 2 exams, and attendance are your grade. Lots of readings, but I did not read anything that didn't have a grade attached to it and it was fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Extremely Soft spoken, boring lectures, and unreasonable. EVEN WITH AN EXCUSED ABSENCE, he wanted me to write a 2-pg paper for both classes I missed + a DB + another paper for him while I'm busy with other exams, and long papers to write for other classes within the week timeframe he gives. Not an anthro major or minor. 2/5 raters were right. Awful

Prepare to read. We had weekly readings and a weekly 200 word discussion post responding to the readings. We also had 3 books. Two super easy essays and an online midterm and online final. Class was mainly him lecturing the whole time but he's very passionate about anthropology so I found the lectures interesting. Overall I enjoyed the class

Most of Prof. Welcome's lectures consist of him talking about himself and his own experiences. It was unclear what info was meant to be taken away for the course and what was him rambling. He is very opinionated and narrow-minded.

-  Heavy on the reading
- Discussion posts every week (around 200 words per post; you can skip two)
- Two essays (very easy; I got a 100 on both)
- A midterm and final (both are online) 
- Attendance isn't mandatory but you'll get attendance credit 

Overall not a bad class; the lectures were a bit boring, but I managed!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: His favorite words to use regardless of if they are applicable are "problematic" and "fundamental". He asks close-ended questions that don't allow for much discussion and there's only one right opinion in his classes. His. Easy grading though because it's mostly busy work for grades. You will read...a lot. Keep up with it or suffer forever in class
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: My favorite professor so far! So chill and caring. Weekly discussion question where you read an article or watch a movie at home. Meet once a week for lecture. There are 2 essays and 2 tests overall. Super easy if you study and listen during lectures. He doesn't track participation but he appreciates it greatly. Attendance checked by quickly.
Dr. Welcome is a great professor; he is funny, knowledgeable in his field, and is happy to help students as much as he can within reason. He is fair, so do the homework.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: the content is interesting, but the lectures are very dry and boring. Prof gratuitously uses the word Fundamentally and sometimes waxes poetic on things that dont add value to the content. I dont appreciate his willingness to express his own opinions about the content, it leaves little room for disagreement or collaboration. wouldn't take again.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: While the actual content of the class is interesting, Welcome's lectures are monotonous and ideologized. Any variance from his personal beliefs/world views are incorrect and graded accordingly. Welcome also has a rude attitude towards his students and expects to be treated with respect despite the fact that he doesn't reciprocate that respect.

Dr. Welcome presents his material very conversationally and engagingly. That combined with his expansive knowledge of the history and current developments in his field convinced me to enroll in another one of his classes.

Very surprised he has such high ratings. Maybe this semester he slacked because my experience was terrible enough to withdraw. He never replied to my emails, had a very inconsistent grading criteria, & gave way too much homework. He also uses websites for videos that are not accessible to those w/o strong wifi accessibility. & TOO MUCH LECTURING.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Go to class and participate and you'll get a good grade

Kind of confused on how Dr. Welcome has so many positive ratings? This class is mind-numbingly boring, to start, he has sort of a rude attitude, and it didn't make anthropology seem as interesting as it actually is. I dreaded going to this class and having to listen to him drone on.

I enjoyed taking Cultural Anthropology with Dr. Welcome. Doing the readings is crucial to getting a good grade in the class. He is clear about what grade you will receive based on how much effort you put in. To get an A do the homework thoroughly and on time and listen during lectures. I would take this class again.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: He doesnt respond to emails EVER. Is NOT forgiving about missed assignments such as lectures, lecture videos and discussion post. Lots of reading and note taking is required to do well in his class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Dr. Welcome just wants everyone to get A's and learn material. Lots of reading but its expected in an anthropology class. Lectures weren't the most fun thing but he is pretty funny and makes them interesting by talking about his own research. Just follow the grading criteria and you will get an easy A.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: you will need to take notes in class. you will NEED to do the readings. the subject matter is genuinely fascinating and it's clear he cares about what he's teaching and the effect it can have.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: This was the most well organized class that I have had during the pandemic. Each week has documentaries, prerecorded lectures, and a WebEx discussion. It respects a bunch of different learning styles. Keep up with h to e reading and youll get an A.

While I can honestly say I did not always like Dr. Welcome's attitude towards his students, he clearly cares a lot about the material he's teaching, and he was more than willing to clarify things people were confused about. The class is easy if you can keep up with the discussion boards, really, and the lectures are pretty student-driven.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Had to take Cultural Anthropology again at UMBC even though I took it before at community college. This class was a bit different than my previous one though. Lots of reading (3 books), two essays and a midterm & final exam. Professor Welcome is okay, he talks a lot about Urban Anthropology which is pretty boring to me but whatever.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Welcome was awesome! Had lots of experience in the field, and gave many real, first-hand experiences. Class had 2 short papers (the second built off the first), and 2 exams which made up 80% of our grades. Study definitions and do the readings and you'll get an A.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This was a great class! We learned about energy and the environment. He used a lot of documentaries and clips which were really eye opening and helpful because they showed us the situations he was lecturing about. Will totally take another class with Dr. Welcome!
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: I didn't know what to expect when I signed up for the class but it was a blast! A couple of short papers and two exams. As long as you come to class and read most of the readings you should get an A. There are a couple of books but they're pretty straightforward. Super interesting!

I didn't find the topics in the class hard and most were interesting. His lectures aren't that bad but be prepared to take notes. Exams and papers are straightforward. Attendance is mandatory or you lose points. The only complaint I have is his attitude. He doesn't like to answer "too many" questions and even argued with a few students in class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Really enjoyed Prof. Welcome's class. I had no idea what this course was about when I signed up for it, but it turned out to be really interesting! He required three books, not textbooks, normal short books that questions about them were present on exams. Read and take notes and it'll be a great class!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Prof Welcome's class is very simple and easy to pass. There are lots of assigned reading but I honestly didn't do most of them, just paid attention to his interesting lectures. Very lenient grader on the two essays we were given. He also gives good opportunity to get 30 points of extra credit.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Nicholas Welcome is an opinionated man to say the least. His lectures consisted mainly of political talking points which he presumably agreed with. Students were not encouraged to express dissenting opinions, as Dr. Welcome tended to demonize arguments that did not fit his narrative. Remarkably easy class if you can repeat his opinions back to him.
Professor Nicholas is great, I am so glad I had the opportunity to take this class with him. Show up to class, participate and do the assigned readings. simple.

I took this class expecting to be bored, scrape up a C, and be done with it. I was wrong. I've never had an interest in anthropology, but I was invested in everything brought up in class. I really feel like I learned a lot, although it wasn't easy. Lots of paper, but the requirements were clear. I would happily take any class by this teacher again.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--SO MANY PAPERS--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: I took this class as my writing intensive and it was fairly easy. We had 4 take home quizzes and 3 papers which we put together at the end of the semester into a single cohesive research paper. Lots of readings every night for class discussions. Participation and attendance are VERY IMPORTANT!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: First of all, this is a real teacher. Don't be fooled by the last name, this is not "Welcome" as in "Welcome to this class!" I'm probably the only one who thought of that, but oh well. He is a great teacher. Make sure you take notes or photos of his slides because he does not give them out. He lets you know what will be on exams, and HW is simple!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Shares his projects with prof Mironov, his lectures are pretty boring and I basically stopped going to them altogether as the class discord with the TAs from mironovs section is a way better resource. His exams are pretty easy, lots of pseudocode but if you study the homeworks before hand you'll be fine. The projects in this class are killer though

Prof. Allgood seemed unprepared for CMSC 313. His lectures involved copying problems to the board, but these often contained errors he struggled to fix and students frequently had to correct him. Combined with unclear project instructions, and lack of standardized grading this made for a frustrating learning experience.
He is not knowledgeable. He did not able to convey the concepts, however he was expecting from us to know everything.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--So many papers--Test heavy

reviews.comment: He is a very funny guy but he is scatterbrained and grades things late. The topic itself is really difficult and the exams were horrendous. Luckily, it seemed like the grades were curved near the end since I thought I was failing for the majority of this class. Again chill guy, but a little chaotic.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Not the best lecturer, especially for a class like 421 where there's not many resources. I had to rely on the TAs a lot. Tests were also like long.

I have taken two courses with him now, professor Allgood is one of the most down to earth, caring professors I have ever had. Grading criteria is clear and slides are helpful for exams. Most of these reviews do not align with anything I have seen in his courses and are most likely written by students who are not locked in.

1. Fair exams: no cheat sheets, short essay style, completely fair.
2. Projects: assigned & graded by other profs. (not great)
3. Lectures: boring, lowkey impossible to listen, can skip, review slides alone.
4. Grading: 3 exams, 30% homework (practically a curve), 4 projects.

Overall: not a bad prof!

Prof taught using other profs slides and did not know the content. Gave a single midterm with 17 pages of work in a 70 min class. Projects were interesting, but rubrics were vague. Very nice person, connects to students well, however prone to frequent tangents about unrelated content.

His lectures and slides are basically the same. Lectures are skippable, and exams are on the easier side. Not a good lecturer. Start projects early since he doesn't do in class coding for topics related to the projects. Besides the projects, it's not that hard to get an A, just study for exams, do homeworks, and start projects early.

I had professor Nick Allgood for Software Engineering I, but my only options on this site were only 341 and 201. His software engineering course actually landed me a valuable software engineering internship. The way he taught it was great. The experience you get in diagrams, Jira, problem solving, documentation, testing, etc. are all important

Lectures are snoozers; distracted easily, reads off the slides, and barely does in-class coding. Projects are difficult but manageable. Exams were nasty but were curved/graded lightly. He also changed the final exam date without announcing it until the day before exams started. Avoid Allgood if you want to learn and avoid tearing your hair out.

Allgood talks in a monotone voice and is impossible to focus on. At some point I stopped attending his class completely and my grade was the same. One time at the end of a lecture he said "Okay, now who wants to watch me play Dark Souls 3?" so definitely a kind and cool guy but not a great teacher unfortunately, I wish him well with his PhD program

Professor Allgood's lectures are monotone and extremely boring. I often tried to ask questions in class and he was unable to answer. Went to his office hours and he turned to the internet to explain one of the more important topics to me. His explanations both in and outside of class are unclear, so be prepared to teach yourself the content.

I would compare Nick Allgood to Ben Johnson. He's like the first form of a Pokemon while Ben Johnson is the final evolution. Except Nick Allgood is like Ash's pikachu who refuses to evolve. Metaphors aside, you'll be teaching yourself this entire semester. He has not been useful what so ever. He can't convey material well to save his life.

Truly "all good," but could be "all great." My main gripe is that he gives out pre-written notes that he also uses as his lecture material, so I never really felt the need to take notes myself, which often led to getting distracted in class. Once I got some TA help, I did good. The exams can be unexpectedly difficult, so be sure to reread your code

He is very knowledgeable on the subject, but his lectures are hard to pay attention. If you don't understand something, I recommend asking him for help. He's a very nice and caring professor always looking to help. Projects are the same for everyone taking the course and they're very hard. Exams are individual to professors. Not easy but not hard.

Allgood just did not teach the content in a way that students could understand. He frequently second guessed his own material and left his class out of luck for the several rigorous projects. Nice guy, not a great professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Beware of pop quizzes--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: When I took Psych 101, there were two discussions and two quizzes per week, instead of one discussion and one quiz per week in the typical class, and the textbook was not written in an accessible way and only someone with a background in psychology could understand it which made the assignments near-impossible to do for a neurodivergent person.
Changes syllabus twice throughout the semester, 100% lack of communication and quizzes, assignments are not engaging at all. Would not take again.

An amazing professor, don't be put off by the "lot's of homework". Taken during COVID, the class was 100% async. Homework is super consistent, everything is due on the same day every week and it's up to you to watch the lectures to complete them. Only problem was due dates for assignments weren't on BB, so they didn't show up on the calendar.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I loved Dr. Tarner! I took her for both PSYC370 and PSYC357, and she was great! The assignments come straight from her lectures! Do her work and it's an easy A! I want to mention that I took both of her classes during the coronavirus pandemic and she did not hesitate to stay in connection with her students! The cutest, bubbliest lady!
Love her! she was so relaxed and not uptight like other professors, made it easy to learn and get work in on time. Id take her again
reviews.rating_tags: BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--Clear grading criteria--Hilarious

reviews.comment: Loved taking her classes! You learn alot and she's not an easy A by any means, but I find her very organized and open to conversations, cery approachable and funny.

reviews.comment: Amazing professor. not "out to get you" you actually learn in her class without it being unbearable. there are quizzes after each lecture and exams. you do have to put some work in if you want a good grade and take really good notes and pay attention in class
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious

reviews.comment: She is really good if youre good at memorization. She teaches a lecture and then has a quiz immediately after. I never even opened the book. I just memorized the lecture as she went. She very nice and funny
Lectures were pointless. Quizzes were detail-oriented and didn't test the actual principles.  Changed the syllabus half-way through the course.  Easy enough, but annoying.
AMAZING prof.  So nice, so helpful. Good hearted & funny. You can tell she really enjoys what she teaches. She takes a potentially awkward subject & breaks it down to a good comfort level.
One of the easiest classes I have taken. Easy A! Just pay attention to the lectures and you will be fine. Took it over the summer; 4 week/hybrid and I highly recommend her!

Dr. Tarner is an experienced and excellent professor. Her lectures and class requirements are crystal clear. Her tests are pretty manageable. She's very down to earth and very approachable. I didn't have many encounters with her since this was a hybrid 4-week class, but I'd definitely recommend her.

She is a wonderful professor! I highly recommend taking any Psychology classes that you can with her! Come to class and take notes. As simple as that. All her questions on the exams are straight forward and she does a very good job at explaining things. She is very approachable, so if you have any questions do not hesitate to ask.
Great professor! My favorite!

SUCCCHH an awesome class. It was one of the higher level classes, and I aced it no problem! I studied hard for her tests, and I think I missed 2-3 questions per exam. She was really funny and interesting, and def fun to have as a professor. DEFINITELY recommend this class!
Easy A, but the class moved at an ungodly slow pace.  I found myself checking collegehumor more often than paying attention to the lectures.  Still, very easy course, almost no effort required.

After Spring 2005, Nina will be moving to Sacred Heart University. She was an awesome professor, very clear, very nice, and very helpful. As long as you show up for class, you can pass her class no prob. her lectures are very eaasy to follow and she repeats everything for you to write down.
Very "hip" and laid-back. Very sweet and she's just such a nice lady.
Def reccomend taking this class. Her notes are clear her tests are easy and she is interesting.
go to class and pay attention and your set. Easy to follow and chill.

She's a good teacher but don't expect your questions to be answered. Just listen to her lectures without asking anything. She's very straight foward and everything on her tests are from the lectures. Classes are easy to sit through and she's not boring. Take her.

I learned nothing. Instructions were never clear. You barely do any work, yet the work you do feels pointless. A lot of group work. Her grading is based on opinion rather than the syllabus. When you ask questions about the assignments she made, she doesn't even know the answer. Does not grade on time, so you arent able to calculate your grade

She's a pretty good professor, she seems sweet and all, but her grading is wack for me. You don't know your grade unless you make a meeting with her or wait until the end of the year. Her work isn't really hard, rather, it's just a lot of things to do. Nice person though.

Prof Pekarske is such a kind person and wants to see her students do well. She creates unique assignments and encourages everyone to participate. She is open about her own family circumstances and offers the same grace to students.

Honestly, she is a hard grader and she is also kind of strict with grades as well. She does not respond fast if you email her or message her on blackboard too, which is also annoying. The course work isn't that bad but the way she explains the assignments is confusing and she also grades assignments late too. I give it like a 5/10 class i guess.

reviews.comment: Cares about students and what she teaches. If you're bad at writing she can give help so long as you seek it. Assignments aren't hard, lots of essays and reading articles, but no books. Stuff you did in high school. However, grades real late, and cancelled class a few times a few minutes before it started, which was a huge bummer as a commuter.
I suure do love not knowing that I'm failing the class until AFTER the semester ends.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Slow at grading and you won't know your true grade until the class is over. It's often unclear what you may need to do for an assignment and when you may need to do it.

Class was overall pretty disorganized and if you don't show up to lectures, it can be difficult to figure out what you've missed. Grading is slow. I didn't know my grade till the end of the semester. Pekarske also never replied to emails. Putting all of this aside, she was passionate about her work and sweet in person.

reviews.comment: Does not reply to emails but occasionally speaks to you in class about said email meaning she clearly reads them

lol.

reviews.comment: A very good teacher if you're taking ENG100. I got 100s on both the major essays she gave out, and she's really lax about topics you can choose to write about. reviews.comment: hhv
