reviews.comment: Anyone who needs a professor to actually teach should stay away from her. She's disorganized, doesn't care about her students wellbeing and cannot help with the homework she assigned.

One day, she decided to have an assignment not graded, without telling/ emailing the class after we already did it. A couple days after the assignment was due, someone had to ask her why for us to know that she wasn't going to grade it.

Due dates for assignments were not made clear in the beginning of the semester nor were they in the syllabus. Canceled a class because she didn't turn in here proposal in time. Often changed the syllabus through the semester.

Absolutely no coherence to the syllabus. She changes assignments as she pleases without proper explanation, extremely emotional, can't use a computer to save her life (ironic, ik). There were multiple instances where she didn't release hw that's supposed to take a week(acording to the syllabus) until 3 days before it's due. I think she has dementia

She is very disorganized I must say and never replies to emails and doesn't know how to teach also barely teaches her students any coding and the exams were so hard for the students to pass!! Please don't take her class unless you want to fail!!!

She was the worst professor I've ever had. She was very disorganized and did not answer emails when students had clarifying questions. If you would like to learn and take a well-structured class, do not take a class with her. By the way, if you want to take 147, your class is considered an experiment and she uses a platform that has you grade peers
this review is for IS428. this is the worst professor at UMBC. do NOT take this professor, by all MEANS.
The worst prof i have taken in my career.. never going to take her class
Very disorganized, can do much much much more better

Prof Patti is a caring and nice teacher and all. But this class was really disorganized. The communication was not always clear and many others in my section learned more from the TA.We had many group project assignment that had little help on actual coding. And there were a few real coding assignments but a small amount.
No commment.
Professor Patti is very disorganized and does not how to teach.

She explained our class is an experiment group for a new way of learning. Due to this, it has affected many students. Biggest issue is I haven't learned much because of this. What I'm afraid of is being unprepared for 247. Past reviews show she is a great Professor. Im sure once she has figured out what to improve, her class will be great.

Professor Ordonez is very disorganize, and she can not teach the class. Everytime she is absent, the class go downhill real fast. Professor Ordonez change assignments last minute. We barely have any lectures slides for  a Exam, causing some people to fail. If we had enough lecture slides maybe some people would able to pass the class.

Really good person, cannot teach. She is very disorganized, changes the assignment scheulde by the week, never prepared for exams. Rushes through material leaving everyone confused. Hardest intro class ever should be labeled advanced.

Professor Ordonez is an amazing teacher. She's passionate about otherwise bland material, and can make death by PowerPoint actually bearable. She's willing to help students with whatever they need help with, regardless of how much they participate. I would definitely take any class that she teaches in the Computer Science department.

She was the best prof I've had in my whole life. She actually wanted her students to learn instead of just getting paid. The only reason some people failed CMSC104 was because they would give up and start playing games or shopping for purses on the web. IDIOTS! You know who you are. Ordonez was the best prof and I wish she would teach CMSC202++
She is very helpful and a very good teacher.  She is always willing to help her students with whatever they need.  She is the best teacher I've had at UMBC so far.
She substituted for our class once, and man she is way better than our original teacher, yayesha. Also I personally have the hotts for her so I had no problem staying awake.  Yeaa mmmm scrumptous.

Very nice.  Willing to go above and beyond to help you understand the material.  Very organized.  Makes sure the entire class understands the content, and likes the whole 'programming experience'.  Exams and quizzes are more than fair.  One of the best instructors I have ever had.  The best CMSC professor at UMBC.
She's very nice.
Very caring teacher show a lot of passion and makes class very easy as long as you read the texts she assigns.

She is wonderful. She's passionate about what she teaches and encourages really fun discussions. There's an assignment that involves memorization, and she was encouraging even if we forgot a part. She made class interesting by letting us explore topics that we were interested in related to the readings and by sharing her own thoughts. Love her!
Literally one of my favorite classes I have ever taken. She is very passionate about the material, well spoken, and encouraging.

I took online classes with her and she really is an amazing professor who is accommodating and does not harshly grade at all. While the class topics can be daunting and sometimes dull, she really knows her material and you will learn a lot. Her assignments are not difficult at all. If you do the work then you should not get a bad grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Graded by few things--Caring

reviews.comment: Dr. Smith is great. I was reluctant to take this class because I'm on the communications track for English and typically don't enjoy literature classes. Unfortunately, it's a required class. But Dr. Smith's reading choices were awesome and interesting. She's also a fair grader and fun lecturer. I'm glad that I took this class with her.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: she literally would tell you to fix something and you fix it in the draft and then she Ill say its not enough she needs more and unclear and I didnt even know my grade for the entire semester and tells u to calculate it like never taking her again.

Very sweet but I could never get over a B on pretty much any of my papers even though I'm usually an A student. Either way, I don't think she really gives lower than a B on anything if you at least try. The class was okay I just don't think she was a fan of me and that may have skewed her grading. Who knows!

Had her for ENGL 301, 305, and 364. She always has the coolest class topics. She's an easy grader and the nicest English professor I've had. She usually has a you do a few papers and they are usually on stories you're reading in class so there's no long nights at the library doing research and reading a whole other novel.

Tells you exactly what you need to do to get a good grade. She is a fairly easy grader and very nice. Make sure to read and participate. Grades : two papers, two exams, reading quizzes, and participation.

Class was kinda boring but she tries. She's super nice and wants you to pass the class. Reading was a lot at times but she knows and takes it easy if you don't read everything. She let's you know when the reading quizzes are too. Overall a decent class.

She is such a great, caring and nice teacher. Her class was a bit boring at times, but she was clear, went over what she wanted to see in essays, and was extremely nice to the students. I would take her upper classes again just because of the experience. You do have to work to get an A on the papers, but just be original and precise about your poin

Had her for 305 and loved her. Took 241 as an elective (Gothic lit) and it was the same deal.  2 blue book exams, 2 papers and several reading-check quizzes. Attendance helps, she'll answer a lot of her test questions then and they're a blast to boot. Responds promptly to emails and is eager to help with paper issues. Definitely recommended.

Phenomenal professor, fantastic class. Makes Milton comprehensible *and* entertaining - that's a lot right there. Very easygoing and chill when it comes to quizzes and papers. Loved her class, would recommend her for anything.

Such a great professor--I highly recommend students to seek her out to take her courses.  She is incredibly intelligent, very helpful, and makes her classes so much fun.  She is very constructive in her grading and will work with you before a paper is due to make sure you are able to turn in your best work.  By far my favorite professor.
She's a great professor--so nice and helpful and really great at responding to emails.  I highly recommend taking a course with her :)

Really fun class. Had her for 301 and 305 too. If you're into the subject you'll find the discussions hilarious, if you're not you might still find them kinda funny. All you have to do is be critical with her papers and you'll do fine. Takes notes, think about the topic, and you'll get a B no worries.
Did not enjoy this class. I wish I would have taken 307

I've had her for: 301, 305, 410, and soon to be 364. I absolutely adore this professor! Sweet, responds to e-mails very quickly, intelligent, passionate about her classes, and interested in her students. She even took us on a FIELD TRIP for our senior seminar, resulting in "Girl Talk Time!" She's amazing! Take any and all of her classes!
She's fabulous--take anything she teaches.
come to class, do the assigned readings, keep up with the work and its a pleasant class. Learned a lot and actually enjoyed it!

Pretty easy courses, but you take a lot away from them.  Both classes are structured similarly, two exams, 2-3 papers, and lots of reading.  Quizzes are easy if you keep up with the readings, and she's pretty lenient with your interpretation of events on said quizzes.  Easily accesible, willing to provide aid to her students.  Fair and objective.
She seems pretty nice and fair.  So far, her pop quizzes don't seem too bad.  There is a fair amount of reading though and active participation in class is very encouraged.

Certainly not an easy class, but she's an awesome teacher and completely approachable. If you're going to skip every other class, she will not give you the time of day. She's not one who makes the class hard for no good reason. Show up, do the work, and ask for help if need be, and there's no reason you're not looking at a B or better.

She makes you work for the grade, which I respect. She really knows her subject and tries to make you understand just how cool it is. Tough class to get through though. Tons of readings, papers that require a lot of effort outside of class, and a class presentation. She can guide you in the right direction if you ask.

One of my all time favorite professors! She genuinely cares about her students and treats them respectfully. Her lectures are always interesting (especially when she reads to us, she turns me into a starry-eyed 4 year old everytime!) She grades fair and will go out of your way to help any student. Plus she made us cookies the last day!!

Possibly one of the best English professors I have encountered at UMBC.  She is a particular grader, but not unfair.  Her lectures are fascinating and the reading and homework assignments are challenging, but enjoyable.  Take her class if you are nerdy and like to read a lot--and if you like Lord of the Rings.

Before taking this class, I dreaded Shakespeare and would not understand what I'd read. Dr O's lectures provide the context/background you need to understand the text. She teaches you how to read Shakespeare so you get the most out of it. For an A, must go to class, reread texts for exams, papers must have a point. Highly recommended.

Did horrible on her exam but then again I am an English major. Did get A's on most of her papers. Cant go wrong if you do what she tells you and send her your paper via email several days before its due. She writes extensive notes so there shouldn't be any excuse for not getting an A on the papers.

I have had this professor for 3 classes. She can be intimidating, but she really doesn't want any student to feel that way. I don't do as well in her class compared to if I took an easier professor, but I learn A LOT more. If you're looking for an easy A- none of her classes are for you. But if you want to learn and challenge yourself- then take he

She is the worst professor. Her tests/quizzes are tough. She gives unannounced quizzes. The material is impossible to understand. There were some homework assignments, but they are worth very little points. Even with the extra credit, you have to be lucky to do well. Many English majors also think she is the hardest professor.

She is a great professor. She's down to earth and is funny. She doesn't tolerate winney babies that failed because THEY didn't do the work. This class is writing intensive so expect to do WRITE! She is awesome and will challenge everything but make you a better writer. Just be prepared to work! Very willing to help students do well in her class!

She was really intimidating...I didn't do as well as I wanted in her class, but she helped me gain a greater appreciation for literature. She's pretty strict on the grading, but if you go to her office hours, she'll help you.

VERY subjective grader (I wrote a midnight paper, my friend's was great and well researched, but we both got the same grade b/c she found mine "interesting.") Her directions are very vague which ends up sucking because she grades on criteria she has never mentioned before. For a techincal writer, her prompts +questions are atrociously worded.
wonderful! So enthusiastic! Just loved her and her class! She was so helpful and so knowledgeable. She is a gem at UMBC!

She's a freakin Nazi and she thinks she's hot****. Ridiculous expectations...for ex: if I wanted to actually LEARN the language of Old English? I'd take a "LANGUAGE" class to do that. I took a class that said: "HISTORY of the Eng. language" do we actually learn Native American  languages when we take American History? NO. We just learn ABOUT them

You should have a love for lit--lots of reading. If you have a question ask it quickly; take too long n she'll interrupt and give you a quick answer. Quiz every week--read the material, memorize important details. Attend all lectures. Participate, she'll give you some pts (gave me a 2%). SHOW HER DRAFTS (short amt of time for them but v important.

Very difficult grader on papers and tests but also approchable if you have any questions and is willing to help. Very interested in the subject which really helped when she taught. Exams cover a TON of literature and expect to have to know everything from the readings.

Hard hard HARD professor. Studied hours every night and BARELY got a B in the class. But she definitely knows her subject. Just DO NOT MISS CLASS. You will fall so far behind. Expect to really know the literature you are reading. You have to in order to do well. I said 304 was the one survey I wasn't taking, but I survived! =)

Maybe Medieval lit just wasn't for me, but wow. Studied for 3 hours and got a 60 on the test. She's not kidding when she says her tests are hard. She spends too much time making sure she has the hardest test in the department and talking really softly when she has something important to say. I advise people to avoid her if they can.
Realllyyy weird professor. Called me 'a medieval squirrel'. Also involved in banned medieval cults, from whose black magic she invents questions for her exams.

I've had Dr. O for three classes, and in every class she's challeneged me to become a better student.  She incredibly tough, but her expectations are simple; do the reading and come to class.  She doesn't test on anything she doesn't review in class, so if you fail, it's your own fault.
Definitely one of the hardest profs I have ever had, but worth it. You will learn a lot about lit and critquing lit and writing, but be prepared to work! Class discussions are really interesting too.
No Comments
She was the best thing about my time at UMBC.  She's so interesting and such a great professor.  I learned so much from her.

One of the best professors I've ever had.  Very interesting, fun lectures, pretty tough grader, but it's worth it--my writing improved tremendously. Very intelligent and funny--keeps you awake+laughing in an otherwise boring class.
Very subjective grading.  If you sit up front and talk a lot, she'll like you.  Dirty jokes and topics ALL the time.

Professsor Osherow is very passionate and well informed about the subject. I took the Shakespeare intro class and loved it! If you like reading and writing then you will too. Prof is understanding, engaging and provides good feedback. Be ready to participate and speak up in class, not only does she appreciate that, your grade is dependent on it too

reviews.comment: Professor Osherow is very passionate and well informed about her subject. She is very good at teaching, keeps the class well engaged and interacts well with her students. I took the ENG 250 Shakespeare class. She is not a very tough grader and provides informative feedback. She genuinely wants her students to do well and is an understanding person.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Great professor if you're looking for a fun class to take.

reviews.comment: Dr. Osherow is one of those rare professors who truly embodies the qualities of an exceptional mentor in just one semester. She is always available for help and guidance, both in and out of the classroom. As a biology major, I was initially nervous about taking a Shakespeare class, but her support made all the difference. Highly recommend!!

Dr. Osherow is AMAZING!!! One of the best profs at UMBC!! I don't usually write reviews but I had to after taking her class! She is incredibly knowledgeable and loves teaching! She really cares about her students' success and goes out of her way for us. Truly inspiring lady. We love you, Dr. Osherow!!!

This is my 2nd class with Dr. Osherow and she's an outstanding professor. Exactly what you hope a prof will be! You learn in every class and she knows crazy amounts about the material. She gets that the reading is hard and helps us through it Can be a tough grader on papers but exams are easy. Mostly I love how much she cares about students: tons!

Professors expectations were too high for a course like this. Too much work for the course and nit picks every little thing you do. Even if you try, it is still not good enough. Take this professor only if you have to.

reviews.comment: Dr. Osherow is one of the best professors I've had at UMBC. She loves the material she's teaching and is very  knowledgeable. She gives a lot of feedback on work and it is designed, not to criticize, but to make us better writers. She wants us to succeed. Would take again. Put in an honest effort and you'll do well.

She wants you to succeed but she's not an easy professor which makes it more meaningful when you do well. Never have I seen someone so knowledgeable and passionate about their area of study and you would have to actively try to not learn something from each class. If you ever have a chance to take a class with her you owe it to yourself to do so.

Should have known this class would be more than arduous when we were asked to read an entire play, BEFORE starting the class. Instructions were completely unclear, and little care was given as to whether we actually understood the material or not. Berated students for not understanding, even when she didnt explain anything. Very tough grader.

reviews.comment: Took her two years ago, and am writing this to let you know she was simply fantastic. Explained the significance of Shakespeare super well, didn't insert any ideology into her lectures, and the class was overall the epitome of what a humanities class should be.

Dr. Osherow is one of the best teachers I've ever had. She is demanding and you have to work for a good grade- I wouldn't take her for an easy A. She made me a better writer and researcher. I'm a highschool English teacher now and I try to channel her teaching, especially when I'm doing Shakespeare or covering religious themes. She's amazing.

I took her Redeeming Eve course and absolutely loved it. She was helpful & engaging. I will say that she grades pretty tough. She penalizes and overanalyzes the little things in your essay that seems pointless to do. I got B's when I usually get A's. She will help you with your draft, but she still has criticism in your graded assignment.

I am really surprised by the comment because I think professor Oscherow is great! I am in 301 now and I think shes awesome! She doesnt let drivel pass for a reading- good on her. Highly challenging course that students feel discouraged.

reviews.comment: Incredibly knowledgeable and passionate, never seen anything like it. She wants you to dig deeper and learn, so she won't take your crap. Do all your assignments, read beforehand. reviews.comment: Truly lovely. The class is heavily discussion based in the best way; we talk about what interests us most. There's a lot of reading for her Shakespeare class but it's also entirely possible to get by without reading. Her teaching style is wonderfully inspirational and at times comedic. It's also adorable watching her try to figure out technology.
Shakespeare was a tough class. Definitely bring your book to class. Prepare to perform a monologue. It's a very interactive class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Gives good feedback--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Great teacher, very helpful in class discussion. Although I've never enjoyed Shakespeare, she made it more bearable.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Great class. Best teacher I've had here. Period.

I wasn't sure about this class at first--def not what you expect in a bible class. But it is awesome. Yesterday's class on Samson was amazing; we always leave talking about the reading. Dr. Osherow knows unbelieveable amounts about the bible and literature. Somtimes doesn't let up so do the reading. GREAT class.

Dr. Osherow is really interesting. She values class participation, and good strong arguments in your writing. Be sure to do ALL the readings, she will be able to tell if you have not read a passage. Generally a good class.

The best professor I've had at UMBC--totally. I didn't even think I'd like this course. She's awesome. Hard on papers, but will look at drafts. I actually like Shakespeare now. Amazing course. Amazing woman.

LOVED THIS TEACHER!! Dr. Osherow made me enjoy and understand Shakespeare (which I did not think was possible!)  She is very passionate about this subject, and really knows her stuff.  She makes learning Shakespeare fun! I plan on taking another class with her.

By far, my favorite professor at UMBC.  She worked hard to make Shakespeare interesting, and seemed to understand the level of interest as not being super high on everyone's agenda. Very kind person who will help you with anything  you need to the best of her ability.  Read the plays (and sparknotes) and go to class.  You'll do fine.

great professor, one of my favorites. before i hated shakespeare, she got me interested in it to the point where i occasionally attend shakespeare clubs and read shakespeare for fun. grades papers pretty hard but if you put in the effort and read, you will do fine. i got a B
I took an independent study with her and it was HARD. But good and I learned alot. Don't be fooled by how nice she is.

A nice person, but not a good professor. Her teaching style is that of a 9th grade high school teacher. I was not impressed at all. There are other, much better professors in the department who teach this class.  Take it with them!

she is nice enough, but she doesn't teach very well.  tends to ignore students if she doesn't think she'll agree with what they say, and also lets the class get away from her (can't keep control).  the class i took could have been a hell of a lot more inte
Best teacher I've had at UMBC; you will learn and enjoy this.

Great teacher and lovely person. Not easy especially on papers, but rewarding class. Pay close attention, do very close readings, and let her look over your drafts before you turn them in. Highly recommonded professor for those willing to put effort into learning about Shakespeare.
Great teacher. Very helpful.
I wasn't terribly interested in the class, but Dr. Osherow is a great professor and willing to help her students out.  She does make you participate in discussion, though.
very helpful. Difficult grader on papers. Take my advice... have her look over your papers it makes a world of difference. Tests on plays include naming quotes!!
She is a great teacher. I have taken two of her classes and would take another.
Very good teacher, lots of fun, and extremely helpful!  You should jump at the opportunity to have this delightful lady as your instructor.
Great Teacher!

Gave hw assignments and didn't grade them. Was unclear about instruction and expectation which led to being graded poorly & didn't give feedback so you don't know what you did wrong. Pretends to care but really doesn't. Never answers emails. Raised word count with every assignment. Terrible final project w/students in Spain. Don't take this class..
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Lecture heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: She grades everything last minute and is unclear with instructions. Does not care that format is online. Assigns WAY too much work. Many of us never knew what was going on. She attempts to "care" and asked us if we ever needed anything to reach out, but she doesn't answer emails. Will also never forget that she defend colonization due to intent.

If your paper isn't what she would have written how she would have written it, don't expect an A no matter how much effort you put in or how good the paper is. Test questions were vague, lectures were frustrating, not sure what else to say. My first B and I don't even care. I'm just glad it's over. So disappointing.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Group projects--Tough grader

reviews.comment: She is a very caring professor but she is a very harsh grader.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Learned a lot about history. If history is your worst subject, refrain from this course. Lots of reading and material.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring

reviews.comment: You get your moneys worth with this professor! Expect to come prepared, participate frequently, study, write extensive exam answers, and to exhaust all of the time allotted for exams and then some. Lastly, a serious student who enjoys learning Spanish and history should expect to learn a ton! Very capable, friendly and knowledgeable professor.

Dr. Oskoz is one of my favorite professors. She has high expectations of her students, so if you're looking for an easy A, her class is probably not for you. However, if you're looking to learn a lot and improve your Spanish, and are prepared to do the work, you'll love her class and do well. She takes time to explain the material clearly.

Do yourself a HUGE favor and REFRAIN FROM taking this Professor PLEASE:  Very disorganized and  lacks clarity-You HAVE to meet with her MANY TIMES. Very rigid and set in her ways. Very Judgemental. Does not bend or give you the BENEFIT OF THE DOUBT(THIS IS HUGE) VERY into HERSELF and HER RESEARCH VERY IMPERSONAL.

She is not the best at being clear from the get go as to what she wants. Be prepared to meet with her a lot in person so as to acquire clarity.  Very tough grader and will not cut corners like other professors would. She is very rigid in that aspect. Not inspirational at all.

Seems mean at first but actually very nice. She'll call on you. forced participation, no escape. Spoke in Spanish the entire class, no English at all. Class consisted of 3 exams, online chat (1hr min requirement), Oral presentation (done in front of class in groups 3/~15 minutes per group), some dumb video proj, discussion board, quia. Tough grader

Took a winter class with her. Very fast paced, and was almost intimidating at first talking in spanish right away. I think that is part of what made her such a good professor. She really makes sure you are learning, but can get kind of repetitive. Very approachable, and overall very enjoyable class.

Course is very time consuming. A ton of thing to do in the calss. Chating, oral exam, Quia, discussions, etcc.. She need her students to talk in class (especially when she walks in the calss with crazy as energy). Long as you do everything (even if you do bad on exams) you still pass a course with B or C. so must try to fail this course.
I took the class during the winter semester, so it was very intensive, but she maintained a very good energy level, and our class had relatively few students drop.  Would take again!!!  A++++

May seem cold at first but she is really a nice person. Expects a lot from students which is why I learned a lot from her class. Expects participation in class which wasn't hard to do because you usually only need to give a lot of short answers. Encourages interaction with her and other students and willing to give individual help.

She does expect a lot from her students. But if you show her you want to learn and make efforts and improvments she will help you learn. I sucked at Spanish before her class, and understood virtually nothing. Now I understand it and almost got a B. She really cares about her students that care enough to put in the time. GO TO HER OFFICE HOURS!!!

She is really nice and really cares if her students understands the language.  She is really interactive during class and you can only speak spanish.  She is from Spain so she will use their type of spanish rather than the american spanish.  As long as you try you can get an A,class participation is a must!

She's very nice and really cares how her students are doing- always asks for inputs. Class structure isn't very organized, but she is happy to help clarify any questions. Tests are not too bad- she tells you everything that is on it

Speaking Spanish throughout the whole class is really helpful -- it keeps you in the Spanish mindset and makes learning much easier and rewarding. The class is difficult, but there are lots of fun activities and she keeps it interesting.

I hated this class.  She expects you to speak nothing but Spanish.  She can hardly speak english herself.  Tests are extremely hard.  She also grades hard.  There are much better professors to take for this class.

A wonderful professor!  I would recommend her to anyone!  I was at first intimidated after 4 years of not speaking spanish, but I picked up quickly because she always speaks to the class in spanish.  You learn much quicker this way and she helps you!  Trust me, these bad reviews are way off!!!

Well, I never asked to have this teacher since my teacher had to leave suddenly. She is HORRIBLE. Not only does she speak to you as if you already know Spanish fluently, she acts like you are wasting her time. Very unhelpful. NEVER take her!

I had Prof. Oscoz for Spanish 103 and 201.yea she does expect alot from you but she is a great teacher!Like any other subject you really have to study--she has weekly quizzes, which have no surprises on them. she has been my favorite and best instructor yet! she really cares about doin a good job!

Got "stuck" with our class when our professor quit, and she made it very clear to us that she did NOT want to be teaching us.  Treated us like we were a waste of her time.  Expects you to speak fluent spanish at 102 level - has little patience for ppl who can't keep up.  Bad professor, stay away!

She is an authentic Spanish Speaker; she's from Spain, so you know you're actually learning the language. I thought she made the class very interesting-she always has fun activities for every lesson.She's a fair-grader but does expect you to speak Span!
Wow, she come of as mean on the very first day, but from there on, she was amazing, very very helpful.
HORRIBLE INSTRUCTOR!! She wasn't very helpful at all! Her office hours were just a waste of time. If you want to get language GFR's out of the way don't take her class.
Easy A class. There were 2 assignments each week but it wasn't a lot at all. There aren't too many papers. He's chill.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Gives good feedback--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Lectures were extremely long (we're talking about 2 and a half hours per week), and although work was relatively easy, there was a lot of tedious busy work that felt unnecessary
This class was so freaking long and boring :( the class itself was easy but please find any other way to get this credit for your own sanity
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Honestly nothing wrong with the guy. The lectures are just incredibly boring and he often goes on tangents that will genuinely teach you nothing. The class it self is not hard to get a good grade in. I would only recommend this class if 1. You have to take it 2. There's no other options available. I've heard worse from other fys classes

Attendance not mandatory but is 10% of grade. 2 1/2 hour long class so was hard to get through some days. Note taking homeworks. Three papers and a final annotated bibliography. Tried to at least make the lectures interesting but I would not take the once a week class again. Overall an easy grader and not a super tough class.
he was okay, but the lectures were a bore.

Easy A, but was it worth it? This class was 2.5 hours, and I had trouble staying awake. Dr. Otten's lectures feel very awkward, and the class was small with minimal participation. 4 easy papers and weekly homework based on textbook readings. Textbook can be found online. If you are fine with a boring lecture, go for attendance and fulfill a req.

Took this to fulfill AH credit. Class was once a week, 2 1/2 hours long, but he made the topics interesting to listen to and would try to end early. 3 essays overall, & notes every week. Very lenient w every assignment. Easiest class ever, easy A. Love the man.

Laura Ott is one of the most organized, fair, and dedicated professors I've had the opportunity to take a class with. She provides you with the recipe to get an A in the class and a plethora of extra credit opportunities. She expects you to put in an effort for success but is extremely fair in her testing. Her teachings go beyond the classroom.
Good professor and cares about her students. If you do the work and show that you care about the class you'll do well.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring

reviews.comment: She grades hard and they can vary depending on if she likes you. The class is overly difficult, 5 labs and lab reports (basically essays) for only a 1 credit class. Ott is very unapproachable towards grades, so do not take her classes expecting to get an easy A. Also it's easy to get on her bad side. As a teacher, Ott can be very unprofessional.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: This teacher is very sweet and she is a good professor, but her quizzes and tests are both vague and hard. You need to go to every class, pay close attention, take really good news, and read, read, read and ace your term paper. If you don't do this, you're screwed. But, she will help if you aren't doing good, which was why I barely passed.
If you need an Arts/Humanities credit, do not take Art 220 or 221!! You only can get an A if you read the book and come to class.

If you can avoid this class,AVOID it!Can't believe its a 200 level course&she expects you to know the terminology&her little mumbling facts as well during her lectures.I am very aware of people w/accents but her's is VERY difficult to understand.She grades very stringent &critical&has written rude comments on my papers(1st time ever in her class!)

Wonderful teacher. Knows her stuff, likes to joke about the subject matter in the pieces. Very relaxing class: a long slideshow with neat history and cultural facts interwoven throughout. Papers and essays on tests were easy, and multiple choice was also easy, as long as you showed up/were intelligent enough to get notes from a classmate. All As.

worst art history teacher ive ever had. The term paper needs to be perfect to even get a grade of a b on it. Her test are very tricky due to her "multiple choice" questions. make sure you know every piece of art she talks about you will get tested on all of it!

cannot understand this woman when she speaks. what she talks about in class does not apply to the quizzes or tests at all. asks the most obscure questions such as the medium of the work, which is almost never mentioned in class.basically this woman is a dumb old lady.

This Art History teacher is surprisingly fit for an older gal.  A wonderful lady, will only be mean if you first show signs of being an idiot, but nice and helpful if you are humble.  Her accent can be charming, but is occasionally a stumbling block.  Also, with 3 As (2 of the 3 quizzes or the paper) and you don't have to take the final!

She is a cute old lady with an accent. The quizes are extremely detailed and it is hard to get an A on them. She doesnt have an assistant in the class and its hard to get help when there 114 people in your class. If you miss a class when there is a quiz or test, it is EXTREMELY hard to get a decent grade. 1 paper, 2 tests, 2 quizes TOTAL
great teacher, very friendly, helpful, and knowledgeable. eager to help all her students
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Participation matters--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: Tough class, but you knew what you had to do in order to do well. Professor Chumak-Strianese is very knowledgeable and helpful

Class was great! Russian is a very tough language for Native English speakers. Oxana does a great job making sure you know the basics. If you want to learn Russian you will have a very strong foundation after this class.

This woman seems lovely but I don't want her as my professor, and I'm planning to go to grad school for Museum Studies! It's not about whether the subject is interesting or the amount of work, but somehow she is just so unclear in the assignments, what she expects us to knowremember, and her tests are very tricky and confusing!

This class was difficult because the final grade was made up of 5 grades. All of the grades were from 4 tests and 1 paper. So you really have to do well on everything. It's important to come to class! You don't have to take notes if you have a good memory. Lectured from book, so no need buy the textbook if you don't have the money.

Lecture can be boring (I fell asleep quite a bit), bombed the first test. Almost never took notes. However, you need to study because it is all memorization, especially on essays. The art covered in the book has a khan academy videos to go with them! So I would watch those to help me study and prep for exams.

This class was difficult for me, because it is predicated on a lot of memorization. Like the person below said. GO TO CLASS, TAKE HER NOTES and READ THE BOOK! The answers are hidden in her lectures. She is extremely helpful, when you need it. Also, she is not afraid to call you a dumb@ss. Not a home-run easy class like some would think.

Had her for modernism. Don't know why people are saying she's unclear/bad. She's really not. She can be a bit dry, and has a thick accent. But not hard at all. Just show up, take notes. All you need is her lecture notes to get straight A's on the tests. Easy.

Very unclear wording on tests, worst I've ever encountered. The entire class had a failing grade but two people on the first test. If that many people fail it is the professor, not the students. A nice person, but a horribly unclear professor and is evasive with answering questions.

First of all - GO TO CLASS. And take thorough notes! That's the only way to guarantee an A. Her quizzes and tests do not just test facts - make sure you know the genre or other tidbits of information she gives you about a specific work. Her accent is a little unusual, but you get used to it. Not an impossible class at all.

She is Not At All clear on how she grades your tests/quizzes. Majority of the things you study won't be on the test (you're required to memorize about 150 works, only be tested on around 40 for the tests/quizzes).

Ah, this little lady. I had her for Art History 2. It's so easy to skip the lecture, but don't do it! Everything you need for the exam is hidden in what seems like useless ramblings. Date, place, style, medium. Everything else is just her talking. Study those points hard and make yourself known to get an A.

Adorable woman, and she really knows her stuff...has seen a great deal of the work in person. Never once read the book but used it to study, got an A on every test just by remembering the facts on each painting given in lecture. One research paper, not too hard at all. Great for an AH class.

I just have to say that this professor is from DENMARK.  She is not german.  Now for the review:  She is so adorable and I hope to heck I am that cute when I am her age.  Not hard to understand. Read the book and go to class.  At the college level you should be doing this anyway - if you keep up your end of being a student you will do well :)

Prof. Ottesen is very interested in the subject she teaches, which is helpful. Easy grader for the most part and an interesting class, would reccommend if you're looking for an AH class or even if you're not.

I enjoyed her class, but I can see how others might not like it. It was impossible to guess what was going to be on her quizzes, but I had no problem studying all of my notes since I'm interested in the material. Also, I'm not sure there's really a point to reading the book. I usually just studied from my class-notes and I got an 'A'

had her for art history II. she's kind of hard to understand sometimes, and some of the test material seemed bogus, but otherwise she's a very quirky, likeable person. she doesn't take attendance, teaches directly from the book, so basically all you need to do is just read the text.

She is a nice person in general but, she teaches class almost directly from the book verbatim if I bothered to read the book for the rest of the term I am sure.  She gives no clear definition on what is going to be on the exams/ quizzes; you have to study everything. SHE IS THE WORSE ART HISTORY TEACHER I HAVE EVER HAD!

Comment below:  she is not German; she is of Dutch origin.  Hard to understand her in the beginning but after awhile, you'll start to figure her out and see that she has a quirky sense of humor.   Typical class:  she talks about 8-15 works of art on large projections each with a little personal or academic story.  Some fun and some boring as hell.

Great Professor. She is very knowledgeable and has a quirky sense of humor. For this class, you need to either attend all lectures and take good notes to study from, or do all the readings and take notes. This is an easy class if you study for the exam and for the paper she will help you out alot with it as long as you dont wait until the last min

Hard to understand but very helpful. She is extremely strict but allow you to make up an exam if you bring in a doctor's note. As for her exams, VERY HARD. But if you know your material espically for the essay portion you are likely to get a B. Should attend all class because most of her quiz/exams are based on what she said during lec

She's German, so to some people, she's hard to understand. But she's very intelligent, and knows what she's talking about. If you get 3 out of 4 A's in the class, you don't have to take the final. Tests can be hard, but they are fair. You have to study, and come to class, or you probably won't pass.

She is very old but FUNNY. Hard to not fall asleep during her slides but your grades DEPEND on you staying awake! Write down mad notes! Her tests are a bit hard. Based on memorization... go to class. Stuff not in the book are put on her tests. For the essay, meet up with her outside of class for help; she's nice if you meet her individually.

Ok, here is the deal with this woman. You have to listen is class very carefully, because she will base a lot of her answers to the questions on the quizes on what she says in class. SO GO TO CLASS and you will be fine. I did just that never read the book and I got a C

Good qualities: She is EXTREMELY helpful if you approach her after class. Ask her questions about what you need to study, and let her proof read your paper. Easy 'A'.  Bad qualities: Her tests are SOMETIMES unfair. She asks trick questions, questions about paintings she did not emphasize, and once included a painting we did not have in the book.

A difficult class. I felt I had to neglect some of the work in my other classes just to be adequately prepared for the tests. Not a very flexible or helpful teacher.Can be forgetful about what she has told us.

Not a very good teacher.  Accent makes her difficult to understand.  INCREDIBLY hard tests and quizzes.  Her essay comparison questions are always out of left field.  Teaches everything from the book, leaves nothing out, so theres A LOT of material.  She is a rather nice person, just not a good teacher.
It's not too bad, a tad boring at times. She's funny and is nice so I like her as a teacher. Not too difficult a class
Accent can be annoying. Tests and quizzes are difficult even though I felt I was fairly prepared. If you take good notes and read, should be an A or B.

Exams can be difficult, she's not very clear on what the essay questions will be.  Tests are always multiple choice + essay.  There is a research paper  due at the end of the semester.  Always go to class and read the book.  It takes effort, you can't coast by in this class.

It's an Art History class. - It's not gonna be a cakewalk. There is alot of memorizing and 'critical thinking' as they say. To get a good grade all you need to do is read and go to the lectures. Her accent can be hard sometimes, but she's really friendly... and oddly funny.

Her accent can be hard to understand at times.  She'll tell you to read the book, but then she says the book is wrong.  If you disagree with an answer or a grade, dispute it.  She was very helpful on the Paper and will literally tell you what to fix before you turn it in, you just have to ask!

Her accent is kind of hard to get through. Make sure you read the book closely, and take notes in class... I went crazy with the notes and studied really thoroughly, and got an A. Her one paper is really easy... you choose what to write about. Got an A on that too.

Took this class last semester and it was an easy A. But only because I took PLENTY of notes and I love art. You really got to love it to do well. She's a little hard to understand but a good explainer. If you ask about whats on the exam, she'll tell you.

Though she seems like a hard teacher, you'll do real well by asking questions (after class...she's a bit hard of hearing) and taking LOTS of notes... and do the readings.  She has an interesting sense of humor.

Hard to understand her. She teaches straight from the text. Extremely boring class. An easy class, but she doesn't tell you what you need to know for tests and quizzes. Grades harsh. She expects detail! Take notes and memorize art titles and the artist.

Out of my entire program (Master's in Cybersecurity), this was the class I was dreading the most as it is law and policy.  However, Ms. Owen does a phenomenal job in ensuring it is not a traditional boring law class.  She kept my interest the entire semester and graded very fairly.  Do your work and you should easily pass.  Definitely recommend!
this class was pretty easy as long as you aren't a complete moron.
Great instructor.  Interesting readings.  Do your readings and you will excel.  Quizzes prepare  you for the final.  It is very much a discussion oriented class.  Have fun with it.
Dr. R is very kind, but her lectures are very long and over complicates some concepts. The class is an easy A just be sure to attend
Sweetest professor that I've had, and her voice is so calming. Workload isn't bad, and she's always excited to answer any questions in class.

Dr. R was an amazing professor and her class is set up for you to succeed as long as you actively participate. I appreciated how clear instructions were and how well study material and assignments correlated with exam questions. There was never a time I felt lost in her class. She was also super helpful during office hours.
One of my favorite professors at UMBC - take her for PSYC 311 if you can

Dr. R is a wonderful professor! You can tell that she is very enthusiastic about teaching the course through her lectures and the materials she puts on Blackboard. Offers tons of opportunities for extra credit and allows for up to 6 absences over the course of the semester (which is very generous as that is 3 whole weeks of the semester)

Dr. R is incredible! I was going through a very tough time mentally this semester and she helped me every step of the way, whether it be through flexibility in completing coursework, offering emotional support/resources, or going above and beyond and helping me find research internship oppurtunities! Her lectures are also very interactive and fun.

Dr. R is a super caring and knowledgable professor. She made an extremely boring and tedious subject more enjoyable and made me want to come to class. Offers a ton of extension opportunities and ways to earn points back.

Dr. R is an a amazing professor who was extremely helpful and caring to all of her students, I went through a tough semester causing me to have to be out of school for a bit.  Throughout that whole process she was extremely helpful and made me feel so seen! I 100% recommend taking this class especially with her!

While attendance was mandatory and we have a few regular assignments every week, she was always compromising and offered freebies/extra credit. She is not out to get you; she genuinely wants you to learn and always prepared us review content and lectures before an exam (all of which were take home). Great professor!
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Great class and great teacher. Easy A if you do the work for it. Super understanding in terms of late work as long as you let her know what's going on. Lectures can be boring as the material is quite boring itself, but we played games sometimes to break up the monotony. All in all, great and easy class, would take again.
She provides a wealth of knowledge and experience to provide context and enhance learning in a practical way. She is impactful in providing such a safe space to learn.
Loved having class with Dr. R. The content was always easy to digest and everything we did in class corresponded to the specific week we were in. She's also really accessible outside of class!
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Dr. R was such a wonderful professor - she was so understanding and gave many extra credit opportunities! Would love to take her course again! :)

Dr. R was a great professor!! I had her for the summer session and she was more than helpful whenever we needed guidance. She is very understanding and gave lots of extra credit opportunities (which really helped since EVERY point matters!). Hopefully, I can take another course with her again! :)

Professor Rakhshan Rouhakhtar was so great! Provides many extra credit opportunities, exam preparation materials (practice exams/kahoots/practice questions on a document), and kept lectures very engaged. There are 3 exams (including the final) She is very sweet and knowledgeable about the content. I would definitely take a class with her again!

Prof Rouhakhtar is one of the best profs I've had in a while. Maybe I've been unlucky in recent classes but this professor genuinely seems interested in the students and was encouraging the whole time. There were also opportunities for extra credit and I didn't stress over my grade too much which was very nice.
Great professor. Willing to help and enthusiastic about teaching. Group assignments for participation grades take away from typical lecture monotony.

She is so wonderful. I highly recommend taking her class. For a writing intensive course, I was very pleasantly surprised with how it was set up. She is extremely kind and caring, you wont regret taking her!
Great professor, interesting class, easy grader.

Perry sensei is one of the best professors I ever had Her teaching style is structured easy to understand. The TA holds helpful study sessions before tests, and offers extra credit for attending. Retake opportunities are available in certain cases. Memorizing hiragana and katakana beforehand makes the class much easier.

Perry-sensei is very caring and understanding. She can be somewhat confusing but a ton of extra credit opportunities are offered (every workbook page is extra credit for the tests). Be prepared for a lot of forced participation and a few group projects.

Perry sensei is an amazing teacher who really does care about the students w/clear instruction makes tough Japanese concepts easy The TAs are helpful to and provide beneficial review sessions though sometimes out of reach You are able to retake tests and kanji quizzes as well Be prepared hiragana and katakana come in no time Plz Memorize them

While she gives students plenty of resources to get help on assignments she grades pretty tough. Loads of assignments are quite tough and confusing. If you're willing to study the textbook, participate in class, and ask questions you'll see success. I would only take this class if you're serious about submitting assignments and know some Japanese.

Learning hiragana before taking this class will save your life. Perry-sensei is very kind and cares a lot about her students, but isn't very good at explaining things and can be impatient with students who don't understand the material well. Study the material on your own before class time and use lecture as review.

I only recommend this class if you're serious about learning Japanese because this will most likely be your hardest class this semester. I went from an F to a B by the end just by putting in extra effort into studying and submitting assignments. Please learn Hiragana prior to enrolling, it will help GREATLY. The professor is really nice and caring.
Perry sensei is a strict but fair grader. If you are seriously interested in the course and actively study you will get along great with her and have a lot of fun.

A good choice if you want to challenge yourself and truly learn Japanese. She can be harsh at times if you don't study, but really rewards students who do. To succeed, definitely complete all homework and put in good amounts of extra studying. Criteria is usually clear and she responds quickly to emails.

She's nice. But stay away from this class. Her instructions aren't clear for most hw. We have 2-4 lessons videos, 1 written hw, and 4 test every WEEK. Lesson videos suck bc they're 10 minutes long & u have sm multiple choice to answer. And for a set of 2 Q's, even if u get 1/2 right, it marks the whole thing as wrong. Test have stuff NotInUrUnitYet

Hard to find things in the Blackboard. Tests every week with short time limits. Short deadlines for kana/kanji writing assignments. Doesn't use limited class time very well -- for first 10 minutes, calls on students at random to answer questions in Japanese (making everyone anxious) or sometimes berates us for not studying enough. Avoid for online.

This's a beginning Japanese course and yet the materials aren't beginner-friendly at all. She expects you to learn all Japanese characters in the first 3 weeks. Heavy testings + giving lectures from other professors. Learn basic Japanese before taking her, or else you don't know wtf is going on. She's friendly but can't explain things well.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Hit or miss. You have to self teach and lecture is going over practice worksheets and speaking, you're expected to know everything. If you don't understand something you're done for. She gets upset when you don't understand something and isn't very good at explaining things. So if you don't understand one thing you'll fall behind.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Easy class. You are expected to learn the materials outside of class first and the lecture is spent doing practices. Attendance is part of your grade. There are quizzes and tests for each lesson (L1-L6). There's an oral test at the end, where you and the partner you chose have to talk about a role and situation that she assigns.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Group projects

reviews.comment: Peggy clearly has a passion for design. Sometimes the projects are overwhelming and hard to understand, though. She's a very "figure it out yourself!" type of professor. Intimidating and confusing. Not my favorite class, but we did get some nice portfolio pieces by the end. She also gives a ton of feedback if you ask for it.

This professor is tough but if you're on her good side you'll do well. She wants you to think critically about her feedback and your work, instead of just telling you what to do. Her projects are very structured and a lot of work all at once sometimes, be prepared to do a lot of sketches.

Peggy is one of my favorite professors at UMBC. I admit, I wasn't too keen at first, I thought she hated me. Her feedback can feel brutal, but it's extremely valuable, listen to her! She's a harsh critic because she gives a damn about preparing her students. Wish I could take this class again because I didn't give it the attention it deserved.

Peggy is very intimidating and no-nonsense at the beginning of the semester, but she will warm up if you warm up to her. Do your homework (all the sketches on time). She is the best design professor on campus - projects seem boring but she is teaching you the rules so that you know HOW to break them in the future.
It was my favorite class of the semester. I learned a lot.

Peggy was one of the best design professors I had at UMBC. Her personality is intimidating at first, but by the end of the semester you'll have so much great design scared out of you you'll really be amazed. Class was a sink or swim situation, but she'll really give you the knowledge and tools to do design portfolio-quality work. Highly recommend!

She is an Awesome professor! She is a bit intimidating at first but you'll get use to it. She clearly knows her stuff and I guaranteed you will learn so much his this class. She is real honest in critiques and this will help bring the best out of you! She's a truly passionate designer! :)

Hated going to class.... didn't enjoy her personality too much. She's intimidating at first and you may cry, maybe. But after a while you get used to the awfulness of projects. I agree, just be glad to graduate soon...

She's pretty intimidating. Pick up the slack. Don't procrastinate.. suck up her sometimes cold personality. Just be happy you're graduating? The workload is do-able and critiques are the usual.. it's just HER that sometimes bothers me.

Peggy is a really good professor and an excellent designer. I never had her as an art history prof, but as a graphic design professor she is practical and you will learn a lot that will help you in your portfolio and career. She's tough and honest, but I improved a lot in her class

does not have a degree in teaching a history course and tells the class this freely. lectures are boring and hard to follow. quizzes are hard bc she doesn't specify what is expected of you. hope to never catch her on a bad day, if you are nice and respectful to her she will return the favor. likes to answer cell phone while teaching, which is odd

She understood that students may have had obligations outside of class and offered to extend deadlines because of that. She presented the material in a way that was easy to understand. She took the time to explain how to utilize the APA format, provided us with multiple resources, and provided us with all the necessary citations for our essays.

We were pretty much only graded by our essays (there's 3) but there were a good amount of in-class assignments but were only 1 point each. Her lectures are boring but I didn't have to pay attention or show up to get an A (you should tho because of the in class assignments). She is an easy grader except she's harsh when it comes to grammar in essays
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Lots of h/w, but you'll be thankful for. It'll help you with the exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Participation matters

reviews.comment: 7 short 1-2 page papers on readings. 1 small test based on first 4 weeks of class. Then the final paper is 8-10 pages. The final paper was really tricky. She's super nice and flexible, just talk to her about anything! She checks attendance. Cancels class every now and then. I really recommend her. She makes the hard readings super easy to understan

By far, one of the best professors that i have ever had. Gives great feedback, extremely lenient, and extremely nice. She's funny and very down to earth. She also understands that you're a student and have other priorities. Will give you extra points if she sees that you're struggling. Tough final paper and her class is a MUST-READ.

Loved this class! Pfeifer is a sweetheart and I hope I get to take another class with her soon. The class is super interesting, and you get into it pretty easily. Our topic was Paradoxes, and it was just great. Take this with her when you can!!

Dr. Pfeifer is a great Professor! Very knowledgeable, clear, fair, and challenges her students to work hard. Not an easy 'A', but if you put in 3-4 hours a week for this class, expect a very good grade. Very fair grader, and offers criticisms to improve your writing. Take her at least once at UMBC!

Dr. Pfeifer is very knowledgeable, clear lecturer, approachable, reasonable grader, and builds her lectures around the class. 2 papers (25% each), 2 exams (15% each), 2 group debates (14%) and attendance is mandatory (6%). Study the 12 question study guide; ace both exams. Papers require effort; she accepts drafts for critique. Good looking lady.
Very interesting class!  She's extremely open to discussion, and plays a very good devil's advocate to draw answers out of you.  Really good at making you thing... and not bad to look at, either. >_>

Great professor, one of my favorites.  Very clear and descriptive while exposing us to abstract concepts.  Study the notes and you'll ace the tests, group debates are pretty easy, but you can't bs the papers.

Very clear and nice. The material is easy, and she makes a concerted effort to explain it. (It doesn't hurt to take notes, but you very well could be able to soak up enough by osmosis in the class.) Class discussions sometimes limited to honors students, as no one else wished to participate. Highly recommended.
No Comments
the best philosophy teacher here. she is very helpful and doesn't make ti difficult to get an A

Sigh... if only she weren't married. She's adorable, patient, logical, helpful,.... Just come to class and pay attention and her classes are great fun. One of, if not my absolute favorite professor here. And philosophy isn't my major at all.
She is a great teacher... and she's very cute too. She gives great review sessions and is willing to help out with anything you might have a problem with. Take this class if at all possible.
best philosophy prof i ever had. clear, well-organized, and always helpful.
Dr.Phillips focuses on useful information and also brings in individuals from the field to provide first hand info.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Beware of pop quizzes--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Dr. Phillip's class was great. Definitely my easiest class this semester. She does pop assessments during class which are always easy. Some weeks we didn't even have class. The only annoying this is the group project because it's an online course. She could also do better with answering emails. Overall a great professor.

Very chill class. She only holds lecture every couple of weeks and generally reads off the PowerPoint slides. An infographic group project, a few pop quizzes, a current events presentation, and 3 exams comprise the grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Beware of pop quizzes--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Really easy professor who cares about helping her students succeed. Made the material interesting to learn.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Group projects--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: This is a professor who not only knows what they're talking about, but wants YOU to know what you're talking about. Her class was extremely immersive and her mantra was, and I quote, "if you have a question, just ask." She really wanted us to be open with her about when and why we were confused, and she was very accessible outisde class.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: This professor is great. I like her method of teaching, she keeps it current and interesting. She leaves room for students to put in effort on their own and learn and not burden you with heavy lectures. There are two presentations and as someone who does not like public speaking it was not bad at all.

reviews.comment: There are easy pop quizes to check attendence. Boring lectures unless people get her off topic. Otherwise, she seems bored and just reads off of her own slides. Very chill class.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Clear grading criteria--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: It is an easy A class but really boring. You dont really need to read the book for an exam. Go through her study guide. Two presentations - easy. Her exams are from her PowerPoint slides and study guides. She goes through her PowerPoints really fast but she posts them online. She is knowledgeable but I didnt learn what I expected.

Dr. Phillips is a good professor in the sense that she is very knowledgeable. With that being said, her lectures are lacking. We only went over the textbook, never any of the additional readings she assigns. She just goes through her powerpoints and provides minimal insight unless you ask. Gives good exam reviews and they shouldn't be too hard.
I think shes a good professor, pretty straight forward 3 exams 1 final paper. Tells you exactly what shes testing and what to expect. Read the book and look at her lectures and youll get an A

Prof Phillips is mediocre at best. Standard format of 3 exams and a semester long group project. The exams are all essay format so if you're not a strong writer then I wouldn't suggest taking this course. She is a harsh grader and gives little to no feedback as to how students can improve their writings. She also takes months to grade assignments.

Weekly DB's and responses to classmates become extremely annoying, huge research paper due at the end of the semester is a real pain (notified class that at least 7 references were needed a week before it was due, which was very frustrating I had already written my paper), &  lectures are very boring and gives a lot of busy work during class.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES

reviews.comment: Prof Philips is one of  the best professors I have ever had at umbc. Her class was super easy. 3 exams and a presentation. She tells you exactly what to study for the exams. Material is easy and she makes her lectures interesting. Show up and pay attention in class and you will get an A.
Resta is a good professor but definitely goes on tangents during lectures sometimes.  He knows the material well, and he's funny.

Took this class for winter sem and it was so easy. Prof gives good examples and theyre easy to understand. u get a midterm, final, and a very easy assignment. exams r open book during winter class since its online
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Graded by few things--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: Really enjoyed his class for Intro to Clinical and Couseling Psychology. It was a 4 week online course and despite it being so short I feel like he really took the time for lectures well. Very few assignment but he was very accommodating
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: LOVE this professor! Graded by only two exams + one big assignment. The exam questions are straight from the things he says in lecture, so attending his in-person lectures, writing notes, and even paying attention to the videos he shows is CRUCIAL. But if you do that, easy A+!!! Exam questions are simple, you can also defend your answer and get pts
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This man was genuinely one of the worst professors I've ever had. There were only three things you were graded on the entire semester. He yaps the whole lecture, and it's hard to follow what he's even talking about. No slides were used the entire semester. I passed the midterm purely by using Quizlet. Would not recommend.

Resta can be ver rude and blunt. Half of the class, he complains about the students who aren't there rather than teaching the one's that are there.  Exams were in person, closed book, and based off of things he says in the lecture so attendance matters. The videos he showed in class were extremely out dated, from the 80's and 90's so beware of that
Prof Resta can be blunt, but his class is doable if you attend lectures and use resources like the textbook and Unstuck ai for study prep. Exams focus on what he covers, so participation is key.

Very openly rude (he does not care), condescending, and tells a lot of unfunny jokes. He spends an hour of a two-hour lecture telling his personal jokes and stories. Would not recommend if you're looking for a serious professor who actually wants to teach and not cosplay as a failed standup comedian.

Good class and funny professor. To do well on the midterm and final, you definitely need to go to class and take notes because he mentions a lot of things during class that are not included on his slides/notes. No graded homework or quizzes, overall easy A if you attend class and pay attention. His stories are also quite interesting!

People seem to love him or hate him. His real life experience is great for this class though, I love his stories and they are relevant. Midterm, final, and one paper are only graded assignments. Just show up and listen to lecture and you will be fine. His sense of humor isn't for anyone but I think he's funny. Definitely interesting guy.

I love him as a professor! He is genuinely so funny and he does care about his students even if it doesn't seem like it. He wants you to do well and makes it easy to do so if you GO TO CLASS! He will emphasize things during class that are relevant to the exams which are a big portion of your grade.

Love Dr. Resta! His personality could be misunderstood but he is sweet and kind and loves/is good at what he does. He is a great lecturer. If you show up, ask questions, and be engaged not much outside work is needed. A midterm, final, and paper make your grade. Tests are off lectures, so don't skip. Be nice to him for me you are in good hands

He is a little straight forward and can be taken as rude if you are sensitive. His tests questions are based off what he says during lectures so don't skip class. He likes to blame students for everything, doesn't take much accountability. Definitely Autistic.,

EASY A!!! 2 exams based on stuff he says irl so u HAVE 2 go 2 every class. SUPER EASY project which is just a summary of 2 disorders. he harps on attendance & has a brash personality but hes a comedian if ur not on the receiving end of his wrath lol. its actually impossible to fail if u just go to class and read the textbook.

He is very rude during lectures, constantly blames students for their performance, and brags about how 1/3 of the class passes. He uses a disorganized sheet of paper as a means of note-taking. There are only three grades for the semester, tests are heavily lecture-based, and 2 out of 3 assignments are due 2 days apart. (aka final and 10-page paper)
test questions are extremely specific and difficult
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Take 285 with him if you're willing to go to class and take notes. It's not very hard, and he can be really interesting. Both the midterm and final are really easy if you pay attention in class. The chapter review assignment is also very easy. I would recommend this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Resta is funny, but he is extremely hard to approach. If you are unclear about something, it's best to ask the other students rather than him. He will belittle you, say that you have psychological problems, and blame any confusion on you being stupid. But, his class was easy if you put in the time in effort.

Prof Resta is not as bad as people may say. While he may be blunt and sarcastic at times he is still a good professor, just don't take everything he jokes about to heart. The course grade is based only on a inperson midterm&final, and a chapter review assignment. The course is fairly easy if you go to/pay attention to lectures (exams are based on).

Dr. Resta is an entertaining and passionate guy. The course was graded by a chapter review assignment (super easy as long as you write enough content), a midterm, and a final. Both exams were super easy and were based off of stuff he said in lecture. The only time I used the book was for completing the CRs. Super chill prof despite what people say.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Hilarious--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The exams are very straight forward and much of the exam is based on what he says in lecture so take notes  and don't miss class. The textbook is necessary and simple to read. The syllabus and class notes is unclear but use it as a guide to review

Dr. Resta is overall an amazing professor. He is very enthusiastic about this course. You have three grades: Midterm, Final, and chapter review. They are all easy if you pay attention and take notes. You would have to go to ALL classes in order to pass, but if you do the test are very straightforward. Incredibly nice prof, and he wants you to learn

Dr. Resta is a funny guy and his class was relatively easy for me. He is very blunt but funny and you are graded on one assignment, the midterm, and the final. If you pay attention in lectures and thoroughly read the textbook, you will be good to go. I cannot stress enough the textbook is the key, I didn't go to lecture and still got a good grade.

Resta definitely has strong opinions but he is a good professor. Attending the lectures is important for your grade since his exams include questions of what he stated in class. He is not that hard of a grader. Just go to class and watch the videos he post and u will be good plus get a few laughs out of his lectures because he is blunt.

The worst professor I've ever had. Only three assignments the entire semester. Doesnt answer emails. Exam questions are phrased like "on the first day of class what word did the professor use to describe (insert whatever)". Makes exams 10X harder than they need to be, as most people don't take notes down to the specific word. 0/10.

He can be very abrupt to the point of rude about some topics and does not care to work with students. There is no homework for the course, only a project, midterm, and final, so you really should not skip class. Class is entirely lecture based so be ready to take good notes. The class itself isn't very hard, but he can be very rude to students.

I love psychology and Resta made me love it more with how he would explain stuff. He grades by only 3 things so I recommend attending all of his classes in order to do well on the mid terms exams and finals because most of what he says is what comes out. He's sometimes funny and really understandable IMO.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The best professor! His British style of sense of humor makes learning fun. You learn things you can apply in your life and career. To get an A, you dont have to mountain climb, write books, or take pop quizzes. Just go to class, pay attention, take notes, and dont wait to the last minute to study! My only regret is not taking more of his classes

He assigns no work, the entire semester he only assigned 3 assignments so if you messed up one there was no chance of recovery. Pretty easygoing guy but the tests were based on what he thinks and what he said in class, so if you miss any classes your grade will suffer for sure.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Resta is a decent guy, lectures are fun but slow. There is only a midterm, a paper, and a final exam for this class. Tests are really easy if you know your material.

Honestly, the people in this class complained sm but it wasn't bad. If people listened carefully, they'd understand that the topics he speaks about aren't his opinions but rather topics of debate between psychologists, instead they all rushed to insult him. He's an ok guy, lectures can be a bit slow but he records so you can watch at 2x speed.

He really just talks to himself but he's easy. Read what you don't know about but everything else is pretty easy tbh. He says some things that might trigger some people but he's really just straight forward so beware. He is really confusing with his grading too. You don't know what you have until the semester is over

Stay away from this guy. He is super rude and unapproachable in person and online. He rambles on and on as if to just head himself speak. You can literally hear the cockyness and smirk in his voice. He does not provide a clear grading criterion nor does he explain anything clearly. It seems his single purpose of teaching is to be belittle.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Rude ! Has no desire to assist students and a very nasty way of expressing himself. Unapproachable and rambles on and on !! Quizzes ? Oh yea they are based upon what HE THINKS so you better pay attention during his rambling spews .

I've taken 3 classes with Dr. Resta. He's "eccentric" but that's why I appreciate him so much. He is not afraid to challenge the norms of the field of psychology. He's a very engaging professor, incorporates humor, & is genuinely a cool person. Grades are determined by a midterm, a final, and some other large project (ie, a paper). Would recommend!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Hilarious
