reviews.comment: His lectures are long and much of what he teaches is opinion based, make sure to pay attention to what he emphasizes. Your grade is compromised of a midterm, final, and reflection paper. Go to class and it's an easy A.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Good lectures but very slow to go over material. If you like learning at a fast pace this class is not for you. He'll probably spend 3 hours to go over cognitive dissonance using two different stories. Still, his lectures are amusing and easy to digest. Tests have questions on them that you'd only know if you were in class. Concepts r from psyc101
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Professor Resta does not use Blackboard, so skipping class will definitely hurt you. He's a very interesting guy, but his lectures are very opinionated rather than fact. Most of his exam questions state, "As per instructor" because he only teaches what he believes in which is pretty biased. You could have a better professor for this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Resta is amazing! I had him in undergrad and I honestly miss taking classes with him. I probably took 4 courses total with him, including really cool special topics in psychology classes. He thinks outside of the box and tells you exactly what is expected. Rare gem. Highly recommended! Youll learn a lot and getting an A is very doable.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious

reviews.comment: He definitely knows what he is teaching as he lectures in class. Long lectures but his humor makes the time pass. Everything he says is easy to understand and if you ask him questions about something, he will answer them with more detail. But he is not the type of teacher that wants to build a relationship with his students; he can be very rude.

took him over the summer and was the easiest class i have taken at UMBC. Go to lecture, be engaged with the lecture, take notes and ask questions. this will guarantee you an A. Grading was based on 2 exams and a paper ( exams based on lecture). Scored a 90 and 95 on the exams without reading the book. Used the book for writing the paper only.

He' s definitely an interesting guy, but his eccentricity makes for an interesting lecture. He keeps your attention well, and gives great examples and clear explanations of the topics. There are only 3 assignments the whole class, as long as you do the one short written assignment and go to the 12 classes over the semester, you will get an A.

Although Dr. Resta is a bit old school and simply lectures the class, he is very knowledgeable and answers any questions you have for him. I advise you attend all his lectures and take notes because if you do, you're guaranteed an A. He is a very easy grader, with only the midterm, a long paper, and the final as grades.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Prof Resta is the most unprofessional individual I have come across in my educational journey. If you'd like to be shamed in front of a class of 80 students, be sure to take his course. He is unapproachable & arrogant. When mentioning and incident at work, one of his former grad students spoke up & said he has a reputation for being sexist.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Tests? Not many--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Excellent professor with enjoyable lectures, but a bit eccentric.

Prof. Resta is a great professor. He is a corny man, but he tries to make the class interesting. If you go to every lecture and pay close attention, you can  easily get an A. He is very detailed in his exams, specifically about the videos he shows you. You do not need the text book except for the semester paper.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious

reviews.comment: He is fantastic! Super interesting! But, if you don't like going to class, don't take him

Easy A. Interesting material. Totally a weirdo. Can be mean to students but only if you dare to raise your hand or ask for help. Midterm40%/Final40%/Paper20%. Always ends early. Hilarious but goes on lots of tangents. Dumbs it down, super short/easy tests. Don't need the textbook. If he doesn't say it, it's not important. Show up every class.
Resta is one of the best professors Ive had at UMBC. Show up to class and pay attention and you will pass. No quizzes or homework; just midterm, final and paper (wasn't long or hard). Easy A.

Dr. Resta is one of the best professors I've ever had! His exams are everything he covers in class, if he didn't talk about it in class you wont need to know it for the exam. He's had a lot of experience in the field and often includes real situations/stories in his lectures. You only need the tb for the chpt summary. Would take again!

Resta is an easy A, but his personality really takes away from the class. I took social psychology out of interest, but found that I actually learned next to nothing. In lectures, he covers 3-4 pages of text max, but you need to attend in order to know what will be on the exams. There were two exams and a paper included in grading - nothing else.

If you like social psychology take him!!! His voice may be loud if you are not used to a guy yelling in a closed space but its just him being very excited to teach the course. He is dedicated to helping students learn and absorb the fun material. Don't miss class cuz you will be called a "bopper." Inspirational class is exciting!!!

Dr. Resta is awesome! This class was one of my favorite classes at UMBC. Attend class because the exams are based on lectures. Dr. Resta is hilarious and makes the lectures interesting. Definitely would recommend him and this class to others.
Funny professor and interesting class!
Dr. Resta gives good lectures with weird humor. Go to class and you'll be fine. I usually read the material assigned however, the lectures will cover everything you need to know. Easy A!

Took this course along with social psych. He's an extremely knowledgable professor who loves what he does and has awesome stories to keep you engaged. Mid-term, final, and a 10 page paper is all there is to these two classes. Exams are easy if you attend lecture and take notes!

Professor Resta is amazing.  He is funny, engaging and very insightful.  I learned so much in the two courses I've taken with him.  You absolutely have to attend class because his exams are based solely on his lectures.  He does not use Blackboard or PowerPoint.  Write down everything he says no matter how insignificant it may seem.

Easiest class of my undergraduate career! NEVER opened a book-just never missed his lectures. Got a 100 on the midterm which is based RIGHT OFF HIS NOTES. Overall, he is a pleasant teacher with a wierd sense of humor
Worst professor I have ever had. He is the reason I refuse to take Social Psych. Avoid unless you enjoy getting abused.

Extremely engaging! I actually like this class and enjoy going to it. He's very knowledgeable and is an excellent lecturer. Never boring. Very down to earth. He can be intimidating to approach though... but I think he's just encountered too many stupid questions that have already been explained. Refreshingly direct. I'd take any of his classes!

He's weird and funny, but at the expense of students. Just attend class, take notes, do the end of the semester chapter summaries in order to get an A. The tests are MC and he lets you defend your answers. He can be very rude and demeaning. Overall, unique professor, but easy.

One of the best professors that I have had.  Straightforward, extremely knowledgable, exams are easy as pie, engaging.  Don't really have any complaints except that he doesn't use Blackboard.  Looked forward to going to class

Very knowlegable, presents information clearly, entertaining, doesn't waste your time, very upfront class, easy A as long as you pay attention, do the chapter review paper, and read the book selections and handouts..one of my favorite profs

I took Paranormal over the Winter. The class was interesting. Guest speakers towards the end were very sincere even if I didn't always agree with them. Grades are based on 1 research paper, 1 exam, and 2 short writing assignments all due by the last day. Exam was multiple choice and open book essay. Very easy if you just go to class.

Awesome professor! This class is the love of his life. Come to class, ask questions, TAKE NOTE OF EVERYTHING HE SAYS, briefly look through the book = easy A. Resta is one of the best professors I had...Funny too! Don't be late for his class!

He knows the material but covers very little info due to constantly repeating himself & telling dumb stories. Don't go to class, get notes & skim the book = EASY A.  Beware: he doesn't truly care about the students - just likes to hear himself talk. And don't ask questions, he'll just give some obnoxious response & try to make you look dumb.

I've never had such a funny and interesting teacher.  He always finds stories to capitivate your attention and manages to link the boring things in the book that we must learn into these high spirited fun classes.  I just wish he had a little more interaction or that the class wouldnt be so big.

Easy and interesting professor.  He is definitely entertaining and enjoys his job. The 2 hour class goes by quickly and actually isn't a pain to sit through. I had to miss a bunch of classes and still got a 95% on the midterm. Awesome guy!

everybody already mention evrything that needed to be said. there was a bopper that got a 54 in the test. he ask for help, the following week after class, he was giving him a class on how to take gd notes and how to be succesful. this was the best class i have ever taken. too easy, but explains the material well. the bomb

Dr. Resta is an interesting, yet easy professor. The grading system is 3 tests (which are extremely easy if you listen in class) and 2 chapter summaries (which are easy as well - they just take time). This is a class where the book is hardly used. Oh.. and don't be a bopper! (you'll  come to know that term very well)

This guy is very annoying. He repeats himself constantly, has a grating sense of humor and is generally rude to students. Come to class because a lot of exam questions are based on things he says or film clips he shows. The class itself was very very easy. 3 MC exams and two chapter summaries. Only a handful of people got less than a C on exams.

Prof Resta is a very interesting guy. He can be hilarious, but often at the expense of calling out students, which I didn't particularly care for. The class consists of a term paper, and a mid-term and final (both multiple choice) which are based entirely from the lecture notes, so take good ones. Overall, an easy A, and relatively enjoyable.

Resta is an interesting and easy Psych professor. He lets you defend your multiple choice answers. The grade is 3 MC tests and two chapter summaries. This is an easy A! He can be pretty entertaining with some of his stories. Take him anytime you can!

I just graduated and I just wanted it to be known that Dr. Resta is the best professor that I ever had while at UMBC. He is EXTREMELY helpful especially if you see him after class. He will keep you updated and go out of his way to help you prepare for your future. I had 2 classes with him (Personality and Controversies) I'm gonna miss him!

Those who said this is the greatest professor around, probably never had the same one I had. Overly loud and random. throws snide insults on your test and the says"im sorry you took it that way" even though he knows and you know it is an insult. The man never stops. He has his plus though I will give him that. But overall classless... beware.

one of the best professors I've had here. he comes off a bit corny in the first couple of lectures, but i think it's to get rid of boppers. PAY ATTENTION IN LECTURE. he emphasizes what he wants you to know. exams are not that hard if you COME TO CLASS, and you will barely need to touch the TB (until the chapter summary assignment).

You won't meet too many professors like Resta; he's quite unique. He knows how to keep a class going, and he's very knowledgeable of his material. He throws in many jokes into his class periods which keeps the class from being boring. Seriously, the only way you can fail is if you "bop" the class (you will hear that a lot). Overall, I recommend him
Just go to class, test are based on his lectures which are easy and simple. Tests are straight to the point. Easy A. He's great! and essays are on a check system, simple and easy! :)

Count how many times he says the word 'bopper'. Resta's classes are extremely easy. His exams are mostly based on his lectures, so go to class. You can probably do just as good if you don't go at all tho. He usually lets you out early. One paper, and it's easy. EASY A, minimal effort.
Easy class, but not my favorite teacher.

easiest professor ever. he is hilarious. his exams are really easy if you were conscious during lecture, you will get a 100. 15 pg paper graded on check system. very lenient, does research on UFOs... great professor, makes abnormal psyc fun...

Very nice professor.His examz are easy as long as u go to class and take notes.examz are right from it. Old examz are extremely helpful since MOST questions are repeatative..15 pg paper is long and painful.. DO NOT think he wont read it b/c he sure WILL..if u actually put sm time for it, u'll b gud..Easy and fun class overall..take him :)

resta is a little out there but he keeps things fun and entertaining. his "Tests" are easy and very redundant but people still manage to get the stuff wrong. as far as the paper on restas top 10 issues that was a little lengthy and i felt like i could only write so much about adhd and the drugs that go with it. over all really good and fun.
funny and helpful. we only had two exams and a paper. the exams were very easy as long as you've been in class. the paper was graded by a check if you did it. so easy to get an a. take him
Take him for as many psych classes as you can. Funny, easy!!! Trust me--I am a psych/bio major I made my life way easier by taking him. Just go to class and pay attention and you'll be fine!
Dr. Resta is hilarious.  I had no idea psychology was so funny.  A good teacher who makes a not so interesting subject fun.  The best lecturer ever!
I loved him he is funny. Pretty easy too. Try to get him for as many psyc classes as possible.

If you're looking for easy, he delivers.  Not only are the tests straightforward and simple if you attend class, he'll curve them a few points (I got a 100 and 103); even the 15-page paper gets full points if done correctly.  Despite this, you will learn a lot with his vast experience.  The big problem I had was that he belittles questioners a lot.

Loves: Aliens, UFOs, etc etc. Hates: Boppers & Loserdudes. You'll see. Anyway, good class, though I regret not taking it seriously enough to go. If you don't go to class you'll do badly on the tests and feel stupid, cause the subject is easy. The 15 pg. paper is graded on a CHECK SYSTEM.
Requires the writing of a 15 page paper, if you're not into that sort of thing I'd avoid this class

This prof is AWESOME. He makes class really worth going to (which is a good thing since if you miss a class, you'll definitely miss questions on the exam) He shows a lot of video clips in class and makes a lot of jokes (sometimes directed to "class boppers" and "sleep boppers" - take his class and you'll find out what those are ;D)

One of the best teachers at the school. The material itself is interesting but his teaching method is so clear and cut to point just like his tests. His tests are not hard at all because the questions are straight to the point. You don't have to read the book, but do take good notes because his tests are based on what he says during the lecture.
interesting topic.  he's a really nice guy, and pretty entertaining.  His tests are pretty easy.
nice guy. class can be a little boring at first, but only because he makes sure you know the basics. just don't take it at night. easy tests.
awesome teacher. He cracks jokes all the time.
freakin awesome. you better be interested in aliens cuz he talks about them every other day. easy tests and nice guy. can be boring or funny depending on his mood.
nice guy, boring class
No Comments

He is a really old style teacher but he is funny as hell. I had him for psy285 at night but his teaching style and crazy personality kept me up.  You only have three exams and one writing assigment in his class, word of evidence do the writing assignment early and get it out of the way.

Very old school teacher, uses a chalk stick (he brings himself) to get his point across, exams are easy, but he assigns written papers for the semester.  He is a unique one and will keep you paying attention and keep the class going well.  Funny and well taught.
No Comments
Very hilarious..will keep you laughing the whole class. Very clear. Also fair exams. Interesting class.

Awesome teacher! His tests are pretty easy and he keeps lectures fun and exciting with his odd personality.  I would definately take another class with him, despite his odd affinity for UFO's and aliens.  Highly recomend to take his classes.

He is just great, always keeping you intrigued, making you want to go to class knowing you'll stay up to pay attention because this guy is very entertaining and knoledgable in psychology, the tests are based mostly on lectures and some of the book, i loved it
Nice guy but totaly crazy :)lectures are very interesting and exams are easy too.
Very nice man & funny. Tells great stories. Very passionate about Psych. Extremely easy exams. No final. New to UMBC in Fall 2003. Very knowledgeable & approachable. Would take him again any day.
Amazing man, very knowledgeable, very funny. Kind of a nutcase, but really enjoyable class, will generally keep you up. Very intresting material.

A somewhat unconventional instructor with a dry sense of humor. I found that simply reading the textbook was sufficient to perform well on exams. Enjoyed time spent in class for her half of the semester.

Dr. Robinson is funny! But her teaching is not as clear. She taught the second half of the semester. Her preparation was good. Technology seemed a big challenge for her during lectures. Her movies would not play which delayed the lecture at times. She is willing to break concepts down! Helpful! Cell biology is a tough course so get ready to read!!!

Nice lady, but a bad lecturer. Reads off slides and doesn't add any other insight. When someone asks a question , she usually doesn't understand the question and does not give a clear response. I got high Bs on the exams, but it was from reading the book and doing the learning objectives-only went to lecture for the clickers. Avoid if you can!
Won't take ever again. I don't know what she is doing at university. No clear explainations. Feeling frustrated why I took her course.

Not a very good professor. She just reads off of the slides and going to the lectures are pointless. Her questions on the exams are confusing and she words them weirdly. Offers little to no explanation. If you actually want to learn something, don't take her.

Honestly the worst professor I've had in 4 years of undergrad education. Illiterate, ill spoken, rude, disrespectful, and unreasonable are just a few descriptive words that come to mind. Although, at least I now feel confident about getting my Ph.D. If /she/ could, heck, anyone could! [Avoid at all costs; some people just aren't meant to teach. :(]

She is the best professor I've had at UMBC. Easy grader, very clear expectations, exams are fair. Before you graduate, take her class! Easiest upper level biology class. This is a joke compared to science of water :). Happy to help!
Sketchy grader.  Grading varies among students with no explanation.  Don't take this class with her unless you are a mind reader. Bad experience.

Dr. Robinson is very subjective when grading exams and papers.  It is difficult to know which answers she is looking for.  She will deduct points with no explanation.  She does not have regular office hours; you have to make an appointment to talk to her.  You can spend many hours on this class each week and still not receive a good grade.  Avoid!

Her lectures are confusing. Talks about biochemical pathways for minutes on end and then says we don't need to know them. Interrupts others during discussions with unrelated questions, very annoying. Sits on her iPad during discussions but yells at students for doing so. Draws pencils like straws to pick who does presentations. Avoid if possible.

Mr. Bovender was extremely knowledgeable of the course content. I found the life experiences that he shared to be eye-opening to what we can expect in the clinical nursing world. I hope to be able to take future courses from him.

He is easy but not very fair. He tries to be nice but gets in his moods. He likes teaching and I got the impression that he wanted his students to succeed, which I can not say for most of the other teachers. But he was lazy about it. If you ask him a Q, he will answer. Overall, better than most of the other crazy clinical instructors at UMSON.
Phillip Bovender was absolutely awesome.  REally likes what he does and is very knowledgeable!  If he is available you should really get into his section for clinicials!!

Dr. Seng is a very talented orator who can turn a dry subject into something you want to learn more about.  Tests were all short answer or essay, but all were open book.  YOU HAVE TO READ THE BOOKS to have a chance at doing well on tests.  He grades hard and is not lenient on "almost" answers, but if you read and listen you will get an A.
good teacher very nice also understands where students are coming from.
Hes a nice guy, cool character, but stop making the tests so hard! Dam I mean I read everyday and still can't get an A in the class.

Had to read 15 to 20 pages a class, than he would give you pop up quiz on the reading at the start of the class without taking about the reading. The test are multiple choice and have to write a final paper. Do not take this guy if u need to meet the GEP there are other professors who don't do this much work. Does not curve at the end.

An AMAZING professor! Dr. Seng teaches VERY well, he is very clear, his exams are fair, and accurately test knowledge of the material. One of the best professors I have had in my entire college career. Philosophy can be a bit dry, but I learned a lot and had a good time doing so, thanks to Dr. Seng

Philip Seng is the man. He's hilarious, knows a lot about the Philosophers and is overall a nice guy. There are pop quizes, but they are nothing to worry about if you get the gist of the readings. He puts a study guide for all the tests which are useful. The hardest part of the class was the movie paper, but it wasn't bad. Great prof.
Seng is the bestest professor ever. He makes me want to philosophize every day.

He's a real nice guy but I really didn't enjoy the class. Every day it was the same thing: read a 30 page article that you have to print out & talk about it in class. Kill me. He is very helpful and will reward you if you use his office hours, have him read over papers, etc. Very understanding & a good guy.

Phil is an awesome guy. There is a lot of reading, but for the most part all of the in class quizzes are pretty easy. The class can be very boring, but he makes it fun with his random humor. He gives you study guides for each test, and every question is on the test, along with exact questions from the quizzes. You should definitely take this class.

This professor was arrogant, and overly-convinced that his answer was always the right one. and you can't do that with philosophy. the course was absolutely horrible and i do not reccomend taking any of his courses unless you are hopelessly obsessed with philosophy and arrogant philosophers

Took the course over winter session online. It was four 3-4 page essays. I usually can't stand philosophy, but this was a truly interesting class, the readings were relevant and thought provoking. Highly recommended.

What a great professor! Very helpful,funny,nice, understanding,and clear. The study guides include every single question on the test, and sometimes even the page numbers on which to find the answers. Alwyas read before class, he gives pop quizzes. Even though he is a very nice guy, don't take adavntage of it and turn in a paper late. He wont let u.

i love him! 1 of my fav at umbc! he knows philosophy is not the most interesting thing in the world, so he  tries to make the class as least boring as possible. he cracks jokes; he's funny and nice. he will cut you some slack and if he sees that you at least try in the class, you will do fine. go to class, take notes, and you'll pass!
Dude is definitely a good professor considering it's Philosophy.  There is no textbook, but there are readings.  Funny guy and made the class better for sure!

I wish I had the room for more classes with Seng. He's comfortable with the material, smart, and brings plenty of insight to discussions and lectures. He's a fair grader and helpful editor. I'm casually trying to get him into the MCS department.

Lectures were great for understanding the readings, and littered with jokes. I thought it sounded a little rehearsed sometimes though. Very clear about what you are expected to know. Great professor, interesting class.

Definitely one of the most intriguing professors I've had.  Explains difficult/poorly written/weird philosophies rather well and with a high level of social grace.  Exams are straightforward and accurately reflect the knowledge you're expected to acquire.  Fun guy, great professor.

Professor Seng's one of those teachers who can get along with students on a humorous level and just go with the flow. He loves telling jokes and being funny, yet he also stays grounded in the lesson at hand. That's what makes him such a good teacher. He can relieve a stressful lesson with a good joke and go right back to it. Highly recommended.

Seng is a really funny guy, and he makes the class fairly easy. About a quiz a week consisting of 2 multiple choice questions that he basically covers before the quiz. If you need this class or are just interested in philosophy, take Seng.

One of the best teachers at UMBC! I was not really into PHIL, but he makes the class really easy! have to write two papers and is a fair grader! does not curve at the end, but there is no curve necessary! if you are taking PHIL just to fulfil the AH requirement, then take it with him! dont really have to read the book, explains very good!
Really good class. I learned a lot about Philosophy. You dont really need to do the readings if you pay attention in class. The guy's a sweetheart and loves his topic of study.
Cancels class all the time.  Assigns heavy readings (3 textbooks for this one class)!!  Pretty much a worthless class.. if you are interested in the subject take Philosophy of Science
Best honors class I ever took. Also very easy.  A lot of reading though.

P. Seng is Peter Griffin with a really nice beard. my man is sarcastic, funny, and about as emotionally mature as any college freshman. Even if you dont read he still makes things pretty clear, and if you go to class youll get an A. Take him over any other philosophy teacher
Very funny and intelligent guy. Talks to class a lot very friendly, and makes good jokes every class. Gives you main points of each book you read and is fair grader, highly recommend him

I took Philosophy 100 and 150 with him.  He's a very good teacher and makes the class straightforward.  If you show up, participate, and glance over the readings you will do fine. I had him for 100 and 150.  Great teacher.
Cool guy. He reminds me of one of my friends. It's boring but reading philosophy is boring, nothing to do about that.
Great teacher.  Made everything more relevant and easier to understand.
A very easy going prof. Nice funny guy
funny, down to earth guy, keeps class interesting. the readings can ge a bit tedious and boring, but the movies are always fun to watch.

Fun class!  Teacher is down to earth, funny, and helpful.  You watch movies and and read philosophy papers, then you compare the ideas in both mediums.  He normally let us out early.  Highly recommended!  The only problem is just doing the readings; they tend to be long and complicated.  Have fun relating Karl Marx to the movie Office Space!
he keeps things interesting. one of my favorite professors since i started at UMBC. i enjoyed reading and attending this class. highly recomended professor.

Farabough has a great sense of humor but his lectures can be a bit boring because he pretty much reads off the powerpoint slides. Fell asleep in class a couple of times. His exams arent too difficult. Textbook is too detailed and expensive so dont waste your money.

He was an OK professor. The exams weren't too difficult, but they were pretty hard-only bc he put problems u didn't really practice on the tests-u basically had to take the best guess.Also,for future students:go to class, and take good lecture notes, do not simply read the book, it has too much detail!! I made this mistake! Take good lecture notes!

he was a good teacher that taught the material well. he was easy to follow in class and helpful outside class. to do well, you have to know background (memorize) but also be able to understand topics and why things happen. if you can explain things inside and out to other people, youll do well.

The nature of this course is that it won't be easy unless you know how to memorize. His tests are extremely hard, and he asks questions on details that may not always seem relevant. It isn't that the material is hard to grasp, there is just a lot of it. Homeworks help to cushion your grade. Generous curve. Funny prof. Very approachable.

Lectures are clear... he does a good job answering questions. Reading the chapter before the lecture helps significantly. His sense of humor is slightly twisted and he seems to have it in for anyone who's won a Nobel prize. He's not the most accessible guy in the world, but that's about what you expect in a 300 person class. I would take him again.

guess it was first time teaching genetics; therefore he gave generous curves, but still got B. studied the textbook, notes, etc...didn't help; just skim thru the book and try to memorize all the ppt notes. i don't think he's gonna teach genetics anymore, but... i still can't figure out how i should study for this class...

Very hard course. Studied night and day and weekends. Memorized the book. So many people repeated the course so you're competing with those already w/ knowledge, making it harder...Professor makes mistakes w/ slides, questions, cannot work cps...horrible class. Lecture is confusing. So much information!!!

If you think you know genetics and that this class will be easy, you're wrong. Professor was nice, but confused. Lots of mistakes on the slides, rarely got CPS working. Exams were almost impossible. Very detailed. To pass, memorize everything in the book and on the lecture slides. There is a generous curve (82 was an A in the class).

He knows what he's talking about and it's mostly pretty clear. He's so boring though and mumbles in a monotone voice. He might be funny but I can never hear the 1 or 2 jokes he cracks in class clearly. Overall he's not terrible but not amazing either. Tests are hard.

Doesn't lecture, he reads his slides in a sleep-inducing monotone. Every day the info on 1+ of his slides is incorrect and he gets mixed up. 350 students; 70 average on exams.  More interested in tricking us than teaching us.  (Very convoluted exam questions--he thinks we should "figure out what is being asked.")

Prof. Farabaugh is a great professor. The class IS difficult so you should be prepared to do the work and study for the exams, but that's not above and beyond what you have to do for any class. Prof. Farabaugh really knows what he's talking about and willing to help if you're having trouble. He cracks a lot of jokes and makes class less tedious.

People end up taking this class because they need a 400-level to graduate and they hear that Farabaugh is a funny guy (true). It's a journal class so you'd better like to read. I think people walk into it expecting a hilarious character who's going to hold your hand and pass you no matter what-- but It's a graduate level course so that's a mistake.
No Comments
An extremely cute professor,  should definitely take!
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Greatest professor in the entity IS department.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Professor Pillai is truly one of the BEST Professors I've had during my time at UMBC. I wish all professors were like him, he makes students feel welcome, confident, and motivated to learn. I wish him all the best and hope he continues inspiring students the way he inspired me.

Pretty chill class. HW is just 8 readings, and you write about them. Attendance is only mandatory for 10 points, so after that, you don't have to come. 3 Exams are online, no camera, and pretty easy as well.  Lectures are alright, some of it is interesting, and sometimes topics are hard to care about if you're a student. 

Overall, Easy/Chill
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: On the last week of class, he went way to deep of irrelevant to the class and continue to talk about his work style about how he work at Howard County for so long etc. It is extremely annoying and so damn boring to read since it not related to the class.

THIS Professor, he ranted way too much and called people out, saying that one of his sections was terrible. It was very annoying—he needs to learn to stop ranting and just teach. He often ranted at his students about how they don't read his announcements. He also shared way too much about his personal issues AND CALLING PEOPLE OUT! TETRIBLE!

Main only complaint is his communication style/personality. Way too opinionated and oversharing. Complains that students do not read his announcements thoroughly but sends essay length communications that are mostly irrelevant or personal information and rants that do not pertain to class. I don't dislike him, but things like this are off putting.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: just no NO no no no
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Easy to focus for someone with ADHD which is saying a lot. Class is filled with entertaining stories and examples from his own life that makes concepts stick in my brain. Enjoyed the lore and also the life/work advice. He stayed after class to help people understand concepts from other classes they were in which was super cool to do.

You just need 10 attendance points, each class equaling 1pt but there are special classes worth 2pts once you get 10pts attendance is not required. Exam is on lockdown, no camera, questions aren't too hard just study the slides. HW was kind of annoying due to the readings might take a while to finish but only 1 HW per week so not too bad

Great professor, very nice and understanding, and explains the material well. You can actually pass the class without the textbook by just attending lectures and reviewing the slides. Attendance is optional but I went to all but the last lecture and every single one was really good. 

Gives lots of practical advice and the hws are easy if you think

Pretty chill guy. Lectures aren't awful, slides are posted online. HW is pretty easy if you write genuine responses and don't copy/paste. Exams are wonky; lockdown with no camera, so make of that what you will. No mandatory attendance. It's an interesting class, but still meh overall.

Very good professor, quite literally the embodiment of Information Systems if there every was one but not in a way that is complex or difficult to understand.

Great Professor,
Good Lectures that are entertaining,
Invest in a water bottle and congratulations on getting married!

Absolute GOAT of teaching. 425 is now my favorite class of my entire undergrad! Everything is explained perfectly. First time I actually enjoyed doing exams and assignments, they are super easy but require critical thinking (which is great). Lectures are short, but you learn so much valuable info from him. I promise you'll love going to class!

I thoroughly enjoyed this class. Prof Pillai introduced many new topics for me and provided reading material for us to gain further knowledge of our field. Could complete assignments early. He also writes messages and provides a FAQ for students to read. You can tell he actually cares about what he is doing and I really respect that.

He is the best example of what and how college professors should be. He is understanding and fair at the same time and teaches his courses with enthusiasm. Always communicate with his students and constantly remind them that he is available for them.
I wish all the IS profs at UMBC were like Pillai, super helpful and caring.
As a professor, he's okay, slightly boring sometimes but his class was very easy to pass. Do the homework, listen to lectures and you'll be fine.
Best professor. Helpful, funny & obviously easy to pass get an A in his class.

Fantastic class. I would recommend for your final semester. Lectures are interesting and engaging, a lot of discussion regarding emerging technologies and the concerns behind them. I actually enjoyed doing this classes homework as well which is extremely rare. The material was engaging the professor clearly cared about us and what he was teaching.
Wants you to do well and very helpful if you come to him with questions. Classes are kind of dry but he does his best to make them interesting and exams are straightforward
Manesh is the GOAT. He shows how this class applies to the real world while throwing in his opinion on. certain topics. Overall great guy and would highly recommend him for any class.
He is an awesome professor. Very knowledgeable. Highly recommended.

Hands down the best professor ever. The instructions were so clear for the homework that you couldn't go wrong. The test were amazing as long as you pay attention to class and follow his slides. He is very open-minded so you can ask him questions if you like. Would give him 6/5 but Ratemyprofessor doesn't let me do that.
Manesh is such a cool guy! Take him if you can!!! Really chill and the class is super easy because he is such a good prof!!!

Really cool and understanding professor. His lectures are interesting as well. You can tell he genuinely has an interest in what he teaches. Homework consists of somewhat long readings, but it's easy as long as you actually read it. Exams are based off his powerpoints.
Honestly the most understanding professor ever. He made online learning interesting and non-stressful. His lectures are interesting and exams are based off slides.

Having him at 10am was a little jarring since he starts off his lectures at a volume level of 7000, but he might be my favorite teacher ever at UMBC. The quizzes have unlimited attempts and are extremely easy; The exams are also exactly like the quizzes/practice exams. He's a stickler for having phones out but other than that he is super nice :)

I loved this guy. The class is so easy, literally unlimited attempts for all the quizzes, and the exam is exactly like the quizzes and practice exams. I personally find his humor and presentation style to be interesting and engaging. I'm a senior and wish I could take another class with him before I graduate.

I had a really bad experience in his class I took during the summer. He has a much heavier focus on statistics than other professors who teach the same course. However, he is very knowledgeable and I would recommend to those who may be interested in really learning the stat portion of research design.
Great professor. Took him for Summer Session II. Lots of opportunities for extra credit (IP points). Overall easy going just a lot of assignments (which pay off in the end).

It was a really cool class. He made what is usually very boring material, fun to learn with his excitable nature. He doesn't count attendance towards your grade (but if you miss two classes you can not participate in the 5% extra credit). Very nice, great in office hours. He might be intimidating because of his high energy, but he is super nice!

Loved his teaching style and made things so clear theough lectures. Alot of extra credit opportunities. Only down side is that he is very intimidating. I literally was scared to answer or ask questions in class or go to his office hours, which cost me my grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Grades heavily influenced by 4 tests. Easy homework and online quizzes. Take the quizzes a million times as the test questions come directly from those quizzes. The teacher is very passionate about the class. He wants students to succeed.

I loved this class! There is very little homework and you can take the online quizzes as many times as you want. There is a lot of reading involved but the topics are really interesting! The lectures are so entertaining and he really tries to make them fun and relatable. Definitely take this class!

Dr. Pitts is a great professor and has an abundance of knowledge. He is rather hyper during his lectures and appears to dislike students asking questions... it seems to throw him off a bit. But he is great and there are very few homework assignments. His tests are really easy and basically composed of the same questions from the bb quizzes.

Great professor, only 3 exams and a final all non cumulative. Blackboard quizzes for each section only a couple of chapters each, can take as many times as you want, which you should take advantage of because the majority of questions on the quiz will be on the exam. HW&Quests 1 for each section, pass or fail work, really simple. Take this class!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: I took his class for the summer.  He offers up to 5% of extra credit to the class. After the first week I stopped reading the book and just went to lecture. In class he'll tell you what questions will be on the  in class quizzes. If I took the blackboard quizzes more serious and just reread my notes a little more than I probably could have got an A
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Mr. Pitts is an excellent teacher. This class is moderately difficult and there is a lot of material but overall it was great!! He makes the lectures interesting and it's awesome that he lets you get partial credit on multiple choice questions (choose two answers). I can honestly say I learned a lot in this summer class. Highly, highly recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: A little unclear in class but he is very good at posting the lectures online and helps a lot in office hours. Blackboard savvy so don't try to put anything past him. A little intimidating but he means well and is super passionate about his field. Tells a lot of jokes in class to make it more enjoyable. MAKE SURE TO PARTICIPATE SO HE KNOWS YOUR NAME

He is an awesome prof, I had him during the summer, his exams were straight forward, no surprises.  He gives detailed slides but also read the textbook thoroughly to ensure you are fully prepared. I look forward to taking more classes with him.

I have never rated a teacher before but it was necessary because Dr. Pitts is in the top 3 teachers i have ever had. He wants you to do well, he is genuinely funny, and he's always ripping a cig outside maths/psych building. HERO!

go to all lectures and labs. you never know when he'll give out extra credit. He tries to help his students pass. the material is VERY boring but he tries to make it fun. I got a D but if i had tried i probably would've gotten a better grade.

"Never overlook the simple answer. Writing isn't a pissing contest. The point isn't to sit there thinking, 'Ha! Ha! I have a higher IQ than you.' The point of writing is to communicate...to inform. Any time the reader cannot understand your writing, YOU as the writer have lost." -Dr. Pitts. My main man. Fair. Funny. Exciting. Brilliant.
Sometimes nice, but mostly abbrasive. Can be overheard trashing students behind their backs. Can become hostile if you do not understand a concept right way.

Have him now for Psych 331 and will for 332. Honest rating is that he is a very very good teacher. Explains material VERY clearly and uses great examples so you get the picture. Very goofy and funny, but that is def needed in such a dry course. Not an easy class if you dont try but if you try, hard not to get an A and very unlikely you will get a B

Steve Pitts gives the students every advantage he can. Of the many professors I've had in my entire college career he is the most sympathetic towards students in the way he constructs his grading and course work. Every professor should follow Pitts' model of teaching.

I thought this class was so hard until I took 332 with Groninger. Pitts is funny, he provides worksheets in lab, and worksheets to review before exams. Utilize these and the online quizes. Best teacher to take this course with, wish I would have waited a semester and took 332 with him as well. I have been using his WS for 332 bc my teacher sucks

Subject is incredibly boring, but as a teacher and a person he's awesome.  I chose him as my advisor.  If you study thoroughly and do the worksheets u should be ok.  Study 2-3 days in advance though.  Take him if you can.  Hes very helpful and very fair.

Great teacher. If you have to take 331 I highly suggest taking it with him. The subject is boring but he does what he can to keep it interesting. I am really bad at math and am expecting an A or B. The class isn't easy if you're not good at math but he makes it easy to do well. Do the worksheets!

Good professor. It's really as good as the material can get, since the class subject is rather dry. He is very helpful as long as you are a good student and not one of the slackers who falls to sleep in class. Picture doesn't do him justice, he's pretty attractive in person, although a smoker. He's pretty funny + excited about the topic he teaches.

Do not really like him. You honestly have to deticate all your time to this class to receieve anything above a D. As a person he is okay. But as a Professor not so great. If you want an easy A. DO NOT TAKE HIM! If you want a B. DO NOT TAKE HIM ALSO! Unless you are super smart with a lot of time on your hand!
I HATE him! An Okay Professor but does not help his students out with grade. You have to study and do well. No extra credits. No second chance!
Pretty Moody and unbalanced.

I loved Dr. Pitts. I received an A in his class & believe it's easy if you just do the work. Taking this class over the summer, with this professor, was one of the best decisions I've made! He's funny & willing to help you if you need it!

HE is an OKAY Professor.... don't really like him though. A little weird and goofy but it helps get you through the class. Must attend class because all exams are taken out of the class lecture. wouldn't recommend the class if you want an easy A. If you love studying go for him. Plus he doesn't really help his students out with grades. What you get

Dr. Pitts is the best Professor I've ever had. His classes aren't EASY, but he is more than willing to help you. He's absolutely hilarious in class, and really makes the BORING material entertaining. If you do the work, you will do well.I failed his class TWICE, but I did the work the 3rd time and got a B. I liked him so much I made him my advisor.

He is an awesome teacher! You must go to class though to pass, EVERYTHING is taken from his slides &  most of the questions of the quizes/tests are from the homework, we did not use the textbook at all. I have had a wide range of professors from horrible to excellent & Dr. Pitts is an excellent, he is what a professor should be.

Disappointing. His office hours (and the TA's) were hard to work with to get help. I wouldn't recommend this professor if you have a really hard time in Statistics. I would go for Stapleton, since she has much better ratings and lets you use notes on your final. His final was 81 slides/14 pages long... The test didn't even cover 1/2 of the review!

The Pitts? No way! A goof? OMG, yes! He's cute though. Smart and funny. He's not Brad Pitt...but he's still easy to look at.  A LOT of work to get an A in this course. Easy to pass, but hard to get a super high grade - unless you work
No way is Pitts the "Pitts". He's the best teacher I've ever had. He is smart, funny, attentive and wayyyy hot.
He is a horrible professor. I did not enjoy this course. His jokes are not funny and he makes the subject boring. HE is the PITTS!
he really knows his stuff. he is energetic and funny.  the material is hard but if you go to class and do the homework you will do fine

Passionate and energetic teacher, pretty easy course-work, and helpful TAs.  The material may not be for everyone (psychology statistics, bleh), though Pitts makes this go smoothly and can keep you from falling asleep as much as humanly possible.  Don't forget to stay for the lecture after quizzes for extra-credit answers.
Awsome prof but very boring subject although he tries to make it interesting.  very clear notes and very helpful no surprises in tests but they are a bit hard. does not curve

He is an awesome teacher, lively, and entertaining. The class is hard but he tells you everything you need for the exams (absolutely no surprises). And he has lecture slides that cover any and everything that will be on the exams. He couldn't make it any easier for a student to do well as long as you come to class and learn the material on slides.
He is a very good teacher. He designs the lectures so that everything is very clear. Make sure to attend lecture because everything is taken from lecture notes, I never used the book and I got an A.

this is the guy to take exp. psyc with! granted it is a late class and boring material, Pitts knows what he is talking about and makes learning stat really easy. the quizzes and labs are easy if you pay attention to the material. you get to drop 2 quizzes, 2 homeworks, and 2 labs. he makes it hard to NOT get an A!!!!
Dr. Pitts was awesome, very lively and lots of fun.
this man cannot come down to teach on an undergrad level. you have know idea whats going on and neither do his ta's
funny and good teacher, hard and boring subject, tests are hard, no multiple choice, all fill in the blank and short answer, hard to get an A

Yeah the topic is hard and he is the best teacher to teach it i think, but for me the class was easy since im good at math, I got an A even though i slept through a couple lectures.  He is funny and excellent at teaching.
Good teacher for a difficult class.  Tries to really help if you meet up with him 1 on 1.  Entertaining while still getting the lecture done, something really nice in a lecture hall.

Very clear, organized teaching method. Print out notes online before class. Listen to good lectures.  Sometimes goes off on interesting and amusing tangents, but then comes right back to where he left off. (Some professors haven't mastered that. They just get lost.) Bonus questions on exams!
Smart, funny, kinda crazy teacher. Loves his caffiene. This is a hard subject, but he is probably one of the best teachers you can get to teach it to you.
He explains the concepts really well and always tries to make time for the students. Helpful and a fair grader
Easiest lab I ever took, not because the class was easy, but because Dr. Pittman made it fun. All grades were fair and I learned a lot.
best teacher at umbc by far. take any class he teaches
best teacher at umbc by far. made lab fun
Indubitably the best professor at UMBC.
Awesome professor.  Really knows what he is talking about and can explain the most complex problems very simply.  If he is teaching a course, take that course!!

Not the best lecturer. The class was 90% homework, so I just focused on the projects and ditched the final. Each of the 4 projects is doable in a day or two, so it's not a tough class. I would try to take it with a different professor tho.

The class was structured pretty nicely. The course is structured with a Group Project, Homework, and Final Exam. Prof was slightly late for the final (5 mins), but it wasn't a problem. Review concepts and understand them properly and you should be set for this class.

You can expect more organized ml stuff in a random youtube video than in his class. Disorganized for the whole quarter and late for 90% of the class even for the final exam. It seems he has no time to prepare for the class and care about the students. TA is not very accessible as well. Dont waste ur time.

most of the class was based on homework but the TAs were incredibly helpful and generous with the grading. everyone i know has an A, most with over 100% because there is so much extra credit. the lectures are a little crazy sometimes but he is very considerate and respectful, and helpful if you ask! definitely recommend this class

Let's examine this professor's responsibility. He displayed a lack of responsibility by frequently arriving late to sessions, being an hour late for the final exam, failing to provide rubrics for homework and the final exam, neglecting to offer sample questions for the final exam, and not providing feedback for final projects, among other issues.
No discipline. No sorted course content. Canceled many classes. Late arrival even in final exam

I have no idea why would some student rate this professor 1/5. As long as you actually spend some time you will get an A in this class. This professor is super responsible. I never saw a professor would be willing to stand outside the classroom and answer all kinds of questions for almost 2 hours. (The class only takes 80 min)

Took him for Computer Vision in Spring 2019. Learnt more in this class than any other at UMBC. The homeworks were challenging, but grading is lenient and there is extra credit. Start the homeworks early! You also get to choose any final project that you like (related to Computer Vision), so you get to be as creative as you like.

Although attendance is not mandatory, you're going to need to study the slides intensively and the lectures do a great job of explaining the topic. The class has few assignments that require strong understanding but the grading is lenient so long as you know what you're doing. It is a manageable class in a light semester.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Lecture heavy--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: He teaches very well and puts effort into it. However, the downside is he assumes that the student has enough knowledge in machine learning fundamentals. He also speaks so fast that you won't be able to catch up with his technical jargons. I believe he should make student understand in plain simple English language rather than jargons.
One of the best professors at UMBC. He knows everything. In Machine Learning, Computer Vision, Maths etc
Exceptionally qualified. Has an excellent understanding of the fundamentals. Explains concepts intuitively. Should have some sufficient stats knowledge as a prerequisite.

Class was Computer Vision, Hamed is incredibly smart and humble - too smart for this school to be honest. Goes very fast, english isn't perfect but he's conscious of it. No tests, no pressure, just START THE HOMEWORKS EARLY. They can take 48-72 straight hours. Be aware of the difference between a test-based and a project-based class.

Dr. Hamed is one of the best professors I have had at UMBC. His homework are interesting and very helpful in understanding the material. His lectures can be confusing but don't be afraid to ask questions (he encourages them). The class isn't easy but you will learn a lot.

Good teacher. Homeworks were appropriate difficulty, no exams,  open-ended semester project. Lectures were mostly clear and well-prepared with real-world applications. He was a little inconsistent with dates and deadlines. Very friendly and helpful in office hours.

Tough but fair professor. Lectures are to-the-point, though attendance is required. Textbook is used but not strictly necessary. unstuck study ai proved handy for quick review before exams. Overall, a challenging class, but manageable with dedication.

This teacher has poor character. A classmate brought up a shared issue, which put Sokolov on the spot. Next class he had a clicker question where he gave the scenario of the raised student, but coupled the answer with something so obviously detrimental to students grades no one selected that answer. Then he smugly commented how he was right.
Pretty tough tests, he retired but I actually love him as a professor!! I'm going to miss him.

Sokolove is tough. If you're looking for an easy A, don't take him. He's tricky and will give you very tough questions to answer. This doesn't make him bad, though. I'd say that Sokolove is a good teacher. I learn a lot from listening to him and his study questions are very helpful. Just study for the tests or they will destroy you.
Overall, solid teacher.

Very sarcastic demeanor, doesn't understand that is out of the scope of the professionalism in an educational educational environment such as this . That being said, exams are fair if you put in the work. And go to class!

Personally, I don't like how this class was taught. Lectures were boring, and you never really get an answer to your question. Even for discussion assignments, your answers are graded based on whether you support your answer with evidence - could be the wrong answer with the wrong evidence, you wouldn't know. I had to teach myself the concepts.

Professors say lecture is not mandatory, but clicker questions you miss in lecture are worth in a 15% of your grade, so GO TO CLASS. Second, (if you are given 1) GO THROUGH THE PRACTICE EXAM! Third, READ THE TEXTBOOK, or you will be clueless about the reading quizzes, clicker questions, and study guide questions (which he bases the exam off of).
He gives handouts but doesn't let you even know if what you are studying is correct.
This class is hard, but not impossible. Find as many people who took the class before and get their advice!

First of all do the reading quizzes textbook readings and go to class (clickers are form of attendance). While his policies  limit the TA's and he never really answers the question, he definitely makes you think about the answer. He does have tests that you must read all the way twice to make sure you have the correct answer. Overall not terrible.

First off, read before coming to class. You won't do well if you aren't prepared for the lectures. Do all the reading quizzes, bring your clickers to class and ask for help when you need it. Also, study from his past exams! He uses the same questions from old exams in his new ones. This helped me get a B in the class.
Sokolove's not to bad for lecture, just the content can be really confusing, especially if you don't go to lectures. He "takes attendance" by clicker questions, so they're easy points. READ
You have to read- trust me

Sokolov wasn't a bad professor. He was definitely very sassy to students who talked back to him. Overall he makes you think more beneath the layer, which is good. It's a pretty good class. I enjoyed it. Feeser wasn't nearly as good as Sokolov.

This teacher was very unhelpful and insulting. The students who had taken AP Biology in HS did better but if this is your first time taking Biology do not do it...  Major time commitment & the professor tells the TA's to not answer your questions.  This class is a weedier out course for STEM majors. DO NOT take for non-lab science credit.

Sokolove can be more than your average professor. Definitely enjoys being condescending at points, but overall not a bad lecturer. Sad to see him retire soon. He wasn't anything like most of these posts say, perhaps it was due to the fact he only taught about 23 of the semester. Overall, nice guy, definitely more bark than bite.
terrible.  very condescending and arrogant.  lectures are boring and rarely answers questions.

In this course, you never receive answers. Everything is always so open-ended, which makes it hard to know whether you're on the right track or not. The lectures did not help me at all, especially since it felt like the PowerPoints were just copied and pasted from the book. I'm pretty sure this was his last semester though.

Sokolove is tough, but he prepares you for the harder courses to come as you progress through umbc. He is researching effective teaching techniques, so everything he does, he does to help you learn. He is tough, but its his job. You get what you put into it. Take time to study for this class. Study the learning goals and his old tests.
He is degrading.

Read the book. Go to class-clickers. You will regret it if you don't. All 3 exams are literally exams from previous years. Do your study questions. The final sucks bc there's no practice exam. If you get A's on all 3 exams then you can get a C on your final and still get an A. GO TO EVERY DISCUSSION & treat it like a real class. DO NOT SLACK OFF.

Attendance taken through clicker questions. TAs are not allowed to answer questions and are sometimes confused about the practice exam Qs. Exams are recycled from every semester so study the previous exams that he posts because they are similar if not the same. ALOT of reading but online quizzes are easy. Take your time on exams and go over twice.

His exams are almost identical to his previous exams so if you study fully you can easily get an A or B. His lectures are incredibly boring and some sleep through it. He will not give you straight answer to your question. he will try to guide you to the right direction but can be really confusing.

The best strategy going in is doing the readings before class, ask him questions, and make a good schedule for reading. A 30 page reading can seem overwhelming the night before, but if you read 6 pgs/day you should be fine--DO THE STUDY GUIDE QUESTIONS ALONG THE WAY! If you dedicate yourself to this class and do his practice exams, you'll get an A.

His job is to weed out pre-med students and he is awesome at that. He's very tricky and condescending. He made me feel dumb when I asked questions. He posts practice exams but does not post the answer keys, you if you take a practice exam, you have no idea what you know or don't know. He drops your lowest exam grade and curves nicely though.

His teaching style is a bit unique, but he isn't a bad teacher at all. The lectures are very helpful if you read before class. His study guides are basically everything on the exam, so make sure you know every single little detail about the questions on the study guide. Aced the class with an A

He was intimidating in the beginning, but tbh the guy was WAY more bark than bite. The exams were straight from the study guides he gives us. And he answers the study guide in order, in class. Do the readings, show up to class for your clicker points, do the study guides, and read the exam questions carefully. Really easy with a little effort.

Sokolove was not good. He hardly taught and instead of teaching the subject he gave us his opinions. He was condescending and very rarely answered questions. You'll ask a question and he says "good question" and doesn't answer it. His exams don't test what you learned, they test your attention to detail and if you can read.  Good luck.

Throughout the semester do not stress too much- he puts no grades online, but everything turns out better in the end. He is a confusing, frustrating, unhelpful, condescending teacher and no one knows what his take on a bio concept is. The structure of his class will drive you bananas. Don't let this course scare you though, bio is actually fun. GL!

I had his class last semester and he was pretty nice. He gives joke breaks, teaches in lectures, and the clicker questions aren't bad. Record the answers to them each class and save exams, he recycles questions. I rarely read but studied the past exams and ended with a B+ overall. Study and read; his class is do-able, the curve helps, you can do it

Sokolove is known to fail a lot of his students. However, I learned to love biology after taking his class. But it's really IMPOSSIBLE to get an A without sample exams. GET THEM NOW. Even if you think you'll be fine, trust me you'll regret it after your first midterm. I would not have been able to get an A without past exams from my friends.
He made me feel worthless.

Worst professor I've never had. I made this account just so I could review him. Very condescending, try to avoid at all costs. Very childish, and requires "name signs" in order to ask questions. Exams are very tricky, not a fair test of your knowledge of the topics. For some reason, he "cannot tell you if your answer is right or wrong". Do not take

Definitely one of the hardest classes you'll take in college, but very worth it if you're willing to put in the work required. I have never been happier or fought so hard for a B in a class before. He will challenge you, but he's willing to answer your questions as long as nobody else asked the same question before you.

Dr. Sokolove is an extremely nice guy when you talk with him OUTSIDE of class, but he is a straight up jerk INSIDE of class.  He's rude and condescending, and if you ask him a stupid question, you will get straight grilled.  Listen: know the study questions inside out, forwards, backwards, and sideways, I guarantee you will get an A.

Know the study questions in and out and memorize past exams. Many of his questions come straight from past exams. Sokolove is condescending and rude to students, and unwilling to listen. He lectures way too fast and much of the time he's very confusing. But I was too afraid to ask questions because he's condescending to those who speak up
He's a great professor. You'll learn biology in a different manner. As long as you read the chapters, do the study guide Qs and understand the practice exams, you'll be fine.

Sokolove goes too fast in lecture, you have to write down everything he says or you'll miss it. Definitely study the study questions in depth. If you do that then you should do ok with the tests and hopefully the curve does the rest.

The class is hard for a lot of people. People will tell you that it's hard without AP bio and I never took it and still did well. Use study questions and STUDY WITH FRIENDS! Attend lecture and use your old exams! He isn't all that bad, he's actually very approachable.

His classes are hard, but if you study, you will get an A or a B with the curve. Sokolove a teaching method is unique, but he went to Harvard, he knows what he is doing. If you can't get a B in his class, you don't deserve to be a doctor
I wanted to be a doctor, and then I had Phil Sokolave.

Unhelpful, condescending, too quick through lectures. Attendance taken through clicker questions, which rarely reappear on tests. Tests are based very loosely on study questions. He loves trick questions, and they all have a "none/two/three of the above" answer option. All of the answers usually sound right. Good luck.

Horrible professor and boring lectures and you have to attend if you want clicker points. But if you work hard and study hard you will have no problem, just make sure you know the answers to study questions. Average on the first exam was a 61, but he curves the class a lot.

The class itself was difficult. His lectures were ok but he rushes at times. His exams are very tricky and hard, and they are solely based off the study questions, so study them a lot. Make sure you understand the reason behind the correct answers.

Lectures were engaging and informative. Important to read required chapters to understand concepts and do well on online reading quizzes. Study Qs and old exams are best exam study tools. Enthusiastic professor. You have to work hard and do all assignments on time to get a good grade. Enjoyed class and learned a lot.

It's not really that bad. Even though its a difficult class, and you have to work hard for the A, I felt like i learned a lot. Make sure to use the study Qs as much as you can and read the relevant sections in the book. He is a good lecturer

He Does not give answers to any questions. You need to find tests from last semester. Expect to learn nothing from his class, and know that his tests are incredibly tricky. he does not test you on if you know the material, but if you can take his tests. Also, the final exam is 90% previous tests. so hold on to them. good luck. hes the worst...

Very difficult course only because he made it that way. Exams are difficult for no reason, and he is very condescending. If you have ANY other options for this class I suggest you take it. Google taught me more than he did. I got an A and I still hated every lecture; possibly the worst professor I've had at UMBC.

He is actually a difficult teacher. He wants students to help other students. His TA's are inconsistent. Just take Bio at a Community College or another institution. It will transfer over so talk to your adviser about it. I took his class and dropped it and took it at HCC and now I am in Med School. Thanks to HCC for getting an A

Pretty much study from peoples past exams and make sure they have circled the correct answers..... about half of the questions from previous exams will have the exact type of question on your exam, the other half will come from study questions which are pretty much the most useful thing in the class to do....with a generous curve ull prlly get a B

TERRIBLE. The problem with Sokolove is that you think you know what he's talking about, that you understand the course fully, then when an exam comes along, you fail. He is not clear on what you should know in depth, or what is important remember. Also, he tends to answer a lot of questions with "I don't know" -_-

Dr Sokolove, to be perfectly honest, is not that bad! Granted at first if you've never had a professor like him before his mannerisms give you a huge culture shock but HE RECYCLES QUESTIONS! How much better could a prof do than giving you questions to which you should, and could have known the answers already. His legend overshadows him negatively.

He really isn't that terrible. Make sure to REALLY memorize the practice exams that he posts and find someone who already took the class to get the answers, because he doesn't post the answers, and a lot of these questions will be on the exams. You have to study a lot, but it is not that hard of a class to get a B or A in if you read and study.

Honestly one of the worst professors I've had.He is very unclear about covering material and about grades,so you're never really sure what you have in the class.He never fully understands questions you ask him,and BS's answers.And has a very time consuming,stupid policy about name tags and clicker questions.He's unfort.the only prof.that teaches it

Really annoying. I love bio, and I'm a bio major, but he really got on my nerves. His tests are really tricky. Even if you know the material, you still probably won't do very well. He never gives you a straight answer, and most of the answers to his study questions are up for interpretation. Very frustrating teacher.

Awful - guy got a degree from Harvard, so he has a very high opinion of himself. Like others said, class is about his view on biology; he is rude, does not take questions seriously (& many times does not answer them), threatens to ban students from BB discussion board for posting their opinions, expects you to read & memorize chapters in 1 night.
The reason I'm no longer a Bio major. Talks way too fast. Condescending and rude. Laughs at students when they ask serious questions.

TOUGH, but clear and makes you actually LEARN. Will not just give you answers. Make sure you READ the textbook, and always keep it as a reference and study for the tests. Tests have TRICKY questions, so carefully read through the question and ALL the answers. Study with a partner or in groups only after you've studied by yourself for some time.
Hard, but very clear and easy to understand. His tests are tickey, but if you read your textbook and do the assigned work you will do fine. One of my favorite professors at UMBC so far!
GREAT teacher. he has VERY challenging tests that test your understanding of the topic very well, the questions are ment to trick you. not at all an easy class.

He is one tough cookie, he definitely expects a lot from you right off the bat. You really need to read the book carefully and ask lots of questions, and do the study Qs, they are really helpful for the exams! Self-correct your exams when you get them and keep them for the final. He's very engaging but very demanding so brace yourself!

Better than Miller, another professor who taught with Sokolove. His exams are okay, but you really need to study the study questions that he gives you. Need to know details for exams, but he puts a fair amount of curve.

I had Dr. Sokolove, who co-taught with Miller, this semester as a freshman for Bio 141. I enjoyed the challenges that this class brought, such as unstop textbook reading, tricky exam questions, and mandatory lecture attendance. A high final grade will result if you put in ALL the effort you could towards grasping the concepts. WORK HARD STUDENTS!

Most of the kids in my class really disliked Sokolove, either because of his confusing tests, work load, or manner of teaching, but I found the class to be a lot of fun. Prof. Sokolove is very engaging and makes it impossible to fall asleep. Biology 141 was by far my favorite class this semester.

Everyone always talks about how they do not like him as a professor, but he is actually a great professor! He definitely gives students the tools they need to do well and if you are having problems in the course he is very available and willing to help you as long as you are driven and put effort forth. Exams are tricky  but make you think!

Coming into UMBC I heard horror stories about this professor. But honestly, if you come to class, do the study questions, and write down the clicker questions the tests are pretty straightforward. Also, don't freak out if you do poorly on the first test... they get far less broad later in the semester.

If someone else taught Biology I could guarantee that NO one would take Sokolove unless they didn't have a choice. It's his exams. You have to think like him to get an A. Biology is about perspective and this class is all about HIS opinion@
Get ready you are going to have to teach yourself pretty much everything. He is not straightforward exams are not structured to test what you know! I love UMBC but this guy is a joke.

He is a nice guy outside of the classroom but his tests are based on trick questions and trick answers. I usually get A+ in bio but his exams are so tricky! I get answers wrong on the exam, but according to the book that's the right answer. It is all about what he thinks is the BEST answer. Horribly structured foundations course!

I just don't like the fact that he makes us do all the work and then he goes over it with little clarity. Plus, when we ask questions he tries to get us to answer them ourselves. I mean, I wouldn't be asking the question if I could answer it myself. If he could just try to be more clear and more helpful, that would be great.

I got a B in his class but it was absolutely ridiculous. He was just a pain. Rude, discouraging and egocentric. He loves to act like a "nutty" and brilliant professor but makes concepts much harder than necessary. I learned more in high school. You basically teach yourself everything because if you listen to him, he'll only teach his opinion.

The only thing about his class is that he teaches through fear.  You have to attend class to get your participation points, and he may just randomly call on you. His tests are tricky, but once you get over that, they are not that bad. He gives study questions that are basically the test itself. Overall, moderate professor. Good wake up call.
He is completely unhelpful! He demands way too much of a 100 level class.

Good lectures and fair assignments, but did have some technical difficulties with exam that took a long time to resolve.

The sweetest and funniest professor i've ever had. Knows everything about anything, and speaks most literally seven languages, though most are dead. A fantastic person, I wish every class I had was his.

Lectures are mandatory, but he's pretty funny, so at least you won't fall asleep in class. All homework was due at the end of the semester as a large word doc. I'd recommend doing this weekly during the semester instead of all at the end (like I did). Tests are online, they are timed but doable. Good class to take if you want to prep for GRE vocab.
There are readings, but the exams are online and so are the readings, legit read, take notes, and go to class you will succeed.

Professor Piana was very knowledgeable and his lectures were very interesting. He also really cares about individual students and wants everyone to do well. The only problem was that some of the readings were long, boring, and didn't relate to class content very much. He didn't grade harshly, but assignments didn't come consistently.

A great professor, there was a lot of reading but all the homework, quizzes, and exams were on Blackboard. Attendance is mandatory but his lectures aren't typical and boring which makes it a lot better
Prof. Piana is hilarious! I'd highly recommend showing up to his lectures, they're wonderfully entertaining and informative.

Dr. Piana was such a great and kind Professor. There was a good amount of reading and online assignments, but we only met once a week so adequate time was given for completion. Also, he offered many chances for extra credit and tried to help everyone succeed. I definitely would recommend him for an easy A or B!

There are a lot of readings so if you're not prepared to read then pick a different class, otherwise, Dr. Piana is an awesome professor that is understanding. The work this year was difficult, but because of feedback from the students in the class he is changing work and adjusting it so it's not as specific. I recommend this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Hilarious

reviews.comment: Be prepared for a TON of extremely detailed and long lectures, quizzes, and tests. Luckily, the assignments were all online, so you could pull up reading material and presentations to help, but some of the questions were so specific (who said a single quote in a 500 page book) it isn't worth the effort. He also gets heated if you don't do perfectly
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: Wonderful professor, very generous grading
