I absolutely love Piana, hes funny, outgoing, and he really makes dry topics interesting. The course is very heavy on reading obscure texts from 3000 years ago, however he knows that so the quizzes and exams are extremely straight forward. 10/10 Piana is a beauty
IMO one of the best professors at UMBC. Yes, his class was a lot of work but he is great!!

Had to email the instructor several times to figure out what my grades were during the semester. Blackboard was not showing grades cause he had to leave discussion forums open for lazy bums who would not respect deadlines. Negative feedback on here is all nasty people. The course was excellent and Prof Piano should really teach more courses!!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Would take again

reviews.comment: I took hybrid mythology with Dr. Piana. I agree that he cancelled class more than once, but he made up for it by posting additional video lectures. His in class lectures were hilarious and he really knows how to keep the class interested and paying attention. Had a chance to talk to him outside of class and felt he really cares about students.

Took this class online & received an A. I had no clue what grade I would get all semester. A lot of reading but discussion posts could be done sometimes by skimming. He was never clear on his expectations and we did not know what was ahead. The class started about a month late due to blackboard issues. Easy but frustrating & a lot at the end.
reviews.rating_tags: Tests? Not many--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: lack of knowledge of black board; inconsistent communication; it is worth taking for culture credit but frustrating not knowing what is expected

Piana was really nice and funny, but clearly very unorganized when it came to running the class. The class met only once a week but almost half of our classes were cancelled. Assignments were posted late and there was poor communication on blackboard. Prepare to teach yourself the materials, and follow a confusing schedule
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES

reviews.comment: Although this semester he was thrown the class very last minute (2 days before classes started), he still did very well. Because of the timing, he wasn't even teaching his own course, rather just using notes from another teacher but putting his own spin on it. A beautiful man with a cute accent that makes Ancient Greek History fun even with reading

Overall very nice. Be prepared to read and learn the material on your own. Often late to classes or cancels entirely. Does not know to much about blackboard (doesn't know how to work it). Assignments will be light until the last two weeks of the semester. He will assign multiple quizzes, discussion boards, papers all in a weeks time.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Overall, he is a very nice person; however, be prepared to read a lot between each class!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: - Expects you to read 100+ pages between classes (A day) - No syllabus or clear grading criteria - No study guide for exams or even area of focus - Random quizzes - He clearly enjoys what he teaches and is passionate but doesn't do a good job sharing it with students
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: She's very understanding, flexible with students, and willing to help outside of office hours. She has a very compassionate demeanor which is perfect for social work.

I had Diana for my field instructor at my field placement. She was extremely condescending, late for appointments, did teach or manage supervision. The level of unprofessionalism she demonstrated was appalling! She also was never available. There are better professors in the social work department. Just avoid her, she’s not worth it.

Prof. Pina was a great professor! We watched a few films & had a lot of lecture time. She did a great job of thoroughly explaining each powerpoint slide. We did read chapters for homework as it helped to reflect in class & hold class discussions. She also uses real-life examples which help with remembering. Prof. Pina is great & incredibly nice! :)

I took his summer course at HCC, it was excellent! It was asynchronous so you could work ahead. The subject was actually really interesting, and he provided encouraging comments. You can sense his personality despite it being fully online. He's great!
Great professor! Greatly recommend him if you can choose him, you won't regret it.

I loved this class! The professor was super understanding and gave really good feedback. Textbook wasn't that important if you just paid attention and took notes in class. Quizzes and exams were pretty straight-forward and easy also. Definitely take this professor, He's awesome!

Class consisted of 3 quizzes (could retake to get a better score), and 3 exams, one being the final. Also, we'd have to make 2 review slides as a grade (vv easy!). He would post pre-recorded lectures on monday, live lectures on wed, then a discussion post on friday. Well-spoken and a very kind and caring professor, especially in times ofa pandemic.

Professor Pitas is a great choice! He's extremely chill and wants his students to do well in his class. He does not grade this class harshly, he is definitely an easy grader. He also always responds to emails. The majority of the grade is based off of quizzes (which have unlimited attempts) and exams which are very similar to the quizzes.

Professor Pitas made sure you understood every concept. Each exam was no surprise as he posted everything in a review quiz online. He genuinely wants you to pass and if you learn along the way that's cool too. He does clickers for attendance and they go towards your grade so DO NOT SKIP.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Dr. Brad rocks. Taking his 313 course really prepared me for 411. He's super understanding, and a genuinely nice guy. He's also great at applying our lessons to real world industry projects. His midterm and final had no surprises. Projects were feasible and he gave plenty of time to complete them. One of the best profs at UMBC.
Super knowledgeable professor who is very caring and patient. He talks a lot about cybersecurity and goes deep in about the field.

Honestly a great professor, he definitely cares about his students. Especially encourages students to learn topics in depth. Prof Brad talks a lot about cybersecurity, pretty awesome stuff! If you don't take his class you're missing out!
A truly amazing professor that makes boring material interesting and relevant. All if the projects are real world which makes the work entertaining.

Best professor I've ever had in 2 years of my life at UMBC. Makes class material very easy to understand. If you have any project questions he will explain them during class or he will quickly respond through email. Unlike most professors, his assignments are more practical than theoretical, and yes we did do some hacking which was quite fun.

I'm currently taking CMSC313 (Assembly) with him for Spring 2020. This is his first semester, and he's off to a great start. Absolutely killed it. He wants you to learn fundamental concepts first and foremost before giving you something hard. He can be quiet in lecture but I believe that will go away as time passes. He went to UMBC and he gets it.
Very effective teacher.  There's a lot of work, but the work is easy.  She does a great job with giving students an introduction or refresher in spanish.

Her class was like watching a one-legged soccer player, in an amateur league, that you are paying to watch.   Went to conferences mid semester and had a colleague proctor a mid-term. Syllabus was 10 pages long and not followed. Assignments were only clarified the day before assigned.  Four different websites and formats for assignment completion.
Not a great teacher.

At first I wasn't sure if I was going to like Carolina, but she is a very good professor. She actually cares about her students, and she tries her best to make the class less stressful. She wants everyone to pass! She will provide opportunities to improve your grade, and she is not a harsh grader. I wish she would have taught SPAN102.

Ideally, a newly-matriculated college student should be able to ace this class with ease. There are a few writing assignments and a huge analytic end-of-semester report. That last assignment is definitely manageable so long as you don't procrastinate. Take Mrs. Porter. Her class is kind of dull, but it's an easy A.
a cool teacher
The class is mostly discussion, the book was used only once or twice. You need a alot of writing for this class.

Probably one of the best professors I have had. Very tough grader but you deserve what you get. Plan out your papers beforehand and you will do great in this class.There is one group assignment worth 25% of the grade and is very easy to do she gives classtime. Nice class i enjoyed it a lot.! She looks like she was pretty hot when she was younger!

There are definitely easier sections to take, but I learned a lot in her class. She grades tough but there are rewrites for C or worse. This class is a lot of work but she recognizes that and is nice and helpful. She flunks you if you miss 5 classes though so if you don't want to attend class don't take it from her.
Fantastic.
Prof Porter is a GREAT Professor.  Very helpful and nice.  I took her for technical writing and technical editing.  You can't go wrong with her.  Pay attention and do your work and you will be fine.
Generally not vailable to discuss problems. Difficult to negotiate solutions with.

One of the best teachers I've ever had... makes this hard class less stressing with her professional demeanor and friendly personality.  She gives the classroom the feeling of a cooperative workplace setting.
Great teacher.  Very helpful.  Re-writes allowed if not so good of a grade.
Pretty good teacher.  She could improve on her lectures.

Professor P is honestly the best. Math has never been a strong subject, but he genuinely cares about his students doing well and keeping up with the class, and keeps you interested in what you're learning. He cracks the occasional joke during class, and always makes sure that he isn't going too fast or slow for anyone. I fully recommend him.

I am in math 106 with Professor P, and he is awesome! I am totally NOT a math person but he is extremely helpful and wants his students to succeed. Adjusting to online work was hard for me but as long as you take good notes and do well on the quizzes (which are once a week) you're fine. All the problems he does in class are on the exams.

Prof. P is super helpful. He wants you to be successful and teaches to test. One warning, don't be lazy or take advantage of him. He'll see it and won't hesitate to call you out. He's nice and cares about students. If you struggle with math take his class!
THE BEST PROFESSOR IVE EVER HAD. So easy, helpful, and nice. Also funny. Definitely take him for math 106!

had him for Math 106, seriously a great guy. He really just wants you to do well; doesn't try to trick you, doesn't try to teach you things beyond the class. I was scared of math before his class; he made it clear and was always there to help. Definitely better than all my high school math teachers put together. Not even exaggerating.

Mr. P is a great instructor. He's very interested in the success of his students and teaches what is "need-to-know" for all quizzes and exams. There is no textbook, but an online HW system. If you need to take MATH 106, definitely take him.
cool teacher. attendence is not mandatory other than tests and quizess. no books used. uses online homework which is easy. very helpful and understanding. sense of humor.
He is awesome. He makes math easy and I hate math. Before a quiz/test he will give you 10 problems and answers and he will use 5 of them for the quiz/test. I love the way he teaches.
Professor Patharaju is The Man. Take him without hesitation, he will help you.
Splendid teacher, he is just the best i just hope he can teach calculus

He explains everything you need to know for the class and constantly asks to make sure you are following what he is trying to teach. Makes the subject seem much easier than it was for me at the beginning. Use Aleks, very helpful. Ask him how to use the online textbook if you can't find it at the beginning of the semester.

He is a very funny guy, wears a different hat every class. Really knows his math, and truly wants to help you understand. Use the online ALEKS homework, which is a big pain. Make sure you study if you arent good at math.

I had a great experience with this professor; she is very knowledgable and gives thorough answers to questions.  Not the most tech-savvy but her lectures were interesting and she has a good sene of humor.  her class is relatively easy if you do all the assigned textbook readings.

If you are interested in the subject, you will like the class. Profesora Poggio covers a lot of information and is very knowledgable on the topics. I recommend taking her, I have had two courses with her, and if this wasn't my last semester, I would take more classes with her again.

Dr. Poggio is an excellent professor and I learned so much in her course. In combination with the service-learning and the class material, I feel like I walked away with knowledge and skills I will carry with me in the future and into the real world. I hope to take more classes with her in coming semesters!

I took two classes with this professor and have learned so much. I took MLL306 where many students encountered practicum issues and blamed her but she has nothing to do with that-it's just 100% Shriver Center. If you are only familiar with mesoamerican/spanish castilian for SPAN308/309 then brush up on the argentinian dialect or it will be hard.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring

reviews.comment: This is officially the first class I have actively disliked at UMBC. This might be due to the language barrier or the fact that classes are online, but she frequently comes off as condescending, impatient and rude. She has no idea how to use any of the tool provided (BB and its various functions).
Nice lady just a hard grader and hard to understand.

We had to do a service site for the MLL306 class. There is a lot of readings and outside time dedicated to this class. She takes attendance every class. She doesn't update grades until the end of the semester. Tests and papers are fairly easy if you follow the guide. Wouldn't take again. Everything previous students have said about her is true.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: She's an absolute mess. She has no clear direction of where the class is going. She creates assignments and deadlines without telling the class. There is an extreme lack of transparency in how she runs the class. She is very knowledgeable on the material but she just does not know how to teach or run a class.

Dr. Sara Poggio is  a wonderful professor, researcher and  experienced professional in her field. She has great human quality and has passion for her class. Dr. Poggio is a professional that inspired me to go on in my researches and in my education in general, I enjoyed very much having her as my adviser.

Señora Poggio is VERY knowledgeable of the material she teacher. However, she has the old school traditional Argentine way of teaching that may come off as lond and tideous to some students.... well... all students. Just smile and say yes and you will get an A.

Okay, Dr. Poggio is one of those teachers that either students love or hate. She has a very South American way of teaching that many American students are not familiar with, but that's the way it is down there. You really have to go with the flow, she's Latina. She knows EVERYTHING so you cannot BS her. She will call you out on it haha.

Avoid taking her class on the Immigration Debate if she continues teaching it for future semesters.  Unlike the engaging seminar I expected (FYSFirst Year Seminar), all I got was just a very quiet and painful-to-understand lecture accompanied by Power Points that were filled with grammatical errors -- very unprofessional.
So hard to understand and such an attitude problem that you should avoid her class at all costs. It's amazing that she is still allowed to teach!

Really knows her stuff but is horrible at teaching it. She is too smart to teach. Her accent is incredibly thick. Her lectures are completely ineffective. She'll put up one power point slide with with 2 bullet points, and then talk for 20 minutes. Avoid this class or you will be teaching yourself.
One of the worst professors I have ever had. Disorganized, rude, and very difficult to understand. I did not learn a single thing from her.

Read the text book and go to class. She is very hard to understand because her accent is so thick, but the group work you do is exactly what she tests you on. I did not like her or the class and I would not take her again, but I made it through and had a decent grade. Very disorganized teacher and her lectures are all over the place. AVOID!

Probably one of the worst professors I have every had. Very disorganized. Never responds to emails. No lecture, only hands out questions then discusses answers but answers are never fully given. VERY THINK accent and very rude.

This is the worst professor I have ever had. I really thought her course was going to be easy and maybe fun but it wasnt at all. She never lecture in class. She only handed out papers in the beginning of class that we had to complete in a group. The material was not easy and it wasnt clear. I do not recommend this course for anyone.

She is a bit disorganized but I have had much worse professors in the MLL department. Her class is so easy. You just listen in class, look over what she says in class within the book and you'll be fine. She doesn't even look at your grammar as long as its legible. Yes, there were few assignments but you should know when you do bad on a test.

She has a tendency to take everything personally and if you get on her bad side she will hate you. That said, if you show interest in the subject and are respectful towards her she will love you and can actually be really cool. A great professor for the intellectual with an interest in Latin America/Feminism; just not for a slacker.

I got an A in class. she is very knowleadgeable and knows alot. for her test listen to what she saids in class because for the test, her questions are going to bthings discussed in class. so is very easy to get an A. before the cass glance at the book and sound like you know what u talking about...so participate.everything else that they said is tr

She's nice enough, but very disorganized. We only have 3 grades in the class so it's hard to do well if you do poorly on one. Her syllabus has proven useless, none of the dates are right and we didn't get through more than half.

MLL280's is "Intro to the Spanish Speaking world," but all she focused on was Latin American feminism, so that was a bit of a surprise. Don't even think about checking the time with your cell phone. She just might flip out and tell the whole class they're losers, like she did this semester. But she does try. Don't be too hard on her, she's not evil
Poor clarity of speech. Dislikes 'smiling' 'laughing' 'whistling'

Can't say she was the worst professor I've ever had, but definitely top 5.  She can't speak English, can't organize her assingments or lectures, and is unclear on assignments.  Tests are based purely on the textbook with absolutely nothing to do with what is discussed in class.

Worst teacher I've ever had. She can't speak english. Everyone's opinion but her's is wrong. She is completely disorganized. Do not laugh in class or she might yell at you for being disrespectful. Exams are in essay form and you must write exactly what she wants to hear to get a good grade. This teacher is not worth your time.

NOT A GOOD TEACHER!!!! if you suck up to her you'll get an A though. If she does not like you, she'll fail you! She gave me an F in the course when i got a 100% on the midterm and final. I had to go in and show the idiot that I had an A. I ended up getting an A, but she is so unorganized and unprofessional

EXTREMELY disorganized. She missed the first two classes of the semester and then several later on.  Changes location of the class two hours before scheduled time.  Very rude when asked to clarify a point or translation.  Doesn't have an organized lesson plan or an idea of what assignments she gives out.  Very poor teaching skills overall.

Very fluent in Spanish not so good in English. Very easy teacher IF you read what she expects you to read. She takes attendance once in a while and has postings in blackboard but doesnt care if you post them a week late as long as you do it.
she lectures alot and she depends on studentsw to ask qeustiosn in participae in class if you do not do that clsss will be boring. Over all I enjoyed the class alot of group work.

Well, poggio is a good SPANISH prof, but a terrible prof for MLL. Her english isn't great and she admits it. In spanish though, its hard to understand at first, but you get used to it. She's actually easy to talk to, very open, laid back and lenient. You just have to ask her questions, make a few comments (right or wrong) and you'll get an A.

The fact that this professor teaches a course in the field of intercultural communication is a joke, because she herself is rather ignorant. Her English is difficult to interpret, but if you ask her nicely to repeat or clarify something, she will either refuse or do it but act offended. Very rude and completely disorganized.

Don't agree with previous comments. I enjoyed her class a lot, the subjects were interesting and she knew a lot about it. The assignements were clear when you paid attention to what you had to do and the tests reflected very much the topics studied in class. I learned a lot in this class.

Knowledgable but has no teaching skills at all. Very unorganized and definitely plays favorites- the reason why I got a C. I did all the work and got good grades back, but she didnt like me enough for an A. Sends assignments on Blackboard the night before or the day of class and gets mad when students can't participate in class bc they didnt read.

She assigns work at the last minute on Blackboard, she's extremely hard to understand, and her tests make little sense. She is a very irritating teacher, but there is no avoiding her if you're a Spanish major... go to class, do all of the work and maybe you won't have as tough a time.

She's very hard to understand at first, but then you kinda get used to her accent. She assigns a ton of work, so I suggest just doing a little every single day to keep from having to cram and going insane. You have a lot of work for the class and the exams are very weird. Her grading style is also very strange, as if she just writes random numbers.

She's pretty crazy, but shes a pretty easy teacher.  you'll never really know what you're supposed to be doing, or when to turn things in, but shes pretty funny(without meaning to be).  She is pretty liberal, compares coca to coffee.  But if you get through the craziness, and her making fun of people, shes not so bad.
Can't add much to the earlier comments.  Nice lady and she seems to care but is very poorly suited to teaching.  Disorganized and inconsistant.
avoid her as long as possible. she favors native speakers of spanish. she is very disorganized and is mean.

Answered cell in class, showed up a half hour late, was so unclear about hw that no one ever did anything, never returned assignments, accidentally assigned the wrong midterm essay, didn't show for appts, and asked us to write a list of what we did & the grades we got because she couldn't remember.
Senora Poggio is the bomb digity.

Disorganized, unprofessional, doesn't show sometimes, doesn't tell you what's going on or ever give grades back, always under UMBC review because she's so out of control but if you can handle it she's not that hard. Totally picks favorites.  DID NOT SHOW TO 3 SCHEDULED ADVISING APPOINTMENTS.

Disorganized, spent much of the class time yelling at people for no reason, you'll have pretty much no idea what is going on in the class or when stuff is due. Often makes you feel like slamming your head against a wall. AVOID!

She tends to bounce around on topics (some of which don't have anything to do with the daily topic) and is quite disorganized.  You're sort of up to yourself to learn, but she does have a lot of interesting things to say.  Don't write her off so easily.

She is horrible and disorganized and you never know when assignments are due and then you never get them back.  She's very unclear and gets angry when you don't answer questions right away.  Just bad all around

I enjoyed professor V! She is very straightforward! Her lectures cover everything you need for your assignments. She doesnt give alot of work and cares about her students. Show up to class, pay attention and youll do great!

One of the best Social Work professors!! She is understanding and truly cares about her students. If the class asked for an extension or extra credit, she would give it! I loved lectures and hearing her stories and experiences! This is my third class with her and I always get an A! The only thing is she grades papers really late, but easy grader!

She is amazing don't know why people are negative about her class Sowk 250 is intro class which can be boring at any school but take one of her others like intimate partner violence and you'll change your mind. This spring will be my 3rd class with her
This professor was very kind and supportive to help students succeed, however the quizzes had a tough grading criteria, and assignments were not graded using good time management.
Due to Covid I took the class online. The book is needed but her powerpoints are pretty straight forward and help as far as the exams. She was a great teacher overall but rarely responded to emails..

This class was straight out of the powerpoint slides, if you attend lecture, watch prerecorded lectures before class and copy down the powerpoint slides you'll be in good shape! Minimal grades, but lots of leniency in due date! She really just wants you to succeed!

The first time Im writing a review for a professor. She is understanding when talking in a personal matter but rude during lecture. You have to teach yourself. Shell say certain things are questions are on the exams but only one is on the exam out of 20 question she says will be on the exam. Dont expect grades to be graded in a timely manner.
reviews.rating_tags: Inspirational--Graded by few things--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Brutal class. 1rst exam mostly SQL, while 2nd exam was PL/SQL and NoSQL. For exams, you need to know SQL and understand the code outputs. His slides didn't help at all for the first exam, but were useful for the second exam. Quizlet helped some. Mandatory attendance. 1 project, a few HWs, some syllabus changes, and 2 exams worth 50% of the grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Best professor in umbc
He literally curve more than 8% of our grade.

Long tiresome lectures and doesn't respond well to emails. Group project was probably the worst i've ever taken. Disorganized and if you have bad group members prepare to suffer. Only got an A because he gave everyone an A without even grading on the final project.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Fairly standard and straightforward class. Labs are where you will learn the most. Lectures are draining but if you pay attention you will benefit from them. The group project was disorganized and messy. The final exam was awful, maybe one of the worst I've taken at this school. Still, you will pass if you apply what you've learned.
Tough class, the professor was alright but a bit tough to get in touch with at times. Group project was a nightmare and I wish it was better organized, but the exams were relatively straightforward

He's alright. Doesn't really reply back to emails, lets the TA handle mostly everything. TA graded all the labs/assignments and he was very strict with grading. Professor messed up on the final exam (Big Time) causing him to give me and the class a 90 on the final exam. I know because the average (mean) and media of the final exam was a 90.

He is a good professor and is very knowledgeable about what he teaches. He works in the same field he teaches, therefore he knows exactly what students need to know to prepare them for the real world. There are 2 exams, few quizzes, and 1 group project. Attendance for this class is mandatory. Pretty lenient with grading. I would highly recommend!

This class is unnecessarily difficult. Midterm is difficult, you have to write SQL code on paper. The labs are okay, don't expect much feedback if you get something wrong. The project is difficult too, it has little direction on what is required, he won't give feedback on the semester deliverables.

Best professor ever! He Gives simple hw! He's helpful during class and gives good feedback. His exams are tricky but doable. Project is very simple.  He lets class out every week. Make sure to get the textBook for homework and studying. If you want a stress free 420 teacher he's your man.

He has a bad personality and is confrontational with students, but he is an easy grader and the class is a breeze if you pay attention to the concepts in class and do the homework seriously. Lets class out early frequently.

The material starts off easy but gets very difficult once PL is introduced. The later HW are very difficult. But he seems to grade based on completion. The project can be difficult but not nearly as difficult as the other class. Exams are easy. He is a very nice guy and good teacher.

Don't underestimate the popularity of this professor; register early because he fills up FAST!  He teaches a very relaxed, stress-free class, is an incredibly lenient grader, and the final project does not need to be nearly as elaborate as the other 420 course.  Exams are multiple choice and open book.
Professor Bandaru is great. He is a professional DBA so he knows exactly what he is talking about. Legend has it that no one has ever failed his class. Great professor overall.

All exams are open book. Mr. Bandaru is friendly and is a straightforward but dull lecturer. This section of 420, from my understanding, was a lot easier than everyone else's. There are weekly homework assignments which are fairly reasonable. There's also a semester-long group project that isn't too bad.

Fairly worthless class.  I can't say I learned anything worth remembering. However, it's a lot easier than what I saw the other kids doing for the other IS420 class. The other class will also teach you the same worthless knowledge just make you work harder.

The comment below accurately sums up the class. Bandaru is very helpful and very nice. He will give you extensions on tough assignments and help you on the project if you need it. He also teaches you exactly how to do the project - make sure you take notes. I recommend him, he made the class very cool.

Great professor!  He does check attendance and hands out hw in the beginning semester.  Towards the middle/end, you just concentrate on your project.  HW's, 2 exams, 1 final, 1 project.  You don't even have to present the project.  He just ask you to run it and make sure it works.  Tests easy as well. Done on comp (Multiple choice & short answers)

assignments were all super easy and simple. the few time i had questions she responded immediately and really nice. all asynch and easy to understand. no textbook, just articles for every topic. super super easy A and def recommend.

She's nice and it's easy to get an A or high B. You can't skip a lot because the graded in-class assignments are unpredictable. The writing assignments aren't hard but her grading is kind of harsh and hard to understand. I wouldn't take her again because of that. Open book take-home exams though :)

She's really nice and understanding. Most assignments are online and involve writing. The only tricky part is she gives in-class assignments on random days, and they're worth a lot, especially later in the semester. Just go to class, do those easy group discussions, and turn in the online work on time. Easy A if you keep up!

Idk why people are saying not to take her. This was the easiest class I have ever taken. Class consists of 4 or 5 discussion posts, 4 exams, and 2 essays (final essay is 10 pages). I barely did anything for this class all semester it was a very easy writing intensive. She has nice engaging lectures and overall easy assignments.
All I can warn you of in the space allowed is to NEVER EVER TAKE THIS CLASS.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: All I can warn you in the space given is to NEVER EVER TAKE HER CLASS PLEASE
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Sort of a meticulous grader but Prof Price was very nice and pleasant to work with. I liked hearing about her personal experiences in aging. The course work was manageable and not all that challenging. The lectures were boring and aren't posted so you will have to take notes. The exams were online and weren't cumulative.

This class is fully online with weekly assignments, a midterm, and a final. The lessons in general are common sense, it is an easy class. You just need to remind yourself of the weekly assignments and take some time to write a good number of essays.

Not a bad professor by any means, personal rating 7-8/10. Only major gripe is grading is very nitpicky, doesn't make sense sometimes. If you have everything correct according to the materials and formatted correctly but also add in something that may be not exact to the provided materials, she takes off 10-20%. Also doesn't post lecture material
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Craziest 100 course I've taken. Midterm + a Final and weekly modules that are sometimes quizzes which are easy usually easy or written work which she grades even harder than my intensive writing course. she even forces the use of intext citations. Responses also cannot come from personal experience only the several sources she posts every week.

Professor Price is very knowledgeable about Aging and I learned a lot. She cares for her students to do well and gives good feedback for all the assignments. Her graduate student, Rebecca, was very helpful in strengthening and assisting me with my 12 page essay throughout the semester. Exams are based on lecture which were pretty straightforward.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: I loved Ms.Price. The way she explained the material was always so interesting! I would definitely take her again if I had the chance. I just took her class as a writing intensive but actually ended up really enjoying and loving it!
I took aging 100 with professor price and it was a completely asynchronous online class. Easy A, clear syllabus, clear and fair grading, highly recommend. She's nice and she sets you up for success.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: If you're taking her course for a writing-intensive requirement credit, you should expect there will be a lot of reading and writing. She is nice and straightforward in all of her assignments, and she is quite helpful in terms of assisting and clearing up any project-related questions, too.

Her weekly assignments are pretty easy but you have to expand your understanding of the materials she has given on the weekly module. One 8-10 pages paper but she breaks it down each week.Two non-accumulative exams but they're not that bad. It definitely feels a little overwhelming at the beginning but it gets easier toward the end.

She's easily one of the best professors I have had here, and I was really glad to take an intensive writing course with her Prof. Price is really nice and completely understanding when it comes to issues that might affect your work. Overall, really recommend taking her!
Shes really cool, if you can take her class, take it.

Amazing professor who gives interesting lectures and has you thinking about the topic at hand. She's very kind and provides good feedback and makes you want to learn more and doesn't feel like a writing intensive class.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Amazing lectures --Graded by few things

reviews.comment: She is one of the nicest professors I have ever encountered. If you want to take the easy writing-intensive class, this is the one for you, and take it with Prof. Price. Only 2 exams and 1 final (which was not cumulative). Exams were easy and consisted of multiple choice and 3 short answer questions. There was only one paper of 10 pages.

LOVE Professor Price !!!!! So sad im graduating and i have taken all of the classes she offers. I took her agng200 class my first semester at umbc and she was one of the best professors Ive had. All of the profs at the Erickson school are great but Price teaches so many classes!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Professor Price is a wonderful professor. She loves what she does and it is very clear, which makes the class that much more exciting and interesting. There aren't too many tests (about 4 including the final, which isn't cumulative- at least this year). Yes this course is lecture heavy, so its good to take notes but it isn't really all that hard.

Prof. Price gives a ton of useful information about retirement, end of life issues, and health concerns. My only complaint is that after turning in a draft of my final paper and getting a 9/10, I turned in a corrected copy and got a 85/100. But otherwise she's pretty clear on grading criteria, and the weekly work is easy.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Professor Price is a gem. She really cares, but understand most people are just taking this class to fulfill a requirement. Still, she doesnt make it harder than it needs to be and the workload was minimal. One big paper and a module a week at most.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures--Caring

reviews.comment: I love this professor! Absolute joy and I definitely recommend for anyone to take her and the class. She cares a lot about your grades and the course is very interesting. You have an assignment once a week and its pretty self explanatory!

Literally the easiest class ever. I took it initially just to get credits and GEP's out of the way but it was so easy and she is the nicest professor I have ever had. Coursework is two short papers, a midterm, and a final that are all so easy.

Professor Price truly is a dear and you only come across professors like her once in a blue moon. She really cares about the topic but understands not everyone else does. The class is fairly easy and she only gave 3 papers (which were also fairly easy). Most of your grade is participation and attendance though, so I don't recommend skipping.

The easiest CS class I've ever taken. The labs are very straightforward and can be done < 10 min to be honest. There are concept sheets for each chapter and they are graded on completion. Month-long projects that take an hour to complete. Exams were take-home, and Priyanka explains things very well in class. There are extra credit opportunities.

Honestly easiest comp sci class I have ever taken. Priyanka makes the class super easy to understand (the book is pretty dense). Our grade consisted of concept sheets after each chapter, 7 labs(easy < 30 min work), 3 projects(takes 3 hours max on a bad day), midterm, and final (open-notes). 10/10 would recommend.

Networks is confusing, but she helped us focus on what was most important. She gives out summary sheets every class that we have to fill out during lecture which help me remember things and with the exams. You get a lot of labs but it helps boost your grade.

Professor Jacob is amazing, I highly recommend taking her course! She is so enthusiastic about teaching that it makes you want to learn more and more! We took a field trip to a museum and got to choose an art piece to do research on based on what inspired us from the specific time periods. Keep up with work and you'll be great. Highly recommend!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: She is one of the nicest people. She has a bubbly personality, but will also show the whole class she is upset with you if you have to leave early (for any reasons, even excused ones) or have any excuses for not reading the materials assigned to you.  She will assign 3-5 50 page readings every class.
Very helpful but very tough.  Don't take this class looking for an easy A

Most adorable professor ever! She showed a passion for what she taught and that made her an effective teacher. I don't like art history, but I was actually interested when she taught it. A fair grader that takes off points for clearly explained reasons, so you never feel cheated. Highly recommended.

MOST AMAZING PROFESSOR YOU WILL EVER ENCOUNTER!  She's so knowledgeable and engaging!  I love art history, and she made my love it even more.  She focuses more on you actually understanding the material than stuffing a bunch of random facts into your head.  She manages the information wonderfully.  Her syllabus is awesome too!  Two words=THE BEST!

Dr. Jacob is an amazing professor! She genuinely LOVES her field and is highly educated. She loves to teach, and it's contagious. Class format this semester was 6 quizzes, 1 paper, 1 cumulative final. The quizzes were one question essays; fairly straightforward as long as you read. I highly recommend her to anyone!

Jacob is generally a very good professor who lectures with great passion for 20th century art and really know what she's talking about. Her lectures are structured nicely before every period and she has fun teaching. As the semester goes along, though, it would seem that she begins to slightly lose focus in the topics and stumble over her words.

She's such a passionate teacher. I really liked her lectures becasue a) she knew what she was talking about and b) loved everything related to art. As for the exams, they were pretty standard short answer and multiple choice. The best part is that the essays she gives  you ahead of time and then you can use your notes for the essay only.

she's very helpful. she does not give specific things to study on quizes which i didn't like. she is passionate about art and really loves what she does. at times it's hard to pay attention and easy to let ur mind wander

If you can get a class with her TAKE IT!  A wonderful lady with a passion for art. She is always willing to help a student better understand art.  There's a large amount of reading which can be tough, but she's not upset at you if you struggle a bit.  She is excellent at teaching and gives abundant chances for extra credit.
No Comments
Quite a good teacher, very enthusiastic about what she does and she will help you with any problems you are having.

Preminda is a very good professor. There is a lot of reading for this class so if you take this class make sure you have the time to read 1-4 reading assignments and view some videos per week. She also rewards you with treats between a class break.
EXTREMELY passionate about the arts... and this helps the students be more motivated about learning and doing well in the class.  Just make sure to attend class regularly and take lots of notes.
Very passionate about art history and is helpful to her students.  Great teacher!

Dr. Purushotham taught Federated Learning course in Spring 2025. He is kind and always takes time to answer questions. This makes it easier to understand the lessons and feel comfortable asking for help. I think the course can be better by having some small projects. I enjoyed this course and in future want to take any course offered by him
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: This review is for IS 755: Advanced AI course, not IS 800. AFAIK, he has not taught IS 800 for the past 4 years. He is very knowledgeable and one of the best AI professors at UMBC. He made significant efforts to engage all students through in-class exercises and group discussions. He gave both positive and constructive feedback for group projects.

Excellent professor! I appreciated how the IS 427 Introduction to AI course was taught. He provided many real-world examples and engaging in-class exercises. We also worked on a group project, and he gave valuable feedback, encouraging us to pursue challenging and innovative project ideas.

Nightmare!! The professor only reads from slides without any coding or problem-solving assignments. He provides constant negative feedback and discouragement throughout the semester. There's apparent bias, as students from familiar labs/working under him receive A\A+ and attention, while others, including me, get ignored and receive lower grades.

He doesn't even leave his seat to teach, reads lecture from the slides which you can do by yourself. Classes won't be challenging at all, people either sleep or mind their own business. If you include some current trending tech words and know how to explain them you can excel in his course. Seems like the technical knowledge ain't that deep.
best prof on the planet. made a hard class easy to learn and i was able to actually leave the class with some skills

IS 800 is an advanced machine learning course (mainly for PhDs) and one of the best courses offered at UMBC. Prof. Sanjay is very knowledgeable and covered a lot of advanced machine learning and deep learning topics. Learned a lot in the class that is useful for my own research.
lectures were very interesting. The projects were interesting to figure out on our own
Honestly, the topic of AI/ML. I took this class as an elective and I am very happy I did. I learned a lot and it is a great class for future job opportunities.
Professor Sanjay gives a lot of extra credit questions to help students to improve grades. I definitely benefitted from it

Enjoyed the group projects. Professor is chill and cares for his students. He didn't miss any classes but had to cancel a class (at the start of his lecture) due to some medical emergency. To makeup for the cancelled class, he uploaded a recorded video of the lecture and also reviewed the materials in the next class.
The content of the course is interesting and professor covers a lot of healthcare topics including about the current pandemic.
Amazing professor. Holds students accountable in group projects. Gives many extra credit questions for students to improve their grades.
Good knowledgeable professor. I like his class as he covers a lot of relevant materials in the class.
He has a hard time teaching this subject... You will sleep in his lecture..
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Professor Purpura was my absolute favorite Prof at this school! Absolutely loved her and learned so much from all her classes and found a love for writing. She's also very encouraging with her feedback and is just generally a very lovely woman to speak with
Dr. Purpura was amazing! She was very involved with every student and was extremely encouraging when it came to writing and presenting new work or thoughts. 10/10 would take again!
Dr. Purpura was my favorite professor. Lovely woman, great feedback, inspiring thoughts.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Not sure why ratings are low but I took her spring 2022 and she was great! reminded me of a high school english class. sat in a circle, wrote poems, and shared them. at the end of the semester, you just have to read a few poems out loud to the class. It's an easy A as long as you participate.
No grades put on blackboard. Attendance policy is horrible. 3 absences basically ruins your chance at succeeding in the class.

Too many offerings, waste of time with discussions that should only take five minutes but instead take a whole hour. Workshops done AFTER submitting the essay? Whats the point of that? Readings are dense and boring. Nor a fan of the topics. Tough grader. Requires attendance. Only benefit is that you dont need to buy textbooks.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: I LOVE Purpura and, if you're passionate about reading or writing, you will to! I will warn you, there was a short reading and brief 1-2 page analysis before every class and attendance is a must. However, she just wants you to prove you are thinking about the writing and it is easy to get an A on them. The class is mostly centered on discussion.
Prof Purpura allows the students to run the discussion. She asks open ended questions, and gives detailed and helpful feedback. I'd recommend her for anyone!

You will regret not taking Professor Purpura if you are ever given the opportunity. She is a beautiful, caring, and amazing professor. You will be excited to go to every class and every assignment she returns has meaningful feedback. I have no regrets taking her class. You will learn a lot and you will likely bond with a few of your classmates.

Lia Purpura is my favorite professor at UMBC! For all of her classes she strays from the norm of teaching. She wants to "live like a writer", and by that she means just be present in everyday life. Not much work at all, but do show up for class because attendance is a grade. 10/10 recommend to everyone and anyone.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--Inspirational

reviews.comment: He's a very kind man who cares about his students. I found his lectures a bit hard to focus on, though that may be my own fault, and I wasn't thrilled about his enthusiasm for using AI in class. I wish in-class quizzes were particiation-based, but he does his best to give us all the information we need (though this is still a chemistry lab...)

He wants his students to understand the material, and it's evident as he teaches in his lectures so far. I had him for an Orgo 2 summer course, and I learned more from him than I did from my other STEM professors during the other semesters. I recommend taking his classes for organic chemistry. Just read and practice the textbook.

Organic Chemistry, its a hard course so you need to really put in the time and hours to do well. Biggest tip, dont get behind in lectures and read the TEXTBOOK. Professor is nice, however, when it comes to grading he harsh, because he wants to see you put in the work. Go to office hours, make study groups and put in the work and you will be fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Not sure why everyone on here is so hard on him. Yes, he has an accent but I never had any trouble understanding him. He is very accessible outside of class and answers emails very fast. He also will take time to answer questions and will not move on until he knows you understand. Overall a very nice man, orgo is hard you just have to put in work.

one of the worst professors a university can have. he has a very thick accent and it's nearly impossible to understand anything he's saying in his so called " lead off lectures ". beware of getting misconducts towards the end of the semester because he digs up stuff from the beginning of the semester that are irrelevant. have fun!

Dr. Ptaszek's in lab quizzes were helpful when he gave a sample question list every week but points would be deducted for small things that were not in his powerpoint. Sometimes hard to understand him in lecture and not very interactive. Go to his office hours if you have questions on the sample questions which definitely help.

I wouldn't recommend Ptaszek. His lecture slides have very few information and if you do not show up to or record lectures you will miss information. His pre lab quizzes are worth too many points, are very meticulous, and can be slightly unclear. He is a kind man, but his teaching style is not for me, beware students with ADHD.

summer course that was poorly organized. only 4 exams as your grade for the entire course. He has awful handwriting that is hard to decipher and doesn't clearly explain the topics. exams are difficult and barely gives any partial credit. no materials given to help study or prepare for exams.

During the semester, you are given sample quiz questions before each lab. He claims that they are almost exactly like the real quizzes, but in reality the questions can be very different. Attendance is mandatory because there are clickers during lecture. Final exam was easy for MC but FRQ's were hard. Keep up quiz grades if you want to get an A.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Tough grader

reviews.comment: PRE/POST LAB ANSWERS ARE SAID BY HIM DURING LECTURE. Most ppl sit there on their phone but if you pull out the pre/post lab on your laptop and write what he says you can finish it during lecture. He is very serious about Chegg. You'll get a 0 for a lab. Dont copy images from internet, draw them, even if you found it on the internet. Quizes are hard

Professor Ptaszek is overall a nice guy. However, he sometimes makes grammar and spelling mistakes on most of the rubrics, procedures, slides etc...I don't blame him because english isn't his first language, but it gets annoying when he continuously makes spelling mistakes on the lab questions that make you answer it wrong and get points taken off.

Felt bad for him in lecture, people used to talk over him all the time. He tries to explain lab concepts that are pretty critical but is unfortunately a poor communicator. His accent makes him very difficult to understand at times. For the amount he teaches, he expects a lot and grades hard. Lots of busy work and the final was pretty difficult.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: Just put enough effort  on prelab and postlab ,you should be fine..

Nice guy, boring lectures, but he gives you the answers to the pre/post-lab questions in them. Walks around the labs and talks to the students, so be prepared to answer qs he'll throw at you! Quizes were fair if you setup your notebook well. Posts everything online. The labs usually took up the entire time + make sure you know how to recrystallize!

Dr, Ptaszek is an amazing lecturer. He gives answers to each & every questions for postlab and prelab during lecture, so take note. He posts lead-off notes as well as solutions to prelab and postlabs, even mentions the goal of the experiment, something that nobody does. Quizzes are easy. There are really no negative points. He is very knowledgeable

Contrary to most of these reviews, I had no problem with Dr. Ptaszek. Lab lecture was pointless, but no more or less than every other Chem lab I've taken so far. Dr. Ptaszek would often walk through labs to make sure everyone was doing well, and was very friendly and knowledgeable when I needed help. I enjoyed having him!
I have no idea what he is saying in lecture. Does not give good instructions on what is to be done in lab and puts information in too many locations on blackboard.

I did horrible in his class quizzes. I continued to work hard and on the final exam review I went in and paid attention to everything he said. I studied that content religiously and aced the exam. He's hard to understand, but he's really helpful if you just approach him. His quizzes are straight from the book and lectures. Study hard.
Nice guy, good lecturer. If you pay attention you'll be fine. I found this lab and lecture much easier and more clear than 102L.

Ptaszek is a really smart and nice guy. His class isn't easy but that makes it more interesting. He does have an accent but it doesn't subtract from the class. His handwriting isn't the best but it is consistent so you might draw a funny looking symbol and find out it is an F later in the semester. But hey, its almost like learning a new language.
He doesn't know how to teach. And not only does he have an incredibly thick accent but his grammar on his slides and press lab questions make it almost undo able. Just awful

yeah yeah yeah... his accent is hard to understand. But give him a break... He's trying. His clicker questions are hard though (teaches w/ Perks). But, I do have to say that it is up to you to figure out the lab when he teaches because his lectures seem unstructured and the class gets loud when he teaches.

Just avoid taking his class if you ever can unless you are a self-learning type. He has a very thick accent and is very disorganized. Honestly, I can't understand what he's saying. So lost lots of clicker points. I don't get any idea about lab in lecture so need extra effort to dig in  lab manual or orgo textbook

His accent is thick, and his tests are hard, but he knows what he is saying and he is really nice. Make sure to read the book, and also take notes in class, since he goes through mechanisms and stuff on the whiteboard.

Very nice guy although he has a thick accent thats very hard to understand. When you can understand him, it doesnt make sense. I ended up withdrawing from the class because I failed my two exams really bad (even after reading the book and studying powerpoints). I went to him for help and he tried to help but was confusing.

He is the worst professor I have ever had. DO NOT TAKE HIM! I had to attend another lecture just to get by. His accent is horrible, his notes and handwriting are unreadable, he is very disorganized, and his tests do not reflect what he taught in class.  He also can not hear or see so forget asking questions in class unless you want to shout at him.

There were two essays and weekly reading checks. Pretty easy, and once we watched a tv series episode & ate snacks. We also had guest lectures, and some lectures were writing halls. You will have to read a lot and, although attendance isn't required, you have in-class (not hard) assignments to complete. Excellent professor. Lectures can get boring.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: One of the best professors I have had the honor to be lectured by. She was just a real person, actually cared about her students and most importantly not once did she ever stress me out like my other classes. Highly recommend her 304 class easiest A you will get in computer science but you do have to read and complete the assignments to get the A.

Williams is a great prof. She is VERY flexible w/ due dates and deadlines. Lots of reading and chapter quizzes in the first half that kinda suck - but she lets you take the quizzes w/ your table and bring written notes. One big project - a good amount of work to do but by no means impossible. Not a class you can coast in tho.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: She overly complicates everything & lacks clarity. UMBC needs higher standards for instructors. Teaching is a skill she lacks. Her homework & assignments are unclear,her comments are contradictory. Despite claiming machine learning expertise, she struggles with basic concepts:confusion matrix & gradient descent. She couldn't plot a graph in class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Create class would take again. Lowest grade you'll get is a C. Even if you only show up sometimes.

Her after-school work wants to take up 30 hours every week! She uses complicated words as if she's advanced. Even native classmates tell me these will never be used. She would post exercises in class and only give 7 seconds to read + answer each question. The class was like a high school English class, simple and useless but with tons of work!

I had Dr. Williams in their first semester. Pretty decent professor. Very laid back and gave lots of time to do assignments that weren't too difficult. Posts slides online, which is a plus, but they weren't super informative and during the lectures she would basically read off the slides. Not a bad class though, definitely one of the easier ones.

This was a group based class, so your experience will depend on how good you are with group projects. She doesn't really lecture, but the class is course heavy so make sure you meet with your group and client often. Most of the time you will have to figure out how to do things as she just tells you what to do but doesn't teach you how to do it.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: Class is primarily graded on the tests, yet there is more homework than in a usual class. If you either come to each class or go through the power points very thoroughly on your own then you should pass. Make sure to really try on the homeworks, understanding them will get you through a lot of the tests.

Great professor! Listened to our feedback on the class and made changes when necessary. Teaches the class in a way that even new coders can understand and do as well as those who have previously coded. I highly recommend her.

The class previous coding experience was the full spectrum, from 4 years in high school to no experience what so ever. Even so, she did manage to teach the class very well, easy enough for new coders to pick up on and hard enough that experienced coders couldn't just walk on by. Overall, I enjoyed the class and would recommend her.
Excellent professor.

Tests are hard, but very fair. She does like to give people partial credit if they seem to understand something about the problem. Projects are hard but there is plenty of extra credit on them that you can use to boost your grades on the tests.

If you want to take Computer Graphics take it with her. Projects are hard, but not as hard as when Olano is teaching it. You do learn a lot and she is fair when it comes to grading. Exams are really hard but she curves them, plus there are a lot of extra credit opportunity with in class exercises and extra stuff you can do in the projects.

Some of the tests questions were things that weren't covered in class, but if you studied well then you should know everything on them.  The projects can be a little annoying, especially when she doesn't make sure everything works, and she can be rather rude in her feedback.  Overall, I'd take more classes with her, but not go out of my way to.

Really fun class, but requires a lot of work. The projects were very time-consuming, but enjoyable. Lectures are sometimes a little boring, but mostly interesting. Despite the fact that she hands out lecture notes every class, read the book and take your own notes! The midterm and final were very difficult. The TA, Josh Barczak, was very helpful.
If you do the work and read it is a very easy B and she even lets you redo assignments if you get a, C or below, that being said it's an extremely hard A.

UMBC has some good 100 profs and I'm convinced Mrs. Putzel is the best.  Highly flexible on papers, always with ample time.  Happy to help with any questions and gets papers and stuff back QUICK.  Grading system is not very clear, and it's a hard A, but an pretty easy B.  No concrete length reqs to papers, up to 4 absences allowed per dept policy.
Professor Putzel is one of my favorite professors here. Class is easy as long as you show up and do the work assigned. Very knowledgeable. Easy 100 class.

Professor Putzel is a very helpful teacher. She provides an ample amount of time to complete major papers and essays and gives a lot of flexibility on the topics. Highly recommend student to take her class. It was an easy A for a student like me who does average in English.

Good professor, very nice and helpful. For this class, follow all her criticisms on your paper and submit all drafts on time for A's on your papers. Be sure to submit all labs on time too for an A in the course.

She was fantastic. Gave roughly 2 weeks to complete most essays; all relatively interesting topics with lots of flexibility to make it your own. Easy A, coming from someone who received straight B's in English throughout high school.

I have always dreaded English, but I found it to be very doable with Ms. Putzel. We wrote 4 essays and completed 4 lab assignments throughout the semester. She is a fair grader and gets papers back pretty quickly. Her expectations are very reasonable, and I would highly recommend her to prospective students!
Such a great teacher. Doesnt expect much. Just a few papers, which she grades really fast and tries to give everyone an A. Loved the class

Mrs. Putzel is one of the best English Professors that I have ever had. I am not a big fan of English but her teaching style made me fall in love with the class. We had 4 Essays to write, and 4 lab assignment that counted as one essay grade. Work load is not overwhelming.  She respected my style of writing and was able to receive an A.

Classes are boring, often spent peer editing or other mindless group work easily done at home. Other than that it is an easy class as long at you attend and no homework other than the 4 papers. Don't be surprised if the highest grade you get on an assignment is an A-/B+ (she doesn't believe in "a perfect paper") Overall take english with Putzel!

I have always dreaded english. When signing up for classes for first semester of freshman year, I used rate my professor to compile a list of decent teachers. I was lucky to find a spot available in one of her classes on orientation day. She is a great teacher. She always made time to help out her students. Not 2 mention we had no HW, n only 5essay
Very nice lady. Will never put you down or refuse to help you. You'd almost wish she was your mother. Easy A/B.

A very good professor for an introductory level English course.  Shares funny stories and is very lenient.  Sends reminders out to the class of the due dates on papers and what to expect of during the next class.  Overall, great experience.

Truly a delightful teacher. Does a great job to keep an introductory class as interesting as possible. Very funny. Not an unreasonable amount of work by any means.  If you have the opportunity to take her class, do it.

really good teacher. I am a computer engineering major and have NEVER enjoyed an english class. English just isn't my thing, i dont work with that side of my brain. She's the only english teacher I've had who made me think i could write a decent paper, and plus she stays really real and down to earth the whole semester. definitely take her class!
I highly recomend taking this class with her.  I don't like writing, but because of how she runs the class not only did I enjoy the class, I even got an A.

Diane Putzel is a great English teacher.  She tells great stories and has a great sense of humor.  Her assignments are actually interesting, and made me want to go to class.  Unfortuneatly, I ended up missing 5 classes overall.  Little did I know, that she would drop a letter grade.  So I ended up with a B.  I still think she's great tho.

One of my best teachers/professors so far in my HS+College career. She will definitely help you learn how to write but she won't do it for you; she'll point you in the right direction and you put in the effort. She's very fair in her grading, etc, always humorous, excitable, and will help you with written work you may have for other classes.
Putzel doesnt teach grammar, vocabulary, and all that. She says " you can know all the vocab and have the best grammar in the world, and sitll be a terrible writer'

Take Putzel for ENGL 100, she's awesome! She's a funny lady, just make sure you're not the person she starts picking on for the entire semester. Four papers and lab assignments with a techincal spin, it can't get any better. She keeps the class interesting by always keeping it real.

I mean ... yes this class is an easy B, but to get an A i guess you have to be Jesus, cuz it aint happenin. I've heard from several english majors that my papers were excellent but im not ... well im not Jesus, so i earned a B in the course.  If thats alright with you, holla at this one.
She's alright; a bit too feministic and politically correct, but otherwise OK. Whoever wrote she's hot must have their own concept of the relationship between beauty and age. - She's a nice lady.

Ms.Putzel is such a sweetheart! She's a wonderful teacher who sincerely cares about her students and goes out of her way to help them. On top of that, she's funny too! What more can you ask? Take her if you can (I can guarantee that you will love her...I do!!!)

One of the best teachers I've had! Very nice and very funny - actually looked forward to attending class. No exams - the grade is based on a few papers and projects. I just wish she taught more classes! Maybe ENGL 393...hint hint :)
Shes Really Really Nice.  SHe doenst give A's and gives A- which means an A in her gradebook.  Shes an ez grader and a very nice person
Great teacher, so nice and the classes are easy. One book to read (very easy) and about 4-5 papers and a few group projects. Attendence is required but not painful. Such a nice lady and an easy A!
Very good teacher.  Very funny always in class laughing.  Grade is based only on about 8-9 papers.  Always willing to help with anything. TAKE ENGLISH WITH PUTZEL
Very cool teacher, helpful with anything you need.  I loved her stories and examples.
No Comments
Nice, friendly, funny, and hot.  What more could you want?
Very nice, very helpful

She is very nice and sweet, but her teaching skills aren't so great. I signed up for this class expecting to have someone teach, half the things I learned were self taught. Her power-points are somewhat helpful, but not enough for the exam. Exams and 4 hw are what your grades rely on  which isn't that helpful.

If you've never taken anatomy & physiology before, this course may seem daunting. But, the homework is easy, and her questions are very straightforward, with ample extra credit. Be smart, and don't put off such a course for last minute studying or cramming! The only students who complained did just that. Else, the class is by no means difficult.

her class is fun, three exams, and hw, but tests are hard. lot of memorized.  very hard to get an A in the class. if u do poor on the two better get an A or B to bring your grade up if not u gonna have to repeated the class bc only 3 exams.

Nice professor, tests are in the form of semi-large in class writing assignments. Group work and discussion boards every once in a while. Rubrics for essays are a little unclear so write more than you think. Overall a pretty good teacher.

Prof S. is very nice, and the class isn't too hard. If you like having some ethical discussions, and don't mind writing 5 semi-large writing assignments in place of exams, take the class. A few group assignments, and attendance is graded. Rubric for the essays is semi-unclear, so just write a little more than you think. Disc. boards every so often.

I agree with many that the feedback can often be unclear, but I found the lectures to be very interesting. The exams are open note, so if you print out the slides text you will have a good idea of the test. Its all paper exams as in writing. I enjoyed the lectures, but you have to understand the material to pass.

Wouldn't take him again. Skipped a few lectures bc they were four hours long and a bore. Wish I couldve taken w another prof. 10 page paper + discussion post, two exams (graded harshly), and article discussions were some of the assignments for this class. Wouldn't round my 89% grade and responded rudely to my several emails. Steer clear of him!

His lectures were alright, I personally didnt show up much because he posts his slides on BB. His grading criteria is very broad, and is hard to understand what he is looking for. He will take a lot of points off if you get a small thing wrong. He grades papers very lenient but the midterm and mini exam is what he grades strictly.

he is a nice man but grading criteria is very unclear, especially for the semester long project which has an extremely loose rubric. very ironic that it is a management class when the class is not very well managed.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Group projects

reviews.comment: He posts his lecture slides, but you get to understand more of it if you attend class. He gives a lot of credit to the discussions and points he explains in lecture for the mini-exam and the midterm, all take home and you have time to work on. He is more than willing to help you out with the prompts and any questions you have for your final paper.

Cool person, just made it difficult to understand what he wanted on assignments. Lots of writing, dont skip class, his exams require use of in class discussions that are not on the slides. Also grades super tough but as long as you come to class, do well on the final project and don't utterly bomb the midterm you can get a B and pass this course.

He doesn't give clear criteria on anything and grades harshly expecting you to know exactly what he wants. Barely communicates, very few things to get points on and every assignment is make or break for your grade because there are so few. I wish the department had a different professor available for this class so badly. Never taking him again ever
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Good professor, his lectures are pretty engaging. If you pay attention, he explain things really well with examples and in detail. Only con is his grading criteria is vague and unclear. He makes the course fairly easy, since there is not much work to complete, but just be ready to write a lot for your exams and project.

He is pretty nice and funny professor. However not when it comes to grading, one of the toughest grading professor i ever had. He takes out many points and is overall hard grader. Theres also a 10 pages essay due so make sure to do that earlier and attendance is only mandatory for presentations.

Pretty good professor. Its an ethics class so parts of it are going to be boring at times but tries to keep the lectures engaging. The only negative is that the grading can be sort of confusing and a little unclear but overall not awful. Only a few major assignments so make sure to work on them and not wait til the very last minute.

He is an active professor but his teaching style is nothing special, you have 3 papers, 2 are a page long but the final paper is 10 pages long which can be confusing as you will not have a rubric. Midterm is written work but you can easily miss points since there is no rubric. You wont be stressed from this class except for big assignments.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: He is a tough grader and takes forever to grade. There are weekly discussions and articles summaries, so this class will take a good amount of your time.

Do not take this class. The class is very uncertain. Long time for grades. Hard to keep track of dates for all of the assignments. A lot of unnecessary anxiety. Not much criteria for exams, feels like it is just made up on the spot. Grading is so harsh and specific for such material which is incredibly vague. Is this ethical?

Fair and decent prof, pretty sure everyone who took him for the summer got As and Bs. Only got a C bc I reneged on the essay portion, so it should tell you even if you skip out on big assignments you can still pass. Great lecturer and grades were given fairly
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Lots of personal stories and jokes to make class fun, will answer emails very quickly. Assignments (Essays) are very vague which will frustrate you when writing them but he will accept almost any answer as long as you can support it with class subjects. As long as you take notes on the ethical theories from the first couple classes you'll be fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Sponaugle is a good professor for this course. He enhanced his lectures using humor, which made the classes more bearable. You don't have to have an extensive background in ethics or philosophy, which is nice because philosophy is a little mind boggling. It is an easy A course for an upper level IS elective.

Participation is 15% of your grade, if you don't like to talk don't take this class. Exams are based on discussions in class and the powerpoints. He grades a little harsh so understand the concepts. Project for the class is 24% of your grade so start early when it's assigned. He's a very nice guy and tries to humor the class from time to time.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Graded by few things--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: The material isn't necessarily interesting, but the professor tries his best. Doesn't take attendance, but grades participation. 3 exams are all written ethical prompts. You don't need to take notes, just show up and participate. There are 2 article presentations, 1 research presentation, and a long essay. It's a lot of writing and presenting.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Participation matters--So many papers

reviews.comment: If you are a graduating IS major and planning on taking him in your last semester I beg you not to. The amount of stress that this class has caused me is absurd. This course turned out to be the toughest class of my semester due to the ridiculous workload. . You can not breeze through. I can't believe the stress this class caused me

One of the worst professors I've had at UMBC. He grades tests and assignments like he's an English teacher and he'll literally find any reason to take off points. None of my classmates understood what to do since he gave us terrible instructions and yet when it came to grading, he graded off some imaginary rubric we never received. Don't take him.

Tests and quizzes were straight from lecture and the textbook. He is a fair teacher and will help you alot if you go to his office hours. Class isnt madatory but it pays off in the end. Overall this class was fairly easy if you put in the effort. There are 4 tests and 10 quizzes (2 are dropped) and one group project and Hw (but he forgot about it).

People started skipping within the first month until there were about 25 people left max. He assigns weekly reading assignments/activities that come with the textbook online. No test reviews, make sure to study. Quizzes are about 10 questions and tests are 50. Should have gotten a C but he bumped me up to a B probably cause I never skipped class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--TEST HEAVY
