reviews.comment: There are a lot of quizzes and tests, but they're all multiple choice. There's also a ton of homework that pile up quickly. His lectures are really boring and a lot of people start skipping after a month or so. Overall, his class isn't that hard to pass if you put in the effort to read the chapters before each quiz or test.

I am currently enrolled in his class for Spring 2018 and he is by far the toughest professor ever! more than half the class gets C's and D's on their exams (50 questions) and yet he does not curve the grade or help out. We can't ALL be lazy or don't study, there has to be something wrong with him. Plus we have a group project, 20 pages long!
Knowledgeable in the subject, exams are fair. , read the textbook, do the homework and study for exams and you should be fine

You will do well in this class if you show up to class and skim through the textbook. Prof. Sponaugle's lectures are hilarious and engaging. He incorporates stories from his own experiences in the field within his lectures. You will not make a mistake taking him.

Really lenient professor. There are 4 exams, group project (debate), 1 article review, 5 annotated bibliography and citation explanation due in this course. The exams are straight-forward and easy. Just make sure you memorize the definitions on the PowerPoint slides and pay attention to your classmates article review presentations.

Really enjoyed this class. You are graded on a few homeworks but mainly a group project and exams. Attendance isn't mandatory but it really helps to show up. As far as exams go it really helps to show up to class and study the powerpoints. His lectures were interesting and I learned many practical concepts.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Great guy and very friendly. If his class seems dry, I'd put it more on the material than the prof. MGMT 210 is heavy on facts, less on concepts. His stories are fun! He grades fairly, admits when he makes mistakes. All quizzes are multiple choice, easy to do well on. Same with tests. Group project is easy if you work hard and take responsibility.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: This class is a lot of fun if you're willing to participate. Nothing is more painful than the professor having to fish for answers. Luckily my class had a lot of good discussions. The exams are take-home, but take them seriously. The final is purely busy-work and is graded leniently so long as you follow directions.

His lectures are engaging and funny. He'll relate his previous work experience in management to each lecture to give students a better understanding of real life applications. Study the book and go to lecture and there is no reason you shouldn't get an A. The students who slack off are usually the individuals who complain about Prof. Sponaugle.

MGMT 210 was a solid class on business management. As long as you read the book and study the lecture slides you have a good chance of doing well on the tests. All tests were multiple choice and one group project. Get a started on the final project as soon as you can.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: I genuinely thought this class would be easy, but that was not the case. He made it clear on the first day that the information we learned would not have any real-world use for us. His lecture slides introduce ideas without explaining how to apply them. The tests include fake scenarios that rarely include lecture slide content. Dont take it!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Great professor. Pretty laid back and easy to approach with questions or concerns. Class isn't difficult if you put a little effort, as you will have to write a decent bit for the 2 take home essay exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: I took this class during summer session 1 and it is a six weeks course.  The assignments were evenly spaced out and lectures are not rushed. I felt like I learned a lot during the summer.  Take notes during class and study the Power Points for exams . He is an amazing instructor. I highly recommend him. His lectures are not boring and he is funny.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: This class is more of a discussion rather than a lecture, so be prepared to discuss your thoughts. He really values that. He makes sure not to go into territory that may be uncomfortable to students, but still teaches very valuable lessons. Tests and assignments are a lot of writing, but if you pay attention in class, you will at least get a B.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Participation matters--SO MANY PAPERS

reviews.comment: I took his class during 2016 summer session 1. This is one of the best classes I have ever taken. He is an Amazing professor. His grading criteria is really clear &the exams are not bad. Study PPT for exams and you should be fine. Within the 6 weeks course, home works and tests were evenly spaced out and I didn't feel like the course was rushed.

Taken as a summer course. Met twice a week for 3 hours, so it was long and boring. DIdn't use the textbook. Lectured from powerpoint and gave examples to clarify concepts. All you need to do is study the powerpoints to be able to pass his written exams based on ethical scenarios. Make sure your answers are logical arguments!

The highest grade for the first exam was 83, yet he didn't give a curve or offer to give any extra credit. He lectures the class with PPTs that he posts on Blackboard, but the exam questions come from the textbook. It seems as though he is not concerned about student's success in the class. He's one of those instructors who does his job and leaves.
Really easy class and great professor. As long as your arguments are logical, he'll give you a good grade

This guy is truly stuck in the past.. Not sure why we're talking about technology from the 90s. This class has a lot of potential that it it doesn't live up to. It's fairly easy but so boring because he's talking about information technology ethics of the early 90s. He should really read up on what's going on today...

Great professor. The class is easy and can be very interesting with class discussions.  The problem though, half the class stopped showing up after the first couple weeks, so discussions were nearly non-existent and lecture a bore.  Assignments and exams are mostly opinion based and not too difficult as long as you can apply it to the course.

Good guy good professor. Class is not too hard consist of one paper few test 2 quizzes 2-3 assignments. Also a presentation on your paper. Not a hard class if people talk the class is can be really fun especially with good input

Great professor, I wish all professors taught like Sponaugle. The class is interesting and you get to take some liberties with the assignments. He's very open minded and encourages you to be also. Take home exams and a take home quiz. The project can be alot of fun if you choose wisely. Got an A. I really enjoyed the course and you will too! Easy!!
Great Class. You won't need a book and he's very lax. Encourages discussion and participation. If you do the take-home exams and do the project you should be just fine.

Nice guy who is interested in the course. Did not use textbook at all, he used powerpoints he created each class. He wants students to do well and be interested in discussion. Good course to take for upper level IS credit.
Great Professor.
easy class and don't need a book.

This is my favorite professor I've ever had. Professor Richburg really strives to make sure her students understand and are prepared for later in life. She is extremely relatable, and she's nice & understanding. I took her both MGMT210 and IS438 and was outstanding in both. I love her, and I know everyone that takes her class will love her too!

Great professor! She shares valuable real-world/industry experience and she's too hilarious - I enjoyed her lectures. One semester-long group project, but nothing difficult at all. Practice exam is almost same to the exam (so do them!). Pay attention in class, do the work, and it's an easy A.

I took this course over this past summer but it was such a breeze. Professor Richburg made the lectures fun and just easy going. There is a group project along with the journal entries (500 words) but it's really easier than you think. Her exams are an exact copy of her study guide so go over that. It's an easy A as long as you do the work.

Easy A. 500 word assignment due every week (its not as bad as it seems). Lectures are from textbook generated slides, makes you do group activities during class. Makes lectures bearable. Exams are the same as the study guides she gives. Group project is easy, just get everything in. Also not strict with due dates and is an easy grader.

She is a good professor. very clear and easy to pass. just pay attention in class, do the your journal entries, and do the practice exams ( they are 99% of the exam) Super Easy and she can seen a little harsh and unapproachable but she is nice and friendly. The only thing she said in class that I didn't like is "I do not reply to emails"
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Group projects--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Never felt stressed about this class. Lectures were involving & always applied to the real world. The prof. has experience in mgmt & applies it to the class. HW was simple. The group project involved creating a 'made-up' business, easy 7-10 pages if you find cooperative groupmates. The exams were made clear by practice tests, make sure to use them!
She doesnt communicate with the class. She switched the due dates without telling anyone

Easy class, make sure you do all the hw assignments. She gives a practice test prior to the exam which is literally her exam so make sure you do it. Group project is easy and straightforward but she picks your team. Make sure you do all the journals too (I missed two but still got full credit). Try not to submit late assignments.

Prof. Richburg is one of the best professors at UMBC. Every class I've taken with her has been an easy A. All you have to worry about is completing all assignments on time, because she won't let you submit anything late. If you show up to every class, submit all assignments on time, and complete weekly journals, then you'll pass the class easily.

If only all professors at UMBC were like Tasha. Funny, real world experience, and doesnt drag you to hell and back for a good grade. Group project was a huge part of the grade, and it can be difficult only because all members really have to work.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Graded by few things--Group projects

reviews.comment: Great professor! I wish she could teach all my classes! She doesnt force you to memorize 99000 slides and call it teaching!
Easy professor, easy A, if you dont like easy things and want to struggle then dont take her.

Never take a class with her. Her lectures are unhelpful and scattered, and she provides no direction for the class. Coursework is all filler or repeats from 200-level classes. Annoyingly condescending. Always says that "this is how it is in the work world". She's a successful project manager, but has no standards and is simply a horrible teacher.

Prof. Richburg is an amazing professor! She made the class really interesting and made the subject simple to understand. Even though it was a late class, she made it seem like it was earlier in the day! She also has much experience in the field and does not mind sharing them. The class has 3 exams and a semester project. Don't forget to do journals

She posts a practice test and takes it away after 2 days. Don't miss that time period to download the practice test or else you're gonna regret it because all the questions on the real exam comes directly from the practice test VERBATIM. Still gotta pay attention during her lectures and keep up with the class tho

Easily the worst professor I've ever had. The class is easy but there were too many things wrong with it to list here, essentially she didnt teach & most things she says are super unclear. In the first 5 weeks she will read the powerpoints to you. After that the students will handle lectures w/ presentations for a group assignment.

I really think the entire class needs to be restructured. I thought that IS425 was very disappointing. This is one of the only classes I have taken in my 4 years of college where I genuinely didn't learn anything. Basically each class a group of students preset parts of the chapter and she sits in the back. This class makes IS/UMBC look bad.

You are in college, don't expect her to hold your hands and tell you when things are due. Check blackboard, refer to the syllabus and do your work. This is an EASY A class as long as you do your work. Exam usually take 5-10 mins if you do the study guide.  She does not like long essays, so keep it short. Class always dismisses early. Easy  A class.
Awful professor. Does not tell students when things are due or posted. Her teaching style is terrible and all over the place. Easy class, though.
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--SO MANY PAPERS--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: This is C Richburg. Easy class. She takes attendance. Make sure you do all homework she will not tell you  when she posts new stuff that is due. So constantly check BB. Tests are the same as the Review which she will take down 2 days after she posts. Group project is easy. Take her if you can classes are short and to the point.
This professor have different name, C Richburg. If you follow the syllabus exactly you will get an A. Very very doable.

Excellent professor! In order to get an A, you have to attend class and do the weekly journals online(what you learned in class that day). They are worth almost 12% of your grade so its best not to miss class because she takes attendance and will know if you were there or not.

I feel I was cheated out of my A. The entire semester the class felt like an easy A, until I was realized I missed a self assessment, that wasn't on the syllabus, just briefly on bb. The missed self assessment cost me 6% of my grade. Completely unfair grading that does not reflect a student's knowledge at all. I personally feel cheated.

One midterm, a final, a group project, and some article reviews. The class is super easy, as long as you read the practice test you will get a 100 on the exams. Only talks about real world stuff, nothing practical what you should be learning from the course

People seem to be really tough on Professor Richburg. I personally think that she is a great professor who teaches her students by giving real world examples instead of following the textbook. Yes, she does not give us the due dates or anything she posts on blackboard, but it is YOUR responsibility to check, not hers. Easy A class.

She is an ok professor. Doesnt really give clear directions, shes funny, talks about her experience alot. Basically all the time. you do alot of group work and dumb assignments. the exam is really similar to the review sheet.

This is an easy A class, but she doesnt tell you deadlines, doesnt give clear directions and penalizes you. 636 students got what she wanted and the rest lost points. She wants you to figure out what she wants from you, if you dont figure it out too bad. She always talks about her work experience. Always check bb, she wont tell you about assignmen
I enjoyed class time. She gives useful advice about navigating the workplace.  You don't need a book, but it's useful to have one among your friends. Tests are easy and just like the study guide.

Although I have not completed this course so far, I dont like this professor. She talks about her work experience every 5 secs. And she barely touches the book. I love active teachers. She is not active. She talks about herself 2 much. Also, the hw due dates & assignments are unclear. This may b an "easy A" but I am expecting 2 learn something.

This class is easy to pass. Do not expect to learn much because this class is pretty basic and straight forward. She does not really know much about anything IT related even though she will tell you she does. Often you will hear her saying "you're going to deep" when you answer her vague questions about IS related topics. Presentation at the end.

Class was definitely easy to pass. 2 exams and a group project that you (and your group) choose. She'll make the groups up, and assign project leads, etc, but after that you pretty much have control of what the group does. Ended up becoming project lead after the leader all but dropped the class. Tests exactly like the practice exams she gives.
Easy A and upper level credit class. Apart from that nothing that usefull u will learn from the class. Group project somewhat challenging. if you are minority you WILL be the group leader!

If you actually want to learn about project management, then don't take her class. There's 2 exams(really easy but you need the book), group project (work is spread out among group members, if you have a good group-great, if not-sorry!,and you don't get to pick your group) Overall its an easy A, but don't expect to learn too much from her.

Terrible professor. Don't learn much about project management, instructions are extremely vague and unhelpful and she won't clarify them. Assignments and due dates are unclear and she likes to shuffle them around a lot.

This instructor does not teach; she briefly discusses the material and talks about IT management. In this course, you must read 50 pages a week if you want to learn something. I have experience in the field and feel that the information is very helpful for anyone in IT. The project is only difficult if you don't understand what needs to be done.

A complete waste of a class. Richburg spends the class going over 5 out of 40 slides and then talks about her previous job experience. The group project is time consuming (you can't pick your teammates), and doesn't teach you anything about project management. This class was supposed to teach Project Management - not her previous job experience.

Prof Richburg took a little getting used to, but she grew on me as the semester progressed. She's easier than she comes off, and possesses a wealth of practical advice. The course consisted of 2 exams (really easy), and a group project. The group project is filled with several deliverables, so manage it well. Don't wait till the last minute! Easy A

Easy A or B class but very disorganized. Two take home exams which but HW on the other hand was annoying in that she never gave notice of when it was due. The project is OK, teaching some elements of Project Management. She taught more on how to get a job than actual project management. Take the class if you want but there are better classes.
she knows her stuff and puts it in plain english for us to benefit in the real world not just in class

Professor Richburg is a wonderful teacher, she is a woman I admire alot.  For all of the haters out there you need to chil. If you do not have anything nice to say, don't say it at all. You will never find a person who is as educated and down to earth as Professor Richburg is.

Easy A.  There are 2 exams, one of which will be a take home because the class does so poorly on the first one.  (Nobody takes it seriously.)  You have a group project that is the majority of your grade.  The professor teaches you real world knowledge but doesn't follow the book at all and as a result we didn't learn a lot of relevant material.

IS students should take courses which develop real job skills- she teaches you none of that. She doesnt act professional and her HWs/project are dumb (hunt for pink stapler!?). EASY A or B, but do yourself a favor & make use of your one elective and pick something else (ie more programming). Still wanna learn PM? Just read the book she assigns.

she gave practice tests.  she doesnt tell you the format of the teat before hand.  she posted a practice on BB and the night we took the test it was the same one she posted.  You will learn alot about project management by doing a community service project.  I never bought the book and was 4 points away from an A.  The final presentation is a skit.
Professor Richburg was a very good teacher. She was very professional and I learned about project management.

Waste of time, unless you dont care about learning. Semester project deals with community service. Tests are a little tricky, easy enough, though.  This was a class where I just read the glossary of the text to study. She's also pretty full of herself. Talks with a lot of slang too. Theres other electives out there to develop useful skills.
Shes not bad, Youd think her clas is a joke with the homework she hands out and the examples she uses in class, and her tests are weird. But you'll learn plenty about project management from her.

One of the best professors I've had.  I learned a ton, was entertained, and didn't have to work too hard to get an A. The class pretty much follows some chapters she picks from the textbook. All of her real-life examples and comments have helped me in my job. Two exams: multiple choice, true/false, matching... no surprises. Even bonus questions!  F

If you want an easy A Ritschel is not your guy. However, I think these reviews are too tough. You can get an A if you attend the lectures and put some thought into your essays. He's actually a really nice guy. His lectures are also really interesting and our class had a lot of great conversations. I would definitely take another class with him!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Ritschel has a vast amount of knowledge and knows what he has to teach. He creates plenty of discussion and greatly enjoys participation. The essays were not bad, the averages were usually B's. He tells you exactly what he wants, but if you have another opinion then you may lose points. To get full credit you have to understand what he wants.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Graded by few things--So many papers

reviews.comment: Uses poor evidence that occasionally disagrees with his point Disorganized Expects you to interpret everything he gives you exactly his way despite its lack of clarity including his own vague directions Googling example of a history paper is far more effective to learn how to write Condescending Regurgitate exactly what he says to pass

very approachable and intensely knowledgeable (this 497 was british homefront in wwii). supportive and encouraging, very helpful. offers clear rubrics and deadlines. can be tough to reach by email. class doesn't meet regularly once it's up and running - kind of like an independent study. nice baritone for lectures.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Dr. Ritschel is an amazing professor! Who knew British History can be this interesting? His lectures are awesome!

Loved Dr. Ritschel, the small class size (only 10 of us) made the class very engaging and discussion orientated. He clearly cares for the subject and the students. He was also a really fair grader who gave clear feedback and gave students a chance to resubmit papers. Instead of punishing us for a bad paper #3 he pushed back paper 4. I love ritschel
He is tough but fair.  Be prepared to write a lot.  He definitely will make you a better writer.  Discussions are awesome
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Great lecturer. It was obvious he was very knowledgeable and cared about what he was teaching. Four 3-page papers with a lot of reading. He also gives good feedback on your papers. Attendance is graded, and especially in the classes before paper is due he'll give class a guide on what to write about.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Great lectures and discussions were awesome.  Lot of reading.  The four papers were hard but you will definitely become a better writer.  Very challenging and rewarding class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: If you are at all interested in a career in history, take this class. You will learn what academic history is all about and your writing skills will dramatically improve. He is a fair grader and his papers are easy and fun to write. He makes a class on methodology really fun, and he explains boring concepts in really interesting and engaging ways.

Dr. Ritschel's class turned an ordinarily boring class about a variety of topics I have little experience with, into something memorable.  The class has a ton of reading and writing, but his feedback on the drafts of the historiographical paper was specific and extremely helpful for shaping myself as a writer.  I

Dr. Ritschel is a great professor. Really enjoyed his class. 4 papers and that's all of your grade with the exception of participation which is about 10% of your final grade, so show up if you want an A. Great lectures, everything he wants in your papers is given to you in the lectures. Papers aren't that bad, first three are 4-5 pages each.

First class I took as a history major and he made me truly understand what would be involved to have a career as a historian. He really took the time to explain the career outlook, what grad school would be like. Teaches you how to really think like a historian. Papers are short but take some real thought. Funny and not bad to look at (Silver fox!)

Great professor.  Lectures a bit dull, but he leads absolutely fantastic discussion groups. Very knowledgeable.  TAs were dodobirds though. On a random note, his voice is freaking amazing.  Could listen to him all day np.

This class is not the most interesting, but it's mandatory for majors. Dr. Ritschel is not so bad. His TAs were very helpful and quite knowledgeable. I learned a lot about writing and history in this course.
I was a student of his in the 1990s and he was amazing.  I still admire and think back to what a wonderful teacher he was.  I still look at British music halls with a smile.
Drink lots of coffee to stay awake in this class.

Class topic was Film and History. Class was a BREEZE--didn't open the textbooks once/watch a movie, and did not need to, exams were based solely on lectures. Attendance was 10% of grade. Has a good sense of humor and overall nice guy. Very heavy reliance on TA, but she was great as well.

Dr Ritschel is a very likeable person and a decent prof. He has a thorough knowledge of hte subjec and his extremely helpful when approached. Big warning here. If you like to use a notebook computer in class, he does not allow them. For that reason I will not take a class from him again.

Dr. Ritschel is one of my favorite professors at UMBC. He does rely on his TA for some things, but it's good experience for the TA and it certainly doesn't take away from his teaching style. If you attend lectures and take good notes, you'll do quite well on the papers. He usually tells you exactly what he wants to see. The rest is writing style.

I have taken several classes with Dr. Ritschel, and he was also my advisor.  I can honestly say that Dr. Ritschel was probably the best teacher I had at UMBC.  You do have to work for your grade in his courses, but the knowledge you gain is priceless.  I would highly recommend any class tought by Dr. Ritschel.
The accent your hearing is Canadian

I don't know what's up with these negative reviews, Dr. Ritschel's a great prof, he had to FAIL ME (my own fault) for 474 and I still like him--not 'snobby' at all. the *best* 201 instructor ever, I think-I back up the 1st comment on this page, the man created a passion for the subject still with me

Basically, the class itself is interesting but he's not.  His teaching style is a huge turnoff and his unknown (possibly faux British) accent drives me nuts.  TAs in the class are good but he's not.  Take this class with Jeffries.

His class is hard and the lectures are a bit of a pain to get through- but its 2 1/2 hours so its to be expected. he does give off a snobbish attitude but he's really helpful and knows his stuff.  A good professor but need to take him with a grain of salt- but id recommend him
Lectures can be a drag sometimes but when approached, is very helpful and informative.  Does sometimes give off a cocky side but is nonetheless a decent professor.

snobby jerk and his TAs run the class-- theyre even more annoying than he is.  the class is boring, he sucks as a teacher.  i switched to american studies as my major because he sucked so bad-- i sure am glad i dropped him!  RUNNNN!
His TAs do the dirty work for him... boring and lousy class-- kind of snobby guy too, i changed my major because his class stunk.

A lot of work, but the class is interesting.  If you're into history and have a great passion for it-- THIS IS A GREAT CLASS FOR YOU with him as a prof.  If history is more of a hobby, don't go for it.

Unfortunately, although this man is a great guy, I didn't really like him as an instructor.  He tends to be very repetitive and sometimes unclear about the concepts he means for you to understand.  On the plus side, he does know his British economic histo

The greatest teacher I have ever experienced. This man taught me at the University of Windsor in the early 90's. He created a passion for the subject that is with me to this day. Now I also teach. I hope to one day do it as well as this man.

Professor Rostamian knows the content inside and out, but it sometimes felt as though he forgot that we were not also experts on the content. His lectures were informative but often difficult to follow. You will be graded almost entirely on a small handful of exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He was a very good teacher at the start of the semester. However, later on, he just started accusing people of cheating, and he has failed me in his class for "cheating" when I didn't cheat and when I am trying to prove it to him. He doesn't want to listen now, I have to retake the class even though I put so much time and effort.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: Cool dude but he's really quiet and has an accent. Also doesn't really explain much.

Very nice guy, but his class is not it. It should say something when 1/3 of the class walks out after the 10min quiz at the beginning of lecture is over. His lectures just aren't very informative or particularly relevant to what we're tested on, and good luck getting any supplemental resources online.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Great, highly articulate speaker, very kind, and clearly really knows his stuff; asking him questions is definitely worthwhile. Maple was used to code in this class; was pretty easy to learn. Sometimes lectures seemed simplified though, or not enough material covered per week. Homeworks and grading were easy.

Dr. Rostamian is a super kind and caring professor. The problems were long, but he walked us through every single step. His exams were very fair, almost identical to homework problems, and he also gave a lot of extra credit on homework. This subject takes a lot of work, but if you put in the effort, Professor Rostamian will make sure you succeed.

Insanley nice professor. If you sit up front, pay attention, and do all the homeworks he's a great teacher. He seriously knows his stuff and it definetly shows. Only small gripe was that the exams were pretty hard. He did however grade exams pretty leniently in my opinion.

Dr. Rostamian is the best professor I've had far. He gives extremely cohesive & thorough lectures that make the material so, so much easier to learn. He occasionally may make a mistake on the board, but they are usually minor. Go to the lectures, do some of the extra HW problems, and you will understand the material, guaranteed.

The course is just 5 grades. Each one is  a project using Maple and LaTex. Each one take 8-15 hours. You get about 2 weeks for each. However, if you come to class, Dr. Rostamian walks you through each project and that makes it alot more doable. It's a good class to take for the WI requirement because it also counts towards your math electives.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Gives good feedback--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: Class is 100% graded on your projects, which there are about 7 of.  They each take a long time to be done well, and in order to do well, you need to satisfy his particular wants.  Very particular about small things, so be sure to proofread and put some real effort into your papers.

Very clear in explanations. Knows what he is talking about and goes direct to the point. Math is easy, However, get ready to spend at least 15 to 20 hours on each paper as writing perfectly in Latex will take forever. Fair grader.
Dr. Rostamian's lectures are very thorough and clear. He responds quickly to emails and is very helpful.

Great professor! Very interesting course, explains what he expects of you very clearly and is willing to answer all questions. Really knows the subject material and explains clearly. Teaches LaTeX and Maple basics so a beginner can understand. I was worried about taking this before real analysis (301) but this was not a problem. Highly recommended!

He knows what he's saying, but that's as far as it goes, unless you're great at math, you'll be lost. He doesn't give enough examples and gives at least 30homework problems each class. This class was a lot of stress.

Rostamian is a great professor.  His lectures are very helpful, and he explains everything in a clear and concise manner.  His Quizzes and exams are based off of hw.  He moves faster than the other Calc 3 teachers that I know of, but as long as you do all of the homework he gives out (which really isnt that much), you should get an A in his class!

Not worth the headache. He makes the class worse than what it should be, and the examples given in class are hardly ever helpful when doing the actual homework, etc. Homework isn't required unless you'd like to pass the class, because quizzes and exams are based off of the homework (supposedly).

Class is not so much about mathematical modeling as it is about your ability to write a scientific paper and mark up perfectly in LaTeX. All the math is basically done for you in class. Grading system is frustrating because there is no rubric, no statement of what mistakes cost you how many points, and seems very arbitrary.

The course itself is tough if you aren't a math person. He has a slight accent that might throw some people off but it was easy to figure out after the first few weeks. Homework is optional but I highly suggest doing it otherwise you may do poorly on the exams. 2 exams and a final are worth 80% of your grade while quizzes are the remaining 20%
WOW. the worst teacher i have ever had. ne one who wants to even pass dont get this teacher. i dropped

He knows what he's talking about, but isn't that great at teaching it. He's often disorganized and scatterbrained. I'm almost certain I failed the class because he did not make it clear what would be on the exams. If you actually do the homework every week and drop by his office and ask him questions, I'm sure you could pass (relatively) easily.
it is my first time in my life to fail a math class while i worked so hard!

I don't suggest anybody to take his class unless you are very very good at math and you don't want any interaction with the professor in the class. his class is extremely boring. only 2 exams in his class which means if you don't do good on either one, you would never get an A. only 6 or 7 questions on the exam. he is a rally hard grader also.

For applied math, I think he is the best teacher in the department.  481 was very interesting and renewed some of my interest in math.  Rostamian is such a good lecturer I actually wanted to go to class.  He's patient and clear without making you fall asleep Rathinam style.
Very clear.  Does not take attendance, but many still went to the classes because he is a good teacher.

Emphasized the writing aspect of 381 so the math was rather easy, stuff we already know in the most part.  It's a time consuming class, but it's very easy to pass if you don't do each of the 10 projects in single sittings.

Overall, he was a very good teacher.  He used Maple to help show hard to visualize 3d functions.  His test were definitley representative of the assigned homework problems.  If you can do the homework, you will be fine.

he said, more than once in my class, "maybe i should have thought about this before i started teaching it". his notes make no sense because they aren't linear, he'll use the first half of the class to talk about what we did the first half of the previous one. so confusing....i don't like math anymore

He's very very good at explaining why you do things to solve problems.  He allows a cheat sheet on tests and his tests come directly from the lectures (Not the HWs, which can be tedious.)  He does expect you to know Maple and/or Matlab but does a quick tutorial session at the beginning of the semester.

His tests are hard, quizzes are very similar to the HW that he doesnt collect. He curves more than he says. I was going into needing an 85% to get a C, but wound up with a solid B. Overall a good guy, I'd recommend Rostamian
Very Good Instructor, Easy A if you go to class and listen. Material can get boring, but it is a math class. He is student friendly and is available if need be.
He's very knowledgeable and teaching very clearly. The exams are very similar with the homework assignments. He's so kind and understanding.
calc 2 is just hard on its own, whether the teacher is easy or not
Explains everything thoroughly, makes it easy to understand.  Do the homework even thought he doesn't collect it because quiz and test questions are very similar.

For Bio-ethics there is no exams or quizzes. Onlv 3 papers and a group presentation. He lets vou rewrite papers for a better arade with comments on what to change. The class itself is easv but the lectures are torture and are the same boring thing every class. He liked my group but will single you out if you do something he doesn't approve of.

Has an incredible knowledge of Engineering and technology with detailed knowledge of contemporary developments in technology. This was my favorite class of the year. I love him. A stimulating professor
Super easy class.  All we had was three papers only.  Although I don't like philosophy, his way make it very easy.

He is not the best professor for Phil 120. It is really hard to get an A in the class as there are only three assignments. All of the assignments are in essay format. He is the worst professor. Goes off topic and his assignments are not clear. Really hard to pay attention in his class. I would not recommend him for Phil 120.

There are 3 exams, each worth a third of the grade. The first exam has terms and some problems. Only proofs and problems on the other exams. Just do all the problems in the book and understand how to prove it then you'll get an A.

He's a nice professor & very smart & intelligent. Although I find the class boring because I'm not interested in Philosophy, he's a great teacher. He's pretty funny & approacheable too. No tests, just essays! He's an easy grader & always there to offer his opinion.

super super easy class, easy A. The professor rambles about nothing and i often want to fall asleep. Even if you skip class you can still get an A b/c he puts practice tests online. You will either find his sense of humor super lame or laugh with him, he's a nice guy though.

Wilson is a great professor. He doesn't teach you the class, rather he makes you think for yourself. This class is more useful in learning how to formulate your own opinions rather than learning history of philosophy. Exams are posted online, no homework, one essay, and attendance isn't mandatory. Don't ask stupid questions. Easy A!

Class is boring but attendance is mandatory. He doesn't take attendance but he knows when you are absent. He posts practice quizzes online. if you memorize those they are the exact questions on the exams. Theres no reason you can't get an A if u go to class &look at quizzes. He doesn't tolerate ignorant questions from people who dont go to class.

Professor Wilson is a great teacher. He loves philosophy and is very passionate about it. Attend classes, take notes and do quizzes he uploads on the BB and you should be perfectly fine. You don't need any textbooks for this class he provides everything.

Wilson is AWESOME! He enters the classroom and moves around, talks to the students, like Russell Crowe in Gladitor, he introduces ideas of great philosophers clearly with precision and an EXCELLENT use of examples from real ife. He reminds me of a white Sidney Poitier in To Sir With Love. Mostly importantly he urges us to think for ourselves.

Easy class, all the quizzes are online and he uses the same questions on the test, with the exception of a "chart", which is a list of words to memorize. The lectures are horrible to sit through and terribly dull. He goes on rants about things for absolutely no reason. I could not tell you anything that he has said in lecture not written on board

Took Wilson's Business Ethics course over the winter, highly recommend it.  Also had him for Phil346 logic class.  Awesome philosophy teacher and is very helpful when u go to him.  Don't be late to class!  It is evident he brings years of experience and knowledge to lectures which is what students want
Prof. Wilson is awesome! He gets off topic sometimes and the class material is somewhat boring but he tries to make it as fun as he can. Plus, he posts the exam questions online so it's super easy.
Very interesting material. Prof. Wilson is a little scatterbrained and sometimes difficult to follow in lecture. This is mainly an example-based class.

Don't forget your phone or laptop when you go to class... otherwise prepare to be bored. He's a great guy and very interesting, he just is very hard to understand at times because of all his tangents. Basically gives you all the exam questions but honestly if you just read you'll get A's on everything.
It's a month into the class and I don't know what I think about him. "Attendence is mandatory" but he doesn't talk about anything relevant. Scatterbrained and confusing.

Enthusiastic and loves the course material. Loves enthusiastic students and hates students who don't show up or miss the point. Assigned one individual paper and two group papers. He wanted "future ethical issues," and he tore apart the groups who did past ones. Just act enthusiastic and follow the rubrics, and you should get an easy A or B.

If you are looking to take this class, then look no further!!! this guy can teach, very nice, funny.  Wants people to learn, enjoys teaching. Oh and get the book. You'll need a book to practice for the test because he doesn't provide practice exams.  The problems in the book were much harder than the exam. therefore you will do well. put in effort!

Professor Wilson definitely marches to the beat of his own drum. His is very passionate about philosophy and sincere but at times difficult to understand. His lectures tend to consist of many anecdotes and sidebars, which makes paying attention difficult. Follow his instructions (and exam keys!) for the 3 exams and one response paper for an easy A.
Easy A. Useless class. No reason to show up except to get the rubric. Follow it exactly to get an A.

1 test, 1 individual paper, 1 group paper, 1 group project. The test was the hardest part about the course. No textbook needed. Had to go to class, but only took notes before the test. After he would ramble on with jokes, but he is a funny teacher. Told us exactly what he was expecting. Gave us alot of additional material for people interested.

I don't think I learned a single thing from his lectures, and I think he only wrote ten words on the board all semester. He will spend 99% of the lecture time telling random life stories. He gives the class sample exams that are exactly like the ones you take. There are three papers to write and one project. Only one has to be done individually.

If you asked me what the class was about, I would not be able to tell you. I did not learn a single thing, but I am positive I will be getting an A. I don't care much for Philosophy so it doesn't matter to me, but he's an awkward guy, funny, easy going and kind-hearted but extremely awkward. If you get to know him, it's an easy A, no doubt!

It's fun to listen to Wilson because he mostly talks about stuff that doesn't pertain to the class. He sometimes tells the same story several times, and he will tell it like he's never told it before. The papers are easy; all he cares about is whether you followed the rubric.

Wilson is a cool person, but this class is a joke. He shows up late, talks about whatever he feels like talking about, and that's it. The papers can get intense, but the process is straightforward. Don?t buy the book. It?s a waste of money. Overall, an easy A.
Awesome course to take. But make sure you chose discussion session with Sofiya (TA). She is the BEST TA I have ever had. Very friendly, relaxed and willing to help you out at every moment.
Very nice teacher.  Knows the material.  Keeps the class interesting.  Only negative was it look a while to get graded material back.  This made the semester project a little tougher.
x
great class ! interestin prof and TA he was awesome

Great professor overall. He is really into the Titanic. The class is intriguing and he tries to be funny. You will do well on the essays if you follow the directions. My only concern is about the T.A's who grade the essays. One T.A graded much more harshly than the other, causing some students to ask the nicer T.A to grade their essay instead.

THATS MY DOGG!!!!!!!!!!! He goes off on tangents all class that have a vague relevance to the material, but is not necessary. You have to teach your self the stuff, but its not that hard. It's pretty funny to hear him make jokes even though he is the only one that laughs at them

Easy class, one test, one individual paper, one group paper. The "textbook" is the biggest waste of money ever. Wilson "wrote" it and you have to pay to access it online. The problem is that the majority of the content comes directly from Wikipedia, and the rest is not worth the money at all. I felt very ripped off. At least the class was easy.
He is a good professor. More than lenient. He hates laziness, but wants all of his students to excel. So do what you are told and you should get an A. Three papers and 1 test.

Very good at keeping the class interested, and work isn't too difficult. However, it often takes a while to get back graded work, rarely checks his email, and repeats stories/information. He's funny, sometimes in a corny way, and is more than willing to help you out after class. But yes, he can be unclear about what he wants.

Really no reason for this guy to be on here cuz hes the only teacher for this course lol either way IT IS an easy class and hes a down-to-earth type of guy..1 individ. paper 1 small group paper, 1 research project, and 1 test all of which are doable..especially the test

This class was easy and fun. All the questions to the exam came from the practice exam he gave in class. He lets you redo the first two papers and this class was easy. Not too difficult. He is a nice teacher and very helpful and The TA for this class was great. He helps you alot. It's like they want you to get an A in this class.

Richard Wilson is an interesting person. Class is pretty boring. Wilson usually goes off on tangents. There are 3 papers and 1 test with a presentation. There is no reason why you shouldn't get an A in this class. not much else to say. Has a dry sense of humor.

Really nice prof. Very entertaining and funny. Definitely one of the better lecturers at UMBC. Only major problem was getting a hold of him through email, but it was during winter semester so it's forgivable. Honestly though, I felt CMSC 304 was a completely worthless endeavor- again, maybe because I took it over the compressed winter semester.
one test, its rediculous..  then a big group project.  get a good group

Man.  This guy jumps around a lot and it's not very clear what he expects out of you until late throughout the course.  Plus, the class is just a bore, I really try to avoid it.  His syllabus is a joke.  It says if you miss 3 classes, you will fail and he doesn't even take attendance.  His syllabus offers points for HW and he never gave it.

I found this class incredibly frustrating. He's kinda boring. Has only one exam halfway through the semester. One individual paper and one group paper to write. The final is a group presentation on another paper and topic of your choice. Class was boring, i dont go when possible.

I've had him for religion, ethics, and logic.  He is very clear on what he wants and believes strongly in attendance.  Very goofy, which I think some people are uncomfortable with, but very intelligent/fair. Tests aren't misleading but they can be difficult.  Come to class and he'll be very lenient/easy!  If you don't, there's no real mercy.

I love this guy. He is a pretty amusing character. The class includes a big group paper, but it's still worth it. My group was a bunch of morons, and I still got an A in the class. Take this class just to experience the professor.

Class was easy. Only 1 individual homework assignment and 1 test which was easy. However, there is a long semester group project that I recommend that u get in a good group. Overall the teacher made the class fun and interesting which I learned alot.

Pretty good professor. Very interested in logic, but often goes off on repeated tangents about Pitt and their superior logic program. Teaches material straight out of the book. Skips over the rules (I guess he expects you to learn on your own ahead of time) and spends all of class doing proofs. Grade based on 3 tests. Tests are curved substantially

Often goes off on tangents and repeats the same concepts. One test which he gives you a study guide for. Don't get the book- you won't use it. You have to write lots of papers and he will help you on them if you ask. Very nice and has lots of bad jokes. Overall  he's a pretty good professor.

Dr. Wilson is a very smart man.  Class is very simple and straight-forward. 1 individual paper, 2 4-5 page papers and 1 20-25 page paper (w/presentation) in a group.  Did not use book at all, although he talked about using it in the future.  Sometimes gets upset with the class for no reason.  Has a strange obsession with the Dean.

Class was interesting.  Def gained new perspectives on ethics.  There was only 1 test, but lots of papers to write with group members.  NEVER used the textbook, but I will def take another class with Wilson.  One of the best prof's at UMBC.
There was no official syllabus for the class. It was an easy class - only one test. But, it was hard to figure out what he wanted.
awesome all around

He's really corny but amusing.  Not really good at fostering class discussion, but it's not that kind of class.  He writes his own reviews on here.  I can pretty much say that if he's got an easiness rating of 3 and everything else is a 5 he did it.  Class consists of no homework, only weekly quizzes.  Drops the lowest grade.  Final was optional.
Lame class. Not helpful, nor approachable. Rarely uses the textbook, nice waste of $100+. Misses class often without informing students. Uses TA to teach often. Lousy.
This professor is extremely knowledgeable and very very funny. He's da man.
He's not someone you want as an enemy, but as long as you do your part, he will make certain you get all the help you need. He's really funny too.
hes scatterbrained and talks about really random things. but it's an easy class
Knows whats he talking about is fair expects you to do the work and treats everyoe Well. If he wasn't married HUMMMMMMM

Very interesting guy. He is smart and knows his stuff for sure. I took this as a pretty random elective, thinking ethics would look good. If your in an IS program this guy would be a good person to have on your side. Not a hard class, can be interesting and Wilson is pretty comical at times. I would advise doing it as a once a week night class.
The class sounded very interesting to me but after sitting through it for a few weeks I had learned nothing. You must teach yourself the material and even the TA was confused.

If you want a class where you get grades back from your teacher, dont take this one.  This professor is bias against student athletes and he picks favorites.  Yes this man is knowledgable but he is rude, concided and never returns e-mails.  Be prepared to work your booty off and get no feedback.

I'm grateful for the privilege of having Prof. Wilson for Philosophy of Religion. He's very enthusiastic about the class and he has a lot of insights on epistemology, God, and morality. Lectures rarely if ever boring. Catch him for additional discussion after class if you're interested, he will like that. Adjunct faculty, can be difficult to reach.
Very good professor. His classes are definatly worth taking.

A great professor and a great guy. Keeps class entertained and the class is more discussion oriented than just lecture. He is one of the best prof. in UMBC and he is really a top professional in his profession. Im glad he still teaches at UMBC, other schools are trying to get him.

GREAT TEACHER!heappreiciateswhenitalkrealfast its not about the class being easy its just that you learn so much in a different way you will def learn in his class, and if you come all the time you'll do good. You just have to take him to know what i mean.DONT LEAVE UMBC WITHOUT taking his class.......
AWSOME PROFESSOR!!!! :):)

He is a very good and laid back professor. He has a very weird sense of humor. There are several quizzes (around 10-13)during the semester - not bad at all.He will drop 2-3 quizzes with the lowest grades. No final! Remember, show up for class. If you miss the class 3 times, he will lower your grade by one. Easy A or B.
get into a good group for the research project. very lenient as long as you do your work. no books needed. great professor
Very good professor although takes very long time to return graded assignments and reply to issues with the class.  Is known to cancel class unexpectedly but a very fun teacher and worth taking.

Intelligent, articulate, and fair. Shows genuine respect for students, even when he disagrees. "Easy" means that if you read the material and think a little, you'll easily be able to develop a viewpoint, engage in debate, and understand a new topic at a deeper level. That's how you make an A. Does it matter whether he's hot? No. (But he is.)

He's a good teacher.  Though the class is early, people rarely fall asleep.  He keeps the class entertaining and he tells you exactly what's going to be on the test.  The tests are very easy, in that they are almost like high school tests.

He is one of the few professors that I have even concidered taking a second class with.  He's a great guy with a sort of dry sense of humor, but occasionally, assuming everyone's awake, the entire class busts out laughing.  The only sure way to piss him off is to skip his class, if you know you're going to miss it, send him an e-mail, or tell a friend in the class to tell him you're sorry you missed it.  If you do that, he'll probably give them an extra copy of whatever for you.  Don't make it a habbit

This man knows his stuff.  he enjoys it when teh students do too!  Read the required material, and listen to his stories about his dog, neighbor, and college years, and it will help you to understand the principle that is taught.  Plus, he makes learning fun.

If you can't get at least a B in this class, something is wrong.  He's kind of awkward, but fun.  Enjoy!
wilson was an odd man, but he made me laugh. he was pretty understanding of the fact that i had the flu for 2 weeks and helped me get ready for the final.
He's a cool teacher. Take his class.
AN EASY A... HE IS SOO EASY..dont buy the book.. he will give u like 4 packets.. and ur straight for the semester... HE'S THE MAN!!!
one of the best professors I had at this school.
He is the man, take this class, you'll like it

This is an easy A.  One of the most laid back teachers ever, he spends a lot of the class talking about himself, making fun of his wife and such.  It's great.  You do end up learning everything you need to in the class as well, so he is a good teacher.  DON'T BUY THE BOOK.

Great teacher, loves the subject and is hilarious. Talks about his dogs all the time and tells great stories that help to understand the subject.Tests are based on quizzes he gives you the answers to.Enjoyable class, should come but at least a "b" if you look at the quizzes.

Wilson is a good proffesor. I never liked Phil but he made quite interesting. When you write your paper make sure that you say something related to what he's talking about in class. The only problem with this class is everyone wants to take his class. He's a gnarly dude. Definitely Recommended!

If you want an easy A, this is the one to take. All his quizzes were almost exact replicas of the ones he posted online. He's a real cool and chill guy;  not hard to approach at all. As for the class itself though, I didn't learn a thing.

Very good and fun professor.  Come to class and try, and u will get a good grade if u do decent on the tests.  easy to talk to and goes off on a tagent almost every day, but some of his stories r funny.  if ur gonna take phil 100, take him no doubt.
Good class. Takes it VERY personally if you dont come to class, but you will do fine if you do. No tests, pretty hard quizzes. Main thing, come to class!

i also had him for phil 100...he's the most sarcastic and conceited person on earth, nevertheless i highly recommend him because 1) his exams are easy, 2) he knows what he's talking about, and 3) his raw sense of humor.
Professor Wilson was one of the best teachers i have EVER had. I wish he could teach all my classes. He is a great guy and i recommend him very highly! Quizzes arent to hard. Take him!
No Comments
Uses a  European  method of teaching, which fits with the material. Fairly hard class, but I learned a lot. Good guy, as well. Likes dogs.
I enjoyed the course and found the quiz method he uses refreshing
Well if its for a requirment, whynot take it.

Dr. Thomas Robinson really blew my mind with how great he was at teaching.  He made the class very fun, and designed it to be a good balance between discussions and lectures.  He grades on essays, exams, assignments, and attendance, which is nice.  Gives great constructive feedback and facilitates the class excellently.  So friendly and kind too.

Dr. Robinson is a great lecturer, a funny person, and an excellent speaker.  He is skilled at talking about difficult and complex subject matter and breaking it down.  His classes tend to be essay and exam heavy, but they are usually relatively easy with clear grading criteria, which helps.  He is super friendly, accommodating, and passionate too.

Love Dr. Robinson! He is retiring but I truly loved every aspect of his course. He taught me so much about myself/life. Classes were more of a conversation than lectures. Go to class ask questions and prepare ahead for the exams/project and you are in good hands. He is nice/hilarious and gave me so much energy. Wishing you the best Dr. Robinson

This class was very simple to pass. I think there were 3 exams and 1 paper. The exams match the study guide and slides that he gives you. I found it easy to study because the information was interesting.  I didn't go to a lot of classes but I still passed. Beware of the in-class videos cause he takes attendance for those.

Dr. Robinson is an ok and kind instructor. Pros: Good lectures, gives study guides. Cons: Does not respond to emails, office hours are by appointment only (which requires students to email). Uploads Blackboard documents in rich text format instead of PDF. Documents have green background.

Dr. Robinson is like a sweet grandpa but don't let his demeanor fool you, he's very sharp and will laugh incredulously when you get the answer wrong to an "easy" question! He's particular in grading but fair.
He is really good professor make sure you study because you will need to for the exams most of the time it class was just a lecture and didnt really have any assignments but 4 exam

reviews.comment: I thought he was a really good professor. He was super nice and a sweet old man like a cute grandpa. His lectures werent too boring so I found it easy to pay attention to them and the tests were easy too. Just take a few minutes to do the practice tests he posts and look at the answers because the questions are exactly the same from the test.

The class is graded by 4 exams, these note cards he passes out as attendance (randomly) and a final paper. The exams are easy. As you take notes in class you won't need to study. He's a nice professor and cares for his students, but his lectures can be a little bit boring. Didn't learn anything amazing, but still an interesting, and easy class.

so you have to come to class because every now and then he hands out these notecards and its for classroom points and I barely went so i dont even know what im getting in the class maybe a c? anyway he gives out like three reg papers but the questions are hard af and really confusing so you have to break down every word. if you can avoid him

DO NOT need the textbook at all, don't buy it. It's an easy A but I was hoping to get more out of it.

Professor Robinson was a good teacher, he made the class very interactive and loved to discuss the viewpoints on the slides. He seemed passionate and knowledgeable about the subject. The only thing is that there's only 4 exams and one research paper used to get a grade, but the exams are easy, all multiple choice, the answers are easy guesses.

Dr. Robinson is the best!!! He is a goofty yet intelligent professor and it really made the class enjoyable. The class is easy too! Attendance is based on note cards given before lecture on random days (there were less than 10) to answer a super easy question. I wish I could take him for every class...

Friendly/chill professor. Likes to tell stories/go off on tangents during the lecture. There is a textbook but you don't need it. Grades are  mainly based off of your 4 exam grades so as long as you thoroughly study the review guide/practice exams, you will do well on the exams. No final, just a final paper. Interesting class

All tests are multiple choice and taken right from the lectures. I didn't have the book and I still got an A. No homework. One paper due at the end of the semester. Gives extra credit points for attendance on random days. He's kind of boring but the material is pretty interesting. Participation isn't mandatory but its helpful to make class fun.
I loved Dr. Robinson. This class was by far one of my favorites. He gives you practice exams that are VERY similar to the test. Simply going to to class and listening will get you an A.

Dr. Robinson  is the most boring professor I have ever had. We didn't do anything in lecture, there was no structure or point to his class. Dated and vague slides, irrelevant and basic movies. I have no idea how he could be rated so high.

Lectures are lively and fun. Professor posts lots of notes on Blackboard which prepare you well if used in combination with textbook. Lectures also help to clarify material. Dr. Robinson is easy to approach if you have any questions or concerns. I highly recommend him for this course.
LOVED Dr. Robinson and the class!  He is funny and intelligent; very easy to get along with !!
Dr. Robinson is one of those professors you will remember.He is very passionate and intelligent. Brings a great sense of humor to class and really helps everyone understand the material.

Dr. Robinson is one of the best professors I have ever had. He is very interested in helping students succeed, and has a deep understanding of Bio-Socio-Cultural aspects of prejudice and racism. If you are interested in gaining insight into psychological aspects of prejudice, stereotyping, and racism, you should take his class.

I love Robinson, he's such a great teacher. He's really intelligent but funny and down to earth when he lectures. AFST/PSYCH 350 was interesting class, and he practically gave exam questions. He emphasises on how the mind and the environment can predispose you to racism but also ways to address it. You leave the class really informed and not angry.
Good for a junior adjunct. Overall good instructor

The weighting of this class is terrible, the final is 40% of your grade and he takes forever to grade and the final and quizzes are on sneaky things he barley goes over. I would avoid this teacher.

Midterm is 30% and final is 40%, but if you do all of the homework, go to office hours, and utilize the resources given, you should be fine.  He also allows a notecard for every quiz, midterm, and final.  Overall, solid choice, good luck!

Genuinely such a kind and caring professor who wants students to succeed. Loves squirrels, his daughter, and discrete mathematics. Passionate about what he teaches and accessible outside of class. Weekly homework and a few quizzes, but if you do well on those you'll do well on the exams. Can't recommend him enough!

Great professor, makes a boring class pretty interesting. He talks a lot about squirrels and brings beanie babies to class. Very cool would recommend. Quizzes are easy enough if you can do the homework.

1 homework a week. Matches exactly what you learn in class some problems being straight from slides. Few quizzes and great practice tools. Worried you'll forget something? Bring an index card with whatever you want to every test, even the FINAL. Lectures are easygoing. Relatable and real, skips stuff you don't need to know and wants you to pass.

One of the best professors I've come across here! His lectures are really good cuz he tries to present the material in a way so that everyone can understand and it really helps! Going to lecture really helps with the hw and exams. Also lets you have a lil card of info to bring with you to exams! Just overall really sweet and wants you to succeed!

He is caring and wants the best for his students. His office hours are very helpful and he gets you through topics that you may be struggling in. The HWs aren't that bad, you just have to pay attention in class and they would be fine. The exams and quizzes are more or less easy if you did all the hws and pay attention in class. Enjoyable class too.

If you're planning on taking cmsc203, take it with this prof! He is an outstanding teacher and has amazing, eazy to digest lectures. Weekly homework that is not strenous at all, keep up with the class and you will be clear!

Professor Rockstroh is a great teacher. Very enthusiastic in lecture and will always be happy to go over certain sections and take questions. Decent amount of homework but nothing overly strenuous. Great instructor. Plenty of experience in the industry, fairly new to teaching. Quickly adopted feedback to become a very good lecturer. I wish I could off myself and i'm only a week in. Do not take this class as a freshman and do work wayyyyy in advance. She does not accept late work at all.

Lecture material really only beneficial for the paper

Dr. Rubin, was a descent professor. Her lectures sometimes can be boring, but you do learn some interesting things in the course. She does give you weekly documents to read they can and will be very long. Be prepared to write some papers, she does give you a guide or rubric  on how to write them. She does give you some time to write the papers.

class is very easy but hard to do well. There are 2 papers, 7 discussion posts a final, and participation. Rubin says she doesn't give 100 on anything so there isn't much margin. Dr. Rubin is a very easy grader. Even though there are a lot of papers, they are easy to understand and gives you around 2 weeks for you to finish it. reviews.comment: Rubin is extremely knowledgeable and enthusiastic about the subject. Only a midterm and final with 2 papers. Go to class and listen carefully to pass. Every other Friday is a discussion OR online paper. Midterm and final are written essays. Highly recommend her if you like history. Good lecturer and answers all questions. She really knows her stuff

I like Rubin because she is loud.  It's almost impossible not to pay attention.  Her passion for 19th century American history will help you in the class.  No mid-term, but you have to do 8/11  weekly discussion board postings, many of which require you to read a whole 300 page book which is just crazy.  Do all of the BB postings to ensure an A

I really liked Dr. Rubin and loved her Civil War class. However, her classes are not easy and she expects alot of of the work you turn in. If you are a weak writer or miss alot of classes, you will not do well in her class. I spent 13 hours on an essay that I thought was AWESOME only to get an 89% on it… and I consider myself a very strong writer.

Dr. Rubin grades essays fairly harshly, and do not expect them back quickly. She is very knowledgeable on the Civil War and if you are interested in the subject you should take her course. If writing is not your strong suit, then it might be more difficult.

Dr.Rubin uses books instead of a textbook, which makes the class more interesting. The lectures were sometimes boring, but for the most part were able to hold attention. The problem with this class was the grading. Essays were graded very harshly and even after having comments saying "good analysis" and then the rubric had points lost on analysis.

I had a great semester in this class. Dr. Rubin is unbelievable. Her knowledge is unparalleled as is her personality. She is willing to meet you half way. That is a very important trait in a teacher. If you're into history, you will absolutely love this class!
Can be scatterbrained at times. PowerPoint lectures are usually good and have interesting links to some really cool stuff.

Dr. Rubin is a good teacher. Her lectures are boring, but her passion about history makes you want to pay attention. Grade consists of a 2 test, and 2 essays which are all easy if you attend class regularly. The TA she had when I took it wasn't very fair in grading and ended up marking down one of my papers because she didnt agree with it.

Her logic didn't seem to make any sense.  She said that Disney's, "Song of the South" movie and the Disney themed ride "Splash Mountain", were racially insensitive.  Thats ridiculous!!!  Far out opinions I would say! Hope you like reading 400 pages per night though!
Class was kinda boring with tons of notes, but the tests were not too difficult if you're good at essays.  She is approachable and understanding.

i took the history of the old south with her and it was so boring.  it should have been the history of slavery.  thats all she talked about.  all the work was easy, but everything was about slavery, not really the south at all.  i was disapointed

I thought Rubin was extremely good, I just had her this semester and she explained everything very clearly, I had no problem with her at all, her lectures were interesting, exams weren't too bad, and papers weren't bad either.  I'd recomend her, she makes history fun!

Dr. Rubin is a tough teacher.  I worked my butt off and got a B.  She is very interesting to listen to and her classes go by really fast.  She is very nice and approachable and likes to chat with her students.  Overall good prof. but she requires A TON of reading... A TON.

Rubin was extremely nice and so easy to talk to.  Her class isn't that interesting in itself, but her enthusiasm for her topics definitely helps getting the class interested. Many debates and discussions helped the class stay awake. If you work hard, you'll definitely get that A.

What a GREAT class, and a GREAT prof.! Dr. Rubin is very funny, outgoing, and makes the Civil War fun. She really knows her stuff and isn't afraid to to help. TAKE HER!!! I'm not normally a UMBC student; I go to TU and came to take the class this semsester because of Dr. Rubin!
I had Dr. Rubin for Hist 101... she is a great teacher and also a great person.. but too much reading and we had to write 2 7-page paper...hmm.

Excellent teacher!  She uses a variety of material inside of class as well as outside of class.  I didn't like the books....but over all I gained a new perspective.  Good class if you like discussion and a new outlook!
Dr Rubin is not only a great professor, but she is also a great person.  I plan on taking classes with her again, and I'm not even a History major!

Dr. Rubin is a great professor!  She was my professor for HIST 101, 419, and 421.  Not only is she friendly and knowledgeable, she is also very helpful to students.  While her classes are very instructional, it has a relaxed atmosphere that a lot of other
Interesting class. She really knows what she is talking about.
There's a lot of reading (some books aren't provided) and papers to write. Honestly a great professor and engages the class in discussion.

reviews.comment: During COVID, this prof was pretty forgiving. Hefty amount of reading, but grades papers mostly based on completion. Just do all the work and you'll be fine. She was super pleasant and her lectures were engaging.

Excellent professor. Easy as long as you do the work and participate in class discussions. Response essays are easy, approx 1-3 pages in length. Only one assignment given per week. Makes it easy to manage, especially if you have other classes to handle.

As long as you read some of the book and participate, you'll be fine. She gives great lectures and the info from this women studies class is really interesting to learn

Professor Rudacille is great, she knows a lot about Journalism and the changing world of Journalism. If you have ever been interested in the field or curious about how to write in AP style, take this professor.

She has some strange guidelines for what she wants changed about papers, things that boil down to personal choice and tonality. Isn't too strict about people doing readings or not, but again, weird requirements for the phrasing of certain things. If you do what she wants, she'll give you a good grade.

This is a visiting professor. I have had Professor Rudacille for two classes so far. She is very nice and provides interesting class discussions. Professor Rudacille can tend to be picky about word choice and language. Do all of the readings and write concisely. Do not take with the expectation of an easy A.

Prof. Cain was passionate about this class and realistic about usefulness/difficulty of different topics. He made it clear what would be on exams. As he advises, make a doc with vocab, diagrams, and examples before each exam. Lots of questions, not a lot of time. HW was pretty easy, the math can be confusing so pay attention to details.

Weekly homeworks, but they aren't too tricky. Highlights material on exam on his slides. Tends to rush through his lectures sometimes but definitely knows his stuff. Online exams are great, and sometimes he brings candy, a great choice for the class. Doesn't announce when he's taking attendance a goo portion of the time though.
