reviews.comment: I like that he typically ends class early. Tries his best to keep class entertaining by bringing candy/demos to class. Super chill and strongly recommend! Online exams are easily the best part of this course :3

The work is easy except for 3 HWs, and his grading is vague but pretty fair. Exams were open note and online so that is good. If you want to take it id say go for it, but it's not a class you can just put on the back burner to boost your GPA, it does take a bit of effort. He's hard to reach by email, and the TAs grade via dart boards apparently too

Great professor. Computer architecture class is designed for computer science students and is not needlessly hard. You can get an A in this class if you spend an hour and a half a week outside of class doing hw and studying.

Excellent professor overall. Good lecturer, usually finished early too. One (usually very easy) homework per week, 2 tests, and a final. The lowest HW grade was dropped. Tests were on Blackboard and open book/notes with a few extra credit questions.

Rambles during lectures while quickly going through the slides, exams will contain a few things he didnt teach, exam grades are inconsistent. If you ask him to reconsider a grade he gave on one of the exam problems, he will say "I have the right to regrade the entire test!", implying he will give an even lower one.
No projects, nothing interesting.

Cain was an interesting professor, overall I personally don't like this subject so the class was difficult for me.  Cain had interesting lectures, homework is a majority of your grade so make sure you do them.  He expresses what the exams are emphasized on.  He's really caring and considerate with grading.

Cain is a really good professor! He really cares about teaching, and he tries to make boring topics seem fun. His exams are based on his lectures, so be sure to review them before a test. Cain is a fair grader, and gives partial credit where it is due. He also is good at reviewing tougher concepts and is understanding of all the students' needs.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy--Caring

reviews.comment: Russ Cain is hard, but fair. If you study the important parts of the lecture, there's not much reason you shouldn't get an A or a B. Homeworks are light (save one), and they do not take much time to do. There are curves if people do bad, and the grading is fair on the exams. You can tell Russ Cain is an expert in his field.

Cain was great. Cain got a webcam to use to demonstrate ideas in class and was very specific about what would be on the test. The test itself was long, open note open internet and I needed the full time but I thought it was more than fair. Would take again.

Pretty easy class for 411. HW fairly easy very little coding. He only focuses on basics no cmpe. Tests mostly defining words he tells you on review day and labeling cpu based on what he gives. Lectures are pretty decent but not exceptional. Pretty easy on grading. Class could have been a whole lot worse. Recommend taking him if you can over others.

Group-oriented class with large semester-long project and a presentation at the end. Professor is energetic. Not always clear, but definitely knowledgeable. The only true bad thing about this is the entire project is graded at the end of the semester so you really won't know how you are doing until then.
Good professor, expert in his field so knows what's really important and isn't that hard on you if you show effort and are a good student. Tests are basically just the review

Hilarious guy. He makes his lectures more entertaining by relating the subject matter to what he does at work, and by explaining how we would use it in real life. Homework isn't too bad, the group project was challenging, but not impossible, and the midterm and final were challenging.
cool professor, very knowledgeable in the field and shows it in class. merciful when grading and knows he makes mistakes

Cain does not explain his expectations for assignments, and then picks very arbitrary, specific things to look for when grading. He often makes mistakes in his lectures, and when he cannot figure something out, mumbles his way through it (but he'll expect you to be able to do it on exams). This professor does not want you to succeed.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Really interesting prof, but isn't clear on grading and does not communicate well with his TA. Midterm was very very hard and the final was only a little better. Not super clear on what he expects you to learn or know for the final. Reading the book saved me so many times so absolutely get it! Definitely wold be easier with another professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: It can be hard not to doze off sometimes, but you need to stay awake cuz he will  talk about projects in his slides and sometimes provide very valuable snippets of code.  He will also bring stuff to class to show us what he has been talking about in lectures.  The class is boring but he does his best to keep everyone interested and says jokes often

This class was pretty easy - didn't learn much that I hadn't already learned in CMSC 313. Weekly homework assignments that could be done quickly. Midterm and final were a large percentage of the grade, so make sure you study. He also decides to take attendance on random days but I don't know if that ever factored into the final grade.

Very nice and funny guy. Lectures are boring, but thats just because of the course content. I'd definitely take 411 with him over the other professors, because he understands CS people aren't going to use much of the stuff typically taught in this class. Tests and homeworks are pretty easy

You can easily ace the first exam solely on his slides. But the second half of the course will require you to do some textbook reading. Check out the book for solving problems involving the topics of cache, pipelining, and multicore processing.  His lectures will often involve fabulous stories of career experiences as an engineer.

Cain is a fun professor, but he does not explain a lot of tough material adequately. He tends to graze over everything and finish early. Ask questions if you don't understand. Takes attendance. He is probably the best professor for the course.

Dr. Robucci was very reasonable with what he taught vs what was tested. The projects were not too difficult and were definitely manageable. Overall his class was pretty straight forward, if you show up and pay attention and you'll be fine. Hes an interesting guy lol and sometimes got off track. But Ive heard better things about Dr. Farrel though.
The worst!!!!!

I recorded watched his lectures every night. If you do that and watch them like a movie you'll do great. I don't know why there are so many negative reviews. He really knows his stuff and is clearly passionate about teaching. Probably one of the most chill down to earth teachers i had while attending. If you can take a class with him, DO IT!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: This professor doesn't really care about his students, makes comments such as "yea you'll get a B, whatever." He should just stick to the lab cause he obviously lacks social skills. He doesn't care about students or teaching, he should stick to being in the lab.

This man is the most unclear, disorganized professor I've come across in the CMPE major. The exams are unfair and have tons of errors in them. The projects were tough, but not impossible. He knows a lot, has a clear passion for this stuff, and usually tries to help, but it doesn't seem to translate very well into teaching ability.
much homework including computer simulation which overwhelmed me
No Comments
Take Him

Nice
Great

Great Professor

extremely boring but the class is not too hard.3 problem sets and 3 exams. Problem sets are graded for completion. Also one group presentation that is super easy. Hardest part is the exams. Final exam was way harder than the rest of the exams randomly First exam is super easy I got a 97 but I recommend reading the textbook if you want an A
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I was given a highly unexpected low grade on an assignment that had unclear instructions. Grade weighting is also not very good.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This professor prepares students well for Econ 102. Everything that you learn in this class, you will be able to apply in macroeconomics. He is a good professor.

Dr. Kearn is a very informative professor. It's best if you take the time and effort to listen to his words during lecture, then go back and study the individual slides outside class. The exams and problem sets are currently mostly all the credit sources. Do the readings and problem sets; you'll be fine, provided you pay attention.

Only two exams plus the final. No quizzes. Each exam is 20 questions and the final is worth 50 points. Lecture's are full of information and content so make sure to attend them. He explains things in a way that makes them easier to understand. We had practice problem sets to do every unit/chapter that helped prepare us for the exams and were graded

This professor knows what economics very well. He encourages people to ask questions since the concepts can seem confusing at times and will clear them up on the spot. Show up to class, participate, do all of the problem sets, and study your lecture notes. Overall a good class.

Prof. Kearns is a great professor because he sincerely respects students and conveys this helping caring, attitude. When the class does not understand an economic concept, he will try and rephrase it in a clearer and concise way. He also points out the contrasts and implications of various economic theories and principles.

Professor Kearns is honestly one of the best professors that I have had at this school. Econ 101 is not an easy class however if you truly put the effort into studying the material and attend office hours, you will pass. Also, pay attention to the lecture notes and problem sets.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring

reviews.comment: Kearns is a solid choice. The lectures were uneventful but with a subject like economics, that's expected. There isn't too much graded work so make sure to do the Problem Sets on time. The class isn't "hard" but will exams will require some time studying beforehand.

Ryan Kearns is a pretty chill guy and definitely knows what he is taking about. His lectures are pretty boring but microeconomics itself isn't that fun so. He gives a set of homework problems about every week and his exams are pretty similar to those. Expect to do a bit of reading and studying outside of lecture, but overall good class.
He's so interesting... visually and intellectually. Like he is so easy on the eyes and the class was so interesting. So easy too.

Take him as a teacher. Will send you notes when you skip classes. The exams are starightforward and he makes everything easy to learn. Dude is a great teacher and a standup guy. Easy A if you study for his exams.

Alright so Mutter is a good professor, he does know his stuff. However his class is TERRIBLY boring. I have him once a week from 7-10pm. He does not let you out a minute early. I usually have about 10-15 pages of notes at the end of every class. He likes to talk about himself and his job. Nice guy, kinda odd. Always available if you need help.

Prof. Mutter knows his stuff and is great at teaching. If you need an upper level Econ class, I'd highly recommend this one. It's relatively easy, all you need to do is attend class and take his notes. I did, and I never needed to touch the book. His tests are very easy and straightforward even if he curves slightly downward. Take this class,easy A

He is a great and nice teacher. The class isn't that bad and I am not even an econ major. He makes everything clear, easy and gives extra credit on the exam. The exams have ALOT OF GRAPH questions. If you come to class everyday and study of your notes you will be FINE. Exam is from your NOTES! And If you miss class, he'll even send you class notes.

Dr. Ryan is a great teacher. He is clear and a light grader. His tests are not too hard, either. Everything is DIRECTLY from his notes and the book. Just read the notes and book, and you will get an easy A in the class.

Mutter is an okay teacher, but the class is horribly boring. I had it at night, and it was all I could do to stay awake the whole time. He never lets you out early either. He's nice, but a little weird, and he rambles on about his day job also. You don't need the book, your notes should be okay if you go every time.

TAKE THIS CLASS. It is super easy plus he is amazing. At first you think he is different. Yet when you go to class you can't wait till next class. 4 grades no papers, but go to class everything is thought in class. Book should be skimmed once in a while if confused.

Super cool, young professor. Kinda looks like a young Matt Dylan. He is a real world economist so he not only knows his stuff but he uses real life economic examples to explain things. Just study his notes as he tests you exclusively on those. The only negative is that you never get out of class early but he even apologized for that! Awesome teach!

Professor is very nice. Gives some extra credit. If everyone is doing bad, he makes some of the questions in the exam extra points. You need to read the book aside from his notes to get an A. The exams are not that difficult. Make sure you study from his notes because the exam questions are from his notes. He explains thoroughly and is very nice.

Lectures aren't too boring but there are a LOT of notes to take so you MUST go to class. Overall an easy class except his exams are very traditional and LONG: averaging 10 pages of questions that includes multiple choice, free response, and apply your knowledge/mathematic problems with charts. and the book is recommended but not really needed

If you get the chance, take econ101 with this professor.  3 exams and a final, and a couple different extra credit opportunities.  If he is going too fast, he doesn't mind slowing down to re-explain somethings.  The exams are mostly based off lectures, but you need to read for the A.

Immersed in real world of economics as a health economist.  Organized with high density for useful information lectures.  I like how he appears non-judgemental.  Answers goofy questions with poise and seriousness--easy to ask questions.  No preaching, no sarcasm, just plain economics.  Very nice young professor, graduate of UMBC.

Dr. Mutter is the most energetic, easy going, and fun professor you will ever have yet at the same time very knowledgable, approachable and fair. He's passionate about many things in life...one being economics. He looks about 23 or 24 yrs old but since he is a Dr. he is probably 25/26. Sorry ladies. I think he's taken. Admire from a distance.

One of the best professors. Very nice and an easy grader. This class is a research writing course, you should work independently in the class. HW is due almost every day but if you start early it's not that bad. If you follow the rubric and participate in the class you will be fine. Make sure methods, results and summaries are to the point.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Professor Bill Ryan is an awesome, understanding guy. Work is made up of discussion posts, and a few homework (article reviews), make sure to write a lot, three tests, and a group project where you interview a manager. We did a Kahoot on class content which was fun.

Easy material, good guy. Pre-covid the tests were mc and essentially definitions from the tb. Post-covid, the tests were essay format and super long and time consuming. The class itself is lectures and discussions with small paragraph hw assignments after EVERY class. Keep up on both & you'll be fine. His lectures are boring tho so beware of that.

Prof. Ryan is very nice and cares for his students. This class requires students' participation and group works. There is a lot of homework, but those are fairly easy, and a total of three exams. If you are an independent learner and fine with studying with a textbook, you will be fine in this class.

Professor Ryan is one of the best I've had. He's not demanding with class participation other than signing in, gives insightful answers, and demonstrates effort to understand at least some students. Readings will take you time to split up. Exams are all skill, no luck. If his course was a company, I'd want the job desperately. Effort+TimeA+
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Caring

reviews.comment: Very good caring professor. Very quick, detailed feedback. Genuinely cares.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: He's a nice guy, but a lot of tedious papers and article reviews. This course truly is writing INTENSIVE. He is pretty lenient on due dates, but be sure to have any major projects submitted on time. Don't panic if you receive a bad grade in the first half of the semester, you're writing will improve and so will your grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--SO MANY PAPERS

reviews.comment: Useless lectures. He uses first a few minutes of 75-minute class to explain what to do, and then you do what he tells you. You don't benefit anything from the class. He gives homework assignment almost every day, and expects you to finish the same day. The class is easy to pass, but we can find articles online and write about them ourselves too..
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--SO MANY PAPERS

reviews.comment: This was one of the worst classes i have ever taken. my friend told me it was and easy class but turned out to berreally hard
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Professor Ryan as a person is good but not the best professor. He is very vague in what he want from presentation.
Very good IS teacher, knows about his material, very up to date with current technology. Great teacher.
Great professor really chill. Just make sure you get the book and do the homework. Tests are really easy, straight forward lectures.

Literally one of the best professors ever! Wish I could have him for every IS class lol. He is one of my favorite professors and is so understanding towards students. Replies fast by email and is a great person to chat with. Just did not like the 8:30 am timing but was worth it because he is awesome. Love this guy

Pretty much the best professor I have had for an IS class. He is lenient and understanding as long as you give him a notice ahead of time. Papers weren't too tough, but a bit tedious. Quizzes are based on the assignments done in class. Go to class, the attendance will help at the end of the semester.
i'm short of words for this teacher. He is the best professor ever i have ever had at UMBC. Take him and you will never regret taking his class.
best writing professor you can take at UMBC 2 quizzes, 3 article reviewspresentations, and several little assignments but everything high school level difficulty

Exam questions are almost straight from his exam reviews, always posts powerpoint notes ahead of time on blackboard, group project is super easy, fun, and creative. Just make sure to do the online homeworks due by midnight, they aren't crucial for your grade, but will definitely rack up points on your final grade if you mess up on the exams.

He is a great professor, and this is the easiest writing intensive course you can take. there are several papers but none are very difficult. and he is not too critical of grammar or anything. mostly presentations.

This class was great. It was a super easy writing intensive. Literally, as long as you come to class and do the work you will do very well because he grades easier than most professors. Plus the assignments are really easy. He's a good guy and he enjoys talking about IT literature.

easy professor he gives you the notes for the test and you do a group project. your grade is based on points you earned on a scale of 0 to 500. come to class because participation is 20 points. Also, his test are easy because it all multiple choice and 3 written response which are easy.  homework is easy too. best professor ever for management

Very easy class. Be prepared to read a lot of scholarly article as this is primarily what you will be doing throughout the course of the class. Avoid skipping class. There are due almost every class, so you'll miss a lot if you skip class too much. Good professor.

His instructions, expectations, and assignments are all unclear. Difficult to get a hold of outside of class. His emails are unhelpful. Told the class that the text edition does not matter but it did. Kept the entire class 30 minutes pass the official class end time. Did not lecture on half of textbook material yet we had to use it on group project

Class was pretty easy and he didn't seem to mind having fun in class.  I had many problems communicating with him through email and trying to get clarification on assignments which absolutely effected my end grade.  Easy class, easy material but not exactly an easy A.
the class was supposed to be hybrid and we only had 2 online classes. The textbook was required, but un-necessary. Overall good class. One of the best prof's at UMBC. Easy A.

This was the first education course and I didn't really like it. A lot of others did. He seemed artificially nice. Like, he was only nice because it was his job and he was being paid to be there. Also, didn't seem very interested in the subject matter. I'd say the class was relatively easy.. not too easy but not bad either.

He doesn't upload ppts so you have to go to class. I spent all my time trying to take notes verbatim rather than absorbing the material and was left with sloppy, incomplete notes to review. Your grade comes from exams that each have 5 questions and the content is a crapshoot. He was most helpful outside of class.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Good professor. I found him a little hard to follow during class but very clear during office hours. He's fairly straightforward about what's going to be on exams.

Dr. White's lectures are well-prepared and focus on exactly what he expects you to know for the exam. His grading is fair and he is always available to answer questions or give extra help. Great professor! Loved analytical chemistry because of him.

First time I took this class I, my grade was 'F' (not this prof), Second time i took this class was with Prof. White. He is very engaging, and willing to help. He definitely knows what he is talking about. His exams are easy if you can work every question he gives in class on your own, go to his office hours, and exam review. Plus he is HOT!!

This class was honestly frustrating. The lectures were often hard to follow, and instead of clarifying things, the professor would sometimes come across as passive-aggressive when students asked questions, which made it uncomfortable to participate. It felt like asking for help was discouraged, so I ended up having to teach myself everything.

The classroom environment did not feel supportive at all. The professor was often passive-aggressive and maintained a very strict demeanor that made it uncomfortable. Lectures involved sudden changes in tone or raised voice which made the environment stressful rather than welcoming. The class atmosphere was unnecessarily tense and anxiety-inducing
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Group projects

reviews.comment: Even the TAs couldn't answer some the the vague final project rubric. Passive-aggressive hatred for any generation younger than him and constantly bring it up in lecturing. He raise his voice suddenly trying to keep class attention & sudden yelling might cause panic attacks. His micro aggressions and racist remarks were unpleasant to say the least

Great Professor but the class is hard for no reason. Weekly papers, semester project, three hand written exams which are heavily graded. As interesting as the subject is, it could be much simpler like the other sections

THE best professor I've ever had. Very lecture heavy, and will make sure you don't have a phone in sight, but his lectures are very well done and it's easy to follow. Recommends taking hand notes, but not mandatory. Weekly group (2 or 3 people) assignments, but fairly easy to do. I would 100 percent recommend taking any of his classes!

Professor Sy is a super great guy with engaging lectures. you can tell he is passionate about management. There was a lecture on Tuesday with a quiz due the next day, and a lab assignment you do on thursday with a partner due on sunday. beware, he teaches a lot of content and might be more difficult than other mgmt210 classes, but great professor.

Lectures were entertaining, taking notes was valuable. I had underestimated the first exam, and it killed my chances of an A, although if you go through the study guide well and do the work, this is a solid class. The textbook is a little long and boring but if you ever have to miss lecture, it is a good go-to. Attendance was mandatory.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Graded by few things

reviews.comment: One of the best lecturers at UMBC! Attendance is important for your grade, so make sure you show up to every class!

He's a very nice professor with good, weekly lectures. Taking notes is crucial as there's two exams that each cover half of the class, so it's a lot to study. There are weekly partner assignments and an interview a manager final partner project. The exams are so heavy that my chance of getting an A was pretty much out the window.

Prof. Saulynas is an amazing lecturer, he finds ways to make the lecture engaging and entertaining. As someone who gets distracted easily, it was nice to be able to stay attentive all class. Midterm and final are worth a good chunk so STUDY!! He's very strict on attendance so do not skip OR be late!!! Besides that class is easy :)

(Easy) weekly assignments and quizzes, a final project, a midterm, and a final exam. The project and weekly assignments are partnered. Attendance GRADED AND MANDATORY. The class is manageable and not too hard, just put minimal effort and youll be fine. Overall pretty easy and would take again. Prof Saulynas is very pleasant to work with.

You should take Prof. S. He is enthusiastic about the material in a good way. Class is essentially lecture (Take notes, makes life easy), a quiz (entirely based off notes) and a lab assignment every week with a partner (find a good one). The midterm was fair, and study guide provided was good. Show up, take notes, do the work, and an A is possible.

Professor Saulynas is a great Professor! He explains his lectures in a fun way that you would understand. All you need to do take notes, read the textbook, and study. Plus, his Quizes is online.  If you this, it would be an easy A for you.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Group projects

reviews.comment: Great professor. He is genuinely interested in the material and he ensures that his students remain interested in the course by holding interactive learning sessions one day a week.  Attendance counts for participation, so go to class.  There is no textbook, just readings provided by him. Go to class, study, and you'll do fine.

Class is more about implementatin of real project ideas which makes the learning experience very practical. You have to deal with JIRA and github which is good i guess.Professor is supportive and approachable but attendance is mandatory. Documentation throughout the project helps to understand how professional software development processes work.

This class is 90% documents 10% actually working on the project. The documents are long and take forever. There is a total of 9 documents done by the end of the semester. The project is just you learning to build something on your own without him teaching really anything. You get experience with Jira which is good ig.

This course is quite challenging and moves at a steady, fast pace. It requires strong time management and consistent effort, but it can also be a valuable learning experience. Professor encourages student participation to keep the class engaging. Someone who enjoy a focused, academically rigorous environment may find this course rewarding.

Take this with any other professor. He will give you, in his words, "a year's worth of work in 4 months". He treats the class like a full-time job and will overwork you to death. His lectures are painfully boring, and he yells the content at you. When he doesn't feel people are participating, he'll randomly call on people. 0/10 do not recommend

Samit is the okayest professor ever, class is somewhat disorganized. Lectures are unhelpful other than for studying for the few tests. but fairly easy, most grades are completion, Getting a good grade is not hard.

This class is fairly time consuming, most of the grade comes from all the software documentation, not the software itself.

Professor Samit is an excellent instructor and a genuinely kind person. His project-based approach provides valuable real-world experience, and he goes above and beyond to manage stakeholder interactions for each team.

Professor Samit gives of the vibe that he loosely read his own syllabus for like 5 minutes then walks into class freestyling off of his slides. Due dates are an enigma, it feels like we find out about assignments when he does. His slides are not very good for independent study but are not as bad as his lectures where he yells vague concepts at you.

He's a really nice professor and cares about students, which makes the class feel welcoming. The lectures are interesting, but sometimes move too quickly or repeat material. Grading and attendance were fair, though a bit more consistency and clarity would help.

He is a very nice person, but the lectures were frustrating. He is very disorganized with grading and assignments, including attendance, where he only chose a few days to check. He makes popcorn calls when he feels no one is listening. He goes over too much material, and it can get redundant. Personal pet peeve: he sort of yells the info at you.

I took this course with him two semesters ago. The live coding during class helped reinforce the topics. While every student learns differently, I appreciated how he supplemented his lectures with support on homework and coding assignments.  He encouraged students to understand the logic rather than just memorize syntax.

Don't take him for 201 and go to a different prof lecture if necessary. He didn't have any class content prepared and would write random code on the board without explaining what we were learning. Had to reference other professors' course content to understand topics discussed in class.

Absolutely take this course !! Instructor values students' time. Group project is the key to learn Github, JIRA . Learning opportunity about how to effectively use JIRA for task management, sprint planning, and issue tracking in this course can give you a significant advantage in demonstrating your project management and collaboration skills.

DO NOT TAKE. Will force you to download malware for his tests that he refuses to let you take in any rational way. Writes nothing down, and has little understanding of what's going on around him and does not respect your time. Take ANYONE else. You will learn nothing and experience only irritation taking his "course."

DONT LISTEN TO THE NEGATIVE FEEDBACKS REGARDING THIS PROFESSOR. Professor Shivadekar is one of the best professors out there. He genuinely cares about his students and makes learning easy. His teaching style is clear, and he's always available to help. If you have the chance to take his class, you'll be in great hands!

This professor is massively underrated. Don't understand the hate he gets. His explanations of the concepts are very thorough and gives fantastic code break-downs and examples in class. Provides all resources for exams. He responds to emails within minutes. My favorite comp sci teacher I've had so far in my life. Prior coding experience helps tho.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: His lectures aren't really helpful, but attendance isn't mandatory. He's kind of rude that if someone asks him a question, he'll make a face like, why are u so stupid or say, "I don't understand what you're saying". So, he's really not helpful and this class itself is pretty hard so go for a teacher who's caring and actually has helpful lectures.

For CMSC 447, the class structure, based on other professors I have spoken to, should be, and often is very practical as it revolves around a semester-long group project. This professor has severe control issues, and tries his best to make a potentially fun class insufferable. He has changed the syllabus several times, and is rude to the nice TA.

He is attentive to student feedback and implements changes to enhance their learning experience. While the course may be a bit disorganized, he takes steps to help students balance it with their other responsibilities.

The most unprofessional professor I've ever encountered. When asked to revise the syllabus to include pop quizzes, he accused multiple students of not attending class. Indecisive and too many assignments combined with a tight schedule. Bare minimum amount of thought put into class planning. Extremely stressful for no meaningful reason. Avoid him.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Lots of homework--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: He will give time to students and ask their opinion. Project is easy going and fun.
"Ask the TA" is Samit's favorite saying. Asked him for help on a group project and he just said "Ask the TA". Poor teacher, unclear instructions, and nothing more than a waste of time. Avoid him.
He is nice professor. Easy going. He helps you in your projects and HomeWorks too. Projects are important in this course. His teaching style is good as well. He goes step by step.

Went to the first two lectures and never showed up to another one after that. I just didn't like his teaching style to be honest. I never did it but I know some kids who went to the other professor's lectures, if that is the case, you might as well just take him instead.
He is easy professor. He debugs the code in the class and shows step by step execution of the code properly.For HomeWorks and project related questions, he solved all my doubts.
Professor is very kind and very flexible. You can go ask anything and he will help you.

Very strict when it comes to grading. Definitely a language barrier, not a very good explainer/skips too many steps. Jumps from topic to topic very fast without much explanation. Homeworks/tasks are very hard. Nice person though. That is about it.

reviews.comment: It was a hard class but professor Carmody is a very nice and caring professor. he is great at teaching. You just have to study hard and complete all the homework assignments. He is also very lenient!
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: If you are taking Spanish at UMBC, make sure you enroll in his class. He is a very reasonable person and is a student himself so he is very lenient about things! I wish I took him in Spanish 101 & 102. I always got a B in those classes because the professors wanted perfection. Sean Carmody understands you're learning so he's not harsh at grading!

I only rate when Profs. are either amazing or terrible. Carmody is by far the best 201 Prof. A language course is intimidating, but he is a non-native Spanish Prof. who is very lenient throughout the course. Lots of online homework, but do all of them & you will pass. 2 major exams but he prepares you well. 3-4 Group Projects to keep your grade up.
Prof, Carmody is very patient with everyone, easy to reach. The textbook and homework is online, I hated that part, but Prof. Carmody offers opportunities for extra credit.

The best foreign language teacher on campus, bar none. Professor Carmody really cares about his students and will do everything in his power to make sure you at least get a 'C'. Three easy group projects, homework that has a check work function, two tests but many extra credit opportunities. He's always available for office hours if you need help.
The most annoying thing about this class is that we had four group projects. Sean Carmody is a super lax grader though. As long as you do all the homework assignments youll be okay.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Group projects--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Take Professor Carmody's class if you want to pass Spanish 201 with a good grade. The best Spanish professor at UMBC. He is very understanding and can actually teach Spanish. English is his first language so he knows how to teach Spanish. Makes sure you do all of your work and you will pass this class.
He has no organization what so ever... kinda seems like he's winging it. His due dates are a little everywhere and are really hard to keep track of. Not a fan.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: I do not like speaking Spanish, but it seems like the most relevant language to learn so I took Spanish 101 and 201 with Professor Carmody (who is VERY cute). He is very fair with tests and grades. Make sure to participate in class and always have your textbook.

Professor Carmody is great. He's always there to answer questions and to help you along the course. He is also forgiving. If you weren't able to submit an assignment online by the due date, he usually is very lenient about it. However, obviously, do not make it a habit. He is very approachable, patient, never gets angry, so please take him.

Prof. Carmody is a good teacher. 201 was the first Spanish class I've taken since my sophomore year of high school and I didn't have much of a problem. Pay attention in class and do the activities he gives out, and you'll learn fairly quickly. Lots of homework, but it's pretty easy overall. Tests were fair, he makes it clear what will be on them.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Participation matters--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: Prof. Carmody is a great teacher. He likes to make jokes and makes it easy to learn. If you miss class, he's good about letting you make up work. The calendar of assignments can be confusing, just make sure to remember your grade depends on the group work. He is a bit disorganized with due dates so just ask him if he's not clear.

He does not design this course and is therefore not responsible for that mess. However, does a good job with what the department makes him teach. You basically teach yourself Spanish from a book in this class which can be super challenging.  Wish UMBC would use the communicative approach to Spanish.

Super nice guy. Lots of good stories. He knows the language well. Isn't the best teacher.. he'll answer specific questions when you ask, but teaches straight out of the book with no further elaboration. Doesn't respond to e-mails, seems too busy to teach. REALLY easy on the eyes.

Carmody is super cool! Fun guy and very into Spanish. He isn't very good at reminding you about due dates so be sure to stay on top of everything. He is a little fast paced. I think sometimes he forgets we don't speak Spanish, but he is very helpful when you ask questions.

Friendly professor and easy to talk to but he does not explain anything or actually teach you. Everything you learn is right out of the book. Never remembers due dates and hardly responds to emails.  Cool professor but not a great teacher

You read straight for the book, and do all the activities from the book. He is funny and entertaining, but not as helpful as I wish he could have been. he gets confused about his own assignments. 2 online homeworks a week, 2 oral exams, tests/quizzes weren't too difficult,  2 chats that were easy. Good amount of work, not hard, just time consuming

His classwork/homework outline is very confusing and when you ask him questions about due date or details he never knows. He does not explain things in class or teach really. All we do is all of the book work with partners and he does not elaborate on the answers when we go over them. He's always lost or confused about his own classwork/homework
The class was always fun because of the way he interacted with the students, he is easy to approach and tries his best to help you stay on track. His tests and  exams were easy.

Very good professor! He is very flexible and is aware that not everyone is a professional when it comes to speaking spanish. As long as your try he pretty much passes you. His exams and quizes are not a surprise. Everything he teaches you are on them. I would def recommend taking him. Easy passing grade. I am not good at spanish so glad i took him.
I took this class about two years ago, best professor there so far. Chill, upbeat, and knowledgeable of Spanish language and culture (his wife is hispanic/latina. Great prof, would highly recommend!

Wow. Only way to describe, if not the best teacher here, definitely one of them. Outlines what's going to be on quizzes/exams. Let's you ask translations during exams if it's not directly related to material. ONLY complaint is the grading. His lack of TA makes you get things back very late. Other than that, couldn't be better. TAKE HIS CLASS!!!!!!!

More work than I was expecting but a fairly easy A. Easy to focus in class, he's upbeat and relatable. Very helpful. Work consists of 5 quias, 3 chats, and 2 responses online (all outside class) and 6 quizes, 2 writing exams, 2 oral exams, and 2 cummalitive exams (all in class)
Great teacher. Easy going,nice, interested in students learning.  I would take him again.
Please take this guy, he is so chill and down to earth, an excellent instructor, and an all around excellent teacher!
Sean is the best

He is very helpful and nice. His class isn't hard and his test are okay. The hardest part of the exams are the listening section but he replays them as much as you need. Very approachable and understanding. One of my favorite professors.

He is very helpful and easy going. The 1st few weeks he will speak in english, after that its str8 spanish and he has no problems explaining or answering Q's, so dont hesitate. All in all, he's very approachable, easy going, and very helpful if you ask. His assignments are fairly ez as well. Great Spanish teacher!
Really nice guy and great teacher. Not strict at all and is understanding if you say things wrong or give incorrect responses.

Awesome professor. He's really friendly and approachable--one of the best in the department. He's an overall nice guy who has a great sense of humor and loves to teach. Prof. Carmody's youth is definitely an asset because he relates well to the students. Take his class! You won't regret it!
This guy is a boss. He will help students and give extra credit, even though he says he won't at the beginning of class. A teacher you MUST take if your learning spanish.
Awesome and friendly. Best Spanish teacher I had.

One of the best professors I've ever had. He speaks fluent Spanish and does a great job in teaching it. He relates to the students and will not hesitate to help anyone that doesn't understand the material. An effective teacher that is easy to talk to. Highly recommended.

An awesome professor. He's super laid back but effective, though it's an introductory class he uses spanish 98% of the time. But he always makes sure that we understand, and tries to help us. He's also pretty funny and easy on the eyes. I definitely recommend him. One thing; he's strict about no phones.

He made learning Spanish seem effortless. After the first couple of chapters he will stop using English all together, but if you don't understand and ask what he's saying, he'll draw on the board or make gestures to try and help you understand.  Awesome teacher, definitely recommend.

Great proff.  he loves spanish and trys to make it fun in every class. the only problem is that on quiz/test he will give u points off if u spell stuff wrong. so make sure u practice spelling the words. and study vocab. rest is easy.
Wonderful mentor and professor.
She is one of the best instructors I ever had.  She cared about the students and was an easy rater.  I don't know how anyone could fail the tests.
I enjoyed her class - serious students do well.  This wasn't an easy A!
I could not stand this professor. She was the worst I've had at UMBC. She sat the entire time, read from the text and hardly engaged with her students. DO NOT take her class. Awful

Even if you wanted to go to class and pay attention, it wouldn't be possible, because she just sits in her chair and lectures straight from the book. She is also a harsher grader than is fair based on how horrible a teacher she is.

Boring!!!!! Can't hear most of what you say. Literally teaches from the book, word for word. If you only go to class on test days, just read the books and watch the movies, and you can do really good. I don't wanna take her other class if I can avoid it, and Judaic Studies courses usually are my favorite classes.

Sometimes go through the material quickly, but he explains the material very well and is always open to questions. He seems to genuinely want his students to succeed, always willing to help and sometimes even give second chances to improve. Highly recommend, don't hesitate to communicate when help is needed and you will do well in the class.
This online course is extremely polished and practically impossible to get a bad grade in. I'd be happy to take a class with Dr. Siu again.
Very knowledgeable about music theory. Overall, easy class if you pay attention and do the work.

First things first, the man is hysterical! This guy has a real sense'o'humor and continued to make me laugh each class! Not only is he funny but he runs the class extremely smooth. There is a two-class-cycle of (1)practicing for a quiz and then (2)performing the quiz for him. Easy to understand, and he's very accessible as well! Just an absolute G!
I took HONR 100 with him, and if you are too, well, you have no choice of professor. Don't worry, though; all of the honors staff are the greatest people you will know.

I took HONR 100 with him, which currently is not available here. He is very well-spoken, and easy to understand. He uses a lot of fancy words that I have never heard of, which always made my friends and I chuckle. He gives great feedback and listens well.

Dr. Stacey is an awesome professor and a brilliant guy. I am a math major and don't know a lot about political theory but Dr. Stacey made it fun and interesting. It's such a shame he left the honors college to be the dean of undergraduate education.  Highly recommended.
He is a great teacher. Nice and friendly. Tests and quizzes very easy they were open book. Lecture was actually interesting. Easy grader to. If you can take one of his classes do it you will love it.
I love him. He's really approachable and really nice, and very helpful and concise in explaining subject material. Plus, he's smokin' hot. My motivation for coming to class every time. =)

Excellent professor. His lectures, though dry, are crystal clear. He provides you with an outline, including quotes, which is extremely helpful on the open book quizzes. I took the class a bit too early for my liking, so often didn't show up, but he didn't seem to mind as long as I knew my stuff. Great class, highly suggest it.
If u r willing to put enought effort take his class. He is OK.

One of the best professors a student can ever have.  Very approachable, easy going, and willing to help students in any way possible.  Be warned though, he can be very dry with his lectures, and if you email him a paper to look it over, don't expect it back very quickly.  But, all in all, a great guy, and a great teacher with many years to grow.

Amazing professor. This dude is very very smart. Philosophy can be a muddy subject but he makes the material accessible and clear. Doesn't grade too harshly on the exams (they're all essay). Really great guy and always willing to talk after class or during his office hours.
An awesome teacher, makes the material interesting... extremelly attractice and obviously knows what he's talking about.

Amazing guy, really interesting and engages everyone who displays ownership of a brain. If you do the reading, think about the reading, and talk in class, you're fine. Ab-sol-ute-ly gorgeous. Maybe it's partly the accent. It's hard not to pay attention in class!

Dr. Stacey is one of the youngest political science teachers that I have seen at UMBC. Yet, he is perhaps the most intelligent professor in his department. Mr. Stacey is very fluent in his knowledge of philosophical theory and is easy able to impress his students. A few more years of teaching and Simon will likely end up to be one of the greatest!

He's an awesome teacher.  I had him for Poli 315 and 210.  He explains everything really well and makes sure that you know the material before moving on.  The only thing is he has a weird way of grading, like he can't make up his mind.  Caution to the girls though, his looks and accent can be distracting ;)
I have taken Dr. Stacey twice. He is fair and expect a lot of reading and a fair amount of writing. He is a decent guy. Worth taking

I wasn't sure what to expect, but it turned out to be pretty fun, even though there was a lot of reading.  Political Philosophy isn't really my favorite subject, but with his South African accent, I had no problem listening to him talk.  He's pretty easy on the eyes, too :)

If you attend the lectures, you are sure to get at least a B on the quizzes. He is very pleasant to listen to with his accent and he is very fond of allowing everyone to speak their mind. The class can sometimes be boring because he feels that he needs to reiterate the important facts to his students. I learned a lot from him.

Somehow, taking a philosophy course with a guy with a British accent just seems right, even if he's from South Africa. If you have a talent for B.S., you can get an easy A in this class with only Spark Notes and skimming the readings (if that).

Topic: Equality. He's good, but young yet. Don't expect him to be as good as Vaughn. He is however interesting and really likes to talk to students. I happened to hate this class though, found I'm not all that interested in Equality. Give Stacey time and I think He'll make an excellent prof
Super understanding professor. The workload is light with just two exams and a group project as the main assignments. Would take his class again.

The group projects we had to do were very complicated, and for no reason, if you didn't want to be in class the whole time. To be honest, it depends on your group members. His lectures were average, and the quizzes were very quick. He grades fairly, and everything is easily accessible. In terms of what I think I learned is closer to a 6/10.
He is great. knowledgeable and engaging. I wishhhh I had him for IS 147 too.

He is a very good professor. I struggle with the class since I am not very good at code (and its late) but he is very willing to help. There is one group project at the end, 5 homework, and one lab every week(total of 10) He is very fair on deadlines and a good teacher to take! He does give a lot of code to help out on his site as well!
Professor Shiva has got to be the best professor I have had at UMBC, he will make sure you understand the material. If you are lost please talk to him he is willing to help! Amazing professor

Typos on most assignments/tests, vague directions, repeated questions with different answers. Quizzes dropped at varying days and times with a 24 hour time limit. No online or in-class notification of them, no schedule. HW didn't line up with what was taught in class. Homework only ever had 3-8 bulleted points of instruction, no matter how complex.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: A good professor. Take him.

I did remote. He expects you to remember all of IS147. No textbook, but he gives Youtube videos (that aren't his) and links to read. No office hours. Doesn't explain well. Get ready to learn on your own. Many mic/technical issues. Quiz, hw and lab each week. Accusatory, loud, blunt teaching style.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Test heavy

reviews.comment: His class has some quizzes, labs, and a semester-long group project. I think he is a fair grader when it comes to the group project, and the class should be fine as long as you get along well with your group members and you all do your work.
HE is bad
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: Honestly the best Professor Ive ever had in the IS department. He explains everything super thoroughly is great for beginners in Java. Highly recommend for IS147.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Incredible professor. You won't worry much about your grade in the class, so you can actually focus on learning. Professor Sharma will showcase in-class demos for software used in the industry and will even tell you what to expect in certain job positions. Definitely take this professor if you want a good grade and especially if you want to learn.
Just the best. I had him for both IS 147 and 247 and I learnt a lot about Java and OOP.

One of the best professors to take at UMBC. He is lenient with deadlines and asks you when the deadline should be. He also raises your overall grade by 3% at the end. Computer programming has a huge learning curve.. heck.. I still don't even know it after completing this course... but I got an A. Final was online.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: 2 Exams 1 final, group project, and Lab/HW all online. He's pretty lenient on deadlines and overall reasonable. Hw/lab wording can be confusing. Pretty open to different teaching methods and will walk through lecture code. Only difficult thing was group project with 20+ requirements and is open-ended on what you create, be ready for questions.
reviews.rating_tags: Tests? Not many--GROUP PROJECTS--Would take again

reviews.comment: Definitely learned many different coding concepts and ideas which I did not know before. Homework and labs are easy as long as you go to class and use his examples. Tests are definitely harder but as long as you study his powerpoints you should be okay. There is a group project at the end but he gives guidelines to follow. Would recommend.

He is just amazing. The best professor ever. He gives amazing lectures, gives homework, helps you with them after class. Also you can send him emails. Extends homework deadlines,  gives easy exams and group projects are really nice too.

Professor Sharma is the best! He is so nice and patient with students, always willing to help and give feedback. I really appreciate that he takes time to meet with students who are struggling with material before and after class.  Tests are not bad and there is 1 group project which is also pretty easy. Labs and homework are also fairly easy.

Fantastic professor, lectures may be long but he makes up for it by always being there to answer questions, and is very lenient. The exams are easy if you pay attention and read his power points. He's a laid back and experienced professor, you won't regret taking his course.
Not very organized but he is very understanding and an easy grader. Long as you do your work, anyone can get an A.
One of the best teacher for is 147 here at Umbc. He is also super helpful. Overall fun class

Avoid Dr. Singer. He lies, has favorites, grades too harshly and puts students down with help of his faculty members. He teaches only one way and expects you teach his way. Also, has recruiters or other professors who are unqualified and unauthorized in grading assignments in your K20 account.

Unclear at times, but I learned something new from ea. class. Prof. Singer has a strong foundation in the educ. field that can be confusing, but his extra support & guidance in and out of class has shown me new depths of understanding, knowledge, and wisdom as I struggled with doubt, exhaustion, and uncertainty w/lesson plans and practice exam.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Great professor. Very nice and a very easy A. You will write several lesson plans and do them in a school. Can be kinda vague on when things are do. Just ask him to clarify. Take him!

CMSC411 with Professor Simon is engaging and rewarding. He's passionate, adds humor, prefers short coding demos over slides, and shares strong opinions. Two exams (cheatsheet allowed) and ~5 assignments, sometimes unclear, graded for completion. Doesn't reply to emails. Heavy on textbook reading. Ensures you gain foundational knowledge at least.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Easily the worst professor I have had at UMBC. Until him, I'd never met an instructor who gets angry when students ask a question. Every response is "did you read the book?" + said in a condescending tone to make you feel dumb for asking. Brutal grader, complains about office hours, and penalizes students for him giving us code that does not run.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Great professor, definitely had some struggles moving to an online format. Really smart guy with a quick wit and dry sense of humor for lectures. He will wait til the last minute to grade everything, the good news is at least he is a very lenient grader, the median for the final was an A. Just make sure you actually show up to class.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The topics of his class are interesting, but his presentation style is very mediocre. He is one of the worst graders I have ever seen, we received our first assigned grades the day of the final and he took until the due date for semester grading to return class grades. I would not take him again for this very reason.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Group projects--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Lectures aren't too bad and he's pretty funny, and if you're interested in the stuff they can be really great. Theres a few homework assignments that are kind of easy and 2 exams which you just need to pay attention in class to do well on. There is one semester long group project worth a bulk of your grade though, but you have the choice of topic.

Makes you work real hard on century old stuff, never grades on time. Doesn't hold office hours and if you drop a mail, don't expect to hear back from him. Take this class if you want to have some good time listen to his sarcastic jokes, don't expect to learn anything.
Great sense of humor, homeworks are tough, time consuming and sometimes even vague. Teaches really old and boring stuff !

There was a lot of reading, and tons of material to go over. Tyler certainly knew what he was talking about, encouraged us to get interested in the field, and facilitated discussions of related comp sci topics. i wish i could remember more of that extra stuff stuff. two examples are: a good book by ritchie and kernighan, for c, and how to use gcc
Difficult programming projects. Try's to make classes entertaining.
He was very interested and knowledgeable about the material. The projects were fun.

Nate is a great choice for THTR 120 so long as you know what you're getting into. His lectures are very well prepared and researched and definitely the highlight of the class. The only issue for some might be the many large group projects and his very strict attendance policy. If you work hard and communicate with him you'll be fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Group projects--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: A solid professor! You can tell that he is passionate about theatre. Wish he gave us more time to work on big projects like papers and presentations but besides that, he's great.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Cool dude. Take his classes.

The class is just stress arts and crafts once you get through the lectures and quizzes in the beginning. He's fine for this class. You only get a certain amount of absences before you get a letter grade deduction. You just gotta show up, participate, and try on the projects.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Group projects

reviews.comment: - Bad Lectures: Unclear speech; messy handwritten lecture notes; difficult to follow - insists on calling students cell phones, which I personally think is weird - No textbook to supplement unhelpful lectures - doesn't name the specific methods he teaches us, making it difficult to look them up to teach myself.

He struggles with technology, can barely upload his notes. His notes are very disorganized, he doesn't teach well. HE ASKS FOR STUDENTS NUMBERS AND CALLs THEM IF UR HW IS BAD. Homeworks are either simple or extremely complicated. Even though the pre req is STAT 355 he expects u to know material from other STAT classes.

Avoid this professor!!! 1. While he understands the material himself, he is not good at teaching or explaining 2. I know I'm not supposed to talk about bias, but this is the biggest reason I suggest to avoid him: he discourages sophomores and freshmen from taking the course, and he discourages women from taking the course, regardless of skill level

He is one of only a couple professors I actively avoid. He is disorganized and his classes lack structure. Nearly all graded work is unrealted to lectures; you will feel like quizzes and homework is the first time you've ever seen it. I have never left a single class feeling like I actually learned anything. He's brilliant, but not a good teacher
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: I don't suggest taking STAT365 with him. He does not know the material, and does not grade anything. I had the correct answers to many problems and he marked them incorrect. I went to him and asked why they were wrong, he did not know or understand the material. No syllabus, no grades uploaded ever, homework and exams are irrelevant from material

If you want to take the actuarial exams, this class does not prepare you for it at all. The textbook is slim and not good. I ended up buying a 700pg book to actually study from, and that's helped a lot, but he doesn't teach the material well at all. Never felt like lectures helped with homework, and does a poor job of explaining concepts. Avoid.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Never goes through any examples and when asked to one time argued with a student. Exams and quizzes make up your entire grade, he never really laid up what to understand or study to prepare for them. AVOID IF POSSIBLE
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious

reviews.comment: Dr. Sinha is a decent lecturer. But the course was very disorganized. There was minimal communication between Dr. Sinha and the TA. He gave us a syllabus but he consistently made changes to the schedule, and threw out quizzes at will. This made it a little difficult to study for.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious

reviews.comment: Dr. Sinha is a great person, he's very smart & cares about students at an individual level, willing to help students at any time. However his class is a little disorganized in terms of structure and what to expect in quizzes/exams. He's more of a "go with the flow" type of guy.  Other than that he loves talking about himself and does magic tricks!
Avoid if you can
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: If I have anything to say about this professor, it's that he's lazy but merciless. Expect very little partial credit and your grade is made up entirely of exams and quizzes, each of which is only about 2-6 questions long, so making mistakes can make or break your grade.  His lectures are useless, other than just knowing the topic to learn myself.

Great professor; approachable and helpful at all times. However, the class seemed a bit disorganized especially concerning what was to be expected on quizzes. Always be prepared for a curve ball. He does magic, yes real magic, in class! That's always a plus.

He's fine. HWs are optional and he gives feedback if you do them, conceptually the course isn't that hard as long as you make good use of youtube/Khan Academy as well as going to discussion and lecture.  Biggest complaint is I never really felt like I fully understood what I needed to know and quizes had lots of curve balls that made things hard.

Dr Sleeman knows what she is doing and a very caring. Her homework assignments are hard but if you go to her or the TA office hours, they will walk you through everything until you understand it. She always makes sure students understand the materials. Shes very inspirational and makes AI my favorite class at UMBC.

You can tell from the start that she loves what she does. The class is more than just teaching, she's raising the next group of students she intends to pass the torch to. The classes were never boring, always instructional. Homework looks hard until you realize they are actually really easy. And she cares about students. Always ready to listen.

This prof actively lowered my interest in the subject. Lectures are mind numbing. There was a midterm and a final. Both were online exams. Both were a terrible experience. Exams questions were weighted unfairly and simply not adaptable to an online format. Gave class a vote to chose final and ignored it by choosing an easier option for herself

Overall a good professor. She definitely understands the material and answers any question you have thoroughly. The semester project was a lot of work, but it was fair and it helped my understanding of the material. The lectures can be boring and she could present the material better. If you go to office hours, she explains it much better.
Smart professor who teaches a pretty tough course. Start your projects the week that you get them or you'll have trouble getting good grades and understanding the material

Cares about her students, but probably is too focused on what type of teacher she is. Assignments in the course ranged from easy to brutal but the course projects are made by the CMSC head not her. One of the two non final exams in the class was easy and the other was the hardest test I've ever taken. She wants to help but taking her is a gamble.

I would definitely recommend this professor for CMSC 341. She does a good job explaining the content and has detailed power points that are posted online. Tests are fair and based on the lectures. Textbook use is not required if you understand the content but would definitely help.

Prof. Sleeman is a very fair professor. Her lectures can be boring sometimes, but she really tries to make sure you understand the material. She goes through and explains each project pretty thoroughly. She makes her own exams, which aren't too bad if you study the lecture powerpoints. She has attendance grades that she takes at the end of class.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Teaches like we are all 3rd graders.  Reads every single word on every single page .  She took an hour long class and extended it to the full 3 hours just because she reads so slowly.

This class was a complete joke. The midterm in class was extremely specific, even though she never went into detail in class. I think it's impossible to get less than a 90% on your speech, as long as you show up and give your speech.

Worst instructor I've had at UMBC, avoid if possible.  Class is not overly difficult, but the teacher is very disorganized; Student homework was frequently lost.  Expensive book  is required yet rarely used. Common for her to give a handout in class, then read it word for word for the next hour. Class was a complete waste of time.

She was an absolute jackass!  She gave me questions wrong on the test that were right and others were given the same question right, but they were wrong.  She refused to change my grade.  She also made **** comments about certain minorities.  She needed to be gotten rid of!  Never take her anywhere else if she ever leaves UMB.  Good riddens.

Not a great teacher.  When doing your project do it her way- if you can figure out what that is! She is not looking for creative thought. Apparently social policy can be viewed in only one way- her way.  Plays favorites.This class was not a good introduction to grad school. Grading policy is odd- tests were easy though.

Worse prof I have ever had! I didnt learn a thing from her class. She only agrees with what she believes n everything else is WRONG in her eyes. She wasnt clear on requirements 4 paper n presentation. Changes her mind EVERY CLASS! Class material wasnt helpful. I wouldnt recommend her...take any1 else but HER! Grading: quiz, presentation n paper.

The course dealt with groups and families.  We got almost no instruction and the role players were not adequate in teaching what the subject matter was.  She is not clear on assigments, expectations, or grading.  Her mantra is that grades are not important as long as you learn something.  Problem is, you learn nothing.

Took her IS246 class during the Summer I session. I found it fairly easy, just follow the ppt slides, especially when setting up Visual Studio (can just use the newest version on your desktop instead of the virtual machine). You usually have 2 easy weekly assignments, and 2 open book exams per semester. Honestly one of the easiest classes I've had.

DO NOT TAKE! this is the worst professor that i've ever had. it's almost the end of the semester, and there is only one grade in our grade book which is the exam (which she took forever to post). the class assignments are so difficult to complete and make absolutely zero sense. the course materials are all over the place. also the exams are HARD
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: When I say SAVE YOURSELF. Believe me!! I have had difficult professors before, but she is by far THEE worst professor. Very sweet, however if you want to pass this class avoid her! Emailed her numerous times for her to respond "Oh, I forgot" asked her to look over my assignments to see if I'm doing them correctly. She gave feedback then gave me a 0

Dana Smith does not respond to your questions. Instead, she provides vague responses and basically tells you to figure it out yourself. She was early to leave class or would sometimes move it virtually, only to not show up. She was also never available outside of class and didn't respond to emails. She's the only prof for this class, so good luck.

I received a C in this class; the gradebook only has two assignments. Given the lengthy syllabus, it's unreasonable not to enter grades or respond to students seeking clarification. I struggled with the final project and emailed weekly without any response, and with class only once a week, she was extremely inaccessible outside of class.
Pretty easy class, just a midterm and final, weekly homework assignments, pretty straightforward. She takes forever to grade and pretty much just reads off a PowerPoint during our "lectures". Easy A.

I've taken her twice for two different IS courses and she's always been the same. The only issue is that she's a strict grader for tests and projects. Not that she'll fail you, but it seems that everyone in the class gets either a B or a C. I once failed a test, and she gave me the opportunity to redo the questions and get at least a 70% on it.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The professor is a nice person. We had a couple of assignments that were graded which was easy. 2 group projects( a little hard). And three exams, her exams are very difficult.

Some exam questions weren't based on previous assignments. She gave low grades for participation even though everyone posted on the BlackBoard Discussion. (Apparently, you have to post 3 or more per thread, which wasn't stated in the syllabus.) She gave me a D on the project paper. I reported her to the IS department, but had no luck.

Easily the worst professor I've ever had. She never actually taught anything and her grading criteria was extremely unclear. Most of the time, her "lessons" consisted of posting textbook page numbers. When I emailed her with a question about the rubric for a project, she simply told me to read the rubric.

I wish I could rate this professor 0. Worst professor I've ever taken, never has any clear instructions! Everything about this class is confusing! When you email her, she responds whenever she feels like it. Terrible.

Alice 3 is one of the most confusing programs to use and I disliked it. I understand the concepts behind using the program, but the program itself is not useful outside of this class. I felt like this class was a waste of time. Professor Smith was a better professor for IS320, but not much better.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: STAY AWAY. Classes were useless. Her lectures do not help with labs and barely help with her exams. In this class it is the students job to figure out what to teach themselves. Is a nice person but terrible professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Dana Smith is ok - 295 is an incredibly easy class and all you have to do is show up, do the in class work, and leave - usually within 30 mins. However when we switched to online the class got a lot more tedious - no online lectures, just assignments - but deadlines were sometimes unmanageable and quizzes had only a 10 minute turnaround to upload.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: She expects the class to teach themselves and will specifically instruct the TA to not help you during lab sessions. She's slow to respond to emails, if at all, and tells us in class repeatedly that she wants us to struggle. She gives vague feedback on exams and will not tell you why certain answers were wrong. Quite a bland personality as well.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Group projects--Tough grader

reviews.comment: she gives pop quizzes every so often, but gives hints as to when they'll be. the class itself is mainly alice and she gives you the code, its up to you to understand it tho. there's one project worth 30% of your grade, and she assigns hw but doesn't grade it. easy A
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Graded by few things--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Dana Smith is very nice professor but her exams are kinda hard. The study guides that are given for the 2 exams are ok. Doesn't really prepare you for the problem solving questions but it does help with short essays. She does take a long time to get back grades for assignments. Office hours are useless. would not recommend taking her.

Prof. Smith is really knowledgeable about this subject has many experience in the field. However this class was a bit difficult. You really have study on your own and self-teach the material. She doesn't require you to go to lecture but she requires you to go to discussion. This is really a class with no clear direction and you have to find it.

The course is very straightforward and can be very easy if you complete all of the in-class and homework assignments which are not themselves graded but essential to doing well on the exams and projects. The professor is very understanding and approachable for any questions. The textbook is necessary for this class.

Great teacher. Textbook is a must to do classwork, homework, and study for exams/projects. Two exams and two projects. Lots of the homework was not graded but you need to do them to know how to use the program for tests/projects.
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--TEST HEAVY--Would take again

reviews.comment: Using Alice program to guide into programming. She gives homework that she rarely checks but trust me you should do the homework. It helps with the 2 projects she gives out later. There is a quiz roughly once or twice a month. The final had an open book portion and was fair.
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--Would take again

reviews.comment: I don't understand all the poor reviews for this teacher. This class was great. If you do the labs, the material is fairly easy to understand. The exams are not difficult as long as you've done the work and actually attend the labs to work through the problems. Everyone warned me about this class, but for NO REASON!

Exams are beyond what you learn in class, make sure you really understand the material, use outside resources. Exams are difficult. Projects are crucial! You just work on assignments in class and ask questions if necessary, she doesn't really teach the Modules

Reads off of powerpoints all class. Tests are ridiculously hard and she will take off points if  your answer is not textbook perfect. She takes forever to grade things and you can figure out what grade you have at the end of the semester.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Really really great teacher. I had her over the summer and she was very kind, caring and respectful to everyone. It was my first course in information systems and she taught it very clearly and has lots of experience in the field. Great lecturer and often talks about how her own experiences relate to the material. 10/10 would recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Caring

reviews.comment: I surprisingly enjoyed this class. Take the final project seriously but have fun with it. I learned a lot. This is a very independent class, meaning you get out what you put in. Prof. Smith is very kind and helpful with debugging. The handwritten programs on the tests are nerve-wracking, but completely doable.

I'm not too sure why there are so many poor reviews for this professor - I personally thought she was great. For those who commented during the spring '16 semester, just know approx. 4 students went to each class. So, there goes their grade.

Dr. Smith is a really nice professor. She is very clear and super helpful. There is a lot of required reading and attending lectures is super important because she doesn't post powerpoints online. Test can be tough but if you keep up with the readings then you should be good.
