terrible professor! Doesn't grade hw on time and her exams are hard as hell. You really need to do good one her exams to pass the class

Doesn't grade until the end of the semester. Lectures are a waste of your time, she just goes through power points that don't contribute to your overall understanding of concepts.  Go to discussion because there are a lot of assignments. She didn't turn in our grades until three days after they were due. Seriously she grades nothing.

She comes off as a very laid back and casual teacher which is great. However there is a ton of tedious ridiculous work and she checks every little thing. She also gives no explanation as to how she grades so don't be surprised when you do great work and get a low grade because of one minuscule error. very frustrating and unclear grading

Smith is the worst prof I've had while at UMBC. She cares little, if any, for her students and her communication skills are are that of a rooster. Please, for your sake, avoid her or you will be dealing with 16 weeks of confusion, frustration, anger, and regret. You have been warned...

you have to memorize every line of code, she takes off for repeated points, one part is worth more than the half the exam itself, class average for exam 2 was 70%  WITH CURVE.  Her exams are killer, everything else is super easy but the exams are 25% each. Start the semester project asap! She takes FOREVER to grade. You have to code by hand on exam

DO NOT TAKE HER FOR IS246!!! The class and coding is easy, there are three tests worth 25% of your total grade each. These test are unforgiving, they are not open book and the coding is done by hand. You need to memorize all the codes exactly as they would be written in VB. She takes off lots of points for each mistake even if they're repeated ones

Smith is very nice, and as helpful as she can be. Quizzes are on the chapters, almost weekly. Wording on quizzes can be tricky.   Projects instead of exams. Ability to be creative is key. Takes forever to grade.

She gives lots of homework but theyre easy if you like coding. The exams are pretty easy as well depending on your coding ability. VB is super easy. She takes FOREVER to grade. Study the powerpoints and in class examples for exams. She lets you out early. All in all its a straightforward class, not much to it.

If you're good with Excel and Access, you don't need to go to class. The first test is a little hard just because it's not what you would expect. Smith spends the class going over PowerPoints which don't really prepare you for the exam, so pay close attention to the assignments.  Once you understand the exam style, you'll do fine on the next exam.

Very sweet woman. Slow on grading ExcelAccess assignments but they pretty much are for completion anyway. Many students bombed the first exam, even though she gave a THOROUGH study guide. She takes education very seriously (Master's degree in Edu) so she works with struggling students. Two exams + weekly assignments similar to IS295

She is really good teacher. She is very helpful and Kind. I am taking this class currently and we are almost done.  I enjoyed it. Actually, it really help me to learn and gain skills. She is very cooperative and expertise on the course. If you have any problem and talk to her, she understand it and help you out. Great teacher.

She is very disorganized and seems to know very little about the class she's teaching and about UMBC in general. She never tells you what to expect on tests and tests are based on the book and not the power points.

I don't know why she has any negative reviews. This professor is an amazing IS professor! She is also my advisor, and she is just so helpful, understanding , & nice. I took 3 classes with her, and they were all easy. Highly recommended, especially from someone who never rates professors!
Anything but dull!!
She is a very easy going teacher. It was her first time teaching 303. 1 take home midterm, 4 easy quizes, and a group project. No final and the project is simple.

She will keep you in class for 15-30 mins of the hour and a half class just to go through a useless powerpoint.  Online discussion board stuff is tedious. Never responds to emails even though she talks about how much she is on the computer. Exams all on the book. Study the book = A on exam = A in class. Going to class is pointless.

Not helpful in exam review or relating material. Cannot answer technical questions; doesn't seem to have grasp of material. Cancels class at last minute, leaving commuters screwed. Poor at responding to students' e-mail, especially regarding project. Exam material does not reflect what learned in class. Seemingly lazy professor.

she doesnt go over anything that is on the test during class... for the 2nd exam we were required to memorize 102 lines of code and write it out on paper- in addition to mult choice... this class is a waste b/c of the teacher... we took it because of her great ratings on this website- misleading for 246... maybe good in other classes but umm... yea

Very easy, just computer assignments that she'll basically walk you through. Only bad part is those aren't worth much, the 3 tests are worth a lot and only from the book. Don't bother buying the Access book, just get the other one. She's very nice, kinda boring but overall made it a very easy class

this class is a very easy higher level elective class. its excel and access and all the assignments are group work. two exams and they are very easy. Smith is very nice and if you ask for help she'll help you easy A class.

Very nice professor. She is very helpful and willing to explain again if something is unclear. Having hw every class was worth it in the end because it meant I remembered everything well. The semester project was not hard and she gives you a lot of creative control with it. Definitely would reccommend for 3rd semester of programming for IS majors.
SUPER easy class. just go to class and do the assignments which are word for word out of the book and are written out step by step. very simple. 2 exams on Access and Excel; super easy. easy A.

Great Professor, very helpful and easy to apporach. Assigns a semester long project about 2-3 week into the class. Read and do the homework and you will be fine. Anyone that fails her class is a lazy person
She made class fun and interesting. It was pretty easy, and she was very helpful. I definitely recommend her.
Great teacher. Very helpful.
Group project at the end. Lots of assignments. Late with grading the assignments. Didn't seem to know VBA down to the technical level. Relied on peer helping over the majority of the assignments.

Good teacher.  She is fairly responsible with her grading.  Sometimes she couldn't answer some of the questions asked of her.  This lead me to believe that she didn't have a real grasp of the material herself.  She was typically late for a lot of the classes and she did leave early a lot of the time.

I was fairly disappointed in the class itself and in how she presented the material. Alot of the tests were very long multi-choice and were sometimes hard to study for.  She seems sometimes hard on grading and sometimes easy on grading, its kind of hard to get a clear picture of how you are doing.  If you have to, shes an alright professor to take.
No Comments

class is pretty easy but she tough on grading epecially lecture attendance and partcipation grade. If you don't attend class very well or do not like to speak up, avoid her period, cuz it's worth 1 letter grade. That's why I end up with a C.

I have not learned a thing in her class. She can't teach. Kip taught more than she has or ever will. she complains about being bumped out of a teaching slot when the teacher who bumped her is way better

The class is fairly easy and straight-forward, especially if you took Visual Basic in high school, like most people who take this 247V.  She is very helpful and is willing to work with you during & outside of class.  The tests are multiple choice with 1 programming problem that comes directly from our classwork/ semester project

This class is EASY!  Just read the book, take some notes on the PowerPoint, & go to class.  In class, she spends only 20 mins lecturing & the rest of the time is spent doing groupwork, discussions, & looking up stuff on the internet.  Definitely an easy A.  The tests are all Multiple Choice & the answers are obvious!

She isn't very organized. There was a lot of group discussions which helped to get the idea but rest of lecture was boring "white-on-black" powerpoint slides. No real fun, but she made the ppt's available online. I studied somewhat for the tests and somehow got away with an A. Very boring class. If you can, take it with someone you know.

I had Dana Smith for Visual Basic.  She is a very nice lady, but she never could answer my questions.  She always responded with "Well..try it and see what happens!"  She did teach well (w/ powerpoints).  Tests were not extremily hard.  The project is worth a lot of your grade.  Final exam is open book.  Good news!  I ended up with a B.

Class tests are harder then the material dictates and the curve to lower grades infuriates many students. Otherwise she is kind and interested in your success as a student. Her class is very laid back and normally ends early rather than covers additional material. Read the notes do the assignments and study for tests and you will do OK.

Horrible professor, can't teach, and doesn't know anything.  If she's your counselor...don't go to her...find another counselor...she would screw you up big time.  She can't answer to anything you like to know, and tell you to go ask someone else...useless person.

horrible teacher i had a 87% she dindt give me an A she doesnt know what she is doing, i had a problem with my project she didnt know how to fix it and she didnt get back to me until 1 week before it was due. very rude.
No Comments
She reads directly from the slides.  Always ends class early.  Tests are multiple choice and you must study for them.
Very nice teacher! Very helpful. She isn't so easy, but she helps you to make feel like it is easy! Great teacher!
Really nice teacher to get along with.  She knows what she's teaching.  Makes the class fun.  Just talk to her, you'll get through with an A.

She's good at demonstrating/explaining experiments, but hard to contact outside of lab, TAs are incompetent. Anytime I ask for help or feedback they just told me they can't give me the answer and I have to figure it on my own, grades take forever. Her lab manual is very disorganized. Sometimes it's hard to tell what to expect for quizzes/exams.

had her for 141 and took 142 summer class after.141 exams were hard, learning objectives/lectures helped but si pass tutoring saved me from a C. very passionate ab her field and kind to talk to for help/ in general, wish there were more ways to help w understanding content tho. 142 was a lot easier esp in summer. dont take 141 if not a bio major.

I'm not even a biology major (I'm comp-sci) and I found her to be an amazing lecturer; she's genuinely very engaging. However, I found her exams to be difficult; studying off of slides and hw problems is the best way to be successful. Is strict with curves even though exams were 60% of our grade. Attendance is mandatory and counts towards a grade.

One of the best stem professors I've had so far. Dr. Smith's lectures are very engaging and interesting. She also cares about her students!! Make sure to study the lectures and its objectives, the discussion material and Pearson HWs over the txtbook. Her exams are very straightforward and she drops the lowest.

Your 300L experience depends on your TA (mine was great), and the course content is fair. However, Dr. Smith is very particular and expects a lot from the student for an introductory lab. The lab manual is created by her and isn't organized well. Looking back, I can say this course was harder than 302L (mostly due to Dr. Smith's expectations).
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: Overall, she was great. She explains things succinctly and really helps people learn. I loved the labs that she taught for and didn't find them difficult at all.

The class is exam heavy so if you fail the exams, you will 100% fail this class. She does drop 1 exam though, but even with the drop, a lot of people have failed the class. The averages for the exams were always a D w/some people getting even below that. A lil tmi, but everyone except for 1 person in my discussion group failed multiple exams;(

if she smells chatgpt she will give you an F. even if you didnt use it and she thinks you did, you wont have a second to explain yourself. you will find out through an email from the misconduct comittee. do not take her
PLEASE RUN AND DONT LOOK BACK. yall will regret the minute you hit on register.
Competent professor who is knowledgeable about her subject. Read the textbook, but you'll need to ask her to figure out what parts of it will actually be on exams

She really cares about her students and will help you improve your grade in any way she can. Has good lectures and exams are not too bad as long as you follow the learning objectives and know what you're doing.

All the grading reports are from the T.A., and Dr. Smith is always there during the lab and demonstrates every procedure that might be challenging. She gives us plenty of practice time for the skills portion and practice questions for the exam, and she is more than willing to stay behind and answer any questions that I have or clarify anything.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: BIOL 300L is a tough class but I recommend taking it over the summer. If you read the manual and watch the videos before coming to class, it makes it much easier and Dr. Smith is there the whole time answering any questions you might have. The TA grades all the assignments, so follow the rubric and keep track of due dates and you'll be set.

Don't get this 5/5 rating fool you, she is the worst professor I have ever had at UMBC. Extremely rude to the students I took her in summer and never had this much hard time for a 300 level lab. there is no guideline you are on your OWN. Her manual is very confusing  before going to her lab I used to wish to get hit by a car AVOID her at all cost.

She really knows what she teaches: she's passionate and covers topics well. A ton of reading though and I found the homework pretty hard. But her exam questions were easier than the homework assignments in my opinion. Pay attention in lecture, she tailors her questions pretty well. Lots of interesting things to learn from her in this class :)

I've had Dr. Smith for both BIOL 123 and BIOL 141 and had amazing experiences with both. She is very engaging, and you can tell she has a passion for what she teaches. She teaches tough courses and knows that but gives you great resources for studying. Complete the learning objectives, the help :) Dr Smith is my favorite teacher this school offers.

Dr. Smith is very kind and always answered my questions. The TAs of the course were not very knowledgeable so that made it a bit difficult but if you knew what you were doing by watching the provided videos before class then lab went smoothly.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Accessible outside class--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: As someone who got stuck with a bad TA for 300L this semester, it's still possible to do well. If you have questions or concerns go to Dr. Smith directly, she is incredibly kind, caring, fair, and always willing to help. It is obvious she cares about her job and students, but that said, you will not get away with bare minimum effort in this class.

People who took her over the summer will tell you it was easy, because over the summer it was in fact easy. BUT DO NOT TAKE this lab with her over the regular semester. The TAs were incompetent and SO MANY people were cheating using people's old content. Because of this the class was overly challenging for the credits it's worth.

I do not think the lab manual is the best. The varying of TA knowledge as well as expectations and grading is horrendous. Some TAs are great, others are gargbage. This is HUGE as they are the intructors for your lab. She is a nice lady and will answer any quesitons but I found the inability of my TA to have tarnished my grade. DO NOT TAKE!

Took this lab over the summer and it went great. Only had five lab reports and the experiments were fun and interesting. Include ALL your data in your results section to get full points since manual doesn't always explicitly say what to include. Tests are specific but fair, make sure to read the lab background info.

Do your work, show up prepared, and you will be good to go. No unreasonable expectations and she answers questions really well. Overall a nice person and will help you. I definitely recommend her for a lab.
Do NOT take this class if you don't have to.

idk where to start but sometimes on my way to lab, I hope I get hit by one of those campus cars so I don't have to go through the lab. basically, the lab is confusing and the manual doesn't really match up, she is also never really around. the TAs are kinda mean and make you feel stupid for asking questions. good luck tho

Professor Smith is a lovely woman but as far as professor shes ok. She made this lab more difficult than it should. Very strict on how to write the lab writeups and you get points taken off for small things. Shes very passionate about teaching  however this lab is intense. Overall if you are looking for an easy lab class, dont take it with her
Truly an amazing professor! She is extremely passionate about what she's teaching and helping her students succeed. Definitely my favorite class and teacher I've taken at this school.

I've taken BIOL142, 300L & 466 with Dr. Smith and I must say she is the BEST professor I've ever had! I can tell that she spends lots of time preparing for all her classes- her lecture slides are organized so beautifully & she teaches/explains very logically! Her exams are not easy but they're fair and will make you think/apply concepts deeper.

I LOVED Professor Tracy! She is very engaging and makes Bio interesting. She also gives a lot of extra credit (but no curves, obviously) so it was 110% my fault for not getting an A. Read textbook ahead of class and GO TO CLASS because there is attendance. I really had to work hard for exams, but the final was a breeze. She's beyond sweet and cares

This class is okay. There are three exams (lowest drop), weekly hw (14), in-class activities (6), and a final exam. Personally, did not use the textbook. Her PowerPoints are enough, you just need to get the concept. Class is more challenging if you don't understand.

Professor Smith is a professor who really cares for the field and her students. She always answered questions during lecture and responds to emails. The exams started out rough but got easier. She has this extra credit opportunity by going to a museum and writing an essay that was fun. This class was fun to learn, although tests are memory heavy

Dr. Smith has long and thorough lectures. While attendance isn't required, if you skip it's gonna hurt a lot. She's a good enthusiastic professor who you can tell enjoys the material and explains things clearly. This class is tough, but if you read the textbook, pay attention in class, and do the learning objectives you will do well in this class.

Dr. Smith organizes this course well, clearly outlining expectations and objectives. Like most courses a fair bit of the grade is determined by exams, but she dropped the lowest exam and provided some extra credit as well. She gives students the tools to succeed, but be prepared to put in the work throughout the entire semester.

Overall, I'd say this class was very interesting. The exams were a little harder than I thought but doable if you actually pay attention in lectures and study the learning objectives. I would definitely be willing to take more classes with her, she's an awesome prof!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Honestly i regret taking her. She is an okay professor and i understood her lectures HOWEVER its very test heavy and she cares about the nitty gritty all the time. She isnt considerate and will not listen to students. Please take anyone else but her if you want a good semester

If you haven't heard that this is one of the easiest Biology classes you'll ever take, I dont know what to say. Fall 2021 semester in person with this class has been far from it, so much that it's like she deliberately goes out of her way to give you a hard time. only one opportunity for extra credit, which weighed nothing Very high drop rate

Online BIOL 300L with Dr. Smith was mainly online labs with simulations. There were no lectures and the class was asynchronous. There was a semester-long partner project with 10% of the final grade. The labs were easy but time-consuming. There were also reading assignments with a quiz at the end each week. If you do the work it's an easy A or B.

I dont know what to say. Her rubrics were not specific and when asked about the rubrics, she would direct us to TAs who were also confused. Never responded to emails and would avoid student interactions like it was the plague. We were graded by a few things but they really added up. We only heard from her 3 times via email. I am at lost for words.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Group projects--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: The other ones does not say how almost one-third of the class had to retake the class. She was not clear with anything and getting an A was based primarily on luck and pass knowledge. Even the TAs and tutors were confused with what she was trying to teach. Though she said the exams were not cumulative, they were. Honestly the worst professor I had.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: A great professor and tries to make her lectures as engaging and as personable as possible. I took BIO123 (Human Genetic) With her and it was super timely with everything COVID related and transitioned the class online really well. You can tell she loves teaching and enjoys engaging her students in the material, even with a large lecture hall.

Dr. Smith has been one of my favorite professors so far. She is very nice and keeps you interested during lectures with her jokes. I honestly liked 142 much more than 141. Make sure to study for exam and pay attention in lectures. Overall, nothing bad to say about her.

She knows the material she is talking about and teaches it very well. She also puts the powerpoints up right before the lecture, so that you can pull them up on your laptop or phone and follow along. Exams questions follow the powerpoints and some are straight off the homework. She drops 1 of the 4 exams and gives extra credit for 2 of the exams.

A very knowledgeable professor. Be sure to take advantage of office hours and pay attention to the learning objectives. Generally, if you are comfortable with the learning objectives you should have at least a B. The tests make the 'A' difficult to achieve, but it is doable. Keep up with the homework!
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Smith has much knowledge on the subject of Genetics. She gives a generally well thought out lecture that encompasses learning objectives and problem solving skills. The tests are very difficult. You may study the lecture slides for hours after class and use the full time to complete only half the questions on the test. Do not underestimate her.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Dr Smith is extremely knowledgeable, and you can tell that she enjoys teaching. Her lectures are engaging, and clearly lay out what you need to know for exams. However, it is a tough class and is mostly exams. Make sure to keep up with learning objectives and redo mastering problems, and you should be able to get at least a B.

I had her for BIOL142 in Summer 2019. As someone who isn't that great in life-science related classes, I was worried coming into this course. However, this is now one of my favorite courses I've taken. Dr. Smith pours her energy and knowledge into this class. She does her best to go as far as applying to real-life applications and not just bookwork
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Prof. Smith is a nice professor who is fairly new to teaching this course. Make sure you pay attention to her lecture slides and don't fall behind on notes. Study ahead for the exams because they are extremely difficult and the practice tests she gives beforehand don't reflect the difficulty of it.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Smith is an absolutely incredible professor. Fall 2018 was her first time teaching the course, meaning we didn't receive any practice exams. She told us what material she found most important, and what to focus on. 4 exams total (including the final) with one dropped. So if you like your first 3 exam grades, you can drop the final.
You will never know how to study for her exams. Try different way every time and not getting high grade. Application based questions not from the textbook or slides.

Do not recommend for genetics at all. Lectures were really good but the exams never seemed to cover the big ideas. All you have to prepare for exams are learning objectives which many times were not sufficient. I never felt prepared for her exams and found them nearly impossible. Overall, Im just really disappointed with this class this semester.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Very difficult exams. She is engaging and funny! Interesting lectures. But her exams require working in a lab, natural intelligence, or hours every week of excessive studying. Her PowerPoints and 70-80 slides long, 0 practice exams, and the lecture slides are disorganized with learning objectives that arent ever up to date.

There are two professors I've had in my life for whom I will forever sing their praises, and Dr. Smith is one of them. Without being long and wordy, I will say that I have struggled for a very long time with test-taking and earning the grades I work so hard for. Dr. Smith went out of her way to work with me and I finally earned my first real A.
reviews.rating_tags: ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Clear grading criteria--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: Tracy is the the way to go for 142 and 302. Her lectures are extremely engaging and always a pleasure to sit through. Do the learning objectives! Her exams are challenging, but in a very fair way that's appropriate for the level of the class. She absolutely loves her dogs and will always try to relate them to the class material.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures--Caring

reviews.comment: so baaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaad
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Dr. Smith is a sweetheart. She's very tough because she cares so much about what she's teaching, and it's apparent in class. ATTEND HER OFFICE HOURS, she's super accessible, incredibly patient and is willing to sit through tons of questions. Textbook wasn't super necessary, tests based off of PowerPoints, so go to class and ask questions!

Took over summer. Pretty easy to get an A, but you must study and make sure you write out answers to the learning objectives for all lecture power points! For extra credit, Make sure you cite all sources if you borrow information from the museum placards. She likes students who go to her office hours. Exams are fair! 6 weeks, 3 exams, drops lowest.
reviews.rating_tags: ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Dr. Smith has my entire heart, she loves bugs and I think that's cool. She also has the most amazing speaking voice.

Definitely one of the best upper level biology courses. Dr Smith is a really great professor and really cares about all of the students. Some of the coursework was confusing at times (especially the statistic programs) but everything was manageable and the content was interesting.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious

reviews.comment: Very solid professor, and very nice. She is upfront about all her expectations in terms of your work and her grading. Some people don't like her because she is harder and doesn't curve anything, not even final grades. But she really knows her stuff and is very passionate about Biology. She co-taught with another professor but I liked Smith better.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: Dr. Smith is one of the best professors Ive ever had. In addition to her passion and knowledge, shes a caring, funny, nerd. Learning is the easiest and most fun when youre learning from someone who truly loves what theyre teaching. Personally, I loafed pretty hard in BIOL466 but she was still helpful and accommodating towards me.

Dr. Smith was by far the best professor I've ever had at UMBC. BIO 466 is the amped up version of BIO 142, there is a good bit of math involved but nothing that's too crazy, it's very manageable. She does give a lot of work but the work is usually very easy and do-able if you attend class. 100% would take this class again, good bio upper level elec
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring

reviews.comment: This class basically the advanced version of BIOL 142. Lots of math and statistics were incorporated in it. Exams are tough but she lets you use a notecard. If you are good at math and stat, you will be good at this class. Also a lot of online work. If you work hard, you will do well. Dr. Smith really cares about the course and her students.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: Not even the worst teacher , but also an uncaring selfish person. very unapproachable . She just does not care about her students at all.

Another terrible bio class!! Thought after 141 it would be better but no!! Tests didn't reflect what was taught. Unnecessarily hard. Active learning did not help at all. She belongs in a research lab and not a classroom. Emails to class were condescending and rude. No guides for tests just basically know everything! UMBC Bio Dpt. should be better!
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Tests are tough--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Very good lecturer and she is funny. She is just very cool and she makes you actually excited to learn about bio. My only gripe is that her tests were rather difficult. I felt like her learning objectives and test material did not always match up. She also gave extra credit for going to the Smithsonian and the Aquarium. I wouldhighly recommend her.

Dr. Smith was a wonderful professor. The class was graded on four exams with lowest dropped (70%), Active learning discussion with lowest dropped (15%), Homework (10%), and reading quizzes with lowest dropped (5%). The class material was not bad, BUT THE EXAMS WERE REALLY, REALLY HARD! Class averages on exams were low-mid 70s and there was no curve
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tests are tough

reviews.comment: Dr. Smith is an amazing professor. Her lectures are great and she is always willing to help out if you are a struggling student. You can tell that she is very passionate about the material. Exams are kind of tough. Coming to class and taking lecture notes are the best ways to do well on them. There are a lot of extra credit opportunities though.

Awesome professor. She's very enthusiastic, helpful, and interested in knowing her students' interests. I went to her office once and she gave me names of people in the dept that I could go to for research in a lab on campus. Exams are a little tough, but are pretty fair. She drops one of your lowest grades in each category. Lots of extra credit.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: Dr. Smith is easily one of the best professors I've had so far. Her lectures were engaging, informative, and you could see how passionate she was about the subject. Most of her test were based of her slides and what she said in class, not the text in the book, so just keep that in mind.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Dr. Smith made the class very enjoyable, even for someone who doesn't really like biology. She presented information very clearly, and provided many examples to showcase what we're learning. Do the reading quizzes, they're easy points. Also, use the learning objectives to help prepare for exams. Exams can be pretty hard, you will need to study.
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--EXTRA CREDIT--Tests are tough

reviews.comment: She is just awesome. The best professor I've had at UMBC so far. She is hilarious, her lectures are amazing and you will stay interested the whole class. Loves her dogs and always relates the material to them. Always respects students' opinion or their vision of a problem. The exams are pretty hard though, so don't be too relaxed.

She is vague and only sympathetic if you're one of the little special snowflakes who can make it to her office hours. If you can't because of conflict, then she makes it feel like it's your fault, even though she has like 200 students. She tells you to focus on concepts but then asks about stupid facts that on exams instead, throwing you off.

Took over summer (recommended, no clickers required). Posts lectures slides, labs are fairly easy. Attendance is recorded (but not usually graded). Gave us an extra credit assignment. Online homework due every class. Took Bio 141 at another school, had no trouble with this class. Loves the subject and cares about students. Easier than CHEM

Took Bio 142 in the summer with Dr. Smith.  Her lectures are great!  She is very engaged in the material and very open to students questions both during and after class. She cares about her students.  The tests are tricky. Class test averages were in the low 70s.  It's definitely possible to get an A with some effort.  I would take her again!
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Topics discussed in class were very interesting. Enjoyed discussing conservation problems and efforts of different species. Learned the statistics and programs used by biologists and conservationists to perform research. Professor was enthusiastic plus willing to help students learn and succeed.

Practical skills exams are very time paced, be ready to finish things fast and master all the lab skills. Quizzes are fair but hard, read the book. Lots usage of math and excel. She responds to email so quickly. Would take her again.

Really nice lady and responds to emails very fast. The labs usually took up the whole time, but weren't difficult. Exams were fair, as long as you understand the key concepts/calculations for each exp you should be fine. The practical is very fast paced, make sure you master the skills in every lab! Be prepared for A LOT of math and Excel usage!

There was tons of material to know and memorize and the tests were pretty tricky, but it helped to read the textbook chapters before each class to stay on top of the info. However, her lectures are really interesting and she clearly enjoys teaching biology, so I did like the class.

Dr. Smith knows what she's talking about, and she makes you want to learn the information. That being said, the tests were unnecessarily tricky. If you study and read, however, you'll be fine. Interesting class, though some of the topics could be a little dry.
AMAZING PROFESSOR. I took this class over the summer and was worried it would be too much material to cram. But I still got an A.

Her presentations are really great. Her portion of the class on evolution was really interesting but the harder half of the class. Her exams were surprisingly very challenging but most say it's because she's a new professor that just got her phD so she still has a lot of the graduate material on her mind. Make sure you do the learning objectives!

Exam averages were in the low 60's. I am sorry, but this is not genetics or cell bio, this is evolution, so you would think the material would be more straight forward. We barely used the book, and the lectures were not that straight forward. I think she is just a little too serious.

She is a great speaker - lectures, including lecture slides, were very clear and filled with essential information. She is willing to help if you ask for it, and she is not judgmental. Would take again just because she is a great lecturer. Exams are moderately difficult. Make sure to review concepts and study objectives.
Lectures were always interesting and made a topic that can sometimes be very boring, to be always interesting. Always open for office hours. Very intelligent and caring.

She is greather lectures are amazing! Take one of her classes. Tough, challenging, but fair. You will have to work to do well. I was always engaged and excited to come to class. I highly recommend her office hours and review sessions. She is clearly passionate about education. Bonus, she looks like a more attractive Sandra Bullock.

Her online lectures very easy to understand. But, be warned! I never read the book and only paid attention to her online lectures and I was doing horrible on the quizzes. Make sure you do the readings as well--the quiz questions will be found in there. Exams are easy if you understand the labs and readings. Make sure to practice for the practical.

I found Dr. Smith's keen investment in the topics and strong speaking skill to result in really enjoyable lectures even if they were content-heavy. She had no problem slowing class down to further explain a concept as necessary. Exams are tough; about 50% of the test is application questions. I wish she taught both halves of BIO142 not just Part 1!

Dr Smith is a really nice, professional person who is really knowledgeable in her field.  Lectures can be a little dry at times, but you'll manage.   Exams are heavily based off of lecture, so attending is a must (plus clicker points). The exams were memory intensive, but were manageable as long as you understand the learning objectives.

He is a very unforgiving grader, he expects a lot of detail when giving your responses during tests or writing assignments. Your writing has to be very clear and free of flaws, one mistake could mess up your grade. He is respectful when asking him questions in person or online, but struggles when students don't get the gist right away.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: The lectures are too long with absolutely little to no participation that included the students. This class is designed to be where we can't survive if we miss even one class. The most frustrating thing was that he expected way too much perfection on essays more than any English professor. Worst of all he is the type to grade based on his emotions.

DO NOT take if you don't like to write. An intelligent man but not suitable to teach. Lectures are old-school and HEAVY, not for visual learners. Written quizzes carry your grade, no redos. Grading is harsh and doesn't inspire improvement. Must attend ALL lectures to pass. There are no breaks or flexibility, beware of burnout.

reviews.comment: DO NOT take if you're not a heavy writer. An intelligent man, but not suited to teach. Heavy lectures in old-school style, not suitable for visual learners. reviews.comment: This was the worst class ive ever taken UMBC. If you want dont have to take a course with him avoid it at all costs. His grading is really unclear and overall thumbs down.

reviews.comment: He was one of the best professors I encountered at UMBC. Amazingly informative and in depth lectures. I still think about his classes even years after I have graduated. I think he deserves a much higher rating:if you are in an upper level art course, you should be able to write about and analyze the art. One on one conversations I had were amazing.

This was the worst experience i ever had, if you cannot regurgitate what he says word for word about some random painting you will fail the class, his feedback is absolutely useless and he acts like he cares about the students but he's UNFORGIVABLE. If you can do not take a class with him. avoid this prof at all costs

If you value your sanity, DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS. If you aren't the best when it comes to writing, AVOID THIS CLASS LIKE THE PLAGUE. This professor is a harsh grader it doesn't matter if you understand the material or not. If you aren't able to communicate it in his eyes, he'll just give you a 5/10 DO YOURSELF A FAVOR AND AVOID THIS CLASS

Im sure that Dr. Smalls was once a well meaning person who cared and respected other people. This guy is more concerned with proving a point than actually helping students. He gives no true rubric and grades based on mood. If UMBC was graded on a letter scale, Dr. Smalls would bring it down one whole letter. One of the worst experiences of my life

If you love art history like I did, dont take this class. The concepts taught in 321 are so interesting, but Dr. Smalls and his plethora of writing assignments will drain the passion out of you. Your papers will be 10% content and 90% trying to write the greatest paper of your life. Dont do this class. Save yourself.
One of the worst teachers at UMBC. Do not take this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: The content he teaches is amazingly interesting to me and I love learning about it. HOWEVER, he is the most inconsistent and grumpy grader ever. This class is not about Art history as one would assume it would be. This class and the Professor is a upper level English composition class and an English composition professor. His feedback isn't helpful

Just don't do it guys. Don't even bother saying "he can't be that bad" because he can. The level of apathy is beyond your imagination. His teaching is horrible and this course is basically a writing class lv. 100. Your understanding of the materials doesn't matter at all, he only wants god-level writing.
bad.

Questions used for quiz papers are very ambiguous, but expects a very specific answer. Also, gives less than 12 hours to complete those quiz papers. Is not considerate to students and treats a history class as a master english class. All I got out of this class was anxiety and harsh feedback on my writing.

It says Art but Professor Smalls will make it into an advanced English class. Make one small mistake in one of the hundred papers he gives you, youre gonna fail. Good luck if you decide to take this class.

Genuinely the worst teacher Ive ever had. Dont take this class. You could have a close relative pass away and he will not care. Hes mean and inconsiderate. The assignments are easy and the class is easy , but you will not have a good time in any of his classes. He is not only bad at teaching, but terrible at showing any type of compassion.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: When we started the semester in person, I didn't think he was bad. Study every painting that you go over, and be prepared to give the name, date, and artist of everything you go over because he won't tell you until you which ones start the quiz). All quizzes are written- luckily online you get more time than in person, and it's obvs open book.
reviews.rating_tags: Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: The powerpoints have absolutely no info on them, he doesn't tell you whats going to be on the quiz, if you don't write the papers in a certain way he gets mad. you would think that at least during the pandemic he would be nicer but no he was not. I wanted to drop this class so badly, don't take it.. it's not worth it at all.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: He teaches Art history in the worst way possible. He wants us to write all the things he says when he doesn't even give us a Powerpoint of his notes and never tells us what the quiz will be on. He's such a tough grader, even during these times. Dude, there's an epidemic going on. Art history sucks when you treat it like an English class.

Never again will I subject myself to this joke of a class. I love movies like the next person, but he is the WORST grader of all time! The assignment was to write no more than 2 pages/week about these films and longwinded PDFs on BB. First 2 papers were As; he became anal with grading the rest. No clear directions on what he is looking for. Done!

Greatest professor I ever had. He is very educated and dedicates his time to teach his students. You must follow his guidelines and must concentrate when he is lecturing. Reason I love Art History because of Professor Smalls.

He's really into what he's teaching, which made it easier to learn the material. You definitely have to work in his class but you learn a lot. I'd say this class would be difficult for someone who is not interested in the subject. I'm not a great student, but I did well in this class because I am very interested in design.
Fantastic and in-depth lectures; makes sure you really understand the contexts and precedents for what he's discussing. Writing assignments are what's expected for a college level course.

NEVER TAKE THIS PROFESSOR!!!! This is a warning for you. He is suchhhhhhhhhhh a tough grader, i mean like really really tough, and gives no idea what the quizzes are going to be on. Even if everyone fails, he says too bad. He doesn't take attendence because you're paying to be in his class.
The best professor I've ever had. He gets very excited and he is a great mentor.

Dr. Smalls is a very intelligent man, who knows his stuff, and expects his students to genuinely process and understand his lectures. Even though most ppl found him difficult, he's actually not that tough if you FOLLOW HIS RULES, tie together different ideas and understand the main points covered in class.. One of the best professors i've ever had!

Had him for 335, and also enligh.-mod. he's strict, but if you just stay EXACTLY within his guidelines you will do very well. The thing about "gay propaganda" someone said is laughable, never encountered that at all. He's really knowledgable and intimidating but once you get to know him he's really not that bad! Don't be scared!!
DONT IGNORE THE MANIFESTO! hes hard on the object descriptions! his test are pretty easy if you dont skip class.

He really knows his stuff, and as long as you go to class and take notes on the lectures, and study for the quizzes, you will do fine in the class. No midterm, No final, just quizzes throughout the semester.

Best professor I ever had. Challenging classes to take with him, but if you embrace it you will learn for life. Write down everything he says, you will need all for the tests. Attendance mandatory. I graduated 10 years ago and I remember him with reverence and fondness.

I have had a lot of professors and this is by far the WORST one I have ever had! He is extremely arrogant and says "bad grammar and writing is an attack on him personally!" I passed my college level English classes with an A and he continually gives me 0's if any part is not how he wants it. This is Art history not English! DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS!

This man is a tyrant. He rules the course with an iron fist and is incredibly arrogant. He is one of those pompous intellectuals who criticizes others for not performing to the strict quality that he wants it done at. The worst part of the course is how strict he is with object descriptions, which only teach how to write pretentious redundancy.

The most arrogant professor I've ever had the misfortune of encountering. The object descriptions are the most tedious exercises ever, and they really have nothing to do with the class subject matter. He will belittle you and make you feel like the slowest person in the world. But he's the only one for this class, so if you need it, you're sunk.

If you are not good at writing and grammar he is not for you. Stay away if possible. Unfortunatley, he is the only professor teaching ART335 right now. He is arrogant and makes you feel stupid. He is one of the worst professors I have ever had!

Dr. Smalls made this class much more tedious than it needed to be, especially through the object descriptions. He definitely had an attitude at times, but if you went to him for help, he was usually reasonable. If you have to take a class with him, it's manageable, but be aware you're in for a headache.

The worst part of this class is the object descriptions.  Essentially, you are forced to describe increasingly complex objects without using any human-specific terminology, and without repeating any words within a paragraph.  He says that this is supposed to improve your writing.  All it really does is teach you how to write pretentious drivel.

He is very serious about the paper assignment.... I got a C- and then a C for the rewrite, I believe he really wants the paper to be spot on with all the grammar and writing style... wrote poorly written on my paper and it was very discouraging... I wouldn't recommend unless you NEED TO TAKE THE CLASS.

He is a challenging teacher but not impossible. The quizes really are not that difficult but you have to write down everything he says so bring your comp if you write slow. He expects everyone to already know what he is talking about and gets annoyed with questions. Stickler for grammer. Worse then any other teacher i have had.(including english)

He is really into his field, extremely intelligent. But he is arrogant, and doesn't understand when others aren't as brilliant at him. He will meticulously pick apart your writing. He made my class write one paper twice based on grammar alone. The tests start off easy but get very difficult. Write down every word he says and you should be okay.

James is s very nice man who can come across as pompous.  He is not that comfoprtable facilitating group discussions, but requires participation-this means he asks each person one quesion per week-and the discussion never really finds its onw flow.  Needs to work on that, but is very passionate about his interests.
Inspirational!
No Comments

everyone here is crazy.  this man is reckless, arrogant, pompous, and overall the worst teacher i've EVER had-- and I've had a LOT.  only take this class with him if you must, unless you have a penchant for depression and anxiety.

One of the best instructors I've had. A little chilly personally, but his enthusiasm for the topic is contagious. I love that he calls it exactly how he sees it, bluntly and without any remorse or apology. He's eloquent and passionate. Just enjoy him while you have the opportunity.

The only way to win here is to copy down his every word and memorize it and recite it on the quizzes.   IF you can master the quizzes, you can win the course, which I found easy - but only cuz I listened and wrote a LOT.  You are forced to learn here.
Makes fun of you for grammer mistakes because he believes highschools teach you enough.
A wonderful teacher, very knowledgable in the feild of art history.  Tests and assignments are somewhat difficult, but to the advantage of the student.
The worst professor I have ever had at UMBC. Just pray you pass and avoid interaction with her because you're going to regret it.
Sigh...take her if it your last resort.
Professor smith was amazing as a person, however as a professor she didnt give much assistance. You have to truly study hard in order to pass. She is a tough grader but its for the greater good.

Dr. Smith is an easy professor however we spent most of the time listening to her presentations for the entirety of the class. Her comments can be snarky and rude if she feels like you're asking her a redundant question. Doesn't really give off the warmest feeling. However, if you pay attention and take notes you will be fine.

While the material for this class was easy to learn, Professor Smith's extremely slow grading and unhelpful feedback made this class painful. Professor Smith also frequently cancelled class, which was frustrating especially due to the large amount of group work. It seemed like she did not devote enough time to teaching this class.

This is the worst professor I have ever had in UMBC. Gives no partial credit for written response, cancels class during a short summer session and expects the students to learn the material by themselves. I felt like that he wanted all the students to repeat his class so UMBC can make more money. I don't recommend this professor.

I never once knew what was expected of me. Please record his lectures, he never posts anything (including grades) to Blackboard, so take notes on what your lab report should say, he isn't going to repeat himself. We were all trying to guess what would be on the final- no study guide or practice exam. I'll never even know what I got on the final.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Critical info is covered in prep. Lab procedures are heavily modified and sourced from various materials, mainly verbal instructions during lecture. Grades/feedback arrive late, mostly during finals. Labs are interesting but lengthy, with high expectations for theory and application. Required notebook prep is time-consuming, often taking hours.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Smith cares about his students, has flexible office hours and is understanding when explaining concepts and quizzes. Lab TA does all the grading and we did not have any midterm or final, but in class quizzes were difficult. Pay attention in lecture because its all fair game on the quiz!

Hard preclass quizzes. Peers who took orgo2 a year ago struggled bc you needed to remember everything. Near the end, we were ahead of reg orgo2 lec by 1-2 weeks. Spec stuff in the first few weeks suck, the packets are lengthy and hard. Experiments almost always worked tho! Take notes during lec, he writes the mechs on the board and erases quickly.

This class is very similar to Orgo Lab I, however, in classes quizzes and exams are now completely FRQ. Lecture is mandatory and there are clickers, but they happened once. The lecture does not really help, it is just whatever tangent the professor wants to talk about that day. He is obsessed with NMR machines and color theory.

Canceled lecture half of the time, but did not offer material otherwise. Content covered in lecture was not available outside of class. Lab report grading was not exactly clear. Starts you at an 8/10 for your in-lab grade; impossible to get a 10. Midterm was really difficult, but final was better. Moved very fast in lecture.

Taking this course was a nightmare compared to 351L. He was very disorganized in his lead off lectures and often went off on unrelated tangents. He also made the quizzes and exams extremely hard for people like me who weren't concurrently taking the lecture course. Lab procedures were also often unclear.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Smith co-taught this course. They never uploaded lecture slides (which were dense so it was hard to get everything we needed to study), didn't consistently give study guides, didn't use blackboard so I had no clue what my grades were, and Dr. Smith even lost our exam grades that he had on his laptop. Topics were interesting though
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I am a visiting student for the summer and felt that Dr. Smith was a great representation for UMBC. His lectures were super informative, he was eager to answer questions, and his exams were fair. While he doesn't use Blackboard, he is still very easy to access by email and you receive grades back really quickly. Just make sure you attend lecture!!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: took a summer course and was by far the worse experience of my life. CHEM 352 was disorganized and there was not homework. Exams were hard for no reason. He gave us little resources outside of the textbook. Miss one question on the exam and you'll be lucky to get a C. Only cares about his research and not teaching.

BEST chem prof I ever had! Taking him over the summer was a great decision because it allowed you to learn the material without forgetting it. Do the HW problems and the test questions will come easily. Had flexible office hours, SI pass helped reinforce the material, and was very open to re-checking exams for grading mistakes. Highly recommend!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: He would talk about things in lecture that had nothing to do with the lab. He wouldn't post anything on Blackboard and would write all lecture notes on the whiteboard in the lecture hall. He would never tell you what he expects on assignments and you would end up getting points taken off all the time. He's so disorganized and scatterbrained.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--So many papers--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Smith is an amazing professor! So knowledgeable about Orgo and spectrometry. Go to lecture and take good notes as this will help you for the quiz/final. The quizzes are incredibly hard but the rest of the class is easy. Try your best to get a good/easy TA and an A is almost guaranteed. Final is really easy and is out of 110 points.

Dr. Smith was an absolutely amazing professor. His lectures actually showed applications of organic chemistry in every day life that were interesting as hell. Labs were engaging and entertaining. Everything about his class was extremely fair, he didn't expect us to know anything not explicitly stated. I would 100% take another class with him.

He is too specified in lab. He makes you put the most random things ever on every single lab report like mechanisms, reactions, and data charts even if it is not mentioned in the lab manual. It is tedious work and everything about it sucks. Also, he is really disorganized on backboard, not clear on what he expects from his students!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: Very passionate in his lectures, and you learn something interesting every time. One negative is that he spends very little explaining the reaction we will be performing in the lab, but the lab manual is good enough, and the procedure is usually modified when you get to lab. Overall, he overlaps with 352 very well which is great.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: The best Chemistry professor at UMBC. Grades only come from Exams, but if you go to class ( occasionally gives a test question in class), read the book, and do the problems he suggest you will do fine. Orgo is a hard class but he makes it tolerable
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Dr. Smith is friendly and enthusiastic about organic chemistry. He was rather disorganized with teaching and it was clear that it was not his priority. He doesn't always respond to emails. Make sure you keep up with your orgo studying because you will need it in lab and the information is cumulative.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: His exams don't reflect the ACS final and are all free response. He barely gives partial credit. Course is based solely on exams. There are no buffers. You fail one and could fail the class. Took 351 with Perks and Geirasch and learned so much more. He even told us that  he wasn't going to look at the final because he was confident in his teaching.

As a person, Smith is kind of nerdy and innocent. However, he is awful at teaching orgo. I learned absolutely nothing. He doesn't put any notes up on BB. Writes it all on the chalkboard. He doesn't really explain the reactions so you can connect it to the book. He didn't keep up with the book so it's finals time and we have to teach ourselves. UGH.

His boring lectures are awful. He only uses the chalkboard. You can't see it half the time and he blocks it as he writes. He doesn't make it clear what he is teaching and just writes random mechanisms. He goes slow on certain things and gets way behind. He refuses to look at the ACS final so he teaches unecessary things and doesn't cover everything
Man oh man this guy was the greatest

He takes the time to make sure the whole class understand the concept. 3 free response exams and 1 final. Second time taking orgo 1 and I feel like everything is making more sense. Also gives tips on finding the info quicker and easier. Really wish professors were like him.

I know him personally and he's a nice guy. Not the clearest teacher but very willing to help if you ask. No homework per se for the summer class (I didn't study as much as I should have) but basically, do as many problems as you can.

his lab quizzes are so hard. ridiculously hard. 2 credits but you will spend a lot of time for this course. also, lab as usual is run by TAs and they are very arrogant and rude. PREPARE to work hard and come to lab prepared...

Avoid taking this class when you have a full schedule and make sure to develop a good study group because Smith or the TAs won't give you enough info to do the work. Pre/postlabs are put out really close to lab time and usually after lecture rather than before so make sure you have a good stretch before lab to work on them.

Dr. Smith is a very good teacher; he's very enthusiastic about chemistry. It's important to attend class since we barely touched the textbook and exams are completely based on what he said in lecture. The material is difficult but the exams are fair. The only problem is that he's a ridiculously slow grader and doesn't put grades on Blackboard.

Dr. Smith is a really nice guy.  He really loves what he's doing and is incredibly helpful.  He loves questions and will make sure you understand everything perfectly.  Also, he doesn't believe in multiple choice questions, so don't expect those.  Lab quizzes were tough but he made the final a breeze.  If you can take Dr. Smith, definitely do it!

Great professor for lab! I like how he writes on the board during leadoff. His lectures were truly enjoyable. Talk to him when he comes and visits your lab section; he's really nice and helpful, and he'll probably remember you. He's really enthusiastic about chemistry and his research. Listening to him makes me excited about organic chemistry!

If you have to take Orgo 2, try to take it with Smith over the summer. Orgo 2 isn't easy by any means, but being able to focus on it over the summer in a shortened semester really worked for me. It's a lot of material that goes by fast, but if you keep up with flashcards, go to class, go to tutoring, and go to his review sessions, you'll do fine.

I took the class over the summer and it was rough, but I don't think I would have done nearly as well if it weren't for Dr. Smith.  He's awesome and he really loves the subject.  Take orgo 2 with Smith if you can.  You won't regret it.

I do by no means recommend taking CHEM 352 over the summer...although Professor Smith does his best to clarify any misunderstandings, the class goes by really quickly and so for most exams, you're struggling to keep 4 chapters worth of RXNs and mechanisms from jumbling together. The class averages are abysmal during the summertime.

Dr. Smith is incredibly bright and loves teaching this class. However, he writes very quickly across the board and you spend a lot of your time frantically trying to copy.      75% of my class failed this last semester. His tests are all free-response. YOu are only graded on the four tests.

If you need to take a chem lab, always try to take it with Dr. Smith. His lab leadoff's are very clear, concise, and organized. All quizzes and exams are fair, and most are relatively easy. Smith is very approachable, he has a good sense of humor, and he really knows his stuff. If you have a choice between Perks and Smith, take Smith.

His lectures are so boring. You don't need them at all if you're in Chem 102. His final is basically Chem 102, shortened dealing with a lot of Acid-Base titrations. Overall, it's a lot of work for a 2 credit class and the labs sometimes take forever. Pretty boring class but with a good amount of work, you can get a B.
Very clear with his lectures but gave unnecessarily hard quizzes. Approachable and willing to help students during lab. If you need help, I suggest visiting him during his office hours.
Mediocre. Really nice guy, really likes his chemistry, but really strict about rules and has a tendency to be condescending. lab quizzes are HARD.

He was obsessed with making the class harder than it should have been. It was a 2 credit Lab and I spent amazing amount of time on it. His quizzes were unnecessarily hard, and he could have made moderately difficult quizzes that still showed students learned the material. If it weren't for my lenient TA, I prolly wouldve gotten a C.

He is a pretty awesome professor. Very approachable and makes the subject really easy. Just make sure to study for the quizes, never really know what to expect. Always ask him what to study for in the upcoming quiz so that you are prepared for it before.

Very clear and helpful. He explains things in a way that makes it easy to learn and understand. I wish that I had the opportunity to take the organic lecture with him because I think I would learn better.

By far the best prof. in the department, and I wish I had the pleasure of taking Orgo with him. His lectures are crystal clear, and he is extremely approachable. The final exam was easy, he made it clear what he expected on reports, and I think he curved.

i took his chem102L chem351 with him It isn't thanks to him though, he NEVER makes sense in chem351 and you TEACH YOURSELF! i ended w/ a B, bc i had outside help; he assumes you understand everything orgo from day one. if you can take it w/ someone else.. DO IT!! i had Dr. Hosmane for orgo2 and orgo FINALLY makes sense. chem102L was easy though

This is not the easiest class, but it is definitely doable. He goes over everything that will be tested, but it helps to go back into the book and get more info. He is extremely helpful and is very willing to go over any problems that you might encounter.

I think he made it more tolerable than the 101 chemistry class I took.  I really liked him as a teacher but I still don't get chemistry.  Dr. Smith really is good about explaining and is really intrested in the subject.

I think he is a nice person, but you have to expect to meet really good TA. TA is grading all lab assignments, and he/she takes off a lot of points even if you got one wrong. They never learned to give PARTIAL pts... maybe it was just my TA... the final exam is pretty easy. Do the lab assignments well then you'll get an easy A.

He is the best professor in the department. Take classes with others and you will see what I mean. Its ORGANIC its supposed to be hard. He does an amazing job preparing his notes for class and goes over everything on exams. Read the book, learn reactions, and pay close attention/ memorize and you will get an A. I wish I had him for every class

very passionate about orgo and that is and UNDERSTATEMENT. he's a pretty good professor but sometimes makes it seem like we should be on his level with comments like "that was way too easy, come on you should know this" when we just learned something a class or two ago. other than this he really is a good professor. 3exams and final + ace organic.

He is very friendly and approachable. His exams are VERY hard.. but there is a trick to do well. During his lectures, he hints on what you "should" know for the exam and if you study/understand everything from his lectures using practice problems from the book... u will do good.

He's good at teaching but his tests are horrible.  I don't find the questions good since he will give no partial credits.  Take Perks instead.  The class average is low and I don't know how I am going to pass the final.  The tests are terrible.  Just hate them.

He's hot, cute, good looking.  but Orgo is not easy or I can say his test is sort of tricky.  You gotta be careful.  It's nice to sit in his class.  It's not too boring.  He has a charming, good charisma for 'style of professor'.  Is he married?  Does anyone know?

I'm in love with Dr. Smith.  Not only is he great to look at during lecture, he explains orgo SO clearly and makes something that can be complex into something so simple.  He doesn't trick you, he just wants you to understand orgo (once you do, it's kinda fun).  Very fun, very nice, very hot.  Four exams, final, with a curve.  ACE organic is 10%.

I LOVE DR. SMITH. He's amazing at teaching, and he's cute. His tests are free response,which in my opinion is easier than multiple choice (esp for orgo). I wish I could take all my classes with him =)

He writes everything down and does a good job of explaining things. dont need the book for his exams. tells you what you need to know, hard material, so the exams are hard. all free response. but he is a good professor, probably my favorite @ UMBC

the discussion sections are pretty pointless with the CPS not working for half the semester. his final is easy, though it is free response, just like his quizes. the only downfall is a bad TA, who messed up your grades, gives you a B wrongfully by losing papers you DID complete correctly.
Very helpfull, but just as far as your understanding.  Your entire grade depends on your TA.  Only test was the Final exam which was very easy! >85 is an A, but still got a B thanks to my awful TA.
Make sure to study hard for the exams and go to ever discovery.
He is a really good proffessor very clear but make sure you do the offline problems and GO TO DISCOVERY
Very clear with lectures.... gives good/helpful notes. exams are OK... need to study in advance!! ask questions... he's ready to help.

He is very approachable and seems to be very dedicated to the subject. He discusses till the very last second of class time and really wants his students to succeed and understand the course material. definitely one take for intro level chem! nice, friendly and pretty good looking for his age. lol

He is very approachable and seems to be very dedicated to the subject. He discusses till the very last second of class time and really wants his students to succeed and understand the course material. definitely one take for intro level chem! nice, friendly and pretty good looking for his age. lol

Dr. Smith is awesome.  He writes everything on the whiteboard along with you so that you have enough time to copy down the notes.  If you go to class and write everything he writes, then when you read the book, you already know most of the stuff it is saying.  You don't have to do a lot of learning from the book because he covers everything.
He is not as easy as everyone seems to think...you have to work to get a good grade in his class.  Very nice guy.

Well i think that smith was very straight forward and clear with what he said... yeah he does forget that were undergrads and loves saying "well this is common sense"... we all don't have phD's in orgo... but his tests are actually pretty fair and if you put in the work and the practice and make use of the free hour time on mondays, an A is do-able

The man is a Sheer genius.  So much so that sometimes he forgets that we're undergrads.  He goes through things VERY VERY QUICK and on pace with syllabus, and although the avg mean score of an exam is between 50-60% he expects you to know 100% of all information that precedes the current lecture.  You'll work your butt off for a C in the class.

Dr. Smith is a great professor, very helpful, good teacher, he teaches in detail and cares whether the students understood it or not, he teaches so in depth that the book is just an extra resource!!! he is a very good professor, and is very approachable!!  plus he's kinda cute!

i had P. Smith for Chemistry 102 and he always drew stupid organic molecules on the board and rambled ON and ON about how he was an ''organic chemist''. Now I'm taking ORGO LAB with him! Lectures are VERY boring, UNCLEAR with what we're supposed to accomplish in lab and quizzes / post lab and assignments are TRICKY! He still rambles too.

Very good teacher.  Doesn't teach from PPTs, rather writes on whiteboard very fast so you have to keep copying notes.  Tests are sometimes difficult, but if you study for them, you will pass them.  4 exams, 1 drop, 1 final, all 25%.  Nothing else, so just study for the tests.  Tests 1+2 are concept based, Tests 3+4 are math based, so prepare well!

He's awesome! I wish I could take all my chem classes with him. His tests are not tricky and its very easy to do well in this class. For him, no question is stupid so dont be afraid to ask questions. He has 4 tests in a semester and drops the lowest one so they dont cover too much material. Do the homework problems and go to lecture and ull do fine

With Dr Smith, you just have to go to class and do the recommended problems for each chapter. He teaches really well. He actually goes really deep in the concept, so you get it easily. The curve is pretty big too... (75% = A )
He's a really good teacher and very excited about the subject. He wants students to be involved in the subject. His exams are very fair and he is very approachable.

chem is def not my forte and i've taken the class twice previously, but i've finally found a prof that can teach!! Dr. Smith is awesome because he actually teaches the concepts in lecture rather than just talking. he goes at a good pace because he writes notes on the board. exams are fair as long as you go to class and study.

Best teacher you can have for Chem. He's very clear and good at answering questions (unlike Carpenter), but Chemsitry is a pretty hard course and if you don't practice the problems like crazy you will fail. Good luck. More coffee too.
No BS, if you're an idiot you will have trouble in his class. Put the hours in...
good teacher, he writes things on the board so that he won't go too fast. he explains things if you ask. good teacher and funny at times
he sucks....you wont have any idea on  how you are doing in the class until you fail
His grading system is really bad as well as his teaching style--take Perks if you can!!

Even though he never returned our quizzes back, and gave a kick ass final, he wasn't bad overall. Taught well. Very clear in what he was teaching. And Lab lecture was interesting because he is good looking
Orgo isn't easy, but he's one of the best teachers you can have for it.
Dr. Smith is awesome... the only chem class I've had where I didn't have to teach myself everything from the book... def the best chem professor I've ever had!
He glosses over material and tries to cram a whole semesters worth of material into one exam (watch out for exan 3. Otherwise he knows his stuff and will entertain questions during class.
No Comments

Professor Smith is ONE OF THE BEST PROFESSORS I HAVE EVER HAD:)  Very thorough in his teaching and extremely approachable.  the most 'willing to help' prof I have ever seen.fair and gives a week after exams so you can talk to him bout it.AWESOME PROFESSOR

Took this class in Spring 2024. Prof. Snyder is very concise and efficient. He explains everything well and the class is structured very simply. The class consists of weekly assignments due before class, and around five small projects (one of which is group work). Just read the textbook and do the assignments ASAP. It's easy, just a lot of work.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Overall amazing professor and an easy class. make sure you attend class and complete your assignments.

It is a lecture heavy class and attendance is required , but it is a pretty chill and easy course. Easy to get an A if you do your work and attend class. He is very nice and chill. I would take this class again if I could.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Snyder is a great professor, he very clearly cares about his students. The class is lecture-heavy, there is group work and in-class assignments. There are 3 essays in the semester, but he gives you a chance to revise them. There is a marketing strategy plan project which will be done throughout the semester in class, and a final writing series.
Go to class, do the work, and you'll get an A. Very straightforward, simple, and easy class.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Go to class and you get an A. He is an amazing professor, very caring and understanding.
Easy class, chill professor. Just do your work and you'll probably get an A.
Prof Snyder is awesome. He really cares about the topics covered in class and he's enjoyable to talk to. The class will be fun if you participate in discussions and stay involved.

Snyder is caring and really connects well with his students. This class requires a lot of reading however. Pre-COVID, I would print out my notes on each reading for the in-class quizzes. Quizzes were every class and you can't make them up. Post-COVID his class required readings and one page assignments each week. Easy, but reading-heavy for sure.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Caring

reviews.comment: He is down to earth and truly cares about students. A tip if you take this class, for notes, I only wrote quotes of his opinions on certain things and would put them in my assignments and got a 100%. If you are taking this online, easy A. In person, make sure you dont skip class, dont mind groups, and READ THE MATERIAL!!! Its comprehensible.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Participation matters--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: My favorite professor by far. Large assignments are clear and he is super open to giving feedback on drafts. He always has an in-class writing assignment at the beginning of class based on an assigned reading, and the lecture goes deeper into that topic. The assignments themselves are interesting but not difficult, and some aren't just papers.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Great guy! He made the class very fun and interesting. There needs to be more professors like him on campus.

Snyder was great, his lectures were always interesting and he seemed to have a really well-rounded understanding of everything he taught. He's more concerned with your learning than with grades, so as long as you do your work and show that you care, you'll do great. He literally lets you pick your grade at the beginning of the semester.
