One of the best professors I've ever had. He's very knowledgable about everything that he teaches and really cares about making sure you do well and understand the material. Highly recommend.

MCS144 is an easy A class and I would recommend it to anyone! Attendance is part of the grade, and lectures can be a bit boring at times, but the class itself is extremely useful to any college student. No tests and no pop quizzes.

Dr. Snyder is great with this class. He really knows what he is talking about and gets you to think in the class, but the assignments and all are a bit weird. The Facebook post and the assignments. Honestly if you read the book and actually do the assignments you will be fine. Overall he's okay.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: This class is a writing intensive course so be prepared to write. Dr. Snyder is super nice and helpful. He's not really great with names but he's there if you need help in the class. He's pretty laid back and makes jokes. Be prepared to read and  class discussions. He's a tough grader on papers. The class isn't super hard, but it does require time.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--SO MANY PAPERS

reviews.comment: Awesome and laid back teacher. Just about the least stressed out I have ever been taking a class. There is virtually no homework except for easy readings and actual projects which are clearly explained and given to you WELL in advance. Expect some one question quizzes on the readings which are very easy. Seriously, take this teacher. He is great!

Dr. Snyder is by far one of the best professors I have ever had the pleasure of taking. I have had him for multiple classes now and each time It was an easy upper level class. The man cares about what he teaches and is very helpful and understanding to students. Dont let my grade fool you, I slacked off. If not it was an easy B, almost easy A.

It's a social media class. To be honest, very useless and his lectures often have nothing to do with what we could do with social media. We had a whole class talking about selfies. It's painful. As a millennial, I could teach the class better than he could. Nice guy though.

His lectures are long and dry in this class but you will need to know them for the final, so take notes. There are no tests, only small projects and one long paper. He does make you do a big group project so start making friends quickly. Overall he likes it when you participate in class, but that does not mean you'll get an A. He is a TOUGH grader.

Nice guy overall. Lectures were dry, but the workload was just right. Beware of group projects, he's a stickler about those even when you're the only one doing work in a sucky group. He says "and the such" all the time.
Don't get me wrong, he's actually a pretty cool professor! However, you kind of have to appeal to things he likes, and give only the exact answer he is looking for, otherwise you'll never get an A.

Don't get me wrong, Dr. Snyder is a great teacher when it comes to lectures, but that's where it ends. Pop-quizzes are confusing and you'd be lucky to get credit for them (oh btw worth 20% of final grade). Papers aren't too hard but you need the book badly to write them. His grading, TOUGH. You could write the perfect paper and still get a 1012.

I would have changed my major to MCS had I taken this class earlier in college. Class discussions were very interesting and fun. Some classes were a bit dull but that happens with all classes. Dr. Snyder is very easy to talk to and cares a lot about this subject. The papers are not easy but not too hard as long as you actually put the time in.

Def a good class if you are an MCS major or interested in technology. Don't ask for help though because he is not that helpful and sorta lives in his own world. Also accused me of not doing my reading...so definitely read or at least look like you did...
Easy class if you just get the work done.He expects you to read and you have to write a lot of blogs,but hes a pretty easy grader and there isn't much studying involved.

Great professor, I have actually had him for 2 classes and both were excellent. He is easy going, informative, his lectures are interesting, and his grading is more than fair. the work load isn't very much either.
Professor Snyder is a great teacher and self-proclaimed "nerd."  He turns what could be boring lectures into interesting conversations with the class.

Snyder is a nice guy and a good teacher, he just needs to teach more. The class is insanely easy because the concepts are so simple and the majority of time is spent on mindless discussion. Anyone can input meaningless, self-absorbed anecdotes! This class needs more structure. Snyder is a good lecturer, he just needs to lecture more.

Easy professor, a little slacker-y.  This class was a little too easy for me to be very enlightening, but I'm sure that's not the case with everybody.  I don't know, I found him to be a little uninspiring, though very congenial and somewhat knowledgeable.  It's really a **** course.
You have to read a lot in the class, their are a lot of little quizzes and no test except final, not much notetaking and he makes class enjoyable
Nice guy but the projects are ridiculous, I have never done any project like this and have no idea what to do, praying for an A, I have one now but will probably get a B because of 1 grade

Donald is a really nice teacher. He will help you understand and make it throught the class. I have a small media class with him in a small room and he knows everyone by name. To me that is a good thing. I havent got a grade from him but i see that he will help anyone pass his class with a B or higher. Very nice guy and good to know.

I took the pop culture class in the summer term and he was really interesting to listen to and an overall friendly professor. He uses lots of different media to keep a 3 hour lecture fresh. Would definately take again.

easy class.. no text.. only problem is that assignments are worth very little (quiz=3pts, final=10pts). everything learned was from reading online. good teacher and know what hes talking about but should structure the class a little different
really cool.  knows subject well.  fun class.

I used to hate English class, but this class made me think otherwise.  It's pretty easy to pass; just do all of the essays/writing assignments and participate. Her reviews and critiques are very helpful. She's very approachable and nice to everyone. Definitely take her for ENGL 100.

This class bugs me. You will get a lot of conflicting reviews of your essay. on my rough draft I was told "I really like this thesis" but then on the final essay she said my thesis was too general. Along with this, the TA doesnt seem to read the essays, but she will still give harsh comments on your work.
Good professor. Just write the essays you'll do fine. Lab part of the class was useless.

I took the intro to creative writing and Professor Sneeringer really encouraged my creativity and furthered my interests in writing. She is a great professor who really loves what she does, and this passion for english is reflected back on to her teaching.

BEST CLASS EVER. I'm an engineer who likes writing and I never wanted to leave this classroom. Fun little writing exercises in class, 3 major essay assignments and just p/f reading responses for the rest (interesting reading too!) Encouraging environment, great teacher!
She was pretty good, but something in the way of her teaching reminded me of high school, which I obviously didn't enjoy. I ended up skipping a lot rather than doing mundane little exercises.
She definitely loves what she does. she is very understandable and she makes the class interesting. I'll recommend her to anyone
Great teacher, very nice & helpful. She loves what she does and as long as you go to class & write the 3 essays, you'll do good.

Basic English comp isn't that fun for anyone, but Sneeringer tries to make the class as interesting as she can. Easy assignments, some engaging readings, and she tries to get everyone involved in class discussions. If I was an English major I'd definitely take another class with her.
She is very helpful! Her assignments are really interesting also. Attendance is taken but her classes are worth it.

Sneeringer was one of the best english teachers I've had.  She was really helpful and made the class interesting.  Lots of class discussions.  I really recommend taking her class!  Getting an A is not difficult and you dont have to attend each class to get one.

Professor Sneeringer is one of the best professors I've ever had. She's very patient with her students and I've learned a lot from her. Very approachable and easy to talk to. Yes she gives work and you write a lot, but remember this is an English class. Take her if you can!
Great Professor. Easy to get an A.
Sneeringer is a good teacher. I enjoyed going to class and she isn't a tough grader.
Awesome teacher, really cares about her students and if you want to do well in her class (participate, come to class, etc) you will do just fine.
She was really helpful with problems, and usually fairly laid-back in class. Kind of funny too.
Excellent teacher who loves good opinions on reading material.  A lot of writing but it's great for practicing if you write a lot.  She's hot too. ;)

Just do your work and she's the kind of teacher that will help you tons and you'll get what you paid for, if you really want to learn. It's a lot of reading and writing but it's great if you're interested in the subject. Don't take her if you plan 2 slack
A poo load of reading and writing for her 100A class

i have had many professors during my education quest she is by far the worst. i agree with the other student that she expects the students to know as much as she does and forgets we are learning. she does any learning institution a injustice. please listen to the students she is a horrible educator

Tries to act interested in helping students when really she does not want to. Quizzes are more like mid terms, she changed the weight of the midterm grade to that of a quiz bc so many ppl did poorly which messes up the final grade. Ridiculous amount of work required for class. Expects students to know as much as she does, impossible to succeed

I hope by spring of 2010 there will be a new teacher that teaches this class. I truly think this teacher is clueless of what she teaches. Getting all these bad reviews are true. Synder is horrible, unclear, and use wikipedia too much for references.

This teacher does not enjoy teaching, helping students, and has no idea how to communicate this information. This class is not hard, but she gives no guidance, and therefore makes it really hard. I would not recommend this class, but unfortunately it is required for the major and she is the only who teaches.

This professor is awful.  She has no interest in teaching this class and her grading makes no sense.  The class average failed the final and she did not curve.  She does not care about the students or their grades.

I had trouble during her online class with turning on my camera and instead of caring, she told me to reread the syllabus, as if I didn't already read it. Her lectures are super heavy and you need to stop yourself from sleeping through them. Only good thing is class discussion and group discussions, which are enjoyable.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I strongly advise against taking her class. She's inconsiderate and sets students up for failure by contradicting her own expectations. Despite emphasizing the importance of participation she doesn't respond to questions and ignores student's contributions, she lacks empathy and understanding. Run far, far away from this class!

I don't know why her rating on here is so low, this is one of my favorite classes. She is a good professor! We had a midterm and a final with weekly quizzes and weekly virtual group discussions. You will have to keep your camera on during the entire class and participate.

Her mid-term and final were tricky, even knowing the information. She is super tough grader on papers. I've had better grades with strict Eng. Prof's. Be sure to participate in class. I felt like I over participated and didn't receive full credit. The exams and grading were unreasonable for an intro class. Do not under estimate this class.

The instructor's strictness and lack of flexibility can be challenging, as she seldom grants extensions unless they are for family or religious reasons. She lacks empathy and understanding. Furthermore, if you happen to miss even a single assignment, there will be no opportunity for redemption. In order words look elsewhere please.

Professor Spinney is amazing. She is strict about attendance, participation and having your camera on. The paper is semester long, plenty of time to get it done. Weekly quizzes. I enjoyed her class, she offered pre-recorded lessons and a power points. I would take her again if I could.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: She's a great professor. On the first day, she asked the class how she can help them pass this course (i.e. what she can do to help us). I never had a professor do that in college. She's nice, intelligent, caring, understanding, and most importantly wants you to learn through discussions. She will late you turn a paper late but takes 5 points off.

Caroline is the best professor I have had in college so far. She is so sweet, and genuinely cares about student's success in social work. She is very approachable, and is always willing to help. Take her any chance you can get!

Great class!! she's really a nice professor. She covers chapters every class so if even if you don't read you'll get in info. she's very clear with instructions for papers/projects... no midterm no final i wish she taught another class :( i'd take it
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--Caring

reviews.comment: I took Great Books 1. It was horrible. You will get a good grade but it takes too much work. She is a good teacher but acts like reading 200 pages a week is okay.

Dr. Spitz talks about art because that's what she's interested in but I found it boring. Also she asks very pointed questions and targets specific students. Only reading homework, all essays in class. Giggles and says "brava!" when you're doing well.

She is a great teacher! You read novels every week and discuss them during class. She is open to the opinions of others and is very passionate about the novels we read. I got to read so many children's stories like a Christmas Carol and Frankenstein. It felt more like free reading than homework. It's pretty easy to get an A in too. Take this class!

This is the hardest class I ever took. There is only a midterm and a final in this class and if you don't do well on them, you're screwed. She is very full of herself and if you disagree with her views, you won't do well. My advice to you is to run as far as you can. Don't take this class with her unless you want to fail. Find another section.

I thought she was a very fair professor and open to a lot of discussion. I don't consider myself a great writer or interpreter of literature but I enjoyed trying so I did well in the class. Read all the material and participate in the seminar and you should do fine. If you don't like discussing literature don't bother.

Walked in the first day and told us that "we will not learn any real world info in class, only inner knowledge."  Asks for your opinion, then dismisses it, regardless of facts, unless it agrees with her.  If you believe yourself very logical, avoid.

Overly dramatic and excessively demanding for a 200-level course. Insisted that students arrive to class 15 minutes early and leave 15 minutes late without regard for other courses immediately before or after. Has no tolerance for anything not done precisely the way she wants, yet is very hypocritical on a number of topics. Avoid!

Spitz is very hypocritical and doesn't say what she means. If you disagree with her opinions (even though literature is all about interpretation) she will garde you poorly. She has favorites and doesn't understand that her's isn't the only class we're taking. Not very approachable. A little self-absorbed.

She teaches her opinions as though they're fact, and doesn't understand what could possibly be wrong with that. She professes that there are no wrong opinions, yet routinely tells students they have misinterpreted one of her beloved texts. Also, she tries to add random French lessons to the class where they don't fit. She is an awful person.

Spitz is a tough, astute woman guised by delicate physical features. Don't let it fool you. Her class was the only class I have ever received a B in - and the class I have worked the hardest for.  I learned so much in her class that I would probably opt to take her again. One thing that some might find annoying, however, is her snobby tendencies.
She's a very tough grader and has favorites.  If she doesn't like you it will be tough to get an A.  However, she's very passionate and knowledgeable.  Don't get on her bad side.

Could easily play Professor Trelawney at Hogwarts. A little over dramatic occasionally but very passionate about the material she covers. She expects the best from you and makes this very clear. Allows you to do creative writing assignments for the midterm and final, which is just cool. Overall, a pretty good professor.

She's a tough but fair grader. She expects a lot of you, so don't take the class for an easy A. But you'll learn a lot, and you'll take a lot away from your experience in her class. I would definitely recommend her, but be ready to work!

At the beginning of our class, I was dreading the thought of spending an entire semester with Spitz.  But now that it is all over...I can say that she has been one of my most influential teachers.  She is tough because she needs to be.  But she really is there to help.  So take advantage of her wisdom.  She's doing it for you!

She's a very sweet woman and very intelligent. I doubt I would have enjoyed a lecture class with her as much, but I thoroughly enjoyed a seminar class with her. I never felt like she played favorites. If you don't do the work and put in the effort, she won't give you a good grade, period. She was very fair and had a lot of good insight.
If she doesn't like you, there's no hope for an A.  Good hope for a B, though.

A little crazy...ok, maybe very crazy, but a very sweet woman. She and I locked horns a couple times over politics and other issues, but she did not let that affect my grades. I'd hardly say she plays favorites...or maybe it was just she likes everyone in my class. Great woman - you just have to give her a chance.
This teacher let her personal prejudices govern the way she treats students in her classes.  If she doesn't like you, you will NOT get an A no matter HOW hard you work.

don't take this class. not only will you spend hours reading 100s of pages a week, but you also need to retain every mundane detail in order to get a measly 80% of weekly quizzes. the effort this class took should have been rewarded by a 400 level history class. this man shattered my 4.0 gpa.

Avoid this teacher. You will spend your entire time reading. He is a very hard grader. The quizzes are difficult and attendance is mandatory. Participation is required not by how many times you participate but the quality of what comes out of your mouth. He gets defensive if he feels like you are wasting class time.

Be prepared to read. And read. And read. You will not have much time for other classes, so be wary of that. The information is interesting, but the work is gruelling; unless you are fortunate enough to have no other classes at all to study for, ever. Also, you have eight texts for the semester, in addition to blackboard readings. Good luck.

Lots of reading. Be prepared to read at least 100 pages of material a week. Very hard, but very fair. He's willing to work with you if you don't understand things, and he is extremely interested in what he teaches.

She goes through a lot of problems, and goes through them really quickly, be prepared. The homework is also RIDICULOUSLY long, I would work on it with people if you can. Quizzes and tests aren't too bad, the final is very hard.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: She is rude, condescending, and always busy. Look the classes she teaches are some of the easiest class taken by engineers. However I am not sure why this women is the head of the engineering department. She is not a great teacher and is extremly rude to some people. Try to avoid her if you want to learn  but dont worry her classes are simple.

Not necessarily to the fault of only Dr. Spence herself, the ENES 101 class was terribly mismanaged. Due dates and assignment guidelines were extremely vague. The main group project is awful if you get stuck with a bad group, so be aware. Spence can be helpful if you ask, but never contradict yourself in front of her because she will pounce on you.

Her aerospace design class seemed less about designing aircraft and more about theory. Be prepared to have to do derivations of equations. If you can't stand derivations you may want to look elsewhere for senior electives. Answers to questions can be a little vague. That said, it's Dr. Spence and you can't go too wrong with one of her classes.

Assumes you're already familiar with most of the material- MATLAB, programming, statics, heat transfer. circuits. Doesn't explain complicated information well. Assigned homework that we were not properly taught how to do. Final was curved a lot. Don't need the textbooks at all.

Institutes "flip the classroom" which basically means she shows up for lecture with  next to nothing prepared other than a problem to solve.  If you're not going to teach the subject, what are you doing? She was helpful if you came to her though.

Even though I received an A, this class was not easy. Make sure that you know MATLAB because this is basically a programming class that incorporates numerical methods. Make sure you do all the HW assignments as well or it will bite you in the butt at the end. Good luck

Worst class I've ever taken. It's not that hard ONLY IF you are a whiz at MATLAB. This is less a Numerical Methods class and more a programming class. There is zero actual instruction, only assigned youtube videos. I study hard and have straight A's so far, but this will almost definitely be a C if I'm lucky. Absolutely hate this class.

She and Zupan co-taught the global engineering course, yet she did not do much of anything.  She sat back and let Zupan take control and just sent out emails every class.  This class would have been better if she had more of a say in it.  I have had her many times before for other classes, and she is a great lecturer.  Just not for this class.

Class always ended 30 minutes early at least (it's only a 50 minute class) because she just told us to go off and work in our groups. The exam was really easy but then the class didn't do very well at all on it. The project parts that were manufactured in the 3-D printer came out broken and most groups didn't even have all of theirs. Lab is tough.

The exams are easy, and she drops your lowest one. The only bad thing is that you are expected to know MATLAB from ENES 101, and nobody learned a thing about it in that class. She was incredibly shocked when everyone but two people in the class said they needed help with MATLAB. People failed because they didn't do the homework.

She is good professor, but you need to make things clear with her at most of the times. This class is fairly easy, needs a lot of effort to be put in. She helps a lot if you ask, but some times she would not answer clearly even if you ask again and again. Only few times it happens that way though. Work hard and get an A. No rocket science.

This teacher is not that bad, I think highly of her. Is somewhat energetic and you can be somewhat comfortable when talking to her. She might be a little bit blunt in talking back to you, but is still an above average teacher. Books weren't used much except for hw reference so far, and its past halfway through the semester.
Dr. Spence is a great teacher. Has real world experience to teach from. Very straight forward  to deal with. Good personality.

A fairly easy professor, though I imagine she'd be a lot more difficult in a more technical course. Uses real-world experience as examples a lot. She seems to be overly self-conscious about being a woman in engineering, though, and mentions it probably more than is necessary. Overall, I would take her class again, though.  You can do much worse.

Dr. Spence was a great teacher for Statics. All of her lectures were well prepared. She was always willing to help even with her seemingly busy schedule. She expected you to do your work and read the book(which she constantly said) Dr. Spence had a great attitude with lots of real-world experience along with a odd sense of humor. Highly recommended

lectures are kinda pointless but if you dont go ask someone if she made any important announcements. she expects some knowledge of physics. dicussion helps a lot and is mandatory. miss more than 3 and you fail the class. great sense of humor. pretty good professor
Best Prof I've had. Relates well with students. Great sense of humor. A natural teacher.
She seems to hold grudges.  Not very clear when it comes to explaining what is required especially on presentations of a project.  Her grading system is absolutely retarded.

The ABSOLUTE BEST TEACHER AT UMBC (in engineering at least). Not easy. Challenging. Has private sector experience to backup her lectures with good examples. Always does her best to be available to help you learn. The only engineering professor there that TEACHES (Charalambides is good too!) as opposed to getting a PhD and taking up space and salary
Great math teacher.  If you have a pulse, you WILL get an A in this class.  She is tons better then I hear the previous teacher was (*cough* CVK! *cough*)!!

I'm pretty sure this is not her fault, however when I came into this class I was expecting to LEARN something not get quizzed on stuff I haven't learned yet. Her lectures are based on the assumption that you've learned the physics behind the problems so it can become very frusterating at times.
WOW. Best professor so far. Everything is right there so you can get it, if your not too lazy. Always willing to help you. I cant wait to have her again!

She is an alright teacher.she is a nice person though and is understanding.what i dont understand is that she had bourner teach her classes for 6 hellish weeks.what was she thinking.that dropped her down
D Spence is a great admin, advisor, person.  Her classes though are unorganized...Ill concieved, and leave you with little learned at the end of the semester.
Great teacher.  Well organized.  Great explanations.  Extremely helpful.  Truly cares about her students.

She is by far the best spanish professor I have had at UMBC. The professor is caring and lenient. Learning another language requires work and dedication that are often not required in other classes; thus, there is a very large amount of homework to facilitate learning. Regardless of the professor at UMBC, the same work is assigned in 201.

Prof. Solano is probably the WORST instructor I've ever had for a language course. She added assignments last minute and provided instructions in spoken Spanish only in a beginner level course. I had to drop the class, I could not succeed with her as my instructor.

Every day on my way to class, I didn't stop at any red lights or stop signs in hopes that god would end my misery of this class. I would definitely take this class again... If I wanted to suffer. i am not a robot bofa dn.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Profesora Solano is very very nice. Well, at first she did not seem it but she is truly a caring professor and will really try to help you do well in her class. She does call on people, even if they do not raise their hand, but not in a way that will humiliate the students. It's to help us. I recommend taking her class. A good, solid professor:)

THe problem isnt her its the criteria shes required to grade by. They make the Spanish teachers grade students as if Spanish is their native language which is absolutely ridiculous. Part of me still feels like another teacher would've graded better She's nice and respected professor, class was pretty fun at times but the grading was too much.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: I really liked Professor Solano, but the course was hard. It's a lot of material and it does go fast so you're probably going to have to put in extra time. MAKE SURE YOU DO THE HOMEWORKS ON TIME. This will help salvage your grade. If you need help ask her, she really tries hard to answer questions.

I think one of the issues with Professor Solano is the curriculum. It seems that as an educator she is not getting much done (which she kind of isn't), but in reality, there is way too much being taught in this course for her to teach it properly and thoroughly, which is why there is such a crazy amount of homework.

This class was probably one of the hardest classes I've ever taken. She's quite literally not able to teach at all and when asking for help she gives a useless answer.way too much material that is very strictly graded and two IN PERSON graded conversations with extensive requirements.Avoid if you value your mental health and stress free lifestyle.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Amazing Professor!!!

SPAN 103 Review : All I can say is, take this class if you want an "easy A", but don't mind being lost the whole time. DO NOT take this class if you actually want to LEARN Spanish or plan on taking SPAN 201. She cancelled class a lot, showed up late, and never really graded anything with feedback so again. I 100% learn more everyday from Duolingo.

Professor is very good. She grades quickly, sets clear expectations, and prepares you for the exams in her lectures. Her rating would be much higher if SPAN201 weren't such a hard course. Highly recommend!

Professor Solano was nice and engaging, but I hated this class. The organization was very different from the past two Spanish levels, confusing everything. Oftentimes, the online assignments didn't match, so I had no idea which ones to do and ended up doing way more than I needed to. There were oral, written, and online exams, which were difficult.

This class was very difficult, but not because of the material. It was mainly because she was almost impossible to contact out of class. Assignments would be due and would not pop up until 2 days before its due, with no extensions. The class is very unorganized as well. 3 oral exams over zoom and camera is required. Overall, way too much stress.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: She was very easy going and a good conversationalist. Even if you made a mistake she is very patient with you.  I took SPAN 102 (n/a option) so for the summer I signed up for her online course SPAN201. I'll be honest, I don't study or practice too much but she is understanding. She makes funny jokes too! And she responds so my emails.

The students saying she was bad likely did not put in effort to do the work. Learning a language takes immense effort and active, diligent practice. You cannot expect a professor to walk you through a language to learn it, you must write, speak, and listen for yourself. Overall, she was lenient on assignments and very patient with students.

The students saying she is bad are likely not doing the work for themselves. Learning a language takes immense effort and active practice, and you need to put the work in to be successful. That being said, she is very lenient on assignments and is very patient.
Great.

Was very skeptical going into her class with the low rating she has on here but was pleasantly surprised. She was very caring for her students and was a pretty lenient grader over all. The worst part of this class was the excessive amounts of homework online, but other than that I'd recommend her.

This professor is highly disorganized in her formatting, unclear in her instruction, not attentive to responding to emails, and does not provide support for students when said issues occur. My class started out with 25 students and very quickly only 8 students remained due to the issues listed above. Not all grades were put in by the end of tern.

Every day on my way to class, I didn't stop at any red lights or stop signs in hopes that god would end my misery of this class. I would definitely take this class again... If I wanted to suffer. i am not a robot bofa dn.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Worst teacher and class Ive taken. The entire class was lost and had to redo assignments because the initial directions werent clear. Takes her months to grade exams and assignments. Cringe teaching style, picked on students in order of seating. I almost failed this class after getting As in previous Spanish courses.

Nice person, but she can't teach. Things had to be explained more than once bc they didn't make sense the first time. Things were always graded wrong and when you tried to email her to fix it, she NEVER answered or answered 1-2 weeks later with a vague answer that doesn't solve your problem. The class was chaos. Please take someone else.

her sweet disposition is all she has going for her. She is inaccessible by email, relies inaccurately on auto-graders, is late to lecture more than half the time and is never early, she will not communicate with you first, due dates and times are weird and change every week, and the class is generally hard. Only got a B because exam 2 was open note

She was an alright professor. I was one of the few people there who was actually okay at speaking Spanish but even I struggled to do well in her class. She's a very strict grader (if you make a small mistake several times it adds up quickly).
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: She caused a lot of undue stress in my life. Everything has to be done and submitted how she wants it, and she won't make it clear what that means. She has unclear grading standards, and will mark you down for any reason she can find. Expects too much from a mandatory intermediate Spanish class, and assigns a lot of busy work.
The professor shows little respect to students and thank god he has left our uni

Good lectures, but homework reading assignments were so overwhelmingly long that when he asked if anyone did them, literally nobody in the class said they did. Was able to adjust for this, however, and helpful in office hours.

Only reason I passed was cuz study group&ASIA100. He puts manuscript of text on each slide or just pictures w/ 0 information, talks nonstop for an hours& assigns 30-60 pages each night to read. Yet some how expects students to be able to answer the most obscure multi choice questions that's 50% of the grade in 15mins or less? AVOID SONGS HIST103!!!

Gives very good feedback, and got me very interested in further perusing history as a major. The advice I've gotten on paper's has given me a better understanding of how to write history paper's and research, which has been a huge help the following semester.

Prepares students for meeting the expectations of the work environment outside of school. Very easy to talk to and provides great feedback. Students that prefer only traditional lecture may be put off from the style of this class. Excellent instructor and would definitely enroll in a second class with this professor.

Knowledgeable, but arrogant. Sadly, this behavior influenced other students to begin acting the same way. The class was supposed to be a history class, yet the focus was on writing. Directions and objectives were unclear. He graded far too harsh, but gave better grades so long as you agreed with HIS point of view.

Focus on the lectures and skim the reading. He does not give tests and focuses on readings and group discussions. Homework assignment heavy and big papers are the main source of the grades. If they aren't done well, you won't pass.
Nianshen Song Professor in the History department at Vassar College, Poughkeepsie, NY same guy Bad professor, dont take, he will put you to sleep
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: I think hes very knowledgeable about East Asian history. However his grading criteria is unclear, and his feedback is short and not helpful at all. Comments like logic weak without any further explanation. I asked to meet with him before the final and he brushed me off. Thanks to extra credit I barely passed. Dont take him unless you have to.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Easy A if you've taken a college level history class before, only 3 test including final and midterm, Criteria for test very clear-post outline on blackboard, gives random take home or group quizzes in class that he tells you to just google answer to, post lecture ppt online, fault: gives written assignments that are ambiguous in Chicago format

Does not communicate his goals for the class clearly. No feedback on your writing to know how to improve. His expectations swing back and forth with no warning. Open note exams, but he looks for ways to deduct points that arent associated with the assignment. Dont take the course unless you absolutely have to.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Dr. Song is extremely knowledgable about history, particularly Chinese history. If you want to learn a lot, take his class. His classes are reading heavy, but you will be able to glean a lot of info from the interesting, relevant readings. Highly recommend the class, but be ready to do a lot of work. If you do the work, it's not hard to get an A.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Get ready to read--Would take again

reviews.comment: Straightforward class, not the most interesting but not hard at all. Squire holds online lecture with hw due every week and a midterm/final.

A piece of cake. Some of the shortest lectures I've ever gone to. Gotta put in a bit of time for HWs but not much. The project took 2 hours to finish, he apparently curved 1/3 of the class to an A. One note, he definitely misunderstood student questions frequently. Emails replies from him read like total gibberish, might be better during in-person.

Class is essentially at your own pace. Easy A with minimal effort as long as you try. Content is not hard and you probably won't ever see/hear Squire now that the class is asynch. Great elective to take with harder CS core classes.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: This man is awesome. He makes the class easy. The homeworks can be challenging but you can ask for help always and whenever in his office hours. The first three projects can be tricky but again he helps in his office. If you want an easy A & a stress less class, take him.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Very easy class with very straightforward professor. Tests very simillar to practice tests. Open notes. HW and projects easy.
Avoid unless you know VHDL. Won't assist you past the first part of the project. Everything else is easy but you will only get a C if you can't do the projects. You will not learn anything.

If you looking for easy way to pass cmsc411,take his course. exams are 99% same if you go to the exam review. HWs are really simple if you spend some time searching through his note/google. Projects is the hardest which is not very challenging. I doubt any can fail in his course. Easy A with effort.

I don't understand VHDL but managed to finish all homework and project except the last part(project was divided into smaller projects). You can email or ask after class when you are stuck. I think he curved our final exam too.
Great professor! Even though the project s are a lot harder than the midterm and final.

He is pretty easy grader and most projects aren't technically due until the end of the semester (I do not recommend starting them so late since you have 5 projects to do). His lecturers are a little boring and he uses a lot of old code that he sometimes needs to look at again to figure out what they do. His exams are pretty easy.
Lots of homework. Curves heavily. Didn't finish parts 2a, 2b, 3a, and 3b of the project and bombed the midterm and final leaving me with a 62% but I still snuck in with a C. Would def take again

Wasn't as easy as I expected. The most challenging thing about his course is that he has been recycling material for over a decade now. The lectures, homework's, and projects are vague. At times he can be very rude, and at times he can be helpful. Be sure not to put off the projects until finals week. No late penalty for submitting late homework.
Classes are boring, tough and late grading... Get ready to warm coding skills before semester starts. Otherwise hard to catch up !

Professor Squire is an awesome guy and very knowledgeable. His classes are never the most rigorous but he's often teaching electives so they don't have to be. Exams are multiple choice and coding projects are very manageable. If you're swamped with classes and need to fit in a CS elective any Squire class will be a joy to take.

Nice old guy, really smart. Unfortunately, he can't teach. At all.  He is very helpful on his projects. If you go to him for help don't be surprised if he basically finished it for you. He also might not help you at all (rarity, but happens). If you want a grade, take this guy. If you want to learn, avoid at all costs.

I took Numerical Computations with him. The class is super easy- 3 quizzes that are open notes (and he gives a study guide with all the answers), 6 homeworks that he practically does for you, and one project that isn't much harder. His lectures are well organized and he has code samples in a ton of programming languages. Very nice guy.

Assignments were easy overall. However, at the end of the semester, he changed his grade breakdown from what the syllabus originally said. His grading was really inconsistent and many students received grades lower than they actually earned. I would avoid this professor for this class.

Assignments are extremely easy because he practically gives you the answers. The later assignments get a little harder, but they are all doable. His lectures are extremely boring though and all of the notes are on the website. I didn't do as well on the tests because of not getting the material in class.  I hear he curves generously though.
Dr. Squire's Hardware Course is pretty simple and straight forward. He does everything he can to help you pass the course.

Notes/lectures on the website. HW and projects get progressively harder. HW eventually strays away from the notes, so it gets frustrating to find answers. Can be rude on random days. Exams are multiple choice. Just study off the past exams he gives. Curve is dependent on how smart the top 1/3 are as 1/3 gets A. No guidance on Proj after part 1.

He is easy. You will pass, but he is EXTREMELY rude. If you are in the class to actually learn, forget it. He will tell you the answer and if you ask why, he will say don't worry about it. If you just want to pass with an A or B, take his class. If you actually want to learn, don't.
This class was a breath of fresh air for a summer course.  Nice way to wind down the year.

Tries to make things easy, material is difficult at times. Uses poor wording on assignments. Class has a 5-part project: the first 3 are fill-in-the-blank, the last 2 require some knowledge/thought. He refuses to help on the last 2 portions but will give the answer to the first 3. Math-based, multiple choice exams with approximated answers.
TAKE IT WITH HIM. WORK A LIL BIT AND YOU WILL GET AN A

I highly recommend Professor Squire for anything you can take with him. He goes over exactly what he expects you to know for every assignment and is extremely helpful in office hours. He even tells you straight up that the tests are made to be easy.

He's nice, but his teaching skills leave something to be desired. Homeworks require some mulling around on the website or textbook to figure out because lectures aren't that helpful. Luckily the "projects" typically involve 20 lines of code max, and practice exams are almost identical to actual exams. Plus he gives 1/3 of the class an A.
There's a reason why his sections fill up immediately

An easy professor, if that's what you want. I wished I'd learned more in his class. He tells you exactly what he expects, and exactly how to do the homework (down to showing you where to type) which makes it less than difficult to do the work.

Squire is an excellent professor. His exams were fairly easy; just memorize the old exams that he gives you as a guide. Also, his homeworks and programs are not that difficult. If you do really well on his exams and attempt at the program, you'll be guaranteed a B.
Very good instructor, makes it very clear what the students need to know and does not burden them with unimportant busy work or unneeded information.

take him !!!!  U shud wait untill he teaches coz its the easiest cmsc class u evr take... Imagine a class easier than CMSC 201. Thats what it like.. HE gives out his questions before both exams so all u gotta do is memorize them.

The class is extremely easy.  You do not need to go to class, he passes last year's midterm and final exam back with answers the day before tests, and if you're a CMPE then you've seen the course content before in 310.  And the project is cake.  He practically gives you the code.

Great teacher to take this course with, he explains everything and will sit with you for hours in his office if you do not understand something. His class is weighted so its easy to do well. He prints out all the slides so you can make notes as you go. Start the project when you get it and see him for help, its in phases so its not difficult.

Excellent professor; explains assignments in detail; makes expectations clear; going into each class I'm not entirely sure about the material, but I leave each class w/ a very good understanding of it. Would take him again.
a third of class gets A's.  Not so much work (as CS courses go). Must take!

The absolute worst professor to teach this class. She has a complete stick up her about doing anything that isnt the way that she taught it. If she suspects anything your automatically screwed before you even have a chance to say anything. She asks the most vague questions on exams, and then makes them worth the same amnt of points as coding parts.

IS472: nice prof, but doesn't always seem like she wants to be teaching. Most graded work is done in linux with java so if you're good at that, it's a nice class. Exams are easier than expected. quizzes are the opposite, 5Q, 5 mins. The better you are at java, the less interaction necessary with her, and the easier the class seems. very mid class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: She is a strict grader, and I would not recommend her. She expects students to master five coding languages in a short period. My experience with her was very negative. Instead, I suggest taking a class with Samson Oni. He is more lenient and an excellent teacher.
She is hard grader.
she is awful. She is the worst. Don't take her.

I had a very disappointing experience with Professor Sreedevi Sampath. She is an incredibly slow grader, and you don't know your grades until the end of the semester, which makes it difficult to track your progress and improve. She also deducts points for the smallest mistakes, which can be frustrating and discouraging. Heavy group projects.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Group projects

reviews.comment: The course is rushed, covering HTML, CSS, JavaScript, PHP, and AJAX all in one course. You will get very little time to finish homework. You'll likely need to learn most of the material on your own, as retaining much from the class sessions will be challenging. For the group project, poor group participation will negatively affect your grade.

Don't be fooled by the positive comments, she is legit awful. Very tone deaf, not understanding, slow grader, all the material was rushed and didn't feel like you learn anything. Unless you like to learn 5 languages in one semester I suggest not taking this class

Expects students to be on point. The material is certainly manageable, but if you can't stay on top of the lectures, I wouldn't recommend. That being said, you will learn a lot if you can stick with it. The group project will be a challenge depending on your teammates.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment:
I took IS740 under her. Although it might show the course as CSXX because the dropdown doesnt have IS740 option.
Anyway the professor tries to put efforts into teaching which was appreciable however the learnings are difficult to grasp. The grading was generous in my opinion. Other than assignments there were some class quizzes too.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Took this class as a third programming language and considering this was a brand-new concept for us, the professor did not do a good enough job teaching the material. This course is/was a grad course and professor did not make it accessible enough for undergrads. She's a tough grader and cuts points on things that we don't even get to fully grasp.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Beware of pop quizzes--Tough grader

reviews.comment: She will be your worst enemy during your time learning with her. She teaches directly from the slides provided to her from the publisher so no effort whatsoever from her end. The pop quizzes will really get you hard and I don't understand why graduate students need pop quizzes.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Great class and prof, will learn a lot. Lenient grader and manageable workload. Group project is pretty interesting.

IS448 with Sampath was one of the best decisions I have made for an upper level IS elective. The material you learn is incredibly valuable if you have minimal web development skills. I'm not sure why this course inst required for IS majors considering how much useful information there is in it.

I really don't like programming, but she's a good teacher. She's always willing to help, which I found useful during labs. Tests were challenging but not too bad if you study, and there was one group project. She's easy to follow during lectures, and encourages questions. Homeworks were time-consuming, especially near the end of the semester.

If you're not a strong programmer, this class will be tricky. There are weekly homework quizzes that are open-book. Dr. Sampath is more than willing to help you with projects & in-class tutorials. Exams are administered through Blackboard & are mostly multiple choice, but they can be tricky. This is definitely a useful and interesting class.

She seems uninterested, but actually she really cares .. . a lot.  She's very nice, the assignments are very doable, but not easy.  She challenges you just enough without you wanting to kill her. She's also cute for an IS professor and if you have the guts to bring it out of her, a pretty good sense of humor as well.

Great Teacher, but I hate programming. I only took this class to gain insight for some of the languages. I absolutely hate programming with a passion. I know how to code so I did all the homeworks perfectly but I bombed all the exams cause I didn't read the questions (yeah I hate it THAT much). If you get 70s on exams and A's on everything else, B.

This prof. is very nice. Her lectures are pretty clear & she's very easy to approach w/ questions. There are 3 exams, about 6 HWs, and weekly quizzes.  Exams, HWs and quizzes all weigh pretty evenly and she's a pretty lenient grader. Her lectures were helpful & the labs included helped alot with the HW. Attendance weighs on participation.

Just unhappy about her... U can read her prior posts and think she hot but she not. Don't be a fool and rush for her cls cause ppl said cute stuff about her! Half posts seem fake and actually are. Make sure u read the ones who make comment with registered acct
She was very helpful when students need help - she is sometimes difficult to understand during lectures. Fair grader.
She's HOT! Must be the hottest Indian professor I have ever seen :). She is a good teacher too, answers questions clearly, responds to emails quick and exams are good assessment. VERY GOOD

One of the Best classes I have ever had. Assignments were tough but if you attend all classes, it will be a piece of cake. She is very HOT in her jeans. I never missed her class. Would definitely suggest taking her class.

She is probably the best programming teacher that I ever had at UMBC. She's detailed with object oriented programming and teaches from the ground up. Just do the homework and start early on the project and the class should be easy. This is definitely one of the most useful class to take as an IT major. Great teacher! A++

She doesn't do a bad job teaching. She likes to stand over you when you are working on in-class examples. I hate that. the quizzes are a bit tricky, the exams are straight-forward, and the homeworks are fine as long as you give yourself enough time to do them. Its probably a good idea not to miss many classes.

Weekly quizzes and in-class exercises.  Homework is weighted heavily in this course but is fairly straightforward.  Exams can be challenging so really study the notes and book.  You should be able to get an A or B as long as you put forth some effort on the quizzes, homework, and score decently on the exams.  Class material is interesting!

Had her for 333, wasn't an option. Very sweet! LOVE HER! You'll learn so much about Indesign features and organizing your files better. You'll also have fun projects that look great when printed. Prepare for many visits to Commonvision. She helped me with honors course by contract as well! Great choice for that!

My favorite professor so far, she's super nice and incredibly helpful within and outside of class. She has an incredible passion for graphic design that infects you. She doesn't really say much during critiques and mostly just has the class share their opinions, but you can always ask her for more in-depth critiques outside of class.

4 projects total, and newer programs were introduced. Manage your time well bc you have to learn programs outside of class on top of your project. She gives slight critiques in class and only provides feedback on BB. Even then, she repeats her project sheets and doesn't give valuable critiques. She writes, "student did [project sheet requirement]"
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Inconsistent feedback and grading criteria, and doesn't even give feedback in person (only adds in blackboard). She also didn't grade 2 out of the 4 projects of the entire semester until grades were due. Projects also tried to cover too many new Adobe programs, which made it difficult to learn the material and finish the projects in time
Super funny, excellent professor, very understanding, and clearly cares deeply about his field of study. Wants his students to learn and succeed.

professor suri is amazing!! you can really tell he's passionate about getting students to like math lol. so accommodating, always gave opportunities to correct work, & explains concepts thoroughly if you don't understand at first. lectures can get a bit confusing but if you just pay attention, take notes, & make an effort then you'll be good

Dr. Suri is a good professor, this was a writing-intensive course. Attendance was required. There was a lot of reading and a multiple-choice reading assignment before each class. Only had two major papers and a final group project/presentation. Class is basically a discussion about the readings. Just stay on top of the work and you can get A or B.

Dr. Suri is a great professor. I've never been good at math and was hesitant about taking it, but he made this class fairly easy for us. There are assignments due each class and in-class work as well, but he always goes over everything. He gives many opportunities to fix mistakes. Also, he is a lenient grader even with exams. Highly recommend!

Dr. Suri really cares about his students understanding the material. He makes you work for your grade but doesn't hold students to impossible standards. If you work hard and reach out to him for advice, you can easily do well. I went from failing 301 exams with another professor to getting As in his class. The two finals he offers help immensely.

Awesome professor! This is a writing intensive class, but we only had 2 major papers and a group project. Lots of reading for homework, then group discussion in class. Suri was really interested in each student and wanted us all to learn and pass.

His literary work is quite inspirational, he was not a very helpful professor.  I would check my homework answers to the solution  manual and he'd  mark them wrong. I had TAs from other sections look through exams (which he failed me on) and they said I deserved around a B every time.  I'm a good math student and even office hours didn't help here.

Best professor I've ever had. I missed a lot of class and he worked with me the whole time. He's always open to different viewpoints and methods, and all he really cares about with grading is that you understand the material.

Great teacher, his lectures are very informative and he tries to mix in some humor. He grades tough, but fair, and he gives 2 finals where you can choose the best of the two to count towards your grade.

It's a tough course, but then Dr Suri goes way far to help learn. Weekly (graded) hws and quizzes were pretty helpful for exams. 2 finals were given so that u've chance to do better on 2nd if 1st didn't met ur expectations. Exams were from important theorems and sample questions were made available and discussed beforehand. Avoid Potra (terrible).
Not an easy class, but lectures are good and he knows the subject matter well. Be prepared to work.
One of the Best,But not easy. Do care about student grade, and helpful. The guy is famous you can find him on wikipedia.

One of the best and most patient professors I have ever had. Incredibly knowledgeable and willing to help. Highly recommended for math majors and such... Do not assume a class will be easy based on the class name. Overall  a great teacher.
he is very concerned that everyone should do well, and goes out of his way to give extra credit, exam make-ups, etc. made a very hard class (math 301) manageable.
Smart men are hot!
it helps a lot if you have knowledge of calc coming into the class.  if not, i can see how you could become lost quickly.

It is obvious that he is very smart.  He also posesses a subtle humor.  However, he tends to assume you know a lot of math to begin with and doesn't typically explain things with much depth.  As opposed to my AP calc teacher from high school, he primarily works problems on the board, rarely explaining methodologies, reasonings, and theories.  Hard.

I have never commented on a teacher before but I had to save everyone from this one. He makes the material harder then it has to be, does not explain things clearly and really does not give a damn if people understand the material or not! Be aware be very aware!
I took math100 with him and I thought he was awesome. He made everything clear that I've trouble with in the past.

He is the absolute worst professor EVER. If u are given a choice take Song instead. i took this class my freshman year first semester and half the people failed. Even though he gave some extra credit assignments, the stuff he teaches in class is much easier than what he gives on the quizzes and so most people didnt do well.

He's hard to understand (him being foreign), and I felt he taught the material as if you already had a great understanding of calculus (which not many people do at Calculus I).  I had to drop his class for fear of failing.  Beware he is tough.  Also you have to turn in your homework every week for a grade, as well as having a quiz every week too!

I love Frau Sutton! The flipped classroom approach is unique, but she genuinely wants you to learn and enjoy the class. She's super kind and breaks down barriers many professors struggle with, focusing on long-term learning, not just exams. She pushes you to be the best student you can be. I'd love to take her again!
Don't take this professor, she is not kind to those students who tick her off. It is extremely easy to do that, and it will cultivate bad mindsets.
Frau Sutton was not only rude and hurtful, but she would single out students and make them feel bad for just trying to learn. I feel bad for anyone who has to take her.

Wonderful professor! Although others might not work well with her style of teaching, I enjoyed the class and her passion for the subject matter. I would definitely take again and recommend her class to other students.

Frau Sutton is a bit harsh but its because she has expectations for her students. She's good at explaining concepts and she speaks German through the whole semester. Participate a lot because it is part of your grade. Class with Frau Sutton was overall fun bc we learned about German culture & language. Quiz, essays and tests are straightforward
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Frau Sutton is knows her stuff and is good at communicating it. She's funny and actually makes me look forward to going to German class. She sometimes calls students out and can be a little harsh but it's not so bad as long as you don't take it personally.

Sutton knows her stuff and is good at getting the class involved. She is VERY approachable, will admit when she is wrong, and is willing to work with you. However, she can be a little harsh on students. If there's a misunderstanding, it can be a mess. But still, good teacher. I'd take her again.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: You're given a bunch of assignments every week so that you retain the information from lecture. It's a lot of work, but easy

Good professor, will make sure you know the material and is very approachable. Makes a foreign language a lot less intimidating with her teaching style(focusing very heavily on one specific aspect of the language at a time and building a pyramid with that). Would recommend.

Great professor. If you keep up with the work it isn't too much to handle. She's a very fair teacher, as long as she knows you are trying (having the homework done/volunteering answers) she will meet you halfway. She is very encouraging, asks students just to try even if they are unsure, and doesn't make you feel stupid for getting things wrong.
Fairly easy teacher. However, she expects to to learn certain concepts all on your own. We just took a quiz on concepts we didn't even speak about in class.

It's easy to get an A AS LONG AS you go to class and study. There is always homework and you use the textbook a lot. You can't skip class and do no work and do well. It doesn't matter if you ace the exams if you don't go to class and ignore your homework. I personally really liked her.

Very good instructor. Attendance is mandatory for topic familiarity, quiz/exam content, and because attendance is graded!  She is very helpful, but don't expect an easy A.  Like any foreign language course, it takes time and effort, and a lot of studying to do well!  Also, the textbook is used every class!

If you get off on a bad foot with her (even in a different semester), she'll hold that grudge against you until you're finally done with her class. I managed to assuage her condescension a little bit by actually impressing her by knowing the material, but it didn't count for much in terms of grading

Tests have some things on them that just drain points. She has a short fuse with people not knowing the answer or not speaking complete German. She is very helpful though. She will make every effort to help you. Papers were easy, tests were okay, and homework was all in the book. Final project isn't very fun though.

I have really enjoyed having her as a professor. She keeps the students engaged and her enthusiasm makes it easy to pay attention and absorb the information. Her grading as been really fair and the tests haven't been bad. You just have to study! She is also more than willing to help you outside of class. I definitely recommend her!

She definitely has her favorites and makes it apparent by giving them different guidelines. Very harsh grader. Expects you to know all vocabulary at all times. If you are unsure, she gets very angry. Puts useless things on exams that just drain points. If Romy Jones is available, take her class.

She's an okay teacher, but doesn't explain anything. She will assign major concepts for homework and just expect you to master them overnight. She gets frustrated if you answer a question incorrectly and definitely picks her favorites, making it very clear who they are. She will call you out if she sees you not paying attention. NOT an easy A.

I LOVE HER. She's fabulous. Probably the best teacher I've ever had. I'm a Modern Languages and Linguistics major, but I just added German to my French concentration recently. She's helped me understand the language so much, even though I'm already busy studying another one. I highly, HIGHLY recommend her.

First of all, her name is Susanne Sutton. She is a bit unfair on participation grades and maybe as a whole. There are a couple of people in 201 and some of us wonder how they got there?! They even wonder! All that aside, she is one of the best profs I've ever had.

Had her for 101 and 102, and I'm glad I did. Excellent foreign language teacher. Teaches by association, rather than memorizing translations, using pantomime to demonstrate new vocabulary. Very helpful if you need it. You will need to study, and there is a fair amount of out-of-class work required, but if you put in the time you WILL learn German.

Dr. Sutton is an excellent German teacher. She knows how to teach English speakers. She is very helpful and the tests really aren't that bad. Just show up to class and do your work study and you will pass.

Even thought, her guidelines for teaching German is the same as Germ 101. The work gets more difficult and the grading gets more tougher. Participation grades are unjust. If you are not doing well, she calls on you less and grades how she sees fit.
We are on the last chapter and we are learning food

Excellent professor--always willing to answer questions and to work with students outside of class. Yes, she does assign a lot of work, but that's what you should expect from any entry level language class. Do the homework, memorize vocabulary, and pay attention, then the tests are a breeze.

Frau Sutton is awesome. She's funny, interesting, and challenging, which excellent teachers are. If you aren't going to put effort then you will fail. Yes, you will actually have to study. This professor is for people who really want to learn German. And the vocabulary isn't even that hard because she's so funny that it stays in your head.

I loved Frau Sutton. She is the epitome of German-ness so be prepared to be held up to strict standards. Very swet and helpful, she is always happy to help. Learn your vocab, and as long as you try a little and put forth some effort in conversation, she will grade you fairly. Exams/quizzes are from the textbook.

I don't know what everyone's problem is that has rated Frau Sutton. OH NO! YOUR GERMAN TEACHER SPEAKS IN GERMAN IN CLASS!! HOW WILL YOU EVER LEARN??!?! The class is hard, but college isn't supposed to be a walk in the park. Take the time to actually study and do your homework and you'll be fine.

If you like German, you'll like Frau Sutton. If you're just doing it for a GFR, take Spanish or something easier, or learn 101 from Dr. May or Dr. Wolff. Frau Sutton takes no prisoners, but like I said, if you like German, then you'll appreciate her class. Oh and I actually remember her vocabulary..but she COULD do more in class-like drills.

Frau Sutton is there to teach German and that is what you are going to have to learn in her class.  The other complaints don't really seem fair: they all chose to attend a "medium sized honors college in Baltimore" where there is a language requirement.  Sutton does give lots of homework but she will also listen to reason, so work with her.

i've had sutton for 102, 319, and 301.  she's very nice, helpful, and clear, though she can be a strict grader.  and by the way. . . stop complaining about having to learn so much vocab.  how on earth do you expect to learn a foreign language if you're only learning one word at a time?

She expects you to know a lot of vocabulary words.  So long as you study the vocab and pay attention you'll do great on the tests and quizes.  She's very helpful when you get stuck on things or if you have a question about anything german. Great teacher, very fun.

She's nice enough, and approachable, but as other people said, she expects a lot out of you, especially for people who just want to get the GFR and get out.  She gives directions and occasionally starts teaching in German... which isn't very helpful if you're trying to learn German...

If you're a German major, then she'll be right up your alley. If you're like me, an engineer trying to squeeze by in a foreign language, she's a little rough.  She expects A LOT out of you. You will spend hours memorizing vocabulary for tests which will be promptly forgotten by next week. And she expects you to be fluent, which is ridiculous.

A fairly good teacher.  She definitely knows German very well and can explain it well.  However, she expects a lot from you early on.  She expects you to be very fluent with speaking and hearing, especially during her oral quiz.
Great teacher! she really knows her stuff, as should she, as she is from Germany! her tests are a bit formulaic, but still they help tremendously, 15% of grade comes from coonversation class

Very chill professor and very accommodating. Exams tested on common sense statistics and assignments in JASP were easy to complete. It is clear that Dr. Swan cares about his class and the field as a whole. Outdoors component was a nice break from lectures, just be sure to beware of ground hornets!

His tone is very direct so he kinda sounds mad all the time, but he's pretty nice. I didn't really go to his lectures since he didn't really teach, just kind of let us ask questions about the readings and then gave us an ungraded activity to work on with classmates, and class usually let out early. Pretty test-heavy, but they're not too hard

I can easily see why some people might view Dr. Swan as intimidating as he comes off as a bit brash, but he is just really passionate about his work. He just wants to make sure everyone shows up on time and is ready for his lectures, which there are a lot of. But they are pretty entertaining subjects. Labs were fun and fairly easy to do.
He's kind of rude but in a nice way. If you talk to him he's helpful and likeable. Study for your tests, it's easy. Don't be late

Dr. Swan is brilliant. Unfortunately, he says things as they are and it is difficult to simplify. Only exams and quizzes so if you mess up, you're a bit screwed. Be honest and ask for help when you need it, he is very willing to help. Loved him despite my grade and would take it again but study harder and review quizzes more.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Take this course with Professor Swan if you are ONLY good at taking exams. 80% of your grade is based off of exams. 25% each Exam 1 and 2 and then 30% worth for the final. Lectures were extremely fast taught and heavy on information. Quizzes were easy but how the exams were weighted in the gradebook were extremely harsh and unfair.

Swan was a phenomenal professor. He really made the course such lighthearted fun and just overall made this class a breeze. He was a great guy and someone who I really look up to. Overall, I'm sure that you will have a great time in this class. Took it in the Summer session, 4 weeks, and it was super easy.

Lets be real. This is the class all of the people who hate science take just to graduate. The professor treats it like that, he teaches it bc he has to and we take it for the same reason and neither of us are happy about it. It didn't move me, change my life, or inspire me to do anything other than work for the A to keep a good GPA.

Professor Swan, at least for SCI 100 realized that many people take this class just for science credit, so made it pretty doable. There was a solid amount of homework, but I took the winter session, so its crammed. Classes never went the full length which was nice. Dates he had for deadlines on BB were all wrong, so we had to ask for clarification.

I mean hes alright, the biggest reason hes rated this low to me is because he made it so if you're 2 minutes late he'll deduct 2% off your total grade. He'll call you out and make jokes about you if you show up just on time which is something that bothered me. He made SCI100 5x harder than it had to be but I'll blame that more on course structure
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: When I took landscapes I expected it to be boring. However, Professor Swan taught in a way that made the class interesting and dynamic. Attendance is mandatory and you should be prepared to write papers. While he is known to generally a bit of a tough grader, he gives great feedback. Professor Swan is one of my favorite GES teachers, def recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Dr. Swan is a great guy! Extremely down to earth, honest and approachable. The lectures are interesting and important when it comes to the material you need for your exams and quizzes. I really enjoyed ecology and would definitely take his course again.

Swan is a very good teacher there is however a lot of information that goes into this course. He is fair and the majority of the grade is based on exams. He talks about a lot of the real world application of ecology which makes the class really interesting. His professional career speaks for itself. Highly suggest taking his class.

Dr. Swan's lecture's are not boring because he uses examples that are easy to understand and he's funny. Your grade is based off online quizzes and 3 exams. If you go to class and take notes you will have what you need for the tests. The quizzes are based off weekly readings. The class was not super stressful, so I would recommend it.

Professor Swan is a good lecturer, and he keeps the lectures interesting. He was out of the country for a good portion of lectures, and the substitutes weren't good lecturers. Not clear on what you need to know for exams. Doesn't post full slides, only outlines. Quizzes are usually not too difficult, but exams can be with the short answer (online).
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Dr. Swan is one of the best professors in the GES department. He's sarcastic but keeps it real. I took 308 and 408 with him and learned a lot.

I'm going into my junior year at UMBC and never have I met a more unprofessional, and just downright rude of a professor here. I always try to stay engaged and do really well in class, but when I go in to ask questions, he doesn't even look at me because he is too busy. He treats his students terribly, doesn't even try to remember student's names.

Dr. Swan was actually one of my favorite professors in the GES department. A lot of people don't like him very much and view him as rude or gruff, but if you go to his office hours he's extremely helpful. As an added incentive, you'll notice he'll be a lot nicer to you if you approach him.

No textbook. Instead SimBio ($36ish) is used and the 4 online sections make up a noticeable part of the grade. The exams are relatively short. Short answer Qs are straight forward while the fill in the blank and mc Qs are  slightly more challenging. Go to class and fill out his lecture slides. Its a ton of material for each exam.

He reads directly off slides, doesn't post slides with updated with the class notes on to blackboard. He goes through the slides so fast you're lucky if you get all the information down. Large amount of material on exams, he makes it unclear what we need to know. Don't take unless you absolutely need it to graduate.

This course was tolerable only because I've had previous ecology courses with other professors. The material was great, however, Dr. Swan didn't show much interest or passion in teaching ecology. That's understandable I suppose, but I'd want to get students excited about ecology! Exams were very easy and Dr. Swan was helpful outside of class.
Good class a good amount of work not terrible hard thought.

He is very helpful. He only let class out early because the course is full of great material and he knows that some students get tired. (8:30am class) Very nice. I would attend class for a better understanding. Online textbook that was fun and interactive.

Very poor professor for Ecology. He shows little interest in subject matter. I hear hes better for 406. Always lets class out early because we run out of material, despite having 40+ slides per class because he simply reads the slides. Doesn't respond to emails.

Dr. Swan openly despises ecology lectures. He's a researcher, not a professor. He reads straight off the slides that are posted on BB. Knowledge required for exams is not clear. Consistently ends class 20-45 minutes early, as if he doesn't know what else to teach. Frequently takes long pauses as if he doesn't know where to go next. Really terrible.

One of my favorite professors. Content is hard if you don't study. ALWAYS COME TO CLASS! He doesn't like people coming late/skipping class and will sometimes penalize ones who don't show. Very funny and will tease students! Lectures from slides, but don't try to write everything, posts lectures on Bb afterwards. Awesome guy to talk to and smart.
He is a very good professor. I learned a lot in his class. The material is hard but he makes everything sound easy. The tests are take home. Only the final is in class.
