Doc Swan is a very good professor. He is very helpful if you have questions or need something clarified. His tests are fair, but not easy. It you have an understanding of the material you should do well. The only kind of odd thing is his "dark" sense of humor. He is all about predation.
Awesome prof.  he da man!
D swan is the man. Very passionate about stream ecology. Will dedicate his time to you even though he is very busy. Funny but will make fun of you too!
Very nice. Fun class. If your in his upper level courses you get to spend tons of time outside

Swan is a great teacher, he is very clear in what he wants from you as a student. He is always ontime for class. He provides a lot of information on Blackboard (definitions, activities). He really understands and is intrested in the subject that he teaches. He is hilarious in class, he has a dry sense of humor. He always lets class out of time.
Interesting class, interesting teacher. Recommended.

I took Dr Swassing's class a few years ago. He promised I'd learn things that I'd apply in real life- at home, in relationships, & at work. He was right. I learned how to manage situations at work because of him. I've kept his PowerPoint decks to share w/ others. He emphasized honor, integrity, character, doing the right thing. I'd like to say TYVM

Professional Swassing is simply a great guy. He cares for students personally and academically. He's a tough grader but you come out for the better of it. A good bit of reading but all relevant and contemporary. Interestingly, he publishes the final assignment during first class. Has great stories and makes them relevant to course topic. Take him!

ENMG 654 w/ Professor Charlie Swassing was incredible. It was a great experience with relevant discussions and rigorous coursework. The workload can be demanding, but if managed well, it can be a rewarding experience. Consistently putting in your best effort and actively engaging in class discussions is crucial, but the benefits gained are immense

Prof Swassing was really a great instructor with inspiring lectures. He tried hard to keep everyone engaged. Lots of reading, but good reading. Project is semester long in preparation and was fun. Final exam issued at first class meeting which is unusual. Take his class!  There are some frustrating moments, but well worth it.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Everyone says Prof. Swassing's tough. He is, but in a good way. He expects quality work. In reality, why not? It's a grad-level course, and the job market demands it. Critical thinking is key. Imagination is key. Realizing activity doesn't equate to achievement is key.  He's compassionate. You'll learn why case studies are important!  Take him.

Only take the class if you can dedicate yourself completely to the subject. There's a lot of readings, homework, assignments and projects involved. It's tough and way more tougher is the professor. But he will guide you. Listen carefully and follow the learns to successfully complete the course.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment:
Be ready to read and learn a lot. No doubt the professor is a lot sticker and gives tons of work to do. But it was a great learning curve. 
Take the class only if you can dedicate yourself completely to the subject and the assignments.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Professor Swassing leads a great class. He cares about our performance, and provides interesting topics thru lecture and readings. Real-world stories add interest to what could otherwise be a boring subject. Rabbit holes are a real thing, and he finds a few, but he walks his talk. A man of integrity, character and personality. Take his class!

The course helped me to develope my interpersonal skills to be a better leader/manager. The professor is really tough interms of grading but we will learn a lot from the feedback received on worksheets/case study. There are number of motivational videos in the course material and i became a fan of simon sinek. I enjoyed his tough class!

I will admit that this class is important; however, I would recommend any other teacher. He is a hard grader who expects perfection 100% of the time. Not considerate of people's time especially as a grad course where most students are adults who work and got to school full time. The lectures are long and boring. Great topics, terrible professor.

This course helped me to read 4 books and a lot of other content which made me to develop skills to be a better leader. I liked assignments such as the Apollo movie study which were fun and educational. Taught beyond the course to develop life skills to be a better leader.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Inspirational

reviews.comment: Not a fair professor, too much to read and hardly receive any of work credit. i would never take his class again.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Professor Charles is the most genuine, inspirational and toughest professor I faced in my academic career. But by taking this class we can improve our communication, leadership and management skills. I faced difficulties, and it is worth to face. For everyone to improve your skills and ability, take this class!

I took Swassing's ENMG 652 course as my first course in the ENMG Program. It's the perfect introductory course to the program. The HBR Case studies, team presentations, online chat topics, and HW assignments will prepare you well to think like a leader. Being a good leader is being a good communicator. You'll be a better one after this course!

He's a good professor, with a lot of real world experience that he brings into the class. Class is a book-club/discussion format, if you read the books the class is redundant. Spent over 15-20hrs a week; the sheer amount of reading/assignments/hw makes me say this class is not catered for a professional with a FT job with 40+hrs. Good Luck.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: He said 9 to 12 hours of effort per week should be expected for study time. It took me 15. I guess Im slow. Killer class. Fascinating class. Great videos. Case studies - not a fan. But darn if his technique didnt help me at work! Its fun to get him down a rabbit hole. He doesnt always find his way out. Great class though. Great professor.

Conversations in class were therapeutic. I had the chance to understand other people's views. Created a safe environment for open conversations was key to make us share our ideas and concerns. Unique course format, and it's perfect! What makes him an effective teacher: Open, Communicative, Strict, Friendly. I won't forget this class.

I learned a lot! What I look away is life changing. Even if his case studies were a pain, I see how I can use the techniques At work. A big lesson learned is that its ok to ask for clarity and assistance. Dont be afraid. Hes a confidence builder. And Im thankful for that.

The class was "Leading teams and Organizations" and I thought the text books were diverse and relevant. There were a few engaging modern-day readings and other more traditional readings. The conversation was good, he brought in guest speakers when the class brought up a topic about equality in the workplace. A lot of work at the end of class.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: There's more interaction in his class than any in recent memory. Students put quality effort in discussion boards- a reflection of interesting material & vigorous student engagement. He related learning to the real-world, gave us tools to use to improve beyond the class, & despite a high workload I'm a better student and more well-round person.

So here's the deal: I took this class a few semesters back. It is well laid out, LOTS of reading and class discussion. The classes are very informal and based on discussion. If you're shy, drop out. You'll cover stuff that is very interesting

As a big data nerd I would not have imagined his hobby of yacht racing is a perfect example of management, leadership, communication, team building, establishing trust and high performance. Take his class. You will be a better person. In the first class he warns hes not an inspirational speaker. He is. Youll laugh, cry, pull out your hair.

Im hoping to take his ENMG654 course! A required course in the major. Best you have some mgt/leadership experience to get the most of the course. You wouldnt think it at first, but his humor makes the course! Its not an ethics course, but youll learn lots about it, plus courage, honor, etc. Its ok to fail he says, just not his class! Omg-

Is there a MVP award at UMBCs Engineering Management Department? If so, he deserves it! Everything you read here is true: tough grader, funny, human, empathetic, storied, engaging, great lectures, & expects great writing skills. Emphasizes communication skills, honor, character, ethics, integrity, mentorship. Ha! And leadership development.

Professor Swassing WILL make you work for your grade but provides good feedback and is ultimately fair. Anyone taking ENMG 652 should and probably will feel better about having of taken this course by the end of it.

Professor Swassing is very direct, knowledgeable and cares that you will learn everything you need to know at his class. Late assignments will for sure get points deducted, but he is very clear about the grading process and the guidelines. He will give you the needed tools for you to success, but you must work hard. I enjoyed his tough class!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: OMG hes a tough grader. Youll enjoy his lectures and stories. Youd best follow his advice about how to tackle assignments. He stuffs a lot into the course, all of which is relevant and intriguing. But theres a lot of it. In short, hes tough, great instructor, humble, funny, enjoys our hearing of our successes. He insists on participation.

Lectures are very good.  Sometimes runs out of time in class between student presentations, side discussions/personal stories (all relevant), and lecture.  Enthusiastic about subject matter and student success.  Participation is encouraged.  Allows us to discuss "sensitive" topics professionally.  A class to take.  Shame he has no follow-on class.

A few words to describe instructor:  reaches deep in his experience for real-world stories & relates to class topics; emphasizes ethics, character, honor and integrity; big on writing/communications skills; good mentor;  strong leader; loves case studies; uses every minute of class time; sense of humor; doesn't just read from powerpoint; not easy.

Professor Swassing takes the time to be sure you learn what you're supposed to.  His lectures run long, they're still interesting when he relates them to real-life stories or examples.  He's enthusiastic about the subject.  He expects you to write well, which is where I fell short.  I didn't get an A, but I'd take another course taught be him.
Professor Swassing looks out for the students.  He counseled me, and it helped turn things around.

Grades tough, enthusiastic about the subjects, includes lessons of life experiences.  Believes in using up every last minute of class time.  Interesting lectures, long, but won't put you to sleep.  Breathes life into management theories by example.  Can go off into tangents, though interesting.

Professor Bagaria gives very informative lectures that dive deeper into the readings. The readings are foundational knowledge, but the discussion/lectures give great notes for interpreting and applying material for papers. It's hard not to pay attention to his lectures - very intelligent and willing to further discuss material outside of class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Difficult but very rewarding course. Professor Bagaria's lectures made otherwise difficult texts quite accessible, and he encouraged us to in turn not settle for easy conclusions
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Bagaria is a tough professor, but he cares about you learning the tough stuff. He doesn't want you to mindless memorize information and write a good paper because it has the right talking points; he wants you to really understand the stuff. It was a tough class, but one where I felt I actually learned something.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Caring

reviews.comment: An expert in the subject matter. Really enjoyed his style of teaching. Plenty of chances to ask alot of questions. Very fair with grading.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Dr. Swayam was an exceptional professor. I was very engaged by the depth of the courses topics. One half of the semester was a curated chronological compilation of religious essays from an anthropological perspective. The second, a modern application of the tools gathered in the first. Prior knowledge in religious study is helpful but not required
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Be prepared to read and take notes. Classes are lecture heavy and expand on the readings. My biggest complaint is this profs irresponsibility to the students: sets deadlines for himself and repeatedly doesnt meet them, dont reply to emails, cancels classes, and doesnt want any negative or constructive feedback from students. Avoid taking
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Graded by few things--Tough grader

reviews.comment: He is new to teaching undergrads, so I understand he will not be perfect yet. However, his lectures aren't very engaging. He just has us do readings and discusses the readings the entire class. He is very harsh/critical when evaluating papers, but at the same time, he doesn't give you clear advice on how to fix things and even contradicts himself.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: More focused on cramming info down throats rather then teaching it effectively, then asks really specific questions on tests. Sadistic: is practically gleeful when talking about giving out D's to everyone, and hard to access. Instills hopelessness and terror.

You know the Wicked Witch on Wizard of Oz?  Shes got the look too.  Worst instructor ever.  Told the class to "stop wasting my time by asking questions". Expects you to know information beyond the prereqs.,  Writes faster than you can think, and refuses to stop and answer questions. Be ready to memorize the Per. Table, and otherwise useless info.

Horrible prof..!! Very hard to follow and comprehend. her lectures were useless for the most part!! i learned more by the dicussions and on my own. Material on tests wasn't clear. Worst chem teacher i have had
This woman is the devil. She does not know how to teach at all. If she ever teaches this class again, be prepared to fail...

The professor is very knowledgeable and enthusiastic about the subject matter. It's a difficult class but if you attend and read the text you'll do fine. The mandatory discussion section is what makes the class unbearable with its tedious and patronizing group work. If I had to do it over again, I'd take this class somewhere nearby and transfer.

Should not be teaching Chem 101.  She is not interested in this material and makes it apparent it is way below her level.  She also says things that can make you feel inferior.  Will defend herself even if you are asking a simple question.  Avoid contact with her.  Luckily she won't teach it next semester.

Always talks about how you will use what she's teaching in organic chemistry. Writes all her notes on the chalkboard, and they are usually really detailed, but she just skips over somethings that are pretty confusing.

Shes really nice when you go up to her and ask her a question or during class I just wish she would the overhead or a powerpoint she writes ridiculously fast on the chalk board with all of the technology I don't see why she doesn't use a powerpoint ?!
No Comments
She can say some mean things to people. Very demanding.
Very qualified as a chemistry professor and she'll probably let you know every time she mentions an experiment, usually followed by a postdoc she did.  Overall very detailed and easy class with her

Dr. Lewis was great. She made the class interesting and genuinely cares for her students. We had weekly reading notes, and were required to do a group presentation and a paper. it wasn't the hardest class I ever took, but also wasn't the easy gen-ed I assumed it would be. If you're looking to knock out 2 gen-eds and enjoy doing it, take this class.

One of the worst instructors I've ever had. She doesn't grade papers for weeks, but when she does she leaves vague feedback and doesn't give us enough time to incorporate it. End result is 6-12 assignments with lower grades halfway through class, but by then it's too late to change anything to help your grade much since she doesn't take late work.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: This professor set up what should be an interesting course with work I was looking forward to doing. Unfortunately, she doesnt respect anyone but herself. Every time someone shared an opinion in class, this professor was ready to tare it to shreds. She once compared a statement of mine to a miss America contestant question - and not in a good way.

Lowkey narcissistic, seems nice but stand offish. she does not get back to you. Takes too long to get stuff graded to the point where you don't get feedback (isn't good feedback) until you turned in more assignments. She claims to look for good faith effort but then grades very tough. Very disappointed, all of my past WMST prof are were wonderful.

Dr. Lewis is awesome. Classes were more discussion than lecture, which was nice. Every discussion was lively and thought-provoking. Lewis also makes a clear effort to connect with students on a personal level, and she's really funny and kind. She also brought in a couple guest speakers which was cool!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Caring

reviews.comment: Expects too much out of a 100 level class. Grades papers and assignments harder than necessary. Wouldn't take unless needed by your major. Should be an easy A but she doesn't make it that way.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Dr. Sy is the best professor you'll ever have for Psychology. She really cares and is passionate about her students passing and doing well in the course. She provides extra credit to help boost your grade up. Lectures are not boring at all and she provides guided notes that you can later use to study for exams. You won't regret taking her.

You get two chances to take every exam, however need to get at least a 50 on the first exam. Class is easy, need to show up to class cause thats what she bases her exam questions on the most. I got the book and didnt crack it open once because i googled all the answers for the course quizzes.

The nicest professor I've come across yet. Your syllabus is your best friend. Stay on top of all assignments. You can retake online quizzes as many times as you want, she gives you plenty of opportunities for extra-credit, and her exams are basically like your reading guides. Attend class and you'll pass. There's no real way to fail
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Dr. Sy does everything in her power to help you get an A. Remedial exams, online quizzes you can retake an infinite amount of times, guided notes for lectures, and lots of extra credit opportunities.
Dr. Sy is my favorite psych professor at UMBC, she clearly outlines very assignment in the syllabus and lets you retake exams a second time for a chance at a higher grade.

Dr. Sy is one of my favorite Psychology professors. She is kind and extremely intelligent about her subject matter. Her assignments are straightforward and clearly defined. She gives lots of extra credit opportunities and even allows you to re-take Exams for a higher grade. I wish she taught more courses, I'd take them all :)

Dr. Sy is a great lecturer. She is clear and gives good examples. She always explains concepts well and explains things in different ways if you do not understand at first. You should use the guided notes that she provides. A lot of the test material comes from the guided notes. She also gives tons of opportunities for extra credit.

Dr. Sy is an amazing professor! She wants her students to learn and grasp the material, and while she does give fair number of quizzes and quarterly exams, you can retake all exams and take quizzes until you get a 100%. You can only do badly in this class if you don't put in any effort. Read the book for quizzes, and show up to class, you cant fail
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Dr. Sy is amazing! You can take the course quizzes as many as you can until you appreciate it! And there are REMEDIAL EXAMS, which means that you can take one exam twice to upgrade your grade! Print the guide note and be super attention on the lecture, and then you can understand all most everything! Highly recommend for international students!!!!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Dr. Sy is a wonderful professor! Makes an A accessible/possible if you put in effort, even if learning psych isn't your thing. Easy to understand, answers questions kindly and detailed. There is extra credit opportunities and you can take exams twice, which really does improve learning, while making getting a good grade even more possible! 10/10
She is an alright professor, but she moves too fast. If you don't have a printer to print the guided notes, you will fail. She helps students to get A's but doesn't teach very well.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Dr. Sy is my favorite professor at UMBC! I wish she taught more classes! If you are on top of your work you will do great!

What she has on the syllabus is what she's going to stick to in terms of grading. No curves, so you work for the A however you want. Still, just study the guided notes (questions on the exam come STRAIGHT from there) as well as remember examples given in the class because those are used too. She gives plenty of extra credit opportunities.

Prof Sy was very nice throughout the entire semester. I for sure recommend her. She does a lot of the work for you (guided notes for lecture) and is very clear in what she expects you to know for exams. Do your guided notes and homework and you'll be good to go

She is a great professor. Always willing to help and gives remedial exams ( you can take the exam again if you didnt do well the first time) for all four exams. Interesting course and lots and lots of videos. She is very nice and sweet.

Dr. Sy has got to be in my top 3 favorite professors at UMBC. Her class is very easy, all you need to do it show up, write the guided notes, and study for the exams. She is EXTREMELY approachable with anything and will help you if you ask. HIGHLY recommended!!

Dr. Sy is amazing! Very clear grading and extremely reasonable exams. As long as you go to class and do your assignments, you've got the A. Her lectures are great too!  She gives great examples from her own research and experiences.

Dr. Sy is amazing!  You don't have to read the book to get a good grade and she makes the class interesting with funny videos and commentary.  She gives a lot of quizzes but they are all online and you can take them over until you get 100%.  And for her tests she offers you a second chance to take all the tests if you are unhappy with your grade.
Professor Gardner is my guy. Honestly the best teacher I've had at UMBC. Totally understanding and gives great feedback. He makes this school a little less crappy.

I am currently taking the class and I am almost done with the summer session 1. It is the easiest class I have ever taken. Mr. Gardner is  very friendly and kind. He cares a lot about his students and always willing to work with you. Honestly, You don't have to be the best artist, but if you try your best, you will definitely get an "A" or a "B"

Symmes is one of the absolute nicest professors I've ever had, every time I see him he says hi and remembers who I am. The projects aren't bad and hes clear about what he wants. There are also two quizzes but they're really easy. I recommend everyone take his class.

A good teacher that seems interested in what he's doing. He provided constructive criticism and was a very pleasant person. My only criticism was that the class itself was pretty pointless, but he is a good teacher.

Professor Gardner is the best! he cares about his students and trying to help all the time. Just take his class, you will learn a lot and have so much fun, because his assignments are extremely easy and he is way too nice!
He is a great guy! He is careful about criticizing your work and abundant in praise for students' art work. I thoroughly enjoyed his class.
He is an awesome teacher and very helpful. He is open to letting you do things the way that you want. That class was good.
great prof, loved the class

This professor will frustrate the hell out of students. I know her evaluations are terrible so why is she still teaching? She is the only teacher that teaches this class so i recommend when you have an assignment due, take it to another Happ professor to get their opinion on how to do the assignment. Can't go wrong with that. Glad i'm done.

Good luck to those who have to take this class with this thing. Very Very unclear of what she wants in her own assignments. Grading is very strict. Most of the time she always have to come back to class with an answer someone ask the week before. She refer to Wikipedia all the time. Many guest speaker will lecture the class. Will be teaching urself

This is the worst teacher ever, I would not recommend anyone to take her. Shes not clear on her assingments, its impossible to find infomation on the topics she wants you reseach because because she not clear on exactly what she wants and she changes what she wants for her assignments at the last minute, she sets the whole class up for failure
Class is dull, seem like her goal is to fail the class. Is the worst teacher in history. Please lighten up next semester.
She is genuinely the nicest professor I have ever encountered. If you are going to take German, PLEASE take her class! She is an easy grader, and gives amazing feedback on assignments and tests.
A great professor, she wants you to succeed. Please take he instead of Frau Sutton. She is an easy grader and I would have tagged more stuff that is great about her, but I reached the limit.

Took Frau Macfarland for German 201. She is excellent. Very patient, very understanding. She is always enthusiastic and encourages participation. Coherent course material and class organization. Lots of homework. Lots of group work and opportunities to practice in class. She gives good feedback on written assignments and grades forgivingly.

hw is group work due before every exam, worth 20% of total grade. 4 exams in total, worth 80% of total grade, so if ur not good at test taking, maybe avoid. prof is extremely sweet and helpful overall. she actually cares about her students, & it's so refreshing to have someone who cares about the content they teach. i'd say stick it thru.

class was online and really easy, tests were all open note/open book. had an issue with cheating in the sem and made them lockdown browser but open book/note. assignments easy, lectures recorded and clear. only met synchronously the first day and before exams. wish i had him in person because he was a really funny guy!! def recommend
Such an easy class! We only had to meet before the exams.

The class is the easiest A you could get. There is a lot of homework, but you're given a month to complete each. It's all online, so you have plenty of time to do everything at your own pace. The professor is kind and understanding. There are polls during the online sessions that you must answer, but the sessions are only once during exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Test heavy

reviews.comment: The HW takes long. I guess it's just me bc it seems many people thought this was an "easy A" It didn't feel that way AT ALL. Well, If you've taken psych in HS you should be able to do things much quicker. For me, with 5 classes to balance", and my psych feeling like the hardest, I'm so THANKFUL I got a B! Great teacher, very challenging course.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Great class, but horrific amounts of work outside. Using InQuizitive & having 3 different things to reach a high goal was a lot of time. Would've gotten an A but missing one meeting cost me 2% and missed instructions given in the meeting that mattered for the exam that I proceeded to do horrible on and cost me a letter, Besides that good class
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Respected

reviews.comment: Class is not hard if you put in effort. The most difficult aspect of this class is that it is mostly asynchronous, with 5 online lectures that serve as exam review. There are 5 open note exams that are administered online, although for our semester, he used LockDown Browser due to "cheating" (how can you cheat on an open note exam).
lots of reading. easy A.

Overall a pretty easy class. You meet a couple times during the semester and attendance is mandatory for it but mostly asynchronous class. Professor is really cool and hilarious. If you remember when stuff is due and when to turn stuff in and don't miss an exam , you will be fine in this course. Would recommend for an easy A or B.
LOTS of work, online lectures mandatory and you need to follow along, exams were sort of hard, hes super cool though!

Was mostly async but there were mandatory review sessions twice a month before exams. Exams were very easy never got lower than 95 percent and are open-book. All the other assignments are pretty easy just don't wait till the last minute to do them because some of them can take a little while. Overall super easy and highly recommended.

Super nice and chill guy. Very nice during the synchronous classes and easily accessible outside of class. I personally struggle with the tests because I don't do well with online class formats, but that is not his fault. As long as you do everything you're supposed to, you'll get a good A or B.

Professor Taylor was a great professor. Easy A or B. Great for GEPs (not psych majors). Make sure you check your grades, as he put the wrong grade on my transcript at first, and then I had to email him to correct it.

Prof Taylor is an amazing guy. Not only is he really funny on meets, he cares about his students and their learning of psychology. I took this for credit, but def take it if you just want to learn about psychology on your own time while getting an easy A!
dude is hilarious
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Hilarious

reviews.comment: Good for GEPs, NOT for psych majors, better irl for communication. Just divide up the chapter sections, read, play Lofi music, and get out those pretty colored pens. Tests are simple, lots of prof/TA opportunities. I usually despise online textbooks, but the textbook kept me engaged with the real-life examples and interactives in each section.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: PYSC 100 was online, 6 synchronous mandatory sessions, 5 exams, and 5 units of homework. There is a lot of homework but it can be done pretty quickly as it's not hard and all exams are multiple choice. W PROF
Asynchronous class. With 6 mandatory meetings. Lots of work. But nothing crazy. Would recommend.

Since this was an asynchronous online course, I mostly had to learn on my own through reading the online textbook chapters. But Professor Taylor also includes several interactive activities to help you better understand the topics/concepts. Super laid back and overall easy class. Just don't fall behind on your reading!!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: THE BEST PROFESSOR EVER! HE MAKES LEARNING FUN. I WENT TO HIM ALL THE TIME IF I NEEDED HELP AND HE WOULD HAPPILY HELP! He's really funny and laid-back. But you have to study for your tests. Great teacher. I wish I could take Psychology  just to have him as my teacher again.

Literally, the best professor I've had. He's so hilarious and make psychology relatable and a very interesting topic. He genuinely cares about his students. The test averages were usually in the high 70s, low 80s. Don't take psych 100 with anyone else!

Pretty easy class. Exams are open-note. Only need to attend the 5 online meetings and the rest is asynchronous. Lots of info to learn but very interesting. Don't slack off and you should be able to get an A.

Highly recommend PSYC100 with Taylor. He's got a sense of humor. Requirements are clear, meet 5 times a semester, all exams are open notes and open book. Stay on top of work and space them out, you'll pass with an A. I recommend taking notes while watching recorded lectures—you'll find the course interesting.
Very easy class. He's cool but there wasn't much interaction or lectures from him. It was practically all online.
Everything is online and the course is easy, from the monthly Zoom meetings he also was a nice person.
Super easy course. The only way you would fail is if you dont do the exams or the online assignments. Everything is online and open book.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Respected--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Taylor himself is very chill and funny. The class was mostly asynchronous with online review sessions before each exam. There are TA-led study sessions throughout the semester in case you need extra help. Overall definitely one of the easiest GEP courses and one of the best professors to teach it
PSYC 100 was heavily asynchronous. But we had mandatory quiz reviews before exams that were largely TA-led which Professor Taylor oversaw. He's super funny and laid-back.
Best professor ever, easiest gen ed especially for freshmen. 100% recommend him

Prof. Taylor is super chill. The class is structured with a lot of interactives in the book. Five exams, quizzes for each chapter, and some ZAP assignments are the only grades. My only wish was that he actually did some lectures instead of just reviews. When signing up for a webex class, I do anticipate a bit more interaction.
He is super funny and wants all of his students to pass. very upfront with the work that you have to do and it is all done asynchronously. take this class!!!

I love Dr. Taylor and would retake this course if I could. This class had plenty of interactive asynchronous work and 5 online sessions in a semester to review content. A lot of reading and work make up your grade, but the class setup allows you to ace all exams if you take your time to do all the assignments. There are 5 online exams (no final).

best prof I had this sem hands down! the class is asynchronous with the exception of 6 required classes throughout the sem, so you won't be seeing him often but he's very accessible outside of class and tries his best to answer your questions to help you understand the material better! easy class as long as you keep up w the work and take notes!
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: don't worry at all about this class. material is easy to understand. the only thing "hard" about this class is the workload. for exams, you have to apply the knowledge you learned in the textbook, not just memorize facts. however, the recorded lecture made it easy to take notes on key points mentioned in the textbook, so you'd just have to skim.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Prof Taylor is a funny and cool guy. His lectures were brief and to the point. Classes didn't usually last the whole 1hr 15min. Papers (2 of them) had clearly defined criteria, making them fairly easy to write (got 100% on both essays). The textbook wasn't required but was really helpful for exams, especially the final.
Highly recommend taking Psych 211 with this professor. I really enjoyed his class and it was really easy... Most of the assignments and quizzes are online and there are two exams.

Prof Taylor is everything that you could ever want in a professor. He's a sweetheart, he's hilarious, he makes the material fun to learn and he's relatable in a sense that he isn't treating you like a child. The homework is easy and he gives you what you need for the exams during the lecture. I would take this class a million times more if I could!

Awesome! He's into pop culture references and his overall energy makes lectures worth going to. There's no way to not like the guy, he's pretty easy going and he tries to help you get points wherever you can (ie. extra credit & review sessions). You get graded on participation though (it's not on accuracy, it's just for attendance).
Professor Taylor is the bed professor that I've had at UMBC. He's great at explaining material and actually makes it fun to learn. I love going to psychology every week specifically because of him.
He's a bit unconventional but gives good lectures.

He is seriously the best professor at UMBC. He's hilarious and knows how to make the subject he's teaching relatable and easy to learn. Test are easy. Memorize lecture slides and do all the labs online. They are worth a huge percentage of your grade!

As most psychology professors at UMBC,  he was very considerate. His instructions for all of his assignments was fairly explanatory . I took this course during the summer and it was most likely the most chill class I've ever taken. While we had long essays assigned, they were very manageable. I would definitely have this professor again.

If you have to to psych 100 with someone take it with him! Heck, take this class just cause he's teaching it. He is so hilarious and makes psychology a very interesting and relatable subject! He's a great professor.

He was so great! Really helps you with any question you have, and explains it in detail. If you listen and read you should do pretty well on the tests. His lecture's are pretty interesting so you won't really fall asleep. I hope Prof. Taylor gets all the credit he deserves he was really great.

Prof. Taylor was a great teacher. I had him for my Psych 101 class in the evening. The lectures were good and he tried to relate the material to everyday life.  I would recommend him as a teacher to anyone! As long as you do your work and study, you will do great!

I thought Professor Taylor was fantastic. He always took a moment to answer my questions, and would often help me to reach conclusions of my own, allowing me to learn more. There is some small group work, but the good news is that it was all in-class and never took more than 15 minutes. Overall, I felt like he worked hard to set me up for success.

prof reynolds is sooo sweet! you have to complete a lab each week in your group which can be both good and bad depending on your group. she and the TA's are quick at responding to emails and do provide good feedback on lab assignments. she does let you have a piece of paper with notes for the exam, but the exam is long.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: The class structure is amazing, lectures, weekly quizzes, and weekly group assignments. You are able to learn the things and put it into use. Exams are straightforward and she lets you have a sheet of notes. There are extra credit opportunities and attendance counts for part of the final grade as well. Overall very nice professor and understanding.

Where do I begin. She EARNED this 5. Really kind professor. If you show up to class late, just as long as she sees you, youll be marked present. Open note/textbook/Internet quizzes. Extra credit opportunities. Curved grades. Take her class.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Great Lectures and caring professor

A very charming man. Tosses coins if you're clever with humor. Beware of clicker questions at beginning of class. Usually solves for things in purely-formulaic terms, and so there is a general lack of example problems that would be really helpful. Come to his office hours, and collaborate with other students. Discussions and exams are a bit tough.

The professor used multiple modalities in his teaching, which was engaging and fun.  Sometimes the homeworks were due before their respective lectures, which was a bit tough at times.  Overall, this is a hard class but Professor Worchesky is a fantastic teacher who uses humor and storytelling a lot, and is just plain nice.

Dr. Worchesky is a very good professor. Homework gets you thinking a lot, but attending lectures and deeply reviewing the general concepts really takes off the edge. His grading is relatively easy for an honors course. He knows his stuff very well, is very focused on helping students succeed.

One of the best professors I've ever had. Cares for his students. Homeworks are always hard and make you think, so give yourself enough time to do them and go to him if you need help. If you know the homeworks well, you are guaranteed an A on the exams. Exams are always a lot easier than the homework. Lectures are easy to follow and he's a fun guy.

Awesome, caring teacher. Makes concepts very clear, and goes into every detail that might make someone not understand the concept. Doesn't jump ahead, or go too fast. I have learned so much in his class.

Good professor overall, a nice guy and knows the content. Some lectures felt unnecessarily slow, some went way too fast. He goes off notes which is useful for staying on track, but explanations sometimes feel lackluster.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Terrible.
Horrible. He grades everything UNFAIRLY. The TA's don't respond it its just like there's so much grades that you barely even understand how it got there. Do not take his class.

He gives no review packet for the exams so you basically have to guess what's going to be on the exams. He throws coins if you get answers correct which is kind of annoying because it gets corny. The exams do not match anything done in the class as all. Clicker Questions are used for ACCURACY. You spend 2 hours in discussion just to be confused.

He's a professor that excellently explains the content well and guides you through deriving & simplifying problems. However he doesn't do a lot of application practice or exam feedback so homework is still important. His exams are easy if you study hard and he cares about his students a lot. Highly recommend taking a summer course with him!

I took this class because of the reviews on this site, actually. Dr Worchesky is a nice guy and he definitely cares, but he should not be teaching introductory level courses. Lectures were disorganized and rarely had examples like ones on homework--which there is, by the way, a rather lot of. Be prepared to spend all your time on this class.

His lecture consists of him deriving formulas.I feel like time would be better spent if he just did application problems like the ones on masteringphysics (which can be hard). Attendance is necessary for clickers which you only get points for correct answers. He is a kind person and very approachable Exams are easier than masteringphysics hw tho

I wish Dr  Worchesky could teach every single class I have to take until I finish school. He is really that good. I have never had a teacher who cared that much about the students and about making them learn in the most convenient and understandable  way possible, and I took the class over the summer. Exam are simple and extremely fair
Wow, this guy is great.  Best prof all year
He is amazing.  If you need a physics class take him.  Clear lectures with lots of participation and overall fun.  Lots of work and he takes it all serious.

Very good physics professor. The first two introductory physics courses at UMBC can be pretty hard at times and a lot of work, but he is very helpful and you should learn a lot. Go to office hours if you ever need to. Unfortunately sometimes expects you to pick up math fast from courses you haven't taken yet and aren't prerequisites, like DiffEq.

Expect clickers also expect to basically teach yourself physics. Lecture is pointless beyond clicker points, he'll show you a large amount of math for 50 minutes straight and you won't be able to apply any of it to an actual test due to lack of time. He's a pretty nice guy but he doesn't know how to reach introductory courses.

He's pretty funny. Tends to try to teach you the origin of most physic equations how they work. Its up to you to teach yourself how to apply them through homework and studying. Ask him questions about the homework during his office hours; he'll tend to lead you towards the right answer.
Great Professor. Easy to understand.

Material and examples are explained well. He does spend a lot of time proving equations, but I appreciate that. Exams are fair and similar to examples in class. Online and written homeworks were both difficult and long. Expect clicker questions. Tries to entertain and crack jokes, so it's not dull. Encourages you to seek help. Overall good.
Really tough class, but he explains well.  Tough but very fair exams.  Lots of work Make sure to take the course when he does it
His lectures are so long and boring but you need to go for clicker points that you may or may not have that day.
Awful teacher you basically have to teach yourself cause his lectures are useless

This class will be a lot of work between WebAssign, written HW, lab, and 4 exams. Some of the HW problems are killer. The exams are fair, and covered by the HW. His lectures are kind of worthless, but you ought to go because of the graded clicker questions. Worchesky is a fun professor, and will help you out if you need it. I'd recommend him.
Greatest professor ever. Crystal clear with what he's teaching, and his tests aren't that hard. HIghly recommend if you want to study physics
Best Physic teacher I've ever had!
if u do all the hw , u will be fine. tests are based on example in class.  Written HW are extremely hard and time consuming. there is NO CURVE

Dr. Worchesky is by far one of the best professors I've had! Very passionate about what he teaches, jokes a lot and does his best to get the students interested in the subject as well! Takes time to help. A lot of HW, written and online, but tests are very similar to written HW. Come to class, do the HW, and read the text book and you'll be fine!

A lot of assignments  including clicker questions, written homework, electronic (web assign)..., they are POUNDED on you. He tends too joke too much, but when he teaches it is very helpful . Don't come late to class, cause he gives out clicker questions at the beginning and they pile up. As do the writtenelectronic. So get ready to learn!

He makes physics 121 so much harder than it needs to be. Exams are exactly like written homework, even though his syllabus says they won't be. He spends most of his time proving equations and not actually teaching any material at all in class. I don't understand how he has such high reviews. He is a terrible professor for an entry level course.

Worchesky is by far my favorite professor at UMBC. If you have a chance to take his class, TAKE IT! He is very passionate about what he teaches and he really tries his best to help you succeed. He's a funny guy too so you'll get a good laugh during lectures. The homework can be challenging but the exams are all fairly easy and very straightforward.
A GREAT TEACHER!! He explains the material in a fun way and makes a super boring class relatively interesting. TAKE HIM IF YOU CAN!!
What a great class.  Tough but I learned so much.  And I can tell what a burned resistor smells like.
Tough final exam. Really great professor, knows his stuff and helps loads.  Practice lots for the final its stuff from all the labs during the semester.
Super hard class  His lectures were clear and his exams really fair.
Lab course with a lecture.  His lectures helped lots with understanding the lab.  Really knows his stuff

The class is very difficult, especially th ehomework.  But he was great!  He went into lots of detail on the really hard stuff.  Also, I feel ready for the future classes with all of the examples from the other classes.

Material was presented clearly and lectures built on previous material.  Best physics lectures I've had.  I don't know where the previous person was during class.  This prof really knows and enjoys his stuff.

I thought he was annoying as a professor.  Exams are incredibly fair and will kick you to the curb if you don't do the homework.  I got a lot out of this class but his lectures were poor, had to do a lot of research myself.

Excellent Professor. Assigns a lot of homework especially for a Summer Session. But if you dillegently do the homework, fully understand the concepts, attend class, and take pre reading sersiously you will do well. I ended up getting a B in the class. He cares about his students be prepared to study a lot. Seek help if you need it.
Now that I have had another physics professor I know.  Get into Dr. Worchesky's class. In a tough class he is the best there is.
He makes you work hard, but he is the very best. get him
Get this guy...  wow he worked hard and descibed everything clearly.  Most prepared I have eveer had.  Tough stuff but made it understandable.  Throws money to class for answers to questions
Works us hard but works hard with us.  Makes things very clear on a tough subject.  Wish there was less math to it

Extremely difficult class. Professor Worchesky is a good instructor but he makes things harder then they need to be. Kept us over class time the entire semester by anything from 10-25 minutes. In class he goes over derivations and touches on subjects you are expected to know extremely well on the exam. Works you hard and then curves in the end.
great professor in a difficult class
excited and exciting professor really knows his stuff and helps students alot
Made a tough class interesting
Awesome dude, really cares about his students.
Best professor in the entire world.  Cares about his students.  Worchesky is the greatest guy!

Fun classroom examples but tests are extremely hard. You have to study hard to get an A in this class. The way tests are scored, you will receive a C everytime just by knowing the bare minimum. Homework is manditory which sucks.
Hard course and dedicated guy who meets with you anytime. Lectures are really good and homework is really hard.  I wish I worked harder
crazy guy who is always ready to answer questions at any time, even if he is in his lab

Dont be fooled by the fun you have in class, the work is hard and either you get it or you fail. It seemed like he said he wanted to help but when you went to him for help I got the vibe that he didnt want to help you, but he still will. I hated thermo tho

Wacky guy, but an excellent teacher. Knows the material cold and expresses it concisely and thoroughly. Extremely eager to have physics students be involved in internships, research assistantships, and other such things. He will hook you up with the likes if you express an interest. More than willing to help out during office hours. Recommended!
very helpful and passionate about physics. most lectures are slow paced and filled with wacky antics.  i cant stand physics, but i didnt mind his class too much.

Fantastic Teacher. The best one I have had so far. Tests are kinda challenging, but not impossible. Will explain just about anything. Throws stuff & Draws on walls but very passionate about teaching and physics.
No Comments
Make sure you take physics with him, he is an AWESOME teacher, really wants his students to do well and the tests are very fair.
Keeps you awake during class.  Not boring.  What sucks is that some questions on his tests are out there, though (tricky).  Be a super-genius, and you'll be fine.

Dr. Worchesky is AWESOME!  Physics is a hard class for a lot of people, but he will do everything he can to help you out.  Was always cheerful and knows how to make the class laugh, mostly by throwing our text book and other things around.
man, even if you don't have to take Phys 121, take it anyway with worchesky

Hands down the best professor I have ever had.  He goes out of his way to help you learn the material.  Even holds reviews in the lecture hall for 3 hours!!!!  The day before the exam a Sunday.  Could not be anymore helpful.  Always smiling makes a difficult class much easier.  TAKE HIM!!!!

He's willing to help the students, fair, expects a lot but helps you along the way.  If you study and do the homework there is no reason you won't pass the course. Definately in the top two professors I've had.  The people who make you work for it are always the people I have the most respect for.
Class sucks but he is very helpful and cares about the students very much.
Worchesky is the man, he goes way out of his way to help out his students. he actually cares about us learning
Awesome...that's all I have to say.
very helpful do your homework several times

physics is hard so you have to do everything he tells you to do: do the hw 2 times (once with help and the 2nd without looking at any notes or books) and STUDY STUDY STUDY! or you'll do bad and fail...like i did

Quite possibly the best professor in the science and engineering field. He's tough, but you can't find a better teacher. He can make the most complicated subject simple and offers so much extra time to help out the students. He's also hilarious. Great great professor!
No Comments

Take Physics 121 with him. If not your going to regret it. The only guy that teaches this class on campus that understands it is an introductory course and 75% of the kids in the class shouldnt fail. The class wasnt easy, but he explains the material grea
Doesn't give you any breaks: you need to know the material by heart. Very good teacher though. Entertaining class but its imperative to do all the required work in it.
No Comments
No Comments
Very clear and enthusiastic.  Actually cares if the students learn the material and is willing to work with you. But you have to be willing to put the work in because it is tough.

Voted top 10 teachers@UMBC. Deserves it. GREAT explanation of material. Loves physics. VERY fair. The best teacher that I EVER had. I recommend him to everyone taking PHYS 121. He gives money out in class. Throws chairs into walls. Funny jokes.

knows his material...great at teaching it!!!  he really explains all concepts well and makes physics easy (he's funny too).  exam q's are tough though...but he's good enough that you'll know what you're doing..nothing out of the blue

Jorge does a lot of great things: gives tons of extra credit and puts HW questions on exams verbatim. However, lectures are boring and the material can be very difficult. His demeanor can be an acquired taste. Can come off as passive aggressive. Most projects and HW are easy but the ones that aren't are very hard if you're new to the material.

Dodges questions. Writes painfully long and difficult exams, and then proceeds to chastise us for not being able to finish in a timely manner, saying "this is easy" to material he barely even covers. Doesn't seem to understand that we don't get it and doesn't even understand his own slides sometimes. DO NOT TAKE.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: He often says "this is easy." Let me clarify, I knew Jorge as a PhD student before I took this class. Good intentions, but his ambitions are extremely high for students. Verified with other students, he is trying to cram almost two courses-worth of CMPE content (CMPE 212 and CMPE 310) into one CMSC 3-credit course. Projects and exams expect a LOT.
He doesn't really teach. He only really reads off of his computer screen and speaks so monotonously that it's impossible to follow along. He seems fairly laid back, but that's it.

I've taken how many classes with him already. I learn more from the students than I do with him. He said his job is to guide the conversation for our personal development, and that he doesn't really lecture. He assigns so much reading, like 8-15 ppg. per article, 2-5 articles per class, PLUS 1-2 chapters. He doesn't always talk about all in class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: Dr. Rosen is fantastic. You have to be able to hold yourself accountable. He is better for more mature students with work experience because he is non traditional and depends on you to decide the topics you'll discuss most. If you don't have a lot of experience you might feel less fulfilled.

In my 1st class with him, it was pretty easy to get an "A", despite the frustration that usually comes with group projects. As many mentioned earlier, it sucks to share a grade with your group partners when it is not reflective of your own efforts. I'm in my 2nd class with him and it seems he's switched up the grading criteria. He's stricter now!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: My best advice is to take advantage of his incredible executive coaching skills and meet with him to get advice, feedback & food for thought on your personal career and professional aspirations. This is his strength & the most important takeaway from the program.

If you read the book you will be prepared for the test. Many of the complaints about the test are due to not reading. The groups can be stressful when paired with lazy people, but reflective of real-lifework situations. You will get the most out of him if you think of him as a mentor, not just a teacher. He has a lot of valuable advice to share.

If you like big group projects and presentations with shared grades--your grade depends on everyone else and everyone gets the same grade--then by all means, take a class with Dr. Rosen.  I guarantee he will make you feel helpless to control your grade because it's determined by classmates.
You will never know what he wants. He will ask for your opinion but if he doesn't agree with it, points will be taken off. Read his mind and you will be fine.

Dr. Rosen's grading is always very unclear and undeservedly strict.   The biggest problem: Group assignments in every Rosen class and always one group grade. It doesn't matter how well you do, a bad groupmate is enough to ruin everything and there are more bad apples than good so chances are against you.  There must be individual accountability!

Professor Rosen really is a sweet man but lecturing is not his forte. His grading system was not clearly defined, we did not receive grades or feedback on almost half of our assignments, and there was no way to see how our overall grade was calculated. There was one group project where his grading seemed extremely subjective. Read the text.

Dr. Rosen is vague with what he wants but he's a nice guy and his lectures are fun if you like discussions.  You WILL need to read the textbook, so don't take the class thinking you can get by without it. He won't spoon-feed you the notes.

I was a 4.0 student in undergrad so I'm used to working hard. I think he leads a pretty tough class to get an AA+ in though. The main "con": Dr. Rosen is a tough grader and unclear with what he wants at times. Pros: His testing method forces you to really learn the material. He is very laid back and approachable. I think he's pretty funny.
He's friendly but vague. Tough to know exactly what he wants. Class is kinda a free for all. Like we talked about how to choose the best airline. Make sure you read the textbook and tag the sections.

He seems like a very nice guy and he'll make you laugh if you have a sense of humor.   He only manages to cover like 1-3 concepts in his 3 hour long classes though.  The hardest thing is he'll refuse to tell you exactly what he wants, then grade harshly.

Not bad, but assignment criteria is vague. Even with little known about the assignments you can still get an A by putting a good deal of effort into them. Lectures easily get off topic in this particular class he teachers. Overall he is knowledgeable & smart but the class is broad and topics are vague- as well as assignments. Don't like groups.

He is absolutely ridiculous when it comes to explaining expectations. He not only refuses to give clear instructions to any assignment but will give you a harsh grade for not following his supposed prompt that gives absolutely no information. All the students are always confused. He doesn''t teach from the readings and lectures are nothing.
One of the best professors or teachers I ever had at any level. Dedicated to the material and expanding students worldview.

Professor Templeton takes seriously the tenets of critical thinking as a means of living; he will not pay credence to fads or fallacies. He believes the classroom is a place for serious discourse and where all ideas should be challenged. If you don't actually want to think critically, don't take this class, you will be called out and rightly so.
I enjoyed His no nonsense approach and you have to keep up.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Took his class twice my freshman year and was not prepared for all of the work. I actually did worse the second time around ... If you have a good memory and are looking to take a class that is straight memorization, this is the class for you. If you are looking for an easy A, don't bother.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Great class!!! Great instructor!!!

Mr. Templeton does not tolerate laziness, lack of preparation, does not coddle you, and does not provide positive reinforcement without merit.   He requires you to be informed for debate; arguing your Google research is a non-starter.  This class requires adult maturity for maximum benefit. Don't be a petulant entitlement turd and you'll excel.
Overall, probably the worst professor I have had at UMBC. He insulted multiple students and was pretty intellectually dishonest in debates and, especially, presenting religious ideas.

Very boring class, he comes off as rude and pretty much against debate. If he likes you he is nothing but nice to you.This class required a lot of memorization. A lot of people dropped because of there poor quiz grades. He is a gentleman and expects his students to show the same respect. Requires more studying than i anticipated but i did learn.

Absolutely no interest or respect for the subject matter. Knows nothing but the textbook about it (very poorly written, do not expect to be examining any primary sources or religious writing. It reads like an elementary history book.) Intentionally vague in his questions, supports a blanket rejection of Asian thought.

He comes across as standoffish, though he is a really nice guy.  He doesn't dismiss dissenting opinions, he encourages people to question what he has said.  He does however dismiss opinions that aren't well thought out or are unreasonable.   The class is relatively boring, but will not take up much of your time.  Easy A.

Templeton uses his text book, speaks clearly in lecture, and gives easy tests but these standards, while necessary, are not sufficient conditions to judge the quality of the professor. The problem is he is an egoistic man who immediately dismisses other people who disagrees with him, especially when the disagreement is reasonable.

Completing the homework & studying for 30 minutes was all I needed to do per week. Though I failed a couple quizzes, the extra credit quizzes he gave were enough to get me over a 100% in the class. As long as you show up every day & aren't late you can get the extra credit points and get an A.

Terribly hard class, even if you study the subject is very confusing and there is no black and white between different types of philosophical fallacies. Even if you do study absolutely everything (which takes a long time) you might get a C, or a B if you're lucky. Don't plan on getting a good grade in this or getting something out of it.

Book is somewhat helpful though we didn't read over the whole thing.Only read description and examples.He hands out a lot of papers.He only has 3 extra credit quizzes.One wrong answer can end you up with -5 to 7 points.Not much half credit.I feel like the class is more on your opinion.Class mandatory.We get out after a half hour of class.Dont argue

His class isn't easy. Whenever you take a quiz, you might as well just flip a coin to see if you passed/failed. He is an atheist. Who cares. That's his view; let him have it. However, I have found this course helpful in recognizing weak arguments, which I realized are everywhere. Take this if you're willing to study a lot(his lectures are boring).

Yeah he's an athiest and if it gets brought up in class he makes his opinion clear;I personally am a christian and found it a little annoying how close minded he was but  has nothing to do with his competency to teach the class.Class was not difficult, if you have half a brain you won't have to study. Got an A w/ maybe 4hr time spent out of class

If you're planning on taking this class, don't. The teacher is uncompromising and difficult. The quizzes are impossible even if you do study. Questions are frequently met with scrutiny and there is an air of tyranny at the front of the class. You will not pass.

He is the worst teacher I have ever had.  Clearly has no interest in students. Thinks the entire world is full of idiots. Guess what Mr., if you are so intelligent why are you a part time professor at UMBC?  He is extremely arrogant and just plain rude but expects you to be polite to him at all times.  I feel sorry for his relatives....avoid him.

Don't be put off by all the bad ratings. I'd bet most of these are religious people and it is true that Mr. Templeton is a staunch atheist. Religion is a touchy hot button and will make it so a fair rating is impossible. Not hard material at all. If you can forget your way of thinking you may be able to learn something.

AVOID this teacher if possible. Exams are without a doubt way more difficult than they need to be and don't seem to test our (the students) knowledge of the material accurately. Turns simple and easy material into perilously difficult exams for no apparent reason.

Avoid. Attendance is mandatory, but barely anything from the lecture is on any exam. Instead the exams are almost entirely based on the readings, which you do not discuss in class. He basically hates you already and won't answer questions. He just reads his [boring] lecture and you go. I don't understand why he still has his job.

This class is for someone truly want to learn not for anyone just going for the credits. He is highly intelligent but he tents not to break down the material and rather expect you to take time thinking. You have to be open-minded or you learn nothing.

Horrible instructor. Calls students "idiot" and frequently shows his dislike for the entire class. The first two quizes had ok scores, but after that, the average dropped to about 52%. Can't teach, expects people to know everything already.

Professor has easy testing method. He is straightforward and his classes are mostly lecture. He will call you out if you sleep or talk but if you stay on his good side he is a great asset to you as a professor. Grading is clearly explained and never changes.

I spent 5 years at UMBC and this is the only professor I can actually say was bad.  Ridiculously arrogant.  Ironic how 80% of the grade in a class called "Critical Thinking" is memorization of terminology you'll never use later.  I would recommend reading or sleeping, but he docks a nontrivial amount of your grade for that.  Bad teacher and person.

Bad professor. Very redundant, old, and senile. He served in Vietnam, and (I'm sorry to say) but probably suffers from Post Traumatic Stress Disorder. He comes into class with an attitude, yells at students who ask questions, and treats his students with the utmost disrespect.

This is the worst professor I have ever taken. Seriously. He is a liberal atheist, who has no respect for his students religious beliefs. He claimed that his intentions were not to try and convert anyone in the class. He insulted my beliefs every class. He said, and I quote, "Religion is a bad habit." The best part about his class was leaving it.

She made the course content interesting.

reviews.comment: I learned a lot in Professor Tinga's class. The readings assigned were relevant, and Media & Globalization as a whole is an interesting topic. Her capstone class is a bit more data-driven than MCS majors might be used to, so be prepared.

Professor Tinga is a great professor. Not a harsh grader, and very reasonable. She always responded quickly through email and her lectures are engaging and easy to understand. Just come to class, do the readings, and you should be fine.

dr. T is the man. this class was easy with minimal studay. you must go to class to see examples done for the hw.  keeps class entertained and not a bore to attend.

his exams are too long and he spends a lot of time ****ting around during the exam which costs you even more time. But, he is a nice guy who is willing to help. I just think he needs to cut down his exam lengths.

reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things
