There are too many things not to like about this guy to list, and the book is horrible.  It has almost no examples.  He makes easy things difficult and whatever course he teaches will be very time consuming.  That said, I did learn a lot in 303.  From where I don't know.

While CVK is a friendly, well-meaning prof, I'm afraid I had to drop his class. Acoustics is an extremely time-consuming subject, so much that it interfered with my other classes. One should enter this class prepared to spend a few hours per homework problem. No joke! Don't make this commitment if you desire to perform well in other classes.

straight forward professor with an old school attitude, the subject is interesting, if you are a MechE major then take a class with this professor and it will do you good, once in a while it is good to do derivations, always willing to help you also, and the exams are pretty easy, most of the people who complain just dont put in any effort...
Horrible instructor. Makes to many mistakes in his lecture. Does not teach the material. Avoid him, especially in the summer sessions.
AWFUL!!

DO NOT TAKE ANYTHING WITH THIS MAN!!! Sad thing is he's an really old and they did things with a lot less technology than we have today and you can tell this guy is THOROUGH and is a true engineering master. But like most "professors" he's more helpful to UMBC's research funding than to any student in his classes. Can't teach worth 2 cents!!

Horrible teacher.  I earned A's in both classes only as a result of teaching myself.  If you can teach yourself (and find a better book) then you'll do find, but if you cannot, this man's incompetence will screw you over.

BAD prof!! He made mistakes every single lecture. Sometimes he'd get so lost, spend 3/4 of lecture on a single problem and then still not figure it out! If you can, don't take CVK. If you do, break through the barrier of hating the senial old man and you will do well. I got a 100~but I'm an anomaly.
Try to avoid him if possible. Look into taking the course at college park or over the summer.
Words can not describe the incompetence of this man. All that i can say is avoid him at all costs. You will regret the day you walk into one of his classes
Love this man baaadddd. He taught doowwwnnnn
He will give you a real feel for things you can encounter within this profession. I think he covers some very important aspects for an introdution to the social work field. Highly recommend!

Kevin is an amazing teacher, he always made class fun. The notes taken pretty much only mattered for the midterm and no other assignments. Just a generally great guy, made class interesting and engaging.

Kevin Wade is the nicest professor I have ever had. He cares about you as a person and is very understanding. He uses a lot of his personal work as a reference and really gives you a look into social work. As long as you have the powerpoints you will pass the midterm. Amazing class.

Really nice guy. Kevin is maybe the most approachable professor I've ever had. That said, I found his class to be so easy to the point where I didn't feel like I learned as much as I'd have liked to. He does give fantastic practical examples from his years of working in the field and they really stick with you, probably the best part of the class.

Take this professor. His 250 is pretty cool too but for SOWK387, there was a take-home midterm and a presentation. His lectures are entertaining and he doesn't make his class boring despite being at night. Also easy to talk to him about anything, he has good knowledge of all the child welfare system.

Mr. Wade makes this class very introductory, which is appropriate. 1 paper, 1 project, exercises on what you would do if treating clients in hard situations for real life application. He isn't bound by textbook requirements but molds to fit his class. He wants everyone to get a good basic understanding of what working in each SW field can be like.
Kevin is an amazing teacher. He wants his students to succeed, and instructs in a manner that is enriching and applicable to the social work profession. He is one of the best teachers Ive ever had.

Very nice professor and you can tell he really cares about his students. The class is fairly easy and to the point. The thing that bothers me about this professor is he is not on top of grading at all. My class did not have ONE grade in until literally the end of the semester. It was very stressful so be weary of that.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Kevin (he insists that you call him Kevin) is one of the greatest professors in the social work department! His class was very straightforward: come to class, take notes on the lecture, and do the assignments and you'll pass with flying colors. His lectures were fascinating since he would provide examples from his experience practicing in the field

Super chill! A safe class to share your opinion. You can choose your own topic for projects and paper. Very laid back and midterm is open notes. Didn't have a final. Will definitely take his 300 level class!

Kevin Wade is great! Many students have complained about the SWK 250 course, but if you can, take it with him! He has tons of experience and will share some amazing stories with you. Seriously don't get the book for his class. Open-note midterm and 2 papers with lots of creative freedom! Fun, interesting, easy class! Take Kevin!

One of the best social work professors at UMBC , wish he taught more classes. He makes the class interesting, and no book required. He gives you all an opportunity to pass this class, just come to class, participate , do the assignments , and youll be fine.

If your interested in working with children than take this class. It's a must if your doing Title 4E. Has a midterm , open book final, and two papers (one interviewing a parent or child and the other on a special population). Class is more of a discussion. There's no textbook. He's very knowledgeable. One of my favorite professors and classes here.

Professor Wade is a published Author and LCSW-C who keeps the class interested through awesome lectures that relate to the profession of social work. Participation is a must in Professor Wade's class. All tests and quizzes are open notes/open book. This class is an easy A.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Prof. Watson is good! If you are organized and can submit assignments on time, then you will pass. There are only 15 quizzes and 3 assignments plus the final. FOLLOW HIS LAYOUT, I cannot stress it enough. He will allow you to submit a revision to improve your grade, IF you submit on time and make changes according to his feedback.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Gives good feedback--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: stay on top of due dates. 15 quizzes 3 papers and a final (w/ 2 essays). Super picky about grammar & essay layout. He gives you examples of the layout he wants and how he wants you to write essays. Its an easy class if you start your assignments before they are due. Answers emails quickly. Try not to turn in stuff youll lose a lot of points.

He's a hard grader , literally no room for mistakes and semi insults you as he grades your work. He gives feedback but some of his feedback and issues on the assignment doesn't even make sense. If you want an A in this class, you better look for a different professor. I would rather walk into oncoming traffic then take this class again.

Good to get a writing intensive done. Online class. Used textbook heavily for papers. Clear in what he wants but does not give specific direction. No room for error when he grades. Hard to figure out citation style as well- not anything I could find. Responds to emails quickly. Once you figure him out you are set for the semester! Material not hard
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--SO MANY PAPERS--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Her exams are better than Tara legates and Javier. However it's really difficult to understand her so you won't be getting a lecture at all. She seems like a nice lady but as a prof the lecture can't be understood. I def recommend another prof

She's not as bad a lecturer as others say; it's easier also when you can review the slides after. It's clear English isn't her first language, but don't be afraid to ask her to clarify something. She loves participation, and wants to get to know everyone. She's a fairly decent professor: Not my first pick, but I wouldn't mind having her again.

Dr. Lin is a caring and nice professor to her students but is not organized at all. Her accent was slightly challenging to understand, but the mumbling and going off on tangents were worse. It also didn't help that she taught all the conceptually harder course components. Her exam questions were also a lot harder than Green's.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Does not lecture well. She just talks and talks and talks and no one is keeping up nor really understanding. Her exams are hard. I learn everything from the textbook. She seems nice, though.

This class was unnecessarily difficult. From a disorganized grading scale, exams weighted 70% of your course grade, and very dense lectures from Dr. Lin yet very specific detailed exams, this class has been the most difficult to date course ever. Went from having a 4.0 Cumulative GPA to being demolished by this course with Dr. Lin. No remorse shown
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Lin is professional and helpful.

Felt sorry for her as a cell professor, people used to disrespect her and talk over her all the time. She tried really hard to help students understand, to her credit, but she was just not a good communicator. Her thick accent made her impossible to understand and her slides were hopelessly out of order. You're better off just reading the book.

I made a big mistake taking her class. Really hard to understand!  Please avoid at all cost. Simply, if she is teaching Animal Physiology, DO NOT TAKE IT WITH HER!!! Go to other college and take it, then come back for other Bio classes, but not her. TRUST ME!!!

She's much better and clearer to understand in a small classroom compared to a huge lecture hall. It's not hard to get an A in neuro.  Just do the writing assignments and study the book and her ppts.  She's very helpful and willing to answer any questions.  If you did well in Animal, then this class shouldn't be bad for you

I LOVE Dr. Lin. She knows her stuff, is funny, and her tests are fair, though not easy. Rather than requiring you to memorize tomes of info, she tests your knowledge of the general principles of bio, as it should be. She only tests on topics discussed in class. I can understand why some people had a hard time understanding her, but I didn't.

I feel bad giving her low marks, because she obviously knows her stuff and she's pretty hilarious.  However, her slides consist almost entirely of diagrams from the text and the lecturing on top of that is a little difficult to understand and only superficially covers the information you need from the text.  To do well you will need to read a lot.

Would not recommend. Her teaching style is rather disorganized. She is also very hard to understand, as her accent, as previously stated, is VERY THICK, and her grammar makes it all the worse. She also doesn't convey the major points of her slides very well. Very difficult to do well in the class, even though material was not that challenging.

The biggest complaint is the most obvious one: she is a terrible speaker. Firstly, her accent is VERY deep. If you can get over that, it's still impossible to hear her because she mumbles and speaks too softly. Doesn't know how to use the mic and keeps making loud whistling noises come out of it = eardrums destroyed. Exams have typos.

I love Dr. Wallace. This was her first semester doing a different version of 355 where the entire class was writing a single paper. It was such a cool concept and is on it's way to being actually published. When I took it there wasn't too much structure but we rarely met and it was just a matter of meeting deadlines. She's really accommodating too!

Quizzes unlock the individual activities so don't miss them. Each activity just has to have meaningful answers that reference a few things from the class. You get 5 attempts per quiz so in less than three attempts you should get a perfect score. Good to review lecture notes before taking exams. Beware of Exam 2: I got 11 free responses in 45min.

take notes on the textbook from the outlines and you will be good. for exams, just know definitions and concepts and how they are applied. many assignments can be done without reading the textbook, so don't slack and miss easy points. the only thing i hated was when i was given 11 short answer questions on one exam to answer in only 45 minutes.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Test heavy

reviews.comment: I think that she was a very caring and understanding professor. However, if you don't like group work then this may not be the best choice as you are assigned to a group and have weekly group projects. Overall the course flows really well and it is not very difficult as long as you keep up with assignments, I would recommend to take it for a GEP!

This was one of the easiest classes I've had. We originally were supposed to meet twice a week, but we only met once for group work. Dr. Wallace was always clear on instructions and this class was a breeze. Homework, tests and exams were online at your own time. I only had to meet for group work which was simple. Love this class!

Dr.Wallace was very nice, friendly and understanding. We met once a week for group assignments, and we took notes on her lecture slides and the book and completed an individual assignment each week on our own. There is no final exam and all her other exams were online. Overall it was a pretty easy class and she was very nice! She did not teach much

For SOCY101 she gives weekly powerpoints/reading/videos, a quiz (w/ multiple attempts), then an assignment. The first class of the week is asynchronous. There is also a weekly group assignment done in a synchronous class period where Dr. Wallace checks on the groups to confirm everyone understands. TA does most of the communicating.

If you want an easy class i would take this one. I never saw her and grading was a bit confusing, I failed due to some mental health problems but the key part to pass this class if you take it online is doing the group work. If you do the group work you'll pass.

I saw Prof. Wallace maybe 1-2 times throughout the entire class. It's mostly her TA who sends out announcements and helps us prepare for the exams. There were 5-6 sync classes throughout the entire semester. It's mostly group assignments and the class consists of mostly textbook reading. She doesn't really offer much help other than the slides.

I've never written a poor review on a teacher before Dr. Wallace. Brandy Wallace is the most lazy and unprofessional teacher I've had the displeasure of meeting at UMBC. In the midst of the pandemic she hasn't created any lecture content, study guides, and her slides aren't even original. the work isn't hard, but you won't learn anything from her

HOnestly can't understand why Dr Wallace has such a low rating either. Her class was amazing and I found myself flourishing in there. We only had two test for the whole semester and a majority of our grade came from group projects
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Group projects

reviews.comment: Professor Wallace is hard to reach by email, unorganized, doesn't give clear instructions, assigns WAYY too many group assignments, pulls assignments out of thin air, the syllabus is inaccurate, and she interrupts students constantly. I would have loved socy of gender if she wasn't the teacher. I don't recommend If you actually want to learn

The TA's teach the class more than Dr. Wallace does. She never posted lectures slides and you can tell she read from her notes most of the time. You watch lots of videos in class and will be asked specific questions about them on the exams. Also there was supposed to be a large portion of your grade from attendance and she only took attendance once
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Very unproductive teacher. Lectures are boring and there is not much material discussed in class, that was on the test. Very tough grader. I did not do well on an exam and when I went to talk to her about it, she changed my grade nearly two whole letter grades because she "made mistakes grading." Nice person, but horrible teacher.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tests are tough

reviews.comment: Dr. Wallace always managed to leave class early to avoid any confronting students after lecture, never posted slides- let alone teach any course material in the first place, left all the work for her TA, and never responds to emails. No clear grading criteria are provided for exams. The exams are also too difficult for a 3 credit 101 class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: I'm not sure why Dr. Wallace has such a low rating. I really enjoyed going to lecture. Although it's true that the TA's teach the class most of the time, you normally watch videos on interesting topics. Dr. Wallace also gives you study guides before exams that give you EVERYTHING you need to know for the exam. As long as you put in effort, easy A.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: Dr. Wallace is very nice and is a decent professor but her TA's really teach the class. It is an easy class if you take the time to read the textbook. All of her quiz questions are on quizlet.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: I took this class as a social science  requirement for my major. The class is led by TA since the professor just stands there and reads materials. She is no help. Lots of group activities, homework, most of people around me  napped( yes, it's extremely boring)or did other hw during her lectures. Exams mostly of the book. TA's are your only help!
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: Ehh, she's a really nice lady but an unorganized teacher. Her TA's basically teach the class. Slideshows aren't helpful nor does she post them. Pretty much have to do all the learning on your own. Attendance is mandatory. Group assignments every day. Quizzes / hw everyday. Actually read the chapters!! Not an easy A

If you read the book, you can get an A easily. But, you have to pretty much read everything. She doesn't make her expectations known. I worked really hard in this class, more than I did for my chem 101 class, and I barely got an A. She reads off her slides, but her exams are mostly out the book.

Seemed like she would be a good professor in a smaller class. There were a lot of students in this class, so she had something like four people helping her lead classes. There were a lot of quizzes and homework assignments. The quizzes all had  answers online. You would think the class would be easier then, but the quizzes and homework barely count
just a bad teacher

I enjoyed this class so much. The lectures never bored me, and I actually looked forward to this class in the middle of a boring day. There were a couple extra credit opportunities as well, so grading is very easy. Exams were easy if you take notes during lectures, as they were open note.

gives too many handouts it seems like a waste of paper. the group presentation in the end of the semester was a joke and harshly grades you on that despite being lenient throughout the semester. did not plan well in terms of presentations because every group went over time and she continued to dock points. just hope you get assigned to good group.

Overall fantastic. I dont know why her ratings are bad because I thought she was great and passionate. She is a grad student so she is a little less experienced than others, but she tries her best. Shes very interested in students opinions. The quizzes and tests are easy as long as you learn. You dont need the book but theres some short readings.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Lecture heavy--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Prof. Weberman is a grad student teaching Abnormal Psyc for the 1st time. She's very upfront about how she's learning how to teach and is very open to feedback. She's very passionate about social justice and incorporates those ideas into her class. That said, she is very lecture heavy and assigns lots of reading w/ only 100 points for the term.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: The lectures are pretty long and can get boring at times, but that's a psych class for ya. I'd cut her lots of slack, she's a student working on her doctorate who also was asked to teach a class. Overall she's fine and knows what she's talking about, but we frequently run out of time because of how much time is spent answering questions in lecture.

Abnormal Psych. Claims she taught this class before. I don't believe it. Doesn't even know the vocab. "these words are hard" Not to someone who has a right to be teaching it! Uses the insulting term LATINX. (I'm latino not x) Hispanic is fine and nongendered. I've learned that white men caused all the world's problems, Little else.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Dr. Zhu is an expert in the field, however the combination of poor lecture style and the difficulty of vibes' material itself made this class one of the most difficult in the curriculum. His lectures consisted of him reading his own hand-written lecture pdfs from blackboard. His handwriting isn't great and his explanations tended to be confusing.

This class is the hardest I've ever taken. The grading is somewhat generous at least, but your final grade will be entirely decided by both exams, which are 40% each. There is 0 extra credit, and the curving is minimal. PDEs and linear algebra SHOULD be prereqs. There's also no textbook, just his handwritten notes which are sometimes hard to read.
reviews.rating_tags: Test heavy--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The material in this class starts off quite straightforward but increases in difficulty as the semester progresses. Dr. Zhus lectures are incredibly difficult to understand as the slides he shows are of extremely poor quality. His utter lack of enthusiasm and tough grading makes for a truly challenging course. Be sure to organize a study group!
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Simply reads off of poorly transcribed content from the textbook. Shows zero emotion; doesnt even care to greet students or tell them goodbye. He simply starts talking, and stops talking an hour later. Thankfully the homework solutions are thorough.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: honestly just BAD. after the move online the lecture "slides" are poorly scanned hand written notes that are barely legible. he literally reads his note to the camera letter for letter, and if asked a question rereads the part in question letter for letter. do yourself a favor break out your diff-EQ text and read the vibrations text, skip lecture.

Dr. Zhu definitely knows his stuff and the things learned in this class could be useful in industry. That being said, his lectures can be difficult to follow, and the text books used for the class are awful. Expect a HW every week. The grading was brutal with essentially no feedback. Midterm was straightforward, final had some curve-balls.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: He goes through a lot of material each lecture but never gives an explanation of application/what we are trying to get from the calculations. The two exams are the majority of the grade each being worth 40% and he does not curve.

Dr. Zhu cares but is so disorganized and relies on his Grd Ass. so much that it makes it hard to learn at all from him. His GAs can be ok to deal with on grading depending on who you get. Daming, is ok but Mao takes off point left and right giving no feedback. Oh also, while exmpls are done, there are not enough done on one subject to help on HWs.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: He is a difficult professor to learn from. Going to his office hours and writing him emails doesn't provide any help. The only thing that makes the class manageable is that his tests are similar to either homeworks or the few examples he does in class. He is obviously a smart guy and passionate about the material, but doesn't explain it clearly.

This is by far the worst prof in the engineering department. His lectures make no sense. He doesnt offer much help outside of class. never responds to emails. No office hours. If you do happen to talk to him outside of class he is as rude as can be. He is not a nice guy and will make you feel stupid. However the material and class is pretty easy.

Lectures are pointless and confusing. If you want to learn the material, just read the book and bug the TAs. His tests are very straightforward and he does not stick to his standards, so the class should be a pretty easy A.

He is hard to understand and his lectures are almost impossible to follow. Yes, his lectures follow a logical order, but he delves so deeply into theory and the derivations that it become impossible to follow and useless, as most of what he does on the board is background stuff that will not help you solve problems.

I literally got nothing out of his lectures, but that's okay because his exams are not based off of them. Read the book and study the easiest example problems from it, and that's pretty much what the exam will be. He would tell us to ask him questions, and then when we did he would tell us to ask the TA instead. It's a pretty easy class.
Zhu is a good guy.  He gives a very fair work load. Exams are straightfoward with no tricks.  This class was a good experience.
The best professor in ME who could give organized materials to the graduate students...

Not clear on what he wants in certain assignments says effort is really just needed but gets all mad and passive aggressive when you don't do it up to his certain standard. Doesn't really take accountability when he makes mistakes as well...
Gives me the creeps. Not gonna say much cause I'm just happy the class is over lol. But, seriously… do not take. Much different class than what I thought it would earlier in the semester…

One of the weirdest classes I've probably taken. Chill guy, but a bit odd. He also overcomplicates things a lot, like it's an intro class but it feels like a major prereq. Also can be a bit of a helicopter on some projects which can get very annoying.

Very knowledgeable about law, I give him that. But as a professor, I don't think this is for him, honestly speaking. Very vague and his lack of a detailed rubric for most big projects could really hurt you if you don't keep in touch with him constantly over email. If you are not passionate about law, take another IS elective. It's not worth it.

Very strange professor. Gets weirdly close with female students .Prior to the semester, he requests a one on one meeting with each student. During the meeting he basically says that he stalked you and asks you questions(Yes, he does search up his students on social media and look at all your grades from before).Also a helicopter during the project.

I had an especially positive experience in this class.The material covered can be boring at times, but professor Whittier clearly cares about his students and tries to present the information in interesting and engaging ways. Always takes the time to be available for students. Grading is fair, if you put in the effort it will be recognized.

Professor Scott Whittier is an outstanding educator whose passion for teaching, expertise in his subject, and unwavering support for his students make him a true asset to the academic community. If you have the opportunity to learn from Professor Whittier, consider yourself fortunate. He has left a positive mark on my educational journey.

Very very nice professor. Amazing. The class is a law class so the content might be a bit difficult to grasp if you are not from a law background, but he explains it very well and is always ready and available to help you whenever you need it. He understands your situation and does whatever he can to help you succeed.
He is fair person and very approachable. Just ask him a question if you are confused. Overall, class is not difficult and I will say this will be good upper level IS electives.

His lectures were terrible. Always late and was never organized. He would spend 15 minuets every class explaining why what we are going to learn is going to be important instead of actually teaching it. He always sounded like he had no idea what he was talking about. He also would make us stay late.

Don't recommend taking for 155. We were 2 lectures behind the other sections, and were basically abandoned when we moved online. One time he spent about 10-15 minutes explaining to a student why he was NOT going to answer his simple question, which was just to show the example on board step by step. Lost my respect for him after that.

He may be good for 104, but please do yourself a favor and don't take him for 155. Not organized, not helpful, poor at giving lectures, never responded to my emails, I could go on. He claims he has a life or teaches other classes besides ours, but same for us. He used this excuse to not make videos to help us while other professors did. Just don't.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: I'm terrible at math but he made this course extremely easy. A very genuine and caring professor, and always open to helping students after class. Lectures can be a bit cringe & self-explanatory at time, but quizzes cannot be easier and often have exact same questions from the worksheets we do. Definitely gonna take MATH120 with him too!!

Quiz keys and class problems are often wrong. Haphazard math instruction, NO step-by-step. Lazy, not serious. Went MIA during COVID and left us to teach ourselves. No online education, only threw us scraps from OTHER classes. Our section was actually moved to another professor because he was that bad. Thank god for TAs. Avoid or teach yourself!

He is horrible at conveying material. Lectures are extremely unorganized and are pretty much useless. The group quizzes and single person are the most difficult things Ive ever done. They have no correlation to the material presented in class. I would highly recommend taking another professor.
lectures were by far the most useless lectures i have been too. he is very quiet and can not teach whatsoever.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: I am not and never have been a math person, and, seeing as this is (I believe) the lowest math class at UMBC, neither were any of my classmates. However, Professor White made math bearable and even downright easy. He's patient and understanding, and really tries to make what is a very boring class fun. Tests were easy. Just keep up with ALEKS.
He cares about his students, and honestly if you need a math credit i vote math 120 with him. Its an easy class with a chill teacher. Need i say more?

I went to maybe half the classes and took about 5 of the 8 quizzes. As long as you do the ALEKS and most of the quizzes you'll be fine. I had only taken up to precalc in high school but this was nothing new. No calculators allowed which is annoying but he tries to use easy numbers, which I respect.

I hate math and find the subject difficult. However, Jordan White is an optimistic and enthusiastic professor. He provides a lot of opportunities for students to earn a good grade. He is readily available to help students and truly wants them to succeed. Very professional and caring, especially compared to the other UMBC math professors.

The class was super easy at first but as it went on, more of the material came from blackboard notes he posted. I recommend doing the practice problems he posts online to prepare effectively for the weekly quizzes. Also make sure you're doing your WEEKLY aleks homework.

Prof. White is very good, really glad I took his class! He presents the material well and it's easy to follow. He's also very good about letting students know about office hours and is always more than happy to help outside of class. He puts practice problems on BB, which is really helpful, and most times he uses similar ones on tests/quizzes.

His lecture's are rushed and unorganized but there is access to everything you need online, so it's easy. Quiz every week, and three tests. Many of his online lecture notes have a lot of mistakes though.
He is a great professor! He really cares about his students and he breaks everything down for you so, you can clearly understand the problem.

He cares about the students and he cares about your success in the class so if you need help/clarification, he will give it to you. His teaching style is not very neat/organized when it comes to writing on the board so you might have a little trouble following if this is an issue for you. Overall, he is a really good professor
Make sure you keep up with homework. Only three exams and a final. Super straight forwards
Really wants you to understand and succeed

Mr. White is the most communicative professor I've had thus far. It is not hard to get an A in this class if you do the assigned work on Aleks. The hws and quizzes were online with assigned due dates. There are 3 in class exams and a final. He puts numerous examples and typed lectures online on Blackboard to look at after class. Very easy A.
Do all the ALEKS and get 100's on your homework and you'll pass.

Should be an easy course as it has no prerequisites. He is often disorganized and unprepared. Lectures have nothing to do with what the exams contain. Lengthy (boring) lectures containing random information. Come to class so you do not miss when he hands out the study guide. Not very willing to give feedback. Not clear on what will be tested on.

He is by far the worst teacher/professor I have ever had. There is no 0 function on this rating scale. He is disorganized and often goes on and on about things that are not in the book and not on the tests. He cares more about showing off his knowledge then he does actually teaching a class.

Mandatory text was not needed; I passed the midterms with internet searches. Lectures too fast, but lulls into unneeded facts. His review-days before exams are good for extra credit but have NOTHING to do with the exam/study guide itself.

One of the worst professors I've ever had. The lectures are boring and seem to steer away from the actual topic, which makes it difficult to determine what information is actually important. His study guides are vague, and he's a strict grader on tests. His slides provide little to no information to study from. The material covered is very dense.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Doesn't teach, presents minimal information and tests you on things you never discussed/weren't in the book. You have to read a chapter for every single class. Review session was a bizarre "game" in which you learned nothing. He seems more focused on proving his knowledge than teaching others anything. I dropped. AVOID.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: This is an introductory course with no prerequisites, yet he has made the course so dense that no one can follow it. His lectures are droning and difficult to follow. His slide shows have little helpful information for either note taking or studying. He also does not make it clear what he expects you to learn from his lectures. Avoid him.
My favorite lab instructor at UMBC! He's very engaging and wants his students to do well.
Cale Whitworth is the man. His lectures are fun and engaging. If you have a chance definitely take a course with him.

Great professor! His lectures are interesting and he uses a lot of videos which help A LOT! Lectures are long (usual for a 400 level course) but he keeps it interesting. One of my favorite professors at UMBC!

He is the best professor I have ever had. He is passionate and dedicated towards teaching students and puts in over a 100% in every lecture. He went out of his way to help students with concepts and homeworks. He responded to emails right away and gave detailed feedback on grades. I entered the class not liking programming and left class loving it.

Best professor ever!! Even though it was my first time taking a programming class, professor White explain it so clearly that I leaned a lot. He was always willing to help, by email and also by video-calls!! It is a shame he is is a part time professor. He makes you work a lot for the class, but it is worthy all that you learn for life.

Although only a part time professor, Dr. Kevin White is a shining example of how most professors should be.  He is extremely helpful, lecturespresents the material well and cares about and his students.  One of the best professors I have had the pleasure to have at UMBC by a mile.

Dr. Whalen is a very nice guy who clearly knows his stuff, but he isn't a very good prof. His lectures were deceptively simple in comparison to his exams, and a little confusing, so I self taught from the textbook. No HW's or clickers, just 3 exams (None are dropped). The grading system is not at all clear. HUGE CURVE!!!!!

A sweet old guy who clearly enjoys teaching, but has past his peak. Not super well organized, 3 exams are the whole grade, confusing in class. His review sessions (when we actually had them) were helpful. Defiantly sit in the front row, teach yourself before class, and ask as many questions as you can to help you understand the material.

He knows his stuff and he is a really nice guy who wants to give you as many chances as possible to pass, but I didn't get much out of his classes. Easy to fall asleep during class or be confused into a coma.

he was a very good teacher...he helped me a lot through orgo..n we all know that orgo isn't the easiest subject out there. i went to his office hours n he actually took time out to explain things to me. he's a fair grader and his exams are tough if you dont' keep up with the material.  i enjoyed having him as a professor for orgo.

Dr. Whalen is really a good teacher. The material is confusing but he goes out of his way to help out. One thing I really liked about his class was you actually had time to finish the test and go back to check things over. He teaches at a very relaxed pace.
Good teacher. Very helpful. Don't expect to understand the material just by coming to lecture though, because you'll be lost. Read beforehand, come to lecture and you'll pass.
Good teacher- read ahead and you will get alot out of his class.

Whalen is very smart but when it comes to teaching, he's not the best at clarifying things (not saying he's bad at it). But the great thing about Whalen is, he's very nice and extremely understanding. He doesn't drop exams but he gives you so many chances to show him that you know the material and if you do, you can end up getting an A in the class

his lab lectures are pointless and confusing. his exams are unreal as far as some of the questions are  concerned. and his grading system is clear to only him. even my ta said he was confusing! if you have him for lab i hope you have a realy good ta.

Horrible, horrible prof. He expected you to not only read ahead, but come to class with a complete understanding. He pretty much lectures right out of the book, so you might as well just read and skip class. His answers to questions were never helpful. Didn't learn a thing.

confusing teacher and class. never really knew what he was talking about but it wasn't hard.  hardly went to class, and still got a B. HUGE GRADE CURVE.  If you just read the book then you will do fine cause the tests are right from the book.

My friend and I dreaded the class, and felt like it was a waste of time. I got nothing out of the jumbled lectures. He seems smart and wants you to do well, but the material is hard and he doesnt explain it. Plan on learning then its your responsability.

extremely boring! he tends to be very confusing and jumps around a lot. seems like a smart man, but it isnt conveyed in his teaching. exams are tricky and tend to not go along with what was taught in class. basically, GOOD LUCK

Dr. Whalen is an experienced professor who can look at you and your work to figure what kind of student you are, working to learn or a pre-med wanting an A by sucking up. To do well, study what he emphazies in class, read book, talk to him, very helpful
EZ as 123
he's the goat for a reason

Alan is the most amazing professor in the world and I cherish the time I spent in his classes! His style of teaching taught me so much about audio engineering and my conception of music and audio would be incomplete without his help. Alan spends time with his students to ensure they are understanding the material in a way that will get them work.
Great teacher and knows what he is doing. very relaxed but not boring. very practical teaching in class, gets us ready for real world.
best teacher i've ever had.  completely involved in the learning process and willing to work with each individual student.  he knows things baout audio that no one else alive can teach you
Very helpful class. Always willing to give extra help and is entertaining as well as fair. I look forward to my next class with him.

I took 300L over the summer and most of the interaction is with the TA. They grade everything. She makes online lectures and they have all the information you need to know. There was a quiz before class online and in class everyday. The summer class is fast paced, but not very difficult. She goes over each lab at the beginning of class.

Dr. Whitworth is an amazing professor who will go out of her way to  help students. She is very informative and well prepared. She explains very well and most of the times I would understand the concepts in class. Sadly, she will be leaving UMBC this summer so I cannot take another class with her! If you can, please take BIOL303 lab with her!

The class was essentially reading scientific papers, which were difficult, but she did an incredible job of simplifying and explaining complex topics. She's very approachable and does not make you feel as if your question is stupid. For papers, her grading criteria and rubric were very clear and she gives exceptional feedback.
She is a great professor. Knowledgeable and clear on what we need to study!!! Love her!

Favorite biology teacher at UMBC.  Her lectures are done at light speed but you have to understand she does it so she can cover all of the material that's on the test in class.  She's great at explaining hard concepts and is willing to tell the Meyerhofs that their questions aren't relevant. She also fits in easily and works well with students.

You don't need to read at all if Whitworth is the only professor for your class. Definitely go to office hours and SI sessions. Especially office hours to understand what she wants you to know for exams!!! Exams were not consistent. Exam 1 was sort of on general bio stuff, and Exam 3 was focused only on a couple major topics. Wish that clickers 1%
Dr. Whitworth is a very good teacher. She knows what she's talking about and explains the material very well. You need to study a lot for her exams, but as long as you study you should be fine.

Dr. Whitworth is an amazing professor with lots of knowledge! Has clear expectations from students and is always friendly and nice when approached. Responds quickly to e-mails too! Great biology professor and def. one of the best I have had at UMBC. Take ANY class you can with her :)

Dr. Whitworth's exams in Cell Biology were very difficult, but she is very sweet and helpful. Her questions go beyond the scope of just theory. Her exams had the lowest averages of the two professors teaching the class, however I would take her again, but be prepared to work very hard for your grade.

I had her last semester and she was so great that I thought that the least I could do was write her the review she deserves. First off, as a senior she is one of the best biology professors here at UMBC. There are no surprises on exams or assignments, she tells you exactly what you need to do. I would recommend her to anyone who wants to get an A
Great professor. Requirements were very clear. Also, very helpful if you attend her office hours.

This class seems extremely easy if you have taken any chem lab at UMBC before. She does very detailed lectures on Blackboard and makes this class entirely painless. She's probably one of the best biology professors at UMBC.

Hands down one of the best bio lab professors I've had throughout my years as a bio major. She's straightforward, friendly and very approachable.She's also fair with grading too, so if you have some sort of concern, she will be reasonable.

Dr. Whitworth is new to UMBC, but she's definitely a great professor. She spells out what she expects you to know. Exams and quizzes can be tricky (what did you expect from a 300 level class?) but she's very fair and willing to help. Loved Whitworth!
For this course, Dr. Whitworth expected (what I consider to be) 4 credits worth of work in a 2 credit lab. She was also sometimes unclear about what you needed in your reports & how they were graded.

Karen is the BEST! I struggled so much with the material in Cell Bio, but when Karen taught similar material in this course, I understood it much better. Online lectures were a big help, and my TA was so helpful. Karen is intelligent, straightforward, and friendly. Definitely recommended!
Dr. Karen is the best professor ever.
For the most part straightforward, fair, leaves room for human error in grading.  If you're a procrastinator, your chances for getting an A=0%. B=70%, C=90%.  That should gauge it for you.

She is one of those professors that whether or not she is doing research, she still tries her best to teach and make sure you understand the concept. It was a good amount of work a little too much for a 2 credit class, but having a teacher like that makes life easy.

She was great - easy to approach, helpful when you asked questions, and funny if you get to know her. Stick around and talk to her; ask her questions - she knows a lot and is eager to share. The quizzes and exams were ridiculously easy if you actually studied in advance. Easy A as long as you put some time in!

She is not specific on what she wants, she doesn't post online so you have to attend and take notes during lectures, she is very mean and is new to teaching so extremely by the book, she doesn't admit when she is wrong. Avoid her at all cost, she is awful I don't know why she is the only one teaching they need someone else and she should not teach

Very good professor.Straightforward, approachable,and very intelligent. She is very responsive to emails/questions and she explains the procedures to students clearly.Weekly quizzes, midterm and final exams are straight from lead off and the lab manual.Easy A class if you put in the effort.

Professor Wood was awesome. Very helpful and friendly. Offered many opportunities to improve your grade and was always willing to explain confusing accounting principles with examples. Tests were online but were difficult if you had no idea what you were doing. Watch out for the final which was straightforward but required some solid effort.

He's a nice professor, but is not very clear. He has a hard time understanding how to answer questions. It's really annoying because he'll just repeat the problem question w/o understanding how to answer the student. He is also quite long-winded and roundabout when answering a question and getting to an answer. Wouldn't take a class with him again.
Very involved teacher. Takes the time to know each student individually.
test are hard. he makes attendance a big deal. boring class

Didn't prep for class.  Read out loud.  He adds no value as a teacher.  Doesn't respond to emails.  Assigned a class project on software he didn't know how to use.  He seems to teach so that he can tell tax clients 'I teach a class in this'.  If you have a chance to take any class he teaches with someone else, go with the other teacher.

He is a nice guy and tries to be funny (not), however, I don't think I've ever had a more boring professor. He makes this constant throat clearing noise which bothers me to no end. Hw's are easy enough bc it gives you an alternate problem that's exactly the same with different numbers. Tests can be tough just have the text nearby. Good luck!

He's not a great professor, but the material is easy enough. You'll have to teach yourself, and attend class for a basic review of the material (must sit in the front to hear) and to turn in homework. Exams were alright. And remember, it's accounting: pretty difficult to make it super interesting.

A very knowledgeable and helpful Professor. Goes out of his way to make class more interesting and is always open to suggestions. Then you have the people who don't show up to class and don't do the work and wonder why they fail. If you do what you're supposed to do you'll do fine and learn a lot!

Worst professor I have ever had.  He lectures right from the book powerpoints and obviously doesn't review the material before he teaches.  Not to mention all the exams are OPEN BOOK, but then the final is closed book.  Worst experience I've had in college.

Do not take Allan wood if you have no prior econ experience. He does not explain and he does not teach. He WHISPERS the entire lecture, he just reads whats on the board and you can barely hear him. Most students stopped coming to class after the third week. Tests are hard and homework are harder.
This was a very easy and interesting class to get the perspective of emergency health. Professor Jae is so nice also!
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Great Professor! First asynchronous summer class I took. His lectures are long but he explains concepts well/simplified way, has funny stories from his own EMS experiences and lenient on grading. There is a research paper but it is not too bad.

Lectures were hilarious whenever he cracked jokes. Kinda upset that I only met this professor for at least 3 lectures and the rest was prerecorded. We had like 5 quizzes, 3 exams, and 1 research paper. Last exam was supposed to be taken by all students but became optional for those who needed it. Not a tough grader at all, chill, and laid back.

Professor Yang makes learning fun. I was not extremely interested in the subject beforehand, but taking his class raised my interest. He was funny and his personal stories helped me really understand the topics.

If I could marry this professor, I would. Jae makes class so fun and interesting. He is very passionate about EHS and has TONS of stories that give a great background on concepts introduced in the class. The grades are made up of tests and quizzes but if you look at the slides, you'll be fine. PLEASE take any EHS class with Jae that you can!

Really chill and laid back, uses powerpoint in lecture which can get pretty boring but he uses stories from his experience as a paramedic to cushion the lecture and give real life examples for the material we cover. Great class overall. I'd take any other class he teaches. Really great guy.
Very funny and keeps lectures interesting with all his joke. Class is easy and fun, and worth your time.
He needs to retire ASAP, I don't even know how they let him teach!
Just don't

Hes a nice dude but he barely speaks english. Never understood what anyone said to him and his lectures were pointless. I stopped going and started learning from tutors,youtube and textbook. If your not prepared to do that I dont advise taking him. Material is hard and about half the class is on second attempt. its ridiculous honestly.
He is a good lecturer, he can be hard to understand at times but if you go to his lectures you will know what to do to prepare for the exam. I would recommend taking him.

This man has to be the worst professor I have ever taken in my entire life. I am a senior right now and it actually unbelievable. You might as well take this class with only gen-ed's because otherwise you will fail. Very difficult.
DO NOT TAKE. DOES NOT TEACH. JUST GOES OVER SLIDES FOR 2HRS.

A student once asked him to slow down in which he simply said "no print out the notes". Absolutely useless professor. Questions on exams are problems that you've never even seen before, so all the studying you will do will hardly help.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--So many papers

reviews.comment: Does not work out examples in lecture, only talks about work that is written on the note sheet he pre-writes. Exams are graded harshly with no feedback. He does not respond well to criticism at all, and turns any suggestions for him around to be lectures for the students. Do not take him if you can avoid him. Exam averages are around 50%.
Horrible Professor.
Exams are pretty brutal, and lectures are pretty dry and incoherent. Nice guy outside of class and genuinely wants students to succeed. Course material is super tough so be ready though
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Accessible outside class--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Fast lecturer so can make your head spin. Well structured lecture with good examples, but if you speak up because you (and half the class) don't understand something, he'll yell at you, which is a bit daunting. It's worth it to speak up because he'll answer your question. He also likes it when people correct math mistakes he made.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Find a group to study the materials and doing the hw by yourself. Excpect to hear that you will faild the final 10 times per semester. I do not know what is wrong with this guy

Li Yan can be difficult to understand at times but he does care about his students. He was very clear about which parts of the material would be important on exams. Make sure to write out every piece of info on exams, otherwise dont expect to claim full points. Overall, Yan is difficult but the best choice for CMPE306.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: The first exam will be somewhat difficult. Second and third exams are challenging. If you do not know the whole materials and practice you will definitely fail the final. Almost third of the class because of the grading criteria. Do all your attemps and effort -> you will not receive anything. He is rude professor when questions asked. Avoid him!

As other students said, Li Yan is the most awful professor that you will ever have at UMBC. If you want to pass this course, go head and study alone from Book. All what he does in the lecture just reading and rewriting the information from the book. He gave us very difficult final which he ended up curving the exam 30% up.

Yan's exams are drastically easier than Laberge's; it is possible to pass this class by just reading the book and showing up for exams. No tricks in the exams, and he actually gives partial credit on test questions (it is not uncommon to get a 0/30 on a Laberge exam for a single question). I think your chances of passing are higher with Yan.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: I love Prof Yan. He's super caring and cracks really funny jokes every class. If you're not sure how to do Thevenin equivalent, make sure to ask before you start chapter 6. Would definitely recommend him for CMPE 314, heck, just take all his classes. Can't get enough!

Best professors I have ever had in my entire life. Would take this class a thousand times again. He helps out during office hours and if you get a 50 percent in his class, you will probably pass the class. Use his old exams and quizzes, they help a lot. Funniest person I have ever met. Ask him a lot of questions and tell him to take off his glasses

One of the worst professors. Instead of making the material easier to understand or provide concrete real life examples to help make the material relatable he makes circuits a drag. One of the most one dimensional and uninspiring courses I have ever taken.
It was hard to understand past his accent and his writing on the whiteboard was almost unreadable at times. This professor was one of the worst I've had so far and I was very disappointed.

306 is a difficult. Yan teaches it pretty well though, and emphasizes what he wants you to know. Exams are hard, but fair. Has an accent, so might be hard to understand him at times, but always answered any questions I've had, only thing is that he expects you to think before you ask. Book is very helpful. Go to office hours if needed. Approachable

Expect to be berated when asking questions. Inconsistent with exam grading. Incredibly smart but nearly unapproachable. Take with Ali Jafari or Dr. Laberge instead if at all possible. Would never take a Yan class by choice again.
It is not an easy class. If you study hard, you will get the grade that you deserve.

Dr. Yan is hard to follow in class and tries to fly through the material very fast. He does not like to have to repeat himself so it is very important to pay attention in his class - unfortunately, he's really boring and it's easy to not pay attention. He is very helpful after class, though. Talk to him in office hours and he's a different person.

Li Yan is one of the best professors at UMBC. This course is very tough, and most people seem to be blaming the professor for their difficulties. Yan does a fine job of delivering heavily rigorous information in a straightforward manner. He is also one of the few professors that actually does a good job on sticking to the syllabus's schedule

He doesn't care at all if you understand the material or not. He asks f there are questions but he constantly is contemptuous and insulting to any student that doesn't completely understand the material. Heavy accent, super fast talker. AVOID AT ALL COSTS.

Taking 306 with him, I thought he was horrible. But 314 was much better. once you get to know him, and he gets to know you a little, he's pretty chill. Go to class and participate; if he knows who you are he'll be kinder when he's grading. Tests are very similar to previous years' tests.

impossible to understand and assigns arbitrary grades. one student got 15 out of 30 on a question and another student with the same answer got a 0. rude if you ask questions and unapproachable. can not wait to be through with him.

Hard class. The exams are hard, but if you study the example problems and chapter problems in the book, you should be fine. Don't look for partial credit on the exams. He's very knowledgeable, but he doesn't convey the concepts well.

This guy is hard. The lecture notes are sparse, unclear, and don't relate very well to the assigned HW problems.  Tests are really difficult as well. I think he's knowledgeable about the material, he just isn't very good at communicating the concepts. The fairly thick accent doesn't help at all. I wish there was a better professor for this course.
Difficult to undestand, heavy accent sometimes talks very fast.  Homework is heavy.  Tests are difficult but not impossible.  There are better teachers that teach this class.

I have not seen any professor in the Computer Engineering departement that explains the material better than him. If you pay attention to what he is saying he might just give you hints on what will be on his exams. Overall he is a great professor.
Very understanding and compassionate, if you show him that you care, he will take care of you.  If you are a slacka** I dont blame him for failing you.
No Comments

I really enjoyed my class with Dr. Malinovski. His lectures were energetic and very well organized. He clearly cared about teaching, and was very accessible outside of class for assistance. His grading was generous, and he made exams as easy as possible for the material being tested. I'd absolutely take more classes with Dr. Malinovski.

If you really pay attention and try to learn, the course really isn't as bad as others say. There are a few tests that outline your grade; however, they are literally homework problems with altered numbers. I memorized the methods for each of the homework problems, and I managed to get through every exam including the final with 105 percent.

I definitely do not recommend Malinovsky unless you're good with just studying on your own, impossible to understand in class. Be ready to study the textbook on your own to get a good grade. Very heavy on the tests too, exams were literally 75% of the grade
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Absolutely horrendous. Difficult to understand, HW is frustratingly graded with little to no good feedback. Grading system is seemingly lenient but difficult anyways. 60% of our class failed first quiz, which is 20% of total grade. 40% failed second. No real outside help, TA useless. Feedback not helpful. Do not take unless you are confident w math

Worst professor ever. Honestly if you're taking his class you better be ready to get 50% on his exams unless you really know your stuff. First exam average was a 50% with only four passing grades: an A, B, C, and D. Not only that his lectures are so hard to understand and his notes all over the place, he gives quizzes on things he never covers.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: We are halfway through the semester and this professor is probably one of the worst I've had. He is totally set in his one way of explaining things and if that doesn't make sense to you he can't help you. If you divert from the exact way he wrote a solution he docs you even if it makes sense and is right. Don't take class w/ him
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Please do yourself a MAJOR favor and avoid this professor. The grading is harsh and the material is not well covered compared to the test/quiz material. There are MUCH better professors that teach the same class.

AVOID THIS PROF AT ALL COSTS. Grades "quizzes" (which are exams) super harshly with little feedback and doesn't teach the material covered well. To make it worse, there is no standardization across classes; other professors cover much less material while Yaakov can run his material up to the moon.

If all he did was open the textbook and read it word for word it would still be better than the laughable attempt at teaching he does. His lecture notes are the biggest set of hieroglyphs I've ever seen. He jumps from topic to topic over and over again and explains nothing.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Tough grader

reviews.comment: He teaches the class as if people already know the material. His notes are almost completely incomprehensible. He doesn't give partial credit on exams which are like 80% of the grade. Honestly just reading the textbook verbatim would be better than the lectures.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Tough grader

reviews.comment: The exams have 4 questions, with no partial credit. The homework assignments are very long. Lectures are impossible to understand. He is very kind as a person, but avoid his classes.
no no no. don't take him online. He grades four question exams with no partial credit. his lectures are wildly hard to understand online.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Very tough class. Lectures were hard to follow and the examples were not very descriptive. No one would have passed the quizzes if not for the super helpful TA. Unfortunately exams were graded by the professor, who is a tough grader. Did curve the class though. Be prepared to teach yourself outside of class. I recommend Professor Leonard on youtube

I currently have Dr. Malinovsky. There is an accent, but I have adjusted to it. He knows what he is doing during lectures and is VERY nice. He is always welcoming during office hours to go over any tough homework questions and he cares for our success. His lectures alone supply me with what I need to know, very nice guy, and very smart

Exams are EXTREMELY difficult, and count for a very large portion of the grade. Expect to spend 3+ hours per week on homework. Bi-weekly quizzes in discussion, based on homework.   He talks quietly, has a thick accent, and writing is frequently too small to read from the back.   Class started with 80 students, now 25 show up regularly for lecture.

The language barrier makes the concepts of the course become even more confusing then they have to be with this professor. However, I will credit him every bit for knowing how to lecture, just not in English. The TA saved my life and deserves recognition

As a professor he's pretty good. The class just sucks. But, if I'm being objective, his exams are very difficult. I lost no more than 10 points on all of my homeworks through the entire semester, aced every quiz, and still had trouble even PASSING his exams. Copy every example he gives in class, they're what his tests are on. HW is irrelevant.
super hard, difficult hw every week, super difficult exam

This class was a bit of a mess, but it was his first time teaching it. He didn't set a good pace in lecture and was often disorganized. Several key concepts were left out. One-on-one, he is the nicest guy in the world, and is very good at explaining things. Tests were hard, with a generous curve. Homework assignments were large but not unexpected.

Hard to understand him because he is a soft speaker and he has a strong accent. Easy quizes based on the HW. Hard tests and had some problems we didn't learn how to do in class or in HW. A lot of people didn't do good at all on the tests, including myself (even though I was in a study group and studied hard for them). Huge curve at the end.

He speaks very softly; he also has a heavy accent.  Even if you sit in the front row in class, its hard to understand what he's saying. His quizzes are easy, but the exams are much harder. On exams you either fail or you do very well. Not much middle ground. HW was manageable. Huge curve at the end though, even with it you might not do well.

Heavy accent + quiet speaker + dry material + 2 hour class in Sondheim = sharp drop in class attendance--and grades. But he decided to curve heavily, so it wasn't bad at all. I just taught myself with the book; never went to office hours, but he may be a more effective teacher one-on-one.

He doesn't teach much during the class and I wish he covered more material or did it in a way that got to people. The class has one assignment the semester long project. There are some documentation you also complete which is not graded throughout the semester.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Laid back and chill professor. Makes the workload for the class very light. The only downside I would say is the lectures could get a little boring.
Awesome Professor at UMBC with a good heart!
Great professor. Easy to follow all the hw and and quizzes are straight forward.
He mumbles to the board a lot and it's hard to hear. A lot of people stopped showing up to his lectures. The class itself isn't hard, but you basically have to learn in your own time.
Lectures felt redundant with distributed materials, concepts were rather simple, but exams could have more complex applications of the concepts than anything in the notes.

Watching his lectures was completely pointless; got by just by reading over lecture slides. Homeworks (4) were only a few problems, and exams (2) were even fewer problems. No TAs for the class, and he was not very friendly or reachable via email.

His online classes are like repeating things 5 times over, or staring at the camera and saying nothing. You need to know sets, contradiction, induction, etc. so far 4 hw, and 2 tests. tests are 50% of your grade. If you need an easy A class to boost your grade he is a good option, but be prepared to teach yourself on your own.

Super boring, does not explain things well, and a good portion of his online classes involve him writing on the board, repeating things 5 times over, or staring at the camera saying nothing. You need to know induction. However, he does not teach induction well at all. He expects you to memorize it for a some problems, but does not actually teach it
Only bothered to show up to professor Yesha's class for exams. 5 homeworks, a midterm, and a 4-question final worth half of your grade. The lectures will literally make you fall asleep.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: 203 with Yesha is honestly a joke. He is hard to understand at first due to an accent but you get used to it. He gives 5 hws that have 5 questions. Easy. One midterm exam which is exactly like hw1, and a final which has 4-5 questions. You dont have to go to class after the first month because you dont learn anything new. Easy A.

Super boring class. Easy A. 4 easy HW's midterm and final. Tests are just DFA's and CFG's now. Only 4 questions each. Take this if you want to take 18 or more credits with no extra effort. Classes / attendance is pointless. Likes to repeat topics frequently.

Yesha was the most boring professor. He doesn't care if you skip. There are 5 homeworks that are a maximum um 5 questions and grades them basically on completion. The midterm exam was practically word for word from the homeworks, he grades on accuracy for exams. I only showed up for classes where we turned in hw or he gave hw back. Easy A with him.

I don't know how I pulled off an A, but I did. Instructed by a professor that barely even understands his own class, he sits in the front of lecture, close to whispering to the class and does not involve student participation. Your grade is guided primarily by the final 50%, with 5 homework's each with an average of 5 questions 20%, and exam 1 30%.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: I would avoid classes where one exam is worth 50% of your grade. Got near 100s on everything and messed up one question on the final -- ruined my grade.   Either way, he is the worst instructor I've ever had.
Worst. Prof. Ever

This is a good class to take as a 400-level elective because, unlike most computer science classes at UMBC, the HW and exams correspond to what you learned in class. The exams are very easy and are almost the exact same problems that were on the homework (which is simple if you attend class. No need to buy the textbook).

Probably my least favorite professor thus far. He just reads off of 10 year old powerpoint slides and doesn't speak loudly or encourage you to listen. There are two exams worth 80% of your grade (the final is 50%) and about 5 homeworks to cover the rest. Going to his lectures is utterly useless, so you will wind up reading the textbook to learn.

I don't know why people complain about this man. I went to 2 classes the entire semester and those were the tests. I got an A. Yes he's hard to understand and yes he's boring. However, at the end of the day. there were 4 homeworks with about 5 questions each, and both tests had 5 questions. It was stupid easy. 100% best teacher ever.

Worst instructor I've had in my life and I'm not exaggerating. Lectures are worthless and he's hard to understand. I learned more reading the textbook for several hours before tests than lectures all semester. Talks to the floor and rambles. But this class is easy. Don't think he fails people or gives less than B's. If you want to learn, stay away.

The worst professor I've had. Lectures are useless, and you'll need to figure homework out on your own, but they're easy. Tests are very easy based off homework. However, final is 50% of your grade, 4 questions and 1 question no one knew how to do. I somehow got an A, but avoid his class. Seems like an easy A but the final will get you.
I came to college and I pay to learn, taking this class you will not learn anything by the end, if you want to have a good experience and stay engaged do not take this class.

Exams are all just 4 questions that are weighted heavily. I guess he really doesn't give failing grades because I should've gotten a D or worse. Small group project that's not worth a lot. Just reads off of slides and belabors very random points, even stuff that doesn't show up on exams. Homework doesn't help you prepare for exams either.

Decent instructor, speaks quietly has a pretty thick accent, but after a week or two it is very easy to understand him. Assigns readings, helpful if your lost but unnecessary to do well. Homeworks are easy, tests are mostly based on in class examples and homeworks. Tests are usually 4-6 questions, and worth most of your grade.

Prof. Yesha assigns a textbook and reading assignments, homework, and exams that relate directly to the homeworks. He does not like to give people bad grades so most people make an A or a B in his classes. What more could you ask for? I guess the only thing is he is not the best lecturer but he seems to try and is always on time.

Hard to understand, but that's his accent, so can't fault him much for that. However, he always goes over the end of class time without realizing it, and pays zero attention to the class while lecturing (talks to the chalkboard). Bad about updating his website with homework too. Ok, but not great overall.

I don't think he's nearly as bad as everyone makes him out to be.  My main complaint was how little material the class actually covered.  If all you care about is a letter you'll love this guy.  I still think he's a good instructor regardless, I was just hoping to learn more than I actually got out of it.  Really friendly and approachable guy.

He was not very good at explaining things BUT his exams were all open book and open notes.  If you can learn from the text then take his class, learn from the text and skip class.  If you need help from a prof you won't get much from him. His office was a mess. I went to his office once for help. You should visit it just to see how messy it is!

horrible teacher, takes like a month to grade exams.. all 2 of them. talks very slowly and goes over 1 thing for the entire class. didn't even complete all of the material described in the syllabus but yet its still on the final which is 50% with 5 questions which is ridiculous. NOT RECOMMENDED.

what a joke! AVOID him if yo want to learn. take him if you want an easy A. 50% of your grade final exam with about 5 questions. 4 easy questions from HWs and one that you might have no idea. I got an A but I'm not sure what I learned from it...
HE CAN'T TEACH.HE DOES EVEN DO EYE CONTACT. NOBODY LISTENS IN HIS CLASS. HE TALKS SO SLOW...SPENDS 40MINS ON ONE SLIDE.

If Rain Man were a teacher, his name would be Yaakov Yesha. I had maintained a 4.0 GPA through 6 semesters prior to my ill fated experience with "Rain Man". His communication skills are non-existent. I believe he is extremely intelligent, but he is lost inside his own mind. At times, he seems oblivious to the fact that he is in front of people. Bad
No Comments

Not bad. Mid/final are 4 questions each, so you better know the proofs (PUMPING LEMMA haah). 2 or 3 hw. That's it for grading. Repeats himself a lot, and cover same stuff alot. and we never opened the book once. He talks towards the board the whole time and paces around looking at the floor. Its funny. Lil eccentric but knows his stuff to a T.

Wow! You will feel very lost in the first 1/2 of the semester because all he does is read off the slides. Once he starts posting homework and gives exams you will find his course is extremely easy. I felt after the course was finished that I could take his exams, but if asked what discrete math is, I couldn't tell you.  I got an A.

His class is excessively easy. Midterm was only 4 questions and the lowest grade in the class was a 70 with 25% acing it and 45% getting A's. He ranmbles in lectures and teaches off of the slides for the most part, but from what I hear this is no different from the other professors teaching this class.

Not only does this guy suck! But his tests are horrible. The midterm was hit or miss with 4 questions. I got a 55 because he gives almost no partial credit. I even had the right answer but didn't do it the way he thought I should of and got 15 points off. The final was 4 questions that covered 1/2 the course.  He even lectured after the final!!!
unclear, wild tangets, ... its all true. But very easy class and you dont have to show up.  if u really want to learn- dont take him.  if u want a good grade w/o doing anything- then do
No Comments

Provides very detailed and lengthy explainations which are hard to understand or follow. He would probably be a good proffesor to take a hard class with, but the class is so easy that coming to lectures isn't worth the boredom.

As long as you pay attention in class to what he writes down on the board, you should have no problem getting an A or a B. He frequently goes over the same thing for several lectures in a row, but the tests are so easy its hard not to do well. Definite recommend if you dont really care about learnin

This guy wears the same shirt every single day.  And sometimes, he might wear a blue shirt, look out for it ;).  His exams are easy as hell, but he doesn't teach anything.  Just read the book and don't come to class.  It's really easy.  Coming to class actually makes you dumber than you already are.

The class is fairly easy if you read and look at the slides. He teaches straight from them. The only problem is it's difficult to follow his lecture. He can be very boring. He treats the class as they don't know anything. You know what a function is, right? One day, the whole class was on one slide.

WORST TEACHER EVER!!!!!!!!!! If u ask him a question he will deviate from the real question and answer all sorts of stuff which u wont understand anyways because of his stuttering.You will most probably hear the word proposition a hundred times for the first 20 meetings.

I transfered here in middle of sophomore yr. This IS the WORST teacher Ive had in college. Seems like nice guy,but once you ask question,its like pullin teeth.final=50%, I got A's on all three tests, and ended up getting a B in the class cause of final:(
