This was one of the worst professors I've had.  He's hard to understand and is not good at handling questions.  I thought I was getting an A in the class and ended up with a C.  I couldn't get in touch with him to get an explanation!  Would not recommend!
No Comments

His tests are fair, not too difficult, the slides for his lectures are very helpful, but there is one problem: YOU CAN'T UNDERSTAND A WORD HE SAYS!!! Yesha will mumble and stutter through his lectures, constantly going off on wild tangents for 20 minutes
No Comments

Honestly an average professor. The homework is graded on completion, but do it twice, once to turn in, and once to practice before the exam.  Don't miss a lecture, you'll get lost immediately.  Don't try to get points back without making sure you're correct, he won't budge.  Make sure you know physics, diff eq, imaginary numbers, and matrix math.

Subpar Lecturer. Not very receptive to questions during lecture. Review material lines up poorly with the actually exam. Around half the class fails every semester. Best advice I can give is to seek out Dr. LaBerge who helps out with the class, 10000x better than Yan

This guy sucks. The lectures are near impossible to learn anything in. The exams are unbelievably hard with grade averages consistently in the 50s. If you wanna pass this class just know you really can't use the lectures.

My worst experience at UMBC. I had never tried so hard to receive such poor grades. Exam averages were consistently below 55%. Lectures unhelpful, learned everything through youtube. Only reason I passed was because of a monster curve, which I am convinced was only implemented because of complaints to administration. Hardest course in curriculum.

Do not waste time going to lecture. Even the worst youtube channel will teach you better than him. The text book is absolutely awful. Teacher can get aggressive when you ask basic questions. His teaching method is pointing at solved equations and saying the steps. He never solved any in class. Turned in HW then left to go teach myself.

It took me 3 tries to pass this class, and it has caused me so much stress doing so. Did not like his class. Difficult to engage with during and outside of class, seems very unenthused to be teaching. Not looking forward to his 314 class next semester. If you complete and understand the labs and HW, you should be alright. Tutoring helps too.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Very hard to understand in lecture. Textbook is a must.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Horrible Horrible Horrible Professor. Does not teach and is UNORGANIZED.

He goes very fast and is hard to follow in lectures, you will have to partially teach yourself. He does not prepare you for the exams and is one of the worst professors Ive had. He gets annoyed when you ask questions or dont understand something.
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Amazing! I love Dr. Yeakley. He is genuinely such a helpful professor, always willing to help outside of class. Lectures are a little boring but not many assignments and they are easy if you are following along in class and with the text book. Clear, straight forward questions on exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Professor Yeakley is great. Very understanding and flexible with office hours. Ensures everybody understands the work.

One of my favorite professors at UMBC. He cares a lot of about his students and the exams/assignments were easy. He gives you a take-home practice quiz before every exam and almost all the questions are similar. There's extra credit assignments and he makes his lectures fun by telling a lot of jokes.

One of the nicest professors I had at UMBC, genuinely cares about his students' success and is very accessible.Overall class was lecture/textbook-heavy, but content wasn't too difficult to understand.He doesn't assign too much and has some extra credit opportunities.Highly recommend his class if you need to satisfy your science w/o lab requirement.

He is very passionate about what he teaches and you can tell he wants to pass on his passion onto his students. Very clear about what will be on tests and lectures essentially fully prepare you for tests, wonderful professor who I even have as my advisor because of this class.
He is a really nice guy and teacher. There are 3 exams, some online quizzes, and learning modules. If you do the study guide and the quizzes, you will pass easily.
Prof Yeakley is very good. Interesting lectures, open to questions during and outside class, fair grader and a nice guy overall. Would definitely recommend him.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Long lectures, good understanding man
Forget the class he is a down to earth person and teaches it like that. Easy course but interesting info thats worth remembering for the sake of it.
Super sweet guy. You can tell he has passion. Prepare for a lot of note taking
Not very hard, a couple of exams and quizes almost every week but those are easy to complete. Very caring Professor and is interested in the subject he teaches.
Prof Yeakley is a good guy who genuinely seems to care about his students, but he can make the material a little hard to understand if you're not a science person.

During COVID, Alan was so pleasant. quite a few assignments, and exams were a bit tough sometime, definitely need to prepare well. Read the text and keep up with the work, he's willing to help however he can and replies to emails quickly.

I took this course as part of my science gen ed and really enjoyed the course because of Professor Yeakley! He truly cares about the students and is passionate about the subject. He is very fair and will prepare you well for the exams. Quizzes every week based on lecture slides that he posts online. Three learning modules that are easy to complete.

Probably one of the most intelligent and knowledgable teachers that I have encountered in the GES dept of UMBC. Amazing person to talk to outside of class about anything GES, he understands that life happens outside of the walls of school and is willing to work with you. I enjoyed taking this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: I'm currently a senior and Dr. Yeakley is one of the best professors I have ever had. Even though he is the head of the dept at UMBC, he still makes time to see you outside of office hours if needed. His lectures are interesting and clear. Dr. Yeakley cares about his students and will ABSOLUTELY make time to help you out with whatever you need.

Professor Yeakley is one of the nicest professors that you'll ever meet. Super caring and willing to help you pass. Class was very informative and interesting. As long as you keep up with the work (news article twice a month) and pay attention in class you'll pass. Would definitely recommend this class to any GES majors.

Dr Yeakley is a really knowledgeable professor who has a great deal of experience in the field, especially with salmonid recovery and stream restoration in the Pacific Northwest. He is very nice and helpful with the assigned work. A few of the papers you read for class are his own publications so he can answer questions on the topic in great detail

Professor Kim is a very kind person, and very smart, however, this class was incredibly difficult. Lectures were not very engaging, and they did not make sense in structure at times. If you can take this class with someone else, I would recommend that.
Don't take her! If you do take her you will fail.

Professor Kim is a nice person, but not a great teacher. Her lectures are bland and put you to sleep, the quizzes are worded weirdly, and the discussion section isn't helpful. In order to succeed you need to read the online textbook thoroughly and get tutoring. Use Khan Academy and online resources for extra help. Take with someone else if possible
just take another prof

She's not the best in terms of explaining as her lectures are always dry and hard to stay focused The quizzes aren't made as straightforward as the assignments or examples are given in class. Attendance is mandatory for grading. Overall take another prof if you can

Amazing. She really cares about the students grasping the information in their own way. Dr. Yesha will always provide thorough feedback and assistance when needed. She is committed to students succeeding. Start assignments early if possible! This class is paper heavy.
She is wonderful.

This class is super easy. I got a 99% and the only reason I didn't receive a 100% was because I missed 5 classes. This class you need the book and all you do is follow instructions on how to make something on excel, word, powerpoint, and access. If you can read and follow basic instructions there is no way you cant get an A.
She's awesome!
Easy class if you study the homework
Great teacher

She is a nice person, soft voice does not have very engaging lectures. Expects a lot from students, grades very hard on presentation and delivery so if you don't like public speaking... Homework is very long and worth a lot of points, shows up on exams. You get a cheat sheet for the exam which is really nice and she gives a lot of extra credit.
Great Professor

Professor Yee was one of the sweetest professors I ever had, but in my opinion, she expects too much from her students. She is always there for you when you need it though. She grades homework very hard, so the extra credit she does give, that only affects your homework, helps.

Health Econ, was a difficult class. 3 Exams, you're allowed an 8x11 cheatsheet front and back. Don't expect an easy A though. Her curves are extremely large. 50% for a C, A is a high 70. One of the best professors that i have had. Hmwk shows up on the tests. She's also very cute!
Great prof, great energy. He makes things as easy for his students as possible, giving clear criteria and explaining assignments thoroughly. One of my favorite profs.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Activities once a week 10%, 6 assignments 60%!- start EARLY, 1 midterm 15%, changed class final to take home 15%. The best at explaining and giving examples. Class not mandatory but you'll be lost not going! He is also pretty funny with his dry humor and he can lowkey be sassy sometimes which makes him unapproachable imo as a tweaker. Def take him!
Great professor, lectures were always helpful. He went over every topic in great detail with easy to understand explanations. 10/10 would recommend.

great lecturer! conducive to note taking, very accessible outside of class, flexible late policy, hw was actually useful and helped u learn and be prepared for exams, exams tested class concepts properly were not difficult, weighting of the class is very reasonable, understands what students are asking and answers succinctly, offered extra credit

Great professor, his grading is very heavy on the assignments you will do, but they aren't too hard, just be sure to be very careful with them. Exams are pretty easy as long as you go to class or read the slides. Very kind, and willing to help you students. Overall a fantastic professor, and makes a class that can feel like a slog interesting.

He will give you all you need to do HW and projects (some professors expect you to learn by yourself and their lectures are bad). Activities make sense, projects are based on activities so they are easy. He answers your questions even during the weekends!
He is a nice person and a helpful professor. I wish every professor at UMBC would be like him.

A must take for CMSC 331. He is caring and good professor. During class time it was either slideshow lecture, group activities or review of assignments and exams. Understand the slideshows and in-class examples is all you need for the 2 exams. The assignments are 60% but had plenty of extra credit and be patient with grading.

Mr. Mahmoud is a great professor. The class was very lecture heavy but everything we needed to know was in the slides. You have to read the slides IN GREAT DETAILS because he is going to ask you about EVERYTHING. Overall the class was not that bad.

He made the class easy and fun. The day consisted of sitting down and he would read off the slides but always explained further and answered any questions, and sometimes there are required in-class activities. One thing is that he grades slowly and it isn't clear what he will grade on when it comes to assignments.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: He is one of the best professors at UMBC. A nice person who cares about teaching. Exams are easy as long as you pay attention. Assignments as well. Not to mention he is very accessible outside of class and will help you on the assignments as well. Overall take him if you want to learn and have fun doing so.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: He is a great teacher you can really tell he cares and he provides excellent feedback. Attendance is kinda mandatory because some classes have in class assignments and he does read off of slides but he provides them and he explains them very well and even includes examples so you actually know what's going on. Would take again.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Great lecturer and a kind professor with good lecture notes. Homework is easy if you pay attention in class but can be figured out using the posted lecture notes. Quizzes aren't too bad and notes are allowed. Long readings. Overall one of the best classes I've taken at UMBC, both from a workload and teaching perspective.
I like his class very much. His sense of humor makes the class atmosphere relaxed and fun. For exams and quizs, I find they are not difficult as long as you actively participate in the class.

Fair class; did only Racket/Lisp, Perl, & Lex/Yacc & bit of Prolog. 50% is one midterm & final. Makes sure no one fail, as long as you try. Participation important (10% grade). Midterm okay; final exam brutal. Failed final but he changed grading policy to ensure people could pass. Don't rely solely on practice slides (use other stuff to learn too).

I took Yus for Data Privacy (CMSC491, no option for it on RMP). Nice guy, lectures are a bit dry but uses humor to keep things from getting too dead. Assignments consisted of short research paper critiques, and a couple presentations related to a semester long research project. Grading is quite lenient; adamant on attendance.

Proff Yus has been a wonderful, the class is challenging but he is always open to help during Office Hours. He is always wondering how to make the class better and it really does help. Participation matters tho so make sure to try even if you're shy.

Nice guy, decent prof. VERY big on participation, so don't take you if skip a lot or don't like talking. 331 focuses more on theory rather than typing away at a keyboard (though you will write Scheme programs later). HWs are ok; go to office hours if you don't understand something. Exams are ok as well; questions are ripped from previous exams.

Around 50% of the grade was your score on two exams: one midterm and a final. It's also not super easy content and is very different than material from other CS classes, but he is very clear about exam content and his expectations. Practice exams were very helpful. 7 homeworks that took me like 3-5 hours a piece, but the last one was extra credit.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Test heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Great professor, and super helpful if you don't understand what's going on.  He lays out exactly what he wants you to know for exams and HW and is helpful when questions are asked.

Professor Yus is a very caring professor. He takes time in classes to make sure you practice and understand the material and is always available outside of class to discuss class material. However he also expects you to participate, so if you don't want to talk in class, don't take this professor.

Dr. Roberto is the most caring professor I ever met in my 3 years of college. He really wants students to learn and understand all the material. He will give you a lot of information but not a lot of homework. If you communicate when you don't understand the material, he will help you until you understand. You won't regret taking his class.

Received a D due to some health reasons I missed a lot classes but honestly Professor Yus was one of my favorite professor this semester, he is incredibly thoughtful and even tried his best to pass me despite my absences. You'll find him eager for you to show up to office hours, use him to your advantage. Take his class!!

He's so sweet. I took this class my first semester here and only picked it because I liked the title. You learn so much about chinese medicine and how it changes over time. He also compares it to American medicine. He always has a problem with technology and it's so cute to see him struggle. He give 2 essays and a final that's an essay

Professor Yip is a sweet and funny guy. He makes you want to attend class--and you'll learn a lot in the process. Two papers and one in-class essay are the only grades you'll receive, but just do the reading and take notes and you'll be fine. He definitely piqued my interest in Chinese history.
go to class every day, study your notes before exams, and you should easily have an A in the class. only 4 exams and a small map quiz. easy class, easy A

I took this class over the summer and this teacher is amazing. He is very sweet and cares about his students. He makes sure everyone understands the content before moving on. He really wants everyone to do well in his class and will help you succeed. Take this professor!

I have no idea how I ended up in Chinese history classes but Yip was such a great professor that I headed up taking 2 or 3 of his classes.  For a subject I didn't know much about, he explained it so well and made it so interesting.  Sweetest man as well, so glad I took his classes.

He is such a nice man. He's so passionate about Chinese History. The lectures can be boring but you learn alot of interesting things. There was no exams just essay and the final was just an essay you had to do in class which he gives 2 weeks before classes end. As long as you take notes and review them your sure to do good. He's not very tech saavy

Hes a nice guy, very knowledgable about the subject and excited to teach it. Works off three books. Pay attention to him moreso what you read. Two exams (one question essay in class) and one final (taken two weeks before schools over) Must do good on all or you will fail. Hes a tough grader, I thought i got As and got Cs on all exams.

Yip's class has a simple design, but when it comes to asking him for help it's the worst. Myself and other students have had our questions reflected back at us. I don't recommend his classes for procrastinators and people who don't like to come to class. Just expect to have never answered emails, other than that he's a very knowledgeable professor.

Dr. Yip possesses a sense of charm and humor that is often absent in academia; it's an underrated quality. He can seem aloof to students, but he really is a great person. The grades for the course are consolidated within 3 exams, so students do need to be prepared. Dr. Yip makes Chinese history accessible to the average layman--and that's not easy.

I LOVE Professor Yip. He is really knowledgeable and interested in his subject, and made the class very fun. His tests can be a little difficult, but if you study they're not a huge problem. Got an A in his class with no problem.

Shares his immense knowledge of Chinese history and culture with indefatigable vitality and engaging anecdotes. As a result: three-hour classes flew by! Both the history and resource books--far more interesting than most books of this type-- complemented Dr. Yip's presentations.

He shares his immense knowledge with enthusiasm, providing multiple points of views, primary sources, brief biographies, audiovisuals, and witty anecdotes to bring history to life! Keep up with the reading and attend class to reap the benefits of a valuable course and a brilliant, fair, and dedicated professor.
super easy. not that interesting though (probably just my own opinion though).

Professor Yip is a VERY hard grader.  The only grades in this class were two papers and the final.  Papers he says are a minimum 1000 word, but you'll only get an A if you write at least 2000 per paper.  Only take his class if you are very good at writing his papers.  If you are, his class is AWESOME.  Interesting material and teacher.

Yip's teaching structure is quite simple. If you come to class, take notes, and have a general understanding of what is happening during the time period you are studying you will get an easy A or B.  Most of his exams are take home; though the final is in class.  All exam questions are discussed throughout the lectures and questions are welcomed.

His Chinese history classes are very interesting and contained a lot of knowledge.  I took hist 480 and 477 and overall each class filled up one and a half of my writing pad.  His third exam (final exam) are very straightforward, he told you a week in advance which question will be on the last exam and you had time to prepare for it. Good professor

He is so adorable!  He can't work technology and it is so cute.  He is so sweet!  Your grades consist of 4 tests, all of which are really easy with a word bank and extra credit.  He is funny, and a really good teacher.  I love his class and highly recomend him.

easy A. however, biased. should be called Chinese history. Shouldn't be called east asin history. he misrepresents other contries. he can't even pronounce word that are not chinese. he shouldn't even try to mention other countries if he doesn't have correct knowledge in them.

Great professor, straightforward grading using tests with questions that come from careful notes in lectures. Sometimes can be hard to understand or difficult to see projector outlines from the back, so get a close seat. Reading the textbook can be dreadfully boring, but literature and pictures are important.

Professor Yip is a wonderful, caring teacher. I took HIST 387 and HIST 388 and received an A. I brought a laptop to class everyday and it helped ALOT.  He knows his information very well and the slight accent actually enhances the material taught than hinders it.  I learned a lot about the Chinese gov't and was able to understand Wild Swans by J.C.

Incredible Teacher! He inspired me to pursue History as a major. Very interesting and interested in his subject. Grade is determined by in-class exams and are based almost solely on the lecture (with text questions as bonus points!). Definitely recommended if you can take him. Probably my favorite professor.
AWESOME professor. Somehow I got 3 mid B's on my exams worth equal amounts and got an A for the course. TAKE ANY OF HIS CLASSES esp if u are a hist major

Amazing teacher! He inspired me to pursue History as a major. Really knows his stuff and is very interested in it. Your grade is made up of 4 non-cumulative exams with attendance affecting the curve. Tests come straight from lectures, so go to class and you'll be fine. He's an amazing teacher anyway so there's no reason to miss his class.

His lectures are very interesting but you HAVE to go to class. He gives two take home exams and one final. He wants you to repeat what he said in class. You don't really need to read the books. When he says 4-5 pages write at least 15 (I am not kidding, he wants a lot of detail). He is one of my favorite professors.

History 103 should not have been a terribly difficult course. Yip however is one of the worst professors I have ever had. He lectures on topics that are not on his test. He is unclear and his accent makes him very difficult to understand. His tests consist of extremely obscure questions. Take him if you enjoy pounding your head against the wall.

He's intelligent, and clearly very knowledgeable with his subject. He doesn't do a great job of communicating his ideas, though, and tends to stick to a very strict, generally ineffective format of plain lectures followed by regurgitative tests. Succeeding in his classes seems to rely upon a lot of memorization, and not always of relevant facts.

Dr. Yip is awesome, he always seems to chinese history to pop culture.  he always has a three test format, which are usually take home.  they tests are kinda hard, but he is entertaining, and i always go to his lectures
He knows his subject very well. I enjoy his lectures. His handwriting is a little messy so reading what he writes on the board can be a challenge. Luckily he uses overheads most of the time.

I've taken every one of prof Yip's Chinese history classes and hes a pretty easy going teacher. 3 take home tests make up your entire grade. I never read any of the books that he told us to read and I still got B's in every class, take notes in class and you'll be straight on the take home tests.

Awesome prof. His accent was a bit hard to understand, but his notes were good, and his lectures were frequently funny if you paid attention. The exams were very easy if you prepared, but could be hard if you don't take notes.
EASY A!!!  you just have to show up to class and take notes.  exams come directly from lecture material and a quick review is enough.

This guy cannot grade essays.  Lectures are boring and unprepared.  I didn't bother showing up to the lectures.  Wrote an "A" paper but received a 65.  Grades as though you are a PHD program on Chinese History.  Do not take at all.  Very unclear also in his speech and syllabus
One of the Best!!
Pretty cool person, nice, and tries to add humor in lectures occasionally.  Exams can be a little tricky.
No Comments
Best professsor I have ever had
No Comments

She is very caring, but part of ur grade is attendence. Its a hybrid class, make sure you do ur hw every week tho. I STRONGLY RECCOMEND DOING THE HW DURING THE ONLINE CLASS. I had her for 102 and 201, but the learning structure was very different. she xpects u to be much more independent when it comes to learning in 201, and doesn't lecture as much
Great professor, would and still taking her class up to 201.

Liu laoshi is very nice and fair as far as grading is concerned.The homework is graded on completion, so make sure to do it. If you have no background in Chinese, you will likely have to do a fair amount of studying outside of class. I enjoyed her class, but sometimes she has some difficulty explaining some concepts, which I why I gave her a 4.
Great Teacher!

I'm currently taking her 201 course. Chinese is one of the hardest language to learn but if you put in the time, you will do well (A). Li laoshi did a good job preparing us for exams and teaching us about Chinese culture. She's also very patient and won't make you feel bad if you make a mistake when speaking Chinese.

I had her last semester. Overall an excellent teacher because she made the course exciting and fun. I have taken Chinese at other schools and I can say she's the best teacher I've had so far. Would def recommend to people looking to take a chinese class at umbc.

Prof. Yu's 432L class feels very unorganized with little direction. But, it's pretty easy as long as you have half way decent group members. Homework is tougher than expected and don't expect help from Yu. Lab videos on blackboard are the best part of the class, they're very good. The TAs are inconsistent and not very helpful / present in lab.

Dr. Yu has made it abundantly clear that he does not care about lecturing. He is nice when lecturing, but only talks about his own research projects. Inconsistent grading between TA's and isn't available during his own office hours. The final exam had question on topics never covered in class.

This professor is hard only because he expects a lot and gives you little if no direction. His lectures are a total waste of time because he jumps from topic to topic constantly and is hard to follow. he expects a lot out of your lab reports but the examples he gives are not what he actually wants. Not a fun class to take. Harder than 4 credits
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--So many papers--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Yu was a pretty good prof. Lectures were dull. Lab reports every other week and a pretty standard final exam. Material isn't the easiest, but lecture slides were pretty useful for reference. Grading is left to the TF, which usually wasn't a problem in my experience. Lab groups are random, so there is that chance that you get NPC groupmates.

Be prepared to write reports and give group presentations. The grading is very lenient so you should expect an easy B. One caveat is that reports, prelabs, and homeworks are usually due around the same time of the week which can be very stressful. Ensure your group is on top of the lab reports at all times and the course will be a good experience.

His best attributes are good lectures with excellent organization skills, clear syllabus, adapts to students best he can. He cares Negative attribute is he jumps back and forth sometimes, rather than trying to get the point across to you.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Dr. Yu is by far one of the best professors that I have ever had! His lectures are very helpful and very VERY ENTERTAINING! He will keep you engaged in the class; I always look forward to going to school because he would be teaching. But don't get me wrong this class is fluid mechanics it is HARD at first and you will have to try and put in time!GL

One of the better professors iv'e had at UMBC. Class is curved, content can be difficult but he wants you to pass. Cares about his students. You have to study if you want to do well. Only issue I really had was that the lectures could be a little too heavy into theory sometimes.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: He's of the nicest teachers in the department and has a clear grading criteria. Tests are very reasonable if you've studied his notes, your homework, and book problems, and he's very kind if you have questions. I wish he taught more classes. Quizzes are also part of the grade.
reviews.rating_tags: ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Clear grading criteria--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: Amazing professor -  was able to teach difficult subjects very effectively and clearly, made class enjoyable and had a great sense of humor.

I am completing my final paper for Yufik for 342 and literally had to stop mid-essay to say that this man has been an incredible professor. His calm, easy going nature is so refreshing. He assigned a total of 3 assignments this semester all of which are essays but imo this man's class is worth it. If you pay attention to class you will be fine
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Worth the wait. When it comes to APA formating, he does care much for the title page or abstract, he asks for proper citations and headings/subheadings

Worth it! Nice and flexible professor, replies fast to emails, provides examples and clarification. PowerPoints and APA help are on Bb. 5 assignments in total: 2 quizzes one replacing midterm, one replacing final; 3 papers1 five-page and 2 five-ten pages. Instructions are vague- not all of us know how to write a Lit. review or a Project proposal.

I am taking him right now and holding off 311 until a better fit for me was worth the wait, so far 2 decent sized assignments, the class has easy enough, accessible powerpoints, engaging, shows some videos; replies fast to emails, and encourages questions

Terrible professor, zones out during teaching. Accent too heavy, does not explain but rather just solves and expects students to magically know the reasoning behind whatever steps she took to solve questions. she sometimes randomlys stops reading slides and says "soo yea ok" and skips the slide and jumps to a different topic.
horrible professor, zero communication, say goodbye to your A
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: She's very smart and kind, and really wants to help students, but has no public speaking skills at all. Lectures were very boring; she claimed mandatory attendance, but only started taking it after no one was coming to lectures anymore. The material was fine, but be ready to teach yourself. The textbook was confusing for me, use Khan Academy.

Seems like a nice person, not the best teacher, however. The slideshows felt rushed and were hardly finished in class. You will find yourself self-learning most of the time. However, she did provide lots of materials for help which was nice. Quizzes and Exams are not too hard so long as you study. They were very lenient on grading.
horrible professor

Really nice and caring, will definitely make the effort to help if you need it. Provides a lot of resources and material even outside of lectures and even gives out a fair bit of extra credit. Only real complaint is the pacing because sometimes she'll start a new topic towards the end of class and kinda rush through it, but otherwise she's good

She explained most topics poorly and never fully explained a topic. She rushed all her explanations and the work we were doing in class. She would never finish any of her slideshow presentations and would leave a lot of information uncovered. Almost every class she would start a new topic with 1 minute left in class and never finish the topic.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Dr. Yu was very kind and helpful. Her quizzes and exams were easier than the other 151 professors.
she was cool not as hard as the other ones from what i hear she seems like she cares
Very clear on what will be on quizzes and exams. All you have to do is study the slides she creates and you will be prepared. Quizzes are pretty easy.

She is extremely friendly and creates slides that make it easy to follow her work. By far the easiest quizzes in all of 151 and Tighes students and TA's can attest to this. A lot of the students who dislike her are putting in little to no effort seeing as she makes everything as easy to understand as possible.

She will spend more time fumbling over her own words then she will teach. I am sure she is a lovely person but as a teacher, absolutely not it. You would be more successful just skipping her lectures and teaching yourself the material. But upon realizing 90% of her students don't come to her lectures shes made attendance mandatory. Waste of time.

As a person she sounds kind and tries her best to teach the course, but she lacks in the lectures. She makes it clear about what material you are going to be quizzed on, as well as the exams. Simply study yourself and you will pass the course, considering her grading system is very forgiving. Attendance mandatory but you get credit for showing up.
Most pointless lectures I've ever attended, she constantly seems lost and it feels like she's learning the material with you rather than teaching it.

It is very hard to understand what she is saying as she is breathing into the mic the whole time when talking. When I tell you that you will and must learn by yourself, it is true. I recommend that you not even go to her lectures because they are useless. The TA's are your best bet and the Organic Chemistry Tutor on Youtube.
she is  better than tighe
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This professor lectures very slow. It is hard to understand what she is saying most of the time in the lectures. Dr. Yu often does not finish the unit being worked on in class and the rest of the material is left for you to learn on your own.
she dont know how to teach. cant hear anything she says. dont take this class.

As much as it hurts me to say this Dr. Yu was not a good instructor. Lord knows she tried, but everything she did fell flat. You 100% can skip every lecture and easily pass. Material isn't difficult but have fun learning it on your own.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I am certain that Mingkai Yu is very intelligent and she was very kind as well, but unfortunately she speaks extremely quietly and only reads off of the projector. Very hard to understand because she speaks quietly, I dropped the class in 2 weeks as I didn't learn anything

Very difficult to understand. I stopped going to her lectures in the middle of the semester and my grade improved. TA was also not helpful and constantly made mistakes while reviewing for the weekly quizzes. Stay away.

Her softspoken nature, even when she has a microphone, makes it difficult to hear her well during the lectures. The TA I was assigned pretty much assumed everybody knew the material and frequently made mistakes on the board. She's a nice person, but with indecipherable lectures and discussion sections with a difficult TA, the class was hellish.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This class required me to teach myself. Lectures are just PDF notes that I ended up reviewing in my room. Instructor isn't. You can only pass this class if you take time to study and go over material. Homework's were due every two weeks and had worksheets every Friday. This class has light workload JUST STUDY!!

Terrible professor. She is incapable of actually explaining anything she is teaching. She just projects notes and expects you to know how to solve everything already. Get ready to teach yourself the entire course.

She doesn't know how to explain any of the things she does. She just does it and doesn't explain why she does things a certain way. When someone asks a question that is hard to explain, she either she overcomplicates it or explains something unrelated to the question. I've honestly learned a lot more from the TA in the discussions than from her.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: She does not know her material we. I wished she would finish her example problems and not leave it at you should know how to solve it when the textbook it self does not show problems solved out. My friend and I in the class tried to do the HW assignments and knew the graphs and motions but could not solve the integrals and it was stressful.
Worst professor I had in college.  Worst.
Undrestanding him is a pain, not clear and bores you to death, have to do homework prior him teaching those materials, very nice person though

Can't understand him at ALL. Projects were extremely difficult and it took just as long to make sure you could turn them in correctly using the CVS utility. Your program could be basically done, but if it fails a single test due to a problem with your build file, you'll be lucky to get a 15% on it. Slides are not helpful at all.

Took Artificial Intelligence. I had a hard time understanding him. For the exams I had to use the slides and the book to learn everything on my own. I wish there had been more homework to force me to learn (on my own) throughout the semester since I really didn't get anything out of lecture.
This guy is still teaching? I was there 20 years ago and he is still around. Can NOT speak English -- and is horribly unclear. Avoid this guy.
interesting topics, but somewhat difficult course

Horrible teacher. Reads off of lectures slides found in the text book and online, so if you dont understand those, too bad. He cant explain anything clearly and didnt seem to care how bad you were doing in the class
This guy cannot speak English. You have first to understand what he's trying to say before understanding the material. Avoid taking him at any cost. Take CMSC 341 with Edelman or Oates instead.

Class is easy as long as you go to lecture and do the homework. He randomly gives extra credit for going to lecture, like when it rains or snows. Speaks with an accent but always answers questions clearly. Obviously very knowledge. Made me actually enjoy a math class.
pretty awesome. he gives a good amount of extra credit if you go to the lectures, the tests are pretty easy if you do the practice exams he posts and the homework.

EASY A! EASY A! EASY A! Posts homework keys a day before. Goes over quiz right before quizzing. Goes over exams a class before the exam day. About 7.5% in extra credit. He practically serves an A on a plate.
super easy, but lots of hw
Great teacher.  He goes over Quizzes before you even take the quiz, and give extra credits.  HW are grade based on completion. Easy A class.

My first hybrid class, and now I wish all classes were hybrid. He has a noticeable accent but speaks clear English. If you ask him to clarify something on an exam, he might accidentally(?) end up explaining how to actually do the problem. Take that any way you wish. :) Read the book religiously.

Hybrid class. Each week Dr. Liu will post on blackboard the assigned Chapters, the hmwk assignment, and accompanying PowerPoint presentation. Each week there is a 50 min lecture and a quiz. He goes over problems that will be on the quiz that week.  Also gives extra credit for attending lecture. 3 exams and 1 final.  Can use a formula sheet. Easy A.

He is a very very nice guy, and people do take advantage of him because of this. However, the only thing that makes this class "easy" is because he gives you extra credit to boost you grade up. I do not doubt he is an expert in stats, but it is easier than what it COULD be. I LOVE HIM

If you're looking for an easy class in a busy schedule, I would advise taking this one. A really nice guy. His lectures are super straight forward and simple. He'll answer your questions for you if you're confused; it's really obvious he knows his stuff. Also, his quizzes and tests are easy, usually predictable. He gives extra credit randomly.

This is honestly one of the easiest courses I've ever taken. He gives you extra credit for attending class at the end of the semester as well as for a discussion board post knowing about the syllabus. He's really nice & the class is simple. If you do your homework, and attend class for the quizzes, it's an A. However, don't take advantage of him.
Other than the fact that the final was quite different from the exam review, it was a decent class.

Please dont take this class if you want to learn about portfolio management.  Horrible, final was nothing like the review, which first two test were.  Examples are hard to come by, and his notation doesn't get it done.

First two exam are just like the review sheet he gives you.  The final is nothing like the review.  About 80% didn't finish the final.  Beware of the final, it will not match his review.  50-75 C 75-90 B, 90 A.  Uses alot of greek notation, since clas is alot of math.  Examples are scarce during lecture.

Not clearify in teaching, since eng is not first language. But, it's impossible to fail his class. literally, impossible. He doesn't give out F's, unless u miss the final. Extra ct he gave is literally gift. after he gave out the questions, he'll help u step by step til it's obvious...

Man where do I start.  Try doing his MATLAB project, after his 5minute instruction on how to use the software.  During class lectures if 2 student out of 30 student understands the material,he takes that as "OK we can move onto the next material". His teaching style is extremely difficult to understand, instruction on BB makes no sense what so ever
He is ok. Getting B is not a problem, just do the problems. But his teaching style is hard to adjust to.

Great professor. The material is fairly difficult, but he repeats the important information over and over. Go to class and you will find that his "examples" are the exact problems on the exams. With his major curve, it is hard to fail. I am going to take him again.

The material covered in this class is fairly difficult and I don't think anyone in class knew what the hell was going except some grad student.  However, Dr. Yuan understands this and makes the mid-term and final 1000x easier.  For example, problems on the exam were verbatim of examples in class.  Plus, his curve is ridiculous: a C is 50%.

His tests are really difficult. Grade consists on 3 tests, 2 midterms and 1 cumulative final. He does random extra credit problems during class but you have to show up to get credit. He knows alot about statistics but he's hard.

She is just an amazing professor. She was really trying to teach and help, and not fail.  She gave every opportunity to get a good grade for this course. At the same time, thanks to her, I really understood the subject

Professor Almutawa is such a caring soul and a great teacher. Her lectures were always helpful and she geuinly enjoys teaching. Attending her class gains you extra credit via attendance, along with many reflection assignments to boost your grade. I couldn't ask for a better professor for calculus.
omg I genuinely thought I would fail this class but the extra credits saved me. If it was any other professor I would not have done well. Take her! you won't regret it! She's very kind and generous.
One of the best professors I had so far at UMBC. She offers a lot of resources which makes preparing for exams and quizzes easy.

Professor Zainab is absolutely amazing! Not only does she explain even the trickiest topics with such clarity that they become easy to grasp, but she also generously offers ALOT of extra credit opportunities.She genuinely cares for each of her students and is deeply committed to their success. Professor Zainab is hands down the best teacher ever!!!

Trust me when i say this. This is my first-time taking time out of my day to rate a professor on this site, i'll keep it short and simple she is the best calculus teacher a student could ever wish for, and she made the class very easy to understand. once again, she is the best trust me!!

Overall, it was a good class, and her teaching style is easy to understand. Many extra credit opportunities are given, which will greatly help your grade, so take advantage of quizzes and tests that are manageable as well.Lectures are 50 minutes, which are nice and only a little homework assigned each week.

She's okay. She provides plenty of resources for you to succeed and is generally nice and responsive. I don't think her accent gets in the way of her speech, but I feel she often does not project or enunciate her words, thus it sounds like mumbling. She can also sometimes make small digs in class about students who aren't knowledgeable.

Really nice professor! It was her first time teaching calculus, so a few bumps were given. She was considerate and understanding of students. You could tell that she put in time and effort for the class.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: The professor is very nice, and you can each her during office hours. She has a very thick accent, and small handwriting. You might have weekly ALEKS hw assignments so be prepared for that. The professor also goes through the notes very fast, so she can get to the next lesson.
The sweetest person ever! But she has a very strong accent.

For me, Professor Zayd stands out as an extraordinary teacher, making his class the most engaging and enlightening experience in my college journey. His unique teaching style, combining interactive discussions with practical applications, made all the topics throughout the semester easily understandable and genuinely exciting.

Professor Zayd demonstrated true commitment to his students including myself. His passion for solution engineering made lectures engaging for everyone. Professor's dedication to his students success set him apart from any other professors I've had.

The class was great no question, but the professor is what makes this course. He truly has a passion for helping students with their career. He is a great resource and even brought in industry friends for guest lectures. Take this class if you don't know what you're going to do after college, this WILL set you up for a real-life industry position!!

Professor Zayd is the greatest teacher I have seen. He always starts his class with a story and interacts with everyone. He pushes us to get comfortable with being uncomfortable. He believes every student can do great things. If you're not very confident, his class will really help you. By the end of it, you'll feel ready to take on any challenge.
Learned a lot

The professor is the most human professor I've ever had. This class always felt like I was with my family and learning by coincidence. He makes the class so much more then just a lecture and he makes the class time so valuable. Class was 7:10 - 9:40 and I've never one thought about complaining after the class because it was much more then class.
He is the best professor, he is so good and he is friendly with the students.
Throughout my entire educational journey, Zayd is one my favourite, Not only course wise but also in general Zayd is Awesome.

So great, GOAT professor! He shares valuable real-world/industry experience every lecture, and will even give you career advice. He keeps the class engaged throughout. Only a few assignments and one major group project - you can really tell he wants every student to succeed though, because he'll help you every step of the class. 100% worth it!

Professor was great, very accessible outside of class and actually cared for us. Made the lectures funny can was very engaging. A group project that was fun because he gave it to us early, and every week we were taught things on how to advance our project. Not many assignments at all during the course. Great class and professor, highly recommend!
Really a great teacher.  Wants his students to do well.  Very funny and down to earth, always willing to help outside of class.  Very VERY cute, so prepare to be distracted.

Really young, teaches as a grad student, but he is really knowledgeable, accessible, and caring. He really wants everyone in the class to succeed. He also shares things about modern French culture, which are specific to people in their 20s. Great experience! Also he is really cute, which actually might end up being a little distracting.

I loved Zach as my FREN101 professor. He is simply a very good professor. He takes his time for you to understand and loves to crack a joke or too. Cultured kid, is a rather young professor but humble. He's able to connect with a lot of students and homework is rather easy. French can be a bit difficult for some but if you show up, you'll be fine.

Zak cares about his students individually and will go the extra mile to make sure you are where you need to be in the class. He cares about the course material and also each student and I would personally recommend him to anyone looking to take a french course, plus he's not bad to look at either. :)

She deducted 10% from my grade for a simple mistake, and I went from an "A" to a "B" just like that. You can never figure out what she wants in an assignment. The rules are so subjective that your grade is basically based on how much she "feels" about your work. I'm usually a near straight-A student, and now my GPA has fallen to 3.7.

Professor Zeltzman's class was interesting. I don't think I would take it with her again. While I do believe her class was very helpful and I really appreciated a lot of the activities she did in class, I will say one thing I didn't like was the way she spoke to students. It was at times with a lack of respect, which I could've gone without.

One of my favorite professors at UMBC. show up, put in some effort, and make an appoint to contribute- you'll do fine. She recognizes students who care. She wants students to challenge themselves and makes an appoint to expose them to some really cool artists and photo exercises. art 211  one of my favorite classes. Thanks, Professor Zeltzman :)

She doesn't know how to work a computer. She believes Art is the only thing you have in your life and you need to make time for it at her convenience and not yours. Lots of things must be bought for this class. Requires photography done exactly her way and she cant decide on what requirements she wants to enact. Being in class is easy though
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Didn't respect the students. Pompous and arrogant. Can barely teach an elementary crash course on art. PLEASE STOP TEACHING AND FIND ANOTHER PROFESSION.
She confused me, I dont know her or what she wants. Although she is nice.

Dominique is fair and her teaching methods are very effective. She is well organized and gives good feedback for students to improve. Projects seem to improve for everyone as the semester continued. She is a very nice person.

she is a nice teacher, but she do not know much about computer, not sure that she is the right teacher for this class. It can also be that this is her first year being teacher. It is easy B, If you want A, you MUSH know what she want
Lovely!!!
One of the best professors!!!
Amazing!! She is good!!
Loved her classes, and she told it like it was, didn't sugar coated anything!!
The worst professor I have ever had
Loved her class, super sweet.
She was sweet and oh so smart. My only complaint is that she didn't use the textbook a a a lot but she came up with interesting exercises. Enjoyed her class.
SUPER COOL, AND SCARY SMART!
She is pretty cool. Kind and considerate. Loved her.

Helpful and very sympathetic to what students might be going through. I actually liked her not only as a professor but also as a human being. She is thorough and extremely meticulous and sometimes she expects everybody to be like her as well. She is good at what she does, but I think her talents are wasted by teaching. She should move on to doing s
Too strict for my liking. But she is very good at what she does. I just wish she would let go of the reigns just a little it. Other than that, she is superb.

Loved her class. She is a little bit to strict, but she is very helpful. She needs to stop giving a quiz every week, but apart from that, she is very good in explaining things and overall, super. Just ease up on the quizzes.
Very strict but she knows her staff. Knows how to explain the most difficult concepts with ease and grace. Loved hed!!

Does not know how to teach, gets mad at you when you ask questions. Spent half the semester going over 147 material. No programming examples in class, just instructions that she expects you to do on your own, or pop quizzes every week. She offers no help.

Terrible way of teaching, and apparently doesnt know how.  Goes over slides and at the end tells you to write programming code.  Well how can we do that if you didnt teach us how ? She doesnt use the book and is disorganized.  3 months into the semester, we've learned nothing.  Dont take her.  She'll lower your IQ

Awful.If you are coming up from IS147, stay away from her.No practicing actual coding in class and just going over lecture notes.When we do code she just tells us "do this" and leaves us alone for 20 minutes.  Then gives us the answer right before class ends.This may sound enticing to try and just get an easy grade but I don't recommend her at all.
You will learn a lot if do what you are expected to do.
Good teacher.
Excellent professor! If anybody wants to learn just take his course. His way of delivering lecture is elaborative & understandable. Be ready to hard work & get good marks.
Hard class, but very good teacher. Will learn a lot if work hard
Great teacher.
need to do homeworks. very demanding proof. will lear a lot. he is alwaye willing to help
overall a very good teacher. Very demanding but also very helpfull.
hard class, but very useful.Prof. Manukyam is demanding, but if you go to classes and do your hw regularly you will learn a lot.
very good proof, alittle hard though. You will learn a lot if do what you are expected to do.
one of the worst math teachers I had ever. This guy does not care about undergraduates.

He definately knows his calc, but isn't effective at breaking it down to less advanced (or interested) students. Too much theory, and his accent doesn't help either. Tests are really hard, so be prepared to do lots of homework and study your butt off

I can't say this class was easy. I got the feeling he didn't want to teach our class and would have much prefered to teach a higher level math course. He definatly knows what he is talking about, but has trouble communicating it. Word of advice; GO TO CLASS

Not a good professor at all.  Usually late to class, gave impossibly long assignments, assumed everyone in the class had taken Calc before, taught too much theory rather than application...the list goes on and on.  He's helpful if you have a specific question but try to avoid him at all costs.

He's nice enough, but he's not that clear all the time. The material isn't straight out calculations, there's a lot of math theory. Word of advice, GO TO CLASS. He's helpful enough if you really want to ask him, but you should know what you're asking before hand.
this is class is VERY hard to follow. If you have never taken calc in high school before,like chingching and M.E., YOU ARE SCREWED FOR LIFE!!!!!

Not an easy class, but very nice and willing to help.  Knows the material.  Expect to get alot out if you put the effort in. Teaches like an upper level course, many proofs and theory but if you like math fun

Wow what can i say this guy is pretty hard to understand when your sitting in the very back of the room. The class was very difficult for most of the students because he is just not a very good teacher at all, i mean he is smart and all so i have to give him that but just cant teachhh!!!
Nice guy but has trouble making calculus understadable for the average student. Class average is low compared to other calc 1 instructors. At least he's nice to look at;)

Not too bad of a teacher.  Goes pretty fast, but that is to be expected of a calc course.  Most of the class seems to be having trouble though.  Takes off mad points for little mistakes though.  I suggest going to class.

Class was easy, participation not really necessary. However this professor is crazy! Do NOT call her professor Forsyth, she insists that you call her Dr. Warwick (even though everything about her at UMBC is under the name forsyth). She is incredibly rude and opinionated, even refusing to answer any questions from students. Class is very boring too.

She goes out of her way to make things regarding the course more difficult for you. Lectures from the book only, & makes what could be very interesting subject material extremely boring. Useless when I went in for help. Has the attitude that all college kids are just looking an easy A, & treats you accordingly.
She is just okay.

Had him for ENME 408 and 332L. Dr. Zupan is a great professor who cares about his students. You will have to work and put in effort. 332L was a lot of written reports and sometimes grading criteria was unclear. However, the benefits of having him outweigh the drawbacks. Global was one of the funnest and most enlightening courses I've taken at UMBC.

I would suggest don't take this professor if you want to get good grades. It is all about grades and by the end of the day, all your struggle goes to vain only because of their tough grading compared to other classes. Be ready to write lot of technical reports and even if you write really good, there will always be something that they will point.

Lab reports are the bulk of this class. You must form your own groups and write a lot. Zupan works hard to help but this course is a lot of work. He knows the material and will help if you ask questions.

Lab reports are most difficult part of the class. He explains things sounding like it makes complete sense. Then when you go to do it, you find multiple things unclear. Lecture structure is unlike any other, but more realistic to life than any other. I learned much from him. Grading is a little inconsistent. He cares deeply about the subject.

He is one of the worst. Really tough grading. I've never gotten a C, and I'm worrying that I will fail thus class. Takes forever to get a feedback. Doesn't cover important things in lecture. Groups are loosely formed, so if you can't write well, you'll  get dropped out of group and he doesn't give a crap. Then you have to write reports alone. Avoid

Not your typical course.  You video conference with a University in Portugal and work in teams on global projects. Zupan is helpful, but you have to ask and you will do well. If you want to just read a book and do homework don't take this course.

We Skyped with a university in Portugal every class.  The assignments forced us to work with the students in Portugal, and they put absolutely no effort into them.  I got bad grades on reports solely because who I was working with in Portugal didn't do their work.  I heard Zupan is a good professor for other classes, but definitely not this one.

Great Teacher. If you wanna good grade he requires you to work HARD. However if you wanna be an engineer that generally goes without saying. Also took him for ENME 332L. The class was particularly difficult however a lot of that had to do with the grad students who graded the papers. I continuously found that they made incorrect corrections.

Can be cryptic about information in his lectures. Expect to spend a LOT of time writing lab reports - don't start these the night before. Seriously. If you work hard on the lab reports the exams are very doable. A really hard class, but you can learn a ton if you put in the work. Very willing to work with students who put in the study time.

I liked him in 301 but 332L is another story. By far the most difficult class I've taken so far. I've never gotten below a B in my entire college career and now I'm fighting for a C in this class. He grades insanely hard. Lab reports with few/minor errors will earn you a 65-75 with no real explanation why your grade is so poor. No curve either.
best teacher i ve ever had in my 4 years at umbc. great lectures, if you study a bit you ll do great. He is a really helpfull professor and funny too. Take a class with him if you can

He spends the entire semester acting like God's gift to teaching. DON'T BUY THE HYPE!  He can't properly explain slip planes, which is half of the course. It's a shame; it was his thesis work, and he'll destroy your grade if you don't know it. He plays favorites; suck up as much as possible. He loves art on exams, so make sure you're very talented.

Awesome teacher, material science could be brutally boring, but he makes it very interesting.  Quizzes are the toughest part, basically just short exams.  Otherwise everything is fairly predictable and fair.
helpful, eagar to get his ideas across

For 301 students Prof Zupan is good, and attendence is not mandatory however if you miss a lecture good luck on knowing how to study the posted lecture notes. Uses lots of charts and graphs and the in class lectures explain the specifics of them. Class is fun and time goes by fast, grades tough during either the first, or the second half semester
The best teacher I've ever had.  Zupan knows how to teach.  Take this class with him.
No Comments

I'm not sure about the previous comment, I've had Zup for two classes and he is definitely one of the most organized professors I've had, especially in the ME department.  His lectures are well prepared and he keeps you interested. He's pretty approachable outside of class. My only problem is he seems to grade pretty tough and play favorites.
he has no common sense, he is not orgonized, he cannot deliver the course and he covers on that with jokes.
Really good professor. Definitely take one of his classes if you have a chance. He actually makes the course as interesting as it can be instead of just talking at you and boring you.
No Comments

Professor Zwi was super nice but oh my god the amount of reading we have to do for this class is insane. You have to read up to 40 pages in a single week, and write a single-spaced, 2 page essay every week. Get prepared to read and interpret some confusing readings if you take this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--So many papers

reviews.comment: It has been amazing working with Dr. Zwi for the last several semesters. His teaching is about so much more than just playing the guitar. He is always pushing his students to think beyond the instrument and to make music on a higher artistic level.
On point. Best class I have ever taken. Best teacher I've ever had.

One thing I would agree on with the previous review: His lectures are amazing. Zwi is a super smart Renaissance man so he seems to forget that a First Year Seminar is for people who never even took college level English. Be prepared to write 2.5 pages each week + 5 page final. A lot of work, unclear grading criteria, not even midterm grade posted.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--SO MANY PAPERS

reviews.comment: We just got done with the last week of lectures for this class. If you are willing to work your ass off with some insanely complex readings, this will be the best class you ever take at UMBC.

I originally came in terrified about this class, but I love it!! The Reading Ensemble is def my favorite class (its actually fun) and as a guitarist I don't know how no one ever taught me these things before. After years of playing guitar, some things are finally coming together for me. Thanks prof. Zwi!

This class is one of a kind! I expected to learn a little bit about art and music, but we ended up getting into the underlying nature of existence. I didnt even know you could get so deep into these subjects, but it's amazing how professor Zwi can expand any topic. This class is fascinating and, if you do the reading, you will get a lot out of it.

Jonathan is a wonderful teacher. He focuses on getting students to play with musicality no matter their experience or skill level. Lesson plans are tailored to individuals' strengths and weaknesses, and a strong emphasis is put on teaching problem solving so you can use his advice when he's not around. He wants to see you succeed.

Tons of work outside of class, and is unclear on how/when to turn things in. The syllabus is missing so much information. He spends more time showing us how to teach simple theory, and concepts we learn in ACTUAL education classes than guitar. Be prepared to learn guitar from the internet because you wont learn it well in this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--SO MANY PAPERS

reviews.comment: Currently in a 1 credit guitar class yet he assigns 2-4 page papers weekly, an hour and a half of logged practice per week, detailed practice journals weekly, and we have to make a website with videos, articles, and assignments (also updated weekly).He's condescending and doesn't give helpful instruction during class so you have to teach yourself.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--SO MANY PAPERS

reviews.comment: the prof is relatively dry it can be excruciating to sit in class for 1.5 hour but the material is so easy & can be taught to oneself that you dont really need to stay in class also the midterm questions were given in advance & a lot of help was provided for the final paper making it a really easy but boring WI 400 level class I didnt go & got an A

if you're a senior looking for a WI run she's so stale, dry and boring, its like watching paint dry in her class there are so many assignments and I feel like Im wasting my life away in this class that had the potential of being so interesting had it been taught by a different prof. I regret signing up for it. i ditched the first month of classes
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--SO MANY PAPERS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Hands down the most boring, useless class. No matter what professor, this class is useless. Didn't help that this teacher was the most boring and stale when lecturing, so much so that I stopped coming to class although there were graded activities taking place. It's a hybrid course, and everything's done online. Those were pretty easy assignments.

Her lectures are VERY BORING. SO BORING that I stopped coming to class. She doesn't grade hard and she's nice. You will need the book and the homework will come from readings.  Class lectures were pretty much her repeating what you read, so it wasn't really helpful. If you're a senior looking for a WI, don't take this.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: She is a good professor, her lectures can get boring but I learnt about random things i didn't know about in that class. There is alot of online assignments and quizzes but if you do them all, you are pretty much guaranteed an A.

Her class was only once a week for 50 minutes everything else is online. Must stay on top of assignments there is A LOT but very easy class, just a lot of assignments online. Offers 2 extra credit opportunities. Easy A

Warwick is a pretty good professor. She tends to read from powerpoints all class. She tries to get people up and moving on occasion but it doesn't always work out.  Midterm and Final are very easy as long as you read.

I felt that the class itself is really self explained.  No attendance so you really don't need to be in lecture, unless you want to. I found her exams to be pretty difficult, unless you give up your soul and really digest the chapters that you need to read for the exam. Final is optional but it is cumulative so there is a TON so study.

Does not take attendance, but it is basically a bio course so attend lecture for clarification on slides. Save your quiz answers! Gives a lot of extra credit and optional final to boost your grade. She can be a little bit monotone and meticulous when it comes to the material but overall a sweet & creative professor. Her examples will make you laugh

She is very nice and helpful. But be prepared to work hard on your papers. the major paper is killer because the instructions are so vague. she takes attendance everyday! Mid-term was super easy. no final, just a major paper. total of 3 other assignment papers which are fairly easy.be sure to keep up with the articles and book chapters!

Warwick is a great prof! I liked physiological psych and was interested in the material. I'd suggest buying the hard-copy of the book; I missed half of the readings because the e-book wasn't user friendly! Exams and quizzes are easy, extra credit galore. Really helpful in finding research too!

It's like a bio course so expect it to be hard.  There is a study guide but it's vague so make sure you know all about what terms she refers to on it.  Get the E-book it's a lot better and easier.  Do all the cengage assignments and take the optional final.  Hard but if you study hard it should not be that bad. Drops lowest test grade. Responsive.

She's the most annoying.  Attending lecture is pointless.  You don't need to take notes because she posts her slides.  Read the book even though it's more info than you need.  Tests are easy and she gives out so much extra credit and an optional final to replace a lower earlier score.

The exams do get harder as you go along. I did not attend her classes just because she read off the slides. What I did was read the entire textbook (whatever chapters for that week) and took notes. She gives out study guides which is EXTREMELY helpful. Then out of no where she gives an insane amount of extra credit. She is also SUPER sweet!

I thought she was a great professor for this class.  Make sure you go to all lectures and discussions, study starting at least a week before for the exams and you will definitely get an A.  I had also taken STAT 121 before this and the material from that class helped a lot.
Great Professor. Easy class. 4 small assignments= short essay, one mid-term, one major paper about 6-10 pages. Extra credit worth 40 points.

I enjoyed her class. She is funny despite how hard the material was. She hands out a study guide with what she will ask you on the exams. She also gives an optional exam at the end of the year, with many of the same questions from the first 4. You can replace your lowest exam score, and you have the opportunity for 100 points extra credit!

She is okay. Exams are HARD. Impossible to receive anything above a C if you do not study for more then 2 hours a week. But she gives out extra credit which can bring you up a letter grade. I suggest you attend all lectures and lab and do all the homework assignment and you should recieve nothing less than a C. She is very nice though.
Her tests are fair, but require studying. Attendance is not mandetory, and all the slides are online. Being is class is beneficial because she makes everything very clear. Great for 331.
shez pretty good. her tests are very hard though she likes to teach every little detail, but there'z a paper on ur class reflection which is an easy 10% of your grade and gives good extra credit

Extremely hard tests. The whole semester you think you will fail this class. Then, she gives you 100 points of extra credit just for writing two short papers. Plus you can take an optional final to replace one of your exam grades, and it is SO much easier than the exams. I ended up with a B, only because I did so badly earlier in the semester.

Tests are extremely difficult. I studied pretty hard for them and I think my highest grade on the tests and I think my highest grade out of the 3 I took was an 88.something. That being said she allowed us to do 2 EC assignments adding up to 10% of the final grade total, more generous than I've seen any other teacher do. Didn't have to take final, A
No matter how hard I study, I cannot compete with her tests.

She is a very clear teacher and if you are having any trouble she  is good at making the time to help out, even thouh she has huge classes and she does make sure you understand what is being taught.  If you slack of though you are going to have trouble making it.  She grades and tests fairly, you just have to put the time and effort in.

the class wasnt hard, but you have to go. The exams were harder than I expected, but there are some easy things like assignments and quizzes to make up for it. If you go to class and study a lot for the exams, i guess you will do well
good teacher. my only complaint is that we spent a month reviewing things like 'what do mode mean and median mean'
she was probably the best prof to take this class with. she made it a painless as possible. she runs it like most of her other classes. online quizzes etc.
No Comments

This class is easy if you put in a solid effort.  If you don't you'll fall behind and it'll be hard to catch up.  I took it with a friend...I normally went to lecture; she never did.  We studied together, but she really didn't know the material like she should have if she attended.  I got an A, she got a C.  It may be long & boring, but go anyway!

She is very nice and gives you part of your notes.  Fill in the blanks and you will be fine for the tests.  There is no book.  Tests are essay and definitions but if you took notes you will be fine.  Interesting class.

This is a stat class...lots of information, but she explains everything very clearly.  You don't have to go to lecture, but you really should.  You can't learn everything from just the lab portion...you'll be totally confused.  At least print out her lecture notes.  Extra credit worth 6% on the final grade, too!!  Excellent class!!

This class was very laid back and easy going.  No need to attend lecture, as long as you attend lab and follow the syllabus reading's/assignments you'll do fine.  She offers extra credit to bring you up a full letter grade, and lab provides you with questions very similar to exams/quizzes.  Can drop 2 quizzes and 1 homework!

dr. warwick makes 331 interesting by relating the material to her own experiments and even jokes around sometimes, the lecture isn't too bad, its the TA's you have to watch out for! they can be tough graders
Pretty decent class.  Keep up with readings, go to class and the lab.  You'll do fine.  Boring material, but if you're required to take it for the PSYC major, go with Warwick.

Dr Warwick is the best. I've had her for PSYC 331, 335 and 363.  She leans on the physiological side of things though, which may surprise many. I liked it though.  FAIRest grader at UMBC (extra credit to bump you up a letter grade!).  Hard classes but clear teacher. You get an A if you put the time
She is the best teacher to have for 331.  She explains things to your as if you are stupid.  Her midterm and final exam are worth tons of points and they are both really hard.
She's a nice lady.  The lectures are extremely boring and the material very dry.  But she grades easy and the tests aren't too bad...
Very nice and willing to answer questions.  Only problem is her tests are HARD even if you know the material.
She is a wonderful teacher for Psyc 331 and Psyc 363, but WATCH OUT for Psyc 335 (Physiological).  The tests are so hard it's like they're in another language.
She is a wonderful teacher for Psyc 331 and Psyc 363, but WATCH OUT for Psyc 335 (Physiological).  The tests are so hard it's like they're in another language.
Very good teacher for clarity, consistency, and managable workload
She's the best prof for 331!!!

Not a great teacher. Makes the subject very difficult without giving much help. I love calculus in general but after taking his class, I just want to get it over with. Homework is not too difficult grading is inconsistent on homework and exams. Exams are very hard and half of the class failed the 1st exam. Please try to find a different teacher.

Dr. Zweck is a difficult professor, but you will learn a lot from him if you care. He has high expectations, and he is willing to help you if you seek him out. His homework and tests are difficult, so working with others and asking him good questions is imperative to do well. He good professor overall, especially if you want to actually learn.

The hard exams and large homework load are trivial compared to how much understanding of the material that is gained from having him as a professor. He is very helpful, but he requires you to think on your own. His lectures are engaging, and he explains hard concepts with clarity. He is hands down the best math professor I have taken.
Avoid him if you are taking more than 5 classes!This Dude is Crazy!! He is a very good teacher, however, his homework problem set are long, and hard.

Best math teacher I have ever had. Even though his tests are tough and my grade suffered, I came out knowing so much. Very clear and understandable with concepts. Definitely worth having him as a teacher if you want to learn a lot.
